roles.title: Nuclear Medicine Technologists
aliases: Nuclear Medicine PET-CT Technologist (Nuclear Medicine Positron Emission Tomography - Computed Tomography Technologist)
roles.description: Prepare, administer, and measure radioactive isotopes in therapeutic, diagnostic, and tracer studies using a variety of radioisotope equipment. Prepare stock solutions of radioactive materials and calculate doses to be administered by radiologists. Subject patients to radiation. Execute blood volume, red cell survival, and fat absorption studies following standard laboratory techniques.

tasks.label: Administer radiopharmaceuticals or radiation intravenously to detect or treat diseases, using radioisotope equipment, under direction of a physician.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine outpatient SPECT tracer injection (Tc-99m MDP bone scan, sestamibi, MAG3, HIDA, etc.) in a hospital or freestanding nuclear medicine department: verify patient ID and dose, apply tourniquet, prep skin, place a 21-23G winged needle in an antecubital/forearm vein of a cooperative adult with visible veins, inject the shielded unit dose, saline flush, withdraw needle, bandage, dispose of radioactive sharps and document activity/time/site.

PET tracer administration (18F-FDG, 18F-PSMA, 68Ga-DOTATATE) in a PET/CT suite: establish peripheral IV access on an adult, connect the patient administration line, deliver the weight-based dose (commonly via an automated dose-on-demand infusion cart), flush, then place the patient in a quiet uptake room for the prescribed interval before imaging.

Adult with difficult peripheral venous access in the same department: elderly, obese, dehydrated, or oncology/chemotherapy patients with fragile, rolling or scarred veins; requires vein-finding (palpation, NIR/ultrasound), warming, small-gauge needle, careful low-pressure injection, sometimes a second attempt or a second technologist.

Pediatric, cognitively impaired, or highly anxious patient, or administration through an existing central venous catheter, implanted port or PICC: requires distraction/comforting, immobilization or parent/nurse assistance, or sterile port access with saline/heparin protocol and confirmation of blood return before injecting the radiopharmaceutical.

Cardiac perfusion study injections timed to stress: mostly pharmacologic stress (regadenoson/adenosine) with the tracer delivered through a pre-placed IV line at the prescribed moment, including Rb-82 rest/stress PET where an elution/infusion system delivers activity to the patient line; a minority are treadmill studies with a bolus injected at peak exercise.

Therapeutic radiopharmaceutical administration (Lu-177 DOTATATE/PSMA slow 20-30 minute infusion, Ra-223 bolus) in a dedicated shielded therapy injection room: dedicated access, co-infusions and antiemetics, continuous patient observation for reactions and extravasation, contamination control, survey and post-dose radiation safety instructions.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: The Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy ... performed venipunctures autonomously on 1,633 patients in three Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments (Amsterdam UMC, St. Antonius, OLVG Lab) in routine practice, with one supervising professional overseeing up to three devices; first-stick success was 94.5%, holding up in difficult-access, obese and elderly patients, with only mild adverse events at 0.6%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. The physical act is the same one that dominates radiopharmaceutical administration: autonomous imaging-guided insertion of a 21G winged needle set into a peripheral arm vein of a seated outpatient, including tourniquet, skin prep and bandaging; only the direction of fluid flow differs, and dose delivery through the placed access is itself performed by commercial automated injectors.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device – CAP TODAY
sources.claim: Aletta is CE-marked and performs the complete blood-draw sequence from tourniquet application and skin prep through vein identification, needle insertion, tube handling and ... using AI-driven Doppler ultrasound guidance.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: the cited capability is autonomous peripheral venipuncture in a clinical outpatient room, the access step of intravenous radiopharmaceutical administration.

tasks.label: Detect and map radiopharmaceuticals in patients' bodies, using a camera to produce photographic or computer images.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine planar/whole-body study on a cooperative ambulatory adult in the nuclear medicine camera room (e.g., 3-phase or whole-body bone scan, thyroid, lung V/Q, parathyroid): verify patient and tracer, select collimator and protocol, lie patient supine with arms positioned, run whole-body sweep and/or SPECT with detectors contoured close to the body, check images for motion/adequacy, reconstruct and send to PACS.

Gated cardiac SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging: patient supine (or prone) with arms above head, ECG gating electrodes applied, 180-degree or 360-degree acquisition with gating, check for patient motion and attenuation artifacts, automated quantitative processing (gated wall motion, perfusion polar maps), repeat views if needed.

PET/CT oncology study (e.g., FDG, PSMA, DOTATATE) on a cooperative adult: position on the PET/CT table with arms up and immobilization cradle, acquire low-dose CT for attenuation correction plus multi-bed PET emission scan over 20-30 minutes, reconstruct with attenuation/scatter correction, review fusion images and SUV quantitation.

Dynamic or multi-phase study requiring timed acquisitions and intra-exam intervention: renal scan with mid-study furosemide via an indwelling line, hepatobiliary scan with CCK and delayed views, gastric emptying with timed 1/2/4-hour images, or add-on SPECT/CT and lateral/pinhole views decided from the initial frames.

Non-ambulatory, confused, painful, or pediatric patient in the camera room: transfer from wheelchair or stretcher onto the imaging table, immobilize (papoose, straps, sandbags), manage lines and drains, monitor a sedated patient, re-position and re-acquire when the patient moves during a 20-40 minute scan.

Imaging outside the standard camera room: portable gamma camera or uptake probe brought to an ICU bedside or the operating room (e.g., bedside lung perfusion, shunt study, sentinel node probe counting, thyroid uptake), positioning the detector over a patient in a bed and acquiring usable counts amid monitors, ventilators and staff.

tasks.label: Calculate, measure, and record radiation dosage or radiopharmaceuticals received, used, and disposed, using computer and following physician's prescription.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General nuclear medicine hot lab in a hospital/imaging center: unit-dose syringes of 99mTc radiopharmaceuticals arrive from a commercial nuclear pharmacy in lead pigs. Tech checks each against the physician's order, assays the syringe in the dose calibrator, decay-corrects to injection time, confirms it falls within tolerance of the prescribed activity, and records assayed activity, time, lot and patient in the department computer/dose log.

PET/CT center: patient-weight-based 18F-FDG dose computed from the physician's protocol, drawn from a multi-dose vial in the hot lab, assayed in the dose calibrator, decay-corrected to injection time, residual assayed after injection, and net administered activity recorded in the computer/RIS-PACS record.

Generator work: daily elution of a 99mTc generator (or Rb-82 generator in a cardiac PET lab); measure eluate activity, compute concentration (mCi/mL) and required volumes, perform and record the breakthrough/QC ratio calculation, and log the elution and remaining inventory in the computer.

Radionuclide therapy: prescribed activity of 177Lu-DOTATATE, I-131, 90Y or 223Ra calculated per physician's prescription (fixed, weight-based or dosimetry-based), the dose assayed in a dose calibrator in the correct geometry before and after administration, and administered/residual activity recorded in the therapy and licensee records.

Receipt of radioactive material shipments in the hospital hot lab: open and inspect the shipping package, measure surface and 1 m exposure rates with a survey meter, perform and count a wipe test, reconcile contents against the packing slip and prescriptions, and enter received activity, lot and calibration time into the licensee's inventory computer.

Radioactive waste and residual accounting: survey decay-in-storage waste bags, sharps containers, vials and syringe shields with a survey meter to confirm they read background, deface/remove labels, and record activity used, decayed and disposed in the computerized isotope inventory and disposal log.

sources.title: MEDRAD Intego PET Infusion System 510(k) Summary K080297
sources.claim: The MEDRAD Intego PET Infusion ... is an FDA-cleared, self-contained shielded cart used in hospital nuclear medicine departments that automatically measures each patient's FDG dose in an integrated dose calibrator, allows dosing by activity or activity per patient weight, and retains and prints dispensing records.

tasks.label: Produce a computer-generated or film image for interpretation by a physician.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General planar / whole-body study (bone scan, HIDA, thyroid uptake, renal, gastric emptying) at the acquisition workstation in a hospital nuclear medicine department: technologist reviews raw frames for motion and artifact, sets intensity scaling and windowing, builds static views and cine loops, annotates markers/laterality, and pushes the completed image set to PACS for the reading physician.

SPECT or SPECT/CT study (bone SPECT/CT, parathyroid, DaTscan, V/Q): technologist runs iterative reconstruction, applies attenuation/scatter/motion correction, reorients into orthogonal planes, fuses emission with CT, generates MIP cines, verifies registration quality, and archives the reconstructed series to PACS.

Myocardial perfusion SPECT (rest/stress) processing on a cardiac workstation: gated reconstruction, axis reorientation into short/vertical/horizontal long axis, polar (bull's-eye) map and quantitative perfusion scoring, LV ejection fraction and wall-motion outputs, side-by-side stress/rest display assembled for the cardiologist.

PET/CT oncology or neuro study (FDG, PSMA, amyloid, cardiac viability): technologist checks PET-CT co-registration, applies SUV normalization with correct dose/weight/time inputs, creates rotating MIP, corrects for respiratory misregistration artifacts, and transfers fused series to PACS or a dedicated review platform.

Legacy or special-request hard-copy output: printing selected images to laser film for an operating room or outside referral, exporting a de-identified image set to CD/USB, or producing screenshot images to accompany a report when digital access is unavailable.

tasks.label: Prepare stock radiopharmaceuticals, adhering to safety standards that minimize radiation exposure to workers and patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Morning hot-lab routine in a hospital nuclear medicine department: elute the 99Mo/99mTc generator behind an L-block, assay the eluate in the dose calibrator, check Mo-99/Al breakthrough, then reconstitute several cold kits (MDP, sestamibi with a heating bath, MAA, mebrofenin) with measured eluate volumes, mix/incubate, record activities, lot numbers and times, and run radiochemical-purity TLC before release for patient use.

Drawing individual patient unit doses of a 99mTc radiopharmaceutical from the prepared multidose vial into shielded syringes throughout the day: decay-corrected volume calculation, draw behind an L-block with syringe shield, assay each syringe in the dose calibrator, adjust, label, cap, and load into a lead pig for delivery to the imaging room.

PET stock preparation and dispensing: receiving a multi-dose bulk vial of 18F-FDG (or eluting a 68Ge/68Ga generator and labeling a PET tracer), dispensing weight/activity-specific patient doses behind tungsten shielding, assaying, labeling, and transporting in a tungsten pig, with contamination surveys.

Therapy radiopharmaceutical preparation in the hospital hot lab: assaying and preparing I-131 capsules/solution, 177Lu-DOTATATE or 177Lu-PSMA patient doses, or Y-90 handling, using heavy shielding, spill trays and remote handling tools, with post-work swipe surveys and dose records.

In-vitro cell labeling at the bench: withdrawing patient blood, sedimentation/centrifugation and washing steps, incubating leukocytes with 99mTc-HMPAO or red cells with the UltraTag 99mTc kit, resuspending, assaying the labeled dose, and maintaining sterile, patient-identity-critical technique.

Centralized/commercial nuclear pharmacy or hospital GMP radiopharmacy batch work: bulk generator elution, batch kit compounding and aseptic dispensing of multi-dose vials and unit-dose syringes in ISO-classified laminar-flow hot cells for a scheduled delivery run, with full documentation and QC.

tasks.label: Explain test procedures and safety precautions to patients and provide them with assistance during test procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ambulatory adult outpatient in a hospital or imaging-center nuclear medicine suite (bone scan, PET/CT, HIDA, thyroid uptake): technologist greets the patient, explains the tracer, imaging steps, timing and radiation-safety precautions, answers questions, then helps the patient up onto the imaging table, positions arms/legs, places headrest, wedges and straps, drapes a blanket, coaches them to hold still, reassures and monitors through a 20-45 minute acquisition, then helps them off the table.

Frail, elderly, post-operative or wheelchair/stretcher-bound inpatient: explanation given simply and often repeated to patient and family, then a physical transfer from stretcher or wheelchair onto the camera table using slide board, draw sheet or lift with a second staff member, managing IV lines, oxygen and drains, positioning limbs of a patient who cannot cooperate, watching for pain or distress, and returning the patient to the ward.

Myocardial perfusion / cardiac stress study: technologist explains the exercise or pharmacologic stress protocol, side effects and safety precautions, obtains cooperation, preps and places ECG leads, supports the patient on the treadmill or recliner, coaches and physically steadies them, watches for chest pain, dizziness or collapse, injects at peak stress, then assists the patient onto the gamma camera for rest and stress imaging.

Pediatric, anxious, claustrophobic or cognitively impaired patient: age-appropriate or simplified explanation, calming and distraction, coaching the parent, then hands-on gentle immobilization (papoose, sandbags, tape, holding a limb), repositioning mid-scan when the patient moves, and continuous physical reassurance so usable images are obtained without sedation.

Radionuclide therapy patient (I-131 thyroid ablation, Lu-177, Y-90, Ra-223): detailed explanation of the therapy and of home/family radiation-safety precautions with written instructions and confirmation of understanding, plus hands-on assistance during administration and, for inpatient therapy, escorting and settling the patient in the isolation room.

Bedside/portable or ED/ICU study, and multi-part studies with interruptions (gastric emptying, renal, ventilation scan): explanation to a critically ill, intubated or sedated patient and to nursing staff, positioning the patient in bed under the portable camera, helping with the radiolabeled meal or aerosol mouthpiece, and assisting the patient to the restroom or to reposition between images.

sources.title: Robotic patient transfer device launches at Ottawa hospital | CBC News
sources.claim: The ALTA Platform is a robotic patient-transfer device rolled out in Canadian hospitals; a staff member positions it beside the bed and initiates a lateral transfer with a button press. It moves an immobile patient between surfaces but does not explain procedures, position a patient for imaging, or work without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is lateral patient transfer, a sub-step of assisting patients onto an imaging table. It does not transfer: the device is operator-driven, handles only flat bed-to-platform moves, and provides none of the explanation, positioning, immobilization or in-scan monitoring the nuclear medicine task requires.

sources.title: Japan's teddy bear nurse robot gets a softer touch | PCWorld
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the best-known patient-lifting humanoid, remained an experimental prototype that required a human operator, was never commercialized, and the RIKEN project was closed in 2015.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is lifting/transferring a patient. It fails to substantiate the imaging-assistance task because the machine is operator-controlled, never left prototype status, and performs no explanation, table positioning or patient monitoring.

sources.title: Electrocardiogram and respiration recordings show a reduction in the physical burden on professional caregivers when performing care tasks with a transfer support robot
sources.claim: Fuji's Hug is a commercially sold transfer-support robot used in nursing facilities; it lifts a care recipient at the push of a ... but requires a caregiver to set it up and a cooperative recipient who leans on and steers the device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is assisted patient transfer from bed to wheelchair. It does not carry over: the robot is a caregiver-operated lifting aid dependent on the patient's own cooperation, and performs no procedure explanation, imaging positioning, or supervision during a scan.

tasks.label: Perform quality control checks on laboratory equipment or cameras.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-day gamma camera QC in a hospital nuclear medicine imaging room: technologist retrieves a Co-57 sheet flood source (or Tc-99m point source) from shielded storage, positions it on/above the collimated or uncollimated detector head, peaks the camera and sets the energy window, acquires a 5-15 million count flood, inspects for non-uniformity/PMT or crystal defects, and logs pass/fail before the first patient.

Daily dose calibrator QC in the hot lab: check zero/background, take the sealed reference source (Cs-137, Co-57 or Ba-133) from its lead pig or source drawer, seat it on the dipper and lower it into the well, read activity on the relevant isotope settings, compare with the decay-corrected expected value against +/-5-10% limits, and log results.

Daily PET/CT QC: run the PET detector/normalization check (internal or Ge-68 source depending on vendor), warm up the CT tube and run the daily CT calibration/water-phantom check by placing the phantom in the gantry holder, review noise/CT-number/artifact and PET block/coincidence results, then release the scanner for clinical use.

Weekly to quarterly extended camera QC with solid test objects: place a four-quadrant bar phantom on the detector for spatial resolution and linearity, acquire high-count floods for collimator/uniformity correction maps, run SPECT center-of-rotation with a point source in a holder on the table, and compare results to baselines.

QC on counting instruments: well counter/automatic gamma counter and thyroid uptake probe - background count, energy peaking with a sealed standard (Cs-137/Co-57), constancy, chi-square reproducibility and efficiency, plus counting of wipe-test tubes; results compared to tolerance and logged.

Periodic non-camera equipment QC: quarterly dose calibrator accuracy with multiple NIST-traceable standards, linearity by decay method or nested lead sleeve sets, geometry check with varying volumes; plus daily response checks of survey meters and contamination monitors against a dedicated check source with battery and background verification.

tasks.label: Dispose of radioactive materials and store radiopharmaceuticals, following radiation safety procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine daily disposal of hot-lab waste in a hospital or outpatient imaging center: used unit-dose syringes, needles, empty vials, elution vial shields, gloves, absorbent bench pads and tubing generated during dose draw-up and injection are segregated by isotope/half-life, dropped into lead-shielded sharps and waste containers, dated/labeled, and moved to the decay-in-storage area; activity and container logs completed.

Receiving and storing radiopharmaceuticals in the hot lab: unit-dose syringes in lead pigs and Tc-99m generator/cold kits arrive by courier; technologist surveys the package exterior, wipe-tests, logs receipt against the manifest, places doses in the lead-shielded safe or refrigerator behind an L-block, and retrieves them in order during the day while keeping inventory records.

Decay-in-storage management and release: after 10+ half-lives the stored bags/sharps containers are retrieved from the decay room, surveyed at contact with a GM survey meter in a low-background area, radiation labels removed or defaced, waste released into the ordinary or regulated-medical waste stream, and survey results recorded for the RSO.

Therapy and long-lived isotope material: storing I-131 capsules, Lu-177 or Y-90 doses in shielded safes, handling and disposing of their vials, shields and used injection sets, and packaging the spent Tc-99m generator or therapy shipping container with surveys and DOT labeling for vendor return pickup.

Contamination/spill response and patient-area radioactive waste: a dose spilled in an injection bay, camera room or therapy room, or contaminated linens, chux and urine containers, must be contained, absorbed, bagged as radioactive waste, and the floor, equipment and staff surveyed and decontaminated until below release limits, with documentation.

tasks.label: Maintain and calibrate radioisotope and laboratory equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-day dose calibrator QC in the hospital hot lab: retrieve the dedicated sealed check source (Cs-137 or Co-57) from the source safe, run auto-zero/background, insert the source in the well on every routinely used isotope setting, compare each reading with the decay-corrected expected value (plus/minus 10%), record in the QC log/software, and flag out-of-tolerance results before any patient dose is assayed.

Daily/weekly gamma camera (SPECT and SPECT/CT) QC in the camera room: peak the detectors on the Tc-99m/Co-57 photopeak, place a Co-57 sheet flood source (or filled fillable flood phantom) on the detector face or acquire an intrinsic flood with a point source, acquire several million counts, inspect and quantify uniformity, run weekly four-quadrant bar-phantom resolution/linearity and center-of-rotation checks, and document.

Daily PET/CT QC before the first patient: run the scanner's detector/normalization QC routine (placing and centering a Ge-68 or Na-22 cylinder phantom in the gantry on source-based systems, or launching the vendor's source-free automated routine), perform CT tube warm-up and air calibration, review pass/fail metrics and act on failures.

Non-imaging instrument checks in the hot lab and department: daily battery/response constancy checks of GM and ion-chamber survey meters against a button check source, energy calibration and efficiency/constancy checks of the well counter and thyroid uptake probe with standard sources, background counts, and counting the weekly wipe-test samples in the well counter with results logged for the license file.

Periodic (quarterly/annual) dose calibrator tests: accuracy against NIST-traceable standard sources, linearity over the clinical activity range by the decay method or graded lead sleeves, and geometry/volume dependence using varying volumes in vials and syringes, with calculation of correction factors and records kept for NRC/agreement-state inspection.

Preventive maintenance, cleaning and troubleshooting across the department: wiping down and decontaminating camera heads, tables and hot-lab bench, filling/emptying and mixing a fillable flood phantom with Tc-99m, exchanging collimators, replacing injector/infusion tubing and other consumables, changing generator shielding components, minor repairs and assisting the field service engineer during scheduled service.

tasks.label: Measure glandular activity, blood volume, red cell survival, or radioactivity of patient, using scanners, Geiger counters, scintillometers, or other laboratory equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine gamma-camera/SPECT(-CT) acquisition on an ambulatory outpatient in the hospital nuclear medicine suite (bone scan, myocardial perfusion, renal, hepatobiliary): verify patient/dose, position the patient supine with arms placed and immobilized, bring the detector heads to within a few centimetres of the body without contact, run the timed acquisition, watch the patient and count statistics, reposition or repeat views as needed.

Thyroid uptake (glandular activity) measurement with a scintillation uptake probe/scintillometer: count the reference standard capsule in a neck phantom, seat the patient and set the collimated probe at the prescribed distance from the neck, count neck and thigh background for fixed times at 4-6 h and 24 h, compute and record percent uptake.

Blood volume / red cell survival / GFR-type study in the nuclear medicine hot lab: inject the tracer, draw timed venous samples, centrifuge and pipette aliquots and standards into counting tubes, load and count them in a well/automatic gamma counter, and compute volumes, survival or clearance for the report.

Direct radiation measurement of a patient with survey instruments: exposure-rate readings at 1 m from an I-131 therapy patient to document release criteria, contamination frisking of a patient's skin/clothing or of the injection area after a spill, and counting wipe tests - all in the nuclear medicine department or the therapy room.

Portable/bedside measurement of an inpatient who cannot come to the department (ICU or ward room crowded with bed, lines, pumps and monitors): maneuver the portable camera or probe/survey meter into place over the patient, obtain the counts or images with the patient in a bed rather than on an imaging table, and verify adequacy.

tasks.label: Position radiation fields, radiation beams, and patient to allow for most effective treatment of patient's disease, using computer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine ambulatory adult in a hospital nuclear medicine / PET-CT or SPECT-CT suite: tech greets and identifies the patient, helps them onto the imaging couch, positions them supine with arms overhead and head in the headrest, applies straps/pillows, then sets table height/isocenter, scan range and CT field limits on the acquisition computer and starts the localizer/attenuation CT.

Whole-body or single-pose planar acquisition (e.g., bone scan, Lu-177 post-therapy imaging): patient placed supine once, detector heads driven down to the body contour and swept head-to-toe; field of view, scan speed and detector orbit set from the console; no change of patient pose during the study.

Multi-view planar / dynamic study (thyroid, renal, hepatobiliary, gastric emptying): patient must be re-posed by the tech between views - turned to obliques/laterals, sat upright, neck extended for pinhole thyroid views - with the detector re-contoured and the field reset for each view.

Non-ambulatory, frail, obese, confused or pain-limited patient arriving on a stretcher or in a wheelchair (inpatient, post-op, ICU): lateral transfer with slide board or lift, limbs supported and padded, IV lines/oxygen/drains managed, patient coached to hold still, then fields and scan range set.

Cardiac SPECT / hybrid CT attenuation study: arms restrained overhead in an arm holder, ECG leads placed, heart precisely centered in the field of view using persistence imaging, detector orbit (180 deg cardiac) and CT range set; sometimes repeated prone or upright.

Therapy-related setup with immobilization: patient immobilized on an indexed couch (headrest, thermoplastic mask or vac bag) for dosimetry SPECT/CT of radionuclide therapy or for image-guided external-beam/radiosurgery alignment; lasers and on-board imaging used to verify and apply 6-DoF corrections before beam-on.

tasks.label: Add radioactive substances to biological specimens, such as blood, urine, or feces, to determine therapeutic drug or hormone levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Batch in-vitro radioassay (RIA/IRMA) of serum for a hormone or therapeutic drug in a hospital or reference in-vitro nuclear lab: label tubes, pipette standards, controls and patient sera, add I-125 tracer and antibody reagent, vortex, incubate, separate/decant, load an automatic gamma well counter, fit the standard curve and release results.

In-vitro Tc-99m red-blood-cell labeling (e.g. UltraTag kit) in the nuclear medicine hot lab: receive 1-3 mL of the patient's heparinized whole blood, inject it into the shielded reaction vial, sequential reagent additions with mixing and timed incubations, add Tc-99m pertechnetate, incubate, assay activity in the dose calibrator and draw the labeled patient dose into a shielded syringe.

Blood volume / red cell mass determination (e.g. Daxor Volumex I-131 albumin): receive five timed venous samples, run duplicate microhematocrits, centrifuge, pipette duplicate 1-mL plasma aliquots into counting tubes, load them with the matched tracer standards and blanks into the counting analyzer, and verify duplicate agreement before reporting.

Autologous leukocyte labeling with In-111 oxine or Tc-99m HMPAO under aseptic technique in a biological safety cabinet: draw ~45 mL blood, sediment, differential centrifugation and visual identification of the leukocyte-rich layer, add tracer, incubate, wash, resuspend, measure labeling efficiency and release the cell suspension for reinjection.

Absorption/excretion study on collected urine (Schilling-type B12 absorption, renal or tracer-excretion quantitation): mix and measure the 24-hour collection, prepare a diluted tracer standard, pipette duplicate aliquots into counting tubes, count in a well counter against the standard and compute percent excretion.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: quantitative radioassay of radiotracer in patient plasma. Same specimen type (blood plasma), same radioactive material handling, same microliter pipetting/extraction/counting precision, same clinical-research laboratory bench.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: adding Tc-99m pertechnetate to a kit reagent with timed incubation and activity assay in a shielded cell. Same radionuclide, same closed-vial sequential reagent additions and volumetric precision as in-vitro Tc-99m blood-cell labeling, in the same hospital hot-lab context.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated addition of a radionuclide solution to a reagent vial with incubation and dispensing in a hospital hot cell; comparable liquids, volumes and radiation-handling constraints to in-vitro radiolabeling of a specimen.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of shielded radioactive vials and withdrawal of measured activity in a nuclear medicine department, the radiation-handling half of adding a radioactive substance to a specimen.

instances.label: Routine in-department radiographic exam of a cooperative, ambulatory outpatient or inpatient in a hospital/imaging-center X-ray room: verify order and identity, explain the exam, have the patient remove jewelry, position the body part (PA/lateral chest at the wall stand, hand/wrist/knee on the table bucky), set SID and collimation, select technique, coach breath-hold, expose, review each image for positioning/exposure and repeat if needed, send to PACS.

In-department radiography of a patient who cannot self-position: ED trauma on a backboard/stretcher, post-op or elderly wheelchair patient, obese or confused patient, or a squirming pediatric patient. Tech physically supports and manipulates limbs, uses sponges/sandbags/immobilizers, may hold the detector or have a parent assist, and improvises cross-table or oblique projections around the patient's condition.

Portable/mobile radiography at the bedside: drive the mobile DR unit to an ICU/ED bay, OR, or nursing-home room, navigate around IV poles, ventilators, monitors and staff, log-roll or lift the patient to slide the detector behind the chest or under a hip, angle the tube, warn the room, expose, and check the image (e.g., line/tube placement chest).

Fluoroscopy and routine contrast studies plus assisting the radiologist with joint/cyst aspirations and arthrograms: prepare barium or iodinated contrast and a sterile tray, position and repeatedly turn the patient on the fluoro table, hand the cup/straw or apply compression, operate the fluoro/spot-image chain in real time following the bolus, and record images for the physician.

Screening or diagnostic mammography in a breast-imaging suite: position the patient at the unit, manually pull and drape breast tissue onto the detector for CC and MLO views, adjust the shoulder/arm, apply and control compression, expose, assess each image for nipple-in-profile, pectoral muscle and skin folds, and repeat views as needed.

Sonographic exam performed by a cross-trained technologist in a hospital or clinic ultrasound room: apply gel and scan a defined protocol (e.g., thyroid, carotid/transcranial Doppler, abdominal/liver, bladder), obtain the required standard planes and measurements on a patient lying on the exam table, and store representative images for interpretation.

tasks.label: Prepare contrast material, radiopharmaceuticals, or anesthetic or antispasmodic drugs under the direction of a radiologist.

instances.label: Routine contrast-enhanced CT in a hospital or outpatient imaging department: technologist checks the radiologist-approved protocol and patient weight/eGFR, draws or loads iodinated contrast (e.g., iohexol) plus saline flush into the dual-head power injector syringes or bulk day-set, purges air, verifies volume/flow rate, and labels the loaded injector for that patient.

Contrast-enhanced MRI: technologist calculates a weight-based gadolinium dose per the radiologist's protocol, draws the dose from a single- or multi-dose vial into a syringe (or loads the MR injector syringe and saline), expels air, labels, and stages it at the magnet-room injector.

Nuclear medicine SPECT hot lab: technologist elutes the Tc-99m generator into an evacuated shielded vial, reconstitutes a cold kit (e.g., MDP, sestamibi) by injecting a measured eluate activity/volume into the lyophilized vial, mixes/incubates, then withdraws and assays each patient dose in the dose calibrator into a shielded, labeled syringe.

PET/CT: technologist draws a patient-specific FDG (or PSMA/amyloid tracer) dose from a shielded multi-dose vial behind an L-block, assays it in the dose calibrator, records residual/decay-corrected activity, and places the shielded syringe in a pig for injection.

Fluoroscopic GI/GU exam: technologist mixes barium sulfate powder or concentrate with water to the prescribed consistency in a cup or enema bag, or dilutes water-soluble contrast for a cystogram/enema, and draws up an antispasmodic (glucagon) or similar drug into a labeled syringe when the radiologist orders it.

Interventional/angiography suite: technologist prepares the procedure table solutions under the radiologist's direction — diluted iodinated contrast, heparinized saline flush, and local anesthetic (lidocaine) — drawn into labeled syringes and handed to or placed on the sterile field, replenished on demand during the case.

sources.claim: Omnicell's IVX Station robotic compounding system is deployed in hospital pharmacies (Ballad Health, three units live as of October 2025) where it pre-fills patient syringes autonomously after technicians load drugs and consumables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sterile compounding of IV syringes. Same objects (drug vials, syringes, needles), same volumetric/gravimetric precision and labeling requirements as drawing up contrast media or gadolinium doses in radiology.

sources.title: IVX - Robotic compounding system by OMNICELL | MedicalExpo

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated syringe filling and dose verification. The dose-checking, air-purging and labeling steps are the same operations a technologist performs when preparing a contrast or drug syringe.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA fully automated compounding system, built around a Staubli robot arm inside an aseptic cell, is installed in hospital pharmacies (e.g., Renown Health, 2025) and prepares patient-specific IV syringes and bags after staff load drugs and consumables into the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated preparation of injectable doses from vials into syringes; identical handling of vials/syringes and dose accuracy needed for contrast, gadolinium, glucagon or lidocaine preparation.

sources.title: Robotic compounding versus manual compounding of chemotherapy: Comparing dosing accuracy and precision - PubMed
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed comparison found robotic compounding produces doses as accurate as manual compounding by trained pharmacy staff, establishing worker-quality output for automated syringe/bag preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic drug compounding accuracy. Demonstrates that automated vial-to-syringe dosing meets human-technician accuracy, the quality bar for preparing contrast agents and adjunct drugs.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic reconstitution of lyophilized vials plus dose withdrawal — the same operation as reconstituting a lyophilized nuclear-medicine cold kit or a glucagon vial before drawing the dose.

tasks.label: Complete quality control activities, monitor equipment operation, and report malfunctioning equipment to supervisor.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily start-of-shift QC on a fixed CT or MRI scanner in a hospital or outpatient imaging suite: retrieve the water/QA phantom from storage, place it in the head cradle or on the couch, align it to the positioning lasers, run tube warm-up and the automated daily QC protocol from the shielded console, compare CT numbers/noise/SNR/uniformity against tolerances, log results, and escalate a failure.

Periodic phantom-based image-quality QC for accreditation/regulatory compliance: weekly ACR mammography phantom image (position phantom on bucky, apply compression, expose, score fibers/specks/masses, check artifacts and density), monthly/quarterly ACR CT or MRI phantom series, CR plate uniformity/erasure checks; document in the QC binder and notify the physicist/supervisor on out-of-tolerance results.

Daily room-readiness checks and hands-on inspection of an installed radiographic/fluoroscopic room: power up and clear error messages, run tube/table/gantry and overhead crane motions, verify collimator light field, lasers, detents, locks, indicator lights and emergency stops, inspect tube housing, high-tension cables and connectors for damage, wipe down table and DR detectors, and inspect lead aprons/gloves/thyroid shields for cracks.

Monitoring equipment operation while imaging patients: noticing artifacts, dropped lines, detector or grid faults, unusual gantry/table noise, console error codes or exposure faults mid-exam; attempting first-line troubleshooting (reboot, recalibrate, swap detector, move to another room), deciding to take the room out of service and tagging it, and reporting the malfunction to the supervisor/biomed/service engineer.

QC of ancillary and mobile equipment in varied locations: display/monitor QC (cleaning, SMPTE/TG-18 pattern or photometer luminance check), laser printer/processor checks, and daily checks on portable radiography units and C-arms (battery charge, brakes and wheels, cable and collimator condition, test exposure) performed in corridors, ICU/OR, or a mobile mammography coach.

sources.system: North Star Imaging RobotiX (X25/X3000 with efX-CT and Assisted Defect Recognition)

sources.claim: NSI's RobotiX product line is a commercially sold industrial X-ray/CT inspection system in which a robot loads parts into a shielded X-ray CT cell, the scan runs, and defect-recognition software analyses the result without an operator in the radiation area.

A daily/periodic imaging QC phantom scan is the same physical loop (rigid object of similar size and mass, millimetre-level placement repeatability, automated quantitative image evaluation and flagging), so performance carries over when the phantom is presented fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.claim: Nikon markets automated industrial CT cells in which robotic sample loading gives unattended inspection, with part loading, program selection, acquisition, analysis and reporting all automated and results fed back to the plant system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended load-scan-analyse-report cycles on an X-ray CT system inside a shielded enclosure. This covers the whole loop a phantom QC run needs (present the reference object, acquire, evaluate quantitatively, report out-of-tolerance results), with comparable object size and placement precision, in a purpose-built E1 cell.

sources.claim: Automated daily QC analysis for a clinical MRI scanner is software that begins only after a human has positioned the phantom and the images have been sent from the console; the physical phantom setup remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (daily imaging QC), but software-only: it substantiates that the evaluation, logging and flagging steps of phantom QC are already automated, while showing that the remaining human contribution is the physical handling and positioning of the phantom.

sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulators have been shown loading samples into shared analytical instruments (LC-MS, benchtop NMR) in a working chemistry laboratory and using the measurements to make go/no-go decisions, over multi-day autonomous campaigns.

It is the closest analogue to carrying a QC phantom to a scanner in a human facility, but the stations are pre-calibrated fixed docks in a research lab and no comparable system has been shown positioning a phantom on an imaging couch or operating a scanner console, so it does not establish the hospital-suite (E2) case.

sources.system: Spot with Automated Visual Inspection / gauge-reading models

It covers only non-contact observation of fixed plant; it does not operate controls, actuate imaging equipment through its motions, wipe detectors, or handle lead aprons, so it does not carry over to the radiology room-check and in-exam monitoring instances.

tasks.label: Position patient on examining table and set up and adjust equipment to obtain optimum view of specific body area as requested by physician.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine ambulatory radiography in a fixed room at a hospital or outpatient imaging center (chest PA/lateral, abdomen/KUB, spine): cooperative walking patient is instructed and physically nudged into position at the wall stand or on the table, tube height/SID/angulation set, collimation and technique adjusted, image checked and repeated if rotation or clipping occurs.

Extremity / musculoskeletal radiography (wrist scaphoid, oblique elbow, knee, ankle, shoulder Y-view): technologist manually manipulates the limb against the receptor, props it with sponges and sandbags, angles the tube, and works around pain, casts or splints.

CT exam setup: patient helped onto the table, head holder or arms-up positioning, knee bolster and straps applied, IV contrast line managed, laser/isocenter alignment and table height set, table advanced into the gantry for the requested scan range.

Portable/mobile radiography at the bedside (ICU, ED bay, OR, or nursing-home round): image receptor slid under a supine or bedridden patient, bed raised, patient rolled or propped, mobile unit maneuvered around lines, drains, ventilator and monitors to align the tube.

Non-ambulatory or trauma patient in the ED: transfer from stretcher or wheelchair with minimal movement, spinal precautions, adapted projections such as cross-table lateral or trauma obliques performed by moving the equipment rather than the patient.

Pediatric, confused/dementia, intoxicated or bariatric patient: coaxing, breathing instruction, immobilization devices (e.g., pediatric chest stand, tape, parental holding), frequent repeats due to motion, and extra staff for support.

tasks.label: Use radiation safety measures and protection devices to comply with government regulations and to ensure safety of patients and staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine radiographic exam (chest, extremity, spine) in a fixed X-ray room at a hospital radiology suite or outpatient imaging center: screen the patient for pregnancy, select the lowest-dose technique/protocol, collimate the beam tightly to the anatomy on a live, sometimes uncooperative patient, place a thyroid or lead shield or drape an accompanying caregiver, clear other people from the room, close the door, wear a personal dosimeter, and make the exposure from behind the leaded control barrier.

Portable/mobile radiography at the bedside in an ICU, ED bay, patient room, or OR: maneuver the mobile unit into a cluttered occupied space, announce 'X-ray', clear or shield visitors, nurses, and adjacent patients (hand out lead aprons to anyone who must stay, e.g., someone holding the patient), collimate tightly, stand back the required distance behind the unit's shield with the exposure cord, and expose.

CT (or other advanced modality) exam in a scanner suite: verify pregnancy/appropriateness, select a dose-optimized protocol with tube-current modulation, center the patient at gantry isocenter to avoid dose penalty, apply shielding to any escort or out-of-field organs when indicated, confirm the room is clear and the interlocked door closed, observe through the leaded window, and check/record the dose index against reference levels.

Fluoroscopy / interventional / OR C-arm case: don a lead apron and thyroid collar and confirm all team members are gowned and badged, position the ceiling-suspended leaded acrylic shield and the table-side drape, set pulsed low-dose fluoro and last-image-hold, keep staff back during acquisitions, and monitor and record fluoro time and cumulative air kerma against notification levels.

Pediatric, pregnant, bariatric, or non-cooperative patient needing extra protection: use immobilization to avoid repeat exposures, apply tight collimation and specialty shielding, fit a lead apron and gloves on a parent or aide who holds the child, and reposition shields between projections while keeping the patient calm.

Departmental radiation-safety program duties: wear and exchange dosimetry badges, inspect and log lead aprons/thyroid collars for cracks (visual and fluoroscopic testing), verify warning lights, signage, door interlocks and shielded-booth integrity, and respond to dose-alert or repeat-rate reviews.

sources.title: Radiaction Medical Gets FDA Clearance for Automated Radiation Shield System
sources.claim: The Radiaction Shield System is an FDA-cleared, motorized shielding accessory that mounts on a cath-lab C-arm and extends tungsten-polymer plates toward the patient and table to block scatter at the source; it is deployed by staff from a table-side controller and uses proximity sensors to stop extension near the patient. It automates only staff scatter shielding, not the technologist's other radiation-safety duties.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the fluoroscopy instance (use of protection devices), but it is a machine-mounted shield operated by staff, not a robot performing the worker's protective actions.

sources.title: VIDEO: Demonstration of the Radiaction Cath Lab Radiation Protection System
sources.claim: The Radiaction shield is deployed and retracted by a human using a table-side controller during the case, with sensors only limiting travel near the patient; a person remains in the loop for deployment, retraction and panning.

sources.system: FAST 3D Camera / FAST Integrated Workflow on SOMATOM CT
sources.title: FAST 3D Camera for CT patient positioning
sources.claim: Commercial CT scanners use a 3D camera and AI to automatically drive the table so the patient is centered at isocenter, improving centering versus technologists and reducing dose; this is an autonomous machine action but covers only one dose-relevant sub-step of the CT radiation-safety instance.
sources.transferJustification: Automatic isocentering is a dose-optimization measure (mis-centering raises dose), so it substantiates machine capability for that element of the CT radiation-safety instance only.

sources.system: Robot-assisted dressing pipeline (Baxter/robot arm, garment manipulation policies)
sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic dressing of a person with a hospital gown — the closest analogue to placing a lead apron or thyroid collar on a patient, caregiver, or staff member — remains laboratory research validated on a medical training manikin, not clinical practice.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting a garment on a person. Draping a lead apron/thyroid collar on a patient or holder is the same class of deformable-garment-on-body manipulation; validation only on a manikin in a lab shows it is not at worker quality in occupied clinical rooms.

sources.title: Making Radiation Mapping Safer & More Reliable
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots carrying radiation detectors perform radiation mapping/survey missions in nuclear facilities, but their demonstrated work is dose-rate mapping in industrial plants, not inspecting lead aprons, exchanging dosimeters, or verifying interlocks in a radiology department.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine radiation surveying/monitoring. It shows autonomous radiation-safety robotics exists in industrial plants, but the protective-device handling and dosimetry logistics of a radiology department are not demonstrated.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Research team, arXiv:2510.08106 (evaluated at Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital)
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic scanning of patients is at the clinical-feasibility research stage and only for non-ionizing ultrasound; no comparable autonomous robot conducts ionizing-radiation exams (and hence their radiation-safety envelope) on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic imaging of a patient. It marks the frontier of patient-contact imaging autonomy; because it uses no ionizing radiation it does not substantiate performing radiation-safety measures, and it is a feasibility study, not worker-quality service.

tasks.label: Position imaging equipment and adjust controls to set exposure time and distance, according to specification of examination.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine general radiography in a fixed X-ray room (hospital or outpatient imaging center): for a chest, abdomen, spine or extremity order, move the ceiling-suspended tube to the wall stand or table bucky, set source-to-image distance, angle the tube, collimate to the anatomy, and select/adjust kVp, mAs and AEC cells for the patient's size per the exam protocol.

Portable/mobile radiography at the bedside in ICU, ED, neonatal unit or a patient room: wheel the mobile unit to the bed, maneuver the tube arm over the patient around IV poles, ventilators, monitors and bed rails, judge SID by tape or eye, align the beam to the DR panel behind the patient, and dial in kVp/mAs manually (no AEC).

CT examination in a hospital or outpatient CT suite: set table height to the correct isocenter, advance the patient into the gantry to the landmark, run the topogram, define scan range and direction, and set kV/mA, rotation time and dose modulation for the protocol.

Interventional or hybrid-OR imaging with a fixed angiography system: position the C-arm to the required projection angles, set SID and detector height over the sterile field, and set fluoro pulse rate, dose level and acquisition parameters for each phase of the procedure.

Dynamic fluoroscopic contrast studies (barium swallow/UGI, cystogram, arthrogram) in a fluoroscopy room: position and continuously reposition the tower/spot-film device over moving contrast, adjust height, angulation and magnification, and set fluoro and spot-image exposure factors during the exam.

Specialty modality units: screening/diagnostic mammography (set gantry angle and height for CC/MLO on the individual patient's habitus, compression, exposure mode) and other dedicated units such as DXA densitometry or dental/panoramic imaging, in a clinic or hospital imaging room.

tasks.label: Operate or oversee operation of radiologic or magnetic imaging equipment to produce images of the body for diagnostic purposes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine general radiography in a hospital or outpatient X-ray room: patient walks in, tech selects the exam protocol, positions the patient at the wall stand or table, aligns tube/detector and collimates, sets kVp/mAs or AEC, gives breath-hold instructions from the shielded booth, exposes, inspects the image for positioning/exposure/motion, repeats views if needed, sends to PACS.

CT exam in a hospital or imaging-center CT suite (head, chest/abd/pelvis, CTA), frequently with IV contrast: patient on the table with arms positioned, power injector connected and armed, protocol chosen for indication and body habitus, topogram then scan range set, bolus tracking monitored, breath-hold coaching, patient watched for contrast reaction, series reconstructed and pushed to PACS.

MRI exam in an MRI suite: ferromagnetic safety screening, patient on table with hearing protection and squeeze bulb, selection and placement of surface coils, landmarking, localizers, then 20-60 minutes of sequences with slice prescription checked and re-run for motion or artifact, patient monitored and coached between sequences.

Portable/bedside radiography in ICU, ED or OR: mobile unit driven to the bedside through occupied space, maneuvered around lines, pumps and vent tubing, detector slid behind or under a supine, often uncooperative patient, tube angled and collimated by eye, area cleared, exposure made, image checked for line/tube position and repeated if clipped.

Fluoroscopy and surgical C-arm/interventional imaging: C-arm or angio system positioned around a draped sterile field, live fluoro and spot images acquired on the operator's verbal request, angulation, magnification, dose rate and table height adjusted repeatedly during the case, runs saved and archived.

Mammography, DXA and other specialized outpatient studies: breast pulled onto the detector and held while compression is applied for CC and MLO views (or patient aligned on a DXA table), image acquired, checked for skin folds/motion/adequate tissue inclusion, views repeated as needed.

sources.system: Autonomous X-ray image acquisition and interpretation system (robotic C-arm)
sources.title: An autonomous X-ray image acquisition and interpretation system for assisting percutaneous pelvic fracture fixation
sources.claim: A Johns Hopkins system autonomously chooses C-arm viewpoints and acquires and interprets intraoperative radiographs; evaluated on cadaveric specimens and an anthropomorphic phantom in a laboratory robotic-imaging setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acquisition of intraoperative fluoroscopic/spot radiographs. Same equipment class (C-arm X-ray), same output (diagnostic projection images of a human body), machine-selected geometry and acquisition, so it substantiates machine-run image acquisition once the subject is presented to the imager.

sources.title: Siemens Healthineers Redefines Biopsy Workflow With New MAMMOMAT Revelation Mammography System
sources.claim: Siemens MAMMOMAT Revelation applies and individually adjusts breast compression force automatically and performs a 50-degree tomosynthesis sweep with automatic exposure control.

sources.system: NovaGuide Intelligent Ultrasound / Lucid Robotic System
sources.title: Safety and efficacy of a novel robotic transcranial doppler system in subarachnoid hemorrhage | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: The FDA-cleared NovaGuide/Lucid robotic transcranial Doppler system, in clinical use in US hospitals, robotically steers an ultrasound transducer and autonomously locates and measures flow in the middle cerebral arteries only; other vessels still require manual insonation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic operation of diagnostic imaging equipment on a hospital inpatient. It marks the limit of demonstrated E2 autonomy on real patients - a head-strapped, single-target ultrasound robot - and does not extend to whole-body positioning, coaching and image QC in a radiography, CT or MR suite.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: academic group with Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv)
sources.claim: A lightweight autonomous ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and autonomously located standard abdominal imaging planes on human volunteers after non-expert staff mounted it on the subject.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous acquisition of diagnostic images of a live human body with a scanning modality. It shows autonomous image-plane search and quality assessment inside a hospital department, but only after a human mounts the probe, i.e. after the subject is presented and fixtured.

tasks.label: Operate fluoroscope to aid physician to view and guide wire or catheter through blood vessels to area of interest.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cardiac cath lab, fixed single-plane C-arm: during diagnostic coronary angiography or PCI the technologist drives the imaging system at the physician's spoken direction — steps through LAO/RAO/cranial-caudal angulations, pans the table to keep the guide catheter and coronary tree in view, sets magnification, collimation/shutters, frame rate and dose mode, runs fluoro and cine acquisitions, coordinates the contrast injector, and archives runs while watching the patient.

Interventional radiology suite, peripheral/visceral angiography and intervention (embolization, angioplasty/stent, fistulogram): technologist sets up DSA masks and roadmapping, coaches breath-holds, pans or step-chases the table as the wire advances down a runoff, re-angulates for oblique views on request, adjusts pixel shift and collimation, and manages dose and archiving over a one-to-three-hour case.

Hybrid OR or OR with a mobile C-arm (EVAR, vascular surgery, pacemaker/ICD lead placement, IVC filter): technologist wheels and parks the portable C-arm around a draped sterile field and crowded staff, aligns it to the target vessel, holds fluoro on the wire or lead tip as the physician advances it, repositions repeatedly, and withdraws the unit when the surgeon needs access.

Routine short vascular-access work under fluoroscopy in an IR suite (PICC, port, tunneled dialysis catheter, catheter exchange): brief intermittent fluoro of chest/neck to confirm wire and catheter tip position, little angulation change, largely repetitive imaging sequence.

Urgent or off-hours case (stroke thrombectomy, GI bleed or trauma embolization): unstable or moving patient, non-standard positioning with lines, ventilator and compression devices in the field, rapid unrehearsed changes of view and table position under time pressure with an ad hoc team.

sources.system: Autonomous fluoroscopic imaging system (bilateral control of robotic catheter + 3-DoF motorised C-arm)
sources.developer: Kenan Niu (University of Twente), published in Machines (MDPI)
sources.title: An Autonomous Fluoroscopic Imaging System for Catheter Insertions by Bilateral Control Scheme: A Numerical Simulation Study
sources.claim: The only published 'autonomous fluoroscopic imaging system' that couples image feedback to C-arm motion during catheter insertion was validated only inside a physics-based simulator with synthetic X-ray images; no physical C-arm, phantom or patient work is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (automatically orienting a fluoroscope to keep a catheter optimally imaged), but simulation-only, so it cannot substantiate completion in any physical environment.

sources.system: MLLM-based agentic C-arm control framework (skeletal landmark localization)
sources.developer: academic group, published in International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
sources.title: Autonomous skeletal landmark localization toward agentic C-arm control
sources.claim: Work toward autonomous C-arm control remains image-analysis research: fine-tuned multimodal LLMs localize skeletal landmarks on X-ray datasets and are said to hold promise for future agentic C-arm control; no autonomous fluoroscope operation during a live vascular case is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (positioning a C-arm for standard projections). It shows the frontier is dataset-level localization, not autonomous imaging support through an endovascular procedure, so capability does not transfer.

sources.system: ARTIS pheno robotic C-arm angiography system
sources.title: Robot-assisted C-arm X-ray systems | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Commercially deployed robotic angiography C-arms (ARTIS pheno/zeego, built with KUKA robot arms) give motorized flexible positioning around the patient, but the arm is positioned on clinician command rather than deciding and executing the imaging itself.
sources.transferJustification: Same equipment class as the task's fluoroscope; establishes that even the most robotic installed angiography systems are human-commanded and do not replace the technologist running imaging through a case.

sources.title: Robotic-assisted percutaneous coronary intervention: experience in Switzerland (Frontiers in Cardiovascular Medicine)
sources.claim: Clinically deployed vascular robotics (CorPath GRX) move guidewires and catheters under remote human control from a shielded cockpit; imaging remains human-operated and the robot is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robotics in the same room and procedure; shows automation there is teleoperated device manipulation, with no system taking over fluoroscope operation.

sources.system: Miniature single-use endovascular robotic system (ACCESS-PVI trial)
sources.developer: multicenter investigators, reported in Journal of Vascular and Interventional Radiology
sources.title: In Vivo Evaluation of a Disposable Endovascular Robotic System for Arterial Peripheral Vascular Interventions: A Multicenter Feasibility Study
sources.claim: Recent in-vivo endovascular robotics trials for peripheral vascular intervention are explicitly remote-controlled by the operator, with conventional fluoroscopy times reported, i.e., the imaging is still run by humans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (endovascular navigation) performed in the same suites; confirms that as of 2026 the robotic element is teleoperated and the fluoroscope remains technologist-operated.

tasks.label: Make exposures necessary for the requested procedures, rejecting and repeating work that does not meet established standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine general radiography in a fixed X-ray room of a hospital department or outpatient/urgent-care clinic: ambulatory, cooperative adult; 2-4 views (chest PA/lateral, extremity, spine); technologist sets/verifies technique factors and collimation, gives breath-hold or hold-still instruction, makes each exposure, inspects each image at the console and repeats the ~5-10% that are clipped, rotated, motion-blurred or mis-exposed.

Portable/mobile radiography at the bedside in ICU, ED, OR, isolation and neonatal units: detector slid under a supine, often intubated or uncooperative patient; tube angled and centered by hand around lines, ventilators and bed rails; exposure factors estimated for grid/SID variation; frequent repeats for clipped lung fields, rotation or motion.

CT examinations (head, chest/abdomen-pelvis, CT angiography) in a hospital or outpatient CT suite: patient on the table, isocentering, topogram, scan-range and protocol selection, automated breath-hold prompts, contrast timing, then review of the reconstructed series for motion, coverage or contrast-timing failure and re-acquisition of inadequate series.

Fluoroscopy, operating-room C-arm and interventional imaging: technologist drives the C-arm or R/F unit under a physician's direction, makes fluoro runs and spot exposures at changing angles around a sterile field, adjusts technique for habitus and anatomy, and reshoots images that are not diagnostic.

Difficult radiography in a fixed room: trauma, pediatric, bariatric, stretcher- or wheelchair-bound and non-cooperative patients requiring cross-table or improvised projections, immobilization, manual technique adjustment and a high rate of judged repeats.

Mobile radiography service outside an imaging facility: ultraportable unit taken to nursing-home rooms, correctional facilities or private residences; furniture and lighting as found, detector propped behind or under the patient, exposures made and reviewed on a laptop, repeats taken on the spot.

sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound system was run on humans in a hospital imaging department, the closest demonstrated analog of a robot autonomously acquiring diagnostic images of a patient; it remains a feasibility evaluation on volunteers rather than a system delivering accepted clinical exams.

tasks.label: Set up examination rooms, ensuring that all necessary equipment is ready.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-patient turnover of a general radiography room in a hospital or outpatient clinic: disinfect table, upright bucky and detector handles, change table paper/pillow cover, restock gowns, wipes, gloves and linens, put out positioning sponges, markers and lead shields, verify the wireless detector is charged and docked, and move the tube/detector to the starting position for the next exam.

CT room setup at shift start and between contrast patients: power up and warm the tube, run daily QC/calibration, load the power injector with contrast and saline (syringes or day set), connect and prime tubing, lay out an IV start tray, stock oral contrast and emergency supplies, wipe the table, place head holder, pads and straps, and load the exam protocol.

MRI suite setup: select and attach the correct RF coil to the table, place pads, cushions, blankets and hearing protection, restock screening forms and earplugs, verify MR-conditional injector/monitoring gear and emergency items, and wipe the table and bore between patients.

Interventional/angiography or fluoroscopy suite setup (also OR C-arm cases): open sterile trays, gowns and drapes onto a back table, establish and drape the sterile field, prepare contrast and heparinized flush, lay out catheters, wires and syringes, hang lead shields and aprons, position table, C-arm and monitors, and check crash cart, oxygen and suction.

Portable/bedside exam setup in an ICU, ED bay, patient room or OR: bring the mobile X-ray unit in, move furniture, lines and chairs clear, clean and bag the detector, fit grid/detector covers, position the machine and shields for staff, then wipe down and restock the unit's supplies afterward.

Mammography, ultrasound or other outpatient imaging room setup, including mobile screening coaches: stock gowns, wipes and warm gel, clean compression paddles or transducers, replace table linens, set out positioning aids and consent forms, and confirm the unit passes its start-of-day check.

sources.title: Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulator is built for AI, says Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator deployed in 25+ US hospitals, autonomously navigates corridors, fetches from central supply and delivers medications, lab samples and supplies; its deployed workflow is point-to-point logistics, not preparing or stocking a clinical exam room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply delivery/fetching. It shows autonomous mobile manipulation is real in E2 hospital settings, but it covers only the supply-transport sub-step of room setup, not cleaning, linen change, equipment positioning or injector/tray preparation.

sources.system: Autonomous wiping + UV-C disinfection robot (Prof. Keehoon Kim group)
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: A POSTECH-developed autonomous robot combines a manipulator that physically wipes surfaces with UV-C irradiation, validated in repeated autonomous runs at a real hospital; it performs surface disinfection only, not restocking or equipment preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital surface disinfection. Comparable environment (hospital rooms) and comparable objects (beds/tables), so it substantiates the wipe-down sub-step of exam-room turnover, but it does not handle linens, consumables, coils, injectors or sterile trays.

sources.system: Multitom Rax Twin Robotic X-ray system
sources.title: Siemens Healthcare Unveils Twin Robotic X-Ray System
sources.claim: Siemens Healthineers' Multitom Rax radiography room has two ceiling-mounted robotic arms carrying tube and detector that move into stored positions automatically under machine control, automating the equipment-positioning part of room readiness while all other setup remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning imaging hardware for the next exam. Same room and same equipment, so it bears directly on one sub-step of 'equipment ready'; motions are operator-commanded preset moves, so autonomy is unclear and it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L + vision pipeline)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A fully automated bench-top robotic cell (Staubli TX2-60L arm with vision) sorts and packs surgical instruments into sterile ... in sterile-processing workflows — instrument-tray assembly done in a purpose-built cell, not in-room procedure setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling instrument trays. Comparable objects and precision to laying out an interventional tray, and it shows the fixtured E1-cell version of that sub-step, but it does not drape a sterile field, prepare contrast, or ready an angiography room.

sources.system: Humanoid embodied-AI OR assistants (proposed staged framework)
sources.developer: Kernbach, Brat, Topol et al. (npj Digital Medicine perspective)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: A July 2026 npj Digital Medicine perspective frames humanoid support for supplies, equipment and preparing/resetting operating rooms as a future, staged possibility requiring laboratory testing and validation, indicating no such system performs procedure-room preparation autonomously today.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: procedure-room turnover and preparation. Cited as context that this capability is prospective and initially teleoperated/supervised, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of exam-room setup at any tier.
