tasks.label: Provide assistance to physicians or other technologists in the performance of more complex procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interventional radiology/angio suite, complex vascular case (angiogram, embolization, port or drain placement): tech scrubs or circulates — sets up sterile tray, gowns/gloves the radiologist, hands catheters, wires, syringes and sheaths on verbal request, loads and operates the power contrast injector, moves the C-arm/table on cue, monitors the sedated patient and documents. Live patient, sterile field, hospital.

Fluoroscopy room, radiologist-performed exam (barium swallow/UGI, arthrogram, myelogram, lumbar puncture): tech prepares and hands contrast and needles, helps the patient roll, sit up and hold awkward positions on a moving table, steadies frail patients, runs spot imaging and image capture, cleans and turns the room over.

Second technologist assisting another tech with a difficult exam — trauma bay, ICU or ED portable radiography on an obese, intubated or unresponsive patient: log-rolling the patient, sliding and holding the detector under them, supporting limbs, managing lines, drains and traction, shielding staff, and repeating views the first tech can't get alone.

CT- or ultrasound-guided biopsy, drainage or injection: tech positions and immobilizes the patient prone/decubitus on the CT table, opens and sets up the sterile tray, preps skin, advances the table and runs limited scans on the radiologist's command, hands needles and specimen containers, monitors vitals, applies dressing and recovers the patient.

Operating room or cath lab, assisting the surgeon with mobile C-arm fluoroscopy (ortho fracture fixation, spine, ERCP, pain injection): sterile-draping the C-arm, maneuvering it into and out of position around the sterile field, staff and anesthesia lines, imaging on verbal cue, holding views, saving/sending images and managing radiation safety.

sources.system: RoboNurse-VLA (Kinova-based robotic scrub nurse with vision-language-action model)
sources.title: [2409.19590] RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model
sources.claim: RoboNurse-VLA is a research robotic scrub-nurse system that autonomously grasps and hands surgical instruments in response to a surgeon's voice commands, demonstrated in laboratory experiments rather than in clinical procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passing instruments and supplies to a physician during a procedure, which is the core motor element of a radiologic technologist assisting in complex procedures. It shows this element exists only as a bench demo of isolated handovers, not as whole-procedure assistance with a live patient.

sources.system: Robotic scrub nurse (RSN) with real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.developer: university hospital research group (Surgical Endoscopy publication)
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis - PubMed
sources.claim: A robotic scrub nurse that anticipates and passes the next laparoscopic instrument was evaluated only in simulated surgery at a university hospital, not in real patient procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: anticipating and handing instruments during an image-guided procedure. Transfer is limited: the demonstration is in simulated surgery on a bench setup, and covers only instrument handover, not patient positioning, contrast handling, imaging equipment operation or patient monitoring.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed at scale in US hospitals, but its work is non-patient-facing logistics — fetching and delivering supplies, medications and lab samples through corridors — not assistance inside a procedure room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving and delivering supplies within a hospital, one incidental part of procedural assistance. It does not transfer to the instance as a whole: Moxi does not enter sterile fields, touch patients, operate imaging equipment, or respond to a physician's intra-procedural requests.

sources.title: Corindus CorPath GRX Robotic PCI System
sources.claim: The robotics actually used in interventional suites (CorPath GRX vascular robot) are physician-operated tools driven from a console, replacing the operator's own catheter manipulation rather than autonomously performing the assisting technologist's role.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting (angio/cath lab, complex procedures) but a different role: the robot is driven by the physician at a console; a technologist is still required at the bedside to load devices, manage contrast and care for the patient.

sources.system: humanoid robots in the operating room (review of proposed roles, e.g., circulating-nurse tasks)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: A 2026 review of humanoid robots in the operating ... describes assistive clinical roles as a future staged development pathway requiring preclinical and simulated validation first, indicating no such robot currently performs assistive roles in real procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses robotic assistance to procedural teams in the OR; establishes that as of mid-2026 assistive procedural roles remain at the preclinical/simulation stage.

sources.title: Siemens Healthcare Unveils Twin Robotic X-Ray System
sources.claim: Commercial robotic radiography systems automate the positioning of imaging hardware around the patient at the push of a ... human operator in control; the patient is still positioned and handled by technologists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning imaging equipment for complex views, a component of assisting with difficult exams. It automates only tube/detector placement in a fixed room under operator command, not patient handling, portable/trauma imaging, or working with a second technologist.

sources.system: autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot was tested performing scans on humans in a hospital ultrasound department, showing autonomous patient-contact imaging is feasible for narrow, single-purpose scan tasks in a controlled room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical contact with a patient to acquire images. It bounds current capability — a single scripted scan target on a cooperative, still patient — well short of multi-step, sterile, physician-paced procedural assistance.

tasks.label: Transport patients to or from exam rooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ambulatory outpatient at a hospital radiology department or outpatient imaging center: the technologist calls the patient from the waiting room, walks them back through the department corridor to the changing room/exam room, and later walks them back out. Patient walks unaided; no equipment.

Patient who needs a wheelchair but gets in and out of it on their own or with light verbal cueing (low-acuity ED patient, elderly outpatient with limited stamina, stable ward patient): wheeled from the ED/waiting area/ward through busy corridors and elevators to the imaging room and back.

Frail or partly dependent inpatient who needs hands-on help: technologist steadies/lifts the patient from bed or chair into a wheelchair, manages IV pole, oxygen tank and drains, wheels them through corridors and elevators to the exam room, then returns them.

Non-ambulatory inpatient moved on a stretcher or in the hospital bed: patient is log-rolled/slid onto a transport stretcher or the bed is unplugged and steered with IV pump and oxygen attached, pushed through corridors and elevators to CT/X-ray and back to the ward.

Critically ill ED/ICU patient going to CT: cardiac monitor, multiple infusion pumps, ventilator or high-flow oxygen; a nurse and often respiratory therapy accompany; continuous observation of the patient's condition and lines during the move.

sources.developer: Cyberworks Robotics (with Compass One Healthcare, North York General Hospital)
sources.title: Autonomous Wheelchair Proof of Concept Pilot Report
sources.claim: Cyberworks Robotics' autonomous wheelchair carried real patients autonomously from the Emergency Department to the Medical Imaging Department at North York General Hospital in a July 2025 proof-of-concept pilot (13 patients, 6 staff), navigating live hospital corridors with obstacle avoidance and a rider manual override.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. / University of Tsukuba Hospital
sources.title: Safety and feasibility of in-hospital autonomous transportation using a driverless mobility for patients with musculoskeletal disorders
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed clinical study transported 51 hospital outpatients with reduced mobility along a mapped 100 m in-hospital route using a WHILL driverless wheelchair; the chair drove itself to the selected destination and no collisions or severe adverse events occurred.

sources.title: Barcelona-El Prat Airport Implements WHILL Autonomous Service
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchairs are in routine commercial service carrying reduced-mobility passengers through terminals at multiple major airports, driving themselves to a destination and returning empty.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pushing a seated person through an institution-controlled facility to a fixed destination. Same object (a seated adult), same kind of crowded corridor, and the service explicitly substitutes for the staff who push wheelchairs — the same conveyance work as moving a patient to an exam room.

sources.title: Haneda International Airport Implements WHILL Autonomous Mobility Service
sources.claim: Haneda Airport put the WHILL autonomous service into operation for passengers with reduced mobility, removing the human wheelchair pusher from the trip to the gate, after 11 trials at airports including DFW, JFK and Winnipeg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: staff-pushed wheelchair transport of a person inside a large institutional building. It substantiates that autonomous conveyance of a seated person along facility corridors is done at worker-replacing quality; hospital corridors are the same class of environment.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi operates autonomously in dozens of US hospitals, opening doors and riding elevators without human control; it logged 110,000 autonomous elevator rides by late 2024 and over a million deliveries by 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point transport of supplies inside working hospitals. It substantiates the navigation half of patient transport — corridors shared with staff, patients and carts, badge-controlled doors, and elevators — in the same buildings where patients are moved.

sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Rovex's Rovi robot autonomously latches onto and tows existing stretchers, beds and wheelchairs through a hospital; in its first pilot at BayCare's Morton Plant Hospital (April 2026) it retrieves empty stretchers and is explicitly not yet moving patients.

sources.title: Able Innovations Deploys Robotic Patient Delivery Platform in the U.S.
sources.claim: Able Innovations' ALTA Platform, the most advanced deployed patient-transfer robot (Lahey Hospital, first US site, March 2026), automates lateral transfers but still requires a staff member to operate it; no cited system performs a bed-to-wheelchair patient transfer autonomously.

sources.developer: Politecnico di Milano / ASST Grande Ospedale Metropolitano Niguarda
sources.title: BUDD-e: an autonomous robotic guide for visually impaired users
sources.claim: The BUDD-e autonomous robotic guide escorted walking volunteers through a working hospital from the main entrance to a clinical department along mapped routes with optional deviations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically escorting a walking person who cannot find their way, through hospital corridors to a named department — the same act as walking an ambulatory patient from the waiting room to the exam room.

tasks.label: Maintain a current file of examination protocols.

tasks.label: Provide assistance in dressing or changing seriously ill or injured patients or patients with disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient imaging center or hospital radiology dressing area: an elderly or disabled but ambulatory patient needs hands-on help removing shirt, bra, jewelry and hairpins, putting on and tying a gown, then redressing after the exam; tech steadies the patient, manages balance and modesty, works in a small changing cubicle.

Hospital inpatient brought to CT/X-ray on a stretcher or wheelchair: patient with limited mobility, IV lines, telemetry leads, oxygen tubing, drains or casts; tech (often with an aide) rolls the patient, opens/removes the gown and hospital garments, threads sleeves around lines, re-gowns and re-covers after imaging.

Portable/bedside radiography on a ward, ICU or nursing home room: tech unties and opens the patient's gown or lifts clothing to place the detector under or against the torso, keeps the patient covered for dignity/warmth, then re-fastens the gown and repositions bedding with the patient still in bed.

Emergency department trauma or acute-injury patient going to CT: clothing removed or cut away, jewelry and metal taken off, patient in cervical collar/on a board, in pain, sometimes combative or unresponsive; tech assists nursing staff in stripping and draping the patient quickly under time pressure.

Bariatric, pediatric or cognitively impaired patient (e.g., dementia, developmental disability) needing substantial hands-on changing help, often with a family member or caregiver present, with unpredictable movement, resistance or the need for two-person assist and coaching.

sources.system: Force-Constrained Visual Policy (FCVP) dressing system (Sawyer arm), CMU Robotics Institute
sources.title: Force-Constrained Visual Policy: Safe Robot-Assisted Dressing via Multi-Modal Sensing
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robot-assisted dressing is a single-arm laboratory system that pulls one sleeve of a hospital gown ... the arm of a seated, able-bodied study participant, covering on average ~86% of arm length; it does not undress a person or complete a full gown change.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the closest related task (putting a hospital gown sleeve on a person's arm); shows the capability frontier is a single sub-step on a cooperative, healthy participant in a lab, not a full gown change on a seriously ill patient.

sources.system: Robot-assisted dressing pipeline (Baxter-class dual-arm, garment unfolding + dressing)
sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: A full robot dressing pipeline for people who cannot move their upper limbs was validated only on a medical training manikin, not on real patients in a care facility.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (dressing a dependent person). Validation on a manikin rather than living, frail patients shows the whole-task capability on real ill patients is not established.

sources.developer: University of York / Honda Research Institute EU / TU Delft (Zhu, Gienger, Franzese, Kober)
sources.title: New dressing robot can 'mimic' the actions of care-workers — University of York
sources.claim: Bimanual dressing assistance that imitates care-worker motions remains a laboratory research prototype; prior assistive dressing robots have all been lab one-armed machines that can be uncomfortable or impractical for the person being dressed.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (assisting a dependent person to dress); the developer's own framing confirms the field is still at laboratory stage as of 2024.

sources.developer: KAIST IRiS Lab with Stanford collaborators
sources.title: Self-Wearing Adaptive Garments via Soft Robotic Unfurling (arXiv:2507.07221)
sources.claim: The most recent autonomous dressing result requires a purpose-built pneumatic garment that crawls onto the body; it dresses a wearer with a special robotic suit rather than handling ordinary clothing or hospital gowns, and it does not undress anyone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous dressing of a person). Transfer fails: it requires a bespoke actuated garment, not the patient's street clothes or a tie-back hospital gown, and provides no undressing or patient handling.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: The main autonomous robot actually deployed in US hospitals performs only logistics and is explicitly non-patient-facing, indicating no fielded hospital robot performs hands-on patient dressing or changing.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (hospital ward/corridor, an E2 facility) but the deployed capability excludes physical contact with patients, so it cannot substantiate dressing or changing patients.

sources.system: Compliant gripper for robot-assisted trouser dressing-undressing
sources.title: Development of a compliant gripper for safe robot-assisted trouser dressing-undressing | Advanced Robotics
sources.claim: Robotic undressing capability is still at the component level: a compliant gripper for trouser dressing/undressing of elderly or hemiplegic people was designed and assessed in the laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Undressing is an essential half of this task (removing street clothes before imaging); the evidence shows only gripper hardware development, so whole-task undressing of patients is unsubstantiated.

tasks.label: Perform general administrative tasks, such as answering phones, scheduling patient appointments, or pulling and filing films.

tasks.label: Operate mobile x-ray equipment in operating room, emergency room, or at patient's bedside.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ICU/critical-care portable chest radiograph: tech wheels a mobile DR unit into a crowded ICU room past pumps, ventilator and lines, slides the flat-panel detector behind a sedated, intubated patient (usually with nursing help to roll or lift), angles the tube, collimates, selects technique, warns staff, exposes, and checks the image for line/tube position before releasing it.

Intraoperative mobile C-arm fluoroscopy for orthopedic/spine/vascular surgery: tech drapes the C-arm sterile, drives it into the field around table, anesthesia and staff, delivers AP/lateral and oblique live fluoro or spot images on the surgeon's verbal request, angles for the anatomy, manages dose and sterility, and stores/sends images.

Emergency department trauma bay: urgent portable chest and pelvis films on a patient on a backboard/stretcher with a full trauma team present; detector slid under the board, rapid tube positioning and exposure, dose control for surrounding staff, images pushed to PACS within minutes.

General ward or ED room bedside radiograph (chest, abdomen, hip, extremity) of a patient with limited mobility: tech assists positioning, props with sponges/pillows, adjusts for patient habitus and contracture, repeats views that are cut off or rotated.

Off-site mobile x-ray service call: portable unit carried into a skilled-nursing facility room or a private residence taken as found (furniture, low light, no fixed layout); frail patient imaged in bed or wheelchair, images transmitted remotely.

sources.title: Twin Robotic X-ray scanner – Multitom Rax
sources.claim: Siemens Multitom Rax is a commercially installed twin-robotic radiography system whose ceiling-mounted robotic arms carry the x-ray tube and detector and move automatically between programmed geometries (e.g., AP to lateral) around a supine trauma patient who is not moved; a technologist selects the exam at the console.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content (positioning tube and detector around a supine patient and acquiring radiographs, including trauma patients imaged without being moved), but performed by fixed robotics in a purpose-built x-ray suite rather than by a mobile unit at the bedside. Cited as context; autonomy of the full exam is not established, so it does not by itself carry a positive judgment.

sources.date: 2019 (textbook chapter); technology in clinical use since 2000s
sources.title: CyberKnife | Radiology Key
sources.claim: CyberKnife robotic radiosurgery systems, deployed clinically worldwide, automatically acquire kV x-ray images of the patient lying on the couch in a shielded vault throughout treatment, register them to reference DRRs, and realign the robotic source before each beam with no staff in the room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acquiring diagnostic-geometry x-ray images of a human patient and acting on them. Comparable object (a positioned live patient), comparable or higher precision (sub-millimeter), and the acquisition/exposure loop runs unattended inside a purpose-built shielded room, which is the E1 counterfactual for bedside radiography.

sources.system: Halcyon linear accelerator (kV/MV CBCT image guidance)
sources.title: Feasibility of using ring-mounted Halcyon Linac for single-isocenter/two-lesion lung stereotactic body radiation therapy (JACMP)
sources.claim: Varian Halcyon ring linacs used in routine radiotherapy acquire kV/MV cone-beam CT of the patient each fraction and apply the computed isocenter shifts automatically as part of a one-step patient setup, with therapists operating from outside the treatment vault.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated x-ray/CBCT imaging of a patient presented on a couch, with image evaluation and geometric correction executed by the machine. Demonstrates that, once a patient is fixtured in a purpose-built radiation room, image acquisition and verification proceed without a human at the machine.

sources.system: ZEISS BOSELLO OMNIA automated 2D x-ray inspection system
sources.title: Automated 2D X-Ray Defect Detection | ZEISS
sources.claim: ZEISS BOSELLO OMNIA is a commercially sold in-line 2D x-ray inspection cell in which robot-loaded workpieces are radiographed and the images evaluated automatically by Automatic Defect Recognition software during multi-shift production, without an operator running each exposure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating x-ray equipment end to end — presenting the object, positioning source and detector, setting exposure, acquiring and judging image adequacy — fully automatically in a fenced purpose-built cell. Transfer covers the acquisition and image-quality-check steps of radiography when the subject is fixtured; it does not cover handling a live patient.

sources.title: Experience Loop-X®: Mobile Robotic Imaging | Brainlab
sources.claim: Brainlab Loop-X is an FDA-cleared mobile imaging robot used in operating rooms that moves autonomously to stored positions to reacquire x-ray projections at one button press, with independently moving source and detector; it is commanded by OR staff from a wireless tablet.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (intraoperative x-ray imaging of a patient on the OR table), showing machine-executed positioning and reacquisition. It still requires staff to transport, drape, initially position and command the device, so it does not show unattended operation in the live OR.

roles.title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Technologists
aliases: MRI QA Coordinator (Magnetic Resonance Imaging Quality Assurance Coordinator)
MRI Special Procedures Technologist (Magnetic Resonance Imaging Special Procedures Technologist)
Research MRI Technologist (Research Magnetic Resonance Imaging Technologist)
Travel MRI Tech (Travel Magnetic Resonance Imaging Technician)
roles.description: Operate Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scanners. Monitor patient safety and comfort, and view images of area being scanned to ensure quality of pictures. May administer gadolinium contrast dosage intravenously. May interview patient, explain MRI procedures, and position patient on examining table. May enter into the computer data such as patient history, anatomical area to be scanned, orientation specified, and position of entry.

tasks.label: Review physicians' orders to confirm prescribed exams.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Conduct screening interviews of patients to identify contraindications, such as ferrous objects, pregnancy, prosthetic heart valves, cardiac pacemakers, or tattoos.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Select appropriate imaging techniques or coils to produce required images.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine brain/neuro MRI in a hospital or outpatient imaging suite: tech reads the order (headache, MS follow-up, stroke), selects the 20- or 32-channel head/neck coil, docks and plugs it into the table port, pads the head, then loads and tailors the protocol (DWI, FLAIR, MRA, post-contrast) at the console.

Spine MRI: uses the table-embedded posterior spine array plus an anterior/extension array that must be selected, laid on the patient and connected; tech then selects sagittal/axial T1, T2, STIR sequences and adapts for hardware or implant artifact.

MSK/extremity exam (knee, shoulder, wrist, ankle): tech picks the dedicated extremity or flexible wrap coil from the coil rack, seats and pads the limb inside it, connects it, and selects high-resolution PD/fat-sat sequences with oblique planning.

Body, abdomen/pelvis, breast or cardiac exam: tech selects and positions body array plus spine array, or a dedicated breast/cardiac coil, attaches gating leads or respiratory bellows, and selects breath-hold, dynamic contrast and gated techniques with timing.

Mid-exam adaptation: initial series shows motion, wrap or coil-element dropout, or the radiologist requests more sequences; tech re-enters the magnet room, reseats or swaps a coil/element and adds padding, then selects revised or additional sequences.

Non-standard or difficult cases: bariatric patients, MR-conditional implants requiring low-SAR protocols, pediatric or sedated patients, claustrophobic or trauma/ICU inpatients; tech improvises coil choice (flex/wrap arrays) and tailors technique to safety limits and patient tolerance.

sources.title: myExam Companion - Siemens Healthineers USA
sources.claim: Siemens Healthineers' myExam Companion (Autopilot / AutoCoil Select) is a commercial scanner software feature that automates protocol steering and coil-element selection on MAGNETOM MRI systems; it runs on the console and performs no physical retrieval, connection or placement of RF coils.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to document automation of the console/decision portion of the task; it is a software-only feature, not a robotic system, and it does not select, fetch, connect or place physical RF coils on a patient.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system
sources.developer: academic research group (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning ... () placed and force-controlled a probe on human subjects in a research feasibility study - the closest robotic analogue to applying sensing hardware to patient anatomy - but it is a research prototype with a conventional ferromagnetic manipulator unusable in an MRI magnet room, and it selects no coils or imaging techniques.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of an imaging sensor on a patient's body. It does not substantiate MRI coil selection - different modality, no MR-conditional hardware, research-stage reliability, and no choice among coil types or pulse sequences.

sources.system: Body-mounted robotic system for MRI-guided shoulder arthrography
sources.title: Body-Mounted Robotic System for MRI-Guided Shoulder Arthrography: Cadaver and Clinical Workflow Studies
sources.claim: MR-safe/MR-conditional robots exist in the MRI suite but are single-purpose needle-guidance devices - e.g. a body-mounted robot for MRI-guided shoulder arthrography tested in cadaver and clinical workflow studies - that are manually mounted and clinician-directed; none select, retrieve or place RF receive coils.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation inside an MRI scanner room. Shows MR-compatible robots are confined to needle guidance and are set up by humans, so capability does not carry over to selecting and applying imaging coils for a diagnostic exam.

sources.system: BEC articulated-arm robot cell (Festo electric cylinders) for MRI magnet coil insertion
sources.developer: BEC GmbH / Festo, for Siemens Healthineers
sources.title: Playing it safe in the assembly of MRI machines - Festo Press
sources.claim: Robotic 'coil' handling in MRI exists only in manufacturing: a BEC articulated-arm robot cell with Festo actuators inserts multi-tonne magnet coils into MRI magnets in a fenced factory assembly hall for Siemens Healthineers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of 'coils' in a purpose-built cell. It does not transfer - the objects, clinical selection logic, patient contact and imaging goal of RF receive-coil selection are entirely different from factory magnet assembly.

tasks.label: Operate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine outpatient brain or lumbar-spine MRI at a freestanding imaging center on a cooperative ambulatory adult: verify MR-safety screening and remove metal, gown/earplug the patient, position supine on the table, place and plug in head or spine array coils with padding, landmark, run the protocol from the console while watching the patient through the window/intercom, check each series for motion or artifact and repeat as needed, then help the patient off the table.

Musculoskeletal/extremity MRI (knee, shoulder, wrist, ankle) in a hospital or outpatient MRI suite: select and strap a dedicated extremity or flexible coil, position the joint at isocenter in an often awkward, oblique or off-center posture, pad and immobilize to prevent motion over 20-40 minutes, monitor comfort, adjust obliques on the console to the anatomy.

Contrast-enhanced MRI (e.g., brain with contrast, MR angiography, liver dynamic): confirm/insert or check IV access, load and prime the MR-compatible power injector, weight-based gadolinium dose, run pre-contrast sequences, trigger injection and time the dynamic phases, watch for extravasation or adverse reaction, and flush/remove the line afterwards.

Inpatient or ED patient arriving by stretcher or wheelchair in a hospital MRI suite: perform ferromagnetic implant/device screening and check lines, drains, telemetry and oxygen for MR conditionality, swap to MR-safe equipment, transfer the often heavy or immobile patient onto the table with help, position and coil a patient who cannot cooperate, monitor a potentially unstable patient throughout the scan, and abort/extract quickly if the patient deteriorates.

Pediatric, claustrophobic, or sedated/anesthetized patient: reassure and coach the patient or parent, immobilize the child with vacuum bags and padding, coordinate with anesthesia and MR-conditional monitoring, position coils around airway equipment, run the scan while watching vitals, and shorten or re-order sequences if the patient begins to wake or move.

Advanced exam requiring real-time operator judgment: cardiac MRI with ECG gating lead placement and repeated breath-hold coaching and on-the-fly plane prescription; or prone breast MRI positioning in a dedicated coil; or MR enterography with oral contrast and antiperistaltic timing — sequences are added, adapted or repeated during the exam based on what the images show.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot (AI agent + 6-DoF cable-driven robot)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital group
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv:2510.08106)
sources.claim: The closest demonstrated autonomous, patient-contacting diagnostic imaging robot: a 588 g cable-driven arm mounted on the abdomen that autonomously acquires standard liver ultrasound planes on human patients, first deployed in the ultrasound ... a hospital. It acquires images on an already-positioned patient; it does not move or position patients, handle coils, or operate a scanner.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous acquisition of diagnostic images on a live patient in a hospital imaging department. Transfer to MRI operation fails: the robot works on a self-positioned patient's abdomen with a hand-held-size probe, and does none of the MRI-specific physical work (patient transfer onto the table, receive-coil selection/placement and plugging, landmarking into the bore, MR-safety screening, in-bore monitoring), nor could a conventional actuated arm of this kind operate inside the magnet room.

sources.title: Siemens Healthineers Announces FDA Clearance of syngo Virtual Cockpit Remote Scanning Technology
sources.claim: State-of-the-art MRI 'automation' of the operator role is human teleoperation, not robotics: FDA-cleared remote-scanning software lets a human technologist run up to three remote scanners via live audio/video.

sources.system: Remote scanning 'cockpit' MRI operation at University Hospital Essen
sources.title: How teleoperation is changing radiology (healthcare-in-europe.com, ECR 2024 report)

sources.system: uMR 588 / uMR 570 with EasyScan one-click scanning and automatic table positioning
sources.title: uMR 588: 1.5T + uCS 2.0 imaging platform | United-Imaging
sources.claim: Commercially deployed MRI automation is confined to console sub-steps performed by the scanner itself: one-click automatic table positioning and automatic slice/orientation planning. The patient and the receive coils are still placed by a human before these functions run.

sources.system: n/a — description of the human MRI scanning workflow
sources.developer: MRI Questions (Allen D. Elster, reference text)
sources.title: MR scanning - Questions and Answers in MRI
sources.claim: The physical work of an MRI exam that a machine would have to take over: placing the patient on the table and arranging receive coils around the anatomy of interest, plus safety screening for metallic foreign bodies.

sources.developer: American College of Radiology (as summarized by MRI Med)
sources.title: MR Zones 1-4: Complete MRI Equipment Guidelines for Safety
sources.claim: Structural barrier to conventional robots doing this work: the scanner room (Zone IV) admits only MR Safe or MR ... because the magnet turns ferromagnetic objects into projectiles.

sources.system: MRI-compatible non-metallic prostate biopsy/ablation robot (Worcester Polytechnic Institute, Fischer lab)
sources.title: Inside an MRI, a Non-Metallic Robot Performs Prostate Surgery - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Robots that do work inside an MRI bore are specialized MR-conditional needle-guidance devices with limited autonomy; they position an instrument relative to imaging, and do not handle patients or run the scanner.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic action inside the MR magnet room. It shows MR-conditional actuation is possible, but the demonstrated capability is needle trajectory positioning under physician direction, not screening, transferring, positioning and coiling a patient or running an exam end to end.

tasks.label: Provide headphones or earplugs to patients to improve comfort and reduce unpleasant noise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine ambulatory adult outpatient, body/spine MRI at an imaging center: after screening, the tech hands foam earplugs (often rolling and inserting them, or checking the patient's insertion) and then places MR-safe pneumatic or fiber-optic headphones over the patient's ears while the patient lies supine on the table, routing the sound tubes, adding pads, and confirming the intercom is audible.

Brain or head/neck MRI in a hospital: earplugs plus ear pads/headphones must be fitted within the tight confines of a head coil, with foam padding for immobilization, without displacing the head, obstructing coil closure, or creating pressure points; fit is verified through the intercom before the coil is closed and the table advanced.

Sedated, anesthetized, intubated or non-communicative inpatient transferred from a stretcher, often with IV lines and anesthesia tubing: the tech must insert earplugs into an unresponsive patient's ears and secure headphones without patient cooperation or feedback, checking skin and pressure points, coordinating with anesthesia staff.

Pediatric patient (awake, anxious child) or highly anxious/claustrophobic adult: child-sized hearing protection, coaxing and reassurance, possibly with a parent present, sometimes selecting music through the headphones; repeated repositioning if the child pulls the plugs or headset off.

Patient with complicating factors: hearing aids or cochlear devices that must be removed and stored, language barrier or cognitive impairment requiring alternative instruction, limited mobility or bariatric body habitus making head access awkward; the tech must still ensure hearing protection is properly fitted and two-way communication (squeeze ball, intercom) works.
Prep/changing/screening area hand-off: a cooperative ambulatory adult is simply given a packaged pair of disposable earplugs to insert themselves while waiting, with brief verbal instruction.

sources.title: Cafe X Opens New Version of its Robot Barista in San Jose Airport
sources.claim: Cafe X operates enclosed robotic coffee kiosks in airport terminals where a six-axis arm autonomously prepares and delivers drinks to arbitrary members of the public, unattended — evidence that an autonomous machine can hand a prepared item to a person at a station inside a structured human facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispensing a prepared item to a walk-up customer. Transfers to the narrow 'hand a packaged pair of earplugs to a cooperative ambulatory patient' instance — comparable object size, no contact with the person's body, and a comparable institution-controlled setting (airport concourse vs. imaging-center prep area).

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark (Odense)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot station performed naso- and oropharyngeal sampling on 52 suspected COVID-19 patients in two clinical studies, driving a swab into a seated, cooperative subject's nose/throat under force-controlled autonomy at a purpose-built station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise autonomous instrument insertion at a human head. It marks the frontier of robot-to-patient head contact, but does not substantiate this task: it inserts a rigid, pre-mounted swab into a fixtured, seated, cooperative adult, whereas providing hearing protection requires compressing deformable foam plugs, manipulating the pinna, and seating a headset on a supine patient inside an MR head coil.

sources.title: Brain Navi Develops New Robot Performing Nasal Swab Tests to Prevent Cross Infections
sources.claim: A nasal swab robot autonomously recognizes a patient's facial structure and nostril location to collect samples, demonstrated in Taiwan; no comparable system has been shown fitting hearing protection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous face/landmark-guided contact with a patient's head. Cited to show the closest existing capability; it performs one programmed insertion on a cooperative seated adult and does not cover selecting, fitting and verifying earplugs or headphones.

sources.title: Panasonic's robot gives a 16-finger, automated hair washing
sources.claim: A head-care robot autonomously 3D-scans a person's head and uses robot-arm-guided fingers to wash and rinse hair with regulated pressure, but only with the head fixtured in a purpose-built basin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous compliant contact with a human head at a purpose-built station. It supports only stereotyped scalp contact in a fixtured basin; it does not place or fit an object on the head, so it does not substantiate providing and fitting headphones or earplugs.

sources.title: Figure humanoid robots organize room, hang clothes, and make bed without humans
sources.claim: Humanoid robots have been shown tidying a room and handling headphones as an object (placing them away), but not placing hearing protection on a person; the demonstration is a released video in a staged home-like room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose manipulation of everyday objects including headphones. Cited only to bound the frontier: object tidying in a staged room does not transfer to fitting hearing protection on a patient's head at clinical safety and comfort standards, and the video's autonomy is not independently established.

tasks.label: Position patients on cradle, attaching immobilization devices, if needed, to ensure appropriate placement for imaging.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine outpatient brain or spine MRI in a hospital/imaging-center MR suite: after safety screening, the ambulatory adult is helped supine onto the scanner cradle, head seated in the head/neck coil with foam pads, knee bolster and blanket placed, earplugs and squeeze-ball given, spine coil position checked, laser landmark set on the anatomy of interest.

Musculoskeletal extremity exam (knee, shoulder, wrist, ankle) on an ambulatory patient: the limb is seated in a dedicated extremity/shoulder coil, held at a specific joint angle (e.g., external rotation, ABER, prone 'superman' wrist), then padded, sandbagged and strapped so it cannot move during a 20-40 minute acquisition.

Body imaging (abdomen/pelvis, breast, cardiac): torso array coil laid over or under the patient, arms raised overhead or positioned off the coil, ECG electrodes and respiratory bellows attached and checked, or prone positioning in a breast coil with the breasts arranged in the apertures, straps applied.

Non-ambulatory inpatient or ED patient arriving on a bed/stretcher: lateral transfer to the MR cradle with slide board, hover mat, lift or 2-3 staff, while managing IV lines, oxygen, drains and MR-conditional monitoring; limbs of a patient who cannot assist are positioned and padded by the technologist.

Pediatric, sedated, anxious/claustrophobic or cognitively impaired patient: coaching and reassurance, head immobilization pads/vacuum bag, straps and sometimes a papoose or parental hold; a sedated infant is placed in an immobilizer with airway and lines protected.

Bariatric, trauma or post-operative patient with casts, contractures, pain or limited range of motion: careful assisted positioning on the cradle with extra padding, non-standard limb placement, custom immobilization and repeated adjustment for comfort and coil coverage.

sources.system: Robotic Patient Positioning System (6-DOF robotic treatment couch) in proton therapy
sources.developer: proton therapy system vendors (robotic PPS as described in clinical proton centers)
sources.title: Real-time Motion Management for Robotic Treatment Couch in Proton Therapy System
sources.claim: Clinically deployed proton-therapy patient positioning systems use a 6-DOF robotic arm carrying a couch top to position an already-immobilized patient to sub-millimetre accuracy under image guidance; the robot moves the couch, while staff place the patient on it and apply the immobilization devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: setting a patient at the imaging/treatment isocenter. Transfer is only partial - the robot repositions a couch whose occupant was already placed and immobilized by humans, so it does not substantiate placing a person on a cradle or attaching immobilization devices.

sources.title: Able Innovations Partners With Lahey Hospital To Launch ALTA Platform In U.S.
sources.claim: The ALTA Platform is a hospital robotic device that performs lateral supine transfers between beds, stretchers, imaging tables and OR tables; it is launched in Canadian and US hospitals but is driven and triggered by an on-site staff operator and performs only the flat lateral slide, not anatomic positioning or coil/immobilization setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a supine patient onto an imaging table. Only the flat transfer is mechanized and a staff member positions the device and controls the cycle, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion of patient positioning for MRI.

sources.title: Robotic patient transfer device launches at Ottawa hospital
sources.claim: Press coverage of the same device confirms each transfer is initiated by a human operator at the bedside ('press of a button') across five Canadian hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient transfer onto a table. Operator-commanded for each transfer, so it counts as operator-controlled and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Reduction of multiple-caregiver assistance through the long-term use of a transfer support robot in a nursing facility
sources.claim: The most capable commercial patient-handling robots in care facilities (Fuji 'Hug', Panasonic Resyone) are caregiver-operated transfer aids: a caregiver positions the device, secures the resident and runs the lift; there is no autonomous placement of a person into a prescribed imaging posture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting/transferring a patient. Requires a caregiver to operate the device and secure the person, so it does not substantiate autonomous patient positioning.

sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the best-known robot able to lift a patient from a bed, remained an experimental caregiver-guided prototype and was never fielded commercially.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and transferring a patient. Experimental and operator-guided, never shown placing a patient in a prescribed imaging position, so it does not substantiate completion.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University with Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound systems can place and force-control a probe on a patient's torso in a hospital imaging department, showing autonomous robot-patient contact is feasible; however the patient positions himself on the bed and the robot neither moves the patient nor attaches immobilization hardware, and such arms are not MR-conditional.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously bringing an imaging device into contact with a patient's body. It covers only surface contact with a self-positioned cooperative patient, not lifting or arranging the body or fastening coils, pads and straps.

sources.system: Body-mounted MRI-compatible robotic assistant for low back pain injection
sources.title: A Fully Actuated Body-Mounted Robotic Assistant for MRI-Guided Low Back Pain Injection
sources.claim: In MRI robotics research the human patient is still positioned by people: in an MRI-guided injection study a volunteer was placed on ... by staff and the robot itself was strapped on by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (MRI scanner table) and same objects (a patient, straps): it shows that even purpose-built MR-compatible robots depend on humans for patient placement and strapping.

tasks.label: Intravenously inject contrast dyes, such as gadolinium contrast, in accordance with scope of practice.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient imaging center MRI suite: cooperative adult with easily palpable antecubital veins, routine non-timing-critical contrast study (brain, spine, MSK). Tech verifies weight-based gadolinium dose and renal/allergy screening, applies tourniquet, starts a 20-22G IV, confirms patency with saline, administers the contrast, watches the site and patient for reaction, flushes and removes the line.

Adult with difficult venous access (elderly, obese, dehydrated, chemotherapy-scarred veins) needing a routine non-timing-critical contrast exam; tech palpates/warms, may use vein-finder, sometimes sticks the hand or forearm, may need a second attempt or help before contrast can be given.

Timing-critical dynamic contrast study (breast MRI, MRA, liver/abdomen dynamic, prostate DCE, cardiac perfusion): IV placed, extension tubing run to an MR-conditional power injector, patient positioned in the bore, bolus plus saline chaser delivered at a set rate synchronized to the pulse sequence, injection site and patient monitored for extravasation from the console.

Patient arrives with vascular access already in place (inpatient/ED peripheral IV, PICC, central line, or implanted port): tech assesses and disinfects the hub, flushes to confirm patency and absence of infiltration, connects the syringe or injector tubing, hand-injects or power-injects the gadolinium, flushes and disconnects, documents.

Pediatric, anxious, cognitively impaired, or sedated/stretcher-bound patient: small or fragile veins, movement, need for coaching, distraction, holding or parental assistance; access is obtained and contrast injected under these conditions, sometimes with a nurse or IV team present.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta performs the complete blood-draw venipuncture autonomously on a patient whose arm is placed in the device: vein selection with near-infrared and Doppler ultrasound, needle insertion, tube handling and ..., with one supervisor overseeing several devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It transfers to the access step of IV contrast injection - the same object (an adult's antecubital vein), the same sub-millimetre needle-placement precision, the same fixtured-arm presentation in a hospital. It does not cover leaving an indwelling catheter, injecting fluid into the patient, or post-injection extravasation monitoring.

sources.title: Automated Phlebotomy Firm Vitestro Eyes 2027 Commercial Launch of Robotic Blood Draw Device | 360Dx
sources.claim: In Vitestro's pivotal clinical study the autonomous device achieved 95% first-stick success overall, including 93% in patients with difficult venous ... and 97% in obese patients; CE-marked, with European commercial launch planned for 2027 and an FDA de novo submission planned.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (venipuncture); the difficult-access subgroup result is what supports judging the difficult-vein contrast instance, since the vein-finding and puncture problem is identical.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70M to ready blood collection robot for US launch | MedTech Dive
sources.claim: The Aletta device automates the venipuncture cycle end to end - tourniquet, imaging-based vein selection with Doppler confirmation that the target is a vein not an artery, needle insertion, sample collection and bandaging - and is being readied for US launch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture. Confirms the machine handles the whole access sequence unattended, including artery-avoidance, which is the safety-critical part shared with starting an IV for contrast.

sources.system: MEDRAD Spectris Solaris EP MR Injection System
sources.title: Medrad Spectris Solaris EP - MR Injection System
sources.claim: MR-conditional power injectors are programmable dual-syringe machines that deliver the gadolinium bolus and saline flush into the patient's vascular system at set rate and volume during MRI exams; a human must still place the IV and connect the tubing.
sources.transferJustification: Not a related task but the same task's delivery step: machine-controlled metered delivery of gadolinium is already standard equipment, so within a purpose-built injection station the fluid-delivery half of the instance is covered; it contributes nothing to obtaining or connecting the access.

sources.title: Hyperion completes first-in-human study of Ivy robotic vascular access platform
sources.claim: The first robotic-assisted peripheral IV catheterization in a human was reported in October 2025 as a first-in-human feasibility study; the Ivy platform holds probe and needle and places the catheter, but it is described as robotic-assisted/semi-autonomous and is not in clinical service.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the catheter-placement step of this task; cited to show that autonomous placement of an indwelling IV catheter is at first-in-human feasibility stage only, which is why the catheter-dependent instances are judged E0.

tasks.label: Test magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) equipment to ensure proper functioning and performance in accordance with specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-day scanner QC phantom scan in a hospital or outpatient MRI suite: technologist carries the vendor QA phantom (spherical/bottle phantom) from the shelf, seats it in the head coil on the table, landmarks it at isocenter with the laser, advances the table, runs the vendor's automated daily QA program (center frequency, transmit gain, SNR, ..., geometric accuracy), confirms results are within tolerance, logs them, and removes the phantom.

Weekly/monthly ACR-type phantom QC for accreditation: technologist levels and precisely aligns the ACR MRI phantom in the head coil, runs the prescribed sagittal localizer and axial series, measures/checks geometric accuracy, slice-position and thickness accuracy, high-contrast resolution, low-contrast object detectability, uniformity, ghosting, records values on the QC form and compares against action limits.

RF coil checks and verification test scans: technologist mounts and plugs in different receive coils (spine, body, knee, flex, breast), places phantoms or fluid bottles in each, runs coil-check/SNR sequences, inspects images for dead elements, artifacts or noise spikes, and repeats test scans after a service visit or when an artifact appears, escalating failures to the service engineer.

Functional and visual checks of scanner-room and ancillary equipment: intercom and patient squeeze-alert, MR-conditional monitors (ECG, pulse-ox), power injector test/purge, helium level and magnet vitals on the display, emergency stop and quench button integrity, door interlock, ferromagnetic detector alarm, table motion and laser lights, and inspection of coils, cables and housings for damage.

Acceptance, post-upgrade or annual performance testing performed with or for the medical physicist: multiple specialty phantoms and coil loadings, longer specialized sequences (large-FOV distortion, spectroscopy, MRgRT end-to-end), setup changes between series, and recording of results against manufacturer specifications.

sources.system: Vendor automated daily QA packages on clinical MRI scanners (Siemens/GE/Philips)
sources.title: Routine Quality Control - Questions and Answers in MRI
sources.claim: Clinical MRI scanners ship with automated daily QA programs in which the scanner itself acquires phantom test images and computes the QC metrics (center frequency, transmit gain, SNR, ..., geometric accuracy) once the phantom is in place; the technologist's remaining role in the phantom scan is placement and logging.

sources.title: QUASAR MRI⁴ᴰ Motion Phantom: IBA Dosimetry
sources.claim: A commercial MR-safe programmable phantom platform with piezoelectric motors operates inside the MR bore, positioning and moving a QA phantom under computer control with sub-millimetre accuracy on MR-linacs and diagnostic MR scanners.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: motion-management QA rather than image-quality QC. It transfers to the physical part of QC scanning because it shows a nonmagnetic, computer-controlled stage can hold and position a QA phantom at a commanded pose inside the bore during QA acquisitions, i.e. the phantom can be fixtured and presented to the scanner without a human in Zone IV.

sources.system: Six-DOF MR-conditional phantom robot (Dunn et al.)
sources.developer: Academic group, published in Physics in Medicine & Biology
sources.title: Design and testing of an MR-conditional six-degree-of-freedom phantom robot - IOPscience
sources.claim: A six-degree-of-freedom MR-conditional phantom robot has been built and tested that positions a phantom inside the MRI bore in translation and rotation with accuracy comparable to commercial single-axis piezoelectric motion phantoms (0.2-0.25 mm translation).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reproducing physiological motion of a phantom in the bore. It transfers because the decisive physical requirement of QC scanning is holding a phantom at a known, repeatable pose at isocentre; this MR-conditional robot demonstrates programmable sub-millimetre phantom pose control inside a scanner.

sources.system: OSAQA (open source automatic quality assurance tool for the ACR MRI phantom)
sources.title: An open source automatic quality assurance (OSAQA) tool for the ACR MRI phantom - PubMed
sources.claim: Automated analysis software evaluates the full ACR MRI phantom test set (geometric distortion, slice position/thickness, high-contrast resolution, uniformity, ghosting, low-contrast object detectability) from the acquired images, cutting evaluation from about 45 minutes of manual work to about 2 minutes with results matching manual measurement.

sources.title: AutoMRISimQA: an automated system for daily quality control of a 3T MRI simulator
sources.claim: A daily QC system for a 3T MRI simulator runs fully automatically once the phantom images leave the console, producing the constancy-check image-quality indices and geometric accuracy report without further human processing.

sources.title: AI as the Invisible Medical Physicist: Automating QA in CT, MRI, and Mammography
sources.claim: In current commercial radiology QA workflows the acquisition step of a phantom QC scan is still performed by a human technologist; only the downstream analysis and reporting are automated.

sources.system: Routine MRI QC program (professional practice description)
sources.title: Routine Quality Control - Questions and Answers in MRI
sources.claim: Daily/frequent MRI QC also comprises visual inspection of scanner hardware, ..., with the technologist judging noises, artifacts and malfunctions.
