tasks.label: Calibrate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) console or peripheral hardware.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily QA/calibration scan in a hospital or outpatient imaging-center MRI suite: tech carries the manufacturer's QA phantom into Zone IV, seats it in the head coil on the table, aligns it with the laser landmark, advances it to isocenter, runs the automated daily quality/calibration series (center frequency, transmit gain, SNR, ...), reviews and logs results, reports out-of-tolerance findings before the first patient.

Peripheral hardware check and setup in the scan room and control room: connect/disconnect RF coils and verify coil elements and cabling, test patient communication (intercom, headphones, squeeze ball), verify MR-conditional physiological monitoring gear, load and prime the MR-conditional contrast power injector (syringes, purge air, verify flow/pressure settings), inspect emergency/safety devices.

Console-level adjustment at the operator workstation: verify and adjust system/protocol calibration values, monitor and display settings, table landmark offsets and reconstruction parameters, re-run software calibration routines or reboot subsystems after error codes, confirm the console reports a passing system state.

Weekly/monthly ACR phantom QC: precise placement and orientation of the ACR large phantom in the head coil (leveling, angulation, landmarking to marked reference), acquisition of the ACR series, measurement of geometric accuracy, slice thickness, high-contrast resolution, uniformity and low-contrast detectability, recording values on QC forms and comparing to action limits.

Recalibration and verification after service or a hardware change in the MRI suite: after a coil, gradient or electronics swap, re-run system calibrations with the service engineer, check helium level and chiller/gradient cooling readouts, scan a phantom to confirm image quality, and sign the scanner back into clinical service.

Mobile MRI trailer or portable/low-field scanner: after transport or relocation, power up, verify leveling and environmental conditions, run system calibration and QA phantom acquisition, and troubleshoot peripheral hardware (coils, injector, monitoring) before scanning begins at the site.

sources.title: Remote Controlled Manipulator – Imaging Solutions
sources.claim: The nearest robotic system that works inside an MRI bore is a remote-controlled needle-guide manipulator for prostate biopsy; it is MR-compatible but is driven by a clinician from the control room, and it manipulates only a needle guide, not phantoms, coils or console hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Closest MR-environment manipulator to this task. It shows in-bore robotics is possible only with purpose-built MR-compatible hardware and, in this case, remote human control; it performs needle-guide positioning, not phantom placement, coil connection, or reading out and logging calibration results, so it cannot substantiate completion of the calibration task.

sources.system: BEC articulated arm robot with Festo EPCC-actuated gripper
sources.title: Playing it safe in the assembly of MRI machines | Festo Press
sources.claim: A very large articulated-arm robot with a 3D-scanner-equipped gripper autonomously inserts multi-tonne coils into MRI magnets on the Siemens Healthineers MRI production line, to 0.5 mm tolerance, with humans only monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling MRI coils. It demonstrates precise autonomous handling of MRI components, but only in a factory assembly hall with unenergized magnets and a fixtured workpiece; the machine is massive ferromagnetic industrial hardware that cannot operate beside an energized clinical magnet, and it performs no calibration measurement, phantom setup or QC read-out.

sources.system: Multitom Rax twin robotic X-ray system
sources.title: Siemens Healthineers Announces First Install of Multitom Rax Twin Robotic X-ray System
sources.claim: A commercial twin-robotic-arm radiography system in hospital imaging rooms moves the X-ray tube and detector into position automatically, showing that automated positioning of imaging hardware exists in a structured hospital imaging room but is limited to moving its own gantry components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated positioning of imaging equipment in a radiology room. It is a dedicated gantry that repositions its own tube and detector under operator command; it cannot carry or seat a phantom, plug in coils, prime an injector, or evaluate calibration results, and it is X-ray, not MR, hardware.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulators are deployed at scale in US hospital corridors, but their demonstrated work is transporting medications, lab specimens and supplies, not equipment calibration or fine hardware manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals (E2). It establishes the current frontier of hospital robots as point-to-point delivery with simple grasping; it does not perform equipment QA, and its ferromagnetic mobile base could not enter the MR projectile area, so it does not transfer to MRI console or peripheral hardware calibration.

tasks.label: Troubleshoot technical issues related to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanner or peripheral equipment, such as monitors or coils.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/outpatient MRI suite, mid-exam: images show poor signal-to-noise, dropout or artifact traced to a surface coil. Tech unplugs and reseats the coil connector at the table port, swaps in a spare coil of the same type, re-runs a localizer/QC scan to confirm the fix, tags the bad coil out of service and logs a service call. Patient is on the table; work occurs partly inside the 5-gauss magnet room.

Scanner console/host or gradient subsystem faults mid-exam (frozen console, sequence abort, error code). Tech clears the error, restarts the sequence, and if needed performs a controlled shutdown/reboot of the host computer and system cabinets in the equipment room (key switches, breakers, reset buttons), then re-establishes the exam and verifies image quality before resuming.

Peripheral/ancillary equipment failure: MR-conditional patient monitor or ECG/pulse-ox telemetry not reading, in-bore camera or intercom dead, headphone/audio fiber disconnected, power injector alarming, or in-room display blank. Tech inspects and reseats cables and fiber leads, replaces electrodes/pads or batteries, tests function with the patient, and works around or escalates if unresolved.

RF interference / image-quality investigation: zipper or spike artifacts prompt the tech to check that the RF door is fully closed and finger stock/gaskets are clean, inspect the penetration panel and waveguides, remove offending devices (unapproved cable, pad, LED light) from the room, run a spike/noise QC sequence, and interpret the result to isolate the source or escalate to service.

Magnet/infrastructure alarms and hardware faults: helium level or cold-head/compressor alarm, chiller or water-flow fault, gradient over-temperature, table/patient-transport motion failure, or vent-path warning. Tech reads gauges and alarm panels, checks the chiller and cold head, resets or power-cycles what protocol allows, decides whether scanning can continue, notifies the service engineer, and documents the event.

sources.system: MR-conditional robotic actuation (review; incl. MR-conditional lumbar spinal injection robot)
sources.developer: Academic groups (review published in PMC; MR-conditional spinal injection robot)
sources.title: MR-Conditional Actuations: A Review - PMC
sources.claim: Ferromagnetic materials and conventional actuators are prohibited inside the MRI scanner room; robots that operate there are purpose-built MR-conditional manipulators for needle guidance/interventions, not machines that service scanner hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot operation inside an MRI magnet room. It bounds the environment for this task: any machine reseating coils, cables or RF door hardware in Zone IV must be MR-conditional, and the only such robots demonstrated are single-purpose needle-guidance manipulators that neither diagnose nor service scanner or peripheral equipment.

sources.title: Moxi, healthcare robot created in Austin, completes 500k deliveries
sources.claim: The most capable robots actually deployed in US hospitals perform point-to-point fetch-and-deliver of supplies and medications along corridors; none is documented diagnosing or repairing imaging equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside a hospital (an E2 facility). Cited to establish the ceiling of deployed hospital robotics — transport and simple pick-and-place — with no fault isolation, connector servicing, or post-repair verification, so capability does not transfer to MRI troubleshooting.

sources.title: AEON humanoid robot deployed in factory to push real-world automation
sources.claim: Humanoid robots entering industrial service in 2025 are limited to inspection routes, part handling, machine tending and data capture in factories; none is shown performing hypothesis-driven fault diagnosis and corrective repair of complex equipment end-to-end.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose humanoid inspection and machine tending in a structured facility. Cited as state of the art for robot work on equipment; scope is predefined inspection and handling rather than diagnosing a fault and effecting a verified repair, so it does not substantiate this task at any tier.

tasks.label: Connect physiological leads to physiological acquisition control (PAC) units.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cardiac MRI gating hookup: in a hospital MRI suite, the tech preps the skin (wipe/abrade, shave if hairy), peels and places 4 MR-conditional adhesive ECG/VCG electrodes in a tight vector pattern on the patient's chest, snaps the lead wires onto each stud, attaches/pairs the wireless VCG module of the PAC unit, routes leads to avoid loops, and checks the gating trace on the console, re-placing electrodes if the R-wave is poor.

Respiratory gating for abdominal/thoracic/pelvic MRI: the tech wraps the respiratory bellows belt around the patient's abdomen or lower chest, tensions and fastens it while the patient lies on the table, connects the bellows tube/cable to the PAC port on the table or penetration panel, and verifies a clean respiratory waveform before coils are placed.

Monitoring hookup for sedated, anesthetized, contrast, or inpatient cases: peripheral pulse/pulse-oximeter sensor clipped on a finger or toe, ECG monitoring leads and sometimes a BP cuff applied, all connected to the MR-conditional monitor/PAC unit, with cables routed away from skin and the bore wall to prevent burns; signals confirmed before the table moves in.

Difficult patients: pediatric, bariatric, frail elderly, tremulous or uncooperative patients, or patients with dressings, lines, or a very hairy chest; requires coaching, log-rolling or repositioning the patient, repeated electrode placement, and sometimes re-attaching leads to the PAC unit partway through the exam with the patient partly in the bore.

Equipment-side only, no patient contact: mating lead sets and sensor cables into the PAC unit ports, docking/undocking or swapping the telemetry module and batteries, plugging PAC cabling into the table or penetration-panel receptacles, and troubleshooting or replacing a faulty connector or cable between exams.

sources.system: Eureka Robotics force-controlled connector insertion (Eureka Controller + 3D camera)
sources.title: Automated Connector Insertion in Automotive Wire Harness Assembly
sources.claim: Commercial vision- and force-controlled robotic system performs automated mating of male-to-female electrical connectors in automotive wire-harness assembly, including grasping connectors off a moving slider, in an industrial cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial connector mating. The equipment-side MRI instance is the same class of act — grasping a flexible lead cable and seating a small multi-pin connector into a receptacle with controlled force — at comparable part scale and insertion precision, so performance carries over when the connectors are presented in known poses as in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Learning-augmented robotic automation for real-world manufacturing
sources.claim: Learned robotic system deployed on a live electric-motor production line autonomously performed deformable cable insertion and soldering for over 5 hours, producing 108 motors at a 99.4% pass rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: insertion of a deformable cable into a fixtured receptacle on a production line. Handling limp lead wires and seating them reliably is the core difficulty of connecting physiological leads to a PAC unit; the demonstrated reliability and cable-handling transfer to an E1 presentation of that work.

sources.title: Vexev's VxWave System Successfully Meets Clinical Endpoints in Landmark Study Evaluating Robotic Ultrasound Scanning for Mapping Vascular Access at U.S. Renal Care Dialysis Clinics
sources.claim: Robotic ultrasound system performs semi-autonomous vascular mapping scans on patients inside dialysis clinics; represents the deployed frontier of robotic patient-contact work in a clinical facility, and involves pressing a rigid probe rather than applying adhesive sensors or connecting leads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous contact of a sensor with a patient's body in a clinical facility. Cited to bound the frontier: the deployed system only presses a rigid probe with force control and does not peel and place adhesive electrodes, wrap a bellows belt, or snap lead wires.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling framework for robotic wound redressing
sources.developer: Liang, Shen, Zhang, Atar, Richter, Yip (UC San Diego)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Research framework demonstrates autonomous detachment and wrinkle-free placement of adhesive tape on anatomical surfaces in a laboratory workspace, as a subtask toward robotic wound redressing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peel-and-place of an adhesive on a body-like surface, the manipulation at the heart of electrode application. Cited as a bound: it is a lab-bench subtask prototype on surrogate surfaces, not a system that completes an electrode-and-lead hookup on a live patient at worker quality.

sources.title: Portable robot for autonomous venipuncture using 3D near infrared image guidance
sources.claim: Image-guided venipuncture robot autonomously inserts a needle into a vein of a human arm placed in the device's fixture, demonstrating autonomous robotic contact with a fixtured human limb.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic procedure on a fixtured human limb. Cited to bound the frontier — the demonstrated act is a rigid needle insertion into an immobilized arm, not adhesive electrode placement on a torso, belt wrapping, or lead-wire connection.

tasks.label: Operate optical systems to capture dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images, such as functional brain imaging, real-time organ motion tracking, or musculoskeletal anatomy and trajectory visualization.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Functional brain MRI (presurgical language/motor mapping or research fMRI) in a hospital MRI suite: technologist screens and positions the patient in the head coil, mounts the mirror on the coil, aligns the in-room projector/screen or in-bore display, connects headphones, button-box responses and sometimes an in-bore eye tracker, verifies the patient can see the stimulus, launches the EPI paradigm synchronized with stimulus triggers, watches motion/quality in real time, and repeats runs that fail.

Dynamic body imaging (cardiac cine, real-time free-breathing abdominal/DCE liver, MRA) in an outpatient imaging center: technologist places surface coils and ECG/vector leads, sets up the respiratory sensor (optical/camera-based touchless sensing or bellows), coaches breath-holds over the intercom, times injector-triggered dynamic series, and monitors real-time reconstructions for motion or timing failure.

Neuro exam with optical prospective motion correction on a restless, pediatric, or movement-disorder patient: technologist mounts the in-bore camera/vision extenders or attaches the Moire-phase marker to forehead or a bite bar, runs the camera-to-scanner cross-calibration, confirms marker visibility inside the bore, then acquires and supervises the motion-corrected dynamic series.

Dynamic/kinematic musculoskeletal MRI (knee, shoulder, wrist, TMJ) in a hospital MRI suite: technologist fits the joint into a dedicated positioning/loading device and coil, rehearses the cyclic motion or serial positions with the patient, runs real-time or gated cine sequences, and checks that the trajectory of the joint is captured within the field of view.

Real-time organ-motion tracking for guided procedures: cine MRI gating on an MR-Linac, MR-guided intervention, or real-time speech/swallowing MRI. Technologist sets up in-room camera/surface monitoring and audio, positions immobilization devices, starts continuous real-time acquisition, and adjusts tracking planes and quality during the session with clinicians present.

sources.title: myExam Companion - Siemens Healthineers
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial automation of MRI patient setup is a ceiling/bore-mounted 3D camera that speeds registration and drives automatic table positioning to isocenter; it senses and moves the table but performs no manipulation — a human technologist still places the patient, coils, mirror and stimulus hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated patient positioning/registration for MRI. It covers only table motion and slice planning, not the physical setup of optical stimulus, mirrors, markers, coils or patient handling required by this task, so it does not substantiate completion.

sources.system: VitalEye (Ingenia Elition and other Philips MR systems)
sources.title: AI-enabled solutions | Philips
sources.claim: Camera-based touchless respiratory sensing removes the operator step of strapping a respiratory belt for dynamic body MRI, but it is a passive optical sensor with no actuation and the operator still performs all patient handling and exam setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: optical/camera sensing during dynamic MRI. It automates one signal-acquisition step only; it is not an embodied system acting on the patient or hardware, so it cannot complete the instance.

sources.title: Markerless motion tracking and correction for PET, MRI, and simultaneous PET/MRI | PLOS One
sources.claim: Markerless optical head-motion tracking for MRI exists as a research/clinical camera system (in-bore vision extenders, out-of-bore electronics), demonstrating that the optical tracking itself can run automatically once a human has installed and cross-calibrated the hardware and positioned the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: optical motion tracking during MRI. The tracker is a sensor operated by a technologist, not a machine that sets up or runs the exam, so it does not substantiate completion of the instance.

sources.system: syngo Virtual Cockpit / Expert-i remote scanning
sources.date: 2024-2026 (FDA/Health Canada cleared; clinical experience published Jan 2026)
sources.title: Remote Scanning | Siemens Healthineers
sources.claim: State-of-the-art 'unstaffed' MRI operation is remote human teleoperation: cleared remote scanning products explicitly require trained personnel physically present at the scanner to prepare and position the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: it is the closest thing to operating an MRI exam without an on-site technologist, and it confirms that a human must still be present at the magnet, so no machine completes the physical portion of the task.

sources.system: auto-RUSS (autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system, 7-DoF arm)
sources.developer: Lin et al., Frontiers in Robotics and AI (Chinese hospital/university group)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: The closest robotic system that performs an imaging exam on a person is an autonomous robotic ultrasound arm using force control and visual servoing, demonstrated on healthy volunteers in a research setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-conducted medical imaging on a patient. Transfer fails: the arm is a conventional ferromagnetic manipulator that cannot enter an MRI magnet room, it only places a probe rather than setting up coils, mirrors, stimulus optics and markers, and it was tested on healthy volunteers in a lab.

tasks.label: Attach physiological monitoring leads to patient's finger, chest, waist, or other body parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult outpatient MRI (contrast, anxious, or at-risk patient): tech clips an MR-conditional fiber-optic pulse-oximeter probe onto a chosen finger while the patient lies on the scanner table, routes the cable straight along the body to avoid conductive loops/burns, tapes it, and confirms a clean plethysmograph/SpO2 trace on the console before the table moves into the bore.

Cardiac / ECG-gated MRI: expose the chest, prep skin (wipe with alcohol, sometimes clip hair or lightly abrade), place 3-4 MR-conditional gel electrodes in the prescribed vector-ECG pattern on the left chest/sternum, snap on the wireless ECG pod or lead wires, then check R-wave trigger quality and reposition electrodes if gating is poor.

Respiratory-gated abdominal/thoracic MRI: wrap the respiratory bellows belt around the patient's waist or lower chest, thread the strap under or around the torso, tension and buckle it under (or over) the body coil without over-compressing, and verify the respiratory waveform on the console.

Sedated/anesthetized adult or pediatric patient: working alongside the anesthesia team, attach pulse-ox probe to a small finger or toe, ECG electrodes, BP cuff and capnography line, on an unconscious or squirming child amid blankets, immobilizers, IV lines and coils, all with MR-conditional equipment and strict cable routing.

Difficult or atypical adult: obese body habitus, tremor or movement disorder, cold poorly perfused fingers requiring a toe or earlobe probe, casts/dressings/IVs occupying limbs, contact-isolation precautions, or a confused patient who needs coaching and re-attachment after repositioning.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device - CAP TODAY
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a CE-marked, commercially launched autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that carries out the whole blood-draw sequence on a patient's arm presented in the machine, including placing a tourniquet band on the limb and applying an adhesive bandage to the skin afterwards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous phlebotomy. Transfer to attaching a monitoring probe/lead: the device autonomously places a band (tourniquet) and an adhesive item (bandage) onto a human limb presented in its purpose-built armrest, in a clinical draw setting, at precision (needle into vein lumen) well above that needed to clip a pulse-oximeter probe onto a presented finger.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: The Vitestro device obtained EU CE marking in 2024 and was launched into European healthcare settings in March 2025, i.e. it is in real clinical use rather than a laboratory demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous phlebotomy); this item establishes maturity/deployment rather than a new capability.

sources.system: Semi-autonomous vital sign measurement sensing robot (PPG robotic arm)
sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot - TechRxiv
sources.claim: A research robotic arm carrying PPG sensors autonomously finds measurement sites on a human arm and acquires photoplethysmography signals to derive heart rate, SpO2 and respiratory rate, validated on 25 adults with varied skin tones.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous acquisition of pulse-oximetry-type signals by bringing a PPG sensor to a human limb. It substantiates autonomous sensor-to-skin placement and signal verification, but the robot holds the sensor rather than attaching a probe that stays on, and it is a laboratory study.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot (588 g cable-driven, Tsinghua University)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous 6-DoF ultrasound robot with an AI agent was run in the ultrasound department of a hospital, autonomously contacting patients' abdomens with a probe to locate liver structures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous probe placement on a patient's body in an imaging suite (an E2 facility). It shows force-controlled contact with patients in the actual kind of setting, but the robot only presses a held probe against skin; it never grasps, adheres or connects a monitoring lead, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: A new standard for Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation - Axilum Robotics
sources.claim: A CE-marked and FDA-cleared clinical robot automatically positions and maintains contact of a TMS coil against a patient's head, with head-motion compensation, in ordinary clinic rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic placement of an instrument at a specified anatomical location on a seated patient in a clinic. It supports precise, safe robot-to-patient contact in an E2 setting, but the coil is held by the robot and nothing is adhered, snapped on or left attached to the patient.

tasks.label: Conduct inventories to maintain stock of clinical supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start/end-of-shift consumable check in the MRI suite itself: the tech eyeballs quantities in control-room and scan-room cabinets and drawers (syringes, needles, IV catheters and tubing, saline flushes, alcohol wipes, gauze, tape, gloves, earplugs), compares to par, then walks to the department supply closet, carries back cartons, opens them and refills drawers and bins between patients while the suite is in use.

Contrast media stock check: count gadolinium vials/prefilled syringes in the locked cabinet or refrigerator in the MRI area, verify lot numbers and expiration dates, reconcile against the usage log, pull replacement stock from pharmacy or place a request, and document the count.

Periodic (weekly/monthly) par-level count of the imaging department's supply storeroom: walk the aisles of shelving/bins, count boxed supplies per location, flag expired or near-expiry stock, and enter counts or generate the reorder list in the materials-management system.

Receiving and putting away a delivery from central supply or a vendor: unpack cartons, verify contents against the packing slip/order, rotate stock so earliest-expiring is in front, shelve items in the storeroom bins and update counts; break down and dispose of packaging.

Ancillary and emergency stock: count and replenish linens, gowns, sheets, positioning sponges/pads, MR-safe accessories and coil covers, and check the MR-conditional code cart / emergency supplies for missing, opened or expired items and reseal/restock them.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Ballad Health unveils three new Omnicell XR2 Central Pharmacy Dispensing Robots at Bristol Regional Medical Center
sources.claim: Omnicell XR2 central pharmacy dispensing ... are installed and running in US hospitals, autonomously storing and dispensing medication stock while maintaining perpetual, barcode-verified inventory with visibility of every dose and its expiration ... and earliest-to-expire dispensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage/dispensing of clinical stock with perpetual inventory. It carries over because the accepted output of the MRI tech's inventory task is an accurate on-hand count with expiry status driving replenishment, which this robot produces continuously for the stock presented to it.

sources.title: BoxPicker - Swisslog Healthcare - PDF Catalogs | Technical Documentation
sources.claim: Swisslog BoxPicker is a robotic automated storage and retrieval system ... hospital pharmacies that stores clinical stock and monitors and optimizes the hospital's medication inventory, requiring barcode scanning with any movement of stock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pharmacy storage with perpetual inventory. Comparable objects (boxed and vialed clinical supplies), comparable precision (unit-level counts, lot and expiry traceability), inside a purpose-built machine enclosure within a hospital.

sources.title: Simbe Tally shelf-scanning robot achieves UL 3300 certification - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robot autonomously drives store aisles several times a day and audits shelves, reporting out-of-stocks, misplaced items and pricing errors that drive replenishment work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf inventory audit in an institution-controlled facility. Transfers to counting boxed clinical supplies on aisled storeroom shelving: same object class (labelled packaged goods on standard shelving), same output (on-hand/par status feeding a reorder list), same class of environment with people present.

sources.title: How Simbe Robotics' retail robots help stores and brands - Fast Company
sources.claim: Tally is deployed at commercial scale across many retail chains and countries, i.e. routine operational inventory auditing rather than a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the item above (autonomous shelf inventory audit); cited for the maturity and scale of the deployment.

sources.system: Dane AiR DC autonomous inventory robot (BrainOS)
sources.title: Brain Corp., Dane Technologies Debut Inventory-Scanning Robot - San Diego Business Journal
sources.claim: The Dane AiR DC autonomously navigates warehouse and distribution-center aisles to perform cycle counts, reading barcodes and RFID at high accuracy and feeding inventory systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cycle counting of stock on shelving in a facility kept to a working standard; the deliverable (accurate on-hand counts driving replenishment) is the same as the department storeroom par count.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously picks and stows individual items into inventory pods in operating fulfillment centers, handling about 75% of stored item types at speeds comparable to employees, with inventory tracked per storage location.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic put-away of mixed individual items into tracked storage locations. Comparable objects (small packaged goods) and comparable precision; supports the receive-and-shelve instance when stock is presented to the machine as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi performs commercial mobile manipulation in working hospitals, autonomously picking supplies out of supply ..., but its workflows are fetch-and-deliver rather than counting stock or replenishing cabinets to par.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level supply handling inside hospital supply rooms. Cited to establish what deployed hospital (E2) mobile manipulation actually covers today - retrieval and transport - and hence the limit of E2 support for counting and restocking.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence TX SCARA robots autonomously restock refrigerated beverage shelves in hundreds of convenience stores, with remote operators intervening only when the AI errs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous shelf replenishment. Transfer is limited: the robot is a rail-mounted arm serving one purpose-built cooler fixture with a single product class, so it supports restocking only where the work is presented to the machine, not open clinical cabinets in a suite.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: A 2025 research prototype (ORB) performed autonomous mobile-manipulation retrieval and restocking of operating-room supplies, but at 80% retrieval success - below employer-acceptable reliability - and only as a lab-validated demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level clinical supply retrieval and restocking in a hospital room. Cited as the state of the art for E2 clinical restocking, showing it remains a below-worker-quality demonstration.

tasks.label: Place and secure small, portable magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scanners on body part to be imaged, such as arm, leg, or head.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital or outpatient MRI suite: tech fetches a rigid two-piece extremity/joint coil (knee, wrist, elbow, ankle), seats the limb in the lower half on the scanner table, closes and latches the upper half, wedges foam pads and applies straps so the joint is centered and immobilized for a 20-40 minute scan.

Hospital or outpatient MRI suite: tech drapes a flexible/blanket surface coil array (shoulder, wrist, hip, torso) over the anatomy of a supine or oblique patient, conforms it to body contour, and secures it with velcro straps, sandbags and pads over gowns and blankets; body habitus and patient positioning vary widely.

Neuro exam in an MRI suite: tech settles the supine patient's head into the fixed head coil base, attaches the coil top, inserts cushions and a chin/forehead strap for immobilization and comfort, and checks that ears and nose clear the coil.

Orthopedic clinic with a dedicated small/extremity MRI unit (e.g., open extremity scanner): seated or reclining patient's arm or leg is guided into the compact magnet's bore/local coil, aligned to the anatomy of interest, and secured with cradles, pads and straps.

Point-of-care portable low-field MRI (e.g., bedside head scanner) brought to an ICU or ED bay: tech maneuvers the scanner to the bed among lines, monitors and ventilator tubing, slides the critically ill patient's head into the scanner's head coil, and secures it with pads.

sources.title: Axilum Robotics TMS-Robot | Neurolite Advanced Medical Solutions
sources.claim: Commercial robot autonomously positions a stimulation coil on a patient's head, establishes and maintains contact, and compensates for head motion throughout a clinical session in a treatment room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic TMS coil placement. It is the same physical act as this task's head/limb coil step - bringing a ~1-2 kg coil to a defined anatomical target on a live patient, making controlled contact, and holding that pose stably for the duration of the procedure.

sources.title: Axilum Robotics wins FDA 510(k) clearance for TMS-Cobot
sources.claim: The robotic TMS coil positioner is a cleared medical device sold in the US and Europe for spatial positioning and orientation of a coil on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes regulatory clearance and commercial maturity of autonomous coil-on-head positioning, the related task cited above.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic device into which a patient places an arm performs venipuncture and applies an adhesive bandage to the limb in routine clinical use, with one professional supervising up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous phlebotomy in a purpose-built limb fixture. It substantiates the E1 counterfactual - a limb presented in a machine-built cradle, a device handled from a known presentation and applied to the skin, and an adhesive dressing secured to the limb - at clinical error rates with only supervisory intervention.

sources.title: Vitestro introduces autonomous robotic device for blood collection
sources.claim: The autonomous blood-draw device is CE marked, commercially launched in Europe, validated in more than 4,000 individuals, and fits lab and hospital workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; establishes deployment scale and patient-contact safety record for a purpose-built machine that engages a fixtured human limb.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital team
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department and performed force-controlled probe placement and scanning on human subjects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of an imaging transducer against patient anatomy with force control. It shows the contact-placement element of this task is achievable autonomously on real patients, but the system neither manipulates bulky coils nor secures anything to the body.

sources.title: MR Safe Robot, FDA Clearance, Safety and Feasibility Prostate Biopsy Clinical Trial
sources.claim: MR Safe robots built from nonmagnetic, non-conducting materials have received FDA clearance and been used in patient trials inside the MRI environment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: MRI-guided robotic intervention. It removes the objection that no robot can act at all near/inside an MRI scanner, showing MR-safe actuation is a solved engineering problem for purpose-built devices.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robot-assisted dressing - the closest demonstrated analogue to wrapping and fastening a flexible coil on a person - remains a laboratory human study with partial success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating a deformable item onto a human limb. Success is partial (85% of arm length) in a lab with healthy volunteers, well below the reliability needed for conforming and strapping a flexible MRI coil array.

sources.title: MR Smart Workflow - Philips
sources.claim: MRI vendors automate coil and accessory placement only as on-screen coaching for the human technologist; the physical placement remains manual.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task: shows the current state of automation in MRI suites is guidance to human technologists, supporting the negative judgment at E2.

instances.label: Custom electron cutout/insert for an electron applicator: aperture shape comes from the TPS or a digitized field outline; the dosimetrist cuts a Styrofoam mold on the block cutter, pours molten Cerrobend, cools, trims, labels the insert and checks aperture size and fit in the cone. Hospital/clinic mold room with fume hood and melting pot.

Patient-specific bolus / tissue-equivalent build-up conforming to a CT- or scan-derived skin surface (nose, ear, scalp, post-mastectomy chest wall): cut and layer sheet bolus, build wax, or fabricate a conformal printed bolus to a specified thickness; verify thickness and conformity before treatment. Mold room / department fabrication lab.

Missing-tissue or intensity-modulating compensator built from a computed thickness matrix or fluence map (brass/aluminum compensator for compensator-based IMRT, custom compensating filter for a sloping surface, TBI compensator from patient thickness measurements); the finished modulator must match the planned thickness map within tolerance. Mold room / machine shop of the department or an outsourced vendor.

Custom photon shielding: divergent Cerrobend blocks for non-MLC or superficial/orthovoltage units, TBI lung blocks, and lead/high-density skin-collimation shields cut to an outlined field. Fabricated in the mold room from a beam's-eye-view outline or scan, then checked against the field outline.

Small custom shields fabricated to a specified geometry off the patient: eye shields for total-skin electron or superficial fields, tungsten/lead inserts, shields for lip/nose fields; made from a design or scan and then dosimetrically QA'd (transmission, thickness) before clinical release. Mold room / fabrication lab.

Devices shaped or trial-fitted against the patient or the machine: lead skin collimation cut and bent to a lesion at simulation with the patient present, wax build-up applied over an internal shield to the patient's anatomy, and custom filters/tray inserts trial-mounted in the linac accessory holder and checked against the light field in the treatment room.

sources.title: Shaping success: clinical implementation of a 3D-printed electron cutout program in external beam radiation therapy
sources.claim: Stanford ran a one-year clinical program in which patient-specific electron cutouts were generated automatically from the TPS aperture by script and fabricated on UltiMaker 3D printers (PLA shell filled with tungsten BBs), replacing Cerrobend pouring for 6x6, 10x10 and 15x15 cm cones; 40 cutouts passed QA and in-vivo OSLD checks.

sources.title: Commissioning compensator-based IMRT on the Pinnacle treatment planning system (JACMP)
sources.claim: Commercially manufactured brass compensators from .decimal are designed from the exported fluence map by the vendor's p.d software, machined to the required thickness matrix, and commissioned for clinical compensator-based IMRT delivery in a TPS.

instances.label: Brain/whole-brain patient at CT simulation: heat a 3-point thermoplastic head sheet in a water bath, drape it over the supine patient on the sim couch, mold it to forehead, nose bridge and chin, index it to the headrest/baseplate, let it cool, trim and label it.

Head-and-neck IMRT or SRS patient at CT simulation: form a 5-point (head-shoulder) or SRS-grade thermoplastic mask on the patient with tight setup tolerance, accommodating trach/PEG, shoulder pull, anxiety or claustrophobia, then index, trim mouth/eye openings and mark.

Thorax/abdomen/pelvis/extremity patient at CT simulation: position the patient on a vacuum-lok bag, alpha cradle or foam cushion, shape the bag around torso, arms or legs, evacuate air / pour and set the foam, verify reproducibility, label and index the cradle for SBRT or pelvic treatment.

Mold-room fabrication of a custom positioning accessory with the patient absent, designed from the simulation images or a prior impression: custom headrest, oral/tongue stent, extremity support, prone-board insert, or shaped foam wedge.

Mold-room fabrication of custom patient-specific beam-modifying devices that accompany the immobilization setup: conformal bolus (wax, sheet or printed), custom electron cutout/shielding, eye shield, cast from a surface contour.

Mid-course repair, refit or remake of an existing immobilization device: mask loose after weight loss, lost headrest cushion, deflated vacuum bag, cutting a relief opening, adding padding — turned around fast enough not to interrupt the treatment schedule.

instances.label: Post-HDR-fraction survey in the brachytherapy suite: immediately after each Ir-192 HDR fraction, enter the shielded vault, sweep a calibrated survey meter over the patient, the applicator/transfer tubes and the afterloader safe to confirm the source is fully retracted, read the dose rate and record it in the treatment record before the applicator is disconnected.

Routine area/equipment radiation surveys in the radiation oncology department: walk fixed survey points with a calibrated ion chamber or GM meter around the HDR afterloader, source safe, brachytherapy vault, storage/decay room, linac vault doors and adjacent occupied areas; record dose rates at each point and compare to limits for the monthly/quarterly radiation-safety record.

Permanent LDR seed implant (I-125/Pd-103 prostate) accounting survey in the OR: after implant, survey the patient, OR table, drapes, linens, sponges, instruments, waste and the shipping/transport container with a low-energy probe to confirm no loose seed remains, then document the seed count and readings.

Radionuclide therapy patient exposure-rate measurement in an inpatient therapy/isolation room (I-131, Lu-177, Y-90): measure exposure rate at the bedside and at 1 m from the patient with a survey meter at set intervals, record readings against release criteria, and repeat until the patient can be discharged.

Sealed-source receipt, inventory and leak-test measurements in the hot lab/source storage area: survey incoming packages of sources or radiopharmaceuticals for surface and 1 m dose rate, take wipe samples of source capsules/containers, count the wipes, compare to the 185 Bq leakage limit and log the inventory.

Incident/contamination survey: after a spill of unsealed radioactive material, a suspected stuck source, or a decontamination event, survey floors, benches, sinks, equipment surfaces and personnel with contamination probes, map the contaminated area and re-survey after cleanup until readings fall below limits.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) with radiation detection payload (Gamma Reality)
sources.title: Dominion Energy | Boston Dynamics case study
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped, carrying radiation-detection payloads, performed the plant's radiation surveys at Dominion Energy's Surry Nuclear Power Station, first supervised and then fully autonomously, taking readings at the same set points as human health-physics technicians and producing more consistent data.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as the dosimetrist's area/equipment survey: carrying a radiation monitoring device to defined survey points in an institution-controlled facility, taking dose-rate readings and logging them; the human workflow replaced is explicitly 'walk through a space holding a radiation detector, take readings at set intervals'.

sources.title: Making Radiation Mapping Safer & More Reliable | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot is marketed and used for autonomous radiation mapping missions with a range of radiation detection payloads in nuclear plant settings.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the detector-carrying survey capability is a productized payload/mission type, not a one-off demonstration.

sources.system: CERN mobile manipulators with Autopilot (CERNbot family; MIRA test campaign)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Execution of Safe and Precise Robotic Radiation Surveys in the Super Proton Synchrotron
sources.claim: Two mobile manipulators operating underground at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron perform radiation surveys fully autonomously in 'Autopilot' mode, including precise radiation monitoring along beam components with a manipulator-mounted radiation sensor, gate crossing, and docking at charging stations, with human supervision and occasional manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous to surveying equipment with a monitoring device: an arm-mounted radiation probe is positioned at defined points next to accelerator hardware inside an institution-controlled facility, exactly the geometry-controlled probe placement a dosimetrist uses on an afterloader, source safe or vault wall.

sources.claim: A nuclear-medicine ward mobile robot (TMI-MD-NM-P, Shanghai Qinmi/TMiRob) measured patients' radiation dose rate and vital signs at the bedside in I-131 isolation wards at three hospitals in a 72-patient randomized paired trial; radiation-residue measurement succeeded on the first attempt in 100% of cases, deviation from the conventional survey meter was within 10%, and no adverse events occurred. Safety criteria assessed whether the robot arrived at the task site by itself, collided, or failed to auto-charge, indicating self-navigation.

roles.title: Emergency Medical Technicians
roles.description: Assess injuries and illnesses and administer basic emergency medical care. May transport injured or sick persons to medical facilities.

tasks.label: Administer first aid treatment or life support care to sick or injured persons in prehospital settings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: 911 medical call in a private residence: EMT enters a cluttered home (stairs, narrow halls, pets, anxious family), finds an elderly patient with chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, hypoglycemia or a ground-level fall; obtains vitals and history, positions the patient, applies oxygen/NRB or nasal cannula, applies a blood-glucose check, dresses skin tears, assists the patient's prescribed nitroglycerin or inhaler, monitors and reassesses until transport.

Trauma on a roadway or other outdoor public scene: motor-vehicle collision, fall, or assault, with traffic, weather, glass and debris; EMT controls external bleeding with direct pressure/hemostatic dressing or tourniquet, maintains manual c-spine stabilization, applies splints, occlusive dressings and oxygen, and keeps the patient warm and monitored during extrication and packaging.

Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest / respiratory arrest resuscitation on scene (bedroom floor, bathroom, or public space): open airway, suction, bag-valve-mask ventilation, high-quality chest compressions, place AED pads and deliver shocks, apply a mechanical CPR device, coordinate with partner and first responders through multiple rhythm-check cycles.

Call inside an institutional or commercial facility with staff present and a known layout — nursing home, school, factory, office, stadium, airport concourse: patient found in bed, on a floor or in a chair; EMT performs assessment and basic interventions (oxygen, bleeding control, splinting, wound care, positioning, spinal precautions, medication assist) with facility staff handing over information.

Continuing care in the patient compartment of a moving ambulance en route to hospital: standardized layout and mounted equipment; EMT maintains oxygen therapy and airway/suction, re-checks and documents serial vitals, adjusts dressings and splints, manages nausea/positioning, keeps spinal precautions, and reassures the patient while the vehicle moves.

sources.date: 2026 (product in EMS use since 2016; page current)
sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: The most advanced fielded 'robotic' EMS treatment device is a mechanical chest-compression machine that delivers compressions only after a human rescuer stops CPR, positions the back plate under the patient, attaches the piston arm and sets the pad on the sternum; it performs no assessment, airway, defibrillation or wound care.
sources.transferJustification: Directly part of the task (life support care), but only the compression sub-step: it is carried, applied and removed by the EMT and cannot assess a patient, choose a treatment, ventilate, defibrillate or handle any non-arrest instance, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion at any tier.

sources.developer: University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine and Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute
sources.title: Pitt and CMU To Create Autonomous Robotic Trauma Care System - Robotics Institute Carnegie Mellon University
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic prehospital trauma treatment remains an R&D goal: a DoD-funded program to build a robotic suit that an injured person is placed into, which would assess injuries and robotically apply IV fluids and medications, was announced as a four-year development contract, not a fielded or demonstrated end-to-end system.
sources.transferJustification: This is the task itself (prehospital stabilizing care) in the most machine-favorable form — the casualty is placed into the machine, i.e. an E1 presentation — yet the source describes an intent to create the system, with no demonstrated autonomous treatment of patients, so it cannot support a positive judgment even at E1.

sources.system: MASH / Medical Swarm Robotics for Extraction and Life-Saving Interventions (STTR solicitation)
sources.title: Medical Swarm Robotics for Extraction and Life-Saving Interventions: STTR | DARPA
sources.claim: As of 2025-2026 the U.S. government was still soliciting proposals to develop and demonstrate robots capable of autonomous field medical interventions such as hemorrhage control and fracture stabilization, indicating no such fielded capability exists.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content (field hemorrhage control, splinting, medication) but this is a program solicitation — an announcement of intent — so under the evidence rules it cannot substantiate capability; it is recorded to document the state of the art.

sources.system: DARPA Triage Challenge systems competition (DART, RoboScout, Coordinated Robotics, PRONTO)
sources.developer: DARPA with university and industry teams
sources.title: DART and MSAI triumph at DARPA Triage Challenge | DARPA
sources.claim: In the DARPA Triage Challenge field events, the best robotic systems performed only non-contact casualty search and injury/vital-sign assessment in staged scenarios; no competing robot administered physical treatment to a casualty.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic activity to prehospital emergency response at real outdoor scenes; it covers only the assessment portion (sensing vitals and injuries) and stops short of first aid or life support, so it cannot substantiate completion of the treatment task.

sources.system: Robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Int. J. Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery)
sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator | International Journal of Computer Assisted Radiology and Surgery
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic airway management, a core life-support intervention, has only been shown on training manikins in the laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Airway management is a life-support sub-step of this task; performance is established only on a fixed manikin in a lab bench setup, with no patients, no scene assessment and no other interventions, so it does not transfer to whole-instance prehospital care.

sources.system: Autonomous medical tape handling system for robotic wound redressing
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic wound dressing is at the stage of first-of-kind manipulation research on individual sub-steps such as removing and re-applying medical tape, not clinical wound care on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Bandaging/dressing is a first-aid sub-step of this task; the work is a laboratory manipulation study on a single sub-step, explicitly framed as progress 'towards' end-to-end autonomy, so it cannot support completion of a first-aid instance.

tasks.label: Assess nature and extent of illness or injury to establish and prioritize medical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: 911 response to a private residence: EMT enters a cluttered home (stairs, pets, family present, poor lighting), performs primary survey (airway/breathing/circulation), takes history from a confused or distressed elderly patient with chest pain, dyspnea, or after a fall, does hands-on exam (radial pulse, skin, lung sounds, palpation for deformity/tenderness, pupils), obtains BP/SpO2/glucose, forms a field impression and prioritizes interventions and transport urgency.

Scene response in a public or outdoor setting taken as found (motor-vehicle collision on a roadway, construction/workplace injury, street or restaurant collapse): rapid trauma assessment of a patient in an awkward position, in traffic, weather, and noise, identifying life threats (hemorrhage, airway, chest injury), deciding load-and-go versus on-scene treatment and spinal motion restriction.

Pickup at a nursing home, assisted-living facility, or hospital unit for a transfer or an acute complaint: bedside assessment of a mostly cooperative patient in a standard bed, with staff handoff and paperwork available; vitals, focused exam, review of baseline versus current status, prioritizing en-route monitoring and interventions.

Ongoing assessment and reassessment inside the ambulance patient compartment during transport: repeat vitals and focused re-exam every 5-15 minutes on a secured patient in a standardized compartment, detecting deterioration, re-prioritizing procedures (oxygen, positioning, airway) and updating the receiving facility.

Event standby or multi-patient incident at a controlled venue (stadium, arena, school, industrial site): rapid triage of one or several patients in a first-aid station or venue area, sorting by acuity, tagging, and prioritizing which patients get procedures and transport first.

sources.system: DARPA Triage Challenge systems (DART, RoboScout, Coordinated Robotics, PRONTO, UAS-DTU)
sources.title: DART and MSAI triumph at DARPA Triage Challenge | DARPA
sources.claim: DARPA Triage Challenge Event 2 (Sept-Oct 2025) fielded autonomous air and ground robots that identified casualties and assessed injuries on staged mass-casualty courses at Guardian Centers, Georgia; the output is real-time decision support to human medics, with the final competition still ahead.
sources.transferJustification: Remote primary triage is the closest robotic analogue to an EMT's assessment and prioritization: it estimates vital signs and injury patterns to rank casualties. Transfer is only partial - the robots sense at a distance, perform no hands-on examination or history taking, and DARPA frames the output as decision support for medics rather than an accepted assessment.

sources.developer: University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University
sources.title: Researchers built an autonomous system to help detect the most urgent victims in mass casualty events | University of Pittsburgh
sources.claim: Pitt/CMU Team Chiron's autonomous triage robots detect and classify human injuries from ... in a simulated soccer-field-sized scenario with 10-15 victims, to help human medical personnel prioritize; researchers state real-world scenarios remain harder.
sources.transferJustification: Mass-casualty triage overlaps the EMT task of assessing injury and prioritizing care, but the demonstrated system is non-contact, research-stage, and tested in a controlled simulated field, so it does not establish completion of a full patient assessment.

sources.system: PRONTO (Penn Robotics Non-contact Triage and Observation)
sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania GRASP Lab and Penn Medicine
sources.title: Autonomous Search-and-Triage Robots for the DARPA Triage Challenge | Eric Eaton
sources.claim: Penn's PRONTO team uses autonomous aerial and ground robots with vision foundation models for victim perception, vital-sign monitoring and injury assessment in the DARPA Triage Challenge; the team advanced to finals scheduled for November 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Non-contact triage assessment is the related task; it shares the goal of judging severity and prioritizing casualties, but it remains a competition prototype whose finals fall after the rating date, and it performs no hands-on exam or procedure prioritization at EMT standard.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensors)
sources.developer: MIT, Brigham and Women's Hospital, Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Robot takes contact-free measurements of patients' vital signs | MIT News
sources.claim: The 'Dr. Spot' quadruped carrying contactless sensors measured skin temperature, respiratory rate, pulse and oxygen saturation on healthy volunteers in a hospital triage context, but the robot was driven by a human with a handheld controller and used for telepresence interviewing by clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Vital-sign acquisition is one component of EMT assessment; this system shows the component achieved only under human teleoperation with a clinician interpreting, so it cannot support autonomous completion of the assessment task.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation
sources.developer: INESC TEC / Polytechnic of Porto (Lopes, Coelho, Silva)
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation
sources.claim: A collaborative robot arm autonomously located auscultation points with 3D vision and placed a stethoscope on the skin of six seated volunteers for a simulated pulmonary auscultation; a laboratory feasibility study covering one exam sub-step.
sources.transferJustification: Auscultation is one hands-on element of the EMT physical exam. The demonstration covers only probe placement on cooperative, prepared subjects in a lab, with no interpretation, history taking, or prioritization, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole assessment even in a purpose-built cell.
