tasks.label: Decontaminate ambulance interior following treatment of patient with infectious disease, and report case to proper authorities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine post-transport decontamination after a patient with a common communicable illness (influenza-like illness, COVID, suspected respiratory infection) with no visible soiling. In the hospital EMS bay or station apparatus floor, the EMT doffs and bags PPE, removes used disposables (electrodes, oxygen tubing, mask, packaging), strips and replaces stretcher linen, wipes all high-touch surfaces (rails, bench, grab handles, cabinet latches, monitor and cables, radio, door handles) with an EPA-registered disinfectant for the labeled contact time, bags waste, restocks, and documents the exposure/notification in the ePCR.

Terminal deep decontamination after a confirmed or strongly suspected high-consequence pathogen (active TB, meningococcal disease, measles, C. difficile, MDRO). Rig is taken out of service at the station; full-compartment cleaning and disinfection of every surface plus reusable equipment, floor mopping, longer contact times, sometimes a vapor or UV adjunct cycle, all disposables discarded as regulated medical waste, and formal notification to the agency's designated infection control officer, receiving facility, and state/local health department.

Decontamination of gross contamination: blood, vomit, diarrhea, or copious sputum on the floor, bench seat, cot mattress, walls, cabinet faces, and equipment cables. Absorbent applied and scooped, gross soil removed, surfaces scrubbed and then disinfected, contaminated cot mattress and straps cleaned or replaced, biohazard bags and sharps handled, then case reported.

Rapid field turnaround between calls: the crew decontaminates at a roadside, scene staging area, or hospital ramp in whatever weather, using only supplies carried on board, under pressure to return to service quickly. Abbreviated wipe-down of high-touch surfaces and cot, linen change, waste bagged and carried until it can be disposed, verbal notification to dispatch/supervisor and later written report.

sources.system: Portable ambulance decontamination systems (e.g., Bioquell BQ-EMS, Ambustat, Steriplex 360 ProMister, Fogmaster)
sources.developer: U.S. Department of Homeland Security System Assessment and Validation for Emergency Responders (market survey of vendors)
sources.title: Portable Ambulance Decontamination Systems Market Survey Report
sources.claim: DHS market survey of portable ambulance decontamination systems (vapor/fog/mist dispersal units used by EMS) states that the ambulance must be manually cleaned before any such automated system can be used, so these machines perform only the disinfectant-application step of the task.

sources.title: Ambulance Disinfection & Ambulance Decontamination: Your Step-by-Step Playbook for a Safer Rig
sources.claim: AeroClave, the leading vendor of automated ambulance decontamination systems, instructs that fogging cannot lift visible soil or dried blood and that manual cleaning must precede the automated cycle; its guidance describes manual wipe-down of high-touch surfaces as the essential first step.

sources.system: AeroClave RDS 3110 / ADS ambulance decontamination system
sources.title: Disinfecting with precision with AeroClave
sources.claim: An automated in-vehicle disinfectant dispersal unit is in routine EMS service: Winter Park (FL) Fire Department runs the AeroClave RDS 3110 daily in its ambulances, with a machine-controlled cycle that disperses EPA-registered disinfectant into the sealed patient compartment while crew stand outside. It applies disinfectant only; it does not remove waste, linens, or soil.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated terminal disinfection of an ambulance patient compartment. It covers only the disinfectant-application sub-step of this task and presupposes manual cleaning, so it cannot substantiate whole-task completion.

sources.title: The use of a UV-C disinfection robot in the routine cleaning process: a field study in an Academic hospital
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed hospital field study of an autonomous UV-C disinfection robot shows it runs pre-programmed autonomous cycles in hospital rooms but is evaluated as an addition to (not a replacement for) routine manual cleaning and disinfection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminal disinfection of a patient care space. Transfer is limited: the robot only irradiates surfaces after humans have cleaned them, and its wheeled base cannot work inside an ambulance module.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.developer: POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology)
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: A research prototype mobile robot with a manipulator physically wipes surfaces and then applies UV-C, validated in tests at Pohang St. Mary's Hospital; it is a university prototype limited to wiping and irradiating room surfaces, not to linen changes, waste handling, or vehicle interiors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact wiping and disinfection of high-touch surfaces in a healthcare facility. Closest cited manipulation-based cleaning system, but it is a prototype sized for hospital rooms and does not handle soiled linen, biohazard waste, or the confined ambulance module.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: A commercially deployed autonomous cleaning robot works in human healthcare and transport facilities, cleaning fixtures and floors and picking up trash in restrooms during normal operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous spray-and-disinfect cleaning of a small enclosed room in an institutional facility. Transfer fails for this task: the robot is a large wheeled unit that cannot enter an ambulance patient compartment and does not handle linens, medical equipment, or regulated medical waste.

sources.system: Tesla robotaxi interior cleaning robot arm (Cybercab hub)
sources.date: 2026-07 (permit closed March 2026; robot first shown January 2025)
sources.title: Tesla readies its autonomous Cybercab and Robotaxi cleaning service
sources.claim: Tesla has shown and installed at its Austin robotaxi hub a fixed robotic arm that cleans vehicle interiors between rides — vacuuming seats and floors and grasping items left behind — a purpose-built vehicle-interior cleaning bay, but it performs tidying and vacuuming rather than disinfectant application, linen change, or biohazard cleanup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning a vehicle interior in a purpose-built bay (the E1 counterfactual). It removes loose debris and litter only; autonomy rests on a company video, and no disinfection to contact time, linen replacement, or infectious-waste handling is shown.

tasks.label: Drive mobile intensive care unit to specified location, following instructions from emergency medical dispatcher.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Code-3 emergency response to a 911 scene: after dispatch gives an address and call type, the EMT drives the ambulance through urban/suburban public streets with lights and siren, exceeding posted speed, proceeding through red lights and stop signs after clearing intersections, passing on the wrong side, and negotiating with drivers who yield unpredictably, while the partner works the radio/MDT.

Routine-speed (no lights/siren) transport of a stable patient from scene to a receiving hospital inside the metro service area: normal traffic-law-compliant driving on surface streets and freeways, smooth acceleration and braking for the crew working in back, ending with pulling into the ED ambulance bay.

Emergent (code-3) transport of an unstable patient from scene to trauma center or STEMI/stroke center: lights and siren en route, time-critical, hospital pre-notified, driving must be both fast and smooth enough for procedures in the patient compartment.

Non-emergency driving inside the metro: interfacility/discharge transfer, repositioning to a system-status posting location on dispatcher instruction, returning to station or restocking, driving in normal traffic with no time pressure.

Degraded conditions: night runs on unlit rural two-lane roads, rain, fog, ice or snow, unpaved shoulders, long private driveways, farm or ranch addresses, poor cell/GPS coverage, addresses given by cross-street or landmark rather than a mapped street address.

Scene access and positioning in congested or chaotic settings: staging and parking at a highway crash behind flares and cones, downtown double-parking or blocking a lane, apartment complexes and parking structures, event crowds, police-directed traffic and hand signals, backing into a tight ED bay with a spotter.

sources.title: Waymo launching driverless robotaxis in 5 more cities
sources.claim: Waymo operates a commercial driverless robotaxi service on public urban streets at large scale, with no human in the vehicle, picking up and dropping off at requested destinations in geofenced metro service areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-to-point passenger transport on public roads. It transfers to routine ambulance driving because the environment (metro public streets), the act (drive to a dispatched destination and stop at the curb), and the required traffic-law compliance are the same; it does not transfer to lights-and-siren driving.

sources.title: Waymo launching driverless robotaxis in 5 more cities
sources.claim: Waymo added driverless freeway operation for public riders in three metros, extending autonomous driving to high-speed highway segments of a trip.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: freeway passenger transport. Transfers to the highway legs of routine ambulance transports and interfacility transfers, which use the same roads at the same speeds.

sources.title: Waymo launching driverless robotaxis in 5 more cities
sources.claim: Waymo's driverless operating domains as of late 2025 exclude regions with regular heavy snowfall; winter-weather operation was still in testing rather than deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Negative-boundary evidence: shows the deployed public-road autonomy does not cover the snow/ice and rural conditions that a share of EMS response driving occurs in.

sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Aurora runs a commercial driverless Class 8 trucking service on public Texas highways with no human aboard, showing autonomous control of a large, heavy vehicle on public roads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless heavy-truck freight hauling. Transfers to ambulance driving on the vehicle-dynamics dimension — an ambulance is a heavy box vehicle — on mapped public highway routes; it does not cover emergency-priority driving.

sources.title: Kodiak achieves autonomous trucking milestone: Atlas Energy integrates driverless RoboTrucks in Permian Basin operations
sources.claim: Kodiak-equipped Class 8 trucks owned by Atlas Energy have been running driverless on the company's private desert road network in the Permian ..., hauling loads between dispatched pickup and delivery points on unpaved industrial roads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispatched heavy-vehicle driving on an operator-controlled private road network (dust, unpaved surfaces, day and night). Transfers to the E2 counterfactual of driving a mobile ICU to a dispatcher-assigned point inside institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: Cat MineStar Command for hauling manages the autonomous ecosystem
sources.claim: Caterpillar's autonomous haulage system runs hundreds of driverless haul trucks at dozens of mine sites, dispatched by a fleet system to loading and dumping points and spotting precisely there among people and light vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispatch-directed autonomous driving and precise spotting of very large vehicles inside an institution-controlled work site. Transfers to the E2 counterfactual for driving to and positioning at an assigned location on controlled premises, including at night and in dust.

sources.title: Waymo keeps blocking SF firefighters, and they're fed up
sources.claim: Deployed public-road robotaxis repeatedly fail around emergency operations: San Francisco fire crews documented dozens of incidents of Waymo and Zoox vehicles blocking firehouse exits, stalling in front of responding ambulances ... engines, and obstructing code-3 responses, sometimes requiring firefighters to drive the vehicle away.
sources.transferJustification: Negative-boundary evidence: the best deployed public-road autonomy cannot reliably even yield at emergency scenes, so it cannot be credited with driving code-3 or positioning at a chaotic scene on public roads.

tasks.label: Immobilize patient for placement on stretcher and ambulance transport, using backboard or other spinal immobilization device.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motor-vehicle collision on a roadway or shoulder: EMT applies a cervical collar to a seated, possibly entrapped patient, performs rapid extrication or KED application, slides the patient onto a long board/scoop, straps torso, pelvis and legs, secures head with blocks, then moves the packaged patient to the cot and loads it into the ambulance — done in live traffic, weather, glass and fuel hazards, with the patient often frightened or altered.

Fall in a private residence (frequently an elderly patient on a bathroom floor, stairs or between furniture): spinal motion restriction with collar and scoop stretcher or vacuum mattress, log-roll or scoop lift with a partner, strapping, then carrying the immobilized patient through cluttered rooms, narrow hallways or a stairwell to the cot outside.

Injury in a public or outdoor place — sidewalk, park, sports field, beach, school gym, retail store, construction or industrial site: ground-level patient with suspected spine injury; collar applied, patient log-rolled onto backboard or scoop, strapped and head-secured, moved across grass/gravel/steps to the cot, often with bystanders present.

Institutional setting under an operator's control — nursing home room, urgent-care clinic, school health room, or hospital ED for an interfacility transfer: patient already on spinal precautions or newly collared is transferred bed-to-cot with a slide board/scoop, straps and head immobilizer verified, and secured for ambulance transport along fixed corridors.

Difficult-access or high-difficulty packaging: patient down an embankment, in a confined space, in water, or a bariatric/combative/pediatric patient needing a vacuum mattress, pediatric board or improvised padding, often with fire/rescue assistance and prolonged carry to the ambulance.

sources.title: A High-Strength, Highly-Flexible Robotic Strap for Harnessing, Lifting, and Transferring Humans | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed robotics work states that safely harnessing and lifting a human body for transfer — the core physical act in packaging a patient onto a board and cot — remains an unsolved problem for robots; the paper presents a laboratory 'Robotic Strap' prototype, not a fielded system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: harnessing/strapping and lifting a human body for transfer. Immobilizing a trauma patient on a backboard and moving them to a stretcher requires exactly this — strap application and full-body-weight lifting with gentle, injury-safe handling — so the stated unsolved status carries over.

sources.system: Flexible robotic limb (patent background survey of RIBA, Toyota Patient Transfer Assist, big-hand gripper)
sources.title: Flexible robotic limbs including rolling contact joints (US Patent 12,384,057)
sources.claim: A 2025 granted US patent's background review of the field states that human attachment of straps is still required and is a bottleneck preventing fully autonomous human ..., and that only the RIBA robots and Toyota's Patient Transfer Assist have safely lifted a person's full body weight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: strapping and lifting a human for transfer. Spinal immobilization is strap-and-lift work on a delicate human body; the patent's survey establishes no system does this autonomously, including in controlled laboratory settings.

sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: The most advanced demonstrated patient-lifting robots remain experimental laboratory machines that lift a cooperative patient between bed and wheelchair under caregiver guidance; none apply collars, boards or straps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting/transferring a patient from a bed. Even in a controlled care setting this is caregiver-guided and covers only the lift, not collar application, log-rolling onto a board, strapping, or securing for ambulance transport.

sources.system: Quadrupedal emergency transport robot / wheeled emergency rescue robot
sources.developer: Chinese emergency-rescue robot program (unveiled Hangzhou/Beijing demonstration)
sources.title: Rescue robot with quadrupedal, wheeled, tracked modes debuts in China
sources.claim: Emergency-response robots shown carrying injured people are staged demonstrations of transport only; the casualty is placed on the machine and no device performs spinal packaging, and control mode is not established as autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving an injured person from scene to transport. It substantiates carriage only, not immobilization; the collar, board transfer and strapping steps that define this task are absent and autonomy is unverified.

sources.system: Autonomous Casualty Extraction (ACE) arms on FLIR Kobra UGV
sources.title: Autonomous Casualty Extraction program awarded to RE2 by U.S. Army
sources.claim: US Army casualty-extraction robotics remains an R&D effort framed around a medic remotely assessing and extracting a casualty, i.e., remote operation rather than autonomous patient packaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: extracting an injured person from a scene onto a litter. Even this narrower goal is a funded development program with remote medic control, so it cannot substantiate autonomous spinal immobilization at any tier.

tasks.label: Maintain vehicles and medical and communication equipment, and replenish first aid equipment and supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift vehicle readiness check in the station apparatus bay: walkaround of the ambulance, check engine fluids and dipstick, tire condition/pressure, all emergency lights and siren, brakes, fuel level, and note defects on the daily vehicle sheet.

Start-of-shift equipment and supply inventory check: open each cabinet, jump bag, airway kit and drug box, verify contents against the unit checklist, check expiration dates and tamper seals, and top up any missing consumables from station stock.

Post-call restock at the station supply room or hospital EMS restock room: pull the used items (gauze, IV/airway kits, saline, electrodes, splints, meds), refill the jump bags and wall cabinets to their standard configuration, reseal kits and log usage.

Post-call cleaning and decontamination of the patient compartment and reusable equipment: remove trash and biohazard/sharps waste, strip and remake the stretcher with fresh linen, wipe/disinfect bench, rails, grab handles, monitor, cables, BP cuffs and suction unit.
Mid-shift vehicle servicing errand: drive the ambulance to the municipal or retail fuel island and refuel it, and run it through the wash bay when soiled.

Equipment upkeep: exchange depleted portable and onboard oxygen cylinders and reattach/leak-check the regulator, rotate and charge monitor/radio/suction batteries, run function tests on the monitor-defibrillator, portable radio and MDT, and tag/report faulty gear for repair.

sources.system: Robotic kit assembly and vision inspection cell
sources.title: Precision in Motion: Robotic Kit Assembly and Vision Inspection - DSI Innovations
sources.claim: A deployed robotic kit-assembly cell uses a SCARA robot with camera-based vision inspection to assemble kits and verify that each component of the kit is correct, i.e. build a kit to a bill of materials inside a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial kitting. Refilling an EMS jump bag or cabinet to a standard checklist is the same operation — picking known small items from fixtured bins into designated pockets of a presented container, with vision verification of completeness — so performance transfers when the kit and bins are presented as a purpose-built cell would present them.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Pharmacy Robot Increases Safety, Efficiency | Owensboro Health
sources.claim: A hospital central-pharmacy robot autonomously picks, scans, sorts, bags, seals and labels medication units for dispensing, running inside its own enclosure in the pharmacy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: medication picking/replenishment. EMS restock of drug boxes and consumables is the same pick-verify-replenish operation on comparable small packaged items, with barcode verification giving the accuracy an EMS supply officer would accept; the robot works only inside its purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Pharmaceutical
sources.claim: A commercial piece-picking robot autonomously picks a wide range of discrete items, including pharmaceutical and healthcare products, into order containers at up to 1,200 items per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order fulfilment piece-picking of medical/pharma SKUs. Replenishing first-aid supplies is picking the same class of small packaged medical items to a list; the demonstrated environment is a fixtured pick cell, matching the E1 counterfactual where the kit and stock are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Autofuel at UNITI expo: Robotic refuelling and world launch of the future of EV charging
sources.claim: A robotic refueling system mounted on a fuel island autonomously opens the fuel flap, handles the nozzle and refuels vehicles; it was run continuously refuelling cars on both sides of a fueling island for three days.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the fueling portion of ambulance servicing: the vehicle is presented at the dispenser bay and the robot performs the whole refuel; the bay is built around the robot arm.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator autonomously retrieves and restocks item-level clinical supplies, achieving 80% success in supply retrieval and 96% in restocking, validated in a simulated operating-room setup rather than a working hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level clinical supply restocking. It shows structured-mock-facility restocking of comparable medical items, but the reported success rates and simulated-OR setting fall short of worker-quality reliability in a real facility, so it supports only the structured-cell (E1) judgment.

tasks.label: Observe, record, and report to physician the patient's condition or injury, the treatment provided, and reactions to drugs or treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform emergency diagnostic and treatment procedures, such as stomach suction, airway management, or heart monitoring, during ambulance ride.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Airway management en route: unresponsive or hypoxic patient on the stretcher in a moving ambulance; EMT positions the head, suctions vomit/secretions with a Yankauer, sizes and inserts an OPA/NPA, ventilates with a bag-valve-mask and oxygen, watches chest rise and SpO2, and re-suctions as needed while the vehicle brakes and turns.

Cardiac monitoring en route: EMT exposes the chest (cutting clothing, drying diaphoretic or shaving hairy skin), places 3-lead or 12-lead electrodes at correct anatomical landmarks on a variably sized body, attaches pulse oximeter and BP cuff, obtains an artifact-free tracing in a vibrating vehicle, repeats serial readings, and relays findings to the receiving hospital.

Serial reassessment of a stable or low-acuity patient (including interfacility transfers): repeat vital signs, blood glucose fingerstick, checking/adjusting nasal cannula or non-rebreather oxygen flow, checking IV site and splint/dressing status, positioning the patient for comfort, and documenting trends during a 10-40 minute ride.

Cardiac arrest or peri-arrest during transport: applying/monitoring chest compressions (manual or mechanical device), attaching defibrillator pads and performing rhythm analysis and shocks, ventilating through a supraglottic or endotracheal airway, suctioning during resuscitation, all inside a moving ambulance.

Trauma, pediatric, or agitated patient en route: reassessing and adjusting hemorrhage control (pressure dressing, tourniquet), chest seal, spinal motion restriction straps and splints, monitoring for deterioration, and managing a combative or vomiting patient while restrained in the moving compartment.

sources.developer: UC Santa Barbara (Elliot Hawkes group) and collaborators
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: A soft robotic intubation device (SRIS) self-guides an endotracheal tube into the trachea, but it is inserted and operated by a human user and has only been tested on mannequins and cadavers, not on live patients or in a moving ambulance.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the airway-management instance, but the device is a hand-held tool an EMT inserts rather than a robot that performs the procedure; testing is limited to mannequins and cadavers.

sources.developer: Hemmerling et al., McGill University / Montreal
sources.title: First robotic tracheal intubations in humans using the Kepler intubation system - British Journal of Anaesthesia
sources.claim: The Kepler Intubation System performed oral tracheal intubation in 12 anesthetized operating-room patients under joystick control by a clinician, succeeding in 11 of 12; it is a research pilot, not a deployed autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic analogue to prehospital airway management; it is joystick-teleoperated on a fixtured, anesthetized patient in an operating room, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.title: LUCAS-3 Device — Brewster Ambulance Service clinical policy
sources.claim: Mechanical chest-compression devices such as the LUCAS 3 are routinely carried on US ambulances and deliver machine-controlled compressions throughout transport, but a human must position the patient on the backplate, apply the device, and perform all other resuscitation steps (pads, airway, ventilation, suction).
sources.transferJustification: Covers only the compression sub-step of the cardiac-arrest instance; the device cannot apply itself, place defibrillation pads, ventilate, or suction, so it does not complete the whole instance.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs needle insertion and blood collection without an operator, CE-marked in 2024 and deployed in European hospitals and labs from March 2025 — the frontier of autonomous invasive patient-contact procedures, done on a stationary arm fixtured in the machine inside a clinical room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous venipuncture) shows the current ceiling: one narrow procedure on a cooperative, fixtured limb in a quiet clinic room; it does not perform airway, suction, or electrode-placement work, nor operate in a moving vehicle.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup - The Robot Report
sources.claim: An autonomous throat-swabbing robot inserted a swab into the oropharynx of cooperative seated humans and completed the sampling cycle without an operator, as a startup prototype during COVID-19 testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (instrument insertion into the human mouth) is the nearest analogue to oral suctioning, but it requires a cooperative, seated, head-fixtured subject in a testing booth and does not handle vomit, an unresponsive airway, or a moving ambulance.

sources.title: New AI-powered robotic system performs heart ultrasounds without guidance - Concordia University
sources.claim: An AI-driven robotic echocardiography system located standard cardiac views autonomously, but only on a cardiac ultrasound training phantom; ... researchers state further testing on real patients is still needed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous cardiac diagnostic probe placement on a torso) is the closest evidence for robotic heart assessment, but it is phantom-only, stationary, and does not involve applying ECG electrodes or working in a moving vehicle.

roles.title: Paramedics
roles.description: Administer basic or advanced emergency medical care and assess injuries and illnesses. May administer medication intravenously, use equipment such as EKGs, or administer advanced life support to sick or injured individuals.

tasks.label: Perform emergency cardiac care, such as cardioversion and manual defibrillation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in a private residence: patient found collapsed on a bedroom floor, in a bathroom, or wedged between furniture. Paramedic positions/drags the patient, bares and dries (sometimes shaves) the chest, applies adhesive defibrillation pads anterior-lateral, interprets the monitor rhythm during a compression pause, selects energy on a manual defibrillator, charges, clears crew and family, delivers the shock, and resumes CPR across a multi-cycle resuscitation with drugs and airway management.

Arrest in a public or workplace setting (street, gym, restaurant, shopping centre, worksite): patient on pavement or floor amid bystanders, variable weather and lighting, possibly wet or metal surface; crew moves the patient to a workable spot, applies pads, runs manual rhythm analysis and defibrillation cycles, sometimes switching a bystander AED over to the paramedic monitor-defibrillator.

Cardiac care continued in the ambulance patient compartment, often while moving: patient already on the monitor with pads attached, rhythm deteriorates to VF/pulseless VT; paramedic recognises it, charges the manual defibrillator, clears the compressor or mechanical CPR device, shocks, and resumes care in a cramped, standardized, agency-controlled vehicle interior.

Synchronized cardioversion of a conscious but unstable tachyarrhythmia (VT with a pulse, AF with RVR, SVT) at the scene or en route: paramedic confirms instability, gives IV sedation/analgesia, places pads, engages sync mode and verifies the R-wave marker, escalates energy across attempts, and monitors for post-shock rhythm and airway compromise.

Response to an arrest or peri-arrest in a nursing home, clinic, dialysis unit, or during interfacility transfer: patient in a bed or chair with staff present, existing lines and monitors, cluttered but institutionally maintained room; paramedic moves the patient to a firm surface, applies pads and performs manual defibrillation or synchronized cardioversion as part of ALS.

sources.title: LifeVest Medical Professional Frequently Asked Questions | ZOLL
sources.claim: The ZOLL LifeVest wearable cardioverter defibrillator autonomously detects VT/VF and delivers a defibrillating shock through electrodes held by a garment the patient already wears; it performs no manipulation - it cannot find a patient, bare a chest, or place electrodes, and it treats only its own wearer.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing machine-delivered defibrillation. It does not transfer to the paramedic task: electrodes are pre-positioned by a garment the patient dons, there is no perception or manipulation of an arbitrary collapsed patient, no manual rhythm/energy decision inside a resuscitation, and no sedated synchronized cardioversion of a third party.

sources.developer: Stryker (Jolife/Physio-Control), deployed by South Central Ambulance Service
sources.title: Robot paramedic delivers CPR to heart attack patients - BBC Science Focus Magazine
sources.claim: The LUCAS 3 mechanical CPR device, in ambulance service since 2021, delivers automated chest compressions, but the crew must position the patient and clamp the device; it does not attach defibrillation pads, interpret rhythms, or deliver shocks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (mechanical CPR in the same resuscitations). It marks the limit of fielded resuscitation automation: a human still sites and secures the device on the patient, and every defibrillation step - pad placement, rhythm interpretation, charging, clearing, shocking - remains manual.

sources.system: Autonomous cardiac ultrasound scanning robotic system (human posture recognition + image servo control)
sources.developer: Tang, Wang et al. (Hebei University of Technology / Yanshan University group)
sources.title: Autonomous ultrasound scanning robotic system based on human posture recognition and image servo control: an application for cardiac imaging
sources.claim: Research robots can autonomously plan a scan path and press an ultrasound probe onto a human chest with servo and admittance force control for cardiac imaging, validated on human subjects and phantoms in a laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous placement of a device against a patient's chest). It does not substantiate this task: the subject is a cooperative, still, supine volunteer in a lab; the robot holds a rigid probe rather than peeling and adhering electrode pads to a wet, hairy, compressing chest, and it delivers no therapy, makes no shock/no-shock decision, and does not clear rescuers before energy delivery.

sources.system: Drone-delivered AED (D-AED) service with winched Schiller FRED Easyport
sources.developer: Copenhagen Emergency Medical Services / Danish drone-AED study group (Jakobsen et al.)
sources.title: Semi-autonomous drone delivering automated external defibrillators for real out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: A Danish feasibility study - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: In the most automated real-world defibrillation service reported - semi-autonomous drones delivering AEDs to real out-of-hospital cardiac arrests in Denmark - the machine only transports the AED; human bystanders must attach the pads and operate it.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related service (defibrillation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest). It shows that the physical acts this task consists of - attaching electrodes to the patient and running the shock sequence in context - are still performed by humans even where robotics has been deployed in the response chain.

sources.title: Sensor-guided robots could boost lifesaving combat casualty care | DARPA
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic intervention on casualties in the field remains an unsolved research goal: DARPA's MASH program is soliciting development of robots that would locate casualties and stop hemorrhage with limited human assistance, indicating no such fielded system exists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous emergency intervention on a patient's torso). Cited only as a negative indicator: this capability is a multi-year research objective rather than a demonstrated system, so it cannot support completion of emergency cardiac care at any tier.

tasks.label: Perform emergency invasive intervention before delivering patient to an acute care facility.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: 911 scene in a private residence or public place: alert, cooperative, hemodynamically stable medical or minor-trauma patient (chest pain, abdominal pain, dehydration, nausea) with visible forearm/AC veins. Medic selects a site, places an over-the-needle peripheral IV catheter, flushes, secures with dressing, and connects fluids/saline lock before transport.

En route in a moving ambulance patient compartment: patient supine and belted on the stretcher, generally accessible veins; medic establishes (or replaces) a peripheral IV line and secures it against vehicle motion so drugs/fluids can run before hospital arrival.

Difficult or uncooperative vascular access at scene or en route: hypotensive/vasoconstricted shock or sepsis patient, opioid overdose, seizing or combative altered patient, obese patient, chronic IV drug user with scarred veins, elderly with fragile veins, or small child. Often requires multiple sites, external jugular, or ultrasound guidance, under time pressure.

Advanced airway management during cardiac arrest or respiratory failure: endotracheal intubation or supraglottic airway placement on a patient on a bedroom floor, in a bathroom, or in the ambulance, with secretions/vomit, ongoing CPR, cervical precautions, and confirmation by waveform capnography.

Intraosseous needle insertion (proximal tibia/humeral head) on an arrested, profoundly shocked, or pediatric patient after peripheral IV attempts fail; includes site identification, drill insertion, aspiration/flush confirmation, and securing the hub.

Trauma-scene invasive procedures at roadside, workplace, or public space: needle chest decompression for tension pneumothorax, finger thoracostomy, or surgical cricothyrotomy, with entrapment, blood, poor lighting/weather, bystanders, and non-standard patient positioning.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: The Vitestro Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed venipuncture autonomously in a multicenter clinical trial with a 94.5% first-stick success rate and low adverse-event rates, comparable to experienced human phlebotomists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture of a peripheral arm vein. It shares the object (a forearm/antecubital vein), the instrument (a needle entering a vein under image guidance), and the millimetre-scale precision required for prehospital peripheral IV cannulation on a cooperative patient with the arm fixtured.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: The trial was run in routine outpatient phlebotomy departments with 1,633 patients, i.e. cooperative seated patients in a clinical facility, not emergency patients.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (diagnostic venipuncture); this item establishes the population and setting in which the autonomous performance was obtained.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: The device is CE-marked and has been deployed in European healthcare settings since March 2025, establishing real deployment rather than a one-off demo.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture; deployment status supports that the autonomous needle-in-vein capability is production-grade, not a laboratory demonstration.

sources.title: The World's First Blood Collecting Robot Is Here, Meet Aletta | Nurse.org
sources.claim: Aletta executes the complete blood-draw workflow autonomously, from positioning the patient's arm in the device through vein location, needle insertion, sample collection and bandaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It shows the machine handles the whole procedure end-to-end with the limb fixtured in the machine's cradle — the E1 presentation of the work — which is the counterfactual condition being judged for prehospital IV cannulation.

sources.title: Hyperion Surgical Announces Completion of First-in-Human Study Using Its Ivy Robotic Vascular Access Platform
sources.claim: The only reported robotic peripheral IV catheterization in a human is Hyperion's Ivy platform, described by the company as semi-autonomous and used by a clinical operator in a first-in-human study; it is not an autonomous system operating without a user.

sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic tracheal intubation has been demonstrated only on a training manikin, taking about 46 seconds per attempt; no autonomous intubation of human patients is reported.

sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation - PubMed
sources.claim: The soft 'vine' robotic intubation device aimed at first responders is hand-guided by a trained user and has been tested in a mannequin and a ..., not operated autonomously on emergency patients.

sources.system: Robotic end effector for tension pneumothorax decompression
sources.title: Robotic end effector for decompression of tension pneumothorax
sources.claim: Robotic tension-pneumothorax decompression remains at the end-effector prototype stage, with teleoperated or semi-autonomous control explicitly identified as future work.

sources.title: Handheld Surgical Robot Can Help Stem Fatal Blood Loss
sources.claim: MIT Lincoln Laboratory's AI-GUIDE device for prehospital deep vascular access is a handheld tool that requires a human operator to hold it and to advance the guidewire and catheter.

tasks.label: Coordinate work with other emergency medical team members or police or fire department personnel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Assess nature and extent of illness or injury to establish and prioritize medical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Medical call at a private residence: elderly patient with chest pain, dyspnea, syncope or altered mental status. Paramedic obtains history from patient/family, performs multi-system physical exam (skin, lung sounds, abdomen, neuro/stroke exam), takes vitals, applies 12-lead ECG and SpO2/glucose, forms a working impression and prioritizes interventions and transport. Cluttered rooms, poor lighting, pets, family bystanders.

Call in a public or workplace setting (restaurant, office, gym, store, sidewalk): collapse, seizure, overdose, allergic reaction or minor trauma. Rapid primary survey (airway/breathing/circulation/mental status), focused exam and vitals amid bystanders, noise and limited access; determines acuity and priority of procedures.

Roadway motor-vehicle collision or outdoor traumatic injury (fall, industrial/farm injury): scene size-up and mechanism assessment, rapid trauma survey with patient partly entrapped or on the ground, spinal/extremity and hemorrhage assessment in weather, darkness, and traffic; prioritizes extrication and life-saving procedures.

Response to or interfacility transfer from a nursing home, assisted-living facility or clinic: patient in bed with staff report and chart/medication list available; paramedic reconciles history, examines the patient, obtains vitals and ECG, and establishes acuity and treatment priority in a standardized, institution-controlled facility.

Ongoing reassessment in the ambulance patient compartment en route: patient secured on the cot with monitor, IV and oxygen attached; paramedic repeats vitals, re-examines the patient, evaluates response to treatment, and re-prioritizes procedures during a moving transport.

Multi-patient scene or mass-casualty incident (multi-vehicle crash, bus rollover, active-shooter aftermath): rapid START-style triage of several patients in under a minute each — ambulation, respirations, perfusion, mental status — tagging and prioritizing who receives care and transport first.

sources.system: DARPA Triage Challenge systems (DART, RoboScout, Coordinated Robotics, PRONTO)
sources.developer: DARPA-funded and self-funded teams (Battelle, Coordinated Robotics, Univ. of Pennsylvania, CMU/Pitt)
sources.title: DART and MSAI triumph at DARPA Triage Challenge | DARPA
sources.claim: DARPA's Triage Challenge fielded autonomous ground and aerial robots that locate simulated casualties and estimate injury/vital-sign signatures in realistic disaster courses; the output is decision support to human medics, not a replacement for their assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Primary triage of casualties is the mass-casualty form of this task (assessing nature/extent of injury to prioritize care); the evidence shows the state of the art is casualty detection and decision support for responders rather than a completed paramedic assessment.

sources.system: Bayesian reasoning framework for autonomous casualty triage (Team Chiron / CMU-Pitt)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University and University of Pittsburgh
sources.title: A Bayesian Reasoning Framework for Robotic Systems in Autonomous Casualty Triage (arXiv)
sources.claim: The best-performing autonomous casualty-assessment pipeline evaluated at the DARPA Triage Challenge reached only ~53% overall triage accuracy in realistic MCI scenarios, far below a paramedic's reliability.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same assessment-and-prioritization task performed on simulated casualties; the reported accuracy shows autonomous systems cannot yet deliver worker-quality assessments even in a controlled competition course.

sources.developer: University hospital research consortium (ProteCT project, Germany)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients (PMC)
sources.claim: Robotic systems that perform the physical examination elements of assessment (vital signs, auscultation, palpation, percussion) on real emergency-department patients operate inside a purpose-built cabin and are driven remotely by a physician, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Emergency-patient physical examination is the core of this task; the system is the closest purpose-built (E1-style) implementation and it requires continuous remote human control, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: FARUS fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system
sources.developer: Chinese research group (published in Nature Communications)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: Fully autonomous contact-based patient examination by robots has been demonstrated only for narrow, single-organ imaging (thyroid scanning with nodule classification) on cooperative seated participants, not for multi-system emergency assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous physical examination of a human body is the transferable capability; its scope is one organ under ideal positioning, showing no autonomous system performs the multi-system history-plus-exam-plus-ECG assessment paramedics complete.

sources.system: Mobile robotic platform for contactless vital sign monitoring (Spot-based)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics collaboration
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring (PMC)
sources.claim: Mobile robotic platforms that measure patient vital signs autonomously are limited to contactless screening of temperature, heart rate and respiratory rate, without physical examination, history taking, ECG acquisition, or clinical prioritization.
sources.transferJustification: Vital-sign acquisition is one sub-step of paramedic assessment; even in a hospital triage setting the robot only screens vitals and the mobile platform's autonomy is not established, so it cannot complete the whole task.

sources.system: Collaborative robotic platform for autonomous auscultation
sources.developer: Academic research group (published in Applied Sciences)
sources.title: Development of a Collaborative Robotic Platform for Autonomous Auscultation (Applied Sciences)
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic auscultation exists only as a laboratory collaborative-robot prototype that positions a stethoscope on a prepared, stationary subject.
sources.transferJustification: Auscultation is a required element of the paramedic exam; the prototype demonstrates only probe placement on a prepared subject in a lab, not an integrated assessment yielding prioritized procedures.

tasks.label: Comfort and reassure patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Administer first aid treatment or life support care to sick or injured persons in prehospital settings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: 911 response inside a private residence: patient found on a bedroom floor, in a bathroom, or in a recliner (chest pain, difficulty breathing, diabetic emergency, overdose, fall). Paramedic assesses airway/breathing/circulation, applies oxygen or CPAP, attaches EKG/pulse-ox, establishes IV access, administers drugs (nitroglycerin, naloxone, albuterol, dextrose), dresses wounds or splints, and packages the patient — in a cluttered, unlit, variable home with family and pets present.

Care delivered in the moving ambulance patient compartment en route to hospital: continued monitoring, reassessment, titrating oxygen/ventilation with BVM, managing IV fluids and drug infusions, repeat 12-lead EKG, bleeding/pain management, and responding to deterioration while the vehicle moves. Fixed, standardized, service-controlled compartment layout.

Roadside or outdoor public scene: motor-vehicle collision, fall, assault, or industrial injury. Hemorrhage control with direct pressure and tourniquets, manual airway maneuvers, spinal motion restriction, splinting, assessment amid traffic, weather, debris, glass, and bystanders, often with the patient in an awkward position or inside a vehicle.

Response inside an institutional facility (nursing home, school, workplace, airport, arena, clinic): patient in a bed, wheelchair or on a corridor floor. Assessment, oxygen, IV/medication, wound care, and stabilization in a fixed-layout, staff-controlled facility with predictable access and lighting.

Cardiac arrest resuscitation (most often in a home, sometimes public): confirm pulselessness, start high-quality chest compressions, place defibrillator pads and defibrillate, manage the airway (supraglottic or intubation with BVM/ventilator), obtain IV/IO access and push epinephrine per ACLS, apply a mechanical CPR device, and reassess in cycles.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: The Aletta device autonomously performs venipuncture (needle insertion for blood collection) on seated, cooperative patients in blood-collection facilities, with an 88.5% overall collection success rate in a multicenter EU trial; a trained operator still prepares and supervises each draw. This is a single sub-step of prehospital care, in a controlled clinic, on a cooperative patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It is the closest robotic analogue to a paramedic's IV cannulation, but it requires a seated, still, cooperative patient with the arm fixtured in the device in a clinic, and covers none of the assessment, airway, drug-selection, hemorrhage-control or packaging steps that make up the paramedic instance.

sources.title: CPR robot that's saving lives is now standard EMS equipment in Honolulu
sources.claim: The LUCAS mechanical CPR device is standard EMS equipment on many ambulances and delivers sustained chest compressions, but it is carried, positioned and started by human responders and performs no assessment; the crew simultaneously performs the IV access, drug administration, airway and defibrillation steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical chest compression during cardiac arrest. It automates one motion of the resuscitation instance but is human-placed on the patient and has no perception, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of the whole instance.

sources.system: DARPA Triage Challenge teams (DART, MSAI, Chiron)
sources.title: DART and MSAI triumph at DARPA Triage Challenge
sources.claim: In DARPA's Triage Challenge systems competition (Sept-Oct 2025, Guardian Centers, Perry, GA), autonomous ground and aerial robots searched simulated mass-casualty courses and produced triage assessments of casualties; the robots assessed and reported, and did not administer treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field casualty triage in disaster settings. It is the most advanced field-deployed robotic casualty work, but it delivers assessment data to human responders rather than first aid or life support, so it cannot substantiate completion of this treatment task at any tier.

sources.developer: academic research group (Int. J. CARS publication)
sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator
sources.claim: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system achieved autonomous intubation only on a training manikin in the laboratory (10/10 trials); robotic airway management has not been shown autonomously on patients, let alone in prehospital conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency airway management, a core life-support intervention in this task. Results are manikin-only in a lab, so they show the airway sub-step is not yet robotically completed on real patients even in a purpose-built setting.

sources.title: Physical artificial intelligence in nursing: Robotics
sources.claim: A 2025 review of robotics in nursing concludes that bedside robotics remains largely human-operated or preprogrammed with limited autonomy and has not been transferred to direct patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hands-on bedside patient care in hospitals, a more structured and less time-critical version of prehospital care. If direct patient care is not yet robotic in hospitals, it is not achievable in the prehospital instances here.

tasks.label: Operate equipment, such as electrocardiograms (EKGs), external defibrillators, or bag valve mask resuscitators, in advanced life support environments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: 911 response in a private residence: paramedic acquires a 12-lead EKG on a conscious chest-pain patient — expose and prep the chest (dry/shave if needed), place 10 adhesive electrodes at anatomic landmarks (V1-V6 in intercostal spaces, limb leads), acquire a clean artifact-free tracing, interpret STEMI criteria and transmit to the receiving hospital, often on a couch, bed or floor in a cluttered room.

Care in the moving ambulance patient compartment during transport: apply 4-lead monitoring electrodes, SpO2/capnography, repeat 12-lead, and if the patient is apneic/hypoventilating, provide bag-valve-mask or in-line BVM ventilation through an airway adjunct, adjusting rate and mask seal while the vehicle moves.

Cardiac arrest resuscitation on scene (home floor, public place): place defibrillator pads on a bare chest, run rhythm analysis on the monitor/defibrillator, charge and deliver synchronized or unsynchronized shocks safely with the crew clear, and deliver bag-valve-mask ventilation with a two-hand seal or via supraglottic airway coordinated with ongoing chest compressions.

Institutional setting — nursing home, clinic, or interfacility/critical-care transport: apply monitor and 12-lead to a patient already in a bed, manage BVM or transport-ventilator ventilation on an intubated or obtunded patient, transfer monitoring leads and defibrillation pads between facility equipment and the EMS monitor.

Roadside, industrial or outdoor public scene under adverse conditions: apply monitor/defibrillator pads and provide BVM ventilation to a trauma or overdose patient in rain, cold, poor lighting, in an awkward position (vehicle entrapment, confined space), with bystanders and other responders present and the patient moving or combative.

sources.system: FARUS (fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning)
sources.developer: Chinese Academy of Sciences / Su et al. (Nature Communications)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: The closest autonomous robotic patient-contact system: a fully autonomous robotic ultrasound arm scanned the necks of 70 volunteers without human assistance, using skeleton-point recognition and force control. It performs one imaging contact task on a still, cooperative, seated subject — not electrode/pad application or ventilation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously positioning an instrument against a human body surface. It shows the state of the art in robot-to-patient contact, but the objects (probe vs. adhesive electrodes, defib pads, BVM mask), the patient state (cooperative and still vs. unresponsive/arresting), and the reliability demands of ALS equipment operation are not matched.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: An autonomous robot has performed an invasive contact procedure on human subjects (oropharyngeal swabbing) in a pilot/testing setting, again on a seated cooperative person with the head fixtured, and only for a single scripted contact motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic contact with a patient's airway anatomy. Even here the patient is seated, cooperative and head-fixtured; the system does not select, place or operate diagnostic/resuscitation equipment such as EKG electrodes, defibrillator pads or a bag-valve mask.

sources.title: Development of artificial intelligence-driven biosignal-sensitive cardiopulmonary resuscitation robot
sources.claim: Robotic resuscitation research remains at animal proof-of-concept: an AI-driven CPR robot was compared with a LUCAS 3 device in six pigs in a laboratory; a human still positions the device, and it performs compressions only, not EKG acquisition, defibrillation or ventilation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated mechanical resuscitation. It is the nearest robotic analogue to ALS equipment operation, but is a laboratory porcine study of chest compressions only, with a human placing the device on the subject.

sources.title: AMBUBOT: Ambulance robot Automated External Defibrillator robotic ambulance
sources.claim: Robotic AED delivery concepts explicitly rely on humans to prepare the chest and attach the defibrillation pads; the robot transports the AED and coaches bystanders, showing that pad application to a patient is not robot-performed.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (defibrillator deployment in the field): the published design keeps pad placement and chest preparation with human rescuers, evidencing that no robotic system completes the physical application of defibrillation equipment.

sources.developer: Haggerty et al., UC Santa Barbara (Science Translational Medicine)
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: Airway-management automation is limited to a self-guiding tube device inserted by a human clinician and tested in models and cadavers; there is no robotic system that establishes a mask seal and delivers bag-valve-mask ventilation to a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency airway management. The device steers itself once a human inserts it into the mouth and has been tested only on manikins and cadavers, so it does not substantiate robotic completion of BVM ventilation of a live patient.

tasks.label: Perform emergency pharmacological interventions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Critical resuscitation on scene (private residence floor, street, or moving ambulance): paramedic recognizes cardiac arrest/shock/status epilepticus, obtains IV or drills IO access on a pulseless or convulsing patient, draws up or spikes epinephrine, amiodarone, or a benzodiazepine, pushes it at the protocol dose and interval, and re-doses based on rhythm and vitals while CPR and airway work continue around them.

Analgesia/antiemetic for a stable but injured or ill patient (hip fracture in a home hallway, abdominal pain in the ambulance): assess pain and contraindications, calculate weight-based fentanyl/morphine or ondansetron dose, obtain peripheral IV in a moving or cramped setting, push slowly, reassess pain, sedation, respirations and BP, re-dose, and document the controlled substance.

IM / intranasal / subcutaneous drug per standing order at an unstructured scene: naloxone IN or IM for a suspected opioid overdose in a public restroom or car, IM epinephrine into the lateral thigh for anaphylaxis at a restaurant, IM midazolam for a seizing patient, glucagon for hypoglycemia — often requiring clothing to be moved, an uncooperative or combative patient to be controlled, and immediate reassessment and repeat dosing.

Non-injectable emergency medication: assemble and run nebulized albuterol/ipratropium by mask or in-line with CPAP for an asthma/COPD patient sitting on a couch, give chewable aspirin and sublingual nitroglycerin to a chest-pain patient after checking BP and PDE-5 history, or oral glucose gel to a drowsy hypoglycemic patient — with coaching, mask fitting, and monitoring for deterioration.

Infusion management in a controlled institutional setting or critical-care transport: at a nursing home, clinic, event medical tent, or during an interfacility transfer, mix/spike a drug bag, program the pump, start and titrate a vasopressor, nitroglycerin, or sedation drip to a target blood pressure or sedation level, respond to pump alarms, and hand off to receiving staff.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device uses AI-guided ultrasound and robotic needle insertion to draw diagnostic blood from a seated patient whose arm is positioned in the machine; CE-marked in 2024 and deployed in European labs/hospitals from March 2025. It performs venipuncture only — no drug selection, preparation, or administration — on stable, cooperative outpatients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It shares only the needle-into-vein step with IV drug administration; the patient is stable, seated and cooperative with the arm fixtured in the device, no drug is chosen, drawn up, pushed, or titrated, and no post-administration clinical monitoring occurs, so it cannot substantiate an emergency pharmacological intervention.

sources.title: Vitestro launches new website and first public video of Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device
sources.claim: Vitestro's own launch material describes the workflow as beginning with the patient positioning an arm at the device, confirming that the system requires a cooperative patient presenting a limb to a fixed station rather than a robot working on a patient found in extremis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic blood collection. Establishes the presentation conditions the only commercially deployed autonomous needle robot requires (patient seated, arm placed at a fixed device), which no prehospital emergency drug administration instance provides.

sources.title: Alumni robot performs first autonomous injection | Engineering | University of Waterloo
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed what was reported as the first autonomous robotic intramuscular ... lidar/AI to select an injection site on a subject and a needle-free injector to deliver a vaccine dose. It was a one-off laboratory demonstration of a single pre-loaded dose on a standing, cooperative subject.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intramuscular vaccination. The delivery motion resembles IM epinephrine or naloxone, but the demonstration involved a cooperative subject with the deltoid exposed, a single pre-set drug and dose, no emergency assessment or route choice, and no monitoring/re-dosing, so it does not carry over to emergency IM pharmacology at worker reliability.

sources.title: Cobionix Secures $3M for Autonomous Medical Robotics Platform
sources.claim: As of mid-2025 Cobionix was still pre-commercial, raising seed funding to begin pilot programs, indicating its injection platform is not in service performing patient drug administration anywhere.
sources.transferJustification: Same system as the injection demo; documents maturity (pilot stage, no deployment) rather than a new capability.

sources.title: Hyperion Surgical Announces Completion of First-in-Human Study Using Its Ivy Robotic Vascular Access Platform
sources.claim: Hyperion Surgical reported the first robotic-assisted IV catheterization in a human in October 2025 — a first-in-human study of vascular access, described as robotic-assisted rather than autonomous, and not involving drug selection or administration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peripheral IV catheter placement, the access step of IV drug administration. Autonomy is not established (described as robotic-assisted) and the study is first-in-human in a controlled clinical setting, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Portable autonomous venipuncture robot / hand-held venipuncture device
sources.title: Portable robot for autonomous venipuncture using 3D near infrared image guidance - PubMed
sources.claim: Rutgers researchers built portable and hand-held robots that autonomously image veins and insert a needle to establish peripheral access; these remain research devices evaluated on volunteers and phantoms in laboratory/clinical study settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous peripheral line placement. It covers only vascular access on a stationary, positioned arm of a stable volunteer, with no drug preparation, administration, or clinical monitoring, and it is not fielded.

sources.title: FDA Grants Premarket Approval (PMA) For The SEDASYS System For Healthy Patients Undergoing Sedation During Routine Colonoscopy And EGD Procedures
sources.claim: The SEDASYS computer-assisted personalized sedation system automatically delivered IV propofol and responded to signs of over-sedation in endoscopy suites; it required clinicians to place the IV and supervise, was limited to healthy patients undergoing elective procedures, and was pulled from the market in 2016.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated titration of one IV drug during elective sedation in a purpose-equipped endoscopy suite. Access is placed by a clinician, a clinician team must be present, and the indication excludes unstable/emergency patients, so it does not substantiate autonomous emergency drug intervention.

sources.title: Johnson & Johnson bails on Sedasys anesthesia device - MassDevice
sources.claim: Johnson & Johnson discontinued the SEDASYS automated sedation system in 2016, so no closed-loop patient drug-delivery machine of this kind is on the US market today.
sources.transferJustification: Documents withdrawal of the only marketed closed-loop IV drug delivery system; relevant to maturity, not to new capability.

sources.title: Wearable device can detect and reverse opioid overdose | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: A University of Washington wearable prototype detected apnea/immobility and automatically injected naloxone into study participants in a supervised injection facility and hospital trial — a closed-loop single-drug injector that must be worn in advance, not a system that responds to an unknown patient found at a scene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated naloxone delivery. It delivers one pre-loaded drug from a device already strapped to a consenting subject, performs no scene assessment, airway/ventilation support, route selection, or re-dosing, and is a research prototype, so it cannot complete the paramedic's naloxone instance.

sources.developer: University of Pittsburgh / Carnegie Mellon University (DoD funded)
sources.title: Army Developing Robotic Trauma Care System | National Defense Magazine
sources.claim: Autonomous prehospital trauma care including robotic drug delivery remains a funded research goal (TRACIR), not a fielded capability; a 2025 Military Medicine review of fully autonomous casualty care treats it as a future paradigm.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targets the task (autonomous prehospital assessment and treatment including drug delivery) but is a development program without a demonstrated end-to-end autonomous drug intervention on patients; it supports a negative judgment only.

tasks.label: Administer drugs, orally or by injection, or perform intravenous procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Starting a peripheral IV and giving IV fluid or medication (e.g., ondansetron, fentanyl, saline bolus) to a stable, cooperative adult at a private residence - patient seated in a chair, on a bed, or on the floor; variable lighting, family/pets present, cramped access, arm resting on whatever surface is available.

Establishing IV access and pushing or hanging medication in the patient compartment of a moving ambulance en route to hospital: patient strapped supine on the cot, arm on an armboard or cot rail, standard fixed cabinet layout, vibration and lateral motion, one medic working.

IV access and drug administration inside an institutional facility - nursing home room, dialysis or urgent-care clinic, or hospital ED bay during an interfacility transfer; patient in a bed or wheelchair, staff and equipment on hand, controlled premises.

Intramuscular, subcutaneous or intranasal injection in the field (epinephrine for anaphylaxis, glucagon, naloxone, midazolam) at a roadside, workplace, restaurant, park or public sidewalk; patient may be altered, agitated, clothed in layers, in poor light.

Oral administration at scene: chewable aspirin for chest pain, oral glucose gel or tablets for hypoglycemia, orally disintegrating antiemetic - the medic checks allergies and ability to swallow, opens the dose, places it in the patient's hand or mouth, and confirms it is taken.

Resuscitation drug delivery: intraosseous drill placement or rapid IV access on a collapsed, hypotensive, seizing or cardiac-arrest patient on the floor, in a bathroom, or in a wrecked vehicle, with CPR and airway work ongoing and repeated timed drug pushes.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Aletta, an autonomous robotic phlebotomy device, performs the complete venipuncture sequence (vein imaging, skin disinfection, tourniquet, needle insertion, sample filling, bandaging) by itself, with one trained supervisor overseeing up to three machines, in Dutch hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It shares the objects (human antecubital vein, hypodermic needle, tourniquet, skin prep) and the sub-millimetre targeting precision required to 'perform intravenous procedures'; the residual difference for paramedic IV work is advancing/securing a catheter and injecting rather than aspirating fluid.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The Aletta procedure requires the patient to place their arm inside the machine's cradle and press start - the work is brought to a fixed device rather than the device going to the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (venipuncture); this item establishes the environment class - the arm is fixtured in a purpose-built cradle, i.e. an E1 presentation, not an in-situ approach to a patient.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: In a 1,633-patient multicenter trial across three outpatient phlebotomy departments the autonomous device achieved 94.5% first-stick success, including 92.7% in self-reported difficult-venous-access patients, with 0.6% mild adverse events.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture. Establishes that autonomous needle-into-vein performance is at or above human first-attempt rates, the quality bar for the vascular-access element of this paramedic task.

sources.title: Vitestro Unveils Aletta: The World's First Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ARPD)
sources.claim: Aletta is CE-marked and commercially launched in Europe for routine diagnostic blood collection in hospitals and laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture; this item establishes commercial maturity rather than a new capability.

sources.title: FDA Grants Premarket Approval (PMA) For The SEDASYS System For Healthy Patients Undergoing Sedation During Routine Colonoscopy And EGD Procedures
sources.claim: The SEDASYS system received FDA premarket approval and was commercially launched in US endoscopy suites to deliver intravenous propofol into a patient through an integrated infusion pump that titrates and stops the drug automatically based on patient monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated IV drug delivery through an established line with closed-loop monitoring. It covers the 'administer the drug' half of the paramedic task once access exists; with autonomous venipuncture it shows both halves are machine-executable when the patient is presented to the equipment.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: The Cobi robot autonomously located an injection site with LiDAR and AI and delivered a needle-free intramuscular injection to a human subject at a kiosk-style station, with no healthcare professional performing the injection.

sources.title: Hyperion completes first-in-human study of Ivy robotic vascular access platform
sources.claim: Hyperion Surgical completed a first-in-human robotic-assisted IV catheterization with its Ivy platform, designed to place the catheter and not only the needle; reports describe a clinician-operated, AI-assisted procedure and do not establish autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peripheral IV catheter placement, the closest match to 'perform intravenous procedures'; autonomy is unclear so it is treated as teleoperated and used only as context.

tasks.label: Attend training classes to maintain certification licensure, keep abreast of new developments in the field, or maintain existing knowledge.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Self-paced online continuing-education modules and live webinars completed at a computer at home or at the station to accumulate NCCP/state CE hours for NREMT or state license renewal; includes post-tests and attendance attestation.

In-person classroom CE at the agency or regional training center: medical-director protocol updates, new-drug and new-equipment briefings, lectures, and case/QA review sessions, with a sign-in roster for CE credit.

Hands-on skills verification and simulation labs: ACLS/PALS/BLS megacodes, airway manikins, IV/IO task trainers, cardiac-arrest and trauma scenarios run with an instructor who signs off competency for card renewal.

Off-site multi-day conferences and certification courses (EMS World, state EMS conference, PHTLS, AMLS, critical-care transport programs) involving travel, lecture tracks, vendor demonstrations, and written exams.
Hospital clinical rotations or refresher ride-time (ED, OR airway time, cath lab observation) arranged to maintain currency in low-frequency skills, supervised and documented by a preceptor.

instances.label: 911 medical call in a private residence (e.g., chest pain, dyspnea, altered mental status, overdose): paramedic gathers history from the patient/family and medication bottles, takes vitals and a 12-lead ECG, radios or patches the report to the receiving ED/medical control, and administers treatment (O2, IV access, aspirin/nitro, naloxone, nebulized bronchodilator) before and during transport.

Trauma or medical emergency in a public/outdoor or workplace setting (motor-vehicle crash on a roadway, fall on a sidewalk, collapse in a restaurant or job site): scene size-up to determine circumstances, rapid assessment and vitals amid bystanders, weather and hazards, trauma-center notification, and treatment such as hemorrhage control, spinal motion restriction, splinting, IV fluids, and analgesia.

Continued care in the ambulance patient compartment en route: repeat vitals and cardiac monitoring on a moving stretcher, radio/phone patch to the receiving facility with vital statistics and history, orders from medical control, and administration of medications, airway management or defibrillation as the patient's condition changes.

Response to or transfer from an institutional facility (skilled nursing home, urgent-care clinic, or sending hospital): obtain vital statistics, medication list and history from facility staff and paperwork/EMR, clarify the circumstances of the emergency with nurses, coordinate with the receiving unit, and administer/maintain treatment such as oxygen, IV drips, or pressor infusions during transfer.

Arrival and transfer of care at the emergency department: coordinate with ED triage and trauma-team personnel, give a verbal report of vitals, history and circumstances, move the patient to the ED bed, and continue treatment (bag-valve ventilation, CPR, drug administration) until the hospital team assumes care.
