sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic blood collection. It shows a robot can place a needle in a vein of a cooperative, fixtured arm in a controlled outpatient room; it does not transfer to obtaining history, judging the circumstances of an emergency, or delivering airway, drug and resuscitation care on an uncontrolled patient.

instances.label: Hospital patient tray-line supervision during a meal period: the technician stands at the moving tray line in the hospital kitchen, checks each assembled tray against the diet-order ticket (therapeutic diets, texture modifications, allergies), spot-checks portions and plate temperatures, physically pulls/corrects wrong items, keeps 6-10 tray-line workers paced to the delivery schedule, and signs off on the line before carts go to the floors.

Production supervision in an institutional kitchen (hospital, nursing home, college, correctional): oversees cooks working from standardized recipes and production sheets, adjusts batch quantities against forecast census, probes food with a thermometer and records HACCP cook/hold temperatures, tastes for seasoning and consistency, inspects sanitation and cooling of leftovers, and redirects staff when items run late or short.

Service supervision on a serving line or in a long-term-care dining room: verifies residents/customers receive the correct diet, texture and portion, checks steam-table and cold-well temperatures, restocks or re-pans items, monitors servers' portioning tools and hygiene, handles substitutions and complaints in real time, and documents intake or service issues for the dietitian.

Assisting the dietitian with food service planning: building cycle menus and production sheets, forecasting quantities and purchasing needs, standardizing and test-batching recipes (weighing portions, tasting, adjusting yields), walking the storeroom and coolers to check par stock and dating, and preparing nutrient-analysis and compliance paperwork for review.

School nutrition serving-line supervision during short, high-volume lunch waves: checks that each served tray meets reimbursable-meal component requirements, verifies scoop/portion sizes, monitors temperatures and holding times on the line, replenishes pans, and directs 3-6 cafeteria workers while students move through the line.

tasks.label: Analyze menus or recipes, standardize recipes, or test new products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Desk work in a foodservice office (hospital, school district, LTC facility): running a cycle menu or a recipe through nutrient-analysis software, comparing results to meal-pattern/therapeutic-diet specs, checking variety, allergens, ingredient spec sheets and cost, and writing up the analysis for the RD. No handling of food.

Standardizing a recipe in the institutional production kitchen: scaling a recipe (e.g., 25 to 200 servings), weighing/measuring ingredients with the cooks, observing and timing the test batch on the facility's kettles/ovens, measuring yield and count of portions with the specified scoop/ladle, checking taste, texture, temperature and appearance, adjusting quantities and method over one or more trials, and issuing the finished standardized recipe card.

Testing a new product (e.g., a lower-sodium gravy base, thickened beverage, fortified pudding, gluten-free bread) in the kitchen or test kitchen: preparing samples per manufacturer directions alongside the current item, coding and plating samples, running a small staff taste panel, tabulating sensory scores plus cost/labor/yield, and recommending accept or reject.

Test-tray / quality audit of a standardized menu item in production: pulling a tray or serving-line sample, checking portion size against the recipe, temperature with a probe, appearance and palatability by tasting, recording deviations, and revising production notes or the recipe so the item meets standard.

Acceptance testing with customers in a dining room, patient unit or school cafeteria: serving samples of a new or reformulated menu item, collecting preference/acceptance scores or plate-waste measurements from residents, patients or students, and summarizing results for the menu decision.

instances.label: Community/retail pharmacy: technician transcribes a new paper or faxed prescription (handwritten or printed) into the pharmacy management system — patient match, drug, strength, directions/sig, quantity, refills, prescriber DEA/NPI — at a counter workstation during walk-in traffic.

Retail chain pharmacy: technician works the electronic-prescription queue, confirming the e-script maps to the right patient profile and drug NDC, editing sig or day-supply fields, and submitting the third-party insurance claim, resolving rejects (prior auth, refill-too-soon).

Retail/independent pharmacy: entry of refill requests, phoned-in prescriptions transcribed from voicemail or a call-in log, and prescriptions transferred in from another pharmacy, into the same dispensing database.

Hospital or health-system inpatient pharmacy: technician enters or verifies physician medication orders (including IV admixtures, unit-dose, and titration orders) into the pharmacy information system linked to the EHR, under pharmacist check.

Long-term-care, mail-order, or specialty pharmacy: high-volume batch entry of cycle-fill and new-patient orders, plus setting up patient demographics, allergies, and insurance/benefit records in the database.

tasks.label: Maintain proper storage and security conditions for drugs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Community/retail pharmacy: the daily wholesaler order arrives in totes; the tech checks it in, scans and shelves stock bottles and cartons in the alphabetized bulk shelving and the pharmacy refrigerator, rotates stock so shortest-dated is used first, places C-II items in the locked safe/cabinet, and keeps the dispensing area secured during and after hours.

Hospital central pharmacy: receive bulk drug shipments, put away into shelving/carousels/automated storage, place refrigerated and frozen items in monitored units, store controlled substances in the narcotics vault with perpetual inventory, keep the vault locked and access logged, and run cycle counts.

Point-of-care storage upkeep: restock automated dispensing cabinets in nursing-unit medication rooms, load pockets/bins with barcode-verified doses, witness/verify controlled-substance counts, check and reseal crash carts and emergency kits, and confirm cabinets and med rooms are locked.

Expiration/short-date audit of pharmacy stock: work shelves and storage bins with an outdate list, pull short-dated and expired product, quarantine it in a segregated 'do not dispense' area, and stage it for return/reverse distribution or destruction.

Cold-chain and environmental/security condition maintenance: check and log refrigerator/freezer temperatures, respond to excursions by relocating stock, keep humidity/light-protection conditions, verify alarms, locks and door security on drug storage areas.

High-volume facility (central fill, mail-order, long-term-care pharmacy, or pharmacy distribution center): keep bulk drug inventory stored in canisters/carousels/automated stockrooms, replenish machine storage, maintain lot/expiry rotation and secure storage of controlled and refrigerated products.

instances.label: Chain retail pharmacy (CVS/Walgreens/grocery) pickup counter: routine will-call prescription handed over — patient name/DOB verified, HIPAA/counseling signature captured on pad, insurance-adjudicated copay charged to a credit/debit/HSA card, receipt printed, bag handed over.

Chain retail pharmacy counter: same prescription pickup but paid with cash — counting bills and coins, making change from the drawer, printing receipt (sometimes applying a discount card or GoodRx price).

Ringing up front-store/OTC merchandise at the pharmacy register: cough syrup, diabetic test strips, vitamins, a device, sometimes together with the prescription; scanning barcodes, applying loyalty/coupon, taking card or cash, bagging.

Drive-thru window transaction: customer stays in the car, tech confirms identity through the glass, passes the bag and card terminal or cash through a sliding drawer/tube, returns change and receipt, answers spoken questions.

Non-routine counter transaction: copay dispute or insurance rejection, price check, partial fill, split tender or manufacturer copay card, refund/void, controlled-substance or pseudoephedrine ID check and logbook, referral of counseling questions to the pharmacist.

Hospital outpatient / clinic / employee-benefit pharmacy window: discharged patient or staff member pays a copay by card, FSA card or payroll deduction; medication released with identity verification, receipt issued.

tasks.label: Price and file prescriptions that have been filled.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain retail pharmacy (CVS/Walgreens/grocery): after a prescription is filled and verified, the technician confirms the price/copay produced by third-party adjudication in the pharmacy system, staples the receipt/paperwork to the bag, and files the bagged vial(s) into will-call storage — alphabetical hanging-bag racks or bins, with fridge items flagged — consolidating multiple scripts for the same patient and later pulling unclaimed ones for return-to-stock.

Independent/small community pharmacy: technician prices cash, discount-card, compounded or non-covered prescriptions (manually applying pricing rules where adjudication rejects), then files the finished package into will-call bins by patient name; items vary widely in size — vials, boxes of inhalers, insulin pens for the fridge, bulky liquids, delivery-route baskets.

Central-fill / mail-order / micro-fulfillment facility: prescriptions priced in batch by the host system; completed, sealed patient packages coming off the fill line are routed and filed into the correct store tote or shipping container by destination store or carrier, then manifested for dispatch.

Hospital / health-system pharmacy: filled patient-specific medication orders, first doses and discharge (meds-to-beds) prescriptions are filed into patient bins, unit cassettes, delivery totes or outpatient will-call storage; charges/pricing posted to the patient account or 340B/insurance billing in the pharmacy information system.

Long-term-care / closed-door pharmacy: filled vials, blister cards and pouch rolls are priced against facility or per-diem billing, then filed into facility-specific and route-specific totes/bins staged for the courier run.

Records filing: hard-copy prescriptions, signature logs, prior-authorization forms and paper claim documents for prescriptions already filled are indexed and filed — scanned into the document system and/or stored in numbered/dated files in the back room for regulatory retention.

tasks.label: Mix pharmaceutical preparations, according to written prescriptions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/health-system central pharmacy IV room: technician gowns into an ISO 7 cleanroom and, in an ISO 5 hood, reconstitutes lyophilized vials with diluent and dilutes drug into minibags or draws syringes for routine formulary items (antibiotics, analgesics, OR syringes), patient-specific and batch, then labels and stages the doses for pharmacist check.

Community/retail pharmacy: technician takes a manufacturer bottle of powder for oral suspension (amoxicillin, azithromycin, cephalexin), adds the label-specified volume of purified water in portions, shakes to a uniform suspension, optionally adds flavoring, caps, labels with beyond-use date and auxiliary labels, at a busy counter workflow with same-visit turnaround.

Oncology/hazardous-drug compounding: technician prepares patient-specific antineoplastic doses (reconstitute vial, withdraw calculated volume, inject into bag or syringe with CSTD) inside a biological safety cabinet or containment isolator in a USP <800> negative-pressure room, with gravimetric/barcode verification.

Parenteral nutrition compounding in a hospital or home-infusion pharmacy: technician loads source containers of dextrose, amino acids, lipids, electrolytes and trace elements onto an automated compounding device tubing set, runs the patient-specific TPN formula into an EVA bag, performs gravimetric checks, and adds any off-device additives, then labels.

Custom non-sterile compounding in a compounding or retail pharmacy: technician weighs multiple APIs and excipients per a written formula and prepares creams/ointments by levigation or ointment mill, hand-filled or machine-filled capsules, suppositories/troches in molds, or suspensions from crushed tablets, with variable formulas, containers and equipment.

Standardized non-sterile oral dosage form prepared from a validated in-house formula (e.g., pediatric propranolol or hydrocortisone liquid/oral film) in a health-system or community pharmacy: fixed formulation with a pre-qualified vehicle/base, mixed and dosed into unit containers, with batch records and dose-content documentation.

sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA is a fully automated IV compounding robot that prepares labeled syringes and IV bags, including from lyophilized (powder) products, inside its own ISO Class 5 enclosure; two units at Mission Health's cleanroom suite produce thousands of doses per month.

tasks.label: Order, label, and count stock of medications, chemicals, or supplies and enter inventory data into computer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Community/chain retail pharmacy, daily wholesaler delivery: technician opens totes, verifies each stock bottle/box against the invoice, checks for damage/shorts and refrigerated items, applies shelf/bin labels, puts stock away on alphabetized behind-counter shelves and in the fridge, and receives the order into the pharmacy management system.

Retail pharmacy inventory control: cycle counts and periodic physical inventory of shelf stock (including counting tablets in open stock bottles and reconciling the controlled-substance perpetual log), checking expiration dates and pulling outdates, reviewing reorder points and transmitting the replenishment order to the wholesaler, entering adjustments into the computer.

Hospital central pharmacy: receiving and putting away bulk medications, IV solutions and supplies into carousels/shelving and the narcotics vault; repackaging and barcode-labeling unit doses; logging lots and expirations; cycle counting controlled substances; entering all inventory data into the pharmacy information system.

Hospital/clinic point-of-use restocking: technician takes picked medications to nursing-unit automated dispensing cabinets and med rooms, scans each item, loads pockets/bins, verifies and corrects counts, pulls expired stock, and confirms the transaction in the cabinet/inventory system.

High-volume central-fill, mail-order or long-term-care pharmacy: receiving bulk drug shipments at the dock, put-away into automated storage, replenishing dispensing-robot canisters/cells with verified drug, bulk labeling, and reconciling counts in the fulfillment/warehouse inventory system.

Compounding, specialty or nuclear pharmacy: ordering bulk chemicals, diluents and supplies; labeling stock and repackaged containers with drug, lot, expiration and hazard information; recording lot numbers and quantities in compounding/inventory records; counting supply par levels.

tasks.label: Clean and help maintain equipment or work areas and sterilize glassware, according to prescribed methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Community/retail pharmacy: end-of-shift and between-fill cleaning of the dispensing bench — wiping counters and counting trays/spatulas with alcohol between antibiotic counts, clearing tablet dust and stray tablets, wiping the vial-filling station and keyboards, tidying and sweeping/mopping the small area behind the counter, all around drug stock, paper, and computers.

Hospital/503A sterile compounding suite: USP <797> cleaning and disinfection — daily wipe-down of the ISO 5 PEC (LAFW/BSC/CACI) interior with sterile alcohol and periodic sporicidal, cleaning carts, counters, floors, and monthly walls/ceilings in gowned ISO 7/8 ante- and buffer rooms, with logged documentation.

Non-sterile/ compounding pharmacy: washing and drying mortars and pestles, ointment slabs, spatulas, capsule machines, graduates and beakers after a compound; washing and autoclaving/depyrogenating glassware per prescribed method and returning it to storage.

Cleaning drug-contact automation: brushing/vacuuming tablet dust from automated counters and pouch packagers, cleaning cells and chutes of a dispensing robot (ScriptPro/Parata), wiping automated dispensing cabinets and refrigerator interiors on schedule.

Helping maintain equipment beyond cleaning: clearing jams, swapping printer ribbons/labels and filters, checking balance calibration with test weights, lubricating or replacing small parts, and logging service issues for the vendor.

Hospital pharmacy general work area upkeep: wiping down carousel shelving, IV room anteroom surfaces, delivery carts and totes, cleaning refrigerator/freezer interiors, restocking cleaning and PPE supplies, and mopping the pharmacy floor.

sources.title: Rosie™ by CleanBotix | Robotic Sanitation for Food Plants
sources.claim: CleanBotix 'Rosie' is a mobile-manipulator sanitation robot that autonomously executes a rinse-foam-rinse-sanitize sequence on food and beverage plant equipment and open plant areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sanitation of processing equipment and work areas to a measured hygiene standard. Transfers to pharmacy equipment/work-area cleaning only where the setting is purpose-built for machine washdown (stainless, drained, no loose stock), so it substantiates E1, not the cluttered pharmacy bench.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: nightly sanitation of industrial food equipment. Establishes worker-quality cleaning (ATP verification) by an autonomous robot in a washdown-designed facility, supporting equipment/area cleaning at a purpose-built (E1) tier.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing and dry-heat sterilizing pharmaceutical glassware. Identical objects and prescribed sterilization method as the pharmacy glassware instance, executed by machine in a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Cleaning-in-Place (CIP) for the Pharmaceutical Industry
sources.claim: Standardized clean-in-place skids automatically clean pharmaceutical process equipment through programmed rinse/detergent/rinse cycles delivering validated results with little manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning pharmaceutical equipment according to a prescribed, validated method with documented cycles — the same output the pharmacy technician's cleaning must deliver, achieved by machine when the equipment is purpose-built for it.

sources.title: Loop Robots - for Hospital Pharmacies

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Community/chain retail pharmacy: for a routine oral-solid prescription, retrieve the bulk stock bottle, count the prescribed number of tablets/capsules into a vial, cap it, print the prescription and auxiliary labels ... affix them to the vial for pharmacist verification.

Retail pharmacy: non-countable / unit-of-use items (inhalers, creams and ointments, insulin pens, eye drops, prefilled manufacturer bottles and boxes) - pull the manufacturer package from stock, print and affix the patient-specific prescription label plus auxiliary labels, bag for pickup.

Hospital inpatient pharmacy: prepack bulk oral solids into single unit-dose packages, each printed/labeled with drug name, strength, lot, expiration and a scannable barcode, then stocked for cart fill and dispensing cabinets.

Central-fill / mail-order or micro-fulfillment pharmacy: high-volume filling of vials and bottles for maintenance prescriptions with label print-and-apply, capping and imaging/verification, thousands of scripts per day.
Long-term-care / adherence packaging pharmacy: fill multi-dose blister ('bingo') cards or strip pouches for a patient's regimen from bulk stock, seal, and apply patient/medication labels.

Retail or hospital pharmacy: prepare oral liquids - reconstitute a powdered antibiotic with a measured volume of water or pour a bulk liquid into a dispensing bottle, cap, and affix the label plus shake-well auxiliary labels.

tasks.label: Transfer medication from vials to the appropriate number of sterile, disposable syringes, using aseptic techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital IV room (USP <797> cleanroom, ISO 5 laminar-airflow hood): technician draws patient-specific adult doses (typically 0.5-20 mL) of antibiotics, steroids, narcotics and other non-hazardous drugs from single- or multi-dose vials into sterile syringes, swabbing septa, labeling and staging for pharmacist check.

Hospital pharmacy batch/anticipatory production: technician fills dozens to hundreds of identical standard-dose syringes (OR trays, heparin/saline flushes, common antibiotic pushes) from vials or reconstituted bulk, using repetitive aseptic draw-up in the hood.

Hazardous-drug room (negative-pressure BSC or compounding aseptic containment isolator): technician prepares patient-specific chemotherapy syringes from cytotoxic vials with closed-system transfer devices, gowned and double-gloved, with strict dose-accuracy and containment requirements.

Community/retail pharmacy or clinic immunization area: technician or pharmacist draws 0.3-1.0 mL vaccine or injectable doses from multi-dose vials into syringes at the counter shortly before administration (immediate-use aseptic technique, no cleanroom), often in bursts during flu/COVID clinics.

Pediatric/neonatal or specialty doses: micro-volume draws well under 0.5 mL, serial dilutions from a vial into multiple syringes, viscous or foaming products, and off-formulary/odd vial presentations not covered by any standard workflow, requiring judgment about dilution and container choice.

503B outsourcing facility or health-system central-fill cleanroom: high-volume production runs of pre-filled syringes from vials or bulk reservoirs under cGMP-style batch records, with in-process weight/accuracy checks and lot documentation.

sources.claim: IntelliFill i.v. is a robotic syringe-filling system used in US hospitals that, in vial mode, autonomously decaps a vial, swabs the septum with alcohol, inserts a needle, draws the dose into a syringe, recaps, labels and weighs it, with validated accuracy from 0.5 to 11.5 mL and media-fill sterility validation.

tasks.label: Restock intravenous (IV) supplies and add measured drugs or nutrients to IV solutions under sterile conditions to prepare IV packs for various uses, such as chemotherapy medication.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient pharmacy IV room: technician gowns, gloves, and prepares patient-specific non-hazardous admixtures (antibiotic minibags, electrolyte additives, IV-push syringes) at an ISO 5 laminar-airflow hood inside an ISO 7 cleanroom, using aseptic technique, barcode verification, labeling, and pharmacist check.

Hazardous-drug/chemotherapy doses (e.g., cytotoxics, monoclonals) reconstituted and drawn into bags/syringes/elastomeric pumps inside a biological safety cabinet or compounding aseptic containment isolator in a negative-pressure USP <800> buffer room, with closed-system transfer devices, double gloves, and gravimetric dose checks.

Batch work in the IV room: parenteral nutrition bags compounded on an automated compounding device from multiple source containers, plus batched syringes/minibags of common drugs for OR and floor stock, with beyond-use dating and quality checks.

Restocking the sterile compounding suite itself: pulling IV bags, vials, syringes, needles, and CSTD components from pharmacy stores, wiping each with sterile IPA, staging through the pass-through into the anteroom/buffer room, and filling hood-side bins and carousel racks between compounding runs.

Replenishing IV supplies outside the cleanroom: running totes of IV fluids, tubing, and admixture supplies from central stores/receiving to the pharmacy, and restocking IV supply carts and nursing-unit stock locations on the floors.

Ambulatory infusion center, community cancer center, or home-infusion pharmacy: lower-volume, more varied orders compounded in a smaller cleanroom/BSC, often same-day for scheduled infusion appointments, with the technician also handling supply stock.

tasks.label: Supply and monitor robotic machines that dispense medicine into containers and label the containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain or independent community pharmacy with a vial-filling robot (ScriptPro SP 200, Parata Max 2, McKesson CountMate): technician pulls bulk stock bottles from the shelf, scans the NDC against the drug cell barcode, opens the bottle and pours tablets into the cell/canister, re-seats it, tops up vials, caps and label/ribbon stock, watches the screen for misfeeds and low-stock alerts, clears jams, and moves finished labeled vials to the pharmacist check bin — all in a busy behind-the-counter workspace shared with other staff.

High-volume central-fill / mail-order fulfillment center: technician monitors a robotic dispensing line and conveyors, swaps or refills dispenser canisters from bulk bottles when reorder alerts fire, keeps vial, cap and label stock loaded, clears conveyor and capper jams, and pulls exception orders off the line for manual handling.

Hospital inpatient pharmacy: technician loads bulk oral solids into unit-dose packager cassettes/canisters (Omnicell packager, Swisslog PillPick/EvoTec, ATP-style machine), loads packaging film and label stock, inducts stock into the automated storage/dispensing robot, monitors runs, clears jams, and inspects packaged/labeled doses before pharmacist verification.

Long-term-care or adherence-packaging pharmacy: technician fills pouch-packager cassettes (Parata PASS, TCGRx, Yuyama, JVM) from bulk bottles, calibrates and swaps cassettes for new NDCs, loads pouch film and print ribbon, monitors for misfills and missed pouches, and inspects the labeled pouch strips.

Hospital sterile compounding room: technician supplies an IV/chemo compounding robot (RIVA, APOTECAchemo, Equashield Pro) with drug vials, diluent bags, syringes and labels in the cleanroom, starts and monitors batch runs, responds to alarms and rejected preparations, and unloads finished, labeled syringes and bags.

tasks.label: Deliver medications or pharmaceutical supplies to patients, nursing stations, or surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient pharmacy: scheduled batch/cart run — tech loads unit-dose cassettes, first doses and floor-stock refills onto a cart, takes elevators through busy corridors, and drops the medications at nursing stations on multiple patient-care units, several times a shift.

STAT / on-demand runs and controlled substances: an urgent single dose or a narcotic order must go from the central pharmacy to a specific nursing unit within minutes, with locked transport, chain-of-custody documentation and a witnessed/authenticated handoff to the receiving nurse, often on off-hour shifts.

High-risk and specialty products: IV admixtures, chemotherapy, refrigerated and light-protected items and total parenteral nutrition carried from the IV room to ICUs, oncology infusion centers and the perioperative area (OR satellite pharmacy / anesthesia workroom), with temperature and integrity maintained and receipt documented.

Meds-to-beds / bedside discharge delivery: the tech brings the discharge prescriptions to the patient's room before discharge, confirms the patient, may collect payment, and hands the bag over (pharmacist counsels), so the patient leaves with medications in hand.

Community/outpatient pharmacy: retrieving the completed prescription from will-call bins and handing it to the patient at the counter or drive-thru window — identity check, signature, payment, offer of counseling.

Off-site courier run: driving medications from a community, LTC or home-infusion pharmacy to a patient's house or a nursing-home nursing station, in traffic and weather, with a signature required at the door.

tasks.label: Maintain and merchandise home healthcare products or services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain-drugstore sales floor: restock the home-healthcare/self-care aisle from backstock totes and cases — unbox and shelve blood-pressure monitors, thermometers, braces, compression stockings, diabetic test strips, incontinence briefs; hang peg-hook items, face product, check shelf tags — while shoppers and carts move through the aisle.

Weekly stock-condition check of the home-health section: walk the section, identify out-of-stocks and low stock, spot misplaced items and missing/incorrect price and promo tags, and produce the restock/reorder list for the pharmacist or buyer.

Date-checking and rotation: pull short-dated or expired home-health items (test strips, wound care, nutritional supplements, OTC drugs), remove crushed or opened packages, rotate remaining stock forward, and process credits/returns to the wholesaler.

Merchandising work: build or refresh an endcap or seasonal home-health display — assemble the cardboard display fixture, arrange product per the planogram, hang signage and promo tags — and execute periodic section resets when the planogram changes.
Receive the wholesaler delivery of cased/boxed home-health stock at the back door: unload totes and cartons, verify against the invoice, break down cartons, and put stock away on backroom shelving.

Customer-facing merchandising of home-health products/services: demonstrate a BP monitor or nebulizer, measure and fit a knee brace or compression stockings, adjust a cane or crutch to the customer's height, assemble a walker for a buyer, or take a DME rental/insurance order.

sources.title: [2505.04572] Stow: Robotic Packing of Items into Fabric Pods
sources.claim: Amazon Robotics' Stow system autonomously places a wide diversity of consumer items onto densely packed shelf bins, running over 500,000 stows in a production fulfillment center at human-level packing density and speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stowing. Stowing diverse boxed/polybagged consumer goods into dense shelf bins is the same manipulation problem as replenishing packaged home-health merchandise onto retail shelving — comparable object sizes, weights and packaging, comparable placement precision — but performed inside a fenced robotic workcell where the goods are conveyed to the machine (E1).

sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the arXiv item: establishes that the shelf-stocking rate and reliability in the purpose-built cell approach a human stocker's.

tasks.label: Price stock and mark items for sale.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain drugstore sales floor: weekly price-change/promotion batch — tech prints new shelf price tags and sale signs, walks the OTC/HBA aisles, pulls old tags from the shelf-edge channels, inserts the new ones, and spot-checks that shelf price matches the POS price. Customers and carts in the aisle.

Pharmacy receiving area/back room: newly delivered OTC, vitamin and sundry stock is checked in against the invoice, cost and retail entered into the system, and a price sticker applied with a price gun/label printer to each unit or carton before it is shelved. Mixed carton sizes, shrink-wrapped multipacks.

Markdown/clearance work: tech pulls short-dated, discontinued or damaged-carton OTC items, looks up the reduced price, applies a markdown sticker over or beside the original price on each unit, and consolidates them on a clearance endcap.

Independent community pharmacy: pricing miscellaneous non-drug stock — durable medical equipment, home-health supplies, braces, gift/sundry items — computing retail from cost and hand-labeling irregular shapes (soft packs, blister cards, bagged items, boxes) with price stickers or hang tags.

Hospital / long-term-care pharmacy: repackaged unit-dose meds, floor-stock items and chargeable supplies are marked with printed barcode/charge labels (drug, strength, lot, expiry, charge code) so they price correctly at administration and in inventory; done at a bench in the central pharmacy.

sources.title: Automatic price labeler GLM-I 40 | Bizerba SE & Co. KG

sources.date: pages dated 2025; systems deployed in thousands of pharmacies

sources.claim: Robotic prescription dispensing systems installed in pharmacies fill and label containers autonomously, presenting vials with the printed label and auxiliary warnings already applied, at up to 150 vials per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic label application to pharmacy stock containers inside a purpose-built machine in a pharmacy. Demonstrates worker-quality, autonomous printing and affixing of item-specific labels on small pharmacy items.

sources.title: How Simbe Robotics' retail robots help stores and brands - Fast Company
sources.claim: Autonomous store robots deployed in US grocery chains navigate aisles and read barcodes and price tags to flag mispriced products and promotion errors, but they only scan and report — they do not print, apply or swap price tags or stickers.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the sales-floor instance: the only autonomous robot working the price-tag task in store aisles performs audit/verification only, providing no evidence of physical tag replacement or item marking at E2.

roles.title: Psychiatric Technicians
roles.description: Care for individuals with mental or emotional conditions or disabilities, following the instructions of physicians or other health practitioners. Monitor patients' physical and emotional well-being and report to medical staff. May participate in rehabilitation and treatment programs, help with personal hygiene, and administer oral or injectable medications.

tasks.label: Provide nursing, psychiatric, or personal care to patients with cognitive, intellectual, or developmental disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Personal hygiene care on an ICF/IID or state developmental-center unit: showering or bed-bathing a resident with a moderate-to-profound intellectual disability, perineal/incontinence care, oral care, shaving, dressing and grooming; the resident may be nonverbal, may resist, grab, or become agitated mid-task, and staff must physically guide, reposition and reassure while checking skin.

Mealtime care in a facility dining room: positioning residents, setting up adapted trays, prompting or hand-feeding residents with dysphagia and aspiration precautions, thickening liquids, watching for choking or pocketing, wiping and cleaning up, and recording intake for several residents in one sitting.

Medication pass on a psychiatric/developmental unit: verifying orders, pouring oral meds from cards, identifying the patient, handing meds and water, coaxing a reluctant patient, checking the mouth for cheeking, occasionally giving an oral-liquid or IM injectable dose, watching for side effects and documenting in the MAR.

Nursing-type checks and mobility support: taking vital signs, weights and blood-glucose readings on patients who may not hold still, applying dressings, seizure and safety observation rounds, toileting schedules, transferring a resident from bed to wheelchair, and walking or wheeling residents between the unit, dayroom and treatment areas.

Behavioral/psychiatric care during agitation: recognizing escalation, verbally redirecting, implementing an individual behavior support plan, blocking self-injurious behavior, and participating in a team physical hold, escort to seclusion, or post-restraint monitoring and comfort of a patient with an intellectual disability.

Care delivered in a community group home or on an outing: assisting a client with bathing, toileting and dressing in an ordinary house bathroom whose layout differs from site to site, giving meds in the kitchen, coaching ADL skills, and providing toileting/behavior support during a shopping trip or clinic appointment.

sources.system: ADA (Assistive Dexterous Arm) robot-assisted feeding system
sources.developer: University of Washington Personal Robotics Lab / Cornell EmPRISE (Bhattacharjee)
sources.title: Real-World Trials: UW's Assistive Feeding Robot Tested Beyond the Lab
sources.claim: The ADA assistive feeding arm was tested outside the lab with care recipients; the arm autonomously delivers a bite only after the user selects it through a web app or voice, with a user-operated kill button, and researchers report frequent off-nominal situations requiring variable autonomy and user/caregiver intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hand-feeding a person who cannot self-feed. It does not carry over to this task's mealtime instance because the users are cognitively intact adults with motor impairment who command each bite themselves, food and mounting are set up by a caregiver, and the system does not monitor for choking or manage a resident who refuses; the psychiatric technician's instance also covers multiple residents, prompting and intake documentation.

sources.title: Comparison of the Physical Care Burden on Formal Caregivers between Manual Human Care Using a Paper Diaper and Robot-Aided Care in Excretion Care
sources.claim: The CURACO Carebidet is a commercially sold excretion-care device for bedridden users that automatically detects excrement, suctions it away, then washes and dries the perineal area; a wearable unit must be fitted to the person by staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: incontinence care. It covers only cleanup for a compliant, bedridden wearer; it cannot bathe, dress, do oral care or handle a resident with an intellectual disability who removes the device or resists, so it does not complete the hygiene-care instance.

sources.title: Expo-Inspired 'Human Washing Machine' Tech Debuts in Japan's Nursing Care, Slashing Bathing Burdens
sources.claim: A bathing system derived from the Expo 'human washing machine', the Miraburu Assist Bath, was installed in June 2026 at an assisted-living home in Osaka; it cleans by microbubbles in a side-access tub, reducing but not eliminating caregivers' scrubbing and physical support of residents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisted bathing. It is a fixed tub appliance, not a system that undresses, transfers, washes hair and perineum, dries and dresses a resident; caregivers still perform the assistance, so it does not complete the hygiene instance even in a purpose-built bathing room.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Leads U.S. Adoption of Hospital Pharmacy Robotics, Redefines the Last Mile
sources.claim: The most widely deployed autonomous hospital robot in the US, Diligent Robotics' Moxi, performs materials and pharmacy transport within hospitals; its reported work is delivery volume, not patient-contact care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: medication logistics inside a hospital (an E2 facility). It substantiates only transport to the unit; it does not identify a patient, hand and observe ingestion of oral medication, check for cheeking, or give injections, so it cannot complete the medication-administration instance.

sources.developer: Foxconn (Hon Hai) with NVIDIA and Kawasaki
sources.title: AI Robotics, Digital Twins, and MONAI Contributions Highlight Hon Hai Foxconn's Smart Healthcare Vision at GTC Taipei 2025
sources.claim: Foxconn's Nurabot nursing cobot, in hospital field trials, is limited to medication and specimen transport, ward patrols and ... education rather than hands-on nursing or personal care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nursing support inside a hospital ward (E2). Its demonstrated repertoire contains no physical patient contact — no vitals taken by hand, no transfers, no hygiene or behavioral intervention — so it does not carry over to any instance of this task.

sources.system: Physically assistive robots (survey of the field)
sources.developer: Annual Review of Control, Robotics, and Autonomous Systems (academic review)
sources.title: Physically Assistive Robots: A Systematic Review of Mobile and Manipulator Robots That Physically Assist People with Disabilities
sources.claim: A 2024 systematic review of mobile and manipulator robots that physically assist people with disabilities in activities of daily living (ambulating, eating, dressing, hygiene) characterizes the field as a research literature rather than fielded caregiving systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical assistance with ADLs, which is the core of this task. The review's coverage is of laboratory and pilot systems, providing no named system that completes bathing, dressing, transfers or toileting for a patient at caregiver quality.

tasks.label: Encourage patients to develop work skills and to participate in social, recreational, or other therapeutic activities that enhance interpersonal skills or develop social relationships.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Restrain violent, potentially violent, or suicidal patients by verbal or physical means as required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient adult psychiatric unit: a patient escalates (pacing, shouting, threatening a peer). Tech approaches, uses verbal de-escalation — non-threatening body positioning, limit-setting, offering PRN medication, moving the patient to a quiet area — while reading second-by-second body-language cues and staying ready to switch to hands-on intervention; ends with the patient settled and the event documented.

Adult inpatient unit or psychiatric ED: verbal means fail and the patient swings or charges. A trained 4-5 person team performs a coordinated hands-on hold and escorted transport to a seclusion room, each staffer controlling one limb, applying only enough force to prevent injury to patient, staff and bystanders, avoiding positional asphyxia and joint injury.

Applying and maintaining mechanical restraints: a combative, actively resisting patient is placed supine on a bed and secured in 4-point limb restraints; a staffer holds an extremity while a nurse gives an IM injection; circulation and skin checks plus range-of-motion release every 15 minutes until release criteria are met.

Suicidal patient on 1:1 observation: tech must physically intervene in real time — cutting or removing a ligature from the neck, blocking head-banging against a wall, prying a sharp object from a clenched hand, or catching a patient climbing a fixture — with minimal force and immediate hand-off to medical staff.

Adolescent/child residential treatment facility or child psychiatric unit: an agitated youth begins throwing furniture and hitting staff; tech performs an approved therapeutic hold (e.g., CPI/Handle With Care) sized to a smaller body, holds until the youth is calm, then processes the incident verbally with the youth.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: The most widely deployed clinical mobile manipulator in US hospitals is explicitly limited to non-patient-facing logistics; it does not touch or physically manage patients.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed hospital robot with arms; cited to show that state-of-the-art in-hospital manipulation stops short of any patient contact, let alone restraint of a resisting person.

sources.title: Hospitals & Clinics | Knightscope
sources.claim: Autonomous security robots deployed in hospitals patrol and sense; any 'intervention' in an incident is a remote human speaking through the machine, with no physical engagement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital security response to aggressive persons. Shows the deployed capability is remote human voice broadcast and alerting, not autonomous verbal de-escalation of a specific agitated patient nor physical control.

sources.system: Socially assistive robots incl. PARO robotic seal
sources.title: Exploring the impact of socially assistive robots on health and wellbeing across the lifespan: An umbrella review and meta-analysis
sources.claim: Pooled evidence across socially assistive robots (PARO and similar) finds no effect on agitation or neuropsychiatric symptoms, so no fielded social robot substitutes for staff de-escalation of an agitated patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered calming interaction in care facilities. Even in the structured facilities where these robots are used they do not reduce agitation, so they cannot deliver the verbal-means half of this task.

sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: The most advanced human-handling care robots lift a cooperative patient between bed and wheelchair as laboratory prototypes under caregiver guidance; none handles a resisting person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot physically handling a human body. Transfer fails: the patient is cooperative and passive, the robot is an experimental prototype operated with caregiver input, and no result covers a struggling, combative adult.

sources.title: China's AI spherical robot cop can capture criminals, patrol streets
sources.claim: Police-style robots that 'immobilize' people do so outdoors with net guns, tear gas and sound weapons — force modalities and injury risk incompatible with clinical restraint of a psychiatric patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic apprehension of a violent person. Transfer fails: street pursuit with net guns and chemical agents is not worker-quality least-restrictive clinical restraint, and no hospital deployment or injury-rate evidence exists.

sources.system: Four-point restraint (human team standard of care; not a robotic system)
sources.title: Four-Point Restraint: Overview, Periprocedural Care, Technique
sources.claim: Clinical standard of care for restraining a violent patient requires a coordinated multi-person team with one member per extremity, defining the accepted-output bar for this task.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to fix the accepted-output bar (coordinated multi-limb control with minimal injury) against which robotic capability is judged.

tasks.label: Lead prescribed individual or group therapy sessions as part of specific therapeutic procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Monitor patients' physical and emotional well-being and report unusual behavior or physical ailments to medical staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled safety/observation rounds (q15 or q30) on a locked inpatient psychiatric unit: the tech walks the hallways and bedrooms, including darkened rooms at night, locates and identifies each patient, verifies they are breathing and not self-harming, notes what they are doing and their apparent state, records a coded observation for each patient on the rounds sheet, and immediately reports anything unusual to the charge nurse.

Continuous 1:1 or line-of-sight observation of a high-acuity patient (suicide precautions, detox, post-restraint): the tech stays within arm's length or direct sight for hours, continuously reads behavior, affect and physical status, positions self between the patient and hazards, documents at intervals, and alerts nursing staff to escalation or physical deterioration.

Ongoing milieu observation across a shift on a psych unit: watching patients at meals, in groups, during med pass and free time; noting mood, affect, sleep, appetite, hygiene decline, social withdrawal, paranoia, escalating agitation, and medication side effects such as tremor, oversedation or akathisia; verbally reporting changes to the nurse and charting them.

Noticing and following up on a physical ailment: a patient complains of chest pain, a headache, constipation or an injury, or shows a rash, swelling, unsteady gait, fever or vomiting; the tech looks at the site, feels skin temperature, checks pulse/vitals informally, questions the patient, and reports the findings to the nurse or physician.

Monitoring residents in a state residential facility or licensed group home for people with developmental disabilities and co-occurring mental illness, many of them nonverbal: detecting behavior changes or physical signs of illness in clients who cannot report symptoms, recording behavior data for treatment plans, and reporting to the facility nurse.

sources.title: Aeolus Debuts aeo Dual-Arm Humanoid Robot at CES 2023 - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Aeolus Robotics' aeo mobile robot performs autonomous night-shift patrols for resident safety in eldercare facilities in Japan, Hong Kong and Taipei, using vision to judge residents' posture and position and alerting connected staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous night patrol of a care facility that observes residents and alerts staff. It is the closest deployed analog to observation rounds, but it detects only a narrow set of safety events (posture/position, out-of-bed) and does not judge mood, behavior or physical ailments, so it does not carry over to the full monitoring-and-reporting task.

sources.developer: Japanese nursing-robot developers (as catalogued in an International Journal of Social Robotics review)
sources.title: Exploring Healthcare Staff's Attitudes and Perceptions of Robot Use in Nursing Care in Germany | International Journal of Social Robotics
sources.claim: 'Kurumi' is a night patrol robot for ... that detects residents with dementia wandering at night and alerts nursing staff; its core functions are speech recognition and person detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: night-time patrol and alerting in a care facility. Transfer is limited: detection of wandering is a single event class, whereas the psychiatric technician task requires per-patient status assessment, behavioral judgment and detection of physical ailments.

sources.system: Autonomous navigating fall-detection patrol robot (Vigorous Mind, NIA SBIR R43AG082599)
sources.title: Robots in Nursing Homes: Helping Nurses Detect and Prevent Falls
sources.claim: An NIA-funded feasibility study deployed an autonomously navigating robot with an infrared camera and machine-learning software to patrol nursing home resident rooms on evening and night shifts and ... staff, who then assess the situation themselves through the robot's camera.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic patrol of resident rooms with automatic alerting. It is a feasibility study limited to fall/fall-risk detection, and the clinical evaluation is explicitly handed back to human staff, so it does not substantiate completing the monitoring-and-reporting task.

sources.developer: Foxconn (Hon Hai) with Kawasaki Heavy Industries and NVIDIA
sources.title: AI Robotics, Digital Twins, and MONAI Contributions Highlight Hon Hai Foxconn's Smart Healthcare Vision at GTC Taipei 2025
sources.claim: Foxconn's Nurabot, an AI nursing robot piloted at Taichung Veterans General Hospital, performs ward patrols, medication delivery, specimen transport and patient education — logistics and guidance rather than clinical assessment of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital-ward work by a nursing-support robot. It shows that deployed autonomous ward robots handle logistics, patrols and education, not observation and clinical reporting of patients' physical and emotional status.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensing)
sources.developer: MIT and Brigham and Women's Hospital
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring - PMC
sources.claim: Contactless robotic measurement of patients' vital signs at Brigham and Women's Hospital used a teleoperated Boston Dynamics Spot ('Dr. Spot') driven by a human operator in a COVID triage tent.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assessment of a patient's physical status. Because operation is teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous monitoring of physical ailments.

sources.title: 'Patient-minding robots' at some PRMC bedsides | hccommunityjournal.com
sources.claim: Continuous in-hospital patient observation marketed as a 'telesitter robot' is in fact a camera unit in the room watched in real time by a human staff member monitoring multiple rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: continuous observation of at-risk patients. The observation and judgment are performed by a remote human, so it cannot support an autonomous-completion judgment for constant-observation instances.

tasks.label: Take and record measures of patients' physical condition, using devices such as thermometers or blood pressure gauges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled shift vitals on a locked inpatient psychiatric unit: ambulatory, cooperative patients come to the vitals cart or med-window station; tech takes temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure (and often SpO2) and charts them in the EHR.

Admission/intake vitals in the assessment or admissions area: newly admitted patient, anxious but cooperative; full vital signs plus height and weight, recorded on the admission assessment and flagged if abnormal.

Protocol vitals tied to medication at the med window on a cooperative patient (BP/pulse before clozapine, lithium or antihypertensive doses; scheduled detox-protocol vitals; monthly metabolic weights); must be obtained and charted before the dose and reported to the nurse if out of range.

Bedside recheck on a sedated, frail, geriatric or medically compromised psychiatric patient: post-PRN-injection vitals on a patient lying in bed, orthostatic lying/sitting/standing BP series, or recheck of an abnormal reading; tech positions the patient, times the readings and guards against dizziness/falls.

Vitals on an agitated, paranoid, refusing or restrained/secluded patient: requires de-escalation and coaxing, timing attempts to the patient's tolerance, safe body positioning, sometimes q15-minute checks through a restraint or seclusion episode, with documented refusals and repeat attempts.

Community or residential setting: group home, residential treatment house, day program or the client's own residence; tech carries a portable cuff and thermometer and takes vitals wherever the client is sitting, on furniture and in lighting taken as found, then records on a paper flow sheet or tablet.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy ... carries out the whole venipuncture sequence on a patient's presented arm without a human operator, including autonomously applying the tourniquet (an inflatable band on the upper arm) and inserting the needle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture. It is performed on the same body site (upper arm/antecubital fossa) as a blood-pressure cuff, requires autonomously locating the limb, applying an inflatable band and making a far more precise contact than seating a cuff or aiming a thermometer, on a seated patient who presents an arm to a fixed station.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: In routine clinical use at three Dutch hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments the robot achieved a 94.5% first-stick success rate over 1633 patients, comparable to human phlebotomists, with 0.6% mild adverse events.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture at a fixed clinical station. Worker-quality reliability on a presented arm establishes that a machine station can obtain a physical measurement/sample from a cooperative patient at rates an employer accepts.

sources.title: Alviscan – Measurements
sources.claim: The Alviscan self-measurement kiosk, a CE-marked medical system installed in hospital outpatient clinics (Erasmus MC, UMC Groningen, Deventer Hospital, Jeroen Bosch Hospital, Ostseeklinik Damp), automatically measures blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation, weight, height and contactless infrared temperature once the patient sits and places an arm in the device.

sources.title: Alviscan - Self measurement kiosk for vital signs
sources.claim: Measurements taken at the Alviscan station are written straight into the electronic health record without a clinician transcribing them, covering the recording half of the task; clinics report it handles roughly 80% of their outpatients.

sources.title: Collaborative study identifies method to make blood pressure monitoring more accessible (Emory News)
sources.claim: Automated self-service blood pressure/pulse/weight stations are deployed at scale in the US: a JAMA Cardiology analysis covered nearly 1.3 million adult users ... Pursuant Health kiosks in Walmart and CVS stores between 2017 and 2024.

sources.developer: Alexandra Hospital / National University Health System, Singapore
sources.title: An Assessment of an Inpatient Robotic Nurse Assistant: A Mixed-Method Study (Journal of Medical Systems)
sources.claim: Florence, a humanoid robotic nurse assistant trialled in a general medicine ward, autonomously navigated the ward and offered vital-signs measurement via an extending platform, but most patients could not complete the measurement; it was a one-time trial, not a working deployment.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot contactless vital sign monitoring platform
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring (PMC)
sources.claim: The mobile robot used at Brigham and Women's Hospital to take skin temperature, respiratory rate and ... from patients in a triage setting was driven by clinical staff rather than operating autonomously, and made no contact measurements such as cuff blood pressure.

tasks.label: Observe and influence patients' behavior, communicating and interacting with them and teaching, counseling, or befriending them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Aid patients in performing tasks, such as bathing or keeping beds, clothing, or living areas clean.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hands-on bathing/showering of a dependent patient on a state hospital geriatric-psych or intellectual-disability unit: escort the patient to the shower room, undress, transfer to shower chair, wash body and hair, rinse, dry, apply lotion, dress, and observe skin and behavior throughout; patient may be resistive or confused.

Prompting and supervising a semi-independent acute-unit patient through a hygiene routine: waking/encouraging a withdrawn or agitated patient, issuing towel, soap, shampoo and a razor under accountability, coaching step by step through showering, shaving and dressing, checking the result, and monitoring safety in the bathroom.

Bed care in a patient room: strip used sheets, pillowcase and blanket (sometimes soiled with urine or food), carry them to the soiled-linen hamper, and remake the bed with fresh hospital linens to unit standard, often while prompting the patient to help.

Personal laundry help in the unit laundry room: gather the patient's dirty clothing, sort and load the washer, transfer to the dryer, fold the clothes, and return them to the patient's locker or wardrobe, with the patient encouraged to participate.

Tidying a patient's room or living area: picking up clothing, papers, food trays and trash from the floor and bed, wiping the bedside table and sink, organizing personal belongings into the locker, emptying the trash, and checking for hazards or contraband as the room is cleared.

Prompt cleanup of a mess in the living area or patient bathroom: spilled food/drink, urine or vomit on the floor or fixtures, plus routine wiping and mopping of shower, toilet and dayroom floor surfaces to keep the area sanitary during the shift.

sources.system: Figure 03 humanoids with Helix-02 VLA policy
sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Two Figure humanoids running a single learned vision-language-action policy autonomously reset a bedroom, including hanging clothes, taking out trash, and cooperatively making a bed by unfurling, spreading and smoothing a comforter.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the physical content of bed-making and living-area tidying in the task (bedding manipulation, clothing, trash), though performed in a curated demo bedroom rather than an occupied patient room.

sources.system: π0 generalist policy on bimanual/mobile manipulators
sources.title: π0: Our First Generalist Policy
sources.claim: A generalist policy autonomously unloads a dryer, carries clothing to a table and folds mixed garments into a stack in an uncut single-policy run.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects and precision as the laundry portion of the task (unloading a dryer and folding a patient's clothing); demonstrated at a fixed folding station rather than in a facility laundry room.

sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator running the π0.5 policy autonomously cleans kitchens and bedrooms in homes not seen in training, performing multi-step chores such as putting clothes in a laundry basket ... dishes in the sink, with partial success rates.
sources.transferJustification: Room tidying with clutter (clothing, dishes, trash) is the same physical work as clearing a patient's living area; it is a research evaluation, not a worker-quality deployment.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous bathroom-cleaning robots that clean fixtures and floors and pick up trash are commercially deployed in hospitals and airports with near-zero staff intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Cleaning toilets, fixtures, floors and picking up trash in an occupied hospital restroom is the same physical work as keeping a psychiatric unit's bathroom and living-area surfaces sanitary.

sources.title: Avidbots Partners with HHS to Deploy Neo Floor-Scrubbing Robots in US Hospitals
sources.claim: Fully autonomous floor-scrubbing robots are deployed ... scale in US acute care hospitals for daily floor cleaning.
sources.transferJustification: Mopping/scrubbing floors of an occupied healthcare facility is the floor-cleaning component of keeping patient living areas clean.

sources.system: Bed-making system on Toyota HSR / Fetch
sources.title: Deep Transfer Learning of Pick Points on Fabric for Robot Bed-Making
sources.claim: Mobile manipulators (Toyota HSR and Fetch) autonomously smoothed and stretched a blanket over a bed, reaching 92% blanket coverage versus 95% for human supervisors, on a quarter-scale twin bed in the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Same deformable-bedding manipulation as bed making in the task, but on a reduced-scale bed testbed in a lab, so it supports only a highly structured setting.

sources.title: Poseidon | Robotdalen
sources.claim: A commercial hygiene 'robotic shower' cabin that washes and dries a seated user was pilot-installed in nursing homes in five Swedish municipalities; it supports users who can shower themselves and does not undress, transfer, or dress the person.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing product to assisted bathing; cited to show that even in a purpose-built shower cabin the machine covers only washing/drying of a self-transferring user, not the whole hands-on bathing instance.

sources.title: Peanut Robotics | Home
sources.claim: A commercially deployed mobile manipulator autonomously navigates and cleans hotel and commercial building rooms and bathrooms around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Wiping fixtures and surfaces in a guest room/bathroom of a managed facility is the same physical cleaning work as keeping a patient's bathroom and living-area surfaces clean.

tasks.label: Collaborate with or assist doctors, psychologists, or rehabilitation therapists in working with patients with cognitive, intellectual, or developmental disabilities to treat, rehabilitate, and return patients to the community.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult unit of a state psychiatric hospital or ICF/IID: the technician carries out the psychologist's written behavior support plan for a client with intellectual disability across a shift — verbal and physical prompting through routines, redirection, reinforcement, blocking self-injury or aggression, and recording behavior data the psychologist uses to revise the plan.

Assisting an OT/PT/recreation therapist during a scheduled rehabilitation session: escorting or transferring the patient to the therapy room, setting up equipment, providing hands-on physical support and cueing while the patient practices mobility or ADL skills (dressing, grooming, cooking in a training kitchen), then reporting performance back to the therapist.

Co-facilitating a skills group (social skills, independent-living, psychoeducation) with a psychologist or activity therapist in the dayroom: preparing materials, keeping 6-10 participants of varying cognitive levels engaged, giving one-on-one prompts, and defusing disruptive behavior so the clinician can run the curriculum.

Interdisciplinary treatment-team rounds and discharge planning inside the facility: presenting the week's observations on a patient with cognitive/developmental disability to the psychiatrist and psychologist, receiving revised assignments, and coordinating with the case manager on community placement steps.

Community reintegration outing off grounds: accompanying one or two patients on a bus ride, store trip, or visit to a prospective group home, coaching in-situ skills (money handling, ordering, crossing streets), managing safety and behavior in public, and debriefing the treatment team afterward.

sources.developer: DREAM consortium (EU FP7), incl. Univ. of Skövde, Plymouth, Babes-Bolyai
sources.title: About the DREAM Project
sources.claim: Robot-enhanced therapy for children with ASD (DREAM project, NAO robot) runs in clinic rooms with the robot autonomous only for limited periods and always under a therapist's supervision; the human clinician remains present and in control of the session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot delivering structured therapy trials to a child with a developmental disability alongside a clinician. It is the closest analogue to a psychiatric technician assisting a psychologist, but it covers only scripted one-to-one interaction protocols with a supervising therapist present, not the technician's whole role (physical assistance, safety management, group and community work).

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Therapy Beneficial for Children With Autism - Psychiatry Advisor
sources.claim: Randomized trials of in-clinic robot-assisted therapy for young children with autism found outcomes equivalent to conventional therapy with greater engagement; the robot is a therapy delivery aid inside a clinic, used within clinician-run treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated developmental-skills training. Shows the state of the art for robots working with patients who have developmental disabilities is a scripted clinic protocol with a supervising clinician, not substitution for a technician's hands-on, judgment-driven support.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest commercial deployment of mobile manipulation robots in US hospitals (Moxi, 25+ facilities) performs supply, medication and lab-sample deliveries; its purpose is to free nurses for patient care, and it does not perform patient-facing therapeutic or hands-on care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile work inside a healthcare institution. Establishes the ceiling of deployed hospital robotics — logistics in corridors — and that no deployed hospital robot handles patients or assists clinicians during treatment sessions.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: General-purpose humanoids intended for personal assistance still depend on remote human operators for complex tasks, so they cannot substitute for a care worker's hands-on assistance autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general in-person personal assistance. Shows the most capable humanoid aimed at helping people in living spaces operates by teleoperation, so it cannot support positive judgments about autonomous patient assistance.

sources.title: Obi 3 Robotic Feeding Device – Adaptive Mealtime Independence
sources.claim: Commercially available assistive robots for people with disabilities, such as the Obi feeding device, are single-function appliances operated by the user via switches rather than autonomous caregivers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical assistance with an ADL for a disabled person. Comparable population and setting, but the device is user-triggered and covers one narrow motion, so it does not transfer to a technician's hands-on rehabilitation support.
