tasks.label: Escort patients to medical appointments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-campus escort of an ambulatory, cooperative psychiatric inpatient from a locked unit to an on-site medical/dental/lab appointment: badge through locked doors, walk corridors and elevators, keep the patient in line-of-sight, wait through the appointment, hand off to and receive from clinic staff, return the patient to the unit and document.

Escort of a high-risk patient (agitated, paranoid, assaultive, suicidal, or forensic/elopement risk), often with a second staff member and sometimes restraints per policy: continuous behavioral observation, verbal de-escalation, blocking exits, and hands-on physical intervention if the patient bolts or strikes out.

Off-site appointment: accompanying the patient in a facility van or medical transport to an outside clinic or ER, through parking lots, public sidewalks, unfamiliar waiting rooms and exam rooms, maintaining custody and supervision throughout, relaying clinical information to outside staff, and returning the patient to the facility.

Escort of a patient with mobility limits (unsteady gait, geriatric or medically ill psychiatric patient): assist with sit-to-stand and wheelchair transfer, position and secure the patient, push the chair or provide gait-belt support through the building, guard against falls, and reverse the process on return.

Escort of a confused, cognitively impaired, or intellectually disabled patient within the facility: repeated verbal cueing and redirection, reassurance about the upcoming procedure, preventing wandering into other units, and coaxing a reluctant patient into the exam room.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Model (Unifi/Delta service at Detroit Metro Airport)
sources.title: Unifi Launches WHILL Autonomous Service at Detroit Airport
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchairs carry passengers along pre-mapped routes to airport gates and return to base by themselves, but serve only passengers who can stand and ... on their own; anyone needing hands-on help still receives a human attendant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a seated person across a large institutional building to a destination. It is the closest deployed analogue to wheeling a patient to an appointment, but it excludes transfer assistance and any supervision of the person, which the psychiatric escort instances require.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous mobile manipulation robot, is deployed in more than 25 ... doing item deliveries (medications, lab samples, supplies) alongside people; it moves goods, not patients, and has no patient-supervision role.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point transport inside a hospital, the navigation half of an escort. It shows hospital-grade autonomous navigation exists, but the payload is carts and supplies, with no responsibility for a human being's safety or behavior.

sources.title: Celebrating 50,000 Robot Deliveries at Upstate!
sources.claim: Aethon TUG fleets navigate hospital corridors autonomously, calling elevators and opening automatic doors, delivering supplies, meals and specimens while avoiding patients and visitors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: traversing the same corridors, doors and elevators an escort walks. Establishes route-following in the hospital environment for cargo, but nothing about accompanying, monitoring, or physically managing a psychiatric patient transfers from it.

sources.developer: Tokyo Women's Medical University research group (Masamune et al.)
sources.title: Exploring the potential of service robots in guiding patients and assisting mobility in medical facilities (Advanced Robotics 38:24)
sources.claim: A pilot study used a mobile service robot to lead outpatients from a clinic to their testing locations; it remains a research pilot with cooperative outpatients and the degree of autonomy is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: leading a patient to an appointment location inside a medical facility. It is a pilot with cooperative outpatients and no custodial or clinical-supervision function, so it does not substantiate escorting a psychiatric inpatient.

sources.developer: CT Asia Robotics (at Charoenkrung Pracharak Hospital)
sources.title: Streamlined patient flows with robots at Charoenkrung Pracharak Hospital
sources.claim: Hospital service robots deployed for patient flow (Dinsaw Intelligent OPD, Bangkok) register patients and verbally direct them to the correct department rather than physically accompanying them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: getting a patient to the right place in a hospital. Shows the deployed capability is information-giving and wayfinding, not accompanying a patient under supervision, so it does not carry over to a psychiatric escort.

tasks.label: Administer oral medications or hypodermic injections, following physician's prescriptions and hospital procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled oral medication pass on an inpatient psychiatric unit: technician works the med room window, checks the MAR against the physician's order, verifies each patient's identity (wristband/photo), pops unit-dose packets into a cup, gives water, watches the patient swallow and does a mouth check for cheeking, answers questions about side effects, and documents; 15-30 patients in a 45-minute window.

Oral medication given to a reluctant, disorganized, paranoid or refusing patient: repeated approaches and persuasion, checking for hoarding/cheeking, crushing tablets into applesauce where permitted, deciding when to hold and notify the nurse/physician, in a state hospital or acute psychiatric unit.

Medication administration/supervision in a community residential setting (group home, board-and-care, supported housing or client visit): meds kept in a lock box or blister packs, client seated at a kitchen table or in a bedroom, technician sets out the dose, observes ingestion, and records it; layout and clutter differ house to house.

Scheduled hypodermic injection to a cooperative patient in a treatment/exam room: long-acting injectable antipsychotic (e.g., haloperidol decanoate, paliperidone palmitate) or routine insulin/B12; verify order and patient, reconstitute or draw up from vial/prefilled kit, select and prep deltoid or ventrogluteal site, inject IM, withdraw, apply pressure, observe for reaction, document.

Emergency/PRN intramuscular injection to an acutely agitated, combative or involuntarily treated patient: given with a team hold or in restraints in a seclusion room or day room, rapid drug preparation, gluteal or deltoid injection through resistance, immediate post-injection monitoring.

sources.title: Vitestro Unveils Aletta™: The World's First Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™ (ARPD™)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a CE-marked, commercially launched autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that performs the whole blood draw (tourniquet, skin prep, AI-ultrasound vein finding, needle insertion, tube filling, withdrawal) on a seated patient whose arm is positioned in the device, with one human supervisor overseeing two devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture. It transfers partially to hypodermic injection because it is autonomous, clinically validated percutaneous needle placement into a live human at a fixed station where the patient's arm is presented to the machine — the same patient-contact precision and needle-handling demands as an IM/SC injection, and a harder target (a vein). It does not cover drug preparation from a vial or site selection on the gluteus.

sources.title: Vitestro launches new website and first public video of Aletta® Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device™
sources.claim: Aletta is CE marked and available for clinical use in ... (not FDA cleared), i.e., in routine clinical rather than laboratory-demo use.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous venipuncture); cited to establish deployment maturity of the needle-placement capability.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection | Waterloo News
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed what is reported as the first autonomous robotic intramuscular ... a needle-free injector on a person's arm with no healthcare professional involved; it was a one-off lab demonstration, not a validated clinical product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vaccine intramuscular administration. Direct analogue of the deltoid injection step of this task (same body site, same delivery direction), though delivery is needle-free jet injection of a low-viscosity vaccine, not a viscous depot antipsychotic drawn from a vial.

sources.title: China releases its first autonomous intelligent robot for needle-free vaccine injection - Global Times
sources.claim: Tongji University's Houyi robot autonomously locates the injection site on a person's body with 3D model recognition and delivers a needle-free jet injection; presented as a research prototype for clinics and mobile vaccination vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vaccine injection. Corroborates autonomous site selection and delivery of an injectate to a human body, the physical core of administering a hypodermic injection at a purpose-built station.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator (30+ US hospitals, 1M+ deliveries), autonomously transports medications through hospital corridors to nursing units and 'meds to beds' programs — the handoff and actual administration to the patient remain with clinical staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital medication logistics. Cited to delimit the state of the art in structured hospital settings: deployed hospital robots move medication to staff but no cited system identifies a patient, gives a dose and verifies ingestion.

tasks.label: Issue medications from dispensary and maintain records in accordance with specified procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled oral medication pass on a locked inpatient psychiatric unit: the technician unlocks the medication room/cart, pulls each patient's unit-dose packages against the MAR, calls patients to the med window one at a time, verifies identity (armband/photo), hands over the cup and water, observes swallowing and performs a mouth check for cheeking, then documents administration or refusal in the eMAR and reports refusals/side effects to the nurse.

PRN / as-needed issuance during the shift: an agitated or distressed patient requests (or is judged to need) a PRN anxiolytic, analgesic or sleep medication; the technician checks the order and last-dose time with the nurse, retrieves the dose from the dispensary, gives it, then documents indication, time and the patient's response.

Doses needing preparation or non-standard handling: crushing or splitting tablets, mixing with applesauce, measuring liquid concentrates, eye/ear drops or topicals, and coaxing patients who are suspicious, disorganized, or have swallowing difficulty into taking the dose, with corresponding documentation.

Injectable medications under RN/physician direction: drawing up or checking a long-acting injectable antipsychotic or PRN IM, positioning the patient (sometimes with staff assistance during an emergency), giving the injection, disposing of the sharp, and documenting site, lot and any wastage of controlled drug.

Dispensary stock and record work: checking in the pharmacy delivery, restocking the medication cart/cabinet with patient-specific unit doses, shift-change controlled-substance counts with a second signature, checking expiration dates, logging destruction/wastage, and reconciling inventory against the MAR.

Community/residential issuance to a stable client (group home, residential treatment, day program, clinic dispensary window): giving out pre-packaged or pre-poured scheduled doses to a cooperative, largely self-administering client at the appointed time, prompting them, and logging that the dose was taken and reporting missed doses to the program.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Pharmacy Robot Increases Safety, Efficiency | Owensboro Health
sources.claim: Omnicell's XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System is an installed hospital pharmacy robot that autonomously scans, sorts, picks, bags, seals and labels patient medications inside its own enclosure, with barcode-based tracking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: central-pharmacy dose fulfilment. It covers the dispensary side of this task (picking the right drug/dose per patient order and keeping an auditable record) with the same objects (unit-dose oral solids), but the work is brought to the machine's enclosure, and the machine never faces the patient.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Launches PillPick Octave, Advancing Medication Safety
sources.claim: Swisslog's PillPick automated unit-dose system packages, barcodes, stores and dispenses patient-specific unit doses with full traceability; the current Octave model was commercially launched in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated unit-dose packaging, storage and dispensing. Same medication objects and the same record/traceability requirement as the dispensary portion of this task, performed inside a purpose-built machine rather than in a human medication room.

sources.system: ZING robotic methadone dose assembly system (with Netalytics Methasoft)
sources.title: First-Ever Robotic Methadone Dose Assembly System Undergoes Beta Testing
sources.claim: The ZING robotic methadone dose assembly system prepares, caps and labels patient-specific liquid doses in an opioid treatment program dispensary, with the Methasoft EMR driving the robot and maintaining all inventory tracking and record keeping; nurses still verify and hand doses directly to patients as federal law requires.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point for the dispensary-preparation and record-keeping half of the task in a behavioral-health clinic, but the source itself states nurses must verify and dispense the dose to the patient, so the patient-facing half is not covered.

sources.system: ZING robotic methadone dosing assembly system
sources.title: Comprehensive Healthcare implements ZING® robot for methadone dosing
sources.claim: A behavioral health provider implemented the ZING robot in its Yakima opioid treatment program dispensary in 2026, where it pours, seals and labels methadone doses about five times faster than nurses did by hand while nurses hand doses to clients at the dosing window.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic dose assembly at a behavioral-health dispensary. Confirms real-world deployment of dispensary automation in exactly the kind of facility a psychiatric technician works in, while the client handoff remains a nurse task.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators have completed over 300,000 autonomous pharmacy deliveries inside hospitals, including controlled substances with maintained chain of custody, navigating corridors and elevators without infrastructure changes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secure medication transport within a hospital. It shows autonomous handling of controlled medication with chain-of-custody records in a human facility, but it is explicitly non-patient-facing and does not issue doses to patients or chart administration.

sources.title: Evondos improves independent living at home for seniors across the Nordics - Verdane
sources.claim: Evondos supplies an automated medicine-dispensing robot used by professional home-care organisations across the Nordics and the Netherlands, serving tens ...; it releases the client's pre-packaged doses on the prescribed schedule and reports back to nurses whether the medication was taken on time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled medication issuance to a client with automatic adherence recording, replacing home-care staff medication visits. Same objects (pre-packaged oral doses) and same record purpose as the community medication run, in unstructured home settings.

sources.title: Reasons for Enrolling in Safer Supply Programs: A Longitudinal Qualitative Study on Participant Goals and Related Outcomes in the MySafe Program (Journal of Studies on Alcohol and Drugs)
sources.claim: The MySafe program dispenses prescription hydromorphone tablets to enrolled participants from biometric dispensing machines sited in supportive housing buildings and an overdose prevention site, with participants accessing doses without staff interaction and the machine recording each dispense.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: identity-verified issuance of a controlled medication to a client with automatic logging. Closest existing analogue to a med window, but dosing is explicitly witness-free, so it does not cover observed ingestion, refusal handling, or clinical assessment.
