roles.title: Surgical Technologists
aliases: OR Surgical Tech (Operating Room Surgical Technician)
OR Surgical Technologist (Operating Room Surgical Technologist)
Travel OR Tech (Travel Operating Room Technician)
roles.description: Assist in operations, under the supervision of surgeons, registered nurses, or other surgical personnel. May help set up operating room, prepare and transport patients for surgery, adjust lights and equipment, pass instruments and other supplies to surgeons and surgeons' assistants, hold retractors, cut sutures, and help count sponges, needles, supplies, and instruments.

tasks.label: Maintain a proper sterile field during surgical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine general/GI case in a hospital OR (lap chole, hernia, appendectomy): the scrub tech gowns and gloves the team, drapes the prepped patient, establishes and guards the back table and Mayo stand, secures cords/suction/light handles, watches team members and room traffic for breaks in technique, and isolates and replaces contaminated items throughout the case.

High-volume ambulatory surgery center: short cases (cataract, arthroscopy, ENT) with rapid turnover; small, tightly defined sterile fields re-established many times a day, sterile supplies opened onto the field by a circulator, constant guarding against splash/strike-through and dropped items.

Orthopedic/spine implant case: draping the C-arm/microscope and the extremity, keeping multiple implant trays, power tools and irrigation sterile under laminar flow, managing heavy traffic of reps and staff, and correcting contamination (glove punctures, drape tears) over hours-long exposure.

Robotic-assisted or laparoscopic case: applying sterile drapes to robot arms, camera and monitors, maintaining sterility through docking and undocking of moving arms, scope and instrument exchanges, and keeping cords and the sterile boundary intact while the console surgeon works remotely.

Emergency/trauma or urgent cesarean: sterile field established under time pressure in a crowded room, gross contamination and heavy blood, patient movement and rapid conversion of the setup, with the tech continuously judging and restoring asepsis on the fly.

Long complex case (cardiac, transplant, craniotomy): multiple back tables, perfusion and device lines crossing the boundary, staff relief and handoff of the sterile field over many hours, re-draping and re-gowning as needed.

sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.claim: TUM research robotic scrub nurse autonomously anticipates and delivers laparoscopic instruments from real-time video; a research prototype limited to instrument handover, not draping, gowning, or sterile-field surveillance and correction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passing instruments as a scrub nurse. Cited as the closest existing capability; it covers only instrument prediction and handover and does not establish, monitor, or restore the sterile field itself.

sources.developer: Academic authors (Li et al., arXiv preprint)
sources.title: RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model
sources.claim: RoboNurse-VLA performs voice-commanded grasping and handover of surgical ... a laboratory setup; it does no draping, contamination detection, or sterile-boundary maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument passing. Shows benchtop autonomous manipulation of surgical instruments, but nothing about establishing or policing a sterile field around a live patient.

sources.title: Enhancing surgical efficiency with an automated scrub nurse robot: a focus on automatic instrument insertion
sources.claim: Third-generation automated scrub nurse robot with automatic instrument insertion targets smoother instrument exchange; an engineering study of exchange efficiency, not of sterile-field maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument exchange in the OR. Demonstrates automated instrument handling, but the robot does not drape, gown, monitor asepsis, or remove contaminated items.

sources.title: Initial clinical experience with a partly autonomous robotic surgical instrument server
sources.claim: Penelope Surgical Instrument Server, used in a live operating room, delivers instruments on command and retrieves them with machine vision; human scrub personnel still established and maintained the sterile field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument passing in a clinical OR. The only in-OR robotic scrub assistant with clinical experience; its scope is instrument delivery and retrieval, not sterile-field establishment, surveillance, or correction.

sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Yip lab)
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid robots performing surgical tasks in vivo operate under teleoperation, indicating no autonomous humanoid capability for OR sterile-field work as of mid-2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid manipulation of surgical instruments in the OR. Establishes that current humanoid OR capability is teleoperated, so it cannot substantiate autonomous sterile-field maintenance.

tasks.label: Count sponges, needles, and instruments before and after operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial (baseline) count in a hospital OR before incision: the scrub tech, gowned at the sterile back table, separates and counts packaged raytec and lap sponges in bundles of 5/10, counts suture needles and blades, and counts every instrument on a standard tray against the printed count sheet, calling each aloud concurrently with the circulating RN, who records the totals on the count board.

Closing/final count during wound closure in a general/OB-GYN/urology case: soiled, blood-soaked sponges retrieved from the field, kick bucket and hanging counter bag are separated and counted; used bloody instruments returned in disarray to the Mayo stand and back table are re-counted; needles are counted on the magnetic counter pad; result must be reconciled and reported aloud to the surgeon within minutes.

Counts of items added mid-procedure (extra sponge packs, additional sutures, an opened loaner tray) and relief/shift-change counts performed with the wound open, instruments in active use on the field and sponges inside the patient's cavity.

High-volume instrument counts in orthopedic/spine/trauma cases: multiple 100-300 piece trays and loaner sets counted before the case and again at close, with many near-identical implants, screws, drills and caddies verified item-by-item against count sheets.

Emergent/trauma cases and count-discrepancy events: abbreviated or waived initial counts in a crowded, fast-moving room, or a final count that does not reconcile, requiring a search of drapes, floor, kick buckets, trash and the wound, and an intraoperative X-ray with reconciliation and documentation.

sources.developer: Robotic Systems & Technologies, Inc. (Michael R. Treat)
sources.title: Robot offers an assist to sterile processing department | HFM Magazine
sources.claim: PenelopeCS, a robot piloted in the clean side of ... NY-Presbyterian/The Allen Hospital, received instruments from a conveyor loaded by a technician and autonomously scanned, identified, counted and segregated each instrument against the tray count sheet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verifying/counting surgical instruments against a count sheet in sterile processing rather than in the OR. Same objects (loop instruments, forceps), same output (item-by-item count reconciled to a printed list), in a conveyor-fed machine cell.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L + dual electromagnetic gripper)
sources.developer: University of Louisville (Sankaranarayanan, Chitalia et al.), ISMR 2026
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell (Staubli TX2-60L arm, calibrated camera, YOLO12 + ResNet perception) autonomously identifies each surgical instrument placed on a staging surface, checks it against a digital checklist of instruments required for the procedure, packs it into the sterile tray and discards items not on the list.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument-by-instrument recognition and verification against a required-instrument checklist, which is the perceptual and manipulation core of counting instruments against a count sheet; identical objects and precision, in a purpose-built robotic cell where items are presented singly.

sources.title: THOR I Robot Separator - Single Piece Separation of Laundry
sources.claim: THOR is a commercial robotic separator installed on the soiled side of industrial laundries that autonomously picks and singulates soiled garments, towels and flat linen one piece at a time from bulk using 3D cameras, at 1,200-1,500 pieces per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating soiled textile items one at a time from a bulk pile and passing each individually for identification. This is the physical core of counting sponges (separating each soiled cloth item so it can be individually accounted for); comparable deformable, blood/soil-contaminated fabric handled in a conveyor-fed machine environment.

sources.system: THOR robotic separator with HEIMDAL camera/RFID identification and ODIN X-ray scanner
sources.title: Smart automation for every laundry size - Laundry & Cleaning Today
sources.claim: Deployed Inwatec/JENSEN soil-side installations (over 170 worldwide; e.g. bardusch Yverdon, Switzerland) autonomously separate bulk-fed laundry into individual items and scan, check and sort roughly 9,000 healthcare garments per day, a job previously done by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-by-item separation, identification and tallying of soiled healthcare textiles at production reliability, including automatic detection of foreign objects such as needles. Transfers to counting soiled sponges when the items are brought to the machine on a conveyor.

sources.system: ReSkin tactile cloth-layer singulation (Franka Panda arm)
sources.developer: CMU / UC Berkeley (Tirumala, Weng, Seita, Held et al.), IROS 2022
sources.title: Learning to Singulate Layers of Cloth using Tactile Feedback (arXiv:2207.11196)
sources.claim: A Franka robot arm with a ReSkin tactile fingertip autonomously grasps a specified number of cloth layers from a stack, using a learned tactile classifier to separate exactly one layer over 180 physical trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: separating exactly one layer of fabric from a stack. Counting sponges requires precisely this action — peeling apart folded/stacked gauze so each piece is separated and seen once; comparable deformable objects and single-item precision, in a fixed lab workcell.

tasks.label: Hand instruments and supplies to surgeons and surgeons' assistants, hold retractors and cut sutures, and perform other tasks as directed by surgeon during operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scrubbed on a laparoscopic/minimally invasive general surgery case (lap chole, appendectomy, hernia) in a hospital OR: passes trocars, graspers, energy devices and loaded needle drivers into the surgeon's hand on verbal or gestural cue, holds the scope or a liver retractor for stretches, cuts suture tails at closing, manages sponges/suction, tracks counts, adapts when bleeding or conversion changes the plan.

Scrubbed on an orthopedic case (total knee/hip, ORIF, arthroscopy): assembles and passes reamers, saws, drills and trial implants sized on the fly from very large trays, holds retractors on bone and soft tissue against heavy force, loads and cuts sutures at closure, works around C-arm and sterile draping changes.

Scrubbed on an open abdominal, vascular or thoracic case: sustained retractor holding for exposure, rapid successive passing of clamps, ties and suture-needle combinations during dissection and anastomosis, cutting suture tails to the surgeon's requested length, responding to unexpected bleeding at high tempo.

Scrubbed on an OB/GYN case (cesarean section, hysterectomy) including urgent/emergent C-sections: fast-paced passing of scalpel, retractors, clamps and sutures, holding a bladder blade or Richardson retractor, cutting sutures, handling neonate hand-off equipment, all under time pressure.

Scrubbed on a short, standardized ambulatory surgery center procedure (cataract, ENT/tonsillectomy, hand or podiatric case, minor excision): small standard instrument set, a handful of instrument passes on request, brief retraction, cutting suture tails at closure, plus counts, with several cases turned over per day.

Scrubbed on a robotic-assisted (e.g., da Vinci) case: docks and undocks arms, exchanges robotic instruments at the cart on the surgeon's call, passes laparoscopic instruments and sutures to the bedside assistant through an assistant port, cuts suture, troubleshoots instrument faults mid-case.

sources.developer: Robotic Surgical Tech, Inc. (Michael R. Treat, Columbia/NewYork-Presbyterian)
sources.title: For the First Time, Newly Developed Robot Assists Doctors and Nurses in Operating Room | NYP
sources.claim: Penelope Surgical Instrument Server autonomously handed and retrieved instruments on voice request during a real minor operation (forearm lipoma excision) in a hospital OR in 2005 - the only clinical instance found of a robot performing part of the scrub role.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (passing instruments to the surgeon during an operation), but it covers only the instrument-handoff element of this task, in one simple case; it is the closest clinical evidence found.

sources.title: For the First Time, Newly Developed Robot Assists Doctors and Nurses in Operating Room | NYP
sources.claim: The same Penelope system was designed to have no contact with the patient, i.e. it did not hold retractors, cut sutures or otherwise act inside the wound.
sources.transferJustification: Bounds what the only clinically used scrub robot did: instrument service only, no retraction or suture cutting, which are explicit elements of this task.

sources.system: Robotic scrub nurse (RSN) with laparoscopic-video instrument anticipation
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / University Hospital rechts der Isar
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis - PubMed
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic scrub nurse research (TU Munich) anticipates and hands instruments in simulated surgery only, correctly anticipating about 72% of instruments in laparoscopic cholecystectomy.

sources.developer: Chinese University of Hong Kong (Ng, Ma, Heng, Chiu, Li)
sources.title: Large Language Model-Embedded Intelligent Robotic Scrub Nurse with Multimodal Input for Enhancing Surgeon-Robot Interaction
sources.claim: A recent LLM-embedded robotic scrub nurse demonstrated instrument transfer, sorting and counting only on a laboratory robotic platform, not on patients.

sources.developer: Kang et al., Advanced Intelligent Systems
sources.title: Vision-Based Handover and Organization of Robotic Scrub Nurse for Seamless Surgical Flow
sources.claim: Another 2026 robotic scrub nurse proof of concept reports handover works but is slower than human scrub nurses, i.e. below worker pace.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help - Johns Hopkins Malone Center for Engineering in Healthcare
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous in-wound surgical manipulation (dissection, clipping, cutting) was demonstrated only on ex vivo pig tissue in a laboratory, not on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Closest evidence for autonomous instrument work inside the wound (relevant to holding retractors/cutting sutures); it is preclinical lab work on ex vivo tissue, so it does not establish worker-quality performance of the assisting role on patients.

sources.title: FDA Clearance for "Follow Me" Image-Guided Software - MST Medical Surgery Technologies
sources.claim: Commercially cleared robotic assistance in the OR that substitutes for a human holding a scope is limited to image-guided laparoscope positioners that follow surgeon-tagged tools; they position a camera, not retractors, and do not pass instruments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: holding/positioning the scope for the surgeon, an assistant duty adjacent to 'hold retractors'. It is surgeon-directed camera positioning only and covers none of the passing, retraction or suture-cutting elements.

tasks.label: Scrub arms and hands and assist the surgical team to scrub and put on gloves, masks, and surgical clothing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-case self-prep: at the OR suite scrub sink the surgical technologist performs a surgical hand scrub/rub (nails, hands, forearms to elbows, per facility protocol and required contact time), enters the OR holding hands up, dries with a sterile towel, then dons sterile gown and dons gloves by closed-glove technique from the sterile back table without contaminating anything.

Gowning and gloving the surgeon and assistant as they come in from the sink: hand each a sterile towel, hold the folded sterile gown open at the shoulders with the cuffs protected, guide their arms into the sleeves, then hold each glove open wide for the surgeon to plunge the hand in and adjust the cuff over the gown knit — all while keeping the technologist's own gloves and the gown fronts sterile; the circulator fastens the back ties and the technologist passes the belt card.

Non-sterile pre-scrub assistance in the OR: helping team members and observers select and put on caps, masks, and eye protection, fitting lead aprons and thyroid shields, confirming glove size and latex sensitivity, and opening sterile gown and glove packages onto the sterile field for others.

Mid-procedure re-gowning/re-gloving: after a glove perforation, contamination, or a gown sleeve strike-through during an open case, quickly supplying and applying a fresh sterile glove or gown to the surgeon at the field, beside an open wound, without breaking the sterile field or delaying the operation.

Rapid or emergency case (trauma laparotomy, crash cesarean) or fast room turnover: an abbreviated alcohol-based hand rub, then gowning and gloving several team members in quick succession in a crowded, noisy, fast-moving room where people and equipment are constantly shifting.

sources.system: Baxter robot-assisted dressing system (Zhang & Demiris, Science Robotics)
sources.developer: Personal Robotics Laboratory, Imperial College London
sources.title: A robot that can put a surgical gown on a supine mannequin
sources.claim: The closest demonstrated autonomous capability to gowning a person is robot-assisted dressing: an Imperial College London system autonomously took a hospital gown off a hook and dressed a supine mannequin in a simulated hospital room, succeeding about 90% of the time over ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted patient dressing with a hospital gown. It is the nearest analogue to gowning a scrubbed team member (same class of deformable garment, human limbs), but it dresses a passive supine mannequin in a lab, involves no aseptic technique, no glove donning onto hands, no tying, and a ~10% failure rate — far below the near-zero contamination tolerance of surgical gowning.

sources.title: Bimanual Robot-Assisted Dressing: A Spherical Coordinate-Based Strategy for Tight-Fitting Garments
sources.claim: As of 2025 the robot-assisted dressing literature is still lab research on getting sleeves onto arms, with loose-fitting garments the main solved case and tight garments an open problem; no sterility or clinical constraints are addressed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting garments onto human arms. Establishes the state of the art for the manipulation skill underlying gowning and gloving; it remains a laboratory problem with no aseptic-technique or glove-donning capability.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid as endoscopic first assistant
sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Johns Hopkins Medical Institutions with NVIDIA
sources.title: Humanoid Robots as First Assistants in Endoscopic Surgery
sources.claim: The first reported instance of a humanoid robot assisting a surgeon during a procedure was fully teleoperated, indicating that humanoid assistance in the operating room is not autonomous as of 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid assistance to the surgical team in the OR. Shows that even the visualization-holding role, far simpler than sterile gowning and gloving, required continuous teleoperation.

sources.system: Humanoid robot surrogates for dexterous medical interventions
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Atar, Liang, Richter, Yip et al.)
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Robot Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: Humanoid robots performing direct clinical ... in hospital settings have been studied only under teleoperation, not autonomous execution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid robots performing bedside clinical manipulation tasks. Establishes that dexterous humanoid work on and around people in hospitals is teleoperated, so it cannot support autonomous completion of scrubbing/gowning.

sources.title: Automated Medical Hand Washing Stations for Healthcare | Meritech
sources.claim: Commercially deployed automated handwashing stations perform a machine-controlled 12-second hand wash and are installed at entry points to high-risk hospital areas, but they wash only the hands of a person who inserts them and do not perform a full surgical scrub of hands and forearms, drying, gowning, or gloving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hand hygiene. Covers only the washing sub-step of one instance, at general hand-hygiene rather than surgical-antisepsis standard (12 seconds, hands only), and the human still presents the hands, dries, gowns and gloves; it therefore cannot complete any whole instance.

tasks.label: Wash and sterilize equipment, using germicides and sterilizers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Point-of-use instrument care in the operating room during and at the end of ... case: wiping blood off instruments with sterile water, flushing suction tips and lumens, applying transport gel/moist towels, separating sharps and delicate scopes, closing transport containers and taking the case cart to decontamination.

Decontamination of a routine general-surgery set (stainless hemostats, retractors, scissors, basins) in the SPD decontamination room: gross-soil removal, pre-rinse, then cleaning and thermal disinfection through ultrasonic cleaner and washer-disinfector cycles with instruments opened and placed in wash racks.

Decontamination of complex, lumened or delicate devices at the three-bay sink: disassembly of multi-part instruments, brushing box locks, serrations and cannulas, syringe-flushing channels of powered drills, robotic-surgery arms and microsurgical instruments per each device's IFU, then rinsing and racking.

Running the batch machine-wash: moving loaded wash racks from the sink counter to an available washer-disinfector, loading it, selecting/starting the correct validated cycle, then unloading the completed rack on the clean side and delivering it to the prep-and-pack area.

Running the sterilization batch: placing wrapped/containerized sets on sterilizer loading racks or carts, loading the steam sterilizer, selecting and running the cycle with load documentation, then unloading, cooling and moving sterile loads to the sterile store or case-cart area.

Urgent and delicate work: immediate-use steam sterilization of a dropped or single-of-a-kind instrument mid-case (retrieve, clean at the sub-sterile sink, load the IUSS sterilizer, run, deliver to the sterile field), plus germicidal wipe-down or high-level disinfection of non-immersible equipment such as camera heads, light cords, cables and scopes.

sources.title: Bryan Health Uses New Robotic Technology to Clean and Sterilize Surgical Instruments
sources.claim: STERIS ATLAS Workflow Automation Vehicle ('Bella') has been in daily production use in Bryan Medical Center's sterile processing department, autonomously collecting racks of hand-cleaned instruments from the sink counter, loading them into washer-disinfectors and starting cleaning cycles, navigating around staff with laser/sonar guidance.

sources.title: Atlas Workflow Automation Vehicle for Washers | STERIS
sources.claim: The commercial ATLAS WAV system automates loading and unloading of washer-disinfectors, washer and cycle selection via barcode, queuing of loads, and delivery of washed racks onward to the prep-and-pack area inside hospital sterile processing departments.

sources.title: Getinge Automation System for Sterilizers (AGS) - Getinge
sources.claim: Getinge's Automation System (Air Glide System) for sterilizers is a commercial CSSD installation that automatically picks up sterilizer racks, loads them into whichever steam sterilizer is free, selects the program and documents the cycle without staff supervision.

sources.title: Getinge transforms sterile reprocessing with Automatiq - a full range of logistic automation modules
sources.claim: Getinge's Automatiq family (launched December 2025) provides a self-navigating mobile robot for moving instruments between CSSD workstations plus robotic loaders that load and unload the 8668 washer-disinfector and GSS67H steam ... under central software orchestration.

sources.system: Gibotech automated sterilization central (Rigshospitalet, Herlev, Køge)
sources.title: Automated Central Sterile Supply Department - Gibotech
sources.claim: Gibotech has installed robotic sterilization centrals in Danish hospitals (Køge 2011; Rigshospitalet and Herlev 2018) in which robots, mobile robots and conveyors handle the loading/unloading of washing and sterilizing plant and the sterile instrument store.

sources.title: R-APPIT - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: The R-APPIT packing robot autonomously wraps, tapes and labels filled instrument trays for steam sterilization in hospital reprocessing departments (installed for example at Jeroen Bosch Hospital), using an AI vision system to choose the packing method, taking over up to 90% of packing work.

sources.title: Getinge launches S-8668T Washer-Disinfector
sources.claim: Getinge's 86-series washer-disinfectors are commercial machines installed in Central Sterile Supply Departments that run validated automated cleaning and thermal disinfection cycles on racked surgical instruments.

sources.system: Automated washer/disinfectors in central processing departments
sources.title: Automated Washer/Sterilizers - Infection Control Today
sources.claim: Trade coverage of automated washer/disinfectors in central processing departments describes machine cleaning taking over work previously done at manual cleaning sinks and enabling automated loading and unloading functions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical cleaning of surgical instruments. It is the same objects (surgical instrument sets in wash racks) and the same accepted output (visibly clean, thermally disinfected instruments) as the decontamination instance judged here.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Stäubli TX2-60L)
sources.developer: University of Louisville / Saint Vincent's Hospital SPD
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A university laboratory system using a Stäubli TX2-60L arm with a dual electromagnetic gripper and top-down vision autonomously sorts and structurally packs surgical ...; a human technician still performs the inspection step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling of surgical instruments by a robot in sterile processing. Cited only to show the current state of robotic instrument manipulation (clean, unsoiled instruments, lab cell) does not extend to soiled-instrument brushing or disassembly.

sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: RIF Robotics piloted a robotic arm in the sterile processing department of Wellstar Windy Hill Hospital that autonomously assembled a minor surgical tray, with the technician still required to inspect instruments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of surgical instruments inside a hospital SPD. Cited to bound capability: even in a hospital pilot the robot handles clean instruments and inspection remains human.

tasks.label: Prepare patients for surgery, including positioning patients on the operating table and covering them with sterile surgical drapes to prevent exposure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR, routine supine general/laparoscopic case (cholecystectomy, hernia, appendectomy): help transfer the anesthetized or awake patient from stretcher to OR table, align on the table, place arms on armboards or tuck at sides with padding, apply safety strap and warming blanket, then after skin prep apply sterile drapes (fenestrated/laparotomy drape, side drapes, adhesive incise film) with the surgeon without breaking sterile technique.

Hospital OR or ortho ASC, extremity/orthopedic case (knee, shoulder, hand, ankle): position with limb holder, beach-chair attachment or traction boot, pad bony prominences, then hold/elevate the prepped limb, roll on stockinette, apply impervious U-drapes, extremity drape and Coban/Esmarch, plus drape the C-arm and image intensifier.

Hospital OR, non-supine positioning: prone spine on a Jackson/Wilson frame, lateral decubitus with bean bag, axillary roll and hip positioners, or lithotomy with candy-cane/Yellofin stirrups; requires coordinated team log-roll of an anesthetized patient, pressure-point and eye protection, securing tape/straps, then draping the surgical field.

Hospital OR, robotic-assisted case (da Vinci prostatectomy, hysterectomy, colorectal): position patient on anti-slip pad with shoulder/chest supports for steep Trendelenburg, arms tucked, confirm slide test, then apply drapes compatible with robot docking and port placement.

Ambulatory surgery center or procedure suite, minor/awake case (cataract, endoscopy, minor derm/plastics, pain injection): the patient walks in and positions themselves with verbal guidance and light assistance on a narrow table or chair; technologist adds head support/pillow, straps, then applies a small fenestrated or eye drape around the prepped site.

Emergency/urgent case (trauma laparotomy, crash cesarean, ruptured AAA): rapid positioning of an unstable or partially immobilized patient (spine precautions, lines, monitors, possible ongoing CPR) with a left lateral tilt or arms out, followed by fast wide sterile draping under severe time pressure and a changing team layout.

sources.system: Robot-assisted dressing system (garment manipulation policies, Imperial College / Science Robotics)
sources.developer: Imperial College London (Fan Zhang, Yiannis Demiris)
sources.title: A robot that can put a surgical gown on a supine mannequin
sources.claim: Closest analog found for robotic draping/covering of a person: a research system autonomously took a surgical gown from a hook and dressed a supine mannequin, succeeding about 90% of trials in a laboratory setting. It is not sterile draping of a live prepped patient and its error rate is far above OR sterile-technique standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = dressing a supine body with a fabric garment, the nearest published analog to covering a patient with drapes. It does NOT transfer: the trials use a rigid mannequin on a lab bed, a single gown type, no sterile field, and ~10% failure, whereas surgical draping requires sterile technique, multiple large drapes, adhesive placement around a prepped incision site, and near-zero contamination tolerance.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulators are deployed in US hospitals, but only for non-patient-facing logistics (medications, supplies, lab samples); no deployed hospital robot positions patients or handles sterile drapes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous mobile manipulation inside the same institution (hospital corridors, pharmacy). It establishes hospital-grade autonomous navigation and simple pick-and-place but does not transfer: Moxi never contacts patients, does not lift or position bodies, and does not manipulate sterile textiles.

sources.system: TS7000dV (TruSystem 7000dV) operating table with Integrated Table Motion for da Vinci Xi
sources.title: TS7000dV Operating Table | Hillrom
sources.claim: Commercially available 'robotic' OR tables move the tabletop with the patient already on it, under surgeon/anesthetist command during surgery; they do not transfer, arrange, pad or strap the patient, nor drape.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = powered patient repositioning on the OR table. Does not transfer: motion is commanded by a clinician, the patient must already be transferred, aligned, padded and secured by staff, and no drape handling is involved.

sources.system: Humanoid robots / embodied AI in the OR (perspective framework)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: As of July 2026 the state of the art for humanoid robots in the operating ... is a proposed staged framework starting with laboratory testing and low-risk, non-clinical perioperative tasks; no validated autonomous OR nursing/technologist role has been demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting (the OR) and adjacent roles (scrub/circulating nurse functions). Cited as a negative/context item: it documents intent and staged proposals rather than demonstrated capability, so it cannot support any positive tier judgment.

tasks.label: Prepare, care for, and dispose of tissue specimens taken for laboratory analysis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine single specimen in a hospital OR or ASC (gallbladder, appendix, uterus, tonsils, skin/soft-tissue excision): surgeon passes the specimen off the sterile field in a basin or on Telfa, the tech confirms the site/name verbally with the surgeon, places it in an appropriately sized container, formalin is added, the container is labeled with patient and specimen designation and passed to the circulator for the lab.

Fresh, unfixed specimen for frozen section or immediate pathology consult (breast lumpectomy margin, lymph node, thyroid): no fixative may be added, orientation sutures/inks must be preserved and reported, the specimen is kept moist and packaged and dispatched to pathology within minutes while the case waits.

Multiple specimens in a single case (nodal dissection, multi-level spine discs, multiple margins, staged excisions): each piece is kept separate, matched to the surgeon's verbal designation, placed in its own labeled container with fixative, and logged so that none are mixed up or lost.

Large or bulky specimen (colon or gastric resection, mastectomy, explanted joint prosthesis or hardware, amputated extremity, placenta): heavy, wet, floppy tissue requiring a large bucket or bag, careful lifting off the field, sometimes sent fresh, then labeled and moved out of the room.

Special-handling specimens: swabs and tissue for culture into transport media, fluid/cytology aspirates into tubes, stones, hardware, foreign bodies or bullets requiring chain-of-custody handling, or specimens sent for intraoperative radiography before packaging.

Care and disposal work around specimens: discarding excised tissue and body fluids that are not sent to the lab into biohazard containers, containing and disposing of formalin and contaminated packaging, and clearing the specimen area at case end.

sources.system: nToto / mini nToto automated grossing platform
sources.title: FormaPath demonstrate 'mini' nToto at CAP
sources.claim: FormaPath's nToto is an enclosed benchtop instrument that uses robotics and computer vision ... tissue biopsies out of specimen jars into the correct cassettes, validating identity at intake and generating the gross record; the first unit was in clinical validation at Mayo Clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pathology grossing intake. It is the downstream half of 'prepare a tissue specimen for laboratory analysis' — soft tissue of the same size and consistency is moved between labeled containers with identity verification, inside a purpose-built machine enclosure.

sources.title: WASP® FAQ - Copan Diagnostics
sources.claim: Copan's WASP is a walk-away clinical specimen processor deployed in hospital microbiology labs that automatically decaps and recaps specimen containers, reads and prints labels/barcodes, and processes swabs and liquid specimens without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-analytical clinical specimen processing. It covers the container-and-label half of specimen preparation — opening/closing specimen containers, handling swabs and fluids, and applying and verifying patient labels — with the same identity-error consequences.

sources.title: Soft Robotics Demonstrates mGripAI™ at Automate 2023
sources.claim: Soft Robotics' mGripAI combines 3D vision, AI and soft grippers to pick, orient and pack raw wet animal tissue (poultry pieces, sausages, beef) from unstructured bulk into trays and cases on commercial food production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk picking and packing of raw protein. Comparable objects (wet, slippery, deformable animal tissue in variable shapes) and comparable precision (grasp without tearing, orient, place into a container) to lifting a specimen into a specimen container.

sources.title: AMP Robotics Launches Automated Secondary Sortation Facilities in Atlanta and Cleveland
sources.claim: AMP Robotics' Cortex robotic sorting systems autonomously identify items on a conveyor and pick them into the correct stream/bin, with hundreds of installations across recycling facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: waste sorting. The disposal step is the same act — recognize presented material and place it into the correct waste container — performed at industrial reliability in a purpose-built picking cell.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed in US hospitals that transports laboratory specimens and supplies through corridors and elevators around the clock; its hospital work is fetch-and-deliver, not specimen preparation or packaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital specimen transport. Shows what is achievable at E2 inside a hospital (closed-tote transport) and that no deployed hospital robot opens, fills, labels or verifies specimen containers at the point of care.

sources.system: Commercial abattoir cutting/handling robots (Marel, Frontmatec, Scott)
sources.title: Robot Technology for Pork and Beef Meat Slaughtering Process: A Review
sources.claim: Automatic carcass-cutting and handling robots for large, heavy animal tissue are commercialized and installed in slaughterhouse lines by several vendors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling large heavy animal tissue on a purpose-built line. Substantiates that bulky, wet organ- or limb-sized tissue can be gripped and moved by machine when the work is fixtured and presented, as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: Humanoid robots proposed for OR roles (review)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: A 2026 review of humanoid robots for operating-room roles concludes that support functions may be feasible but autonomous clinical use in the OR is not yet validated.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative E2 judgment: no humanoid or mobile manipulator is validated for autonomous work at the sterile field of a live operating room.

sources.title: World’s First Automated Tissue Grossing Platform Uses AI to Assess Specimens
sources.claim: VistaPath's Sentinel is an automated tissue grossing platform used in pathology labs that images the specimen container and label, continuously checks container/cassette identity to prevent mix-ups, and generates the gross report; the tissue transfer step is performed with the operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: specimen accessioning/identity control in pathology. Shows machine-executed label matching and lock-out for the same specimen-identity function the surgical tech performs, but manipulation is not machine-performed, so it is supporting context only.

tasks.label: Monitor and continually assess operating room conditions, including patient and surgical team needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scrubbed at the sterile field during a routine scheduled general/ortho case (e.g., lap chole, appendectomy, total knee): continually watching the progress of the operation and the surgeon's hands to assess what step is coming, whether the field needs suction, irrigation, or better exposure, and whether the surgeon or assistant is signaling a need.

Monitoring the patient and the sterile barrier during a case: drape integrity, patient positioning and skin/pressure points, prep margins, fluid pooling, and watching team members and traffic for breaks in sterile technique that must be flagged to the circulator or surgeon.

Monitoring equipment and supply status throughout a case: suction canister level, irrigation volume, electrosurgical unit and insufflator settings and alarms, camera/light output, implant and suture inventory on the back table, assessing when a resupply or device change will be needed.

High-acuity or emergent case (trauma laparotomy, ruptured AAA, emergency C-section, cardiac case going on pump): rapid, unpredictable changes in blood loss, team composition, and instrumentation demands, with continuous reassessment of what the surgeon and anesthesia team need next.

Non-scrubbed or between-case monitoring: assessing room readiness and conditions (temperature/humidity, room traffic and door openings, equipment staged and functioning, count status, next-case needs) and reporting concerns to the RN circulator or charge nurse.

tasks.label: Prepare dressings or bandages and apply or assist with their application following surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Minimally invasive or minor case (lap chole, hernia, arthroscopy, robotic ports, minor excision) in a hospital OR or ASC: at the end of the case the tech opens small adhesive/island dressings onto the sterile field, wipes and dries the closed port sites, and applies 1-4 small adhesive dressings to flat, accessible skin while the patient is anesthetized and drapes are coming off.

Open case with one linear incision (C-section, hip/knee arthroplasty, laparotomy, thyroid): tech readies the dressing at the back table and applies a one-piece adhesive post-op dressing, or a gauze pad secured with several tape strips, over a 10-25 cm incision on a moderately contoured area, avoiding wrinkles and sealing edges.

Assist variant: the surgeon applies the dressing while the tech prepares and hands materials in sequence - opening peel-pouch gauze, ABD pads and tape onto the sterile field, cutting tape strips to length, cutting slit drain sponges, moistening or folding gauze, and passing each item across the field on request.

Bulky or extremity dressing: orthopedic soft dressing, Robert Jones dressing, circumferential roll gauze (Kerlix) and elastic (Ace) wrap around an arm or leg held up by an assistant, webril padding under a splint, or a compression wrap - applied under even tension over joints on a limp anesthetized limb.

Specialty or awkward dressing: negative-pressure (VAC) foam cut to wound shape with drape sealed under suction, open-wound packing, dressings around drains/tubes/ostomy sites, patient prone or lateral, bleeding or hairy skin, or an emergent case where the dressing must be improvised quickly.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Aletta, a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device, autonomously performs the whole venipuncture sequence on real outpatients, including picking up an adhesive bandage and applying it to the patient's arm at the end; multicenter trial of 1633 patients in three Dutch hospital phlebotomy departments, one supervisor per three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying an adhesive bandage to live human skin over a fresh puncture site immediately after a procedure. Same object class (peel-and-stick adhesive dressing), same substrate (compliant live skin), and comparable precision to covering a small closed incision; done autonomously at clinical scale with the limb fixtured in the machine.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device - CAP TODAY
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a commercially released, CE-marked device that automates the full blood-draw workflow including skin preparation and bandage application.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: commercial CE-marked status and scope confirm that autonomous application of an adhesive dressing to skin is a fielded machine capability, not a one-off demo.

sources.system: Autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing (Inspire RH56DFTP hand on manipulator, ATI force sensor)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing (arXiv 2510.06127)
sources.claim: UCSD research system for robotic wound redressing: a dexterous hand on a manipulator autonomously detaches medical tape (force-feedback imitation policy learned from teleoperated demonstrations) and places tape wrinkle-free on anatomical surfaces via trajectory optimization; validated in lab experiments and an integrated redressing pipeline. The paper notes wound care today is done entirely manually by clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: redressing a wound (removing old tape/dressing, placing new dressing and tape). Same materials (gauze dressing, medical tape) and same substrate class (skin over anatomy) as post-surgical dressing, demonstrated on a lab bench with the site presented to the robot, i.e. an E1-style fixtured presentation.

sources.title: R-APPIT - Steelco
sources.claim: R-APPIT is a commercial hospital sterile-processing robot that autonomously wraps instrument trays in sterile nonwoven wrap, tapes the wrapped packs and labels them, using AI vision to size the wrap; rated to pack up to 525,000 trays per year without manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing sterile soft goods - handling limp nonwoven sheets, folding them over a set and applying tape to secure them. Comparable deformable materials and comparable (low) precision to preparing gauze/ABD dressings and tape, performed autonomously in a purpose-built cell inside a hospital.

sources.system: da Vinci Research Kit (dVRK) multilateral pattern-cutting system
sources.title: Multilateral surgical pattern cutting in 2D orthotropic gauze with deep reinforcement learning policies for tensioning (ICRA 2017)
sources.claim: Autonomous gauze cutting: using the da Vinci Research Kit, a learned tensioning policy lets the robot cut patterns in surgical gauze held in a frame, reacting to gauze deformation during the cut.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting gauze to shape, part of preparing dressings (cutting drain sponges, trimming gauze). Same material and same tolerance, performed autonomously with the gauze fixtured in a frame - exactly the E1 presentation.

sources.system: Dented-roller flap-separation gripper for sealed sterile pouches (UR5e arm)
sources.title: A gripper for flap separation and opening of sealed bags (arXiv 2603.10890)
sources.claim: A gripper designed specifically to open the sealed sterile pouches used when preparing an operating room; experiments are bench tests with bags clamped to a table and the pipeline is still open-loop, with sensor-based autonomy and clinical validation listed as future work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening sterile peel pouches for OR preparation, the first step of preparing dressings at the sterile field. Cited as limiting evidence - the capability is still an open-loop bench demonstration, so it cannot support completion at a live sterile field.

sources.system: Scrub Nurse Robot (SNR), third generation with AISI
sources.title: Enhancing surgical efficiency with an automated scrub nurse robot: a focus on automatic instrument insertion (Int J CARS)
sources.claim: Third-generation scrub nurse robot detects when a surgeon withdraws an instrument and automatically conveys and tip-inserts the next instrument into the cannula; evaluated in laboratory experiments with surgeon stand-ins, and 53% slower at targeting than a real OR nurse-surgeon pair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handing supplies from the sterile setup to the surgeon during a case, the 'assist' half of this task. Shows autonomous hand-off is at prototype stage and only for rigid instruments presented in fixed holders, not deformable dressing materials at a live field.

tasks.label: Clean and restock operating room, gathering and placing equipment and supplies and arranging instruments according to instructions, such as a preference card.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-case room turnover in a hospital OR: bag and remove trash, soiled linen and sharps, change suction canisters, wipe and disinfect the OR table, arm boards, lights, booms, monitors, cables, kick buckets and furniture with hospital disinfectant, damp-mop the floor, reposition furniture and replace liners and disposables so the room is ready for the next case, inside a 15-30 minute turnover window with the anesthesia and nursing team also working in the room.

Fetching a handful of specific additional or missing items during or just after a case: walking to the sterile core or supply closet, locating a few named packaged supplies (an extra suture, a drain, a stapler reload, gloves in a given size) and bringing them back to the operating room.

Pulling a full case per the surgeon's preference card the day before or morning of surgery: picking 20-40 varied items (custom pack, gowns, sutures, blades, implants, disposables) from sterile-core and supply-room shelves, checking size and expiration, loading a case cart and moving it to the assigned OR.

Setting up the sterile field per the preference card: draping back table and Mayo stand, opening peel packs and instrument trays onto the field, arranging instruments in the order specified, assembling items (blade onto handle, suction tubing, ESU pencil, loading suture, filling basins) so the setup is ready and sterile for the surgeon.

Restocking the OR and sterile core after cases: replenishing cabinets, wall shelves and supply carts to par levels from a restock cart or supply exchange, rotating stock, pulling expired items, and refilling the room's standard disposables.

Gathering and placing capital equipment and devices called for by the card: rolling in and positioning the electrosurgical unit, tourniquet, video tower, microscope, warming units, positioning devices and specialty tables; plugging in cords, connecting foot pedals, gas and suction lines and routing cables safely.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals — IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously picks supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects (packaged hospital supplies) and same premises (hospital supply closets and corridors) as the surgical technologist's errand to fetch a few named items for an OR.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi fleets operate at scale in US hospitals, having completed over one million deliveries ... by mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes sustained, worker-quality reliability of autonomous fetch-and-deliver work inside hospital premises, the environment of the supply-errand instance.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers — Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick piece-picking system is commercially deployed picking varied packaged items to order at fixed goods-to-robot stations, including pharmaceutical and healthcare verticals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking of many varied packaged SKUs against a pick list into a destination container. A preference-card case pull and a par-level restock are the same pick-and-place of boxed and pouched supplies, at comparable precision, once stock is presented to the machine in a purpose-built station.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation (arXiv:2509.15600)
sources.claim: The CMU Operating Room Bot (ORB), a Fetch mobile manipulator, autonomously retrieved and restocked OR supplies in a mock hospital supply room with 80% retrieval and 96% restocking success on three designated items.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the OR supply retrieval and restocking task, but conducted in an environment that 'simulated ..., i.e. a purpose-arranged lab setup rather than a working hospital.

sources.developer: Chitalia lab (University of Louisville) et al.
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated lab cell with a Staubli TX2-60L arm and electromagnetic gripper autonomously sorts surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays using 3D-printed dividers and holders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: arranging surgical instruments in a specified layout per a list, the instrument-placement portion of preference-card setup. It does not cover opening sterile packaging, draping tables, or device assembly, and the paper reports continued fine-grained instrument misclassification.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR autonomously cleans commercial restrooms, including fixtures, floors and trash pickup, and is offered as a deployed service in facilities such as hospitals and airports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cleaning of a whole room in a managed facility. It transfers only partially: the no-touch power-wash and vacuum method suits tiled restroom fixtures, not disinfectant-wiping of OR tables, booms, monitors and cables, nor handling soiled linen, sharps and biohazard waste.

sources.title: How Robots Improve Cleaning Performance in Healthcare Facilities — Brain Corp
sources.claim: BrainOS-powered autonomous floor scrubbers (Tennant hardware) are deployed cleaning floors in hospitals such as Scripps Memorial Hospital La Jolla ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: floor cleaning inside a hospital. It covers only the mopping sub-step of an OR turnover and involves no manipulation of waste, linen, furniture or equipment surfaces.

tasks.label: Provide technical assistance to surgeons, surgical nurses, or anesthesiologists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During a live case in a hospital OR, the tech provides technical support with equipment for the team: connecting and troubleshooting the laparoscopic tower/insufflator/light cord and camera, setting and correcting electrosurgical unit and suction problems, running an arthroscopy pump or tourniquet, repositioning overhead lights and the microscope, draping and positioning the C-arm, and draping/docking or undocking the surgical robot and exchanging its instruments when the surgeon asks.

Serving as an extra pair of hands for the surgeon at the sterile field on verbal direction: holding a retractor for exposure, suctioning and irrigating in a bleeding field, sponging, cutting suture tails, holding tissue or a limb under traction, steadying a specimen or a graft while the surgeon works.

Assisting the anesthesiologist and the circulating RN with the patient: lateral transfer from stretcher to OR table, positioning and padding (lateral, lithotomy, prone), holding an arm/leg or the head during line, block or airway management, applying cricoid pressure at induction, and handing anesthesia supplies and drugs during induction and emergence.

Preparing and handing instruments, loaded needle drivers, sutures, blades and supplies to the surgeon and assistants on verbal request and by anticipation from a back table and Mayo stand, taking used items back, keeping the field organized, and tracking/counting sharps, sponges and instruments with the RN.

Mid-case, obtaining an item the team needs that is not in the room — an extra suture, an implant or sizer, an instrument tray, irrigation or a medication — from the sterile core, storage room or pharmacy and getting it into the OR to the circulating nurse in time to serve the case.

Acting as camera assistant for the operating surgeon during a laparoscopic/endoscopic case: holding the scope steady, following the working instruments, zooming and re-centering the view on request for the duration of the procedure.

sources.system: Penelope Surgical Instrument Server (Robotic Surgical Tech / Columbia)
sources.developer: Robotic Surgical Tech, Inc. (Michael Treat, Columbia University)
sources.title: For the First Time, Newly Developed Robot Assists Doctors and Nurses in Operating Room | NYP
sources.claim: The Penelope Surgical Instrument Server, a vision- and voice-driven robotic arm with its own instrument tray, handed and retrieved instruments for the surgical team during an actual tumour-excision operation at NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital in 2005; it remained a one-off prototype and never became a product.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the surgical technologist's instrument-handling assistance to a surgeon; the robot worked from a purpose-built instrument server tray rather than a human back table.

sources.system: SASHA-OR (Situation Aware Handling Arm for the OR)
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich / MITI, Klinikum rechts der Isar
sources.title: Versatile end effector for laparoscopic robotic scrub nurse - PubMed
sources.claim: SASHA-OR, a robotic scrub nurse built on a Franka Emika Panda arm with a purpose-built instrument rack, drop zone and 3D camera, picks, manipulates and returns laparoscopic and da Vinci instruments on voice or gesture request in laboratory grip tests.
sources.transferJustification: The robotic scrub-nurse instrument handover task is the same physical act a surgical technologist performs when handing instruments; objects and precision are identical, though the setting is a purpose-built rack rather than a back table.

sources.developer: Chinese University of Hong Kong (Li, Wang, Hu, Li et al.)
sources.title: [2409.19590] RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model
sources.claim: RoboNurse-VLA is a vision-language-action robotic scrub nurse that autonomously grasps surgical instruments from a table and hands them to a surgeon on spoken request, reporting high handover success rates in laboratory evaluation, including on unseen tools.
sources.transferJustification: Instrument handover to a surgeon is exactly the technical assistance a surgical technologist gives; the demonstration uses real surgical instruments presented on a fixed table.

sources.system: Robotic scrub nurse with instrument anticipation
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Wagner, Wilhelm et al.)
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis - PubMed
sources.claim: A robotic scrub nurse system ... watches the laparoscopic video feed anticipates and delivers the instruments needed in laparoscopic cholecystectomy, correctly predicting about 72% of instruments in advance; the work is a research prototype, not clinical practice.
sources.transferJustification: Anticipating and delivering the next instrument is the core of a surgical technologist's assistance to the operating surgeon.

sources.developer: Chinese University of Hong Kong (Ng et al.)
sources.title: Large Language Model-Embedded Intelligent Robotic Scrub Nurse with Multimodal Input for Enhancing Surgeon-Robot Interaction
sources.claim: An LLM-embedded robotic scrub nurse platform (Franka Emika Panda arm, custom electromagnetic gripper, two depth cameras, dedicated instrument tables) performs instrument transfer, sorting and counting tasks in the laboratory; the authors state real-OR testing remains future work.
sources.transferJustification: Covers both instrument handover and item counting, two components of the technologist's technical assistance, but only with instruments laid out on purpose-built tables in a lab.

sources.title: First experience with THE AUTOLAP™ SYSTEM: an image-based robotic camera steering device | Surgical Endoscopy
sources.claim: The AutoLap image-based robotic camera steering device replaced the human camera assistant in 66 laparoscopic operations performed by nine experienced surgeons across two multi-centre clinical studies in real hospital operating rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Holding and steering the laparoscope for the operating surgeon is precisely the camera-assistant role a surgical technologist fills; the device is designed to take the scope out of the assistant's hands.

sources.title: AutoLap received FDA clearance (surgrob)
sources.claim: AutoLap is a regulatory-cleared product used in clinical practice, steering the laparoscope by image analysis with minimal user interaction rather than by continuous manual control.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes commercial/clinical maturity of the robotic camera-holding assistant that substitutes for the human scope holder.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous mobile manipulation robot, is deployed in more than 25 ... and has completed over 1.25 million autonomous ... of supplies, medications and lab samples between hospital storage areas and clinical units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching and delivering supplies, medications and samples through a hospital. Transfers to obtaining an extra item for an OR mid-case — same building, same corridors, same class of small packaged items, hand-off to a staff member.

sources.title: New kid on the block at Upstate: The transport robot | Upstate News | SUNY Upstate
sources.claim: A US academic medical centre operates a fleet of 14 Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots that haul supplies and materials through the hospital, including linens, meals and clinical supplies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital transport of supply carts. Transfers to the runner element of OR technical assistance — moving needed supplies and trays from storage to a specific room in a controlled hospital facility.

sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Michael Yip lab)
sources.title: Surgeons Use Teleoperated Humanoid Robots to Perform Live Surgery–a World First | Newswise
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid robots yet used in live surgery, demonstrated in July 2026, performed the procedure under human teleoperation; developers state an autonomous surgical assistant that could fetch tools or clean the OR remains a research goal.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to characterise the state of the art for general-purpose robotic assistance in an OR: it is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment for equipment handling, field assistance or patient handling.

tasks.label: Operate, assemble, adjust, or monitor sterilizers, lights, suction machines, or diagnostic equipment to ensure proper operation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-case OR setup of suction: surgical tech opens a disposable canister/liner, snaps it into the wall-mount bracket, connects vacuum tubing to the regulator and to the sterile field suction tip (Yankauer/Poole), turns on wall vacuum, checks the regulator setting and confirms suction pull, and routes/secures the tubing off the field. Done in a working OR amid anesthesia, circulator and setup traffic, under time pressure before incision.

Pre-case assembly and function check of other OR equipment: positioning and connecting the electrosurgical generator, pencil and dispersive pad; laparoscopic tower with insufflator, CO2 hose, camera head, light cord and monitor (white balance, focus, gas flow test); tourniquet cuff and pump; drills, warmers, microscope drapes. Cords and hoses are passed off the sterile field and connected, and each unit is powered up and verified working.

Adjusting the overhead surgical lights: placing sterile light handles, positioning and focusing two or three light heads over the incision before and during the case, and repositioning/refocusing on the surgeon's request or when staff cast shadows, throughout an open procedure in a standard hospital OR.

Operating sterilizers: loading wrapped trays/rigid containers or an immediate-use load into a steam autoclave in the sub-sterile room or sterile processing department, selecting and starting the correct cycle, watching cycle parameters and process indicators, unloading and cooling, and documenting the load. Standard hospital equipment, institution-controlled premises.

Intraoperative monitoring and troubleshooting of equipment: noticing loss of suction or a full canister and swapping it mid-case, responding to insufflator/ESU alarms, changing generator settings on request, restoring a failed camera or light cord, and pulling and replacing malfunctioning units while the case continues at the sterile field.

sources.system: SteelcoBelimed TS MST-V automatic loading/unloading unit for MST-V sterilizers
sources.title: TS MST-V — Automation for MST-V sterilizers
sources.claim: Commercial sterilizer automation (SteelcoBelimed TS MST-V) transports the loaded batch cart into the steam sterilizer and starts the sterilization cycle automatically once the transport cart is docked, with a queue line for successive batches and automatic unloading.

sources.system: SteelcoBelimed MST-V Series steam sterilizer with SmartHub
sources.title: MST-V Series — SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: The MST-V steam sterilizer performs warm-up and daily test cycles and shutdown automatically, and machine data/cycle status is monitored in real time by the SmartHub software, covering the 'operate and monitor sterilizers to ensure proper operation' function without operator input.

sources.title: Automated Sterilization Center — Gibotech A/S
sources.claim: Gibotech has installed automated central sterile supply departments (Køge 2011, Rigshospitalet, Herlev) in which robot arms, mobile robots, conveyors and automated storage handle surgical instrument containers through the wash/sterilize/store workflow in a purpose-built, largely unmanned plant.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L + YOLO12/ResNet perception)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A robotic cell with a Staubli TX2-60L arm, vision pipeline and custom gripper autonomously sorts surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays in a sterile-processing workflow, with evaluated perception accuracy and reduced tool-to-tool collisions versus human-assembled trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing instrument trays for sterilization in the SPD. It transfers to the sterilizer-operation instance because the objects (surgical instrument sets and trays), the department, and the fixtured cell layout are the same as those used by automated sterilizer loading lines.

sources.system: SmartOT autonomous module-based surgical lighting system
sources.developer: University of Bremen / Pius-Hospital Oldenburg (Mühlenbrock, Cetin, Weyhe, Zachmann)
sources.title: A Novel, Autonomous, Module-Based Surgical Lighting System — ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare
sources.claim: The SmartOT module-based surgical lighting system is a physically built array of swiveling, ceiling-mounted light ... whose orientation and intensity are controlled autonomously by depth-camera-driven algorithms to keep the surgical site illuminated and shadow-free without manual lamp adjustment; a prototype was installed at Pius Hospital Oldenburg.

sources.title: Evaluating the efficiency and ergonomics of a novel smart surgical lighting system (Frontiers in Medical Technology)
sources.claim: In a controlled study with participants performing simulated surgical tasks under the SmartOT smart lamp versus a conventional manually adjusted surgical lamp, the automatically adjusting system produced fewer errors and lower measured workload, indicating the autonomous lamp delivered acceptable illumination without a human adjusting it.

sources.system: Maquet Volista surgical light with Automatic Illumination Management (AIM)
sources.title: Maquet Volista Surgical Light — Getinge
sources.claim: Commercially deployed surgical lights in hospital ORs already automate part of the light-adjustment function: Maquet Volista's Automatic Illumination Management detects obstructions and redistributes output from unmasked LEDs to keep the field lit without a technologist repositioning the head.

sources.system: Machine Vision-Based Surgical Lighting System (YOLOv11 + pan/tilt servomotors)
sources.title: Machine Vision-Based Surgical Lighting System: Design and Implementation (arXiv:2510.17287)
sources.claim: A servo-driven machine-vision surgical lighting prototype that autonomously aims an LED source at a detected marker over the surgical site reports that it has not been trialled in a real operating room because non-certified devices are barred from sterile environments.

tasks.label: Maintain supply of fluids, such as plasma, saline, blood, or glucose, for use during operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During an active case, the scrub tech keeps sterile fluids available at the sterile field: receives 1 L bottles of warm irrigation saline from the circulator, fills the back-table basin, pitchers and bulb syringes, watches the level as the surgeon irrigates, and calls for more before it runs out — all inside the sterile field, without contaminating drapes, instruments or the wound.

Pre-case setup: the tech pulls the case's fluid stock (1 L irrigation saline/sterile water, IV bags of NS or LR, D5W/glucose, antibiotic irrigant components) from the OR core and warming cabinet, checks expiration dates and container integrity, and opens/dispenses them onto the sterile field or stages them on the anesthesia and back tables.

Mid-case replenishment: the room runs low on warm irrigation or IV fluid during surgery; the tech/circulator must locate the correct fluid in the sub-sterile room or core supply, bring it into a running OR quickly, and deliver it to the field or to anesthesia without breaking sterility.

Between cases: restocking the room's fluid par levels — carrying cases of saline bottles and IV bags from central/core supply, loading the fluid warming cabinet, rotating stock by expiry, and recording usage/charges so the next case is covered.

Blood and colloid products: retrieving units of packed cells or plasma from the blood bank refrigerator or validated cooler for a case with expected blood loss, performing identity/expiry verification, transporting them to the OR at temperature, and passing them to anesthesia or setting up cell-saver/rapid-infuser fluids.

sources.title: ARxIUM Celebrates Major RIVA Milestone | The National Law Review
sources.claim: RIVA is a commercially deployed, fully automated robotic IV compounding system that uses robotic arms inside a closed ISO Class 5 enclosure to prepare sterile IV bags and syringes with gravimetric verification and walk-away automation; over 19 million doses prepared across its installed base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aseptic sterile-fluid transfer in hospital pharmacy. It handles the same objects (sterile fluid bags, bottles, vials, syringes), transfers measured sterile fluid into receptacles under stricter asepsis and higher precision than filling an OR basin or staging IV fluids, and does so unattended in a purpose-built enclosure, so it substantiates E1-level fluid provisioning.

sources.title: Omnicell Unveils Innovative IVX Station Robotic Compounding Technology in Winter 2022 Release
sources.claim: Omnicell's IVX Station is a fully automated IV compounding robot for hospital pharmacies with the footprint of a four-foot hood, marketed commercially since 2022 as a replacement for manual sterile compounding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated aseptic preparation and dispensing of IV fluid containers. Same class of objects (IV bags, vials, syringes of saline/glucose-based fluids) handled robotically in a purpose-built cabinet, supporting the fluid-handling element of maintaining an operative fluid supply at E1.

sources.title: Pharmacy Robot Increases Safety, Efficiency | Owensboro Health
sources.claim: Omnicell's XR2 central pharmacy robot is installed in US hospitals and autonomously pulls specified stock items, barcode-scans, bags, seals, labels and dispenses them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated retrieval of specified stock items from a hospital's inventory. Pulling a named, in-date container from stock and presenting it for use is the same operation as pulling saline/glucose/IV stock for a case, performed inside a purpose-built enclosure (E1).

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks and moves individual items of varied consumer inventory from cluttered containers into specific totes inside fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking of individual packaged goods, including bottles and bagged items, at production reliability. It substantiates that at a fixtured station a robot can select and transfer the kinds of containers (bottles, IV bags, boxed sets) that make up an OR fluid restock.

sources.developer: Hera Scientific (Hemosafe automated blood bank refrigerator)
sources.title: Automated blood bank refrigerator Hemosafe 2.0 (product brochure)
sources.claim: Hemosafe 2.0 is a commercial automated blood bank refrigerator whose mechanical arm stores and issues blood bags on request, reading unit barcodes automatically and syncing with the blood bank management system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the blood-product element: machine-controlled storage, identity verification and issue of blood units in a purpose-built refrigerated cabinet, i.e. the retrieval-and-verification portion of maintaining a blood supply for a case.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators autonomously perform point-to-point deliveries of pharmacy items, lab samples and supplies in more than 30 US hospitals, including autonomous elevator rides, with over a million deliveries completed; staff load and unload its locked compartments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital transport of supplies and medications. It establishes that the corridor-transport leg of fetching fluids is autonomous at E2, but the deployed workflow is point-to-point delivery with staff loading and unloading, so it does not cover shelf retrieval or delivery into a sterile field.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores | NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots autonomously restock bottled and canned beverages onto refrigerated store shelves in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, succeeding automatically over 98% of the time with remote operators handling the rare failures; the robot is installed on a fixed rail in the store's cooler.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking of bottles and cans. Comparable objects to 1 L saline bottles and comparable placement precision, but performed by a rail-mounted arm at one fixed, pre-arranged shelving bay, so it supports fixtured restocking rather than roaming an as-found hospital supply room.

sources.title: RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model (arXiv:2409.19590)
sources.claim: RoboNurse-VLA is a laboratory research system for robotic scrub-nurse instrument handover in the operating room; robotic assistance at the sterile field remains at the research-demonstration stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic assistance to the scrub role in the OR. Cited only as context showing that sterile-field assistance is a laboratory demonstration, not a deployed capability; it is not used to support any positive tier judgment.
