tasks.label: Administer emergency first aid, such as performing emergency resuscitation or other life saving procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal ER/treatment area: dog or cat arrests (CPA) on arrival or in-house. Tech recognizes arrest, starts external chest compressions per RECOVER, intubates and ventilates 30:2 or bags the patient, places IV/IO access, draws up and gives epinephrine/atropine on the vet's order, monitors ECG and ETCO2, applies the defibrillator, rotates roles over 2-minute cycles on a flaccid, blood-slick patient of 2-60 kg.

Triage/stabilization of a trauma or shock patient (hit-by-car dog, dog-fight wounds, bleeding mass) in the clinic treatment room: direct pressure and pressure bandage or tourniquet on an actively bleeding limb or wound, muzzle and restrain a painful struggling animal, place a peripheral IV catheter, start shock-rate fluids, give oxygen and analgesia per order, keep the patient warm.

Respiratory emergency in the clinic: dyspneic/cyanotic cat or brachycephalic dog. Tech provides flow-by/mask oxygen or an oxygen cage, suctions the airway, performs or assists emergency intubation, bag-ventilates, and assists the veterinarian with thoracocentesis while stabilizing a fragile, panicking patient.

Perioperative/anesthetic crisis in the clinic OR or dental suite: an intubated, draped, monitored patient becomes apneic, hypotensive, or arrests. Tech turns off the vaporizer, hand-ventilates with the circuit, starts compressions on the table, gives reversal and emergency drugs, and manages monitors alongside the surgeon.

Out-of-clinic emergency first aid: large-animal or ambulatory setting (barn aisle, pasture, trailer, roadside) — control hemorrhage on a horse or calf, stabilize a downed or entrapped animal, give oxygen or emergency drugs at the scene, or first aid in the clinic parking lot on arrival, with uneven footing, poor light, and an uncontrolled, frightened animal.

Emergency first aid on non-traditional patients in institutional facilities: exotic pets, birds, small mammals, or research/shelter animals — tiny or unusual anatomy, oxygen supplementation, warming, hemorrhage control, and species-specific resuscitation in a shelter, university, or laboratory animal facility.

sources.system: AI-driven biosignal-sensitive CPR robot (compared with LUCAS 3)
sources.developer: Korean research group, published in Resuscitation
sources.title: Development of artificial intelligence-driven biosignal-sensitive cardiopulmonary resuscitation robot - PubMed
sources.claim: An AI-driven robotic chest-compression device delivered feedback-guided compressions to anesthetized, instrumented pigs in a laboratory cardiac-arrest model — autonomous compressions only, with no airway management, vascular access, drug delivery, or patient handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical chest compressions in an animal cardiac-arrest model. It covers only one sub-step of resuscitation, on an already anesthetized, positioned and instrumented subject, so it does not substantiate completion of the whole first-aid instance.

sources.title: Quality of cardiopulmonary resuscitation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest before and after introduction of a mechanical chest compression device, LUCAS-2; a prospective, observational study
sources.claim: Commercially deployed mechanical chest compression devices (LUCAS-2/3) perform only the compression component of CPR on human-shaped torsos and must be positioned on the patient by clinicians who manage airway, drugs and monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: human out-of-hospital CPR. Shows the most mature automated resuscitation hardware still executes one sub-step after human placement and cannot perform triage, hemorrhage control, intubation, or drug administration on an animal patient.

sources.title: Robot performs first realistic surgery without human help | Hub
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous robotic intervention on animal tissue is planned laparoscopic surgery on anesthetized or ex vivo pigs in a highly controlled setup, not emergency stabilization of a conscious patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue surgery on pigs. Performance does not carry over: the subject is anesthetized, immobilized and draped with the operative field fixed, whereas emergency first aid requires restraining and assessing an unrestrained, deteriorating animal and delivering multi-modal care under time pressure.

sources.title: Surgeons use teleoperated humanoid robots to perform live surgery—a world first
sources.claim: Humanoid robots performing live medical/surgical procedures as of mid-2026 are teleoperated by surgeons, with autonomy stated only as a future goal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid-executed clinical procedures. Because it is continuously teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous emergency first aid.

sources.system: MASH / Medical Swarm Robotics (DARPA program solicitation)
sources.title: DARPA solicits swarm-capable, automated robotic medics to treat battlefield casualties
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic trauma care (wound assessment, hemorrhage control, IV access) is at the solicitation stage: DARPA is seeking such robots, indicating no fielded system performs these tasks today.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous casualty first aid. It is an announcement of intent with no demonstrated system, so per the rules it cannot substantiate any positive judgment.

sources.developer: UC Santa Barbara and collaborators (Science Translational Medicine)
sources.title: A soft robotic device for rapid and self-guided intubation | Science Translational Medicine
sources.claim: Robotic airway devices for emergency intubation have been validated only on manikins and cadavers and are operated by trained human users; fully autonomous intubation trials remain manikin-only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency endotracheal intubation. The device is human-operated on human-anatomy manikins/cadavers, so it does not substantiate autonomous airway management of dogs, cats, or exotics during resuscitation.

tasks.label: Clean and sterilize instruments, equipment, or materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic: after each surgery or dental procedure, reprocess hand instruments — rinse/soak off blood and tissue, brush or ultrasonic-clean hinged instruments, rinse, dry, lubricate box locks, inspect for damage and residue, count and arrange into packs/pouches with chemical indicators, seal or wrap, load the steam autoclave, run and log the cycle, unload, cool and store sterile packs.

Anesthesia and respiratory equipment after each case: disconnect and disassemble endotracheal tubes, breathing circuits, rebreathing bags, masks and laryngoscopes; wash and disinfect (including tube lumens and cuffs), rinse, hang to dry, reassemble the circuit on the machine, replace/clean the soda lime canister and leak-test.

Equipment cleaned and maintained in place around the treatment area: clipper heads and blades (hair, blade wash, lube), dental unit handpieces and water lines, suction units and canisters, patient monitors and cables, ultrasound probes, surgery/exam tables and lights, hematology/chemistry analyzers and centrifuge; plus laundering and folding surgical gowns, towels and drapes.

Portable labware, containers and consumable materials: wash, rinse, dry and where required autoclave reusable glassware, sample jars, slide/tube racks, dosing syringes, bowls, water bottles and cage accessories; autoclave gauze, bowls and kit materials and biohazard waste; move loads to and from the washer and autoclave.

Ambulatory/large-animal or shelter field work: clean and disinfect heavily soiled field equipment at the barn, chute or truck — buckets, OB chains and handles, stomach tube and pump, hoof knives and nippers, dehorners, rectal ultrasound probe, boots and coveralls — scrubbing off manure and blood with limited water, disinfecting between farms, then sterilizing surgical items back at the clinic.

sources.title: Automation - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: Commercial CSSD automation: an automatic transfer shuttle loads and unloads wash carts into washer-disinfectors and sterilizers and moves loads through the cleaning-to-sterilization stages of a purpose-built reprocessing line.

sources.title: Automation - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: Commercial packing robot that wraps assembled instrument trays using the correct packing method, tapes and labels them, replacing manual wrapping in the sterile-processing line.

sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: A robotic arm with computer vision autonomously assembled a minor surgical instrument tray during a pilot inside a hospital sterile processing department.

sources.title: RIF Robotics Corp | Southeast Venture Showcase
sources.claim: The same product is built to automate inspection of surgical instruments for ... together with tray assembly for hospitals and ambulatory surgery centers.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L with dual electromagnetic gripper)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: Research system: a 6-DOF Staubli arm with vision autonomously sorts and packs 31 classes of surgical instruments into structured sterile trays, reporting high perception accuracy and fewer instrument collisions than human-packed trays.

sources.title: Getinge transforms sterile reprocessing with Automatiq - a full range of logistic automation modules
sources.claim: Automated loaders for washer-disinfectors and steam sterilizers handle loading and unloading and move clean goods onward to sorting, inspection and packing stations in sterile reprocessing departments.

sources.system: Staubli Stericlean and pharma robot cells
sources.title: Robotic solutions for pharmaceutical and healthcare industry | Staubli United States
sources.claim: Industrial robots are supplied commercially for loading and unloading autoclaves and parts washers in pharmaceutical production and laboratory settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading and unloading autoclaves and washers with racks of items. Same class of objects (racks, trays, containers) and the same accept criterion (a validated wash/sterilization cycle) as washing and autoclaving veterinary labware and pack materials.

sources.date: product page current 2026; system marketed since ~2019
sources.title: Cosmos - Tecniplast UK
sources.claim: Patented robotic cell handles reusable animal-housing items (cage bases, tops, wire lids) into and out of tunnel washers in vivarium wash rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing reusable animal-care containers and accessories. Objects, soil type (bedding, urine, feces) and the validated washer cycle match cleaning veterinary labware, bowls, bottles and cage accessories.

sources.system: Vivarium cage-wash robotic automation (Technopark Skolkovo installation)
sources.developer: Perkins&Will design with vivarium automation vendors
sources.title: Vivarium Solution for a Labor Shortage: Kinder, Gentler Robots - Tradeline
sources.claim: In an operating 65,000-sf animal facility, multi-axis robot arms were installed on the soiled and clean sides ... cage-wash operation and robots further automated the washing process, cutting wash staffing from nine to five.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reprocessing reusable animal-care hardware through washers. Shows a deployed robotic wash cell doing dirty-side loading and clean-side unloading, the same material flow as washing veterinary labware and containers.

tasks.label: Provide veterinarians with the correct equipment or instruments, as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal surgery or dental suite: during a spay/neuter, mass removal, or dental extraction the tech supplies the veterinarian with instruments as the procedure unfolds - passing hemostats, scalpel, needle holders, suture, gauze from the sterile pack on verbal request or by anticipation, and taking used instruments back.

Exam room / treatment area during an appointment: the veterinarian, hands occupied with the patient, asks for the next item (otoscope cone, thermometer, slide, needle and syringe, ear cleaner, clippers, muzzle, drawn-up sedative) and the tech pulls it from a nearby drawer, counter or cart and places it in the vet's hand within seconds, often while also steadying the animal.

Fetching from elsewhere in the clinic: the vet needs something not in the room - a vaccine or drug from the pharmacy or fridge, a fluid pump, an ultrasound unit, a larger endotracheal tube, extra gloves - and the tech walks to pharmacy/supply/another room, retrieves the correct item and brings it back.

Pre-procedure setup: for a scheduled procedure the tech selects the correct instrument pack/kit and supplies from storage, opens the pack sterilely and lays out instruments, blades, suture and ancillary items so they are ready for the veterinarian at the table.

Emergency / critical care: during a crash, dystocia or trauma triage the tech supplies items on shouted demand under time pressure - ET tubes and laryngoscope, IV catheters, emergency drugs drawn up, chest tube kit, clippers - in a crowded, fast-moving treatment area.

Large-animal / ambulatory field call: at a barn, stall, pasture or chute the tech retrieves instruments and supplies from the truck's compartments (obstetric chains, hoof knife, dehorner, syringes, suture, lavage fluids) and hands them to the veterinarian working on a restrained cow or horse, in mud, poor light and varied footing.

sources.title: Initial clinical experience with a partly autonomous robotic surgical instrument server (Surgical Endoscopy)
sources.claim: Penelope Surgical Instrument Server, a voice-commanded robot arm with machine vision, delivered and retrieved surgical instruments for the surgeon during an actual operation in a hospital operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Human OR instrument passing on the surgeon's request is the same act as passing instruments to a veterinarian in a surgery suite: comparable steel instruments, comparable precision, comparable institution-controlled operating room.

sources.title: For the First Time, Newly Developed Robot Assists Doctors and Nurses in Operating Room
sources.claim: The same robot functioned in the operating room as an independent assistant to ..., identifying instruments, handing them to the surgeon and returning them to the tray.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: supplying a clinician with the correct instrument on demand in an operating room.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals (IEEE Spectrum)
sources.claim: Moxi, a commercial mobile manipulator, autonomously picks supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Fetching a needed supply item from clinic storage and bringing it to the clinician who needs it is the same act as a vet tech retrieving equipment from the pharmacy or stockroom for the veterinarian.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi fleets are deployed across more than 25 US hospitals and have completed over one million supply, specimen and pharmacy deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment scale and reliability of autonomous item retrieval and delivery inside institution-controlled clinical facilities.

sources.developer: RIF Robotics (pilot at Wellstar Windy Hill Hospital)
sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: A vision-guided robot arm piloted in a hospital sterile processing department autonomously assembled a minor surgical instrument tray, leaving technicians to inspect rather than select and place each instrument.
sources.transferJustification: Selecting the correct instruments and laying them out in the tray the clinician will use is the preparation half of providing the veterinarian with the correct instruments.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv 2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic workcell sorts surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays with consistent localization and precise placement.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects (surgical instruments) and same output (a correctly composed instrument set) as preparing the pack a veterinarian will operate from; performed at a fixtured bench workcell.

sources.title: RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model (project page)
sources.claim: A robotic scrub-nurse system grasps and hands over surgical instruments in real time in response to the surgeon's spoken request, in a laboratory bench setup.
sources.transferJustification: Voice-requested grasp-and-handover of instruments from a staged tray is the machine-side equivalent of handing the veterinarian the instrument asked for, with the work presented to the robot.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation (arXiv 2509.15600)
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile manipulator built for operating-room logistics retrieved item-level OR supplies from marked shelf bins with an 80% success rate and restocked with 96% success in a research setting.
sources.transferJustification: Item-level retrieval of clinical supplies for a procedure; the 80% rate shows current item-level fetch in clinical rooms remains below the reliability a clinician would accept from a technician.

sources.title: BD and Henry Ford Health partner to automate pharmacies - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Commercial pharmacy robots automatically store and retrieve requested medication packs at high speed and are being deployed in US hospital pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: On-request retrieval and presentation of the correct stocked item within seconds from a purpose-built rack - the E1 form of handing a clinician the item they call for.

tasks.label: Perform dental work, such as cleaning, polishing, or extracting teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine canine dental prophylaxis in a small-animal clinic dental suite: dog under general anesthesia, intubated and cuffed, positioned on a wet table with mouth gag/props; tech performs full-mouth ultrasonic scaling plus hand scaling of subgingival calculus on ~42 teeth, probes and charts pocket depths, polishes with prophy paste and rubber cup, rinses sulci, monitors anesthesia throughout.

Feline dental cleaning with full-mouth intraoral radiographs in a clinic: small oral cavity, delicate teeth prone to fracture and tooth-resorption lesions, careful supra/subgingival scaling and polishing, radiograph sensor placement and charting, all under short anesthetic time.

Extraction/oral-surgery work in a clinic dental operatory: sectioning multi-rooted teeth with a high-speed bur, elevating and luxating roots, removing mobile periodontally diseased teeth, alveoloplasty and suturing gingival flaps (performed by the tech where state practice acts allow, otherwise the tech performs the assisting, suction, retraction, radiographic verification and instrument work while the veterinarian extracts).

High-volume shelter, low-cost or mobile-unit dental: heavily calculus-encrusted mouth with multiple loose teeth, brachycephalic or crowded dentition, older or shared equipment, tight time budget, output still must meet clinic standards for tartar removal and smooth polished crowns.

Large-animal dentistry on the farm: sedated standing horse in a barn aisle or portable stocks, full-mouth speculum and head support, tech operates a motorized float to reduce enamel points, hooks and ramps, and assists with extraction of loose caps or wolf teeth in variable footing, lighting and dust.

sources.title: US-Based AI Company Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human - Oral Health Group
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-guided robotic arm completed an automated crown preparation on a single tooth of a human patient rigidly splinted in a dental chair; it is the most advanced autonomous intraoral robot demonstrated on a live patient, but it prepares one tooth for a restoration and does not perform full-mouth scaling, subgingival calculus removal, polishing or extraction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crown preparation in human dentistry. It is the closest cited robotic capability to veterinary dental work (intraoral instrument control under 3D imaging), but transfer fails: it is a single-tooth restorative cut on a cooperative, splinted human, not full-arcade scaling, probing, polishing or surgical extraction across varied canine, feline and equine dentition.

sources.system: Shapeshifting microrobotic microswarm (iron oxide nanoparticle system)
sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania (Penn Dental Medicine / Penn Engineering)
sources.title: Penn Study Shows Shapeshifting Microrobots Can Brush, Floss Teeth
sources.claim: Penn's magnetically driven iron-oxide microrobot swarm removed biofilm from mock and extracted human teeth in bench experiments; it is a laboratory proof of concept for plaque removal, not a clinical system that performs a complete dental prophylaxis including subgingival calculus removal, charting and polishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated plaque/biofilm removal from teeth. Objects (teeth, biofilm) are comparable, but the demonstration is ex vivo bench work on isolated teeth and cannot remove hardened subgingival calculus, polish crowns or work in an anesthetized animal's mouth.

sources.developer: University research team (reported in IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics)
sources.title: Wine-cork-sized dental robot could automate crown preparation - Oral Health Group
sources.claim: The Miniature Intraoral Robot, an in-mouth robot held by a custom splint for automated crown preparation, has been evaluated only on synthetic resin and ceramic tooth models, confirming that automated intraoral tooth-cutting robots remain at bench-test stage in mid-2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated tooth preparation with a rotary bur. Shows the state of the art for machine-controlled cutting of teeth is phantom-model testing, so it cannot substantiate whole-procedure dental work on live animals.

sources.system: da Vinci Surgical System and related veterinary robotic platforms
sources.title: The Role of Robotics in Veterinary Surgery - What Does the Future Hold? - Vet Help Direct
sources.claim: Robotics entering veterinary surgery (e.g., da Vinci-type platforms) is surgeon-controlled teleoperation that augments the veterinarian rather than operating autonomously; no autonomous veterinary dental cleaning, polishing or extraction system is described.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic soft-tissue surgery on animals in veterinary hospitals. Establishes that veterinary robotic systems in clinical use are teleoperated master-slave devices, so they cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for dental prophylaxis or extraction.

tasks.label: Observe the behavior and condition of animals and monitor their clinical symptoms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ward rounds on hospitalized dogs and cats in a small-animal hospital: every 1-4 hours the tech opens each kennel, restrains the patient, takes temperature/pulse/respiration, checks mucous membrane color, capillary refill, hydration, pain score, attitude, appetite, urine/feces output, IV catheter and bandage sites, and records/reports changes to the veterinarian.

Monitoring an anesthetized patient during surgery/dentistry and through recovery: watching respiratory pattern, jaw tone, eye position and palpebral reflex, mucous membranes, placing and troubleshooting ECG/pulse-ox/capnograph/BP leads on a draped animal, and observing extubation and post-op recovery for pain, dysphoria, vomiting or bleeding.

Exam-room intake and triage of an owned pet with the client present: observing gait, posture, demeanor, respiratory effort, coughing/vomiting, body and coat condition, weighing and restraining the animal, obtaining vitals, and reporting observations to the veterinarian.

High-volume caged-animal facility rounds (shelter, boarding kennel, or research vivarium): daily walk-through of rows of runs/cages checking each animal for lethargy, coughing/sneezing, diarrhea, poor body condition, wounds, tumors, dystocia or abnormal behavior, flagging animals for veterinary attention.

Large-animal or equine work: observing an individual cow, horse, sheep or goat in a barn aisle, stocks, chute or pasture -- lameness and gait, rumen fill and motility, respiratory rate, udder or wound condition, attitude -- often in variable footing, weather and lighting with the animal loose or minimally restrained.

Flock/herd-level surveillance inside an intensive production house (broiler house, layer barn, swine barn): walking the house to assess bird/pig distribution, activity, litter and air conditions, and to spot sick, lame or dead animals among thousands, reporting welfare and disease indicators.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: challenges and opportunities
sources.claim: Scout (formerly ChickenBoy, Faromatics/AGCO) is an autonomous ceiling-rail robot that patrols commercial broiler houses, using thermal and RGB cameras plus environmental sensors to assess bird distribution and to detect sick and dead birds ... litter/drinker problems, alerting the farmer.
sources.transferJustification: Direct match to the task at flock level: the robot's output is observation of animal behaviour/condition and flagging of clinically abnormal animals, the same product a technician's house walk-through produces.

sources.title: AGCO Acquires Faromatics, a Precision Livestock Farming Company
sources.claim: ChickenBoy is a commercially sold, ceiling-suspended monitoring robot installed on working broiler farms in Europe; AGCO acquired the developer in 2021 to sell it as a livestock product.

sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Brigham and Women's Hospital tests MIT's 'Dr. Spot' robot for contactless vital signs monitoring
sources.claim: The closest robotic analogue to bedside patient observation, Dr. Spot, is a quadruped carrying cameras that measures skin temperature, respiratory rate, SpO2 and heart rate on cooperative human patients; it was operated by remote control in a hospital emergency department and does not touch or restrain the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (patient vital-sign observation) but it is remote-controlled and relies on a still, cooperative human patient, so it cannot support a positive judgment for hands-on assessment of restrained animals.

sources.title: The VETGuardian Revolution: How Remote Patient Monitoring is Transforming Veterinary Care
sources.claim: Automation of veterinary patient monitoring in clinics is delivered by stationary, non-robotic contactless sensor units (VETGuardian streams vitals and video to a phone); nothing in the product acts physically on the patient, opens kennels, restrains animals or performs hands-on assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to document the state of the art in veterinary ward monitoring; it is a fixed sensor, not a physically embodied machine acting on the world, so it cannot support a positive robotic judgment.

sources.system: Vivarium automation (Tecniplast cage-handling robots, sensor-equipped racks)
sources.title: Automation: robots in the vivarium
sources.claim: Robotics in research vivaria is applied to cage handling and cage washing; animal health/status monitoring there is done by sensors and cameras embedded in cages and racks rather than by any robot that inspects or handles the animals.
sources.transferJustification: Cited for the absence of a robot performing per-animal clinical observation in vivaria; the robots there move cages, and the monitoring components are non-robotic sensors.

tasks.label: Give enemas and perform catheterizations, ear flushes, intravenous feedings, or gavages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic treatment area: place a peripheral IV catheter in the cephalic vein of a conscious or lightly sedated dog or cat — restrain/position the animal, clip and prep the leg, have the vein held off, insert and advance the catheter, secure with tape/bandage, flush, and connect the fluid or parenteral-nutrition line; patient may squirm, be dehydrated with collapsed veins, or be fractious.

Small-animal clinic: urinary catheterization of a dog or cat (male cat with urethral obstruction, sterile urine sample, indwelling catheter with closed collection system) on a treatment table with the patient sedated or anesthetized and positioned by an assistant; requires aseptic prep, locating the urethral opening, atraumatic passage, and suturing/taping the catheter in place.

Small-animal exam/treatment room: ear flush of a dog (or cat) with otitis externa — instill cleaner, massage the canal, flush with a bulb syringe or ear-flush unit, suction/wipe out debris and exudate, sometimes under otoscopic or video-otoscope guidance, with the head restrained or the patient sedated; endpoint is a clean, dry canal without damaging the eardrum.

Small-animal and exotic patients in a clinic: warm-water or lactulose enema for a constipated cat/dog, orogastric tube feeding of neonatal kittens/puppies, crop gavage of a bird or tube feeding of a reptile, and feeding through a nasoesophageal/esophagostomy tube in an anorexic cat — measuring the tube, confirming placement, delivering warmed formula slowly, and monitoring for regurgitation.

Large-animal/equine ambulatory work in a barn aisle, stall, or field: passing a nasogastric tube in a colicky horse (restrained in stocks or by a handler) to check for reflux and administer fluids/mineral oil, or giving an enema to a newborn foal for meconium retention, under variable footing, lighting, and animal cooperation.

Laboratory animal research vivarium procedure room: repeated IV dosing/tail-vein injections and cannulation of rodents at a procedure bench in a barrier facility — animals retrieved from cages, warmed/restrained, vein located, dose delivered and recorded, high throughput across a study cohort.

sources.system: Automated handheld venipuncture device (VascuLogic / Rutgers, VenousPro lineage)
sources.developer: VascuLogic LLC / Rutgers University (Leipheimer, Balter, Yarmush)
sources.title: First-in-human evaluation of a hand-held automated venipuncture device for rapid venous blood draws | TECHNOLOGY
sources.claim: A handheld image-guided robotic venipuncture device (VascuLogic lineage, Rutgers) autonomously identifies a vein with ultrasound and robotically drives a needle into the lumen, evaluated first-in-human on adult volunteers' arms; it performs venous blood draw/cannulation on bare human skin with the arm supported, not on furred veterinary patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture/cannulation in humans. It is the closest demonstrated capability to placing an IV catheter, but the demonstrations are on bare human forearms with the limb supported; there is no demonstration on clipped, furred canine/feline limbs, nor of advancing the catheter off the stylet, taping it in, and connecting a fluid line, so it does not substantiate completion of the veterinary instance.

sources.system: Stereo-vision high-throughput mouse tail vein injection robot
sources.title: Development of a Stereo-Vision Based High-Throughput Robotic System for Mouse Tail Vein Injection (arXiv:2205.12756)
sources.claim: A robotic mouse tail-vein injection system uses stereo NIR vision plus a purpose-built mouse holding mechanism (tourniquet, vacuum port, adaptive tail-end fixture) to autonomously locate the vein and inject unanesthetized mice, succeeding in 37 of 40 in vivo injections (92.5%).
sources.transferJustification: Directly on point for the research-vivarium instance: automated intravenous access and dosing in a rodent, the same procedure a laboratory-animal vet tech performs, but only with the animal loaded into the machine's own holding fixture.

sources.system: A-VAS automated mouse tail vascular access system
sources.title: An Automated Mouse Tail Vascular Access System by Vision and Pressure Feedback - PubMed
sources.claim: An automated vascular access system ... vision-based vein/needle detection and real-time pressure feedback performs murine tail-vein drug delivery on an animal holding platform; reported successful intravenous injection rates around 90% and more consistent than a routine (non-expert) human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same procedure class as the research-vivarium instance (intravenous access/dosing in a laboratory rodent), performed by a benchtop machine with its own animal holding platform; corroborates the Preferred Networks result.

sources.title: RDP | Rodent Dose Puller | Instech Laboratories
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial automation for rodent oral gavage automates only syringe filling from a LIMS-specified dose; a human technician still restrains the animal and passes the feeding tube into the esophagus.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: oral gavage dosing. It shows the state of automation for gavage stops short of the physical intubation and delivery step, so it cannot substantiate completion of any gavage instance.

tasks.label: Fill prescriptions, measuring medications and labeling containers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic pharmacy area: tech fills a take-home oral-solid prescription (e.g., 60 carprofen tablets, 14 clavamox capsules) by counting tablets from a stock bottle on a counting tray, pouring into a vial, capping, printing and affixing the patient/owner label with directions and warning stickers.

Clinic pharmacy: prescription is filled with a manufacturer's original package — a box of flea/tick preventive, a tube of ophthalmic ointment, a bottle of ear drops, an insulin pen — pulled from the shelf and a dispensing label with patient name and directions printed and applied to the package.

Clinic pharmacy: measuring a liquid — pouring/pumping a measured volume of oral suspension into a dispensing bottle, or drawing a weight-based dose of liquid (e.g., 2.5 mL metronidazole suspension per dose) into oral dosing syringes — then labeling with dose and directions.

Treatment area/pharmacy of a clinic or referral hospital: drawing an injectable dose from a stock vial into a syringe, or reconstituting a lyophilized product (vaccine, chemo agent, insulin dilution) to a prescribed concentration, then labeling the syringe/vial with drug, concentration, dose and date for in-hospital or take-home use.

Large-animal/ambulatory practice: dispensing medication at the farm or from the practice truck — counting boluses, filling a bottle of oral drench or measuring an injectable, hand-writing or printing a label with withdrawal times, in variable weather on uneven ground away from the clinic.

sources.system: ScriptPro SP 200 robotic prescription dispensing system
sources.title: SP 200 with Open Control Center - ScriptPro
sources.claim: ScriptPro SP 200 robotic dispensing system counts tablets and capsules into standard pharmacy vials and prints and applies the prescription ..., presenting the finished vial for staff verification; installed behind pharmacy counters as a fixed, cell-fed machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in human pharmacy: count a prescribed quantity of solid oral dosage forms into a vial and label it. Veterinary oral-solid prescriptions use identical dosage forms, vials and label stock.

sources.title: ScriptPro Robot Fills Pet Prescriptions at 1-800-PetMeds
sources.claim: ScriptPro vial-filling robots are used by a pet pharmacy to fill veterinary prescriptions for dogs, cats and horses, showing the same automation applied to animal-patient prescriptions.

sources.title: Parata Max™ 2: High-Speed Automation for Smarter Vial Filling - RXinsider
sources.claim: Parata Max 2 vial-filling robot automates every step of oral-solid dispensing — labeling, counting, filling, capping and sorting — in production pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Human-pharmacy prescription filling is the same physical operation (count solid dosage forms into a labeled vial) that a veterinary technician performs for take-home animal prescriptions.

sources.title: Fully Automated Vial Filling Robot | McKesson Pharmacy Automation
sources.claim: McKesson CountMate uses two robotic arms to ..., photograph, label and sort prescription vials with minimal human intervention inside a self-contained cabinet in the pharmacy.
sources.transferJustification: Same counting-into-vial-and-label operation as a veterinary technician filling an oral-solid prescription.

sources.title: World's first fully robotic pharmacy automates prescription dispensing
sources.claim: Queue's autonomous robotic pharmacy accepts sealed manufacturer bottles and, using robotics and computer vision, handles storage, counting, dispensing and verification to produce patient-ready labeled prescription vials; kiosks were placed in One Medical clinics in Los Angeles from December 2025.
sources.transferJustification: End-to-end prescription filling (stock bottle to labeled patient container) is the same operation the veterinary technician performs; the machine is a purpose-built enclosure sited inside a clinic.

sources.title: Startup Queue lands $12.6M to launch autonomous robotic pharmacy kiosks
sources.claim: Queue's fully autonomous prescription kiosks were launched commercially in One Medical clinic locations, stocked with commonly prescribed medications.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment evidence for the same prescription-filling machine cited above.

sources.title: Process performance of a new liquid medication dispensing robot - PubMed
sources.claim: The Nooddis liquid medication dispensing robot fills exact prescribed volumes of oral liquid medication into containers with in-line gravimetric checkweighing, and met required pharmaceutical quality standards in a peer-reviewed process evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated measuring of prescribed volumes of oral liquid into dispensing containers, the same physical operation as a vet tech measuring an oral suspension dose; comparable volumes, viscosities and accuracy requirements.

sources.title: IV Compounding Robot - ARxIUM (pppmag findit)
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA is a fully automated IV compounding robot that withdraws measured drug volumes from vials into syringes, labels them and requires no operator intervention ... run; it has prepared over 14 million doses across hospital pharmacy installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: drawing a measured injectable dose from a stock vial into a syringe and labeling it — the same operation a veterinary technician performs when preparing and labeling injectable doses.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: A US hospital placed the RIVA robotic IV compounding system into routine pharmacy production, confirming deployment of automated syringe/bag preparation at worker-replacing quality.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment evidence for the measured-dose-into-labeled-syringe operation cited above.

sources.title: Performance evaluation of the compounding robot, APOTECAchemo, for injectable anticancer drugs in a Japanese hospital
sources.claim: The APOTECAchemo compounding robot prepared injectable doses (including reconstitution of lyophilized drugs) in routine hospital practice with dose accuracy and precision better than manual preparation by pharmacists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measuring drug from vials and reconstituting powdered product to a prescribed dose — matches the vet tech's vaccine/injectable preparation step in objects handled and precision required.

sources.title: Labelers | Print and Apply Labeling | Label Applicators | Videojet
sources.claim: Print-and-apply labeling machines automatically print a made-to-order label and apply it to boxes and other package surfaces on a production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a printed prescription label to a manufacturer's carton or bottle — identical physical act to the vet tech labeling an original-package dispensing item, on comparable objects.

tasks.label: Collect, prepare, and label samples for laboratory testing, culture, or microscopic examination.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic treatment area: draw blood from a conscious dog or cat (jugular, cephalic, or medial saphenous) while a colleague restrains the patient; select needle and tubes, hit the vein without hematoma or hemolysis, fill EDTA/serum/citrate tubes in order, invert, and label each tube with patient ID.

Small-animal clinic: non-blood diagnostic sampling from conscious patients - free-catch or catheterized urine and holding for ultrasound-guided cystocentesis, fecal loop sampling, skin scrapes, ear swabs, fine-needle aspirates and impression smears, culture swabs - then making, fixing and labeling the resulting slides and containers.

In-house or reference lab bench: process already-collected blood - spin down and pipette serum/plasma into aliquot tubes, run hematocrit tubes, make and stain a blood film, label tubes and slides with patient ID, load analyzers.

Preparing and labeling heterogeneous specimens for the outside reference lab: place surgical biopsies into formalin jars, decant owner-brought urine or feces into transport containers, match each container to the requisition and patient record, bag and assemble the courier shipping kit.

Large-animal or ambulatory work at a farm, barn or stable: jugular blood draw from cattle in a chute or horses in stocks, fecal collection per rectum, aseptic milk samples for mastitis culture; outdoors or in a barn aisle with variable footing, lighting and animal cooperation; tubes labeled in the field.

Research vivarium or CRO: serial blood sampling from catheterized rats or mice on a pharmacokinetic schedule, with aliquots collected into chilled, pre-identified vials at precise timepoints and logged against the study protocol.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Aletta is a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that identifies veins with multimodal imaging and performs diagnostic venous blood draws on humans in outpatient phlebotomy departments; it is the nearest existing analogue to venipuncture on a patient, but it operates on a bare, cooperative human arm positioned in the device's own armrest fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: human diagnostic venipuncture. Cited to establish the state of the art ... its limits: the device draws from a bare human arm immobilized in its armrest, with standard adult anatomy and voluntary cooperation. It does not transfer to a furred, unanesthetized dog, cat, or cow whose vein must be raised by a restrainer, so it cannot support a positive judgment on any animal-facing instance.

sources.title: SP-50 - Products Detail (Sysmex Europe)
sources.claim: The Sysmex SP-50 autonomously prepares and stains blood films from whole-blood tubes and prints the sample identification barcode onto each slide; a configuration is sold specifically for veterinary diagnostics with animal blood ....

sources.title: cobas 8100 automated workflow series
sources.claim: The cobas 8100 pre-analytical automation series, deployed in core clinical laboratories, autonomously centrifuges tubes, decaps and recaps them, applies barcode labels to secondary tubes, prepares aliquots from primary samples, and sorts and transports them to analyzers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: human clinical specimen pre-analytics. Transfers to veterinary sample preparation because the objects (barcoded blood tubes), the operations (spin, aliquot, label) and the laboratory setting are the same; veterinary reference labs use the same tube formats and instruments.

sources.system: FlexLab total laboratory automation (Aliquoter, Centrifuge modules)
sources.title: Pre-analytical Modules for FlexLab
sources.claim: Inpeco FlexLab pre-analytical modules automate centrifugation and generate labelled secondary tubes by aspirating configurable volumes from primary tubes, at up to 500 tubes per ..., in installed clinical laboratory automation lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: human clinical specimen pre-analytics. Same tube handling, aliquoting and labelling operations on the same consumables as veterinary in-lab sample preparation.

sources.system: Culex NxT Automated Blood Sampling System with Raturn caging
sources.title: BASi Culex NxT (product brochure)
sources.claim: The BASi Culex NxT automated in vivo sampling system, used commercially by pharmaceutical companies, CROs and universities, programmatically collects blood and other fluids from awake, freely moving catheterized rodents and larger species into refrigerated vials with automatic logging, replacing manual serial sampling.

sources.system: Herd Navigator (with DeLaval VMS robotic milking)
sources.title: Dairy farm reaps benefits from milk analysis technology
sources.claim: DeLaval Herd Navigator takes milk samples automatically through a sampler built into the milking system and routes them one by one to an analysis unit on commercial dairy farms; it does not perform aseptic sampling for external culture or any blood or fecal collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated on-farm milk sampling. Cited to bound the large-animal instance: it shows the only deployed automated farm sampling covers inline milk to a fixed analyzer inside the milking box, not jugular blood, fecal or aseptic culture sampling, so it cannot complete that instance.

tasks.label: Prepare animals for surgery, performing such tasks as shaving surgical areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal general practice: routine elective surgery (spay/neuter, mass removal, dental extraction) on a dog or cat. Tech restrains the awake, often anxious patient, induces anesthesia, intubates, places an IV catheter, clips fur over the surgical field with electric clippers, vacuums loose hair, performs the chlorhexidine/alcohol aseptic scrub, carries and positions the patient on the table, and attaches monitoring leads.

Emergency/specialty referral hospital: prep of a sick, painful, or unstable patient (GDV, C-section, fracture repair, exploratory laparotomy). Large or hanging-limb clips, sterile limb wrap, careful handling of a fragile or fractious patient, multiple catheters, prep done under time pressure alongside anesthesia induction.

High-volume spay/neuter or shelter clinic: assembly-line prep of dozens of cats and dogs per day, standardized small clip areas (ventral midline or scrotum), rapid injectable induction, quick scrub, patients moved on gurneys between induction and surgery stations.

Equine/large-animal hospital surgical suite: horse induced in a padded induction stall, hoisted by hoist and positioned on a tilt/surgery table, large clip area, hoof wrapped, extensive aseptic scrub of a limb or abdomen, tech works around a 1,000+ lb sedated animal.

Laboratory animal facility: rodent (mouse/rat) surgery prep — anesthetize in an induction chamber, weigh, clip or depilate a small site, apply antiseptic and ophthalmic ointment, position on a warming pad or stereotaxic frame under a hood.

On-farm/field large animal prep: standing flank surgery on a cow in a chute or barn alley, or on-farm equine castration/laceration repair — restrain, sedate, clip the site with a hand clipper, scrub, and prepare for a local block, on uneven footing with variable lighting, dust, and manure.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Dairy Farming: How Robots Benefit Cows & Farmers - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Commercial robotic milking systems autonomously clean a live cow's teats and attach teat cups using laser/3D-camera guidance inside a purpose-built milking box — the strongest existing example of autonomous manipulation on a live, unrestrained animal, but limited to one fixed contact action in a machine-built enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated udder cleaning and teat-cup attachment on a live animal. It shows live-animal contact manipulation is possible in a purpose-built box, but it is a single repetitive action on one anatomical target with no fur clipping, aseptic scrub, intubation, catheterization, or patient transfer, so it does not transfer to surgical prep.

sources.system: Stereo-vision high-throughput mouse tail vein injection robot
sources.title: Development of a Stereo-vision based High-throughput Robotic System for Mouse Tail Vein Injection | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: A research robot performs mouse tail-vein injection with the animal held in a purpose-built fixture and stereo-vision vein detection; a laboratory prototype for one needle-insertion step, not for anesthesia, clipping, or antiseptic prep.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated vascular access in a fixtured rodent, comparable to placing an IV line during rodent prep. It covers only needle insertion into an immobilized tail and does not perform induction, site clipping, antiseptic scrub, or positioning, so it cannot complete a whole prep instance.

sources.title: Robot Automates Blood Drawing and Testing - Tech Briefs
sources.claim: Automated venipuncture robots that autonomously image a vein and insert a needle have reached human clinical trials, but remain research devices covering only the cannulation step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle placement in a fixtured human arm, analogous to IV catheter placement during surgical prep. It requires a cooperative, immobilized limb in a fixture and does not address animal restraint, anesthesia, clipping, or aseptic scrub of a surgical field.

sources.system: Australian robotic sheep-shearing prototype (SCU/Rethink Robotics arms)
sources.title: Australians developing robotic sheep-shearing system
sources.claim: Robotic shearing of animals — the closest analogue to clipping fur from a live animal's body surface — remains a prototype effort; the Australian robotic sheep-shearing work was tested on a 3D-printed sheep rather than live animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic clipping of fur/wool from an animal body surface, the mechanically closest analogue to shaving a surgical field. Testing on a rigid printed model rather than a live, deformable, breathing animal means it does not substantiate clipping a live patient at any tier.

sources.system: Veterinary surgical robot platforms (e.g., CMR Surgical-type systems)
sources.title: Can Robotics and AI be useful for Automating Tasks in Veterinary Clinics
sources.claim: Coverage of robotics in veterinary medicine describes surgical robots as teleoperated instrument platforms controlled by the veterinarian, with no autonomous system performing patient preparation tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic veterinary surgery. These are master-slave teleoperated instrument platforms operating inside an already-prepped patient; they perform no restraint, clipping, or aseptic prep and are continuously surgeon-driven, so they cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Take and develop diagnostic radiographs, using x-ray equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Survey radiographs (thorax and/or abdomen) of a dog or cat in a small-animal clinic's radiology room: retrieve the patient, lift it onto the table, restrain it manually or with V-trough, sandbags, ties and foam wedges (often awake or lightly sedated), take right-lateral and ventrodorsal views, set/verify technique, check each image for positioning and exposure, retake if needed, label and send to PACS.

Orthopedic/appendicular or spinal study on a sedated dog: extended-hip pelvic (e.g., OFA-style) views, stifle/elbow/carpus views, requiring precise pulling, rotating and holding of limbs, collimation to the joint, multiple orthogonal views with repositioning of the animal between exposures, and image QC before the vet reads them.

Full-mouth dental radiographic series on an anesthetized dog or cat: repeated placement of a small intraoral sensor or plate inside the mouth, bisecting-angle aiming of a dental tube head for each of roughly six to ten views, repositioning the head and sensor between exposures, and reviewing each image for diagnostic quality.

Equine limb/foot radiographs taken in a barn aisle, stall or at a show with a portable generator and a plate in a holder: horse standing (possibly on positioning blocks), handler holding the head, tech kneeling beside the limb to place the plate and aim the beam at multiple oblique angles, variable footing, lighting and distractions.

Emergency/critical or exotic patient: a painful trauma dog imaged where it lies (cage-side or on a gurney with a portable unit), or a bird, reptile or pocket pet taped to an acrylic board; views improvised around the patient's condition, minimal handling tolerated, images needed within minutes.

sources.system: Definium 656 HD (with Intelligent Workflow Suite, Auto Protocol Assist, Auto Field of View, Helix)
sources.title: Definium™ 656 HD | GE HealthCare
sources.claim: GE HealthCare's Definium 656 HD fixed radiography system automates the equipment side of a radiographic exam: protocol selection from the worklist, motorized 5-axis tube/table/wall-stand positioning to the location for the selected view, automatic collimation field size, automatic technique setting from measured patient thickness, and AI image processing of the acquired radiograph.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is human diagnostic radiography. Same modality, same equipment class, same acceptance standard (diagnostic image quality) as veterinary DR; once a patient/animal is presented in a known position, the machine-controlled steps (view geometry, collimation, exposure factors, image processing) are identical.

sources.title: Twin Robotic X-ray scanner – Multitom Rax - Siemens Healthineers
sources.claim: Siemens Healthineers' Multitom Rax twin-robotic X-ray system moves its tube and detector robotically to acquire complex projections, self-positioning and self-aligning for exams such as an axial hip that otherwise require laborious manual detector placement, and moving from AP straight to a ... without repositioning the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is human radiography of orthopedic/trauma patients. It shows a robot, not a person, establishing view geometry and acquiring orthogonal views around a stationary patient — the step that in veterinary radiography otherwise forces re-handling the animal between lateral and VD views.

sources.system: Language-promptable digital twin control of a robotic C-arm X-ray device
sources.title: Intelligent Control of Robotic X-ray Devices using a Language-promptable Digital Twin (arXiv:2412.08020)
sources.claim: A research robotic C-arm X-ray system autonomously finds anatomy-specific views and collimates on a real body: a language-promptable digital twin drives patient-specific viewfinding and automatic collimation, validated in a cadaver study with 84% end-to-end success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous radiographic view-finding on a human cadaver. It substantiates the perception step a vet tech performs — choosing beam geometry and collimation for the requested anatomy — on a subject that is presented and does not move.

sources.system: Asto CT Equina standing equine CT scanner
sources.title: Virginia Equine Imaging Introduces Asto CT Equina® Standing CT Scanner - EquiManagement
sources.claim: The Asto CT Equina is a commercially installed veterinary X-ray-based scanner in which a mildly sedated standing horse is led into a purpose-built machine and the scanner acquires limb and head/neck images automatically, without general anesthesia; multiple US equine hospitals have installed it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is X-ray imaging of equine limbs. It is the same anatomy and patient species as barn-side limb radiography, and shows that once the horse is presented in the purpose-built cell the imaging geometry and acquisition are executed by the machine rather than by a technician holding a plate.

sources.system: Vimago HDVI robotic veterinary imaging platform
sources.date: 2016 (product listing); in clinical veterinary use through 2025
sources.title: Veterinary CT scanner - Vimago™ - Epica Medical Innovations
sources.claim: Epica's Vimago is a robotic veterinary imaging platform combining CT, fluoroscopy and digital radiography, installed in general veterinary hospitals and in mobile units, imaging anesthetized/positioned animal patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is veterinary diagnostic X-ray imaging. Supporting context that robotic X-ray gantries are already the acquisition device in veterinary practice; autonomy of the console workflow is not documented, so it is not relied on for a positive judgment.

sources.system: Automated inline X-ray inspection systems (food processing)
sources.developer: Multiple vendors (e.g., Nordson AXI, Sesotec, Mettler-Toledo); described by Province of Manitoba Agriculture
sources.date: Undated government guidance page, current as of 2026
sources.title: Province of Manitoba | agriculture - X-ray Inspection Systems in Food Processing Plants
sources.claim: Industrial X-ray inspection lines acquire radiographs of objects presented by a conveyor or fixture and evaluate the resulting images entirely under machine control, with no operator viewing the image.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is radiographic image acquisition and evaluation of biological material (bone in meat, foreign bodies). It establishes that the full loop — present object, expose, produce and judge the radiograph — runs unattended in a purpose-built cell, though the objects are inanimate.

tasks.label: Discuss medical health of pets with clients, such as post-operative status.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Clean kennels, animal holding areas, surgery suites, examination rooms, or animal loading or unloading facilities to control the spread of disease.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal practice dog ward/boarding runs: after a patient is moved out or discharged, the tech removes bedding, bowls and toys, scoops feces and hoses urine to the drain, scrubs the run floor and gate, applies disinfectant for contact time, rinses, squeegees dry and re-beds; adjacent runs are occupied and animals are barking and moving.

Cat ward and small-enclosure cages in a clinic or shelter: remove soiled litter box, towels and dishes, wipe cage interior walls/floor/door with disinfectant and let it dwell, dry, then replace bedding, litter and bowls; done cage-by-cage in a banked ward with patients present.

Exam-room turnover between appointments: spray and wipe the exam table, scale, counter and door handles with disinfectant, sweep or vacuum shed hair, mop urine/vomit accidents on the floor, discard used gauze/needles into biohazard and sharps containers, restock supplies - under time pressure with the next client waiting.

Surgery suite and prep/treatment area: between procedures wipe down the surgery table, lights, anesthesia machine, monitors and instrument tables, mop the floor, remove contaminated drapes and waste; end-of-day terminal clean of the suite before restocking sterile packs.

Daily floor care in a larger referral hospital, shelter or university teaching hospital: sweeping, mopping/scrubbing and disinfecting corridors, ward aisles, treatment-room and lobby floors on a set schedule.

Equine/food-animal clinic: muck out stalls and isolation stalls, scrape and pressure-wash concrete holding pens, and wash and disinfect the loading chute, ramp and trailer surfaces after animals are unloaded.

sources.title: EVO Cleaner for pig barns - Envirologic
sources.claim: EVO Cleaner is a commercially sold washing robot that washes pig barn pens and interiors on taught routines, running unattended around the clock and notifying staff when finished.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: biosecurity washdown of emptied animal housing. Same objective as cleaning kennels/animal holding areas (remove organic soil, apply disinfectant to floors, walls and pen partitions), same hard concrete/steel surfaces and same soil (manure, urine); it operates only in emptied, drained, purpose-built animal rooms after per-building teaching.

sources.title: Go Cleaner for poultry barns - Envirologic
sources.claim: Go Cleaner is a fully ... that positions itself with radar and washes an entire emptied broiler house - floors, ceilings and feed/water lines - with seven degrees of freedom.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing and disinfecting an entire animal holding room including its fixtures. Transfers to cleaning kennels/holding areas because the workpiece (soiled animal-room floor, walls and fittings) and the disease-control purpose are the same; it requires the room to be emptied of animals and people.

sources.title: Cage automation - Tecniplast - PDF Catalogs
sources.claim: IWT/Tecniplast Apollo robots automate cleaning of laboratory animal cages: the robot disassembles the cage, dumps soiled bedding and waste feed, and presents the parts to the washer-disinfector in a dedicated cage-wash area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sanitizing animal enclosures in an animal facility. It is the same work as cleaning kennels/cages (empty soiled bedding, wash and thermally disinfect the enclosure, return it ready for an animal), performed on caged-animal housing, but in a purpose-built cage-wash line the cages are brought to.

sources.title: AUTOMATION MAKING THE DIFFERENCE IN A MODERN VIVARIUM - Panorama Newsletter
sources.claim: Robotic cage-processing systems are installed and in routine production use in vivaria, including a university facility that cleans about 5,000 individually ventilated cages weekly with an Apollo robot.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: evidences real, sustained deployment (not a demo) of robotic animal-enclosure cleaning inside purpose-built cage-wash rooms.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot autonomously cleans fixtures and floors and picks up trash in restrooms, and is deployed in hospitals and airports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: turnover cleaning and disinfection of a small, hard-surfaced room in an institutional facility - spraying disinfectant on fixtures, wiping, and vacuuming/mopping the floor. Comparable in room size, surfaces and precision to disinfecting a veterinary exam room, though fixtures are standardized and each room is taught in advance.

sources.title: Those viral bathroom-cleaning bots won't be saving our butts anytime soon (Popular Science)
sources.claim: Somatic's robot does not handle consumable restocking or trash removal, which still require facility staff.
sources.transferJustification: Limits evidence: shows the residual manual steps (waste handling, restocking) that keep exam-room and surgery-suite turnover from being fully completed by these robots in a working human facility.

sources.title: Primech launches upgraded bathroom cleaning robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Primech's HYTRON mobile manipulator cleans restrooms in airports, hospitals, hotels and offices, navigating tight spaces autonomously; it completed first commercial trials in September ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-arm surface cleaning and disinfection of small institutional rooms, corroborating that spray/wipe room turnover is within reach of fielded mobile manipulators in standardized rooms.

sources.date: 2025-11 (case study); deployed in US hospitals since 2019
sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals (Onshape case study)
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo autonomous floor scrubbers are deployed in hospitals and other large facilities, scrubbing floors without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled scrubbing and disinfecting of corridor and ward floors in a healthcare facility - the same open-floor cleaning that veterinary hospital corridors, treatment rooms and lobbies require.

sources.title: Revolutionizing Dairy Farming: How Robots Benefit Cows & Farmers - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Lely's Discovery Collector is an autonomous manure-vacuum robot, commercially introduced in 2016, that cleans barn floors day and night on programmed routes while cows are present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing manure from large-animal holding floors in an occupied livestock building. Relevant to cleaning large-animal holding areas, but it only collects manure from alley floors - it does not muck bedded stalls, wash, or disinfect.

sources.title: Biosecurity Wash Systems For Farms and Transport Fleets - InterClean
sources.claim: Automated biosecurity vehicle-wash installations wash and disinfect livestock trailers and trucks in purpose-built drive-through wash bays to prevent pathogen transfer to farms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine washing and disinfecting of animal loading/unloading equipment (livestock trailers) for disease control, done in a fixed wash bay the work is driven into - the E1 presentation of the loading-facility cleaning instance.

sources.title: Disinfection robot boosts sanitation at veterinary medical teaching hospital (Texas A&M / TechXplore)
sources.claim: A UV-C disinfection robot in service at a veterinary medical teaching hospital is used only as an adjunct after manual cleaning and must be placed in the room by staff.
sources.transferJustification: Directly in the task's setting (veterinary hospital rooms and surgery suites), but it disinfects only after humans have removed the soil and it does not move itself, so it cannot substantiate completion of the cleaning instances.

tasks.label: Take animals into treatment areas and assist with physical examinations by performing such duties as obtaining temperature, pulse, or respiration data.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal general practice: technician leashes a dog in the exam room or lobby, walks it back to the treatment area, weighs it, lifts small dogs onto the table or kneels for large ones, restrains the patient while obtaining a rectal temperature, palpating a femoral pulse, and counting respirations, then records vitals and assists the veterinarian's physical exam (holding for otoscopy, auscultation, abdominal palpation).

Feline patient: technician removes a cat from a carrier (or unscrews the carrier top), carries it to the treatment area, uses low-stress or towel restraint, obtains rectal or axillary temperature, heart rate by auscultation/femoral pulse, and respiratory rate, while managing a squirming, hissing, or fear-aggressive cat.

Difficult or urgent patient in a companion-animal hospital: aggressive or painful dog requiring muzzle and two-person restraint, or a recumbent/collapsed emergency patient moved by stretcher or gurney into the treatment area for rapid triage vitals (TPR, mucous membranes, capillary refill) delivered within seconds to minutes.

Exotic/pocket pet, bird, or reptile in a companion-animal or exotics practice: technician transfers a rabbit, ferret, guinea pig, parrot, or lizard from carrier to treatment area with species-specific handling, obtains temperature, heart rate (Doppler or stethoscope), and respiration on a fragile, easily stressed patient.

Research vivarium, teaching hospital, or animal shelter: technician moves dogs, rabbits, or rodents from housing rooms/kennels into a procedure or exam room, restrains for health checks, and records temperature, heart rate, and respiration under institutional SOPs.

Large-animal/equine practice: technician leads a horse from stall or trailer into stocks or an exam bay (or restrains cattle in a chute on-farm), holds the animal while obtaining rectal temperature, pulse at the facial/coccygeal artery, and respiratory rate, in a barn aisle, farm handling facility, or field setting.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Autonomous rail-suspended robot in commercial broiler houses monitors flock conditions with thermal and light cameras and environmental sensors; it monitors birds at flock level but does not move individual animals or obtain individual temperature, pulse, and respiration measurements.
sources.transferJustification: Closest commercial robot for animal health monitoring; cited to show the limit — it senses flock-level thermal/behavioural indicators from above and never handles an animal or obtains individual TPR, so it cannot substitute for the technician's exam duties.

sources.title: The history of the milking robot Lely Astronaut
sources.claim: Commercial robotic milking systems autonomously locate teats and attach cups to live dairy cows that enter the box voluntarily, demonstrating reliable autonomous physical contact with livestock in a purpose-built cell, but they measure milk parameters rather than the animal's temperature, pulse, or respiration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (attaching milking cups to a live cow) shows autonomous manipulation on an animal's body in a purpose-built cell; cited to bound the capability — no rectal thermometry, pulse palpation, or respiration counting is performed, and the cow presents itself voluntarily rather than being handled.

sources.title: A barn divided: How to get the most out of a separation pen in a robotic milking facility
sources.claim: In robotic milking facilities, automatic sort gates route individual cows needing treatment into separation pens as they leave ... box — an automated way of directing an animal into a treatment area in a purpose-built dairy, without any physical examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (moving an animal to a treatment area) is partially automated by gates in a purpose-built dairy; it covers only the transport half of the task for self-locomoting cattle and provides no restraint or vital-sign acquisition.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with vital-sign camera payload)
sources.developer: MIT / Boston Dynamics / Brigham and Women's Hospital
sources.title: Robot Takes Contact-free Measurements of Patients' Vital Signs | MIT for a Better World
sources.claim: A quadruped robot carrying cameras measured skin temperature, breathing rate, pulse ... oxygen saturation of human patients contactlessly at 2 m in a hospital triage setting, but the robot was driven to each patient by a health care worker with a handheld controller.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (obtaining temperature, pulse and respiration data on a live patient) is the closest robotic demonstration, but it is teleoperated, contact-free on cooperative bare-skinned humans, and does not transfer to furred, uncooperative animals requiring rectal thermometry and manual restraint.

sources.developer: University of Sydney Australian Centre for Field Robotics / Agerris
sources.title: Robot Leads Cattle to Greener Fields (VOA Learning English)
sources.claim: An autonomous field robot moves cattle between paddocks on Australian grazing land, showing autonomous livestock movement outdoors, but performs no handling, restraint, or clinical measurement of individual animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (moving animals from one place to another) is demonstrated autonomously for herd-level cattle movement; it does not extend to leading an individual animal into an exam area or to obtaining temperature, pulse, or respiration.

sources.title: Robotic Cage Handling System for Tunnel Washers - Getinge
sources.claim: Robotic automation in laboratory animal facilities handles cages and racks in the wash process, not the animals themselves; no commercial vivarium robot removes an animal from its enclosure or takes its vital signs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated handling in a vivarium) is limited to empty caging equipment; because the robot never contacts a live animal, it gives no support for transferring animals to a procedure room or obtaining TPR.

tasks.label: Prepare treatment rooms for surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal general practice: turnover of the surgery suite between scheduled procedures (spay/neuter, dental extraction, mass removal). Disinfect table and counters, mop/spot-clean floor, empty waste and sharps, set up the anesthesia machine (attach breathing circuit, check O2 tank and scavenging, fill isoflurane vaporizer, leak-test), connect monitor leads/ETCO2, place warming device, open a wrapped sterile pack aseptically onto a Mayo stand, lay out drapes, gown, blade, suture, and stage clippers and scrub solutions.

Emergency/specialty hospital: rapid, case-specific setup for an urgent or specialty procedure (orthopedic repair, GDV, C-section, endoscopy-assisted). Bring in and position case-specific equipment — power drill and implant sets, suction, fluid warmer/pump, cautery, C-arm or scope tower — plus the standard anesthesia and sterile setup, under time pressure and with the case type sometimes changing mid-prep.

High-volume spay/neuter or shelter clinic: repetitive prep of several identical surgery stations. Wipe/disinfect tables between patients, replace drapes and pads, pull autoclaved packs and open them to the sterile field, refill scrub and suture stations, reset anesthesia circuits and warming pads on a fast cycle.

Start-of-day / end-of-day readiness of the surgery and treatment rooms: terminal clean of floors, tables, lights, and equipment surfaces; restock cabinets, drawers, and crash cart with gauze, gloves, ET tubes, syringes and fluids; check oxygen supply and scavenging canister; stage the day's sterilized packs, gowns, and drapes for scheduled cases.

Equine/large-animal hospital: prepare padded induction and recovery stalls and the surgical suite — hose and disinfect walls and floor, position the hydraulic surgery table and hoist, set out the large-animal anesthesia machine and demand valve, hang fluids, and lay out large sterile packs and drapes.

Ambulatory/field call: create a working surgical area at a client's barn or pasture — clear and sweep a stall or aisle, set a tailgate or portable table, lay out a clean drape, buckets of scrub, portable light and clippers from the truck for a standing procedure or field castration, with variable footing, lighting, dust, and livestock nearby.

In-house laboratory equipment upkeep: run QC control material on the hematology and chemistry analyzers, verify calibration, swap reagent/consumable packs and waste, run cleaning/rinse and probe-wash cycles, plus clean the centrifuge rotor and microscope optics.

Routine cleaning and lubrication of powered and hand instruments: flush and oil dental high- and low-speed handpieces, check ultrasonic scaler tips, clean, disinfect and oil clipper blades, leak-test and reprocess a flexible endoscope, ultrasonically clean and lubricate hinged instruments.

Animal-housing and washing equipment upkeep in a clinic kennel or research vivarium: run cages, racks, bowls and bottles through the cage/rack/tunnel washer, keep washers and bedding-disposal units charged and functioning, sanitize and check cage doors, dryers and water systems.

Scheduled preventive checks, calibration and minor repair/troubleshooting across mixed clinic equipment (scales, dental unit compressor, radiography and ultrasound units, IV/syringe pumps, warming devices, autoclave gaskets and water), completing logs and staging items for vendor service; in mixed/ambulatory practice this work is done on the practice truck and at farms.
