emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

emergingTasks.label: Perform examinations using ophthalmic equipment, such as autorefractors, phoropters, tomographs, or retinoscopes.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
aliases: Home Health Licensed Practical Nurse (Home Health LPN)
Long Term Care LPN (Long Term Care Licensed Practical Nurse)
Nursing Home LPN (Nursing Home Licensed Practical Nurse)
Private Duty Licensed Practical Nurse (Private Duty LPN)
roles.description: Care for ill, injured, or convalescing patients or persons with disabilities in hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, private homes, group homes, and similar institutions. May work under the supervision of a registered nurse. Licensing required.

tasks.label: Observe patients, charting and reporting changes in patients' conditions, such as adverse reactions to medication or treatment, and taking any necessary action.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing facility / long-term care shift rounds: LPN observes 15-30 residents (skin integrity, mental status, appetite and intake, pain, breathing, gait), spots a change such as new lethargy or confusion after a medication change, takes vitals and a fingerstick glucose, charts in the facility EHR, reports to the charge RN/provider, and acts (repositions, applies oxygen, holds the next dose, initiates fall precautions).

Hospital or subacute inpatient unit: LPN monitors a medically complex or post-op patient after a medication or treatment, watching for adverse reaction (rash, itching, hypotension, dyspnea, infiltrated IV site, bleeding), stops or slows the infusion, checks vitals, escalates to the RN/rapid response, and documents the event and response in the chart.

Home health or hospice visit in a private residence: LPN observes the patient in a cluttered, non-standard home (dim light, pets, family present), assesses vitals, wound, edema, and medication side effects, notes decline, phones the case-manager RN or physician, adjusts care (elevates legs, replaces a dressing, coaches the caregiver), and charts on a laptop/tablet.

Physician office, clinic, or infusion suite: LPN rooms the patient, takes vitals, observes the patient for 15-30 minutes after an injection, vaccine, or allergy shot for adverse reaction, documents observations in the EHR, alerts the provider to abnormal findings, and administers emergency treatment (epinephrine, oxygen) if anaphylaxis occurs.

Group home, assisted living, or correctional infirmary med pass follow-up: LPN observes residents/inmates after administering medications for sedation, GI upset, tremor, behavior change, or blood-pressure drop, documents on the MAR/nursing note, reports to the supervising RN or provider, and takes action such as withholding a dose or arranging transfer.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The most widely deployed autonomous hospital robot in the US, Diligent Robotics' Moxi, performs supply and medication delivery and item fetching in hospital corridors; its deployed capability set does not include patient observation, clinical assessment, charting of patient condition, or clinical intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital logistics. Cited to establish the ceiling of fielded, autonomous hospital robotics in the same E2 setting (patient units and corridors); the deployed function is fetch-and-deliver, so it does not transfer to bedside observation, charting of condition changes, or intervention.

sources.title: Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulator is built for AI, says Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi's deployed duties in over 25 US hospitals are routine logistics such as delivering medications and supplies; Moxi 2.0 was still pre-deployment as of late 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital delivery. Establishes that the leading commercial hospital robot's autonomous repertoire covers transport, not patient monitoring or nursing judgment, so no transfer to this task.

sources.developer: academic hospital research team (Journal of Medical Systems study)
sources.title: An Assessment of an Inpatient Robotic Nurse Assistant: A Mixed-Method Study
sources.claim: A robotic nurse assistant ('Florence') was trialled on a general medicine ward to support vital-sign measurement, medication and item delivery; it is a research prototype evaluated for usability and acceptance, and it measures vitals rather than detecting and acting on clinical changes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated vital-sign collection on an inpatient ward. This is the closest robotic analogue to nurse observation, but it is a prototype limited to numeric vitals and delivery; it does not perform head-to-toe observation, charting of condition changes, escalation, or intervention.

sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic vital-sign sensing is limited to locating a measurement site on the arm and extracting heart rate, SpO2, respiration and estimated blood pressure; the system is described as semi-autonomous and was validated on healthy adult volunteers, not on detecting or acting on patient deterioration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated physiological measurement. Even under laboratory conditions with cooperative healthy subjects it delivers only numeric vitals, so it cannot substantiate observing a patient for adverse reactions, charting the change, reporting, and taking nursing action.

tasks.label: Measure and record patients' vital signs, such as height, weight, temperature, blood pressure, pulse, or respiration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing / long-term care facility: LPN makes a routine vitals round on generally cooperative residents, going room to room or to the dining area. For each resident (seated in a wheelchair or lying in bed) she rolls up a sleeve, applies and inflates a BP cuff, takes a temporal or tympanic temperature, clips a pulse oximeter, counts respirations by watching the chest, and charts T/P/R/BP/SpO2 in PointClickCare.

Physician office / outpatient clinic: LPN rooms an ambulatory patient — measures height at a wall stadiometer, weight on a standing scale, then seats the patient, places an automated cuff on the bare upper arm at heart level, takes oral or temporal temperature, pulse and respirations, and enters the full set into the EMR before the provider enters.

Hospital or inpatient rehab unit: scheduled q4h/q8h vitals on inpatients who are in bed in gowns, often with IV lines, telemetry leads, or on contact precautions; LPN wheels a vitals machine to the bedside, positions the arm, cuffs it, gets temp and SpO2, counts respirations, obtains a daily standing or bed-scale weight, and documents in the hospital EHR.

Home health or hospice visit in the patient's private residence: LPN carries a bag with cuff, thermometer, pulse oximeter and portable scale into a home of unknown layout (recliner, sofa, hospital bed in the living room, pets, poor lighting), positions the patient, takes the full vitals set and documents on a tablet.

Difficult / exception cases across settings: an agitated or dementia resident who pulls away from the cuff, an obese or edematous arm needing a thigh cuff or manual auscultation with a stethoscope, an orthostatic BP series lying/sitting/standing, weighing a bedbound patient with a bed or Hoyer-lift scale, or pediatric/infant length and weight.

sources.system: Florence robotic nurse assistant (NCS / Alexandra Hospital)
sources.title: An Assessment of an Inpatient Robotic Nurse Assistant: A Mixed-Method Study (Journal of Medical Systems)
sources.claim: Florence, a humanoid robotic nurse assistant, autonomously navigates hospital wards, locates and identifies patients, and measures their vital signs (SpO2, blood pressure, body temperature) via an extending sensor platform in an inpatient ward study.

sources.title: Robot Nurse Takes Pulse in Singapore (CDOTrends)
sources.claim: Florence completed an eight-month trial at Alexandra Hospital taking patients' vital signs at the bedside using camera, sensors and a pulse ..., with results written directly into the national electronic health record.

sources.title: Giant Eagle to deploy higi health stations (Supermarket News)
sources.claim: higi self-service health stations, machines with a motorized blood-pressure cuff and integrated scale into which a seated user places a forearm, measure weight, BMI, pulse and blood pressure and store the readings to the user's health record; thousands are installed in US retail pharmacies and supermarkets.

sources.title: Rite Aid introduces interactive higi health stations across the chain (Drug Store News)
sources.claim: higi stations were rolled out at scale across a national US drugstore chain, showing this is a fielded, commercially operated automated vital-signs measurement machine rather than a prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated measurement and logging of blood pressure, pulse and weight is the same measurement-and-record act the LPN performs; the machine performs it with the patient's arm presented in a fixed cuff, i.e. a purpose-built presentation.

sources.title: New Robot Does Superior Job Sampling Blood (Rutgers University)
sources.claim: An autonomous venipuncture robot located a vein with ultrasound and inserted a needle into a volunteer's fixtured forearm in a human clinical trial, with success rates comparable to or exceeding clinical standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture requires autonomous machine action on a patient's forearm held in a fixture — the same body part, greater precision than cuff or sensor placement — establishing that a purpose-built device can act on a presented human arm at clinical quality.

sources.system: Semi-autonomous automatic vital sign measurement robot
sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot (TechRxiv)
sources.claim: A robotic arm with vision-based forearm targeting and PPG sensors estimated heart rate, respiration rate and SpO2 on 25 adult volunteers with small errors versus ground truth, but the system is described by its authors as semi-autonomous.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign camera system)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring (Cyborg and Bionic Systems)
sources.claim: The Dr. Spot mobile platform measured skin temperature, respiratory rate and ... contactlessly on patients in a hospital COVID triage tent, but the robot was teleoperated by clinical staff throughout.

sources.title: Smart Epidemic Prevention and Control Robots serve in Chinese hospitals (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: Autonomously navigating service robots deployed in Chinese hospitals performed no-contact body-temperature measurement of people on the premises, showing one vital sign can be taken by a mobile robot in a working facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fever screening is the temperature component of the vitals set, taken contactlessly by an autonomous mobile robot in a hospital, but it yields screening-grade skin temperature only, not the charted core temperature an LPN records.

tasks.label: Administer prescribed medications or start intravenous fluids, noting times and amounts on patients' charts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing/long-term care scheduled med pass: LPN pushes a med cart down a hall, for 20-30 residents pops punch-card doses, crushes tablets and mixes them in applesauce for some, gives eye drops, inhalers and topicals, checks pulse/BP/glucose hold parameters, identifies each resident, watches them swallow, handles refusals, and charts time and amount in the eMAR.

Long-term care or subacute bedside parenteral and non-oral doses: subcutaneous insulin per sliding scale after a fingerstick, heparin/B12/IM injections with site rotation, medications crushed and flushed through a PEG tube, suppositories, nebulizer treatments, often with frail, contracted or dementia-resistant residents in their own rooms; documented in the eMAR.

Physician office, clinic or occupational-health setting: ambulatory patient presents for a scheduled vaccine or routine IM/SC injection (flu, Depo, B12, allergy serum); LPN verifies identity and allergies, selects or draws the dose, injects the deltoid, applies a bandage, observes briefly, and records lot, site, time and amount in the EHR/immunization registry.

Hospital, subacute or infusion unit: start a peripheral IV on an adult in bed or a recliner - select and cannulate a vein, advance the catheter, withdraw the needle, flush and secure with a transparent dressing, prime tubing, spike and hang the ordered fluid bag, program the infusion pump, then chart site, gauge, fluid, rate, time and volume.

Home health or assisted-living visit for a cognitively intact client on a stable oral regimen: the scheduled multi-dose pouch is presented to the client at the right time, the client takes it, and the dose taken or refused is recorded and reported to the care organization.

Home health, group home or private-duty visit requiring hands-on administration: the client cannot self-manage (post-stroke, advanced dementia) or needs an injection, insulin, eye drops or a home IV antibiotic infusion; LPN assesses the client, administers in a cluttered private residence, and charts times and amounts.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performs the complete venipuncture procedure on humans without an operator - arm cradle, alcohol prep, ultrasound/NIR vein selection, tourniquet, needle insertion, tube handling and ... - with one professional supervising up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture rather than drug administration. It transfers to clinic injections and to the puncture step of an IV start - same objects (human arm, needle, skin prep, bandage), precision higher than an IM injection, same institution-run outpatient setting.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: In a multicenter trial in Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments the autonomous device achieved a 94.5% first-stick success rate in routine use, comparable to manual phlebotomy, with mild adverse events in 0.6% of punctures.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: establishes worker-quality reliability for autonomous needle placement in a human arm in an institution-run outpatient department.

sources.title: Vitestro launches new website and first public video of Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device
sources.claim: The Aletta device is CE marked and available for clinical use in European healthcare facilities (not FDA cleared for US use).
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment maturity of the venipuncture system cited as related-task evidence for autonomous needle procedures on patients.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection - University of Waterloo News
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed an autonomous needle-free intramuscular injection on a person: cameras confirm the patient's identity, a lidar-equipped arm maps the body and selects the injection site, and the dose is delivered with no healthcare professional involved.

sources.system: Ivy robotic vascular access platform (Hyperion Surgical)
sources.title: A Serial Entrepreneur: Miller School Neurosurgeon Leads World's First Robotic-Assisted IV Catheterization - InventUM
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic peripheral IV catheterization system reported its world-first in-human procedure only in late 2025, and the platform is described as making IV placement a semi-autonomous, clinician-guided process rather than an autonomous one.

sources.system: Evondos E300 / Anna medicine dispensing robot
sources.title: Medication safety with automatic medicine dispensing - Evondos
sources.claim: Evondos automated medicine dispensing robots are installed in older clients' private homes across the Nordics, releasing each pre-packaged multi-dose sachet at its scheduled time, prompting the client, and alerting home-care professionals when a dose is not taken.

sources.system: Medication management robots (MMRs, incl. Evondos-type dispensers)

sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of medication management robots in home care and long-term care found they automatically dispense correct doses and reduce caregiver workload, but they serve users who manage their own medications and are incompatible with liquid medications.

tasks.label: Provide basic patient care or treatments, such as taking temperatures or blood pressures, dressing wounds, treating bedsores, giving enemas or douches, rubbing with alcohol, massaging, or performing catheterizations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing / long-term care facility: routine vital-sign rounds on a hall of residents — oral or tympanic temperature, blood pressure with a manual or automated cuff, pulse, respirations, SpO2 — taken at the bedside or in a chair on frail elders, many with dementia, contractures, tremor, fragile skin, or resistance to touch; abnormal values re-checked and reported.

Long-term care treatment-cart rounds: pressure-ulcer and chronic wound care — removing soiled dressings, cleansing, measuring/assessing the wound bed, applying ointments and new dressings on sacrum, heels or legs; requires turning and positioning a dependent resident and clean/sterile technique.

Long-term care or hospital: elimination and intimate-hygiene procedures — inserting or removing an indwelling/straight urinary catheter, catheter and peri-care, administering a cleansing enema or douche, cleaning an incontinent bedbound patient and inspecting skin.

Hospital medical/surgical or subacute inpatient unit: bedside basic care bundle on acute patients — vitals on patients with IV lines and monitors, simple dressing changes, comfort measures such as back rubs and alcohol/lotion rubs, repositioning and skin checks, all around bed rails, lines and tubing.

Physician office or outpatient clinic: rooming an ambulatory, cooperative adult patient — temperature, blood pressure, pulse, SpO2, height/weight recorded into the chart, plus an occasional simple wound check or dressing reapplication before the provider enters.

Home health visit in a private residence: vital signs, wound or ulcer dressing change, indwelling catheter care or irrigation, and comfort measures, performed on the patient's own bed, recliner or bathroom, with pets, clutter, poor lighting and no standard equipment.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device is CE-marked and commercially launched in European healthcare settings, performing venipuncture on seated patients in hospital/lab blood-collection rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic venipuncture rather than vital signs. It transfers to taking temperature/blood pressure on a cooperative seated clinic patient because it is a machine-controlled contact procedure on the same body part (the arm) in a healthcare facility, requiring far greater precision (needle in a vein) than seating a cuff or probe.

sources.title: Vitestro Publishes Landmark Peer-Reviewed Multicenter Clinical Study of Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy in Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed multicenter trial in Dutch hospitals and labs reports 94.5% first-stick success for the autonomous device, with a professional supervising up to three devices rather than operating them.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: it establishes worker-comparable reliability for an autonomous contact procedure performed on a patient's arm at a fixed station inside a clinical facility, which bounds what a station-based machine can do for basic measurements like blood pressure.

sources.title: The World's First Blood Collecting Robot Is Here, Meet Aletta | Nurse.Org
sources.claim: The device itself positions the patient's arm, locates the vein, draws the sample and applies the bandage, i.e. it handles the physical contact steps without a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (venipuncture) but shows the machine fixtures and manipulates a living patient's arm autonomously, which is the physical prerequisite for machine-performed cuff blood pressure and temperature measurement at a station.

sources.title: Kroger expands deployment of higi stations | Supermarket News
sources.claim: higi operates roughly 11,000 FDA-cleared self-screening health stations in US retail pharmacies and stores where users obtain blood pressure, pulse, weight and BMI measurements from the machine.

sources.developer: multiple (review by ETH Zurich / Khalifa University authors)
sources.title: Vital signs-based healthcare kiosks for screening chronic and infectious diseases: a systematic review | Communications Medicine
sources.claim: Systematic review of vital-signs healthcare kiosks reports kiosk blood pressure measurements equivalent to those taken by nurse clinicians in healthcare settings.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Aescape's AI-driven robotic massage table autonomously delivers hands-free massage to clients lying on its purpose-built table, and is commercially deployed at Equinox gyms and select Massage Envy franchises.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: therapeutic massage of an able-bodied client who walks in, changes into provided garments and lies prone on the robot's own table. It does not transfer to bedside back/alcohol rubs on frail or bedbound patients, who cannot be transferred onto the machine's table.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Robotic wound redressing remains at laboratory sub-step stage: the state of the art is a first autonomous approach to peeling and placing medical tape, trained from human teleoperated demonstrations, not a complete dressing change on patients.

sources.title: Foxconn Taps NVIDIA to Accelerate Physical and Digital Robotics for Global Healthcare Industry
sources.claim: Deployed hospital ward robots such as Foxconn's Nurabot perform logistics — delivering wound-care kits and education materials to bedsides — and do not perform hands-on patient treatments.

tasks.label: Answer patients' calls and determine how to assist them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital med-surg/acute unit: patient activates the call light; LPN answers over the intercom, walks to the room, reads the patient's condition, and resolves or triages the need — water, blanket, TV remote, help repositioning, an infusion-pump alarm, a question about a medication — escalating to the RN when the complaint is clinical.

Skilled nursing / long-term care: resident presses the call bell, often repeatedly; LPN goes to the room, determines the need (toileting, pain, adjusting a brief or pillow, anxiety, a dropped item, a confused resident who cannot state the problem), and either performs the assistance or delegates it to a CNA.

Urgent call in a facility: call bell or shout signals a fall, chest pain, shortness of breath, bleeding, or choking; LPN responds within seconds, assesses the patient at the bedside (level of consciousness, vitals, injury), begins initial intervention, and summons the RN/rapid response.

Physician office or clinic: LPN answers incoming patient phone calls, elicits symptoms, applies triage protocols, gives advice within scope, schedules or routes the call to the provider, and documents the encounter.

Home health or private-duty shift in a patient's own home: patient calls out or rings a bell from bed or bathroom; LPN responds in an as-found household (clutter, pets, poor lighting, non-standard furniture), determines the need and assists.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0, Advancing The Largest Fleet of Deployed AI-Powered Mobile Manipulation Robots
sources.claim: Moxi, the largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators, autonomously navigates hospitals and delivers medications, lab samples and supplies for nursing and pharmacy staff; its work is staff-initiated logistics, not answering patient call lights or assessing patients at the bedside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intra-hospital delivery. It establishes that autonomous navigation and light object handling work in an E2 hospital, but the cited scope contains no patient-call response, no bedside need determination, and no handover of items to patients in bed, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: Kawasaki Develops Nurse Assistant Robot with Foxconn
sources.claim: Nurabot, a two-armed nurse-assistant robot in verification trials at Taichung Veterans General Hospital, performs specimen transport, medication delivery, facility guidance and patient hygiene education — not call-bell response or patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nurse-support logistics and patient-facing information delivery in a hospital ward (E2). The demonstrated repertoire stops short of eliciting a patient's need at the bedside and acting on it, so it cannot substantiate completion of call-light response.

sources.title: Aeolus Aeo Care Home Monitoring Robot - MetaDolce Technologies
sources.claim: The Aeo care-home robot autonomously patrols eldercare facilities, opens doors and rides elevators, and detects falls or distress, but its response is to alert human staff and wait — it does not determine and deliver the assistance itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wellbeing rounds in an eldercare facility (E2). Detection-and-escalation is only the first step of answering a call; the instance requires bedside assessment and provision or delegation of assistance, which this system explicitly leaves to staff.

sources.title: Innovative Mobile Telehealth Robot for Enhanced Care Delivery - OhmniLabs
sources.claim: The one hospital robot product marketed for call-light response is a telepresence platform: it drives itself to the room, but a remote human clinician conducts the interaction and decides how to assist.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: robot-mediated call-light response in hospitals. Because a remote clinician performs the determination and any decision to assist, this is continuous human control and cannot support a positive capability judgment.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Consumer home humanoids intended for household assistance still rely on remote human operators for complex tasks, so no autonomous system responds to a person's call for help in a private home.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general in-home physical assistance (E3). It is cited to show the home-assistance state of the art remains teleoperated, which cannot support a positive judgment for responding to a patient's call at home.

tasks.label: Supervise nurses' aides or assistants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Evaluate nursing intervention outcomes, conferring with other healthcare team members as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute care (hospital med-surg or post-acute unit): after an intervention such as a PRN analgesic, antipyretic, nebulizer treatment, repositioning, or a dressing change, the LPN determines from the patient's report, recorded vitals, and observation whether the intended outcome was achieved, documents the evaluation, and reports/escalates to the charge RN or provider when the response is inadequate.

Long-term care / skilled nursing facility: over a shift, week, or at an interdisciplinary care-plan conference, the LPN judges whether care-plan interventions (wound treatment, fall precautions, bowel/bladder program, behavior plan, weight-loss interventions) are producing the goals set, and confers with the RN supervisor, dietitian, therapy, or attending provider to revise them.

Clinic or physician office: the LPN evaluates a patient's response to prescribed treatment or teaching between visits (blood-pressure control, glucose logs, medication side effects, post-procedure healing), reviews the record and patient-reported data, and confers with the provider or RN about whether the plan is working.

Home health / hospice visit: the LPN determines whether the plan of care interventions are effective in the patient's home (symptom relief, wound progress, caregiver adherence, equipment use), then telephones or messages the case-managing RN, hospice team, or physician with the evaluation and recommendation.

Other institutional settings (correctional infirmary, school health office, group home, behavioral health unit, dialysis or infusion center): the LPN evaluates whether an intervention achieved its goal for a specific patient and confers with the supervising RN, provider, or interdisciplinary staff about continuing or changing it.

tasks.label: Work as part of a healthcare team to assess patient needs, plan and modify care, and implement interventions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing facility / nursing home: LPN as unit charge nurse for 20-30 residents — rounds and focused assessments (vitals, skin/wound checks, pain, intake/output, mental status), notes changes in condition, reports to the supervising RN/provider, contributes to and updates the interdisciplinary care plan at care conferences, and carries out the resulting interventions (med pass, dressing changes, repositioning/turning schedules, catheter and ostomy care, feeding-tube care, behavior interventions) on residents who are frail, sometimes combative or cognitively impaired.

Physician office / outpatient clinic: LPN rooms patients, collects history, medications and vitals, performs point-of-care testing, flags abnormal findings to the provider, then implements the ordered plan — injections and immunizations, ear lavage, simple wound/suture care, glucose checks — plus patient teaching and follow-up phone triage, across a wide mix of ages and complaints in exam rooms.

Hospital medical-surgical, sub-acute or rehab unit: LPN works alongside an RN on a team, participates in shift huddles and bedside rounds, gathers assessment data (vitals, blood glucose, wound and drain checks, intake/output, pain reassessment), escalates changes to the RN, and implements interventions — dressing changes, catheter care, ambulation and repositioning, oral/IM medications, oxygen and suction — on patients with lines, tubes, and varying mobility.

Home health / private-duty visit in the patient's own residence: LPN travels to a home taken as found (pets, clutter, family present), performs a visit assessment, compares findings to the RN-written plan of care, communicates changes to the RN case manager, and delivers the interventions — wound care, medication setup and administration, tracheostomy or feeding-tube care, teaching the caregiver — then documents the visit.

Other institutional settings (correctional infirmary, behavioral-health unit, group home for people with disabilities, hospice inpatient unit): LPN performs sick-call or shift assessments, participates in the treatment team, adjusts interventions within protocol (comfort measures, de-escalation, seizure or diabetic protocols, PRN medications), and escalates to the RN or provider, often with limited equipment and unpredictable patient behavior.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0, Advancing The Largest Fleet of Deployed AI-Powered Mobile Manipulation Robots
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of mobile manipulator robots in US hospitals, Diligent Robotics' Moxi, performs logistics work — delivering supplies, medications, lab samples — and is dispatched by staff via an app; it does not assess patients, contribute to care plans, or perform nursing interventions on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest deployed hospital robot to nursing work; its demonstrated scope is intra-facility transport, which does not include patient assessment, care planning, or hands-on intervention, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.developer: Foxconn (Hon Hai) with NVIDIA, Taichung Veterans General Hospital
sources.title: AI Robotics, Digital Twins, and MONAI Contributions Highlight Hon Hai Foxconn's Smart Healthcare Vision at GTC Taipei 2025
sources.claim: Nurabot, the Foxconn/NVIDIA nursing collaborative robot field-tested and commercialized in hospital wards, is limited to medication and specimen delivery, ward patrols, guidance and patient-education playback; clinical assessment, care planning and hands-on interventions remain with nurses.
sources.transferJustification: Marketed as a nursing robot, so directly relevant; the enumerated deployed capabilities are transport and patrol, none of which is assessment, care-plan modification, or a nursing intervention on a patient.

sources.system: Robotic wound redressing / autonomous tape handling framework
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic wound care remains at the level of isolated sub-steps in the laboratory: the state of the art is removing adhesive tape from a dressing, not completing a dressing change on a real patient.
sources.transferJustification: Wound dressing change is one of the most common LPN interventions; evidence that only a single sub-step is autonomously achievable in the lab shows the intervention component of this task is not robotically completable in any environment.

sources.system: Automatic vital sign measurement robot (robotic arm with PPG sensors)
sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot
sources.claim: Robotic measurement of patient vital signs — a basic component of LPN assessment — exists only as a semi-autonomous laboratory robotic arm with PPG sensors, not as a deployed clinical system.
sources.transferJustification: Vital-sign collection is the data-gathering step of patient assessment; only a semi-autonomous bench prototype exists, so even this sub-step is unsubstantiated in a working clinical facility.

sources.system: Transfer, mobility and monitoring care robots in nursing homes (Japan)
sources.developer: various (surveyed in nursing-home robot adoption study)
sources.title: New Study Reveals Using Robots in Nursing Homes Correlates with Higher Employee Retention
sources.claim: Robots adopted in nursing homes fall into monitoring, mobility and transfer categories and function as aids operated by or supporting human care workers (lifting, moving and rotating residents), rather than autonomously assessing residents or executing care plans.
sources.transferJustification: Long-term care is the largest LPN setting; the deployed robots there are caregiver-operated assistive devices, confirming no autonomous system performs the assess-plan-intervene cycle in that facility type.

sources.developer: AIST / CNRS-AIST JRL with Tokyo Robotics
sources.title: Humanoid Robot RHP Friends: Seamless Combination of Autonomous and Teleoperated Tasks in a Nursing Context
sources.claim: Research humanoids built specifically for nursing tasks (assisted dressing, transfer support) explicitly combine autonomous modules with human teleoperation and remain laboratory demonstrations.
sources.transferJustification: This is the closest humanoid effort at bedside nursing interventions; its reliance on teleoperation for the manipulation steps means it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous completion of nursing interventions.

tasks.label: Record food and fluid intake and output.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Assemble and use equipment, such as catheters, tracheotomy tubes, or oxygen suppliers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital or nursing-home bedside oxygen therapy: LPN attaches flowmeter to wall outlet or sets up a concentrator/portable E-cylinder with regulator, fills and connects humidifier bottle and tubing, applies nasal cannula or mask to the patient's face, titrates flow to ordered liters, checks SpO2, skin behind ears/nares, and tubing patency.

Indwelling urinary catheter work in hospital/long-term care: position and drape the patient, open and set up the sterile Foley kit, perineal cleansing, insert catheter, inflate balloon, connect and hang drainage bag, secure to leg; also routine catheter care, bag changes, irrigation, and catheter removal.

Tracheostomy/airway equipment in a subacute or vent unit: assemble and check the suction machine, canister, tubing and sterile suction catheter, suction the trach, change inner cannula, dressing and ties, connect humidified trach collar or ventilator circuit, monitor patient tolerance.

Home-health visit in a private residence: set up or troubleshoot a home oxygen concentrator/portable tank and tubing, run a nebulizer treatment, perform catheter or trach equipment care amid household clutter, pets, and non-standard furniture; teach the family how the equipment is assembled.

IV and enteral equipment in a hospital, infusion clinic, or LTC: spike and prime IV tubing, load the pump, insert a peripheral IV catheter (IV-certified LPN) and secure the dressing, or assemble feeding-pump tubing and connect it to a PEG tube, verify placement and rate.

Other bedside devices in a clinic or LTC facility: assemble and use portable suction, CPAP/BiPAP circuit, wound drain or negative-pressure dressing canister, ostomy or drainage collection systems, checking fit and function on the patient.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator in the US, is limited by design to non-patient-facing fetch-and-deliver work; it does not assemble or apply clinical equipment to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hospital supply logistics) in the same E2 environment; cited to show the frontier of deployed autonomous hospital manipulation stops short of patient-contact equipment setup, not to substantiate completion.

sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Nurabot, an AI nursing humanoid in field trial at Taichung Veterans General Hospital, performs delivery and patient-guidance work rather than hands-on equipment procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (ward nursing support) in an E2 hospital ward; shows the scope of current nursing robots is transport and guidance, not assembling or applying catheters, trach or oxygen equipment.

sources.title: Vitestro introduces autonomous robotic device for blood collection
sources.claim: Aletta performs autonomous needle insertion and blood collection on a patient's arm placed in the device, CE-marked and commercially launched in European hospitals and labs; it is a single-procedure venipuncture station, not a device that assembles or applies oxygen, tracheostomy or urinary catheter equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (venipuncture) — the closest autonomous patient-contact procedure in a structured clinical facility. It handles one pre-fixtured limb and a fixed consumable path; it does not assemble multi-part tubing/humidifier/suction sets, place indwelling catheters, or secure devices on a patient, so capability does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot performed naso- and oropharyngeal sampling on humans in two small clinical studies, showing autonomous insertion of a simple instrument into a patient orifice under force control, but only at study scale for a single sampling motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (specimen swabbing) involving autonomous contact with a patient's airway; cited as the frontier of autonomous instrument insertion. It involves no sterile field, no equipment assembly, and no indwelling device placement, so it does not substantiate catheterization, trach care, or oxygen setup.

sources.title: Clinical Efficacy and Safety of an Automatic Closed-Suction System in Mechanically Ventilated Patients with Pneumonia
sources.claim: An automatic closed-suction device can perform tracheal suctioning by machine once a clinician has connected it to the airway, but in a multicenter randomized ICU trial it did not meet its non-inferiority margin against manual nurse suctioning.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related sub-step (tracheal suctioning). It automates only the catheter stroke after a nurse assembles and attaches the circuit, and worker-equivalent quality was not established, so it cannot complete the whole assemble-and-use instance.

sources.title: Corindus Receives FDA Clearance for First Automated Robotic Movement in technIQ Series for CorPath GRX Platform
sources.claim: The clinically deployed catheter robots are vascular intervention systems driven by a physician at a console, not autonomous devices that place or manage nursing catheters.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (catheter manipulation) in a cath lab; cited to show catheter robotics in clinical use is physician-teleoperated intravascular work, which cannot substantiate autonomous LPN catheter assembly and use.

tasks.label: Collect samples, such as blood, urine, or sputum from patients, and perform routine laboratory tests on samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Physician office, outpatient clinic, or hospital outpatient draw station: routine venipuncture on a seated, cooperative adult patient — verify order and ID, apply tourniquet, select antecubital vein, draw 1–4 vacutainer tubes, invert/label, bandage, send to lab or run a waived test.

Nursing home or hospital ward: bedside venipuncture on a frail, often bedbound elderly resident with fragile, rolling or sclerosed veins, sometimes confused or resistant; nurse works at the bedside/wheelchair with a butterfly set, then labels and sends the sample.

Fingerstick capillary blood testing at the bedside or chairside (accuchecks before meals, POC hemoglobin/INR): lance the fingertip, milk the drop onto a meter strip, read the result within seconds and document/act on it. High frequency in long-term care and clinics.

Non-blood specimens in a facility: clean-catch urine (instructing the patient), urine from a Foley port, bedpan or commode hat for an incontinent resident, plus sputum expectoration, stool, or wound swab; then a dipstick urinalysis or send to the lab.
Clinic visit: throat or nasopharyngeal swab from a seated patient for rapid strep/flu/COVID testing, followed by running the waived rapid test and reporting the result.

Home health visit: LPN travels to a private residence and collects blood (venipuncture) and/or a urine specimen from a homebound patient in a living room or bedroom, packages it and transports it to ... lab.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performed venipuncture on 1633 patients in the outpatient phlebotomy departments of three Dutch hospitals (May–Sep 2025), with 94.5% first-stick success, 92.7% in difficult venous access and 93.4% in patients aged ≥65; adverse events 0.6%, all mild.

sources.title: Aletta® – Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta is a fixed station that carries out the whole blood-draw sequence itself (tourniquet, vein finding by NIR/Doppler ultrasound, needle insertion, tube changing and inversion, bandage); it holds CE mark certification in the EU and one supervisor can oversee up ... devices in blood draw centers.

sources.system: Intelligent blood collection robot (MagicNurse-class commercial device)
sources.developer: Chinese manufacturer reported in Frontiers review (e.g., MagicNurse)
sources.title: Intelligent blood collection robot: key technologies, clinical applications, and future challenges (Front. Bioeng. Biotechnol.)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed review reports an intelligent venous blood collection robot in routine hospital service since September 2021 at Zhongshan (Sun Yat-sen) Hospital of Fudan ..., Shanghai, with data from 6,255 consenting patients and a 94.3% puncture success rate, outperforming manual collection on volume, pain and success.

sources.developer: Hitachi High-Tech Corporation with Fujita Health University Hospital
sources.title: Hospital robots collect and deliver blood samples (Nature, partner content)
sources.claim: A Hitachi High-Tech / Fujita Health University Hospital automated fingertip blood collection device, trialled at the hospital, maps fingertip capillaries with near-infrared cameras, grips the finger, punctures it and cycles an automated tourniquet to collect up to 400 µL; results correlated well with venous blood in volunteers.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (capillary/fingerstick blood collection from a patient) as the LPN accucheck/POC instance; the device selects the puncture site and collects the sample itself, the step a nurse performs.

sources.title: Evaluation of Blood-Sampling Performance of Automatic Fingertip-Blood-Sampling System … (Fujita Health University research portal)
sources.claim: Evaluation of the automatic fingertip-blood-sampling system with vessel-puncture function in 18 human participants (ages 20s–60s) showed sub-millimetre puncture accuracy and characterised the blood volume obtained.
sources.transferJustification: Direct evidence on the collection half of the fingerstick instance: automated selection of a fingertip puncture site and puncture on real human fingers.

sources.system: Total laboratory automation (cobas connection modules, Abbott GLP, Beckman/Siemens tracks)
sources.developer: Roche, Abbott, Siemens Healthineers, Beckman Coulter
sources.title: Collaborative Robotics, Mobile Platforms, and Total Laboratory Automation in Clinical Diagnostics (Diagnostics)
sources.claim: Total laboratory automation lines from Abbott, Roche, Siemens Healthineers ... are in routine use in high-volume clinical laboratories, mechanically handling, sorting and analysing specimen tubes and cutting turnaround time, error rates and labour; the ADOPT samples were likewise processed and analysed under local ISO 15189 lab protocols.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the second half of the task — performing routine laboratory tests on collected samples — with machines that physically decap, aliquot, transport and analyse tubes; it does not cover collection from the patient.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: SR-NOCS, a force-controlled autonomous swab robot station, took combined naso-/oropharyngeal specimens from 52 suspected COVID-19 patients in a hospital clinical study and at a public screening station, with results matching manual sampling and only supervisory oversight (operator on an e-stop).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collecting a respiratory-tract swab specimen from a seated patient — the same procedure an LPN performs for a rapid strep/flu throat swab, with comparable contact precision and the same clinic setting.

tasks.label: Prepare or examine food trays for conformance to prescribed diet.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing / long-term care unit: the charge LPN meets the meal cart arriving from the facility kitchen and checks each resident's tray against the diet card and roster — right name, right diet (pureed, mechanical soft, no-added-salt, carb-controlled), correct thickened-liquid consistency — pulls prohibited items, and sends wrong trays back for replacement before trays go out to residents.

Hospital acute care unit (med-surg/telemetry): LPN checks each delivered tray against the current diet order in the chart before it reaches the patient — catching NPO/held diets, clear vs. full liquid, allergy items, carbohydrate counts — and holds, corrects, or returns the tray.

Facility kitchen tray line or serving window (small hospital, correctional infirmary, psychiatric or group-home setting): LPN stands at the assembly line/serving counter and portions or assembles trays to the diet slips, or inspects each completed tray against the slip before it is loaded into the cart.

Unit pantry/nourishment room: LPN assembles between-meal nourishment or snack trays to a prescribed diet — diabetic HS snack, renal-restricted items, prescribed oral supplement, late tray plated from stock.

Unit pantry or bedside: LPN modifies tray items to the prescribed consistency/texture — thickening beverages to nectar or honey level per IDDSI order, pureeing or cutting food for a dysphagia or edentulous resident — and verifies the result before serving.

Home health visit or small group home: LPN prepares a meal or tray in the client's own kitchen per the prescribed diet (low-sodium cardiac, diabetic, renal), using whatever food and equipment the household has, and checks it against the care plan.

sources.title: Chef Robotics and ILPRA Partner to Deliver Flexible Automation for Meal Assembly and Packaging | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-driven robotic arms autonomously portion and deposit multiple different food ingredients into meal trays on customer production lines, packaged by partner tray sealers; commercially deployed under a robotics-as-a-service model with tens of millions of servings produced.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling meal trays to a defined recipe/portion specification on a line. It transfers to 'prepare food trays for conformance to prescribed diet' because the objects (compartmented meal trays, portioned foods, sauces, purees) and precision (specified item in specified compartment at specified portion) are the same; the diet order simply supplies the spec.

sources.system: Chef Robotics robotic meal assembly cell at Chef Bombay
sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: A Chef Robotics system deployed at a customer plant picks and places multiple ingredients with varying portion ... and tray positions, attached to existing production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: high-mix tray assembly to per-SKU specifications is the machine analogue of building a tray to a prescribed diet, with trays presented on a conveyor in known positions.

sources.system: RoboEatz Autonomous Robotic Kitchen (ARK) — 'Fresh Take Eatery'
sources.developer: RoboEatz with ABB Robotics / WellSpan Health
sources.title: WellSpan Health Unveils First-of-Its-Kind Full-Service Robotic Kitchen at WellSpan York Hospital
sources.claim: WellSpan York Hospital deployed RoboEatz's Autonomous Robotic Kitchen with ABB robotic arms, performing autonomous ingredient storage and retrieval, cooking, plating and serving in a self-contained 400-square-foot unit inside the hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous made-to-order meal preparation in a healthcare facility. It transfers because each output is built to an individually specified ingredient list, which is what conformance to a prescribed diet requires; the machine works inside its own purpose-built enclosure with ingredients presented in bins.

sources.system: RoboEatz ARK at Fresh Take Eatery, WellSpan York Hospital
sources.title: WellSpan York Hospital unveils robotic dining system
sources.claim: The hospital's robotic dining unit uses a robotic arm to take ingredients from bins and prepare up to four individually customized bowls, pasta dishes or ..., on demand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: per-order customized food assembly. Transfers to preparing a tray to a prescribed diet because the item set is chosen per individual order rather than in a batch, matching the per-patient variation that diet conformance requires.

sources.system: Ishida IX-series X-ray inspection systems with reject devices
sources.title: X-Ray Inspection Systems for Food | X-Ray Product Inspection | Ishida
sources.claim: Ishida inline X-ray inspection systems on food production lines automatically count components, check fill levels and identify missing items in packs, and physically remove non-conforming packs using pusher, slap-arm, drop-belt or paddle reject devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inline inspection of ready-meal trays against a stored specification with automatic physical rejection. It transfers to 'examine food trays for conformance' because the check (are the specified components present, in the specified quantity) and the corrective act (pull the non-conforming tray off the line) are the same, with trays presented one way on a conveyor.

sources.system: Aethon TUG T3 autonomous mobile robots
sources.title: Franciscan Health Crown Point Robots Assisting In Kitchen, Environmental Deliveries
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots deployed in US hospitals transport carts of meal trays from the kitchen to floors, but staff meet the robots and handle the trays from there; no in-facility robot checks trays against diet orders.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E2 case: the only robots operating in the nursing-unit/hospital-corridor environment move trays, they do not inspect tray contents against a prescribed diet or remediate errors.

tasks.label: Help patients with bathing, dressing, maintaining personal hygiene, moving in bed, or standing and walking.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing home / skilled nursing facility: complete bed bath of a dependent resident — undressing, washing face, torso, limbs, perineal/incontinence care, oral care, drying, skin inspection, fresh gown and linens, with the resident rolled side to side.

Hospital or LTC facility: dressing/undressing a partially dependent patient — hospital gown or street clothes over an IV line or hemiparetic arm, plus socks, non-skid slippers, brace or compression stockings, patient seated on the bed edge or in a chair.

Hospital / LTC: scheduled turning and repositioning of a bed-bound patient (roughly every two hours, day and night) for pressure-injury prevention and comfort, including boosting a patient who has slid down and bracing with pillows/wedges.

Facility: transferring a patient bed-to-wheelchair/commode or assisting a sit-to-stand — applying gait belt, blocking knees or using a mechanical/sit-to-stand lift, managing lines, catheter bag and IV pole, weight-bearing status varies.

Facility corridor: standing a patient up and ambulating them 50-200 feet with a gait belt and walker, monitoring for orthostatic dizziness, pain and fatigue, guarding against a fall, then returning them to bed or chair.
Home health / group home visit: bathing (tub, shower chair or bed bath), dressing and mobility assistance in a private residence with non-standard bathrooms, clutter, pets and family present.

sources.date: 2025 (product page; product on market for years)
sources.title: About The Freedom Bed™ By ProBed Medical
sources.claim: ProBed Medical's Freedom Bed is a commercially sold, computer-controlled bed that automatically turns an immobilized bed-user through a 60-degree range on a programmed schedule without caregiver involvement, for pressure-injury prevention; it is used in private homes and care settings.
sources.transferJustification: This is the 'moving in bed' component of the task itself: mechanically repositioning a bed-bound patient side to side on a set schedule, the action an LPN performs q2h for pressure relief. It does not perform boosting up in bed or pillow bracing.

sources.title: Effectiveness of Freedom Bed Compared to Manual Turning in Prevention of Pressure Injuries...
sources.claim: A clinical trial was registered comparing the Freedom Bed with manual turning for prevention of pressure injuries in ..., indicating the automated turning is evaluated as a substitute for the nurse-performed turning schedule.
sources.transferJustification: Directly compares the machine's repositioning with the nurse-performed manual turning that constitutes this part of the task.

sources.title: Automated Systems and Early Mobilization Programs for Bedridden Patients: A Systematic Review
sources.claim: A systematic review of automated systems for bedridden patients found robotic/automated repositioning and mobilization systems were associated with fewer pressure injuries and better caregiver efficiency across nine studies of 380 patients.
sources.transferJustification: Aggregates clinical evidence for the same repositioning/mobilization actions the LPN performs in bed.

sources.title: SkinGrip: An Adaptive Soft Robotic Manipulator with Capacitive Sensing for Whole-Limb Bed Bathing Assistance
sources.claim: SkinGrip, a soft robotic manipulator on a robot arm, autonomously wiped the arms and legs of human subjects in bed-bathing trials, achieving 88.8% (arms) and 81.4% (legs) cleaning effectiveness in a laboratory setting; it covers limb wiping only.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (bed bathing), but only the limb-wiping sub-step on cooperative subjects in a lab; no undressing, perineal care, turning, drying, or gown change.

sources.developer: EU I-SUPPORT consortium (NTUA, Univ. of Pisa, et al.)
sources.title: I-Support: A robotic platform of an assistive bathing robot for the elderly population
sources.claim: The EU I-SUPPORT project built a prototype soft robotic arm in an instrumented shower cabin that washes areas such as the back and lower limbs of frail seniors who sit in a motorized bathing chair; it was validated in clinical/rehabilitation environments as a research prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (assisted bathing) in a purpose-built shower cabin, but it serves seniors who can sit and wash reachable areas themselves; it does not undress, dry, dress, or bathe a fully dependent resident.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy robot-assisted dressing system
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: A robot-assisted dressing policy was evaluated on real human participants over 264 trials with varying garments and ..., dressing on average 85% of a participant's arm length — i.e., a single sleeve, in a lab.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (dressing assistance), but limited to pulling a sleeve up one arm of a seated, cooperative participant in a lab, not dressing a patient in a full outfit around lines and braces.

sources.title: Acceptability of Using a Robotic Nursing Assistant in Health Care Environments: Experimental Pilot Study
sources.claim: The Adaptive Robotic Nursing Assistant (ARNA) is a university research prototype mobile manipulator with an instrumented handlebar for patient walking assistance; pilot studies with 24 participants and later with 58 nursing students assessed acceptability of the robot for ambulation tasks, with the robot driven by the patient's tactile cues.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (walking a patient), but the device is a shared-control walker steered by the patient's own force on a handlebar in a simulated hospital setting; it does not stand the patient up or guard a fall autonomously.

sources.title: Care Service Robot is First in the World to Obtain ISO13482
sources.claim: Panasonic's Resyone, the first ISO 13482-certified care service robot, is an electric care bed whose half detaches into a reclining wheelchair so a bedridden user can be moved without being lifted; it is a caregiver-operated powered device.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (bed-to-chair transfer), but each motion is commanded by the caregiver, who still positions the patient, feet and lines; it is an operator-driven assistive device, not an autonomous transfer.

sources.title: ROBOHELPER SASUKE (Muscle, Inc.)
sources.claim: ROBOHELPER SASUKE is a commercially available transfer-assist robot used in Japanese elderly care homes that lifts a resident with a sheet placed under them; the lift is operated by a caregiver.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (patient transfer), but the caregiver places the sheet and drives the lift throughout — continuous operator control, not autonomous completion.

sources.title: AI robots may hold key to nursing Japan's ageing population (Reuters)
sources.claim: AIREC, an AI-driven 150-kg humanoid at Waseda University, was demonstrated in the lab rolling a man onto his side and can help a person sit up or ..., but its developer does not expect it to be usable in nursing-care facilities until around 2030.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targets repositioning and dressing tasks, but only as staged laboratory demonstrations of a prototype whose autonomy in these contact manoeuvres is not established and which is not expected in care facilities before ~2030.

sources.title: human washing machine at expo 2025 osaka cleans you up
sources.claim: Science Co.'s 'Mirai Ningen Sentakuki' bathing capsule shown at Expo 2025 Osaka automatically washes a person's body with fine bubbles while they sit inside; users walk in and seat themselves, and it was exhibited as a public attraction.
sources.transferJustification: Automated whole-body washing, but only for a user who can enter, undress and seat themselves; it does no transfer, perineal care, drying or dressing of a dependent patient, so it does not complete the nursing bathing instance.

tasks.label: Prepare patients for examinations, tests, or treatments and explain procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing home / long-term-care unit: prepare a frail or cognitively impaired resident for a treatment or exam — reposition or transfer the resident in bed or to a chair, loosen or remove clothing, expose a wound, ostomy or catheter site, place an underpad and drape, set up supplies, and explain and reassure step by step.

Physician office or outpatient clinic: room the patient — escort them to the exam room, take vital signs (BP cuff, temperature, pulse ox), height/weight, have them undress and put on a gown, position them on the exam table for the specific exam, lay out the tray/instruments, and explain what the provider will do.

Hospital med-surg, pre-op or endoscopy unit: prepare a patient for a procedure — verify orders/consent, remove clothing, jewelry, dentures, apply a gown, clip hair and apply antiseptic skin prep, place monitoring leads, position the patient in bed or on the procedure table, and explain the procedure and answer questions.

Outpatient clinic or lab draw station: prepare an ambulatory patient for a venous blood draw — seat the patient, confirm identity, explain the procedure, position and support the arm, apply the tourniquet, select and disinfect the puncture site so the draw can proceed.

Clinic or hospital: prepare a patient for another diagnostic test — expose the chest and place ten electrodes for a 12-lead ECG, instruct on specimen collection, prepare for spirometry or imaging (remove metal, position limb/body), explaining each step.

Home health visit in a private residence: prepare the patient for a treatment (dressing change, injection, catheter care, infusion) — clear and set up a workspace amid household clutter and pets, help the patient onto their own bed or recliner, expose and position the site, establish a clean field, and explain the procedure to patient and family.

sources.title: Aletta for Laboratory specialists - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomously performs the full patient-side venipuncture sequence, including the preparation steps a nurse would do (arm positioning, tourniquet, site selection and skin prep) through bandaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (performing a diagnostic blood draw) subsumes the LPN prep step for that test: same patient, same arm positioning, tourniquet and site antisepsis, in the same clinic draw-station setting.

sources.title: Phlebotomists - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta instructs the patient through each phase of the procedure, covering the 'explain the procedure' element of patient preparation for a blood draw.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Aletta was evaluated on real patients in hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments in a peer-reviewed multicenter trial, establishing the environment as a structured human clinical facility.

sources.developer: Foxconn / Kawasaki Heavy Industries with NVIDIA
sources.title: Foxconn Unveils Physical AI Vision for Next-Generation Smart Hospitals at NVIDIA GTC Taipei at COMPUTEX 2026
sources.claim: Hospital-deployed nursing robots handle logistics (medication and specimen transport, patrols, guidance), not hands-on physical preparation of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Most mature hospital nursing robot deployment; its task list shows that autonomous in-facility nursing robots do not undertake gowning, positioning, draping or skin prep of patients.

sources.title: Multidimensional Capacitive Sensing for Robot-Assisted Dressing and Bathing
sources.claim: Robot assistance with gowning and body cleaning of a person exists only as laboratory research on isolated sub-steps (pulling a hospital gown sleeve onto a participant's arm), not as a fielded system completing patient preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest research analogue to gowning/skin-prep sub-steps of patient preparation; it is a single-arm lab demonstration on seated able-bodied participants, so it does not substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot - TechRxiv
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic vital-sign measurement remains a semi-autonomous research prototype limited to optical (PPG) sensing on the arm, not cuff-based clinic vitals plus gowning and table positioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (taking vital signs) is one component of clinic rooming; the prototype's laboratory maturity and narrow scope show the rooming instance is not completed by any cited system.

tasks.label: Apply compresses, ice bags, or hot water bottles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Long-term care or hospital unit: LPN applies an ice bag or warm pack to a cooperative patient's knee, shoulder, hip or lower back (arthritis pain, edema, post-fall bruise, or warming an arm before venipuncture). Nurse fetches the pack from the unit freezer/warmer, wraps it in a towel, positions the resident, places and secures the pack over intact skin, times 15-20 minutes, removes it and checks skin.

Long-term care or hospital: same thermal application but the patient is confused, agitated, or has contractures, spasticity, or paper-thin fragile skin; requires repositioning in bed, pillow support, coaxing, holding the pack in place, and continuous re-checking because the patient shifts, pulls at the pack, or cannot report pain.

Hospital med-surg/post-op or infusion area: cold pack to a fresh surgical site over a dressing, to a swollen IV infiltration site, or to a hematoma; patient in bed in a gown with IV lines, drains, tubing and dressings; the pack must be placed adjacent to but not on the incision/IV, secured without pressure, and the site reassessed.

Outpatient clinic or physician office: warm moist compress applied to a patient's eyelid (hordeolum/chalazion), facial abscess, or lanced boil; patient seated in an exam chair; nurse prepares warm water, wrings the cloth, holds it gently on the delicate area, re-warms and repeats for several minutes.

Rehabilitation / therapy or wound-care clinic: hydrocollator moist hot pack (or paraffin/warm pack) applied over layers of toweling to a patient's back, shoulder or knee while the patient lies prone or supine on a treatment plinth; timed 15-20 minutes, removed, skin inspected before exercise or dressing change.

Home health visit in a private residence: LPN applies a heating pad, hot water bottle, or warm compress to a homebound patient's back, abdomen, or limb on the patient's own bed, recliner or sofa; variable furniture, clutter, pets, poor lighting; also instructs the patient/family on safe use and timing.

sources.system: Intelligent moxibustion rehabilitation robot (Shanghai Junkong Robotics)
sources.developer: Shanghai University of Engineering Science / Shanghai Junkong Robotics Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Intelligent Robot for Moxibustion Has Come—Reducing Burn Risks & Easing Doctors' Workload, With Sales Over 100 Million yuan
sources.claim: An intelligent moxibustion robot (Shanghai Junkong Robotics / Shanghai Univ. of Engineering Science) delivers a half-hour timed heat therapy to designated points on a patient's back in hospital treatment rooms; deployed in a rehabilitation hospital, community hospitals and rehab centers, Class II medical device, sales over 100 million yuan, more than a thousand patients served.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering therapeutic heat to a designated body region of a patient for a timed session with burn-risk control. Transfers to applying hot compresses/hot water bottles — same body regions, same thermal-safety precision, same clinical setting — except that heat is radiated rather than delivered by an object placed in contact.

sources.system: Intelligent moxibustion rehabilitation robot (Shanghai Junkong Robotics)
sources.developer: Shanghai University of Engineering Science / Shanghai Junkong Robotics Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Intelligent Robot for Moxibustion Has Come—Reducing Burn Risks & Easing Doctors' Workload, With Sales Over 100 Million yuan
sources.claim: The same moxibustion robot runs autonomously: it performs 3D acupoint localization, infrared temperature control, adaptive distance ..., retracts and alarms if the patient moves, and one therapist can direct eight robots; only consumable replacement is manual.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy and thermal safety monitoring for the heat-application evidence above; the patient-movement retraction behaviour also bounds performance with restless or confused patients.

sources.title: Aescape | The Aescape Experience
sources.claim: Aescape's robotic massage table uses a 3D body scan to guide two arms that make force-controlled contact with a person's back and limbs using heated end effectors; it is commercially available and installed at Equinox clubs and Massage Envy locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of a temperature-controlled applicator against a designated region of a person's body with regulated force, on a purpose-built table. Transfers to holding a warm/cold applicator against a knee, shoulder or back for a timed therapy session.

sources.title: Equinox Locations Add Aescape, a Fully Automated Massage Bed - Athletech News
sources.claim: Aescape's fully automated massage system was launched commercially and installed at Equinox clubs, with the client lying on a purpose-built table and no therapist performing the treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes commercial deployment and autonomy of the force-controlled body-contact system cited above; the purpose-built table is the fixtured presentation of the person that an E1 setting would provide.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance | alphaXiv
sources.claim: Cornell's RABBIT system autonomously performs bed-bathing motions on a real person lying in bed, using RGB/thermal perception of the body and software plus hardware compliance to keep contact safe and comfortable; validated with a participant with ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained compliant contact between a robot-held item (wiping tool) and a designated limb of a real person in bed. Transfers to pressing and holding a wrapped compress against a limb — comparable objects, contact force, and body-part targeting.

sources.system: Bodies Uncovered (bedding manipulation policies on a real robot)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon / Georgia Tech (Puthuveetil, Kemp, Erickson)
sources.title: Bodies Uncovered: Learning to Manipulate Real Blankets Around People via Physics Simulations
sources.claim: A robot autonomously grasps and manipulates a real blanket over a real person lying in bed, uncovering a specified target body part while leaving the rest covered.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grasp, transport and placement of a deformable cloth relative to a named body part of a real person. Transfers to placing and removing a towel-wrapped compress over a limb — same deformable object class and same body-part targeting.

sources.system: Autonomous robot-assisted feeding system (inside-mouth bite transfer)
sources.developer: Cornell EmPRISE Lab (Jenamani, Bhattacharjee et al.)
sources.title: Robotic system feeds people with severe mobility limitations | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: Cornell's autonomous robot-assisted feeding system, which holds a utensil and brings it into contact with a care recipient's mouth while tracking movement and reacting to physical contact, fed 13 individuals with severe mobility limitations across a lab, a New York City medical center, and a care recipient's home.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an autonomous arm carries a held object into controlled contact with a specific part of a real patient's body, adapting to movement. Transfers to carrying a wrapped pack from a presented position onto a designated body site with safe contact.

tasks.label: Provide medical treatment or personal care to patients in private home settings, such as cooking, keeping rooms orderly, seeing that patients are comfortable and in good spirits, or instructing family members in simple nursing tasks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing portion of a home visit to a homebound patient (post-surgical, diabetic, CHF): hand hygiene and setup on the patient's own furniture, vital signs, wound assessment and dressing change, insulin or other medication administration and reconciliation, catheter/ostomy care, then settling the patient comfortably before leaving. Pets, clutter, poor lighting and variable home layouts are the norm.

Hands-on personal care in the home: bed bath or shower assist, perineal/incontinence care and toileting, oral care, dressing, skin inspection, repositioning a dependent patient in bed and transferring bed-to-chair with a gait belt or lift, in a cramped bedroom or bathroom.

Preparing a meal in the patient's own kitchen consistent with a therapeutic diet (low-sodium, renal, diabetic, pureed/thickened), using whatever food is on hand; plating, serving to the patient, assisting with feeding if needed, then cleaning up.

Keeping the patient's room and immediate area orderly: picking up clutter and putting personal items away, clearing dishes, cups and trash to the kitchen, straightening or making the bed, keeping the walking path and bedside table clear of fall hazards, restocking supplies within reach.

Instructing a family caregiver in simple nursing tasks: demonstrating a dressing change, glucometer use, insulin injection, tube feeding, or a safe transfer on the actual patient and equipment in the home, then watching the family member's return demonstration and correcting technique.

Seeing that the patient is comfortable and in good spirits during a shift or visit: adjusting pillows, blankets and bed position, checking for pain or distress, bringing water, snacks, glasses, phone or call device within reach, conversation and reassurance, reorienting a confused or anxious patient.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 vision-language-action model autonomously drives a mobile manipulator to clean ... kitchens and bedrooms — picking up clutter, putting dishes in the sink, putting away items — in entirely new, previously unseen real homes, though reliability is imperfect.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying/cleanup. It transfers to 'keeping rooms orderly' because the objects (dishes, cups, clothes, small personal items), the precision required, and the setting (an ordinary residence taken as found) are the same as an LPN straightening a patient's room.

sources.title: Figure AI Demonstrates Humanoid Robots Making a Bed
sources.claim: Two Figure 03 humanoids running the onboard Helix-02 policy autonomously tidied a staged bedroom and made a bed, including hanging clothes and smoothing a comforter, in under two minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bedroom reset/bed making in a home-like room. Same objects (bedding, clothing, small items) and same tolerance as straightening a patient's bed and room, so it supports the housekeeping instance; it is a staged room, not a patient's occupied bed.

sources.title: Posha Delivers Autonomous Countertop Cooking Experience
