sources.claim: Posha is a shipping countertop cooking robot that autonomously cooks one-pot meals from ingredients the user preps and loads into its dispensers, using computer vision and a robotic stirring arm; it does not shop, chop, plate or wash up.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended cooking of a meal. It covers the cooking step of the meal-preparation instance only when ingredients are pre-portioned into its fixtured dispensers — i.e. the work presented to the machine, which is the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: Robotic wound redressing research platform (autonomous tape handling)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic wound care is at the research stage: published work automates only isolated steps such as dressing removal or tape handling, not a complete dressing change on a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant negative evidence for the skilled-nursing instance: it shows the state of the art in robotic wound care is sub-step automation, not an accepted nursing dressing change.

sources.title: Labrador Systems Announces First Business Customers of its Award-Winning Personal Assistive Robots
sources.claim: Labrador's Retriever is an autonomous mobile home robot, deployed with care-provider customers, that navigates a mapped home and carries items (up to 25 lb) such as drinks and meals to a person; it has no arms and does no hands-on patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching and delivering items to a person in a home. It covers only the 'bring items within reach' fragment of the comfort instance; it cannot reposition a patient, adjust bedding, or assess pain.

sources.title: Robotic Healthcare | Shower automation
sources.claim: The Poseidon automated shower cabin used in elder and disability care is operated by the bather via a control panel so that the user washes themselves; it is a user-controlled washing installation rather than an autonomous robot that bathes a dependent patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisted bathing. Cited as context for the personal-care instance: the marketed systems require the care recipient to operate them and cannot perform incontinence care, transfers or skin assessment, so they do not substantiate completion.

tasks.label: Sterilize equipment and supplies, using germicides, sterilizer, or autoclave.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Physician office / outpatient clinic: after minor procedures (suturing, biopsy, IUD insertion, nail surgery), the LPN gathers soiled instruments, pre-cleans/scrubs them at the dirty sink or ultrasonic, dries and inspects them, pouches and seals them with chemical indicators, loads a tabletop steam autoclave, runs and logs the cycle, then unloads, checks indicators and stores the packs. Small varied instrument sets, mixed hinged and sharp items, done between patients.

Nursing home / long-term care unit: germicidal disinfection of shared resident-care equipment between residents — glucometers, BP cuffs, thermometers, stethoscopes, pulse oximeters, mechanical lift slings/frames, wheelchairs, walkers, nebulizer cups — using EPA-registered wipes or germicidal solution with a required wet contact time, done at the bedside or in a utility room amid residents and staff.

Hospital or LTC soiled utility room: emptying, cleaning and disinfecting bedpans, urinals, wash basins, commode buckets, emesis basins and suction canisters, running the bedpan washer-disinfector or soaking items in germicidal solution, then drying and returning them to service.

Hospital sterile processing / procedure suite support: a batch of used instrument sets or semicritical devices is decontaminated, racked, run through a washer-disinfector and then a steam sterilizer (or high-level disinfection for scopes/probes), with load records, biological and chemical indicators, cool-down and transfer to sterile storage.

Home health / group home visit: disinfecting reusable supplies and equipment in the patient's own home — nebulizer cups and tubing, tracheostomy inner cannulas, irrigation and suction equipment, glucometer — by soaking in germicide or boiling, in a kitchen or bathroom whose layout, sink and clutter differ at every house.

sources.title: Atlas Workflow Automation Vehicle for Washers | STERIS
sources.claim: STERIS ATLAS Workflow Automation Vehicle is a commercial system that automatically picks up instrument racks, selects and loads washer/disinfectors, queues loads and delivers clean racks to the prep-and-pack area in hospital sterile processing departments.

sources.system: STERIS ATLAS WAV ('Bella') at Bryan Health
sources.title: Bryan Health Uses New Robotic Technology to Clean and Sterilize Surgical Instruments
sources.claim: The ATLAS vehicle is deployed at Bryan Health, where it autonomously collects racks of used surgical instruments from the counter by the decontamination sink and loads them into the washer/disinfectors to start the cleaning cycle.

sources.system: Belimed WA 290 washer automation with WD 290 IQ washer-disinfectors
sources.title: WA 290 - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: Belimed WA 290 is a commercial automation line for CSSDs in which a shuttle system moves instrument racks between hygiene zones and loads and unloads the WD 290 IQ washer-disinfectors without staff handling.

sources.system: Belimed TS MST / TS 16 sterilizer automation for MST-V steam sterilizers
sources.title: Sterilizer Automation | Belimed
sources.claim: Belimed sells automated loading/unloading transport systems for its hospital steam sterilizers, giving fully automated handling of batch carts into and out of the sterilizer chamber.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L, YOLO12 + ResNet perception, dual electromagnetic gripper)
sources.developer: University of Louisville (Sankaranarayanan, Stuart, Ahn, Sungarian, Chitalia) — ISMR 2026
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated fixed robot cell (Staubli TX2-60L arm with vision) autonomously identifies, sorts and packs surgical instruments into sterile ..., the assembly step that precedes sterilization in sterile processing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument identification, handling and tray packing in sterile processing. It transfers because the objects (hinged surgical instruments), the precision (correct set composition, damage-free handling) and the purpose-built cell are the same ones needed to prepare instruments for the autoclave in the rated task.

sources.title: Machine disinfection of bedpans - MEIKO
sources.claim: MEIKO bedpan washer-disinfectors, standard fixtures in hospital sluice rooms and care-home utility rooms, empty, clean, thermally disinfect and dry bedpans and urine bottles fully automatically once the item is placed in the chamber.

sources.title: commercial dishwashers, bedpan washers and disinfection - MEIKO
sources.claim: MEIKO also markets a fully automatic washer-disinfector for cleaning and disinfecting non-immersible reusable equipment such as breathing masks, regulators and harnesses without damaging the materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cleaning and disinfection of reusable non-instrument equipment. It transfers to disinfecting resident-care items (masks, tubing, nebulizer parts, basins) because the items, the required disinfection standard and the chamber-presented workflow are comparable.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: POSTECH's autonomous wiping and UV-C disinfection ... uses a robotic manipulator to physically ... before UV-C irradiation, and was tested with repeated autonomous operation in a working hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic germicidal wiping of clinical surfaces. It transfers to wiping down patient-care equipment because the action (mechanical wipe with disinfectant to a validated bacterial-reduction standard) and the objects (hard clinical surfaces and equipment) are comparable, though it is a research prototype.

sources.system: Getinge Roller Conveyor System (GRCS) for GEV/GTS sterilizers
sources.title: Loading and unloading system for GEV sterilizers from Getinge - Cleanroom Processes
sources.claim: Getinge's Roller Conveyor System is a modular, fully automatic system that loads and unloads batches of product into and out of GEV/GTS terminal sterilizers, removing all manual handling of sterilizer loads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated loading and unloading of steam sterilizers in pharmaceutical production. It transfers because the physical act rated here — presenting loads to a sterilizer, running the validated cycle and removing the sterile load — is the same, on comparable racked loads in a purpose-built line.

tasks.label: Make appointments, keep records, or perform other clerical duties in doctors' offices or clinics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Set up equipment and prepare medical treatment rooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Physician office / outpatient clinic: turning over an exam or treatment room between patients — wipe and disinfect the exam table, counter and high-touch surfaces, tear off and pull fresh table paper, empty trash/sharps as needed, restock gloves, gauze, specimen cups and drapes, and lay out the instruments the next visit needs (otoscope tips, speculum, suture-removal kit) with equipment checked and ready.

Nursing home / clinic: stocking and replenishing the treatment cart or procedure kit from the stock room — pulling dressings, saline, tape, syringes, catheters and gloves to par levels and assembling a per-resident wound-care set for the treatment round.

Long-term care or hospital: readying a resident/patient room for a treatment or new admission — making the bed with clean linen, bringing in and positioning an IV pole, oxygen concentrator, suction unit or bedside commode, placing call light and supplies within reach, clearing space around the bed.

Hospital or clinic: setting up bedside treatment equipment for a specific therapy — hanging and spiking a fluid bag, loading and priming the administration set into an infusion pump, connecting suction canister and tubing to wall vacuum, attaching oxygen tubing/humidifier to the flowmeter, setting up a nebulizer or EKG, and verifying each functions.

Clinic, hospital or LTC treatment room: setting up a sterile field/tray for a minor procedure (suturing, biopsy, catheter insertion, dressing change) — opening sterile packs onto a Mayo stand without contamination, arranging instruments in order of use, adding antiseptic and solutions, positioning light and waste receptacle.

Home health visit: preparing a treatment area in the patient's own home — clearing and cleaning a table or bedside surface, unpacking and laying out supplies from the nursing bag, setting up a nebulizer, infusion pump or wound-care field amid household furniture, pets and variable lighting.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator deployed in US hospitals, autonomously picks supplies from supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms; it performs fetch/deliver and restocking logistics, not room preparation or equipment setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply logistics. Shows autonomous manipulation inside a structured hospital (E2) but covers only the fetch-and-deliver fragment of preparing a treatment room; no cleaning, room restocking, linen/paper change or device setup is claimed.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics humanoid MMR performs one million deliveries - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Diligent's Moxi fleet has passed one million deliveries across hospital customers, automating delivery and restocking runs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital logistics at commercial scale; establishes maturity of autonomous transport/restocking runs but not of preparing or equipping a treatment room.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR autonomously cleans restrooms in hospitals and airports, scrubbing fixtures and floors, opening doors and picking up trash, offered on a commercial monthly lease.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous room cleaning inside an institution-controlled facility (E2). Covers only the surface-cleaning fragment of exam-room turnover; the system restocks nothing, changes no linen or table paper and sets up no medical equipment.

sources.system: Autonomous UV-C Disinfection and Wiping Robot
sources.developer: POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology)
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed autonomous robot combining physical wiping with UV-C irradiation was assessed disinfecting a real hospital environment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: surface disinfection of hospital rooms. Substantiates autonomous wiping of room surfaces in an E2 hospital, but is a research assessment and covers no stocking, layout or equipment-setup step of room preparation.

sources.developer: UVD Robots / Blue Ocean Robotics (deployed via RobotLAB)
sources.title: UV-C Disinfection Robots · RobotLAB
sources.claim: Fully autonomous UVD Robots Model C units are sold and deployed for patient-room turnover sanitization, while manual cleaning of visible soil is still done by staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminal room disinfection during patient-room turnover. Adjacent to room preparation but supplies only the pathogen-reduction step; the vendor states manual cleaning is still required.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick system autonomously picks a wide range of small items into kits and totes and is deployed for around-the-clock order filling in pharmaceutical distribution facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated kitting of small packaged pharmaceutical/consumer items in a fixtured picking cell. Stocking a treatment cart or assembling a wound-care supply kit handles comparable small packaged consumables at comparable placement precision once stock is presented in bins.

sources.title: ARxIUM: New RIVA Automated IV Compounding System - Healthcare Packaging
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA is a fully automated robotic compounding cell that prepares syringes and IV bags aseptically in an ISO Class ... enclosure for hospital and 503B pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aseptic preparation of treatment materials inside a purpose-built robotic enclosure. Objects (syringes, vials, IV bags, spikes) and the sterility discipline match or exceed those of laying out a sterile procedure setup, supporting E1 when the setup is brought to a machine.

sources.title: Ballad Health expands patient safety with new robotic pharmacy technology
sources.claim: Ballad Health placed Omnicell IVX Station robots into service for IV compounding in its hospital pharmacies in 2025, extending earlier robotic dispensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sterile dose preparation in a hospital. Confirms current commercial deployment of enclosed aseptic robotic cells preparing treatment materials, the E1 analogue of preparing a sterile setup.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A robotic bench cell autonomously sorts surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays with dividers, in a hybrid workflow where a technician inspects and the robot arranges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile processing tray assembly. Same objects (surgical instruments) and same output form (an ordered, sterile-ready tray) as setting up a procedure tray, performed in a fixtured benchtop cell.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: CMU's Operating Room Bot, an autonomous mobile manipulator for item-level OR logistics, achieved 80% success in supply retrieval and 96% in restocking in system-level tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-room item-level supply handling for surgical rooms. Closest research system to preparing a treatment room in situ; its retrieval reliability remains well below what a nurse's employer would accept.

tasks.label: Wash and dress bodies of deceased persons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing home / long-term care: after an expected resident death, the LPN (with an aide) does postmortem care at the bedside — flattens the bed and positions the body in alignment, removes tubes, dressings and catheter, washes the whole body including turning for perineal and back care, changes soiled linen, dresses the resident in a clean gown or personal clothing, combs hair, applies ID tags, wraps in a shroud/body bag, and readies the body for funeral-home pickup, often with family in the room.

Hospital med-surg/telemetry or inpatient hospice unit: patient dies with IV lines, drains, oxygen and monitor leads; nurse removes or secures devices per policy, cleans blood and secretions, redresses wounds, pads or packs draining orifices, washes and dries the body, dresses it in a clean gown, applies wrist/toe/bag ID tags, positions it for family viewing, then bags the body and helps transfer it to the morgue cart.

Private home (home hospice / home health visit): LVN arrives at the residence after a death and works in a bedroom or living-room hospital bed with variable clearance, pets, clutter and family present; washes the body, removes catheter or pump, dresses the deceased in their own clothing, positions it, and waits with the family for the funeral home.

Complicated body in a facility room: obese, contracted or rigid body, heavy fecal/urine/blood soiling, wounds or ostomy, isolation precautions requiring PPE; two-person log-rolling, repeated washing, absorbent padding, gown and shroud application, ID tagging, and careful lifting onto the stretcher.

Facility death with religious or cultural requirements and family participation: family or clergy present and assisting, specific positioning, restrictions on who may touch or wash the body, particular garments or shroud, jewelry and religious articles handled per instruction, body prepared for immediate viewing.

sources.title: Georgia Tech's Cody Robot Makes Progress Towards Autonomous Bed Baths for Patient Hygiene | hizook
sources.claim: Cody, a research robot with compliant arms and ... bath-mitt end effector, autonomously performed wiping motions to clean operator-selected patches of skin (upper arm, forearm, thigh, leg) on a live person in a lab — a sub-step of bathing only, with a human selecting each area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (bed bathing a living patient) is the closest robotic analogue to washing a body; it shows the state of the art is operator-selected wiping of single limb segments in a lab, far short of whole-body washing, turning and drying of a limp adult body.

sources.title: Robotic-assisted dressing system accommodates different poses, body types and garments
sources.claim: Carnegie Mellon's robot-assisted dressing system, trained in simulation with reinforcement learning, pulls a hospital gown or shirt sleeve up a seated person's arm in the lab; the researchers note prior work assumed limited arm poses and a single fixed garment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (assistive dressing of a person) directly bears on dressing a body; the demonstrated scope is one sleeve onto one arm of a cooperative, upright person, not gowning or shrouding an unresponsive supine body.

sources.system: Compliant gripper for robot-assisted trouser dressing/undressing
sources.title: Development of a Compliant Gripper for Safe Robot-Assisted Trouser Dressing-Undressing
sources.claim: A December 2025 study on robot trouser dressing reports prior humanoid trouser-dressing assistance succeeding about 73% of the time with care recipients who can stand or walk, and its own system begins with the garment already held by the robot — partial, cooperative-user dressing at lab reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (dressing lower-body garments on a person) is the nearest match to putting clothing on a deceased person; ~73% success with mobile, cooperative recipients shows no system reaches worker-quality dressing of a limp body.

sources.system: Miraburu Assist Bath (Mirai Ningen Sentakuki technology)
sources.title: Expo-Inspired 'Human Washing Machine' Tech Debuts in Japan's Nursing Care, Slashing Bathing Burdens
sources.claim: The 'Miraburu Assist Bath', derived from the Expo 2025 'human washing machine', was deployed in June 2026 at an Osaka assisted-living home; it is a microbubble tub with a side-access door that cleans a seated occupant, but performs no undressing, turning, drying, dressing, tagging or body handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (mechanized bathing in a care facility) is the strongest purpose-built washing machine actually in service, but it requires a living occupant to be seated inside by staff and does no dressing, shrouding or body transfer.

sources.title: Automated Processes of Preparing and Washing Deceased during Pandemic
sources.claim: The closest purpose-built concept for this exact task, the patented 'PaakShooy' corpse preparation machine (washing chamber, drying cell, shrouding unit), is described by its own authors as semi-automated and presented as design work with simulation/animation rather than an autonomous system in service.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (washing and shrouding a deceased body) in a purpose-built machine, but autonomy is not established and the reported work is design and simulation, so it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

tasks.label: Clean rooms and make beds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Long-term care facility: after a resident is up for the day, the LPN tidies the resident's room — straightens the bedside table, puts personal items and mobility aids back in place, empties the small trash can, wipes the overbed table — and remakes the bed with the existing clean linens (smooth bottom sheet, pull up top sheet and spread, arrange pillow). No soiling involved.

Nursing home or hospital, unoccupied bed: full linen change — strip used top/bottom sheets, draw sheet and underpad, bag soiled linen in the hamper, apply a fresh fitted sheet with mitered corners, draw sheet, top sheet, blanket and pillowcase, then wipe down the bedrails, call light and bedside surfaces.

Occupied bed: patient is bedbound or unable to get up, often after an incontinence episode or spill. Nurse rolls/repositions the patient, removes wet or soiled linens and pads from under them, cleans and disinfects the mattress and surrounding area, places clean linens under and around the patient, and bags contaminated material as biohazard.

Hospital room or clinic exam room turnover between patients or after discharge: strip the bed/table, dispose of used paper and waste, disinfect all high-touch surfaces (rails, tray table, chair, counters, exam table) to infection-control standard, pull a fresh sheet of exam-table paper, restock gloves/gauze/linen supplies, and remake the bed for the next patient.

Private home (home health or hospice visit): while the patient is up in a chair, the nurse tidies the bedroom — clears clutter and used supplies from the nightstand, removes trash, straightens the room for fall safety — and makes the bed with the bedding already on it.

Private home: change the bed of a bedbound patient during a visit — soiled sheets and incontinence pads replaced with fresh linens around the patient, area wiped down, soiled linen handled — in a cluttered, non-standard room with pets, family members, low lighting and varied bed types (including rented hospital beds).

sources.title: These robots read head nods, not code, to tidy a bedroom | The Daily Star
sources.claim: Two Figure F.03 humanoids running the Helix-02 VLA policy autonomously reset a staged bedroom in under two minutes — hanging clothes, putting objects away, taking out trash, and cooperatively making a bed by spreading and smoothing a duvet — with no teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly matches the light variant of this task: tidying a room, removing trash and making a bed with bedding already present; the objects (duvet, pillows, loose items) and precision demands are comparable to remaking an unsoiled resident bed.

sources.title: These robots read head nods, not code, to tidy a bedroom | The Daily Star
sources.claim: An earlier Figure demonstration showed a single F.03 tidying a living room, including spraying and wiping surfaces and replacing cushions, using the same learned policy.
sources.transferJustification: Room cleaning: spraying and wiping household surfaces and putting objects away is the 'clean rooms' half of this task at the level required for a non-clinical tidy-up.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's autonomous bathroom cleaning robot is commercially deployed in hospitals and airports, cleaning fixtures and floors and picking up trash after a one-time VR-based mapping of each fixed-layout restroom.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue for cleaning inside a healthcare facility; it covers fixture/floor cleaning and trash pickup in restrooms but not bed linens, exam-table paper or restocking consumables.

sources.title: Those viral bathroom-cleaning bots won't be saving our butts anytime soon | Popular Science
sources.claim: Somatic's CEO states the robot leaves restrooms indistinguishable from human cleaning, but restocking consumables such as paper remains a human task.
sources.transferJustification: Documents the boundary of deployed facility-cleaning robots: consumable replacement and restocking, which room turnover in a clinic requires, are still done by people.

sources.title: UV Robot Automates Coronavirus Disinfection, Streamlines Hospital Processes - Inside Unmanned Systems
sources.claim: UVD Robots' self-navigating UV-C robots disinfect hospital patient rooms autonomously and are deployed in hospitals worldwide, but they only irradiate surfaces — they do not physically clean, remove waste, or handle linens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (terminal room disinfection) in the same setting; shows what deployed hospital room robots do — light-based disinfection only, no physical cleaning or bed making.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection - TechXplore
sources.claim: POSTECH researchers built an autonomous hospital robot that navigates wards and uses a manipulator to physically wipe surfaces plus UV-C to disinfect; validated in real-world hospital testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (surface wiping/disinfection in patient areas); shows manipulator-based wiping is feasible in a hospital, but the system does no linen handling, waste removal or bed making.

sources.title: Weave Robotics launches Isaac, its first mobile humanoid robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Weave Robotics launched Isaac 1, a $7,999 wheeled home robot advertised to make beds and tidy rooms, with deliveries starting in fall 2026; it runs autonomously by default but falls back on remote teleoperation whenever it cannot finish a task.
sources.transferJustification: Home bed-making and room tidying, but the degree of teleoperation is undisclosed and units had not shipped as of July 2026, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Toyota Human Support Robot (HSR) bed-making policy
sources.title: Robot Bed-Making: Deep Transfer Learning Using Depth Sensing of Deformable Fabric (ResearchGate)
sources.claim: UC Berkeley's AUTOLAB used a Toyota Human Support Robot in a laboratory setup to learn autonomous bed-making, formalized as maximizing blanket surface coverage on a bed frame; the work does not include stripping or applying fresh sheets.
sources.transferJustification: Bed-making research in a lab-fixtured setup; relevant to the E1 counterfactual for linen work, but limited to pulling a blanket for coverage, not fitted-sheet application or soiled-linen handling.

tasks.label: Inventory and requisition supplies and instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing / long-term care facility: LPN inventories the medication cart and treatment cart (drawers, bins, blister cards, narcotics count), then checks the unit supply closet (briefs, dressings, gloves, syringes, feeding supplies) against par levels and submits a weekly requisition to central supply or the contract pharmacy. Items are in closed carts, cabinets and a small closet; staff and residents circulate.

Physician office, urgent care or outpatient clinic: LPN/LVN restock-checks exam-room cabinets and drawers, the vaccine refrigerator, and the supply cupboard; notes low or expired items (needles, swabs, dressings, specimen containers, vaccines) and places the order through a vendor portal or an internal requisition form.

Hospital or large clinic clean supply room: LPN walks the open wire shelving of labeled bins, scans/records par-level shortfalls of standardized packaged supplies (IV tubing, catheter kits, gloves, dressings) and submits a requisition to central supply/materials management. Storage is open-shelf, mapped and standardized; corridor traffic is routine.

Home health / private-duty visit: LPN inventories the patient's supplies stored in the home (closet shelves, bedroom bins, partially used boxes of wound-care, ostomy or catheter supplies), estimates weeks on hand, checks expirations, and phones or e-requisitions the agency or DME supplier for a resupply.

Instruments in a clinic, ambulatory surgery center or LTC treatment room: LPN counts and inspects instrument sets and sterile packs (suture-removal kits, forceps, scissors, trays), verifies pack integrity and sterilization/expiration dates, logs quantities on hand, and requisitions replacements or repairs for missing, dull or damaged instruments.

sources.title: Simbe upgrades vision platform with AI-powered capabilities - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Tally is an autonomous shelf-scanning mobile robot that navigates retail stores and produces SKU-level stock, out-of-stock and shelf-tag data; it is commercially deployed across grocery and home-improvement chains (e.g., 17 Harmons stores).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory audit. It transfers to par-level counting of packaged medical supplies on open shelving because both require SKU-level recognition of boxed goods on labeled shelving in an occupied, institution-controlled facility, at counting (not manipulation) precision.

sources.title: Inventory Replenishment | Simbe Robotics
sources.claim: Simbe's platform closes the loop from robot-collected shelf counts to replenishment ordering, i.e. the counting robot's data feeds the reorder/requisition step rather than requiring a human to re-key counts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail replenishment ordering. The requisition half of the nursing task is likewise a min/max-triggered order generated from counts, so integration of robot counts with an ordering system covers the same output.

sources.system: Dane AiR DC (Brain Corp autonomy stack)
sources.title: Dane Technologies and Brain Corp launch new inventory scanning robot
sources.claim: Dane AiR DC is an autonomous inventory-scanning mobile robot for warehouses and distribution centers, reported at 99.5% scanning accuracy over 200,000+ sq ft.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting. Transfers to storeroom par-level counting: same labeled-shelf/rack scanning, same count-accuracy requirement, in an institution-controlled indoor facility.

sources.title: Verity, On and Maersk Pilot RFID Technology with Autonomous Drones in Warehouse Inventory Management
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous inventory drones fly warehouse aisles unattended and read RFID/barcode locations at high accuracy; deployed with UPS Supply Chain Solutions and piloted with On/Maersk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stock counting of tagged goods in a human work facility; transfers to counting RFID/barcode-tagged medical supply bins where the output is an accurate on-hand count feeding replenishment.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Multiple Hospitals Adopt Omnicell's XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System to Enhance Medication Inventory Management
sources.claim: The XR2 is a robotic central-pharmacy storage, picking and dispensing system installed in US hospitals; every item is barcode-scanned into and out of the enclosed robot, which maintains accurate perpetual inventory and dispenses earliest-expiring stock first.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated perpetual inventory of packaged clinical stock inside a purpose-built robotic enclosure. It is the E1 form of 'inventory supplies': quantities and expirations are known continuously and drive replenishment without a human counting.

sources.date: 2026-04-13 (product page, product commercially installed for years)
sources.title: Automated Pharmacy Storage System - Swisslog BoxPicker
sources.claim: BoxPicker is a fully robotic high-density automated storage and retrieval system used by hospital pharmacies, controlling storage, retrieval and stock records of medications and supplies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic storage/retrieval with system-of-record stock counts. Transfers to the inventory half of this task at E1, where stock is presented to the machine rather than counted in place.

sources.title: AutoStore ASRS | High-Density Storage & Retrieval by Kardex
sources.claim: AutoStore robotic bin-storage grids are marketed and installed for healthcare and life-sciences stock, giving item-level inventory tracking and controlled quantities for surgical-pack and diagnostic-kit kitting; Medline runs large AutoStore installations for medical supply distribution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic goods-to-person storage of medical supplies with perpetual quantity control. At E1 this is exactly how 'inventory supplies and instruments' arises: every unit is machine-handled and counted, and min/max triggers the requisition.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L arm, dual electromagnetic gripper)
sources.developer: University of Louisville / Georgia Tech authors (ISMR 2026 paper)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)

tasks.label: Measure clients' bridge and eye size, temple length, vertex distance, pupillary distance, and optical centers of eyes, using measuring devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cooperative adult in an optical dispensary; single-vision order where the only client measurement needed is distance (and sometimes near) pupillary distance, taken with a pupillometer or read from the exam autorefractor; frame's boxed eye size/bridge/temple length are read from the temple stamp or catalog and the lab uses the frame's boxed center vertically.

Cooperative adult in a dispensary ordering progressive or bifocal lenses: optician seats the client at eye level, places and pre-adjusts the selected frame, measures monocular PDs and fitting/segment heights relative to the worn frame (felt-pen marks on the demo lens, seg-height gauge, or digital centration photo), and records frame A/DBL/temple.

Premium free-form/personalized lens order in a dispensary: full 'as-worn' parameter set on the pre-adjusted frame - monocular PDs, fitting heights, vertex distance with a distometer or side image, pantoscopic tilt, face-form wrap - plus frame dimensions, with the client in habitual posture and natural gaze.

Pediatric dispensing in an optical shop or pediatric clinic: young or squirmy child, small facial features, frequent head movement and poor fixation; optician kneels or crouches, coaxes fixation, and measures PD and heights quickly with a ruler/pupillometer, often repeating and cross-checking.

Older adult or client with atypical anatomy/mobility in a dispensary: wheelchair or scooter user, tremor, ptosis, strabismus or prosthetic eye, deep-set eyes or asymmetric face; optician adapts technique (corneal-reflex method, monocular measurement, occlusion) and works at whatever height and posture the client can hold.

Off-site dispensing: nursing-home room, school vision program, mobile clinic van, home visit, or an employer's site for safety eyewear; measurements taken with handheld pupillometer/PD ruler and a portable tablet system in whatever space, lighting and seating is available.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated objective refraction/keratometry. It transfers because the machine must find and align to the client's pupils in three dimensions and capture the same ocular landmarks used for pupillary-distance measurement, on the same object (a seated client's eyes), at sub-millimetre precision, in the same room type.

sources.title: A Comparative Analysis of Interpupillary Distance Measurement Techniques Evaluation in Modern Times: From Rulers to Apps
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed comparison of interpupillary-distance methods found autorefractor IPD agrees closely with the pupillometer, the clinical reference used by dispensers (mean difference 0.15 mm), i.e. instrument-derived PD is of dispensing quality.
sources.transferJustification: Accuracy benchmark only: it establishes that machine-measured PD matches the optician's pupillometer standard. The examiner-operated device's autonomy is unclear, so this item is not relied on for the autonomy of any positive judgment.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic alignment of an ophthalmic instrument to a person's eye. It shows a robot can localize pupils in 3D on an unrestrained client - the perceptual core of PD/optical-centre measurement - but it involves no spectacle frame and yields no frame-referenced dispensing values.

sources.claim: The Duke robotic OCT system has been run on more than 40 human subjects under IRB approval, combining coarse face tracking with fine pupil tracking to bring the scanner to the subject.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the Nature BME paper; it establishes repeatability of autonomous robotic eye alignment on real people rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.title: Optikam - Fitting & Dispensing Tool for Eye Care Professionals
sources.claim: The accepted output of dispensing measurement is monocular PDs, multifocal fitting heights, ..., wrap and frame dimensions taken with the chosen frame worn and pre-adjusted; the commercial systems that capture this set (Optikam, ZEISS i.Terminal 2) are camera-and-software units with no actuator, operated after a person fits the frame.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to define the accepted output and to show the frame-referenced part of it is achieved today only by non-actuated camera systems that depend on a person placing and adjusting the frame; being non-actuated, it cannot support a positive robotic judgment.

sources.claim: Where no digital centration unit is used, the optician physically marks the pupil positions on the demo lens of the worn frame with a felt pen and measures the separation - a contact, hand-tool procedure on the client's face and eyewear.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish the physical content of the task (hand tools applied to the client's face and worn frame), not to support any positive capability judgment.

tasks.label: Verify that finished lenses are ground to specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail optical shop (chain or private practice): a single-vision job comes back from the outside lab in a job tray; the optician reads the Rx/work order, puts each lens on the lensmeter, verifies sphere, cylinder, axis, optical-center/PD placement and any prism, checks the lenses and mounting under a lamp, then accepts the job or returns it to the lab.

Retail dispensary: a progressive or multifocal job is verified — locate the laser engravings/reference marks, re-mark the lens, verify distance and near (add) powers at the reference points, verify fitting-cross/segment height and unwanted prism against the ordered measurements, and confirm the design/brand supplied.

Store with an on-site finishing lab: the optician verifies lenses just edged and mounted in house — power and axis after mounting, lens shape/size and bevel fit to the frame, absence of chips, waves or mounting stress, before the job goes to the dispensing table.

Specialty/complex job: high powers beyond about ±10 D, high cylinder, prescribed prism, slab-off, lenticular, occupational lens, ANSI Z87.1 safety eyewear or children's polycarbonate — the optician measures power, prism, thickness and markings and judges conformity against ANSI Z80.1/Z87.1 tolerances.

Cosmetic and coating inspection of the finished job: examining lens surfaces under a lamp for scratches, pits, coating comets/waves, haze, edge chips and polish quality on the finished (edged) lenses before dispensing.

Non-power attribute verification of the finished job: tint density and uniformity between the pair, polarization axis orientation, photochromic behavior, and confirming the correct lens material/design/brand was supplied (UV lamp, engraving check, thickness gauge).

tasks.label: Assist clients in selecting frames according to style and color, and ensure that frames are coordinated with facial and eye measurements and optical prescriptions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain retail optical store (LensCrafters, Costco Optical, Walmart Vision, Target Optical, Warby Parker): walk-in adult with a routine single-vision or progressive Rx browses a frame wall of several hundred frames. Optician pulls candidate frames, hands them to the client, seats them on the face, discusses style/color against face shape, skin tone and wardrobe, checks eye size, bridge and temple length against the client's face, takes/verifies PD and fitting height, and confirms the chosen frame will carry the Rx (lens thickness, minimum blank size, decentration).

Independent optometrist's dispensary or boutique optical shop: seated one-on-one consultation with a smaller curated frame inventory. Optician repeatedly retrieves frames from cases and drawers, places them on the client, holds a mirror, adjusts temples/nose pads enough to judge fit, narrows choices with the client (and often an accompanying spouse), then measures monocular PD and segment/fitting heights on the selected frame.

Complex or specialty prescription: high myopia/hyperopia, prism, anisometropia, first-time progressives, or occupational/sports/safety eyewear. Frame choice is heavily constrained by measurements and Rx (small eye size and low fitting height for thick lenses, wrap angle limits, minimum B-measurement for progressives, ANSI-rated frames). Optician steers the client's style preferences toward the small set of workable frames and explains the trade-offs while trying them on.

Pediatric fitting in a store or pediatric practice: child (toddler to teen) who squirms, resists, or has strong preferences; parent present and often deciding. Optician holds frames on the child's face, checks bridge fit on a low nasal bridge, temple wrap, and small PD, tries multiple frames quickly, and manages the child's and parent's expectations on color/character branding versus fit and Rx requirements.

Mobile/on-site dispensing: optician travels with a frame board or case to a nursing home resident's room, a homebound patient's living room, or an employer safety-eyewear fitting event. Layout, seating and lighting are as found; the client may have limited mobility, tremor, dementia or low vision, so the optician holds frames up, describes colors verbally, and takes facial measurements in a non-standard setup.

sources.title: In-Store Robot Makes Your Glasses While You Wait
sources.claim: JINS operates an in-store automated machine ('Kanna') that edges and mounts prescription lenses into a customer-chosen frame in about 30 minutes; it is a lens-processing machine and does not interact with the client or assist in choosing frames.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = in-store lens edging/mounting, a downstream fabrication step performed on fixtured lenses inside a machine enclosure. It does NOT transfer to this task: it never handles a client, never presents frames for try-on, and makes no style/color or face-measurement judgment, so it cannot substantiate completion of frame-selection assistance at any tier.

sources.system: ZEISS VISUFIT 1000 digital centration and virtual try-on platform

sources.transferJustification: Related task = capturing centration/facial measurements and on-screen frame try-on. It does not transfer: the platform is a sensing/display device, not a physically embodied machine acting on the world, and it is operated by the optician, who still retrieves, presents and fits the physical frames.

sources.claim: Robots actually deployed in retail sales floors perform inventory scanning, wayfinding, cleaning and greeting; none retrieve merchandise, hand it to shoppers, or fit products on a customer's body.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous operation on a retail sales floor among shoppers. It shows navigation in an E2 retail setting is solved, but the capability does not transfer: Tally has no arms and performs no customer-facing object handling, consultation, or measurement of a person, which are the substance of this task.

tasks.label: Heat, shape, or bend plastic or metal frames to adjust eyeglasses to fit clients, using pliers and hands.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dispensing a new pair with an acetate/zyl (plastic) frame in an optical retail dispensary: optician seats the frame on the client's face, judges four-point touch, pantoscopic tilt and vertex distance, softens the frame at a hot-air warmer, hand-bends temples, ear bends and bridge, and re-tries on the face several times until the client says it is level and comfortable.

Dispensing or refitting a metal/titanium frame at the dispensing table: aligning the frame front, twisting endpieces, bending pad arms in three axes with pad-adjusting pliers, setting temple spread and ear bends, with repeated try-on and client feedback.

Walk-in service adjustment of a client's existing, worn glasses (crooked, loose, spread out, slightly bent): optician diagnoses the misalignment on the face, takes the pair to the bench or warmer, straightens and re-bends, then verifies fit back on the client.

Bench pre-adjustment of a finished job received from the lab, no client present: bringing the assembled frame back to standard/nominal alignment (frame front flat and untwisted, temples even, tips at the stock heat-set curve) at the finishing bench before the client arrives.

Difficult or delicate cases: rimless drill-mounts and three-piece mounts, memory-metal frames, children's frames, thin high-value wire frames, or clients with markedly asymmetric faces, hearing aids, or who cannot describe comfort; high risk of cracking lenses or snapping the frame.

Off-site dispensing: adjusting eyeglasses during nursing-home, home-bound or school-program visits with a portable kit, in a resident's room or on a borrowed table, often without a frame warmer and with a client of limited mobility or cognition.

tasks.label: Show customers how to insert, remove, and care for their contact lenses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: First-time soft contact lens wearer at an optical dispensary/exam room: optician washes hands, demonstrates lens handling on a real lens, often inserts the first lens into the patient's eye, then coaches the anxious patient through repeated insertion and removal attempts (holding lids, guiding the hand, checking lens centration) until the patient succeeds unaided; then demonstrates rubbing/rinsing, case filling, and wear schedule. 20-45 minutes.

Existing wearer changing modality (daily disposable, toric, multifocal, or new solution system) in the dispensary: brief demonstration of the handling differences (lens orientation/inside-out check, no-rub vs rub regimen, peroxide case), plus a quick verification that the patient can insert and remove the new lens.

Specialty lens (scleral or RGP) training in a specialty contact lens clinic: teaching the patient to fill a scleral bowl with preservative-free saline without bubbles, use a DMV plunger or tripod technique, insert while bent forward, and remove with a plunger; plus cleaning and storage instruction. Long, high-dexterity, high-stakes session.

Child or teenage first-time wearer with a parent present: squeamish patient, heavy blink reflex, optician holds lids and repeatedly re-demonstrates, coaches parent as well, may take multiple visits; hygiene and wear-schedule instruction tailored for a young wearer.

Older adult or dexterity-impaired patient re-trained after poor technique: tremor, dry eye, long nails, or a lens the patient cannot remove; optician removes the stuck/decentered lens, re-demonstrates technique, may introduce an insertion tool, and re-teaches cleaning and case hygiene.

Care-only instruction at the dispensing/pickup counter: handing over the lens supply and care kit while explaining solution use, case replacement, rub-and-rinse, wear/replacement schedule and red-flag symptoms, with a short demonstration on a sample lens; no insertion into the patient's eye.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Dispensary bench/counter: customer's metal or zyl frame has a loose or missing hinge or rim-lock screw (temple falling off, lens loose). Optician inspects, sometimes extracts a stripped/broken screw, selects a matching screw from a multi-size assortment, aligns hinge barrels or rim, drives and torques the screw, trims/peens if long, checks temple action.

Replacement of small worn or broken components on an arbitrary frame model: silicone/PVC nose pads (screw-in or snap-in on pad arms), temple tips/ear socks, rim-lock hardware, spring-hinge parts sourced from a parts kit; fitted at the bench without damaging plating or acetate.

Metal frame bent out of shape (sat on, dropped): splayed or twisted temples, twisted bridge, distorted eyewire with lenses mounted. Optician grips with lined pliers and fingers, applies corrective bends with springback judgment, repeatedly checking four-point touch, temple alignment and lens plane symmetry until the frame sits true.

Plastic/acetate frame distorted or lens popped out: optician uses a frame warmer/salt pan to heat the front or temple, reshapes the warped eyewire or bridge, re-seats or snaps the lens back into the groove without chipping it or over-stretching the frame, then restores pantoscopic tilt and temple spread.

Structural break in a metal frame — snapped bridge, endpiece or temple. Optician judges repairability, jigs the pieces in alignment, protects/removes lenses, solders or laser-welds the joint, cleans, files and touches up the finish, or substitutes a replacement temple/hinge from stock and refits.

Broken plastic frame: hinge pulled out of the acetate temple or front, cracked rim or bridge. Optician heat-inserts a new hinge shield into the plastic at the correct depth and angle, or bonds/pins the crack, then refinishes and re-fits the frame to the wearer.

roles.title: Orthotists and Prosthetists
aliases: Orthotic and Prosthetic Technician (Orthotic and Prosthetic Tech)
roles.description: Design, measure, fit, and adapt orthopedic braces, appliances or prostheses, such as limbs or facial parts for patients with disabling conditions.

tasks.label: Fit, test, and evaluate devices on patients, and make adjustments for proper fit, function, and comfort.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Definitive delivery/fitting of a custom lower-limb prosthesis (transtibial or transfemoral) in an O&P clinic: don liner and socket on the residual limb, assess pressure/total-contact fit by palpation and patient report, set static and dynamic alignment, watch the patient walk in parallel bars, then heat-spot, grind, or pad the socket and adjust suspension until fit and gait are acceptable.

Follow-up adjustment visit on an existing prosthesis: patient reports pain, skin breakdown, pistoning, or limb volume change; prosthetist inspects the limb, locates the offending area, adds/removes sock ply or pads, relieves or builds up the socket, tweaks alignment, and re-tests the patient walking.

Fitting a custom-molded orthosis in clinic — AFO/KAFO, scoliosis TLSO, or cranial remolding helmet, often on a child — including trimline reduction, heat-gun flare and spot relief, pad and strap placement, checking skin blanching after wear, and verifying knee/ankle control while the patient stands and walks.

Fitting a prefabricated/off-the-shelf device in clinic or at hospital bedside: cervical collar, spinal orthosis, functional knee brace, fracture walker, diabetic shoes with custom foot orthoses; select size, don on the patient (sometimes in bed with precautions), adjust straps/uprights/heat-mold inserts, verify immobilization or fit, and instruct the patient.

Upper-limb prosthesis fitting (body-powered or myoelectric): check socket/frame fit on the residual limb, site and test electrodes for reliable EMG signals, adjust harness or suspension, program/tune grip modes, and have the patient perform functional tasks while making iterative adjustments.

sources.title: Equinox Locations Add Aescape, a Fully Automated Massage Bed - Athletech News
sources.claim: Aescape is a commercially deployed, fully automated two-arm robot that makes sustained physical contact with a human body on a purpose-built table in gyms, hotels and spas; it is the closest deployed system to hands-on work on a patient's body, but it only applies massage pressure and does not don, assess, or modify an orthopedic device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical contact with a human body in a structured facility. Transfer FAILS for orthotic/prosthetic fitting: the user is posed on a machine-specific table, the robot manipulates no objects, does not don a custom device, and cannot palpate for pressure points or grind/heat-adjust a socket.

sources.system: Self-Wearing Adaptive Garments via Soft Robotic Unfurling
sources.title: KAIST team wins IEEE RA-L Best Paper Award for second year in a row | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous dressing assistance is a laboratory soft-robotic garment that unfurls itself along a user's limb; it is a research demonstration, and does not involve fitting a rigid custom device or evaluating and modifying its fit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: donning an item onto a patient's limb. Transfer FAILS: a compliant sleeve unfurling on an arm is not equivalent to seating a rigid total-contact socket or thermoplastic orthosis, and the demonstration includes no fit evaluation, alignment, or device modification.

sources.claim: A humanoid built specifically for close-contact nursing work in human environments relies on remote human operation for the non-routine, close-human-contact portions of care tasks, indicating that autonomous hands-on work with a patient's body remains unsolved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hands-on assistive care with a person in a care facility. It shows the ceiling: close-contact patient tasks are teleoperated, so it cannot support autonomous completion of device fitting.

tasks.label: Instruct patients in the use and care of orthoses and prostheses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Delivery appointment in an O&P clinic for a new lower-limb prosthesis (transtibial/transfemoral): the practitioner explains and demonstrates donning and doffing with liner/sleeve or suction suction, sock-ply management, the graduated wear schedule, daily residual-limb skin inspection, and cleaning of the liner and socket; patient and clinician talk through problems and the patient teaches back.

Fitting/delivery of an orthosis in clinic (AFO, KAFO, custom knee brace, spinal orthosis, wrist splint, cranial helmet): instruction on correct strap tension and shoe/clothing interface, wear-time schedule, red-mark and skin-tolerance checks, cleaning and when to call the clinic.

Instruction directed to a caregiver or parent rather than the patient - e.g., parents of a child with a scoliosis brace or AFO, or a family member/aide of an elderly or cognitively impaired patient - covering application, wear schedule, skin checks and cleaning, often with written handouts and repetition.

Follow-up or adjustment visit instruction: reviewing care and troubleshooting for technology-heavy devices (myoelectric hand, microprocessor knee, elevated-vacuum system) - charging batteries, mode switching, app use, moisture precautions, component maintenance and replacement intervals for liners, sleeves and socks.

Instruction delivered outside the practitioner's own clinic - bedside at an inpatient rehab unit, a nursing facility, the patient's home, or by phone/telehealth follow-up - reinforcing wear schedule, skin care and cleaning, and coordinating with therapy staff.

tasks.label: Maintain patients' records.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Examine, interview, and measure patients to determine their appliance needs and to identify factors that could affect appliance fit.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial prosthetic evaluation in an O&P clinic exam room: new lower-limb amputee (often diabetic/dysvascular). Practitioner interviews about medical history, comorbidities, prior devices, home environment and K-level goals; visually inspects and palpates the residual limb for scar adherence, bony prominences, redundant tissue, neuromas, edema and skin integrity; measures limb length and serial circumferences with tape, joint ROM with a goniometer, and checks for hip/knee contracture; observes sitting/standing balance and transfers; concludes with a documented determination of socket design, suspension and componentry plus fit-affecting factors.

Custom lower- or upper-limb orthosis evaluation in a clinic (AFO/KAFO, knee brace, wrist-hand orthosis), often for a stroke, CP or post-injury patient. Practitioner interviews patient/caregiver, assesses muscle tone and spasticity, manual muscle strength, sensation, joint alignment and ROM, skin condition and edema, palpates malleoli/condyles, watches the patient walk, and takes limb measurements; pediatric patients may be squirmy or uncooperative. Output is a determination of orthosis design, trimlines and factors affecting fit.

Spinal orthosis evaluation in clinic (adolescent scoliosis TLSO, or post-op/fracture spinal brace). Practitioner interviews patient and parents about growth, maturity, symptoms and compliance concerns; reviews radiographs; palpates spinous processes, iliac crests and ribs; assesses curve flexibility, trunk shift and respiratory considerations; measures trunk circumferences and heights; determines brace type, pad placement and fit-affecting factors (body habitus, skin sensitivity, growth).

Follow-up/problem-solving examination in clinic of a patient with an existing device reporting pain, rubbing or skin breakdown. Practitioner interviews about wear time, activity and symptom pattern; inspects skin for redness, blistering or ulceration; palpates pressure areas; has patient don the device and assesses fit statically and in gait; re-measures limb volume/sock ply; determines whether adjustment, new socket/liner or replacement is needed and what caused the fit problem.

Bedside evaluation in a hospital ward, inpatient rehab unit or skilled nursing facility: post-amputation or post-surgical patient partly undressed in bed with dressings, lines and limited mobility. Practitioner interviews patient and family (sometimes with cognitive impairment or language barriers), inspects and gently palpates the wound/limb, measures around dressings, checks ROM and contracture, coordinates with nursing/therapy, and determines preparatory device needs and fit constraints.

Home or community-site visit for a homebound patient: exam performed in a living room or bedroom taken as found, with variable lighting, furniture, pets and family present. Practitioner interviews patient and caregiver about the home layout and daily routine, inspects and measures the limb or trunk with portable tools, observes mobility over the home's own surfaces, and determines device needs and factors that could affect fit.

sources.claim: ProteCT is the closest robotic analogue to a hands-on patient examination: a purpose-built examination cabin with robotic arms through which a remote physician performed vital signs, auscultation, palpation and percussion on emergency-department patients. It is physician-teleoperated throughout, not autonomous.

It shows the state of the art requires a clinician in the loop driving the arms, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.system: Robotic ultrasound scoliosis scanning system (UR5 + FT300 + ultrasound probe)

sources.claim: A UR5 robot arm with force sensing and deep-learning spine tracking autonomously scanned the backs of 23 scoliosis patients with ultrasound, yielding deformity angles comparable to manual scanning. This covers only an imaging measurement, not the interview, skin/tissue examination, or determination of brace needs.

Transfer is partial only: it produces one imaging metric and does no interview, palpation for skin/bony landmarks, or clinical determination of appliance needs.

sources.title: Technical challenges in autonomous robotic ultrasound examinations: perception, planning, and control
sources.claim: A 2026 review of robot-assisted ultrasound covering 2021–early 2026 concludes that autonomous robotic examination of human patients has not made the transition to full autonomy, identifying perception, planning and control bottlenecks in the face of patient variability and motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic examination of a patient's body surface. It bounds the state of the art for any robot that must contact and assess a live human, which is what examining and measuring an orthotic/prosthetic patient requires.

sources.system: Clinical 3D scanning / photogrammetry for prosthetic socket design
sources.title: Smartphone-Based Automated Photogrammetry for Reconstruction of Residual Limb Models in Prosthetic Design
sources.claim: In current orthotic and prosthetic practice, residual-limb shape capture is done with human-held scanners or casting; the literature characterizes available techniques as operator-dependent, with no robotic system performing the capture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: capturing residual-limb geometry, the measurement sub-step of this task. It shows even the narrowest measurable sub-step is performed by a human holding a sensing device, not by a robot, and sensing devices alone do not act on the physical world.

tasks.label: Design orthopedic and prosthetic devices, based on physicians' prescriptions and examination and measurement of patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Custom lower-limb prosthetic socket design (transtibial or transfemoral) in a private O&P clinic: reads the physician's prescription and K-level, reviews the residual-limb cast or 3D scan and circumferential/length measurements, determines socket shape rectifications (reliefs over bony prominences, load-bearing build-ups), and specifies suspension, liner, foot, and knee componentry and alignment as a design/spec for fabrication.

Custom lower-limb orthosis design (AFO, KAFO, or custom foot orthosis) from a cast/scan and clinical measurements: sets trimlines, plantarflexion/dorsiflexion stops or joint selection, posting, padding, and material/thickness, and documents the design for in-house or central fabrication.

Selection and specification of a prefabricated or off-the-shelf device with custom modifications (functional knee brace, fracture orthosis, diabetic footwear with inserts, prefab spinal orthosis): measures/reviews measurements, chooses model and size from the catalog per the prescription and insurance code, and writes up the modifications required.

Spinal or cranial device design (scoliosis TLSO, corset/body jacket, cervical orthosis, or infant cranial remolding helmet): works from torso/head scan or cast plus radiographs and correction goals, designs corrective pressure zones, expansion reliefs, and closure system, and issues the design to the fabrication shop.

Upper-limb or partial-hand prosthesis and cosmetic restoration design: from prescription and limb measurements/scan, designs the socket/frame interface, specifies body-powered vs. myoelectric control, electrode sites, terminal device, wrist unit, and cosmetic cover color/finish.

tasks.label: Repair, rebuild, and modify prosthetic and orthopedic appliances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Follow-up/fitting visit in the clinic: patient wears a custom thermoplastic orthosis (AFO, wrist-hand orthosis, TLSO) that rubs or fits poorly. Practitioner marks the pressure area, spot-heats and reforms the plastic with a heat gun, grinds/trims a trimline, adds or removes padding, relocates a strap, then re-checks fit on the patient's limb and repeats until acceptable.

Bench repair of a patient's prosthesis in the practice lab: diagnose the fault, then replace worn or broken components (foot/pylon, knee unit, suspension sleeve or liner, valve, upper-limb cable and harness, cosmetic cover), unbolt/rebolt and torque, re-establish bench alignment, and function-test. Every device is a different make, model and vintage.

Socket rebuild/reline in the fabrication lab: grind out relief areas, add build-ups or pads, re-line or re-laminate, or remake the socket over a rectified positive model (plaster/foam), then trim, smooth, attach adapters and transfer the patient's existing components to the new socket.

Metal-and-leather orthosis rework: bend KAFO/AFO uprights with bending irons to change alignment, adjust or replace joints and stops, drill and rivet, re-sew or replace straps, leather and foam interfaces on braces and spinal orthoses.

Off-site repair or adjustment away from the lab: hospital bedside, nursing home room, school, patient's home or outreach clinic, with portable tools (heat gun, hand grinder, riveter) in a cluttered space around a seated or bedbound patient.

Footwear and foot-orthosis modification at the shop bench: grind and add posts, wedges, heel lifts, metatarsal pads or rocker soles; rough and cement sole additions on the patient's shoe; grind or remake a modified custom EVA insole.

sources.title: The 3-Axis Carver - CAD CAM for Prosthetics & Orthotics - Vorum
sources.claim: Vorum's 3-Axis Carver is a commercial, self-contained CNC carving machine used by O&P clinics and central fabs: an operator imports the CAD file and loads a blank, and the machine carves a prosthetic or orthotic mold to 0.1 mm in 5-20 minutes. It automates only the mold-shaping step of socket rebuilding, not thermoforming, lamination, trimming or component transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC rectification/mold carving used in socket rebuilds. It shapes plaster/foam positives inside a purpose-built machine enclosure; it does not repair or modify the appliance itself, so it covers only one step of the rebuild instance.

Chairside modification and finishing during a fitting appointment: spot-heating and reforming plastic, grinding a relief over a bony prominence, adding a pad or wedge, riveting a strap, with the patient waiting in the exam room.

Supervising and directing technicians in the fabrication lab: assigning and sequencing jobs, demonstrating technique, inspecting finished devices against the prescription, approving or rejecting them before delivery.

instances.label: Lower-limb prosthetic socket (transtibial/transfemoral): in a clinic exam room the prosthetist palpates and marks bony prominences and pressure-sensitive/tolerant zones on the live residual limb, applies wet plaster splints/bandage, hand-molds and applies selective compression while the plaster cures, removes the negative, then pours the plaster positive and rectifies it (build-ups over sensitive areas, removal over load-tolerant areas) in the attached fabrication lab.

Upper-limb, partial-hand, or facial/other small-anatomy impression: delicate plaster wrap on a patient's forearm, hand, digits or face with careful landmark capture, followed by pouring and detailed hand modification of a small, intricate positive model.

Lab-only model episode with no patient present: in the O&P fabrication lab a practitioner or technician produces and rectifies a positive model to prescribed measurements from an already-captured shape (negative cast received from another clinician/central fab, a duplicated model, or a model revised after a fitting problem), shaping it to the specified contours so it can be used for thermoforming or lamination.
