tasks.label: Conduct tests to determine cerebral death, the absence of brain activity, or the probability of recovery from a coma.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult ICU bedside EEG for suspected brain death (electrocerebral inactivity study): tech wheels cart to a ventilated, line- and drain-laden patient, measures 10-20 landmarks, abrades scalp and applies ~10-21 collodion/paste electrodes with double interelectrode distances, verifies impedances 100-10,000 ohms, records >=30 min at 2 uV/mm with ECG and artifact monitors, performs somatosensory/auditory/noxious reactivity testing, annotates ventilator and IV-pump artifact, then removes electrodes and cleans the patient's hair.

Emergent or routine bedside EEG on a comatose patient in ICU or ED to assess presence/pattern of brain activity and prognosis (anoxic, metabolic, post-status): rapid hookup at a crowded bedside, reactivity testing to name-calling and noxious stimulus, recording through nursing care and transport interruptions, technologist flagging burst-suppression or seizure activity for the reading neurologist.

Long-term continuous video-EEG hookup and maintenance in the neuro ICU for a comatose patient (days): collodion application with head wrap, twice-daily impedance/electrode integrity checks, re-gelling and replacing lifted electrodes on a patient with head dressings or an EVD, artifact troubleshooting, camera alignment, and final electrode removal and scalp cleaning.

Bedside evoked potential study for coma prognostication after cardiac arrest (median-nerve SSEP, sometimes BAEP): placing Erb's point, cervical and scalp recording electrodes, siting and adjusting the wrist stimulator to obtain a thumb twitch at tolerable intensity, averaging thousands of trials while suppressing ICU electrical noise, replicating waveforms and marking N20/N9 peaks.

Neonatal or pediatric ICU EEG for coma assessment or brain-death ancillary testing: small or fragile head in an isolette or with respiratory support, reduced electrode array, paste application on delicate skin, coordination with bedside nurses and parents, minimum recording durations per pediatric protocol.

sources.system: NovaGuide / Lucid Robotic System (NovaBot automated headset)
sources.title: Safety and efficacy of a novel robotic transcranial doppler system in subarachnoid hemorrhage
sources.claim: NovaGuide (Lucid Robotic System with NovaBot headset) is an FDA-cleared robotic transcranial Doppler system whose headset automatically steers the transducers to find and track cerebral artery signals in hospital patients; a clinician still fits the headset, and the study is a cerebral blood-flow test, not an EEG hookup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic insonation of the head in an ICU. It shows machine-controlled probe positioning against a human head, but the robot works only inside a human-fitted headset over the temporal windows; it does not measure 10-20 landmarks, part hair, abrade scalp, apply or remove multi-electrode arrays, verify impedances, or perform reactivity testing, so it does not substantiate completion of any EEG or evoked-potential instance.

sources.title: Axilum - TMS Robot By SYNEIKA
sources.claim: Axilum Robotics TMS-Robot / TMS-Cobot are CE-marked clinical robots that automatically position and hold a stimulation coil in contact with a patient's head under neuronavigation, compensating for head motion — the closest commercial case of autonomous robotic manipulation on a human scalp.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of an instrument on the scalp of a seated, cooperative outpatient. Transfer fails for this task: a single rigid coil resting on hair is not equivalent to parting hair, skin-prepping and adhering 10-21 gel/collodion electrodes to impedance criteria on an intubated ICU patient, nor does the robot run or troubleshoot a diagnostic recording.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital research team
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot performed self-directed probe placement and scanning on human subjects in a hospital ultrasound department, demonstrating autonomous force-controlled contact with patient skin for imaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot-patient contact for a bedside diagnostic study in a hospital. It involves one smooth probe on exposed abdominal skin of a cooperative patient; it provides no capability for hair manipulation, scalp abrasion, adhesive multi-electrode montage, impedance verification, noxious-stimulus reactivity testing, or 30-minute artifact-free electrophysiological acquisition.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Moxi mobile manipulators operate autonomously in more than 25 US ..., showing that mobile robots can navigate structured hospital corridors and units at scale, but their deployed work is logistics and supply delivery rather than patient-contact diagnostic procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospitals. It substantiates only navigation and transport of supplies; the deployed system is explicitly non-patient-facing and performs no electrode application or neurodiagnostic recording, so it cannot substantiate these instances.

tasks.label: Attach electrodes to patients, using adhesives.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine outpatient/inpatient EEG in a hospital or clinic EEG lab: technologist measures the head to the 10-20 system, marks sites, parts hair, abrades scalp with prep gel, and affixes ~21 cup electrodes with conductive paste (or collodion + gauze and air dryer) on a seated/reclined cooperative adult, then checks impedances and re-does poor sites.

Polysomnography hookup in a sleep-center bedroom: scalp cup electrodes with paste/collodion plus adhesive spot electrodes for EOG, chin and leg EMG, and ECG, tape/collodion securing, on an adult patient (often obese, bearded, or with thick hair) before an overnight recording; wires bundled and impedance-verified.

Bedside continuous/long-term EEG in an ICU or epilepsy monitoring unit: collodion-applied electrodes on a critically ill, sedated, agitated or post-operative patient among lines, tubes, ventilator and head dressings, with limited access to the head and frequent electrode replacement over days.

Pediatric or neonatal EEG: electrodes applied with paste/collodion to an infant in an isolette or a squirming, crying toddler, small delicate head and skin, often requiring rapid application while a parent or nurse holds the child.

Nerve conduction studies and evoked potentials: placing self-adhesive surface recording/reference/ground electrodes and stimulating electrodes at measured distances on limbs, face or scalp of a patient on an exam table in an EMG/EP lab, with skin cleaning and taping.

Ambulatory EEG hookup performed in the patient's home or a mobile service visit (or at a nursing facility): full collodion hookup in an uncontrolled room with variable lighting, furniture, seating and patient positioning, wrapping the head before the patient is left unsupervised.

sources.title: Soft and Compliant Contact-Rich Hair Manipulation and Care (arXiv:2501.02630)
sources.claim: Frontier robotic hair-care research (MOE-Hair, CMU) performs head patting, finger combing and ... with a soft end-effector, but is validated on a force-sensorized mannequin head and does not part hair for, prep, or affix electrodes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of human hair on the head, the key obstacle to scalp electrode application. It falls short because the demonstrated tasks are patting/combing/grasping on a mannequin head, with no scalp abrasion, paste or collodion application, or placement and securing of electrodes at measured 10-20 sites.

sources.system: ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration System
sources.title: ARTAS® Robotic Hair Restoration Treatments — Venus Concept
sources.claim: The ARTAS/ARTAS iX robotic hair-restoration system works on a live human scalp through hair in a clinic, but is an FDA-cleared computer-assisted follicle harvesting device operated under a physician's guidance; it punches and extracts grafts and attaches nothing with adhesive.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise image-guided robotic work on a hairy human scalp in a clinical procedure room. It does not substantiate this task because it neither manipulates small compliant adhesive electrodes nor applies conductive paste/collodion, and it operates under physician guidance on a tensioner-fixtured scalp for a single repetitive punch motion.

sources.developer: University of Manchester / University of Leeds (review authors)
sources.title: Robot-assisted Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation (Robo-TMS): A Review (arXiv:2507.04345)
sources.claim: Robot-assisted TMS systems position a coil against a patient's head with neuronavigation and force control, but the review reports clinical applicability is unverified and adoption is limited; no adhesive sensor application is involved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic placement of an instrument at a landmark-referenced position on a human head. It does not transfer because the coil is held above/against hair without parting it, nothing is attached, no skin preparation or adhesive is used, and the systems remain research prototypes.

sources.system: auto-RUSS (7-DoF autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system)
sources.developer: Frontiers in Robotics and AI study authors
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound systems achieve force-controlled probe contact and repeatable scanning, but the reported autonomous comparison was run on phantoms, and the task is sliding a rigid probe rather than affixing adhesive electrodes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous force-controlled contact of an end-effector with a gel-coated body surface in a clinical setting. It does not substantiate electrode attachment: no small deformable adhesive object is grasped, positioned to a measured landmark, or secured, and the autonomous trials used phantoms.

tasks.label: Measure patients' body parts and mark locations where electrodes are to be placed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine diagnostic EEG in a hospital or clinic EEG lab: cooperative adult seated/reclined; technologist uses a tape measure for head circumference, nasion-inion and preauricular distances, computes 10%/20% fractions, and marks ~19-25 scalp sites with a grease pencil, parting hair of varying length and texture.

Polysomnography hookup in a sleep lab: technologist measures the head to mark the AASM montage sites (F4, C4, O2, M1/M2) and locates and marks facial (EOG), chin EMG, chest and leg sensor sites on a cooperative adult in the evening before lights-out.

Portable/bedside EEG in an ICU, ED or inpatient room: patient sedated and ventilated, or confused and agitated; scalp may carry dressings, staples, an EVD, edema or matted/oily hair; access limited by lines, bed rails, monitors and head-of-bed position.

Pediatric or neonatal EEG in a children's hospital lab or NICU: infants and young children who squirm, cry and resist; very small heads with soft fontanelles; measurements taken while a parent or second tech holds the child, or through an incubator port.

Nerve conduction study prep in an EMG lab: technologist measures standard distances (e.g., 8 cm, 14 cm) along the arm or leg with a tape over curved limb surfaces and marks stimulation and recording sites over nerve courses with a skin pencil.

Ambulatory EEG or home sleep study hookup performed in the patient's home or another off-site location: measuring and marking the head on a couch or kitchen chair, variable lighting and layout, pets and family present.

sources.system: On-scalp EEG e-tattoo printing system (5-axis printing robot + automated sensor layout algorithm)
sources.developer: University of Texas at Austin / UCLA (Nanshu Lu, Ximin He)
sources.title: On-Scalp Printing of Personalized EEG E-Tattoos (MRS 2024 Fall Meeting abstract)
sources.claim: A UT Austin/UCLA system uses an automated layout algorithm tailored to each person's head shape together with a 5-axis printing robot ... place EEG electrode material at the computed scalp locations of human participants (through hair, non-contact).
sources.transferJustification: Same anatomy and same output geometry as the rated task: the machine determines where each EEG electrode belongs on an individual patient's head and deposits material exactly there, which subsumes measuring the head and marking the electrode sites.

sources.developer: University of Texas at Austin / UCLA
sources.title: First-of-Its-Kind Digital Scalp Tattoo Reads Brain Activity (Psychology Today)
sources.claim: In the same system the measurement step is machine-performed: a 3D scanner mounted on the five-axis robot moves around the seated participant's head to digitize it, and electrode coordinates are then computed from the scan with MeshEEG.
sources.transferJustification: This is the measurement half of the rated task performed by machine: robot-borne 3D digitization of the individual patient's head replaces tape measurement of nasion-inion/preauricular distances, and the 10-20 coordinates are derived from it.

sources.title: Application of the robot-assisted implantation in deep brain stimulation (Frontiers in Neurorobotics)
sources.claim: In 30 clinical deep-brain-stimulation implantations the Remebot robotic arm automatically marked the ... for electrode placement, with average radial error 1.28 mm, using frameless videometric registration to the patient's head.
sources.transferJustification: Literally the same act as the rated task - marking on a patient's scalp the locations where electrodes will be placed - at higher precision (~1.3 mm) than the 10-20 system requires, though the head is stabilized and registration comes from imaging rather than a tape measure.

sources.system: ARTAS / ARTAS iX robotic hair restoration system
sources.title: Robotic Hair Restoration | ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant (Bernstein Medical)
sources.claim: The commercial ARTAS robotic hair-transplant system scans the scalp surface with an optical imaging system and, in recipient-site creation, drives a blade to create sites at the locations of a physician-designed plan on an awake patient held in a dedicated chair with a scalp tensioner.
sources.transferJustification: Same workpiece (an awake patient's haired scalp) and same function - placing precisely located marks/sites on the head where items will subsequently be placed - at sub-millimeter precision and commercial throughput, in a clinic room built around the robot's chair and tensioner.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy ... performed venipuncture on 1633 outpatients in routine use across Dutch phlebotomy departments, imaging the arm placed in the device and achieving a 94.5% first-stick success rate with one supervisor per three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously locating an anatomically defined target on a patient's arm resting in the machine's cradle and acting on that exact skin point. Marking an NCS stimulation site demands the same limb-surface localization and skin contact at lower precision and without skin penetration.

sources.title: A robot to assist in transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS / rTMS) - TMS-Robot Features
sources.claim: The CE-marked Axilum TMS-Robot, a 7-DOF arm with a computer-controlled patient seat, automatically executes a planned session by positioning a coil at defined scalp targets on an awake patient, maintaining head contact and compensating for head movement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeatedly bringing an end-effector to specified points on an awake patient's scalp and holding contact despite motion - the physical core of marking electrode sites - but only inside a purpose-built robot seat, and with target definition supplied by a human-run neuronavigation step.

tasks.label: Submit reports to physicians summarizing test results.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Calibrate, troubleshoot, or repair equipment and correct malfunctions, as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine pre-study calibration and verification in a hospital/clinic neurodiagnostic lab: connect the headbox/jackbox and electrode board, run the system (square-wave/known-signal) calibration and channel check on the EEG/EP/PSG amplifier, confirm all channels respond correctly, set gains, sensitivities, filters, and paper/display speed, verify stimulators (photic strobe, click intensity, pattern-reversal monitor), and document. No fault is found.

Troubleshooting a malfunction discovered during an active recording at the bedside (routine EEG, long-term monitoring room, ICU cEEG cart): identify 60 Hz interference, electrode pop, high impedance, or a dead/disconnected channel; physically correct it by re-abrading and re-gelling the electrode under the patient's hair, re-taping or re-collodioning the lead, reseating the pin in the jackbox, rerouting or replacing a cable, or unplugging offending nearby equipment, then re-check impedances and resume acquisition.

Overnight sleep lab: a sensor or device fails mid-study; the technologist enters the darkened bedroom and repairs or replaces the failing item on a sleeping patient with minimal arousal — reseating a displaced nasal pressure cannula or thermistor, replacing an oximeter probe, re-securing chest/abdomen effort belts or EMG/EOG leads, resolving a CPAP mask leak or pressure fault, or swapping a failed headbox/interface — and verifies signals from the control room.

Bench maintenance and repair in the lab workroom between studies: continuity-test suspect lead wires and electrodes with an ohmmeter, cut back and re-solder or discard and replace faulty leads, clean and repair corroded connectors and cup electrodes, swap out an amplifier/headbox or photic stimulator, reboot/reinstall or patch acquisition software and restore network/archive links, and log the fault or hand the unit to biomedical engineering.

Portable and out-of-lab work: resolving equipment malfunctions on ambulatory EEG hookups or home sleep apnea test units at the patient's home or a nursing facility — recorder not writing data, battery/SD card faults, loose leads under a wrap, sensor failures — often with the patient and family present and no lab support, plus checking returned units for damage.

sources.system: HAHN Automation Group medical device assembly & test system (lean cell)
sources.title: Medical Device Assembly & Test System | HAHN Automation Group case study
sources.claim: Commercial purpose-built medical-device assembly and test cells hold workpieces in dedicated fixtures and run an automatic, scheduled self-calibration routine on the cell's measuring/monitoring instruments, plus automated end-of-line functional test and pass/fail verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated calibration and functional verification of measurement instrumentation inside a fixtured production cell. It transfers to the technologist's routine instrument calibration instance because both consist of applying a known reference to an electronic measuring channel, checking the response against tolerance, and recording the result on a device presented in a fixed, known position; it does not transfer to diagnosing and repairing an unknown fault.

sources.title: Check out Hyundai's new robot that will automatically charge your EV
sources.claim: An autonomous robot arm locates a vehicle charge port with 3D vision and inserts and removes the connector without human input, running at an airport charging site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mating of an electrical connector to a port. It supports the cable-connection sub-step of a fixtured calibration station (connecting a headbox or reference-signal lead) with comparable object scale and insertion precision; it says nothing about fault diagnosis or work on a patient.

sources.system: Lucid Robotic System / NovaGuide 2 Intelligent Ultrasound (NeuralBot robotic headset)
sources.title: Incorporation of robotic automated transcranial Doppler to screen for patent foramen ovale (PFO)...
sources.claim: An FDA-cleared robotic transcranial Doppler system uses a motorized headset with five degrees of freedom to position and steer ultrasound probes on a patient's head to acquire and maintain a usable signal in hospital settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic adjustment of a head-mounted sensor to correct a poor signal. It is the closest patient-contact analogue to fixing a bad EEG channel, but it only re-aims a probe held by a headset; it does not part hair, abrade skin, apply gel or collodion, re-tape leads, or swap electrodes, so it cannot complete the troubleshooting instance.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: The autonomous mobile manipulator deployed at scale in US hospitals performs supply, lab-sample and pharmacy deliveries along corridors; its deployed duties do not include calibrating, troubleshooting, or repairing clinical equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize what autonomous robots actually do inside the hospital environment (E2) that these instances occupy: point-to-point logistics, not equipment service work. It supports negative judgments at E2, not any positive one.

tasks.label: Adjust equipment to optimize viewing of the nervous system.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine or stat EEG in a hospital/clinic EEG lab or at an inpatient bedside: during a 20-60 minute recording on an adult, pediatric or confused patient, the tech watches the live trace, identifies electrode 'pop', high impedance, sweat, muscle or 60 Hz artifact, physically re-abrades/re-gels or re-seats scalp electrodes under hair, adjusts sensitivity, low/high filters, notch, timebase and montage on the amplifier and software, repositions the photic stimulator, and verifies a clean, interpretable display.

Overnight polysomnography in a sleep lab bedroom: from the control room the tech calibrates and adjusts channel gains, filters and sensor sensitivities through the night; enters the darkened room to reattach a displaced EEG/EOG/chin electrode, nasal pressure cannula, thermistor, oximeter probe, effort belt or CPAP mask and re-checks impedances without waking the sleeping patient.

Long-term video-EEG monitoring in an epilepsy monitoring unit or ICU: over days the tech re-gels/re-wraps collodion electrodes, re-seats headbox and amplifier connections, checks impedances, re-frames/re-focuses and re-aims the room camera and adjusts lighting so the patient stays in view, and troubleshoots artifact from ventilators, pumps and patient movement.

Nerve conduction study in a neurodiagnostic lab: the tech adjusts the hand-held bipolar stimulator's position, angle and pressure over the nerve and raises intensity until a supramaximal, artifact-free CMAP/SNAP is obtained, repositions the active/reference recording electrodes over the motor point, and adjusts gain, sweep speed, filters and stimulus duration while managing patient discomfort.

Evoked potentials in a lab or intraoperative neuromonitoring in an OR: adjust stimulus parameters (pattern-reversal screen distance and check size, click intensity/rate/masking, SSEP stimulator site and intensity to a visible twitch), reposition scalp cup or subdermal needle electrodes, adjust filters, averaging and rejection levels, and hunt down electrical interference from surgical and room equipment until reproducible waveforms are visible.

Ambulatory EEG or home sleep apnea test at the patient's home or a nursing facility: the tech works in a living room or bedroom of unknown layout with pets, family and poor lighting, applies and adjusts electrodes/sensors, adjusts recorder gain and settings, and verifies signal quality on a laptop before leaving the equipment with the patient.

sources.title: A robot to assist in transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS / rTMS) - Healthcare Professionals - Axilum Robotics
sources.claim: Axilum Robotics TMS-Robot is a commercially available (CE-marked) robot with a 7-DoF arm and computer-controlled patient seat that automatically positions a stimulation coil on a patient's head, maintains coil-scalp contact, and compensates for head motion during a clinical session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic positioning/adjustment of a neurophysiologic stimulating device against a patient's body surface. It transfers partially to 'adjust equipment to optimize viewing of the nervous system' because it involves the same class of object (a hand-applied stimulating head pressed to the skin), mm-scale positional accuracy, closed-loop compensation for patient movement, and a clinical neurophysiology room; it does not cover recording-electrode preparation or impedance troubleshooting.

sources.system: Automated hotspot-hunting (AHH) with robotic coil positioning
sources.developer: Dept. of Clinical Neurophysiology, University Medical Center Göttingen (using a robotized TMS positioning system)
sources.title: Automated TMS hotspot-hunting using a closed loop threshold-based algorithm - PubMed
sources.claim: A fully automated, investigator-independent motor hotspot search combined robotic TMS coil positioning with a closed-loop algorithm that measured evoked responses and iteratively moved the coil to the position giving the optimal neurophysiologic response, tested in 8 subjects at a university clinical neurophysiology department.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop robotic adjustment of stimulating equipment driven by the recorded neurophysiologic signal (motor evoked potentials), i.e. the same optimization loop a technologist runs when moving a stimulator and raising intensity until a supramaximal, clean response is displayed. Comparable precision (mm CoG shift), comparable signal chain, subject fixated in the robot's dedicated patient chair.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital research group
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot performed autonomous scanning on human subjects, adjusting probe pose and contact force to obtain diagnostic-quality views, and was deployed in a hospital ultrasound department for clinical feasibility evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously adjusting a hand-held sensor on a patient's skin, in closed loop on the acquired signal, to optimize the diagnostic view inside a structured hospital department. It shows the frontier of autonomous probe-pose optimization on patients, but it images organs with a single passive transducer and does nothing with recording electrodes, gel/abrasion under hair, impedance, or amplifier montage/filter troubleshooting.

tasks.label: Measure visual, auditory, or somatosensory evoked potentials (EPs) to determine responses to stimuli.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient neurodiagnostic lab: adult pattern-reversal visual evoked potential. Tech measures the head, marks Oz/O1/O2 and reference sites, parts hair, abrades skin, applies paste/collodion cup electrodes, verifies impedance <5 kOhm, seats and occludes one eye, instructs the patient to fixate on the checkerboard monitor, runs replicate averages, rejects blink/eye-movement artifact, and marks P100 latency/amplitude.

Clinic or inpatient lab: brainstem auditory evoked potential (BAEP/ABR) on an adult or a sleeping/sedated child. Tech places vertex, mastoid/earlobe and ground electrodes, inserts foam insert earphones in the ear canals, delivers click trains at graded intensities with contralateral masking, repeats runs, quiets muscle artifact, and labels waves I-V.

Outpatient lab: median and posterior tibial somatosensory evoked potentials. Tech places stimulating electrodes at wrist and ankle, raises current until a visible thumb/toe twitch, applies recording electrodes at Erb's point, cervical spine and C3'/C4' scalp sites through hair, keeps the patient relaxed and warm, runs and superimposes replicate averages, and marks N9/N13/N20 or P37.

Operating room intraoperative neuromonitoring: after induction, tech inserts subdermal needle electrodes for SSEP/MEP/BAEP on the anesthetized patient, secures and routes leads around the sterile field and positioning devices, obtains baselines, troubleshoots cautery and line noise during the case, replaces dislodged electrodes under drapes, and reports amplitude/latency changes in real time.

Bedside inpatient study: SSEP for coma prognostication in a busy ICU, or BAEP on an infant in a NICU isolette. Cluttered bedside with lines, ventilator and infusion pumps, high electrical noise, uncooperative or unresponsive patient, electrodes applied around dressings/EVD and around hair, with repeated runs to prove reproducibility.

sources.system: On-scalp e-tattoo microjet printing robot (UT Austin / UCLA)
sources.developer: University of Texas at Austin (Nanshu Lu lab) and UCLA
sources.title: On-scalp printing of personalized electroencephalography e-tattoos: Cell Biomaterials
sources.claim: A 5-axis microjet printing robot deposits conductive ink electrodes directly on a human scalp after a 3D head scan — the closest existing robotic system to automated EEG/EP electrode application — but it is a laboratory research demonstration of the electrode-application step only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying scalp EEG sensors. It covers only the electrode-application sub-step of an evoked potential study and does not deliver stimuli, insert earphones, stimulate peripheral nerves, verify impedance on a moving patient, or judge waveform reproducibility.

sources.title: Inkjet-printed scalp tattoos may allow for on-the-go brain monitoring
sources.claim: The scalp-printing robot works only on short hair; the researchers have not solved hair parting, which is routine in scalp electrode placement for EPs.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; the quote establishes the limitation that prevents transfer to routine EP electrode placement through hair.

sources.title: Axilum Robotics TMS-Robot | Neurolite Advanced Medical Solutions
sources.claim: A commercial clinical robot autonomously positions and maintains contact of a TMS coil on a patient's head with motion compensation, showing robots can safely contact the head in a clinic, but it places no electrodes and records no evoked potentials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of an instrument against a patient's scalp under neuronavigation. It transfers only for gross head contact; it does not involve skin prep, adhesive/paste electrodes, impedance verification, stimulus delivery, or waveform acceptance.

sources.system: ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration System
sources.title: ARTAS® Robotic Hair Transplant | Venus Treatments USA
sources.claim: An FDA-cleared robot autonomously harvests hair follicles from a patient's scalp under image guidance, demonstrating precise robotic work on the scalp in a clinical procedure room, but restricted to prepared, trimmed scalp areas held in a tensioner and to a different procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic manipulation on a human scalp in a clinic. Transfer is limited: the scalp is shaved and clamped in a fixture, and the robot performs punches rather than applying and validating recording electrodes or running a stimulus-locked averaging study.

sources.system: Automated ABR screeners (e.g., Interacoustics Sera, Natus ALGO)
sources.title: Hearing Screening: OAE vs Automated ABR | Interacoustics
sources.claim: In the most highly automated form of evoked potential testing — automated ABR newborn hearing screening — the stimulus delivery and response detection are automated by an instrument, but a human still places the scalp electrodes and ear couplers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the auditory EP instance: it shows the automated instrument is not a robot and that the physical patient-preparation portion of the task remains manual.

sources.title: Evoked Potentials Devices | Grason-Stadler
sources.claim: Evoked potential testing as practiced requires a clinician to place electrodes on the patient's head and present the stimulus, with a clinician interpreting the resulting waveforms.
sources.transferJustification: Describes the task itself; establishes that commercially available EP equipment automates signal averaging only, with human electrode application and interpretation.

tasks.label: Assist in training technicians, medical students, residents, or other staff members.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Precepting a new END trainee during a routine EEG in the lab: walking the trainee through 10-20 head measurement, electrode application, and impedance checks, watching the trainee work, correcting technique verbally, and confirming competency.

Sitting with residents, medical students, or junior techs at a review workstation explaining recording criteria, montages, filter settings, artifact recognition, and normal-versus-abnormal waveform patterns from stored or live studies.

Orienting rotating medical students, residents, or newly hired staff to the sleep lab / epilepsy monitoring unit: explaining equipment, protocols, patient-prep standards, safety and infection-control rules, and documentation requirements.

Coaching a trainee through a nerve conduction study or evoked potential test: explaining stimulator and recording-site selection, stimulus intensity, troubleshooting noise and poor responses, and giving feedback on the trainee's technique.
Preparing and delivering in-service or competency training material — building a short presentation or checklist, running a staff in-service, and documenting each trainee's progress and sign-offs.

tasks.label: Participate in research projects, conferences, or technical meetings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

roles.title: Ophthalmic Medical Technologists
roles.description: Assist ophthalmologists by performing ophthalmic clinical functions and ophthalmic photography. Provide instruction and supervision to other ophthalmic personnel. Assist with minor surgical procedures, applying aseptic techniques and preparing instruments. May perform eye exams, administer eye medications, and instruct patients in care and use of corrective lenses.

tasks.label: Conduct tonometry or tonography tests to measure intraocular pressure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ophthalmology clinic exam lane: technologist instills anesthetic/fluorescein drops, cleans and mounts the Goldmann prism on the slit lamp, seats the patient at the headrest, holds lids if needed, advances the prism to touch the cornea, judges the applanation mires under cobalt blue light, dials the endpoint, and records IOP for both eyes for a glaucoma or comprehensive patient.

Pretest/workup room: cooperative adult is seated at a table-mounted automated non-contact (air-puff) tonometer or combined auto ref/kerato/tono unit; the technologist positions the chin/forehead, instructs the patient to fixate, triggers the measurement, and transfers the IOP reading (with pachymetry correction if available) into the record.

Exam chair or clinic room: technologist takes IOP with a handheld device (iCare rebound tonometer or Tono-Pen) on a cooperative adult who cannot use the slit lamp, or where rebound/applanation-by-pen is the practice standard — aiming the probe 4–8 mm perpendicular to the corneal apex, taking a series of readings, and recording the averaged value.

Difficult or non-standard patient inside the facility: young child, patient with dementia, blepharospasm, wheelchair user, or a supine/reclined patient at the hospital bedside, ER consult, or in the OR/recovery area — requires lid retraction, coaxing, repositioning the device to the patient, and repeated attempts with a portable tonometer.

Serial/repeat pressure work in the clinic: post-intravitreal-injection or post-laser IOP checks, diurnal IOP curves, water-drinking or provocative testing, and (rarely) electronic tonography with the probe held on the anesthetized cornea for four minutes while the tracing is recorded.

instances.label: Pre-operative optical biometry for cataract/IOL planning in an ophthalmology clinic: cooperative adult seated at a table-mounted optical biometer (IOLMaster/AL-Scan/OA-2000 class), chin and forehead on the rest, fixating a target; tech obtains axial length, keratometry, ACD, lens thickness and white-to-white, checks signal quality, repeats scans, exports to IOL calculation.

Functional/refractive workup measurements at an instrument in a clinic or optical dispensary: autorefraction/auto-keratometry, non-contact (air-puff) tonometry for IOP, lensometry of habitual glasses, pupil size/pupillometry, on cooperative ambulatory adults during pre-testing.

Automated static perimetry (Humphrey-type visual field): tech occludes the fellow eye, seats and positions the patient at the bowl, sets refractive correction, instructs the patient, monitors fixation and reliability indices during the 3-6 minute test, and repeats or coaches when reliability is poor.

Measurements on uncooperative or non-ambulatory patients and contact/handheld techniques: contact or immersion A-scan ultrasound biometry on dense cataracts and poor fixators, handheld keratometry/pachymetry/tonometry at the bedside, wheelchair or supine patients, exams under anesthesia and pediatric/infant measurements.

External and adnexal measurements of surrounding tissue with hand-held tools: Hertel exophthalmometry against the lateral orbital rims, margin-reflex distances, palpebral fissure height, levator function with a ruler at the lid, and prism-and-ruler ocular alignment measures.

tasks.label: Measure visual acuity, including near, distance, pinhole, or dynamic visual acuity, using appropriate tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine cooperative adult in an ophthalmology/optometry clinic exam lane: technologist seats the patient, has them occlude one eye at a time, presents a projected or LCD distance chart at ~20 ft, elicits and scores letter responses with and/or without habitual correction, and records OD/OS/OU acuity in the EHR.

Near visual acuity on a cooperative adult (presbyope, cataract, post-op, pre-op work-up): hand the patient a near card / reduced Snellen at 40 cm with their reading correction, control the working distance and occlusion, score each eye and both, record the result.

Adult whose measured acuity is reduced (e.g. 20/60): technologist places a pinhole occluder over the eye, re-presents the chart, coaxes the patient to find the best aperture, and records the pinhole acuity to distinguish refractive from pathologic loss.

Pediatric, preverbal, non-English-speaking or cognitively impaired patient: LEA/HOTV matching cards, Allen figures or Teller preferential-looking cards; requires patching or hand-occluding a squirming child, coaxing, judging fixation-and-following behaviour, and adjusting test distance.

Very-low-vision or limited-mobility patient (dense cataract, retinal disease, post-op patch removal, wheelchair or hospital bedside): walk the chart closer, then count fingers, hand motion, light perception/projection with a transilluminator; hold near card and occluder for a patient who cannot self-position.

Specialized acuity testing ordered for a work-up: dynamic visual acuity (examiner oscillates or the patient rotates the head at ~2 Hz while reading the chart, sometimes with a head-velocity sensor attached), potential acuity meter, or glare/BAT acuity.

tasks.label: Administer topical ophthalmic or oral medications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine mydriatic/diagnostic drops in a clinic exam room: tech confirms patient identity, order and allergies, seats the adult patient, tilts the head back, retracts the lower lid, instills one drop of tropicamide and phenylephrine in each eye without touching the lashes or cornea, has the patient close/blot, notes the time of instillation in the chart, and rechecks dilation.

Topical anesthetic (proparacaine) with or without fluorescein immediately before a contact procedure (applanation tonometry, pachymetry, gonioscopy, lash/foreign-body work) in the exam lane: correct drop, correct eye, correct timing, no corneal contact with the bottle/strip, then hand off to the examiner within the anesthetic window.

Drops in a difficult or uncooperative patient in the clinic: cyclopentolate/tropicamide in a squirming infant or child, or a patient with blepharospasm, tremor, dementia or severe photophobia; requires positioning, lid separation or holding, coaxing, sometimes a second attempt or a parent's help, while avoiding eye injury.

Peri-procedural medication in a procedure room or ambulatory surgery suite: a timed sequence of dilating, antibiotic, anesthetic and povidone-iodine drops or ointment to a reclined pre-op or post-injection patient, sterile technique, repeated at set intervals, documented on the pre-op record.

Oral medication in the clinic under physician order: e.g., an acetazolamide tablet for an acute pressure spike, oral fluorescein before angiography, or an analgesic; tech verifies patient, order and allergies, retrieves the dose from clinic stock, gives it with water, observes the patient take it and documents.

tasks.label: Measure and record lens power, using lensometers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine clinic workup in an ophthalmology practice: the technologist takes the patient's current single-vision or bifocal spectacles, neutralizes each lens on a manual or automated lensmeter, notes sphere/cylinder/axis (and add for bifocals), and records the values in the chart/EHR before refraction.

Patient presents with progressive/multifocal or prismatic lenses: technologist locates the progressive engravings/segment, measures distance and near powers, any prescribed prism, checks optical-center height and PD against the frame, and records all values.

Pre-dispense verification in the practice's optical dispensary: newly fabricated or lab-returned eyewear (including tinted, AR-coated, rimless/drilled jobs) is checked lens-by-lens on the lensmeter against the written Rx and ANSI tolerances, and the result is documented before the glasses are released.
In-house finishing lab work: verifying power of uncut or finished lens blanks and stock lenses before edging/mounting, marking optical centers, and logging measured powers on the job ticket.

Contact-lens or trial-lens power verification: a rigid or soft contact lens (with contact-lens holder) or a trial/loaner lens is placed on the lensmeter, power read and recorded in the patient record.

Difficult specimens: heavily scratched, crazed or dirty older lenses, warped or broken frames, heavy tints/mirror coats, or lenses brought in bedside/pediatric situations, where the technologist must clean, orient and judge an uncertain reading before recording an acceptable value.

tasks.label: Calculate corrections for refractive errors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinic exam lane: technologist converts gross objective findings (retinoscopy or autorefractor printout) into a net refraction  ioptric value for working distance subtracted, cylinder transposed to the practice's preferred plus/minus form, sphere/cyl/axis recorded in the chart for the ophthalmologist.

Routine adult refraction workup: technologist derives the final distance correction from subjective responses and the objective starting point, balances the two eyes, compares against the habitual prescription read from lensometry, and documents the resulting correction and best-corrected acuity.

Presbyopic patient: technologist computes the near add and intermediate power from age, measured amplitude of accommodation and the patient's working distance, then derives the bifocal/progressive or single-vision reading prescription values.

Contact lens or high-ametrope case: technologist applies vertex-distance compensation to convert spectacle-plane power to corneal-plane power, and combines a trial-lens power with over-refraction results to compute the lens power to order.

Special calculations: spherical equivalent, comparison of achieved versus target refraction after cataract or refractive surgery, prism amounts by Prentice's rule, and adjustments for anisometropia/aniseikonia.

Pediatric or cycloplegic case: technologist computes the correction to be prescribed from cycloplegic retinoscopy findings, deducting for cycloplegia/tonus and applying partial-correction conventions for esotropia or amblyopia.

tasks.label: Collect ophthalmic measurements or other diagnostic information, using ultrasound equipment, such as A-scan ultrasound biometry or B-scan ultrasonography equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cataract pre-op clinic: contact (applanation) A-scan axial-length biometry for IOL power calculation. Tech instills topical anesthetic, holds a handheld 10 MHz probe lightly on the cornea aligned with the visual axis while the patient fixates, captures several readings per eye, rejects those with corneal indentation or poor retinal/scleral spikes, and checks SD between eyes.

Immersion A-scan biometry with a Prager/Hansen scleral shell and saline, patient reclined: used for dense cataracts, staphyloma, silicone-oil eyes, post-refractive eyes or when optical biometry fails. Requires shell placement between lids, filling with coupling fluid, probe positioning without corneal touch, and repeated readings.

Diagnostic B-scan ultrasonography through the closed eyelid with coupling gel: opaque media (vitreous hemorrhage, dense cataract), suspected retinal detachment/PVD, foreign body. Dynamic kinetic scanning with the patient directed to move gaze, transverse/longitudinal/axial probe orientations chosen in response to what appears on screen, gain adjusted, representative images and video saved.

Standardized echography of intraocular/orbital lesions: quantitative A-scan plus B-scan to measure a choroidal nevus/melanoma height and base, characterize internal reflectivity and vascularity, or assess optic nerve/extraocular muscles; requires precise probe placement over the lesion meridian and repeated measurement for follow-up comparison.

Anterior-segment high-frequency ultrasound / UBM: sulcus-to-sulcus and ACD measurement for phakic IOL (ICL) sizing, corneal epithelial thickness mapping, angle or iris-cyst evaluation. Performed with immersion coupling (eyecup/water bath or arc-scanning instrument) with the patient seated at a chin rest.

Ultrasound in nonstandard contexts: pediatric or uncooperative/photophobic patients, exam under anesthesia in the OR, inpatient bedside consult with a portable unit, or recent trauma/periocular swelling requiring minimal-pressure scanning over a lid protected by a shield.

sources.title: Insight 100 Operator FAQ | ArcScan
sources.claim: The ArcScan Insight 100 is a commercially sold, FDA-cleared ophthalmic very-high-frequency ultrasound instrument in which a motorized ('robotic') transducer sweeps an arc inside a water bath while the patient's head rests in a chin rest and the eye is coupled through a disposable saline-filled EyeSeal; the machine, not a hand-held probe, executes the scan.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (collecting ophthalmic measurements with ultrasound equipment), anterior-segment variant: the device acquires the ultrasound scan set and biometric measurements itself once the patient is coupled to it.

sources.title: Insight 100 Auto-Centration | ArcScan
sources.claim: Image acquisition on the Insight 100 is machine-controlled: the device scans the eye, computes the corneal apex position, auto-centers, and then completes the programmed scan set over selected meridians without the operator steering a probe.

sources.title: ArcScan's Insight 100 Ophthalmic Ultrasound Imaging System Approved in China
sources.claim: The Insight 100 is regulatory-cleared in the US, EU and China and is in clinical use for anterior-segment ultrasound imaging and biometry (epithelial mapping, sulcus measurement for phakic IOL sizing).

sources.title: Contactless optical coherence tomography of the eyes of freestanding individuals with a robotic scanner
sources.claim: The closest demonstrated autonomous robotic ocular imaging is a robot-mounted OCT scanner that aligns itself to a standing person's eye and captures retinal volumes without operator intervention - but it is optical and never touches the eye, so it neither replaces ultrasound information nor demonstrates safe contact scanning of the cornea or lid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous acquisition of ophthalmic diagnostic images in a clinic. Transfer FAILS for this task: OCT is non-contact optical imaging and cannot provide A-scan biometry or B-scan echography, and it never demonstrates the anesthetized corneal applanation or gel-coupled lid contact this task requires.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound has been demonstrated on human subjects only for large body regions (liver/abdomen, carotid, thyroid, heart) using force-controlled probes pressed on skin at multi-newton contact forces, in hospital ultrasound departments; no ocular application is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ultrasound image/measurement acquisition on a human patient. automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Clean or sterilize ophthalmic or surgical instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Exam-lane turnover in an ophthalmology clinic: between patients the technologist removes the Goldmann applanation prism (or a gonioscopy/fundus contact lens, pachymeter or A-scan probe tip), wipes it, soaks it in the prescribed disinfectant (e.g., 1:10 bleach or hydrogen peroxide) for the required time, rinses with water, dries it and returns it to the slit lamp. Small fragile optics; heat and alcohol prohibited; must be done in the few minutes between appointments.

Office minor-procedure reprocessing: after chalazion excision, lid lesion removal, punctal plugs or an injection tray, the tech carries soiled instruments to the clinic utility/sterilization room, rinses and scrubs them at the sink with enzymatic detergent, runs an ultrasonic cycle, dries and inspects them, pouches or cassettes them, loads and runs the tabletop steam sterilizer, and records cycle and indicator results.

Ophthalmic ASC or hospital OR between cataract/retina cases: point-of-use flushing with sterile water of cannulated instruments and phaco/I-A handpieces, transport to decontamination, manual and mechanical cleaning with lumen flushing and critical-water rinsing (TASS-driven protocol), inspection of delicate microsurgical tips under magnification, tray assembly and steam sterilization for the next case.

Between-patient cleaning and low-level disinfection of fixed and bulky lane equipment that contacts patients: slit-lamp chinrest and headrest, tonometer arm and body, autorefractor and visual-field forehead rests, trial frames and occluders, wiped down in place in the exam lane during room turnover.

Upkeep and quality control of the reprocessing equipment itself: draining, cleaning and refilling the ultrasonic bath and changing enzymatic/disinfectant solutions, cleaning the autoclave chamber, gasket and water reservoir, running and interpreting weekly biological (spore) tests and chemical indicators, and documenting results for the practice infection-control log.

tasks.label: Conduct ocular motility tests to measure function of eye muscles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine comprehensive eye exam, cooperative adult or older child in a standard clinic exam lane: technologist directs the patient to follow a fixation light/target through the cardinal/nine positions of gaze, grades any over- or underaction, performs cover-uncover and alternate cover at distance and near, checks near point of convergence, and records findings in the chart.

Cooperative adult or older child with manifest strabismus or diplopia: full prism-and-alternate-cover measurement of the deviation in prism diopters at distance and near (and in secondary gaze positions), documented for prism prescription or strabismus surgical planning.

Young child, infant, or developmentally limited patient in a pediatric ophthalmology clinic: Hirschberg/Krimsky corneal reflex testing, cover testing with toys and animated targets, coaxing fixation, parent holding the child's head, repeated brief attempts to obtain usable measurements.

Neuro-ophthalmic or complex motility case: cranial-nerve palsy, restrictive/thyroid myopathy or nystagmus workup requiring ductions vs versions, saccade and pursuit quality assessment, three-step head-tilt testing, double Maddox rod for torsion, and diplopia field / Hess-Lees charting.

Motility assessment performed outside the standard exam lane: inpatient bedside or emergency-department consult, post-operative or wheelchair-bound patient examined in the chair or on a gurney with a hand-held light and occluder.

sources.developer: 2nd Department of Ophthalmology, Pomeranian Medical University, Szczecin, Poland
sources.title: Usefulness Assessment of Automated Strabismus Angle Measurements Using Innovative Strabiscan Device (J. Clin. Med.)

sources.title: Usefulness Assessment of Automated Strabismus Angle Measurements Using Innovative Strabiscan Device (J. Clin. Med.)
sources.claim: The Strabiscan measurement takes place with the patient's head and chin held in a permanently fixed frame integrated into the instrument housing, i.e. the patient is fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.title: Usefulness Assessment of Automated Strabismus Angle Measurements Using Innovative Strabiscan Device (J. Clin. Med.)
sources.claim: Strabiscan replaces the technologist's physical occluder paddle and prism bars with machine-controlled LCD shutters and algorithmically displaced fixation points, so the occlusion and target motion of the cover test are actuated by the machine rather than by a person.

sources.title: Contactless optical coherence tomography of the eyes of freestanding individuals with a robotic scanner (Nature Biomedical Engineering)
sources.claim: A Duke robotic OCT scanner autonomously positions an imaging head to a freestanding person's eye and tracks the pupil, showing that a true robot can safely approach and align to an unrestrained patient's eye for an ophthalmic measurement.

It shows robotic alignment to an unfixtured human eye in a clinical setting, but it acquires retinal images and does not present targets, occlude eyes, or quantify extraocular muscle function, so it cannot by itself substantiate motility testing.

tasks.label: Assess refractive condition of eyes, using retinoscope.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine cooperative adult in an ophthalmology clinic exam lane: tech seats patient at phoropter (or trial frame), darkens room, performs streak retinoscopy at working distance to obtain objective sphere/cylinder/axis as the starting point for subjective refraction; clear media, normal pupils.

Cooperative school-age child or teen (~5-17) in a pediatric or comprehensive clinic, usually 30-40 min after cycloplegic drops; child sits at the phoropter or in the chair with a trial frame/lens rack, fixates a distance target, retinoscopy yields the prescribing refraction.

Preverbal or uncooperative patient - infant/toddler (6 mo-4 y) held on a parent's lap, autistic or developmentally disabled patient, or a child anesthetized in the OR for an exam under anesthesia; cycloplegic retinoscopy with handheld retinoscope and loose lenses/lens bars, chasing a moving, non-fixating eye.

Adult with degraded optics or poor cooperation in the lane: dense cataract or corneal scar/keratoconus/post-graft, small or irregular pupil, nystagmus, aphakia, low vision, or dementia - exactly the patients for whom autorefraction fails and the tech is asked to retinoscope, often with radical (close-distance) technique and clinical judgment of a dim, irregular reflex.

Immobile but cooperative patient inside the facility away from the lane: inpatient at the bedside, wheelchair-bound or post-op reclined patient, or nursing-home resident; handheld retinoscope and lens bars, non-standard working distance and room lighting.

Community outreach/mobile screening of mostly ambulatory adults - health fair, worksite, senior center, mobile eye van - portable retinoscope and lens rack, variable room layout and ambient light, high patient throughput, screening-grade objective refraction.

sources.title: This AI Bot Has A Rapid View on Vision Testing - Techstrong.ai
sources.claim: Eyebot S1/S1+ is a self-serve, standalone kiosk that autonomously captures refraction, lensometry and visual acuity from a standing adult in ~90 seconds with no operator present; a remote licensed doctor reviews the data to issue the prescription.
sources.transferJustification: Same task output: an instrument-based objective assessment of refractive condition (sphere/cylinder/axis) of an unrestrained human eye, the deliverable of retinoscopy.

sources.title: Automated vision-testing kiosks face concerns amid national expansion (Eyes On Eyecare Glance)
sources.claim: Eyebot kiosks are commercially deployed in malls, universities, retail stores and grocery chains in four US states, and in a blinded comparison prescriptions from Eyebot sessions gave the same 20/20 acuity rate as prescriptions from the patient's own optometrist.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes worker-quality output for machine-derived objective refraction, the product of the retinoscopy task, in institution-controlled retail/university premises.

sources.system: Chronos Automated Binocular Refraction System (with SightPilot)
sources.title: ROB Tech Review: Automated Binocular Refraction System - Review of Optometric Business
sources.claim: The Topcon Chronos is a commercially sold, free-standing, fully automated binocular refraction instrument that performs objective autorefraction (motorized eye-tracking alignment) plus guided subjective refraction and acuity in ordinary eyecare practices, reducing technician involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Automated objective refraction replaces retinoscopy as the objective step: same measured quantities (sphere, cylinder, axis) on the same patients in the same clinic lane.

sources.title: Clinical validity of automated refraction with the Chronos binocular refraction system compared to standard refraction techniques (J Fr Ophtalmol)
sources.claim: In 361 eyes of 182 patients, automated objective and guided subjective refraction by the Chronos agreed closely with conventional autorefraction plus manual subjective refraction, with clinically acceptable mean differences.
sources.transferJustification: Quantifies that the automated device's objective refraction matches the output a technologist's refraction workup would deliver for routine adults.

sources.title: Cycloplegic Autorefraction as a Substitute for Cycloplegic Retinoscopy in the Pediatric Population - PubMed
sources.claim: Cycloplegic autorefraction in children is comparable to cycloplegic retinoscopy: a chart-review study found no significant sphere, cylinder or axis differences, and an AAO evidence review found most studies report mean differences under 0.5 D.
sources.transferJustification: Directly benchmarks the machine measurement against the retinoscopy task output in children, establishing worker-quality equivalence for cooperative cycloplegic pediatric refraction.

sources.developer: American Academy of Ophthalmology (Wilson et al.)
sources.title: Accuracy of Autorefraction in Children: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: An AAO evidence assessment of autorefraction accuracy in children reports that most studies comparing cycloplegic autorefraction with ... mean spherical-equivalent differences below 0.5 D, though individual variability can be clinically relevant.
sources.transferJustification: Same comparison as the task: instrument-derived objective refraction versus retinoscopy, in the pediatric population where the technologist's retinoscopy is the reference.

sources.developer: Duke University (Draelos, Izatt, Kuo et al.)
sources.title: Contactless optical coherence tomography of the eyes of freestanding individuals with a robotic scanner | Nature Biomedical Engineering
sources.claim: A robot-arm-mounted OCT scanner autonomously located, aligned to and tracked the eyes of freestanding people with no operator and no chin rest, producing images comparable to tabletop clinical systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous optical measurement of an unrestrained human eye): shows robotic pupil finding, alignment and motion compensation - the physical positioning skill retinoscopy requires - achieved autonomously in a clinical research setting.

sources.system: plusoptiX A12C pediatric autorefractor / vision screener
sources.title: Portable Paediatric Autorefractor plusoptiX A12C | Plusoptix
sources.claim: The plusoptiX A12C pediatric photorefractor measures both eyes' sphere, cylinder and axis in under a second at 1 m and works on children from 6 months, but it is a hand-held device aimed by an operator and is used as a screening instrument.
sources.transferJustification: Closest instrument analogue for infant retinoscopy, but the human holds and aims it and its output is screening-grade, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of prescribing-grade pediatric retinoscopy.

tasks.label: Conduct visual field tests to measure field of vision.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine standard automated perimetry (Humphrey 24-2/30-2 SITA or equivalent) on a cooperative adult glaucoma/glaucoma-suspect patient in an ophthalmology clinic perimetry lane: enter patient/Rx data, patch the fellow eye, adjust chair and table height, seat the patient with chin on the rest and forehead against the bar, set the corrective trial lens, give standard instructions and a practice run, align the pupil, monitor gaze/fixation and blinks during the 3-6 minute test, encourage the patient, then check reliability indices and release the printout to the chart.

Same clinic perimeter, but an elderly or fatigable yet cooperative patient: blinks frequently, drifts off fixation, needs pauses, repeated verbal encouragement and reminders to keep pressing the button; the technologist stays in the dark room coaching and watching the gaze trace so the test stays reliable.

Clinic perimeter with a patient needing hands-on adaptation: wheelchair transfer or support positioning, taping a ptotic lid or lifting a brow, dry-eye drops, hearing or cognitive impairment requiring re-instruction, aborting and restarting the test, deciding to switch strategy or defer testing.

Patient who cannot do standard automated perimetry as presented: a young child (video-game/VR pediatric perimetry with constant engagement), or a very low-vision or neurologic patient needing Goldmann/kinetic manual perimetry or confrontation fields, with the technologist manually presenting and plotting stimuli and keeping the patient engaged.

High-volume screening or short-strategy field (suprathreshold screening, FDT/Matrix, or SITA Faster repeat) run in an optometric/ophthalmic pretesting lane on an experienced, cooperative adult who has taken the test before; quick setup, brief instructions, short test, results filed for the doctor.

Field testing away from the fixed lane: hospital bedside, nursing-home or community outreach/mobile-van visit with a portable or head-mounted perimeter, in a room taken as found, with an immobile or frail patient the technologist must position, hold steady and coach throughout.

sources.system: ZEISS Humphrey Field Analyzer 3 (HFA3 Model 860) with lens-based head tracking / automated alignment
sources.date: 2019-07 (ARVO 2019 abstract; gaze/head tracking shipped in HFA3 840/850/860)

sources.title: ZEISS Humphrey Field Analyzer 3 | Dauh Eye Care
sources.claim: The HFA3 removes the manual trial-lens step: a machine-actuated liquid lens applies each patient's refractive correction automatically from entered data, eliminating one of the technologist's hands-on setup steps at the instrument.

sources.system: iCare COMPASS automated fundus perimeter (formerly CenterVue Compass)

sources.title: Taking visual field analysis to a higher level with the iCare COMPASS automated perimeter - iCare
sources.claim: The iCare COMPASS fundus automated perimeter auto-focuses (no trial lens), auto-aligns, tracks the retina in real time and automatically re-presents stimuli lost to blinks, fixation loss or head movement, so the threshold test runs to completion without technician involvement once the patient is at the instrument.

sources.claim: Peer-reviewed comparisons of COMPASS against the Humphrey Field Analyzer in normal and glaucoma subjects conclude the two are interchangeable, i.e. the automated instrument's output is of the quality clinicians accept for glaucoma diagnosis and monitoring.
