tasks.label: Clean and sanitize athletic training rooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-athlete turnover of treatment tables/plinths in a high school, college or pro athletic training room during busy pre-practice or treatment hours: strip used paper/linen, spray EPA-registered disinfectant, wipe the padded vinyl surface and adjustable head/leg sections, observe dwell time, re-cover for the next athlete.

Daily floor care in the training room and adjoining taping/hydro area: sweep or vacuum, then damp-mop or scrub with disinfectant, working around treatment tables, rolling stools, modality carts and power cords, plus edges and corners.

Cleaning and disinfecting hydrotherapy equipment and plumbing fixtures: drain whirlpools/cold tubs/Hubbard tanks, scrub interior walls, turbine and jets, apply and rinse disinfectant, wipe exteriors, clean sinks and ice machine bins, and record the sanitation log.

Wiping and disinfecting modality units (ultrasound heads, e-stim, laser), rehab equipment (mats, foam rollers, bands, weights, bikes), taping stations and cluttered countertops; clearing tape scraps and used supplies, emptying trash, and restocking supplies and linens.

Bloodborne-pathogen cleanup after an injury: blood, vomit or other body fluid on a table, floor, wall or piece of equipment; don PPE, absorb, clean and disinfect with bleach solution per OSHA protocol, bag sharps/soiled material and dispose in biohazard containers.

Periodic deep or end-of-season terminal clean: move tables and carts, scrub floors and baseboards, wipe walls, cabinets and shelving, launder and restock towels and linens, disinfect all equipment and restock the room.

tasks.label: Apply protective or injury preventive devices, such as tape, bandages, or braces, to body parts, such as ankles, fingers, or wrists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-practice/pre-game prophylactic ankle taping in the athletic training room: a line of athletes sits on taping tables; the trainer applies heel-and-lace pads and pre-wrap, then anchors, stirrups, horseshoes, heel locks and figure-eights with rigid athletic tape at controlled tension, adjusting to each athlete's foot size, hair, skin condition and dorsiflexion, checking for wrinkles, gaps and circulation, in roughly 3-5 minutes per athlete.

Hand, wrist, thumb and finger taping in the training room: buddy taping adjacent fingers, thumb-spica checkreins, wrist figure-eights or a lineman's club wrap over small, closely spaced, mobile structures, with tension tuned to allow required grip and range of motion.

Sideline or field-side application during practice or competition, including at away venues: quick re-taping of a loosened ankle, taping over a shoe (spatting), a compression wrap on a contusion, or a finger tape job, done on a bench, on the ground, or with the athlete standing, under time pressure, weather, sweat and crowd noise.

Fitting and applying prophylactic or functional braces and supports: sizing and donning a lace-up ankle brace, wrist splint, thumb spica or hinged knee brace over sock/skin, threading laces and straps, tightening to the correct fit, and checking the fit under movement.

Protective padding and bandaging in the training room: dressing turf burns and blisters with non-adherent pads and gauze, cutting and applying felt/foam donut or horseshoe pads over contusions or heel bruises, and securing them with elastic wrap, cohesive tape or adherent spray.

sources.system: Autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing (UCSD, dexterous hand + manipulator + ATI Axia80 F/T sensor)
sources.developer: University of California San Diego / Cornell (Liang, Shen, Zhang, Atar, Richter, Yip)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing (arXiv:2510.06127)
sources.claim: The closest published robotic work on applying adhesive tape to human anatomy is a 2025 UCSD lab framework that automates only sub-steps of wound redressing (tape initial detachment and tape placement), using imitation learning trained from human teleoperation, validated in bench experiments rather than on athletes or patients in a workplace.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing a dressing with medical tape. It shares adhesive-tape handling on skin, but it is an isolated sub-step demonstrated on bench/anatomical surfaces in a lab, with no wrapping of a limb under tension, no brace fitting, and no evidence of whole-job, worker-quality output; it therefore cannot substantiate completion of an athletic taping instance at any tier.

sources.title: RoboTAPE: Automated Tape Application System | AV Flexologic
sources.claim: Fully automated tape application exists commercially only for rigid industrial workpieces inside a fenced cell: a robot spirals mounting tape onto a printing sleeve loaded by an operator onto a mandrel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated spiral tape application. It does not transfer: the workpiece is a rigid cylindrical sleeve fixtured on a mandrel behind a safety fence, whereas athletic taping requires wrapping a compliant, hair-bearing, movable human limb with graded tension and anatomical judgment, and explicitly requires a human inside the robot's workspace.

sources.title: Equinox Locations Add Aescape, a Fully Automated Massage Bed - Athletech News
sources.claim: Autonomous robots that make sustained, force-controlled physical contact with a human body are deployed commercially in fitness and spa facilities, but they only perform massage strokes; no cited system applies tape, wraps or braces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manual therapy contact with an athlete's body in a gym. It shows body scanning and safe force-controlled contact, but involves no manipulation of deformable materials, no wrapping around a limb, and no fastening of a device, so it does not substantiate applying tape, bandages or braces.

sources.system: Self-Wearing Adaptive Garments via Soft Robotic Unfurling (vine-robot garment)
sources.title: Robot Vines Dress You in About 10 Seconds - Technology Org
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing (putting garments, shoes or socks onto a human limb), the nearest analogue to fitting a brace or wrap onto a body part, remains a laboratory research problem in 2025-2026 with bimanual and soft-robotic prototypes, not a deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously placing a flexible covering onto a human limb. It does not transfer: the garment is a specially engineered self-actuating device, not a standard brace or tape roll applied by a robot, and the work is a laboratory demonstration without clinical fit, tension control, or acceptance standards.

tasks.label: Collaborate with physicians to develop and implement comprehensive rehabilitation programs for athletic injuries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High school athletic trainer: after an athlete's physician visit (e.g., ankle sprain, post-op ACL), the AT reviews the physician's protocol, designs the day-to-day progression, and runs daily rehab sessions in the school athletic training room — hands-on stretching/manual therapy, guided therapeutic exercise with bands/weights/balance boards, modalities (ice, e-stim, ultrasound), taping/bracing, documenting progress and phoning or messaging the physician to adjust or clear progression.

College/university sports medicine: AT attends physician clinic with the athlete, co-develops a multi-phase rehab plan with the team physician (e.g., shoulder labrum, hamstring strain), then implements it over weeks in a well-equipped athletic training facility and on the practice field — joint mobilization, manual resistance, pool/AlterG work, isokinetic and functional testing, sport-specific progressions, and periodic re-checks with the physician.

Outpatient/clinic-based AT acting as a physician extender in an orthopedic practice or hospital sports medicine clinic: implements the surgeon's post-operative rehab orders on patients — range-of-motion and strengthening exercise instruction, manual therapy, modality application, brace fitting and adjustment, wound/swelling checks, patient education, and charting back to the physician.

Professional or elite/collegiate-revenue sport: AT coordinates with the orthopedic surgeon and team medical staff on a post-surgical or complex injury, implements a detailed return-to-play program in the team performance center and on the field/court — hands-on soft-tissue work, loaded strength progressions, sprint/agility reconditioning, force-plate and functional criteria testing, daily adjustment with physician sign-off at milestones.

Industrial/occupational, military or performing-arts AT: implements a physician-approved rehab program for a work- or performance-related musculoskeletal injury at an on-site plant clinic, base clinic, or theater/studio space — job-specific functional progressions, manual therapy and modalities, ergonomic/technique modification, and written progress reporting to the physician for work or performance clearance.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology – AlleyWatch
sources.claim: Aescape's AI-driven massage table uses robotic arms to autonomously perform soft-tissue massage on people lying on a purpose-built table; it is commercially deployed in Equinox fitness clubs. It performs one hands-on modality only, with no assessment, program design, exercise supervision, or physician communication.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed system to a hands-on rehabilitative treatment on a human body (soft-tissue work an athletic trainer might perform). Transfer is only partial: it treats a passive client on a fixed table and does not deliver a rehabilitation program, exercise progression, or physician collaboration.

sources.title: Revolutionize Mobility: Ekso Bionics' Robotics & Rehabilitation
sources.claim: EksoNR is a commercially deployed rehabilitation exoskeleton used in rehab hospitals; it provides gait assistance and feeds information back to a human therapist who runs the session, rather than conducting therapy independently.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted therapeutic exercise delivery. It shows that deployed rehab robots act as clinician-operated tools within a session, not as systems that design and carry out a rehabilitation program end to end.

sources.title: Lokomat Robotic Gait Rehabilitation | UM Shore Regional Health
sources.claim: Lokomat robotic gait training is deployed in hospital outpatient rehabilitation departments, but clinical decision-making about participation, dosing and safety remains with the patient's physician and therapist, who set up and supervise every session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: implementing a prescribed rehabilitation exercise program. Demonstrates that even in a purpose-built rehab device the program design, screening, progression and supervision are performed by human clinicians.

sources.system: robot-aided rehabilitation assistive controllers (survey of autonomous assistance methods)
sources.title: A deep learning model for assistive decision-making during robot-aided rehabilitation therapies based on therapists’ demonstrations - PMC
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed study notes that autonomous assistance strategies in rehabilitation robots do not incorporate therapist clinical judgement, and that therapists remain better at deciding how and when to assist patients during exercises.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about implementing rehabilitation exercise therapy with robots; establishes that autonomous robotic assistance does not reach clinician-level progression and assistance decisions.

sources.system: Socially Assistive Robot rehabilitation coaches (conceptual autonomous coaching framework)
sources.title: Conceptual Framework for Autonomous Coaching in Orthopaedic Rehabilitation with Socially Assistive Robots
sources.claim: Socially assistive robots proposed as rehabilitation exercise coaches remain research prototypes: current systems use predefined exercise scripts and heuristic ..., and autonomous orthopaedic coaching is presented as a conceptual framework rather than a deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Direct evidence on the exercise-supervision portion of implementing a rehabilitation program: no fielded robot autonomously plans and coaches an orthopaedic rehab progression.

tasks.label: Travel with athletic teams to be available at sporting events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Secondary-school athletic trainer rides the team bus to an away football/soccer/basketball contest at another high school: loads and transports the med kit, AED, splint bag, hydration gear; sets up on the visiting sideline or bench area; remains on hand for the whole contest; evaluates and treats injuries (taping, wound care, ice, on-field spine/concussion assessment) as they arise; packs out and returns with the team.

College/university athletic trainer travels on a multi-day road trip by charter bus or plane: packs and moves equipment trunks and modalities, sets up a treatment area in a hotel room or visitor locker room, provides pre-competition taping and post-competition treatment, covers walk-through practices and the competition itself, coordinates with host medical staff and EMS.

Coverage of a multi-day tournament or meet at a neutral, non-campus outdoor site (cross-country course in a public park, club soccer complex, wrestling/track invitational): drives a van with supplies, works out of a pop-up tent with limited power/water, monitors several fields at once, deals with weather, unfamiliar terrain and mixed crowds of athletes, parents and spectators.

Short local travel in a personal or school vehicle to a nearby off-campus but institution-run venue (city stadium, natatorium, ice rink, community gym), carrying a kit and standing by courtside/poolside for the duration of the event, then treating any injuries that occur before returning.

Professional or elite team athletic trainer traveling on team charter flights: manages medical equipment logistics, sets up a hotel treatment room, provides pre-game and post-game hands-on care, and stands by on the bench during competition as part of a larger medical staff.

sources.system: VGo telepresence robot (Dartmouth-Hitchcock Center for Telehealth sideline concussion program)
sources.title: Sideline Robot Helps Trainers Spot Football Concussions : Shots - Health News : NPR
sources.claim: The closest thing to a robot on an athletic sideline is a telepresence robot (VGo) that lets a remote physician look at a possibly concussed player; the robot itself provides no hands-on care and is driven/operated by the remote clinician, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote sideline concussion evaluation. It does not transfer to this task because the machine only carries a screen and camera for a human clinician; it cannot travel with the team, carry supplies, or deliver physical care.

sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | spabusiness.com
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic bodywork exists only as a fixed installation: Aescape's two-armed table delivers automated massage to a client who lies on the machine in a studio, gym or spa; it does not travel, does not respond to acute injury, and requires the person to come to it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hands-on soft-tissue work on an athlete. It does not substantiate this task: the machine is a stationary table in a fixed facility, so the travel-and-be-available element cannot arise, and it performs no injury evaluation or emergency care.

sources.title: Hyundai Motor Brings Atlas Humanoid Robot to FIFA World Cup 2026 in First-Ever Live Match Environment Robotics Integration
sources.claim: Humanoid robots have appeared inside major sporting venues only as staged entertainment activations (Boston Dynamics Atlas delivering the ceremonial match ball and performing celebrations at a World Cup halftime), with no medical or athlete-care function and no evidence of unsupervised autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a legged robot operating on a competition field. It does not transfer: the activation was a choreographed halftime performance of ball delivery and celebration moves, not travel with a team, event standby, or injury care.

tasks.label: Plan or implement comprehensive athletic injury or illness prevention programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High school athletic trainer designs/updates a preseason injury-prevention program for fall sports: selects screening protocols (movement screens, baseline concussion testing schedule), chooses an evidence-based neuromuscular warm-up (e.g., FIFA 11+ style), writes the protocol document, and gets coach/administrator sign-off.

Athletic trainer implements and monitors an ongoing neuromuscular/ACL-prevention program across several teams: schedules sessions with coaches, tracks athlete compliance and adherence data, reviews injury surveillance numbers, and adjusts exercise selection or dosage over the season.

Athletic trainer develops and administers environmental-illness prevention policy: heat-acclimatization schedules, WBGT activity-modification thresholds, hydration and rest-break rules, cold/lightning policies, integrated with the emergency action plan and distributed to coaches and administrators.

College or professional setting: trainer plans an illness-prevention and health-maintenance program (infection control and hygiene protocols in the athletic training facility, immunization/screening coordination with team physicians, sleep/nutrition/load-management education plan, travel illness policy) and coordinates its rollout with the sports medicine staff.

Non-traditional setting (industrial/occupational or performing arts) athletic trainer plans a musculoskeletal injury-prevention program for workers or performers: job-task/risk analysis, prevention exercise and ergonomic recommendations, program scheduling, and outcome reporting to management.

tasks.label: Inspect playing fields to locate any items that could injure players.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-practice/pre-game walk of a natural-grass football, soccer or lacrosse field at a high school or college athletic complex: the trainer covers the playing surface and sidelines looking for rocks, broken glass, sticks, litter, exposed sprinkler heads and other loose items, removing them or flagging them for the grounds crew before athletes take the field.

Inspection of an artificial-turf game field or stadium pitch: the trainer scans the synthetic surface for foreign objects (bottle caps, screws, tent stakes, spectator litter, equipment left out), plus debris in the run-off area and around goals, before practice or a contest.

Indoor gymnasium, court or wrestling-room check before activity: walking the hardwood/mat surface for water, sweat or condensation, dropped debris, loose screws or tape, and objects intruding on the playing area, then clearing them or having them cleaned.

Baseball/softball field check: walking the skinned infield, mound, base paths and outfield grass looking for rocks, pebbles, glass, litter, and hardware near bases and fences, removing hazardous items before batting practice or game time.

Away game or event at a community/municipal park or shared public field complex with public access: the trainer walks an unfamiliar grass field before play, finding glass, cans, dog waste, sharp trash and other debris left by the public.

Off-campus venue taken as found: cross-country course, trail loop, park hillside or temporary event site — walking the route for roots, holes, wire, rocks, glass and other hazards over irregular terrain and brush.

sources.title: Product – Angsa Robotics
sources.claim: Angsa's autonomous outdoor cleaning robot uses camera-based AI detection to find and vacuum small hazardous litter — including glass shards — from grass, gravel and paved surfaces, covering up to 8,000 m² per shift (about the area of a soccer pitch).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous litter detection and removal on green space. The objects (glass shards, caps, small hard debris) are exactly the 'items that could injure players', the surface is grass/gravel like a playing field, and the robot both locates and removes them.

sources.title: GaLaBau | Autonomous garbage removal on unpaved surfaces
sources.claim: The Angsa robot plans its own coverage path over grass, gravel or cobblestone and automatically detects and avoids obstacles and people while cleaning.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (litter detection/removal on turf and gravel); establishes autonomous area coverage and safe operation around bystanders, as required when sweeping a field before athletes arrive.

sources.system: Angsa robot operated with Berliner Stadtreinigung (BSR)
sources.title: Dieser autonome Roboter räumt in Berlin auf – t3n
sources.claim: An Angsa/Berliner Stadtreinigung autonomous cleaning robot has been run in Berlin public parks (Spreebogenpark, Weinbergspark) picking small litter off publicly accessible lawns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous litter clearing of a public park lawn taken as found, with the public present — the same open-set small-debris problem as inspecting a public community field for injurious items.

sources.system: Turf Tank One / Turf Tank Two
sources.title: GNSS-guided Turf Tank employed to paint stadium lines – GPS World
sources.claim: Turf Tank's autonomous GNSS-guided robots systematically cover full athletic fields (soccer field in under 30 minutes) and are deployed in the hundreds at US schools, colleges, parks departments and NFL stadiums.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous line marking. It establishes that mobile robots reliably and unsupervised traverse and cover entire natural-grass and synthetic playing fields inside US athletic facilities — the traversal half of a field sweep.

sources.title: TurfRouter TR500: Autonomous, mobile robot for cleaning and maintaining artificial turf
sources.claim: The SMG TurfRouter TR500 is an autonomous mobile robot ... cleans and maintains artificial turf, covering a full-sized football pitch in about three hours using GPS/GNSS navigation with ultrasonic obstacle sensors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended cleaning of a synthetic sports pitch. It removes surface debris from the same playing surface, on the same field-scale coverage, that a trainer walks when looking for injurious items.

sources.title: BUKY ONE – autonomous maintenance robot for artificial turf fields
sources.claim: The BUKY ONE autonomous maintenance robot services a full artificial-turf football field in roughly four hours with RTK-GPS navigation and LIDAR detection of people and obstacles, running unsupervised at scheduled times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous artificial-turf grooming/cleaning. Same environment (sports field inside an athletic facility), same requirement of full-surface coverage without a human operator.

sources.title: Vallarta Supermarkets Test Badger Technologies Data-Gathering, Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: Badger Technologies' Retail InSpect robot autonomously patrols store floors and automatically detects hazards such as spills of ... bulk foods, alerting staff — deployed to complement manual floor inspections at Vallarta Supermarkets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated floor-hazard inspection indoors. Detecting spills and debris on a hard floor in a human-occupied institutional building is the same perception-and-reporting job as a pre-practice gym floor check.

sources.title: Badger Technologies robots working 6 Vallarta Supermarkets – Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Badger's floor-scanning robots are fully autonomous, navigating stores with onboard cameras to scan for hazards, and were rolled out across six Vallarta Supermarkets locations.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (indoor floor hazard scanning); establishes autonomy and multi-site commercial deployment rather than a one-off demo.

sources.title: Robotics company testing a new debris collecting robot at Ford Airport | WGVU NEWS
sources.claim: Airtrek Robotics' autonomous robot patrolled the ramp at Gerald R. Ford International Airport monitoring the tarmac for foreign ... and warning operations teams, collecting items from zipper pulls and bolts to plastic bottles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: foreign-object-debris inspection of a large paved operating surface at an institutional facility — the same open-set 'find any loose item that could cause injury/damage and report or remove it' task on a hard playing-type surface.

sources.title: TerraClear launches autonomous farm robot to capture images for tackling rocks, weeds and more – GeekWire
sources.claim: TerraClear's TerraScout autonomously drives outdoor fields capturing imagery and turning it into real-time maps of rocks and weeds, mapping over 1,000 acres per day; field trials began in early 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously locating and mapping rocks across an open outdoor field surface — the same detection problem (small hard objects on soil/turf) as spotting rocks on an infield or grass field.

sources.title: Building Services Contractor Bee Clean Deploys BrainOS-Powered Tennant Robotic Scrubbers at Canadian Polytechnical Institute
sources.claim: BrainOS-powered Tennant T7AMR autonomous scrubbers are deployed to clean large institutional floors daily, including 58,000 sq ft at a polytechnic campus, navigating human-occupied buildings unsupervised.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous coverage and cleaning of large indoor institutional floors (including school gym-type spaces), showing reliable unsupervised traversal of the same indoor playing surfaces a trainer inspects.

tasks.label: Massage body parts to relieve soreness, strains, or bruises.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Athletic training room, treatment table: routine post-practice or post-competition rubdown of the posterior chain (low and upper back, glutes, hamstrings, calves) for a healthy athlete with generalized soreness/DOMS or tightness; 10-20 minutes, pressure adjusted to the athlete's verbal feedback.

Athletic training room, treatment table: soreness and tightness in anterior/lateral leg regions - quadriceps, hip flexors, IT band, shins - worked supine or side-lying before or after practice, for general soreness rather than a diagnosed injury.

Athletic training room: short targeted work on regions off the posterior torso and legs - neck and upper trapezius (often seated), shoulder/deltoid, forearm and hand (throwers, swimmers, gymnasts), foot and plantar fascia - performed with thumbs, knuckles and elbows.

Injury-specific soft-tissue treatment: palpating to locate a strained hamstring/groin/calf or a quadriceps contusion, then applying graded effleurage, cross-friction or instrument-assisted work around (not over) the acute lesion, continuously monitoring the athlete's pain response and stopping if symptoms worsen.

Sideline, court-side or field-side during practice or competition: rubbing out a cramping calf or hamstring with the athlete on a bench, on the ground or in a gym corner, sometimes in heat, rain or cold, aiming to return the athlete to play within a couple of minutes.

Off-site/road settings: hotel room, visiting locker room, team bus, or a tent at a road race or tournament; a general leg/back rubdown on a portable table, a bed or the floor with whatever space is available.

sources.title: Aescape raises $83M to bring robotic massager to more locations - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Aescape's two-armed robotic massage table scans the body and delivers fully autonomous massage; it launched commercially at Equinox clubs in New York City and is expanding to 60 locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial recovery massage of major muscle groups. It transfers to the athletic trainer's soreness rubdown - same body regions, same soft-tissue strokes and pressure range, same indoor treatment-room setting, with the recipient prone on a table.

sources.title: Equinox, Aescape Launch Pre and Post-Workout Massage Series - Athletech News
sources.claim: Aescape robots are live in more than 50 ... delivering coach-designed pre- and post-workout recovery massages targeting back, hips, hamstrings and glutes; about 130 machines deployed running roughly 12,000 sessions a month.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-exercise recovery massage for athletes in a fitness club. Same purpose (relieving exercise soreness), same muscle groups an athletic trainer works after practice, delivered autonomously in a structured indoor facility.

sources.title: aescape | Club Fitness
sources.claim: Aescape's deployed system covers only the posterior chain - back, shoulders, glutes, hamstrings and ... - with the user selecting focus areas and pressure on a touchscreen.
sources.transferJustification: Defines which body parts the cited system can and cannot massage, bounding transfer from club recovery massage to the trainer's task.

sources.title: I Tried Aescape, the High-Tech Robot Massage-Here's My Review - Parade
sources.claim: A reviewer of the commercial Aescape service reports the robot does not work on hands, arms, feet, neck or ....
sources.transferJustification: Bounds the cited system's coverage; relevant because a large share of athletic-trainer massage is on neck, forearms, feet and anterior surfaces.

sources.title: Aescape AI Robot Massage at Lotte New York Palace in NYC | Giftory
sources.claim: Aescape's published health limitations tell users to avoid the robotic massage if they have a recent surgery or injury, among other conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the deployed system screens out exactly the acute strain/contusion cases that make up the injury-treatment portion of this task.

sources.title: Dubai-Based Robot Masseur Shifts Focus Toward Athletes | Fitt Insider
sources.claim: roboSculptor, a fully autonomous robotic massage platform sold to spas, wellness centres and clinics, added 20-minute leg-recovery and back-relief programs aimed at muscle tension and post-workout recovery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-workout leg recovery massage in a wellness facility. Covers whole-leg (including anterior thigh) soreness work that Aescape cannot reach, with comparable pressure, client supine or prone on a table.

sources.title: RoboSculptor introduces its robotic, AI massage technology in the U.S. - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: roboSculptor is an autonomous robotic arm with a 72-sphere roller and four LiDAR sensors that scans the client in real time and adapts its massage path, offering focused leg and back treatments; it was presented commercially in the US in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Independent trade-press confirmation of autonomy and of leg/back coverage for the system cited for anterior-leg soreness work.

sources.title: Massage Envy Adds Aescape Robotic Massages, Testing Low-Labor Model - Athletech News
sources.claim: Massage Envy began offering Aescape robotic massage at select franchised locations as a staff-free service option, extending robotic massage into standard commercial treatment rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: paid therapeutic massage delivered in a human-run facility; demonstrates the robot working unattended in ordinary treatment rooms rather than a fenced cell.

tasks.label: Accompany injured athletes to hospitals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High school or college game/practice: an athlete with a suspected fracture, concussion or heat illness is transported by EMS. The trainer helps EMS package and load the athlete, rides in the ambulance (or follows by car), monitors the athlete en route, gives ED staff mechanism of injury, vitals, medications and allergies, calls parents/coaches, and stays until family or the team physician arrives.

Urgent but non-emergent injury (deep laceration, dislocated finger, suspected wrist/ankle fracture): the trainer drives the athlete in a personal or team vehicle to an ED or urgent care, physically supports the ambulating athlete in and out of the car, carries crutches/splint/ice, handles registration, remains through exam and imaging, and brings discharge and follow-up instructions back to the team.

Catastrophic event at a stadium or arena (suspected cervical spine injury, cardiac event): the trainer assists EMS with spine boarding and airway/equipment management, accompanies the athlete in the ambulance while maintaining immobilization and control of athletic equipment, and assists with helmet/shoulder-pad removal and history handoff in the trauma bay.

Travel or tournament away from home: the trainer accompanies an athlete (often a minor) to an unfamiliar local hospital, physically assists them through an unknown facility, obtains phone consent and insurance details from parents, advocates during evaluation, and arranges return transport to the team hotel or bus.

On-campus escort: an ambulatory athlete is walked or carted from the athletic facility across campus to the affiliated university hospital or student health center; the trainer steadies the athlete, delivers the injury handoff, waits during evaluation, and escorts the athlete back to the residence hall or athletic training room.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous mobile manipulator, is commercially deployed in US hospitals where it navigates corridors and elevators among people to deliver supplies, labs and medications; it does not escort, monitor, physically support or clinically hand off patients.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed hospital robot, cited to show the limit of transfer. Moxi performs item logistics, not patient accompaniment: it does not assist an injured person's movement, monitor their condition, or deliver a clinical history handoff to ED staff, so it does not substantiate this task at any tier.

sources.title: Waymo begins fully autonomous ops with 6th-gen Driver, targets 1M weekly rides
sources.claim: Waymo operates driverless passenger vehicles on public roads at commercial scale, so a person can be conveyed to a hospital without a human driver, but the vehicle provides no companion, no physical assistance and no clinical handoff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous passenger conveyance. It covers only the travel leg; accompaniment requires embodied assistance with a possibly non-ambulatory injured athlete, en-route monitoring, and an information/advocacy role in the emergency department, none of which the vehicle performs.

sources.developer: Foxconn / Kawasaki Heavy Industries with NVIDIA
sources.title: Foxconn Uses NVIDIA Isaac for Smart Hospital Solutions - Customer Story
sources.claim: Nurabot, an autonomous nursing-assistant robot tested in Taiwanese hospitals, performs ward logistics (medication and specimen delivery) and staff/patient interaction; it does not transport or accompany patients out of the facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is in-facility clinical logistics in a structured hospital. It does not transfer: accompanying an injured athlete requires physical support of a patient, travel by ambulance or car on public roads, and clinical communication with emergency staff.

tasks.label: Lead stretching exercises for team members prior to games or practices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-practice dynamic warm-up on an outdoor school or college athletic field/track: the athletic trainer stands in front of 25-60 athletes, calls and bodily demonstrates a sequence of dynamic movements (leg swings, lunge walks, high knees, hamstring sweeps) while the group travels 20-30 yards down the field, sets cadence and holds, scans athletes for poor mechanics or tightness, and adjusts the routine for weather, sport and the day's practice plan.

Pre-game warm-up at a competition venue (home or visiting field/court): the trainer leads the team through the established pre-competition stretch/warm-up on a fixed clock, in crowd noise, sharing space with officials, opponents and media, modifying stretches for athletes with existing injuries and communicating with coaches about timing.

Fixed-location group stretch routine indoors (field house, gym floor, wrestling room or athletic training room) before practice with a smaller group of roughly 8-20 athletes: trainer demonstrates and calls a standard sequence of standing and floor static/mobility stretches, counts holds, encourages, and corrects obvious form errors from the front of the group.

Individual or paired hands-on assisted stretching before activity (athletic training room table or sideline): trainer physically grasps and moves an athlete's limb through range - PNF contract-relax hamstring, hip flexor, adductor or shoulder stretches - sensing tissue resistance and end-feel, coordinating with the athlete's breathing and pain feedback, for athletes with tightness or returning from injury.

Youth/club/tournament or road settings taken as found: a rented public park field, a multi-team tournament site, a hotel ballroom or parking-lot staging area with no dedicated space, uneven ground, bags and equipment scattered, spectators and passersby present, and variable weather; trainer improvises the stretch routine for whichever athletes are present.

roles.title: Surgical Assistants
aliases: Med Surg Nursing Assistant (Medical Surgical Nursing Assistant)
Med Surg PCA (Medical Surgical Patient Care Assistant)
OR Surgical Tech (Operating Room Surgical Technician)
Travel RNFA (Travel Registered Nurse First Assistant)
roles.description: Assist in operations, under the supervision of surgeons. May, in accordance with state laws, help surgeons to make incisions and close surgical sites, manipulate or remove tissues, implant surgical devices or drains, suction the surgical site, place catheters, clamp or cauterize vessels or tissue, and apply dressings to surgical site.

tasks.label: Monitor and maintain aseptic technique throughout procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine inpatient hospital OR case (general, gyn, ortho; 1–3 hours). Scrubbed assistant continuously watches the sterile field: gown/glove integrity of every scrubbed member, drape position, back-table and Mayo stand, items opened onto the field by the circulator. Corrects minor breaks in real time — discards a contaminated instrument, re-drapes a sagging edge, re-gloves after a suture-needle stick, keeps hands above waist and within the field.

Ambulatory surgery center / outpatient short cases (ophthalmology, plastics, hand, arthroscopy, hernia) with fast turnover and a small team. Assistant maintains asepsis through prep-and-drape, the procedure, and closure, while equipment and personnel move in and out quickly; must catch and correct breaches without slowing the case.

Long, complex case (cardiac, spine, neuro, robotic-assisted) with implants, grafts, C-arm or navigation, and a draped robotic platform. Assistant monitors sterility of implants and instruments delivered mid-case, drapes and re-drapes equipment brought into the field, tracks traffic of perfusion/imaging/vendor staff, and maintains asepsis over many hours.

Contamination event requiring active correction mid-procedure: glove perforation, drape strike-through from irrigation or blood, an unsterile person or unsterile equipment contacting the field, dropped instrument, or breach discovered on an implant package. Assistant identifies the breach, calls it out, isolates and replaces the contaminated items/gown/drape, and re-establishes the field without contaminating the wound.

Non-OR procedural setting: cath/EP lab, labor-and-delivery cesarean room, endoscopy suite, trauma bay, or office-based surgical suite. Assistant maintains aseptic technique with less controlled traffic, tighter space, and mixed sterile/non-sterile equipment (fluoroscopy, monitors, lines) crossing near the field.

sources.system: Humanoid laparoscopic teleoperation framework (UC San Diego, in vivo porcine study)
sources.developer: UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering / Department of Surgery
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery
sources.claim: The most advanced 2026 evaluation of general-purpose humanoid robots in real surgery used teleoperation for laparoscopic tasks on anesthetized pigs; human staff performed sterile prep and draping, sterility of the robot was improvised with gloves, and the authors state preserving sterility is an unsolved barrier.
sources.transferJustification: Closest embodied system to the surgical sterile field. It does not perform aseptic monitoring/correction; sterility of the robot itself is unresolved and humans did the sterile prep and draping, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task in any environment.

sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: A humanoid 'scrub nurse' that maintains the sterile field and monitors for contamination exists only as a conceptual proposal with a staged validation roadmap beginning in the laboratory; autonomous clinical use is described as premature.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses the target task (maintaining the sterile field, monitoring for contamination) but as an envisioned capability, not a demonstration, so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: The state of the art for autonomous mobile manipulation in an operating room is item-level supply logistics in a simulated OR, at reliability well below human standards (80% retrieval success), with sterility handling named as an open challenge.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling sterile OR supplies. Transfer fails — it fetches and restocks items in a simulated OR at sub-worker reliability and performs no monitoring of team technique or correction of contamination events.

sources.title: Compounder robot scores with health systems | Drug Topics
sources.claim: Commercially deployed aseptic robots maintain sterility autonomously throughout a preparation procedure, but only inside a closed, purpose-built ISO Class 5 enclosure with no patient, no drapes, and no human participants inside the aseptic space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maintaining asepsis throughout a procedure in a purpose-built cell. Transfer to surgical aseptic technique fails — the objects (vials/syringes vs. drapes, gowns, implants, a live patient) and the core function (perceiving and correcting breaks in a human team's technique) are absent, so it cannot substantiate this task even at E1.

sources.system: Robotic scrub nurse (RSN) with instrument prediction
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.claim: Robotic scrub nurse research systems target autonomous instrument handover based on laparoscopic video, positioned beside the operating table; they are research prototypes and address instrument passing, not surveillance and correction of aseptic technique.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile instrument handling in the OR. Transfer fails — the demonstrated function is predicting and passing instruments in a research setup, with no capability to detect or remediate breaks in aseptic technique.

tasks.label: Maintain an unobstructed operative field, using surgical retractors, sponges, or suctioning and irrigating equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open abdominal / OB-GYN case in a hospital OR (colectomy, hysterectomy, cesarean): assistant holds and continuously repositions Deaver/Richardson/malleable retractors on request, packs and swaps laparotomy sponges, suctions blood and electrocautery smoke, irrigates the cavity, adapting second-by-second to the surgeon's dissection and to bleeding.

Orthopedic or spine case (total knee/hip, laminectomy, fracture fixation): forceful retraction of muscle and soft tissue with Hohmann/Bennett/Taylor retractors held for long stretches, suction of blood, marrow and bone debris, pulsed-lavage irrigation, sponging of the deep wound; force must expose without crushing nerves or skin edges.

Laparoscopic or robot-assisted case with the assistant at the bedside: driving the laparoscope, retracting bowel/liver/uterus with a grasper through an assistant port, using the suction-irrigator to clear blood and smoke, cleaning the lens, inside a moving insufflated cavity and coordinated with the surgeon at the console.

Cardiothoracic or vascular case (CABG, valve, AAA repair): sternal/self-retaining retractor management, vessel-loop and cardiac positioning exposure, near-continuous suction of blood from a deep confined field, sponging and irrigation during anastomoses, with brisk bleeding events requiring instant field clearing.

Ambulatory-surgery-center or minor case (hernia repair, ENT, hand, plastics, podiatry): small handheld skin/soft-tissue retractors (Senn, army-navy), gauze sponging to blot the field, Frazier-tip suction, syringe irrigation, in short cases with a small superficial field and frequent surgeon-directed repositioning.

sources.system: Autonomous tissue retraction pipeline on da Vinci Research Kit

sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review | npj Digital Medicine
sources.claim: Systematic review of FDA-cleared surgical robots finds clinically cleared systems top out at conditional (Level 3) autonomy; none is cleared to autonomously retract, sponge, suction and irrigate to maintain the operative field in human surgery.
sources.transferJustification: Context on the clinical state of the art: establishes that no cleared system provides autonomous operative-field maintenance; supports negative judgments only.

tasks.label: Pass instruments or supplies to surgeon during procedure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Major open abdominal/pelvic case in a hospital OR (colectomy, open hysterectomy, C-section, open hernia/urology): assistant serves from a large back table and Mayo stand — clamps, retractors, scissors, needle holders loaded with suture, ties, laparotomy sponges, syringes, drains — with many rapid exchanges, much of it anticipated without a verbal request, sharps passed hands-free, sterility and counts maintained.

Laparoscopic/endoscopic or robotic-assisted case (lap chole, appendectomy, lap hernia, da Vinci case) in a hospital OR or ASC: passing trocars, graspers, hook cautery, clip applier, scissors, suction-irrigator, stapler, specimen bag, and exchanging robotic instruments at the cart; a moderate set of rigid shafted instruments plus skin knife and closure suture.

Orthopedic or spine case in a hospital OR or ortho ASC (total knee/hip, fracture fixation, laminectomy): serving heavy multi-tray sets, powered saws/drills/reamers with battery and bit changes, mallets, broaches, screws and implants presented from caddies, plus irrigation and sponges, at the surgeon's pace.

High-acuity or emergency case (cardiothoracic, vascular, neurosurgery, trauma laparotomy) in a hospital OR: long instrument inventory, fine instruments, shodded clamps, pledgeted sutures, and unpredictable urgent demands where an instrument must reach the surgeon's hand within a second or two during bleeding.

Minor/ambulatory procedure in an ASC, minor OR or procedure room (lipoma or skin lesion excision, hand or podiatric case, minor plastics, ophthalmic case): a small tray of a dozen or so instruments, a modest number of exchanges over a 20-45 minute case, requests usually spoken.

sources.developer: Ng et al., published in Advanced Intelligent Systems
sources.title: Large Language Model-Embedded Intelligent Robotic Scrub Nurse with Multimodal Input — Advanced Intelligent Systems
sources.claim: An LLM-embedded robotic scrub nurse executed instrument transferring, sorting and counting on a real robot platform with multimodal voice/vision input, tracking the surgeon's hand for handover; experiments were laboratory bench experiments, not clinical use.

sources.title: Chinese humanoid robot used in landmark surgery — China Daily
sources.claim: The most recent humanoid-robot work inside a live operating room (UC San Diego, live in-vivo procedures, July 2026) was performed under teleoperation, not autonomy, indicating that general-purpose robotic handling of standard OR instruments in real cases is still human-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot manipulation of standard surgical instruments in a live OR); cited only to show that current real-OR instrument handling by general-purpose robots is teleoperated and therefore cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Assist with patient resuscitation during cardiac arrest or other life-threatening events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intraoperative cardiac arrest during a case: the surgical assistant delivers external chest compressions at the table on a draped, positioned patient, rotating with the code team, while the sterile field is protected and the surgeon halts the procedure.

Intraoperative arrest escalating to open-chest resuscitation (emergency thoracotomy/sternotomy, internal cardiac massage): assistant retracts, suctions blood, delivers or supports internal cardiac massage and positions internal defibrillator paddles under the surgeon's direction.

Non-arrest life-threatening event, most often massive hemorrhage (major vessel injury, uncontrolled bleeding, coagulopathy): assistant applies direct manual pressure or packing, suctions to keep the field visible, holds clamps/retraction while the surgeon gains vessel control.
Code outside the OR but inside the facility (PACU, endoscopy suite, procedure room, inpatient floor): assistant responds and performs manual chest compressions on a bed or gurney until relieved.

Same codes: assistant applies defibrillator pads/monitor leads to bare skin, assists bag-mask ventilation, performs suctioning of the airway, hands laryngoscope/ET tube and applies cricoid pressure for the intubating clinician.

Support role during a resuscitation: retrieve the crash cart/defibrillator/blood products and emergency supplies within seconds, open sterile packs and drug packaging, pass syringes and equipment to the team on verbal order, help reposition or transfer the patient.

sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system | Stryker
sources.claim: The LUCAS 3 piston-driven chest compression system is a commercial, widely fielded device that, once strapped to the patient, autonomously delivers continuous guideline-rate/depth compressions without human control of each cycle; used in hospitals during transport, PCI in the cath lab and ECMO cannulation.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: delivering external chest compressions during cardiac arrest is the principal physical act the surgical assistant contributes to resuscitation. Device placement on the patient is still performed by clinicians.

sources.system: LUCAS-2 mechanical chest compression device (PARAMEDIC trial)
sources.developer: Physio-Control/Jolife; trial by University of Warwick
sources.title: Mechanical chest compression in the PARAMEDIC trial - The Lancet
sources.claim: A large pragmatic cluster-randomised trial delivered mechanical chest compressions to hundreds of real cardiac-arrest patients, with 30-day survival comparable to (not better than) human manual compressions, establishing that machine-delivered compressions are clinically usable output rather than only a laboratory demonstration.

sources.title: Mechanical CPR, stay and play, epi and more: Top takeaways from the 2025 AHA CPR/ECC Guidelines
sources.claim: Current resuscitation guidelines treat mechanical CPR devices as a bounded alternative, not a routine replacement for human compressions, and require clinicians to minimise interruptions during device deployment and removal — i.e., humans still perform the placement step of the instance.

sources.system: ROSCER remote-controlled automatic chest compression device
sources.title: A remote-controlled automatic chest compression device capable of moving compression position during CPR: A pilot study in a mannequin and a swine model of cardiac arrest
sources.claim: Chest-compression robots that can reposition the compression point or close the loop on physiologic feedback remain preclinical: ROSCER is remote-controlled and was tested only on a mannequin and in a swine arrest model.

sources.developer: Seoul National University Hospital (Kim, Suh et al.)
sources.title: Development of artificial intelligence-driven biosignal-sensitive cardiopulmonary resuscitation robot - Resuscitation
sources.claim: An AI-driven CPR robot using closed-loop biosignal feedback has been demonstrated only in an animal (swine) laboratory model against LUCAS 3, showing autonomous compression control is at research stage rather than clinical deployment.

sources.system: Robotic scrub nurse (RSN) with laparoscopic video anticipation
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis | Communications Medicine
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic scrub nurse work anticipates and hands laparoscopic instruments correctly about 71% of the time in a research setting — far below the reliability needed for instrument/equipment handling during a code.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passing instruments/equipment to the operative team. Performance here bounds what a robot could contribute to handing defibrillator paddles, airway gear or drugs during a resuscitation, and it falls short of worker reliability.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulators are deployed at scale inside hospitals for scheduled supply and pharmacy deliveries along corridors, but the demonstrated work is non-time-critical logistics, not bedside emergency retrieval and handoff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital supply transport. It shows autonomous E2 navigation, but not the seconds-scale crash-cart retrieval, package opening and sterile handoff the resuscitation support role requires, so it does not transfer.

tasks.label: Verify the identity of patient or operative site.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Obtain or inspect sterile or non-sterile surgical equipment, instruments, or supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-case pull: in the hospital sterile core / OR supply room, gather the instrument sets, implants, sutures, drapes and disposables listed on the surgeon's preference card, checking each item's identity, size, lot/expiration date and package integrity, and load the case cart for the room.

Setup inspection at the sterile field: open wrapped trays and peel packs aseptically onto the back table, verify external/internal chemical indicators and package integrity, inspect instruments for cleanliness, corrosion, alignment, sharpness, insulation and ratchet function, and assemble laparoscopic/powered instruments before the incision.

Intra-operative obtain: during a live case the assistant identifies a needed additional instrument or supply (extra suture, different retractor, larger implant, replacement cord), obtains it from the room, the sterile core or via the circulator, confirms it is the correct undamaged sterile item, and gets it to the field within seconds to a minute.

Equipment obtain and inspect: locate and bring in capital equipment and accessories (electrosurgical generator, suction, insufflator, camera/light cord, tourniquet, headlamp, positioning devices, robot arm drapes), verify function and settings, connect cords and tubing, and troubleshoot faults before or during the case.

Post-case / SPD side (common in ASCs and small hospitals): inspect used and reprocessed instruments for residual soil, damage and function, verify sets against the tray count sheet, flag or replace missing/broken items, and obtain loaner or replacement trays for the next case.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a commercially deployed hospital mobile manipulator, autonomously picks supplies from hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching packaged medical supplies inside a hospital. It bears on the 'obtain supplies' half of this task, though the items are ward stock rather than case-cart sterile inventory and no expiry/integrity inspection is reported.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics hits 1M picks with Moxi robot in healthcare settings - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi fleets are in routine hospital service at scale, doing autonomous point-to-point transport of supplies, medications and specimens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply transport. Establishes what fielded hospital robots reliably do (transport) versus item-level picking and inspection, which they do not.

sources.system: ORB (Operating Room Bot, Fetch mobile manipulator)
sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation (arXiv:2509.15600)
sources.claim: Item-level retrieval of OR supplies by an autonomous mobile manipulator is still research-grade: 80% success in a mock hospital supply room with three ....

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Stäubli TX2-60L arm, dual electromagnetic gripper, YOLO12/ResNet perception)
sources.developer: University of Louisville (with Saint Vincent's Hospital SPD)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell autonomously recognizes 31 surgical instrument types and sorts and packs them into sterile trays, targeting the SPD inspection/assembly stage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: identifying and handling individual surgical instruments to build a correct set. Verifying that the right instruments are present and placing them in a tray is the same perception-plus-manipulation problem as checking a set against a count sheet.

sources.title: Automations - Steelco
sources.claim: A commercial packing robot automates wrapping, taping and labeling of surgical instrument trays inside hospital sterile processing departments (installed e.g. at Jeroen Bosch Hospital).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and correct labeling of surgical instrument trays in a fixture-fed station within a hospital SPD; comparable objects and precision to preparing/verifying trays for the next case.

sources.title: Automated Pharmacy Storage System - Swisslog BoxPicker
sources.claim: Fully automated robotic storage-and-retrieval machines pick individual packaged medical items to order inside hospitals, with scan-in/scan-out verification at dispense.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic retrieval of specified packaged, barcoded medical items from dense enclosed storage with identity verification and expiry-managed inventory — the same physical operation as pulling packaged sterile supplies to a pick list when the stock is brought into a purpose-built machine.

sources.system: AutoStore robotic storage/fulfilment system in Medline distribution centers
sources.title: Warehouse Robotic Technology Picks The Exact Goods You Need - Medline
sources.claim: Robotic order-fulfilment cells (AutoStore) run medical-surgical supply distribution for hospitals, surgery centers and physician offices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage and order assembly of the same sterile packs, sutures and disposables a surgical assistant pulls; substantiates that the 'obtain supplies' work is done by robots when inventory is presented in a purpose-built system.

sources.developer: Multi-Scale Medical Robotics Centre / Chinese University of Hong Kong
sources.title: RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model (project page)
sources.claim: A robotic scrub nurse autonomously selects and hands over named surgical instruments from a bench tray on voice command, with high reported handover success in lab evaluation.

sources.system: Scrub Nurse Robot (SNR) with automatic instrument insertion (AISI)
sources.developer: Tokyo Women's Medical University (Yoshimitsu, Masamune et al.)
sources.title: Enhancing surgical efficiency with an automated scrub nurse robot: a focus on automatic instrument insertion - PubMed
sources.claim: A third-generation scrub nurse robot with automatic instrument insertion performs instrument exchange with the surgeon in experimental surgical workflow studies.

tasks.label: Assist members of surgical team with gowning or gloving.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR, case start: after the surgeon scrubs, the assistant (already scrubbed and gowned) opens the sterile gown pack, unfolds the wrap-around gown without touching the outside, presents it so the surgeon slides both arms into the sleeves, then assists closed gloving — stretching each sterile glove cuff over the gown's stockinette cuff — and hands off the wrap-around belt card. Any contact with a non-sterile surface means discarding the gown/glove and restarting.

Mid-case glove change in a hospital OR: a team member's glove is perforated or contaminated; the assistant must, at the sterile field, strip the soiled glove and present a fresh sterile glove open-cuffed for the surgeon to plunge into (or re-gown entirely), while instruments are in play and the case continues, within seconds.

Case start with several people to gown and glove in sequence (first assistant, resident, second scrub) in a crowded OR with equipment booms, back tables, and staff moving; varied gown and glove sizes, some double-gloving, all under time pressure before draping.

Ambulatory surgery center or small procedure/endoscopy room with rapid back-to-back turnovers: cramped space, limited staff, the assistant gowns and gloves the surgeon quickly between cases using standard disposable gown/glove packs.

Emergent case (trauma laparotomy, crash cesarean, hybrid OR/cath lab conversion): gowning and gloving must be done in seconds amid a crowded, noisy room, sometimes with the surgeon already moving toward the table, and with imaging or resuscitation equipment in the way.

sources.system: Imperial College Personal Robotics Lab dual-arm dressing robot (Zhang & Demiris, Science Robotics)
sources.title: A robot that can put a surgical gown on a supine mannequin
sources.claim: A dual-arm robot at Imperial College London autonomously took a back-opening hospital/surgical gown off a hook and dressed a supine mannequin's arms, succeeding about 90% of 200 trials in a simulated hospital room — the closest published robotic capability to gowning a person, but on a passive mannequin, without aseptic technique, ties, or gloving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robot-assisted dressing of a patient. It is the nearest demonstrated capability to gowning, but transfer fails: the subject is a supine immobile mannequin in a lab, the garment is a loose back-opening patient gown rather than a wrap-around sterile surgical gown, no sterile technique or belt/tie handling is involved, no gloving is performed, and a ~10% failure rate is far above the near-zero contamination tolerance of surgical gowning.

sources.system: IGIN / IGIN Smart automatic glove-donning device
sources.title: Smart Device Helps Don Sterile Gloves Automatically - HospiMedica
sources.claim: IGIN's automatic glove-donning station uses sensors and vacuum to fit a disposable glove onto hands inserted into the machine; it is a fixed dispensing appliance for bare hands in general clinical/industrial settings, with no evidence of assisted surgical gloving over a sterile gown cuff at the sterile field, and it performs no gowning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = machine-assisted glove donning. It does not substantiate the surgical instance: the user must walk to a fixed station and insert bare hands, whereas assisted surgical gloving requires presenting a sterile glove cuff over the wearer's gowned stockinette cuff at the sterile field without contaminating gown, glove, or field.

sources.system: Bimanual robot-assisted dressing strategy (University of York / Honda Research Institute EU)
sources.developer: University of York and Honda Research Institute EU
sources.title: Bimanual Robot-Assisted Dressing: A Spherical Coordinate-Based Strategy for Tight-Fitting Garments
sources.claim: As of 2025, robot-assisted dressing research remains at the level of loose-fitting garments on cooperative subjects in laboratory setups, with imitation-learned trajectories validated in experiments rather than deployed clinical use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robot dressing of a human limb. Establishes the state of the art for garment manipulation on people as of 2025: lab validation on loose garments, well short of aseptic gowning of a scrubbed surgeon.

sources.system: Scrub Nurse Robot (SNR), third generation with automatic instrument insertion
sources.developer: Tokyo Women's Medical University / Industries-Academies Liaison System Research Institute
sources.title: Enhancing surgical efficiency with an automated scrub nurse robot: a focus on automatic instrument insertion - PubMed
sources.claim: The most advanced operating-room assistant robot for scrub-nurse duties automates rigid laparoscopic instrument delivery, and its third generation was still evaluated in laboratory experiments with surgeon stand-ins; it performs no gowning or gloving of staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = scrub-nurse assistance in the OR. It shows what is substantiated for robots in the sterile field — handling rigid, fixtured instruments — and does not transfer to unfolding and presenting deformable sterile textiles or making contact with a colleague's hands and arms.

tasks.label: Cover patients with surgical drapes to create and maintain a sterile operative field.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine open general-surgery case (hernia, appendectomy, laparotomy, cholecystectomy conversion) in a hospital OR: after skin prep dries, the assistant (scrubbed, gowned/gloved) squares off the site with towels, applies an adhesive incise drape, unfolds a large fenestrated laparotomy drape with a second scrubbed person over the supine patient without touching non-sterile surfaces, secures suction/cautery lines, and monitors and corrects the field throughout the case.

Orthopedic extremity case (total knee, shoulder, hand, ankle): limb elevated and held while stockinette, impervious U-drapes and split sheets are wrapped and layered, extremity drape fenestration positioned around the joint, elastic/adhesive bands applied, tourniquet area isolated; drapes re-secured as the limb is moved through flexion/extension during the procedure.

Minimally invasive / robotic-assisted case (laparoscopic or da Vinci): patient draped for port placement, plus sterile draping of robotic arms, camera, cords, and C-arm or microscope covers; drape integrity maintained while arms are docked, the table is tilted, and equipment is repositioned.

Major open specialty case (cardiac/CABG, C-section, vascular, spine) with very large multi-layer drape sets, drape screens/ether screens at the anesthesia boundary, multiple limb or graft-site fields, tubing and line management, and continuous maintenance of the field over hours including re-draping after a contamination event.

Small-field head/neck, ophthalmic, ENT or dental-surgical case: precise drape placement around the face and airway with head wrap and adhesive drapes, working around the endotracheal tube and anesthesia circuit, fenestration aligned within centimeters of the operative site, patient awake-to-just-anesthetized and sometimes moving.

Non-standard or urgent case: trauma or emergency laparotomy under time pressure, prone/lateral/lithotomy positioning, bariatric body habitus, external fixators or traction hardware, pediatric patient, or a field that must be extended intraoperatively when the incision is enlarged.

sources.system: Humanoid robots as embodied AI teammates in the OR (conceptual framework)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: A July 2026 perspective proposes a staged framework ... ORs (supplies, equipment, room turnover, supporting sterile conditions); it is conceptual, with no demonstrated system performing these roles, and states that evidence of safety or clinical benefit is lacking.
sources.transferJustification: Closest OR-role evidence for humanoids; it is a roadmap rather than a demonstration, so it cannot substantiate completion of patient draping at any tier.

sources.system: Surgie (Unitree G1 humanoid laparoscopic teleoperation system)
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery
sources.claim: The first in vivo humanoid-robot surgery study (Unitree G1 platform, 'Surgie') had the robot teleoperated by a surgeon to hold laparoscopic instruments; sterility was approximated by gloving the robot arms rather than by real sterile workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of the art for humanoids physically working at the sterile field in 2026: teleoperated, with sterility only simulated, so it cannot support autonomous patient draping.

sources.system: RoBE / Bodies Uncovered bedding manipulation (mobile manipulator)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon RCHI Lab (Puthuveetil, Erickson et al.)
sources.title: Robust Body Exposure (RoBE): A Graph-based Dynamics Modeling Approach to Manipulating Blankets over People
sources.claim: Research robots can autonomously manipulate a blanket over a person lying supine in bed, adapting to body shape, pose and blanket configuration, validated with 12 human participants in a laboratory setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing/moving a large cloth over a supine person. Transfer to surgical draping fails — it is a single non-sterile blanket in a lab, with no sterile technique, no multi-drape layering, no adhesive incise film, no fenestration alignment to an incision, and no contamination monitoring.

sources.system: CMU robot-assisted dressing system (reinforcement-learning garment manipulation)
sources.title: Robotic-assisted dressing system accommodates different poses, body types and garments
sources.claim: Carnegie Mellon researchers demonstrated a learned robot-assisted dressing system that pulls garments such as a hospital gown along a person's arm across varying body shapes, arm poses and garments, in laboratory experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating fabric onto a human body. It does not transfer to surgical draping because it is non-sterile, single-garment, slow, lab-only, and has no requirement to establish or preserve an aseptic field.

sources.system: Robotic scrub nurse (RSN) with laparoscopic video-based instrument anticipation
sources.developer: Wagner et al. (academic consortium), published in Communications Medicine
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.claim: A robotic scrub nurse system autonomously predicts and hands over laparoscopic instruments during cholecystectomy workflows, showing that OR-adjacent robot autonomy so far addresses instrument delivery, not patient draping or sterile-field creation.
sources.transferJustification: Same occupation and setting (sterile OR support work); the demonstrated scope is instrument handover only, with draping still performed by human staff, so it provides no support for robotic patient draping.

tasks.label: Coordinate or participate in the positioning of patients, using body stabilizing equipment or protective padding to provide appropriate exposure for the procedure or to protect against nerve damage or circulation impairment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supine positioning for a general/abdominal, laparoscopic, vascular or cardiac case in a hospital OR: after induction the assistant helps lift/slide the anesthetized patient onto the table, places arms on padded arm boards at <90 degrees or tucks them with draw sheets and elbow padding, positions a head donut, places gel pads under heels, sacrum and elbows, applies the thigh safety strap, and rechecks pressure points and line clearance before prep.

Prone positioning for spine or posterior cranial surgery: coordinated log-roll of the anesthetized, intubated patient from the stretcher onto a Jackson table or Wilson frame with chest rolls, seating the face in a foam cradle or Mayfield holder with eyes and airway free, arms tucked or brought to 'superman' on padded boards with shoulder abduction <90 degrees, padding knees, ankles and genitalia, then periodic re-checks of eyes and pressure points.

Lithotomy positioning for GYN, urology, colorectal or robotic pelvic surgery: legs lifted simultaneously into Allen or candy-cane stirrups, boots padded at the fibular head to protect the peroneal nerve, hips/knees flexed to surgeon preference, buttocks at the table break, arms tucked, non-slip pad or shoulder support for steep Trendelenburg, with stirrup height adjusted during the case.

Lateral decubitus positioning for thoracotomy/VATS, nephrectomy or hip arthroplasty: team log-roll of the anesthetized patient onto the operative side, placement of an axillary roll, bean bag or pegboard/hip positioners, pillows between legs, dependent-arm padding and an elevated arm holder, taping across hip and shoulder, then verification of head/neck alignment and dependent eye and ear position.

Beach-chair/sitting position for shoulder arthroscopy or some neuro cases: raising the back section, securing the head in a padded head holder with neutral cervical alignment, padding the non-operative arm, hips and knees flexed with heel padding, safety strap and lateral supports applied, operative limb placed in a limb positioner or traction device.

Intra-operative repositioning or conversion: shifting the patient or table mid-case (supine to lithotomy, adding steep Trendelenburg or lateral tilt, flexing the table, re-padding a slipped heel or arm), re-securing stabilizing devices, and re-verifying that no bony prominence or nerve is compressed after the change.

sources.system: Dry-AIREC dual-arm humanoid (deep predictive learning repositioning assistance)
sources.developer: Waseda University / AIREC project (Miyake, Saito, Ogata, Sugano)
sources.title: Deep Predictive Learning with Proprioceptive and Visual Attention for Humanoid Robot Repositioning Assistance
sources.claim: The most advanced published attempt at a robot manipulating a reclining human body is a dual-arm humanoid that autonomously slid its hand under a mannequin's back in a bed and supported a supine-to-lifted transition in a laboratory - a sub-step of repositioning, not positioning with padding and stabilizing devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nursing repositioning of a person lying in bed. It is the closest demonstrated robot-on-human-body manipulation, but it is performed on a mannequin in a lab, covers a single sub-motion, and includes no padding, stirrups, bean bags or straps, so it does not transfer to completing surgical positioning.

sources.title: SOT-100 Vercia Robotic Operating Table | Medicaroid
sources.claim: Commercial 'robotic' operating tables move the tabletop and thus the patient's gross posture, but are driven by OR staff via controller or preset recall and do not place padding, tuck arms, log-roll patients or apply stabilizing equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Same domain (positioning a patient in an OR) but only the powered table-articulation portion, commanded by a human operator; none of the padding, limb arrangement or nerve-protection judgment in the task is performed by the machine.

sources.system: Siemens six-axis robotic patient positioners, Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center
sources.developer: Siemens / Heidelberg Ion Beam Therapy Center
sources.title: Accuracy of robotic patient positioners used in ion beam therapy | Radiation Oncology
sources.claim: In radiotherapy, six-axis robotic positioners routinely and accurately move patients in daily clinical operation, but human therapists first place and immobilize the patient on the couch; the robot only translates and rotates the whole couch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise positioning of a patient for a clinical procedure. Transfer is limited: the machine moves a rigid couch carrying an already-immobilized, cooperative patient, while humans perform all body handling, padding and immobilization - the substance of the surgical positioning task.

sources.title: Giving patients a lift - the robotic nursing assistant (RoNA) | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: Patient-handling robots able to lift a human body remain human-guided prototypes rather than autonomous clinical systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and transferring a dependent patient. It shows that even gross body lifting by a robot is nurse-guided, so it cannot substantiate autonomous surgical positioning with padding and stabilizers.
