sources.system: Humanoid robots in the operating room (staged framework perspective)
sources.developer: academic surgical/robotics authors (perspective article reported by News-Medical)
sources.title: Humanoid robots could take on low-risk operating room tasks before assisting surgical teams
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 the published frontier for humanoid robots in operating rooms is a staged proposal limited to low-risk perioperative tasks such as supplies, equipment and room turnover; autonomous clinical use, which would include patient positioning, is judged premature.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting (the OR) and adjacent tasks; documents that no fielded humanoid performs patient-contact OR tasks such as positioning.

tasks.label: Determine availability of necessary equipment or supplies for operative procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Gather, arrange, or assemble instruments or supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-case sterile setup in the OR: after scrubbing and gowning, receive/open sterile instrument sets and supplies onto the sterile field, drape the back table and Mayo stand, and arrange instruments, sutures, sponges and blades in the standard order of use for the scheduled procedure, verifying set completeness with the circulator.

Assembling instruments and devices at the sterile field: mounting blades on knife handles, loading suture/needles into needle holders, connecting laparoscopic instruments, trocars, light cords, camera and insufflation tubing, fitting burrs/blades to powered drills and saws, assembling retractor systems or robotic-arm attachments.

Fetching a modest number of specific packaged supplies (extra sutures, sponges, dressings, a disposable stapler) from the OR core or central supply and bringing them to the room before or between cases.

Pulling a complete case cart against the surgeon's preference card: dozens of heterogeneous items plus heavy wrapped instrument sets, implant trays with size/lot verification, checking sterility indicators and expiry, loading the cart and moving it to the OR.

Mid-case gathering and preparation of additional items: obtaining an extra instrument set, an implant of the correct size, or additional supplies once the case is underway, and preparing/assembling them (loading an implant onto an inserter, assembling an added retractor) in time for the surgeon.

Post-case / sterile-processing-side work, common in ASCs and small hospitals: gathering used instruments, sorting them back into their correct sets, checking counts and completeness, and arranging trays for reprocessing and future cases.

sources.system: RIF Robotics PacR tray assembly system
sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: RIF Robotics' robotic tray-assembly workstation, piloted inside a Wellstar hospital sterile processing department, autonomously assembled a minor surgical instrument tray, selecting and placing instruments in their correct tray positions.
sources.transferJustification: Assembling a surgical instrument set into a defined tray layout is the same act of gathering and arranging instruments the surgical assistant performs when building a set-up: same objects (steel instruments) and same placement precision.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell (Staubli TX2-60L arm, dual electromagnetic gripper, calibrated top-down vision, 3D-printed dividers/holders) autonomously sorts 31 classes of surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays in reproducible layouts.
sources.transferJustification: Sorting and structured packing of surgical instruments into a tray is the arranging/assembling of instrument sets performed by the assistant; same reflective steel instruments and comparable placement accuracy.

sources.system: ACA/Addtronics automated surgical instrument assembly and inspection system
sources.title: Case Study: Surgical Instrument Assembly Automation
sources.claim: A commercial fully automated assembly cell builds a surgical instrument from fed components: vision-guided 6-axis robots pick parts from bowl feeders, drawers and tray handlers, install and press-fit them, and vision-inspect each assembly step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory assembly of a multi-part surgical instrument. Transfers to the assistant's instrument assembly (blade onto handle, laparoscopic parts, drill attachments) because the parts, mating tolerances and verification are comparable when components are fixtured and presented.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals — IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a commercial hospital mobile manipulator, autonomously picks well-known supply items out of bins in hospital supply rooms and delivers them to drop-off points on nursing units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving stock supplies from a hospital supply room and delivering them to a clinical area — the same packaged supply items, storage rooms and corridors as the assistant's supply runs.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi is in routine service across more than 25 US hospitals with over one million autonomous deliveries completed, roughly a third of its time spent delivering supplies and equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes current deployment scale and reliability of autonomous supply retrieval and delivery inside hospitals, the environment of the assistant's supply-fetching instances.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: ORB, a Fetch-based autonomous mobile manipulator built for operating-room logistics, retrieved requested OR supplies from shelves and restocked items in a simulated hospital supply room, with 80% retrieval and 96% restocking success without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the gathering of OR supplies from storage; cited to show that as-found OR supply-room picking remains at laboratory success rates (80% retrieval), below worker quality.

sources.title: Case Studies | Explore our automation and robotics solutions — Gibotech
sources.claim: Gibotech has installed robot-based automated sterile stores and sterilization centrals in hospitals, where sterilized surgical instrument containers and disposables are automatically stored and retrieved by storage robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage and retrieval of sterile instrument containers and disposables for surgery — the machine-side equivalent of gathering the instrument sets and supplies needed for a case.

sources.title: Decontamination of a robot used to reprocess reusable surgical instruments — Journal of Hospital Infection
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed infection-control literature notes that robots are already used in central sterile supply departments to take over sorting and handling of heavy instrument sieves.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that instrument-set handling and sorting automation is in real hospital sterile-processing use, supporting the instrument-gathering instances at machine-centric workstations.

tasks.label: Operate sterilizing devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Immediate-use steam sterilization ("flash") in the OR sub-sterile room during a case: a dropped or single unwrapped instrument is retrieved, hand-cleaned, placed in an IUSS container, a rapid cycle is run on the tabletop/small chamber sterilizer, and the hot item is unloaded and passed to the sterile field within minutes.

Ambulatory surgery center or office-based surgical suite: after cases, the assistant hand-cleans and inspects instruments, pouches or wraps them, loads a tabletop/small steam sterilizer (e.g., Midmark, Tuttnauer), selects and runs the cycle, then unloads, cools, and stores the packs.

Hospital sterile processing department: wrapped trays and rigid containers are loaded onto sterilizer shelf racks/batch carts, a large steam sterilizer cycle is run, the load is unloaded and cooled, and chemical indicators and load records are checked before release to the sterile store.

Low-temperature sterilization of heat-sensitive items (camera heads, scopes, robotic accessories): items are placed in the H2O2 plasma/VHP chamber trays, a cassette is loaded, the cycle is selected and run, and the load is unloaded and released.

Sterilizer quality control and documentation: assembling and placing a biological-indicator challenge pack or Bowie-Dick pack in the load, running the test cycle, retrieving, activating and incubating the BI vial in an auto-reader, reading the result, and logging cycle parameters and load contents.

Operating the upstream cleaning/disinfection equipment: loading instrument racks into an ultrasonic cleaner and washer-disinfector in the decontamination area, selecting and starting the correct cycle, and unloading to the clean side.

sources.system: Belimed/SteelcoBelimed TS MST-V automatic loading-unloading unit with MST-V steam sterilizer
sources.title: TS MST-V - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: Commercial sterilizer automation loads the sterilizer and starts the sterilization cycle with no operator input once a standardized batch cart is docked, and unloads it afterwards; batch cart positions are tracked by sensors throughout.

sources.system: Getinge Automatiq (Loaders, Envoy mobile robot, Depot, Hub)
sources.title: Getinge transforms sterile reprocessing with Automatiq - a full range of logistic automation modules
sources.claim: Getinge launched a commercial CSSD automation family in 2025 comprising machine-side loaders for its washer-disinfector and steam sterilizer, a self-navigating mobile robot that moves instruments between workstations, and orchestration/traceability software.
sources.transferJustification: Covers chamber loading/unloading and cycle handling for both washer-disinfector and steam sterilizer chambers; the same machine-tending action (insert fixtured rack into a chamber, run cycle, extract) transfers to other chamber sterilizers such as low-temperature H2O2 units, which use comparable trays and load weights.

sources.system: Steelco M-ATS Self-Driving Robot Transfer System
sources.title: M-ATS Self-Driving Robot Transfer System - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: A commercially offered self-driving robot moves washing loads and sterilization containers between automatic loading trolleys and machines in central sterile supply departments without direct human control, operating safely around people.

sources.system: Getinge Air Glide System with 86-series (S-8668T) Washer-Disinfector
sources.title: Getinge launches S-8668T Washer-Disinfector
sources.claim: Washer-disinfectors are sold with an automatic loading and unloading ... that identifies the load from a barcode on the wash ... starts the correct cleaning/disinfection program by itself.

sources.system: Gibotech Automated Central Sterile Supply Department
sources.title: Automated Central Sterile Supply Department - Gibotech
sources.claim: Automated sterilization centrals built from robot arms, mobile robots and conveyor systems have been installed in working hospitals since 2011, sited in basements where staff are not present, and automatically sterilize the hospital's instruments with full traceability.

sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: A robotic arm with computer vision autonomously assembled a minor surgical tray during a pilot inside a hospital sterile processing department, but the technician still inspects instruments and the system does not run the sterilizers.
sources.transferJustification: Instrument tray assembly is the SPD step adjacent to sterilizer loading; it shows the current frontier for robot manipulation of surgical instruments in a hospital SPD — a fixed workcell handling presented instruments, still partial and technician-supervised — which bounds what can be claimed for un-fixtured (E2) sterilizer operation.

sources.system: Copan WASPLab / BD Kiestra Total Lab Automation
sources.date: 2023 review article; systems in hospital use since ~2017
sources.title: Understanding Laboratory Automation in Clinical Microbiology
sources.claim: Total laboratory automation systems in hospital microbiology labs autonomously convey specimen plates into incubators and digitally image and read them, handling small vials/plates and reading growth results without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Biological-indicator quality control requires the same class of actions as automated microbiology: handling small sealed vials/plates, placing them into a controlled incubator, and reading the growth/fluorescence result — comparable object size, precision and machine-fed track environment.

tasks.label: Clamp, ligate, or cauterize blood vessels to control bleeding during surgical entry, using hemostatic clamps, suture ligatures, or electrocautery equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open abdominal/pelvic entry (laparotomy, hernia repair, cesarean section) in a hospital OR: as the surgeon incises skin, fat and fascia, the assistant grasps spurting or oozing subcutaneous/fascial bleeders with hemostats, 'buzzes' them with the monopolar Bovie, and places suture ligatures on larger vessels while the field is partly obscured by blood, retraction and drapes.

Orthopedic, spine or trauma exposure: assistant cauterizes muscle and perforator bleeders in a deep, narrow retracted exposure, applies bone wax and clamps/ligates larger vessels at the fascia and periosteum, working around retractors, irrigation and the operating surgeon's hands.

Cardiothoracic/vascular case: hemostasis at sternotomy edges (cautery plus bone wax) and endoscopic or open saphenous-vein/radial-artery conduit harvest, where the assistant clips or ties many side branches along the vessel and divides them without avulsing the conduit.

Laparoscopic or robot-assisted case: with the target vessel already dissected and exposed on camera (e.g., cystic artery, gastric or splenic branch), the assistant applies clips or a bipolar/ultrasonic vessel sealer to the discrete named vessel and divides it.

Laparoscopic or robot-assisted case: controlling unexpected bleeding during access - port-site/epigastric vessel bleeding from a trocar, adhesiolysis oozing, or a slipped clip - requiring the assistant to suction, find the source in a blood-filled field, and clamp, cauterize or suture-ligate it under time pressure.

Ambulatory surgery center / minor procedure (ENT, plastics, podiatry, dermatologic excision, hand surgery): quick pinpoint cautery of small dermal and subcutaneous bleeders at the incision, occasional fine tie or clamp, with local anesthesia and a small superficial field.

sources.title: SRT-H: A Hierarchical Framework for Autonomous Surgery via Language-Conditioned Imitation Learning (project page, Science Robotics 2025)
sources.claim: SRT-H autonomously executed clipping and cutting of the ... during ex vivo porcine cholecystectomy on a da Vinci research platform, with 100% success over 8 gallbladders and no human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clip-ligation and division of the cystic duct and ... is the same act as ligating a vessel to prevent bleeding, with comparable instruments (clip applier, scissors) and millimeter precision; transfer is limited because the ex vivo tissue is not perfused, so no active bleeding is present.

sources.system: CUHK surgical embodied intelligence framework on the Sentire Surgical System
sources.developer: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CU Medicine / Faculty of Engineering, Multi-Scale Medical Robotics Center)
sources.title: CUHK's newly-created embodied intelligence platform successfully completes the world's first multi-task surgical automation tests on a live animal
sources.claim: A CUHK embodied-AI framework integrated with the Sentire surgical system performed autonomous blood vessel clipping, tissue retraction and gauze picking in a live animal in a pre-clinical hybrid operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant sub-act (clipping a vessel in vivo); transfer is limited because the demonstration is a researcher-configured, robot-docked porcine setup performing individual tasks, with no reported handling of active bleeding or clinical-grade reliability data.

sources.system: Autonomous robotic suction for hemostasis (da Vinci Research Kit)
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Richter et al.), IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics
sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Suction to Clear the Surgical Field for Hemostasis Using Image-Based Blood Flow Detection
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed autonomous-surgery work states that automation had not been applied to hemostasis; its contribution automated only suction to clear blood from the field, evaluated on tissue in a laboratory dVRK setup.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (hemostasis): establishes that the identify-and-treat-a-bleeder loop has been automated only as far as suctioning blood, not clamping, ligating or cauterizing the bleeding vessel.

sources.title: Interview with Axel Krieger and Justin Opfermann: autonomous robotic laparoscopic surgery for intestinal anastomosis (Robohub / Science Robotics)
sources.claim: STAR performed supervised-autonomous laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis in four live pigs, using fluorescent tissue markers in a laboratory animal-surgery setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous suturing of living soft tissue shows needle and suture manipulation in vivo, but on marked, presented tissue in a planned anastomosis, not detection and ligation of bleeding vessels.

tasks.label: Prepare and apply sterile wound dressings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End of a laparoscopic or minor open case in a hospital OR or ambulatory surgery center: assistant cleans prep/blood from the skin, applies Steri-Strips or reinforces skin closure, then opens a sterile adhesive island dressing (Tegaderm/Primapore) and applies it over each small closed incision or port site while maintaining sterile technique.

Larger closed incision on trunk or extremity (laparotomy, C-section, joint arthroplasty): select and cut sterile gauze/ABD pads to size, layer them over the incision, secure with tape or adhesive dressing conforming to a curved body surface, and dress around exiting drains with slit drain sponges.

Specialty dressings: incisional negative-pressure wound therapy (Prevena/V.A.C.) sized and sealed airtight, sterile packing of open or contaminated wounds, tie-over bolster dressings for skin grafts, or burn dressings — requiring exact sizing, seal integrity and strict sterile handling.

Orthopedic bulky dressing and post-op immobilization: sterile gauze over the incision, then cast padding, ACE/compression wrap applied at controlled tension, and a plaster or fiberglass splint molded over the surgical site on a limb held by another team member.

Awkward or delicate anatomic sites: eye pad and rigid shield after ophthalmic surgery, mastoid/head wrap, nasal drip pad, neck or tracheostomy dressing, perineal or facial dressings — small fields, sharply contoured surfaces, little tolerance for misplaced adhesive.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling framework for robotic wound redressing (Liang et al.)
sources.developer: University of California San Diego / Cornell University
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: State-of-the-art research robots automate only isolated subtasks of wound redressing — initiating tape detachment and placing tape on anatomical phantom geometries in a lab workspace; tape grasping is still done manually or by teleoperation, tape preparation (cutting/orienting) is unsolved, and coverage was incomplete on curved sites.
sources.transferJustification: Chronic-wound redressing is the closest published robotic analogue to preparing and applying a sterile dressing: same deformable adhesive materials and skin contact. Its explicit remaining gaps (grasping, cutting, incomplete coverage, no sterile technique) show the surgical dressing task is not completed by any system.

sources.title: AutoPeel: Adhesion-aware Safe Peeling Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Wound Care
sources.claim: The first robotic system for ... performs autonomous peeling trajectories, validated on synthetic skin phantoms and real ... — removal only, not preparation or application of a new sterile dressing.
sources.transferJustification: Dressing removal is the inverse half of a dressing change on the same materials and skin; that removal was only first demonstrated as a research prototype in 2024 indicates no system performs the full prepare-and-apply sterile dressing task.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help (ScienceDaily)
sources.claim: Autonomous surgical robotics has reached supervised autonomous soft-tissue suturing in live animals in a research operating room, but is confined to needle and thread manipulation on tissue; no dressing preparation or application is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous intestinal anastomosis. It shows autonomy on tissue in a controlled surgical setting, but rigid needle driving under a fixed laparoscopic view does not transfer to opening sterile packaging, cutting gauze and conforming adhesive dressings to external skin, so it cannot substantiate this task.

sources.developer: Research consortium publishing in Communications Medicine (Nature)
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic assistance inside the operating room is limited to anticipating and handing over surgical instruments (about 71.5% anticipation accuracy in a research system); no patient-contact dressing application is included.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile-field instrument handling by a robot in the OR. It bounds what OR robots do today — passing rigid instruments — and demonstrates no handling of sterile dressing packages, gauze or adhesives on a patient, so it cannot substantiate this task.

tasks.label: Assess skin integrity or other body conditions upon completion of the procedure to determine if damage has occurred from body positioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine 1–2 hour supine case in a hospital OR (lap chole, hernia, breast, arthroscopy). After closure, the surgical assistant removes drapes, checks the electrosurgical dispersive pad site, arms/armboards and IV sites, safety-strap area, occiput, elbows and heels, blanch-tests any redness, and reports/documents findings before transfer to the gurney.

Long (3+ hour) case in a non-supine position — prone spine on a Wilson/Jackson frame, lateral hip or thoracotomy, lithotomy, or steep Trendelenburg robotic pelvic case. Positioning devices, gel rolls, stirrups and head cradle are removed; assistant inspects dependent surfaces (face and eyes, chest/breasts, iliac crests, genitals, knees, peroneal/ulnar nerve areas), palpates for induration or swelling, and helps log-roll the anesthetized patient to view the dorsal surface.

High-risk patient (elderly, obese, diabetic, poor perfusion, fragile skin, on vasopressors) in a hospital OR: meticulous head-to-toe check against the documented pre-op baseline, distinguishing blanchable erythema from deep-tissue injury or thermal/chemical burn, escalating findings to the surgeon and circulating nurse and initiating wound-care documentation.

Ambulatory surgery center with fast turnover and a small team: abbreviated but complete skin/positioning check performed quickly around lines and dressings while the patient is being moved to the stretcher, sometimes with the patient emerging from anesthesia and moving.

Emergency, trauma, or hybrid-room case with unplanned intraoperative repositioning: the check is done amid ongoing resuscitation, with multiple lines, drains, traction devices, blood and prep solution on the skin, and an unstable patient who cannot be fully turned.

sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system
sources.claim: UltraBot is a fully autonomous robot that scans a human neck with an ultrasound probe at expert-level quality, i.e. a robot making controlled physical contact with a live patient's body and interpreting the result — the nearest demonstrated analogue to robotic bedside patient examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic ultrasound examination of a human. It is the closest evidence for a robot physically examining a patient, but it covers one small anatomical region with a probe on a cooperative, unclothed, seated/supine subject; it does not remove drapes or positioning devices, cannot reposition an anesthetized patient, and performs no skin-integrity or pressure/thermal injury judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous robot-driven chronic wound 3D reconstruction and analysis system
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Robotics, MDPI)
sources.title: Autonomous Robot-Driven Chronic Wound 3D Reconstruction and Analysis System
sources.claim: A research robot arm with a 3D scanner autonomously reconstructs and measures chronic wounds presented to it, but it measures already-identified wound sites in a laboratory setup rather than searching a whole anesthetized body for new positioning damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wound documentation. Transfer is limited: the robot scans an exposed, known wound region on a stationary subject using a preprogrammed camera path; it does not undrape a patient, inspect occluded dependent surfaces, palpate, blanch-test erythema, or render the clinical determination the post-operative skin assessment requires.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital collaboration
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot has been operated inside a hospital imaging department on patients, showing that autonomous patient-contact robots exist in E2 clinical settings — but only for probe scanning of a defined body region, not for whole-body post-operative inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic sonography on patients in a hospital. It establishes only that a robot can contact a cooperative patient's abdomen in a clinical room; it does not establish handling or turning of an anesthetized patient, drape/device removal, or skin-damage assessment.

sources.title: RIKEN's ROBEAR robot assists nurses when caring for their patients
sources.claim: Robotic patient lifting and turning — a prerequisite for inspecting dependent skin surfaces — exists only as operator-guided research prototypes, not as an autonomous or commercially deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic patient handling. Cited as the state of the art for moving a human body; it is a caregiver-guided experimental prototype, so it cannot support autonomous log-rolling or limb lifting needed to view dependent skin surfaces after surgery.

tasks.label: Apply sutures, staples, clips, or other materials to close skin, facia, or subcutaneous wound layers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR / ambulatory surgery center: closing the skin of a straightforward open incision (general surgery, orthopedics, C-section) after the surgeon finishes - running subcuticular absorbable suture or a row of skin staples along a clean linear incision on a draped, prepped patient, under surgeon supervision and OR time pressure.

Open abdominal/orthopedic case: closing deep layers - fascia with heavy running or interrupted sutures under tension, then subcutaneous/dermal layers - on live, bleeding, ventilator-moving tissue, judging bite size, spacing and tension per the surgeon's technique preferences.

Laparoscopic/robotic case: closing port sites - fascial closure of 10-12 mm trocar defects deep in subcutaneous fat (suture passer or needle driver), then skin closure with subcuticular suture, adhesive strips or staples; small, deep, poorly exposed openings.

Cosmetically sensitive closure (plastic surgery, facial, pediatric, breast): fine interrupted dermal and subcuticular sutures with eversion, precise edge alignment and buried knots to a cosmetic standard the attending accepts.

Complicated closures: obese or edematous patients with thick fatty layers, contaminated/irregular or traumatic wounds, oozing fields, retention sutures, closure around drains, or sternal closure with wires/clips after cardiac surgery.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: STAR autonomously performed laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis - a running suture line closing tissue - in four live pigs, with results reported better than surgeons performing the same procedure; done in an animal-research surgical setup with a custom 3D endoscope and NIR markers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intestinal anastomosis is suture closure of a soft-tissue defect with a running suture line, requiring the same needle driving, spacing and tension control on comparably deformable living tissue as fascial or skin closure.

sources.title: Vaginal Cuff Closure With Dual-Arm Robot and Near-Infrared Fluorescent Sutures | IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: A dual-arm STAR autonomously performed vaginal cuff closure (suture closure of a tissue layer) on ex vivo porcine tissue, outperforming human surgeons on all but one metric, and completed a cuff closure in an in vivo porcine experiment; it relies on NIR fluorescent sutures/markers delimiting the task in a lab surgical setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cuff closure is closure of a tissue layer with a suture line - the same operation an assistant performs on fascia and subcutaneous layers - with comparable objects (soft tissue, curved needle, suture) and precision.

sources.system: Task-autonomous incision stapling/staple-removal robot (Wang et al., IEEE RA-L 7(2))
sources.developer: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications / Soochow University et al.
sources.title: Task Autonomous Medical Robot for Both Incision Stapling and Staples Removal
sources.claim: A task-autonomous medical robot detected an incision with binocular vision, planned staple positions and pressed skin staples into a simulated wounded-skin phantom, then removed them, without human intervention, on a bench with the phantom presented to the manipulator.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy) on da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: Johns Hopkins teaches robot to perform a gallbladder removal on a realistic patient | The Robot Report
sources.claim: SRT-H autonomously executed a 17-step cholecystectomy phase on ex vivo pig gallbladders in the lab, including identifying ducts and arteries and placing surgical clips, with a 100% success rate across ... specimens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous placement of clips on tissue is the 'apply clips' element of this task, on comparable soft tissue at comparable precision, though on ex vivo organs rather than a skin wound.

sources.system: Sentire Endoscopic Surgical System with VPPV embodied-intelligence framework
sources.developer: Cornerstone Robotics / Chinese University of Hong Kong
sources.title: Cornerstone Robotics Completes World's First Clinical Validation of Autonomous Surgery Performed by Robot-Assisted Surgery
sources.claim: CUHK/Cornerstone Robotics' embodied-intelligence platform on the Sentire endoscopic system autonomously executed tasks including blood-vessel clipping on ex vivo porcine tissue and in a live ~30 kg pig, under a supervised-autonomy safety mode in an animal-research setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous clip application to vessels in living tissue; shows clip placement transfers from bench to live animal tissue, but only in an animal lab under human supervision.

sources.title: Autonomous Surgical Robots Enhance Precision in the OR - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: STAR's autonomous suturing depends on a purpose-built presentation of the tissue - the earlier system could suture intestine only when the bowel was exteriorized through a skin incision - and on markers plus custom 3D imaging in a research setting; no autonomous closure on human patients is reported.

tasks.label: Assist in the insertion, positioning, or suturing of closed-wound drainage systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Open or laparoscopic general/abdominal case (e.g., colectomy, hernia, hepatobiliary) in a hospital OR: at closure the assistant makes/receives a separate stab incision, passes a Jackson-Pratt drain with a trocar or clamp, positions the fenestrated tip in the correct anatomic space alongside the anastomosis or resection bed under the surgeon's direction, anchors it to skin with a purse-string/roman-sandal suture, connects and compresses the bulb to confirm suction, and confirms no kinking with the patient draped and the field bloody.

Breast/plastic reconstructive case (mastectomy, abdominoplasty, flap reconstruction) in a hospital OR or ASC: the assistant tunnels one to three soft silicone flat drains subcutaneously into flap pockets through separate lateral stab incisions, positions them along dependent portions of the dissected pocket without kinking or contacting the pedicle, secures each with a skin anchoring suture, and connects closed-suction bulbs before layered closure.

Orthopedic or spine case (total joint arthroplasty, spinal fusion) in a hospital OR: the assistant places a Hemovac or similar deep drain in the joint capsule or paraspinal wound bed while retracting, brings the tubing out through a skin exit site, secures it with suture, connects to the evacuator, activates suction, and applies dressings, working amid irrigation fluid, bone debris, and heavy retraction.

Cardiothoracic or trauma case: the assistant assists in placing mediastinal/pleural chest drains into the thoracic cavity, positions them apically or posteriorly per the surgeon, secures with heavy horizontal-mattress or purse-string sutures to skin, connects the tubing to a closed water-seal/suction drainage unit, and confirms tidaling/air-leak status before transfer.

Robotic-assisted (da Vinci) or fully laparoscopic urologic/gynecologic case: the bedside assistant introduces a drain through an assistant port, hands the tip to the console surgeon's instruments for intracorporeal positioning near the anastomosis, withdraws slack, secures the tubing at the skin with suture, and attaches the closed-suction reservoir after desufflation.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot ... supervised-autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis (soft-tissue suturing) in live pigs — the most advanced autonomous soft-tissue suturing demonstrated — but only in preclinical animal research with marker-guided vision, on bowel, not on drain placement or drain anchoring in human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing (bowel anastomosis). It bears on the suturing component of drain securement, but transfer fails: STAR sutures a fixtured, marker-tagged bowel segment in an animal lab and has never manipulated a flexible drain tube, tunneled it through tissue, positioned it in a wound cavity, or anchored it to skin.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning - PubMed
sources.claim: SRT-H, a language-conditioned imitation-learning policy on a da Vinci Research Kit, autonomously executed the dissection/clipping steps of cholecystectomy, but only on ex vivo (excised) porcine gallbladders in a laboratory bench setup — no live patient, no drain handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of surgical steps (dissection, clip application) on soft tissue. It marks the frontier of surgical autonomy, but is confined to ex vivo tissue on a bench, does not include drain insertion, positioning, or suture anchoring, and has no live-patient validation.

sources.title: Surgeons Use Teleoperated Humanoid Robots to Perform Live Surgery – a World First
sources.claim: The first use of humanoid robots in a surgical first-assistant role was reported in July 2026 by UC San Diego, and the robots were teleoperated by surgeons during preclinical animal procedures, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: robots acting as surgical first assistants. It cannot support a positive judgment because the robots were continuously teleoperated by human surgeons and the work was preclinical.

sources.title: XACT Robotics nets FDA clearance for 2nd-generation needle surgery system | Fierce Biotech
sources.claim: XACT Robotics' ACE system is FDA-cleared for hands-free CT-guided percutaneous needle/probe insertion and steering, including drainage procedures, in an interventional radiology suite; it inserts a rigid needle along a planned trajectory and does not place, position, or suture a closed-wound surgical drainage system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-driven insertion of a percutaneous drainage catheter. Transfer fails: the system inserts a rigid needle/introducer along a physician-planned CT trajectory in a radiology suite, and performs none of the intraoperative steps of this task — tunneling a soft drain into an open wound bed, positioning it in a cavity, anchoring it with sutures, or establishing closed suction.

tasks.label: Adjust and maintain operating room temperature, humidity, or lighting, according to surgeon's specifications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-procedure adjustment of overhead surgical light heads in a hospital OR: on the surgeon's verbal request ('a little more to the left', 'tighten the field', 'brighter'), the scrubbed assistant grabs the sterile handle and re-aims/refocuses one or two ceiling-suspended lightheads onto a moving, deep surgical field while avoiding heads, arms, drapes, booms, and the sterile field. Happens repeatedly through the case.

Pre-incision setup of the surgical lighting per the surgeon's preference card: swinging lightheads over the table after draping, setting field diameter, intensity and color temperature, checking for shadowing with the team in position, and confirming the surgeon accepts the illumination.

Adjusting ambient/room lighting levels for the case phase: dimming or extinguishing overhead room lights for laparoscopic/endoscopic or microscope portions and bringing them back up for open work, counts, and closing, using wall dimmers or the integrated-OR touch panel.

Setting the OR temperature and humidity before the case to the surgeon's/patient's requirement (e.g., cool 62-65 F for a long ortho case in exhaust suits, 75-80 F for a pediatric, burn, or trauma patient), entering the setpoint on the wall thermostat/OR control panel and confirming the room reaches it before incision.

Mid-case environmental changes and monitoring: surgeon or anesthesia asks for the room to be warmed or cooled after prep, assistant changes the setpoint, watches the temperature/humidity readout, and escalates to facilities/biomed if humidity or temperature drifts out of the compliant range.

Supplemental and task lighting: connecting and adjusting a fiber-optic headlight and light-source console for the surgeon, handling the sterile light cable, or wheeling in and aiming a portable exam/satellite light or in-light camera on request.

sources.system: Autonomous module-based surgical lighting system (Mühlenbrock et al., Univ. Bremen / Pius-Hospital Oldenburg, Dr. Mach consortium)
sources.developer: University of Bremen CGVR with University of Oldenburg / Pius-Hospital and Dr. Mach GmbH
sources.date: 2024-10 (ACM Trans. Comput. Healthcare, vol 6 issue 1, Jan 2025)
sources.title: A Novel, Autonomous, Module-Based Surgical Lighting System | ACM Transactions on Computing for Healthcare
sources.claim: A real prototype surgical lighting system of 56 swiveling, ceiling-mounted light modules with three depth sensors autonomously controls module intensity and orientation to keep the surgical site illuminated and shadow-free; it outperformed conventional OR lights in measurements and in a surgeon user study for abdominal surgery.

sources.system: Touch-free (speech + gesture) control of the smart ceiling surgical lighting system
sources.title: Using Gesture and Speech to Control Surgical Lighting Systems: Mixed Methods Study — JMIR Human Factors
sources.claim: The same motorized ceiling light modules (7x8 grid, two motors per module, central computer control, three Kinect sensors for shadow avoidance) were driven by speech and gesture commands in a living-laboratory study with 12 surgeons and surgical assistants, i.e. the machine executed the surgeon's spoken lighting specification (switch, position, intensity, field size).

sources.system: Intelligent OT lighting (Smart-OT project, consortium led by Dr. Mach GmbH)
sources.developer: University of Bremen / University of Oldenburg / Pius-Hospital / KIZMO / Dr. Mach
sources.title: Surgery: Intelligent OT Lighting - Universität Bremen
sources.claim: The intelligent OT lighting system is developed and evaluated in a purpose-built Living Lab where simulated surgeries are carried out; it is a research/industry project, not a clinically installed product.

sources.developer: Gharghabi et al. (Iran Univ. of Science and Technology, WWL NHS Trust)
sources.title: Machine Vision-Based Surgical Lighting System: Design and Implementation (arXiv 2510.17287)
sources.claim: A machine-vision surgical lighting prototype detects a marker above the target surgical site with YOLOv11 and automatically aims a high-power LED at it using two servomotors on a pan-tilt bracket, replacing manual light adjustment on a bench setup.

sources.system: Green Surgical Block 4.0 — MYSPHERA RTLS-driven automatic OT climate and lighting control at Vall d'Hebron University Hospital
sources.developer: Vall d'Hebron University Hospital with MYSPHERA SL
sources.date: 2023-03 (Future Healthcare Journal; system running ~4 years prior)
sources.title: The Green Surgical Block 4.0: Automation of the operating theatre's climate conditions through a real-time patient-flow solution
sources.claim: In a 19-theatre hospital surgical block, an installed RTLS-driven building-control system automatically switches each operating theatre's HVAC and perimeter lighting between modes (perimeter lighting 100/60/10%, temperature held at 21°C ±0.5°C, ventilation high/low) according to real-time patient flow, without staff intervention; staff can also set perimeter light in 20% steps and temperature 19-23°C from a theatre screen that displays humidity and pressure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated maintenance of OT temperature, humidity and perimeter lighting. The actuation (HVAC dampers/coils/humidifiers and dimmable room luminaires) is machine-controlled equipment physically changing the same room variables the assistant adjusts, in real hospital ORs.

sources.system: Maquet PowerLED II surgical light with Automated Illumination Management (AIM)
sources.title: Getinge announces the US launch of Maquet PowerLED II - BioSpace
sources.claim: A commercially marketed surgical light installed in general and hybrid ORs automatically increases light output when staff partially block the light path, and an optional Luminance Management Device automatically regulates illumination reaching the surgeon's eyes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic maintenance of illumination on the surgical field. It shows machine-controlled lighting adjustment running inside real ORs, but it compensates intensity only and does not re-aim the lighthead.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals — The Robot Report
sources.claim: A single-arm mobile manipulator works 24/7 in US hospitals, autonomously navigating corridors and using its arm to open doors and push elevator buttons; it has completed over 110,000 autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pressing wall-mounted buttons and operating fixed building interfaces inside an institution-controlled hospital. Comparable objects (button/keypad), comparable precision (centimetre-level press), same facility type as an OR wall thermostat or light-dimmer panel.

tasks.label: Assist in applying casts, splints, braces, or similar devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the OR after fracture fixation (ORIF): surgical assistant holds the anesthetized limb in the reduced position and/or applies stockinette, cast padding, and a plaster or fiberglass posterior/sugar-tong splint slab, molds it three-point while the surgeon confirms reduction under fluoroscopy, then secures with elastic bandage.

Circumferential cast application under anesthesia (short arm/leg, long leg, or pediatric hip spica): wrapping padding and casting tape at even tension over bony prominences, molding while curing, trimming edges, and bivalving or windowing with a cast saw.

End-of-case fitting of prefabricated devices in OR/PACU: knee immobilizer, hinged ROM brace, CAM walker boot, shoulder sling/abduction pillow, cervical collar — positioning the device on a sedated or drowsy patient, adjusting hinge stops and straps to fit.

Applying bulky soft compressive dressings over the surgical site (Jones dressing, ABD pads, Ace wrap) prior to or in place of a splint, avoiding pressure points and maintaining sterility of the incision area.

Clinic, ED, or post-op check setting: assisting with cast removal by saw and re-application, splint or brace changes, wound check with re-dressing, adjusting a halo vest or spinal orthosis on an awake, sometimes uncooperative or painful patient.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing (single-arm manipulator, lab)
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robot-assisted dressing research can autonomously pull a long-sleeve garment onto a seated human participant's arm in a university lab, but this is a research demonstration on everyday garments, not application of casts, splints, braces or compressive dressings on surgical patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting a garment sleeve onto a human arm — the closest published robotic capability to placing a device or wrap on a patient's limb. It does not transfer: casting/splinting requires tensioned circumferential wrapping of padding, three-point molding of curing fiberglass to hold a fracture reduction, cast-saw trimming, and strap fitting on an anesthetized surgical limb, none of which is demonstrated; the demo is lab-only with healthy seated volunteers.

sources.system: Autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Robotic wound-care research as of late 2025 is still working on isolated subtasks such as detaching and placing adhesive tape; clinical wound dressing remains an entirely manual, clinician-performed process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying and securing dressings/tape on a patient's body, which overlaps the soft-dressing portion of this task. Transfer fails: only sub-steps (tape detachment and placement) are automated in a lab, with the surrounding redressing workflow and any splint/brace application still manual.

sources.title: Robot performs first laparoscopic surgery without human help
sources.claim: Autonomous surgical robotics that touches patients is limited to narrow in-vivo tasks such as bowel anastomosis suturing in animal models; no system performs the assistive limb-immobilization work of casting, splinting, or bracing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic performance of an operative step in a surgical setting. It establishes the frontier of clinical robot autonomy (single narrow suturing task, animal model, research setting) and shows nothing covering external limb immobilization or device fitting.

tasks.label: Remove patient hair or disinfect incision sites to prepare patient for surgery.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard single-field antiseptic prep of an anesthetized patient positioned supine or prone in the OR: after positioning and before draping, the assistant opens the sterile prep tray, applies chlorhexidine-alcohol or povidone applicators with back-and-forth/concentric strokes over a wide accessible flat field (abdomen, chest, flank, back, thigh), keeps solution from pooling under the patient, and lets it dry before drape application.

Orthopedic extremity prep: the arm or leg is elevated or held in a limb positioner/stirrup and prepped circumferentially from fingers/toes proximally (knee, shoulder, hand, foot, ankle cases), including web spaces, heel and axilla, with the holding point re-prepped or handed off, then the limb is passed into a stockinette/drape.

Preoperative hair removal over an accessible flat region — abdomen, chest, back, or scalp for craniotomy — using a single-use vacuum-assisted surgical clipper immediately before prep, capturing loose hair so none contaminates the field, without nicking skin.

Perineal/genital-region work in lithotomy or frog-leg position: clipping groin, scrotal, axillary or fold hair, and vaginal/rectal/perineal antiseptic prep (including combined abdominal-plus-vaginal preps for GYN and urology cases), where mucosa, folds, catheters and 'dirty-last' sequencing must be managed.

Head, face, eye, ear or neck prep with the airway secured: prepping around endotracheal tube, eyes (shielding or ophthalmic-grade prep), ear canal, tracheostomy or head-holder pins, avoiding antiseptic runoff into eyes/ears, for ENT, ophthalmic, neuro and facial plastics cases.

Complex, multi-region or emergent prep: cardiac/vascular preps running chin-to-toes with both groins, trauma and emergency cases with dirt, blood, wounds, stomas or existing lines and monitors in the field, obese or contractured patients, and awake patients under regional or local anesthesia in the holding area or OR.

sources.system: RABBIT (Cornell EmPRISE Lab, Kinova arm bed-bathing system)
sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance (ACM/IEEE HRI 2024)
sources.claim: RABBIT is a robot-assisted bed bathing system that autonomously washes, rinses and dries bare human skin on a person lying on a bed, using RGB/thermal perception of soapy and wet skin and compliant force control — the closest demonstrated analogue to wiping antiseptic over a defined skin field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robot-assisted bed bathing. Same object (bare human skin on a supine person), same class of motion (compliant liquid application and wiping over soft, curved tissue), and comparable cm-scale coverage tolerance to painting an antiseptic field; performed at a fixed, purpose-built robot workstation, matching the E1 counterfactual for a prep.

sources.system: SkinGrip adaptive soft manipulator (whole-limb bed bathing)
sources.title: SkinGrip: An Adaptive Soft Robotic Manipulator with Capacitive Sensing for Whole-Limb Bed Bathing Assistance (arXiv)
sources.claim: SkinGrip is a soft robotic end effector with capacitive servoing that detects contact around the circumference of a ... and traverses the limb to perform bed bathing; it was evaluated in a bathing study with human participants of varying limb sizes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = whole-limb bed bathing. It is circumferential wet cleaning of a live human arm/leg — the same geometry and contact problem as a circumferential extremity surgical prep — on a limb presented passively in a fixed robot workspace, matching the E1 counterfactual (limb in a positioner).

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M in Strategic Funding, Announces US Expansion With Equinox (Athletech News)
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage tables are commercially deployed in gyms and hotels, where two robot arms 3D-scan a client's body and apply controlled pressure across bare skin over body contours without an operator, showing mature, at-scale force-controlled contact with human bodies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic massage. It demonstrates commercial-grade autonomous, force-regulated tool/end-effector coverage of a whole human body's contours from a 3D scan, the motion-and-safety half of applying prep solution — but always with the person presented in a fixed pose on the machine's own table (a machine-centric station).

sources.title: The current state of robotics in total knee arthroplasty (EFORT Open Reviews)
sources.claim: THINK Surgical's TSolution One (ROBODOC) autonomously executes pre-planned bone cuts on a patient in the operating room, but only with the limb rigidly fixed to the robot and registered beforehand — i.e., clinical-grade autonomous work on patients today requires the patient be presented to the machine as a fixtured workpiece.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous robotic bone milling in the OR. Cited to establish the environment ceiling rather than the motion: the only autonomous robots working on patients in real ORs demand rigid fixation and pre-registration, so free-form work on an unfixtured patient in a live OR (E2) is not substantiated.

sources.system: ARTAS / ARTAS iX robotic hair restoration system
sources.title: A Comparative Study on the Application of Robotic Hair Restoration Technology Versus Traditional Follicular Unit Excision in Male Androgenetic Alopecia
sources.claim: The ARTAS robotic hair restoration system autonomously identifies and harvests hair follicles from a patient's scalp in a clinical procedure room, with the donor scalp held flat by a skin tensioner and the patient in a dedicated chair — an FDA-cleared instance of machine-controlled hair removal from a live patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic follicular unit excision. It is machine-controlled removal of hair from a patient's skin at far finer precision than a clipper pass, with vision-guided depth/force control and clinically accepted outcomes — but only over a flat scalp region immobilized in a tensioner fixture, i.e. an E1-style presentation.

sources.system: Autonomous beard shaving assistance robot (UR-10 + Kinect)
sources.developer: Ajani & Assal (Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology)
sources.title: Development of an autonomous robotic system for beard shaving assistance of disabled people based on an adaptive force tracking impedance control
sources.claim: The published autonomous beard-shaving robot (face detection, beard-region estimation, adaptive force-tracking impedance control on a UR-10) was validated only in simulation, so no system has been shown to shave or clip hair from a real human body over irregular regions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous shaving of a human face. Cited as a negative/limiting datapoint: it is simulation-only, so it cannot support positive judgments for hair removal over contoured or delicate regions (groin, face, folds).

tasks.label: Monitor patient intra-operative status, including patient position, vital signs, or volume and color of blood.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine general or ambulatory surgery (e.g., laparoscopic cholecystectomy, hernia repair, appendectomy) in a hospital OR or ASC: the assistant, scrubbed at the table, keeps an eye on the anesthesia monitor display (HR, BP, SpO2, EtCO2, temperature), watches the surgical field for oozing or color change of blood, tracks suction canister volume and sponge saturation, and periodically confirms the patient's arms, head, and pressure points remain safely positioned; abnormalities are called out to the surgeon and anesthesia provider.

Long orthopedic, spine, or neurosurgical case with position-sensitive risk (prone, lateral, beach-chair, steep positions, limb tourniquets): the assistant repeatedly checks that padding, limb alignment, eyes/face, and pressure points are undisturbed after table tilts or repositioning, notes tourniquet time and perfusion, and correlates observed field bleeding with the monitor's trend over several hours.

Major open high-blood-loss case (cardiac, vascular, hepatobiliary, obstetric hemorrhage, transplant): the assistant continuously judges rate, volume, and color of blood loss (bright arterial vs dark venous, canister volume net of irrigation, saturated laps), watches for hemodynamic deterioration on the monitor, and reports estimated blood loss and trends to the surgeon and anesthesia team in real time.

Emergency or trauma case with an unstable patient: rapidly changing vitals, transfusion in progress, alarms firing, crowded room and frequent team turnover; the assistant integrates monitor data, field appearance, and verbal reports, distinguishes artifact from true deterioration, and escalates immediately.

Robotic or minimally invasive case where the assistant is bedside rather than at the console: monitors insufflation-related changes in vitals, watches the endoscopic view and the patient's external position for arm/cart collisions and steep-Trendelenburg-related slippage, tracks small-volume suction canister blood, and relays findings to the console surgeon.

tasks.label: Discuss with surgeon the nature of the surgical procedure, including operative consent, methods of operative exposure, diagnostic or laboratory data, or patient-advanced directives or other needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Coordinate with anesthesia personnel to maintain patient temperature.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-incision setup in a hospital OR: after the patient is positioned on the table, the surgical assistant obtains and applies a forced-air warming blanket (underbody or upper-body) over/under the anesthetized patient, routes and connects the hose to the warming unit, checks that anesthesia's esophageal/skin core-temperature probe is in place, sets the unit's target, and confirms the plan verbally with the anesthesiologist/CRNA before draping.

Intraoperative maintenance during a 1-4 hour case: the assistant and anesthesia watch the continuously displayed core temperature and keep the patient at 36-37 C by raising or lowering the forced-air unit's output, switching on the in-line blood/fluid warmer, and turning warming down if the temperature drifts high; the warming devices are already applied and the patient is immobile on the table.

Warm irrigation and intraoperative coverings: at the surgeon's request the assistant obtains warmed saline from the circulator or warming cabinet, pours/lavages it into the body cavity at a safe temperature, packs warm moist laparotomy sponges, and re-covers exposed extremities, head or skin edges with warmed towels/blankets while keeping the sterile field intact.

Pre-induction and ambient measures: applying warmed cotton blankets from a blanket warmer to the patient in the holding area or on the OR table before induction, requesting or adjusting the OR thermostat (e.g., raising room temperature for pediatric, burn or trauma cases), and closing doors/limiting exposure, all coordinated verbally with anesthesia personnel.

Hyperthermia or crisis cooling: in a malignant-hyperthermia event, febrile sepsis case or an overheating pediatric patient, the assistant shuts off warming, helps apply ice packs to axillae and groin, pours cold irrigation into the cavity, assists with a cooling blanket, and works rapidly with anesthesia while the operation continues.

End of case and handoff: after dressings are applied, the assistant covers the patient with warmed blankets for transfer from table to bed, keeps the patient covered during transport to PACU, and reports the final temperature and warming measures used to anesthesia/PACU staff.

sources.system: Warm6200 IoT closed-loop patient warming system (Beijing Yingtai Nuo Medical Technology)
sources.developer: Beijing Yingtai Nuo Medical Technology Co., Ltd.
sources.title: Closed-loop temperature management with internet of things technology support in elderly laparoscopic rectal cancer surgery: A randomised controlled trial (PLOS One)
sources.claim: A commercial closed-loop patient warming system (Warm6200) autonomously adjusted heating power from a wireless core-temperature sensor to hold elderly surgical patients in a preset 36-37 C target range throughout laparoscopic rectal cancer surgery in a hospital operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the intraoperative monitor-and-adjust loop of this task: the machine reads core temperature and regulates the warming blanket output instead of a human coordinating adjustments with anesthesia.

sources.system: Intelligent closed-loop warming system (wireless sensors plus automated feedback-controlled warming unit)
sources.developer: Chinese manufacturer (Heilongjiang) evaluated by Beijing Tongren Hospital, Capital Medical University
sources.title: Efficacy of an Intelligent Closed-Loop Warming System in Preventing Perioperative Hypothermia and Improving Recovery in Video-Assisted Thoracoscopic Surgery: A Randomized Controlled Trial (TCRM)
sources.claim: A randomized trial in video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery used an automated feedback-controlled warming unit with wireless sensors that regulated a warming blanket, blood/fluid warmer and peripheral heating device to a 36.5-37.0 C target and stopped warming automatically when temperature exceeded the range.
sources.transferJustification: Same task content as the intraoperative instance: keeping an anesthetized surgical patient normothermic by automatic adjustment of warming devices, in a real operating room, replacing manual coordination of warmer settings.

sources.title: Arctic Sun 5000 - Intensive care patient temperature management system by BD (MedicalExpo)
sources.claim: The BD Arctic Sun 5000 is a commercially marketed hospital thermal regulating system that monitors patient temperature through a probe and automatically adjusts circulating water temperature in adhesive pads to hold a clinician-set target between 32 and 38.5 C.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the closed-loop maintenance portion of patient temperature control (warming or cooling to a target) in hospital settings once pads and probe are placed by staff.

sources.system: RoBE / Bodies Uncovered bedding-manipulation robots (Stretch/PR2-class mobile manipulators)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University / Georgia Tech (Puthuveetil, Kemp, Erickson)
sources.title: Robust Body Exposure (RoBE): A Graph-based Dynamics Modeling Approach to Manipulating Blankets over People (arXiv)
sources.claim: Research robots can manipulate real blankets over people lying in bed, uncovering targeted body parts while keeping the rest covered, validated in a laboratory human study with 12 participants; no comparable system applies warming devices to patients in an operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Closest demonstrated capability to draping warming blankets on a patient; it is a lab bed setup with a single plain blanket and no device hose, sterile field, lines or drapes, so it does not substantiate the OR blanket-application instances.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous hospital mobile manipulator, is deployed in more than 25 ... for non-patient-facing logistics such as supply, medication and lab-sample deliveries, having completed over a million autonomous deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the state of deployed hospital mobile manipulation is corridor logistics of packaged supplies, not patient-side handling of warm blankets, irrigation fluids or warming devices in a sterile OR.

tasks.label: Incise tissue layers in lower extremities to harvest veins.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elective/urgent CABG in a cardiac OR: endoscopic vein harvest (EVH) of the greater saphenous vein through a small knee/thigh incision using a hand-guided Vasoview/VirtuoSaph device — create the tunnel, dissect the vein circumferentially, seal and divide side branches, extract and prepare the conduit, close and dress the leg on a live anesthetized patient.

CABG where endoscopic harvest is unsuitable or fails: open or bridged 'skip-incision' saphenous harvest in obese, diabetic, varicose or scarred legs — longitudinal skin/subcutaneous incisions along thigh and calf, ligating tributaries with clips/ties, tunneling between skip incisions, layered closure with attention to wound-healing risk.

Emergency or complex cardiac case: unstable patient, redo sternotomy, intra-aortic balloon pump in one groin, prior harvest scarring, or need for extra conduit length down to the ankle — harvest performed fast, in parallel with the chest team, in variable anatomy and with bleeding/hemodynamic pressure.

Vascular surgery OR: harvesting the greater or small saphenous vein from the leg as autogenous conduit for femoropopliteal/distal bypass, infected-graft reconstruction, or dialysis access — often long segments, sometimes in ischemic or previously operated limbs.

Short supplemental harvest: taking an additional segment of saphenous or small saphenous vein (patch, extra graft, or vein cuff) through a limited incision at ankle or calf, including sizing, distension check, and closure.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy, on dVRK-Si hardware)
sources.title: Hierarchical Surgical Robot Transformer (SRT-H)
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue surgical robot demonstrated to date, SRT-H (Johns Hopkins), autonomously performed the steps of cholecystectomy, but only on excised (ex vivo) pig gallbladders in a laboratory, not on a live human limb.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of the art in autonomous soft-tissue dissection/clipping/cutting; it establishes the ceiling of autonomous soft-tissue surgery (bench-top excised organs) and therefore that no system autonomously harvests a saphenous vein from a live leg.

sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: STAR performed autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis on a live pig in a research laboratory with human supervision and tracking markers; no equivalent capability has been shown on human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous soft-tissue suturing) cited to bound autonomous capability: it is animal-model research, not human operative care, so it does not carry over to harvesting a conduit from a patient's leg.

sources.system: FDA-cleared surgical robot fleet (da Vinci, Mako, ROSA, ARTAS, etc.)
sources.title: Levels of autonomy in FDA-cleared surgical robots: a systematic review
sources.claim: A systematic review of all FDA-cleared surgical robots (2015-2023) found the overwhelming majority operate under continuous surgeon control (robot assistance), with only a small minority reaching conditional task autonomy in narrow, rigid-anatomy applications; none performs autonomous open or endoscopic vessel harvest.

sources.title: Robotic single-port femoral artery dissection and anastomosis with the da Vinci system: a cadaveric feasibility study
sources.claim: Robotic dissection in the lower extremity around the greater saphenous and femoral vessels has been shown only as a surgeon-teleoperated da Vinci procedure in cadavers, not autonomously and not as a completed vein harvest in a live patient.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published robotic work on the same anatomy (lower-extremity vessel dissection); it is fully teleoperated and cadaveric, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for this task.

sources.title: Vasoview Hemopro 2 Endoscopic Vessel Harvesting System - Getinge
sources.claim: Current endoscopic vessel harvesting is performed with a hand-held, surgeon/assistant-manipulated instrument, not a robot: the Vasoview Hemopro 2 system is an operator-guided endoscopic device for saphenous vein and radial artery harvest.

sources.system: ARTAS / ARTAS iX robotic hair restoration system
sources.title: ARTAS Robot Efficiently Harvests Follicular Units in Korean Patients
sources.claim: The ARTAS system autonomously makes punch incisions in skin and harvests follicular units in a clinic, i.e., machine-controlled skin incision and tissue harvesting exists commercially, but only for ~1 mm superficial grafts on a tensioned, fixtured scalp.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic skin incision and tissue harvest) considered for transfer, but it does not carry over: ARTAS punches 1 mm superficial follicles on a clamped flat scalp, whereas vein harvest requires deep layered incision, circumferential dissection of a 20-40 cm conduit, side-branch sealing, hemostasis and layered closure on a live limb.

tasks.label: Postoperatively inject a subcutaneous local anesthetic agent to reduce pain.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR or ASC, laparoscopic/robotic-assisted case (cholecystectomy, appendectomy, hysterectomy, prostatectomy): after fascia and skin closure the assistant infiltrates 3-5 port sites (5-12 mm) on the abdominal wall with 0.25-0.5% bupivacaine, aspirating before each injection, patient anesthetized, supine and draped, team working around the field.

Hospital OR, open abdominal or pelvic case (cesarean section, hernia repair, open colectomy): assistant infiltrates the subcutaneous layer along a 10-25 cm incision line with local anesthetic in a fan pattern at closure, staying within the surgeon's dose limit and avoiding intravascular injection.

Hospital OR, orthopedic or spine case (TKA, shoulder, laminectomy): patient in lateral, beach-chair or prone position with limb holders; assistant infiltrates dilute large-volume local anesthetic subcutaneously around the incision and drain sites at closure.

Ambulatory surgery center or office-based procedure room, minor case (breast lumpectomy, hand surgery, skin excision, ENT, plastics): assistant infiltrates a short wound with a few milliliters of local anesthetic at closure under fast turnover pressure.

Difficult case: morbidly obese patient, irregular or multiple wounds plus drain sites, head-and-neck or perineal field with restricted access and altered anatomy, or a dose-restricted patient where the surgeon directs on-the-fly changes to volume, concentration and plane of infiltration.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: Vitestro's Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device autonomously locates a vein with ultrasound/AI and inserts a needle percutaneously through human skin and subcutaneous tissue, achieving 95% first-stick success in a 609-participant pivotal trial, comparable to human phlebotomists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous percutaneous needle placement in a human. Venipuncture drives a hypodermic needle through skin into subcutaneous tissue to a sub-millimetre target and then handles fluid through it - the same objects (human skin/subcutis, hypodermic needle, metered fluid) and tighter precision than subcutaneous infiltration of local anesthetic. It operates with the patient's arm placed in a purpose-built cradle, i.e. the work brought to the machine (E1 presentation).

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness
sources.claim: The Vitestro autonomous venipuncture robot is CE-marked and has been placed in European laboratories and hospitals for routine patient blood collection since March 2025, after clinical validation in more than 4,000 individuals.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous needle insertion into a human); this item establishes that the capability is fielded at clinical quality rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.system: ARTAS / ARTAS iX robotic hair restoration system
sources.title: Robotic hair restoration - PubMed
sources.claim: The ARTAS robotic hair transplant system, FDA-cleared and used in hair-restoration clinics, images the patient's scalp and autonomously drives a needle/punch into skin and subcutis at hundreds to thousands of planned sites while the patient's skin is held by a tensioner fixture and a physician supervises.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated image-guided needle penetration of a patient's skin at many planned sites across a body region, with controlled depth and angle, on a live (locally anesthetized) human in a clinic, with the target area stabilized by a tensioner fixture. Objects (human skin/subcutaneous tissue, small-gauge needle), depth control and site planning are comparable to infiltrating anesthetic along a wound; precision required is higher.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy) on da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: Johns Hopkins teaches robot to perform a gallbladder removal on a realistic patient
sources.claim: The SRT-H system autonomously executed a lengthy multi-step phase of a cholecystectomy (clipping and cutting cystic duct and artery) on ex vivo porcine gallbladders with 100% task success, adapting to anatomical variation and blood-like dyes, with only occasional spoken corrections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument manipulation on soft tissue inside a surgical field. It shows a robot can perceive a wound/tissue scene and carry a multi-step manipulation to completion, but only on ex vivo tissue in a laboratory bench setup built around the robot, not in a live human OR.

sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: The STAR robot performed supervised-autonomous laparoscopic intestinal anastomosis suturing on live pigs, placing sutures in moving soft tissue with results comparable to or better than manual suturing, in a laboratory operating setup using tissue markers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle-and-tissue work (suturing) on live soft tissue in a surgical field. It substantiates needle handling in living tissue under machine control, but in a purpose-built animal-lab setup with fiducial markers and a predetermined plan - E1 conditions, not a live human OR.

tasks.label: Insert or remove urinary bladder catheters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Insert an indwelling Foley catheter in an anesthetized female patient in the OR before a gynecologic, colorectal, or long general-surgery case: position legs, perform sterile prep of the perineum, drape, identify the urethral meatus among variable anatomy, advance the lubricated catheter, confirm urine return, inflate the balloon, connect the drainage bag, and secure the tubing to the thigh.

Insert an indwelling Foley catheter in an anesthetized male patient in the OR: retract foreskin, sterile prep of the glans, drape, hold the penis at the correct angle, advance the catheter past the prostatic urethra with graded force, confirm urine return before balloon inflation, connect drainage and secure.

Difficult or non-routine catheterization in the OR or pre-op holding: BPH, urethral stricture, false passage, morbid obesity, prior pelvic/urologic surgery, or pediatric patient — requiring coudé or smaller catheters, repositioning, extra lubricant/lidocaine, gentle troubleshooting, and escalation to urology if resistance persists.

Remove a urinary catheter at the end of the case or in the PACU: verify order, don gloves, aspirate the balloon fully with a syringe, withdraw the catheter gently while observing the patient, inspect the tip and meatus, measure and document output, and provide perineal care.

In-and-out (straight) catheterization for bladder decompression or a urine specimen in pre-op holding or the OR, on an awake or lightly sedated patient who must be coached, positioned, and kept covered, using full sterile technique.

Intra-operative catheter management: repositioning or re-securing a catheter that has migrated during patient repositioning, troubleshooting no-flow or kinked tubing under the drapes, or reinserting a catheter dislodged during the procedure while maintaining the sterile field.

sources.system: Novel automatic urinary catheterization device (Kang et al., Korea University Guro Hospital / Eulji University)
sources.developer: Korea University Guro Hospital and Eulji University (Kang, Yoon, Lee, Kim, Choi, Kim, Park)
sources.title: A feasibility study using cadaver: Efficacy and safety of the novel automatic urinary catheterization device - PubMed
sources.claim: The closest thing to an automated urinary catheterization machine is a motorized 'automatic urinary catheterization device' for male self-intermittent catheterization, tested only on four fresh cadavers; a human must fit a penis cap and hold the correct angle, and insertion failed when the penis was held at 135 degrees.
