No sterile prep, balloon Foley placement, female anatomy, or live-patient use was demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task (transurethral catheter insertion), but limited to male cadavers, intermittent catheters, and human-performed fixation and positioning, so it does not substantiate completion of any listed instance.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot performs laparoscopic surgery, suturing intestinal tissue - ASME
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue surgical robot performed laparoscopic bowel anastomosis on a live pig under human supervision in a research laboratory, relying on specially marked tissue and a predetermined plan; it is a research demonstration, not a clinically deployed system, and it does not perform bedside procedures such as urethral catheter placement or removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of live soft tissue in a surgical setting. Cited to show the ceiling of autonomous surgical robotics — marker-based, pre-planned, research-only — which does not transfer to sterile perineal prep and blind urethral catheter passage in varied human anatomy.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk — Serve Robotics
sources.claim: Robots actually deployed at scale inside US hospitals perform logistics — delivering medications, supplies, and lab samples along corridors — and do not perform invasive patient-contact procedures such as urinary catheterization.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation in a hospital (E2) facility. Cited as the state of deployed hospital robotics to show that patient-contact catheterization is well outside demonstrated capability, supporting a negative judgment.

tasks.label: Assist in volume replacement or autotransfusion techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-blood-loss case with intraoperative cell salvage (cardiac, spine fusion, revision arthroplasty, ruptured AAA, obstetric hemorrhage): scrubbed assistant holds and directs the cell-saver suction wand in the open, bleeding surgical field, skims pooled blood without entraining air or damaging tissue, keeps the surgeon's view clear, and coordinates reservoir/anticoagulant use with the autotransfusionist while surgeons operate on live tissue.

Acute intraoperative hemorrhage / massive transfusion event: assistant applies direct pressure or packs the bleeding source and assists with clamping while simultaneously supporting rapid volume replacement at anesthesia's direction  agging fluid bags, hanging crystalloid/colloid or blood units onto a rapid infuser/fluid warmer, and reporting field conditions. Time-critical, crowded room, live patient.

Preparing the fluid and autotransfusion circuit for a case: spiking anticoagulant (heparinized saline) and crystalloid bags, priming administration sets and the salvage collection line, attaching filters, connecting suction tubing to the reservoir, and labeling/handing off the reinfusion bag. Done at a back table or beside the salvage machine in the OR with sterile supplies opened onto the field.

Routine case fluid and blood-loss accounting: measuring suction canister volumes net of irrigation, weighing blood-soaked sponges/laps on the scale, tracking salvaged and returned volumes, and reporting estimated blood loss to anesthesia so replacement can be titrated.

Vascular access support for volume replacement in the anesthetized, draped patient: positioning/prepping a limb or neck, assisting the surgeon or anesthetist with a large-bore peripheral IV, introducer sheath, or central line, holding pressure, suturing/securing the line, and connecting and de-airing the infusion tubing.

sources.system: dVRK autonomous blood suction (sim-to-real RL policy, Ou & Tavakoli)
sources.developer: University of Alberta (Telerobotic and Biorobotic Systems Group)
sources.title: Autonomous Blood Suction for Robot-Assisted Surgery: A Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning Approach
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic blood suction has been demonstrated only on a benchtop da Vinci Research Kit using 3D-printed tissue models and red-dyed liquid as simulated blood, not on patients in an operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing pooled blood from a surgical cavity with a suction tool, the core motor act of cell-salvage suction. It shows the frontier of autonomous blood suction is a fixtured laboratory phantom, so it cannot substantiate field suction on a live patient.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy) on a da Vinci research platform
sources.title: Robotic Surgeon Flawlessly Removes Pig Gallbladder Without Human Control
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous surgical manipulation to date was performed on ex vivo pig gallbladders in a laboratory, not on live patients in an operating room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tissue manipulation at the surgical field, the environment in which cell-salvage suction and hemorrhage control occur. It bounds the state of the art at ex vivo tissue in a lab, so no cited system works patient-side in a live OR.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: A commercially deployed robot autonomously prepares intravenous syringes and bags inside an enclosed, purpose-built aseptic compounding cell in hospital pharmacies; staff only load barcoded vials, syringes and IV bags into the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling, piercing/spiking and filling of IV bags and syringes with fluid. Comparable objects (infusion bags, syringes, ports) and precision to spiking and priming infusion sets, but only inside a fixtured enclosed cell.

sources.title: Automatic compounding system - KIRO - robotic / laboratory
sources.claim: The KIRO Oncology robot uses two robotic arms inside an enclosed cabinet with a preparation bay for infusion bags and an in-process gravimetric weighing device, verifying each preparation by weight before release.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pick-place-and-weigh of fluid containers with gravimetric accounting. Transfers to measuring salvaged/irrigation volumes and weighing items to compute fluid balance, provided items are presented in fixtures inside a cell.

sources.title: Automated Phlebotomy Firm Vitestro Eyes 2027 Commercial Launch of Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs ultrasound-guided venipuncture on patients in hospital laboratory settings at first-stick rates comparable to human phlebotomists, but it draws diagnostic samples from a seated patient whose arm is placed in the device; it does not place an indwelling catheter or connect an infusion line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous needle insertion into a vein. It is the closest system to assisting vascular access, but it collects samples rather than establishing and securing a fluid-administration line, and requires a cooperative patient's arm in its fixture.

tasks.label: Transport patients to operating room.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine pre-op case in a hospital OR suite: assistant goes to the pre-operative holding bay, verifies patient identity/procedure with the chart and wristband, releases stretcher brakes, and pushes the awake or lightly premedicated adult (IV line, warming blanket, sometimes O2) through semi-restricted corridors and through OR doors, parks and locks the stretcher alongside the operating table, and hands the patient off to the OR team.

Inpatient or ICU case: assistant/transport team collects the patient in a hospital bed from a nursing unit or ICU, manages IV pumps, drains, telemetry, oxygen cylinder and chart, rides a designated elevator to the OR floor, negotiates unit doors and busy corridors, and delivers the patient into the OR or its holding area.

Ambulatory surgery center or outpatient case: gowned, mobile patient is walked or wheeled the short distance from the pre-op bay into the operating room, escorted by the assistant who steadies them, keeps IV tubing clear, answers questions, and guides them beside the operating table.

Emergent/urgent case: rapid transport from the ED, ICU or L&D to the OR with an unstable or anesthetized patient — bag-valve ventilation, ongoing monitoring, pressors or blood running, corridor cleared, multiple staff moving together at speed.

Special-handling case: frightened child or confused/dementia patient needing continuous reassurance, or a bariatric / traction / multi-drain patient requiring several staff, a heavy-duty bed and careful line and limb management during the move to the OR.

sources.title: Industry Insights: Rovex Makes Autonomous Transport Robots for Hospital Patients
sources.claim: Rovex's Rovi is an autonomous robot that clamps onto stretcher casters and tows stretchers around a hospital; in its first hospital pilot (BayCare Morton Plant Hospital, April 2026) it is moving empty stretchers and is explicitly not yet moving patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous towing/navigation of the exact object used in this task (a hospital stretcher) through hospital corridors; it substantiates the machine-side mobility and stretcher-coupling capability, but not carriage of a patient.

sources.system: Rovi (Rovex); Sphaira Autopod; MOVED autonomous bed
sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Trade-press survey of the patient-transport robotics field as of May 2026: Rovex's hospital pilot is limited to navigation rather than patient movement, and rival autonomous patient movers (Sphaira Autopod, OGGMA MOVED bed) are renderings or concepts rather than deployed patient-carrying systems.

sources.title: Wayne County Airport Authority partners with Unifi to bring autonomous wheelchairs to DTW
sources.claim: WHILL's Autonomous Drive System carries seated human passengers autonomously along mapped routes inside large institutional facilities; more than 100 units are in service across airports with over 400,000 autonomous rides completed, and it is offered as a commercial service (e.g., Unifi at Detroit Metro Airport).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a human occupant to a designated destination inside a controlled facility. Same payload (a person) and comparable navigation demands as moving a patient to a procedure room; it does not cover recumbent patients, lines/monitors, or clinical handoff.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. / Japanese university hospital study team
sources.title: Safety and feasibility of in-hospital autonomous transportation using a driverless mobility for patients with musculoskeletal disorders
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed clinical study transported 51 real hospital patients with reduced mobility using WHILL driverless mobility that drives autonomously from a start point to a stored destination inside the hospital; no collisions or severe adverse events occurred.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-hospital transport of a seated patient to a destination. Same environment (hospital corridors) and same payload class (an ambulatory-limited patient), short of entering a restricted operating room or handing off to the surgical team.

sources.title: Robots and a COVID Note | What's Up at Upstate | SUNY Upstate
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots operate in fleets in US hospitals, navigating corridors with lidar/sonar/infrared, calling and riding elevators and opening doors, hauling heavy wheeled loads (some models up to 1,000 lb) of supplies, meals and medications.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hauling of heavy wheeled loads over fixed hospital routes including elevators and doors. It substantiates the transport mechanics (route following, load towing, door/elevator integration) that a fixtured patient trolley would require, but not care of a human payload.

sources.title: Able Innovations Deploys Robotic Patient Delivery Platform in the U.S.
sources.claim: Able Innovations' ALTA robotic platform performs lateral patient transfers between beds, stretchers and OR/procedure tables in acute care and is deployed in Canadian sites and at Lahey Hospital & Medical Center in the US, but each transfer is carried out by a staff member operating the device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-assisted movement of a patient between surfaces at the end of transport. Cited only to show this step is operator-driven, not autonomous; it cannot support a positive judgment.

roles.title: Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Workers, All Other
roles.description: All healthcare practitioners and technical workers not listed separately.

roles.title: Midwives
roles.description: Provide prenatal care and childbirth assistance.

tasks.label: Monitor maternal condition during labor by checking vital signs, monitoring uterine contractions, or performing physical examinations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital labor & delivery room, active labor: midwife performs routine periodic maternal assessment every 15-60 min — BP, pulse, temperature, respirations; hands-on palpation of the fundus to time contraction frequency, duration and strength; checks IV/epidural site, hydration, bladder, pain and coping — on a woman who shifts position, is in bed or on a ball, and is having painful contractions.

Hospital or birth center: sterile-gloved digital vaginal examination during labor to assess cervical dilation, effacement, position, station of the presenting part and membrane status, timed between contractions and interpreted against labor progress.

Hospital: placing and adjusting external monitoring equipment on the maternal abdomen (tocodynamometer/CTG belts, BP cuff, pulse oximeter), repositioning transducers when the signal is lost as the woman moves, and reading the toco/vitals trends alongside hands-on checks.

Freestanding birth center: intermittent monitoring of an ambulatory laboring woman — vitals and contraction palpation while she is in a tub, on hands and knees, walking the hall or in the shower; handheld Doppler and abdominal palpation rather than continuous monitors.

Planned home birth in the client's private residence: full maternal assessment (vitals, abdominal palpation, cervical exam, assessment of bleeding, hydration, temperature) in a bedroom or bathroom with variable lighting, furniture, pets and family present.

Hospital, deteriorating or complicated labor: focused reassessment for hemorrhage, hypertensive crisis/pre-eclampsia (repeat BP, deep tendon reflexes and clonus, epigastric pain), fever/chorioamnionitis, or rapid reassessment during second stage, requiring urgent judgment and escalation.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot (588 g cable-driven, AI agent)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous AI-driven ultrasound robot performed liver scans on human subjects in a hospital ultrasound department — the closest demonstrated case of a robot autonomously making instrumented physical contact with a patient's abdomen — but it images a still, supine, cooperative patient and performs no vital-sign, palpation or labor-progress assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abdominal ultrasound scanning. It shows force-controlled autonomous probe contact with a human abdomen in a clinical facility, but transfer to maternal labor monitoring fails: the patient must lie still and supine, the robot measures no vital signs, performs no fundal palpation of contraction tone and no cervical examination, and has not been shown on contracting, mobile laboring women.

sources.title: Robotic Phlebotomy Study Signals Automation Shift for Clinical Labs
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device completed venipuncture on outpatients across three clinical sites at near-human first-stick rates, showing that a narrowly scoped, fixtured patient-contact procedure can be automated — but it performs only blood draw at a dedicated station, not multi-modal maternal assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture on a fixtured arm in an outpatient draw station. It demonstrates safe autonomous contact with a patient's body at a purpose-built station, but the maternal-monitoring instance requires roving vital signs, hands-on uterine palpation and internal examination on a moving, contracting patient — none of which this single-purpose device performs.

sources.system: MELODY tele-robotic ultrasound (robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound program)
sources.developer: AdEchoTech / University Hospital of North Norway
sources.title: Introduction of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Northern Norway
sources.claim: The only robotic system in routine obstetric clinical use for hands-on examination of pregnant women is teleoperated: a remote sonographer drives the probe while an on-site midwife physically moves the robot arm on the woman's abdomen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obstetric abdominal ultrasound on pregnant patients. It is the closest robotic system operating in the obstetric domain, but it is continuously teleoperated and still requires a midwife at the bedside to position the arm, so it cannot support a positive autonomy judgment for any part of maternal labor monitoring.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The most widely deployed autonomous hospital robot in the US performs only non-clinical fetch-and-deliver logistics in corridors; it does not touch or assess patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile work inside hospital wards (E2). It establishes that hospital corridors are navigable autonomously, but the system has no patient-contact capability, so it contributes nothing to vital-sign taking, uterine palpation or physical examination.

sources.system: Humanoid robot with 3D-printed origami blood-pressure sensors
sources.developer: Simon Fraser University (Woo Soo Kim lab)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots Could Reach Out and Take Patient's Blood Pressure
sources.claim: Robot-mounted sensors able to read blood pressure by touch exist only as a laboratory research demonstration on a small humanoid; no clinical use or autonomous patient workflow has been shown.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acquisition of a maternal vital sign. Even for this single sub-step the evidence is a bench demonstration with unclear autonomy, so it cannot substantiate completing a periodic maternal assessment during labor.

tasks.label: Identify tubal and ectopic pregnancies and refer patients for treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide necessary medical care for infants at birth, including emergency care such as resuscitation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital labor & delivery room, uncomplicated vaginal birth: midwife receives the slippery, wet newborn at delivery, dries and stimulates with a warm towel, positions the airway, places the baby skin-to-skin on the mother's chest, manages delayed cord clamping and cuts/clamps the cord, keeps the infant warm, and assigns Apgar scores at 1 and 5 minutes while continuously assessing tone, color, and respiratory effort.

Hospital birth where the newborn needs brief transitional support: bulb-syringe or wall suction of secretions/meconium from mouth and nose, vigorous tactile stimulation of back and soles, repositioning the head to open the airway, applying pulse oximeter probe to the right hand, blow-by oxygen or CPAP, and deciding whether to escalate to the neonatal team.

Hospital or birth center: full NRP resuscitation of a depressed newborn on a radiant warmer - achieving a mask seal for positive-pressure ventilation with bag-mask at 40-60 breaths/min, MR SOPA corrective steps, coordinated chest compressions at 3:1, possible intubation, UVC access and epinephrine, while directing the team and timing events.

Hospital/birth center newborn assessment and prophylaxis within the first hours: weighing and measuring, full head-to-toe physical exam of a squirming infant (fontanelles, clavicles, heart/lung auscultation, hips, reflexes, genitalia, spine), vitamin K intramuscular injection into the vastus lateralis, erythromycin eye ointment, hepatitis B vaccine, heel-stick glucose check, and first latch support.

Freestanding birth center birth: immediate newborn care and transition monitoring with limited equipment and no in-house neonatal team - drying/stimulating on the mother or a portable warmer, cord management, thermoregulation, serial vitals, and preparing for transfer if the infant does not transition well.

Planned home birth in a client's private residence: newborn care on a bed, sofa, or floor in variable lighting and space, with pets and family present - drying, stimulating, skin-to-skin, cord management, newborn exam, and, if needed, resuscitation on an improvised flat surface using a portable self-inflating bag-mask and oxygen tank while arranging EMS transport.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is the largest autonomous mobile-manipulation deployment in US hospitals, but its work is last-mile logistics (supplies, labs, medications), not physical patient care; no patient-contact or newborn-handling capability is claimed.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish the state of the art for autonomous robots inside hospitals (an E2 facility). It does not transfer to this task: Moxi transports items along corridors and does not touch, assess, or treat patients, let alone handle a newborn.

sources.title: Robot performs autonomous needle-less injection | Robotics and Automation
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform performed a first autonomous needle-free intramuscular injection, a one-off demonstration on a cooperative adult subject; it is not a deployed clinical system and has not been shown injecting infants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = intramuscular injection. Transfer fails: the demo targets a static adult deltoid, not the vastus lateralis of an unrestrained newborn, and it covers only one sub-step of the newborn exam-and-prophylaxis instance, not the whole instance.

sources.system: Automated mechanical chest compression device (research prototype)
sources.developer: University of Alberta neonatal resuscitation research group
sources.title: Comparison of hemodynamic effects of chest compression delivered via machine or human in asphyxiated piglets
sources.claim: Automated mechanical chest-compression delivery for newborns exists only as an experimental device tested on asphyxiated newborn piglets in a laboratory; the device is positioned and operated by humans and does not perform airway management, ventilation, or assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = neonatal chest compressions. Transfer fails: it is an animal-model device placed and controlled by clinicians, covering one sub-step of resuscitation, with no autonomous perception, decision-making, or infant handling.

sources.title: Mama Anne robot gives birth to train midwifery students at York St John
sources.claim: Robotics in the childbirth setting is represented by patient simulators such as the Mama Anne birthing manikin used to train midwifery students - the robot plays the role of the mother/newborn, not the caregiver, confirming no robot delivers newborn care.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a negative-context item: the only robots present at simulated births are manikins that receive care from human midwives, not machines that provide newborn care.

tasks.label: Conduct ongoing prenatal health assessments, tracking changes in physical and emotional health.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine mid/late-pregnancy office visit at a midwifery practice or clinic: greet and interview the client about symptoms, take weight and blood pressure, urine dipstick, measure fundal height with a tape, perform Leopold's maneuvers to assess fetal lie and presentation, auscultate fetal heart tones with a handheld Doppler, screen mood (e.g., EPDS/PHQ) and social stressors, compare against prior visits, counsel, and document a plan.

Initial/comprehensive early-pregnancy assessment in the practice office: full history, baseline vitals and weight, head-to-toe physical including heart/lung auscultation, breast and pelvic exam, order/collect labs, dating by exam or point-of-care ultrasound, baseline emotional-health and psychosocial screening, establish the care plan.

Home prenatal visit by a community or home-birth midwife: assessment performed in the client's living room or bedroom with the client on a couch or bed, using portable equipment (BP cuff, tape, Doppler, urine dipstick), amid family members, pets, and variable lighting and clutter; includes assessing emotional state and home circumstances.

Hospital-based antepartum/triage or high-risk clinic assessment prompted by a change: e.g., elevated blood pressure, reduced fetal movement, swelling, or worsening mood; repeat vitals, abdominal palpation, apply and interpret external fetal monitoring/NST, targeted physical exam, assess distress and safety, escalate to physician as needed.

Interval telehealth or phone check-in between in-person visits: review client-reported home blood pressure, weight, and fetal movement counts, ask about symptoms, conduct emotional-health screening and counseling by video from the practice office while the client is at home, and document changes since the last visit.

sources.system: DNN-based autonomous fetal ultrasound scanning robot
sources.developer: Advanced Robotics paper authors (Japanese university group)
sources.title: Autonomous scanning motion generation adapted to individual differences in abdominal shape for robotic fetal ultrasound
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic fetal ultrasound scanning exists only as research: a deep network generates scan motions for a robot adapted to individual abdominal shapes, tested on volunteers/phantoms, not as a clinical prenatal assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic acquisition of fetal ultrasound images on a pregnant abdomen. It is the closest automated analogue to a midwife's abdominal assessment, but it covers only probe placement/imaging, not fundal height, Leopold's palpation, Doppler auscultation, history-taking, or emotional-health assessment, so it cannot substantiate completing the whole instance.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital group
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: An autonomous ultrasound robot has been evaluated performing abdominal (liver) scans on humans inside a hospital ultrasound department, showing autonomous probe placement on patients is feasible but limited to imaging a single organ.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abdominal imaging contact on a human patient in a structured hospital facility. It shows safe autonomous probe-to-abdomen contact, but delivers only an image acquisition sub-step, not the interview, palpation, vitals, screening and clinical judgment that make up a prenatal health assessment.

sources.title: Remote and Telerobotic Ultrasound Imaging (PMC)
sources.claim: Obstetric robotic examination that is actually in clinical use is teleoperated: a remote clinician drives the probe and an on-site assistant positions the robot on the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obstetric examination performed via a robot. It is the deployed state of the art for robotic prenatal assessment and is fully human-driven, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: Robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound service, Northern Norway
sources.developer: University Hospital of North Norway / regional study group
sources.title: Introduction of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Northern Norway
sources.claim: Robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound introduced in rural clinics is remote-controlled by an obstetrician at a hospital rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetal assessment via robot in a clinic. Demonstrates that even in structured facilities the fetal-assessment portion of prenatal care is performed by a remote human operator, not autonomously.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: The largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators performs only logistics and is explicitly non-patient-facing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot work inside hospitals and clinics. It marks the boundary of deployed clinical robotics — logistics only — indicating no fielded system conducts patient assessment even in a structured facility.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device — CAP TODAY
sources.claim: The only autonomous robot in clinical use that makes instrumented physical contact with patients performs venipuncture, a single procedural step, not a health assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic contact with a seated patient's body in a clinical setting. It shows what deployed patient-contact automation can do — one fixtured, narrowly scoped procedure on a presented arm — far short of a multi-modal prenatal assessment with clinical judgment.

tasks.label: Monitor fetal growth and well-being through heartbeat detection, body measurement, and palpation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine 2nd/3rd-trimester prenatal visit in a midwifery or OB outpatient clinic: client semi-reclined on an exam table, midwife exposes the abdomen, performs Leopold's maneuvers to establish lie/presentation/engagement, measures symphysis-fundal height with a tape from pubic symphysis to fundus, locates the fetal back and auscultates the fetal heart with a handheld Doppler for a timed count, plots growth against the customized curve, and documents/communicates findings.

Intermittent auscultation during labor in a hospital labor room or birth center suite: midwife palpates the moving, contracting abdomen to find the fetal back, applies Doppler through and after contractions in varied maternal positions (side-lying, hands-and-knees, in a tub), counts and distinguishes maternal from fetal rate, repeats every 15-30 minutes, and interprets baseline/accelerations/decelerations.

Antepartum triage or focused assessment in a hospital assessment unit (reduced fetal movement, size-dates discrepancy, suspected malposition): palpation for size and presentation, fundal height, Doppler/NST transducer placement and repositioning as the fetus moves, sometimes a bedside ultrasound check of presentation or fluid, with escalation decisions.

Home-based care by a home-birth midwife (CPM/CNM): prenatal visit or labor monitoring in the client's own home, client on a sofa, bed or birth pool, with family, pets and clutter present; same palpation, fundal-height and Doppler assessment carried out with portable equipment in whatever space and lighting the home offers.

Early-pregnancy or small-uterus visit at a clinic/birth center (roughly 12-20 weeks, or with obesity/anterior placenta): fundus low or barely palpable, patient anxious, midwife must search patiently with the Doppler over the lower abdomen to obtain fetal heart tones and confirm well-being, while measuring fundal height where applicable.

sources.system: Robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound (MELODY-type telerobotic arm), UiT / Finnmark hospital
sources.developer: AdEchoTech / University Hospital of North Norway (Olsen et al.)
sources.title: Introduction of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Northern Norway - PubMed
sources.claim: Robotic systems in clinical obstetric fetal assessment are teleoperated: in rural Northern Norway a remote obstetrician controls the ultrasound probe while a local midwife holds the robot arm on the pregnant abdomen; 46 pregnant women studied.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robotic system for fetal well-being assessment; it is fully teleoperated by a remote expert and a local clinician still positions the arm, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.title: Robotic prenatal ultrasound for rural areas - AdEchoTech
sources.claim: The commercial MELODY prenatal tele-ultrasound workflow requires a human on site holding the robot against the patient and a remote specialist steering the probe.
sources.transferJustification: Prenatal fetal imaging is the related task; the commercial system provides no autonomy in locating the fetus or contacting the abdomen, so it cannot substitute for the midwife's independent assessment.

sources.system: Telerobotic ultrasound system (MELODY), University of Saskatchewan
sources.developer: AdEchoTech / University of Saskatchewan (Adams et al.)
sources.title: Telerobotic ultrasound to provide obstetrical ultrasound services remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic - PMC
sources.claim: Telerobotic obstetrical ultrasound has been delivered in a remote Canadian community with a sonographer 605 km away ... controlling the probe for 21 exams.
sources.transferJustification: Remote fetal assessment is the related task; continuous human teleoperation means the system does not satisfy the limited-intervention requirement.

sources.system: Cobotic obstetric ultrasound systems (review of field)
sources.title: Cobotic Ultrasound Systems in Obstetric Assessment: A Scoping Review
sources.claim: A scoping review of robotic/cobotic systems in obstetric ultrasound finds the clinical evidence base is teleoperated remote ultrasound with a small combined cohort and incomplete fetal visualization.
sources.transferJustification: Field-level review of robotics for fetal assessment; it shows no autonomous obstetric system has reached clinical completion of fetal well-being assessment.

sources.developer: Chinese research group (Su et al.), Nature Communications
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scans the thyroid on human participants without human assistance, producing scans close to clinician quality.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous probe placement on a human body is the nearest autonomous analogue to Doppler auscultation, but the target is a fixed superficial neck structure, not a moving fetus, and the system performs no palpation for fetal lie or tape measurement of fundal height.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Chinese PLA General Hospital (Jiang et al.), Nature Communications
sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system | Nature Communications
sources.claim: UltraBot performs autonomous carotid ultrasonography on humans with over 90% success rates and expert-level accuracy in clinical validation.
sources.transferJustification: State of the art in autonomous contact sonography on people; restricted to the neck of cooperative adults in a hospital ultrasound room, with no demonstrated transfer to locating a moving fetus, abdominal palpation, or fundal-height measurement.

sources.system: Robotic examination system for emergency telemedicine
sources.developer: German clinical research group (telemedical diagnostics study)
sources.title: Toward telemedical diagnostics—clinical evaluation of a robotic examination system for emergency patients - PMC
sources.claim: Robotic systems used for remote physical examination, including abdominal palpation of patients, are operated by a physician through a haptic interface with force feedback rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Abdominal palpation of real patients is the related task; the only clinically evaluated systems are human-in-the-loop teleoperation, so no autonomous robot is shown performing Leopold's maneuvers.

tasks.label: Establish and follow emergency or contingency plans for mothers and newborns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prenatal visit at a birth center/clinic office (occasionally the client's living room): the midwife works through the individualized emergency and contingency plan with the client and family — risk screening, what happens if hemorrhage, fetal distress or a non-breathing newborn occurs, which hospital they transfer to, who drives, informed-consent signatures, written instructions handed over, plan documented in the chart and posted with the birth kit.

Readiness maintenance between births at the birth center or the midwife's office/vehicle: open and inventory the emergency kits, check oxygen cylinder pressure and tubing, test suction and neonatal bag-mask/PEEP valve, verify oxytocin/misoprostol/anti-hemorrhagics and IV fluids are present and unexpired, restock consumables, confirm transfer forms and phone numbers, and run a periodic skills drill with the birth assistant.

Postpartum hemorrhage at a home birth: recognize excessive bleeding within seconds, deliver vigorous fundal massage, draw and give IM/IV uterotonics, empty the bladder, start IV fluids, perform bimanual uterine compression while assessing tone and clots, take serial vitals, direct the assistant, and call EMS if bleeding continues — all on a soft bed in an ordinary bedroom.

Newborn not breathing at birth (home or freestanding birth center): dry and stimulate, position the airway, suction, initiate positive-pressure ventilation with bag and mask within the first minute, auscultate heart rate, add chest compressions if needed, maintain warmth, and simultaneously activate the neonatal emergency plan (911, receiving hospital notified).

Hands-on intrapartum maneuvers under the contingency plan: shoulder dystocia (McRoberts, suprapubic pressure, Gaskin all-fours, internal rotational maneuvers), cord prolapse (manual elevation of the presenting part maintained continuously), tight nuchal cord or breech — performed on a laboring woman in a home bedroom or birth-center room with an assistant.

Executing a transfer of care: decide to transfer, call EMS/receiving obstetric unit, package the mother and/or newborn (IV in place, warmth, monitoring), assist the ambulance crew moving her from a bedroom or birth-center room to the stretcher, ride along or follow, carry the chart, and give a verbal SBAR handoff to hospital staff.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulation robot deployed commercially in more than 25 US ..., doing fetch-and-deliver of supplies, medications and lab samples inside structured hospital facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply logistics. It marks the current ceiling of autonomous robot work inside a structured care facility — moving and stocking supplies among people — and shows that even the supply-readiness portion of the midwife's contingency-plan work is only partially covered (fetch/deliver, not functional equipment checks or drills), with no hands-on patient care.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals — IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi's autonomy consists of picking supplies out of supply ...; it is a logistics robot, not a clinical care robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supply restocking in a hospital. Establishes what the leading deployed clinical-facility manipulator actually does, bounding the readiness-maintenance instance: no evidence it tests oxygen/suction/bag-mask, verifies drug expiry, or assembles a midwifery emergency kit.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous patient-contact procedure in routine clinical use is robotic venipuncture on seated, cooperative outpatients in accredited hospital laboratories, with a human professional supervising up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vascular access, the single hands-on clinical sub-step closest to emergency IV placement. Transfer fails in the other direction: autonomy exists only for an immobilized arm presented to a fixed device in a laboratory, not for cannulating a shocked, bleeding postpartum woman on a bed, and it covers none of the rest of an emergency response.

sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery (Nature)
sources.claim: Hands-on clinical manipulation by humanoid robots remains teleoperated and pre-clinical; a 2026 in vivo feasibility study evaluated humanoids performing laparoscopic surgical tasks only through teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous clinical intervention on a patient. It is the strongest recent demonstration of humanoid hands-on medical work, and it is teleoperated and pre-clinical, so it cannot support autonomous completion of obstetric or neonatal emergency care.

sources.system: assistant nurse robots for obstetrics and neonatal care (design study)
sources.title: Evaluation of nurses' perspectives on the design and use of assistant nurse robots in obstetrics and neonatal care: a mixed-method study (BMC Nursing)
sources.claim: Assistant robots for obstetrics and neonatal care are still at the concept/design-evaluation stage, studied through nurses' preferences rather than deployed to perform care.
sources.transferJustification: Direct domain evidence: the state of robotics in obstetric and neonatal care is design preference research, confirming that no fielded system performs maternal or newborn emergency care.

tasks.label: Identify, monitor, or treat pregnancy-related problems such as hypertension, gestational diabetes, pre-term labor, or retarded fetal growth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine prenatal office visit in a clinic/birth-center exam room: measure BP (repeat if elevated), weight, urine dipstick for protein, palpate and measure fundal height, auscultate fetal heart tones with Doppler, elicit preeclampsia symptoms (headache, RUQ pain, visual changes), check reflexes/edema, then decide on labs, repeat surveillance, antihypertensive or low-dose aspirin, and counsel the patient.

Gestational diabetes work-up and management in clinic: order/administer glucola and draw blood, review home glucometer logs, counsel on diet and exercise, initiate and titrate metformin or insulin with injection teaching, and arrange added fetal surveillance.

Antenatal surveillance for suspected fetal growth restriction in a clinic or hospital antenatal testing unit: apply toco and ultrasound transducers for a non-stress test and interpret the tracing, perform or order limited bedside ultrasound (growth biometry, amniotic fluid index, umbilical Doppler), compare to gestational-age norms, and decide on repeat testing, MFM referral or delivery timing.

Hospital L&D triage/inpatient acute management: patient presents with preterm contractions or severe-range hypertension; perform sterile speculum and cervical exam, collect fetal fibronectin/GBS swabs, place continuous fetal and contraction monitoring, start IV, order and administer magnesium sulfate, betamethasone, tocolytics or IV labetalol/hydralazine with titration and side-effect monitoring, and coordinate transfer/consult.

Home-based prenatal or postpartum visit in a home-birth practice: assess BP and pulse on the client's couch or bed, palpate fundal height and fetal position, Doppler fetal heart tones, dip urine, review warning signs, and decide whether the pregnancy remains low-risk or requires consultation/transfer of care.

sources.date: 2025-04 (device unveil); 2024-08 CE mark; multicenter trial results 2024-2026
sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device – CAP TODAY
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that performs the full blood-draw sequence (tourniquet, skin prep, AI ultrasound vein selection, needle insertion, sample collection) in hospital outpatient blood-draw departments; a multicenter trial reported ~95% first-stick success. It covers only venous sampling, not clinical assessment, diagnosis or treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture for prenatal labs (glucose tolerance testing, preeclampsia labs). Transfer is only partial: it substantiates autonomous skin-contact sampling on a seated patient in a structured facility, but not fundal palpation, fetal auscultation, obstetric ultrasound, diagnosis or therapy.

sources.system: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital research group
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography (arXiv 2510.08106)
sources.claim: An autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot performed self-directed abdominal scanning (aorta, IVC, liver planes) on humans in a hospital ultrasound department without teleoperation, demonstrating autonomous probe placement and force control, but limited to specified single-organ imaging tasks rather than obstetric biometry with clinical decision-making.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous abdominal ultrasound acquisition. It is the closest evidence for the imaging portion of fetal growth surveillance, but the demonstrated targets are fixed vascular/liver planes in a hospital imaging room, not fetal biometry, AFI or umbilical Doppler in a gravid abdomen.

sources.date: 2025-11 (study publication); MELODY FDA-cleared for obstetric remote ultrasound
sources.title: Introduction of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Northern Norway - PubMed
sources.claim: Robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound used in rural Norway lets a hospital obstetrician remotely drive a probe to obtain fetal biometry, but the arm is teleoperated by the distant clinician with an on-site assistant positioning it on the patient, so no autonomous performance is demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (obstetric growth assessment), but it is continuous remote human control, so per the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: Cobionix demonstrated a robot autonomously administering a needle-free intramuscular injection to a person, a one-off laboratory demonstration rather than a validated clinical medication-administration system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering a parenteral medication (e.g., betamethasone, insulin teaching, labetalol). Transfer is weak: a single demo of a needle-free IM shot does not establish dose selection, titration, IV therapy or monitoring for treatment of pregnancy complications.

tasks.label: Assess the status of post-date pregnancies to determine treatments and interventions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine prenatal office visit at 40w0d-41w0d in a midwifery clinic/OB office: confirm dating, take BP and weight, measure fundal height, perform Leopold's maneuvers to confirm presentation, auscultate fetal heart with handheld Doppler, review fetal movement counts, offer/perform a digital cervical exam (Bishop score, membrane sweep), then counsel the patient and set the plan (expectant management with surveillance vs. scheduling induction).

Antenatal surveillance appointment at 41+ weeks in a hospital/clinic antepartum testing unit: position the patient, place tocodynamometer and ultrasound transducer belts for a non-stress test, adjust for fetal movement and maternal habitus, interpret the 20-40 minute tracing, obtain or order a limited ultrasound for amniotic fluid index / biophysical profile, and determine the intervention (repeat testing, ripening, or induction).

Labor & delivery triage/admission assessment of a post-date patient (41-42 weeks, sometimes with decreased fetal movement or suspected rupture of membranes): full vitals, continuous fetal monitoring, sterile speculum and digital cervical exam for Bishop score, estimated fetal weight by palpation, record review, consultation with the collaborating physician, and initiation of cervical ripening/induction orders.

Community/home-birth midwife assessing a post-date client in the client's home or a freestanding birth-center room: abdominal palpation and fundal height on a bed or sofa, Doppler heart tones, maternal vitals, optional cervical check/sweep, discussion of nonpharmacologic ripening, and decision on continued community care vs. transfer of care for induction at 42 weeks.

Remote review and counseling at 40-41 weeks with no hands-on exam: re-verify dating criteria from records, take the patient's report of fetal movement, review recent NST/AFI results, discuss risks of continuing the pregnancy, and arrange testing or induction scheduling by phone/telehealth from the office.

sources.title: MELODY - Remote ultrasound robot | AdEchoTech
sources.claim: MELODY is a commercially deployed, FDA-cleared robotic tele-ultrasound system used for obstetric scanning, but the probe is driven in real time by a remote physician while a person holds the robot against the patient - teleoperated, not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Obstetric ultrasound (AFI/BPP/biometry) is the imaging component of post-date assessment, so this is the closest robotic system to the task; it is cited to show the state of the art in obstetric robotics is human-in-the-loop teleoperation.

sources.developer: Finnmark Hospital Trust / UiT (Olsen et al.), AdEchoTech hardware
sources.title: Introduction of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Northern Norway
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed study of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Norway had every scan driven by a sonographer at an expert site with an assisting midwife physically present with the pregnant patient; no autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Prenatal ultrasound assessment in a clinic is the sub-step of post-date assessment most amenable to robotics; the deployment shows a human midwife is still required at the patient's side and a human expert drives the probe.

sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... has been demonstrated on human volunteers, but only for a narrow superficial region (thyroid/neck) in a research setting; no equivalent autonomous obstetric examination exists.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous ultrasound scanning is the nearest demonstrated autonomous capability; it does not transfer to post-date assessment, which also requires abdominal palpation, CTG placement and interpretation, digital cervical examination and a management decision on a pregnant patient.

sources.system: Melody (AdEchoTech), as assessed in telerobotic ultrasound review
sources.title: Remote and Telerobotic Ultrasound Imaging - PMC
sources.claim: A 2025 review of remote and telerobotic ultrasound confirms that the FDA-approved obstetric robotic ultrasound system is remotely operated and still requires an assistant with the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the MELODY product evidence: obstetric imaging is a component of post-date assessment, and the review establishes no autonomous obstetric ultrasound robot is cleared or deployed.

tasks.label: Set up or monitor the administration of oxygen or medications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital labor & delivery room: midwife sets up an IV oxytocin infusion for induction/augmentation — selects/verifies the premixed bag, spikes and primes tubing, connects to the patient's IV port, programs the smart pump, then titrates the rate up or down over hours in response to contraction pattern, cervical change and the fetal heart-rate tracing, stopping for tachysystole.

Hospital L&D/postpartum unit: midwife draws up and administers injectable medications to the patient — IM/IV oxytocin or misoprostol after delivery, IV GBS antibiotics, IV/IM analgesia, Rh immune globulin, terbutaline — verifies patient/drug/dose, gives the injection or IV push, then monitors vitals, bleeding and for adverse reactions.

Hospital or birth center: for non-reassuring fetal heart tones, midwife sets up oxygen — connects tubing to wall/tank flowmeter, sets 8-10 L/min, places and adjusts a non-rebreather mask on the face of a laboring, often restless woman in varying positions, and monitors the fetal tracing and maternal SpO2 for response.

At the birth: midwife sets up and delivers oxygen/positive-pressure ventilation to a newborn on the resuscitaire or mother's chest — attaches mask to T-piece/bag, achieves a seal on a small wet face, titrates blended FiO2 to the SpO2 target, monitors chest rise and heart rate.

Out-of-hospital birth (client's home or freestanding birth center room): midwife lays out a birth kit on whatever surface is available, starts an IV or gives IM oxytocin/methergine for postpartum hemorrhage, sets up a portable oxygen cylinder, and monitors the mother in a cluttered, variable, low-light setting.

Prenatal/postpartum clinic exam room: midwife administers office injections and medications — Tdap or influenza vaccine, RhoGAM at 28 weeks, Depo-Provera, iron infusion or oral dose — confirms identity and allergies, injects, documents, and observes the client for reactions.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs intramuscular injection without needles
sources.claim: Cobi, an autonomous robot platform, demonstrated a needle-free intramuscular injection; it is a 2021 university-spinoff proof-of-concept, not a clinically validated or deployed medication-administration system, and it does not draw up drugs, verify orders, or monitor patients afterward.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vaccine injection. It shares the act of delivering a drug into a patient's muscle, but it is a single lab proof-of-concept covering only the injection step, so it does not substantiate whole-instance medication administration and monitoring by a midwife.

sources.title: China releases its first autonomous intelligent robot for needle-free vaccine injection - Global Times
sources.claim: Tongji University's 'Houyi' robot autonomously locates an injection site on the body and delivers a needle-free jet injection; it is a research release with no reported clinical deployment or reliability data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vaccine injection into a seated cooperative adult. It covers only the injection act in a booth-like setup and provides no evidence of drug preparation, patient verification, or post-administration monitoring.

sources.title: A Serial Entrepreneur: Miller School Neurosurgeon Leads World's First Robotic-Assisted IV Catheterization
sources.claim: Hyperion Surgical's Ivy platform completed a first-in-human robotic-assisted IV catheterization in late 2025, but the process is described as semi-autonomous and is an investigational study, covering only vascular access rather than infusion setup and titration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peripheral IV placement, a precursor step to setting up an infusion. It is semi-autonomous and first-in-human only, so it cannot support autonomous completion of infusion setup and titration.

sources.title: Ballad Health expands patient safety with new robotic pharmacy technology
sources.claim: Omnicell IVX Station compounding robots are deployed in hospital central-fill pharmacy cleanrooms, where they autonomously prepare IV admixtures inside an enclosed cabinet; they do not connect or administer medication to a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: IV medication preparation inside a purpose-built enclosure. It shows syringe/bag handling by a robot but stops at the prepared dose; the midwife instances require bedside connection to a patient and clinical titration, which this system never performs.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Deployed hospital mobile manipulators such as Moxi carry out medication logistics — transporting pharmacy items along corridors to nursing stations — and are not reported to set up or administer medications or oxygen to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-hospital medication transport. It establishes the current ceiling of deployed hospital robots (delivery to a station) and does not extend to patient-contact administration or monitoring.

sources.title: Closed-loop automated oxygen control in late preterm and term, ventilated infants: A randomised controlled trial
sources.claim: Commercially available closed-loop FiO2 controllers automatically titrate oxygen to a saturation target in ventilated infants, but they are ventilator control algorithms acting through an already-established airway interface, not machines that set up oxygen delivery or place a mask on a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated oxygen titration during respiratory support. It covers the monitoring/adjustment portion for an already-connected patient, but no cited system performs the physical setup, mask application, or maternal oxygen delivery that these instances require.

tasks.label: Suture perineal lacerations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital labor-and-delivery room, immediately after a spontaneous vaginal birth: midwife inspects the perineum/vagina, grades a first- or second-degree laceration, infiltrates lidocaine, and closes vaginal mucosa, perineal muscle and skin in layers with absorbable suture while the patient is awake in semi-lithotomy on a birthing bed, with ongoing lochia, an oozing field, the newborn skin-to-skin, and the patient shifting position.

Hospital: repair of an episiotomy or a more extensive second-degree tear with labial/periurethral extension. Requires locating the apex above the visible tear, achieving hemostasis on a bleeding field, sometimes moving the patient to stirrups and overhead lighting, plus a rectal exam to exclude third/fourth-degree injury and referral to an OB if found.

Freestanding birth center: laceration repair on the birthing bed or a low futon shortly after birth, with portable/goose-neck lighting, one assistant, a sterile suture tray, local anesthetic only, and the patient in whatever position she can tolerate.

Planned home birth: repair performed in the client's bedroom on the family bed or floor mattress, with headlamp or lamp lighting, variable bed height and surfaces, family members and pets in the room, portable suture kit, and no institutional control of the space.

Minor injuries: assessment of small first-degree perineal, labial or periurethral tears, deciding whether suturing is indicated, and placing one to a few interrupted sutures for hemostasis or approximation, often in a hospital or birth-center room minutes after delivery.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performs laparoscopic surgery on pig soft tissue without human help
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot ... supervised-autonomous laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis suturing in living pigs in a research/animal-lab operating setting; it relied on near-infrared markers placed by humans and on exposed, ported bowel tissue, and has not been applied to human patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to perineal laceration repair, but the transfer fails: STAR sutures a single tubular bowel structure presented through laparoscopic ports in an anesthetized animal with human-placed fluorescent markers, whereas perineal repair requires grading the tear, locating a retracted apex, infiltrating local anesthetic, and closing three tissue layers on an awake, moving human in an actively bleeding field.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy) on a da Vinci platform
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning | Science Robotics
sources.claim: SRT-H, the current frontier of autonomous surgical robotics, completed the clipping-and-cutting phase of cholecystectomy fully autonomously, but only on ex vivo pig gallbladders in a laboratory bench setup — not on live patients and not for wound closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of a surgical phase. Cited to establish the state of the art as of 2026: autonomy is demonstrated on excised animal tissue mounted in a lab rig, so it does not substantiate completing a multi-layer repair on an awake postpartum human in any environment.

sources.system: Surgical robotics autonomy landscape (STAR, autonomous laparoscopic anastomosis)
sources.title: ArthroCut: Autonomous Policy Learning for Robotic Bone Resection in Knee Arthroplasty
sources.claim: Reviews of surgical autonomy as of 2026 place STAR and porcine anastomosis as the landmark autonomous soft-tissue results, with clinical practice still spanning teleoperation and shared control rather than autonomous execution on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue suturing generally. Used only as corroboration that no autonomous suturing system has moved beyond animal/ex vivo models to patient care; it supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Perform post-partum health assessments of mothers and babies at regular intervals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital or birth-center inpatient postpartum rounds in the first 24-48 hours: midwife enters the mother's room, takes vitals, palpates the uterine fundus for tone and height, inspects perineal tears/sutures or a cesarean incision, quantifies lochia, checks legs for DVT signs, assesses breasts and observes a breastfeeding latch, then examines the newborn (weight, color/jaundice, cord stump, tone, reflexes, heart/lung auscultation, feeding and output), and documents findings with a plan.

Clinic/office postpartum visit at 1-2 weeks and again at ~6 weeks: blood pressure, weight, abdominal and pelvic/speculum exam for uterine involution and healing, incision or perineal check, breast exam, review of bleeding and pain, depression screening and contraception counseling, plus a hands-on component such as pelvic floor assessment.

Home postpartum visit 24-72 hours after an out-of-hospital birth: midwife travels to a family's home with a kit, assesses mother (vitals, fundus, perineum, lochia, breasts) on a bed or couch in variable lighting, weighs the newborn on a portable sling scale, performs a full newborn exam including jaundice/bilirubin check, newborn screening heel stick and pulse oximetry, amid pets, siblings and clutter.

Immediate postpartum assessments at intervals during the first 1-2 hours in the birth room (hospital L&D or birth center): repeated fundal checks and massage, quantified blood-loss assessment, maternal vitals, perineal inspection, plus newborn Apgar scoring, temperature, respiratory effort and first latch during skin-to-skin.

Newborn-focused follow-up visit at day 3-5 (clinic or birth center): undress and weigh the infant, assess hydration, jaundice by exam and transcutaneous/serum bilirubin, cord and skin, hips and reflexes, observe feeding and counsel the mother, with brief maternal check.

sources.title: This Humanoid AI Robot Is Being Tested in Hospitals—Plus 7 More Transforming Healthcare
sources.claim: The most widely deployed hospital robot, Diligent Robotics' Moxi, autonomously navigates hospitals to run logistics (supplies, specimens, pharmacy deliveries) and is explicitly limited to non-patient-facing tasks; it performs no clinical examination of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital nursing-support work in the same E2 setting (postpartum units, corridors). It bounds what deployed clinical-setting robots do — transport, not maternal/newborn physical assessment — so no transfer to hands-on postpartum exam exists.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi is deployed at scale in US hospitals (25+ hospitals, over one million autonomous deliveries), confirming that the mature clinical robot fleet performs materials transport rather than patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital delivery. Cited to establish the state of deployed healthcare robotics in the same E2 facilities; it involves no contact examination of mothers or infants, so it does not transfer to postpartum assessment.

sources.developer: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai and collaborators
sources.title: iApp: An Autonomous Inspection, Auscultation, Percussion, and Palpation Platform
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic physical examination remains a laboratory proof of concept: the iApp platform performed automated inspection/auscultation/percussion/palpation on 30 healthy young volunteers, classifying abdominal regions, not producing a clinical assessment of a postpartum patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated abdominal physical examination, the closest analogue to fundal palpation. It is a healthy-volunteer feasibility study limited to region classification, so it does not substantiate completing a whole postpartum maternal or newborn assessment at worker quality.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound systems can acquire images of a positioned adult subject using force control and visual servoing, but they cover only one imaging sub-step and remain research/pilot systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous contact-based patient scanning. It shows controlled probe placement on a cooperative, positioned adult torso, but not perineal/breast inspection, newborn handling, or the integrated clinical judgment a postpartum assessment requires.

tasks.label: Test patients' hemoglobin, hematocrit, and blood glucose levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine prenatal visit in a midwifery office or hospital-affiliated clinic: midwife (or the practice's draw station) performs antecubital venipuncture on a seated pregnant patient for the prenatal panel including CBC (hemoglobin/hematocrit); tubes labeled, order of draw observed, sent to the practice or hospital lab; results reviewed and charted.

Point-of-care capillary test at an office or birth-center visit: fingerstick with a lancet, blood drawn into a HemoCue cuvette (or microhematocrit capillary spun in a table centrifuge), analyzer read within minutes, value charted and acted on the same visit (e.g., iron therapy).

Gestational diabetes screening/monitoring in the clinic: patient drinks 50 g glucola, venous draw one hour later for plasma glucose (or a fasting/2-hour venous glucose for a 3-hour GTT); specimen sent to the chemistry analyzer, result interpreted.

Home visit by a home-birth midwife (prenatal, intrapartum, or postpartum): fingerstick hemoglobin on a portable analyzer and/or glucometer glucose check performed in the client's living room or bedroom, with variable lighting, seating, and no institutional control of the space.

Intrapartum or immediate postpartum testing at the bedside in a hospital L&D room or birth center: hemoglobin/hematocrit check after postpartum hemorrhage on a patient lying in bed, glucose checks on a laboring diabetic patient, or a newborn heel-stick glucose in the first hours of life; results needed stat.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Aletta, an autonomous robotic phlebotomy device, performed venipunctures on 1,633 routine outpatients across Dutch hospitals with a 94.5% first-stick success rate and 0.6% mild adverse events, comparable to human phlebotomists.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: obtaining the blood specimen that hemoglobin, hematocrit and glucose testing requires. Trial excluded pregnant women for EU MDR benefit-risk reasons, not technical ones; antecubital venipuncture is unchanged in pregnancy.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The device performs the venipuncture sequence autonomously (vein finding by NIR/Doppler ultrasound, disinfection, needle insertion, tube filling, bandaging) with one trained professional supervising up to three devices; the human only loads a cartridge of labeled tubes.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The robot was used on unselected patients arriving at hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments for routine blood draws — an institution-controlled clinical facility, not a purpose-built robot cell.

sources.title: Vitestro Raises $70 Million in Oversubscribed Series B Financing to Advance Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy and Commercial Readiness
sources.claim: Aletta is CE-marked and is being placed in European clinical settings for diagnostic blood collection (full European commercial launch planned for 2027; no FDA authorization yet).

sources.system: MagicNurse intelligent puncture blood collection robot (and Fudan-affiliated hospital blood collection robot)
sources.title: Intelligent blood collection robot: key technologies, clinical applications, and future challenges (Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology)
sources.claim: Intelligent blood-collection robots are in routine hospital service in China: three MagicNurse puncture robots staff a blood-collection area at the First Hospital of Anhui ... that drew blood from over 5,100 patients, and a robot at Zhongshan/Sun Yat-sen Hospital of Fudan University achieved a 94.3% puncture success rate over 6,255 patients.

sources.developer: Hitachi High-Tech Corporation with Fujita Health University Hospital
sources.title: Hospital robots collect and deliver blood samples (Nature partner content)
sources.claim: An automated fingertip blood-sampling device trialled at Fujita Health University Hospital maps finger capillaries with near-infrared imaging, pricks the finger and collects up to 400 µL, with results well correlated to venous samples in volunteers.
sources.transferJustification: Capillary fingerstick sampling is the collection step of point-of-care hemoglobin and glucose testing; the device is a prototype under hospital trial and does not itself report a test result.

sources.system: cobas clinical chemistry analyzers (laboratory analysis of robot-drawn tubes)
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Specimens collected by the robot were analyzed on standard automated clinical chemistry platforms in the hospital laboratories, and robot-collected samples were analytically equivalent to manually collected ones.
sources.transferJustification: Related step: once the tube is drawn, the hemoglobin/hematocrit/glucose measurement itself is performed by automated analyzers, so the machine-performed chain from patient to reported result is complete inside a lab.
