tasks.label: Assist maternal patients to find physical positions that will facilitate childbirth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital labor & delivery room, unmedicated/mobile patient in first stage: midwife assesses labor progress and fetal position, then hands-on guides and physically supports the patient through position changes — walking the hall, lunging on a step stool, squatting at the bed's squat bar, kneeling over the raised head of the bed, rocking on a birth ball — steadying her body weight during contractions and adjusting monitor belts, IV pole and gown as she moves.

Hospital L&D, patient with epidural or otherwise limited mobility: midwife (usually with a nurse) rolls and repositions a partly numb adult in bed every 30–60 minutes — side-to-side with a peanut ball between the knees, semi-Fowler's, exaggerated Sims, throne/tucked positions — lifting legs, tucking wedges and pillows, moving catheter, IV lines and fetal monitor leads, and checking the tracing and patient comfort after each change.

Second stage: midwife positions the patient for pushing (supported squat, side-lying with upper leg held, hands-and-knees, semi-sitting with legs in stirrups or held by support people), holds/repositions legs between contractions, and executes rapid urgent repositioning when needed — McRoberts hyperflexion for shoulder dystocia, all-fours Gaskin maneuver, knee-chest for cord prolapse — with seconds-scale timing and coordinated force on a straining, moving body.

Hydrotherapy: midwife helps the patient step into and out of a birth tub or shower, supports her while wet and slippery, positions her kneeling over the tub rim, floating semi-reclined or seated on a shower stool, and repositions her for intermittent auscultation with a waterproof doppler.

Planned home birth (or freestanding birth center room furnished like a home): midwife works in a bedroom, bathroom or living room she did not design, using the family's bed, floor mats, a rented pool, a birth stool and rebozo, physically supporting the patient into hands-and-knees, standing lean, side-lying and stool sitting, in variable lighting and clutter with partner and family present.

sources.system: AIREC (AI-driven Robot for Embrace and Care)
sources.title: Japan tests AIREC robot to roll patients, easing caregiving challenges
sources.claim: AIREC, a 150-kg humanoid caregiving robot from Waseda University, demonstrated gently rolling a person onto their side in a laboratory setting; the project is a research effort and its developers state technological obstacles remain before wide use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repositioning a bedridden person. It is the nearest demonstrated analogue to rolling a laboring patient side-to-side, but it is a lab demonstration on a passive, cooperative subject with no clinical judgment, no line/monitor management, and no upright or ambulatory support, so it does not carry over to assisting a laboring patient into birthing positions.

sources.title: Eldercare robot helps people sit and stand, and catches them if they fall | MIT News
sources.claim: MIT's E-BAR robotic handlebars can support a person's full body weight and lift them from sitting to standing, but the current version is a prototype operated by remote control, with autonomy only planned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically supporting an adult's body weight through sit-to-stand and bathtub entry, the closest analogue to steadying a laboring woman into squats or helping her into a birth tub. It cannot support a positive judgment because it is remote-controlled and a laboratory prototype.

sources.developer: RIKEN and Sumitomo Riko Company Limited
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the RIKEN/Sumitomo Riko nursing-care robot able to lift a patient from bed to wheelchair and assist standing, was an experimental system, and the research center developing it closed in March 2015.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-body patient handling and transfer. This is the most-cited hands-on patient-handling robot; it was operated by a caregiver via tactile guidance, never commercialized, and the program was discontinued, so it substantiates no autonomous positioning of a laboring patient.

sources.system: Two-stage soft growing robot for patient repositioning
sources.title: Dynamic Modeling and Model Predictive Control of Soft Growing Robot for Safe and Assisted Patient Repositioning
sources.claim: A two-stage soft growing robot ... assisting patient repositioning from supine to side-lying is at the modeling-and-control research stage as of mid-2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-bed repositioning of a patient. Shows that even the narrowest sub-step of this task (a supine-to-side roll) remains a laboratory control-theory problem in 2026, rather than a fielded capability.

tasks.label: Assess birthing environments to ensure cleanliness, safety, and the availability of appropriate supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital labor & delivery suite: CNM walks the assigned birth room before/at a laboring patient's admission — checks the room was cleaned after the prior turnover, that the infant radiant warmer is plugged in and warming, wall oxygen and suction work, neonatal bag-mask/laryngoscope and delivery instrument pack are present and sterile, oxytocin and hemorrhage drugs are stocked, bed breaks down correctly, lighting and floor are clear of cords/trash; calls housekeeping or fetches missing items.

Between-birth / shift-change supply audit and restock in a hospital or birth-center birth room: counting consumables in the delivery cart and cabinets, checking expiration dates on drugs and sterile packs, verifying oxygen cylinder pressure and battery charge on the resuscitaire, and replenishing from the supply room so the room is 'birth-ready'.

Freestanding birth center suite preparation: midwife checks room warmth, cleanliness of tub/shower and linens, fills/tests the birth tub, verifies emergency kit contents (portable O2 tank, neonatal resuscitation gear, anti-hemorrhagic medications, IV supplies, suture), and confirms transfer equipment and route are ready.

Planned home birth: at the ~36-week home visit and again on arrival in labor, the midwife assesses the client's own home — which room and surface will be used, lighting, heat, hot water and electricity, floor protection, stairs/access for a stretcher, pets and other children, phone signal — and confirms the family assembled the birth kit supplies, filling gaps from her own bag.

Non-standard or improvised setting: precipitous birth in a triage room, ED bay, vehicle, shelter, or a rural/underserved clinic where the midwife must judge on the spot whether the space is clean and safe enough and assemble whatever supplies are at hand.

sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs repeatable autonomous Autowalk inspection missions in industrial facilities covering thermal monitoring, acoustic leak detection ..., and can now use its arm to open doors autonomously to move room to room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine industrial inspection rounds. It is the same act as a room-readiness walk-through — traverse a fixed route, verify equipment state from gauges/indicators, log anomalies — with comparable objects (valves, gauges, panels) and no fine clinical precision required.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics Spot uses DeepMind for machinery inspections
sources.claim: Spot's Orbit AIVI reasoning layer lets the robot visually read analogue gauges, detect ... on industrial sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: safety/condition inspection of a plant. Spill detection and gauge reading are the cleanliness and equipment-status components of a birth-room readiness check, on comparable object scales.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomous shelf-scanning robot is deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores, capturing shelf-level data on product availability and flagging out-of-stocks in place of manual associate scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf stock verification. 'Availability of appropriate supplies' is the same verification act — comparing what is present at known storage positions against an expected list — on similarly sized packaged goods.

sources.title: RFID inventory robot - TORY® - METRALABS - autonomous / mobile
sources.claim: MetraLabs' TORY RFID inventory robot navigates stores fully autonomously and captures about 99% of RFID-tagged articles, replacing manual inventory counts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous stocktaking. Where supplies are tagged and held at known positions, presence/absence verification for a birth room's consumables is the identical perception problem.

sources.title: BD Rowa - store & pick medications automatically
sources.claim: BD Rowa automated pharmacy storage-and-picking robots run a purpose-built machine stockroom with optical expiry-date recognition at input and continuous stock management by batch and expiry, cited at 99.9% reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated medication stock management. It covers the expiry-date and stock-level portion of 'availability of appropriate supplies' for exactly the drug packages a midwife checks, in a purpose-built (E1) robotic stockroom.

sources.title: Serve Robotics agreement to acquire Diligent Robotics (SEC Exhibit 99.1)
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed in over 25 US hospitals, having completed more than 1.25 million fetch-and-deliver runs of supplies and medications.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetch-and-delivery. It substantiates the remediation half of 'ensure availability of supplies' — retrieving missing items from central supply to the unit — in real hospital corridors.

sources.title: GSX 2018: Cobalt Robotics Adds Leak and Spill Detection to Security Robots
sources.claim: Cobalt Robotics' indoor patrol robots autonomously patrol human-occupied buildings and can be programmed to detect leaks and spills in a defined area and notify a remote specialist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor facility patrol. It shows gross cleanliness/safety anomaly detection inside human work facilities, but only for open floor areas — not contents of carts, cabinets or clinical equipment function.

sources.title: UV Robot Automates Coronavirus Disinfection, Streamlines Hospital Processes
sources.claim: UVD Robots' self-navigating ultraviolet robots disinfect hospital patient rooms and operating theatres autonomously in 10-20 minutes and are deployed in hospitals internationally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital room turnover hygiene. It shows machines act on clinical-room cleanliness in real E2 hospitals, but the robot executes a disinfection cycle; it does not inspect or judge whether the room is birth-ready.

tasks.label: Provide comfort and relaxation measures for mothers in labor through interventions such as massage, breathing techniques, hydrotherapy, or music.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital labor & delivery room, active first-stage labor: midwife applies hands-on comfort — sacral counterpressure and low-back massage timed to contractions, hip squeezes, shoulder/foot massage — while the laboring woman shifts between birth ball, hands-and-knees, side-lying and standing, and while the midwife simultaneously watches fetal heart tones, contraction pattern and maternal response, adjusting technique to her verbal and nonverbal feedback over several hours.

Hospital L&D room, non-contact comfort: coaching paced breathing and relaxation through contractions, verbal reassurance and reframing, dimming lights, setting up the mother's music/playlist, offering ice chips and cool cloths to the face and neck, warm blankets, repositioning pillows and the bed, and coaching the partner to help.

Hydrotherapy: midwife helps a laboring woman (with IV/monitor leads, unsteady, sometimes needing physical support) into and out of a shower or deep birth tub, sets and checks water temperature, directs the warm spray onto her back or braces her in the tub during contractions, monitors her and the fetus intermittently, and gets her out safely if labor progresses or complications arise.

Freestanding birth center suite: continuous one-to-one labor support — rebozo sifting, counterpressure, massage with oils, aromatherapy, music, encouraging position changes and slow dancing, with minimal technology and the midwife present at the bedside for hours.

Planned home birth in the client's own home: comfort measures improvised in whatever space exists — massage on a bed, sofa or bathroom floor, filling and managing an inflatable birth pool, moving furniture, working around pets, family members and variable lighting and heating.

sources.title: AI-Powered Massages? Automated Massage Robots Already at Work | Associated Bodywork & Massage Professionals
sources.claim: Aescape is a commercially deployed, autonomous two-arm massage robot built into a proprietary table, installed in gym/spa locations; it is the most capable fielded massage robot but works only on a client lying still on its own table in a spa setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = therapeutic massage. It does not transfer to labor comfort: the robot requires a stationary client positioned on its purpose-built table, addresses posterior-body muscle groups on a booked 15-60 minute program, and cannot follow a laboring woman through changing upright positions, time pressure to contractions, or combine massage with fetal/maternal surveillance.

sources.title: Aescape | Contraindications
sources.claim: Aescape's own safety documentation lists pregnancy as a contraindication, i.e. the system is not to be used on pregnant clients at all, let alone women in labor.
sources.transferJustification: Directly rules out transfer of the leading fielded massage robot to any instance of this task, all of which involve a pregnant woman in labor.

sources.title: Massage robot iYU provides relaxation in everyday life | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Capsix's iYU single-arm massage robot is offered for wellness settings, but the developer describes full autonomy as still under development, with external intervention otherwise needed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = seated/lying back massage in a spa. Autonomy is not established and the client must be seated/lying at the machine, so it cannot support labor-support judgments.

sources.developer: I-SUPPORT EU consortium (NTUA, UCL and partners)
sources.title: I-Support: A robotic platform of an assistive bathing robot for the elderly population — Robotics and Autonomous Systems
sources.claim: Robotic assistance with washing/showering a person exists only as a research prototype (motorized chair plus soft robotic arm in a fixed instrumented bathroom), not as a deployed system that moves an unsteady person into and out of a tub.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = assisted bathing. It does not transfer to labor hydrotherapy: it is a prototype that scrubs a seated user in a fixed shower under user/carer commands, and cannot transfer, support or supervise a laboring woman in a deep birth tub.

sources.developer: York St John University / simulator manufacturer
sources.title: Mama Anne robot gives birth to train midwifery students at York St John | Fox News
sources.claim: The only robots actually present in midwifery labor settings are childbirth-simulation manikins used to train students — machines that receive care rather than provide comfort measures to a real laboring woman.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to show the state of robotics in labor rooms; it is a patient simulator, so it provides no capability to perform this task and supports no positive judgment.

tasks.label: Collect specimens for use in laboratory tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine prenatal venipuncture in a midwifery office/clinic: seated, cooperative adult patient; midwife applies tourniquet, draws maternal venous blood for the initial prenatal panel, CBC/antibody screen, or 24-28 week glucose and anemia labs, fills and labels several vacuum tubes, and packages them for the reference lab.

Urine specimen at a prenatal office visit: midwife labels a cup, gives clean-catch instructions, receives the voided sample from the patient, runs a point-of-care dipstick and/or transfers and packages the sample for culture at the lab.

Genital-tract specimens during a pelvic exam in the clinic: 35-37 week vaginal/rectal group B strep swab, Pap smear using speculum and cervical brush/spatula, chlamydia/gonorrhea swabs; midwife positions and drapes the patient, inserts the speculum or swab, and transfers the sample to transport medium.

Maternal blood specimens on a hospital labor & delivery or postpartum unit: CBC, type and screen, or repeat labs drawn at the bedside from a woman lying in a bed, often with an IV in one arm, contractions, epidural, or an infant at the breast.

Specimens from the newborn or placenta at birth: umbilical cord blood sample for blood type/Coombs or cord blood gases drawn from the clamped cord, and newborn screening heel-stick blood spots collected onto a filter-paper card from a squirming neonate.

Home-visit specimen collection by a community/home-birth midwife: venous blood draw for prenatal or postpartum labs at the client's kitchen table or couch, variable seating and lighting, pets and family present, supplies carried in a bag and specimens couriered to the lab.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performed venipuncture on 1,633 patients in routine clinical use in the outpatient phlebotomy departments of three Dutch hospitals, with 94.5% first-stick success and analytical equivalence to manually collected samples.

sources.title: Aletta for Laboratory specialists - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta performs the whole draw autonomously alongside manual draw stations - tourniquet, vein identification by near-infrared and Doppler ultrasound, needle insertion, filling of up to 10 pre-labeled tubes, and bandaging - with one trained supervisor overseeing up to three devices.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: The Aletta blood-drawing robot received an EU CE mark in August 2024 and has been commercially deployed in European healthcare settings since March 2025.

sources.date: 2026 (product page; system in clinical labs since 2009 JCM evaluation)
sources.title: Copan WASP DT: Walk-Away Specimen Processor | Beckman Coulter
sources.claim: The Copan WASP walk-away specimen processor is a commercial robotic front-end that autonomously uncaps and samples clinical containers, labels plates and slides, and plates quantitative urine cultures using the CLSI 1 microlitre loop protocol in clinical microbiology laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-analytical processing of clean-catch urine specimens. The midwife's urine step after the patient voids - handling the container, labeling, and transferring the sample into the testing medium - involves the same objects (standard urine containers and tubes), the same millilitre-scale precision, and the same clinical-laboratory setting, so a machine that does it walk-away covers the collection-to-lab portion once the specimen is presented to it.

sources.title: Sysmex UN-Series | Urinalysis analyser
sources.claim: The Sysmex UN-Series is a commercially deployed, fully automated urinalysis line that mechanically handles urine sample tubes and performs test-strip and particle analysis without hands-on work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated urine test-strip and sediment analysis. It substitutes for the dipstick reading and sample handling the midwife performs on a collected urine specimen, on the same specimen type and containers, once the sample is presented in a standard tube.

sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device (Center for Phlebotomy Education)
sources.claim: Independent phlebotomy-education commentary reports that the autonomous phlebotomy device is scoped to routine, straightforward outpatient venipuncture and does not handle pediatric draws, patients requiring special positioning, alternative-site draws, or emergency situations.

tasks.label: Respond to breech birth presentations by applying methods such as exercises or external version.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine third-trimester prenatal visit in a midwifery clinic or birth center (~34-37 weeks): midwife performs Leopold's maneuvers on the bare abdomen, confirms breech lie with a handheld/bedside ultrasound, then counsels the woman and hands-on demonstrates and spots positional techniques (forward-leaning inversion, breech tilt, hands-and-knees), positioning her safely on table/floor and documenting the plan.

External cephalic version at ~37 weeks in a hospital labor-and-delivery unit with OB backup: NST and ultrasound confirmation, IV/tocolytic, then the midwife places both hands on the abdomen, disengages the breech from the pelvis and applies firm sustained pressure to rotate the fetus 180 degrees over several minutes, monitoring fetal heart rate continuously, aborting for bradycardia or maternal pain, plus re-scan and post-procedure monitoring.

Community/home-birth midwife on a home prenatal visit finds a suspected breech at term: palpates on the client's own bed or couch in a variable, uncontrolled home layout, confirms with a portable ultrasound, teaches positional exercises with the partner present, and arranges referral for hospital ECV or a change of birth plan.

Adjunct-modality visit in clinic for a confirmed breech: midwife applies moxibustion/acupressure at BL67 (bilateral fifth toes) for 15-20 minutes while monitoring fetal movement, or teaches the woman and partner to perform the moxa/acupressure protocol daily at home, then re-checks presentation at a follow-up palpation.

Undiagnosed breech found at admission or in early labor at a hospital or birth center: midwife re-assesses by palpation, vaginal exam and bedside ultrasound, coaches maternal positioning to relieve pressure, and either supports a vaginal breech birth with hands-on maneuvers or summons OB/arranges transfer, under time pressure with the woman contracting and moving.

sources.system: Manual external cephalic version (clinical procedure reference, not a robot)
sources.title: External Cephalic Version (ECV): Procedure & Risks
sources.claim: External cephalic version, the core physical method named in the task, is a two-handed manual manipulation of a pregnant abdomen with firm sustained pressure for several minutes, with pre- and post-procedure fetal assessment; no robotic system performing it was found in search.
sources.transferJustification: Included to characterize the physical demands of the instance (force, ultrasound-guided fetal manipulation, abort criteria) against which candidate robotic systems were assessed; it is not evidence of a robotic capability.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Beijing Tsinghua Changgung Hospital team
sources.title: Beyond hospital reach: Autonomous lightweight ultrasound robot for liver sonography
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound has been demonstrated on humans in a hospital sonography department, but only for imaging organs such as the liver/aorta - it does not perform obstetric palpation, fetal manipulation, or patient counselling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous probe placement on a human abdomen. Cited to test whether the assessment step of the breech instance could be automated; it covers imaging only, with no force-based fetal manipulation or counselling, so it cannot complete the instance.

sources.system: Robotic fetal ultrasonography platform / DNN-based autonomous fetal scan motion generation
sources.developer: Tsumura & Iwata, Waseda University (and follow-on Advanced Robotics work)
sources.title: Autonomous scanning motion generation adapted to individual differences in abdominal shape for robotic fetal ultrasound
sources.claim: Robotic fetal ultrasound scanning remains at the level of research prototypes evaluated on phantoms and scan-motion models, not a clinically accepted autonomous obstetric examination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic scanning of a pregnant abdomen. Cited as the closest work to the assessment sub-step; proof-of-concept work with agar phantoms and scan-motion models does not establish worker-quality determination of fetal presentation, let alone version.

sources.developer: University Hospital of North Norway / Norwegian rural telemedicine programme
sources.title: Introduction of robot-assisted obstetric ultrasound in rural Northern Norway
sources.claim: Obstetric robotic ultrasound that is actually in clinical use is teleoperated: a remote obstetrician drives the probe, so it does not satisfy the autonomy requirement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obstetric imaging by robot in a clinic. Shows the deployed obstetric robots are human-driven, so they cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous breech assessment or version.

sources.developer: Shanghai University of Engineering Science (Prof. Xiong Genliang team)
sources.title: Intelligent Robot for Moxibustion Has Come-Reducing Burn Risks & Easing Doctors' Workload, With Sales Over 100 Million yuan
sources.claim: A moxibustion robot executes acupoint heat therapy on patients in hospital treatment rooms after a clinician selects the points on a tablet; it applies moxa to back acupoints, not fetal-version protocols, and performs no assessment or counselling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of moxibustion to a patient in a clinical facility. Cited for the moxibustion instance; it covers only the heat-application sub-step on clinician-selected back points, not breech confirmation, the BL67 protocol, response monitoring or client teaching.

sources.developer: Aescape (deployed at Massage Envy, Equinox locations)
sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic manipulation of human bodies exists commercially only as generic soft-tissue massage on a fixed table in wellness studios; it involves no diagnostic assessment and no force-critical manipulation of a fetus.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot arms applying controlled pressure to a human body in a commercial facility. Cited as the upper bound of deployed human-contact manipulation; it targets muscle groups on a prone client and cannot substitute for ultrasound-guided fetal rotation on a pregnant abdomen.

tasks.label: Perform annual gynecologic exams, including pap smears and breast exams.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine annual well-woman visit in a midwifery/OB-GYN office exam room: healthy adult patient undresses and is draped; midwife reviews history, performs clinical breast exam (bilateral palpation, axillary nodes), external genital inspection, speculum insertion, cervical visualization, liquid-based cytology/HPV brush collection, bimanual pelvic exam, then labels the specimen and documents findings.

Annual exam at a community health center, FQHC or family-planning clinic: high-throughput schedule, chaperone present, added STI swabs and contraception counseling, patients with limited English or discomfort; same breast exam plus speculum/pap plus bimanual sequence performed on standard exam table with stirrups.

Annual exam in patients where the exam is technically or emotionally difficult: high BMI, postmenopausal atrophy or stenosis, prior pelvic surgery, an adolescent's first exam, or a trauma survivor needing paced, consent-driven handling; requires speculum size changes, repositioning, and verbal coaching to obtain an adequate cervical sample.

Annual exam that turns up an abnormality: palpable breast lump or nipple discharge, visible cervical lesion, friable cervix with bleeding, or abnormal discharge; midwife modifies the exam, takes additional swabs/samples, characterizes the finding by palpation and inspection, and arranges referral or follow-up.

Well-woman/gynecologic exam performed outside a fixed clinic: home-birth or community midwife doing the exam in the client's bedroom or living room on a bed, or a rural/mobile outreach visit in a borrowed room or van, with portable lamp, speculum kit and sample transport media.

sources.system: IRIS (robotIc Radial palpatIon mechaniSm for breast examination)
sources.developer: University of Bristol / Bristol Robotics Laboratory
sources.title: Your next breast exam could be performed by a robot
sources.claim: IRIS, a 3D-printed robotic radial palpation manipulator built to perform clinical breast examination, has been evaluated only in simulation and on a silicone breast phantom, not on patients; it represents the state of the art for robotic breast palpation.
sources.transferJustification: Clinical breast examination is one component of the annual gynecologic exam; the evidence shows the component itself is only at phantom-stage prototype, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole exam.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system
sources.developer: Chinese academic hospital research group (Lin et al.), published in Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning systems that contact patients with force control exist only as research systems tested on healthy volunteers for imaging reproducibility; they perform imaging, not physical examination or specimen collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot-to-patient body-surface contact under force control. It is the closest demonstrated patient-contact autonomy, but it only sweeps a probe over skin on healthy volunteers in a research setting; it does not palpate for lumps, insert a speculum, or collect cervical cells, so capability does not carry over.

sources.system: Lifeline Robotics autonomous throat swabbing robot
sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics (spin-out of University of Southern Denmark)
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: The closest demonstrated robotic collection of a clinical specimen from a human body orifice is an autonomous throat-swabbing prototype that inserts a swab into a seated person's open mouth in a purpose-built booth; it remained a prototype pending medical-device approval.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous swab-based specimen collection from a body orifice. It does not transfer to a pap smear, which requires draping, speculum insertion and opening in a collapsible cavity, visual identification of the cervix and transformation zone, brush sampling, plus a separate breast and bimanual exam; the swab robot handles one rigid, directly visible, patient-cooperative target and never moved beyond prototype.

tasks.label: Treat patients' symptoms with alternative health care methods such as herbs or hydrotherapy.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Home birth: midwife sets up and fills the client's birth pool (hose to faucet, liner, pump), keeps water at 95-100F, helps the laboring woman in and out, pours warm water over her back, applies warm perineal compresses, listens to fetal heart with a waterproof doppler between contractions, and drains/decontaminates the tub afterward — in a bathroom or living room she did not design.

Freestanding birth center or hospital LDR room: midwife uses the built-in tub or shower for pain relief in active labor — adjusts water, supports position changes in and out of the water, applies warm compresses to sacrum/perineum, monitors mother and fetus, and gets the client out quickly if the fetal heart rate or labor progress requires it.

Prenatal or postpartum office visit: client reports a common complaint (nausea, heartburn, insomnia, anemia, low milk supply); midwife selects an herbal remedy, measures/blends and packages the tincture, capsules or tea, and dispenses it with dosing and safety instructions in a clinic dispensary.

Postpartum home visit: midwife prepares an herbal perineal soak or sitz bath (brews the herb infusion, fills the basin, sets it up in the client's bathroom), applies warm compresses for engorgement or a herbal poultice, and instructs the mother on continued use — in the client's own home.

In-office applied alternative therapy on a treatment table: moxibustion at BL67 for a breech presentation at 34-36 weeks, acupressure, or heat/cold therapy applied to the client's body for a defined session, in the midwife's clinic.

sources.system: Intelligent moxibustion rehabilitation robot (Shanghai Junkong Robotics / Shanghai University of Engineering Science)
sources.developer: Shanghai Junkong Robotics Co., Ltd. with Prof. Xiong Genliang's team, Shanghai University of Engineering Science
sources.title: Intelligent Robot for Moxibustion Has Come—Reducing Burn Risks & Easing Doctors' Workload, With Sales Over 100 Million yuan
sources.claim: An intelligent moxibustion robot is in service in hospital treatment rooms in Shanghai: after a clinician selects acupoints and technique on a tablet, the robotic arm localizes the acupoints in 3D, hovers over the patient's back and delivers a half-hour moxibustion therapy with infrared temperature control and body-motion detection; over a thousand patients served, burn incidence down 90%.
sources.transferJustification: Moxibustion is an alternative-medicine therapy midwives themselves apply (moxa at BL67 for breech presentation). The physical act — positioning a controlled heat source over a defined point on a client lying on a treatment table in a clinic, holding distance and temperature for ~20-30 minutes — is the same act and precision as the midwifery use.

sources.system: ABB Robot Mini Load + 3D bin-picking pharmacy automation system
sources.title: Robots revolutionize drug dispensing at Shanghai Seventh People's Hospital | News center | ABB
sources.claim: Two ABB robots autonomously store, retrieve, pick and sort medicines according to prescriptions in the inpatient pharmacy of Shanghai Seventh People's Hospital, a hospital that practices both traditional Chinese and Western medicine, dispensing more accurately than human staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: prescription dispensing. The physical work of a midwife's herbal dispensary — retrieving the right preparation, measuring/packaging it accurately, and releasing it for a named patient — is the same handling, accuracy and traceability requirement, in the same class of institutional facility.

sources.developer: Beijing hospital / unnamed integrator (reported by Xinhua)
sources.title: Inside China's 24/7 robot pharmacy - Xinhua
sources.claim: A Beijing hospital pharmacy dispenses medication to patients around the clock with a robotic arm that picks the medicine after the patient scans a code, with camera verification, in 2-3 minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient-facing dispensing. It substantiates that handing a prepared remedy directly to the patient inside a clinical facility is done autonomously today, which is the delivery step of dispensing an herbal preparation at a prenatal visit.

sources.transferJustification: Directly the herbal half of this task: handling loose, irregular botanical material, weighing it to formula and packaging it — the same objects and precision a midwife's herbal dispensary requires.

sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | spabusiness.com
sources.claim: Aescape's two-armed robotic massage tables deliver fully autonomous 15-60 minute bodywork sessions and are installed at roughly 100 commercial locations across North America (gyms, hotels and spas), including Equinox and select Massage Envy franchises.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: therapeutic bodywork. It shows force-controlled robotic contact with a human body for a timed therapy session, unsupervised, in an institution-controlled facility — the same class of hands-on complementary therapy delivered in a clinic treatment room.

sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator in the US, operates in over 25 hospital facilities and has completed more than ... — its work is fetching and delivering supplies and specimens, not hands-on patient therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the state of the art inside hospitals: the leading deployed clinical mobile manipulator performs logistics only, supporting the negative judgments for hands-on hydrotherapy and comfort care in labor.
