roles.title: Home Health Aides
roles.description: Monitor the health status of an individual with disabilities or illness, and address their health-related needs, such as changing bandages, dressing wounds, or administering medication. Work is performed under the direction of offsite or intermittent onsite licensed nursing staff. Provide assistance with routine healthcare tasks or activities of daily living, such as feeding, bathing, toileting, or ambulation. May also help with tasks such as preparing meals, doing light housekeeping, and doing laundry depending on the patient's abilities.

tasks.label: Plan, purchase, prepare, or serve meals to patients or other family members, according to prescribed diets.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Simple meal in the client's own home kitchen: aide checks the care plan (e.g., diabetic or 2g-sodium order), retrieves items from the client's fridge/pantry, makes breakfast or lunch (oatmeal, eggs, toast, sandwich, coffee) on the client's own appliances, plates it, carries it to the table, and cleans up. Layout, cookware and stock differ in every house.

Full hot meal cooked from scratch in the client's home kitchen: washing and chopping vegetables, browning meat, boiling/simmering on the client's stove, seasoning to a renal or low-sodium restriction, portioning, serving the client at the table, and storing labelled leftovers for later days.

Menu planning and grocery purchase: aide builds a week's menu around the prescribed diet, drives to a neighborhood supermarket, selects and label-checks items, pays with the client's funds/card, transports the bags to the home and puts them away in the client's kitchen.

Serving a meal to a dysphagia or bed-bound patient in the home: thickening liquids to nectar/honey consistency, cutting or pureeing food to the ordered texture, repositioning the patient upright, setting up the bedside tray, assisting with eating and monitoring for coughing/aspiration, then recording intake.

Meals for several residents in a group home, small assisted-living house, or adult day program: aide works from the facility kitchen with standing diet orders and a posted menu, cooks or reheats standardized dishes, plates by resident diet card, delivers trays to the dining room or rooms, and clears up.

sources.title: Physical AI Company Chef Robotics Completes 100 Million Servings in Production
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' ChefOS-driven robotic arms autonomously portion and assemble meal components into trays on live production lines at food companies (Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Cafe Spice), passing 100 million servings produced by April 2026 — i.e., meals built to a specified recipe/portion spec in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial meal assembly. Transfer: the physical act rated here is portioning specified ingredients into a plated meal that matches a prescribed spec; Chef's robots do exactly this across many recipes/portion sizes, though on a fixtured line rather than a home kitchen.

sources.system: Chef Robotics + Packline end-to-end meal production line
sources.title: Chef Robotics and Packline Partner on End-to-End Meal Production Automation
sources.claim: Chef Robotics systems handle high-mix production where each SKU has different ingredients, portion sizes and tray positions — the closest analogue to plating different diet-specific meals from one line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix prepared-meal manufacturing. Transfer: 'prescribed diet' plating is a variant-per-order portioning problem with the same objects (cooked proteins, grains, vegetables) and comparable portion precision.

sources.title: AI Cooking Robots Have Flopped. Will the Nosh One Be Any Different? Here's My Take
sources.claim: The Nosh One is a commercially launched countertop cooking robot that, once a user loads ingredients into its trays and cartridges, autonomously executes a multi-step hot recipe (measuring, adding at the right time, stirring, camera monitoring) from a 500+ dish library; shipments were set for summer 2026.

sources.title: Nosh AI Robot Chef Automates 500+ Recipes for Easy Home Cooking at CES 2026
sources.claim: Nosh's operating model is the E1 pattern: the human presents ingredients into fixed compartments and the machine then cooks the dish unattended, measuring and adding ingredients at the right times under camera control.

sources.title: Miso Robotics develops smaller, faster Flippy
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy fry station autonomously runs an entire hot-cooking station (basket loading, timing, shaking, dumping) and is installed in real quick-service restaurant kitchens at White Castle and Jack in the Box, showing autonomous hot cooking to a set spec in a purpose-built station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial fry-station cooking. Transfer: it demonstrates unattended hot cooking of food to a timed doneness spec, the cooking element of meal preparation, but only within a station rebuilt around the robot.

sources.title: Sweetgreen's Automated 'Infinite Kitchen' Readies for a Step Up in 2025
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline assembles and portions customer bowls on a conveyor in operating restaurants, with roughly 25 locations targeted for 2025 — a commercially operating purpose-built meal-assembly cell with exact portioning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bowl/plate assembly to order. Transfer: composing a portion-controlled meal from many ingredient bins to a per-order specification is the same physical operation as plating a diet-restricted meal.

sources.title: The technology Re:Imagining online grocery
sources.claim: Ocado's On-Grid Robotic Pick arms autonomously pick and pack grocery orders across 45,000 SKUs in live customer fulfilment centres, having completed over 350 million picks and handling about half the order volume at its Luton site — the machine-side equivalent of assembling a shopping list.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic grocery order picking and packing. Transfer: the physical content of 'purchase food per the prescribed diet' is selecting the specified grocery items and bagging them; Ocado's arms do this for a full supermarket range, with the list supplied rather than shopped in-store.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi autonomous mobile robots are deployed to run food and bus dishes in senior living dining rooms as well as restaurants and hospitals, showing autonomous tray delivery inside a structured care facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: food running in dining rooms. Transfer: covers only the 'serve' step of the task in an institutional dining room; it does not cook, plate to a diet card, or hand a tray to a resident.

sources.title: 1X's $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the 'Creepy' Factor
sources.claim: Home humanoids marketed for household chores including kitchen work are not autonomous for these tasks: 1X's NEO ships to homes with human teleoperators driving the harder chores.

sources.system: π0.5 vision-language-action model on a mobile manipulator
sources.title: π0.5: a VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: The strongest autonomous open-world home manipulation result, π0.5, covers tidying tasks in unseen homes (placing dishes in the sink, wiping spills, putting items away) and is explicitly imperfect; no cited home system cooks or plates a meal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household kitchen tidying in unseen homes. Cited to bound the home tier: it shows autonomous pick-and-place and wiping in real homes, but not ingredient retrieval, stovetop cooking, or plating to a prescribed diet.

tasks.label: Care for patients by changing bed linens, washing and ironing laundry, cleaning, or assisting with their personal care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Personal care for a frail or disabled client in the client's own home: bed bath or shower/tub bathing, perineal and incontinence care, toileting, dressing, grooming, and transfers/ambulation. Direct hand contact with a person whose skin, balance, pain and cooperation vary day to day; layout and fixtures differ in every home.

Changing bed linens in the client's home: stripping soiled or wet sheets (sometimes rolling a bedbound client side to side to change an occupied bed), fitting a fitted sheet on a sagging home mattress, making up flat sheet, blanket and pillowcases, bagging soiled linen.

Laundry on a routine home visit: gathering and sorting the client's clothes and linens, loading and running the household washer and dryer, folding, ironing shirts and linens, and putting items away in closets and drawers.
Floor cleaning on a routine home visit: vacuuming carpets and rugs, sweeping and mopping kitchen and bathroom floors, in a lived-in private residence with furniture, cords and pets.

Kitchen cleanup after preparing/serving a meal in the client's home: clearing the table, hand-washing dishes or loading/unloading the dishwasher and putting dishes away, wiping counters, stove and table, cleaning the sink, and emptying the trash.
Cleaning the client's bathroom: scrubbing toilet, sink, tub/shower and mirror, wiping grab bars and commode, mopping the floor, emptying the wastebasket, restocking towels and supplies.

sources.date: 2026-07 (vendor site, current); product commercially leased since ~2021
sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is a commercially leased, autonomous restroom-cleaning robot deployed in institutional facilities (hospitals, airports, office buildings); it cleans toilets, urinals and floors, picks up trash, navigates the building itself and refills its own water and chemicals with near-zero staff intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial restroom cleaning. Same objects and chemistry as the aide's bathroom-cleaning instance (toilets, sinks, floors, trash), same scrub/spray/vacuum precision, performed in an institution-controlled facility, so it substantiates the E2 counterfactual of that instance.

sources.title: Roborock Saros Z70 review: grasping the future, one sock at a time
sources.claim: Consumer robot vacuum-mops clean the floors of ordinary occupied homes autonomously to a standard reviewers judge excellent, including obstacle avoidance and pet hair pickup.

sources.title: Roborock Saros Z70 Review: A Robot Vacuum with a Mechanical Arm?
sources.claim: The same home robot's manipulator arm, the only shipping consumer system that picks objects off the floor, succeeds only about half the time even on the narrow set of items it recognises, so tidying and object handling in homes is not at worker reliability.

sources.system: THOR robot separator (Inwatec / JENSEN-GROUP sorting system)
sources.date: 2024 (product line installed in laundries; Inwatec product page Oct 2024)
sources.title: Creating the future in laundry automation | JENSEN-GROUP
sources.claim: In installed commercial laundry plants, the THOR robot separator automatically takes bulk soiled laundry and singulates it into the processing line at ~1,500 pieces per hour with minimal manual interaction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: institutional laundry processing. It is the same washing/ironing/folding work on the same articles (sheets, towels, garments) that the aide does by hand, executed in a purpose-built plant, so it substantiates the E1 counterfactual for the laundry instance.

sources.system: JENSEN industrial flatwork ironer lines (separators, cornerless feeders, ironers, folders, stackers)
sources.title: Industrial Flatwork Ironer | JENSEN-GROUP
sources.claim: Commercially sold flatwork finishing lines automate the whole ironing and folding chain for sheets and linens: separators, high-speed feeders, chest ironers, folders and stackers integrated by software.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial flatwork ironing and folding. Identical output (washed, ironed, folded linens) to the aide's laundry instance, produced in a purpose-built plant, supporting E1 only.

sources.title: Automation & Robotics: The Future of Textile Care (Texcare)
sources.claim: Trade coverage of textile-care automation confirms the THOR sorting robot is a fielded product using 3D camera vision, handling 1,200-1,500 items per hour of mixed soiled textiles.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the JENSEN evidence above: plant-based laundry handling, substantiating only the purpose-built (E1) environment.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: The leading consumer home humanoid performs household chores (laundry, dishwasher loading) through remote human operators rather than autonomously; autonomy for these chores has not been delivered.

sources.title: Physical Intelligence – Blog (π0.5 open-world generalization)
sources.claim: A research foundation model drove a mobile manipulator to tidy kitchens and bedrooms (dishes into sink, items into drawers, wiping) in homes not seen in training - autonomous, but a research demonstration with partial success rather than a fielded, worker-reliable service.

sources.title: Figure humanoid robot masters dishwashing after folding laundry
sources.claim: A humanoid loaded a dishwasher autonomously under the Helix vision-language-action model, handling dishes with centimetre-scale tolerance - a company demonstration in its own test kitchen, not a deployed cleaning service.

sources.title: Robotic Healthcare | Shower automation
sources.claim: The Poseidon 'hygiene robot' is an automated shower cabin in which the user, not the machine, directs washing of their own body; it substitutes for staff only where the client retains enough ability to operate it.

sources.title: Welfare Technology and User Experience: A Study of Seniors' Expectations on and First Impressions of a Robotic Shower
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed study of the same robotic shower describes it as a late prototype existing in only five units, pilot-installed in Swedish nursing homes.

sources.title: Japan tests AIREC robot to roll patients, easing caregiving challenges
sources.claim: AIREC, the most advanced caregiving humanoid for patient handling (rolling patients, transfers), remains a laboratory prototype undergoing testing in Japan, not a deployed system.

sources.title: DART: Noise Injection for Robust Imitation Learning – BAIR Blog
sources.claim: Academic robot bed-making work is limited to learning to grasp and stretch a sheet over a small bed frame in a laboratory - a sub-step of a linen change, not stripping and remaking a bed.

tasks.label: Bathe patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Complete bed bath for a bedbound client in a private home: aide gathers basin/towels, undresses the client in bed, washes face, torso, limbs, skin folds and perineum (often after incontinence), rolls the client to wash the back, rinses, pats dry, applies lotion and redresses, watching for skin breakdown and fragile skin.

Assisted tub/shower bath in the client's own bathroom for a mobility-limited but cooperative client: transfer from bed/wheelchair to a shower chair or tub bench over a threshold, adjust water, wash hair and body including areas the client cannot reach, rinse, towel dry, apply lotion and dress; tight, non-standard bathroom layouts and slip hazards.

Standby/partial assistance bath at home for a largely independent client: aide sets up, supervises for falls and dizziness, washes back, feet and hair, hands soap and towels, and helps in and out of the shower.

Bathing a client with dementia or behavioral resistance at home: coaxing, redirecting, working around refusal, agitation or grabbing, adapting mid-task (switching to a sponge bath, covering for modesty), while keeping the client safe and calm.

Bathing a resident in a group home / small assisted-living or adult family home where the aide works: accessible shared bathroom with roll-in shower or mechanical bath equipment, institutional supplies and scheduling.

sources.system: Mirai Ningen Sentakuki (human washing machine of the future)
sources.title: "Human Machine" Can Wash & Dry a Person in 15 Minutes (My Modern Met)
sources.claim: Science Co.'s 'Mirai Ningen Sentakuki' is a fully automatic bathing pod that washes and dries a seated person in about 15 minutes using water jets and microbubbles, with sensors monitoring the bather; shown at Expo 2025 and being commercialized/exported.

sources.developer: Science Co. / deployed at Mazeran Morinomiya (SOYOKAZE)
sources.title: Expo-Inspired 'Human Washing Machine' Tech Debuts in Japan's Nursing Care, Slashing Bathing Burdens — BigGo Finance
sources.claim: The Expo washing-machine technology was productized as the 'Miraburu Assist Bath', a fine-bubble care bathing unit with a side-access door, and put into operation at an assisted-living home in Osaka in June 2026; staff report that the need for scrubbing dropped dramatically.

sources.title: 福祉用具・介護ロボット出張デモ 対象用具・機器一覧表（あいちサービスロボット実用化支援センター）
sources.claim: The 'Dream Shower' is a commercially sold care bathing machine for facilities that performs washing of the bather automatically, from cleansing through lotion application, listed in a municipal care-robot/assistive-device demonstration catalogue.

sources.title: 介護用シャワー入浴装置『ドリームシャワー DS-3300-A』 タイガー医療器 | イプロスものづくり
sources.claim: The Dream Shower DS-3300-A is a stretcher-type enclosed care shower device in which a recumbent bather is washed by an automatic shower system that can wash the whole body and the hair at the same time, with an assist window for caregiver spot-washing.

sources.system: Dreamer (自動排泄処理装置 ドリーマー)
sources.title: スペースケア，『自動排泄処理装置：ドリーマー』の販売・介護保険レンタルを開始（InnerVision）
sources.claim: The 'Dreamer' automatic excretion-processing device, rentable under Japan's long-term care insurance, is worn like a diaper by bedridden users and automatically suctions urine and stool and then washes and dries the buttocks/perineum.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: perineal/peri-care cleaning of a bedbound person, which is the most soil-critical component of a bed bath; the device performs the wash-and-dry step automatically on a fixtured body region, supporting that this component can be machine-performed when the body is presented to the device.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance (arXiv)
sources.claim: RABBIT is a research robot-assisted bed-bathing system using multimodal perception and compliant wiping; it was evaluated in a lab user study with 12 participants, wiping limbs of people lying in bed.

sources.system: review of bathing assistive devices and robots
sources.title: Bathing assistive devices and robots for the elderly - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of bathing aids and robots for the elderly concludes that no convenient, safe and effective autonomous bathing mode exists yet for severely disabled elderly people, with reclining bathing aids remaining the most widely used devices.

sources.developer: BioRobotics Institute, Scuola Superiore Sant'Anna and EU consortium
sources.title: A robotic shower system: Acceptance and ethical issues (PMC)
sources.claim: The EU I-SUPPORT project built a robotic shower system with a motorized chair and a soft robotic shower arm that washes the back and lower limbs, validated in clinical trials with elderly users; it targets partial washing tasks rather than a complete bath.

tasks.label: Maintain records of patient care, condition, progress, or problems to report and discuss observations with supervisor or case manager.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide patients with help moving in and out of beds, baths, wheelchairs, or automobiles and with dressing and grooming.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private home/apartment: aide helps a partially weight-bearing elderly client transfer from bed to wheelchair or recliner — repositions the client to sit at the bed edge, applies a gait belt, positions and locks the chair, cues and stabilizes the client through a stand-pivot transfer, manages oxygen tubing/catheter lines, and settles the client with cushions and footrests.

Private home: non-weight-bearing or bariatric client transferred with a manual sling (Hoyer) lift or sit-to-stand lift, or by a two-person assist — rolling the client in bed to place the sling, hooking straps, raising, guiding the swinging body over to wheelchair/commode, lowering and removing the sling, checking skin and comfort.

Dressing assistance in the client's bedroom: selecting clothing, donning underwear, pants, socks/shoes, pullover or button shirt for a client with hemiparesis, contracture, arthritis or dementia; guiding the affected limb through sleeves first, rolling the client side to side in bed to pull pants over hips, fastening buttons/zippers, sometimes donning compression stockings or a brace.

Grooming at the bedside or bathroom sink: brushing and combing (sometimes tangled or long) hair, shaving with an electric razor, oral/denture care, applying deodorant, lotion and skin barrier cream, filing nails, adjusting eyeglasses and hearing aids — with the client seated in a wheelchair or propped in bed.

Bath/shower transfer in a standard home bathroom: undressing the client, transferring onto a tub bench or shower chair over the tub rim or through a narrow shower entry, supporting a wet, slippery, sometimes unsteady body during and after the bath, then transferring back out, drying and re-dressing.

Automobile transfer at the driveway or curb: wheeling the client outdoors, positioning the wheelchair at the car door, assisting a stand-pivot or scoot-board transfer into the passenger seat, lifting legs in, buckling the belt, folding and stowing the wheelchair or walker, and reversing the process at the clinic entrance.

sources.system: Hug T1 / L1 transfer support robot
sources.title: Electrocardiogram and respiration recordings show a reduction in the physical burden on professional caregivers when performing care tasks with a transfer support robot
sources.claim: Fuji's 'Hug' transfer support robot, commercially deployed in Japanese nursing facilities, lifts a care recipient at the push of a ..., but the caregiver must position the recipient against the device and then push the device to the destination — the human performs the task with a powered aid rather than the robot completing a transfer autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the transfer task in instances 0-1, but the cited operation is caregiver-positioned and button-driven step-by-step, so it cannot support an autonomous-completion judgment.

sources.title: Care Service Robot is First in the World to Obtain ISO13482 | Panasonic Newsroom Global
sources.claim: Panasonic's Resyone, the first ISO 13482-certified care robot, is an electric care bed whose half detaches as a reclining wheelchair; a caregiver still positions and operates it, and one caregiver is still required for the transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Same bed-to-wheelchair transfer as instances 0-1; cited as the most mature commercial 'transfer robot', but it is an operator-driven mechanism, not an autonomous system completing the transfer.

sources.title: Giving patients a lift - the robotic nursing assistant (RoNA) | Semantic Scholar
sources.claim: Hstar Technologies' Robotic Nursing Assistant (RoNA) is a research prototype able to lift patients up to 500 lb in healthcare facilities, but a nurse guides the lift; it was never deployed as an autonomous transfer system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the lifting/transfer task; nurse-guided operation means it cannot support an autonomous completion judgment even in a purpose-built setting.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for robot-assisted dressing (Kinova/robot arm in lab)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute (Erickson/Bhattacharjee-affiliated group) with IIT Madras
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions (arXiv 2509.12741)
sources.claim: The most advanced robot-assisted dressing system (CMU, 2025) autonomously pulls a pre-grasped sleeve onto a single arm of a seated participant in a lab, evaluated with 12 participants over 264 trials; it does not perform whole-garment or lower-body dressing and requires manual initialization of the shoulder point.
sources.transferJustification: Single-arm sleeve dressing is a sub-step of the dressing instance; it is cited to show the ceiling of demonstrated capability, which falls short of dressing a dependent client in full garments.

sources.title: Soft and Compliant Contact-Rich Hair Manipulation and Care (arXiv 2501.02630)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic hair care (MOE-Hair, 2025) demonstrates head patting, finger combing along a user-defined trajectory, and hair grasping with a soft end-effector, tested on a sensorized mannequin head and rated by 12 participants — a laboratory sub-task, not a complete grooming routine.
sources.transferJustification: Hair combing is one element of the grooming instance; cited to show demonstrated grooming capability is limited to isolated hair-contact skills under user-specified trajectories.

sources.system: Survey of learning-based robotic caregiving (feeding, grooming, dressing, body repositioning)
sources.title: Feeding, grooming, dressing, and body repositioning: categorizing four pillars of learning-based manipulation for robotic caregiving
sources.claim: A March 2026 survey of learning-based robotic caregiving identifies body repositioning (repositioning limbs, transferring body weight) as an open research pillar demanding strength, whole-body coordination and compliant ..., indicating no fielded autonomous system performs human transfers.
sources.transferJustification: Covers exactly the manipulation classes in this task (dressing, grooming, body repositioning); establishes that these remain research problems as of 2026.

sources.title: 1X Details NEO's 'Human-in-the-Loop' Strategy and Hardware as $20,000 Pre-Orders Go Live | Humanoids Daily
sources.claim: Home assistive mobile manipulators evaluated with professional caregivers (Stretch) autonomously perform item fetching and delivery and telepresence, not physical handling of the person; the consumer home humanoid NEO relies on remote human pilots for complex household tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Cited for the in-home robot category most often claimed for caregiving; shows the physically capable home robots shipping in 2026 are teleoperated for non-trivial manipulation and do not touch or move the client.

tasks.label: Check patients' pulse, temperature, and respiration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine scheduled vital-signs check during a home visit: an alert, cooperative client sits in a chair or on the sofa in their own home; the aide takes a temporal/oral temperature, counts or reads the radial pulse (often with a fingertip pulse oximeter), counts respirations by watching the chest for 30-60 seconds, and records the readings on the care plan/app for the supervising nurse.

Cooperative but bed- or chair-bound client with limited mobility in a private home: the aide reaches over bedding, positions the client's arm or exposes the forehead, applies a thermometer (temporal or axillary) and pulse oximeter, and counts respirations while the client lies in whatever position they are in; lighting, bed height and clutter vary by home.

Client who cannot cooperate: advanced dementia with agitation or resistance, delirium, hearing/vision loss, or severe contractures and fragile skin. The aide must coax, redirect, hold or reposition a moving limb, retry the thermometer or oximeter several times, and judge when a reading is artifact.

Vitals rounds in an institutional residential setting (group home, adult family home, small assisted-living unit) where the aide serves several residents in sequence using facility-standard equipment and charts in the facility's system; layout and equipment are fixed and staff control who is present.

Change-of-condition or urgent check in the home: the client reports dizziness, chest tightness, fever or has just fallen; the aide takes pulse, temperature and respiration wherever the client is (bathroom floor, recliner, bedside), repeats readings, notes irregular or thready pulse and labored breathing, compares to the nurse's parameters and reports/escalates.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Shows High Success Rates in Multicenter Trial | Clinical Lab Products
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed diagnostic venous blood draws on patients presented at a fixtured arm station in outpatient phlebotomy departments, with clinically comparable success and safety in a premarket multicenter trial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture. It requires a robot to autonomously localize anatomy on a presented human limb, make safe force-controlled contact and tolerate small patient motion — strictly harder and riskier than placing a thermometer, pulse-oximeter clip or cuff on the same presented limb, so placement capability for vital-sign sensors carries over at a fixtured station.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Haddadin group) and collaborators
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: The SR-NOCS station drove a swab autonomously into the naso-/oropharynx of subjects seated at a purpose-built head-rest station, with results matching manual sampling in two clinical studies of 52 patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: specimen swabbing. It shows autonomous, force-limited robotic contact with the head/face of real, still, cooperative patients at a fixtured station — the same class of contact needed to apply a temporal thermometer or tympanic probe, at far greater precision and risk.

sources.system: Automated robotic platform for remote auscultation (Tsumura et al.)
sources.title: Toward Fully Automated Robotic Platform for Remote Auscultation (arXiv:2201.05272)
sources.claim: A robotic platform autonomously positions a stethoscope on a body using LiDAR-camera registration and force-limited contact, giving heart and breath sounds (i.e., pulse and respiration), but validation used a torso mannequin rather than human subjects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chest auscultation. Autonomously registering a body surface and placing a contact sensor with controlled force is the same physical action needed to place a vital-sign sensor on a presented patient; auscultation additionally yields heart and respiratory rate.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensing)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring (Cyborg and Bionic Systems)
sources.claim: The Dr. Spot mobile robot measured skin temperature, respiratory rate and ... contactlessly on patients in a hospital emergency department using IR and RGB cameras, but the platform was teleoperated by clinical staff.

sources.system: temi robot with Thermal temi infrared sensor
sources.title: Thermal temi (3rd party) - temi robot
sources.claim: A commercially sold thermal add-on lets the temi service robot capture guests' temperature autonomously as it operates in a building, but it provides only temperature screening, not pulse or respiration.

sources.title: Dr. Temi, The Autonomous Robot Will See You Now | Healthcare IT Today
sources.claim: The Dr. Temi autonomous robot navigates by itself to a patient's bedside in hospitals, nursing homes and home care carrying a blood pressure cuff, pulse ..., ECG and digital stethoscope, but it has no arms and the devices must be applied by a person.

tasks.label: Entertain, converse with, or read aloud to patients to keep them mentally healthy and alert.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide patients and families with emotional support and instruction in areas such as caring for infants, preparing healthy meals, living independently, or adapting to disability or illness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Direct patients in simple prescribed exercises or in the use of braces or artificial limbs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Stroke survivor at home with a hemiparetic hand/wrist or ankle/foot: the aide prompts the patient to do the PT-prescribed repetitive limb exercises, helps the patient complete each repetition through range, counts reps, encourages, and notes tolerance for the nurse's log. Patient is seated, cognitively intact, cooperative.

General home exercise program written by the visiting PT for a deconditioned or post-op elderly client: seated marches, sit-to-stands from the sofa, heel raises at the counter, theraband arm work, standing balance. Aide demonstrates, counts, cues form and breathing, and stays within arm's reach to steady the client. Cluttered living room, pets, family present.

Bed-level passive/active-assisted range-of-motion for a largely immobile client (advanced MS, late-stage dementia, contracture risk): aide repositions the client in bed, cradles and moves each joint of the affected limbs through range 10 times, watching the face for pain, checking skin, then documents. Variable bed height, lines and tubes, spasticity.

Prescribed ambulation practice: aide applies a gait belt, positions the walker or cane, walks the client a prescribed distance down the hall, to the bathroom, or to the mailbox, guarding against buckling knees and catching stumbles, monitoring shortness of breath, and returning the client to a chair.

Orthosis/brace: aide applies and removes an AFO, knee immobilizer, wrist splint or back brace per the wearing schedule - donning sock, seating the heel, tensioning straps, checking skin for redness - and then directs the client in standing/walking correctly with it on.

Prosthetic limb: aide assists a transtibial or transfemoral amputee to roll on the liner, add or remove sock plies, seat and lock the socket, inspect the residual limb for skin breakdown, and then coach the client in standing and walking with the limb.

sources.title: Lokomat Robotic Gait Rehabilitation | UM Shore Regional Health
sources.claim: Lokomat is a commercially deployed robotic gait trainer in US rehabilitation hospitals: the patient is harnessed over a treadmill and the robot's motorized legs drive the prescribed gait exercise, automatically tapering assistance as the patient improves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered gait training. It is the same prescribed walking exercise a home health aide supervises, for the same client population (stroke, SCI, MS), with the machine rather than the aide providing movement guidance and fall protection.

sources.title: HOCOMA LAUNCHES A NEW VERSION OF ITS ESTABLISHED GAIT TRAINING DEVICE LOKOMATPRO - Hocoma
sources.claim: Lokomat gait-training robots are installed at scale worldwide, i.e. routine clinical equipment rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.title: Intended Use & Indications - Hocoma (ArmeoPower)
sources.claim: ArmeoPower is a commercial motorized arm exoskeleton that supports and assists a patient's arm through prescribed upper-limb exercises and can passively mobilize the limb through range of motion; the therapist only sets parameters via a user interface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered assisted/passive range-of-motion therapy. Same limb movements, same neurologic clients, and the same purpose as the aide's hands-on ROM, once the limb is strapped into the orthosis.

sources.title: Continuous Passive Motion (CPM) Device in the Home Setting - BlueCross BlueShield of Tennessee Medical Policy
sources.claim: Motorized continuous-passive-motion devices move a post-operative knee through a set range of flexion and extension without any manual assistance once the limb is fixtured in the frame, including in the home setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-delivered passive range of motion. Identical objective and joint excursion to the aide's hands-on passive ROM, with equal or better repeatability once the leg is fixtured.

sources.title: Keeping His Balance with New Technology - Holy Name
sources.claim: hunova is a commercially installed robotic rehabilitation platform used in US hospitals: after an automated assessment it delivers hundreds of prescribed postural-control, balance and core exercises to a patient seated or standing on the robotic platform, with automated feedback and scoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-guided balance and strengthening exercise. Covers the same prescribed exercise categories (weight shifting, sit-to-stand, trunk and limb strengthening) an aide cues at home, delivered with the client secured on the machine.

sources.title: Classifying Residual Stroke Severity Using Robotics-Assisted Stroke Rehabilitation: Machine Learning Approach (JMIR Biomedical Engineering)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed study of Motus Nova's wearable rehab robots: 33 stroke patients carried out prescribed in-home therapy sessions with the Motus Hand and Motus ..., which actively assist each repetition and record movement and assistance data for clinician review.

sources.title: Classifying Residual Stroke Severity Using Robotics-Assisted Stroke Rehabilitation: Machine Learning Approach (PMC)
sources.claim: The same study states the Motus robotic devices are intended for stroke survivors to perform their prescribed limb exercise at home with no clinician or caregiver present.

tasks.label: Accompany clients to doctors' offices or on other trips outside the home, providing transportation, assistance, and companionship.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Frail but ambulatory client (walker or cane) has a routine doctor's appointment. Aide helps the client dress and get out of the house, steadies them down porch steps, helps them into the car and buckles them, drives on public streets, parks, walks them into the clinic, checks in, waits with them, helps relay symptoms and instructions, then reverses the trip home.

Wheelchair-using client with limited transfer ability travels to a specialist or dialysis appointment. Aide assists the pivot transfer, folds/loads the chair or rides paratransit and secures the chair, pushes over sidewalks, curb cuts, doorways and elevators, manages coat/bag/oxygen, waits through the visit, and returns.

Client goes out on errands - pharmacy pickup, grocery store, bank. Aide drives or walks with the client, offers an arm for support, fetches items from shelves, handles the cart and payment help, carries bags, watches for fatigue or confusion in crowded aisles and parking lots.

Recreational or social outing: a walk around the neighborhood, a park, a senior center, place of worship, or a family visit. Aide provides conversation and companionship, monitors gait, fatigue and orientation, assists with seating and restroom use, and gets the client home safely.

Client lives in an assisted-living or independent-living residence and can board and ride a powered mobility chair unaided. Aide simply takes them along mapped interior corridors and elevators from the apartment to the on-site clinic, therapy room or lab, and back - conveyance only, no hands-on help needed.

Client in an assisted-living residence needs hands-on help for an on-site appointment: transfer from bed or recliner into a wheelchair, positioning, being pushed to the clinic, staying present during the visit to answer questions and monitor the client, and the return trip.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Service (WHILL Model F/Autonomous Drive), operated with Unifi
sources.title: Wayne County Airport Authority partners with Unifi to bring autonomous wheelchairs to DTW
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs are deployed in US airport terminals, autonomously conveying a seated passenger along pre-mapped routes to a destination and then returning to base under remote supervision; over 100 units and 400,000+ autonomous rides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: airport wheelchair-attendant escort. Transfer holds for conveyance-only escort of a mobility-limited person along known interior routes of an institution-controlled building (same passenger weight, same doors/elevators/crowd conditions), but not for hands-on transfers or staying with the client.

sources.title: WHILL - Winnipeg Airports Authority
sources.claim: Same system in routine airport service moving passengers who need assistance across a terminal from check-in through security to the gate.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: escorting a mobility-limited person on a fixed interior route inside a facility whose operator controls the premises.

sources.title: Waymo goes driverless in Las Vegas, with Denver, San Diego, Tampa next | Electrek
sources.claim: Waymo operates commercial driverless robotaxi service with no human at the ... in many US cities, roughly 500,000 paid rides per week - i.e., the vehicle-driving portion of a trip is automated on public roads, but the service provides no door-through-door physical assistance or accompaniment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passenger transport by car. It covers only the driving sub-step of the aide's trip; it supplies no help entering/exiting the home or vehicle, no ambulation support, and no in-clinic accompaniment.

sources.title: Eldercare robot helps people sit and stand, and catches them if they fall - Technology Org
sources.claim: State-of-the-art eldercare robots for physically supporting an older adult during sit-to-stand and walking, and catching falls, remain remote-controlled laboratory prototypes, not autonomous deployed systems.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant sub-capability (physical ambulation support and fall prevention for an older adult); its teleoperated, prototype status means it cannot support a positive judgment for instances requiring hands-on assistance.

sources.title: US firm claims 'world's first' autonomous patient transport robot
sources.claim: An in-hospital autonomous patient-transport robot that attaches to stretchers and navigates corridors and elevators has been unveiled by a startup, but as a newly announced product without evidence of routine deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility patient transport. Product announcement with unverified autonomy in service, so treated as non-qualifying; it also does not cover transfers or staying with the client.

tasks.label: Administer prescribed oral medications, under the written direction of physician or as directed by home care nurse or aide, and ensure patients take their medicine.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private home; cognitively intact or mildly forgetful client who can swallow pills handed to them. At the scheduled time the aide prompts the client, opens the pharmacy blister/pouch or weekly organizer, hands over the scheduled solid oral doses with a glass of water, watches them take it, and records the dose on the visit note; reports a refusal or missed dose to the case-manager nurse.

Private home; client with moderate-to-severe dementia or behavioral resistance. The aide must find the client, gain cooperation, hand or place the pills, watch for spitting/cheeking or hiding of pills, sometimes crush tablets into applesauce per nurse instruction, re-approach after a refusal, and document/report.

Private home; physically dependent client (bedbound, post-stroke, advanced neuromuscular disease, dysphagia). The aide brings meds and fluids to the bed or recliner, positions the client upright, places tablets in the mouth or in a spoon of puree, helps with a cup or straw, checks the mouth for retained pills, and documents.

Private home; regimen with non-solid or variable elements: liquid medications measured in an oral syringe or cup, half-tablets, as-needed pain/laxative doses given on request, doses timed with meals or held per the nurse's written instruction depending on symptoms, plus checking the med list against multiple loose bottles and flagging refills.

Congregate setting (group home, adult family home, assisted living) with a fixed layout and institutional control; the aide/med tech gives scheduled oral medications room-by-room to several residents from a medication administration record, most of whom can swallow pills when handed, signing each dose off on the MAR.

sources.system: Evondos E300 in-home medicine dispensing robot / telecare system
sources.title: An In-home Advanced Robotic System to Manage Elderly Home-care Patients' Medications: A Pilot Safety and Usability Study (PubMed abstract)
sources.claim: The Evondos medicine-dispensing robot was evaluated in a nursing home (17 residents, 457 device-days) and in the private homes of 27 long-term-medication home-care patients; the robot dispensed the correct multi-dose sachet on schedule, logged retrieval, and alerted providers on missed doses.

sources.system: Evondos automated medicine dispensing robot service
sources.title: The leading Nordic Automated medicine dispenser (AMD) — Evondos presentation (UK Telehealthcare)
sources.claim: Evondos medicine-dispensing robots are commercially deployed at scale in ordinary private homes across the Nordics, substituting for routine home-care medication visits with high measured adherence and no reported medication errors in a Stockholm home-care provider study.

sources.title: A randomized controlled efficacy study of the Medido medication dispenser in Parkinson's disease (BMC Geriatrics)
sources.claim: The Medido Connected automated home medication dispenser, used in a randomized controlled trial with 87 Parkinson's patients living at home, autonomously opens and presents the pre-packaged dose at programmed times and escalates to a caregiver if the patient does not respond.

sources.system: Automated home medication dispenser (AHMD), e.g. Medido
sources.title: Automated home medication dispensers — JBI news/evidence summary
sources.claim: Automated home medication dispensers integrated with pharmacy unit-dose packaging are used in Dutch home care to remind patients and dispense correct doses, raising adherence and reducing the frequency of nursing visits for medication assistance.

sources.system: Medication management robots (MMRs) reviewed across six studies from Sweden, Finland and the USA
sources.title: Robot-assisted medication management in home care and long-term care settings: a mixed-method systematic review (PubMed abstract)
sources.claim: A 2025 mixed-method systematic review of medication management robots in home care and long-term care found improved adherence and fewer medication errors, but identified incompatibility with liquid medications as a key technical limitation.

sources.developer: HiDO / Rush University Medical Center study
sources.title: A Comprehensive Self-Medication Management System to Reduce Medication Errors Among People Living With Dementia (JMIR Human Factors)
sources.claim: An AI-enabled dispensing device aimed at people living with dementia was tested only in clinic with 35 caregiver-patient dyads using simulated medication-taking; it automates dispensing and camera-based verification but still depends on the person self-medicating.

tasks.label: Perform a variety of duties as requested by client, such as obtaining household supplies or running errands.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Out-of-home shopping trip for the client: aide takes a list, travels to a supermarket or big-box store, walks aisles selecting 10-25 varied items (produce, refrigerated goods, paper goods, the client's preferred brands/sizes), pays with the client's money, transports the bags back, carries them inside and puts them away in fridge and cabinets.

Out-of-home single-purpose pickup errand: go to the pharmacy for a refill (sign for it, verify it is the right client's prescription), or collect a package at the post office, dry cleaning, or one hardware/store item, then return to the home and hand it to the client or put it in its place.

In-home restocking as requested: fetch standard household supplies from the client's own storage - toilet paper and towels from the hall closet, incontinence supplies or bottled water from the garage/basement - and bring them to the bathroom, bedside or kitchen where the client wants them.

Ad-hoc fetch-and-hand requests from a seated or bedbound client: bring eyeglasses, the TV remote, a book, a sweater, a glass of juice, a phone charger, or the mail from the curbside box; objects are wherever the household last left them and must be handed directly to the client.

Requested take-away chores: carry kitchen and bathroom trash and recycling out to the curb or dumpster on collection day, take soiled laundry to the washer or laundry room, remove clutter/boxes to the bin.

Other odd requests around the home: water houseplants, feed or let out the pet, change a burned-out lightbulb, replace batteries in a remote, tidy or reorganize a drawer or shelf at the client's direction.

sources.title: The technology Re:Imagining online grocery
sources.claim: Ocado's On-Grid Robotic Pick robotic arms autonomously pick and pack individual grocery and household items into customer orders at commercial scale in automated fulfilment centres (work brought to the machine).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a customer's grocery/household-supply order. Same objects (packaged groceries, paper goods, toiletries) and same accepted output (the requested set of items collected together) as the aide's 'obtain household supplies' errand, with items presented to the machine in totes as an E1 setting would present them.

sources.title: Amazon deploys robot for heavy lifting in fulfillment center
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual consumer products for picking, stowing and packing in fulfillment centers at scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking a requested item from a presented tote. At E1 the requested household or personal item is presented at a known pose, so fetch-and-place reduces to the item handling Sparrow performs commercially on millions of everyday consumer SKUs.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals
sources.claim: Moxi performs commercial mobile manipulation in hospitals: it autonomously picks supplies out of supply closets ... delivers them to patient rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining requested supplies from a storage closet and bringing them to the person who needs them in their room - the same fetch-and-deliver errand the aide runs, with comparable objects (packaged consumable supplies), inside an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulator is built for AI, says Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi is deployed in more than 25 ... and navigates autonomously between floors, having logged over 100,000 autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment scale and route autonomy (doors, elevators) for the fetch-and-deliver errands cited above, i.e. that the errand is completed end-to-end in a working facility rather than in a one-off demo.

sources.title: Meet Moxi, the newest nurse assistant of Trinity Michigan medical team
sources.claim: Moxi autonomously fetches medications and pharmaceutical items and delivers them along hospital routes, using a secure badge-access drawer for handover.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the prescription pickup errand. Collecting a dispensed medication from the pharmacy and carrying it to the person who needs it is the same errand, with the same object class and secure-handover requirement, inside a structured facility.

sources.title: TUG Robot Is Working Harder Than Ever
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots work around the clock in US medical centers delivering drugs, supplies, linens and meals and hauling trash and soiled linen away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the requested take-away chore (trash and soiled laundry moved from where the client is to the collection point) and supply delivery, performed autonomously on institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: At Froedtert Hospital a TUG fleet completed over 78,000 deliveries in 2024, including hauling more than 6 million lbs ... plus recycling and regulated medical waste.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trash and soiled-linen removal at production volume and worker-acceptable reliability, matching the aide's requested take-away chore, in a facility kept to a working standard.

sources.title: Starship Technologies surpasses 8M autonomous deliveries
sources.claim: Starship's sidewalk robots have completed over 8 million autonomous deliveries on public sidewalks; the transport leg is autonomous, but merchants load the robot and the recipient unloads it outdoors, so no in-store selection or in-home handover occurs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the transport leg of an outside errand in an unstructured public setting. It shows E3 goods transport is solved while the selecting, paying, carrying inside and putting away that the aide's errand requires are not performed by the robot.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, shipping to consumer homes from 2026, relies on human teleoperators for complex household tasks; no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore end to end.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: the leading home-deployed humanoid performs client-requested household duties only under teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment at E3 (private homes).

sources.title: Figure humanoid robots use Helix VLA model to demonstrate household chores
sources.claim: Figure's Helix VLA model drove two humanoids to autonomously identify grocery items and place them in a fridge and cabinets from a single prompt - a staged demo at the developer's facility, not a deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting purchased supplies away in a kitchen. It is a single curated demo in a staged kitchen at the developer's site, so it does not establish worker-quality completion of the shopping errand in real client homes.

tasks.label: Change dressings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Simple dry dressing change on a client's forearm or lower leg (skin tear, abrasion, healed IV/port site) in the client's private home: aide gathers supplies from the client's bathroom, washes hands and gloves up, peels off tape and soiled gauze, inspects the site, cleanses with saline, applies fresh gauze and secures it. Client sits in a recliner in a cluttered living room with variable lighting, pets, and family members present.

Dressing change over a pressure ulcer (sacrum, hip, or heel) for a bedbound client at home: the aide repositions and holds the client on their side, removes a soiled foam/hydrocolloid dressing that may be adherent or soiled with stool or drainage, cleanses the periwound skin, applies the nurse-specified dressing, repositions the client, and reports drainage/odor changes to the supervising nurse.

Post-surgical incision dressing change at home (hip/knee replacement, abdominal or cardiac incision): remove the old dressing without disturbing staples, sutures, or steri-strips, observe for redness or drainage, apply a new sterile dry dressing over a curved or awkwardly located body area while the client stands or lies on a bed or sofa.

Diabetic foot ulcer or venous leg ulcer dressing change with wrap at home: unwrap a multi-layer bandage, peel a dressing that has partly adhered to fragile tissue, cleanse, apply the prescribed dressing, and re-wrap the lower leg or foot at even tension while supporting the client's limb on an ottoman or bed.

Dressing change performed by an aide employed in a residential setting the employer controls (group home, assisted-living or residential care apartment): standard bed or chair, supply cart with stocked dressing kits, staff nearby, consistent layout; a routine gauze or foam dressing on an arm, leg, or sacral area is changed per the nurse's instruction and documented.

sources.developer: UC San Diego Advanced Robotics and Controls Lab (ARCLab)
sources.title: AutoPeel: Adhesion-aware Safe Peeling Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Wound Care
sources.claim: AutoPeel (UCSD ARCLab) is described as the first robotic system for ...; a Franka Emika Panda arm autonomously optimizes and executes peeling trajectories, validated on foam/synthetic skin phantoms with a demonstration on a human subject. It covers only the peel-off sub-step, not cleansing or reapplying a dressing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: peeling an adhesive wound dressing off skin is one sub-step of a dressing change. It does not transfer to the whole task, which also requires wound cleansing, assessment, and application/securing of a new dressing on a moving patient in a home.

sources.system: Robotic wound redressing tape-handling framework (robot arm + Inspire RH56DFTP dexterous hand)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: A 2025 UCSD/Cornell lab study automates two sub-steps of wound redressing (adhesive tape initial detachment and tape placement) using imitation learning trained from human teleoperation on a benchtop arm with a dexterous hand; the paper states wound care remains an exclusively manual clinician process and that full end-to-end autonomous wound dressing is not yet achieved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adhesive tape detachment and placement are two of four steps of a dressing change. The authors themselves note the remaining steps (removing the secondary dressing, cleaning the wound, reapplying the primary dressing) are unsolved, so it cannot substantiate whole-task completion.

sources.developer: Academic clinical research group (PLOS ONE publication)
sources.title: Robotic waterjet wound debridement – Workflow adaption for clinical application and systematic evaluation of a novel technology
sources.claim: A robotic waterjet debridement system autonomously generated and executed a cleaning path over a registered wound surface in a clinical-technology evaluation, showing that autonomous robotic contact with wound tissue has been attempted, but only for debridement in a controlled surgical setting, not for removing and reapplying dressings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wound-surface treatment in a fixed surgical setup. It does not transfer to a home health aide's dressing change, which requires handling adhesives and soiled gauze, cleansing, and securing a new dressing on an unfixtured patient.

tasks.label: Care for children with disabilities or who have sick parents or parents with disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hands-on personal care for a physically disabled child (e.g., cerebral palsy, spina bifida) in the family's private home: bathing, toileting/diapering, dressing, oral care, lifting/transferring to wheelchair or bath chair, hand-feeding a modified-texture meal, and repositioning, in a cluttered household with pets, siblings and no fixed layout.

Supervision, safety and ADL prompting for a child with autism or intellectual/behavioral disability at home: keeping the child safe from hazards and elopement, prompting/assisting toileting and hygiene, dressing, mealtime support, engaging in play and structured activities, de-escalating behavioral episodes.

Caring for typically-developing children in the home while the parent is ill or disabled: preparing and serving meals, feeding a toddler, dressing and getting children ready for school, bathing, diaper changes, play and homework supervision, tidying up child areas and laundry, all while keeping continuous watch on the children.

Accompanying a child with disabilities outside the home: pushing the wheelchair or walking the child to a school classroom, therapy appointment, playground or store; managing the vehicle/bus transfer, assisting with toileting and feeding in unfamiliar restrooms and cafeterias, and keeping the child safe among crowds and traffic.

Medically involved child care at home under nurse direction: monitoring vitals and symptoms, positioning/turning, oral suctioning or tracheostomy site care, G-tube feeding setup, administering ordered medications, skin and wound checks, and responding to seizures or respiratory distress, often overnight.

sources.title: 1X Neo is a $20,000 home robot that will learn chores via teleoperation - Engadget
sources.claim: The most advanced consumer home humanoid shipping to houses can autonomously handle only basic tasks (opening doors, fetching items, lights); more complex household work is performed by remote human teleoperators, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of child personal care in homes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household assistance in private homes. It bounds what any home-deployed humanoid does autonomously today; child bathing, dressing, transfers and supervision are far beyond fetching and door-opening.

sources.title: Obi Robotic Feeding and Dining Assistant
sources.claim: Commercial assistive feeding devices exist for people who cannot use their arms, but they are switch-triggered dining aids taught by a caregiver, not autonomous caregivers; they cover only a mealtime sub-step and require the user to operate them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisting a disabled person to eat. Directly comparable to hand-feeding a disabled child, but the device is user-switch-triggered and covers only feeding, not the whole care instance.

sources.title: Japan: Meet Robear, a robot bear nurse that can lift patients into wheelchairs | IBTimes UK
sources.claim: Robotic lifting/transfer of a care recipient exists only as an experimental, operator-guided research prototype, never as a deployed autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring a dependent person between bed and wheelchair, the core lift in disabled-child personal care. It shows the capability remains a lab prototype with human operation.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: Robot-assisted bathing/hygiene of a human body remains a laboratory research system, evaluated in controlled lab settings rather than deployed in homes or facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bathing/hygiene of a dependent person, a core element of caring for a disabled child. It is a lab demonstration on limited body regions, not accepted-quality whole-body child bathing.

sources.title: QTrobot – Robotics and Autonomous Systems Center (USC)
sources.claim: Social robots used with children with autism are tabletop interaction tools for therapists and educators; they teach communication and emotion skills but provide no physical care, supervision or ADL assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: structured interaction with a child with a developmental disability. Relevant to the engagement portion of care, but it is a therapist's tool with no manipulation, hygiene or safety-supervision capability.

sources.title: 'iPal' robot companion for China's lonely children
sources.claim: Consumer 'babysitting' companion robots interact with and monitor children through a screen and cameras while parents watch remotely; they do not feed, dress, toilet or physically safeguard a child.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: child companionship/monitoring. It is the closest commercial product to child supervision, and it shows available systems supply screen interaction and remote parental monitoring, not care.

tasks.label: Massage patients or apply preparations or treatments, such as liniment, alcohol rubs, or heat-lamp stimulation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Private home, after a bath or bed bath: aide applies lotion/emollient over the client's back, arms, hands, legs and feet and smooths it in, moving and supporting limbs, turning a partly immobile older adult in bed, avoiding broken skin and watching for redness or breakdown.

Private home: aide gives a back, shoulder or leg rub / gentle massage for comfort, relaxation, stiffness or circulation; client lies prone or side-lying in bed or sits in a recliner; pressure adapted to the client's verbal feedback.

Private home: aide applies a specific preparation named in the care plan to a target site / menthol or capsaicin analgesic liniment on a knee, shoulder or low back, an alcohol rub, an antifungal or barrier cream / gloved, measured amount, avoiding broken skin, then reports any skin reaction.

Private home: aide applies a heat or cold treatment - heating pad, warm moist compress, or positioning a heat lamp at the prescribed distance - to a designated body area for a set time, checking the skin repeatedly for burns on a client who may have reduced sensation.

Group home, assisted-living apartment or small residential care facility (institution-controlled premises): aide applies lotion/skin-care preparation to a resident's back, legs and feet after personal care, in the resident's room or bathroom.
Group home or assisted-living facility: aide gives a resident a back or leg rub / massage for stiffness and comfort, with the resident in bed or in a chair in their room.

roles.title: Personal Care Aides
roles.description: Provide personalized assistance to individuals with disabilities or illness who require help with personal care and activities of daily living support (e.g., feeding, bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, and ambulation). May also provide help with tasks such as preparing meals, doing light housekeeping, and doing laundry. Work is performed in various settings depending on the needs of the care recipient and may include locations such as their home, place of work, out in the community, or at a daytime nonresidential facility.

tasks.label: Administer bedside or personal care, such as ambulation or personal hygiene assistance.

instances.label: Bathing a frail client in their private home: undressing, transferring into a tub/shower chair or giving a full bed bath, washing whole body including hair, skin folds and perineal area, checking skin, towel drying, applying lotion, redressing. Bathroom layout differs house to house; client may be unsteady, obese, contracted, or cognitively impaired.

Assisted toileting in a private home for a partly mobile client: recognizing/anticipating need, walking or transferring the client to toilet or bedside commode, lowering clothing, providing support while seated, perineal cleansing, redressing, emptying and cleaning the commode.

Incontinence care for a bed-bound client at home: rolling the client, removing a soiled brief, perineal cleansing, barrier cream, fresh brief, changing soiled linens, waste disposal, pressure-area repositioning.

Ambulation and mobility assistance: walking the client with a gait belt from bed to bathroom or around the house/yard, sit-to-stand and bed-to-chair/wheelchair transfers, steadying on stairs or curbs, catching or easing a client who buckles, in the home and out in the community.

Grooming and dressing in the home: oral care/denture care, shaving, hair washing and combing, nail and skin care, applying deodorant, and dressing/undressing a client with limited range of motion, hemiparesis or contractures.

Personal care delivered inside an institution — assisted living/residential care facility, group home, or adult day program: scheduled bathing in a shared shower room, toileting rounds, transfers with facility lifts and shower chairs, grooming per care plan, with standard equipment and staff-controlled premises.

tasks.label: Perform healthcare-related tasks, such as monitoring vital signs and medication, under the direction of registered nurses or physiotherapists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Home visit: routine vital-sign check on a client in their living room or bedroom — place the cuff and take blood pressure, count pulse and respirations, take temperature, sometimes pulse-ox or weight; write the readings on the care plan and phone/flag abnormal values to the supervising RN. Client may be frail, obese, tremulous, or confused; furniture and lighting vary.

Home visit: oral medication reminder and set-up for a client who self-administers with cueing — bring the pill organizer or bottles at the scheduled time, open containers, put out the correct doses with water, prompt and watch the client take them, record the dose and notify the nurse of missed doses.

Home visit: hands-on medication assistance under nurse delegation — instilling eye drops, steadying an inhaler or nebulizer mask, applying a transdermal patch or topical ointment, crushing pills into applesauce and giving them to a bed-bound client, then watching for and reporting side effects.

Home visit: carry out the physiotherapist's prescribed program — guide and physically assist the client through range-of-motion and strengthening exercises, sit-to-stand practice and ambulation with a walker, apply compression stockings or a hot pack, and report progress and any pain to the therapist.

Facility shift (assisted living, group home, or adult day health program): under an RN's direction, take and chart vitals for several residents in their rooms or at a nursing station, and carry out the scheduled medication pass reminders with pre-poured or packaged doses, reporting exceptions to the nurse.

Out in the community or at the client's workplace: accompany the client to a job site, day program, or medical appointment, watch for symptoms (dizziness, low blood sugar, breathing trouble), prompt and hand over the midday dose, and act/report if the client becomes unwell.

sources.developer: Alexandra Hospital / National University Health System (Singapore)
sources.title: Robotic nursing assistant can take patients' vital signs, freeing up nurses for other tasks
sources.claim: Florence, a robotic nurse assistant trialled at Alexandra Hospital (Singapore), autonomously navigates a general-medicine ward, identifies the patient, measures vital signs with an integrated sensor/oximeter platform, and writes the readings straight into the electronic health record.

sources.developer: Alexandra Hospital, National University Health System
sources.title: An Assessment of an Inpatient Robotic Nurse Assistant: A Mixed-Method Study
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed evaluation of Florence in a hospital ward: the robot autonomously navigates wards, locates and identifies patients, measures SpO2, blood pressure and body temperature ..., and delivers/dispenses pre-loaded medication.

sources.title: Robot Nurse Takes Pulse in Singapore
sources.claim: The Florence bedside vital-signs trial ran eight months in a hospital ward and was reported to substitute for about two nursing staff over a year, indicating facility-acceptable throughput and quality for the vital-signs round.

sources.title: Hero Pill Dispenser Review – Forbes Health
sources.claim: The Hero smart dispenser is a commercial countertop machine used in private homes that stores, mechanically sorts and dispenses up to 10 medications on schedule, alerts the user by light/sound/app, and sends adherence data and missed-dose alerts to a caregiver.

sources.title: How does the Hero dispense medications? | Hero Help Center
sources.claim: Hero's dispenser uses a rotating turntable over numbered medication cartridges to assemble and drop the scheduled dose into a cup in the user's home, with caregiver notification on missed doses.

sources.claim: Aletta is a CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device that positions a seated patient's arm, locates the vein, draws blood and applies a bandage, clinically validated in over 4,000 people and commercially launched in European labs/outpatient settings with one supervisor overseeing two devices.

It requires arm positioning, skin contact and far higher precision than wrapping a cuff and reading blood pressure, so an arm-presented vital-sign measurement is within reach of the same class of purpose-built patient-facing device.

sources.title: HOCOMA LAUNCHES A NEW VERSION OF ITS ESTABLISHED GAIT TRAINING DEVICE LOKOMATPRO

tasks.label: Care for individuals or families during periods of incapacitation, family disruption, or convalescence, providing companionship, personal care, or help in adjusting to new lifestyles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-home care for an older adult convalescing after hospital discharge or surgery: aide arrives at the client's house, helps them out of bed, assists with a shower or sponge bath and dressing over wounds/braces, prepares breakfast and lunch, gives medication reminders, does light tidying and laundry, walks the client to build strength, and provides conversation and reassurance during recovery. Layout, clutter, pets and bathroom fixtures differ at every house.

In-home long-term personal care for a client with a major disability adjusting to a new way of living (post-stroke, spinal cord injury, advanced MS or dementia): bed bath and incontinence care, repositioning to prevent pressure sores, dressing, transfers between bed, wheelchair, toilet and shower chair (sometimes with a Hoyer lift), hand-feeding, and coaching/encouragement as the client learns new routines. Client may be uncooperative, contracted, heavy, or cognitively impaired.

Personal care shift in an assisted living residence or adult day program: aide works through a caseload of residents in a fixed, institution-controlled building - morning grooming, toileting and continence care, dressing, escorting residents down corridors to the dining room, assisting at meals, running or joining a group activity, and sitting with a newly admitted resident who is upset about the move.

In-home support to a household in disruption (parent hospitalized, new baby, bereavement, or serious illness in the family): cooking meals, dishes, laundry, changing bed linens, grocery shopping and errands, supervising or transporting children, keeping the household routine going, and giving emotional support to family members. Every home is different and tasks change day to day.

Companionship and community-outing visit: several hours of conversation, games, reading and reminiscence with an isolated client, plus preparing a snack or tea, steadying the client on a walk around the block, and escorting them to a medical appointment, church or shopping - helping in and out of the car, pushing a wheelchair over curbs and through store aisles, and helping with purchases.

sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: bed repositioning/diaper-change assistance is a core personal-care action; it shows the frontier of robotic hands-on body care is a lab demo, not a deployable worker substitute.

sources.claim: The most advanced deployed personal-hygiene machine in eldercare is an automated microbubble bathing tub installed in an Osaka assisted-living home; it reduces scrubbing and some transfers but caregivers still position and assist residents, and it performs no other care task.
