sources.transferJustification: Related task (assisted feeding) within personal care; cited to bound the commercial state of the art - a fixtured 6-DOF arm with pre-taught bowl positions requiring caregiver setup and cleanup.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: No humanoid home robot performs household chores end to end autonomously; the leading consumer home humanoid ships relying on remote human operators for tasks it cannot do itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-home housekeeping, laundry, meal support) that makes up the homemaking side of this task; cited because the leading home humanoid still requires teleoperation in exactly these unstructured home settings.

sources.developer: Intuition Robotics (with New York State Office for the Aging)
sources.title: Transforming Care for Older Adults Across the State of New York (NYSOFA ElliQ project update)
sources.claim: Robots deployed at scale with older adults in their homes are conversational tabletop companions that provide social engagement only; they perform no bathing, dressing, transfer, meal or escort work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (companionship), the social half of this task; cited to show the deployed system covers conversation only and cannot deliver the physical assistance bundled into an aide's companionship visit.

tasks.label: Perform housekeeping duties, such as cooking, cleaning, washing clothes or dishes, or running errands.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Meal preparation in the client's own kitchen: aide selects/reheats or cooks a simple meal (eggs, soup, sandwich, one-pot dish) respecting diet restrictions (low-sodium, diabetic, pureed), using the client's own cookware and whatever groceries are on hand, and serves it at the client's usual mealtime.

General light cleaning of the client's living space during a shift: scrub the bathroom (toilet, sink, tub/shower, mirror), wipe kitchen counters and stovetop, dust surfaces, tidy clutter and personal items, empty trash, make or change the bed. Cluttered, variable home layouts; must not disturb the client's arrangements.
Floor care in the client's home: vacuum carpets and rugs, sweep and damp-mop kitchen/bath hard floors, wipe up crumbs and small spills around chairs, walker or bedside.
Kitchen cleanup after meals: scrape and hand-wash dishes, pots and utensils or load/unload the dishwasher, dry and put items away in the client's cabinets.

Laundry: gather soiled clothing, towels and bed linens (sometimes soiled with incontinence), sort, run the washer and dryer in the home or a facility laundry room, then fold and put garments away in the client's drawers/closet and remake the bed.
Errands in the community: grocery shopping from the client's list, picking up prescriptions at a pharmacy, paying with client funds, transporting items to the residence and putting them away.

sources.claim: A robotic dish station of three arms is deployed live in restaurants, running around the clock and washing thousands of dirty dishes — including plates, glassware and silverware pulled from bus tubs — autonomously.

sources.title: Physical AI Company Chef Robotics Completes 100 Million Servings in Production
sources.claim: Robotic meal-assembly cells portion cooked ingredients into meals in production at more than a dozen food plants, having completed 100 million servings — food handling of the deformable, variable kind a meal requires, in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial meal assembly. Transfer: same deformable foods, same portioning precision and food-safety standard as plating a client's meal, but with ingredients presented in fixtured hoppers — the E1 presentation.

sources.title: Miso Robotics' Flippy Fry Station robot surpasses 5M baskets | Fast Casual
sources.claim: A robotic fry station cooks food to order in commercial restaurant kitchens, having fried over 5 million baskets across live restaurant operations, with the fryer, hoppers and baskets built around the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: short-order cooking. Transfer: same hot cooking of a portion to a doneness standard, but ingredients arrive in dedicated fixtured hoppers rather than from a client's fridge.

sources.title: Posha Delivers Autonomous Countertop Cooking Experience
sources.claim: A commercially shipping countertop cooking robot autonomously cooks one-pot meals in home kitchens using camera-based monitoring and automated dispensers, once a human has prepped and loaded the ingredients.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity
sources.claim: A pair of fixed robotic arms folds textiles (napkins, linens) autonomously for 24 hours straight at production-grade quality with no human intervention, in commercial laundry/hospitality settings.

sources.title: Within Reach: Robotics in Laundry Operations (Part 2) | American Laundry News
sources.claim: Robotic soil-side sorting systems that separate and batch dirty laundry are installed at more than 170 industrial laundry sites worldwide, automating the sorting step ahead of washing.

sources.title: Industrial Solutions - Continental Laundry Solutions
sources.claim: Industrial tunnel-washer lines move laundry loads automatically from washing through pressing to drying, without manual transfer between machines, in healthcare and hospitality laundries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial linen washing. Transfer: the wash/dry stage of a client's laundry is the same operation on the same fabrics, executed by machine once the soiled load is presented to the line.

sources.claim: A humanoid robot performed a four-minute end-to-end kitchen sequence — walking to a dishwasher, unloading ..., stacking them in cabinets, reloading and starting the machine — described by the developer as fully autonomous with no resets, in the company's own test kitchen.

sources.title: 1X Neo is a $20,000 home robot that will learn chores via teleoperation - Engadget

tasks.label: Train family members to provide bedside care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a client's private home, the aide teaches a spouse or adult child how to safely reposition, boost, and transfer a bedbound client (bed-to-chair, log-rolling, use of draw sheet), explaining body mechanics and safety cues, showing the technique once, then talking the family member through doing it.

In the home or at bedside in an assisted-living/board-and-care room, the aide instructs a family member in personal hygiene care: bed bath, peri-care and incontinence brief changes, oral and skin care, and changing linens with the client in bed, including infection-control and dignity/privacy practices.

The aide verbally reviews the care plan with family: feeding and hydration schedules, medication reminders, pressure-injury and skin checks, signs of decline, documentation, and when to call the nurse or 911; often includes handing over written instructions or agency materials.

The aide shows family members how to operate bedside equipment — hospital bed controls, Hoyer/sit-to-stand lift and slings, gait belt, wheelchair, bedside commode, oxygen concentrator, emptying a catheter or ostomy bag — including troubleshooting and cleaning.

Coaching and follow-up: the aide observes the family member performing bedside care during a shift, gives corrective feedback and encouragement, answers questions, and reinforces instruction later by phone/video or at the next visit.

tasks.label: Plan, shop for, or prepare nutritious meals or assist families in planning, shopping for, or preparing nutritious meals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Everyday simple meal in the client's private home: aide works in the client's own kitchen (layout, appliances and stored food differ house to house) to make breakfast or lunch — oatmeal, eggs and toast, a sandwich and soup, reheating leftovers — accommodating the client's preferences, then serves it at the table and wipes up. Client, pets and family may be in the room.

From-scratch dinner cooked to a therapeutic diet in the client's home: aide selects the recipe, washes and chops produce, cooks on the client's stovetop/oven to a low-sodium, diabetic, renal or soft/pureed order, plates the correct portion, and packages and refrigerates leftovers for later meals.

Grocery shopping trip for the client: check pantry and fridge, write the list to a budget, travel by car or bus to a neighborhood supermarket, select items including fresh produce judged for ripeness and store-brand substitutions when items are out of stock, pay with the client's money/SNAP card, carry bags into the home and put perishables away.

Assisting the client or family member to plan and cook rather than doing it for them: sitting with them to plan the week's menu and list, then coaching and physically steadying/handing items to a client with cognitive or physical impairment while they cook, taking over the hot pan or knife when unsafe, in the family's own kitchen.

Meal preparation in a group home, adult day program or assisted-living satellite kitchen: aide cooks and plates lunch or dinner for several residents in the facility's standard kitchen using its commercial-grade equipment, following posted diet orders and portion sheets, then serves trays in the dining room and cleans down.

tasks.label: Transport clients to locations outside the home, such as to physicians' offices or on outings, using a motor vehicle.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ambulatory, cognitively intact client (e.g., cannot drive due to vision loss, seizure disorder, or license loss) who walks to the curb, gets in and out of a sedan unaided, and navigates the clinic lobby alone. Aide drives from the client's home across town (surface streets, sometimes freeway) to a physician's office, then home again.

Frail elderly client using a cane or walker. Aide steadies the client by the arm from the front door down porch steps, physically helps them lower into the car seat and fasten the belt, folds and lifts the walker into the trunk, then reverses all of this at the medical office and escorts them door-through-door into the waiting room.

Client who uses a manual folding wheelchair but can bear some weight. Aide pushes the chair to the driveway, performs a stand-pivot/assisted transfer into the passenger seat, collapses and lifts the 25-35 lb chair into the trunk, drives to the appointment or outing, and repeats the transfer at the destination.

Client remains seated in a power wheelchair; aide drives a ramp- or lift-equipped van, positions the chair, operates the lift, secures the chair with four-point tie-downs plus occupant lap/shoulder belt, drives to a dialysis center or specialist, and unloads at destination.

Community outing — grocery store, bank, senior center, park, church. Aide drives, parks, assists the client from the car, accompanies and supervises them through the store or venue, handles cart and bags, loads purchases, and returns the client home.

Client with dementia, behavioral needs, or medical fragility (oxygen, post-procedure sedation, seizure or fall risk) who cannot be left unattended. Aide must supervise and redirect the client in the vehicle during the drive as well as at pickup and drop-off.

roles.title: Nursing Assistants
aliases: Long Term Care CNA (Long Term Care Certified Nursing Assistant)
Med Surg CNA (Medical Surgical Certified Nursing Assistant)
roles.description: Provide or assist with basic care or support under the direction of onsite licensed nursing staff. Perform duties such as monitoring of health status, feeding, bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, or ambulation of patients in a health or nursing facility. May include medication administration and other health-related tasks. Includes nursing care attendants, nursing aides, and nursing attendants.

tasks.label: Turn or reposition bedridden patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing home / long-term care: scheduled ~2-hourly turn of a cooperative but immobile resident for pressure-injury prevention — roll supine to 30° left/right lateral, place pillows/wedges, float heels, quick skin look, straighten gown and brief. Standard electric care bed in a resident room.

Acute hospital ward or ICU: scheduled turning of a heavy-care, often ventilated or sedated patient with ET tube, central lines, drains and catheters; turn side to side on a therapy surface without dislodging lines, typically with a second staff member.

Patient has slid down toward the foot of the bed or needs to be brought upright: boost/pull-up toward the head of the bed with slide sheet (usually two aides), reposition in a semi-Fowler position for a meal or for breathing comfort, re-center in bed.

Repositioning to enable another care episode: log-roll the patient onto the side and hold them there while linens are changed, incontinence/peri-care is given, or a sacral dressing is changed, then return them to a supported position.

Difficult handling: bariatric, severely contracted/spastic, painful, or agitated/dementia resident who resists; requires hands-on limb positioning, pillows between contracted limbs, two or three staff and/or a ceiling or floor lift with slings.
Private home: home-care aide turns a bedridden client in a family bedroom on a rented hospital bed or ordinary bed, working alone, in cramped and non-standard surroundings.

sources.title: Toto Automated Lateral Turning System | Frontier Medical Group
sources.claim: Toto is a commercial automated lateral turning platform placed under the mattress that tilts the patient from side to side at prescribed intervals, day and night, without carer intervention; sold through NHS Supply Chain for acute, care-home and homecare use.

sources.title: Transforming recovery time with the Toto® Lateral Patient Turning System
sources.claim: In a real care setting (Gilmerton Physiotherapists, Edinburgh), the Toto system replaced manual repositioning that had required three staff every two ..., turning the patient hourly and holding her tilted overnight, with clinical improvement of her pressure ulcer.

sources.title: About The Freedom Bed™ By ProBed Medical

sources.title: ProBed Medical and the Freedom Bed for SCI Care at Home (NASCIC)
sources.claim: The Freedom Bed is fielded in private homes for people with spinal cord injury who cannot reposition themselves, performing programmable overnight lateral rotation with nobody entering the room.

sources.system: Freedom Bed automated continuous lateral rotation therapy system
sources.developer: ProBed Medical Technologies / Northeast Center for Rehabilitation and Brain Injury
sources.title: Effectiveness of Freedom Bed Compared to Manual Turning in Prevention of Pressure Injuries (NCT03048357)

sources.claim: LINET's Multicare intensive-care bed rotates critically ill, ventilated patients up to 30 degrees automatically on a programmed schedule (Automatic Lateral Therapy), and is indicated for patients who do not tolerate manual turning.

sources.claim: AIREC, an AI-driven humanoid, has been shown in a Waseda University laboratory rolling a person lying supine onto their side — the manoeuvre used for diaper changes and bedsore prevention; developers target practical use around 2030.

tasks.label: Answer patient call signals, signal lights, bells, or intercom systems to determine patients' needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital med-surg unit: an alert, oriented patient presses the pillow-speaker call button; the aide answers (station console, mobile handset, or at the bedside) and asks what is wanted 	he To determine the request \/ water, bathroom, pain, remote), then acknowledges and cancels the call.

Skilled nursing / long-term care facility: a resident, often cognitively impaired or hard of hearing, activates a call light or bed-exit alarm; the aide goes to the room, greets the resident, and questions and observes to work out what is needed.

Call answered remotely over two-way audio at the nurse station console or on a smartphone/badge app; the aide speaks with the patient, determines the need, and either resolves it verbally or dispatches the right staff member.

Urgent or repeated signal (bathroom emergency pull cord, code-assist tone, repeated calls): the aide responds quickly, determines whether it is a fall, distress, or routine request, and summons the nurse when the need exceeds the aide's scope.

Non-verbal, aphasic, sedated, or non-responding patient: no useful answer comes over the intercom, so the aide must be at the bedside and read gestures, expression, and the situation to determine the need.

tasks.label: Feed patients or assist patients to eat or drink.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing home or hospital: CNA delivers the meal tray to the right resident against the diet card, raises the head of bed / seats the resident, positions the over-bed table and clothing protector, opens milk cartons, condiment packets and lidded containers, cuts meat into bite-size pieces, hands utensils, cues and supervises a partially-dependent eater, then returns to remove the tray and chart percent intake.

Nursing home or hospital: CNA spoon-feeds a totally dependent, frail elderly resident in bed or geri-chair — pureed/mechanical-soft diet with swallowing precautions, upright positioning, small bites alternated with sips, watching for pocketing, coughing or choking, wiping the mouth, pacing over 20-45 minutes, documenting intake.

Long-term care dementia unit: CNA feeds a resident with moderate-to-severe dementia who is inattentive, distracted or resistive — repeated verbal cueing, hand-over-hand guidance, redirecting wandering or agitation, coaxing intake, adapting to refusal and to behaviors during the meal.

Hospital or rehab facility: CNA assists an alert, cognitively intact patient with impaired arm/hand function (spinal cord injury, ALS, stroke, bilateral casts/IV lines) who chews and swallows safely and directs the pace — delivering bites and drinks from a standard tray at a table or bedside.

Facility hydration assistance between meals: CNA offers water or thickened liquids to a cooperative patient, holds the cup or positions the straw at the lips, tilts for sips, wipes, refills the pitcher and records fluid intake during hydration rounds.

Private-duty / home-based CNA assists a client to eat in the client's own home — family-cooked or reheated food, an as-found kitchen or bedroom, client often post-stroke or with dementia and variable swallowing ability.

sources.claim: Obi's stated user requirements exclude the dependent, dysphagic or cognitively impaired eaters that make up most CNA feeding assistance: the diner must be able to operate the device and to chew and swallow without ....

sources.developer: Westphalian University of Applied Sciences (Try, Schöllmann, Wöhle, Gebhard)

sources.transferJustification: Directly the 'assist patients to drink' portion of the task: cup held to the lips of a seated, cooperative person who swallows safely.

sources.developer: Liu, Li & Hu (Technology and Health Care)
sources.title: Robot-assisted feeding: A systematic review and future prospects
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of robot-assisted feeding finds adoption still limited by adaptability, safety and cost, with unresolved problems in handling diverse foods and real-time responsiveness.

tasks.label: Measure and record food and liquid intake or urinary and fecal output, reporting changes to medical or nursing staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mealtime intake charting in a nursing-home dining room or at a resident's bedside: the aide passes the tray, opens containers, encourages/assists eating, then estimates the percentage of each food item consumed and the milliliters of coffee, juice, water and supplement taken (including thickened liquids), and enters it on the meal/I&O flow sheet.

Hospital or long-term-care patient with an indwelling Foley catheter: at end of shift (or hourly in higher-acuity units) the aide drains the collection bag into a graduated container, reads and charts the volume, notes color/sediment/odor, empties into the hopper, cleans the container, and tells the nurse if output is low or bloody.

Continent-but-assisted patient on strict I&O who voids into a urinal, bedpan, or commode 'hat': the aide answers the call light, retrieves the vessel from the bedside/bathroom, carries it to the soiled utility room, measures the volume in a graduate, notes appearance, empties and disinfects the vessel, and charts the void.

Incontinent, often bedbound resident: during rounds or repositioning the aide finds a wet/soiled brief, performs peri-care and changes the brief, judges and documents the amount of urine and the size/consistency of any bowel movement (e.g., Bristol-type description), and reports diarrhea, no-BM-in-3-days, or unusual output to the nurse.

End-of-shift reconciliation: the aide totals all recorded intake (meals, fluids, ice chips) and output (voids, incontinence episodes, catheter, emesis, liquid stool) for each assigned patient in the EHR/kiosk, flags residents whose totals differ from baseline, and gives a verbal report of changes to the charge nurse.

sources.claim: The Accuryn Monitoring System is a commercial, FDA-cleared critical-care device whose Foley catheter and measurement cassette automatically measure urine output in real time and actively clear the drain line (pumping to move fluid), removing the manual read-and-empty measurement step.

sources.title: Potrero Medical, Inc. Receives FDA Clearance for the Accuryn™ Monitoring System
sources.claim: Accuryn received FDA 510(k) clearance for real-time urine output measurement with automatic drain-line clearing and out-of-the-box EMR integration, i.e. it both measures the output and writes the record clinicians accept.

sources.title: The technology | RenalSense Clarity RMS for acute kidney injury | Advice | NICE
sources.claim: RenalSense Clarity RMS, used in hospital ICUs (including a UPMC study), automatically measures urine flow in real time and sends the data to hospital information systems, replacing the nurse's manual urometer reading and charting step.

sources.title: Development of a urinometer for automatic measurement of urine flow in catheterized patients
sources.claim: A purpose-built automated urinometer measured urine flow and urine color automatically and continuously for catheterized patients, validated as accurate enough to support nursing documentation and clinician decisions.

sources.title: Machine disinfection of bedpans - MEIKO
sources.claim: Bedpan washer-disinfectors installed in hospital sluice rooms and care-home utility rooms automatically empty, clean, disinfect and dry a bedpan or urine bottle once it is loaded into the machine.

It carries over because it handles the same objects (urinals, bedpans) in the same institutional utility room, covering the disposal/clean-up half of the measurement workflow once the vessel is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Effects of a Flipped Learning-Based Integrated Theory and Practice Educational Program on Excretion Care Robot
sources.claim: The Curaco Carebidet is a commercially deployed 'excretion care robot' (thousands of units in Korea and Japan, used in hospitals and nursing homes) that autonomously senses urine and feces from a bedbound patient, suctions the waste away, then washes and air-dries the patient; no evidence found that it measures or charts output amounts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated incontinence (excretion) care. Cited to show the closest deployed robot to instance 4; it handles the same material in the same setting but produces no measured, charted output, so it does not complete the measure-and-record task.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest commercial hospital mobile-manipulator fleet performs supply, lab and pharmacy deliveries in corridors and elevators; it does no bedside measurement or patient-fluid handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous work inside hospital wards. Cited as a boundary marker: state-of-the-art hospital robots move carts and supplies along corridors and do not retrieve, measure, or dispose of patient body fluids or meal trays.

sources.system: AI food intake estimation model (hospital liquid food leftovers)
sources.title: A Food Intake Estimation System Using an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Estimating Leftover Hospital Liquid Food in Clinical Environments
sources.claim: Automation of hospital meal-intake measurement exists only as image analysis of photographs taken by a person of leftover trays — software with no embodied machine performing the measurement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: estimating meal intake from leftovers. Cited to show the best available automation for instance 1 is a software model fed human-taken photographs, not a robotic system that handles the tray.

sources.title: Toi Labs TrueLoo: the 200 Best Inventions of 2024
sources.claim: TrueLoo is a sensing toilet seat used in more than 50 senior living communities that optically logs stool and urine events and flags abnormalities; it has no actuators and performs no physical handling, so it is instrumentation rather than a robotic system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated recording of urinary/fecal output events in senior living. Cited for transparency: it automates part of the record but is a camera/sensor device with no action on the physical world, so it cannot support a robotic-system judgment.

tasks.label: Provide physical support to assist patients to perform daily living activities, such as getting out of bed, bathing, dressing, using the toilet, standing, walking, or exercising.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing facility: getting a dependent resident out of bed and transferring bed-to-wheelchair (or chair-to-bed) — repositioning the resident, applying a sling or gait belt, operating a sit-to-stand or ceiling lift, guarding a partially weight-bearing, sometimes confused or contracted resident, settling them safely in the chair.

Hospital or nursing home: bathing — bed bath or wheeling the resident to a shower room, undressing, washing skin folds, hair and perineum, checking skin, rinsing, drying and re-dressing a frail, often resistant or cognitively impaired patient.

Facility: toileting — assisting the resident from bed/chair to toilet or bedside commode or placing a bedpan, managing clothing, performing perineal care and incontinence brief changes, hand hygiene, returning the resident to bed or chair.

Facility: dressing and undressing — putting on/removing shirts, pants, socks, compression stockings and footwear over stiff, painful or paretic limbs, plus grooming assistance, for a seated or supine resident.

Facility hallway/room: standing, ambulation and restorative exercise — gait-belt assisted stand from bed or chair, walking with a walker down a corridor with standby fall protection, range-of-motion exercises, then reseating the resident.

Private residence (home health/hospice CNA): assisting a client with a mix of ADLs — getting out of bed, tub or shower bathing in a non-adapted bathroom, dressing and toileting — in a cluttered, variable home with no lift equipment or institutional standard.

sources.system: AIREC (AI-driven Robot for Embrace and Care)
sources.title: AI robots may hold key to nursing Japan's ageing population (Reuters)
sources.claim: AIREC, the most advanced humanoid aimed at hands-on physical caregiving (rolling a person in bed for diaper changes/bedsore prevention, helping a person sit up, putting on socks), is a 150-kg university laboratory prototype; its developer does not expect it usable in care or medical facilities until about 2030.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: repositioning, sitting up and dressing a person in bed are the physical-support acts nursing assistants perform.

sources.title: User comments | Mobility Support Robot – Hug
sources.claim: Hug, a commercially deployed stand-assist transfer robot with 6,000+ installations in Japanese hospitals and care homes, still requires a caregiver to position the care receiver against the body holder and press stand/sit buttons; it reduces a two-nurse lift to one nurse rather than removing the human.

instances.label: Complete bed bath for a fully dependent, bedbound long-term-care resident: remove gown/brief, wash face, torso, limbs, back and perineum with basin and washcloths while log-rolling the resident, dry, apply barrier cream, then put on a clean brief and gown/clothing and change linens as needed.

Scheduled shower in a nursing-facility shower room: undress a partially mobile resident, transfer via sit-to-stand lift or shower chair, wash hair and whole body including skin folds and peri-area, dry, then dress in street clothes including socks, shoes and sometimes compression stockings.

Hospital inpatient bath and gown change: wash a post-op or acutely ill patient in bed or at the bedside while protecting IV lines, drains, telemetry leads and wound dressings; thread the gown around tubing, observe activity and weight-bearing precautions, and report skin findings.

Morning dressing of a resident with contractures, hemiparesis or dementia who resists care: coax cooperation, ease a stiff arm through a sleeve without injury, manage agitation and pulling away, and finish grooming and dressing on a shift schedule.

Home-care aide/CNA bathing and dressing a client in a private home: variable bathroom layout, no lift equipment, client's own clothing and toiletries, tub or shower with grab bars, family and pets present.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: RABBIT is a research bed-bathing system (Cornell) that autonomously washes, rinses and dries skin regions on a limb using RGB/thermal perception and compliant hardware, validated on an instrumented nursing manikin and in a small user study; it does not undress, reposition or dress the person.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related sub-step (washing exposed skin of a person in bed); cited to show the frontier covers only the wiping portion of a bed bath, on an exposed limb, in a laboratory, not undressing, peri-care or dressing.

sources.transferJustification: Repositioning is a prerequisite motion inside a bed bath; cited to show that even this single sub-step of dependent personal care is a laboratory demonstration, not a fielded capability.

tasks.label: Observe or examine patients to detect symptoms that may require medical attention, such as bruises, open wounds, or blood in urine.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Head-to-toe skin check while bathing, doing peri-care or repositioning a resident in a nursing facility: expose skin, inspect sacrum, heels, hips, skin folds and limbs for redness, bruises, skin tears and open wounds, then report findings to the charge nurse.

Opportunistic observation during routine rounds and ADL care in a hospital or long-term care unit: while feeding, dressing, toileting or ambulating a patient, notice changes such as new bruising, swelling, pallor, drainage strikethrough, altered behavior or complaints of pain, and report them.

Toileting and output care in a facility: empty a catheter bag or bedpan, look at urine color/clarity for blood or sediment, check incontinence briefs, record output and report abnormal findings to the nurse.

Home-care CNA/home health aide in a client's private home: during a bed bath or assisted shower, check skin and existing wounds, look at urine in a commode or catheter bag, and report concerns by phone to the supervising nurse.

Post-fall or acute-complaint check in facility common areas or a resident room: inspect the resident for lacerations, bruising, swelling or deformity, ask about pain and head strike, and immediately alert licensed staff.

Focused monitoring of a known site in a hospital: check a dressing for strikethrough or odor, look at surrounding skin and IV/catheter sites for redness or leakage during a shift check, and report to the RN.

sources.title: SquareMind raises $18M for robotic dermatology platform — The Robot Report
sources.claim: SquareMind's Swan is a robotic arm that autonomously acquires standardized, full-body dermoscopic images of a patient's entire skin surface in a private exam room, with AI software flagging new or changing skin findings for clinician review.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-body dermatologic skin examination. A CNA's skin check is the same act at far lower precision — scan the entire skin surface for abnormal findings (bruise, skin tear, open wound) and escalate to a licensed clinician who judges. Swan images the whole skin surface at dermoscopic resolution and flags new/changed findings, so gross lesions such as bruises and open wounds are well within its imaging and change-detection envelope; like the CNA, it does not diagnose.

sources.title: SquareMind raises $18M for Swan skin imaging robot backed by Fred Moll's Sonder Capital — MassDevice
sources.claim: Swan holds CE marking and is FDA-listed (Class I, 510(k) exempt), with commercial rollout in the US and Europe underway in 2026, i.e. it is a real regulated product rather than a lab prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Swan capability item: establishes maturity of the whole-body robotic skin-imaging station used for the E1 judgment.

sources.date: 2015 (product literature; ATBM in worldwide clinical use since)

sources.claim: Automated total body mapping systems in routine dermatology use position the camera automatically to photograph ... whole patient head to toe, showing that standardized machine-driven whole-skin-surface examination is an established clinic workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: standardized whole-body skin documentation. Supporting context only — the patient is positioned and the session run by a technician, so autonomy is unclear and this item is not decisive for any positive judgment.

sources.claim: State of the art for autonomous robots inside nursing facilities is patrolling resident rooms with cameras to detect falls and fall risk and alert staff; the robot does not examine residents' skin, wounds or output, and staff must evaluate the alert.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous in-facility patient observation. Cited to bound E2 capability — the only autonomous observation robots operating in nursing facilities detect falls, not the bruises, wounds or hematuria this task targets, and they hand video to staff for evaluation.

tasks.label: Lift or assist others to lift patients to move them on or off beds, examination tables, surgical tables, or stretchers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing / long-term care resident room: seated transfer of a partially weight-bearing resident between bed and wheelchair (or wheelchair and toilet/shower chair) using a gait belt, pivot, or sit-to-stand aid; resident may be stiff, confused, agitated, or unpredictable in how much they help; done 1-2 aides, several times per shift, in a cluttered room with a roommate, bedside table, and IV pole.

Long-term care or hospital: fully dependent, non-weight-bearing resident moved out of bed into a wheelchair/geri-chair using a mechanical floor or ceiling sling lift; two aides roll the patient side to side to place the sling, hook the straps, hoist, steer, and lower the patient into the seat, managing contractures, catheter and dignity.

Acute care hospital: supine lateral transfer of a patient between bed and stretcher/gurney, imaging table, or procedure/OR table using a slide sheet or friction-reducing board, with 2-4 staff on a count; patient may be post-op or sedated with IV lines, drains, oxygen and telemetry to protect.

Hospital or rehab unit: helping a weak but partly cooperative patient out of bed into a bedside chair, commode, or wheelchair (and back), guarding against buckling knees, managing lines, drains, a Foley and gown, often with only one aide available.

Clinic, dialysis, or outpatient procedure room: assisting an ambulatory but frail or unsteady patient on and off an examination table, treatment chair, or scale — steadying, boosting with a hand or step, lifting legs onto the table.

Non-routine facility lift: bariatric patient, or a patient found on the floor after a fall, or an emergency move onto a backboard/stretcher in a tight bathroom or hallway; extra staff summoned, awkward angles, urgency, and assessment for injury before moving.

sources.title: Able Innovations Deploys Robotic Patient Delivery Platform in the U.S.
sources.claim: ALTA Platform is a robotic patient-transfer device deployed in acute-care hospitals that automates lateral (supine) transfers between beds, imaging tables, OR/procedure tables and stretchers with a single staff member operating it; first US deployment at Lahey Hospital & Medical Center in March 2026.

sources.title: MIX Profile: Able Innovations Is on a Mission to Protect Frontline Healthcare Workers
sources.claim: ALTA executes the transfer of the patient off the bed itself, semi-autonomously, with a single nurse supervising rather than lifting; the company reports installations in six North American health systems.

sources.claim: Bruyère Health (Ottawa) procured four ALTA units for routine care; the device performs a lateral surface-to-surface patient transfer with only one staff member instead of the usual multi-person manual lift.

sources.claim: Hug is a commercially sold transfer-support robot used in Japanese nursing homes and hospitals for bed-to-wheelchair and wheelchair-to-toilet transfers, but each transfer requires the caregiver to position the care receiver against the machine and press buttons.

sources.claim: Resyone is a certified robotic care bed whose half detaches as a reclining electric wheelchair so a caregiver can get a user out of bed without lifting; the transformation is commanded by the caregiver, and staff must still position and secure the user.

tasks.label: Supply, collect, or empty bedpans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Long-term care facility, bedbound resident needing full assist: CNA brings the bedpan to the bedside, rolls/lifts the resident onto it (often two-person or with a lift sheet), gives privacy, returns, removes the pan without spilling, performs perineal cleaning, changes soiled linen if needed, empties and sanitizes the pan and stores it.

Acute hospital ward, partial-assist patient who can lift hips or use a fracture pan: nurse aide positions the pan, waits, removes it, measures and records urine/stool output (sometimes collecting a specimen for the lab), empties and disinfects the pan, documents in the chart.
Supply/stocking only: fetching clean bedpans, urinals and graduates from the clean supply closet and delivering/stocking them in patient rooms or the unit's bedside cabinets ahead of need.

Collect and reprocess only: picking up a used bedpan left at the bedside or on a commode, carrying it to the soiled utility room, emptying contents into the hopper or bedpan washer, running the disinfection cycle, and returning the clean pan to the room.

Private home (home-care client of a nursing agency): non-standard bedroom layout, clutter, pets, ordinary furniture and bathroom; aide supplies the bedpan, assists the bedbound client on and off, cleans the client, empties the pan in the household toilet and washes it.

Complex case: bariatric resident, hip-fracture patient requiring a fracture pan, or patient on contact/C. diff isolation precautions; gowning and gloving, two-person turn, containment of spills onto linens and floor, specimen handling and terminal cleaning of the pan.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator, autonomously picks lightweight supplies from hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms in working US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetch-and-deliver of lightweight hospital supplies. A bedpan is a light molded-plastic item stored in the same clean supply rooms and delivered along the same corridors to the same patient rooms, so the pick-and-deliver capability transfers to the 'supply' portion of this task.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi's hospital deployment is at commercial scale: nearly 100 robots in over ... US hospital facilities with more than 1.25 million autonomous ... completed.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (supply logistics in hospitals); establishes maturity and reliability at scale in institution-controlled wards, the setting of the supply instance.

sources.title: Machine disinfection of bedpans - MEIKO
sources.claim: Commercial bedpan washer-disinfectors installed in hospital and nursing-home dirty utility rooms empty, clean, disinfect and dry a bedpan fully automatically once it is loaded into the machine's holder and the door is closed.
sources.transferJustification: This is the emptying/sanitizing step of the task itself, performed by a machine acting on the physical world under machine control; a human presents the pan to the fixture, which is exactly how a purpose-built (E1) setting presents work.

sources.title: Japan tests AIREC robot to roll patients, easing caregiving challenges
sources.claim: The most advanced nursing-care humanoid aimed at bedside patient handling can demonstrate rolling a person onto their side in a university lab, but is a research prototype not expected in care facilities before 2030.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repositioning a patient in bed, a prerequisite motion for placing/removing a bedpan. Cited to show the state of the art is a lab prototype, so it cannot support a positive judgment for patient-facing bedpan instances.

sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: Robots capable of lifting or handling a patient's body remain experimental caregiver-operated prototypes rather than autonomous deployed systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically handling a patient's body in bed. Cited as context for the negative judgments: the operator guides the robot via tactile controls, so it is not autonomous completion.

tasks.label: Record vital signs, such as temperature, blood pressure, pulse, or respiration rate, as directed by medical or nursing staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital med-surg/telemetry unit: patient care tech takes q4–8h vitals on an assignment of inpatients at the bedside — patient supine or semi-recumbent in bed, gowned, with IV lines, telemetry leads and sequential compression devices, sometimes asleep or post-op; aide wraps the cuff on the upper arm (or repositions to the other arm because of an IV), takes oral/temporal temperature, clips the SpO2 probe, counts respirations, then documents the set in the EHR and flags out-of-range values to the RN.

Skilled nursing facility routine vitals round: alert, cooperative resident sitting in a wheelchair or armchair in the room or day area; CNA brings the vitals cart, takes BP, pulse, temperature, SpO2 and respirations, and charts the set on the point-of-care kiosk/tablet.

Nursing home resident who is bed-bound with contractures, obese or edematous arms, or has dementia with agitation/resistance, or is on contact isolation; CNA must reposition the resident, choose an alternate site (axillary temp, forearm or thigh cuff), steady the limb, reassure or re-approach the resident, then chart the values.

Ambulatory intake vitals: assisted-living clinic day, rehab gym pre-exercise check, hospital admission/pre-op rooming or outpatient clinic; cooperative ambulatory patient sits in an exam chair, aide takes a full vital-sign set plus weight and height and records it in the chart.

Abnormal or acute reading: automated monitor gives an implausible or out-of-range value, so the aide rechecks with a manual auscultated BP, counts an apical pulse for a full minute, or takes orthostatic vitals across lying/sitting/standing on a patient who may be in respiratory distress, tremulous, or in atrial fibrillation, and immediately reports to the nurse.

Home health / private-duty visit: aide takes vitals on a frail client in a recliner or bed in the client's own home, with variable equipment, poor lighting, pets and clutter, and records on a paper flow sheet or agency app.

sources.title: An Assessment of an Inpatient Robotic Nurse Assistant: A Mixed-Method Study (Journal of Medical Systems)
sources.claim: The same hospital trial found the robot unsuitable for patients with limited mobility or cognitive impairment, with navigation and face-detection failures causing long waits and no EMR integration of the data.

tasks.label: Wash, groom, shave, or drape patients to prepare them for surgery, treatment, or examination.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Complete bed bath of a dependent, bedbound patient in a hospital or nursing-home room before a physician exam, wound treatment, or procedure: undress and cover the patient, wash face, torso, arms, legs, skin folds and perineum, roll the patient to wash the back, dry, apply lotion, re-gown and reposition, while managing IV lines, drains, contractures, incontinence and pain.

Assisted shower or tub bath of a semi-mobile, cooperative resident in a facility shower room before a clinic visit or treatment: transfer into shower chair or tub, undress, wash whole body and shampoo hair, rinse, towel dry, then dress and groom (comb hair, deodorant), observing skin for breakdown.

Bedside grooming of a patient before an exam, procedure, or visit: lather and shave the face with a safety or electric razor around jaw, neck and lips, comb or brush hair, provide oral care and nail care, and clean the patient's face and hands.

Pre-operative preparation in a pre-surgical bay: assist the patient to wash or apply chlorhexidine wipes to the surgical area, clip hair at the surgical site, remove clothing and jewelry, put on hospital gown and cap, and cover/drape the patient with warm blankets for transport to the OR.

Draping and gowning a patient for an examination or bedside treatment in a clinic exam room or ward: help the patient undress, position gown and drape sheets to expose only the area to be examined while preserving warmth and modesty, and adjust drapes as the clinician works.

Bathing and grooming a client in the client's own home (home health / private-duty aide) before a visiting nurse's or therapist's examination: bed bath or tub/shower in a domestic bathroom of unknown layout, with pets, clutter, and no lift equipment.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance (arXiv:2401.15159)
sources.claim: RABBIT is a robot manipulator system that autonomously washes, rinses and dries a person's limbs while they lie on a bed, using RGB/thermal perception and a compliant 'Scrubby' end-effector; validated in a lab user study with 12 participants ... with severe mobility limitations. It covers limbs only, not a full bed bath (back, perineum, undressing, re-gowning).
sources.transferJustification: Directly the wash element of this task (bed bathing a person in bed), but demonstrated only on limbs in a laboratory bed setup.

sources.transferJustification: Directly performs the whole-body wash element of the task, but for an occupant able to enter and recline in a purpose-built pod, not for a bedbound patient.
