sources.title: Panasonic Testing Head Care Robot At Salon - SlashGear
sources.claim: Panasonic's Head Care Robot scans a customer's head with sensors and then shampoos, rinses, conditions, massages and dries the hair with 24 mechanical fingertips; it was trialed on real customers at a salon in Nishinomiya, ..., and was targeted at hospitals and nursing homes.
sources.transferJustification: Hair washing is a washing/grooming sub-element performed at a purpose-built basin; it does not cover shaving, body washing or draping.

sources.title: China-made robotic arm autonomously shaves beard - Xinhua
sources.claim: Xinhua reported a demonstration of a robotic arm from an unnamed Shanghai company that shaves a man's beard using pressure and tangential force sensing. The system is not named and the report is a single promotional demonstration clip, not a validated deployment on patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the shaving element, but the system is unnamed, autonomy is only asserted in a clip, and no work on frail patients is shown.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Healthcare Robotics Lab (Kemp, Erickson)
sources.title: Robot Teaches Itself How to Dress People - Neuroscience News
sources.claim: Georgia Tech's healthcare robotics lab demonstrated a PR2 robot that pulls a hospital gown onto a seated person's arm using haptic model-predictive control learned in simulation; it is a laboratory demonstration of a single garment-on-arm motion, not full gowning or draping of a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Gowning/draping a patient is the closest related task; the demonstration covers only sliding a sleeve over one arm of a cooperative, healthy participant in a lab.

tasks.label: Prepare or serve food trays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital or skilled-nursing unit tray pass: a food-service cart of covered trays arrives on the unit; the CNA reads each diet card, matches it to the patient's name band/room, carries the tray into an occupied room, clears and swings the overbed table into place, raises the head of the bed, and sets the tray within the patient's reach, reporting refusals or wrong diets to the nurse.

Long-term-care dining room service: CNA brings plated meals and trays from the kitchen/steam table to residents seated at tables, places the correct diet-specific plate in front of each resident, pours and distributes beverages (including thickened liquids), responds to requests for substitutions, and clears dishes afterward.

Unit pantry/kitchenette preparation: assembling trays and between-meal nourishments — pouring juice, milk, coffee and thickened liquids, making toast/sandwiches or pudding, adding condiments, straws, napkins, adaptive utensils and diet-card labels, and loading the completed trays onto a cart for the unit.

Bedside tray setup and post-meal handling for a dependent resident: opening milk cartons, juice cups, condiment packets and lidded dishes, cutting meat, buttering bread, seasoning, positioning the tray and utensils within reach of a person with limited dexterity, dementia or contact precautions, then collecting the tray, estimating percentage eaten and recording intake.

Home health / hospice or small residential care setting: CNA prepares a simple meal in the client's own kitchen, arranges it on a tray with drink and utensils, and carries it to the client in a bedroom or recliner, then returns to clear it.

sources.title: The robotic delivery of hospital meals
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots move loaded meal-tray carts from the hospital kitchen to drop-off points on patient floors, but hospital staff take the trays the rest of the way to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: the transport leg of serving hospital meal trays. Establishes that the deployed system stops at the floor drop-off and does not perform the tray pass into patient rooms.

sources.title: Franciscan Health Installs 6 Food Service Robots
sources.claim: TUG robots are deployed in US hospitals to carry carts of meal trays from the kitchen to hospital floors.

sources.title: How Food Robots Can Improve Senior Living Dining | Direct Supply
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi runs plated food from the kitchen to senior-living dining rooms and returns dishware, working alongside human servers who still handle the residents.

sources.title: Meet Servi the robot, a one-of-its-kind server in Idaho Falls
sources.claim: In a senior-living deployment, Servi navigates mapped routes to specific tables and waits for a person to lift the plate off its tray; it does not place food in front of a resident.

sources.title: Food Service Robots: Chef Robotics Is Making Them Work - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' vision-guided arms autonomously portion ingredients into meal trays moving on conveyor lines in food-production facilities, having produced tens of millions of meals in North America.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on the 'prepare food trays' half of the task: assembling portioned food components into compartmented meal trays, the same operation a hospital/LTC tray line performs, though on a purpose-built conveyor line.

sources.title: Chef Robotics Physical AI Models Can Help Automate Produce Packing
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' systems complete full tray assembly, placing multiple items into a container in one automated pass with no manual intervention between picks; the company markets the same robots for healthcare patient trays and airline catering.
sources.transferJustification: Tray assembly of discrete food items is the same manipulation and precision class as assembling a patient meal tray from portioned components.

sources.system: RoboEatz Autonomous Robotic Kitchen (ARK) 'Fresh Take Eatery'
sources.developer: RoboEatz with ABB Robotics / Aramark / WellSpan Health
sources.title: Aramark and RoboEatz launch round-the-clock robotic meal service for healthcare staff
sources.claim: A robotic kitchen using ABB arms and RoboEatz ARK technology was launched at WellSpan York Hospital, autonomously assembling personalized meals from ingredient bins around the clock for patients, staff and visitors.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on the 'prepare' half of the task: dietary-customized meal assembly, performed by a self-contained robotic cell whose inputs are presented in fixed bins.

sources.title: Moxi 2.0 mobile manipulator is built for AI, says Diligent Robotics - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator, is used for logistics deliveries (medications, lab samples, supplies) in more than 25 US ..., not for patient-facing meal service.
sources.transferJustification: Closest hospital mobile-manipulation deployment; shows the state of the art in ... same setting is point-to-point logistics, not placing trays at a patient's bedside.

tasks.label: Change bed linens or make beds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing home / hospital resident room, morning routine: resident is up in a chair or at breakfast; the aide makes the existing bed — pulls up and straightens the bottom sheet and underpad, squares the top sheet and blanket/spread, fluffs and repositions pillows, leaves call light and side rails as required. Linens are reused, not replaced.

Complete linen change on an unoccupied bed (scheduled linen day, after discharge/transfer, or after a shower): strip flat sheet, fitted sheet, draw sheet, underpad and pillowcases into a soiled-linen hamper; apply a fresh fitted sheet stretched over all four mattress corners, draw sheet/underpad centered, top sheet with mitered/tucked corners, blanket, spread and pillowcases, on a variable-height hospital bed pushed near a wall.

Occupied-bed linen change for a bedbound or dependent resident: raise bed, lower rails, log-roll the person to one side while protecting IV lines, catheters, drains and skin, fan-fold the soiled linen against their back, place and tuck clean linen on the exposed half, roll the person back over the ridge, finish the second half, reposition and cover the resident, restore rails and call light. Often a two-person job.

Urgent change of soiled linen after an incontinence episode, emesis, wound drainage or a spilled meal tray: contaminated wet linen removed and bagged per infection-control rules (sometimes an isolation room with gown/gloves), mattress surface wiped, clean sheets and underpads applied, often interleaved with peri-care and changing the resident's gown, under time pressure with call lights waiting.

Home health / private-duty setting: a client's own bedroom with a non-standard bed against a wall or a rented hospital bed, mismatched or worn bedding, clutter, pets and limited floor space; the aide makes the bed and changes sheets, frequently with the client in or beside the bed.

sources.system: Figure 03 humanoid with Helix-02 VLA policy
sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Two Figure humanoids running the Helix-02 vision-language-action policy autonomously reset a staged bedroom in under two minutes, including cooperatively making the bed by lifting, unfurling, spreading, folding and smoothing a comforter and correcting wrinkles. No linen stripping, fitted-sheet application or tucking is described.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the 'make beds' half of the task: same object class (large deformable bedding on a standard bed), same required outcome (a smooth, spread cover), performed on a normal human-sized bed rather than a fixtured workpiece.

sources.title: Figure humanoid robots organize room, hang clothes, and make bed without humans
sources.claim: Press coverage of the same demonstration confirms the two robots operated without human control while making the bed in a furnished room.

sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator running the pi-0.5 VLA was placed in entirely new homes (not in training data) and asked to make the bed, put away dishes and clean bedroom floors, executing multi-stage behaviors such as picking up a pillow and spreading a blanket autonomously; the developers state it does not always succeed ....
sources.transferJustification: Same task verb ('make the bed') on ordinary residential beds; establishes that bed tidying — blanket spreading and pillow placement — has been done autonomously outside a fixtured setting, though not linen replacement.

sources.title: AI Robots May Hold Key to Nursing Japan's Ageing Population
sources.claim: AIREC, a 150 kg AI-driven care humanoid from Waseda University, was shown rolling a person lying in bed onto his side — the maneuver used for diaper changes and bedsore prevention — but it remains a laboratory prototype whose developers estimate readiness for nursing or medical facilities only around 2030, and the demonstration's autonomy level is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Closest cited work to occupied-bed linen change (patient log-rolling); cited only to show that even the patient-handling sub-step is a pre-deployment prototype, not a system that changes linens.

sources.system: Commercial housekeeping robots (floor-cleaning and delivery units)
sources.title: How AI Agents in Housekeeping are Improving Room Readiness
sources.claim: Trade coverage of hospitality housekeeping automation as of mid-2026 reports that fielded robots are limited to floor cleaning and linen transport, with human room attendants still required for beds.
sources.transferJustification: Hotel room bed making is the closest commercially attempted analogue of facility bed making; the absence of any bed-making deployment supports the negative judgments on linen-change instances.

tasks.label: Exercise patients who are comatose, paralyzed, or have restricted mobility.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing facility, resident's room: CNA performs passive range-of-motion to all extremities at the bedside of a bedbound resident (dense hemiplegia, advanced dementia, or minimally responsive), lifting and cycling shoulder, elbow, wrist/fingers, hip, knee and ankle through range, watching for pain, spasticity and skin integrity, then repositioning the resident. 10-20 minutes, once or twice a shift.

Nursing home restorative program: CNA ambulates a resident with restricted mobility - sit-to-stand transfer from bed or chair, gait belt and rolling walker, 50-150 feet down the corridor and back, pausing for fatigue or dizziness, guarding against falls, then seating the resident and documenting distance.

Hospital acute care/ICU bedside: nursing assistant or patient care tech assists early mobilization of a critically ill, sedated or paralyzed patient - passive limb exercises, ankle pumps, dangling or in-bed cycling - around ventilator tubing, IV lines and monitoring leads, under nurse direction.

Nursing home day room or therapy room: CNA leads seated/chair exercises for wheelchair-dependent residents (arm raises, leg extensions, pedal exerciser, theraband), cueing each resident and providing hands-on assistance to those who cannot complete the motion themselves; often a small group.

Private home (home health aide/CNA): ROM exercises and assisted walking for a paralyzed or post-stroke client in a bedroom or living room taken as found - variable furniture, rugs, pets, family present - following the therapist's written exercise plan.

sources.title: Safety and Feasibility of a Protocolized Approach to In-Bed Cycling Exercise in the Intensive Care Unit: Quality Improvement Project (Physical Therapy)
sources.claim: MOTOmed letto2 is an FDA-approved motorized in-bed cycle ergometer used to deliver passive and active leg exercise to critically ill ICU patients lying in bed; the patient's legs are placed/strapped into the device and it drives the movement for scheduled 30-60 minute sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task: machine-driven passive/assisted limb exercise of an immobile patient, the same objects (a patient's legs), same purpose (maintaining muscle and joint mobility in the immobile).

sources.title: Feasibility of Muscle Activity Assessment With Surface Electromyography During Bed Cycling Exercise In Intensive Care Unit Patients (PMC)
sources.claim: In ICU practice the patient is positioned semi-recumbent in bed with both legs ... the motorized cycling device, which then performs the movement - the fixturing step is done by staff, the exercise itself by the machine.

sources.title: Doctors & Therapists - MOTOmed
sources.claim: MOTOmed motorized movement-therapy devices are marketed and used in nursing homes and long-term care as well as clinics, delivering motor-driven cyclic leg and arm exercise to residents from a chair, wheelchair or nursing bed, including people with paralysis.

sources.title: Paraplegia | Personal health benefits - MOTOmed
sources.claim: MOTOmed enables patients with paralysis and restricted mobility to receive motor-driven and motor-assisted leg and/or ..., with spasm detection to reduce muscle tone.

sources.title: Technical Data - Erigo - Hocoma (PDF catalog, MedicalExpo)
sources.claim: The Hocoma Erigo is a computer-controlled robotic tilt table with an integrated leg-movement mechanism used in acute care and early rehabilitation to verticalize and passively move the legs of severely impaired, bed-bound patients, including patients with severe brain injury.

sources.title: Erigo®Pro - Hocoma
sources.claim: ErigoPro therapy is used for patients who are immobile in ... wheelchair-dependent, to build lower-extremity strength and functional independence - the population of the CNA exercise task.

sources.title: Intended Use & Indications - ArmeoPower - Hocoma
sources.claim: The ArmeoPower is a commercial motorized arm exoskeleton for patients with severe upper-limb impairment that can deliver passive mobilization of the patient's arm - the upper-extremity equivalent of the CNA's passive range-of-motion routine.

sources.title: The effect of the Lokomat® robotic-orthosis system on lower extremity rehabilitation in patients with stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis (Frontiers in Neurology)
sources.claim: The Lokomat is a globally deployed robotic gait orthosis that drives a patient's legs along a prescribed gait pattern on a treadmill, used in stroke units and inpatient rehabilitation centres for severely impaired patients who cannot walk unaided.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot-assisted gait training) transfers to CNA-assisted ambulation exercise: same patient population with restricted mobility/paralysis, same purpose of repeated weight-bearing walking exercise, but with the patient harnessed into the machine rather than walked down a corridor.

sources.title: Toyota Refines Rehabilitation Assist Robot and Launches New Welwalk WW-2000
sources.claim: Toyota's Welwalk WW-2000 is a commercially sold gait rehabilitation robot for people with lower-limb paralysis after stroke, delivered to Japanese hospitals from February 2020.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic gait training for paralysed patients) transfers to assisted ambulation exercise: same patients, same walking-exercise purpose, with the leg braced and driven by the machine on a treadmill.

sources.title: Andago® - Gait rehabilitation system by Hocoma (MedicalExpo)
sources.claim: Hocoma's Andago V2 is a commercial mobile robot that follows a harnessed patient overground while providing dynamic body-weight support, used by therapists for gait and balance training inside clinics; a therapist still harnesses and supervises the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (overground gait training) is the closest robotic analogue to walking a resident down a corridor; it shows the robot supports weight and follows, but the patient must be harnessed and clinician-supervised.

sources.system: UR10e collaborative robot with rehabilitation adapter
sources.developer: Silesian University of Technology (Universal Robots hardware)
sources.title: Comparative Analysis of Passive Movement During Robot-Assisted and Therapist-Led Rehabilitation Exercises (Sensors)
sources.claim: A 2025 controlled comparison of therapist-led versus robot-executed passive upper-limb exercises found the UR10e cobot, running pre-programmed position-controlled trajectories with a custom arm adapter, achieved a markedly smaller range of motion than the physiotherapist and did not adapt to the person during the session.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (passive range-of-motion exercise); cited as evidence that a general-purpose arm brought to an unfixtured patient does not yet match therapist-quality PROM.

sources.title: Inside Use of Robots in Nursing Homes: From Monitoring and Cleaning to Therapy Bots - Skilled Nursing News
sources.claim: As of early 2026, humanoid or semi-humanoid robots capable of direct hands-on patient interaction and repositioning in US nursing homes are still anticipated rather than deployed; deployed nursing-home robots are cleaning, delivery and companionship units.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative E2 judgment: no fielded robot performs hands-on physical care on residents as found in a facility.

tasks.label: Restock patient rooms with personal hygiene items, such as towels, washcloths, soap, or toilet paper.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital med-surg unit round: CNA pulls towels, washcloths, gowns, soap and tissues off a hallway linen cart and stows them inside occupied patient rooms - bathroom shelf, bedside stand, over-bed table - working around the patient in bed, visitors, IV poles and call-light cords.

Long-term care / nursing home resident room: CNA places clean bath towels, washcloths, resident-labeled soap and personal hygiene items into a resident's private bathroom and closet or drawers; rooms are personalized and cluttered with furniture and belongings, layouts differ room to room, resident often present.
Bathroom consumables: replacing spent toilet paper rolls on wall dispensers, refilling wall-mounted soap/sanitizer dispensers and paper-towel dispensers in patient bathrooms and at bedside sinks.

Discharge/turnover prep: after housekeeping terminal-cleans a vacated room, the CNA stocks the empty room with a full hygiene set - towel and washcloth stack, admission kit (soap, toothbrush, basin), toilet paper - placed in the bathroom and bedside stand before the next admission arrives.

Ad-hoc mid-shift request: a nurse or patient asks for extra towels, washcloths or soap; the CNA fetches them from the unit linen closet/supply room and brings them to the specific patient room, handing off or setting them down in the room.
Bulk replenishment: hauling stocked linen and hygiene-supply carts from central linen/central supply up to the nursing unit and swapping the depleted cart out, so room-stocking rounds can be run.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator, autonomously picks supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Fetch-and-deliver of unit supplies to patient rooms is the delivery half of restocking: same corridors, same supply closets, same class of small consumables.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is a commercially deployed fleet: nearly 100 robots in over ... US hospitals with 1.25 million deliveries completed.

sources.title: Nurse robot Moxi gets schooled by Texas nurses | ZDNet - Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: In hospital trials Moxi's patient-room handoff is to a drop-off box outside the room, not stowing items inside the room; it also moved linen bags between rooms and the cleaning area.
sources.transferJustification: Admission kits contain the same hygiene items (soap, basin, toiletries) CNAs stock; the report shows where the robot's delivery stops - outside the room.

sources.title: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robot showcased at RIA
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots deliver clean linen and other supply carts on mapped routes through hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Bulk cart haulage of clean linen between central linen and nursing units is exactly the bulk-replenishment instance.

sources.title: Those viral bathroom-cleaning bots won't be saving our butts anytime soon
sources.claim: The leading autonomous restroom-cleaning robot explicitly does not restock consumables; paper towels, toilet paper ... refills still require local staff.
sources.transferJustification: Somatic works inside institutional restrooms including a medical facility - the closest fielded system to in-room consumable restocking, and it excludes that work.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout - GeekWire
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow arm autonomously picks individual consumer products out of a presented tote and places each into a tray inside a fulfillment center cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-picking of varied consumer goods (soap, packaged toiletries, paper goods) from a presented bin into a fixtured receptacle - the E1 form of restocking, with items and destination brought to the machine.

sources.title: Automated Handling of Soiled Textiles - Inwatec | Robotics for Industrial Laundries
sources.claim: Automated robotic systems in industrial laundries handle and sort individual textile pieces including towels and linen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of individual towels/washcloths and directing each to a designated destination in a purpose-built line - the deformable-textile handling a fixtured restocking cell would require.

sources.title: The Housekeeping Robots Driving Hospitality Industry Innovation
sources.claim: A humanoid marketed for in-room hotel housekeeping including restocking toiletries in bathrooms remains an early-stage pilot; autonomy of the restocking itself rests on company footage.
sources.transferJustification: Hotel-bathroom amenity restocking is the closest analogue to stocking a patient bathroom; cited only to show no verified autonomous system yet completes that work.

tasks.label: Clean and sanitize patient rooms, bathrooms, examination rooms, or other patient areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine daily tidy and disinfection of an OCCUPIED patient/resident room in a hospital or nursing home: wipe overbed table, bed rails, call bell, remote, bedside stand and chair with disinfectant wipes, empty trash, clear clutter and personal belongings, spot-mop, all while the patient is in bed or in a chair and may move, cough, or need help mid-task.

Cleaning and sanitizing a patient bathroom or shared shower room: toilet and bedside commode, sink, mirror, grab bars, shower chair and shower floor, mopping the floor, emptying the trash, restocking gloves/paper/soap; small enclosed space, sometimes visibly soiled.

Immediate spot cleanup of body-fluid soiling that occurs during care: urine, feces, emesis or blood on the floor, bed frame, wheelchair, chair or bathroom fixtures; absorb and remove soil, apply disinfectant per isolation/bloodborne-pathogen protocol, bag contaminated waste, done within minutes and around the patient.

Discharge/terminal turnover of a vacated patient room: remove trash and used supplies, wipe down every surface and item of equipment (bed frame, mattress, IV pole, pumps, call cord, over-bed light, door handles), clean floor, and prepare the room for the next admission to infection-control standard.

Exam or treatment room turnover between patients in a clinic or outpatient unit: dispose of used table paper, drapes and trash, wipe and disinfect the exam table, counters, stool and equipment, tidy the room for the next patient within a few minutes.

Floor and surface care of common patient areas and corridors in a long-term care or hospital unit: vacuum/mop dayroom, dining room and hallway floors between meals and activities, wipe spills, in an institution-controlled, standard-layout space with residents and staff moving through.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's Bathroom Cleaning Robot is a commercially leased mobile manipulator that autonomously cleans restroom fixtures, floors and picks up ... in mapped commercial restrooms, running with almost no staff intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial restroom cleaning. Same objects a nursing assistant cleans in a patient bathroom (toilet, fixtures, floor, trash), same chemicals and wipe/spray/dry precision, inside an institution-controlled building.

sources.title: These bathroom-cleaning bots won't replace human janitors any time soon (Popular Science)
sources.claim: The Somatic robot has been shown working through a medical facility, entering single and multi-stall restrooms and performing disinfectant spraying and floor vacuuming; day-to-day operation is autonomous after a one-time VR-based mapping/teaching setup, though in 2023 restocking consumables and taking trash out still needed staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restroom cleaning in a healthcare facility. It is the same setting class (institution-controlled medical building) and the same fixtures found in a patient bathroom; the article also records the limits (messes, restocking) that keep it short of full patient-area cleaning.

sources.title: Building Robotics That Work Outside the Lab (Analytics Insight)
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics built an autonomous mobile manipulator that cleans hotel guest bathrooms in occupied hotels, accumulating over 13,000 hours of commercial cleaning ... at Sheraton- and Hilton-associated properties.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hotel guest-bathroom cleaning. A hotel en-suite is the closest analogue to a patient bathroom in size, fixture set (toilet, sink, mirror, shower, floor) and required wiping precision, and both sit inside an institution-controlled facility.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.developer: POSTECH / KIST / Korea Institute of Robot and Convergence / Elphoton, with Pohang St. Mary's Hospital
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection (ScienceDaily / IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine)
sources.claim: POSTECH and collaborators built an autonomous robot that physically wipes hospital surfaces with a manipulator and adds UV-C irradiation, and validated repeated autonomous operation and bacterial reduction in a working hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: mechanical wiping plus disinfection of hospital patient-area surfaces, on the same objects (bed rails, tables, fixtures) a nursing assistant wipes, but demonstrated on pre-identified target surfaces rather than a cluttered occupied room.

sources.title: Avidbots partners with US provider to deploy floor-scrubbing robots in hospitals (BetaKit)
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robot is a commercial product deployed at scale in acute-care hospitals through facility-services provider HHS, cleaning corridors and common areas of working healthcare facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hard-floor scrubbing in hospital corridors and common areas, which is the floor-care content of cleaning common patient areas; same floors, same facility, autonomous navigation among staff and patients.

sources.title: UVD Robots wins EU contract to deploy 200 disinfection robots in hospitals (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: The UVD Robot autonomously drives itself around a patient room and disinfects surfaces and air with UV-C in about 10-15 minutes; it is sold to and deployed in hospitals worldwide, but performs disinfection only, after manual soil removal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminal disinfection of patient rooms. It substantiates the 'sanitize' step only; hospital protocol still requires human cleaning of soil beforehand, so it cannot by itself complete a room-cleaning instance.

tasks.label: Assist nurses or physicians in the operation of medical equipment or provision of patient care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care hospital unit: CNA responds to a nurse's call to be the second pair of hands at the bedside — turning and holding a patient on their side while the nurse does a sacral wound dressing change or Foley insertion, boosting the patient up in bed, changing linens on an occupied bed, steadying a confused or heavy patient who has IV lines, drains and a telemetry box attached.

Hospital or skilled-nursing unit: at the nurse's direction the CNA applies and operates basic equipment on the patient — telemetry leads, BP cuff and pulse oximeter, sequential compression sleeves, nasal cannula/oxygen tubing, glucometer, bladder scanner setup, positioning the patient and equipment for a portable X-ray or EKG — then reports readings back to the nurse.

Long-term care or rehab facility: two-person mechanical transfer with the nurse — applying a Hoyer or sit-to-stand lift sling to a dependent resident, operating the lift, gait-belt or slide-board transfers bed-to-chair or chair-to-toilet, and applying positioning wedges, braces or splints afterward.

Assisting a physician, NP or nurse through a bedside exam, procedure or emergency: positioning and draping the patient, holding a limb or holding suction, handing supplies onto a sterile field, chaperoning a pelvic or rectal exam, and during a code doing chest compressions, fetching the crash cart, running specimens.

Hospital unit: nurse asks the CNA mid-care to fetch and bring items — extra dressing supplies from the supply closet, an IV pole or wheelchair, warm blankets, a specimen carried to the lab, a medication or fluid bag picked up from pharmacy — and deliver them to the patient room or nurse station.

Patient's private home (home-health/hospice CNA): assisting a visiting nurse during a home visit — helping position the patient in a home bed or recliner for a wound care or catheter change, holding the patient steady, helping set up home oxygen, suction or feeding-pump equipment amid household clutter and pets.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator, performs fully autonomous fetch-and-deliver work in working hospitals, picking supplies out of supply ... for nursing staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching and delivering supplies/specimens at nurses' request. This is the same errand a CNA runs when a nurse needs an item mid-care — same hospital unit, same items (dressing supplies, specimens, medications), same delivery endpoint (patient room/nurse station).

sources.title: Diligent Robotics hits 1M picks with Moxi robot in healthcare settings - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi fleets are deployed across multiple US health systems at scale, having passed one million autonomous picks and 125,000 autonomous elevator rides while delivering supplies, lab specimens and ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital supply/specimen errands for nurses, which is the fetch-and-deliver component of assisting nurses during patient care; scale and reliability figures come from ordinary hospital wards, not a test cell.

sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Nurabot, an autonomous nursing robot, has been under hospital testing in Taiwan doing delivery of medication and guiding patients around the ward — logistics and escort work, not hands-on clinical care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ward-level errands and patient escorting on behalf of nurses; shows the frontier of deployed hospital robots is logistics/escort, with no hands-on assistance in patient handling or equipment application.

sources.system: AIREC (AI-driven Robot for Embrace and Care)
sources.title: AI Robots Could Ease Japan's Elderly Care Crisis by 2030 - Technology Org
sources.claim: AIREC, a 150-kg humanoid caregiving robot, has been shown in a university laboratory rolling a volunteer onto his side, the maneuver used for bedsore prevention and diaper changes; it is a research prototype targeted at commercialization around 2030.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: patient repositioning is the core of the two-person bedside assist instance. Cited to show the state of the art is a single sub-step performed with a healthy volunteer in a lab, not whole-instance completion in any setting.

sources.title: Investigating proficiency using a lift-type transfer support device for effective care (Disability and Rehabilitation: Assistive Technology)
sources.claim: Fuji's Hug transfer support robot, with thousands of installations in Japanese care facilities, is a caregiver-operated device: the worker positions the care recipient and presses a button to drive the stand-up motion.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: mechanical transfer of a dependent resident. Cited as evidence that the most widely installed transfer robot is a powered aid requiring a human to position, secure and command it, i.e., it does not replace the assisting worker.

sources.system: Semi-autonomous vital sign measurement robot (robotic arm with PPG sensors)
sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot - TechRxiv
sources.claim: Automatic bedside vital-sign measurement by a robot arm remains a semi-autonomous laboratory prototype using PPG sensors, not a deployed clinical system that applies monitoring equipment to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: applying sensors to a patient and obtaining vital-sign readings for the nurse. Cited to show only semi-autonomous prototypes exist, short of applying cuffs, leads, cannulas or compression sleeves to real patients.

tasks.label: Record height or weight of patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fully ambulatory, cooperative, self-directing adult at clinic visit or hospital admission: aide directs the patient to a stand-on scale, measures height at a stadiometer, and enters/confirms values in the EMR. No physical support needed.

Ambulatory but assisted patient/resident (hospital inpatient in gown with IV pole, elderly resident with walker or unsteady gait): aide removes footwear/braces, steadies or gait-belts the person onto a platform scale with handrails, guards against falls, reads and records the weight.

Wheelchair-dependent long-term-care resident on scheduled weekly/monthly weights: aide tares the chair or wheelchair scale, transfers or rolls the resident on, ensures feet and limbs are off the floor and clothing/blankets accounted for, records to the weight log/EMR and flags significant changes.

Bed-bound or heavily dependent patient (ICU, bariatric, hospice, contractures): weight via in-bed scale or sling/lift scale requiring rolling the patient, sling placement, clearing linens, pumps and equipment; height by tape measure or knee-height estimate; documented in the chart.

Home-care/home-health client weighed in a private residence: portable scale placed on carpet or uneven floor, client assisted from bed or chair, values recorded on the visit note or app; no standard equipment or layout.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; product commercially available since ~2017)

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; product on market for several years)

sources.transferJustification: Same task content (obtaining and outputting a patient's height and weight); differs only in that the person must stand unaided on the platform.

tasks.label: Transport patients to treatment units, testing units, operating rooms, or other areas, using wheelchairs, stretchers, or moveable beds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient wheelchair transport: aide goes to the room, verifies ID, helps a weak or partially dependent patient out of bed into a wheelchair (gait belt/stand assist), manages IV pole, oxygen and drains, covers the patient, wheels through busy corridors and elevators to imaging/PT/dialysis, waits, and returns the patient to bed.

Hospital stretcher or moveable-bed transport: post-op, sedated or bedbound patient moved on a gurney or in the bed with IV poles, monitors and oxygen tank, often with a second staff member, through corridors and elevators to OR, ICU or CT, with a lateral transfer at each end.

Nursing home resident who needs transfer assistance (two-person assist, sit-to-stand or sling lift) or has dementia/contractures, wheeled from room to dining room, therapy gym or activity room, positioned at a table and reassured en route.

Nursing home or assisted-living resident who is cooperative and can seat himself in a wheelchair, wheeled along familiar mapped corridors from room to dining room, activity room or facility clinic and parked at the destination.

Ambulatory outpatient or discharge escort inside a hospital/clinic: patient boards the wheelchair essentially unaided and is wheeled on a single-floor route from registration or clinic to lab/imaging, or from the unit to the main entrance for pickup.

High-acuity or behaviorally complex transport: agitated, confused or behavioral-health patient, bariatric patient, isolation precautions, or telemetry/oxygen-dependent patient who must be watched continuously and may need immediate intervention during the move.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. / University of Tsukuba Hospital, Mitsubishi Electric

sources.claim: WHILL's driverless mobility (autonomous wheelchair) autonomously transported 51 hospital outpatients with gait disturbance along a 100 m in-hospital route from the orthopaedic outpatient reception ..., with no collisions or adverse events reported.

sources.title: WHILL Expands Global Autonomous Mobility Network with Heathrow Airport Launch
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous mobility service is commercially operating at 26 airports and ... worldwide with over one million autonomous rides delivered, carrying reduced-mobility passengers from a station to designated destinations and returning to base by itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wheeling a seated person with reduced mobility along mapped routes inside an institution-controlled building (airport terminal). Same payload (a seated adult), same speeds and clearances, same pedestrian-shared corridors as a nursing assistant wheeling an ambulatory patient to a testing unit.

sources.title: Keio University Hospital Trials WHILL Autonomous Technology
sources.claim: Keio University Hospital ran a technical trial of the ... that carried patients with limited mobility to designated locations inside the hospital without staff accompanying them, with the vehicle returning to base afterward.

sources.title: Autonomous robot company begins pilot with BayCare

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously navigates working US hospitals, opening doors and riding elevators, having logged 110,000 autonomous elevator rides across health systems while delivering supplies and specimens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous multi-floor navigation of occupied hospital corridors, doors and elevators. It shows hospital wayfinding is solved for cargo payloads, but Moxi carries supplies, not people, so it does not by itself substantiate patient transport.

tasks.label: Collect specimens, such as urine, feces, or sputum.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine urine specimen from a cooperative, ambulatory resident/patient in a nursing home or hospital: CNA labels the container, explains clean-catch technique, walks the resident to the bathroom, places a collection 'hat' in the toilet or hands over the cup, retrieves it, pours/decants into the specimen container without spilling, caps it, bags it, records volume/time, and takes it to the lab or refrigerator.

Urine specimen from a bed-bound, weak, incontinent or cognitively impaired patient: positioning and rolling the patient onto a bedpan or placing a urinal, providing peri-care, or drawing urine from an indwelling catheter's sampling port/drainage bag; transferring the urine into a specimen cup without contaminating it, cleaning the patient and equipment, labeling and transporting.

Stool specimen (C. difficile, occult blood, ova & parasites) collected from a commode hat or bedpan: assisting the resident onto the commode/bedpan, waiting for the bowel movement, avoiding urine or toilet-water contamination, scooping the required portion of soft/formed/liquid stool into the container with a spatula, capping, cleaning the patient and equipment, labeling and transporting under isolation precautions.

Sputum specimen, usually early morning: positioning the patient upright, having them rinse their mouth, coaching repeated deep coughing (sometimes after chest physiotherapy or with a weak/confused patient), holding the cup at the mouth, judging whether the sample is sputum rather than saliva, capping the infectious sample, and labeling/transporting under respiratory precautions.

Specimen collection by a nursing assistant working in a client's private home, assisted-living apartment or hospice residence: unfamiliar bathroom layout, non-standard equipment (household toilet, personal commode), pets and clutter, patient alone with the aide, then bagging the specimen and getting it to the agency or lab.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics unveils Moxi 2.0 with Nvidia AI for world's largest mobile manipulation robot fleet
sources.claim: Moxi, a deployed autonomous mobile manipulator, fetches and delivers items including lab samples and specimen-collection kits in US hospitals, but the specimen collection from the patient itself is done by clinical staff; Moxi only carries the kit and the already-collected sample.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital specimen logistics. It substantiates only transport of a sealed specimen through an E2 corridor; it does not substantiate obtaining urine, stool or sputum from a patient, which is the substance of this task.

sources.developer: Diligent Robotics / American Nurses Association pilot sites (UTMB, HMH)
sources.title: ROBOTICS AND THE IMPACT ON NURSING PRACTICE: Case Study and Pilot Site Analyses
sources.claim: In hospital pilot studies of Moxi, the robot's role with specimens was limited to delivering urine, sputum and stool collection kits to nursing staff, who then performed the collection.
sources.transferJustification: Same workflow, adjacent step: the robot supplies the collection kit while the human performs the collection, showing the collection step itself is not automated in deployed hospital robotics.

sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Haddadin et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening (Scientific Reports)
sources.claim: An autonomous robot station performs naso- and oropharyngeal swab sampling on human subjects inside a purpose-built swabbing booth, with a human supervisor present; it is the closest demonstrated case of a robot obtaining a clinical specimen directly from a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic specimen collection from a cooperative seated patient in a purpose-built booth. It does not transfer to urine/stool/sputum collection, which requires toileting assistance, bedpan/commode handling, transfer of soiled liquid or semi-solid excreta into a container, and judgment of sample adequacy — none demonstrated.

sources.system: Intelligent blood collection robot (e.g., Magic Nurse-type venipuncture robot)
sources.developer: Chinese robotics vendors with Zhongshan/Sun Yat-sen Hospital, Fudan University

sources.claim: Intelligent blood-collection (venipuncture) robots have been installed in hospital phlebotomy stations in China and evaluated clinically, showing a robot can obtain a blood specimen from a seated cooperative patient at a fixed station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated collection of a patient specimen (blood) at a purpose-built station. It does not carry over to urine, feces or sputum: those require patient toileting, handling of bedpans/commode hats and non-sterile excreta, and delivering a labeled, uncontaminated container — a different manipulation problem entirely.

sources.title: 'Smart' toilet seat tracks patients' health, aids in diagnoses (McKnight's Senior Living)
sources.claim: The most advanced excreta-related automation actually installed in senior-living facilities is a sensing toilet seat that images and classifies urine and stool events for documentation; it has no manipulator and produces no collected, labeled specimen for laboratory testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated observation of elimination in nursing facilities. It is a passive sensor, not a machine acting on the physical world, and cannot produce the labeled specimen container the task's output requires.

tasks.label: Provide information, such as directions, visiting hours, or patient status information to visitors or callers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Position or hold patients in position for surgical preparation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital OR/procedure room: after the anesthetized patient is slid from the gurney onto the operating table, the aide aligns the body supine on the table, places arms on armboards at less than 90 degrees, pads heels/elbows/occiput, and applies the safety strap, then holds the alignment while the table is tilted for prep.

Hospital OR: aide holds a patient's arm or leg elevated, steady and free of the table for several minutes while the circulating/scrub nurse applies antiseptic prep circumferentially to the extremity, then maintains the hold through the initial drape hand-off without contaminating the sterile field.

Hospital OR: team log-rolls an anesthetized patient from supine to lateral decubitus or prone onto chest rolls/spinal frame for spine or thoracic surgery, with the aide supporting torso/hips, placing the axillary roll, and holding head and arms in position while positioners and tape are applied.

Hospital OR/procedure room: aide raises both of the patient's legs simultaneously into boot stirrups for lithotomy (GYN, urology, colorectal), setting hip and knee angles, padding the peroneal nerve, and holding the legs steady during perineal skin prep.

Pre-op/OR: aide physically supports a conscious, often anxious or obese patient in a flexed sitting or curled lateral position (chin to chest, back arched) while the anesthesia provider preps the skin and places a spinal/epidural, coaching the patient and preventing movement.

Ward or nursing-facility patient room: aide positions and holds a patient (sometimes confused, agitated, in pain, or contracted) on a bed for prep of a minor bedside procedure such as wound debridement, chest-tube or line insertion, or catheterization, in a cluttered room with lines, drains, and portable equipment.

sources.system: RoboCouch Patient Positioning System (Accuray CyberKnife, KUKA robot)
sources.title: Robot-assisted system for precision radiation | KUKA Global
sources.claim: The RoboCouch, a KUKA robot-guided treatment table integrated with the CyberKnife radiosurgery system, moves the patient's whole body into the planned treatment position in clinical treatment rooms without manual alignment by staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: positioning a patient's whole body precisely for a clinical procedure (radiosurgery) rather than surgery. Transfer: same object (an adult human lying on a table in a clinical room), the machine carries out the body-pose change to a tighter tolerance than surgical positioning requires; it does not, however, pad, strap or manipulate limbs.

sources.title: CYBERKNIFE® TREATMENT DELIVERY SYSTEM Technical Specifications
sources.claim: Accuray's product technical specification states the RoboCouch provides a six-degree-of-freedom mechanism that positions the patient automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-body patient positioning for image-guided radiosurgery. Transfer: the machine sets the patient's body pose in six DOF on a couch, the same physical outcome as placing a patient supine/tilted on an operating table, though without limb placement or padding.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise clinical positioning of a real patient's whole body by a robot in a purpose-built treatment room. sources.title: Bed Aids in Prone Positioning to Improve ARDS Oxygenation | NKC Health
sources.claim: The RotoProne bed is a mechanical hospital bed in clinical use that automatically rotates a secured patient from supine into the prone position.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: turning a sedated ICU patient from supine to prone for therapy rather than for surgical prep. Transfer: same object and hazard profile (unconscious adult, pressure/line management), and the machine performs the actual supine-to-prone rotation once the patient is secured in the frame, which is the physical core of prone surgical positioning.

sources.claim: Clinicians used the RotoProne automated kinetic system to place a real, critically ill ECMO patient into the prone position, reported as a clinical case.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-executed prone turning of a real patient with lines and tubes in place; the physical act (secured patient rotated by the machine) is the same manoeuvre required when turning a patient prone for spine surgery prep.

sources.title: Manip4Care: Robotic Manipulation of Human Limbs for Solving Assistive Tasks
sources.claim: Robotic grasping and repositioning of human limbs for assistive care is, as of 2025, presented as a simulation pipeline rather than a system operating on real patients.

sources.claim: A research robotic assistance system for nurse repositioning tasks at the care bed was evaluated on a patient simulator (manikin), moving it from supine to lateral.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (repositioning a patient's body in bed). It was demonstrated on a manikin in a lab, so it does not substantiate positioning or holding real patients for procedure prep.

sources.system: Integrated Table Motion (da Vinci Xi + TruSystem 7000dV OR table)
sources.title: Intuitive Surgical and Hill-Rom Announce U.S. Clearance for Integrated Table Motion
sources.claim: Powered OR tables that reposition the patient during robotic surgery move under surgeon command from the console, with the surgical robot's arms adjusting in synchrony, rather than positioning the patient autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repositioning a patient's body in the operating room by machine. It is surgeon-commanded (teleoperated) and covers only whole-table tilt, so it cannot support a positive judgment on autonomous surgical positioning.

tasks.label: Set up treating or testing equipment, such as oxygen tents, portable radiograph (x-ray) equipment, or overhead irrigation bottles, as directed by a physician or nurse.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital or nursing-facility patient room: set up oxygen therapy as ordered — attach flowmeter/regulator to the wall outlet or position a concentrator/portable cylinder, fill and screw on the humidifier bottle, run tubing, apply the nasal cannula or mask to the patient, set the ordered liter flow, check for leaks and comfort, report to the nurse.

Patient room: assist with setup of portable radiograph or other bedside testing equipment — clear/move furniture, IV poles and bedside tables, roll and hold the patient, slide the imaging detector under the patient, help the tech position the mobile x-ray unit, put on/hang lead shielding; similarly hook up a bedside ECG/monitor/telemetry unit at the nurse's direction.

Patient room: hang or exchange overhead irrigation containers (e.g., 3 L bladder-irrigation bottles/bags on a pole above the bed, or wound-irrigation solution) — spike the new container with the irrigation set, hang it, purge air, open the clamp and set the drip rate; the distal end is already connected to the catheter.

Patient room: set up other bedside treating devices applied to or around the patient — nebulizer with mask/mouthpiece, sequential compression sleeves on the legs, CPM machine on a limb, alternating-pressure mattress overlay on an occupied bed, suction canister with Yankauer within reach, bed/chair alarm.

Clean utility/supply room: prepare, assemble and stage equipment before it goes to the bedside — fill humidifier bottles with sterile water, assemble suction canister and connecting tubing, attach a fresh drainage bag to tubing, mount bottles/bags on an IV pole, prime an irrigation set, then wheel the assembled setup to the room.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics – Ortho Spine News
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator in the US, performs autonomous point-to-point delivery of supplies, specimens and pharmacy items in hospital corridors; it is explicitly used for non-patient-facing tasks and does not set up treatment equipment at a bedside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hospital materials transport) cited to establish the state of deployed hospital robots: it shows autonomous work in E2 hospital corridors is limited to transport, not bedside equipment setup.

sources.title: This Humanoid AI Robot Is Being Tested in Hospitals—Plus 7 More Transforming Healthcare | Nurse.Org

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health | Renown Health
sources.claim: The RIVA robotic IV automation system, in use in US hospital pharmacies, autonomously handles IV bags, vials and syringes — spiking/needling containers, transferring fluid, weighing and barcode-verifying each component — inside its enclosed purpose-built cell after staff load consumables.

sources.title: Foxconn’s Nurabot: AI-Powered Nursing Robot Aims to Solve Global Healthcare Worker Shortage

tasks.label: Administer medications or treatments, such as catheterizations, suppositories, irrigations, enemas, massages, or douches, as directed by a physician or nurse.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Medication pass in a nursing home: a certified medication aide/CNA takes the med cart room to room, identifies each resident, pops oral tablets from blister cards (crushing in applesauce for some), instills eye drops, applies prescribed topical creams, watches the resident swallow, manages refusals, and documents on the MAR under the charge nurse's direction.

Rectal treatment in a skilled nursing facility or hospital ward: aide positions a dependent, often confused resident on their side in bed, provides privacy, gloves and lubricates, inserts a prescribed suppository (or administers a cleansing/oil-retention enema), holds position, monitors for discomfort, assists with bedpan/toileting and perineal cleanup, and reports results.

Catheter and irrigation-type treatments in a facility: indwelling urinary catheter care and emptying/irrigation set-up, intermittent straight catheterization in states/facilities where delegated, plus ear or eye irrigations, vaginal douches and prescribed soaks, performed on a patient in bed or on a commode with clean/sterile technique and nurse oversight.

Comfort treatment for a frail, bed-bound or chair-bound resident: back rub with lotion during or after a bed bath, positioning for pressure relief, limb massage for stiffness or edema, applied at the bedside with the resident turned on their side and skin observed for breakdown.

Massage for an ambulatory resident in a rehab or assisted-living unit who can walk to a treatment room and lie prone on a table for a back/shoulder/leg massage ordered for muscle tension or relaxation.

Private home or hospice residence visit: aide administers a prescribed suppository, enema, or applies a treatment (soak, irrigation, massage) to a client in a bedroom or bathroom that varies house to house, with pets, clutter, family present and no institutional control of the setting.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology – AlleyWatch
sources.claim: Aescape's AI-powered robotic massage table autonomously massages a clothed human lying on its purpose-built table and is being installed commercially at scale (about 60 Equinox club locations after a 10-location trial).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial bodywork massage. Transfer to the nursing assistant's ordered massage is partial: same object (a human back/limbs), same contact modality and comparable force control, but the client must be ambulatory and positioned prone on the robot's own table.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Aescape robotic massage is a self-guided, sensor-driven session deployed in franchised Massage Envy locations; the user lies clothed on the table and the system adapts to body contours and pressure preferences without a therapist performing the work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial massage delivered on a fixtured table. Supports only the ambulatory-resident massage instance; it does not reach a resident lying in a hospital bed and does not apply lotion to bare skin.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics

sources.title: AI nursing robot Nurabot helps Taiwan hospitals combat global healthcare shortage | Fox News

sources.claim: Commercial automated incontinence-care appliances for bedridden elders sense excretion and wash and dry the perineum automatically, but they are fixed bedside washing appliances, not systems that administer medications, suppositories, enemas or catheters.

tasks.label: Apply clean dressings, slings, stockings, or support bandages, under direction of nurse or physician.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing home or hospital unit: CNA applies anti-embolism/compression stockings (TED hose) to both legs of a frail, often bedbound elderly resident — positioning the leg, rolling/pulling the tight elastic over heel and calf, smoothing wrinkles, avoiding skin tears on fragile skin, checking toes and skin, per nurse's direction.

Long-term care or hospital room: CNA applies a clean dry dressing to a minor wound, skin tear, abrasion, or protective pad over a bony prominence — removing/discarding the soiled dressing, positioning gauze or a foam pad, securing with tape or a tubular net, using clean technique on a possibly restless patient.

Hospital, rehab, or SNF: CNA wraps an elastic support bandage (ACE wrap) on an ankle, knee, or lower leg, or reapplies an abdominal binder — spiral/figure-eight wrapping with even tension and overlap, distal-to-proximal, securing the clip, and checking circulation afterward.

Hospital, clinic, or rehab: CNA applies or re-adjusts an arm sling or shoulder immobilizer on a seated, cooperative patient — supporting the injured arm, threading the strap behind the neck, adjusting length so the elbow is at the correct angle, padding the strap.

Home health / hospice visit: aide applies compression stockings, a clean dressing, or a support bandage to a client in the client's own bedroom or living room — variable furniture and lighting, pets and family present, client seated in a recliner or lying on a domestic bed.

sources.title: AI robots may hold key to nursing Japan's ageing population (Reuters)
sources.claim: AIREC, a 150-kg AI-driven humanoid caregiving robot at Waseda University, gives laboratory demonstrations of care tasks including rolling a person over and putting on socks, but its developer does not expect it to be usable in nursing-care or medical facilities until around 2030.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available system-level evidence for hands-on personal care by a robot (sock donning, repositioning) on a human body; shows such caregiving contact remains a laboratory prototype rather than a deployable capability.

sources.system: Close-fitting dressing assistance method (AIREC caregiving robot)
sources.title: Close-Fitting Dressing Assistance Based on State Estimation of Feet and Garments with Semantic-based Visual Attention
sources.claim: A Waseda research team (AIREC platform) developed a multimodal sock-dressing assistance method using vision, proprioception and tactile force to generate dressing motions on a human foot; it is a laboratory motion-generation study, and the authors state close-fitting garments remain particularly challenging for robots.
sources.transferJustification: Sock donning is the nearest researched analogue to applying anti-embolism/compression stockings: same deformable close-fitting garment pulled over a human foot and leg. It is offered as the best case, and it is a lab motion-generation demo, not worker-quality completion.

sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: CMU's force-modulated visual policy dresses long-sleeve garments onto seated human participants' arms in a laboratory human study (12 participants, 264 trials), achieving partial coverage (about 85% of arm length) rather than complete, reliable garment application.
sources.transferJustification: Robot-assisted garment dressing of a human arm is the nearest analogue to applying a sling or support garment to a patient's arm: same soft-fabric manipulation in contact with a moving human limb. Even here only partial arm coverage is achieved, in a lab.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling framework for robotic wound redressing
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab) and Cornell University
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: A UCSD/Cornell system automates sub-steps of wound redressing — detaching adhesive tape and placing tape smoothly — validated in the lab on phantom surfaces and anatomical leg, hip and heel ..., with policies trained from human teleoperation demonstrations; the authors frame it as a step toward, not an achievement of, practical robotic wound care.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to applying a clean dressing, but covers only the tape sub-step on phantoms/anatomical models, not removal-clean-pad-secure on a live patient, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion at any tier.

sources.title: Moxi Robot RGH Unity Hospital | Rochester Regional Health
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed hospital robot in US hospitals, performs supply, lab-sample and medication delivery in corridors and explicitly does not provide direct patient care or hands-on tasks with patients.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the scope of actually deployed hospital robotics: even in a structured E2 hospital, fielded systems handle logistics, not physical contact care such as applying dressings or stockings.

tasks.label: Stock or issue medical supplies, such as dressing packs or treatment trays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restocking a unit's clean supply room or par-level supply cart in a hospital or nursing facility: unpacking cases delivered from central supply, counting against par levels, placing mixed items (gauze, dressings, catheter kits, briefs, saline flushes) into labeled bins and shelves, rotating stock and checking expiration dates, in a small room shared with staff traffic.

Restocking supplies at the point of care: refilling glove-box holders, PPE stations, wipes, briefs, linens and bedside drawers in occupied resident/patient rooms and hallway alcoves, working around beds, visitors, IV poles and clutter.

Issuing a specific item on request during care: a nurse or resident needs a foley kit, dressing pack, wound-care supply or extra linens; the aide walks to the supply room or clean utility, selects the correct item, and hands it to the nurse or brings it to the bedside.

Setting up a dressing pack or treatment tray for a procedure: gathering gauze, saline, tape, gloves, scissors and a dressing kit onto a tray or into a basin in the clean utility room per the nurse's request, then carrying the assembled tray to the bedside.

Moving bulk supplies between departments: picking up or receiving a loaded supply cart, exchange cart or bin of stock from central supply/the storeroom and transporting it through corridors and elevators to the nursing unit, staging it for put-away.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient unit: aide takes a labeled, bagged specimen (urine, stool, sputum, blood tube) from the patient room or soiled utility, logs it, and carries it to the unit specimen fridge/tube station or down to the lab on another floor, handing it to lab staff. STAT / special-handling transport: blood bank crossmatch tube, blood gas on ice, frozen or light-protected specimen, or an urgent pharmacy dose that must reach a named technologist or nurse immediately with a signed hand-to-hand receipt.

Cross-building transport: carrying specimens, lab supplies, or pharmacy items outdoors across a hospital/campus walkway to another building or to a courier vehicle at the loading dock, in whatever weather.

roles.title: Orderlies
aliases: PCT PRN (Patient Care Technician Pro Re Nata)
roles.description: Transport patients to areas such as operating rooms or x-ray rooms using wheelchairs, stretchers, or moveable beds. May maintain stocks of supplies or clean and transport equipment. Psychiatric orderlies are included in Psychiatric Aides.

tasks.label: Lift or assist others to lift patients to move them on or off beds, examination tables, surgical tables, or stretchers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ward/ICU patient room: lateral transfer of a supine, non-weight-bearing patient between the hospital bed and a stretcher/gurney for transport to radiology or a procedure, done by two staff with a slide sheet or friction-reducing board; patient has IV lines, monitor leads, oxygen; bed and stretcher locked and matched in height.

Imaging/exam room: moving a recumbent patient from a stretcher onto an X-ray, CT or examination table and back, two to three staff, tight space beside the gantry, patient must end squarely positioned for the study, then returned to the stretcher.

Operating room: team transfer of an anesthetized or unresponsive patient between the stretcher and the surgical table, three to four staff on a count with a lift sheet or roller board, airway, IV lines, drains and catheters managed, patient placed precisely for positioning and strapping.

Ward or clinic: assisting a weak but partially weight-bearing, cooperative patient to get off a bed or onto an examination table - steadying them to sit at the edge, sit-to-stand with a gait belt, pivot, and lifting the legs onto the surface; one or two staff.

Difficult or non-routine lift: bariatric patient, or one with spinal precautions, fractures, contractures, wounds or agitation, moved between bed and stretcher/imaging table with a ceiling lift, sling or air-assisted device and three to four staff; or lifting a patient who has slid to the floor or is in a cramped bathroom.

sources.date: 2026 (approx.; undated OMARI blog describing post-pilot clinical use)

sources.claim: ALTA was being implemented and evaluated at five Canadian hospitals (Halifax, Ottawa, London, Toronto, Vancouver) as of April 2025, indicating repeated real clinical use of automated patient transfers rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.claim: Humanoid RHP Friends autonomously fetched a commercial transfer-support device (Fuji Hug L1) and used it to move a cooperative person from a bed to a ..., shown three times a day over four days at the IREX 2023 exhibition booth; the person had to lean forward onto the device's handrail themselves.

tasks.label: Transport patients to treatment units, testing units, operating rooms, or other areas, using wheelchairs, stretchers, or moveable beds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wheelchair transport of an ambulatory or minimal-assist patient inside the hospital: transporter answers a dispatch request, collects a chair, verifies patient ID at an outpatient clinic reception or waiting area, patient seats themselves, then rides busy corridors and a passenger elevator to radiology, lab, PT or an inpatient room, and hands off to the receiving department.

Wheelchair transport of an inpatient who needs hands-on help to get in and out of the chair (post-op, elderly, weak, dizzy): transporter locks the chair, uses a gait belt or two-person pivot from bed to chair, hangs IV pole and portable oxygen, wheels the patient from the ward to imaging or treatment and back, and helps them back into bed.

Discharge transport: wheelchair the patient from their room, with belongings, flowers and paperwork, down through the lobby to the covered entrance/pickup drive, wait at the curb, and steady the patient as they get into a private car or paratransit van.

Stretcher/gurney transport of a non-ambulatory patient to or from the OR, ED or endoscopy: lateral bed-to-stretcher transfer with a colleague using a slide board or sheet, side rails up, chart/ID and consent check, steering the gurney through doors and elevators, and handing off to OR staff.

Movable-bed transport of an inpatient with attached equipment (IV pumps, drains, catheters, portable oxygen, telemetry) from the ward to CT/MRI or a procedure area: unplug and stow lines and pumps, steer a heavy bed through tight doorways and elevators, position it in the scanner room, then return the patient.

Transport of patients requiring hands-on clinical management: bariatric or total-assist patients moved with a mechanical ceiling/floor lift, confused or agitated patients who resist or try to stand, isolation-precaution patients requiring gowning and equipment wipe-down, and ICU/ED critical transfers where a nurse or respiratory therapist walks alongside a ventilated, monitored patient.

Shows the routing, door/elevator integration and pedestrian navigation of a hospital transport route are solved at deployment scale, though the payload is supplies, not patients.

sources.claim: Rovex's Rovi robot clamps onto the caster wheels of existing stretchers, beds and wheelchairs and moves them autonomously around a hospital after the building is mapped; in the BayCare Morton Plant Hospital pilot begun April 2026 it retrieves empty stretchers.

sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport - The Robot Report
sources.claim: As of May 2026 the Rovex system at BayCare's Morton Plant Hospital is being tested only on navigation; it is not moving patients, and the company is still working toward the regulatory clearance needed to transport patients autonomously.

tasks.label: Disinfect or sterilize equipment or supplies, using germicides or sterilizing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between patients, an orderly wipes down transport equipment — wheelchairs, gurneys, stretchers — with hospital-approved germicidal wipes or spray in an ED bay, corridor or equipment alcove: seats, armrests, straps, side rails, push handles and wheels, with occasional visible soil, done in a few minutes so the chair or stretcher can go back into service.

After a discharge or transfer, the orderly cleans and disinfects the bed frame, mattress, side rails, IV pole, overbed table and commode chair in the patient room, applying germicide with the required wet contact time before the bed is remade and the room released.

In the soiled utility room, the orderly empties and disinfects reusable patient-care items — bedpans, urinals, wash basins, emesis basins, commode buckets, graduates — using the bedpan washer-disinfector or a germicidal soak, then returns them to clean storage.

The orderly handles reusable instruments and procedure trays: transports soiled sets to the decontamination area, loads the washer-disinfector or autoclave rack, runs the cycle, checks indicators/printout and unloads the processed load to the clean side.

Between imaging or surgical cases, the orderly disinfects removable procedure accessories — table pads, positioning sponges and wedges, transfer boards, immobilization straps, lead aprons — with germicidal wipes so they are ready for the next case.

Between imaging or surgical cases, the orderly disinfects fixed room equipment — the x-ray or OR table surface, tube head, control console, monitor arms and IV pumps in place — within a five- to ten-minute turnover window, removing contrast, blood or body-fluid soil first.

instances.label: Between patient transports on an acute-care unit or ED: orderly wipes down a wheelchair or stretcher (frame, seat, armrests, side rails, handles) with hospital disinfectant wipes in a corridor, equipment alcove or ED bay, checks brakes/footrests, and tags/reports anything broken.

After a patient discharge or transfer: orderly cleans and disinfects a hospital bed and mattress in the patient room or equipment bay (frame, rails, hand controls, mattress cover), then reports a non-working motor, torn cover or broken side rail to biomed.

Soiled-utility/equipment room: orderly cleans non-electronic portable equipment returned from units — IV poles, commodes, walkers, shower chairs, basins, over-bed tables, transport carts — and returns them to clean storage, noting bent frames or missing parts on a work order.

Wipe-down of electronic portable medical equipment between patients — vital-signs monitors, infusion/SCD pumps, portable ultrasound or x-ray units, cords, screens and keypads — using approved low-level disinfectant wipes with no liquid ingress, plus tagging damaged cables/casings for repair.

Batch reprocessing in the hospital's central equipment decontamination / bed-processing area: dirty beds, wheelchairs and carts staged from units, run through cleaning and drying, returned to par-level storage; damaged units diverted to the repair queue with documentation.

Long-term care or rehab facility: cleaning shared mobility and care equipment (wheelchairs, walkers, shower chairs, mechanical lifts, geri-chairs) in resident rooms, shower rooms and equipment rooms, often with heavy soiling from bodily fluids, with defects reported to maintenance.
