tasks.label: Respond to emergency situations, such as emergency medical calls, security calls, or fire alarms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Code blue / cardiac arrest on an inpatient unit: orderly hears the overhead page, runs to the room, pulls the crash cart and backboard, moves furniture and the bed away from the wall, takes turns doing chest compressions during the code, fetches additional equipment, and helps roll/transfer the patient afterward.

Security / behavioral emergency call (combative or agitated patient, elopement, visitor altercation) in an ED or unit: orderly responds as part of the response team, uses physical presence and hands-on holds, helps place soft restraints on limbs, and helps move the patient onto a bed or to a seclusion room without injuring the patient or staff.

Rapid response / patient fall or found-on-floor: orderly rushes to the room, helps assess whether the patient can be moved, retrieves a floor lift or backboard, and lifts/transfers the patient from the floor back to bed with 2–3 staff while protecting head, IV lines, and drains.

Emergency transport: STAT move of an unstable patient on a stretcher or bed to CT, cath lab, or the OR, or receiving a trauma/ambulance arrival at the ED door — clearing hallways, managing oxygen tank, monitor, IV pole and pumps, holding elevators, and helping slide the patient onto the scan table or OR table.

Fire alarm or facility emergency (fire alarm pull, smoke, code triage/severe weather): orderly closes patient room doors, moves stretchers, carts and beds clear of corridors and fire doors, checks rooms, moves ambulatory and non-ambulatory patients away from the affected compartment, and assists horizontal evacuation if ordered.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0 ...

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital-corridor delivery. It shows navigation of an E2 hospital environment is solved, but it does not transfer to emergency response, which requires hands-on physical work on patients (compressions, lifting, restraint) under time pressure that Moxi has no manipulator capability or clinical role for.

tasks.label: Change soiled linens, such as bed linens, drapes, or cubicle curtains.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital patient room after discharge/transfer: strip soiled fitted sheet, draw sheet, underpads, pillowcases and blanket into a linen hamper, then remake the bed with fresh fitted sheet (corners over a pressure-redistribution mattress), draw sheet, top linen and pillowcases, leaving a taut, wrinkle-free bed ready for the next admission.

Occupied bed change on an inpatient unit: patient remains in bed (often frail, lines/drains attached, linens soiled with urine, stool or blood); worker log-rolls or side-turns the patient with a partner, rolls soiled linen against the patient's back, places clean linen half-width, turns the patient back and completes the change without dislodging devices or injuring skin.

Rapid linen turnover on stretchers, gurneys, OR tables, and imaging/exam tables between patients in ED, surgery and radiology: pull soiled sheet and pillowcase, wipe/allow disinfection, apply fresh sheet, draw sheet and pillowcase within a few minutes under queue pressure, in a room with mobile equipment, cables and staff moving through.

Changing privacy/cubicle curtains on ceiling tracks and window drapes: work from a ladder or with a hook tool, unclip 20-40 carrier hooks along a curved track, bag the soiled curtain, hang and clip the replacement, plus occasional shower and window drape swaps in patient rooms and ED bays.

Long-term care / rehab resident room: routine and as-needed bed changes on low beds, bariatric or air-fluidized specialty mattresses, in cluttered personalized rooms with resident belongings, mobility equipment and often the resident present nearby.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: 'making a bed' (arranging the top covering). It shares the deformable large-fabric manipulation of linen changing, but omits removing soiled linens, fitting a bottom sheet to a mattress, and pillowcasing, so it substantiates only part of the task.

tasks.label: Carry messages or documents between departments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine intra-hospital paper run: orderly picks up charts, signed consent forms, requisition slips or printed reports at a nursing-unit desk and walks them through corridors and elevators to medical records, admitting, radiology or the business office, handing them to a clerk or placing them in an in-tray. Non-urgent, scheduled or on request.

Document delivery attached to a physical item with chain-of-custody expectations: lab requisition accompanying a specimen to the lab, blood-bank paperwork with a unit of blood, pharmacy order slips, signed narcotic/consent forms. Often flagged stat, must reach the receiving department promptly and be signed for.

Delivery into access-controlled departments: paperwork taken to the OR front desk, ICU, sterile processing, pharmacy or the lab, passing badge-controlled doors, staff-only corridors and department reception counters, following hospital protocols for who may receive the item.

Ad-hoc multi-stop courier round across floors and connected buildings on the hospital campus: collect outgoing envelopes from two or three units, drop at several departments, bring back signed forms or wristbands, dispatched verbally by a charge nurse mid-shift.

Carrying a verbal message only: orderly is told to inform another department something (e.g., that a patient is ready, that a transport is delayed), walks there, finds the right person, delivers the message, sometimes waits for a spoken reply and reports it back.
Off-campus leg: envelope or document packet hand-carried to an adjacent medical office building or clinic across a public street or parking area, along public sidewalks, in whatever weather.

tasks.label: Clean and sanitize patient rooms, bathrooms, examination rooms, or other patient areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Discharge/terminal clean of an inpatient room in a hospital or nursing facility: strip and bag soiled linens, empty trash and sharps-adjacent waste, wipe and disinfect all high-touch surfaces (bed rails, over-bed table, call button, IV pole, chairs, door handles), clean the in-room bathroom (toilet, shower, sink, grab bars), mop the floor, remake the bed and restock supplies, working around furniture and equipment left in varied positions.

Daily cleaning/tidy of an occupied patient room while the patient (and sometimes visitors) are present: empty trash, remove meal trays and clutter, damp-wipe surfaces and equipment, clean the in-room bathroom and commode, spot-mop, working around IV lines, monitors and mobility devices without disturbing the patient.

Turnover of an examination, treatment or procedure room between patients in a clinic or ED bay: dispose of used supplies and linens, disinfect the exam table/stretcher and change table paper, wipe instruments, stands and computer touchpoints, spot-clean the floor and restock consumables, all under time pressure before the next patient enters.

Called to clean up a spill or bodily-fluid contamination (blood, vomit, urine) in a patient room, bathroom or hallway: don PPE, contain and absorb the material, apply hospital disinfectant with required dwell time, bag as regulated waste, and place wet-floor signage.

Routine cleaning of a shared or public restroom in a patient care area (visitor restroom, multi-stall staff/patient restroom near a waiting room): scrub and disinfect toilets/urinals, sinks, mirrors and fixtures, empty waste bins, mop and dry the floor.

Cleaning of other patient areas' floors and common spaces: mopping/scrubbing corridors, waiting rooms, lounges and nurses'-station areas, picking up litter and spot-cleaning, typically on a scheduled route during or after hours.

tasks.label: Collect and transport infectious or hazardous waste in closed containers for sterilization or disposal, in accordance with applicable law, standards, or policies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing-unit round: orderly goes floor to floor, pulls filled red-bag biohazard liners out of covered bins in patient rooms and soiled utility rooms, closes/ties each bag, drops it into a covered waste cart, relines the bins, then wheels the cart through occupied corridors and elevators to the central soiled-waste holding room.

Cart haul: pick up loaded, closed waste carts, tubs and RMW bins staged at unit soil rooms and department collection points, tow/push them through corridors and elevators to the central waste holding area, compactor bay or loading dock, and return clean empty carts to the units.

OR / procedure-area turnover: after a case, gather sealed biohazard bags, suction canisters and full sharps containers from cluttered rooms, place them in closed transport containers, and move them to soiled holding or decontamination quickly enough for the next case.

Sharps container exchange round in patient rooms, clinics and labs: check fill levels, close and lock full wall-bracketed or counter containers, mount replacement containers, place the sealed full ones in a closed transport tub and deliver to the secure waste storage room.

Contaminated instrument transport: collect closed case carts / covered biohazard transport containers of soiled surgical instruments and scopes from ORs and units and deliver them to the sterile processing decontamination area for sterilization; return clean carts.

Chemotherapy/trace hazardous pharmaceutical and pathology-lab waste pickup: collect sealed yellow, black and pathology containers from pharmacy, oncology and laboratory, verify labeling and segregation, log the pickup, and deliver to the secure hazardous-waste accumulation area for licensed disposal.

tasks.label: Transport specimens, laboratory items, or pharmacy items, ensuring proper documentation and delivery to authorized personnel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine intra-hospital specimen round: orderly collects labeled blood/urine/tissue specimen bags from nursing units, ED and clinic draw stations, verifies labels/requisitions, rides elevators through busy corridors and delivers to the central lab receiving window, logging the handoff in the tracking system.

Pharmacy run: picks up filled medication orders from the inpatient pharmacy (including narcotics and chemo requiring chain-of-custody signature), carries them to nursing units or the OR desk, and hands them only to a verified nurse/authorized staffer who signs or badges for receipt.

Urgent but not emergency transport: stat medication, an urgent add-on lab specimen, or a cooler of blood products from the blood bank to a unit; must arrive promptly with temperature integrity preserved and receipt verified by the receiving nurse.

Minutes-critical hand-carry: OR frozen-section specimen run to pathology while the patient is on the table, or a massive-transfusion cooler to the trauma bay; requires entering restricted OR/trauma areas and hand-to-hand transfer to named staff within a few minutes.

Bulk lab/pharmacy items: moving carts or totes of reagents, IV fluids, specimen collection kits and refrigerated boxes from the dock or central storeroom to lab and pharmacy areas, using service corridors and freight elevators, with delivery signed for by department staff.

Transport outside the main building: carrying specimens or pharmacy items across the hospital campus to a cancer center, outpatient lab or another building — outdoor walkways, weather, parking areas — and occasionally an off-site run to a clinic or reference lab over public roads.

tasks.label: Collect soiled linen or trash.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Empty waste receptacles in occupied patient rooms, patient bathrooms and nursing stations: pull the filled liner out of the can, tie it off, insert a fresh liner, and drop the bag into a collection cart. Rooms are cluttered with visitors, IV poles, over-bed tables and cords.

Strip used or soiled linen from beds and stretchers after a discharge or after a patient transport: pull sheets, pads and blankets (sometimes wet or contaminated) off the mattress without shaking them, bundle them and place them in the linen hamper or bag.

Unit round: walk the floor collecting filled linen bags and trash bags from hallway hampers, soiled utility/chute rooms and service closets, tie and lift them, and load them onto a transport cart or send them down the linen/trash chute.

Haul loaded soiled-linen and waste carts from unit collection points and mustering areas through corridors and service elevators to the laundry/sanitation dock or compactor, and return empty carts to the units.

Operating-room / procedure-room turnover: after a case, gather soiled drapes and linen into the linen hamper and segregate regulated medical waste bags into the correct containers, then remove them from the room within a tight turnover window, working around booms, cords and equipment.

tasks.label: Provide physical support to patients to assist them to perform daily living activities, such as getting out of bed, bathing, dressing, using the toilet, standing, walking, or exercising.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/skilled-nursing room: get a partially or fully dependent patient out of bed and into a wheelchair, chair, commode or stretcher (and the reverse) — raising the head of bed, swinging legs over, gait-belt pivot or sling/ceiling-lift transfer, plus boosting and repositioning a heavy or bariatric patient up in bed while managing IV lines, drains and catheters.

Ambulating a patient: helping them stand from bed or chair, supporting part of their weight with a gait belt or walker while walking in the room or down the unit corridor, watching for dizziness or knee buckling, and easing them back into bed or chair.

Toileting a weak but partly mobile patient: walking or wheeling them to the bathroom or bedside commode, managing gown/clothing and lines, steadying them on and off the toilet, perineal cleaning and hand hygiene.

Elimination care for a fully bedbound patient: rolling and holding the patient to place/remove a bedpan or change an incontinence brief, cleaning and drying the perineum and buttocks, changing soiled linen.

Bathing and dressing a dependent patient: bed bath or shower-chair shower including hair, back and perineal washing, towel drying, skin checks, and putting on a gown or the patient's own clothing over weak or contracted limbs.

Carrying out a prescribed mobility/exercise program on a rehab or med-surg unit: passive and active range-of-motion, sitting-balance and sit-to-stand practice, supported standing and walking distance per the therapy plan.

tasks.label: Separate collected materials for disposal, recycling, or reuse, in accordance with environmental policies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Patient-care unit round: bags and bins pulled from patient rooms and the soiled utility room must be kept in their correct streams — red-bag regulated medical waste, sealed sharps containers, clear-bag general trash, and unit recycling — with misdirected items pulled out and re-bagged before the carts go to holding.

Operating-room turnover, bulk stream split: blue sterile wrap, rigid plastics/basins, packaging and paper pulled out for recycling and separated from general trash and red-bag waste, done under time pressure between cases.

Operating-room turnover, judgment items: triaging unopened/unused sterile supplies for reuse or charitable donation (checking package integrity and dating) and segregating fluid-filled suction canisters and loose sharps from the rest of the case waste.

Central soiled-holding room / loading dock: consolidating carts arriving from all units, opening and re-sorting mixed or contaminated bags, breaking down and baling cardboard, and feeding the correct recycling bins and compactors for hauler pickup.

Reusable-item routing: separating soiled linens and gowns from waste bags for the laundry contractor, and routing reusable basins/instrument trays, reusable rigid sharps containers, and equipment to reprocessing rather than the trash.

Non-clinical areas (break rooms, nurses' stations, lobbies, offices): pulling commingled recycling and trash, separating paper/cans/bottles/cartons and removing contaminants such as liquids, food, and PPE before consolidating for pickup.

sources.title: This Denver waste business is adding AI robot arms to ramp up its recycling efforts. Here's how.
sources.claim: Glacier's AI-guided robotic sorting arm, installed May 2026 on the single-stream line at Republic Services' north Denver MRF, autonomously plucks cardboard off the conveyor faster and with fewer errors than a human sorter on the same line, and can be re-stationed to pick plastic, glass or ferrous metal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: separating collected mixed materials into disposal vs. recycling streams. Same objects an orderly separates (cardboard, plastics, glass, metal, refuse), same accepted output (clean streams), performed on conveyor-fed presentation, i.e., the purpose-built (E1) version of the orderly's sorting.

sources.title: AMP Robotics' recycling robots bring in $91M - The Robot Report
sources.claim: AMP's Cortex robotic sorting system picks recyclables from mixed streams on conveyors at high speed and accuracy in material recovery facilities.

sources.title: AMP to Operate Waste Connections Recycling Facility with AI-Powered Sortation Technology
sources.claim: AMP's robotic sortation technology is in large-scale commercial service, with hundreds of AI-guided systems installed in recycling facilities across three continents plus company-operated sorting facilities.

sources.claim: ZenRobotics Fast Picker robots sort lightweight municipal solid waste into plastics, fiber and metal streams using a vacuum gripper on a sorting line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: separating collected mixed refuse into recyclable and disposal streams, the same operation an orderly performs on collected hospital general waste, executed in a purpose-built conveyor cell.

sources.title: Robotic Waste Sorting for C&D and C&I | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: ZenRobotics robots sort mixed commercial & industrial and construction waste — bulky, bagged, heterogeneous material — reaching purity levels of up to 99%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic separation of heterogeneous commercial waste including bagged and rigid items, comparable in object variety and required stream purity to the bag/container-level separation an orderly performs on collected hospital waste.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: Autonomous TUG mobile robots at Froedtert Hospital haul carts of trash, recycling and regulated medical waste through hospital corridors, but they transport already-separated streams; hospital staff perform the separation.

sources.title: CleanRobotics announces new features for TrashBot autonomous scrap-sorting bin - Recycling Today

tasks.label: Restrain patients to prevent violence or injury or to assist physicians or nurses to administer treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Behavioral emergency in a hospital ED or inpatient psychiatric unit: orderly joins a response team to physically hold a combative, agitated adult (often intoxicated or psychotic), takes the patient to the floor or bed, controls limbs and head, and holds while nurses apply 4-point restraints and give IM sedation.

Confused, delirious or dementia patient on a med-surg floor or in a skilled nursing facility pulling at IV lines, catheters or dressings: orderly physically holds/redirects the patient's arms and applies soft wrist restraints, mitts or a lap belt at nursing direction, keeping the patient safe and skin intact.

Assisting a procedure: orderly holds a resistant or frightened patient (adult or child) still — immobilizing an arm, leg, head or torso — while a nurse or physician starts an IV, draws blood, sutures a wound, places a catheter, or positions for x-ray, adjusting hold as the patient struggles and releasing on cue.

Escalation during transport or ambulation in a corridor, elevator or radiology suite: orderly blocks, steadies or bear-hugs a patient who suddenly becomes combative or begins to fall off a stretcher/wheelchair, controlling them until help arrives.

Maintenance of an existing restraint on a hospital unit: orderly repositions a restrained patient, loosens and re-applies straps for range-of-motion, circulation and toileting checks, and holds limbs while restraints are removed or re-secured.

sources.developer: RIKEN-SRK Collaboration Center for Human-Interactive Robot Research / Sumitomo Riko
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the most advanced physical patient-handling robot reported, is an experimental prototype that lifts a cooperative patient from bed to wheelchair under caregiver direction; it has no capability to control a resisting or combative patient and was never commercialized or deployed in hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically lifting/transferring a patient. It is the closest robotic system that makes forceful body contact with a patient, so it bounds the state of the art; even there the patient is passive and cooperative, the robot is a 140 kg lab prototype, and nothing in the report indicates it can absorb or counter the dynamic forces of a struggling patient or apply restraint straps.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The largest fleet of autonomous mobile manipulators actually working in US hospitals, Moxi, performs only logistics (supply, lab-sample and pharmacy deliveries); its deployed capability involves no physical contact with patients, let alone restraint.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside hospital wards. It establishes that hospital-deployed robots operate at the level of fetching and carrying objects; patient-contact tasks such as manual holding or restraint are outside their demonstrated envelope.

sources.title: PARO ROBOT INTERACTION DECREASES PAIN AND AGITATION SCORES IN HOSPITALIZED OLDER ADULTS WITH ADRD AND/OR DELIRIUM
sources.claim: The robotic technology used for agitated hospitalized patients is non-contact therapeutic/social robotics (PARO seal) aimed at reducing agitation, not physical control or restraint of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: managing agitated patients with robots. It shows the only clinically used robotic approach to agitation is soothing interaction with a small companion device; it provides no force-applying or holding capability and therefore cannot substitute for manual restraint.

tasks.label: Turn or reposition bedridden patients, alone or with assistance, to prevent bedsores.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care hospital med-surg/telemetry ward: an immobile but medically stable adult is turned side-to-side roughly every two hours on a standard hospital ... using a draw sheet, positioned at ~30 degrees with wedges/pillows and heels floated, usually with a second staff member.

ICU/critical care: a sedated, mechanically ventilated patient with endotracheal tube, central lines, arterial line and drains is log-rolled/turned on a specialty therapy surface every two hours by two to three staff, with lines managed throughout.

Skilled nursing facility: a bedbound, passive frail resident is repositioned on a fixed schedule day and night on a pressure-redistribution mattress, side to back to side, as part of routine pressure-injury prevention rounds.

Patient with contractures, hemiplegia, severe pain, post-op precautions, or dementia-related resistance: hands-on turning with verbal coaxing, individual limb positioning, pillow between knees, heel offloading, and adjustment to the patient's tolerance.

Bariatric or very heavy patient (>350 lb): repositioning in bed using air-assisted lateral transfer devices, repositioning slings or ceiling lift with three or more staff, taking care with skin folds and tubing.
Boosting a patient who has slid down toward the foot of the bed, or correcting a slumped/asymmetric position for pressure relief; ad hoc during rounds, often with a slide sheet and one or two staff.

tasks.label: Position or hold patients in position for surgical preparation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine supine case in a hospital OR: after the slide-over from the stretcher, the orderly aligns the anesthetized or pre-anesthetized patient on the table, places arms on padded boards or tucks them, applies the safety strap and heel/knee padding, and adjusts table height and tilt (Trendelenburg, lateral tilt) as the team directs, holding the patient steady while skin prep is done.

Prone positioning for a spine or neuro case: with the team, log-roll the anesthetized patient from the stretcher/table onto chest rolls or a prone frame, support the head and arms during the turn, and hold the body while padding and positioners are placed and the back is prepped.

Lateral decubitus, lithotomy, or beach-chair positioning: hold the anesthetized patient on the side while a beanbag, axillary roll and hip/back supports are placed; or lift both legs into stirrups simultaneously; or sit the patient up with a head holder — then hold the pose while it is secured and prepped.

Hold a limb, head or body part in position during skin prep and draping: e.g., hold a leg elevated by the foot for several minutes for a circumferential knee or ankle prep, hold an arm abducted, or hold the head turned, adjusting on verbal direction and without contaminating the sterile field.

Hold a conscious patient in position for regional anesthesia or induction: support a seated patient curled forward (or in the lateral fetal position) for a spinal/epidural, steadying and coaching them and adapting to their movement, or steady an anxious patient during induction.

Positioning that needs special handling: bariatric, frail/contracted elderly, pediatric, or confused/agitated patients in an OR or procedure room — multiple staff, ceiling lift or air-transfer mattress, careful skin and joint protection, and physically holding a patient who is moving.

sources.title: Medicaroid Launches the SOT-100 Vercia, Operating Table with the Function to Move Patients Widely
sources.claim: Medicaroid's SOT-100 Vercia is a regulatory-approved (Japan) robotic operating table whose robot drive moves the patient on the tabletop to stored positions such as the anesthesia position, the surgical position and the fluoroscopy position inside a real operating room; staff still place the patient on the table.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as the orderly's: bringing a patient lying on an operating table into, and holding them in, the pose the team needs for anesthesia, prep and surgery — same object (adult patient), same room (OR), and far tighter precision than hand positioning.

sources.system: Robotic patient positioners (six-axis industrial robots with couch top), HIT Heidelberg

sources.transferJustification: Related task = patient setup for particle therapy: an immobilized patient presented on a couch is moved by machine into a prescribed whole-body pose and held there while a procedure is performed. sources.transferJustification: Closest commercial system for lifting/handling a patient's body; cited to show that patient body-handling products on the market are caregiver-operated, so they cannot substantiate autonomous completion of free-form positioning instances.

sources.developer: AIREC project / Waseda University et al.

sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous manipulation of a human body by a humanoid robot is at laboratory-demonstration maturity: a dual-arm humanoid inserted a hand under a mannequin's back and assisted a supine-to-raised transition in a research setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = repositioning a body in bed. Cited to establish that unfixtured handling of a human torso by robots is still a mannequin-level lab demonstration, supporting the negative judgments on team turning, conscious-patient holds and special-handling instances.

tasks.label: Stock utility rooms, nonmedical storage rooms, or cleaning carts with supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nursing-unit clean utility room / supply closet par restock: the orderly brings supplies up from central supply and puts individual mixed items away - glove boxes, dressing packs, IV sets, syringes, PPE, irrigation bottles - into labeled bins and wire shelves to par levels, rotating older stock forward, in a small crowded room off an active patient corridor.

Cart exchange / bulk cart delivery: pulling a stocked exchange cart, linen cart or case cart from materials management or the dock to a unit's utility room, parking it in place and taking the depleted cart back, moving through corridors and elevators shared with patients and beds.

Restocking housekeeping/cleaning carts: filling a janitor cart parked in a housekeeping closet or corridor with chemical spray bottles, paper towels, toilet tissue, boxes of liners, folded cloths and gloves pulled from closet shelves; loose, bulky and floppy items, cart layout varies by user.

Stocking nonmedical storage/stock rooms: receiving an incoming supply delivery at the dock or storeroom, breaking down cases and shelving cartons and bulk paper goods on storeroom racking, keeping locations and labels correct.

Replenishing clean linen and PPE on open shelves, corridor alcoves and nurse-server cabinets: stacking folded sheets, towels, gowns and blankets and topping off isolation-cart PPE during a shift while staff and visitors pass by.

sources.claim: Moxi was reported doing commercial mobile manipulation in Texas hospitals, picking supplies out of supply ..., autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking supplies off hospital supply-closet shelves, the inverse motion of stocking them. Same rooms and objects; later deployment reporting describes transport and delivery work rather than item-level put-away to par levels.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading and handling shipping cases. Same objects (cartons) and comparable handling to breaking down an incoming supply delivery, though Stretch places cases on conveyors and pallets rather than on stockroom shelves.

tasks.label: Stock or issue medical supplies, such as dressing packs or treatment trays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restocking a nursing-unit clean supply room to par: the orderly brings up totes/cases from the central storeroom, breaks open cartons of mixed SKUs (glove boxes, dressing packs, IV sets, catheters, irrigation trays), places them into labeled wire bins and shelves that clinical staff use all shift, rotates stock and pulls expired items.

Restocking treatment/exam rooms, isolation carts, procedure carts and bedside stock on an occupied unit: small quantities into drawers and wall cabinets in rooms containing beds, IV poles, visitors and staff, sometimes while a patient occupies the room.

Issuing a requested supply on demand: a nurse calls for a specific item (dressing pack, suction canister, specimen kit); the orderly retrieves it from the unit supply room or central storeroom and hands it off at the unit or patient room, often urgently.

Bulk transport and cart exchange: moving loaded supply carts, linen carts and OR case carts from the dock or central storeroom through corridors and elevators to units/ORs and swapping them for empty carts.

Assembling and issuing a treatment tray or dressing pack: gathering a defined set of items (gauze, saline, gloves, instrument pack, tape) onto a tray or into a kit and delivering it to the treatment room or bedside before a procedure.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking of medical-supply SKUs. Same objects (packaged medical supplies) and same action as stocking/issuing (retrieve item, place into a designated container), with the work presented to the machine as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level picking and placing of packaged goods including pharmaceutical items into order containers, the manipulation required to fill bins or build a supply tray once work is brought to the machine.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence TX SCARA robots restock refrigerated shelves with bottles and ... in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores, running autonomously with rare remote human takeover; the robot is installed on a rail inside a purpose-fitted beverage cooler.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment in a human-facing facility. Transfer to hospital supply rooms is limited: it handles only uniform bottles and cans from crates into a cooler fitted around the machine, not mixed-SKU cartons on shared clinical shelving.

tasks.label: Transport bodies to the morgue.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Medical/surgical ward or ICU death in a hospital: after care-after-death (shroud, ID tags), the orderly and a partner slide a 70-100 kg limp body from the bed onto a concealment-covered mortuary trolley, cover it, move it through occupied corridors and a service elevator while avoiding visitors, badge into the morgue, slide the body onto a refrigerated rack shelf and log the decedent.

Emergency department or operating room death, often a medical-examiner/coroner case: lines, tubes and clothing retained for evidence, body may be soiled or unbagged, the bay or table is needed urgently; transfer from ED stretcher or OR table to a morgue trolley, transport, and placement in the cooler with chain-of-custody tagging.

Bariatric or otherwise difficult decedent (150-250 kg, rigor mortis, contractures, or a body that must stay flat with devices attached): requires extra staff, slide boards or a mechanical lift, a wide-deck trolley and a freight elevator to reach the morgue and get the body onto a rack or floor tray.

Nursing home, hospice or long-term care facility: deceased resident moved from a resident room onto a covered cot or trolley and taken along carpeted corridors past other residents and family to a holding room or directly to the funeral director's vehicle at a side entrance/loading dock.

Infant, neonatal or fetal remains, or anatomical specimens/amputated limbs: small remains placed in a labeled covered container or small carrier and moved discreetly, often hand-carried or on a small cart, to the morgue refrigerator with meticulous labeling and register entry.

Morgue-side movements: retrieving a stored body from a cooler rack onto a trolley for the pathologist's autopsy suite, weighing it, and later transferring it onto a funeral home cot at the dock after verifying identification bands and release paperwork.

sources.system: Frontmatec chill room / storage conveyor system (Duoplan overhead conveyors)
sources.date: 2025 (product line in commercial use for years)
sources.title: Chill room for pigs - Professional carcass chilling system
sources.claim: Frontmatec's fully automatic chill rooms convey heavy limp pig carcasses from the processing line into refrigerated storage and sort them by weight onto storage conveyors, then load them back out automatically - machine-controlled handling of 80-120 kg limp bodies into and out of cold storage in a purpose-built facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated conveyance and cold-room storage of animal carcasses. It transfers to transporting a body to a morgue cooler because the payload is a comparable-mass (80-120 kg), limp, deformable body that must be moved without damage from a presentation point into refrigerated racking and retrieved on demand; only the E1 fixturing (carcass on a rail/tray) makes it tractable, which is exactly what the E1 counterfactual grants.

sources.system: Swisslog ASRS (Vectura cranes, SynQ software) at Agile Cold Storage
sources.title: Agile Cold Storage, USA: Maximizing storage and uptime with Swisslog's advanced automation
sources.claim: Swisslog's ASRS with Vectura stacker cranes automatically stores and retrieves palletized loads inside a working cold-storage facility, showing automated insertion and retrieval of heavy unit loads into refrigerated racking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cold-store pallet storage and retrieval. At E1 a decedent is presented on a fixtured tray, which is mechanically a unit load of similar mass and footprint; morgue racks are themselves rollered shelves, so insertion and retrieval into refrigerated racking is the same materials-handling operation the ASRS performs unattended.

sources.title: MiR250 Hook
sources.claim: The MiR250 Hook autonomously identifies carts by fiducial marker, couples to them, and tows them to defined destinations in production, logistics and healthcare settings without a person attaching the load.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pickup and towing of wheeled carts. A mortuary trolley is a wheeled cart of similar size and weight, so the coupling, routing and delivery legs of moving a body to the morgue are the same operation.

sources.system: Aethon T3 / T3 XL autonomous mobile robot
sources.title: T3 Autonomous Mobile Robot | Aethon
sources.claim: Aethon's T3 autonomous mobile robot hauls the heaviest carts hospital staff routinely move (750-1,000 lbs) through corridors, ramps and elevators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hauling of heavy hospital carts. A loaded mortuary trolley (body plus trolley, typically 300-500 lbs, bariatric cases more) falls inside the demonstrated payload range and follows the same corridor/elevator routes.

sources.system: Aethon TUG fleet at Upstate University Hospital
sources.title: New kid on the block at Upstate: The transport robot
sources.claim: A US hospital operates a fleet of 14 Aethon TUG autonomous hauling robots that ferry materials around the hospital, establishing real deployment of autonomous transport in occupied hospital corridors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point material transport inside a hospital. It substantiates the corridor/elevator transport leg only; it does not substantiate moving a decedent between a bed and a trolley or racking a body.

sources.title: RIBA robot nurse bear
sources.claim: The most capable human-lifting robots (RIBA/RIBA-II) lift a person from a bed only under a caregiver's direct tactile guidance, i.e. they are human-commanded lab systems, not autonomous body-handling machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting a human body off a bed. It is the closest existing capability to lifting a decedent from a hospital bed, and it remains operator-guided and confined to research demonstrations, which is why no E2 judgment is supported.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi mobile manipulators operate autonomously in more than 25 US ... and have completed over a million deliveries in occupied hospital corridors, but the deployed work is small-item fetch-and-deliver, not moving people or bodies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation and delivery in occupied hospital corridors. It shows the E2 navigation problem is solved for light payloads, while the manipulation demonstrated (supplies, totes, pressing elevator buttons) is far below handling an adult decedent.

tasks.label: Serve or collect food trays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care hospital ward at mealtime: orderly takes individual covered meal trays off a delivered nutrition cart in the corridor, matches the tray ticket to the room/patient, carries the tray into an occupied room, clears and swings the overbed table over the bed, sets the tray within the patient's reach and removes the cover; rooms vary in clutter (IV poles, chairs, visitors, bed height).

Same ward after the meal: orderly re-enters each room, checks intake, lifts used trays with dirty dishes, liquids and scraps off overbed tables, floors or bedside stands, loads them back into the tray cart slots, and wheels the loaded cart toward the kitchen or dish room.

Bulk transport leg: orderly moves loaded hot/cold tray carts from the kitchen or tray-line dock through corridors and elevators to nursing-unit pantries at set meal times, and returns soiled carts and stacked dirty trays to the dish room.

Skilled nursing / rehab dining room: orderly carries plated trays from a steam table or cart to residents seated at tables, places the tray and utensils in front of each resident per diet card, then clears tables, stacks trays and wipes up after the meal.

Non-routine trays: isolation/contact-precaution or ICU rooms requiring gowning, NPO/diet-hold checks with the nurse, and trays that must be set up for a dependent patient (opening cartons and condiment packets, cutting food, repositioning the patient and bed) before the tray is usable.

sources.title: Hospital Robots | Solutions for Healthcare — Aethon
sources.claim: Aethon's TUG autonomous mobile robots are sold and deployed in hospitals specifically for food service: delivering meal carts/trays from the kitchen to patient floors and returning dirty trays to nutrition services.

sources.title: Franciscan Health Installs 6 Food Service Robots
sources.claim: A US community hospital installed six TUG T3 robots that carry and deliver carts of meal trays from the kitchen to hospital floors.

sources.title: The robotic delivery of hospital meals — FoodService Director
sources.claim: At UCSF, TUG robots carry patient meal trays through hospital corridors and elevators to the units, but hospital staff still take the trays from the robot and deliver them to patients.

sources.system: Robotic tray handling system at Johnston's Bakery

sources.claim: Industrial robotic tray-handling cells autonomously pick filled food trays off conveyors and place them into ... in food production lines, accommodating variations in tray sizes and rack configurations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring loaded food trays between a presented (conveyor) position and a rack slot. Same object class, mass and placement precision as a meal tray, and it is exactly the transfer step of serving/collecting trays once the work is brought to the machine.

sources.title: Robotics and automation by WP Riehle | WP BAKERYGROUP
sources.claim: WP Riehle supplies commercial robot cells in which one robot removes empty trays and places them on a ... and a second robot takes full trays from the conveyor and loads them into trolleys.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading and unloading trays to and from wheeled trolleys. This is the same physical act as taking trays off a meal cart or returning used trays to cart slots, performed in a purpose-built cell where trays arrive fixtured.

sources.title: Chef Robotics completes 100M meal servings milestone — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-enabled robotic arms are deployed in food production facilities assembling meals into trays at very large scale, including institutional and healthcare meal trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of food and meal trays on a purpose-built line, showing reliable work with variable food-laden trays presented in fixed positions — the E1 form of serving/collecting trays.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest commercial hospital mobile-manipulation deployment, Diligent's Moxi, performs autonomous fetch-and-deliver runs in 25+ hospitals, but its manipulation is limited to picking up and handing off supplies/bins, not placing meal trays at patients' bedsides.

sources.title: Assisted Living Robots — Care & Support | RobotLAB
sources.claim: In senior-living facilities, commercially available service robots transport meal trays from the kitchen to dining rooms or residents' rooms, while care staff still do the serving and resident assistance.

roles.title: Psychiatric Aides
roles.description: Assist mentally impaired or emotionally disturbed patients, working under direction of nursing and medical staff. May assist with daily living activities, lead patients in educational and recreational activities, or accompany patients to and from examinations and treatments. May restrain violent patients. Includes psychiatric orderlies.

tasks.label: Listen and provide emotional support and encouragement to psychiatric patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide patients with cognitive, intellectual, or developmental disabilities with routine physical, emotional, psychological, or rehabilitation care under the direction of nursing or medical staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hands-on personal care for a resident with an intellectual/developmental disability on a state psychiatric unit or ICF/IID: showering or bed-bathing, toileting and incontinence care, dressing, oral care and grooming, plus nurse-directed routine physical care (skin checks, repositioning, vitals, documenting). Resident may resist, be nonverbal, or need hand-over-hand prompting.

Mealtime assistance in a unit dining room: positioning the resident, setting up the tray, hand-feeding or cueing a resident who cannot feed himself, pacing bites and watching for choking/aspiration in a dysphagia-risk patient, then clean-up and intake documentation.

Scheduled comfort and companionship time with a settled patient: sitting with a withdrawn or anxious resident, reassurance and conversation, sensory/pet-therapy-style calming, per the treatment plan on the unit or day room.

Acute emotional/behavioral response: continuous 1:1 safety observation of a self-harm-risk patient, calming a resident whose agitation is escalating, verbal redirection and de-escalation, and assisting the team with physical intervention or restraint when ordered.

Leading or assisting scheduled rehabilitation/habilitation and recreation groups on the unit per the care plan: chair exercise and walking groups, range-of-motion, cognitive-stimulation games, music and craft activities with 4-10 residents of mixed ability.

Mobility and transport work: bed-to-chair and chair-to-toilet transfers with a gait belt or lift, ambulation assistance, wheelchair positioning and pushing, and escorting/accompanying patients through the facility to therapies, exams and treatments while supervising their behavior en route.

sources.title: FEAST: A Flexible Mealtime-Assistance System Towards In-the-Wild Personalization
sources.claim: The FEAST mealtime-assistance system was evaluated by feeding two care recipients three full meals each in their own homes across diverse scenarios.

sources.claim: SARA, an autonomous humanoid social robot, was used in Dutch long-term care wards for people with dementia and people with intellectual disabilities, running music, video, quiz and cognitive game activities with residents.
sources.transferJustification: Same population (institutional residents with intellectual disabilities) and same activity as the aide's recreational/cognitive-stimulation group work.
