tasks.label: Complete physical checks and monitor patients to detect unusual or harmful behavior and report observations to professional staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine timed safety rounds (q15-minute or q30 checks) on a locked inpatient psychiatric unit: aide walks the hallway and enters bedrooms, bathrooms and dayroom, physically locates and identifies each assigned patient, confirms the patient is breathing/asleep vs. hiding under bedding, notes location and behavior code, documents on the rounds sheet or handheld, and immediately reports anything unusual (missing patient, self-harm, ligature) to the nurse.

Continuous close observation (1:1 or arm's-length "suicide watch") of a high-acuity patient for an entire shift, including in the bathroom and shower and during meals and sleep; the aide watches for concealed items, self-injury, medication cheeking, or sudden aggression, intervenes or calls for help, and gives a running verbal/written report to the nurse.

Scheduled physical/vital sign checks on the unit: aide takes blood pressure, pulse, respirations, temperature, pulse oximetry, sometimes weight or blood glucose on cooperative-to-reluctant patients, notes physical findings (tremor, unsteady gait, new bruises, self-harm wounds, intoxication signs), records the values and reports abnormals to the nurse.

Admission and post-visit contraband/safety checks: pat-down or belongings search of a patient returning from pass or newly admitted, inspecting shoes, clothing and personal items for sharps, cords, lighters or drugs, plus environmental safety sweeps of bedrooms and bathrooms for ligature points and hoarded items; confiscated items and findings reported to nursing staff.

Milieu monitoring during dayroom time, groups, meals and med lines: aide sits in the common area watching a mixed group of patients, reads escalating agitation, isolation, inappropriate peer contact or paranoid behavior, redirects verbally, and reports behavioral observations to the charge nurse for the shift report.

sources.title: Aeolus Debuts Autonomous Dual-arm Humanoid Robot at CES
sources.claim: Aeolus Robotics' aeo dual-arm mobile robot is deployed in Japanese eldercare facilities and hospitals, where it performs autonomous night-shift patrol for resident safety, using vision to determine residents' posture and position; it opens doors and rides elevators.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to psychiatric safety rounds: an autonomous robot circulating a care facility at night and flagging resident-safety anomalies to staff. Transfer is only partial - vendor material describes posture/position detection of cooperative elderly residents, not per-patient identification, behavior coding, documentation, or detection of self-harm/contraband on an acute psychiatric unit.

sources.developer: Foxconn (Hon Hai) with Kawasaki Heavy Industries and NVIDIA
sources.title: AI Robotics, Digital Twins, and MONAI Contributions Highlight Hon Hai Foxconn's Smart Healthcare Vision at GTC Taipei 2025
sources.claim: Foxconn/Kawasaki's Nurabot nursing robot is being field-tested at Taichung Veterans General Hospital, where it delivers medication and supplies, transports specimens and conducts ward patrols; commercial launch was targeted for 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Ward patrolling and delivery in a real hospital ward is the nearest deployed-scale hospital patrol capability; it demonstrates autonomous navigation among patients but no evidence of clinical observation of patient behavior, physical checks, or documented reporting of harmful behavior.

sources.title: Knightscope Deploys at Second of Three Locations for New Healthcare Client
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot patrols healthcare facilities in the US around the clock, detecting and reporting anomalies to human security staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol of an institutional facility with anomaly detection and reporting to staff. It substantiates reliable autonomous indoor/outdoor patrol at hospitals, but the detections are security events (people, vehicles, doors), not clinical judgments about patient behavior, and the robot performs no physical checks on people.

sources.developer: study authors / hospital research team (published in Journal of Medical Systems)
sources.title: An Assessment of an Inpatient Robotic Nurse Assistant: A Mixed-Method Study
sources.claim: Florence, a humanoid robotic nurse assistant, autonomously navigated a hospital general medicine ward, located and identified patients by facial recognition, and measured their blood oxygen saturation, blood pressure ... via an extending platform with a ..., in an observational mixed-method study.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the vital-sign portion of "physical checks": the robot autonomously acquires SpO2, blood pressure and temperature from an inpatient at the bedside and records them. It was a research pilot with cooperative, recruited patients, so it supports only a presented-cooperative-patient (E1-style) setting, not acute psychiatric ward conditions.

sources.system: autonomously navigating fall-detection patrol robot (nursing home feasibility study)
sources.title: Autonomous Navigating Robot for Detecting Falls and Risk of Falls in Nursing Home Residents With Alzheimer Disease/ADRD - Feasibility Study
sources.claim: Autonomous patrol robots that check on residents in their rooms and detect falls in a long-term care facility are still at the feasibility-study stage, with nursing staff assessing the situation remotely through the robot's camera.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic room-by-room observation rounds in a care institution with escalation to nursing staff. It shows that even the far simpler fall-detection version of observation rounds is being tested for feasibility rather than performed at worker quality, which is why psychiatric safety rounds are judged unachievable.

tasks.label: Restrain or aid patients as necessary to prevent injury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Behavioral emergency on a locked adult inpatient psychiatric unit: an agitated patient escalates to assault or property destruction; the aide joins a 3-5 person team to perform a manual therapeutic hold, controlling limbs and torso of an actively resisting adult without causing injury, while a nurse directs and the patient is de-escalated or medicated.

Preventing a fall: a frail, sedated, or medication-unsteady patient (often geriatric psych or detox) sways, stumbles, or slides while walking a corridor, standing from bed/toilet, or transferring to a chair; the aide steadies the person, bears part of their weight, guides them to a seat, or eases them to the floor.

Applying and monitoring mechanical restraints or seclusion: escorting/carrying a resisting patient to a seclusion room or bed, holding a limb still while a nurse gives an intramuscular injection, buckling four-point limb restraints at correct tightness, and periodically checking circulation and repositioning.

Dayroom or hallway altercation: two patients square off or grapple, or an intrusive patient crowds a peer; the aide physically interposes, blocks, separates, and walks one patient away, judging force and proximity moment to moment among bystanding patients and staff.

Blocking self-injury during close/1:1 observation: intervening as a patient bangs their head, bites or scratches themselves, attempts a ligature, or swallows an object; the aide physically blocks the movement, pads or removes the hazard, and takes contraband from the patient's hands.

sources.title: Andago | Hocoma
sources.claim: Hocoma's Andago V2.0 is a commercially sold mobile robot used in rehabilitation clinics that carries part of a patient's body weight during overground walking and catches the patient if they lose balance, relieving clinicians of physically supporting the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted overground gait and balance training. It transfers to the aide's fall-prevention instance because the physical act is the same one the aide performs - bearing a share of an unsteady adult's weight during walking and arresting a stumble before impact - with a comparable object (an adult human) and comparable precision requirements.

sources.title: Gait rehabilitation system - Andago - Hocoma
sources.claim: Andago senses the patient's own movement intention and follows the walking patient automatically while providing dynamic body-weight support, i.e., the support and fall-arrest function runs without step-by-step operator commands.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; this item establishes the autonomy of the following/support behavior rather than the capability itself.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest commercial deployment of mobile manipulation robots in US hospitals, Moxi, performs autonomous logistics (supplies, meds, lab samples) in patient-care corridors; its deployed capability set involves no physical handling of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize what deployed hospital robots actually do (item transport, not patient contact); it substantiates no positive judgment for restraint or patient handling.

sources.title: What is Hug? | Mobility Support Robot – Hug
sources.claim: FUJI's Hug transfer-support robot, with over 6,000 installations in nursing homes and hospitals, lifts a cooperative care recipient between sitting positions, but the caregiver positions the person against the machine and presses stand/sit buttons.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisted patient transfer. Cited to show the state of deployed patient-handling machines: they require a cooperative person and a caregiver operating controls, so they do not substantiate autonomous intervention with a resisting or falling patient.

sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: ROBEAR, a RIKEN/Sumitomo Riko experimental nursing-care robot, lifts a person from a bed into a ... assists them to stand; it remained a laboratory prototype and was never commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting/supporting a human body. Cited as the outer limit of demonstrated whole-body patient handling; it is an experimental prototype with a passive, cooperative subject, so it cannot substantiate restraint of a combative patient.

tasks.label: Work as part of a team that may include psychiatrists, psychologists, psychiatric nurses, or social workers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient psychiatric unit: aide attends the daily interdisciplinary treatment team meeting/rounds with the psychiatrist, nurse, psychologist and social worker, reporting behavioral observations (sleep, appetite, agitation, peer interactions) from the shift and answering clinicians' questions about the patient.

Shift change on a locked unit: aide gives and receives verbal handoff with the charge nurse and other aides — precaution levels, one-to-one observation assignments, changes in the care plan — and is assigned patient coverage for the coming shift.

Throughout the shift on a hospital or state facility unit: aide informally consults with the nurse, social worker or psychologist about a patient's behavior, relays requests, and coordinates timing of groups, visits, exams and treatments around the clinical schedule.

Residential or long-term psychiatric/behavioral health facility: aide contributes written observations, behavior logs and progress notes to the shared record that the treatment team uses to update the plan of care, and reviews notes/plan updates from other disciplines.

Post-incident: after a behavioral crisis, seclusion or restraint event, aide participates in the team debrief and incident review with nursing and clinical staff, describing what was observed and agreeing on the response plan going forward.

tasks.label: Record and maintain patient information, such as vital signs, eating habits, behavior, progress notes, treatments, or discharge plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Maintain patients' restrictions to assigned areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine milieu supervision on a locked adult inpatient psychiatric unit: aide is stationed in the day room/hallway, tracks where each patient is, performs q15-minute location/safety checks, and verbally redirects patients who drift into off-limits spaces (other patients' rooms, nursing station, exit doors, unit kitchen) and documents the checks.

Constant 1:1 or close observation of a patient at high elopement or self-harm risk: aide stays within arm's reach for a whole shift, follows the patient everywhere on the unit, and steps between the patient and the exit door or restricted space when the patient moves toward it.

Redirecting a confused, wandering, or acutely psychotic patient (geriatric-psych/dementia or intoxicated/disoriented adult) who has entered an unassigned area, using verbal cueing plus light hands-on guidance (hand on elbow, walking alongside) back to the assigned area.

Supervising patients off the unit but inside the facility or on its grounds — cafeteria, courtyard, smoke break, gym, escort to a medical exam — keeping restricted patients within the designated area, counting heads, and preventing wander-off through shared corridors, elevators, and outdoor gates.

Active elopement attempt or unauthorized entry by an agitated or assaultive patient: aide blocks the doorway, calls a behavioral code, and participates in a team physical escort/hold to return the patient to the assigned area or seclusion, per restraint policy.

sources.title: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR) - VA Privacy Impact Assessment
sources.claim: Knightscope autonomous security robots are deployed at healthcare campuses (including a VA health care system) where their role is to patrol defined areas, monitor activity, and report anomalies to human police/security staff — not to physically stop or redirect people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patrolling an institutional healthcare campus to keep unauthorized activity out of defined areas. It is the closest deployed analogue to keeping people within/out of assigned areas, and shows the deployed capability stops at observation and alerting human officers.

sources.system: SMP Robotics S5.2 / security patrol robots
sources.title: Security robot outdoor patrolling, video & thermal surveillance
sources.claim: Commercial autonomous patrol robots explicitly divide labor so that the robot detects and reports while a human guard performs any physical intervention against a non-compliant person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: enforcing area restrictions on people. The vendor's own description establishes that state-of-the-art autonomous patrol robots cannot perform the physical blocking/redirection component that maintaining a psychiatric patient's area restriction requires.

sources.developer: Asian Forum for Corrections / Kyonggi University
sources.title: South Korea's 'humane and friendly' robotic prison guards
sources.claim: In a maximally structured secure institution (a Korean prison), robot guards piloted for corridor patrol were limited to monitoring inmates and summoning human guards; they did not confine or physically manage inmates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping confined persons under supervision in a locked institutional setting. Objects (people), environment (locked ward-like corridors) and purpose closely match; the pilot shows only observation-and-alert capability, with humans retained for any intervention.

sources.system: Autonomous navigating fall-detection patrol robot (nursing home study)
sources.developer: University research team (NIH-funded nursing home robot study)
sources.title: Robots in Nursing Homes: Helping Nurses Detect and Prevent Falls
sources.claim: Autonomously navigating patrol robots trialed in nursing homes for resident safety patrol resident rooms and alert staff, who then evaluate and act; the robot itself takes no action on the resident.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: continuous observation rounds on cognitively impaired residents in a care facility — the same monitoring component as q15 checks. It shows the deployed/trialed capability is detection plus staff notification, not maintaining a resident's location.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA / Taichung Veterans General Hospital
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Hospital-ward humanoid/mobile robots being introduced in 2025-2026 are scoped to logistics, delivery, guidance and patient-education support alongside nurses, not to supervising or physically managing patients' movement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-ward nursing support. Included to show the frontier of hospital-ward robots in institution-controlled settings is delivery/guidance work, with no system performing patient supervision or physical redirection.

tasks.label: Organize, supervise, or encourage patient participation in social, educational, or recreational activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide patients with assistance in bathing, dressing, or grooming, demonstrating these skills as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient psychiatric unit, morning care: aide escorts an ambulatory, cooperative patient to the unit shower room, issues controlled supplies (soap, shampoo, towel), prompts and supervises for safety and privacy, gives light hands-on help (adjusting water, washing back or hair), and checks the result.

Geropsych or severely regressed/catatonic patient who cannot wash independently: full hands-on bed bath or shower-chair bath, including transfer, undressing, washing face, torso and limbs, perineal/incontinence care, skin inspection, drying and gowning.

Dressing assistance in the patient's room: selecting clean, weather- and unit-appropriate clothing (no drawstrings or belts on a ligature-risk unit), threading arms and legs into shirt, pants, underwear, socks and shoes, and fastening buttons, zippers and laces for a partially cooperative patient.

Grooming at the sink or bedside: shaving with a supervised safety/electric razor, combing and washing hair, tooth or denture care, nail trimming and cleaning, applying deodorant and lotion, for a patient with poor self-care.

ADL skill training: aide demonstrates and models hygiene steps (how to lather and rinse, how to brush teeth, how to shave), breaks the task into steps, uses hand-over-hand guidance and verbal cueing, and grades assistance down as the patient learns.

Patient refuses or resists hygiene 	reic; aide negotiates and de-escalates, times the attempt, coaxes the patient into the shower or into clean clothes, and sometimes performs assisted care with a second staff member while managing assault risk.

sources.system: Mirai Ningen Sentakuki (human washing machine of the future)
sources.title: 'Human washing machine' displayed at Osaka-Kansai Expo set to go overseas | The Phnom Penh Post
sources.claim: Science Co.'s 'Mirai Ningen Sentakuki' is a fully automatic bathing machine: the occupant sits in an enclosed pod and the machine washes and dries the whole body on an automatic cycle with sensors monitoring the occupant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated whole-body washing of a seated adult. It substantiates the washing core of bathing assistance for a cooperative patient when the person is brought to a purpose-built machine \soap and water on the same body surfaces the aide handles.

sources.title: "Human Washing Machine" Can Wash & Dry a Person in 15 Minutes | My Modern Met
sources.claim: The automatic bathing pod completes a whole-body wash and dry in about 15 minutes using water jets and microbubbles.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task: establishes cycle time and completeness (wash plus dry) comparable to the output an aide is expected to deliver for a patient's shower.

sources.title: Japan's Human Washing Machine Is Here and You Can Try It for Free | Tokyo Weekender
sources.claim: The machine is a sold product rather than an exhibit: the first unit entered service in a hotel in December 2025, and it is marketed to medical facilities and nursing homes.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes maturity (real commercial installation) of the automated whole-body washing station cited for the bathing instance.

sources.title: Expo-Inspired 'Human Washing Machine' Tech Debuts in Japan's Nursing Care, Slashing Bathing Burdens — BigGo Finance
sources.claim: A nursing-care derivative of the Expo washing machine, the 'Miraburu Assist Bath', was installed in an assisted-living home in Osaka in June 2026 to reduce the burden of bathing assistance; caregivers remain part of the routine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: facility bathing of dependent residents. Cited only as context on how far automated bathing has reached care settings; the care version's autonomy is not established, so it supports no positive judgment.

sources.title: Panasonic Tests a Hair Washing Robot - TFOT
sources.claim: Panasonic's hair-washing (Head Care) robot autonomously 3D-scans the head and shampoos and rinses with robotic fingers at a purpose-built basin; it was trialled with real customers at Japanese salons in 2012 and aimed at hospitals and care facilities, but was never commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shampooing another person's hair, one component of grooming. Shows autonomous contact care of the head at a fixed station, but covers only hair washing, not shaving, oral, nail or whole-body care.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance (arXiv:2401.15159)
sources.claim: State of the art in robot bed bathing is a laboratory system: RABBIT wipes the limbs of participants lying on a bed with a compliant end-effector in a user study; it does not perform a complete bed bath (undressing, perineal care, turning, drying, gowning).
sources.transferJustification: Directly the hands-on bathing instance, but only the limb-wiping sub-step in a lab, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance at any tier.

sources.system: CMU robot-assisted dressing system (Yufei Wang et al.)
sources.title: Robotic-assisted dressing system accommodates different poses, body types and garments | TechXplore
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing remains a research demonstration: learned systems pull a hospital gown up the arm of a cooperative seated participant in a laboratory; no system dresses a person in full clothing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the dressing instance, but limited to one sleeve on a cooperative participant in a lab; it cannot substantiate whole-outfit dressing of a psychiatric patient.

sources.system: Humanoid care robot platforms (review of 25 platforms)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots for Elderly Care: A Family Guide (2026)
sources.claim: Reviews of humanoid and care robot platforms as of 2026 find no evidence of robots performing complex physical personal care such as bathing, dressing or patient transfers.
sources.transferJustification: Survey-level corroboration for the negative judgments on hands-on bathing, dressing, grooming, skill demonstration and resistant-patient care; no specific system is credited.

tasks.label: Aid patients in becoming accustomed to hospital routines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Serve meals or feed patients needing assistance or persuasion.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mealtime on a locked psychiatric inpatient unit: the aide takes labeled trays off the delivered food cart, matches each to the patient and diet order (allergies, tyramine/fluid restrictions), places trays and drinks in front of patients seated in the unit dining room, supervises the meal, counts utensils in and out, and clears trays.

A patient refuses or will not engage with food (paranoid belief the food is poisoned, anorexia nervosa, profound depression, mania with distractibility). The aide sits with the patient, coaxes and negotiates, offers alternatives, keeps the patient at the table through the meal, and reports intake/refusal to nursing.

Mealtime setup and light assistance short of full feeding: opening milk cartons, condiment and juice cups, peeling lids, cutting meat into bite-sized pieces, positioning the tray and adaptive utensils, prompting a distracted or disorganized patient bite by bite, and watching for choking, hoarding, or pocketing of food.

Hand-feeding a physically dependent but cooperative patient (geriatric-psych, post-stroke, severe parkinsonism, heavily medicated) at a dining table or bedside: spoon-to-mouth bites at the patient's pace, alternating food and drink, wiping the mouth, watching swallowing, and recording percentage consumed.

Hand-feeding a resistive or severely cognitively impaired patient (advanced dementia, catatonia, agitation): the patient does not open the mouth on request, turns away, may swat at the spoon or spit food; the aide uses verbal and tactile cueing, repositioning, and constant aspiration monitoring, stopping if the patient becomes assaultive.

Meal service in a community residential program or group home for the mentally ill (or at bedside in a patient's room): the aide plates food in an ordinary kitchen, carries plates to a dining table set for several residents, provides drinks and seconds, prompts residents to come to the table, and clears afterwards.

sources.system: ADA robot-assisted feeding system (personalrobotics/ada_feeding, HRI'25 out-of-lab system)
sources.developer: University of Washington Personal Robotics Lab / Cornell EmPRISE
sources.title: Lessons Learned from Designing and Evaluating a Robot-Assisted Feeding System for Out-of-Lab Use
sources.claim: An end-to-end robot-assisted feeding system (ADA arm, Cornell/UW) fed users with motor impairments entire meals of their choice outside the lab — in a cafeteria, office and conference room — and for 10 meals over 5 days in a user's home, with the robot autonomously acquiring and transferring bites under user command.

sources.system: Feel the Bite (ADA / Kinova JACO feeding system)
sources.title: Feel the Bite: Robot-Assisted Inside-Mouth Bite Transfer using Robust Mouth Perception and Physical Interaction-Aware Control
sources.claim: A robot-assisted feeding system performed inside-mouth bite transfer with real-time mouth tracking and interaction-aware control, feeding 13 care recipients with severe ... at a university, a medical center, ....

sources.developer: RoboEatz with Aramark, ABB Robotics and WellSpan Health
sources.title: Aramark and RoboEatz Develop Robotic Meal Service to Support Healthcare Workers Around the Clock
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic kitchen installed in a hospital footprint prepares, plates and serves personalized bowl meals to order from up to 80 ingredients, handling storage, preparation, cleaning and plating with minimal staffing and compliance with nutritional standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing and dispensing a complete, diet-specific meal to a person at a fixtured serving station. It substantiates the serving leg of the aide's task at E1 — the same objects (portioned hot meals in bowls/trays, dietary-rule compliance) presented to a diner who comes to the machine.

sources.system: Chef / Chef+ AI food assembly robot
sources.title: 100 Million Servings and Counting | Blog | Chef Robotics
sources.claim: AI-enabled food-assembly robots deployed in more than ... have plated over 100 million servings, placing varied ingredients into specific compartments of meal trays, including healthcare/hospital patient trays and airline catering trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling and portioning meals into tray compartments to a specified diet on a fixtured line. Transfers to the E1 counterfactual of 'serving a meal' — the correct meal placed complete on the patient's tray — with commercial reliability on the same food objects.

sources.title: Bringing Comfort & Care to Senior Living with Servi — Bear Robotics
sources.claim: Autonomous food-running robots are commercially deployed in senior-living dining rooms and hospital dining, carrying trays of meals from the kitchen to resident tables; staff load the robot and remain responsible for serving residents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restaurant/dining-room food running. Shows the transport leg of meal service is automated in E2 facilities, but loading and handing food to the diner remains human, so it does not by itself complete tray service to identified patients.

sources.title: Franciscan Health Installs 6 Aethon Robots for Food Service and Environmental Logistics
sources.claim: Hospital logistics robots autonomously carry carts of meal trays from the kitchen to inpatient floors; nursing staff still take the trays to the correct patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital meal-tray cart transport. Establishes autonomous meal logistics inside an E2 facility, but stops at the floor pantry; the patient-facing serving step is not performed.

sources.title: Obi Robotic Feeding Device | School Health
sources.claim: A commercially sold robotic feeding device scoops food from a plate and delivers it to caregiver-taught mouth locations, but the diner must trigger each bite with a switch and must be able to chew and swallow unaided.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assistive self-feeding. Listed for context only; bite delivery is a taught, switch-triggered trajectory, so it is treated as scripted and does not support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Clean and disinfect rooms and furnishings to maintain a safe and orderly environment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled disinfection rounds on the inpatient psychiatric unit: wiping down high-touch hard surfaces and furnishings with disinfectant — door handles, handrails, light switches, dayroom tabletops, chair arms, counters, shared equipment — in fixed, spartan, anti-ligature-furnished spaces between shifts.

Cleaning a patient bedroom: daily tidy and wipe of bed frame, built-in desk/dresser and window ledge, emptying trash, spot-cleaning the floor around the patient's belongings (sometimes with the patient present), plus full turnover after discharge — strip and remake bed, wipe mattress and every furnishing, clean the ensuite, mop, check for hazards/contraband.
Open-floor care in unit corridors, dayroom and dining room: vacuuming, dust-mopping and damp-mopping clear floor areas on a routine schedule while patients and staff move through.

Cleanup of the dayroom and dining area after meals, snacks and groups: clearing trays, cups, food debris and craft materials off tables, wiping and disinfecting tabletops and chairs, wiping spills and sticky residue, resetting furniture.

Cleaning and disinfecting patient bathrooms and shower rooms: toilets, sinks, mirrors, shower stalls and bathroom floors, plus restocking soap/paper, in the small institutional-fixture bathrooms attached to patient rooms or shared on the hall.

Immediate cleanup and disinfection of bodily-fluid and biohazard messes after incidents — vomit, urine, feces, blood after self-harm or a restraint episode, thrown food or drink — anywhere on the unit, often with an agitated patient nearby and under time pressure.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.developer: POSTECH / KIST / Korea Institute of Robot and Convergence / Elphoton, with Pohang St. Mary's Hospital
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: POSTECH's autonomous wiping and UV-C disinfection ... uses a manipulator to physically wipe surfaces ... then UV-C for hard-to-reach areas; it was validated with repeated autonomous operations and bacterial culture testing in a working hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class as a psychiatric aide's disinfection round: wiping hard high-touch surfaces and furnishings under a disinfection protocol inside an occupied healthcare facility; objects, precision and setting match.

sources.title: Building Robotics That Work Outside the Lab
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields an autonomous mobile manipulator that cleans hotel bathrooms and wipes surfaces with a cloth in active hotels, with over 13,000 hours of commercial cleaning ... at Sheraton- and Hilton-affiliated properties.
sources.transferJustification: Hotel guest bathrooms and wiped room surfaces are the same objects and precision class as psychiatric-unit bathrooms and hard furnishings, in an equally institution-controlled building.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot autonomously navigates a building and cleans restroom fixtures, floors and trash during operating hours; the company states units are deployed in hospitals and airports.

sources.title: Automating Clean for Better Care: Gausium's Phantas at Alvaro Cunqueiro Hospital
sources.claim: Two Gausium Phantas autonomous cleaning robots were deployed in March 2025 at Alvaro Cunqueiro Hospital to clean corridor and lobby floors, navigating and docking without assistance.

sources.title: Avidbots partners with US provider to deploy floor-scrubbing robots in hospitals | BetaKit
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo fully autonomous floor-scrubbing robot is deployed at scale in acute-care hospitals and other healthcare facilities through services provider HHS.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (pi-0.5)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 model drove a mobile manipulator to clean ... homes never seen in training, but the developers state the system frequently errs in both semantic reasoning and motor commands.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available evidence for whole-bedroom tidying and table clearing with clutter; cited to show the capability exists only at error-prone research-demo level, not at worker-acceptable reliability.

sources.title: Watch A New Humanoid Robot Clean A Hotel Room Like It Owns The Place
sources.claim: Zerith's H1 humanoid is presented as a hotel housekeeping robot that cleans floors, restocks amenities and scrubs toilets; the demonstration is vendor-produced and the degree of unaided autonomy is not independently established.
sources.transferJustification: Whole-guest-room housekeeping is the analogue of patient-room cleaning; autonomy is unverified, so it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Complete administrative tasks, such as entering orders into computer, answering telephone calls, or maintaining medical or facility information.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Accompany patients to and from wards for medical or dental treatments, shopping trips, or religious or recreational events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Escorting an ambulatory psychiatric inpatient from the locked ward to an on-site medical, dental, lab, or ECT-consult appointment: unlocking/relocking doors, riding elevators, walking beside the patient through corridors, watching for elopement or agitation, staying with the patient during the appointment and returning them to the unit.

Wheelchair or gurney transport of a less mobile or sedated patient within the facility to a treatment area (ECT suite, exam room, imaging): assisting the transfer into and out of the chair, steadying the patient, pushing through corridors and doors, handing off to and receiving back from treating staff.

Escorting/leading a group of patients on grounds to recreation, gym, chapel service, courtyard, or dining hall: gathering and counting patients, keeping the group together, redirecting wanderers, supervising during the event, returning all patients to the unit.

Off-grounds community outing: loading patients into a van, driving or riding to a store or community religious/recreational event, supervising them on public sidewalks and inside shops, handling money and crowds, keeping the group intact and returning them.

Escorting an agitated, resistive, confused, or high-risk patient (elopement, self-harm, assault risk) between wards or to treatment: verbal de-escalation, hands-on guidance, physical support, and occasional therapeutic hold or restraint, often with a second staff member.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed at scale in US hospital corridors, but its work is non-patient-facing logistics (supply and pharmacy deliveries), not escorting or supervising patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation of hospital corridors, elevators and doors. It shows the navigation substrate of an in-facility escort is solved for cart-like payloads, but Moxi carries supplies, never a patient, and performs no behavioural supervision, physical support, or hand-off of a person, so it does not substantiate accompanying a psychiatric patient.

sources.title: Unifi Aviation Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchairs commercially carry passengers along pre-mapped airport routes to their gate and return empty, but the service is explicitly limited to passengers who can stand and ... and provides no hands-on care or supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a seated person to a destination inside a structured facility (airport concourse, E2). Transfer fails because the service requires an independent, cooperative rider, offers no assistance with transfers and no monitoring of a cognitively impaired or agitated passenger — precisely the custodial functions that define the psychiatric aide's escort.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Drive System (Keio University Hospital trial)
sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. and Keio University Hospital
sources.title: Demonstration Experiment Begins for In-Hospital Patient Transport Using Personal Mobility with an Autonomous Driving System
sources.claim: In-hospital autonomous personal mobility has been run only as technical trials in which patients travel to destinations by themselves, without staff assistance and without any supervisory function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-hospital transport of a patient. It is a demonstration, restricted to self-directed cooperative patients on mapped routes, and replaces the pushing of a chair rather than the accompaniment, monitoring and hand-off that the psychiatric-aide task consists of.

sources.title: A Comprehensive Review of Autonomous Mobile Robots in Healthcare: Implications for Patient-Transporting Human-Following Robots
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed review of healthcare mobile robots treats patient-transporting/following robots as an emerging research area whose commercialization still lies ahead.
sources.transferJustification: Directly surveys the closest related task (robots that move with or transport patients in hospitals) and characterizes it as pre-commercial research, supporting negative judgments on autonomous patient accompaniment.

sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous one-person patient shuttles for hospital hallways are at the development-agreement stage; the deployed Sphaira product at Charite is a protective transport enclosure, not an autonomous patient mover.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous movement of a patient through hospital hallways. It is an announced development program rather than a demonstrated deployment, so it cannot support a positive judgment on any instance.

sources.title: Eldercare robot helps people sit and stand, and catches them if they fall | MIT News
sources.claim: Robots that physically steady a person while walking and catch them if they fall remain laboratory prototypes aimed at the home, not deployed care systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically supporting a person while they walk. It is a research prototype without established autonomy, so the hands-on steadying and support component of escorting a psychiatric patient is not substantiated by a deployed system.

tasks.label: Participate in recreational activities with patients, including card games, sports, or television viewing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Day-room television viewing: the aide sits with a mixed group of 5-15 inpatients on a locked psychiatric unit, watches the program with them, comments and chats, mediates channel/seating disputes, and continuously reads the group for rising agitation or withdrawal.

Card games at a day-room table with 2-4 patients (spades, UNO, poker, rummy): shuffling and dealing a deck, holding and playing a hand, keeping turn order and scoring, simplifying rules for cognitively impaired or medicated patients, keeping conversation going and the game from breaking down.
One-on-one table game with a single patient at a fixed board or table: chess, checkers, or a ping-pong rally in the rec room; the aide plays the opposing side at a level the patient can enjoy.

Gym, courtyard or hallway sports and movement games: shooting baskets, volleyball or catch, a walking group around the grounds; the aide plays alongside, retrieves balls, and supervises a moving group of patients in an open space.

Structured seated group recreation the aide co-runs in the activity room: bingo, trivia/quiz, music or sing-along, seated exercise/stretching with 6-20 patients, calling items, prompting participation, and giving individual help.

One-on-one engagement during recreation time with a withdrawn, disorganized, or agitated patient: coaxing a patient off the bed into an activity, holding attention through psychotic or manic speech, redirecting and de-escalating when the activity triggers frustration.

sources.system: Tangy (Univ. of Toronto ASBLab / Dr. Robot Inc.)
sources.developer: Autonomous Systems and Biomechatronics Lab, University of Toronto
sources.title: Robot-Delivered Cognitive Stimulation Games for Older Adults: Usability and Acceptability Evaluation
sources.claim: The Tangy socially assistive robot learned from caregivers and then autonomously ran full bingo game sessions for a group of 18 older-adult residents in a long-term care facility, calling numbers, checking cards and giving individual assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: facilitating a group bingo session for cognitively impaired residents in an institutional activity room. Same deliverable and setting type as a psychiatric aide co-running a bingo/quiz group: seated group, standard game materials, verbal prompting and per-player help.

sources.developer: University of Toronto ASBLab / SoftBank Robotics hardware
sources.title: Long-Term Exercise Assistance: Group and One-on-One Interactions between a Social Robot and Seniors (Robotics 12(1):9)
sources.claim: Pepper autonomously facilitated repeated upper-body exercise sessions, both group and one-on-one, with residents of a geriatric care facility, monitoring participants' poses and adapting its encouragement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading a seated group exercise/movement activity for institutionalized, cognitively and physically impaired adults - the same recreation-group format psychiatric aides run in an activity room.

sources.date: 2015-12 feature; product pages current as of 2026
sources.title: PALRO for elderly welfare facilities (Fujisoft)
sources.claim: PALRO is a commercially sold humanoid used in Japanese nursing homes and adult day-care centres, where it runs recreation sessions - games, quizzes, dances, exercise - for groups of residents while staff supervise.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading group recreational games for residents of a care facility. Included as deployment context only; how much staff operation is involved is not documented, so autonomy is marked unclear and this item is not decisive.

sources.title: Achieving Human Level Competitive Robot Table Tennis (arXiv:2408.03906)
sources.claim: A learned agent on a gantry-mounted ABB arm with a paddle played full competitive table-tennis games against human opponents of varying skill, winning 45% of 29 games and beating all beginners, in a purpose-built instrumented lab rig (it could not serve).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: playing a rally sport against a human opponent for full games. Comparable to a ping-pong game with a patient, though the demonstrated environment is a fixed instrumented table rig and the robot cannot serve.

sources.developer: University of Washington / Intel Labs Seattle
sources.title: Gambit: An autonomous chess-playing robotic system (ICRA 2011)
sources.claim: Gambit is a 6-DoF manipulator with vision that autonomously plays physical board games (chess) against human opponents seated across a normal table.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking the opposing side of a physical board game with a human, perceiving board state and moving rigid pieces - the manipulation and turn-taking core of a one-on-one checkers/chess game with a patient.

sources.developer: Delft University of Technology researchers (Zhang et al.)
sources.title: An open-source robotic system that can play chess with humans (TechXplore)
sources.claim: OpenChessRobot, built on a Franka Emika Panda arm with a stereo camera, recognizes chess pieces, executes its own moves on a real board, and interacts with the human ... by voice and gesture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously playing a physical board game against a seated human with spoken interaction, i.e. the mechanics plus a light social channel of a one-on-one game with a patient.

tasks.label: Perform nursing duties, such as administering medications, measuring vital signs, collecting specimens, or drawing blood samples.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine vital-signs round on a locked inpatient psychiatric unit: aide seats a cooperative or easily redirected patient at the nursing station or bedside, takes temperature, pulse, respirations, blood pressure and pulse oximetry (sometimes weight), charts the values in the EHR and reports out-of-range readings to the charge nurse.

Vital signs on a patient who will not cooperate: agitated or paranoid patient refusing the cuff, post-restraint or post-IM-medication q15-minute checks on a restrained or secluded patient, or a withdrawn/catatonic patient who must be approached in bed and coaxed; aide must improvise, obtain what values are possible and document.

Medication pass on the unit under nurse direction: identify the patient, hand over oral doses in a cup with water, watch the patient swallow, do a mouth check for cheeking/hoarding, crush or mix doses when ordered, apply topicals or eye drops, document administration and handle refusals or diversion attempts.

Specimen collection: directly observed urine drug screen or clean-catch urinalysis in the unit bathroom, occasionally stool or sputum; aide instructs the patient, observes voiding to prevent tampering, caps, labels and bags the specimen with the requisition and sends it to the lab.

Venipuncture on the unit: fasting morning blood draws for lithium, clozapine/ANC or metabolic panels; aide verifies ID and orders, applies tourniquet, selects a vein (often poor access in long-term or dehydrated patients), draws the ordered tubes in order of draw, labels at bedside and routes to the lab.

Nursing duties in a community residential/group-home or crisis-stabilization house: aide takes a resident's blood pressure and pulse in the living room, assists the resident with self-administration of a pre-poured medication dose, watches for ingestion and records it on the MAR.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performs the whole venipuncture sequence autonomously (vein imaging, alcohol spray, tourniquet, needle insertion, tube filling and inversion, needle withdrawal and bandaging) with one supervising professional per three devices; in routine use across three Dutch hospital/lab sites it achieved 94.5% first-stick success in 1633 patients.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70m to fuel blood-drawing robot's global commercial readiness - Medical Device Network
sources.claim: The Vitestro ARPD is a CE-marked commercial product that has been placed in European healthcare settings since March 2025, i.e. it is beyond prototype and used for routine diagnostic blood draws in phlebotomy departments.

sources.system: Designated BP kiosk (Omron i-Q142) at Föllinge Health Centre
sources.title: A comparative trial of blood pressure monitoring in a self-care kiosk, in office, and with ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (BMC Cardiovascular Disorders)
sources.claim: A comparative trial at a primary-care health centre found that unattended automated blood-pressure measurement by a patient at a designated kiosk station (Omron i-Q142) performed diagnostically as well as nurse-measured office BP, i.e. the automated station reaches the quality a clinic accepts from a nurse.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nurse/aide office measurement of blood pressure. Same physiological measurement, same cuff hardware and same patient population sitting at a fixed station, so measured-value quality carries over to the aide's vital-signs check.

sources.system: Vital-signs health kiosks (systematic review of 36 deployed/tested kiosk systems)
sources.developer: multiple (review by Nature Communications Medicine authors)
sources.title: Vital signs-based healthcare kiosks for screening chronic and infectious diseases: a systematic review (PubMed record)
sources.claim: Self-service health kiosks that automatically measure a set of vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, temperature, SpO2, weight) are an established, commercially deployed technology used in clinics and other healthcare settings, with the measured values pushed to the record.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine vital-signs measurement by clinical staff. The kiosks acquire the same parameters with the same contact sensors from a patient presented at a fixed station, so the measurement step of the aide's task transfers.

sources.developer: Hitachi High-Tech Corporation with Fujita Health University Hospital
sources.title: Hospital robots collect and deliver blood samples (Nature partner content)
sources.claim: A fixed automated blood-collection device trialled at Fujita Health University Hospital autonomously maps finger capillaries with near-infrared imaging, grips the finger, applies an automated tourniquet and takes up to 400 microlitres of blood once the patient rests a palm on it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: capillary blood sampling rather than venipuncture; cited only as corroboration that patient-presented, fixtured blood-sampling stations work inside hospitals.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics (University of Southern Denmark spin-off)
sources.title: Lifeline Robotics automates swab testing in fight against Covid-19 - PLM Group
sources.claim: An automatic throat-swab robot collects an oropharyngeal specimen once the patient places their head on a forehead rest, i.e. specimen collection can be automated when the specimen is a swab taken at a fixtured station; no comparable system exists for the observed urine collection psychiatric aides perform.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: specimen collection by swab. Cited to bound the specimen instance: the automated case is a swab from a head-fixtured cooperative patient, not a directly observed urine drug screen with chain-of-custody handling.

tasks.label: Interview patients upon admission and record information.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

roles.title: Occupational Therapy Assistants
aliases: Acute Care Occupational Therapy Assistant (Acute Care OT Assistant)
Certified Travel OTA (Certified Travel Occupational Therapist Assistant)
Home Health COTA (Home Health Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant)
Nursing Facility COTA (Nursing Facility Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant)
