roles.description: Assist occupational therapists in providing occupational therapy treatments and procedures. May, in accordance with state laws, assist in development of treatment plans, carry out routine functions, direct activity programs, and document the progress of treatments. Generally requires formal training.

tasks.label: Instruct, or assist in instructing, patients and families in home programs, basic living skills, or the care and use of adaptive equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab unit: OTA instructs a post-stroke or post-hip-fracture patient (and often a family member) in basic living skills - one-handed dressing, toileting, bed-to-chair and sliding-board transfers - in the patient's room or the facility's ADL suite, using demonstration, hand-over-hand facilitation, verbal cueing, physical guarding for safety, and return demonstration by the patient/caregiver.

Acute-care hospital, pre-discharge: OTA instructs patient and family in the care and use of adaptive equipment (reacher, sock aid, long-handled sponge, tub bench, 3-in-1 commode, walker, hip kit) - unpacking and adjusting the device to the patient's height and precautions, demonstrating its use on the patient, watching the family try it, and reviewing the written home program.

Home health visit in the patient's own house: OTA instructs the patient and an informal caregiver in a home exercise/home program and in safe bathroom and kitchen technique using the home's actual furniture, thresholds and grab bars, physically positioning the patient, adjusting equipment to that home, and coaching the caregiver's hands through an assisted transfer.

Outpatient clinic (hand therapy, orthopedic or neuro): OTA instructs a patient in a home exercise program and in orthosis/splint wear-and-care schedule and skin checks, demonstrating each exercise, manually positioning the limb and correcting compensations, then confirming the patient can perform them unassisted and issuing the handout.

School-based or early-intervention setting: OTA instructs a parent, teacher or aide in carryover strategies and in the care and use of adaptive equipment (pencil grips, adapted seating, weighted vest, adapted feeding utensils) - fitting/positioning the equipment on the child, demonstrating handling, and observing the adult's return demonstration.

sources.system: Poppy humanoid robot coach (R-COOL / KERAAL project)
sources.developer: University Hospital Brest / IMT Atlantique consortium
sources.title: Technical Feasibility of Supervision of Stretching Exercises by a Humanoid Robot Coach for Chronic Low Back Pain: The R-COOL Randomized Trial
sources.claim: A humanoid robot coach (Poppy) was tested in a randomized feasibility trial to supervise stretching exercise sessions for chronic low back pain patients in a clinical setting; the trial concluded that in its current state the robot is not feasible for supervising physical activity sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: robot-delivered instruction/supervision of a therapeutic exercise (home) program. Cited to establish the ceiling of robot exercise coaching; it falls short of worker-quality instruction and involves no manipulation of clothing or adaptive equipment and no hands-on facilitation of the patient.

sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics (pilot study by university research group)
sources.title: A pilot study for assessing NAO humanoid robot assistance in shoulder rehabilitation
sources.claim: The NAO humanoid was studied in a pilot for guiding patients through shoulder rehabilitation exercises using audiovisual stimuli; it demonstrates motions and cues timing but does not handle objects, fit equipment, or physically guide the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guiding a patient through prescribed exercises, the informational core of instructing a home program. Cited as demonstrated ceiling; it is a limited pilot and includes none of the object handling, equipment fitting, or hands-on facilitation this task requires.

sources.title: Robots invade Tokyo nursing home
sources.claim: Pepper robots placed in a Japanese nursing home lead groups of residents through gentle exercise sessions using scripted dialogue - pre-scripted group recreation rather than individualized instruction with hands-on demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading residents through exercise inside a care facility (an E2 setting). It is scripted group activity, not individualized patient/family instruction in living skills or adaptive-equipment use, and involves no equipment manipulation or patient contact.

sources.title: NEO humanoid designed for household use, available for preorder - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Consumer humanoids intended for household chores still rely on human teleoperators for tasks they cannot do, indicating that manipulation-heavy work in private homes is not yet autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general object manipulation inside a private home, a prerequisite for demonstrating adaptive-equipment use and coaching ADLs during a home-health visit. Continued reliance on teleoperation shows the prerequisite capability is not autonomous.

tasks.label: Maintain and promote a positive attitude toward clients and their treatment programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Report to supervisors, verbally or in writing, on patients' progress, attitudes, and behavior.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Implement, or assist occupational therapists with implementing, treatment plans designed to help clients function independently.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing / long-term care facility: 30–45 min individual session with a frail older adult after hip fracture, stroke or deconditioning — retraining dressing, grooming and toileting at bedside and in the bathroom, sit-to-stand and bed-to-chair transfer training with gait belt and hands-on assist, adaptive-equipment (reacher, sock aid) practice, plus short day-room group activity programs; clients often cognitively impaired, fall risk, rooms crowded with equipment.

Acute hospital or inpatient rehab unit: bedside/bathroom session with a post-surgical, stroke or post-ICU patient — bed mobility, edge-of-bed balance, functional transfers (sometimes two-person or mechanical lift), grooming/dressing retraining around IV lines, drains and telemetry, hip or sternal precautions, energy conservation education, documentation in the EHR.

Outpatient hand/orthopedic clinic: session for a client after tendon repair, distal radius fracture or carpal tunnel release — manual edema and scar work, graded passive/active ROM, dexterity and functional activity (fasteners, tools, keyboard), thermoplastic orthosis fabrication and adjustment, modalities, home-program instruction.

Neuro rehab clinic (inpatient or outpatient) device-based block: high-repetition, task-specific motor retraining of a hemiparetic arm/hand as part of the OT plan of care — hundreds of graded reaching/grasp repetitions with assistance titrated to the client's effort, difficulty progressed within the session, performance recorded, delivered at a workstation in the therapy gym.

School-based or pediatric outpatient clinic: 30-minute session with a child with autism, cerebral palsy or developmental coordination disorder — handwriting and fine-motor practice, scissors and manipulatives, sensory-motor circuit, self-care skills (zippers, shoe tying), behavioral redirection and cueing, in a classroom, hallway or shared therapy room.

Home health visit in the client's own home taken as found: bathing/toileting retraining in the client's own bathroom, meal-prep and other IADL practice in their kitchen, DME (tub bench, walker, commode) fitting and training, clutter and home-safety modification, caregiver education; stairs, pets, variable layout and lighting.

sources.title: Technical Data Sheet - Hocoma (ArmeoPower)
sources.claim: ArmeoPower is a commercially sold motorized arm orthosis for upper-limb rehabilitation that provides assist-as-needed movement guidance and arm ..., i.e. the device itself titrates assistance during functional training rather than a therapist guiding each repetition.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: robot-delivered upper-limb functional training is one form of implementing an OT treatment plan aimed at restoring independent function.

sources.title: Arm and Hand Rehabilitation with the Armeo®Power — Paraquad
sources.claim: ArmeoPower is installed and used routinely at a US rehabilitation center (Orthwein Center, Paraquad), where it reduces the need for continuous therapist guidance during arm and hand therapy sessions.

sources.title: Inmotion ARM Neurological Rehabilitation Robot (product listing)
sources.claim: The InMotion ARM robot delivers repetitive goal-directed motor therapy with real-time Assistance-as-Needed: the client is seated at the workstation with the paretic hand fixtured in a customized arm support on the robot end-effector, and the robot monitors and assists movements to complete therapy activities.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: this is delivery of the repetitive task-specific motor practice component of an OT/rehab plan of care.

sources.system: Electromechanical and robot-assisted arm training devices (45 trials, 1619 participants)
sources.developer: Multiple (Cochrane review by Mehrholz et al.)
sources.title: Featured Review: Electromechanical and robot-assisted arm training ... after stroke | Cochrane
sources.claim: High-quality pooled trial evidence shows electromechanical/robot-assisted arm training improves activities of daily living, arm function and muscle strength after stroke, supporting that device-delivered repetitive training reaches clinically acceptable output for this therapy component.

sources.system: Robotic rehabilitation gym (multi-device, multi-patient supervision model)
sources.developer: Multiple device makers; analysis published in Scientific Reports
sources.title: Breaking down costs: rehabilitation robotics vs. usual care therapy in diverse healthcare models | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: Robotic rehabilitation gyms operate with one therapist supervising several patients on devices simultaneously, indicating the devices run therapy sessions with intermittent rather than continuous human control.

sources.title: Motus Nova Stroke Rehab Recovery at Home
sources.claim: The Motus Hand/Foot are FDA-listed active-assist robotic rehab devices shipped for home use since 2020 and used by thousands of ... to run gamified repetitive therapy sessions without a therapist physically present.
sources.transferJustification: Same task component: device-delivered repetitive limb motor retraining prescribed within a therapy plan of care; cited only as supporting evidence for unsupervised session delivery.

sources.developer: Universidad Carlos III de Madrid / consortium
sources.title: Automated planning and scheduling in robot-aided rehabilitation: a review | Journal of NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation
sources.claim: NAOTherapist autonomously ran non-contact upper-limb pose exercise sessions (warm-up, pose maintenance, cool-down) with real-time movement assessment, but only as a research pilot with three pediatric patients plus healthy children, and with no physical contact or hands-on task training.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (pediatric rehab exercise coaching); cited to show the limits of transfer — non-contact posture games do not cover hands-on pediatric OT sessions.

tasks.label: Monitor patients' performance in therapy activities, providing encouragement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient rehab unit or skilled nursing facility: OTA watches a patient perform self-care retraining (dressing, grooming, sit-to-stand practice), tracks reps, form, fatigue and pain signs, and gives verbal cues and encouragement to keep the patient engaged through the session.

Outpatient OT/hand-therapy clinic: OTA observes a patient working through prescribed fine-motor, strengthening, or ADL simulation activities at a table or workstation, counts repetitions, notes quality of movement and compensation patterns, and praises/motivates the patient.

School-based pediatric OT: OTA runs a handwriting or sensory-motor activity with a child in a classroom or therapy room, watches attention, tolerance and skill performance, and provides frequent praise and motivating feedback.

Home health visit: OTA observes the client performing everyday tasks (kitchen activity, bathing setup, home exercise program) in the client's own home, judges performance and safety, and encourages continued effort.

Group activity program (community mental health, adult day program, or rehab group): OTA monitors several clients simultaneously in a craft, cooking, or leisure activity, tracks each one's participation and performance, and offers encouragement.
Telehealth session: OTA watches the patient perform therapy activities over video, monitors performance and technique, and verbally encourages the patient.

tasks.label: Observe and record patients' progress, attitudes, and behavior and maintain this information in client records.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Select therapy activities to fit patients' needs and capabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Attend continuing education classes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Aid patients in dressing and grooming themselves.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient rehab hospital or acute-care patient room: OTA runs an ADL dressing session with a post-stroke or post-hip-fracture patient — transfers/positions the patient at edge of bed or chair, guards balance, hands and teaches use of reacher, sock aid and long-handled shoehorn, provides graded hand-over-hand assist to don gown/shirt, pants, socks and shoes over a hemiparetic side, manages lines/precautions, then documents assist level.

Skilled nursing / long-term care facility morning grooming routine: OTA sets up a resident (often with dementia or low vision) at the sink or bedside, cues and physically guides washing face, brushing teeth with adapted toothbrush, combing hair, shaving with electric razor, applying deodorant; must manage resistance, agitation, and skin/denture care.

Home health visit in a private residence: OTA works in the patient's own bedroom and bathroom with the patient's own clothing, furniture, clutter, pets and family caregivers present; practices dressing and grooming in the real setting, adapts technique to the actual closet, chair and bathroom layout, and trains the caregiver.

Outpatient rehab clinic or hospital ADL suite: patient seated at a mat table or in a simulated bedroom practices one-handed dressing, buttoning/zipper and fastener management, bra and shoe-tying with adaptive aids after hand injury, arthritis or SCI; OTA demonstrates, provides tactile facilitation, grades difficulty and records performance.

School-based or pediatric clinic session: OTA helps a child with autism or cerebral palsy don a coat, manage a zipper and snaps, put on shoes and socks, and complete hand-washing/hair brushing routines in a classroom, cubby area or therapy room, with behavioral cueing and physical prompting.

sources.system: One Policy to Dress Them All (Sawyer/Franka-class arm, learned RL policy)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University (Wang, Sun, Erickson, Held)
sources.title: One Policy to Dress Them All: Learning to Dress People with Diverse Poses and Garments (arXiv:2306.12372)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robot-assisted dressing (CMU/Held lab) autonomously pulls a single garment sleeve onto a seated participant's arm in a lab, reaching only ~86% of arm length; it does not perform a whole dressing sequence, lower-body garments, fasteners, or therapeutic guidance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted upper-body dressing of a human. It is the closest analogue to the OTA's dressing assist, but covers only one sleeve on a cooperative healthy adult in a lab, so it does not substantiate whole-session assistance.

sources.system: Close-fitting sock-dressing robot (hierarchical LSTM, tactile + vision)
sources.developer: Waseda University (Tsukakoshi, Miyake, Ogata, Sugano et al.)
sources.title: Close-Fitting Dressing Assistance Based on State Estimation of Feet and Garments with Semantic-based Visual Attention (arXiv:2505.03400)
sources.claim: A Waseda University robot arm autonomously put socks on the feet of 10 seated human participants in a laboratory after training on a mannequin — the most advanced close-fitting lower-body dressing result, still a single-garment sub-step under controlled lab conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting socks on a person. It covers one element of the OTA's lower-body dressing assist, but the participant's foot is presented statically in a lab and no cueing, transfer, or grading of assistance is involved.

sources.system: PR2 robot-assisted dressing with capacitive proximity sensing
sources.developer: Georgia Institute of Technology, Healthcare Robotics Lab (Erickson, Kemp)
sources.title: Tracking Human Pose During Robot-Assisted Dressing using Single-Axis Capacitive Proximity Sensing (arXiv:1709.07957)
sources.claim: Georgia Tech's PR2 autonomously pulled a hospital gown or cardigan sleeve onto the right arm of 10 human participants using capacitive proximity sensing, demonstrating single-limb dressing assistance in a research lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: donning a hospital gown sleeve. Same object class (garments) and same body region as OTA dressing assistance, but limited to one arm of a cooperative healthy participant in a lab, so it does not carry over to a full session.

sources.developer: MIT CSAIL and Harvard Soft Math Lab
sources.title: MIT unveils robot that can brush your hair
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic hair-grooming system, MIT/Harvard's RoboWig, brushed wigs mounted in a lab rig with a sensorized soft brush; it has not been shown grooming a patient's head, and no shaving, tooth-brushing or washing routine is completed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hair brushing, a core grooming element. It shows force-controlled brushing of hair fibers, but on detached wigs in a lab rather than on a seated patient, so it cannot substantiate a grooming session.

sources.system: Hybrid control strategies for safe and adaptive robot-assisted dressing (Franka Emika Panda)
sources.title: Hybrid Control Strategies for Safe and Adaptive Robot-Assisted Dressing (arXiv:2505.07710)
sources.claim: Even 2025 robot-assisted dressing work runs with two healthy in-group participants on a Franka Emika Panda arm inside a university human-robot interaction laboratory, indicating the field remains at controlled lab-scale feasibility trials rather than care-facility deployment.

sources.title: Current state and future perspectives on robotic technology for improving efficiency of nursing care
sources.claim: A 2025 review of nursing-care robotics describes robot-assisted dressing as a technology still under development, with work on individualized, autonomy-preserving assistance at an early stage — i.e., no fielded dressing/grooming care robot.

tasks.label: Evaluate the daily living skills or capacities of clients with physical, developmental, or mental health disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing/long-term care facility: OTA evaluates an elderly resident (post-CVA, hip fracture, or dementia) in the resident room — observes and hands-on assists bed mobility, sit-to-stand, toilet and shower transfers, dressing and grooming with a gait belt, cues a confused resident, and grades level of assistance for Section GG/ADL documentation.

Acute hospital or inpatient rehab: bedside ADL/functional evaluation of a patient with lines, drains, weight-bearing or hip precautions — guarded transfer to bathroom, toileting and upper/lower body dressing trial, cognitive-functional screen, vitals/pain monitoring, adjusting or aborting the eval based on patient tolerance.

Outpatient clinic (including hand therapy): goniometric range-of-motion, grip and pinch dynamometry, manual sensation and coordination testing, dexterity tests (9-hole peg, Box and Block), plus simulated ADL/IADL tasks in the clinic ADL kitchen or bathroom, with results recorded for the supervising OT.

Home health: OTA evaluates ADL/IADL performance in the client's own house or apartment — bathroom and tub transfer, stairs, meal prep in the client's kitchen, medication management — amid clutter, pets, family members, variable lighting and non-standard fixtures.

School-based pediatrics: evaluate a child's self-care and fine-motor/sensory capacities in a classroom, cafeteria or therapy room — fasteners and shoe tying, handwriting, self-feeding, toileting routine — with hand-over-hand facilitation and behavioral redirection of a distractible or nonverbal child.

Behavioral/mental health setting (inpatient psychiatric unit, day treatment or community re-entry program): evaluate IADL capacity — meal preparation in the unit kitchen, money management, medication routine, task initiation and safety awareness — with clients who may be agitated, withdrawn or cognitively disorganized.

sources.system: Kinarm Exoskeleton / End-Point Lab with Kinarm Standard Tests (Dexterit-E)
sources.title: BKIN Technologies Clinical Applications — Kinarm
sources.claim: Kinarm is a commercially sold robotic exoskeleton/end-point system that runs automated standardized upper-limb tasks and generates normative reports, but it is marketed as instrumentation for clinical researchers, and the patient must be seated, strapped and aligned in the robot by an operator; it measures sensorimotor/cognitive capacity rather than performing an ADL evaluation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrumented assessment of a client's sensorimotor 'capacity'. It does not transfer to this task — the robot only records kinematics of a pre-positioned limb; a human sets the patient up and the output is not the observation-based ADL performance/level-of-assist evaluation an OTA must produce.

sources.system: RABBIT robot-assisted bed bathing system (Kinova arm)
sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: State-of-the-art physical caregiving robots that make contact with disabled users achieve only single-limb, single-task autonomy in lab trials, indicating hands-on handling of a client's body by a robot is not at deployment quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hands-on physical contact with a mobility-limited client, the closest robotic analogue to the physical handling in an ADL evaluation. It falls short — a forearm-only lab trial provides no grading of assistance, no safety guarding during transfers, and no evaluative judgment.

sources.system: Socially assistive robot (SAR) geriatric well-being assessment study
sources.developer: academic research group (published in Innovation in Aging / PMC)
sources.title: Examining Discrepancies in Social Robot Versus Human Assessments of Geriatric Well-Being
sources.claim: Socially assistive robots in eldercare have administered standardized geriatric screening instruments, but only as verbal questionnaire delivery in a controlled facility, with no physical handling or observation-based grading of daily living performance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering standardized assessments to older clients. It does not transfer — delivery of a spoken questionnaire involves no action on the physical world and cannot substitute for performance-based ADL observation, hands-on measurement, or safety guarding.

tasks.label: Communicate and collaborate with other healthcare professionals involved with the care of a patient.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Work under the direction of occupational therapists to plan, implement, or administer educational, vocational, or recreational programs that restore or enhance performance in individuals with functional impairments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing/long-term care facility: OTA runs a therapeutic activity or recreation program (seated exercise, ball toss, cooking or craft group, reminiscence) for 4-8 frail older adults. Sets up the room and materials, positions/transfers residents, gives hand-over-hand cueing and fall guarding, grades each participant's activity to their OT goals, documents skilled participation.

Inpatient/outpatient rehab gym: one-on-one session with an adult (stroke, TBI, ortho) consisting mainly of graded, repetitive upper-limb task practice on therapy equipment with performance tracked and difficulty progressed within the session.

Inpatient/outpatient rehab clinic: one-on-one session implementing the broader restorative program - ADL/self-care retraining, adaptive-equipment training (reacher, sock aid, built-up utensils), transfers, manual facilitation and safety guarding, patient/family education, documentation.

Public school: OTA carries out the educational program written by the OT with a child - fine-motor/handwriting practice, sensory-motor circuit, positioning and adaptive tools in a classroom or therapy room; physical assist, behavior redirection, teacher consultation, data collection.

Client's private home (home health or early intervention): OTA implements the program in the home as found - sets up and trains a home activity program, adapts household tasks and furniture, physically assists with transfers and ADL practice, trains the caregiver.

Behavioral-health day program, clubhouse, or work-hardening/vocational unit: OTA administers a vocational or life-skills program - job-task simulation, work-station setup and body-mechanics coaching, money-management or cooking group - adapting demands to each participant's tolerance.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Rehabilitation Engineering Lab / Clinica Hildebrand
sources.title: Neurocognitive robot-assisted rehabilitation of hand function: a randomized control trial on motor recovery in subacute stroke
sources.claim: Rehabilitation robot delivering hand-function therapy autonomously during inpatient rehabilitation achieved motor recovery non-inferior to dose-matched conventional therapy, framed as a step toward minimal therapist supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered repetitive upper-limb task practice. It is the same graded, performance-restoring activity block an OTA administers in a rehab gym, with the same client population and equipment-based presentation.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich (Devittori, Lambercy, Gassert) with Clinica Hildebrand
sources.title: Unsupervised robot-assisted rehabilitation after stroke: feasibility, effect on therapy dose, and user experience (ETH Research Collection)
sources.claim: In a clinical feasibility study most stroke patients used the therapy robot without supervision, increasing therapy dose; the authors position it as a complement to usual ... clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unsupervised robot-delivered upper-limb training. Establishes that the machine, not the clinician, runs the exercise program once the limb is placed in the device, which is the delivery step of the OTA's repetitive-practice block.

sources.title: Arm mobility rehabilitation system - InMotion ARM HAND - BIONIK Laboratories
sources.claim: Commercial upper-limb therapy robot sold in over 20 countries senses patient movement and supplies assistance-as-needed in real time so clinicians can deliver intensive sensorimotor therapy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-administered graded upper-limb exercise program in a rehab clinic. Same objects (patient's arm in a fixture), same precision class, and the same purpose of restoring performance, so the delivery of the practice block transfers.

sources.title: Armeo®Spring - Hocoma
sources.claim: Passive/sensor-based arm therapy exoskeleton marketed for self-directed therapy, letting one therapist supervise more than one patient ... in rehab clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: equipment-delivered therapeutic activity program. Shows the standard clinic workflow in which the device, not the aide, carries the exercise session once the patient is set up; autonomy of the device itself is not established.

sources.title: NAO Zora Robot — Healthcare Solution — Price & Specs
sources.claim: Humanoid activity robot deployed in nursing homes leads group exercise, dance and memory games, but each routine is triggered by activity staff from a tablet.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: robot-led recreational/exercise programming for residents with functional impairments. Cited to show the deployed form is a staff-operated tool, with no autonomous setup, hands-on assistance, grading, or documentation.

sources.title: Co-STAR: Cognitive Stimulation Therapy by an Autonomous Robot for Dementia -- A One-Week In-Home Study
sources.claim: Social robot autonomously delivered daily cognitive stimulation therapy sessions in the homes of nine people with dementia over one week; participants completed about half the scheduled sessions and family members played a crucial role.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: an autonomously delivered structured cognitive/recreational program for people with functional impairment, in the home setting; cited to test whether the home instance can be met.

sources.title: Robots For Autism Teach Human Emotion
sources.claim: Over 400 Milo robots are used in schools to deliver a scripted social-skills curriculum to students with autism, with a trained facilitator and student iPad mediating each lesson.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered educational program for children with impairments in a school. Cited to show the deployed school form is facilitator-driven verbal instruction, with no fine-motor, positioning, or hands-on component.

tasks.label: Alter treatment programs to obtain better results if treatment is not having the intended effect.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Assemble, clean, or maintain equipment or materials for patient use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital rehab gym or outpatient OT clinic: between-patient cleaning of treatment surfaces and shared equipment surfaces — mat tables, plinths, therapy tables, exercise equipment, splint pan carts — sprayed and wiped with hospital disinfectant per infection-control protocol, done in the few minutes between scheduled patients.

Clinic: cleaning and reconditioning small therapy items after use — therapy putty, hand-exercise tools, adaptive utensils and ADL-kit items, pediatric toys and sensory items, pegboards — gathered from around the gym, washed at a sink or wiped/sanitized, dried, and sorted back into labeled bins.

Preparing materials for a specific treatment session in a clinic or SNF: gathering the items the planned activity requires (theraband, cones, weights, ADL kit, splinting stock, worksheets), assembling them onto a tray or cart, and positioning mat table, chair or adaptive equipment in the treatment area.

Assembling and adjusting adaptive equipment and durable medical equipment for a named patient in a clinic or skilled nursing facility: attaching wheelchair leg rests, armrests and cushions, adjusting walker/cane/commode heights, assembling a tub bench or reacher/sock-aid kit, fitting splint straps and hardware, replacing worn parts.

Routine upkeep and stocking in the department: inspecting equipment for wear or damage, cleaning and charging devices, laundering towels and pillowcases, restocking treatment carts and supply bins, transporting equipment between storage and treatment areas.

Home-health or school-based practice: cleaning and setting up equipment on site in a patient's home or a classroom — wiping therapy toys used with a child on a living-room floor, assembling and adjusting adaptive equipment in an unfamiliar bathroom or kitchen, laying out a home exercise kit.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.developer: POSTECH with KIST, Korea Institute of Robot and Convergence, Elphoton
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: POSTECH's 'Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C ...' autonomously navigates a working hospital, physically wipes surfaces with a manipulator and adds UV-C irradiation; it was validated with bacterial cultures and repeated autonomous runs at Pohang St. Mary's Hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical wipe-down plus disinfection of clinical high-touch surfaces in an occupied hospital. Transfers to wiping OT treatment surfaces (mat tables, plinths, equipment tops): same wipe motion on flat hard/vinyl surfaces, same infection-control acceptance criteria, same institution-controlled setting.

sources.title: Toilet-cleaning robot makes us feel better about all this AI business (New Atlas)
sources.claim: Somatic's Bathroom Cleaning Robot autonomously cleans and disinfects restroom fixtures, floors and trash in commercial buildings on a day-to-day basis after a one-time VR-based setup of the fixed-layout room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spray-and-wipe disinfection of fixtures in a facility kept to a standard layout. Comparable to wiping clinic treatment surfaces — mapped hard surfaces, chemical application, institutional cleanliness standard — though it works only in rooms it was configured for.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics operates autonomous dishwashing robots (three 7-DoF vision-guided arms) live in multiple restaurants, handling soiled plates, glassware and silverware presented at the dish station and washing thousands of items per day; it has been deployed for about a year and a half.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing varied soiled small objects (plates, glasses, utensils) brought to a purpose-built wash station. Comparable objects, dexterity and soil-removal standard to washing small therapy items (adaptive utensils, hand tools, toys) at a clinic wash station.

sources.system: CapSen PiC medical kitting cell (Yaskawa MOTOMAN GP7 + Zivid Two)
sources.title: Medical kitting with CapSen PiC and Zivid Two | Zivid
sources.claim: A commercial medical kitting and packaging cell built on a Yaskawa MOTOMAN GP7 with Zivid 3D vision and CapSen PiC software autonomously picks a wide variety of small products from cluttered bins and places them into kits at production cycle times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling kits of many different small medical items from bins. Transfers to assembling a tray/kit of therapy materials, and to restocking bins, when the items are presented to the machine in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: UR10 / UR3 assembly and screwdriving cells
sources.developer: Universal Robots (deployments at PSA Group, JVC Kenwood Electronics Indonesia)
sources.title: Five examples of automated industrial systems crafted by Universal Robots
sources.claim: Universal Robots cobots perform production assembly work such as screwdriving in deployed factory cells — a UR10 doing screwdriving at PSA Group's Sochaux plant, and seven UR3s doing screwdriving, soldering and pick-and-place at JVC Kenwood Indonesia.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening and inserting parts presented in fixtures. Transfers to assembling adaptive equipment/DME (wheelchair leg rests, tub bench, height-adjustment pins) when the components are jigged and presented as a purpose-built assembly cell would present them.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators autonomously fetch and deliver supplies, medications and lab samples in more than 25 US ..., with over one million deliveries completed including 300,000 pharmacy deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous retrieval and transport of clinical supplies through occupied hospital corridors. Covers the transport/restock-run portion of maintaining materials for patient use, but not equipment inspection, laundering or shelf stocking.

tasks.label: Transport patients to and from the occupational therapy work area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab: cognitively intact patient who is weak or deconditioned but can sit and board a chair with supervision only. The OTA brings a wheelchair to the room or day room, seats the patient, sets footrests, and pushes them 30-100 m through corridors and elevators to the therapy gym, then returns them after the session.

SNF or inpatient rehab: dependent patient who needs a hands-on transfer out of bed or recliner into the wheelchair - gait-belt stand-pivot, two-person assist, or a mechanical/ceiling lift with a sling - before being wheeled to the OT area and transferred back afterward.

SNF/long-term care: resident with dementia, agitation, or impulsivity. The trip requires cueing and redirection, keeping the resident seated (they may try to stand or grab rails and doorframes), and continuous supervision along the corridor to the therapy room.

Acute-care hospital: patient with IV pole, oxygen tank, chest tubes/drains, telemetry, or precautions. The OTA manages lines and equipment, monitors color, tolerance, dizziness and saturation en route, and transports by wheelchair (occasionally in the bed) to the OT area, stopping if the patient becomes symptomatic.

Outpatient OT or hand-therapy clinic: OTA greets an ambulatory adult patient in the waiting room and escorts them walking 10-30 m to the treatment table or work station and back to the front desk; some patients use a cane or walker and are given standby supervision.

Home health/community settings and school-based practice: assisting a client to move from bedroom to the kitchen or other functional space used as the work area, or walking a student from classroom through busy school hallways to the OT room, with hand-holding and behavior management.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. / University of Tsukuba Hospital
sources.title: Safety and feasibility of in-hospital autonomous transportation using a driverless mobility for patients with musculoskeletal disorders
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed clinical study: a WHILL driverless wheelchair autonomously carried 51 hospital outpatients with gait disturbance 100 m along hospital corridors from the orthopaedic reception to the payment counter, with no collisions or adverse events, then returned to base by itself.
sources.transferJustification: Same act as the task: conveying a mobility-impaired patient over a corridor route inside a care facility to a clinical destination.

sources.title: Keio University Hospital Begins Technical Trial of WHILL Autonomous Driving Technology to Improve Patient Mobility
sources.claim: Keio University Hospital ran a seven-month in-hospital trial of WHILL's autonomous drive system moving patients with limited mobility between mapped points without staff pushing them.
sources.transferJustification: Hospital-internal transport of mobility-limited patients over corridor routes; same objects (seated patients) and same institutional setting as the OT transport task.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. with NANA Management Services / Alaska Airlines
sources.title: WHILL Autonomous Service Expands North American Footprint with Alaska Airport Debut
sources.claim: Commercial revenue service: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs carry mobility-limited passengers curb-to-gate through the terminal at Anchorage International Airport (service started March 31, 2026), one of several airport deployments including Haneda, Winnipeg and Schiphol.
sources.transferJustification: Routine paid transport of elderly and injured people who cannot walk the distance, through crowded institution-controlled corridors - the same conveyance the OTA performs.

sources.title: LG's CLOi GuideBot is designed to revolutionise the customer service experience
sources.claim: Commercially sold guide robot with an escort mode that autonomously navigates lobbies and corridors and physically leads a visitor to a chosen destination; deployed in airports (Incheon since 2018, DFW).
sources.transferJustification: Related task - escorting a walking person along a route inside a managed facility - transfers to walking an ambulatory outpatient from the waiting room to the treatment area: same distances, same pedestrian environment, no patient handling.

sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport
sources.claim: Rovex's tow robot for beds, stretchers and wheelchairs is in a first hospital pilot at BayCare's Morton Plant Hospital in Florida; as of May 2026 it is not yet moving patients, only being evaluated for navigation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (towing occupied wheelchairs and beds in a hospital) but shows the capability is not yet in service for occupied transport.

sources.title: Able Innovations Deploys Robotic Patient Delivery Platform in the U.S.
sources.claim: ALTA is a robotic patient-handling platform deployed in Canadian care sites and, from March 2026, at Lahey Hospital in the US; it automates lateral transfers but is a single-operator device positioned and commanded by a staff member.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the bed-to-surface transfer step of the task; operator-directed, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.title: RIBA the friendly robot nurse
sources.claim: RIBA/ROBEAR, the best-known robots able to lift a person from a bed into a ..., are experimental prototypes whose motion is commanded directly by a caregiver through tactile sensors; they were never commercialised.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the patient-transfer step of the task; operator-guided prototype, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

tasks.label: Design, fabricate, or repair assistive devices or make adaptive changes to equipment or environments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient hand/rehab clinic: OTA fabricates a custom low-temperature thermoplastic upper-extremity orthosis (resting hand splint, wrist cock-up, thumb spica) — heats the sheet, molds it directly on the patient's arm/hand while positioning joints, trims edges, flares, rivets/attaches straps and padding, checks for pressure points, then re-heats and adjusts after a wear trial.

Clinic, bedside, or SNF room: OTA adapts everyday tools and ADL equipment to one client — builds up utensil/pen handles with foam tubing cut to size, adds a universal cuff, bends a spoon, adds Velcro/D-ring straps or non-slip material, drills/cuts a reacher or dressing stick, and trials each change with the client, revising until it works.

Clinic/SNF: repairing and readjusting existing devices and DME — re-molding a cracked or loosened splint, replacing worn straps and padding, adjusting walker/cane/wheelchair heights, armrests and footplates, tightening or replacing hardware on a shower chair or commode, fixing a broken adaptive gadget.

Client's private home during a home visit: adaptive environmental changes — locating studs and mounting a grab bar or handrail, adding bed/chair risers, installing a raised toilet seat and tub bench, removing or ramping thresholds, rearranging furniture and cords for wheelchair clearance, adding lever handles or reachable storage.

Clinic with digital fabrication access: producing a device to an already-fixed digital design rather than hand-crafting it — printing a known assistive gadget (key turner, bottle opener aid, pencil grip, custom cuff) from a design library on the clinic's 3D printer, or ordering a scan-driven custom orthosis/foam seating insert from a central fabrication lab; accepted output is the fabricated part delivered to the clinician.

sources.system: ActivArmor in-clinic 3D printed casts/splints (Fusion3 EDGE printer + scanning app)
sources.title: How to 3D Print Casts At Your Clinic | ActivArmor
sources.claim: ActivArmor's turnkey package (scanning app, design software, desktop 3D printer) lets clinics fabricate custom casts and splints on site in hours; the printer produces the device unattended from the design file, while a clinician captures the scan and applies/fits the device to the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the 'fabricate an assistive device' part of the task: the machine makes a patient-specific orthosis, but scanning, design approval and fitting/strapping on the patient remain human steps.

sources.title: 3D Printed Casts Can Now Be Made In-Clinic, Thanks to This Turnkey Solution | Additive Manufacturing
sources.claim: Trade press confirms ActivArmor's point-of-care package combining scanning app, design ... a 3D printer enables medical facilities to print custom immobilization devices in hours.
sources.transferJustification: Same fabrication step as the task's 'fabricate' verb; independent trade-press confirmation that the fabrication machine is deployed commercially in clinics.

sources.system: Ortis 7-axis robotic carving system at WCBL central fabrication
sources.title: Prosthetic Orthotic Central Fabrication Services | WCBL
sources.claim: A commercial orthotic/prosthetic central fabrication lab uses a 7-axis robotic carver that turns a patient scan into an exact foam positive in about 30 minutes to 0.1 mm accuracy; human technicians then fabricate the actual device over that mold.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (custom orthosis fabrication in O&P): shows a robotic machine in a purpose-built fab lab can produce custom-shaped patient-specific parts from a digital file, while the shaping, trimming, strapping and fitting of the finished device is still done by human technicians.

sources.system: Amfit 3D foot scanner and custom orthotic manufacturing (central-fab lab, optional in-clinic milling)
sources.title: Amfit — 3D Foot Scanner & Custom Orthotic Manufacturing Since 1977
sources.claim: Automated scan-to-manufacture pipelines exist for custom foot orthoses (3D scanning plus central-fab or in-clinic milling/printing), but a clinician performs the capture and the delivery/fitting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (custom body-fitted orthosis production): demonstrates automated fabrication of an individually shaped device, but the shape capture is a fixtured foot digitizer and no machine molds, trims or fits a device on a patient's hand or arm.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid | The Robot Report
sources.claim: Home humanoid robots marketed for household work still depend on remote human operators; no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore end to end autonomously as of late 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (general in-home manipulation): the closest system to in-home adaptive modification work is not autonomous, so it cannot support a positive judgment for grab-bar installation or furniture/equipment adaptation in a private home.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: The Hilti Jaibot is a commercially deployed semi-autonomous jobsite robot that drills ceiling holes according to a digital (BIM) drilling plan after a human sets out the site with a total station; it drills and marks but does not install fixtures or hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (drilling anchor holes in a building): the nearest deployed capability to grab-bar installation, but it only drills pre-planned overhead holes on a prepared construction site and does not locate studs, place hardware, or fasten and load-test a bar in an occupied home.

tasks.label: Attend care plan meetings to review patient progress and update care plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Demonstrate therapy techniques, such as manual or creative arts or games.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult outpatient OT / hand-therapy clinic: OTA demonstrates manual techniques and object-based methods to a patient — tendon glides and putty/theraband exercises, joint-protection technique, and how to use adaptive equipment (button hook, reacher, dressing stick, built-up utensils) — adapting grip and effort to the patient's impairment and confirming the patient reproduces it.

Individual therapeutic-exercise demonstration for an adult in a clinic or rehab gym: OTA shows seated/standing shoulder and arm range-of-motion, pendulums, and strengthening movements for a home program, counts repetitions, watches the patient imitate and verbally corrects form. Body-motion demonstration with little fine manipulation.

Skilled nursing facility or hospital, individual bedside/room session: OTA demonstrates self-care techniques on a frail older patient's own equipment — one-handed dressing, sit-to-stand and bed-to-chair transfer technique, toileting/bathing methods, energy conservation — with hands-on cueing and safety supervision.

Group activity program in a skilled nursing facility, assisted living, senior day program or psychiatric day program: OTA leads and demonstrates seated exercise routines, ball toss, and games such as bingo or card games for 6-15 clients in the activity room.

Pediatric school or outpatient pediatric clinic: OTA demonstrates fine-motor games and creative/manual arts to a child — scissors use, beading, play dough, drawing and pencil grasp, obstacle-course and sensory play — modeling the movement, then hand-over-hand adjusting the child's grasp.

Home health visit in the client's own house or apartment: OTA demonstrates techniques using the client's furniture, bathroom, and kitchen — safe tub transfer, dressing with a reacher, meal-prep simplification — with clutter, pets, and family members present.

sources.developer: Ngee Ann Polytechnic / Infocomm Development Authority of Singapore
sources.title: Robots to lead fitness lessons for the elderly in Singapore
sources.claim: RoboCoach, a robot deployed at Singapore senior activity centres, leads exercise routines for groups of elderly participants and uses motion sensors to check that participants perform the movements correctly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading/demonstrating a therapeutic exercise routine for elderly clients to imitate. It transfers to the OTA instance of demonstrating body-motion exercise technique — same movements, same client population, same facility type — but not to demonstrations requiring manipulation of tools or craft materials.

sources.title: Singapore's New Exercise Coach for Seniors Is a Bit Robotic
sources.claim: RoboCoach runs senior exercise classes without a human instructor, demonstrating fitness movements with its arms and chest screen; it was rolled out toward 25 senior centres.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: autonomous demonstration of exercise movements to a class of seniors in an institution-run activity centre, matching the group activity-program instance.

sources.developer: Görer, Salah & Akın (Boğaziçi University), Autonomous Robots

sources.transferJustification: Related task: demonstrating a prescribed exercise for a client to copy and correcting the client's performance — exactly the OTA's exercise-demonstration instance, run in an institution-controlled day-care/nursing setting. It does not cover demonstrations involving handling therapy objects or adaptive equipment.

tasks.label: Assist educational specialists or clinical psychologists in administering situational or diagnostic tests to measure client's abilities or progress.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School-based OTA assists the school psychologist or special-education evaluator during a student's evaluation in a school testing room: lays out test kits, administers and scores the motor/visual-motor portions (pegboard, bead stringing, copying, handwriting samples), keeps the child engaged and on task, times items, records observations for the evaluator.

Rehab hospital or outpatient clinic: OTA assists the psychologist/OT in administering a standardized cognitive-perceptual screening to an adult (MMSE/MoCA-type items, clock draw, trails, stimulus cards) at a table in a treatment room; seats and positions the patient, presents items verbally and on cards, times, records and scores responses.

Clinic treatment area: OTA administers the discrete physical performance measures within an evaluation battery - grip and pinch dynamometry, goniometric range of motion, nine-hole peg / box-and-block coordination timing - applying instruments to the client's limb, positioning the limb, timing and charting values against norms.

Situational functional assessment in a psychiatric unit, day program, or rehab ADL apartment: client performs a real task (simple meal preparation, money handling, medication sorting) while the OTA sets up the materials, supervises for safety, grades cues, and scores observed performance for the psychologist.

Work-hardening / vocational rehab situational evaluation: client performs simulated job tasks and material handling (lifting, carrying, sorting, assembly work samples) in a work-simulation lab or occasionally at a job site; OTA sets up stations, spots and guards the client, monitors vitals and effort, and records performance.

sources.system: Pepper (SoftBank Robotics) with Choregraphe-programmed MMSE protocol
sources.developer: Italian clinical/robotics research group (Frontiers in Psychology, 2025)
sources.title: Humanoid robots for psychological assessment in mild cognitive impairment: from evaluation to the future of AI-driven data prediction systems
sources.claim: Humanoid robot Pepper administered the MMSE to 50 mild-cognitive-impairment patients in a clinical study; the robot managed all instructions and test execution while a psychologist only monitored, and robot-administered MMSE scores did not differ significantly from psychologist-administered scores.

sources.system: Kinarm Exoskeleton / End-Point Lab with Kinarm Standard Tests
sources.title: Kinarm Standard Tests - Kinarm | Interactive Robotics Brain Injury Research
sources.claim: Kinarm is a commercial robotic assessment system (exoskeleton and end-point labs) that runs pre-programmed standardized protocols measuring sensory, motor and cognitive function and converts results to normative Z-scores, with the participant's arms fixtured in the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-administered standardized assessment of a client's sensorimotor and cognitive-motor ability. It substitutes for the human-administered diagnostic testing the OTA assists with - same purpose (quantify ability against norms), same client population, with task presentation, timing and scoring done by the machine once the client is seated and fixtured.

sources.developer: Sgandurra et al., IRCCS Stella Maris (J NeuroEngineering and Rehabilitation)
sources.title: Feasibility study of the assessment of upper limb function in children with Unilateral Cerebral Palsy using an end-effector robotic device
sources.claim: A planar end-effector rehabilitation robot (MOTORE) was used to run an upper-limb robotic assessment protocol on 28 children and adolescents with unilateral cerebral palsy alongside standard clinical scales (Melbourne Assessment 2, Box and Block Test) in a pediatric clinical setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine administration of a standardized ability test to a child. The robot delivers the test items and computes the performance indices that a human examiner would otherwise obtain by hand-timed motor tests (Box and Block, Melbourne), i.e. the same measurement purpose and pediatric population.

sources.title: Evaluation of finger strength and spasticity in hemiplegic patients using hand-finger robotic device: A validity and reliability study
sources.claim: The Amadeo commercial hand-finger robot, with each finger attached by magnetic connectors, measures active and passive range of ... and isometric grip/extension force per finger; its measurements were validated for reliability against clinical strength and spasticity scales in 161 participants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrumented measurement of hand strength and range of motion. It covers the same measurements (grip force, finger ROM) an OTA takes with a dynamometer and goniometer during a diagnostic battery, performed by the machine once the hand is fixtured in it.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot administration of standardized psychological instruments to children, the same class of testing an OTA assists a school psychologist with; autonomy of the session is not established in the source, so it is treated as non-supporting.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-supervised administration of neuropsychological screening tests. Same instruments and elderly clientele as the clinic screening the OTA assists with; demonstrated in the less structured home setting, which supports the structured-clinic case a fortiori.

roles.title: Occupational Therapy Aides
aliases: SNF COTA (Skilled Nursing Facility Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant)
roles.description: Under close supervision of an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant, perform only delegated, selected, or routine tasks in specific situations. These duties include preparing patient and treatment room.

tasks.label: Encourage patients and attend to their physical needs to facilitate the attainment of therapeutic goals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient OT clinic (adult ortho/neuro): aide readies the patient at a therapy station, applies a gait belt, guides a wheelchair-to-mat-table or chair transfer, positions the hemiparetic arm on a skateboard/table, hands over theraputty, pegboards and weights, counts repetitions, gives verbal encouragement, watches for fatigue, pain or dizziness, fetches water, and helps don/doff a resting hand splint before the patient leaves.

Acute hospital / inpatient rehab bedside: aide helps the patient sit up at the edge of the bed, puts on non-skid socks and shoes, applies a gait belt and assists a stand-pivot transfer to a chair or commode, repositions pillows and limbs, assists with toileting/hygiene and clothing, watches lines and telemetry, and coaxes a fatigued or discouraged patient through ADL retraining before returning them to bed.

Skilled nursing / long-term care facility: frail elderly residents, some with dementia; aide assists ambulation with a walker, seats and positions a resident in a wheelchair with cushions and footrests, adjusts an orthosis or splint, assists with hydration and snacks at a therapy session, and redirects, reassures and encourages a confused or resistant resident to participate.

Pediatric OT clinic or school-based setting: aide physically spots and supports a child on a platform swing, climbing wall, therapy ball or scooter board, provides hand-over-hand assistance, manages behavior and safety during sensory activities, helps with toileting, dressing and shoe fastening, and keeps the child motivated with praise and play.

Home health / community-based visit: in the patient's own cluttered home with pets and family present, the aide assists transfers from bed or recliner, steadies the patient practicing kitchen or bathroom ADLs, arranges cushions and adaptive equipment, and encourages the patient through the home program.

sources.system: ROREAS robot coach (TU Ilmenau / MetraLabs SCITOS platform)
sources.developer: Ilmenau University of Technology and partners (ROREAS project)
sources.title: ROREAS: robot coach for walking and orientation training in clinical post-stroke rehabilitation—prototype implementation and evaluation in field trials
sources.claim: ROREAS is a socially assistive mobile robot coach that autonomously accompanies and motivates post-stroke patients during self-directed walking and orientation training in a rehabilitation clinic; it provides no physical support or hands-on care.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to the 'encourage patients' half of the task: an autonomous robot motivating rehab patients in a clinic. It is cited to show that even this best case involves no attending to physical needs (no transfers, positioning, splints, hydration or hygiene).

sources.system: Socially assistive robots in physiotherapy (review of multiple platforms, e.g., NAO, Pepper)
sources.developer: Multiple (scoping review, JMIR Rehabilitation and Assistive Technologies)
sources.title: Use of Socially Assistive Robots in Physiotherapy: Scoping Review
sources.claim: Socially assistive robots in physiotherapy provide feedback, motivation and encouragement, but their use with clinical populations is still scarce and deployment status unclear; they do not provide hands-on physical care.
sources.transferJustification: Reviews the related task of robot-delivered rehabilitation coaching/encouragement, establishing that clinical deployment is limited and confined to non-contact motivational roles rather than the aide's combined encouragement-plus-physical-care task.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: The largest real hospital deployment of mobile manipulation robots, Moxi, performs supply, medication and lab-sample delivery in hospital corridors; it does not perform hands-on patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Represents the state of the art for autonomous mobile manipulation inside structured healthcare facilities (E2). Its scope is logistics delivery, so it establishes an upper bound on deployed hospital robot capability that stops short of patient-contact care.

sources.developer: RIKEN and Sumitomo Riko Company Limited
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: ROBEAR, an experimental nursing-care robot able to lift a patient from bed into a wheelchair, remained a laboratory prototype operated via tactile input rather than an autonomous, deployed caregiver.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targets the physical-assistance half of the task (patient lifting/transfer). Cited as a negative bound: it is an experimental, human-operated prototype, not an autonomous system that could attend to a patient's physical needs at worker quality.

sources.developer: VA Human Engineering Research Laboratories (HERL), University of Pittsburgh
sources.title: New robotic system improves wheelchair transfers to bed
sources.claim: Robotic patient transfer between wheelchair and bed requires a purpose-built docking wheelchair-and-bed pair and is user/caregiver operated; it remains a VA research system tested with volunteers.
sources.transferJustification: Covers transfers, a core physical need the aide attends to. Even in this maximally engineered (E1-like) configuration the system is operated by the user/caregiver and handles only the transfer step, not the surrounding care and encouragement.

sources.system: ADA assistive feeding robot (Kinova JACO arm)
sources.developer: University of Washington Personal Robotics Lab
sources.title: Video: Assistive-feeding robot gets tested outside the lab
sources.claim: Robot-assisted feeding, one of the most mature physically assistive capabilities, was tested outside the lab in 2024 with six users with motor impairments in a cafeteria, office and conference room; it is a user-directed research system.
sources.transferJustification: Feeding/hydration is one of the physical needs an aide attends to. Cited as a bound: the most advanced physically assistive manipulation around a human body is still a small-n, user-commanded research study, not autonomous worker-quality care.

tasks.label: Prepare and maintain work area, materials, and equipment and maintain inventory of treatment and educational supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-patient and end-of-day cleaning of the treatment area in a hospital or outpatient OT department: wiping down mat tables, plinths, hand-therapy tables, counters and high-touch equipment surfaces with facility disinfectant, spot-cleaning the gym floor, emptying trash. Fixed room layout, staff and patients present during the day.

Setting up the treatment area and materials before scheduled sessions per the therapist's plan: pulling the specified items from storage (theraputty, therabands, hand weights, cones, splinting material, adaptive utensils, craft/educational supplies), carrying them to the treatment room, laying them out on the table or mat, positioning mats, bolsters, chairs, and adjusting plinth height. Item mix changes with each patient's plan.

Breaking down and resetting after sessions: collecting used equipment scattered across the gym floor and tables, cleaning/sanitizing loose items (toys, putty tools, splints, utensils), stripping and bagging soiled linens/towels for laundry and restocking clean ones, returning each item to its labeled shelf or bin in the storage room, and restoring the gym to its standard configuration.

Restocking consumables: pulling par-level items from central supply or the department stock room, transporting them to treatment rooms, and stocking cabinets, drawers and mobile carts; receiving deliveries, unpacking boxes, rotating stock and shelving items.

Periodic inventory maintenance: walking the stock room and treatment-room cabinets to count and scan supplies, checking expiration dates on splinting/skin-care items, logging levels against par, and flagging or preparing a reorder list.

Preparing and maintaining materials and equipment outside a controlled clinic: school-based OT (classroom carts, sensory materials set up in varied classrooms), home-health kit packing and setup in a client's home, or a community/mobile program where layout and clutter differ site to site.

sources.title: Peanut Robotics | Home
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields a mobile manipulator that autonomously navigates rooms in hotels and corporate buildings and wipes hard surfaces with a cloth; the company reports 13,000+ cleaning hours across 25+ sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping and disinfecting bathroom and room surfaces in a hotel/office. Transfers to wiping OT treatment tables, plinths and counters — same class of large hard surfaces, same disinfectant-cloth action, same mapped, institution-controlled indoor facility, and no tighter precision requirement.

sources.date: 2023-08 (report); product marketed as deployed in hospitals/airports 2025

sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom-cleaning robot operates in commercial and medical facilities, autonomously moving between restrooms, spraying disinfectant, cleaning fixtures and floors and picking up trash; staff still handle consumable restocking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-to-end surface disinfection and trash pickup in a healthcare facility restroom. Transfers to the surface-cleaning portion of OT area upkeep: same building type, same chemicals and hard-surface wiping, comparable hygiene standard.

sources.title: Avidbots Partners with HHS to Deploy Neo Floor-Scrubbing Robots in US Hospitals
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robots are deployed by facility services provider HHS in acute-care hospitals and in airports, schools and warehouses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: floor cleaning in occupied hospital space. Covers the floor-care element of keeping the therapy gym clean, in the same E2 facility type and among moving people.

sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi performs autonomous mobile manipulation in working hospitals, picking supplies from supply closets and delivering them ... units and patient rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving individual supplies from a hospital stock room and delivering them. Covers the fetch-and-transport part of setting up and restocking a treatment area, but the cited deployments end at drop-off, not at arranging materials or shelving cabinets.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi is in commercial service at scale in US hospitals, with more than 25 hospital deployments and over one million completed deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: establishes current, at-scale autonomy of hospital supply transport, the transport component of restocking.

sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomous shelf-scanning robot is deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores, traversing aisles to capture shelf-level stock data, out-of-stocks, pricing and placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: walking shelved aisles to count stock and flag low/out-of-stock items in a store. Same physical act and object class (labelled packaged goods on shelves) as counting clinic supply-room stock and producing a reorder list; both settings are institution-controlled indoor premises.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick piece-picking cells are deployed across Staples' North American fulfillment centers, autonomously picking and placing diverse individual items 24/7 in fixtured goods-to-robot workcells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order kitting and put-away of thousands of small consumer/office/pharma SKUs presented in totes. Transfers to assembling a set of therapy supplies and returning items to bins when the work is fixtured and presented, as at E1.

sources.title: Pitney Bowes taps new Ambi Robotics system for middle-mile sortation
sources.claim: Ambi Robotics' AmbiSort conveyor-fed robotic sortation cells autonomously sort large volumes of varied items into destination bins in commercial logistics facilities, with millions of parcels sorted in deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting heterogeneous presented items into the correct destination bin. Transfers to putting therapy items away into labelled bins when items are conveyed to the machine, i.e., the E1 counterfactual for the put-away instance.

sources.title: Chicago Dryer Flatwork Finishing Equipment | Western State Design
sources.claim: Automated commercial laundry finishing machines, including Chicago Dryer's Genesis ATM, use vision and deep learning to sort, fold and stack towels and small linens hands-free in commercial laundries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: processing soiled/clean towels and flat linens. Covers the linen-handling element of resetting a therapy area when linens are fed to the machine, i.e., the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: Washing and Decontamination Systems for Hospitals | STERIS
sources.claim: Automated washer/disinfectors and cart washers process instruments, utensils and equipment loaded into them on unattended machine cycles in hospital sterile processing departments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cleaning and disinfection of loose clinical items brought to a fixed station. Transfers to sanitizing loose therapy items (tools, utensils, hard toys) under the E1 counterfactual where items are presented to the machine.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator (ORB) autonomously retrieved and restocked operating-room supplies in real-world experiments, at 80% retrieval and 96% restocking success — below worker reliability and not a fielded system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level retrieval from carts and shelving of clinical supplies. Shows the closest analogue to shelving/setup work in a clinical room is still a laboratory prototype below worker-quality reliability.

tasks.label: Transport patients to and from the occupational therapy work area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care or inpatient-rehab hospital: aide goes to the patient's room, verifies ID, assists a dependent or partially dependent patient from bed to wheelchair with a gait belt or mechanical lift, manages IV pole, oxygen, catheter and monitor lines, wheels them through busy corridors and an elevator to the OT gym, positions and locks the chair, then reverses the trip after the session.

Hospital or skilled nursing facility: patient can stand-pivot or board a wheelchair with minimal help but cannot walk the distance; aide brings a chair, seats the patient, wheels them along a standard corridor route to the therapy area and back, then returns the chair.

SNF or rehab unit where the plan of care calls for ambulating the patient to the gym: aide walks an unsteady patient with a gait belt, walker or cane, giving contact-guard/standby assist and trailing a wheelchair for rest or emergency, watching for dizziness, buckling knees and fall risk.

Outpatient OT or hand-therapy clinic: aide greets an independent, ambulatory patient in the waiting room, calls their name, and escorts them down a hallway to the treatment bay or work table, then walks them back out to the front desk after the session.

Long-term care: resident with dementia, agitation or refusal behavior, or with complex positioning equipment (tilt-in-space or Broda chair, oxygen tank, tube feeding pump, pressure cushions); aide coaxes and reassures the resident, adjusts positioning and equipment en route to and from the therapy room.

Pediatric setting (school-based OT or children's clinic): aide collects a child from a classroom or waiting area, manages the transition and the child's behavior, walks the child or pushes an adaptive stroller/wheelchair to the therapy room, and returns them to class or to a parent.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Drive System / Autonomous Mobility Service
sources.title: Haneda International Airport to Offer WHILL's Fully Autonomous Mobility Service for Social Distancing Practice
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous drive system carries mobility-limited passengers seated in a self-driving wheelchair from a station to a designated destination inside an airport terminal and then returns itself to base, in commercial airport operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a seated person with reduced mobility across a large institutional facility to a destination and back — the same physical act, comparable payload and speed, as wheeling a patient to a therapy area.

sources.title: WHILL Accelerates Global Expansion Across North America, EMEA, and Asia, Reaching 25 Airports and Facilities Worldwide
sources.claim: By 2026 WHILL operated its autonomous mobility service at 25 airports and facilities worldwide, including healthcare institutions, describing itself as the only commercial operator delivering autonomous mobility services at scale.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (autonomous conveyance of a seated, mobility-impaired person inside a controlled facility); establishes commercial scale and continued operation as of 2026.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. / Japanese hospital research team
sources.title: Safety and feasibility of in-hospital autonomous transportation using a driverless mobility for patients with musculoskeletal disorders
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed clinical study: a WHILL driverless wheelchair autonomously transported 51 outpatients with gait disturbance 100 m through hospital corridors from orthopaedic reception to the payment counter; no collisions or adverse events occurred and 86% rated satisfaction 3+.

sources.developer: Cyberworks Robotics / Compass One Healthcare / North York General Hospital
sources.title: Autonomous Wheelchair Proof of Concept Pilot Report
sources.claim: Cyberworks' autonomous wheelchair carried thirteen patients between the Emergency Department and Medical Imaging at North York General Hospital over three days in July 2025, navigating hospital corridors with onboard obstacle avoidance and no infrastructure changes; a porter accompanied each trip for data capture.

sources.title: LG Airport Robots Take over Korea's Largest Airport
sources.claim: LG's CLOi GuideBot has been in service at Incheon International Airport since 2017-2018, autonomously leading travelers on foot to their departure gate after scanning a boarding pass.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting an ambulatory person through an institutional facility to a specific destination — the same act as walking an outpatient from the waiting room to the treatment bay.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi robots operate autonomously in hospital corridors across many US health systems, completing over 1 million deliveries and 100,000 autonomous elevator rides by mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point navigation of occupied hospital corridors and elevators (supply delivery, not patient carriage); it substantiates the route-following and elevator-use portion of patient transport, not any patient handling.

sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport
