sources.claim: Rovex's click-and-tow robot, which is designed to move existing hospital beds, stretchers and wheelchairs, is in a BayCare pilot focused on navigation and is not yet moving patients, indicating that automated movement of occupied hospital equipment remains pre-deployment.

sources.developer: RIKEN and Sumitomo Riko Company Limited
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the best-known bed-to-wheelchair patient-lifting robot, remains an experimental laboratory system operated at close range rather than an autonomous deployed product.

tasks.label: Instruct patients and families in work, social, and living skills, the care and use of adaptive equipment, and other skills to facilitate home and work adjustment to disability.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inpatient rehab or hospital room: aide reinforces the OT's plan by instructing a patient and a family member in the use and care of adaptive dressing equipment (reacher, sock aid, long-handled shoehorn), explaining and demonstrating the sequence and answering questions.

Skilled nursing facility or hospital discharge prep: aide reviews home-safety and daily-living routines with patient and caregiver — bathing setup with tub bench, grab bar use, toileting equipment care — walking through written handouts and confirming understanding.

Outpatient OT clinic: aide instructs a patient in the care, cleaning, and daily use of a mobility/adaptive device (wheelchair cushion checks, walker adjustment, splint wear schedule) as delegated by the therapist.

Outpatient or work-hardening clinic: aide coaches a patient through practicing a work routine or social/community skill (pacing, body mechanics, simulated job task, money handling), giving cues and feedback under therapist supervision.

Home health or community visit: aide instructs family members in the patient's own home in living-skill routines and use of installed equipment in the actual kitchen or bathroom, adapting explanations to that home's layout.
School, day program, or community setting: aide instructs a client and caregivers/teachers in social and living-skill routines and the use of adaptive utensils, seating, or communication supports.

tasks.label: Assist occupational therapists in planning, implementing, and administering therapy programs to restore, reinforce, and enhance performance, using selected activities and special equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient OT clinic / rehab gym: the therapist prescribes a repetitive exercise or activity set (arm ergometer, ROM and strengthening drills, therapy putty, grip/pinch work). The aide sets the patient at the station, demonstrates, counts reps, adjusts resistance/range, cues technique and watches for pain or fatigue while the OT treats another patient.

Preparing and resetting the treatment area between patients in a hospital or clinic: wiping and disinfecting the mat table, plinth and equipment, changing table paper/linens, retrieving and laying out the specific items the OT selected for the session (splint blanks, weights, adaptive utensils, pegboard, hot pack from the hydrocollator), adjusting chair/table height, and putting away the previous patient's items.

Materials logistics for the day's programs in a hospital or large rehab department: pulling therapy supplies and prepared materials from central storage, transporting them to the therapy gym and treatment rooms, and restocking carts and shelves so the planned activities can run.

Escorting a patient who can sit and transfer independently: bringing them by wheelchair from the waiting area or ward room through corridors and elevators to the therapy gym at the scheduled time, and returning them afterward.

Hands-on patient work in inpatient rehab or a skilled nursing facility: assisting bed/wheelchair/mat transfers with a gait belt or mechanical lift, positioning and guarding a dependent patient, and giving physical assistance and hand-over-hand help during functional/ADL activity training (dressing, grooming, kitchen or hand-skills tasks) under the OT's direction.

Community or home-based work: accompanying the OT on a home health visit or working in a client's home/school-based sensory gym — carrying in and setting up equipment (mats, bolsters, swing, adaptive equipment) in a space taken as found, assisting the client through the activity, then breaking the setup down.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare, Diligent Robotics to bring last-mile delivery to hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous mobile manipulation robot, is deployed in more than 25 ... doing supply, lab-sample and pharmacy fetch-and-delivery runs, with over 1 million deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetch/delivery/restocking. An OT aide's materials-logistics run (pull supplies from storage, move them to the therapy gym, restock carts) uses the same objects, the same corridors and the same precision as Moxi's routine deliveries.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics unveils Moxi 2.0 with Nvidia AI for world's largest mobile manipulation robot fleet
sources.claim: Moxi navigates hospitals, opens doors, presses elevator buttons and delivers items independently; it has a gripper for picking up and delivering supplies, samples and medications.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; establishes that the delivery loop (doors, elevators, item handoff) is completed without a human operator inside an occupied healthcare facility.

sources.title: Unifi Launches WHILL Autonomous Service at Detroit Airport
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchairs are in commercial service at Detroit Metro Airport, carrying passengers who can transfer independently along pre-mapped routes to their gate and returning empty to base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting a seated person through an institution's corridors on a fixed route among pedestrians. An aide's wheelchair escort of a self-transferring patient from ward to therapy gym is the same act, same payload, same indoor traffic conditions.

sources.title: Amadeo: Robotic Hand Rehabilitation Device | Tyromotion
sources.claim: Amadeo is a commercial end-effector hand/finger rehabilitation robot used in occupational therapy; the patient's fingers are fixed into the device and the robot drives hundreds of assisted grasp repetitions in a session and logs progress.

sources.title: Robotic Assisted Upper Limb Training Post Stroke: A Randomized Control Trial Using Combinatory Approach Toward Reducing Workforce Demands
sources.claim: In a randomized controlled trial, stroke patients received 60 minutes of minimally-supervised robot (H-Man) upper-limb training per session and achieved clinical improvements similar to fully therapist-supervised 1:1 conventional therapy, with no training-related adverse events.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Consumer home humanoids are not yet autonomous for household chores; NEO relies on remote human teleoperation for complex tasks, and no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore start to finish.

sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous in-hospital patient transport remains at the pilot stage; BayCare's Morton Plant Hospital trial of Rovex is testing navigation, not moving patients.

tasks.label: Demonstrate therapy techniques, such as manual and creative arts and games.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult rehab setting (hospital therapy gym, outpatient clinic, SNF therapy room): aide demonstrates and leads standardized therapeutic exercises/movement routines — seated calisthenics, range-of-motion, warm-ups — for one patient or a small group to copy, cueing pace and effort while the OT/OTA supervises.

Skilled nursing facility, adult day program or hospital day room: aide demonstrates and runs a therapeutic game or recreational activity (quiz/word games, ring or flag games, ball toss, bingo, simple card/board game), explaining the rules and modeling play with residents.

Therapy room craft session: aide demonstrates a manual or creative-arts technique with real materials — cutting and gluing, lacing/beading, clay, painting, weaving, woodworking kits — step by step so the patient can copy and complete the project.

Pediatric clinic or school therapy room: aide demonstrates play-based imitation activities, gross/fine motor games (gesture imitation, animal walks, ball games) or letter-formation/handwriting practice to a child, keeping the child engaged and repeating the model as needed.

ADL/adaptive-equipment demonstration in an ADL suite or at the bedside: aide shows how to use a buttonhook, reacher, sock aid or dressing stick, one-handed techniques, splint donning, or a therapy-putty/hand-exercise routine, then watches the patient try it.

Home-health visit: aide demonstrates a prescribed technique (exercise, adaptive-equipment use, safe activity method) to the patient and a family caregiver in the patient's own home, working around whatever furniture, clutter and equipment are present.

sources.title: News on Aging | ILC-Japan — The Future of the Robot-led Nursing Care
sources.claim: PALRO, a 40-cm humanoid, is used as a 'robot instructor' at an ARFIT adult day-care facility in Yokohama focused on functional training: it leads the opening exercise segment of a 3-hour function-recovery rehabilitation program and a closing oral-motor exercise, with residents following its demonstrated movements.
sources.transferJustification: Same act as the aide's: modeling a prescribed movement routine that patients imitate, in a therapy facility; the robot performs the movements itself and paces the group.

sources.title: PALRO for welfare facilities for the elderly (Fujisoft product site, English)
sources.claim: PALRO is a commercial eldercare product that autonomously acts as master of ceremonies for recreation: it leads residents through games, quizzes, dances and preventive-care exercises from a downloadable program library, reducing staff burden in nursing homes and day-service facilities.

sources.title: A Clever and Caring Companion | Highlighting Japan (Government of Japan)
sources.claim: PALRO had been introduced at roughly 300 Japanese eldercare facilities by 2015 (about 900 by 2019 per ILC-Japan), where it converses, plays games, presents quizzes and dances for residents.

sources.developer: Aldebaran/SoftBank Robotics; study by Raso et al. (Journal of Experimental Orthopaedics)
sources.title: A pilot study for assessing NAO humanoid robot assistance in shoulder rehabilitation
sources.claim: A pilot study with the NAO humanoid had patients with shoulder musculoskeletal disorders replicate rehabilitation exercises demonstrated by the robot with audiovisual cueing, with kinematic measurement of range of motion, timing and smoothness.

sources.title: LuxAI, LIH and University of Birmingham launch the first large-scale study of at-home, robot-led early development support for autistic children with QTrobot
sources.claim: QTrobot is a commercial socially assistive humanoid whose Special Needs Education version is used by schools worldwide to deliver robot-led play-based developmental and therapy activities to autistic children; a large-scale study of the robot-led at-home programme with 69 families began in Dec 2025.
sources.transferJustification: The robot models gestures, movements and play routines that the child imitates in a school/therapy room — the same demonstrate-and-have-the-child-copy act pediatric OT aides perform.

sources.developer: EPFL CHILI Lab (with GAIPS, Nazarbayev University)
sources.title: A Comparison of Social Robot to Tablet and Teacher in a New Script Learning Context (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: The CoWriter system pairs an autonomous NAO robot with a tablet and digital pen so children practice and improve handwriting; the robot produces its own handwriting for children to correct, and the approach has been run with children in classrooms since 2014.
sources.transferJustification: Handwriting/letter-formation practice is a standard pediatric OT activity; the robot autonomously demonstrates letter forms and runs the practice session with the child in a classroom.

sources.system: Collaborative checkers-playing robot (UR-type cobot with vision)
sources.developer: Academic team, published in MDPI Robotics
sources.title: Playing Checkers with an Intelligent and Collaborative Robotic System (Robotics, MDPI)
sources.claim: A collaborative robot system plays checkers against a human opponent, sensing the board with a camera, choosing moves, and physically picking and placing the game pieces on a real board.
sources.transferJustification: Tabletop board-game play with a human partner involves the same objects, precision and turn-taking as a therapeutic board-game activity demonstrated to a patient.

sources.title: Painting Robot Uses AI to Help Cook Children's Patients Connect to Creativity
sources.claim: CloudPainter, an AI painting robot that makes its own artistic decisions, served as robotic artist-in-residence at Cook Children's Medical Center, creating artwork with hospitalized pediatric patients as a creative activity.
sources.transferJustification: Closest cited system for creative-arts activity with patients in a clinical facility; cited to show its scope (the robot makes the art itself) rather than demonstrating a craft technique for a patient to copy.

tasks.label: Manage intradepartmental infection control and equipment security.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-session infection control in a hospital or outpatient rehab OT gym: wipe down and disinfect mat tables, plinths, therapy chairs, arm bikes, splinting bench and other equipment surfaces with hospital-grade disinfectant wipes, observing contact time, in a few minutes of turnover while therapists, patients and wheelchairs are in the room.

Reprocessing handled therapy items after use: collect hand-therapy tools, splinting scissors and pans, pegboards, cones, theraputty containers, ADL kitchen utensils and pediatric toys; wash/soak or run them through disinfection, dry, reassemble kits and return them to labeled storage bins in the OT department.

Keeping infection-control supplies stocked in the department: bring cases of gloves, gowns, masks, disinfectant wipes and hand-sanitizer refills from the supply room and refill wall dispensers, treatment-room shelves and therapy carts; flag low or expired stock for reorder.

End-of-day equipment security: gather adaptive equipment, weights, splinting tools, hot packs and loaner devices left around the gym, return them to the storage room, lock cabinets holding sharps/tools/valuable devices, and verify inventory counts of loaner and check-out equipment, logging discrepancies.

Same cleaning/securing duties in unstructured settings: school-based OT using a shared classroom or multipurpose room, or community/home-visit programs, where equipment is carried site to site, cleaned wherever a sink or table is available, and secured in a shared closet or vehicle.

sources.system: Getinge Automation System (AGS 2.0) with 8666/8668 and 88-Turbo washer-disinfectors
sources.title: Getinge Automation System for washer-disinfectors
sources.claim: Getinge's Air Glide automation system autonomously loads and transports wash-carts of soiled instruments into a bank of washer-disinfectors in hospital sterile-processing departments, running cleaning, disinfection and drying cycles without supervision and documenting them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated reprocessing of medical instruments and utensils. It transfers to cleaning/disinfecting OT therapy tools and plastic items because the objects are comparable small rigid medical items, the required output (validated cleaning plus thermal disinfection, dried and ready for storage) is stricter than OT-department disinfection, and the work is presented to the machine on racks/carts as a purpose-built setting would present it.

sources.title: LC 80 BOT - SteelcoBelimed
sources.claim: A commercial washer-disinfector reprocesses bulky items such as hospital bed frames, operating tables, carts and bowls in an automatic PLC-controlled wash/disinfect cycle, with automatic loading/unloading options for highly automated departments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cleaning and disinfection of large patient-contact furniture (bed frames, operating tables, trolleys). This transfers to disinfecting OT mat tables, plinths and therapy chairs: same vinyl/steel patient-contact surfaces, same disinfection standard, with the item brought to the machine as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: Swisslog BoxPicker automated pharmacy storage system
sources.date: 2026-04 product page; installed in US hospital pharmacies for years
sources.title: Automated Pharmacy Storage System - Swisslog BoxPicker
sources.claim: A robotic high-density storage and retrieval system in hospital pharmacies stores stock securely, controls who can access it, releases only one box at a time and keeps a scanned inventory of what enters and leaves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secure automated storage, access control and inventory accuracy for controlled hospital stock including narcotics. This transfers to OT 'equipment security' — stowing items in locked storage, restricting access and verifying counts — because the accepted output is the same (items secured, access logged, inventory reconciled) for comparably sized boxed items presented at a workstation port.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: An AI-controlled restocking robot autonomously places bottled and canned drinks onto refrigerated display shelves from crates in a fixed back-of-case bay, deployed at 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, with remote operators intervening only when an item is dropped or misplaced.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking of packaged goods from crates presented in a fixed, purpose-built bay. Transfers to refilling glove, wipe and gown supplies on department shelves: comparable rigid packaged items and placement precision, with stock presented to the machine as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.title: Blue Ocean Robotics builds UV-D disinfection robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile UV-C disinfection robots navigate hospital rooms on their own and irradiate surfaces; they have been deployed in hospitals in Europe, the US and Asia.

sources.system: UV-C disinfection robot (academic hospital field study)
sources.developer: Antimicrobial Resistance & Infection Control study authors
sources.title: The use of a UV-C disinfection robot in the routine cleaning process: a field study in an Academic hospital
sources.claim: A hospital field study of a UV-C disinfection robot applied the robot cycle only after standard manual terminal cleaning and disinfection, i.e. as a complement rather than a replacement for wiping surfaces.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.developer: POSTECH with KIST, KIRO, Elphoton and Pohang St. Mary's Hospital
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: A research prototype combines autonomous navigation with a manipulator that physically wipes hospital surfaces plus UV-C irradiation; it was developed with a hospital infection-control team and published in IEEE Robotics & Automation Magazine.

sources.title: Independent US grocer Harmons deploys Simbe Tally inventory robot across 17 of its locations
sources.claim: An autonomous shelf-scanning robot performs inventory verification in grocery stores during operating hours, deployed across 17 stores of one chain after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inventory auditing of stocked shelves in a working human facility. It substantiates only the counting/verification portion of OT equipment security (verifying loaner-device counts on shelves), not gathering, stowing or locking equipment.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Mobile manipulator robots run autonomous supply and pharmacy deliveries inside working hospitals at scale, but items are dropped off for staff rather than shelved or stowed by the robot.

tasks.label: Perform clerical, administrative, and secretarial duties, such as answering phones, restocking and ordering supplies, filling out paperwork, and scheduling appointments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Front-desk phone coverage in an outpatient OT/rehab clinic: answering incoming calls from patients, physicians' offices and vendors, screening and routing them, taking and relaying messages, answering questions about hours, insurance and home programs, and returning calls.

Scheduling work at a clinic or hospital rehab department: booking, rescheduling and cancelling patient appointments in the EMR/scheduling system, matching patients to therapist availability and equipment, making confirmation/reminder calls, and printing or distributing daily schedules.

Paperwork at a desk in the department: completing intake/registration and charge sheets, transcribing treatment logs and attendance records, faxing referrals and authorization requests, photocopying handouts, filing and pulling paper charts, handing clipboards to patients.

Supply runs inside the facility: fetching therapy supplies and linens from the central stockroom or receiving dock and transporting them by hand or cart to the OT gym and treatment rooms (hospital rehab department or larger clinic, fixed layout, staff and patients present).

Putting stock away: unpacking cartons of delivered supplies (gloves, theraputty, splinting material, elastic bands, hot-pack covers, paper goods) and placing each item in its place on treatment-room shelves, cabinet drawers, wall bins and mobile carts, rotating older stock forward.

Ordering supplies: walking the stockroom and treatment rooms to check par levels and note shortages, compiling an order, placing it with vendors through an online portal or by phone, then receiving the delivery and checking cartons against the packing slip.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores | NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocks refrigerated beverage shelves in FamilyMart convenience stores, running autonomously the great majority of the time with remote operators only handling exceptions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking of small consumer items. Transfers to putting clinic supplies away in that it is repetitive pick-and-place of palm-sized packaged goods into fixed shelf locations, but only in a workspace engineered around the arm.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: In routine operation the TX SCARA restocking robots run under AI control; remote staff take manual control only to recover from dropped or misplaced items, without on-site staff involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Same restocking transfer as above; establishes that the deployment is autonomous with occasional remote assistance rather than teleoperated.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics humanoid MMR performs one million deliveries - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously gathers supplies from central supply and delivers/restocks them on hospital units, including riding elevators, in live US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply fetch-and-delivery in hospitals. Directly comparable to an aide's supply run from the stockroom to the OT gym: same building type, same cart/tote-scale loads, people present.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is a commercial fleet: nearly 100 robots in more than 25 US hospital facilities have completed over 1.25 million autonomous ....
sources.transferJustification: Establishes scale and worker-quality reliability of the hospital supply-transport deployment cited above.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics receives investment from Rockwell Automation - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick systems autonomously pick and place millions of varied individual items per month in warehouse cells with intervention rates as low ...%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking and put-away of mixed small SKUs presented in totes at fixed stations. This is the purpose-built (E1) form of stock put-away: same object class (packaged consumables), same precision, work brought to the machine.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously scans store shelves to audit inventory and flag out-of-stocks, deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous stock-level auditing in a human retail facility. Covers only the counting sub-step of ordering supplies; it relies on barcoded shelf labels and does not place vendor orders or receive deliveries.

tasks.label: Supervise patients in choosing and completing work assignments or arts and crafts projects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Adjust and repair assistive devices and make adaptive changes to other equipment and to environments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In an outpatient rehab clinic or hospital OT gym, the aide sizes and adjusts a mobility or positioning device to a specific patient per the therapist's prescription: setting walker/crutch/cane height by spring buttons, sliding and re-bolting wheelchair footrest length, armrest height, back cane height, headrest or lateral support position, then checking the fit with the patient standing or seated.

Routine part-swap maintenance on standard clinic devices in the equipment/storage room: replacing worn rubber tips on canes/walkers, swapping a cracked caster or wheel, replacing batteries, re-tightening loose bolts and knobs on standard, current-model equipment.

Diagnostic repair of an assorted, aged device fleet: a wheelchair whose brake will not hold, a frayed or torn seat sling/upholstery, a stretched Velcro or buckle strap on a splint or gait belt, a bent frame, a sticking recliner mechanism, a power chair joystick or charger fault — the aide must find the fault across many models and wear states and restore function.

Fabricating or adapting small adaptive equipment to therapist specification in the clinic workshop: building up utensil, pen or toothbrush handles with foam tubing cut to length, adding non-slip matting or Dycem, trimming and riveting splint straps, extending a reacher or dressing stick, adding Velcro closures and padding.

Adaptive changes to equipment and environment inside the facility: rearranging treatment-room furniture and clearing floor space for walker/wheelchair clearance, adjusting mat table/plinth and chair heights, repositioning items in the ADL kitchen or training bathroom, mounting or repositioning a grab bar or rail in the training bathroom, setting up ramps and transfer boards.

Home or long-term-care room visit with the therapy team: adapting the patient's own living space — installing or adjusting grab bars and a raised toilet seat, fitting a tub bench, removing throw rugs and cords, moving furniture to widen paths, raising or lowering a bed, adjusting a device the patient already owns.

sources.system: Robotiq Screwdriving Solution (SD-100 screwdriver + SF-300 feeder on UR cobot workcell)
sources.title: Screwdriving Solution | Robotiq
sources.claim: Commercially deployed robotic screwdriving workcells autonomously drive and inspect fasteners on parts held in fixtures, with automatic error detection and recovery — the fastener loosening/tightening and re-setting operations that dominate wheelchair and walker adjustment when the device is presented fixtured in a cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured fastening assembly. Wheelchair/walker adjustment and reassembly is bolt-and-detent work on rigid tubular metal parts at millimetre precision; in an E1 cell the device arrives fixtured with a target dimension, making it the same class of fastener-driving and part-repositioning operation this deployed cell performs.

sources.title: RoboTire installs another system with Discount Tire — The Robot Report
sources.claim: A robotic system installed in Discount Tire service bays located and removed lug nuts, lifted wheel/tire assemblies off vehicles and re-installed and re-torqued them, working on varied wheel sizes and bolt patterns with technician oversight rather than step-by-step control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unbolt-and-replace of a worn wheel. Swapping a wheelchair caster or re-torquing a loose armrest bolt is the same operation class (vision-locate fastener pattern, unbolt, remove worn part, fit replacement, re-torque) on smaller, lighter hardware in a purpose-built bay.

sources.system: Daisy disassembly robot (Material Recovery Lab, Austin)
sources.title: Apple expands global recycling programs — Apple Newsroom
sources.claim: Apple operates a purpose-built automated disassembly line that takes apart many known models of a manufactured device at high rate, removing screws and separating components without human handling of each unit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of known device models in a fixtured line. It substantiates the part-removal half of routine part-swap maintenance for standard, catalogued device models when the device is brought to the machine; it does not substantiate fault diagnosis on aged, heterogeneous devices.

sources.system: Aetrex 3D Printed Custom Orthotics (Albert 3D scanner + EOS additive machine)
sources.title: Aetrex Launches its Thinnest 3D Printed Insole Yet — 3DPrint.com
sources.claim: A commercial pipeline scans a customer's foot in a store and an additive manufacturing machine produces a custom-fit orthotic device from those measurements, shipped within days — machine fabrication of a personalised assistive device to individual specification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing a patient-specific assistive device from measurements taken by machine. It transfers to the aide's fabrication/adaptation of small adaptive equipment to a therapist's spec: same customisation logic, comparable millimetre precision, work done in a purpose-built production cell.

sources.system: EnvisionTEC additive production of Phonak/Unitron custom hearing aid shells
sources.title: How EnvisionTEC 3D printing is enabling the mass manufacture of hearing aids — TCT Magazine
sources.claim: Custom-fit hearing device shells are mass-produced by additive machines from individual ear impressions, at a scale of over a million unique custom pieces a year.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine fabrication of one-off, patient-specific assistive-device parts. Establishes that purpose-built cells reliably turn individual patient geometry into accepted clinical devices, the output an aide's adaptive-equipment fabrication must deliver.

sources.title: Prosthetic Orthotic Central Fabrication Services | WCBL
sources.claim: A central fabrication lab uses a seven-axis robotic carving system to cut patient-specific positive models from digital scans to 0.1 mm, from which orthoses and prostheses are built.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic shaping of custom assistive-device components in a purpose-built fabrication cell; supports E1 fabrication/adaptation of adaptive equipment to individual specification, though it is a shaping cell, not an in-clinic device-repair system.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: The most widely deployed mobile manipulator in US hospitals performs autonomous point-to-point fetch-and-deliver of supplies and medications; its deployed duties do not include tool use, equipment repair, or rearranging rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound what mobile robots actually do inside structured clinical facilities (E2): transport, not device adjustment, repair, or environmental modification.

sources.system: π0.5 vision-language-action model on mobile manipulator
sources.title: π0.5: a VLA with Open-World Generalization — Physical Intelligence
sources.claim: State-of-the-art generalist manipulation policies can tidy kitchens and bedrooms in previously unseen homes, but this is a research demonstration of cleaning-type manipulation, not tool-based repair or fixture installation at professional quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unstructured-home manipulation. It marks the ceiling of demonstrated home capability (picking and placing household objects) and does not extend to drilling, anchoring, or fitting assistive hardware in a home.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot — Hilti GB
sources.claim: A semi-autonomous construction robot marks and drills anchor holes in ceilings from a digital plan on active jobsites, but only drills holes after human total-station setup; it does not set anchors or install fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ hole drilling in a built environment. Cited to show the nearest deployed capability to grab-bar/rail installation; it stops at drilling from a pre-surveyed plan and does not cover stud location, anchoring, fastening, and load checking in a small bathroom.

tasks.label: Evaluate the living skills and capacities of clients with physical, developmental, or mental health disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Accompany patients on outings, providing transportation when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Community reintegration outing from a rehab hospital or SNF: aide drives the facility van to a grocery store, restaurant, or bus stop, loads and secures the patient's wheelchair or walker, then accompanies the patient through the store aisles, guards against falls, cues and assists with reaching, paying, and re-boarding, and returns the patient to the unit.

Transporting a patient in the facility car or van to an outside appointment, home evaluation, or discharge: helping the patient out of the building, into and out of the vehicle, securing seat belts/wheelchair tie-downs, driving on public streets, escorting the patient to the door, and monitoring their condition en route.

Group outing from an adult day program, behavioral health day treatment, or pediatric/school-based program to a park, library, or mall: aide supervises several clients at once, manages behavior and wandering, assists with mobility and toileting, and keeps the group together in a public setting.

Walking outing on and just off facility grounds for endurance and community-mobility practice: aide walks beside the patient with a gait belt or trails with a wheelchair over curbs, ramps, uneven pavement, and street crossings, providing standby physical assistance and stopping to rest as needed.

Taking a medically stable, self-transferring wheelchair patient to an on-campus destination inside the building (cafeteria, gift shop, atrium, therapy garden entrance) and back; the work is essentially conveyance along known corridors and elevators with no hands-on assistance required.

Escorting a frail, confused, or post-surgical patient within the facility to an on-site group activity: assisting the transfer from bed or chair into a wheelchair, managing IV pole/oxygen, monitoring status, providing verbal cueing and reassurance, and returning and transferring the patient back.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Drive System (autonomous personal mobility device)
sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. (with American Airlines / Miami-Dade Aviation)
sources.title: New autonomous wheelchairs at Miami International Airport
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchairs are deployed for public use at Miami International Airport, autonomously carrying seated passengers from a pick-up point to a gate they select on a touchscreen, then returning empty.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting a seated person through a large institutional building to a chosen destination. The payload (a seated adult), the route type (corridors, crowds, elevators/lifts) and the accepted output (person delivered safely to destination) match an in-facility patient escort by wheelchair.

sources.title: WHILL Expands Global Autonomous Mobility Network with Heathrow Airport Launch
sources.claim: The same WHILL autonomous service has continued to expand into other institution-controlled facilities (Heathrow, Anchorage, Schiphol, Winnipeg), navigating crowded public terminal space with onboard sensing and automatic stopping.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: autonomous conveyance of a seated person through an institution-controlled facility corresponds to wheeling a stable patient to an on-site destination.

sources.title: Keio University Hospital Begins Technical Trial of WHILL Autonomous Driving Technology to Improve Patient Mobility
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous drive system has been trialled inside a hospital to move patients with limited mobility between departments without staff pushing them.

sources.system: Driverless in-hospital mobility (autonomous personal mobility vehicle)
sources.developer: Japanese hospital research group (clinical study, PMC11067163)
sources.title: Safety and feasibility of in-hospital autonomous transportation using a driverless mobility for patients with musculoskeletal disorders
sources.claim: A clinical study of in-hospital autonomous (driverless) mobility carrying musculoskeletal patients between hospital points found the service safe and satisfactory, with no severe adverse events.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving an impaired patient between points inside a hospital. It substantiates that the conveyance element of an in-facility escort is achievable autonomously with clinically acceptable safety.

sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous one-person patient shuttles are being commercialized for hospital patient transport, with reported use at Charité Berlin and a development agreement with Mayo Clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital transport of a patient seated in a powered pod, supporting the conveyance-only element of an in-facility patient escort in an institution-controlled building.

sources.title: Waymo written testimony, U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
sources.claim: Waymo operates fully driverless passenger rides at scale on public roads, but the vehicle only drives; it does not assist a rider into or out of the car, secure mobility equipment, or accompany the rider at the destination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving a passenger door-to-door. It covers only the vehicle-operation portion of "providing transportation"; it does not substantiate boarding assistance, wheelchair securement, or accompaniment at the destination.

sources.title: Autonomous Taxis Won't Be Accessible With Laws Like These
sources.claim: Wheelchair-accessible rides in robotaxi fleets are still supplied with human drivers; the autonomous fleets themselves are not wheelchair accessible.

tasks.label: Assist educational specialists or clinical psychologists in administering situational or diagnostic tests to measure client's abilities or progress.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient OT clinic, no client present: aide pulls the standardized test kits ordered by the OT/psychologist (pegboard, blocks, cards, dynamometer, forms, stopwatch) from storage, checks the kit is complete, lays the items out on the testing table in the prescribed order, then re-assembles, cleans and restocks the kit after the session.

Adult outpatient rehab clinic, client present: aide assists the therapist/psychologist during a table-top standardized diagnostic test - escorts and seats the client, positions test materials in front of them on cue, hands and retrieves items between subtests, times trials with a stopwatch, records raw responses on the score form, redirects and encourages a fatigued or confused client.

Inpatient hospital / SNF rehab unit: aide assists with a functional (ADL / mobility) performance assessment - applies a gait belt, transfers and positions the patient, guards the patient during dressing, grooming, sit-to-stand and short ambulation trials, sets out ADL items in the bathroom or ADL kitchen, and records observed performance for the evaluating clinician.

School or pediatric clinic: aide assists an educational specialist with a child's developmental, sensory-processing or visual-motor assessment - sets up mats, balance equipment and manipulatives, positions and physically supports the child, presents test items, keeps the child engaged, safe and on task, and tallies the score sheet.

Work-hardening / vocational situational assessment area: aide sets up work-simulation stations (crates, weights, tool-sorting boards, work simulator settings), loads and adjusts resistances, observes and times the client performing simulated job tasks, guards for safety, resets the station between trials and logs results.

sources.system: Roboception 3D stereo vision + industrial robot kitting cell (Danfoss Drives A/S)
sources.title: Case Studies: Automated Kitting Solution with 3D Robot Vision | Roboception GmbH
sources.claim: A production kitting cell at Danfoss Drives uses a Roboception 3D stereo vision system to let an industrial robot autonomously locate and pick small varied parts and place them into kit trays, with sub-millimetre detection and 25-second cycle times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial kitting. Assembling and laying out a standardized test kit is the same operation - identifying small hand-sized items and placing each in a prescribed position in a tray - at comparable precision, so performance carries over when the materials are presented to the machine in a purpose-built cell.

sources.date: 2026-05 (page updated); product commercial for over a decade
sources.title: Kinarm Standard Tests - Kinarm | Interactive Robotics Brain Injury Research
sources.claim: Kinarm Standard Tests are a commercially sold suite of pre-programmed robotic protocols: a subject seated in the Kinarm robot performs standardized motor, sensory and cognitive tasks and the Dexterit-E software automatically analyses performance against a normative dataset, characterizing performance in 30-60 minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic administration and automatic scoring of standardized ability tests. It shows a machine can run and score an ability test when the person is brought to and coupled with the machine, but it is a research tool and the seating, coupling, cueing and monitoring of the subject - the aide's actual contribution - is still done by a person.

sources.title: Exoskeleton Lab - Kinarm | Interactive Robotics Brain Injury Research
sources.claim: The Kinarm Exoskeleton Lab is a fixed laboratory workstation into which the subject must be seated, harnessed and coupled: it ships with an integrated wheelchair-style chair with removable foot/arm/head rests, optional child-size arm troughs and an optional subject harness for stroke subjects.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the Kinarm Standard Tests item; cited to show the demonstrated setting is a purpose-built robot lab and that positioning, strapping and supervising the client during testing is still performed by a human, not the robot.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator works autonomously inside hospitals, having completed more than a million deliveries including 300,000 pharmacy ... and 100,000 autonomous elevator rides; its deployed work is fetching and transporting supplies, not setting up or assisting patient assessments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous supply logistics inside a hospital (an E2 facility). It substantiates transporting materials between rooms but not the client-facing setup, item presentation, guarding or handling this task requires, so it does not support positive judgments for the client-facing instances.

emergingTasks.label: Sanitize equipment.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Physical Therapist Assistants
aliases: Home Health Physical Therapy Assistant (Home Health PTA)
Nursing Facility PTA (Nursing Facility Physical Therapy Assistant)
Per Diem Physical Therapist Assistant (Per Diem PTA)
SNF PTA (Skilled Nursing Facility Physical Therapy Assistant)
roles.description: Assist physical therapists in providing physical therapy treatments and procedures. May, in accordance with state laws, assist in the development of treatment plans, carry out routine functions, document the progress of treatment, and modify specific treatments in accordance with patient status and within the scope of treatment plans established by a physical therapist. Generally requires formal training.

tasks.label: Instruct, motivate, safeguard, and assist patients as they practice exercises or functional activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/musculoskeletal clinic: PTA takes a patient through a varied multi-exercise program on a gym floor (bands, weights, step-ups, squats, balance boards, functional drills), demonstrating, counting reps, correcting form by hand, spotting, and providing manual stretch/resistance; equipment and exercises change every few minutes.

Post-operative or single-region rehab (post-TKA knee, shoulder, hand/wrist): repetitive range-of-motion and strengthening practice for one limb segment, patient seated or supine, PTA assisting the movement, resisting, cueing effort and monitoring pain.

Acute-care hospital / inpatient unit: gait and functional-mobility practice with a weak or unsteady patient - bed mobility, sit-to-stand, transfers, ambulating a corridor with a walker while the PTA holds a gait belt, manages lines and IV pole, and guards against a fall.

Inpatient neurorehabilitation gym (stroke, SCI, TBI, and pediatric cerebral palsy): intensive, high-repetition gait training on a treadmill/parallel bars with body-weight support, or repetitive upper-limb reaching practice, with the PTA facilitating limb movement and encouraging effort over a 45-60 minute session.

Skilled nursing facility / geriatric rehab gym: frail, often cognitively impaired elders practicing sit-to-stand, seated and standing strengthening, and short ambulation; heavy verbal motivation and redirection, hands-on guarding, high fall risk, frequent rest breaks.

Home health visit: exercise and functional-activity practice in the patient's own home - bed/chair transfers, stair practice, walking through cluttered rooms, home exercise program on whatever furniture is available, with the PTA guarding and physically assisting.

sources.title: Unsupervised robot-assisted rehabilitation after stroke: feasibility, effect on therapy dose, and user experience (J NeuroEng Rehabil)
sources.claim: Subacute stroke inpatients completed daily 45-minute robot-assisted hand/arm therapy sessions with the ReHapticKnob with no therapist present after a training-in phase; the robot's algorithms monitored, controlled and adapted the therapy content and no adverse events occurred.

sources.title: Lokomat Software "Sensation" - Hocoma
sources.claim: The Lokomat is a commercial robotic gait trainer in which the patient is harnessed over a treadmill with body-weight support; it drives and assists the gait pattern automatically (assist-as-needed), delivers game-like feedback exercises to motivate effort, and stops automatically if safety limits are exceeded.

sources.developer: Hocoma; rehabilitation centers in the PeLoGAIT bicenter trial
sources.title: Effectiveness of robot-assisted gait training in children with cerebral palsy: a bicenter, pragmatic, randomized, cross-over trial (PeLoGAIT) - PubMed
sources.claim: Lokomat gait training is applied to children with cerebral palsy: the device automates treadmill gait therapy with two actuated leg orthoses fitted to the child's legs while a harness secures and unweights the patient.

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Stair Climbing Training on Postural Control and Sensory Integration Processes in Chronic Post-stroke Patients: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial (Frontiers in Neuroscience)
sources.claim: The G-EO System end-effector gait robot, with the patient harnessed and feet secured to powered footplates, delivers repetitive practice of floor walking and of stair climbing up and down, modulating force to support the patient's own effort; used for 50-minute outpatient sessions in a neurorehabilitation unit.

sources.title: Robot-assisted rehabilitation and mobilization | KUKA Global
sources.claim: ROBERT is an FDA-cleared rehabilitation robot in hospital use (Denmark, Germany, Houston) that holds a bedridden or post-surgical patient's leg, learns the therapeutic movement from staff demonstration, then repeats it independently as often as required and stops immediately on unexpected forces.

sources.developer: Life Science Robotics / Odense University Hospital (ROBUST trial)
sources.title: ROBot Assisted Physical Training of Older Patients During acUte hospitaliSaTion (statistical analysis plan, NCT05782855)
sources.claim: A 488-patient randomized controlled trial at a geriatric department gave acutely hospitalized older patients active robot-assisted resistance training of the leg with the ROBERT robot in addition to standard physiotherapy.

sources.developer: BIONIK Laboratories (deployed at Barrow Neurological Institute)
sources.title: Neuro-Rehabilitation Robotics & Technology | Barrow Neurological Institute
sources.claim: The InMotion Arm/Hand robot is in clinical use at a neurorehabilitation institute: the patient's arm is placed in a grip attached to the robot arm, which provides guidance, assistance or resistance during highly repetitive exercise while a screen supplies interactive activities and real-time feedback.

sources.title: Andago® - Hocoma
sources.claim: Andago V2.0 is a commercial mobile robot used in therapy gyms that harnesses the patient, follows them automatically during overground walking and provides body-weight support and fall protection, but is a tool clinicians use to deliver training rather than a substitute for the clinician.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: overground gait/balance training in a therapy gym. It demonstrates autonomous patient-following fall protection, i.e. only the safeguarding component, with the therapist still instructing, grading and progressing the session.

sources.system: Salt socially assistive robot (and comparable SAR exercise coaches)
sources.developer: academic groups reviewed in Robinson & Nejat
sources.title: An analysis of design recommendations for socially assistive robot helpers for effective human-robot interactions in senior care
sources.claim: Socially assistive robots have autonomously led exercise sessions for older adults in long-term care, guiding repetitions of upper-body exercises - instruction and motivation only, with no physical support or hands-on guarding of the participant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading exercise practice in a care facility. Shows autonomous instruction and motivation in an E2 setting, but provides no physical assistance or fall-guarding, so it cannot complete a PTA instance on its own.

tasks.label: Document patient information, such as notes on their progress.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Observe patients during treatments to compile and evaluate data on their responses and progress and provide results to physical therapist in person or through progress notes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic: PTA supervises a post-op knee or shoulder patient through a therapeutic exercise progression, watching movement quality, counting reps/sets, noting pain ratings, fatigue and swelling reports, then writes the daily SOAP/progress note in the EMR and verbally briefs the supervising PT at the end of the session about tolerance and readiness to advance.

Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab: PTA performs gait and transfer training with an older adult, observing balance, level of assistance required, distance ambulated, endurance and any dizziness or pain, documents functional measures in the facility EMR for billing/Medicare compliance, and reports notable changes (declining tolerance, new confusion) to the PT.

Neurologic or pediatric rehab setting: PTA observes quality of movement, tone, motor control and functional performance against plan-of-care goals during treatment, compiles data on progress toward goals, and flags to the PT that a reassessment or plan modification is warranted.

Acute care hospital: PTA mobilizes a medically complex patient, monitoring vital-sign responses (HR, BP, SpO2, RPE, pain), lines and precautions, halting or modifying activity when responses are adverse, then charting the response and immediately communicating findings to the supervising PT and nursing staff.

Home health, school-based or community/aquatic setting: PTA treats a patient in a non-clinic environment, observes performance and safety in that context (home layout, caregiver carryover, classroom participation), documents on a laptop/tablet, and conveys results to the PT by phone, secure message or the shared visit note.

tasks.label: Instruct patients in proper body mechanics and in ways to improve functional mobility, such as aquatic exercise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic: teach a low-back-pain or post-op patient proper body mechanics — safe lifting, hip-hinge bending, log-roll, sitting/standing and workstation posture. PTA explains, demonstrates, watches the patient rehearse with a box or chair, and corrects errors with verbal and hands-on tactile cues, adapting to pain response.

Inpatient rehab hospital or skilled nursing facility: instruct a post-stroke, post-hip-fracture or deconditioned patient in functional mobility — bed mobility, sit-to-stand, bed-to-chair/toilet transfers, walker or cane gait, curbs and stairs — with a gait belt, hands-on guarding against falls, and manual facilitation while cueing sequence and technique.

Clinic gym / mat area: lead an individual patient through the prescribed therapeutic exercise and mobility program (range-of-motion, stretching, strengthening, seated and standing balance drills), counting reps, correcting form, adjusting difficulty within the PT's plan, and monitoring exertion.

Facility therapy pool: instruct a patient in aquatic exercise — entering via steps or lift, walking patterns, buoyancy-assisted limb exercises, use of noodles/kickboards — with the PTA on the deck or in the water providing support, stabilization and safety supervision.

Home health visit: instruct the patient and a family caregiver in body mechanics and safe mobility using the home's own furniture — the patient's bed, recliner, bathroom, and stairs — with clutter, pets, and no standardized equipment.

Group session in a clinic classroom or facility day room: back-school / fall-prevention class teaching body mechanics and mobility strategies to several patients (or to facility staff and caregivers) at once, with individual correction during practice.

sources.system: Stretch with Stretch (SWS) / ZEST-E on Hello Robot Stretch RE1
sources.developer: Georgia Tech (Kemp lab) with Emory University
sources.title: Stretch with Stretch: Physical Therapy Exercise Games Led by a Mobile Manipulator (arXiv:2312.13279)
sources.claim: Stretch with Stretch (SWS/ZEST-E) is an autonomous mobile manipulator that visually and verbally guides older adults with Parkinson's disease through prescribed physical-therapy stretching exercises, customizing targets per person; evaluated in a user study with 10 participants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led therapeutic exercise sessions. Transfers partially to 'instruct patients in ways to improve functional mobility' because the robot verbally and visually cues prescribed movements to a patient, the same instructional act, though without hands-on correction or guarding.

sources.system: ZEST-E (Zesty Exercise System for Therapeutic Engagement)
sources.title: Exercise Specialists' Evaluation of Robot-Led Rehabilitative Exercise for People with Parkinson's Disease
sources.claim: A 2025 mixed-methods evaluation by exercise specialists of the ZEST-E robot-led physical therapy platform for Parkinson's disease found promise but concluded the robot's instructional abilities are not yet adequate for routine therapy.

sources.developer: Hello Robot, Emory University School of Medicine, Georgia Tech
sources.title: Stretch Community News - March 2026
sources.claim: A pilot study by Emory and Georgia Tech reported that Stretch-led physical therapy sessions for people with Parkinson's disease produced exercise intensity and joint range of motion comparable to human-led sessions, using a soft pressurized bubble as the reach target.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-guided range-of-motion exercise. Supports the exercise-leading portion of mobility instruction, but the reported outcome is joint ROM and intensity, not instruction in body mechanics or safe transfers.

sources.title: ETD | Zesty Exercise System for Therapeutic Engagement (ZEST-E)
sources.claim: The ZEST-E pilot interventional study tested whether a robot-led exercise system could lead 11 older adults with Parkinson's disease through range of motion at different ... whether they could execute the exercises as instructed ....

sources.title: Technical Feasibility of Supervision of Stretching Exercises by a Humanoid Robot Coach for Chronic Low Back Pain: The R-COOL Randomized Trial
sources.claim: The R-COOL randomized trial tested a humanoid robot coach supervising stretching exercises for chronic low back pain in a rehabilitation setting; adherence to the robot-supervised movements fell steeply over three weeks, usability was rated lower than the control, and clinical outcomes did not differ.

sources.developer: Aldebaran/SoftBank Robotics, Zora Bots (distributed by RobotLAB)
sources.title: NAO Zora Robot — Healthcare Solution — Price & Specs
sources.claim: The NAO/Zora humanoid is sold as a care-facility product that leads seated exercise and dance ... and other group activities for residents; the routines are selected and run by staff from a tablet interface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading group exercise in a care facility. Would transfer to group mobility instruction, but the routines are staff-launched scripted behaviors with no individual form assessment or correction, so autonomy is unclear.

tasks.label: Secure patients into or onto therapy equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic: PTA positions an ambulatory patient on strength/exercise equipment (leg extension machine, isokinetic dynamometer, upper-body ergometer), adjusts seat height and pads to the patient's limb lengths, aligns the joint axis with the machine axis, and fastens thigh/shin cuffs and a torso stabilization belt snugly without pinching, then verifies fit and comfort before loading.

Inpatient/neuro rehab gym: PTA fits a patient with hemiparesis or spinal cord injury into a body-weight-support harness (straps between the legs, around trunk) and attaches leg cuffs of a robotic gait trainer or overhead BWS system (Lokomat, ZeroG, treadmill harness), assisting the transfer from wheelchair, aligning hips/knees to the orthosis, and checking strap tension and skin.

Acute care or skilled nursing facility: PTA secures a largely dependent patient onto a tilt table or standing frame using chest, pelvic, and knee straps, often after a sling-lift or two-person transfer, managing lines/catheters and monitoring tolerance and skin integrity during strapping.

Clinic or bedside: PTA applies a gait belt, or seats and secures a patient on a mat table / in a wheelchair with a lap belt and lateral supports, or straps a limb into a CPM machine or traction unit, before beginning the exercise or modality.

Pediatric or aquatic therapy: PTA secures a child into adaptive equipment (stander, pediatric gait trainer, therapy swing, adaptive tricycle) or secures a patient into an aquatic pool lift chair; the patient may be small, uncooperative, spastic, or moving during fastening.

Home health visit: PTA secures a patient onto home-based or portable therapy equipment (pedal exerciser, portable stander, recliner with support straps) in the patient's own residence, with variable furniture layout, clutter, pets, poor lighting and no standardized equipment.

sources.title: Using Human Ratings for Feedback Control: A Supervised Learning Approach with Application to Rehabilitation Robotics
sources.claim: The most robotized physical-therapy equipment in routine clinical use — the Lokomat driven gait orthosis — is attached to the patient's ... a human therapist using Velcro straps; the robot itself performs no securing of the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the instance: it documents that securing the patient into the therapy device is performed by the human clinician, not by the commercial rehabilitation robot.

sources.title: ZeroG (Body Weight Support System) | Brooks Rehabilitation
sources.claim: In a clinical deployment of an overhead robotic body-weight-support system, human therapists place the patient into the harness and secure it to the robot; the robot's autonomy covers unweighting and tracking, not patient securing.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the instance (harnessing a patient onto therapy equipment) and shows the securing step is done by clinicians even where a rehabilitation robot is installed.

sources.system: Force-Constrained Visual Policy robot-assisted dressing system
sources.title: Force-Constrained Visual Policy: Safe Robot-Assisted Dressing via Multi-Modal Sensing
sources.claim: The research frontier for autonomous robot manipulation of fabric against a human body is a laboratory study in which a single-arm robot pulls a gown sleeve onto a seated participant's arm, evaluated with 10 participants; no strap fastening, tensioning, or whole-body securing is demonstrated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a garment onto a human limb is the closest demonstrated autonomous manipulation to placing cuffs/harnesses on a patient. It does not transfer to this task because it is a lab bench setup handling one sleeve on one cooperative arm, with no strap tensioning, transfer assistance, or safety verification at clinical reliability.

sources.system: AIREC (AI-driven Robot for Embrace and Care)
sources.developer: Waseda University (Shigeki Sugano lab), Japan Moonshot program
sources.title: Japan tests AIREC robot to roll patients, easing caregiving challenges
sources.claim: The most advanced demonstrated robot for physically handling patients rolls a person lying in bed onto their side in a university laboratory; it is a 149 kg research prototype and researchers state caregiving robotics remains limited by unresolved technical obstacles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical patient handling (repositioning a body). Even this frontier demonstration is a lab prototype performing one bed maneuver, so it cannot substantiate autonomous securing of a patient onto therapy equipment at clinical quality.

sources.system: PTR Robot (patient transfer and rehabilitation robot)
sources.title: Features - PTR Robots
sources.claim: Commercially sold patient-lifting/rehabilitation robots in care facilities are driven by a caregiver, who fits the patient's vest or sling and navigates the machine; the robot does not autonomously secure patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring and supporting patients with a machine. It shows the commercially available class of patient-handling robots is caregiver-operated, so it cannot support autonomous completion of securing a patient onto equipment.

tasks.label: Confer with physical therapy staff or others to discuss and evaluate patient information for planning, modifying, or coordinating treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Administer active or passive manual therapeutic exercises, therapeutic massage, aquatic physical therapy, or heat, light, sound, or electrical modality treatments, such as ultrasound.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic: PTA performs therapeutic massage / soft-tissue work (effleurage, petrissage, trigger-point pressure) on a patient's back, neck-shoulders or legs while the patient lies on a treatment plinth in a curtained bay; pressure and duration adjusted to patient tolerance.

Outpatient clinic gym: PTA administers active and active-assisted therapeutic exercise - guiding a post-op knee/shoulder or deconditioned patient through ROM, stretching, band/dumbbell strengthening with manual resistance, spotting and hands-on cueing; a small minority of these sessions are run in a therapy pool as aquatic therapy.

Clinic or hospital treatment bay: PTA applies a thermal or acoustic physical agent - a hydrocollator hot pack wrapped in towels (or an ice pack) laid on the lumbar spine/knee for 15 minutes, or ultrasound gel and a transducer moved over a shoulder/knee for 6-10 minutes at set parameters - then removes it and checks the skin.

Clinic or SNF: PTA sets up an electrical stimulation treatment - selects and places 2-4 adhesive electrodes at anatomically determined sites (motor points, painful region, over a quadriceps for NMES), sets waveform/intensity to patient tolerance, monitors, and removes the electrodes.

Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab: PTA administers passive and active-assisted ROM to a frail elderly or neurologically impaired patient at bedside or in the rehab gym, plus assisted gait/limb training; involves positioning a dependent patient, handling contracted or painful limbs, and reading patient responses.

Home health visit: PTA administers the exercise program (assisted ROM, sit-to-stand, ambulation) and occasional hot pack in the patient's own home - variable furniture, floor surfaces, pets and family present, patient often transferred from bed or recliner.

sources.title: Aescape raises $83M to bring robotic massager to more locations - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Aescape's Aertable is a commercially operating, fully autonomous two-armed robotic massage table that scans the body and delivers a table massage without a human therapist, rolled out in fitness-club spas.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Aescape robotic massage is being installed in Massage Envy franchise clinics, treating paying clients in ordinary massage-clinic treatment rooms with coverage of the posterior body from upper back to calves.

sources.developer: Adamo Robot / Servicio Riojano de Salud (trial)
sources.title: Using a Robot to Treat Non-specific Low Back Pain: Results From a Two-Arm, Single-Blinded, Randomized Controlled Trial
sources.claim: The ADAMO massage robot delivered 10-minute therapeutic trigger-point massage to low-back-pain patients in a hospital rehabilitation service in a randomized controlled trial; robot-treated patients' pain scores improved significantly versus the sham-robot control receiving therapist care.

sources.title: Harmonic Bionics Installs First of Two Harmony SHR Robotic Rehabilitation Systems Purchased by Top Neurological Hospital in Phoenix
sources.claim: Harmony SHR, an FDA-registered bilateral upper-extremity rehabilitation exoskeleton, moves a strapped-in patient's arms and shoulders through therapy motions and has been purchased and installed for inpatient and outpatient therapy programs at a US neurological hospital.

sources.title: Lokomat Robotic Gait Rehabilitation | UM Shore Regional Health
sources.claim: The Lokomat robotic gait orthosis is installed in roughly 25 US hospitals and rehabilitation centers, where it moves a harnessed patient's legs through gait cycles and automatically reduces assistance as the patient improves - i.e. the machine administers the passive/active-assisted exercise.

sources.system: Electromechanical/robot-assisted gait trainers (Lokomat, Gait Trainer GT I, etc.)
sources.title: Electromechanical-assisted training for walking after stroke - Cochrane Library (2025)
sources.claim: Cochrane systematic review evidence shows machine-delivered gait training combined with physiotherapy yields outcomes at least as good as therapist-delivered gait training, supporting that robot-administered exercise meets clinically accepted quality.

sources.title: MOTOmed letto2 Leg trainer - MOTOmed
sources.claim: The MOTOmed letto2 is a commercially deployed motorized movement-therapy device that delivers passive, motor-assisted and active limb movement to bedridden patients from a hospital bed or therapy chair in inpatient, ICU and care-home settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: motor-driven passive/assisted ROM of the lower limbs. This is the same physical act a PTA performs as passive ROM/assisted cycling for dependent SNF patients, on the same body segments, with the limbs fixtured into the pedals.

sources.developer: Su, Liu, Ren et al. (Nature Communications)
sources.title: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound system for thyroid scanning | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robotic ultrasound ... scanned the thyroid region of 70 human volunteers without human assistance, using skeleton-point recognition, reinforcement learning and contact-force feedback to keep the probe on the skin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: diagnostic ultrasound scanning. Therapeutic ultrasound delivery is the same physical act - coupling gel plus a transducer held on bare skin at regulated contact force and swept over a body region for several minutes - but with looser targeting tolerance, since no diagnostic image must be obtained.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Chinese PLA General Hospital
sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system
sources.claim: UltraBot, a learning-based autonomous carotid ultrasound robot, achieves human-expert-level scanning performance on human subjects, planning and executing probe placement and sweeps on the neck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ultrasound probe manipulation on a human body. Transfers to therapeutic ultrasound and to gentle instrument-on-skin modality application: same compliant contact with living tissue, same force regulation, same sweep motions over a treatment region.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance (ACM/IEEE HRI 2024)
sources.claim: RABBIT autonomously performed washing, rinsing and drying passes with a compliant end-effector on the limbs of 12 human participants lying in a bed, including a fully autonomous cleaning trial ... person with severe mobility limitations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing and moving a soft, deformable item (wet cloth/wiping tool) in sustained compliant contact against a reclining person's skin. Applying a towel-wrapped hot pack or ice pack to a limb or the back demands the same perception of body pose, same gentle contact-force control, and lower placement precision.

tasks.label: Transport patients to and from treatment areas, lifting and transferring them according to positioning requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing facility / inpatient rehab: dependent (max-assist) resident is transferred bed→wheelchair using a mechanical lift or two-person assist, wheeled down the corridor to the therapy gym, then transferred onto a mat table and positioned for treatment (hip precautions, weight-bearing status, limb support).

Outpatient orthopedic/neuro clinic: patient ambulates with supervision, contact-guard or minimal assist (gait belt, walker/cane) from the waiting room to a treatment cubicle; PTA guards, steadies, and assists them onto the plinth/equipment and positions them.

Acute-care hospital bedside: patient with IV lines, drains, O2 and telemetry is mobilized — bed mobility, sit-to-stand, moderate-assist transfer to recliner or wheelchair, sometimes transported to the PT gym; lines managed and hemodynamic tolerance monitored throughout.

Hospital / SNF / large outpatient center: patient sits safely and transfers with supervision only; the PTA simply wheels them in a wheelchair from room, ward or lobby along corridors and via elevators to the therapy gym and back at the end of the session.

Home health: transfer of a frail patient in a private home — bed→wheelchair or chair→toilet, over rugs and around furniture, often without ceiling lift or hoist equipment, in tight bedrooms and bathrooms.

Pediatric/school-based therapy: lifting a child with cerebral palsy or other disability out of a wheelchair or stander onto a mat, bolster or equipment, and positioning per the therapist's specifications.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. / University of Tsukuba Hospital
sources.title: Safety and feasibility of in-hospital autonomous transportation using a driverless mobility for patients with musculoskeletal disorders
sources.claim: WHILL's driverless wheelchair autonomously carried 51 outpatients with musculoskeletal gait disturbance 100 m inside a hospital (reception to payment counter), navigating with stored maps and sensor-based collision avoidance, with no collisions or adverse events; the chair returns to base by itself.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element — moving a seated mobility-impaired patient between points inside a healthcare facility — with comparable occupant weight, corridor traffic and institutional setting.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Model (with Unifi/Envoy airport services)
sources.title: Wayne County Airport Authority partners with Unifi to bring autonomous wheelchairs to DTW
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs are in commercial service carrying mobility-impaired passengers to gates across multiple airports; over 100 units deployed and more than 400,000 autonomous rides completed, with pre-mapped routes, collision avoidance and remote supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting a seated person who cannot walk far through a busy institution-controlled facility; the concourse is at least as crowded and dynamic as a hospital corridor, so navigation performance carries over to wheeling a patient to a therapy gym.

sources.title: Rovex is Speeding Up Patient Transport With Robots (A3 Industry Insights)
sources.claim: Rovex's Rovi robot attaches to standard stretchers and moves them autonomously through hospitals (elevators and doors included); its first pilot at BayCare's Morton Plant Hospital began with retrieving empty stretchers before it moves actual patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the transport half of the task (moving patients on wheeled equipment through hospital corridors), but as of the pilot it moves only empty stretchers, so it does not yet substantiate patient carriage.

sources.developer: RIKEN-SRK Collaboration Center for Human-Interactive Robot Research
sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: ROBEAR, an experimental RIKEN/Sumitomo Riko nursing-care robot, can lift a patient from a bed ... and help a patient stand; it is a laboratory prototype operated by a caregiver rather than a deployed autonomous system.
sources.transferJustification: This is the lifting/transfer half of the task, but the system is an experimental caregiver-guided platform (autonomy not established), so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: VA Human Engineering Research Laboratories / University of Pittsburgh
sources.title: New robotic system improves wheelchair transfers to bed (VA Research news brief)
sources.claim: The Powered Personal Transfer System, a VA/HERL research prototype, is a custom powered wheelchair and ... so a user can move between them without being lifted; it was usability-tested with wheelchair users and caregivers.
sources.transferJustification: Closest thing to a purpose-built (E1-style) patient-transfer setup: matched bed and chair engineered for each other. It is a user-commanded research prototype limited to bed↔chair, not an autonomous therapist-quality transfer with clinical positioning.

sources.title: Features - PTR Robots
sources.claim: Blue Ocean Robotics' PTR Robot is a commercially released mobile lifting robot for transferring and mobilizing patients, but it is driven and commanded by the caregiver through its control system rather than acting autonomously.
