sources.transferJustification: Directly the lifting/transfer element of the task, but the caregiver operates it continuously (drives it, applies the sling/vest), so it is an operator-controlled aid, not an autonomous substitute.

tasks.label: Clean work area and check and store equipment after treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports PT clinic, between back-to-back patients: wipe down the vinyl plinth, mat table and any exercise equipment used with hospital-grade disinfectant wipes, strip and replace linens/pillowcases, return cuff weights, dumbbells, resistance bands, balls and wobble boards to their racks/bins, coil e-stim and ultrasound cables and peel off used electrodes, wipe the ultrasound head, check the hydrocollator water level and unit function, and report/tag anything damaged.

Acute-care hospital / inpatient rehab unit: after a bedside or gym session, disinfect the gait belt, walker, wheelchair, transfer board and pulse oximeter, return borrowed equipment to the therapy storage room or the patient's room, wipe the mat table and parallel bar rails, restock the gait-belt and linen supply, and check equipment for cracked frames, worn brakes or missing parts, flagging defects for repair.

Skilled nursing facility therapy gym and resident rooms: sanitize NuStep/recumbent bike seats and handles, pedal exercisers, therapy putty, therabands and hand weights after each resident, wipe mats and treatment tables, wheel equipment back to designated spots in a crowded shared gym, check equipment safety (brakes, straps, cords) and log/report issues.

Pediatric PT clinic / sensory gym: after a session, collect and disinfect balls, bolsters, foam mats, swings, scooter boards and small toys, place mouthed or soiled toys into the soiled-toy bin, re-stow items on shelves and hooks, and inspect for broken pieces, tears or loose hardware before the next child arrives.

Home health visit in a private residence: after treating the patient, wipe down the portable equipment used (gait belt, goniometer, portable e-stim, pulse oximeter, exercise bands) and any household surfaces used as a treatment area, repack the therapy bag in order, dispose of used supplies, and restock/organize supplies in the car for the next visit.

Aquatic therapy pool deck: after a pool session, rinse and hang flotation belts, noodles, water dumbbells and kickboards to dry, wipe the transfer bench, hoist chair and deck rails, return the wet gait belt and towels for laundering, and check the pool lift and gear for wear or damage.

sources.title: Building Robotics That Work Outside the Lab
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields a commercially deployed autonomous mobile manipulator that navigates and wipes surfaces with a cloth in occupied hotel bathrooms — spaces designed for human workers, not machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: disinfecting/wiping hard surfaces and fixtures in a human-built facility. Transfer to the PTA task's surface-cleaning component is direct (cloth wiping of hard surfaces), but the demonstrated scope is fixed bathroom fixtures on a pre-learned static layout, not retrieving and racking loose therapy equipment.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom-cleaning robot autonomously cleans fixtures and floors, opens doors and picks up trash, and is deployed in hospitals and airports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restroom cleaning and trash pickup inside a healthcare facility. It shows autonomous spray/wipe cleaning plus limited object pickup in an institution-controlled setting, but the objects and layouts are restroom-standard, not a therapy gym's assorted weights, bands and modality cables.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo autonomous floor scrubbers are commercially deployed in hospitals and other healthcare facilities, cleaning floors without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated floor cleaning of a clinical work area. It covers the floor portion of 'clean work area' in an institution-controlled facility, but performs no manipulation, so it cannot check or store equipment.

sources.title: The use of a UV-C disinfection robot in the routine cleaning process: a field study in an Academic hospital
sources.claim: A UVD Robots UV-C disinfection robot ran autonomous disinfection cycles in two hospital outpatient clinics as part of the routine cleaning process, using pre-programmed maps of furniture positions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: terminal disinfection of an outpatient clinic treatment room. It substantiates autonomous pathogen reduction of a clinic work area, but it supplements rather than replaces manual wiping and does not handle, inspect or stow equipment.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously identifies and picks individual products of many kinds out of containers and places them into designated totes, operating in fenced fulfillment-center cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level picking and sortation of heterogeneous goods presented in bins. Transfers to the 'store equipment' component when the equipment is presented to the machine in totes at a fixtured station — comparable object size, weight and variety — but not to retrieving items scattered around a gym.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell ... Staubli TX2-60L arm, vision-based fine-grained classification, and fixtured 3D-printed holders sorts, checks and packs surgical instruments into sterile ... in a hospital sterile-processing workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inspecting and stowing reusable clinical equipment after use. It is the closest analogue to 'check and store equipment' — identification, defect/identity verification, and placement into designated holders — performed in a purpose-built fixtured station with items presented to the arm.

sources.title: Dürr Ecoclean Supplies its 100th EcoCFlex System to BMW Group Austrian Plant
sources.claim: Dürr Ecoclean's EcoCFlex robotized cleaning cells, in which a manipulator carries workpieces through spray/flood washing stations, have been in volume production service at BMW engine plants, with the 100th unit installed in 2017.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic washing of items brought to a machine. Transfers to the E1 rendering of 'clean equipment after treatment' — a robot handling presented objects through a wash/dry cycle at production reliability — though the cell itself is fenced and takes only fixtured parts.

tasks.label: Communicate with or instruct caregivers or family members on patient therapeutic activities or treatment plans.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/neuro clinic: at the end of a visit the PTA explains the home exercise program to the spouse, parent, or adult child who accompanied the patient — reviewing sets/reps, frequency, precautions, red flags, and handing over a printed or app-based handout, then answering their questions.

Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab, discharge teaching: the PTA instructs family members in safe transfers, gait-belt use, walker/wheelchair handling, and weight-bearing precautions, demonstrating the technique and then coaching the caregiver through a return demonstration with the patient.

Home health visit: the PTA educates a family caregiver in the patient's own home on bed mobility, positioning, fall-prevention and home-layout modifications, and the prescribed exercise routine, tailoring the explanation to the caregiver's literacy, language, and physical ability.

Facility hand-off communication: the PTA briefs nursing staff, CNAs, or restorative aides on the patient's current mobility status, assist level, precautions, and the therapeutic activities they should carry over between therapy sessions; documented in the chart or communicated at a care-team huddle.

Remote contact: phone call, telehealth session, or secure-portal message with an out-of-town family member or paid caregiver to update them on progress toward the plan of care, clarify the exercise program, and answer questions.

tasks.label: Measure patients' range-of-joint motion, body parts, or vital signs to determine effects of treatments or for patient evaluations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports clinic: PTA measures joint range of motion of an extremity (knee flexion/extension after TKA or ACL reconstruction, shoulder elevation/rotation after rotator cuff repair, elbow, ankle dorsiflexion) with a universal goniometer. Patient lies or sits on a plinth; PTA stabilizes the proximal segment, palpates bony landmarks, takes the limb passively to end-feel and/or has the patient move actively, reads degrees, and documents against prior values.

Inpatient rehab hospital, skilled nursing facility, or neuro therapy gym: PTA measures joint ROM and joint mobility on patients with hemiparesis, spasticity, contracture, or post-immobilization stiffness. Patient may be in bed, wheelchair, or mat table; limb is heavy, tone-affected, and sometimes painful; measurement is repeated session to session to document treatment effect.

Vital signs before, during, and after exercise (outpatient clinic, acute-care hospital, cardiac/pulmonary rehab): apply BP cuff and auscultate or use an automated monitor, palpate or read pulse, clip pulse oximeter, count respirations, note exertion; interpret whether the response permits continuing treatment and record it.

Home health visit: PTA measures joint ROM with a goniometer on the operated or affected limb with the patient in a recliner, bed, or on a sofa, in a room of unknown layout with variable lighting and space, and documents progress toward goals.

Anthropometric measurement in the clinic: circumferential limb girth at marked intervals for edema/lymphedema or quadriceps atrophy, leg-length measurement, or wound/limb dimensions, using a tape measure and skin marks, compared with the contralateral side and with prior readings.

sources.title: Software - Hocoma (Lokomat)
sources.claim: The Lokomat, a commercial robotic driven gait orthosis used in rehabilitation clinics, includes a built-in standardized assessment tool (L-ROM) that measures range of motion of hip and knee flexion/extension while the patient is strapped into the exoskeleton.

sources.title: Assessing Stiffness, Joint Torque and ROM for Paretic and Non-Paretic Lower Limbs during the Subacute Phase of Stroke Using Lokomat Tools (Applied Sciences)
sources.claim: At a rehabilitation hospital (IRCCS NEUROMED), stiffness, joint torque and range ... were measured for each stroke patient at admission and at one-month follow-up using the Lokomat's robotic assessment tools as the clinical instrument, with results recorded in the patient's medical file.

sources.title: Assessing Stiffness, Joint Torque and ROM for Paretic and Non-Paretic Lower Limbs during the Subacute Phase of Stroke Using Lokomat Tools (Applied Sciences)
sources.claim: In the same routine clinical protocol the robot itself executes the joint measurement: the Lokomat drives move the hips and knees through controlled flexion/extension displacements at set velocities and the tool automatically runs repeat trials and reports the result to the therapist.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: the robot, not the clinician, moves the patient's hip and knee through a defined arc and quantifies the joint's response; this is the physical act underlying passive ROM measurement, and the same encoders yield the L-ROM degrees.

sources.title: Intended Use & Indications - Hocoma (ArmeoPower)
sources.claim: The ArmeoPower, a commercially sold motorized arm exoskeleton used in rehabilitation clinics, objectively assesses joint range of motion of the upper limb and produces reports for tracking patient progress.

sources.title: Kinarm Standard Tests - Kinarm
sources.claim: Kinarm robotic assessment workstations run standardized protocols in which the robot itself moves a subject's limb through defined angular ranges (elbow extension/flexion, passive arm positioning) and quantifies the response, in labs and clinical-research settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic quantification of passive joint behaviour): the robot performs the same physical act as a PTA taking passive ROM — moving a relaxed limb through a known angular range while recording joint angle — with the arm fixtured in the exoskeleton.

sources.title: Robotic Physical Therapy with AMADEO | Brooks Rehabilitation
sources.claim: The Amadeo robotic hand device, in clinical use at Brooks Rehabilitation (a US rehabilitation provider), moves the patient's fingers and tracks their range of motion so the therapist can monitor progress; the therapist positions the hand in the device beforehand.

sources.title: Evaluation of finger strength and spasticity in hemiplegic patients using hand-finger robotic device: A validity and reliability study
sources.claim: Measurements produced by the Amadeo hand-finger robot were validated for reliability and clinical relevance against clinician assessment in 161 participants, supporting that robot-generated joint measurements can substitute for manual clinical measures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic measurement of finger joint mechanics) establishes that measurements taken by a rehabilitation robot on a fixtured limb reach clinically acceptable reliability, which is the quality bar for the PTA's joint measurements.

sources.date: 2024 (facility equipment page); device commercial for years
sources.title: Biodex S4 Pro Isokinetic and Isometric Dynamometer | Core Facilities (ASU)
sources.claim: Biodex System 4, a commercially deployed robotic dynamometer in clinics and labs, quantifies range of motion along with torque and force while the patient's limb is strapped into the device; ROM limits are set with operator involvement.

sources.system: semi-autonomous vital sign measurement robot (PPG sensing robotic arm)
sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot - TechRxiv
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic vital-sign measurement found is a research prototype robotic arm that locates sites on a subject's arm and records photoplethysmography to derive heart rate, SpO2, respiratory rate and estimated blood pressure; it is described as semi-autonomous and is not a deployed clinical system.

tasks.label: Train patients in the use of orthopedic braces, prostheses, or supportive devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic: PTA trains a post-op or injured patient in a knee brace, walking boot, wrist splint or shoulder sling — applies it correctly the first time, aligns hinges to the joint line, sets tension/straps and ROM stops, checks skin and fit, then coaches the patient through donning/doffing themselves, corrects hand placement and sequencing, and confirms independent, safe use before discharge from the session.

Acute-care hospital (post-op ortho, med-surg, or ICU step-down): PTA sizes and adjusts a walker, crutches or cane to the patient's height, applies a gait belt, teaches sit-to-stand, weight-bearing restrictions, three-point gait, turning, and stairs, guarding a weak or dizzy patient in the room and hallway with lines/drains attached, and grades assistance to the patient's response.

Inpatient rehab / prosthetics clinic: PTA trains a new lower-limb amputee to don the liner, sock plies and socket, inspect the residual limb, and progress from parallel-bar weight shifting to ambulation with the prosthesis, giving hands-on correction and physically guarding against falls.

Home health visit: PTA trains an older adult in the patient's own house to use a rollator, cane, AFO or bath transfer equipment within the actual home layout — narrow hallways, throw rugs, pets, porch steps — adjusting the device and coaching safe negotiation of those obstacles.

Skilled nursing facility: PTA repeatedly trains a resident, often with dementia or low vision, to use a walker or wheelchair correctly — cueing, re-positioning the hands, applying a brace or bilateral AFOs, guarding transfers, and instructing the nursing aides on carryover.

sources.system: ROGER SAR self-training robot (TU Ilmenau / Waldkliniken Eisenberg)
sources.developer: Ilmenau University of Technology, Neuroinformatics and Cognitive Robotics Lab
sources.title: Robot-Assisted Gait Self-Training: Assessing the Level Achieved (Sensors)
sources.claim: The ROGER socially assistive robot autonomously accompanies post-hip-surgery patients during gait self-training in a hospital, classifying gait features in real time and giving corrective feedback, including on correct forearm-crutch three-point gait — but it only reinforces lessons already taught by physiotherapists and performs no physical handling, fitting or guarding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coaching correct use of forearm crutches during gait. It is the closest cited system to 'training patients in the use of supportive devices', but it delivers only screen/voice feedback during self-training in a hospital corridor; it cannot size or fit a device, apply a brace, guard a patient, or certify independent safe use, so it does not carry over to completing the instance.

sources.system: Force-modulated visual dressing policy (robot-assisted dressing system)
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: A learned, force-modulated visual policy autonomously dressed long-sleeve garments onto the arms of 12 human participants across 264 trials in a laboratory setup, adapting to arm motion — the frontier of robotic manipulation of deformable items onto a live human limb.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a deformable item onto a human limb, comparable to sliding a sleeve-style brace on. It does not transfer to this task: it handles loose everyday garments in a fixed lab cell, does not align hinges, tension straps to a clinical target, inspect skin, or teach and verify the patient's own independent donning.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology – AlleyWatch
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage tables are commercially deployed in gyms, hotels and wellness clubs, applying controlled force to a human body lying on a purpose-built table without a therapist operating the arms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical contact with a client's body in a human-use facility. It does not transfer: the client is prone and passive on a machine-specific table, the robot manipulates no objects, fits no device, and provides no instruction, fit verification, or fall guarding for an ambulating patient.

tasks.label: Monitor operation of equipment and record use of equipment and administration of treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic clinic: PTA has a patient on an electrical stimulation, ultrasound, or mechanical traction unit; watches the unit's display/timer and the patient's tolerance for the treatment interval, then charts the modality, parameters (intensity, frequency, duration, electrode placement) and the exercises performed into the clinic EMR flowsheet/daily note.

Skilled nursing facility / inpatient rehab: PTA records therapy minutes, equipment used (gait belt, mechanical lift, parallel bars, NuStep, NMES unit), assistance level and billing units in the facility EMR, checking that timers and treatment logs match what was administered for Medicare documentation.

Acute-care hospital: PTA monitors bedside equipment during mobilization (telemetry, pulse oximeter, IV pumps, CPM machine, oxygen flow) and documents vitals, tolerance and equipment use in the hospital EHR at or shortly after the session.

Routine equipment operation checks and logs: verifying a modality unit powers up and outputs correctly, checking hydrotherapy/paraffin/hot-pack temperatures against limits, noting a malfunction for repair, and signing calibration, safety and cleaning logs.

Home health, school, or mobile setting: PTA documents on a tablet or laptop the equipment brought or already in the home (portable TENS, walker, CPM, exercise equipment), its use and the treatment administered, syncing the visit note to the agency system.

tasks.label: Assist patients to dress, undress, or put on and remove supportive devices, such as braces, splints, or slings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports PT clinic: PTA helps a seated patient don and later doff a hinged knee brace, ankle-foot orthosis, or wrist splint before and after gait/exercise training — aligning the hinge with the joint line, tensioning straps, seating the AFO in the shoe, checking skin and fit.

Acute hospital or inpatient rehab: PTA dresses a post-stroke or post-op patient at bedside (shirt over a hemiparetic arm, pants over lines/drains, socks and shoes) prior to gait training, working around IV lines, hip or sternal precautions, and a patient who cannot hold a stable posture.

Skilled nursing facility: PTA helps a frail elderly resident with socks, shoes, compression stockings and a gait belt in a resident room, managing edematous limbs, fragile skin, contractures, and intermittent patient resistance or confusion.
Home health visit: PTA assists the patient in their own home to don a lumbar/TLSO brace or compression stockings, in a bedroom or bathroom with variable furniture, lighting, clutter, and pets.

Post-op shoulder sling/immobilizer: PTA applies and removes an arm sling with torso strap in the clinic, positioning the arm in the prescribed angle, routing and tensioning straps around the trunk without stressing the repair.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy (FMVP) robot-assisted dressing system, Sawyer arm
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute (Hao, Wang, Held, Erickson)
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robot-assisted dressing (CMU, Sawyer arm) dresses only a single sleeve onto one moving arm of a seated able-bodied participant, starting from a garment already grasped by the robot, and achieves on average 85% of arm length covered — partial, single-sub-step performance in a lab, not a full dressing episode.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task family (assisting a person into a garment); cited to show that even the best autonomous system covers only part of one sleeve, from a pre-grasped garment, in a lab.

sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: The same CMU system explicitly excludes garment pickup/grasping: the robot begins each trial already holding the garment's shoulder opening, so retrieval, orientation and unfolding of clothing are outside its demonstrated capability.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family; establishes the scope limits of the leading autonomous dressing demonstration.

sources.developer: Waseda University (Shigeki Sugano lab), JST Moonshot program
sources.title: AIREC — Waseda (project top page, application movements)
sources.claim: Waseda's AIREC humanoid demonstrates caregiving motions including assisting a person to put on socks and rolling a person in bed, shown in the university laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Sock donning is a component of the dressing task; cited as the closest care-robot demonstration, but autonomy level and reliability are not established and it is a single lab demonstration.

sources.title: AI robots may hold key to nursing Japan's ageing population (Reuters)
sources.claim: AIREC's own lead researcher states the robot is not expected to be usable in nursing-care or medical facilities until around 2030, confirming that no such patient-contact caregiving robot is deployed at worker quality today.

sources.system: Survey of learning-based robotic caregiving (feeding, grooming, dressing, repositioning)
sources.title: Feeding, grooming, dressing, and body repositioning: categorizing four pillars of learning-based manipulation for robotic caregiving
sources.claim: A 2026 survey of learning-based robotic caregiving covering dressing concludes that dressing and related physical-assistance tasks remain research challenges because of deformable garments, diverse human behavior and safety-critical contact.

sources.title: Researchers prepare robots for an aging society — Stanford Report
sources.claim: Stanford research on assistive dressing takes the form of robotic garments (vine-robot shirts, self-assembling panels with automated zippers) demonstrated in the lab, rather than a robot that fits ordinary clothing or orthoses onto a patient.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (donning/doffing clothing); cited to show the alternative approach is a special robotic garment in a lab, which cannot substitute for fitting a patient's own clothing, braces, splints or slings.

tasks.label: Fit patients for orthopedic braces, prostheses, or supportive devices, such as crutches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic PT clinic: sizing and fitting a knee, ankle, wrist, or lumbar brace on a post-op or injured patient — positioning the brace on the limb relative to bony landmarks, tensioning straps in sequence, setting hinge/ROM stops, checking skin and circulation, adjusting on patient-reported comfort, and teaching don/doff.

Acute hospital or inpatient rehab unit: measuring the patient and adjusting axillary crutches, a rolling walker, or a cane to correct height (hand grip at greater trochanter, 20-30 deg elbow flexion, axillary clearance), then verifying fit while the patient stands and ambulates, with a gait belt and fall precautions.

Skilled nursing / subacute facility: donning and adjusting AFOs, resting hand splints, shoulder slings, or heel-offloading boots on frail, edematous, or contracted patients in bed or wheelchair; managing spastic limbs, checking for pressure/redness, re-strapping and padding.

Amputee rehab session in a clinic: assisting with prosthetic liner and limb donning, checking socket fit and suspension, adding or removing sock plies for volume changes, inspecting residual limb skin, and flagging alignment or fit problems to the PT/prosthetist.

Home health visit: fitting and adjusting a brace, sling, or ambulatory device in the patient's own home — variable furniture, lighting, floor surfaces and clutter, patient often seated on a couch or bed, family caregiver present and being trained.

sources.system: CMU Robotics Institute robot-assisted dressing system (Yufei Wang, David Held, Zackory Erickson)
sources.title: Robotic-assisted dressing system accommodates different poses, body types and garments
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robot-assisted dressing (CMU Robotics Institute) autonomously pulls a garment sleeve up a seated participant's arm in a lab; averaged over test cases the system covered 86% of arm length — partial task success on garment donning only, no strap tensioning, sizing, or fit assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing. It is the nearest demonstrated capability to placing an orthosis or sling on a limb (deformable material, contact with a human limb), but it stops at getting a sleeve onto an arm and does not perform sizing, strap tensioning, hinge setting, or fit/skin verification, so it does not transfer to whole-task device fitting.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University (Hao, Wang, Held, Erickson)
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: The most recent CMU dressing system (CoRL 2025) handles arm motion and occlusion, evaluated in a real-world human study ... 12 participants over 264 trials, dressing two long-sleeve garments — still a laboratory research system, not a deployed clinical one.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing with limb motion. It shows the current frontier of physical human-robot contact with deformable items in a lab; it does not demonstrate fitting orthopedic braces, prostheses, or adjusting ambulatory devices, and is not deployed at clinical reliability.

sources.system: RHP Friends humanoid (AIST) in nursing context; Moxi/Nurabot hospital robots

sources.claim: Humanoid robots being introduced into hospitals and rehab settings perform logistics, guidance, monitoring and gait-training supervision; physically manipulative nursing-care tasks on patients (e.g., transfer support) are demonstrated with substantial teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical nursing-care assistance (patient transfer support). Shows that even the most advanced humanoid patient-contact work in care settings relies on teleoperation, so it cannot substantiate autonomous brace or assistive-device fitting.

tasks.label: Perform postural drainage, percussions, or vibrations or teach deep breathing exercises to treat respiratory conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute-care hospital ward: post-operative or pneumonia inpatient. PTA sits the patient upright, teaches and supervises diaphragmatic/segmental deep breathing, incentive spirometry and splinted coughing, corrects technique by hand placement on the ribs/abdomen, watches SpO2, respiratory rate and pain, adjusts dosage, documents.

Hospital ward or ICU patient with retained secretions: PTA turns the patient into prescribed postural-drainage side-lying/head-down positions around lines, drains and IV poles, applies cupped-hand or mechanical percussion and expiratory vibrations over the affected lung segments, coaches huff cough, monitors tolerance and stops for desaturation or arrhythmia.

Skilled nursing / subacute facility: frail, often cognitively impaired resident with COPD, CHF or resolving pneumonia. PTA repeatedly cues pursed-lip and diaphragmatic breathing during activity, positions the resident for lung expansion, occasionally adds percussion or a mechanical percussor, and coordinates with nursing.

Outpatient clinic / pulmonary or post-surgical rehab: ambulatory patient taught diaphragmatic and pursed-lip breathing, breath-to-movement pacing and airway clearance technique with tactile cueing, given a home program, progressed within the PT's plan of care.

Home health visit: PTA works in the patient's own bedroom/living room, uses the household bed and pillows to set drainage or lung-expansion positions, performs percussion or teaches breathing and huff-cough technique, and trains a family caregiver to repeat it, amid clutter, pets and variable lighting.

Pediatric chest physiotherapy (cystic fibrosis, neuromuscular disease) at home, school or a children's clinic: manual percussion and vibration over anterior, lateral and posterior segments of a small, squirming child in several tilted positions, with play-based breathing games and caregiver instruction.

sources.system: Intelligent percussion-based sputum clearance robot (Beihang / Hunan Intelligent Rehabilitation Robot center)

sources.title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Percussion-Based Sputum Clearance Robot — Chinese Journal of Mechanical Engineering
sources.claim: A research group built an intelligent percussion-based sputum clearance ... (mobile base, 6-DoF arm, damped vibration percussion head, Kinect vision) that autonomously detects the human back, plans the percussion path excluding spine and scapula, and delivers force-controlled percussion under staff supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the percussion/vibration component of this task: mechanical percussion over the lung fields of a patient lying in a hospital bed for airway clearance.

sources.developer: Yue Pan, Diansheng Chen et al. (tested at Shengjing Hospital, China Medical University)
sources.title: Design and Implementation of an Intelligent Percussion-Based Sputum Clearance Robot (Section 7.3 Sputum Clearance Operation Effectiveness Test)

sources.transferJustification: Percussion for sputum clearance on a patient in a hospital bed is the percussion/vibration element of this task; the test shows the delivery step, not patient positioning, cough coaching or physiologic monitoring.

sources.title: AI and Robotic Massage, Delivered On-Demand — ASME
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage table applies force-controlled bodywork to a client lying on a purpose-built table without a therapist operating it, and is commercially deployed in fitness clubs and spas (Equinox, Life Time, Massage Envy).

sources.title: Breathe with Me: A Breathing Exercise Guided by the Robot NAO Reduces Stress

tasks.label: Prepare treatment areas and electrotherapy equipment for use by physiotherapists.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic PT clinic: between back-to-back patients the PTA resets a treatment bay — sprays and wipes the vinyl plinth and contact surfaces with hospital-grade disinfectant, pulls fresh table paper or a clean sheet and pillowcase, drops used towels/linen in the hamper, clears the previous patient's props and lays out the bolsters, belts and bands the next plan calls for.

Setting up electrotherapy and other modality equipment for a scheduled treatment: wheeling or lifting the e-stim/TENS/NMES, ultrasound or traction unit into place, plugging it in, connecting lead wires and electrodes or the sound head, dispensing gel, powering up and verifying settings/self-test, and preparing an adjunct hot pack from the hydrocollator wrapped in towel layers or a cold pack.

Hospital or skilled-nursing facility: preparing the space for a bedside or gym session — clearing the area around an occupied bed (moving the overbed table, chair, IV pole, lines and personal items), wiping the mat table, bringing gait belt, walker or portable stim unit, and setting up parallel bars, mats and chairs in a shared therapy gym.

Home health visit: in the patient's own home, clearing floor space of rugs, cords and furniture, positioning a sturdy chair or setting up a portable mat, checking lighting and trip hazards, and laying out the portable e-stim unit and supplies brought in the bag.

Between-session stocking and equipment upkeep in the clinic: restocking linens, towels, gel, electrodes and gloves from the supply closet into bays and modality carts, refilling/skimming the hydrocollator, cleaning ultrasound heads and cords, charging and function-testing portable units, and logging equipment checks.

sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Two Figure humanoids running a single learned vision-language-action policy autonomously reset a staged bedroom, including tidying objects, taking out trash, pushing furniture and collaboratively making a bed with a deformable comforter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: resetting a room and making a bed. Transfers to resetting a treatment bay — same deformable flat linen, same clear-and-place tidying of light props, at comparable (low) precision; a fixtured, standardized bay presents the work more predictably than the staged bedroom.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.developer: POSTECH / KIST / Korea Institute of Robot and Convergence / Elphoton
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile manipulator physically wipes hospital surfaces with a manipulator and adds UV-C, validated by repeated autonomous runs and bacterial culture testing at a working hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact wiping/disinfection of clinical surfaces. Same objects (bed and table surfaces), same chemical-wipe action required to sanitize a plinth between patients.

sources.system: Inwatec soiled-side sorting robots (robot separator, THOR/ODIN line)
sources.title: Automation for soiled side sorting - Inwatec | Robotics for Industrial Laundries
sources.claim: Robotic systems in industrial laundries automatically separate and handle soiled flat linen and garments, including hospital laundry, with over 100 robots deployed ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of soiled hospital linen in a purpose-built line. Substantiates that stripping and disposing of used linen/towels is achievable when the work is presented to the machine (E1 conditions).

sources.system: Dürr EcoRS Clean F / EcoClean car body cleaning robots
sources.title: Car Body Cleaning - Dürr
sources.claim: Robot-guided cleaning systems with feather rollers/dusters clean fixtured vehicle bodies conveyed through paint shops before painting, as standard production equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated surface cleaning of a workpiece brought to the machine. Establishes reliable, production-grade robotic wiping of large fixtured surfaces, the E1 analogue of wiping down a treatment plinth.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: A fully automated compounding robot prepares IV syringes and bags in ..., handling vials, syringes, needles and fluid transfer inside an enclosed aseptic workspace.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing clinical consumables/equipment sets to a clinical standard inside a purpose-built enclosure. Comparable objects (small clinical devices, connectors, fluids) and higher precision than assembling an e-stim setup.

sources.system: Eureka Robotics force-controlled connector insertion cell (Eureka 3D camera + force control)
sources.title: Automated Connector Insertion in Automotive Wire Harness Assembly
sources.claim: A vision- and force-controlled industrial robot grips and mates electrical connectors on a moving line, a task previously done manually, with force feedback preventing pin damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mating electrical connectors under force control. Directly comparable to plugging lead wires into an electrotherapy unit and snapping electrode leads, at equal or finer precision.

sources.system: RIF Robotics PacR (Wellstar Windy Hill pilot); autonomous instrument tray assembly system
sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: A robotic arm with computer vision autonomously assembled a minor surgical instrument tray during a hospital sterile-processing pilot; a research system also fully automates sorting and packing instruments into sterile trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a defined set of clinical items into a tray for a procedure. Same class of work as laying out and kitting modality supplies (electrodes, gel, leads, towels) for a treatment.

sources.title: Telexistence Deploys AI and Remote-Controlled Robots in 300 Convenience Stores, Utilizing Azure
sources.claim: A robot installed in convenience-store backrooms detects empty shelf slots and restocks beverages automatically, deployed at hundreds of stores, with remote staff intervening only when AI stocking fails.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment of standardized stock from a fixed station. Comparable objects and precision to restocking gel bottles, glove boxes and linen packs into clinic shelving when items are presented to the machine.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals (IEEE Spectrum); Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: Mobile manipulators pick supplies out of hospital supply closets and deliver them to units and patient rooms completely autonomously; the fleet has passed 1.25 million deliveries across 25+ US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving and transporting clinical supplies inside a working healthcare facility. Covers the fetch-and-deliver portion of stocking a clinic, but not shelf placement, hydrocollator service or equipment testing.

tasks.label: Administer traction to relieve neck or back pain, using intermittent or static traction equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic PT clinic, mechanical lumbar traction: PTA positions the patient supine or prone on a split traction table, fits and snugs thoracic and pelvic harnesses over clothing, hooks the spreader bar to the traction unit, dials in the poundage/hold/rest pattern from the PT's plan, hands the patient the safety cut-off switch, checks in over a 10-20 minute pull, then releases tension, removes the harnesses, assists the patient up and documents response.

Outpatient clinic, cervical traction: patient supine with a head halter or a Saunders-style cervical device; PTA seats the occiput in the cradle, adjusts chin strap or neck wedges and the angle of pull, sets poundage and intermittent/static mode, monitors for dizziness, nausea or peripheralized symptoms during the 10-15 minute session, then unloads and removes the halter.

First traction trial or symptom-modification session in the clinic: PTA titrates poundage and pull angle, repositions the patient (e.g., adds a pillow, shifts to prone), and reduces or aborts the session mid-pull based on the patient's report of increased or peripheralizing symptoms, then reports the response back to the supervising PT.

Inpatient hospital, subacute rehab or SNF: traction delivered on a plinth or bed to a partly dependent patient; PTA assists the transfer and positioning, works around lines, braces or post-op precautions, fits the harness on a frail patient who may not reliably use a cut-off switch, and monitors tolerance and vitals throughout.

Home health visit: PTA sets up a portable home traction unit (over-door cervical halter or a portable lumbar device) in the patient's residence, fits the halter/belts, demonstrates a safe pull and hold, watches the patient perform it, and instructs the patient and caregiver on the home program.

sources.title: TRITON DTS TRACTION UNIT - Chattanooga
sources.claim: Clinical traction units are purpose-built machines that deliver static, intermittent and cyclic pull to a harnessed patient under fully programmable machine control, with stored clinical protocols.

sources.system: Chattanooga clinical traction line (Triton / Triton DTS)
sources.title: Traction Therapy | Chattanooga
sources.claim: The traction pull pattern itself is automated by the device once parameters are entered; the vendor markets protocol automation for clinic throughput.

sources.developer: n/a — coding/practice guidance published by SPRY
sources.title: CPT Code 97012 : Mechanical Traction Therapy Code
sources.claim: In routine US clinical practice the traction pull is delivered machine-only: once the patient is set up and holding the cut-off switch, the treatment runs unattended with periodic check-ins.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: it describes how the traction modality is administered in clinics, establishing that the force-delivery and monitoring phase already runs under machine control with a patient-held safety switch.

sources.system: BackHug (26 robotic fingers, app-controlled robotic back therapy bed)
sources.title: Using Science & Technology To Fix Your Back Pain | BackHug
sources.claim: A commercially sold robotic therapy bed autonomously delivers targeted mechanical spinal mobilization to a person who simply lies on it, used in clinics, wellness centers and homes and studied in clinical pilots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (machine-delivered spinal mobilization): the patient positions himself on a purpose-built therapy bed and the machine applies programmed, force-controlled mechanical treatment to the spine — the same delivery-and-monitor phase that mechanical traction requires.

sources.title: Equinox | The World's Most Advanced Massage
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic table scans a clothed client and applies force-controlled therapeutic contact to the body, deployed commercially in gyms and hotels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot-applied soft-tissue therapy): shows commercial-grade autonomous force application to a person lying on a purpose-built table, supporting the physical-contact-with-patient portion of modality delivery, though it involves no harnessing.

sources.title: AI-powered massage robot to start product evaluation in the United States and clinical trial in Singapore
sources.claim: An autonomous therapy robot has been deployed for paid treatment hours in physiotherapy clinics and hospitals, sensing tissue stiffness and applying controlled pressure to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot-delivered physical therapy modality in a clinic): demonstrates autonomous, force-controlled machine treatment of patients inside human clinical facilities; it does not include fitting straps or harnesses to a patient.

sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robot-assisted dressing — the closest analogue to fitting a traction harness on a person — reaches high success only on a manikin in the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (placing a garment/harness onto a body): fitting pelvic, thoracic or cervical traction harnesses requires equivalent or harder deformable-object manipulation on a live person; manikin-only lab results do not substantiate clinic-quality harnessing.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Healthcare Robotics Lab (Charlie Kemp)
sources.title: Robot Helps People Get Dressed - ASME
sources.claim: Research robots dressing actual human participants remain single-arm laboratory demonstrations, not clinical-quality performance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (garment/strap placement on a person): shows that autonomous manipulation of straps and garments onto a live human is still at lab-demo maturity, so harnessing a patient in a working clinic (E2) is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Perform therapeutic wound care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab bedside: resident with a stage 3 sacral or heel pressure ulcer. PTA positions/turns the patient, removes soiled adhesive dressing from fragile peri-wound skin, cleanses with saline, performs selective (non-sharp or sharp) debridement of slough, assesses tunneling/undermining, applies topical agent and new dressing, repositions patient and documents.

Outpatient wound care clinic: patient with a neuropathic diabetic foot ulcer on a treatment table. PTA removes dressing, measures/photographs the wound, performs selective sharp debridement of callus and nonviable tissue, delivers pulsed lavage with suction or whirlpool, applies dressing and offloading, instructs the patient in home care.

Acute care hospital bedside: post-surgical dehisced abdominal wound, amputation site, or trauma wound on a patient with IV lines, drains and mobility precautions. Sterile technique, removal and reapplication of a negative-pressure wound therapy dressing or packing of a cavity wound, pain monitoring, charting.

Home health visit: venous leg ulcer in the patient's own home. PTA works in a cluttered living room or bedside, removes multilayer compression wrap, cleanses and dresses the ulcer, reapplies a multilayer/Unna compression wrap at correct tension, manages pets, poor lighting, and caregiver instruction.

Hospital hydrotherapy/burn unit: partial-thickness burn or large draining wound treated on a shower cart or in a whirlpool tank — dressing removal (often adherent), irrigation/hydrotherapy, non-selective debridement, redressing of a large irregular body surface with a pain-sensitive patient.

sources.system: Autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing (force-feedback imitation learning + differentiable-simulation placement, general-purpose manipulator)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: As of late 2025, robotic wound care exists only as research on isolated subtasks; the first autonomous medical-tape detachment/placement work was demonstrated on phantoms, human skin and anatomical leg/hip/heel models in a lab, and the authors state clinical wound care remains entirely manual.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (wound redressing), but covers only tape detachment and re-securing on phantoms/anatomical models — not dressing removal, wound cleansing, debridement, or work on a live patient.

sources.system: DLR MIRO robot with MICA instrument actuating an ERBEJET 2 waterjet probe
sources.developer: German Aerospace Center (DLR) / university clinical partners
sources.title: Robotic waterjet wound debridement – Workflow adaption for clinical application and systematic evaluation of a novel technology
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic waterjet debridement system generated and executed cleaning paths on wounds, but only on ex vivo porcine skin models in a laboratory bench setup after human registration of the wound area; authors note in vivo trials are still needed.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step (debridement) of therapeutic wound care; it does not transfer to the whole task because it was performed on excised porcine skin fixtured on a bench, with no dressing removal/application, no live-patient safety handling, and no clinical follow-through.

sources.system: Autonomous robot-driven chronic wound 3D reconstruction and analysis system
sources.title: Autonomous Robot-Driven Chronic Wound 3D Reconstruction and Analysis System
sources.claim: A robot arm with an industrial 3D scanner autonomously reconstructs and measures chronic wounds, automating only the assessment/documentation portion of wound care in a laboratory setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step (wound measurement/documentation). It involves no tissue manipulation, dressing handling, or debridement, so it cannot substantiate completion of therapeutic wound care.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer-Hierarchy) on a da Vinci platform
sources.title: A Robot Performed Surgery All By Itself (Science Friday)
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue manipulation demonstrated to date, SRT-H, performed a gallbladder removal on a pig cadaver in a laboratory, indicating that autonomous robotic tissue work remains preclinical and bench-mounted.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous soft-tissue manipulation). It is performed inside a cadaveric abdomen through fixtured laparoscopic ports in a lab, not on external wounds of live patients, and involves no dressings, so it does not transfer to therapeutic wound care.

roles.title: Physical Therapist Aides
roles.description: Under close supervision of a physical therapist or physical therapy assistant, perform only delegated, selected, or routine tasks in specific situations. These duties include preparing the patient and the treatment area.

tasks.label: Clean and organize work area and disinfect equipment after treatment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient PT clinic, between-patient turnover of a treatment table/cubicle: strip used table paper, pillowcase and towels into the hamper, spray-and-wipe the plinth, headrest, bolsters and adjacent rails/counter with hospital-grade disinfectant (observing wet dwell time), put straps, wedges and props back in place, and quick-tidy the cubicle while other patients and therapists move through the area. Done many times per shift in 2-4 minutes.

Therapy gym after an exercise session: wipe down high-touch equipment left sweaty or gel-smeared (mat tables, bike/treadmill handles and seats, pulley handles, parallel bars, exercise balls) and return loose items to storage — dumbbells and weight plates onto racks, therabands coiled onto hooks, cones/steps/balance pads and mats stacked in their bins, cluttered floor cleared of trip hazards.

Modality and small-equipment reprocessing after treatments: wipe the ultrasound transducer head and gel bottle, clean or discard e-stim electrodes and wipe lead wires, clean hot/cold packs and the hydrocollator/freezer area, drain, scrub and disinfect a whirlpool/hydrotherapy tub or paraffin unit per clinic protocol.

End-of-day or after-spill floor and area cleaning of the clinic: sweep/vacuum and mop or scrub the therapy gym and treatment-room floors, spot-clean spills of water, gel, or lotion, leaving floors dry and safe before the next session.

Hospital inpatient rehab unit or skilled nursing facility: after a bedside or ward-gym session, disinfect the gait belt, walker, wheelchair, transfer board, and portable equipment used with the patient, wipe the shared mat table, and wheel the equipment back to the therapy storage room, working around beds, IV poles, and staff.

Turnover logistics and restocking that finish the clean-up: collect soiled linens/towels into a hamper and haul it to the soiled utility/laundry room, empty trash and biohazard bins and reline them, restock table paper rolls, disinfectant wipes, gloves, gowns and gel, and keep supply and equipment shelves organized.

sources.title: Avidbots partners with US provider to deploy floor-scrubbing robots in hospitals | BetaKit
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo autonomous floor-scrubbing robots are deployed in US acute-care hospitals by support-services provider HHS, cleaning floors without an operator so staff can focus on ... cleaning work.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element (cleaning the floors of a clinical work area) in the same class of institutional facility; PT clinic gym floors are the same hard-floor surfaces these robots scrub in hospitals.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals (Onshape case study)
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo is a fully ... scrubber deployed at scale in airports, hospitals, malls, schools and factories worldwide.

sources.system: FANUC robotic part-washing cells / FANUC R-2000iC/210WE washdown robot
sources.title: Robotic Part Washing Automation | FANUC Solutions | Matrix
sources.claim: Industrial robotic part-washing cells clean fixtured workpieces automatically inside a purpose-built enclosure, with the robot either loading parts into a washer or manipulating cleaning tools itself; FANUC sells IP67 washdown robots specifically for these wet cleaning cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cleaning/washing of presented items in a fenced cell. Transfers to disinfecting PT equipment when the item is brought to the machine — comparable object sizes, wet chemistry, and no precision beyond surface coverage.

sources.title: LC 80 - Steelco
sources.claim: Steelco LC 80 is a commercial hospital washer-disinfector that automatically cleans and thermally disinfects bulky reusable items including wheelchairs, hospital furniture, trolleys, basins and instruments, with optional automatic loading/unloading systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine reprocessing of patient-care equipment in a hospital decontamination room. The objects (wheelchairs, walkers, basins, small devices) are exactly the equipment a PT aide disinfects after treatment.

sources.title: Business Talk AI: Let's talk about Artificial Intelligence for recycling with AMP Robotics
sources.claim: AMP Robotics' Cortex robots autonomously identify, pick and place heterogeneous items — including paper, film and other deformable waste — off moving conveyors in fenced sorting stations at recycling facilities, with over 125 units deployed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grasping of crumpled paper, film and mixed refuse presented on a conveyor. Transfers to removing used table paper, towels and trash and to sorting items when the work is presented to the machine at E1.

sources.system: FANUC RPL-2000 palletizing cell / vision-guided depalletizer
sources.title: Robotic Palletizing Systems | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC palletizing cells autonomously place products, slip sheets and mixed-size cartons into ordered stacks and racks and convey finished loads out of the cell, including vision-guided handling of mixed loads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ordered placement of presented objects into defined storage positions. Transfers to 'organizing' — returning weights, packs and supplies to racks and shelves — when items arrive fixtured on a conveyor at E1.

sources.title: Hospitals Set Disinfection Records; LightStrike Germ-Zapping Robots Complete 35 Million Cycles in Healthcare Facilities Worldwide
sources.claim: Xenex LightStrike UV-C room disinfection robots are used in more than 1,000 healthcare facilities, but they are positioned as a supplement that kills pathogens remaining after manual cleaning, not a replacement for wiping surfaces.

sources.title: Blue Ocean Robotics builds UV-D disinfection robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The UVD Robot is an autonomously navigating mobile UV-C robot that disinfects an emptied hospital patient room in about 15 minutes; it irradiates exposed surfaces but performs no wiping, soil removal, or object handling.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: A POSTECH-led team built an autonomous robot that both physically wipes hospital surfaces with a manipulator and applies UV-C, validated in repeated autonomous runs at Pohang St. Mary's Hospital; it is a research prototype, not a deployed product, and does not handle linens, clutter, or equipment put-away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface wiping/disinfection in a hospital. Shows the closest E2 capability, but only for pre-mapped surfaces, without soiled-linen handling, tidying, or restocking.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's Bathroom Cleaning Robot autonomously cleans fixtures and floors and picks up trash in restrooms of hospitals and airports, after a one-time VR-based setup for each fixed-layout restroom.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cleaning/disinfection of a small institutional room including trash pickup. Bounds what deployed E2 cleaning robots do: fixed sanitary fixtures in mapped restrooms, not varied clinic equipment, linens, or restocking.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators operate autonomously in hospital corridors and have completed hundreds of thousands of supply and pharmacy deliveries, but their work is fetch-and-deliver logistics, not cleaning or disinfection.

tasks.label: Secure patients into or onto therapy equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic PT clinic: aide guides an ambulatory adult patient onto a treatment table/mat or into an exercise machine (leg press, recumbent bike, upper-body ergometer), adjusts the seat/pads for the patient's body, fastens the machine's lap or limb strap, and applies a gait belt if the patient is unsteady.

Rehab gym (outpatient or inpatient): aide fits and secures a body-weight-support harness on a patient for treadmill or overhead-track gait training (LiteGait, ZeroG, Lokomat), threading and buckling torso and thigh straps snugly around the patient's body, checking fit and comfort, and attaching the harness to the device before unloading begins.

Hospital/inpatient rehab: aide helps move a dependent or partially dependent patient (post-stroke, post-op, deconditioned) from bed or wheelchair onto a tilt table, standing frame, or mat table using a sling lift or two-person assist, then fastens chest, pelvic, and knee straps and confirms alignment and skin/line safety.

Skilled nursing facility therapy room: aide positions a frail elderly patient, often with cognitive impairment and variable cooperation, onto/into equipment such as a NuStep, seated stepper, or restorator — placing feet in pedal straps, fastening the seat belt, and guarding against sliding or falls.

Clinic or hospital: a wheelchair-using patient is rolled up to a stationary therapy station (arm ergometer, traction/e-stim unit, standing table); the aide positions the chair squarely at the machine, locks it in place so it cannot roll during treatment, and secures the chair's belt.

sources.system: Q'STRAINT QUANTUM / QUANTUM GEN II automatic rear-facing wheelchair securement station
sources.date: 2013 launch; Gen II 2020; product page retrieved 2026
sources.title: Q'STRAINT: QUANTUM Automatic Rear-Facing Wheelchair Securement System
sources.claim: QUANTUM is a commercially deployed automatic wheelchair securement station: after the occupant backs the chair against the backrest and presses a button, powered arms clamp the wheelchair and continuously adjust their grip, with no attendant performing the securement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: securing a seated mobility-device user into fixed equipment (a transit securement station) rather than therapy equipment. Comparable object (an occupied wheelchair), comparable precision (clamp to prevent movement), and the securing act is machine-executed once the chair is presented in the station.

sources.title: Japan's teddy bear nurse robot gets a softer touch | PCWorld
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the best-known patient lift-and-transfer robot, is an experimental research device that still requires a human to control it during lifting and transfer.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: lifting and transferring a patient onto beds/wheelchairs is the physical-handling core of securing a patient onto therapy equipment; the source shows this remains human-controlled and experimental.

sources.system: PTR Robot (mobile patient transfer and rehabilitation robot)
sources.title: PTR Robots announces mobile robot for lifting and rehabilitating patients | The Robot Report
sources.claim: The PTR mobile lifting robot, developed and tested with a university hospital and a nursing home, is a caregiver-operated device: it enables a caregiver to perform transfers and gait training, rather than performing the transfer or securing autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patient transfer/lifting in hospitals and nursing homes, the same physical handling required to place and secure a patient on therapy equipment; the deployed state of the art is a powered aid a caregiver drives, not an autonomous securer.

sources.title: ZeroG (Body Weight Support System) | Brooks Rehabilitation
sources.claim: Even in a rehabilitation hospital equipped with a robotic overhead body-weight-support system, human staff place the patient into the harness and secure it to the robot; the robot itself does not don or fasten the harness.
sources.transferJustification: Same task in a robot-equipped clinic: the harnessing/securing step remains manual even where the therapy equipment itself is robotic, indicating no fielded system performs the securing.

sources.system: PR2 with multidimensional capacitive sensing (robot-assisted dressing and bathing)
sources.title: Multidimensional Capacitive Sensing for Robot-Assisted Dressing and Bathing (arXiv)
sources.claim: Robot manipulation of garments on a human body remains laboratory research: a robot pulling a hospital-gown sleeve onto a participant's arm was evaluated with a handful of able-bodied study participants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously manipulating fabric/straps against a human body, the nearest analog to buckling harnesses and limb straps. Performance does not carry over — it is a lab demo on able-bodied volunteers with a single sleeve, far from the reliability and tension-critical fastening a PT aide must deliver.

tasks.label: Instruct, motivate, safeguard, or assist patients practicing exercises or functional activities, under direction of medical staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports clinic gym: aide walks a post-op or low-acuity patient through a prescribed therapeutic exercise circuit (bands, cuff weights, mat and table exercises, ROM and strengthening sets), counts reps, cues and corrects form, encourages effort, stands ready to steady the patient, and reports completion to the PT.

Clinic or hospital gym: aide sets a patient on exercise equipment (recumbent bike, treadmill, upper-body ergometer, pulleys, CPM) for a timed bout, adjusts resistance/speed per the PT's parameters, watches for fatigue or pain, and motivates the patient to finish the bout.

Gait/ambulation practice: aide ambulates a fall-risk patient with a gait belt and assistive device in parallel bars, a clinic gym, or a hospital/SNF corridor, guarding and physically supporting, cueing step length and weight bearing, and stopping the activity if the patient falters.

Standing balance and gait-adaptability drills in the rehab gym: weight shifting, tandem stance, stepping over obstacles, reaching tasks on a mat or foam, with the aide guarding closely and providing verbal targets and encouragement.

Inpatient rehab unit or SNF: aide assists a dependent patient practicing functional activities - bed mobility, sit-to-stand repetitions from mat or wheelchair, transfers, stair training - providing manual assistance and hands-on safeguarding.

Patient needing heavy engagement/behavior management: pediatric patient, patient with dementia or post-stroke cognitive-communication deficits, or a pain-avoidant/anxious patient; the aide must continuously motivate, redirect, adapt the activity, and physically guard unpredictable movement.

sources.title: Lokomat Software "Sensation" - Hocoma
sources.claim: The Lokomat robotic gait trainer (harness plus motorized leg orthoses over a treadmill) runs a therapist-created therapy plan in which the patient is advanced from exercise to exercise automatically, with smart algorithms adapting difficulty; deployed in rehabilitation hospitals worldwide.

sources.title: Lokomat - Hocoma
sources.claim: The Lokomat performs the physical support and limb guidance that a human otherwise provides during gait practice, freeing the clinician from manually supporting the walking patient; the harness provides fall safety.

sources.title: Neuro-Rehabilitation Robotics & Technology | Barrow Neurological Institute
sources.claim: At a US neurological institute, the InMotion ARM/HAND robot holds the patient's limb in a fixture and delivers guidance, assistance or resistance through repetitive exercise with on-screen instruction, i.e. the machine performs the instructing, assisting and safeguarding of the practiced movement.

sources.title: BIONIK Reports 72% Increase in Sessions on InMotion Robotic Devices
sources.claim: Roughly 280 InMotion robotic therapy systems were in clinical use delivering patient sessions, showing this is routine deployed clinical practice rather than a demonstration.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich / University Hospital Balgrist group (Novak et al.)
sources.title: Automated patient-robot assignment for a robotic rehabilitation gym: a simplified simulation model (J NeuroEng Rehabil)
sources.claim: Robotic rehabilitation gyms - several patients each fixtured into a therapy robot in one room - are an established clinical model in which one clinician oversees several simultaneous robot-delivered exercise sessions, which is the supervisory/assisting role the aide fills.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered therapy sessions in a clinic. It transfers because the aide's role of supervising and safeguarding patients practicing exercises is exactly what the robot-delivered session displaces, with the same patients and the same exercises.

sources.title: C-Mill Treadmill for Balance and Gait Training | CHI Health
sources.claim: The C-Mill instrumented treadmill delivers balance and gait-adaptability training with projected targets, acoustic cues and force-plate feedback while a fall-safety harness/bodyweight-support system protects the patient; installed in US outpatient rehabilitation departments.

sources.title: tigo | Motor-assisted Cycling Trainer | THERA-Trainer
sources.claim: The THERA-Trainer tigo is a commercially sold motor-driven cycling trainer that drives, assists or resists the patient's legs or arms for an exercise bout, used in clinics, long-term care and homes.

sources.title: Andago - Gait rehabilitation system by Hocoma | MedicalExpo
sources.claim: Andago is a commercial mobile robot that moves with a patient walking overground in a therapy gym, sensing movement intention and following automatically while unloading bodyweight; it does not instruct, correct form, or decide when to stop the activity.

sources.title: ZeroG (Body Weight Support System) | Brooks Rehabilitation
sources.claim: ZeroG, an overhead track-mounted robotic bodyweight-support trolley installed in rehabilitation gyms, automatically monitors the patient and catches falls during gait and balance practice; deployed at US rehabilitation hospitals such as Brooks and St. Luke's.

sources.system: NAO socially assistive robot exercise coach
sources.title: A socially assistive robot exercise coach for the elderly | Journal of Human-Robot Interaction
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid acted as an autonomous exercise instructor with older adults at a senior living community, demonstrating autonomous instruction and motivation for exercise, but with no physical support, guarding or hands-on assistance, and only as a research study.

tasks.label: Confer with physical therapy staff or others to discuss and evaluate patient information for planning, modifying, or coordinating treatment.
