tasks.label: Change linens, such as bed sheets and pillow cases.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient PT clinic, between patients: aide strips the used sheet or table paper (and soiled pillowcase) from a treatment plinth, drops it in the soiled-linen hamper, and lays a fresh flat sheet or fresh roll paper smoothly on the table, in a 3-5 minute room turnover with other patients and staff moving through the gym.

Clinic pillows, bolsters, wedges and face cradles: aide removes soiled slip covers/pillowcases, slips fresh cases over odd-shaped foam pillows and bolsters, replaces towels on hot/cold pack stations, and restocks the clean-linen shelf in each treatment cubicle.

Inpatient rehab therapy gym (hospital or SNF): aide changes linens and pads on mat tables, tilt tables and treatment cots, including sheets soiled with sweat, gel, wound drainage or incontinence, requiring gloved handling and segregation of contaminated linen per infection-control policy.

Hospital or skilled-nursing patient room: aide performs a full bed linen change on an adjustable hospital bed — fitted bottom sheet with tucked corners, draw sheet/underpad, top sheet, blanket and pillowcases — sometimes with the patient in the bed and rolled side to side.

Home-health / patient residence: aide accompanying therapy changes sheets and pillowcases on a non-standard bed in a cluttered bedroom (bed against a wall, pets, clutter, variable mattress and linen types).

sources.title: Helix 02 Bedroom Tidy
sources.claim: Two Figure 03 humanoids running the Helix-02 policy autonomously reset a staged bedroom in under two minutes, including bimanual manipulation of a comforter (lift, unfurl, spread, smooth). This is bed-making with existing bedding, not stripping soiled linen or applying fresh sheets and pillowcases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making a bed / spreading bedding. It is the closest demonstrated capability to changing linens (same class of large deformable textiles), but the demonstration never removes used linen from a mattress nor fits a clean sheet or pillowcase, so it does not substantiate completion of a linen change.

sources.title: π0.5: a VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 VLA autonomously performs multi-step tidying in previously unseen real homes, including putting clothes into a laundry basket and cleaning bedrooms, but the reported behaviors are pick-and-place and wiping, not stripping and re-dressing a bed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household cleanup including moving laundry items. It shows soiled-textile pick-and-place in unstructured homes, which is one sub-step of a linen change, but no cited result covers removing bedding from a mattress and installing fresh sheets/pillowcases at worker quality.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity
sources.claim: DYNA-1 drives a pair of stationary arms that autonomously folded 800+ napkins over 24 hours with no human intervention in a commercial (restaurant/laundry) setting, showing sustained autonomous flat-textile manipulation in a fixed, purpose-built workstation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: folding flat textiles at a fixtured station. It establishes reliable fabric handling at E1-style structure, but the objects (small napkins on a table) and the goal (a folded stack) differ from removing soiled bed/table linen and dressing a mattress or plinth with a fitted sheet and pillowcase.

sources.system: Toyota HSR / Fetch bed-making policy (Seita et al.)
sources.developer: UC Berkeley AUTOLAB with Honda Research Institute
sources.title: Deep Transfer Learning of Pick Points on Fabric for Robot Bed-Making
sources.claim: Berkeley/Honda research robots (Toyota HSR and Fetch) autonomously learned pick points to grasp and pull a blanket for bed-making, reaching ~92% coverage on a quarter-scale twin bed ... single sub-step (increasing blanket coverage), not a linen change.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot bed-making. It is the canonical academic attempt at bedding manipulation, yet it only pulls a blanket toward corners on a reduced-scale bed and does not remove used linen, fit a sheet, or case a pillow.

sources.title: 1X's $20,000 NEO Humanoid Robot Launches With A Catch: It Needs Humans To Do Your Chores
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the most widely covered consumer robot for household chores such as tidying and laundry, relies on remote human teleoperators for tasks it cannot handle, and in press testing performed tasks under remote control rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general home chores including bedroom tidying. Cited as negative context: the leading home humanoid marketed for such chores does them under continuous teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment for linen changing.

tasks.label: Administer active or passive manual therapeutic exercises, therapeutic massage, or heat, light, sound, water, or electrical modality treatments, such as ultrasound.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic PT clinic: aide pulls a moist hot pack from the hydrocollator (or a cold pack from the freezer), wraps it in layered towels, positions it on the patient's low back, neck or shoulder while the patient lies on a treatment table behind a curtain, checks skin tolerance a few minutes in, and removes it after ~15 minutes.

Clinic exercise gym: aide takes a patient through the PT-prescribed active therapeutic exercise program — stationary bike, shoulder pulleys, TheraBand rows, mat and step exercises — setting resistance, counting reps, cueing and correcting form, and giving hands-on assistance or spotting where the patient is weak or unsteady.

Clinic treatment bay: aide sets up an electrical modality (TENS/NMES/interferential) — cleans the skin, places 2-4 adhesive electrodes over the target muscle or region, sets intensity to patient tolerance, checks in during the 15-minute treatment, then removes the pads and cleans up.

Hospital or skilled nursing facility, bedside or mat table: aide performs delegated passive range-of-motion and gentle stretching on an affected limb (shoulder, elbow, hip, knee, ankle) for a partly immobile patient, moving the joint through prescribed arcs within pain limits, or sets up and monitors a motorized passive-motion device.

Clinic: aide administers therapeutic ultrasound — applies coupling gel to a shoulder, knee or lateral epicondyle, keeps the soundhead in continuous slow contact-motion over the treatment area at prescribed intensity for 5-10 minutes, asks about heating sensation, wipes the patient and transducer down.

Clinic treatment room: aide gives delegated therapeutic soft-tissue massage/effleurage to a patient's back, shoulders or legs on a massage/treatment table for 10-20 minutes at pressure the patient tolerates, before or after other treatment.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology – AlleyWatch
sources.claim: Aescape's fully automated, AI-driven robotic massage table delivers bodywork to clients autonomously and is being rolled out commercially across 60 Equinox gym locations in the US after a New York pilot.

sources.title: Equinox Locations Add Aescape, a Fully Automated Massage Bed - Athletech News
sources.claim: Aescape is a commercially available, fully automated massage product sold to consumers in gyms and massage chains; it scans the body and delivers targeted pressure to back, shoulders, glutes, hamstrings and ... with dual robotic arms.

sources.title: Lokomat Therapy for Neurological Disorders - Moody Neurorehabilitation Institute
sources.claim: The Lokomat is a commercially deployed robotic gait-training device used in rehabilitation hospitals that moves a harnessed patient's legs through repetitive gait training — 'automated locomotion therapy' — once staff have fitted the patient into the exoskeleton and harness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered gait exercise. It is the same act the aide performs — putting a patient through prescribed repetitive active/passive lower-limb exercise at controlled dose in a clinic — with the patient fixtured into the device.

sources.title: Technical Data Sheet - ArmeoPower - Hocoma
sources.claim: ArmeoPower is a commercial upper-limb rehabilitation robot used in clinics that provides assist-as-needed guidance and arm weight support, driving joint-specific, 2D and 3D therapeutic movements and reporting range of motion after the patient's arm is strapped into the exoskeleton.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered upper-limb exercise. Same objects (a patient's limb), same prescribed active-assisted/passive exercise dose, same clinic setting as the aide's exercise and range-of-motion work.

sources.system: Continuous passive motion (CPM) machines (e.g., Kinetec, Artromot)
sources.title: Continuous Passive Motion (CPM) - Physiopedia
sources.claim: Continuous passive motion devices are standard motorized clinic and hospital equipment that carry a joint through a prescribed arc at a set speed without patient effort, once the limb is strapped into the carriage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-delivered passive range of motion. It is the same output the aide produces — a joint taken through prescribed passive arcs — with the limb fixtured to the machine.

sources.title: Axilum Robotics wins FDA 510(k) clearance for TMS-Cobot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The TMS-Cobot is an FDA-cleared, CE-marked collaborative medical robot deployed in clinics that automatically positions a stimulation applicator against a seated patient's head, controls contact in real time and compensates for patient motion throughout the treatment session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement and contact-holding of a stimulation applicator on a patient for a timed modality treatment. Comparable objects (applicator against skin), comparable or tighter precision, and a clinic treatment room — the same act as holding an electrotherapy or ultrasound applicator on a body region.

sources.system: auto-RUSS (7-DOF autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system)
sources.developer: Lin et al., Frontiers in Robotics and AI
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning ... with force control and visual servoing performed repeated probe sweeps over a human volunteer's neck, with contact force continuously regulated, and its reproducibility was compared against eight physicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous force-controlled sweeping of an ultrasound transducer over gelled human skin. Therapeutic ultrasound requires the same motion and contact-force control but no image interpretation, on a limb positioned at the machine.

sources.title: Inside Use of Robots in Nursing Homes: From Monitoring and Cleaning to Therapy Bots - Skilled Nursing News
sources.claim: Robots in nursing homes today are task-specific (cleaning, food service, logistics); humanoid or semi-humanoid robots able to assist with direct patient interaction and repositioning are not yet in use, with dexterity remaining a major challenge.

tasks.label: Transport patients to and from treatment areas, using wheelchairs or providing standing support.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient PT clinic: aide brings a clinic transport wheelchair to the waiting room for a patient with limited walking tolerance who can stand, pivot and seat himself with at most standby assistance; wheels him 100-200 ft down the clinic corridor to a treatment table/mat area, parks and locks the chair, and later returns him to the lobby and stows the chair.

Outpatient PT clinic: aide escorts an unsteady patient on foot to and from the treatment area, providing hands-on standing support - helping the patient rise from the waiting-room chair, applying a gait belt or contact guard, steadying the patient over 50-150 ft, managing a walker or crutches, and reacting to knee buckling, dizziness or a stumble.

Acute-care hospital: aide goes to an inpatient's room, helps the patient from bed or bedside chair into a wheelchair with hands-on assistance, manages IV pole, oxygen tubing, telemetry leads, drains and gown, then transports the patient through corridors and an elevator to the therapy gym and back, checking tolerance en route.

Skilled nursing facility or inpatient rehab unit: aide collects residents from their rooms for scheduled therapy, providing sit-to-stand or pivot transfer assistance into a wheelchair, verbally cueing residents with cognitive impairment, and wheeling them down resident-hall corridors to the therapy gym and back afterward.

Hospital or SNF therapy gym: aide provides hands-on standing support to move a dependent patient a short distance within the treatment area - assisting a sit-to-stand from wheelchair, steadying the patient during a pivot or several steps to the mat table or parallel bars, and easing them back down.

Complex transport: bariatric patient, a patient requiring two-person assist or a mechanical lift, a post-op patient moved on a stretcher/gurney, or a confused/agitated patient who resists; aide works with a second staff member, secures equipment, and moves the patient to and from the treatment area.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Drive System (with Unifi Aviation)
sources.title: Unifi Aviation Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchairs are in commercial service at Detroit Metro and other major airports, autonomously carrying passengers with reduced mobility along pre-mapped routes through the concourse and returning empty to base; they are limited to passengers who can board themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting mobility-limited people seated in a wheelchair across an institutional indoor facility shared with pedestrians. Same payload (a seated human), same precision demands (doorways, corridors, docking at a destination) and longer distances than a clinic transport; the boundary condition - riders must board themselves - is stated explicitly.

sources.developer: WHILL Inc. / University of Tsukuba Hospital
sources.title: Safety and feasibility of in-hospital autonomous transportation using a driverless mobility for patients with musculoskeletal disorders
sources.claim: A prospective clinical study at University of Tsukuba Hospital transported 51 outpatients with gait disturbance 100 m from the orthopaedic ... in a WHILL driverless wheelchair that navigated autonomously and returned to base; no collisions or adverse events occurred.
sources.transferJustification: Nearly the same task: moving a gait-impaired patient by wheelchair between departments of a healthcare facility. Distance, patient population (musculoskeletal gait disturbance) and setting (outpatient department corridors) match the PT-aide instance directly.

sources.title: Autonomous Wheelchair Proof of Concept Pilot Report
sources.claim: Cyberworks Robotics ran a live autonomous wheelchair pilot at North York General Hospital in July 2025, moving patients between the Emergency Department's low-acuity zone and Medical Imaging; crowded corridors sometimes required the rider to take manual override.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inter-departmental patient transport by wheelchair inside a working acute hospital, i.e. the navigation half of the PT-aide transport instance, in the same corridors and crowd conditions.

sources.title: Intended Use - Andago - Hocoma
sources.claim: Hocoma's Andago V2.0 is a commercial mobile robot that provides dynamic body-weight support and actively follows a patient walking overground in a rehab clinic, but it is sold as a tool for a therapist to use: the clinician harnesses the patient, performs and supervises the training.
sources.transferJustification: Closest commercial analogue to 'providing standing support' while a patient walks: it holds body weight and prevents falls. It is cited to show the limit - harnessing and supervision remain clinician work, so the whole instance is not machine-completed.

sources.system: Hug T1 / L1 mobility support robot
sources.title: Mobility support robot | FUJI Corporation
sources.claim: Fuji's Hug is a commercially sold mobility-support robot used in Japanese nursing facilities to move care receivers up to 100 kg between bed, wheelchair and toilet; it is operated hands-on by a caregiver who positions and secures the person, and it assists rather than replaces the caregiver.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the sit-to-stand/pivot transfer that begins most wheelchair transports; cited to establish that the state of the art in deployed transfer robotics is a caregiver-operated assist device, not autonomous patient handling.

sources.title: New robotic system improves wheelchair transfers to bed - VA Research
sources.claim: VA Human Engineering Research Laboratory built and user-tested the Powered Personal Transfer System, a custom powered wheelchair and ... so a person moves between them without being lifted; it is a research prototype requiring purpose-built matched furniture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bed-to-wheelchair transfer, the step that precedes inpatient transport. Cited as the strongest purpose-built (E1-style, fixtured bed plus matched chair) approach, and to show it remains a prototype with unclear autonomy.

sources.title: How Sphaira plans to clear the roadblocks for its autonomous hospital transport tech
sources.claim: Sphaira's Moby P1 single-occupant patient pod is in clinical use at Charite Berlin's pediatric oncology unit, with an autonomous version only at the pilot stage at University Hospital Schleswig-Holstein and a development agreement with Mayo Clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: purpose-built pod for moving one patient through hospital corridors. Cited as context for the E1 counterfactual (patient loaded into a dedicated transport vehicle); autonomy is still at pilot stage, so it does not by itself support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Arrange treatment supplies to keep them in order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient PT clinic / hospital rehab gym reset between patients: collect dumbbells, cuff weights, medicine and therapy balls, wedges, bolsters, resistance bands and gait belts left on mats, tables and the floor, and return each to its labeled rack, hook or bin; straighten mats and equipment. Done repeatedly during clinic hours with patients, therapists and equipment moving through the space.

Linen upkeep: pull clean towels, pillowcases and sheets from a laundry cart or dryer, fold them to the clinic's standard, and stack them on shelves and carts in treatment rooms, the gym and the modality station; keep stacks squared and replenished as they are used; move soiled linen to hampers.

Restocking consumables into treatment-room drawers, cabinets and modality carts from a delivery carton: ultrasound gel bottles, electrode packs, kinesiology tape, gauze, gloves, alcohol wipes, paper table rolls; each item into its labeled bin/drawer, front-faced, older stock rotated forward, expired items pulled.

Hydrocollator / cold-pack station upkeep: lift wet, floppy hot packs out of the 160F water tank with tongs and re-hang them in the correct size slots, arrange terry covers and towels at the station, refill and stack cold packs in the freezer, wipe and re-order the counter.

Periodic reorganization of the supply closet/storeroom: pull mixed returned and overstocked supplies out, sort them into labeled bins and shelves, consolidate partial boxes, discard expired stock, and note what needs ordering.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi is a wheeled mobile manipulator deployed commercially in US hospitals that autonomously picks supplies out of supply closets ... delivers them to patient rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetch-and-deliver. It shows autonomous mobile manipulation of clinical supplies inside an E2 facility, but the deployed workflow is transport, not folding, re-racking or ordered placement of heterogeneous items on shelves.

sources.title: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force sensing to stow items - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot, with force/touch sensing, picks and stows individual items into fabric pod compartments at fulfillment-center stow stations, handling about 75% of warehouse items at speeds comparable to human ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stowing miscellaneous consumer goods into small labeled compartments. Comparable objects (bottles, boxes, poly-bagged soft goods) and comparable precision to placing clinic consumables into bins; work is brought to the fixed cell by AMR-carried pods, i.e., an E1 presentation.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Sparrow is a fulfillment-center robotic cell that detects, selects and handles individual products from Amazon's diverse inventory and places them into the correct container, covering roughly 65% of sortable inventory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level sortation into designated containers. Same core act as sorting mixed supplies into labeled bins, on comparably varied small goods, in a fenced cell where totes are conveyed to the arm.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cases from trailers and containers in DHL warehouses at rates up to 700 cases per ..., with DHL committing to a further 1,000 units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive vision-guided handling of heavy, rigid objects presented as a wall of cases. Shows worker-rate autonomous handling of heavy items, transferable to placing weights and heavy supplies when the items are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model
sources.claim: Dyna Robotics' DYNA-1 pair of stationary arms folded 800+ napkins over a continuous 24 hours with zero human ... at production-grade quality, and is being used in commercial settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: folding flat textiles at a fixed workstation. Same deformable-object skill and quality bar as folding clinic towels and pillowcases when the linen is presented at the station.

sources.system: Chicago Dryer Genesis ATM / Air Chicago folders and stackers
sources.title: Chicago Dryer Flatwork Finishing Equipment | Western State Design
sources.claim: Chicago Dryer's Genesis ATM (Automated Towel Machine) ... vision and deep learning to sort and fold towels hands-free on commercial laundry finishing lines, with companion stackers that stack folded small pieces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sorting, folding and stacking of terry towels and small linens. Identical objects and output standard to clinic linen folding and stacking, achieved in a purpose-built machine line (E1 presentation).

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: ORB, a Fetch-based autonomous mobile manipulator, restocked supply-room bins from a rolling cart with 96% success and retrieved items with 80% success in a simulated hospital supply room using ArUco-marked bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restocking medical supply shelves from a cart. Close to stocking clinic supply bins, but demonstrated only in a lab mock-up supply room with fiducial markers on bins and with boxes and bottles, so it evidences an engineered (E1-style) setting, not a working clinic.

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated store shelves with bottled and canned ..., up to about 1,000 units a day, deployed in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, with a remote operator intervening only on exceptions such as a dropped bottle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking inside a human retail facility. Transfer is limited: the arm is rail-mounted in one standardized cooler and handles uniform beverage containers, not heterogeneous clinic supplies in drawers and cabinets.

sources.title: Soft Robotics food-grade gripper boosts productivity and reduces waste - FoodBev Media
sources.claim: Soft Robotics mGrip modular soft grippers are deployed worldwide on food production lines, reliably picking irregular, delicate, wet products such as chicken, bread and produce at high speed in washdown environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of wet, floppy, irregular items on a production line. Comparable object properties to soggy hydrocollator packs and pack covers when they are presented to a fixed cell.

sources.title: TidyBot: Personalized Robot Assistance with Large Language Models (arXiv)
sources.claim: TidyBot, a research mobile manipulator, put away 85.0% of objects in ... household tidying scenarios, taking 15-20 seconds per object.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking up scattered objects and returning them to designated storage. Directly analogous to resetting a therapy gym, but 85% object-level success in staged lab rooms with light objects is below the reliability an employer would accept.

tasks.label: Assist patients to dress, undress, or put on and remove supportive devices, such as braces, splints, or slings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports PT clinic: aide helps an ambulatory patient prepare for treatment — removing a jacket, shoe and sock, rolling up a pant leg, or changing into shorts/a gown behind a curtain — then helps re-dress afterward, working around pain, guarding the patient's balance, and preserving modesty.

PT clinic: aide applies or removes a prescribed supportive device per the therapist's instruction — knee immobilizer or hinged knee brace, ankle stirrup brace, wrist/thumb splint, shoulder sling — positioning the limb, aligning the joint, threading and tensioning straps to correct snugness, and checking skin/fit before the patient leaves.

Hospital or skilled-nursing rehab unit: aide assists a post-surgical or post-stroke patient at bedside or in the gym to don/doff shirt, pants, socks, shoes and gown, working around a hemiparetic arm, IV lines, drains, and hip or spinal precautions, often while the patient is seated on the edge of the bed.

Patient with substantial impairment (spasticity, contracture, obesity, severe pain, or cognitive impairment): aide, often with a second staff member, rolls or supports the patient to get clothing on and off and to don a rigid orthosis such as a TLSO back brace or AFO with a shoe, adjusting for skin integrity and correct alignment.

Home-health or community-based PT visit: aide/tech helps a patient in the patient's own bedroom or bathroom dress, undress, and put on or remove a brace or sling, in a cluttered, non-standard space with the patient's own clothing and footwear.

sources.system: CMU Robotics Institute robot-assisted dressing system (Wang, Erickson, Held; RSS 2023)
sources.title: Carnegie Mellon University robot puts on shirts one sleeve at a time | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: CMU's reinforcement-learning robot-assisted dressing system autonomously pulls a garment sleeve onto a seated person's arm in a laboratory setting, but on average covers only 86% of the arm's length and addresses only the sleeve sub-step, not full dressing/undressing.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: robot-assisted garment dressing of a human arm. It is a sub-step of 'assist patients to dress/undress' and is performed on healthy seated volunteers in a robotics lab; partial sleeve coverage (86%) is well below the reliability a PT clinic would accept, and no brace, fastener, footwear or lower-body dressing is demonstrated.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing (robot arm, sim-to-real fine-tuned policy)
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions (arXiv:2509.12741)
sources.claim: A 2025 force-modulated visual dressing policy dresses long-sleeve garments onto moving human arms in a lab human study, still limited to one-arm sleeve dressing with roughly 85% arm-length coverage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot dressing a human arm with a sleeve. It shares the objects (garments) and contact with a person, but covers only the single-sleeve sub-step in a controlled lab with able-bodied participants; it does not demonstrate whole-garment donning/doffing, footwear, fasteners, or orthotic devices on patients.

sources.system: Baxter-based dressing pipeline (Zhang & Demiris, Science Robotics 2022)
sources.developer: Personal Robotics Laboratory, Imperial College London
sources.title: A robot that can put a surgical gown on a supine mannequin
sources.claim: The state-of-the-art hospital-gown dressing pipeline works on a mannequin lying supine in a mock hospital room and only partially dresses it, succeeding about 90% of trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic gown dressing of a supine body. Even in a purpose-built mock room with a rigid, motionless mannequin the result is partial dressing at ~90% success, so it does not substantiate completing dressing/undressing of a live, impaired patient at worker quality.

sources.system: Franka Emika Panda dressing controller (University of Sheffield)
sources.developer: University of Sheffield Human-Robot Interaction Laboratory
sources.title: Hybrid Control Strategies for Safe and Adaptive Robot-Assisted Dressing (arXiv:2505.07710)
sources.claim: Hybrid-control robot-assisted dressing research as of 2025 remains at the level of a single compliant arm tested with a small number of healthy volunteers inside a university human-robot interaction laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: safe physical human-robot contact during dressing. It shows the field's current ceiling — lab experiments with two healthy participants — which is far from a clinic aide dressing patients, and no cited system handles braces, splints or slings.

tasks.label: Maintain equipment or furniture to keep it in good working condition, including performing the assembly or disassembly of equipment or accessories.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient PT clinic: routine daily/between-patient upkeep of standard equipment and furniture — checking treatment tables, plinths, bikes and treadmills for condition, tightening loose knobs/bolts, replacing table paper rolls, plugging in/charging modality units, refilling ultrasound gel, replacing worn straps and batteries.

Clinic: an item is malfunctioning (treadmill belt slipping or off-track, frayed cable on a pulley machine, e-stim unit not outputting, torn upholstery, wobbly stair unit). Aide diagnoses the fault, performs the minor repair or part swap, or tags it out and arranges service.

Clinic: assembly/disassembly of equipment and accessories — uncrating and bolting together a new exercise unit or mat table per instructions, swapping cable handles/attachments and weight pins on pulley systems, mounting arm-ergometer or bike accessories, attaching resistance bands/pulleys to walls, breaking equipment down for storage.

Clinic gym: moving and reconfiguring furniture and equipment — wheeling plinths and machines, stacking and stowing exercise mats and bolsters, arranging chairs, steps and parallel bars, hauling equipment to and from a storage room between sessions.

Clinic: upkeep of modality units and soft goods — refilling and de-scaling the hydrocollator, cleaning and topping up the paraffin bath, draining/sanitizing whirlpool tanks, laundering and replacing linens, pillowcases and bolster covers.

Off-site / bedside (home-health or mobile PT support, or a patient's room in a facility): assembling and adjusting patient equipment — sizing a walker or crutches, fitting accessories to a home exercise device, breaking down and transporting portable treatment tables.

sources.title: BMW Group bringing Physical AI to Europe — pilot project at BMW Group Plant Leipzig; first humanoid deployment completed at Spartanburg
sources.claim: Figure 02 humanoid worked ten-hour production shifts at BMW Spartanburg for ten months, autonomously removing and precisely positioning sheet-metal parts in the body shop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise part removal and positioning in a fixtured production cell. Transfers to fitting and bolting equipment parts presented in a purpose-built cell — comparable rigid parts, sub-centimetre placement precision, sustained production-grade reliability.

sources.system: NTU IKEA chair-assembly robot (two Denso VS-060 arms, Ensenso 3D camera, ATI force sensors)
sources.title: Dual-armed robot with 3D vision assembles IKEA chair
sources.claim: A dual-arm robot with 3D vision and force sensing autonomously assembled a flat-pack IKEA chair from its loose parts in a laboratory cell.
sources.transferJustification: Directly analogous: assembling flat-pack furniture from loose parts (pin insertion, alignment, fastening) in a fixtured cell — the same class of work as assembling a PT mat table or exercise unit from a kit.

sources.system: ASG AX-10 assembly cell (Cartesian robotic screwdriving)
sources.developer: ASG, a Division of Jergens Inc.
sources.title: Robotic Cell Automates Screwdriving Process | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Commercially sold purpose-built assembly cells automatically drive and torque screws on parts presented in the cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fastening of parts in a fixtured cell. Assembly, disassembly and re-tightening of PT equipment accessories is dominated by threaded fasteners and knobs of similar size and torque class.

sources.title: AI-Driven Robots Have Started Changing Tires In The U.S. In Half The Time As Humans
sources.claim: RoboTire robotic tire-changing systems in US tire shops use vision to locate and remove lug nuts and remount wheels of varying size and bolt pattern, with the vehicle brought onto a dedicated platform.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine mechanical service — unbolting and re-bolting a component on a unit brought to a purpose-built bay, with unit-to-unit variation handled by vision. Same fastener sizes, torque control and tolerance class as swapping PT equipment accessories or re-torquing loose hardware.

sources.title: From Manual to Robots: RoboTire's Impact on the Tire Shop Floor
sources.claim: RoboTire's arms use onboard cameras to find the wheel and lug nuts and then remove them, indicating vision-driven autonomy rather than step-by-step human control.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the fastener disassembly/reassembly work cited above is machine-perceived and machine-executed, not teleoperated.

sources.title: DHL buying 1,000+ Stretch robots from Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Stretch is deployed commercially by DHL to unload and handle heavy cases in warehouses at rates up to 700 cases per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive lifting, moving and stacking of heavy, variably-placed items by a manipulator at a fixed station. Transfers to stowing and stacking mats, bolsters and accessories when the items are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare, Diligent Robotics to bring last-mile delivery to hospitals
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously performs supply and pharmacy deliveries in more than 25 US ..., with over a million deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Marks the ceiling of deployed mobile manipulation inside clinical facilities: transport and simple fetch/place of supplies, not maintenance, repair, or assembly of equipment — supporting the negative E2 judgments.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics Robot Dog Spot Inspects for Safety Hazards
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous routine maintenance-inspection and safety rounds inside processing plants, capturing thermal, acoustic and gauge data; its arm in autonomous missions is limited to actions such as opening doors.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed system for mobile equipment upkeep inside a facility: it inspects and reports on equipment condition but does not perform the adjustment, repair or assembly steps the aide's task requires.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's NEO humanoid
sources.claim: 1X's NEO humanoid, the leading home-setting humanoid, still relies on remote human operators, and no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore end-to-end.

tasks.label: Record treatment given and equipment used.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Measure patient's range-of-joint motion, body parts, or vital signs to determine effects of treatments or for patient evaluations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic/sports PT clinic: aide takes vital signs (BP with cuff and stethoscope or automated monitor, pulse, SpO2, sometimes respiratory rate) on an ambulatory, cooperative patient seated in the gym or at a treatment table, before and after an exercise bout, and records values in the chart for the supervising PT.

Hospital, inpatient rehab unit, or skilled nursing facility: aide takes vitals on a partially dependent patient at the bedside or in a wheelchair (supine or semi-reclined, gown/lines/hemiplegic arm, cuff must be sized and placed on the correct arm) before, during, and after ambulation or transfers, and reports abnormal readings.

Goniometric range-of-motion measurement in a clinic: aide palpates bony landmarks, passively or actively moves the knee, shoulder, elbow, hip, or ankle to end range, aligns the goniometer axis/arms, reads degrees, and records flexion/extension values for a re-evaluation or progress note.

Anthropometric 'body part' measurements: tape-measure limb girth at marked landmarks (e.g., 10 cm above patella) to track edema or atrophy, leg-length and limb-circumference comparisons, plus height and weight, recorded on a flow sheet.

Measurements taken outside a controlled facility — a home-health or community/school visit where the patient sits on their own sofa, bed, or wheelchair, layout and lighting vary site to site, and the aide brings a cuff, pulse oximeter, goniometer, and tape measure.

sources.title: Robot-Assisted Arm Assessments in Spinal Cord Injured Patients: A Consideration of Concept Study
sources.claim: The ARMin exoskeleton robot performs standardized arm assessments on spinal-cord-injured patients whose arm is strapped into the device, extracting active and passive range of ... at joint level along with torque and stiffness — the same output an aide records with a goniometer.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (joint ROM measurement); the robot substitutes for the therapist's goniometry once the limb is fixtured in the device.

sources.system: Automated robot-assisted wrist ROM assessment platform (admittance-controlled wrist robot)
sources.developer: Zhang, McDaid, Xie et al. (SUSTech / University of Auckland / University of Leeds)
sources.title: Automated robot-assisted assessment for wrist active ranges of motion - PubMed
sources.claim: A rehabilitation robot with a reconfigurable handle automatically measured wrist active range of motion in flexion/extension and radial/ulnar deviation on 11 human subjects with reliability comparable to clinical goniometry (ICC >= 0.89, SEM <= 2.36 degrees).
sources.transferJustification: Same task (measuring a patient's joint ROM) at the wrist; driving a joint toward end range under admittance/force control and recording the angle is the same operation performed at knee, elbow, hip, or shoulder by fixtured rehabilitation robots such as ARMin and Lokomat.

sources.system: Automated robot-assisted wrist passive ROM assessment platform
sources.developer: Zhang, Zhang, McDaid, Davies, Xie (University of Auckland)
sources.title: Automated objective robot-assisted assessment of wrist passive ranges of motion - PubMed
sources.claim: The same group demonstrated automated robot-assisted measurement of wrist PASSIVE range of motion — the robot moves the fixtured wrist and determines end range objectively — with ICC > 0.857 and SEM < 3.38 degrees.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (passive ROM measurement, which is what an aide performs with a goniometer), demonstrated at the wrist; transfers to larger joints served by equivalent fixtured rehabilitation robots.

sources.system: Lokomat (LokomatPro) with L-ROM / L-STIFF assessment tools
sources.title: Software - Hocoma (Lokomat)
sources.claim: The commercially deployed Lokomat gait-training robot includes a built-in L-ROM assessment that reports range of motion of hip and knee flexion/extension for patients strapped into the exoskeleton, used routinely to monitor progress in rehabilitation clinics.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (joint ROM measurement) for hip and knee in a commercial clinical device; cited as supporting context only because published descriptions leave unclear whether the drives or the therapist move the limb during L-ROM.

sources.developer: Alexandra Hospital / National University Health System, Singapore
sources.title: An Assessment of an Inpatient Robotic Nurse Assistant: A Mixed-Method Study (Journal of Medical Systems)
sources.claim: Florence, a humanoid robotic nurse assistant, autonomously navigated a general medicine ward at Alexandra Hospital (Singapore), located and identified patients by face recognition, and measured their vital signs (SpO2, blood pressure, body temperature) via an extending platform holding a CNOGA sensor.

sources.system: A&D TM-2657P waiting-room / kiosk automatic blood pressure monitor
sources.title: TM-2657P BIHS Approved Kiosk & Waiting Room Automatic Blood Pressure Monitor
sources.claim: Free-standing automatic blood-pressure kiosks with motorized cuffs that inflate around an inserted arm are commercially deployed in ordinary clinic waiting rooms, GP surgeries and pharmacies, producing clinically used BP and pulse readings without staff involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (measuring a patient's blood pressure and pulse); the machine's cuff mechanically acts on the patient's arm and outputs the reading the aide would chart, though the patient positions their own arm.

sources.system: Semi-autonomous vital-sign sensing robot (Intel D435i + PPG end-effector)
sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot - TechRxiv
sources.claim: A sensing robot arm using a depth camera and a YOLOv5-derived detector autonomously locates the measurement site on a seated subject's forearm and acquires PPG signals, yielding heart rate, SpO2, respiratory rate and correlated blood pressure in under 30 seconds.

sources.system: Mobile robotic platform for contactless vital sign monitoring
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring - PMC
sources.claim: A mobile robotic platform carrying robot-controlled infrared and multi-monochrome cameras automatically tracks people and measures skin temperature, heart rate and respiratory rate for screening, demonstrating autonomous contactless vital-sign acquisition from a moving robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (contactless vital-sign screening) covering temperature, HR and RR but not cuff blood pressure; cited only to corroborate that a mobile robot can autonomously acquire vital signs from people in a facility.

tasks.label: Train patients to use orthopedic braces, prostheses, or supportive devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic PT clinic: post-op knee or ankle patient is issued crutches or a rolling walker. Aide sizes and adjusts the device to the patient's body, physically demonstrates the gait pattern and weight-bearing restriction, applies a gait belt and guards the patient hands-on while they practice on level floor and a practice stair set, correcting hand and foot placement by touch and cue until safe.

Acute hospital bedside/hallway: aide helps a patient don and doff a prescribed brace (knee immobilizer, TLSO, sling, CAM boot) over a hospital gown, checks strap tension and skin, teaches log-roll and sit-to-stand with the brace on, then guards ambulation with a front-wheeled walker down the corridor with lines, drains and IV pole present.

Skilled nursing facility or subacute rehab gym: elderly patient with a new AFO, hip precautions, or a new walker practices repeatedly. Aide dons the AFO with shoe, adjusts walker height, provides physical cueing and contact guard for a cognitively impaired or deconditioned patient, and reinforces the therapist's instructions over multiple short sessions.

Inpatient/outpatient prosthetic gait training: lower-limb amputee is taught to don liner, socket and suspension, inspect residual limb, and progress from parallel bars to walker/cane. Aide sets up parallel bars and mirror, assists donning, guards weight shifting and initial steps, and reports fit or skin problems to the therapist.

Home health visit: aide (under therapist supervision) trains a patient in their own house to use a walker, cane or brace within their actual furniture layout, thresholds, rugs and bathroom, including transfers to bed/toilet and negotiating porch steps, with family members and pets present.

sources.developer: TU Ilmenau and MetraLabs Robotics GmbH
sources.title: ROREAS: robot coach for walking and orientation training in clinical post-stroke rehabilitation—prototype implementation and evaluation in field trials
sources.claim: ROREAS is a socially assistive mobile robot coach that autonomously accompanies stroke patients during walking and orientation self-training in a rehabilitation clinic; it navigates and motivates but provides no physical support, device fitting, or hands-on guarding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: accompanying/coaching patients during mobility practice in a rehab clinic. It is the closest deployed-adjacent robot to 'training patients to use supportive devices', but it performs no device fitting, no manual correction, and no physical guarding, so capability does not transfer to the hands-on parts of this task.

sources.title: Andago® - Hocoma
sources.claim: Andago V2.0 is a commercially sold mobile body-weight-support robot used in rehab clinics, but it is explicitly a tool that therapists operate: the clinician still harnesses the patient, directs the training, and delivers the instruction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fall-protected overground gait training in a clinic. It substitutes for the physical body-weight support a therapist gives, but the robot does not fit braces or devices, does not instruct the patient, and requires a clinician to set up and run the session, so it cannot complete this task.

sources.system: Dual-arm dressing-assistance robot with semantic visual attention (Waseda University)
sources.developer: Waseda University (Tsukakoshi, Miyake, Ogata, Sugano et al.)
sources.title: Close-Fitting Dressing Assistance Based on State Estimation of Feet and Garments with Semantic-based Visual Attention
sources.claim: State of the art for a robot physically putting a close-fitting item onto a person's body (a sock onto a foot) is a laboratory manipulator study with limited generalization, not a clinical-grade capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot placing a garment onto a human limb, comparable in object type and skin-contact force control to donning an AFO, brace sleeve or prosthetic liner. Performance does not carry over: results are lab-bench, single-item, and do not reach clinical reliability or include patient instruction.

sources.system: Social robot physiotherapy instructor (Pepper-class social robot, RL instruction policy)
sources.title: Policy Learning for Social Robot-Led Physiotherapy
sources.claim: Robot-led physiotherapy instruction remains at the research stage: social robots demonstrate and count standardized upper-limb exercises using learned policies, with no physical contact with the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot instructing a patient through therapy movements. It covers only the verbal/demonstration portion of training and involves no device fitting, adjustment, or physical guarding, so it cannot complete this task.

tasks.label: Administer traction to relieve neck or back pain, using intermittent or static traction equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient orthopedic PT clinic, lumbar mechanical traction: aide explains the procedure, positions the patient supine on a split traction table with knee bolsters, fits and snugs thoracic and pelvic harnesses over clothing, attaches the tether to the traction unit, enters the PT-prescribed force/hold/rest/duration, hands the patient the interrupt switch, monitors for 10-20 minutes, then releases tension and removes the harness.

Outpatient PT clinic, cervical traction: patient supine or seated, aide fits a head halter or seats the patient's head in a Saunders-type cervical device, sets the pull angle and low force per the PT's order, starts the intermittent or static cycle, watches for dizziness, jaw discomfort or symptom peripheralization, then terminates and removes the halter.

Spine-specialty, chiropractic or decompression clinic: aide sets the patient up on a computerized decompression table (DRX9000, Kinetrac, Triton DTS type), applies pelvic and thoracic harnesses, selects the stored protocol and angle, runs the programmed distraction/relaxation cycles, and logs the session.

Hospital inpatient, SNF or rehab unit: traction for a frail or post-acute patient - transfer and position the patient (lines, drains, weight-bearing or spinal precautions), adjust harness placement on a deconditioned or cognitively impaired body, monitor tolerance, vitals and distress continuously throughout the pull, and stop early if the patient reacts poorly.

Patient's home or home-program setup: aide sets up or instructs the patient in a portable over-the-door cervical unit or pneumatic lumbar traction belt, adapting to the door frame, chair and furniture on hand, checking fit and safe force, and confirming the patient can apply it alone.

sources.system: Chattanooga Triton / Triton DTS traction unit
sources.title: Triton Traction Unit User Manual (Enovis/Chattanooga)
sources.claim: Commercial clinical traction units (Chattanooga Triton) deliver static, intermittent and cyclic traction under digital machine control, executing stored, patient-specific protocols with defined hold, rest and treatment times once the patient is harnessed into the device.

sources.title: Triton DTS Traction Unit | Chattanooga
sources.claim: The machine's programmed pull patterns are used as a substitute for clinician hand-delivered traction force, with independent control of pretension, progression, traction and regression phases.

sources.system: KINETRAC KNX-9900 lordotic-curve-controlled traction (KNX-7000 lumbar variant)
sources.developer: Hanmed Co., Gimhae, Republic of Korea
sources.title: The Functional and Morphological Changes of the Cervical Intervertebral Disc after Applying Lordotic Curve Controlled Traction: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Study (IJERPH)
sources.claim: A commercial computerized traction system automatically tracks and elevates the C4-6 segment to control the lordotic curve while applying cervical traction to outpatients, in a double-blind randomized clinical trial.

sources.title: Aescape raises $83M to bring robotic massager to more locations - The Robot Report
sources.claim: A fully autonomous robot delivers force-controlled bodywork to a person lying on a table in institution-controlled facilities (gyms, hotel spas), but the client positions and prepares themselves; the robot fits no straps or harnesses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous contact therapy applied to a human body on a treatment table inside a structured facility. It shows machine-delivered physical treatment is feasible once the person is in position, but involves no harness or strap application, so it cannot substantiate the patient-setup portion of administering traction.

sources.title: US patent: Flexible robotic limbs including rolling contact joints
sources.claim: Attaching straps to a person remains a manual step that blocks fully autonomous robotic handling of human bodies; the only robots demonstrated lifting a person's full weight still require humans to attach the straps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: strapping or slinging a person for handling. Fitting a traction harness is the same class of action (fastening tensioned straps around a human torso and pelvis), and this source states it is not yet autonomous.

sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robot-assisted dressing - the closest published capability to fitting a garment or harness onto a person's body - is validated on a medical training manikin, not on patients in clinical service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: manipulating a deformable garment onto a human body, the same manipulation problem as fitting a traction harness or head halter; performance is only manikin-level, so it does not carry over to worker-quality harnessing of patients.

tasks.label: Fit patients for orthopedic braces, prostheses, or supportive devices, adjusting fit as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient PT/orthopedic clinic: aide fits a hinged or soft knee brace, ankle brace, or walking boot on a seated patient — selects size from stock, positions the device over the joint, threads and tensions straps in order, checks for pinching/skin pressure, then re-adjusts after the patient stands and takes a few steps.

Clinic or hospital outpatient room: aide fits a shoulder sling, wrist/thumb splint, cervical collar, or lumbar corset — positioning the soft device on the trunk or limb of a patient who may be in pain or guarding, fastening hook-and-loop closures, and re-adjusting to patient-reported comfort while instructing on wear.

Clinic/hospital: aide sizes and adjusts supportive mobility devices — axillary crutches, walker, or cane — to the patient's height by depressing spring buttons and re-pinning telescoping tubes, then checks fit with the patient standing (elbow flexion, axillary clearance) and re-adjusts.

Inpatient rehab unit or SNF bedside: aide assists a patient in donning an ankle-foot orthosis or a lower-limb prosthesis — aligning the AFO in the shoe, or rolling on the liner, seating the residual limb in the socket, adding/removing sock ply, checking alignment and skin condition, and re-adjusting straps.

Home health visit: aide fits or re-adjusts a brace or supportive device in the patient's own home — variable furniture and lighting, patient seated on a sofa or bed, no standard equipment on hand, improvising padding or strap trimming.

Clinic re-check: patient returns wearing a previously issued brace complaining of slippage or rubbing; aide inspects the fit, repositions pads, trims or re-routes straps, changes hinge stop settings, and re-verifies fit through movement, under PT supervision.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing (CMU/Held lab, robot arm dressing system)
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robot-assisted dressing: an autonomous learned policy pulls long-sleeve garments onto the arms of human participants in a laboratory human study; this is the closest robotic capability to placing a wearable device on a live person, and it stops at loose garments on an arm, with no strap tensioning, joint alignment, or fit verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robot-assisted dressing (placing a wearable item on a person's limb). It is the nearest analogue to brace/orthosis fitting, but it is a laboratory human study with two known garments and a single arm; it does not demonstrate selecting/sizing a rigid orthosis, aligning it to a joint axis, sequencing and tensioning straps to a target pressure, or verifying and re-adjusting fit, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.title: AI robots that cost over P3-M may hold key to nursing Japan's ageing population
sources.claim: The most advanced physical-caregiving humanoid demonstrated on tasks such as rolling a person and putting on socks remains a laboratory prototype, not usable in care facilities for years.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = physical caregiving contact with a patient's body (repositioning, sock donning), the human-contact component of brace fitting. The source itself states the platform is a prototype not ready for care facilities, so it cannot substantiate worker-quality completion of fitting tasks.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: A commercially deployed robot does make sustained autonomous physical contact with human bodies inside structured facilities (spa/gym/hotel locations), but only as massage strokes delivered to a person lying on a proprietary table; it manipulates no devices, garments, or straps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous robot contact with a patient's body in a human work facility. It shows safe body contact is commercially feasible, but the end effector applies pressure to a prone body on a fixed table; it performs no grasping, no deformable-strap manipulation, and no device fitting, so capability does not carry over.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics CEO discusses road to 1M hospital deliveries, future Moxi destinations
sources.claim: Robots deployed at scale in US hospitals are confined to non-patient-facing logistics; their dexterous repertoire is limited to items like elevator buttons and doors, not patient-contact device fitting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = mobile manipulation inside clinical facilities (E2). Establishes what is actually deployed in hospitals today — supply fetch-and-deliver — and shows no deployed clinical robot performs manipulation on or around a patient's body, so it cannot substantiate brace fitting.

tasks.label: Participate in patient care tasks, such as assisting with passing food trays, feeding residents, or bathing residents on bed rest.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Skilled-nursing / rehab unit meal service at the bedside: aide takes trays off the delivery cart, matches name and diet card to the resident, carries the tray into the room, raises the head of bed and clears/positions the overbed table, sets the tray down, removes covers, opens cartons and condiments, cuts food, then returns later to collect the tray and note intake.

Dining-room meal service in a nursing home or assisted-living community: aide helps move plated meals/trays from the kitchen cart to residents seated at tables, places each meal and drink in front of the correct resident, adds adaptive utensils/clothing protectors, refills beverages, and clears dishes afterward.

Feeding a resident who is alert and can communicate but cannot self-feed (stroke, quadriplegia, severe arthritis, post-op): aide sits with the resident at bedside or table, spoon-feeds a full meal at the resident's pace in the order the resident asks for, offers sips of liquid, wipes the mouth, and cleans up.

Feeding/assisting a resident with dementia, agitation, or dysphagia precautions: aide positions the resident upright, gives verbal cues and hand-over-hand help, alternates bites and sips, watches for coughing/pocketing and stops if the resident is unsafe, coaxes intake, and reports poor intake to nursing.

Bed bath and related hygiene for a resident on bed rest: basin and washcloths, washing face, torso, arms, legs, back and perineum, log-rolling or turning the resident with staff, applying lotion, changing gown and bed linens, and repositioning the resident afterward.

Home-health or small residential-care setting: aide assists a client at home with a meal — setting the food up within reach and feeding a client who cannot self-feed, offering drinks, and cleaning up in a room laid out as the household keeps it.

sources.system: Cornell EmPRISE robot-assisted feeding system (Feel the Bite / ADA)
sources.title: Robotic system feeds people with severe mobility limitations | Cornell Chronicle
sources.claim: Cornell's autonomous robot-assisted feeding system (EmPRISE 'Feel the Bite' / ADA) performed inside-mouth bite transfer for 13 care recipients with severe ..., in a lab, a New York City medical center, and a care recipient's home.

sources.system: ADA robot-assisted feeding system (Kinova arm + user interface)
sources.developer: University of Washington / Cornell Personal Robotics & EmPRISE labs
sources.title: Lessons Learned from Designing and Evaluating a Robot-Assisted Feeding System for Out-of-Lab Use (HRI 2025)
sources.claim: The ADA feeding system was used out-of-lab by five users with motor impairments plus a community researcher to feed themselves meals of ... institutional settings (cafeteria, office, conference room), with autonomous food detection, bite acquisition and transfer under user direction.

sources.developer: University of Washington / Cornell Personal Robotics & EmPRISE labs
sources.title: Lessons Learned from Designing and Evaluating a Robot-Assisted Feeding System for Out-of-Lab Use (HRI 2025)
sources.claim: The same ADA feeding system was deployed in a care recipient's own home for five consecutive days, ... varied spatial, social and activity contexts (in a wheelchair, in bed, while watching TV).

sources.title: FEAST: A Flexible Mealtime-Assistance System Towards In-the-Wild Personalization
sources.claim: FEAST, a mealtime-assistance robot with autonomous bite acquisition/transfer plus drinking and mouth-wiping tools, fed complete meals to two care recipients in their own homes across diverse scenarios.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: RABBIT autonomously performs the wash/rinse/dry phases of a bed bath on an exposed limb in a lab, evaluated with 12 participants; whole-body bathing (moving around the bed, manipulating limbs, reaching hidden areas) remains future work.

sources.title: Franciscan Health Installs 6 Aethon Robots for Food Service and Environmental Logistics
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots are deployed in US hospitals to haul carts of meal trays, linens and supplies from the kitchen to inpatient floors; nursing/food-service staff still take individual trays to patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk meal-tray transport inside a hospital. It covers the corridor-navigation half of tray passing in an institution-controlled facility, but the robot does not hand a tray to a patient or set the meal up at the bedside.

sources.title: Elevating Senior Living Dining with Foodservice Robots: Innovative Senior Care Solutions
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi food-running robots are commercially deployed in senior-living dining rooms, autonomously carrying plated meals from the kitchen to the dining room and bussing dishware, working alongside human servers who place and clear the food.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running plated meals to residents' tables in a senior-living dining room. Same objects and destination as passing trays, but the human server still lifts each plate onto the table, so the hand-off step is not automated.

sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $20.6 million to continue building AI robot arms | CNBC
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' autonomous robotic arms work on meal-assembly lines at food manufacturers, scooping ingredients and portioning them into meal trays; the fleet has produced tens of millions of servings in commercial production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling food and meal trays at fixed, fixtured positions on a purpose-built line. It substantiates that, when trays and destinations are presented at known poses, robots move food and trays reliably at production quality — the E1 form of passing trays.

sources.title: Digit's Next Steps | Agility Robotics
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid has run full-time commercially at GXO's Flowery Branch facility, autonomously unloading totes from mobile robots at its station and placing them on a conveyor, surpassing 100,000 totes moved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated pick-and-place of flat carried containers between a delivery cart/AMR and a fixed surface — the same motion class as taking a tray off a meal cart and setting it on a known surface, demonstrated at commercial reliability in a machine-structured station.

sources.system: AIREC (AI-driven Robot for Embrace and Care)
sources.title: Japan tests AIREC robot to roll patients, easing elderly care challenges
sources.claim: Waseda University's AIREC humanoid was shown in a Tokyo laboratory rolling a person onto their side, a maneuver used for diaper changes and pressure-sore prevention; researchers describe practical caregiving use as years away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: turning/repositioning a person in bed, a required sub-step of bed bathing. Shown only as a laboratory demonstration with unclear autonomy, so it cannot support completion of bathing care.

roles.title: Massage Therapists
roles.description: Perform therapeutic massages of soft tissues and joints. May assist in the assessment of range of motion and muscle strength, or propose client therapy plans.

tasks.label: Massage and knead muscles and soft tissues of the body to provide treatment for medical conditions, injuries, or wellness maintenance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-body Swedish/relaxation massage in a day spa, resort spa, or franchised massage clinic: 60-90 min, client undressed under draping on a table, oil or lotion, prone and supine positions, therapist works back, posterior and anterior legs, feet, arms, hands, shoulders, neck and scalp, adjusting to verbal feedback.

Targeted posterior-body wellness/recovery massage in a gym spa, hotel spa, recovery studio, or franchise clinic: 15-60 min, client prone the whole session, clothed or draped, work confined to shoulders, upper/mid/lower back, glutes, hamstrings and calves at a client-chosen pressure.

Deep-tissue/clinical therapeutic massage for a specific injury or medical condition (nonspecific low back pain, whiplash, rotator cuff strain, sciatica) in a chiropractic office, PT clinic, or medical massage practice: palpation to locate restrictions and trigger points, cross-fiber friction and sustained pressure on back, neck and limbs, session adapted continuously to tissue response, with charting.

Sports/event massage in a team training room, athletic facility, or event tent: pre- and post-event soft-tissue work on quads, hamstrings, calves, IT band, shoulders and arms, combined with assisted stretching and passive range-of-motion work on hips, knees and shoulders.

Mobile/outcall massage: therapist travels to a client's home, hotel guest room, or office, carries in and sets up a portable table in whatever space is available, and delivers a 60-90 min full-body oiled, draped massage, then packs out.

Seated chair massage, fully clothed, 10-20 min, at a corporate office, conference, health fair, or airport: compression, kneading and percussion through clothing on neck, shoulders, upper back, arms and hands with the client in a face-cradle massage chair.

sources.title: I Tried Aescape, the High-Tech Robot Massage-Here's My Review (Parade)
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage table is deployed at roughly 100 US gyms, hotels and spas, but its coverage is limited to the posterior body - it does not work the hands, arms, feet, neck ....

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Massage Envy franchised locations began selling Aescape robotic massage as a self-guided service in 30- or 60-minute sessions with the client clothed and the system adapting to body contours and pressure preference.

sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | Spa Business
sources.claim: Aescape states its system runs without a staff member present in the room at partner spa/gym/hotel locations, with only a call button for exceptions; sessions run 15-60 minutes and focus on upper, middle and lower back, glutes and hamstrings.

sources.title: Product focus - AI and robot massage | Spa Business
sources.claim: Capsix's iYU robot (Kuka LBR Med arm with a patented articulated hand) is sold commercially to spas, gyms and hotels and has a fully autonomous mode in which the user manages the whole session; it massages directly on skin, with or without oil.

instances.label: Between-client turnover in a day-spa / massage-clinic treatment room (~10 min between appointments): strip oil-soiled fitted sheet, top sheet, face-cradle cover and towels into a hamper; remake the narrow table with fresh linens and re-dress the bolster; spray and wipe the table, face cradle and stool with disinfectant; refill the lotion/oil bottle from a bulk jug; empty trash and reset the room.

End-of-shift deep clean of the massage area: wipe counters and cabinetry, drain and sanitize the hot-stone warmer and hot-towel cabi, wash and disinfect reusable tools/stones, damp-mop the floor, haul soiled linens to the washer and start a load, take out trash, and top up the room's consumables.

A sanitizing-only pass in a spa or clinic room where linens are handled by an aide or disposables are used: wipe and disinfect the table surface, face cradle, bolsters, arm rests and high-touch surfaces (door handle, lotion bottle, light switch) with hospital-grade disinfectant between clients or on a scheduled infection-control round.

Restocking run: check what is low, fetch clean sheets, towels, face-cradle covers, lotion/oil, gloves and disposables from the central stockroom or linen closet, transport them to one or more treatment rooms, and place them on the room's shelves and in the supply cabinet.

Mobile / in-home or on-site therapist: after a session in a client's home or office, disinfect and dry the portable table, face cradle and bolsters, fold and pack the table and kit into a carry case, bag soiled linens, and later launder linens and restock the kit at home.

instances.label: Routine spa/wellness session: therapist briefly interviews the client, observes posture, then palpates the back, neck and shoulders on the table, judging tissue texture, tone, temperature, tender points and adhesions, screening for red flags (bruising, inflammation, lumps), and adjusting technique and pressure accordingly. Spa treatment room, standard table, dim lighting.

Clinical/medical massage intake in a chiropractic, PT or integrative-medicine office: posture and gait observation, active and passive ROM testing of the involved joints (visual or goniometer), resisted/manual muscle testing, orthopedic screening tests, region palpation, contraindication screening, and written findings that feed a documented treatment plan.

In-home / mobile massage: therapist sets up a portable table in a client's living room or bedroom, takes the history, palpates the complaint region and checks gross joint mobility (e.g., shoulder circumduction, cervical rotation) before and during the session. Variable furniture, lighting, pets, no institutional control.

Sports/orthopedic massage at a team training room or event massage area: pre-event palpation of muscle tone and tenderness, quick joint ROM and flexibility screening, post-event check for strains, cramping or swelling, and a decision to treat, modify, or refer to medical staff.

Mid- and post-session reassessment: re-palpating the tissue that was worked to judge change in tone and restriction, retesting the client's range of motion and comfort against the baseline, eliciting client feedback, and recording the change to adjust the plan for the next session.

Assisting an instrumented ROM/strength measurement in a clinic: a single joint (e.g., elbow, shoulder, wrist) is positioned and measured for active and passive range of ... and force output for documentation, with the limb supported/strapped in a measurement device rather than assessed free-hand.

instances.label: Machine/implement-delivered thermal adjunct inside a spa or clinic treatment room: heated stones or heated probes glided over the oiled back and shoulders, warmed massage tools, an infrared/heat lamp or heated table used to warm a region before deeper work. Client lies draped on the therapist's table; room, linens and equipment are the employer's.

Consumable- and linen-based adjuncts in the clinic/spa: pulling a hydrocollator moist-heat pack, wrapping it in towels and placing it on the low back, hot-towel wipe-downs, paraffin dips for hands/feet, ice packs, plus applying and removing cupping sets or kinesiology tape and spa scrub/wrap rituals. Requires fetching, draping, positioning, monitoring and removing implements on a partially undressed client.

Assisted stretching added to or sold alongside the massage: PNF/static stretching of hamstrings, hips and shoulders, passive range-of-motion and gentle joint mobilization with the client supine or prone on the table, therapist controlling end range by feel and client feedback.

Mechanical device modalities: percussion/vibration therapy gun over tight muscle groups, mechanical vibrocompression or lymphatic-drainage tool work, compression therapy, instrument-glide soft-tissue work over a broad body region in the clinic or sports-recovery studio.
Topical/aromatherapy adjunct: selecting and blending an essential-oil or analgesic/CBD preparation and spreading it over the client's back, limbs or feet during the session in the spa or clinic room.

Adjuncts delivered in an unstructured setting: mobile/in-home massage in a client's living room or bedroom, or an on-site corporate chair-massage event, where the therapist adds hot towels, topical liniment and assisted stretching in a space and layout the therapist does not control.

instances.label: Day spa / massage franchise, 60–90 min full-body Swedish or deep-tissue session: therapist selects a standard massage oil or lotion, warms and dispenses it into the hands, and applies it region by region — back and posterior legs while the client is prone, then arms, hands, anterior legs, feet, neck and décolleté after the client turns supine — reapplying under draping as the session proceeds.

Focused-region session (30–45 min) at a spa, franchise or wellness center: client stays prone; therapist applies a ready-made oil or lotion only to the back, shoulders and glutes/posterior legs and works that area.

Clinical/medical massage in a chiropractic, PT or wellness clinic: therapist warms unscented lotion or oil and applies it to a single treatment region (low back, hamstring, shoulder) while working around linens, tender tissue and injury sites.

instances.label: Spa or massage-franchise treatment room: therapist takes a moist hot pack from a hydrocollator (or hot towels from a towel cabbie, or heated stones from a stone warmer), wraps/tests it, drapes it on the client's back or shoulders while the client lies draped on the table, checks comfort and skin, and removes it after 10-20 minutes.

Clinical/sports-oriented practice room: after or during work on an acute or inflamed area, therapist gets an ice or gel cold pack, covers it with a towel, places and sometimes secures it on the knee, shoulder or low back, times 10-15 minutes, checks skin for adverse reaction, removes and disposes/returns it.

Clinic or spa room with a radiant heat source (infrared/TDP heat lamp): therapist positions the lamp head over a specified body region at a safe distance, sets duration and intensity, drapes the client, monitors skin and comfort during the exposure, then swings the lamp away and shuts it off.

Spa/athletic-facility hydrotherapy suite: therapist fills and tempers a whirlpool or hydro tub, sets jets and timer, escorts and assists the client in, monitors the client during immersion, assists the client out and dries/robes them, then drains and sanitizes the tub.

Mobile/outcall work in a client's living room or bedroom, or on-site at an event tent or office: therapist brings a portable towel warmer, instant cold packs or heat wraps and applies hot or cold aids to the client on a portable table or massage chair, in a layout taken as found.

Relaxation add-ons inside the spa treatment room: warm eye pillow or warm scented towel placed on the face/eyes, heated table pad switched on and adjusted, warm compress applied over draped areas, aromatherapy towel presented during the session.
