roles.title: Dental Assistants
roles.description: Perform limited clinical duties under the direction of a dentist. Clinical duties may include equipment preparation and sterilization, preparing patients for treatment, assisting the dentist during treatment, and providing patients with instructions for oral healthcare procedures. May perform administrative duties such as scheduling appointments, maintaining medical records, billing, and coding information for insurance purposes.

tasks.label: Prepare patient, sterilize or disinfect instruments, set up instrument trays, prepare materials, or assist dentist during dental procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chairside assisting a dentist during a restorative procedure (composite filling, crown prep, cementation) in a private-practice operatory: maintaining a clear field with HVE suction and air/water syringe, retracting tongue and cheek, transferring instruments hand-to-hand on cue, holding the curing light, handing mixed material within its working time, adjusting the operatory light, all around a conscious, moving patient.

Chairside assisting during other procedure types: surgical extraction/implant placement (suction of blood, retraction, passing elevators/forceps, gauze), endodontics, sealants/hygiene, and pediatric patients who squirm or need behavior management; includes reacting to unexpected bleeding, gagging, or a change in the dentist's plan.

Preparing the patient: greeting and seating them in the chair, draping the bib, adjusting chair/headrest for the procedure, placing protective eyewear, verifying/updating health history and consent, applying topical anesthetic, and positioning the patient for the operator.

Reprocessing a batch of contaminated instruments in the office sterilization area: transporting soiled cassettes from operatories, pre-cleaning in an ultrasonic bath or instrument washer, rinsing and drying, inspecting, packaging in pouches/wrap with chemical indicators, loading and running the autoclave, unloading, checking indicators, and storing sterile packs.

Setting up the instrument tray/cassette for a specific scheduled procedure: pulling the right sterile pouches and burs, arranging instruments in order of use on the tray, adding cotton rolls, gauze, matrix bands, assembling the anesthetic syringe (carpule + needle), and covering the tray until the patient is seated.

Preparing dental materials on cue: proportioning and mixing cement, glass ionomer, or alginate; loading impression trays or syringes; dispensing and shaping composite or temporary crown material; triturating capsules - each with a short working time tied to the procedure step.

sources.title: Bryan Health Uses New Robotic Technology to Clean and Sterilize Surgical Instruments
sources.claim: STERIS ATLAS Workflow Automation Vehicle is deployed in a hospital sterile processing department, where it autonomously navigates, picks up racks of hand-cleaned instruments and loads them into washer-disinfectors.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family as the dental sterilization instance: moving soiled instrument racks/cassettes into washer-disinfectors within a reprocessing area.

sources.claim: A 6-DOF Staubli robot with vision autonomously sorts and packs surgical instruments into sterile ... in a calibrated workcell, with instruments presented on a staging surface by a technician.
sources.transferJustification: Setting up a dental procedure tray is the same operation on comparable objects: selecting stainless steel hand instruments from a checklist and arranging them in fixed positions on a tray.

sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: RIF Robotics' vision-guided robotic arm autonomously assembled a minor surgical instrument tray during a pilot inside a hospital sterile processing department.
sources.transferJustification: Surgical tray assembly matches dental tray/cassette setup: identifying similar stainless instruments by sight and placing each in its correct tray position.

sources.claim: Getinge's Automatiq family combines a self-navigating mobile robot and automatic loaders that load and unload its washer-disinfector and steam sterilizer in central sterile supply departments.

sources.claim: MULTIVAC supplies purpose-built medical packaging lines in which a SCARA robot loads medical products into sterile-barrier pack cavities that are then sealed.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: The ARxIUM RIVA robotic compounding system autonomously measures, reconstitutes and fills medications into syringes and bags inside an enclosed ISO-5 cell, and is in routine hospital pharmacy use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing clinical materials to spec - proportioning, mixing and loading them into delivery devices (syringes) with volumetric precision inside an enclosed purpose-built cell, comparable to mixing dental cement or impression material and loading a syringe or tray.

sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis
sources.claim: Robotic scrub nurse research achieves only partial autonomy on the narrow sub-task of anticipating and handing instruments, in laboratory/simulated settings.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to chairside assisting; it covers only instrument handover, at about 72% autonomy, with no suction, retraction, or intraoral field management.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive's autonomous dental robot performed a crown preparation on a human patient, showing autonomous intraoral work by a dentist-side robot, not any dental-assistant function.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the chairside instance: the only autonomous intraoral robot performs the operator's cutting on a stabilized patient and does not suction, retract, pass instruments, or hand materials to a dentist.

tasks.label: Record treatment information in patient records.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Assist dentist in management of medical or dental emergencies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vasovagal syncope: a patient faints in the dental chair during or just after an injection/extraction. Assistant recognizes the collapse, places chair in supine/Trendelenburg, loosens tight clothing, applies cold compress and ammonia inhalant, takes pulse/BP/respiration, attaches pulse oximeter, sets up and holds oxygen by nasal hood, stays with the patient until recovered, and records the event.

Mild-to-moderate medical event in the operatory: hyperventilation, hypoglycemia in a diabetic, postural hypotension, or a mild allergic reaction (rash/itching). Assistant fetches the emergency kit, hands the dentist diphenhydramine or oral glucose/juice, helps position the patient, monitors and repeats vital signs, times the event, calls for backup, and documents.

Life-threatening event: anaphylaxis, cardiac arrest, generalized seizure, or aspirated/swallowed object with airway obstruction. Assistant retrieves oxygen tank, emergency drug kit and AED, opens ampoules/loads syringe for the dentist, applies AED pads and performs chest compressions in rotation, suctions the airway, protects a seizing patient, calls 911, times drug doses, and directs EMS to the operatory.

Dental emergency walk-in or post-op call-back: uncontrolled post-extraction hemorrhage, avulsed/fractured tooth, or acute abscess with swelling. Assistant sets up the operatory and instrument tray on short notice, seats the patient, takes a radiograph, places and holds gauze pressure packs, suctions and retracts while the dentist sutures/drains, mixes hemostatic or sedative dressing material, and gives post-op instructions.

Emergency preparedness upkeep between events: monthly check of the emergency drug kit for expired vials, verifying oxygen cylinder pressure and regulator function, AED pad/battery expiry and self-test, restocking consumables, and running a mock emergency drill with the dental team.

sources.system: Lifeline ARM ACC / LUCAS 3 mechanical CPR devices
sources.title: Automated CPR Machine - Henry Schein Medical
sources.claim: Mechanical chest-compression machines such as Defibtech's Lifeline ARM and Stryker's LUCAS 3 deliver automated compressions, but they are devices a human must position on the patient's sternum and activate; they perform no assessment, airway, drug or monitoring work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical CPR during cardiac arrest. It covers only the compression sub-step of instance 3 and requires humans to bare the chest, position the device and start it, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole emergency-assist instance.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed in more than 25 ... for fetching and delivering supplies and medications, but its workflows are explicitly non-patient-facing logistics in corridors and supply rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fetching of clinical supplies inside a healthcare facility. It could plausibly bring an emergency kit to a room, but the vendor states the robot handles non-patient-facing tasks only, so it does not substantiate patient assessment, positioning, oxygen, drug preparation or CPR.

sources.title: Dental AI Robotics Startup Dentronic Raises $1M Pre-Seed from South Park Commons - WOWTALE
sources.claim: Dentronic's Dexor is an early-stage chairside robotic arm intended to perform suction and retraction during routine dental procedures; the company is a pre-seed startup with a first production batch, and the degree of autonomous operation on live patients is not documented.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chairside suction and retraction, a sub-step of assisting during an urgent dental procedure. It does not cover operatory setup, radiographs, gauze pressure packing, material mixing or post-op instruction, and its autonomy on patients is unestablished.

sources.title: Robot Performs First Ever Fully Autonomous Dental Surgery on Live Patient
sources.claim: A robotic system has performed a fully automated restorative dental procedure on a human ..., showing patient-contacting dental robotics is feasible for planned, imaged, single-tooth work under controlled conditions; it is a first-in-human demonstration outside the US, not an emergency-response capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous work inside a cooperative patient's mouth. The transfer fails for emergencies because the procedure is pre-planned from 3D imaging on a stable, consenting patient, whereas emergency assisting requires recognition of a deteriorating patient, whole-body handling, drug and oxygen delivery and improvisation.

tasks.label: Order and monitor dental supplies and equipment inventory.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekly walk-through of the supply closet and operatory drawers in a general dental practice, checking on-hand quantities of consumables (gloves, burs, anesthetic carpules, impression material, composite) against established par levels and building a reorder list.

Placing the order itself: logging into a distributor portal (Henry Schein, Patterson, Benco) or working with a sales rep, comparing prices, promotions and substitutions, entering quantities, and submitting the purchase for the dentist's or office manager's approval.

Verifying an arriving shipment against the packing slip and invoice, logging what was received into the inventory record, and following up with the vendor on backorders, shortages, or incorrect/damaged items.
Monitoring expiration dates and lot numbers on materials, anesthetics, sterilization indicators and emergency-kit drugs; flagging short-dated stock and adjusting order quantities accordingly.

Tracking durable equipment and its consumables: counting handpieces, curing lights, sensors and instrument cassettes, noting service/repair and warranty status, and requesting quotes or arranging repair/replacement with vendors.

Maintaining the inventory records in practice-management or dedicated inventory software (including barcode/QR scan-based systems), reconciling counts, and reporting supply spend against budget to the dentist.

tasks.label: Expose dental diagnostic x-rays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine recall bitewings (2-4 images) on a cooperative adult in a general-practice operatory: place lead apron, seat sensor in a bite-wing holder, position it against the lingual surfaces of the posterior teeth, have the patient bite and hold, align the tube head to the holder ring, set kV/mA/time, expose from behind the barrier, check images for overlap/cone cuts and retake if needed.

Full-mouth series or several periapicals on an adult (new patient, perio exam): 14-20 receptor placements including maxillary molars and anterior regions, managing gag reflex, tori, shallow palate, limited opening, or an anxious patient; bisecting-angle technique where holders don't seat; all images must show apices and be free of cone cuts.

Single diagnostic image during an active procedure in the operatory: endodontic working-length film with a file in the canal and rubber dam clamp in place, post-op check, crown seating check, or an emergency toothache periapical; awkward receptor placement around dam frame/instruments, done quickly mid-treatment.

Radiographs on a pediatric patient in a general or pediatric practice: size-0/1 sensors or occlusal film, child may be wiggly, gag, or refuse; assistant uses behavior guidance, may need parent to stabilize, reduced exposure settings, frequent retakes.

Extraoral imaging in the office's x-ray alcove: panoramic, cephalometric, or CBCT scan for a new patient, third-molar or implant/ortho planning; remove jewelry/glasses/partials, guide the patient into the unit, set chin rest and bite block, close temple supports, align midsagittal/Frankfort planes with laser lights, instruct on tongue position and stillness, select program and exposure, run the scan, verify the image.

Off-site radiography with a portable/handheld unit: school-based sealant program in a gym or classroom, nursing-home bedside, or mobile dental van; patient in a folding chair or bed, improvised positioning, handheld x-ray unit with backscatter shield, portable sensor and laptop.

sources.system: Perceptive dental robotics system (AI-driven robotic arm + hand-held OCT volumetric scanner)
sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous dental robot (Perceptive) performed a crown preparation on one patient, but its 3D imaging is acquired with a hand-held scanner operated by a person, and the system was not cleared for use; nothing in it exposes or positions diagnostic radiographs.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing dental-chairside robot. Transfer to exposing radiographs fails: the imaging step is performed by a human holding the scanner, the robot only cuts a fixtured tooth, it never places a receptor or aligns an x-ray beam, and the single procedure was a one-off unapproved demonstration.

sources.system: SR-NOCS autonomous swab robot (Franka Emika arm, Cartesian impedance control)
sources.developer: Technical University of Denmark / partners (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous force-controlled robot arm can insert a swab into the mouth/nose of a seated human and reach a sampling target, validated in two clinical studies with 52 suspected COVID patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion of an instrument into a patient's oral cavity. It shows entry into the mouth is feasible, but does not transfer to exposing radiographs: a soft swab touching the pharyngeal wall is far coarser than seating a rigid receptor parallel to specified teeth, and the system performs no beam alignment, exposure-factor selection, or image-quality check.

sources.system: Multitom Rax Twin Robotic X-ray (RAXalign/RAXtrack, ceiling-mounted robotic arms)
sources.title: Twin Robotic X-ray scanner – Multitom Rax - Siemens Healthineers USA
sources.claim: Robotic radiography systems deployed in hospitals automatically align x-ray tube and detector around a patient, but a technologist still positions the patient and triggers each exposure; the systems are general-purpose radiography, not dental receptor placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine positioning of an x-ray source and detector for human imaging in a clinical facility. It does not transfer to dental radiography, because the receptor is placed inside the patient's mouth by hand and the patient is positioned by the technologist; the robot only moves equipment along preset paths under operator command.

sources.system: RobOralScan (Franka Research 3 arm + Huvitz Lilivis intraoral scanner)
sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction
sources.claim: Robotic automatic intraoral imaging is still at the research stage: a reinforcement-learning policy drives an arm-mounted intraoral optical scanner, demonstrated in simulation with zero-shot transfer to a bench setup, not on patients and not with x-rays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously moving an imaging device within the oral workspace. It is the closest work to robotic intraoral image acquisition, yet it is optical scanning of models in a bounded bench workspace with no live patient, no radiation receptor placement, and no diagnostic acceptance criteria, so it cannot substantiate completing a radiographic exposure.

tasks.label: Take and record medical and dental histories and vital signs of patients.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Established adult patient at a routine recall/hygiene or restorative visit in a general dental operatory: assistant seats the cooperative patient and verbally updates the medical/dental history (changes in health, new medications, allergies, recent hospitalizations, dental complaints), then records the update in the practice's chart. No vital signs are taken at most such visits.

New patient or annual comprehensive exam, cooperative ambulatory adult: assistant reviews the completed health-history form item by item, clarifies conditions/medications/surgeries, records dental history and chief complaint, then places an automatic cuff and records blood pressure and pulse in the chart before the dentist's exam.

Oral surgery, implant, extraction, or nitrous/sedation appointment: assistant takes baseline vital signs (BP, pulse, SpO2, sometimes respirations/temperature) with cuff and pulse oximeter, records them on the anesthesia/treatment record, and reviews the medical history, medication list, NPO status and any medical clearance in detail.

Medically complex, elderly, or disabled patient: polypharmacy, cognitive impairment, hearing or language barrier, history partly supplied by a caregiver; BP reading must be repeated or taken manually by auscultation because of arrhythmia, large arm, or an implausible automated reading; patient may be in a wheelchair.

Pediatric patient accompanied by a parent: history obtained from the parent with the child present, anxious or squirming child, pediatric-size cuff or temperature check when infection is suspected, and charting in the pediatric record.

sources.system: Pepper social robot (v1.8a, NAOqi 3.9, SoftBank Robotics) PROM interview system
sources.developer: Eindhoven University of Technology / Máxima MC (Netherlands) research team
sources.title: Quality of Care Perceived by Older Patients and Caregivers in Integrated Care Pathways With Interviewing Assistance From a Social Robot: Noninferiority Randomized Controlled Trial (JMIR)
sources.claim: A SoftBank Pepper social robot autonomously conducted a 36-item patient-reported outcome interview with older outpatients in two hospital outpatient clinics; perceived quality of care was equal to clinician-conducted interviews, and the robot displayed/recorded answers and produced a report used in the subsequent consultation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-administered structured health questionnaire in a clinic room. It transfers to dental history taking because the objects are the same (a seated patient answering a fixed health-history instrument) and the output is the same (structured answers recorded to the record).

sources.system: Social robot health-data acquisition system (PROM interview robot)
sources.title: Robot for health data acquisition among older adults: a pilot randomised controlled cross-over trial (Age and Ageing) – TU/e research portal record
sources.claim: In a randomised cross-over trial in a clinical outpatient setting, a social robot autonomously administered three health questionnaires (52 questions) to community-dwelling older adults, completing 39 of 42 interviews, with data comparable to nurse-administered interviews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous administration and recording of structured patient questionnaires. Dental medical-history intake uses the same instrument type (fixed health-history items) with the same cooperative seated patient, so interview performance carries over.

sources.title: Implementation of a New Kiosk Technology for Blood Pressure Management in a Family Medicine Clinic (JABFM)
sources.claim: An FDA-cleared self-service blood-pressure kiosk was installed in a family medicine clinic waiting room; patients sit, place the arm in the cuff and obtain a measurement with classification without staff help. The clinic kept the kiosks after the pilot and medical-assistant time was saved; newer kiosk models upload readings directly into the EHR.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element (measuring and recording a patient's blood pressure and pulse), performed by a machine that mechanically inflates and deflates a cuff on the presented arm under machine control; it substantiates vital-sign acquisition when the patient is presented to the machine as a purpose-built station would present them.

sources.date: 2024-05 (trial results); Northwestern Medicine multicenter validation announced 2025-03; Series B 2026-03
sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints (Clinical Trials Arena)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs diagnostic blood draws on a patient's arm placed in the device, using ultrasound imaging and AI-guided needle insertion; in clinical trials it achieved 95% first-stick success across 1,500 draws on more than 1,000 patients in hospital/blood-collection settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical procedure on a seated patient's arm presented in a purpose-built station. Venipuncture demands far more precision and carries more risk than placing/inflating a cuff or a pulse-oximeter probe, so clinical-quality performance transfers to station-based vital-sign acquisition.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensing)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring (Cyborg and Bionic Systems)
sources.claim: The MIT/Brigham and Women's 'Dr. Spot' quadruped measured temperature, respiratory rate, pulse and oxygen saturation contactlessly from patients in a hospital emergency department, but the robot was driven and operated by clinical staff rather than acting autonomously.

sources.title: Applications of Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Technologies During COVID-19: A Review (Disaster Medicine and Public Health Preparedness)
sources.claim: UBTECH's AIMBOT and Cruzr anti-epidemic robots navigate hospitals and other facilities autonomously and perform infrared temperature screening of people, i.e. autonomous acquisition of a single vital sign in an as-found human facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous measurement and logging of body temperature in a hospital. It covers only one of the vital signs a dental assistant records and involves no contact measurement, so it supports temperature screening only.

tasks.label: Apply protective coating of fluoride to teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine chairside fluoride varnish in a dental operatory: cooperative adult or older child reclined in the chair after a prophylaxis; assistant isolates and dries the teeth with gauze/air-water syringe and suction, paints 0.25–0.5 mL of 5% NaF varnish onto all accessible facial, lingual and occlusal surfaces of the full dentition with a micro-brush, checks coverage, and gives post-op eating/brushing instructions.

Pediatric patient age 1–6 in a pediatric operatory or knee-to-knee exam: child is small, may cry, squirm, close the mouth or bite; assistant stabilizes the head with a hand, uses a mouth prop or finger retraction, wipes teeth dry with gauze and quickly paints varnish over primary dentition in under a minute, then instructs the caregiver.

Fluoride gel/foam tray treatment in the operatory: assistant selects and loads upper and lower foam trays with APF gel, seats them over the arches with the patient upright, holds high-volume suction for 1–4 minutes to prevent swallowing, removes trays, has the patient expectorate, and gives post-treatment instructions.

Public-health/portable setting: school-based varnish program in a gym, classroom or mobile dental van, or a long-term care facility room; portable chair or ordinary chair, headlamp illumination, screening plus varnish on a queue of many children or residents, layout and lighting differ site to site.

Special-needs, medically complex or frail geriatric patient: wheelchair transfer or wheelchair-seated treatment, involuntary movement, strong gag reflex, xerostomia, limited mouth opening; assistant uses props, suction and repositioning while applying varnish, sometimes quadrant by quadrant.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm performed an autonomous single-tooth crown preparation on one human patient (2024) — the most advanced autonomous in-mouth robotic work reported. It is a drilling/restorative system, not a system that dries teeth and paints a varnish coating over the full dentition; no fluoride application capability is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic crown preparation) is the closest in-mouth autonomous robotic work; transfer to fluoride application is NOT supported, because varnish application requires soft-tissue retraction, drying/suction, and brush coverage of every surface of ~20-32 teeth rather than rigid cutting of one immobilized tooth.

sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed dental literature confirms the July 2024 autonomous robot procedure was a crown preparation on a single human patient; the review describes robotics in dentistry as emerging, with no reported autonomous system performing preventive fluoride treatments.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic crown prep); cited to establish the state of the art in autonomous intraoral robotics, not to substantiate fluoride application.

sources.system: Hesy Tech robotic dental hygiene arm
sources.title: Hesytech | AI-Guided Robotic Dental Hygiene
sources.claim: Hesy Tech advertises an AI-guided robotic dental hygiene system covering caries prevention, probing, polishing and scaling, but its own site states the system is still under development — an announcement of intent, not a demonstrated capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic prophylaxis/polishing) would be adjacent to fluoride application, but the vendor states the system is under development, so it cannot substantiate completion of any instance.

sources.title: At last: A fully robotic toothbrush for disabled patients
sources.claim: The Samba is a mouthpiece-style powered/robotic toothbrush marketed for people with disabilities; it brushes teeth when placed in the mouth by the user or caregiver. It is a hygiene aid, not a system that autonomously isolates, dries and coats a patient's dentition with professional fluoride varnish.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (mechanical tooth brushing) shares the intraoral workspace, but the device is positioned and held by a person, delivers no professional varnish dose, and provides no per-surface coverage verification, so it does not transfer to professionally applied fluoride.

sources.system: Penn magnetically actuated dental microrobots (CARS platform)
sources.title: Scientists Have Created Microrobots That Can Automatically Brush and Floss Your Teeth
sources.claim: Microrobot systems for dental biofilm removal (magnetically actuated iron-oxide nanoparticle swarms and bristle/floss-forming microrobots) remain laboratory and pre-clinical work on extracted teeth and in vitro biofilm models, not clinical chairside treatment of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic plaque removal on tooth surfaces) operates on the same objects, but the work is in vitro/pre-clinical and externally magnetically steered, so it cannot substantiate chairside fluoride varnish application on patients.

tasks.label: Schedule appointments, prepare bills and receive payment for dental services, complete insurance forms, and maintain records, manually or using computer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Make preliminary impressions for study casts and occlusal registrations for mounting study casts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General/orthodontic practice operatory: assistant selects and tries in a stock tray for a cooperative adult or teen patient, mixes alginate, loads and seats maxillary and mandibular trays, holds until set, removes, inspects for voids/drags, disinfects and stores the impressions for study casts.

Digital records visit: assistant captures a full-arch intraoral scan (both arches plus buccal bite scan) with a chairside scanner in place of an alginate impression, retracting cheek/tongue, managing saliva and moisture, and re-scanning gaps until the model is accepted for study-cast/record purposes.

Pediatric or gag-prone/anxious patient in a dental operatory: assistant must coach breathing, seat a small tray with minimal material, control the gag reflex and patient movement, often repeating the impression after a failed attempt.

Edentulous or partially edentulous, often elderly patient (practice operatory or on-site/nursing-home visit): preliminary impressions of resorbed or flabby ridges with edentulous stock trays and adhesive, manipulating lips and cheeks to capture the sulcus for denture study casts.

Occlusal/bite registration only: assistant places wax or polyvinyl siloxane bite registration material, guides the patient into centric occlusion, holds while it sets, then removes and trims the record so casts can be mounted (e.g., for an occlusal guard or ortho records).

sources.title: Perceptive completes automated dental procedure with AI-driven robot
sources.claim: Perceptive's dental robotic arm performed an autonomous crown preparation on a human patient, but the 3D imaging step that produces the digital model of the mouth is done with a clinician-held handheld OCT scanner, and the event was a one-off milestone demonstration, not a deployed workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is crown preparation (drilling), not impression making; the robot never handles trays or impression materials and the mouth-mapping step is performed by a human, so no transfer to making a preliminary impression or occlusal registration is established.

sources.developer: Perceptive, reviewed in British Dental Journal
sources.title: The future of dentistry through robotics | British Dental Journal
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed dental review confirms the July 2024 Perceptive event was the first autonomous robot procedure on a human patient (tooth preparation for crowns) and that mouth mapping uses a hand-held volumetric scanner.
sources.transferJustification: Crown preparation is a different task; it shows robotic instruments can work in a live mouth but does not substantiate seating, timing and removing an impression tray or recording occlusion.

sources.title: RobOralScan: Learning Active Intraoral Scanning for Robotic Dental Reconstruction
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 the digital equivalent of a preliminary impression - full-arch intraoral scanning - is still described in the robotics literature as having limited automation; the first RL-based robotic intraoral scanning pipeline is a research system evaluated on reconstruction coverage, not a clinically validated patient workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic intraoral scanning is the closest analogue to taking a preliminary impression digitally; the paper's own framing (limited automation, research-stage coverage around 92%, no in-vivo validation) shows no system completes patient full-arch acquisition at clinical quality.

sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous force-controlled robot has performed naso- and oropharyngeal swab sampling on real patients in clinical studies, showing robots can insert a slender tool into a live human mouth under machine control in a clinical setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is oropharyngeal swabbing: it shares the live oral cavity and force-sensitive insertion, but an impression requires mixing and loading viscous material, seating a full-arch tray against teeth and soft tissue, waiting for set, atraumatic removal and quality inspection - none demonstrated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: University of Basel / University of Zurich
sources.title: A mini robot to simplify dental treatment (EurekAlert release)
sources.claim: The most recent intraoral dental robot prototype (MIR) is designed only for crown preparation and was tested on synthetic tooth models, with sensors and cameras still to be added before practice use; taking the impression remains a human step in the described workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Crown preparation on bench models; no patient testing and no impression or bite-registration capability, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: From AI in the office to robot-assisted dental implant surgery - Oral Health Group
sources.claim: The only FDA-cleared commercial chairside dental robot in wide clinical use, Yomi, is a haptic guidance system for implant placement that is manipulated by the surgeon rather than operating autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Implant surgery guidance, surgeon-driven; establishes that commercially deployed chairside dental robots are co-manipulated guidance devices, not autonomous performers of chairside assistant tasks.

tasks.label: Pour, trim, and polish study casts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General dental practice, in-office lab bench: assistant hand-mixes dental plaster/stone to the correct water-powder ratio, pours a single alginate impression on a bench vibrator (small increments, tipping the tray to avoid bubbles in tooth indentations), lets it set ~45 min, separates the set cast from the alginate without fracturing incisal edges, trims the base on a wet model trimmer, then smooths/polishes the art portion. One or two casts per case, done between patients.

Orthodontic practice: batch of upper and lower alginate impressions from several patients poured the same session, anatomic portion plus a base (rubber base formers or double-pour), then trimmed on the model trimmer to the conventional symmetric orthodontic geometry (base parallel to occlusal plane, 65-degree back cuts, heel and side cuts) with the casts held in occlusion via a wax bite, finished with soap/gloss for patient presentation and records.

Restorative/prosthodontic case: die stone or improved stone poured into a VPS/PVS impression for a solid working cast and its opposing cast, boxed or based, then trimmed to expose preparation margins and clear the base, and lightly polished before being sent to the lab or articulated. Higher surface-detail and handling-fragility demands than a diagnostic model.

Dental school clinic, hospital dental department, or large group practice with a dedicated model room: high-volume pouring, trimming and polishing of study casts on standard lab equipment (vacuum mixer, multiple vibrators, several trimmers), often dozens of casts per day, to a written departmental standard.

Digital-first practice: intraoral scan replaces the impression, models are 3D printed in-office; the assistant sets up the print job, removes the printed arch models from the build platform, washes and cures them, removes any supports/raft and smooths the base so the model can serve as a study cast or thermoforming model.

sources.system: Sacmi ALV / RobotCasting cell with Gaiotto automation
sources.title: GSI invests in Sacmi ALV | Ceramic World Web
sources.claim: Sacmi/Gaiotto supply fully robotized high-pressure casting cells for sanitaryware in which slurry is cast into moulds and the fragile cast pieces are automatically demoulded and transferred for further processing; a two-module ALV cell was installed at GSI Ceramica.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: casting a settable slurry into a mould and demoulding the set piece. Pouring dental stone into an impression and separating the set cast is the same operation class - controlled fill of a cavity, timed set, careful release of a fragile cast body - performed here fully automatically inside a purpose-built cell, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual (work fixtured and presented to the machine).

sources.title: Ceramica Alice chooses Sacmi RobotClean | Ceramic World Web
sources.claim: Sacmi RobotClean is a fully automated finishing cell with two finishing robots and automatic piece handling that performs, with abrasive tools and software-defined recipes, the surface finishing of cast ceramic ware that was previously done by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive trimming/finishing of a cast, unfired ceramic body (edges, rims, seams). Trimming and polishing a gypsum cast is the same abrasive material-removal operation on a softer, smaller cast body at looser tolerance (about a millimetre and a degree or two on base and back cuts).

sources.system: Glidewell BruxZir Factory automated crown manufacturing line (Beckhoff control)
sources.title: Glidewell and Beckhoff | Automated BruxZir Manufacturing
sources.claim: Glidewell's BruxZir production lines handle patient-unique dental parts fully automatically: robots transfer blanks to milling towers for anatomical shaping, the parts are glazed, and optical scanners verify geometry against the design file to within 50 microns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated shaping and surface finishing of a one-off, patient-specific dental object inside a purpose-built cell. It shows that per-case geometric variability - the reason cast trimming is judgment-driven for a human - is handled by scan-driven toolpaths at tolerances far tighter than study-cast trimming requires.

sources.system: KUKA gravity die casting robot / KRC ROBOTstar
sources.title: Gravity die casting | KUKA Global
sources.claim: KUKA supplies commercial gravity die casting robot cells in which the robot performs the pour into the mould, with the pouring motion synchronised to the mould's tilting for controlled, defect-free filling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic pouring of a liquid into a mould cavity with motion profiled to fill it without entrapped defects. Pouring stone into an impression is the same operation - a metered, incrementally tipped pour combined with vibration to avoid voids in the tooth indentations.

sources.system: FANUC material removal / polishing robots with force sensing
sources.title: Robotic Cutting, Deburring, Polishing, Buffing & More | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC sells force-sensor-equipped robots for material removal including grinding, deburring, buffing and polishing, used in production to hold consistent surface finishes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled robotic grinding and polishing against an abrasive wheel or tool. Trimming a cast on a model trimmer wheel and polishing the base are the same contact operation on a much softer workpiece (gypsum) at coarser tolerance.

sources.title: Automated Trimmer Completes Jobs in Minimal Time - Dentistry Today
sources.claim: Axsys Dental Solutions markets TrimExpert, an automated trimming system for dental appliances that computes trim lines from digital case data and is offered in configurations up to a fully automated robotic cell for dental labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated, digitally driven trimming of patient-specific dental workpieces inside a lab production cell. It substantiates that trim geometry for a dental case can be derived from case data and executed by machine, the step a human performs by eye on a model trimmer.

sources.system: Formlabs Automation Ecosystem (Form Auto, Fleet Control, High Volume Resin System)
sources.title: Automation Ecosystem | Formlabs Dental
sources.claim: Formlabs sells a dental Automation Ecosystem whose Form Auto module removes finished printed parts from the build platform and starts the next print ... operator interaction; dental labs use it to increase model production.

sources.system: Fully automated SLA printing and post-processing line for dental aligner molds
sources.title: Fully Automated Resin Model Production for Clear Aligner Manufacturing by DHR Engineering
sources.claim: An engineering integrator describes a delivered, fully automated SLA production line for clear-aligner resin dental arch models in which robots transfer parts between printers and post-processing so the models flow through continuously without operator availability limiting throughput.

tasks.label: Fabricate temporary restorations or custom impressions from preliminary impressions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Direct chairside single-unit provisional: before the dentist preps a molar, the assistant takes a preliminary alginate/putty impression, then after the prep loads bis-acryl into that matrix, seats it intraorally over the prepared tooth, removes it after set, trims the margins with an acrylic bur, checks contacts/occlusion, and polishes the temporary crown. Done in the operatory with the patient in the chair, in a few minutes.

Multi-unit or long-span provisional (3-unit bridge, anterior veneer temporaries, or interim implant-supported provisional) fabricated from the preliminary impression matrix or on a poured cast at the in-office lab bench; requires relining, adding pontics, trimming and polishing to acceptable contour and margins.

Custom impression tray for a final crown-and-bridge, implant or denture impression: pour the preliminary alginate in stone, trim the cast, adapt spacer wax, adapt and cure self-cure or light-cure tray acrylic, trim borders and attach a handle; done at the in-office lab bench between patients.

Vacuum-formed/thermoformed appliance made over a cast from the preliminary impression: bleaching tray, Essix-type temporary retainer/tooth-replacement stent, or a clear matrix shell used later to form a provisional; sheet heated and formed on the office vacuum former, then cut and trimmed to the gingival outline and polished.

Digital chairside workflow: intraoral scan (or scanned preliminary impression), CAD design of the interim restoration with AI-assisted software, then milling a PMMA block or 3D printing the provisional in the office unit, followed by sprue/support removal, polishing and delivery to the dentist for try-in.

sources.system: CEREC Primemill with Ivoclar Telio CAD PMMA blocks
sources.title: Telio CAD Blocks for CEREC, Refills - Patterson Dental
sources.claim: Chairside CAD/CAM milling units mill temporary crowns and bridges from PMMA blocks inside an enclosed, fixtured milling chamber in the dental office; the milling run is executed by the machine from the approved digital design.

sources.title: SprintRay Store Product: SprintRay Midas 3D Printer
sources.claim: A chairside 3D printer fabricates crowns, inlays and veneers from a digital design in under ten minutes inside a sealed resin-capsule build chamber, i.e. the restoration is fabricated by the machine rather than hand-formed.
sources.transferJustification: Printed crowns/inlays include interim (provisional) restorations; the fabrication step, material handling and precision are the same as for a temporary crown.

sources.system: Glidewell BruxZir Factory automated production lines
sources.title: Robotics and Automation | Chairside Magazine Vol. 21 Issue 2
sources.claim: A purpose-built production facility uses robotic arms to select the correct patient-specific blank and feed interconnected mills, producing patient-specific crowns and bridges at industrial scale.
sources.transferJustification: Same class of patient-specific restoration fabrication (crown/bridge geometry from an impression or scan); the interim PMMA version is a simpler, lower-tolerance case of the same machine process.

sources.system: Glidewell AI restorative design (fastdesign.io / Crown AI) feeding the automated factory
sources.title: AI-Driven Manufacturing and Design | Chairside Magazine Vol. 21 Issue 2
sources.claim: The design step that precedes machine fabrication is itself automated at scale: the overwhelming majority of restoration designs are produced by AI without a technician designing them by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the CAD step between impression/scan and machine fabrication no longer requires a human designer, so the fabrication pipeline can run with limited intervention.

sources.system: Formlabs Form 3B/Form 4B with Custom Tray Resin
sources.title: Custom Tray Resin | Formlabs Dental
sources.claim: Custom impression trays are directly manufactured by SLA 3D printers from a biocompatible resin, replacing hand-adapted acrylic tray fabrication.

sources.title: Form Auto: Automation Hardware for Formlabs Dental SLA 3D Printers
sources.claim: Automated hardware removes finished printed parts from the build platform and starts the next job without operator interaction, enabling unattended lights-out production of dental appliances.

sources.system: Hamer TVP12 / TVP25 automated dental thermoforming lines
sources.title: Automated Clear Aligner Thermoforming - Hamer Packaging
sources.claim: In-line automated machines thermoform plastic sheet over patient-specific dental models and handle the parts at industrial rates, with integrated vision and marking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vacuum-forming a thermoplastic sheet over a patient's dental cast and trimming it. This is exactly the operation a dental assistant performs for bleaching trays, Essix stents and clear provisional matrices — same objects, same materials, same fit tolerances.

sources.title: Smartee Unveils Modular Automated Production Line, Redefining Clear Aligner Manufacturing
sources.claim: A second industrial automated line for thermoformed patient-specific dental trays, with independently controlled units and controlled forming precision, is in production use.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the Hamer line: automated thermoforming of a patient-specific plastic tray over a printed dental model, matching the assistant's vacuum-formed appliance work.

sources.title: Automate Dental Restoration Finishing | Zahn Dental
sources.claim: Bench machines automatically smooth, buff and polish finished restorations and printed appliances, covering the post-fabrication finishing step.

sources.title: Ceramill Matron from Amann Girrbach offers maximum precision and surface quality in a new design
sources.claim: A dental milling machine with a multi-blank changer runs fully automated production cycles without an operator changing workpieces between jobs.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: An AI-controlled robotic arm autonomously performed a restorative dental procedure (preparing a tooth for a crown) on a human patient in a dental operatory; the system does not fabricate or hand-form provisional restorations.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to bound the E2 judgment: it is intraoral tooth preparation, a one-off pre-FDA demonstration, and does not cover fabricating a temporary restoration or a custom tray in the operatory/office lab.

tasks.label: Clean and polish removable appliances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Recall/denture-check appointment in a general dental office: patient hands over a complete or partial denture; assistant rinses it, places it in an ultrasonic bath with denture cleaning solution, brushes off plaque and light stain, then polishes the external surfaces on the lab lathe with pumice and a rag wheel (avoiding the intaglio/fit surface), rinses, disinfects and returns it during the visit.

Denture/partial delivery or adjustment appointment: after the dentist relieves sore spots or adjusts a clasp/acrylic with a bur, the assistant smooths and re-polishes the adjusted areas to a high shine on the lathe (pumice then high-shine compound), keeping contours and occlusion unchanged and avoiding heat distortion, and returns the appliance chairside within minutes.

Orthodontic office: Hawley retainers, expanders and clear thermoplastic retainers/aligners are cleaned at check appointments - ultrasonic bath with cleaning solution, brushing of the acrylic body and wires, rinsing and drying; acrylic bodies may receive a light buff, clear plastic is cleaned only (no heat/lathe).

Night guards, occlusal splints, sports mouthguards and interim 'flipper' partials cleaned and buffed at delivery or a follow-up visit: debris and biofilm removed, acrylic buffed to a smooth shine, appliance disinfected and bagged for the patient.

Heavily soiled appliance from a long-term wearer (often geriatric or long-term-care patient): tenacious calculus, tobacco/coffee stain and denture-adhesive residue require an extended soak in a calculus/stain dissolver, repeated ultrasonic cycles, mechanical removal of hard deposits, then a full re-polish to restore shine without abrading the acrylic or denture teeth.

sources.system: AutoFinish DCPC250 / DCPC500 dental finishing machine
sources.title: Automate Dental Restoration Finishing | Zahn Dental
sources.claim: AutoFinish DCPC250/DCPC500 are commercially sold dental finishing machines that automatically smooth, buff and polish removable appliances including printed dentures and nightguards, replacing manual bench polishing in dental laboratories.

sources.title: AutoFinish DCPC500 is the Secret to Dental Finishing Success
sources.claim: The AutoFinish machine performs the polishing cycle itself using media, soap and centrifugal force in a closed, door-interlocked barrel, and is validated for conventional, milled and 3D-printed dentures, partial frameworks, flexible partials and temporary partial dentures (stayplates).

sources.title: Top 5 Advantages the AutoFinish Will Give Your Lab - Zahn Dental Labs
sources.claim: Zahn/AutoFinish states the machines are validated with defined workflows and materials, with approved workflows covering removable dentures, implant restorations and crown and bridge work.

sources.system: Robosonic robotic ultrasonic cleaning cell (Fanuc CR-7i)
sources.title: Ultrasonic Robotic Parts Cleaning Cell Provides Precision Cleaning and Maximum Efficiency
sources.claim: The Robosonic robotic parts-cleaning cell uses a Fanuc CR-7i collaborative robot to move small precision parts through spray wash, ultrasonic immersion wash, ... and dry stations automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated ultrasonic cleaning of small precision parts. A denture, retainer or night guard is a small (<0.2 kg) contoured part cleaned by exactly this chemistry-plus-cavitation sequence (soak, ultrasonic, rinse, dry) that a dental assistant runs manually; the robot performs the load/transfer/unload the assistant would do.

sources.system: AV&R robotic polishing / robotic buffing machines
sources.title: AV&R | Robotic Polishing Machines / Robotic Buffing Machines
sources.claim: AV&R builds robotic polishing and buffing machines that hold complex free-form parts (knee, hip and ankle orthopaedic implants) against abrasive and buffing media in production cells, achieving mirror finishes with closed-loop inspection feedback and part-to-part consistency of about ±15 micrometres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic buffing of small free-form medical implants to a mirror finish. The motion is identical to lathe polishing a denture - a gripped part presented under controlled force to a rotating wheel with compound - on parts of comparable size and with tighter tolerance than acrylic appliance polishing.

sources.title: Active Contact Flange Kit - FerRobotics
sources.claim: FerRobotics Active Contact Flange kits give industrial and collaborative robots constant, actively controlled contact force for polishing, brushing and cleaning operations, including on plastic workpieces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-compliant robotic polishing of plastic parts. Acrylic appliance polishing requires light, constant contact force to avoid heat distortion and contour loss; commercially available force-compliant flanges provide precisely this control on plastics.

sources.system: Ultrasonic denture cleaner (ultrasonic cleaner plus cleanser immersion)
sources.developer: Lim, Burrow & McGrath, University of Hong Kong (Journal of Dentistry)
sources.title: Efficacy of ultrasonic home-care denture cleaning versus conventional denture cleaning: A randomised crossover clinical trial
sources.claim: A randomised crossover clinical trial found that machine-driven ultrasonic cleaning combined with denture cleanser immersion cleaned dentures better than the conventional soak-and-brush routine, improving denture cleanliness and reducing denture stomatitis.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects (worn complete/partial dentures) and same cleaning endpoint the assistant is judged on; establishes that the machine-executed cleaning step reaches or exceeds the cleanliness of manual brushing, including on deposits brushes cannot reach.

tasks.label: Clean teeth, using dental instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine coronal polishing of an adult recall patient in a general dental operatory: after scaling by the dentist/hygienist, the assistant (expanded-function/coronal-polishing certified) uses a slow-speed handpiece with rubber cup and prophy paste over all accessible surfaces of ~28 teeth, retracting cheek and tongue, using air-water syringe and high-volume evacuation, then flossing and checking for remaining plaque/stain.

Coronal polishing of a child or adolescent at a pediatric prophy visit: small mouth, frequent movement and repositioning, need for behavior coaching, flavored paste, careful avoidance of gingiva and erupting teeth, followed by fluoride application.

Polishing as preparation for another procedure in the operatory: pumice-only polish before sealant placement or orthodontic bracket bonding, or removal of residual adhesive/cement after debonding, with cotton-roll or isolation device in place and a clean, dry field required.

Adult with heavy extrinsic stain (tobacco, coffee, chlorhexidine) or heavy plaque and light supragingival deposit: repeated passes with coarse paste, bristle brush or air-polishing device, tactile/visual verification that stain is removed without abrading enamel or traumatizing gingiva.

Off-site/community setting: school-based sealant or prophy program, mobile dental van, or portable unit in a nursing home; patient in a portable chair or wheelchair, cramped and improvised operating position, limited suction, variable lighting, sometimes limited patient cooperation.

Patient with special needs, medical complexity, strong gag reflex, or limited mouth opening: cleaning must be done in short segments with protective stabilization or assistance, careful soft-tissue handling, and constant monitoring of patient tolerance.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive's AI-driven robotic arm autonomously performed a crown preparation on a live human patient (Barranquilla, Colombia) in 2024 — the only demonstrated fully autonomous intraoral robotic procedure on a patient — but it is a single-case demonstration on one tooth for restorative dentistry, not a dental prophylaxis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic crown preparation on one tooth. It does not transfer to cleaning teeth: prophylaxis requires sweeping soft-contact instrumentation over all surfaces of a full dentition adjacent to mobile soft tissue, tactile detection of residual deposit, retraction and evacuation, and repeatable worker-quality results across many patients; the cited demonstration is a single fixtured single-tooth cutting procedure.

sources.system: Hesy Tech AI-guided robotic dental hygiene system
sources.title: Hesytech | AI-Guided Robotic Dental Hygiene
sources.claim: Hesytech advertises an AI-guided autonomous robotic dental hygiene system performing scaling, polishing and probing, but its own site states the system is under development and it solicits pilot clinics; no completed procedure on a patient is documented.

sources.system: Surface topography-adaptive robotic superstructures (STARS) microrobot swarm
sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania (Koo and Steager labs)
sources.title: Swarm of tiny robots scrub teeth | National Institutes of Health (NIH)
sources.claim: The most advanced automated tooth-cleaning research system, Penn's magnetically controlled microrobot swarm (STARS), removes biofilm from 3D-printed models, extracted human teeth mounted on artificial gums, ... pig jaw sections in a laboratory chamber — not in a patient's mouth in a clinic, and it does not perform instrumented scaling or stain removal to prophylaxis standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated plaque/biofilm removal from teeth. It does not substantiate the work task because the demonstrations are ex vivo bench setups with electromagnets around isolated teeth in a fluid chamber; no clinical prophylaxis on a live patient (including calculus/stain removal, suction, and soft-tissue safety) has been shown.

sources.developer: Chinese dental robotics groups (clinical case series)
sources.title: Accuracy of autonomous robotic surgery for dental implant placement in fully edentulous patients: A retrospective case series study - PubMed
sources.claim: Autonomous robot-assisted implant surgery systems do drill in patients' mouths in dental hospital operatories, with the jaw registered via a fixed marker splint, showing autonomy is achievable only for rigidly registered, single-site cutting tasks — not for full-mouth soft-contact cleaning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous intraoral drilling in a dental operatory. Transfer fails for teeth cleaning: the implant robot works on a rigidly splinted, pre-planned single site with no requirement to traverse all tooth surfaces, judge residual plaque/stain tactilely, retract soft tissue, or evacuate slurry.

tasks.label: Fabricate and fit orthodontic appliances and materials for patients, such as retainers, wires, or bands.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chairside archwire work in the operatory of an orthodontic practice: remove ligatures/elastomerics from a bonded fixed appliance, select and place the next archwire, seat it in each bracket slot, cinch and cut distal ends, ligate, and check for irritation, working in a wet, moving mouth with a conscious patient.

In-office/laboratory fabrication of a removable appliance: pour or 3D-print a working model from an impression/intraoral scan, thermoform an Essix retainer sheet (or bend clasp/labial wires and cure acrylic for a Hawley), then cut, trim, smooth and polish it to the trim line and hand a finished appliance to the doctor for delivery, at a dental-office lab bench with a model trimmer, thermoformer, handpiece and pliers.

Retainer/appliance delivery appointment: seat the finished retainer in the patient's mouth, check fit and occlusion, relieve pressure points or adjust clasps and labial bow with pliers/torch or an acrylic bur, reseat and verify comfort and retention, then instruct the patient on wear and care.

Sizing and fitting molar bands and placing separators: try successive band sizes on the molars intraorally, seat with a band pusher/bite stick to the correct depth, mix and load cement, seat the band and clean up excess, all inside the patient's mouth.

Chairside repair or adaptation of an existing appliance or materials: re-adapt a distorted clasp or labial bow, add self-cure acrylic to a fractured retainer, re-bond/replace a loose band or wire segment, or trim an over-extended flange, working from the patient's own appliance with hand instruments.

sources.claim: Dentsply Sirona's SureSmile system produces patient-specific custom-bent orthodontic archwires on a wire-bending robot from the doctor's digital plan, and ships the finished wires to the practice; robotically bent wires are a long-standing commercial product with published clinical studies.

sources.claim: Align Technology manufactures a rigid removable orthodontic appliance (the Invisalign Palatal Expander) entirely by direct 3D printing from intraoral scan data in its automated production facilities, and sells it commercially in many markets.

sources.claim: Ortho-Automation's Trimlign / Trimlign2 is a commercially sold robotic table-top trimmer that automatically cuts thermoformed or printed aligners and retainers to the digital trim line, replacing hand trimming in practice and lab production.
sources.transferJustification: Trimming and finishing a thermoformed/printed retainer is the finishing step of the in-office retainer fabrication instance; the source names retainers explicitly.

sources.transferJustification: Thermoformed retainers are produced by the identical print-model / thermoform / trim sequence as aligners; the line's output is the same class of appliance the assistant fabricates.

sources.title: Fully-automatic robot dentist performs world's first human procedure — New Atlas
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous intraoral robot demonstrated to date performed a crown preparation on a single human volunteer; it is a prototype demonstration of tooth cutting, not of placing, seating or adjusting orthodontic appliances in the mouth.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the frontier of autonomous intraoral robotics; it substantiates cutting a fixtured tooth, not archwire placement, band fitting or retainer seating/adjustment, so it does not transfer to the chairside instances.

roles.title: Medical Assistants
aliases: OB/GYN Medical Assistant (Obstetrics and Gynecology Medical Assistant)
roles.description: Perform administrative and certain clinical duties under the direction of a physician. Administrative duties may include scheduling appointments, maintaining medical records, billing, and coding information for insurance purposes. Clinical duties may include taking and recording vital signs and medical histories, preparing patients for examination, drawing blood, and administering medications as directed by physician.

tasks.label: Interview patients to obtain medical information and measure their vital signs, weight, and height.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine rooming of a cooperative, ambulatory adult in a primary-care or specialty physician office: MA calls the patient from the waiting room, weighs and measures height at the hallway scale/stadiometer, seats the patient in the exam room, takes blood pressure (correct cuff size, arm supported), pulse, temperature, SpO2 and respirations, then asks the reason for visit, symptom detail, and reconciles the medication and allergy list, documenting all of it in the EHR before the physician enters.

Rooming an older, obese, or disabled patient in the same office: patient arrives with a walker or wheelchair, needs steadying or a wheelchair/chair scale for weight and cannot stand straight for a stadiometer; arm size or atrial fibrillation forces a large cuff or manual auscultation; hearing loss, dementia, or a family caregiver as historian makes the interview slow and improvised.

Pediatric visit: infant or young child undressed and weighed on an infant scale, recumbent length or stadiometer height, head circumference, tympanic/temporal temperature and pulse on a squirming or crying child, with the parent interviewed for symptoms, feeding, immunizations and medications.

Same-day sick visit or urgent-care/walk-in triage: acutely ill or injured adult in pain, fever, or distress; rapid full vital set including counted respiratory rate and pain score, sometimes repeated or taken in an alternate limb/position, with a focused symptom interview and immediate escalation of abnormal values (hypotension, hypoxia, high fever) to the clinician.

Focused pre-procedure or specialty intake on a cooperative adult (pre-op clearance, dermatology, ophthalmology, annual-wellness or physical exam): abbreviated vitals plus weight and height and a scripted history/questionnaire (medications, allergies, tobacco, screening items) entered into the EHR.

Off-site work: MA at a mobile clinic van, employer or community health-screening event, or a home-based primary care visit — portable scale, stadiometer rod or tape, portable BP monitor and thermometer used in a gym, church hall, van, or the patient's living room, with an intake interview done on a laptop or paper.

sources.claim: In a comparative trial in primary care, blood pressure measured by patients themselves at an automated kiosk had diagnostic accuracy close to nurse-measured office BP against ambulatory monitoring, supporting worker-comparable quality of kiosk vitals for cooperative adults.
sources.transferJustification: Same measurement as the task's BP component; establishes that an unattended automated station's reading is of comparable quality to a nurse/MA-taken office reading.

sources.title: HIGI Blood Pressure Kiosks: Health Monitoring Solutions | Kiosk Industry
sources.claim: higi Smart Health Stations — arm-in-cuff kiosks measuring blood pressure, pulse, weight and BMI — operated unattended at roughly 10,000 US retail locations with over a million tests per week.

sources.claim: Commercial self-service health-check kiosks sold for hospitals and clinics add automated height, temperature, SpO2 and body composition to weight/BMI/BP, with results uploaded automatically to the EMR.

sources.title: Patient Check-in Kiosk, Self Service Medical Kiosk | CharmHealth
sources.claim: EHR-integrated patient check-in kiosks in US practices collect demographic, family and social history and pre-appointment questionnaires directly into the chart before the visit.

sources.claim: OnMed CareStation walk-in stations deployed at pharmacies, employers and schools contain a blood pressure cuff, pulse ..., thermal scanning and a floor scale for patient weight, with the history taken by a remote clinician over video.

sources.title: Brigham and Women's Hospital tests MIT's 'Dr. Spot' robot for contactless vital signs monitoring - Becker's Hospital Review
sources.claim: The most capable mobile robot demonstrated taking patient vital signs inside a clinical facility (skin temperature, respiratory rate, heart rate, SpO2 in an ED triage tent) was remote-controlled, not autonomous, and measured no weight, height or blood pressure.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed ultrasound-guided venipuncture on seated patients in a multicenter clinical trial, showing autonomous machine-to-patient arm contact is achievable at a dedicated clinical station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (venipuncture) at a fixed patient station: shows an autonomous machine can locate and safely contact a cooperative seated patient's arm, the physical precondition for cuff/probe placement, but only at a purpose-built station.

tasks.label: Clean and sterilize instruments and dispose of contaminated supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary care/family practice clinic: after a minor procedure (suture removal, skin biopsy, IUD insertion, laceration repair), the MA collects used stainless instruments (forceps, hemostats, scissors, needle holders, specula) from the exam-room tray, pre-rinses/soaks them, scrubs or runs an ultrasonic bath, rinses, dries, inspects hinges and tips, pouches and heat-seals, loads a tabletop steam autoclave, runs and logs the cycle, unloads and stores. Small batches done between patients amid interruptions.

During and immediately after patient encounters in an exam or treatment room, the MA disposes of contaminated supplies at point of use: used needles, syringes, lancets and blades into the wall sharps container; soiled gauze, dressings, gloves, drapes, disposable specula and swabs into biohazard red-bag or regular waste per policy; strips soiled table paper; segregates correctly with patients and staff present.

High-volume specialty clinic (dermatology, podiatry, urgent care, OB/GYN) with a dedicated soiled/clean reprocessing room: batch decontamination of dozens of instrument sets in enzymatic soak, ultrasonic and washer-disinfector; drying, inspection, pouching/sealing or cassette wrapping; autoclave loading and multiple cycles per day; chemical and biological (spore) indicator testing, cycle documentation, and restocking sterile packs.

High-level disinfection of heat-sensitive semicritical devices per manufacturer IFU: flexible nasopharyngoscope in ENT, transvaginal ultrasound probe, laryngoscope blades - leak test, manual pre-clean/brush, timed soak in chemical high-level disinfectant or an automated reprocessor cycle, critical-water rinse, drying, hanging/storage and logging.

Regulated medical waste management for the clinic: sealing and replacing full sharps containers, tying and consolidating red bags, wheeling or carrying them to the locked soiled-utility/waste storage area for hauler pickup, wiping down and re-lining receptacles, and completing tracking documentation.

sources.system: Getinge Automatiq (Envoy mobile robot, Depot, Loaders, Hub)

sources.claim: Getinge's Automatiq line, launched commercially in 2025, combines self-navigating mobile robots, conveyors and automatic loaders that load and unload washer-disinfectors and steam sterilizers in central sterile supply departments under software orchestration.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: mechanical cleaning/disinfection and steam sterilization of surgical instruments with the machine loading/unloading step automated, i.e. the wash-and-sterilize core of the MA's reprocessing instance carried out in a purpose-built line.

sources.claim: A 2026 research system autonomously perceives, classifies, picks and packs 31 classes of surgical instruments into sterile trays with 3D-printed dividers/holders using a 6-DOF Staubli industrial arm, replacing manual inspection and assembly of trays.

sources.title: Robot offers an assist to sterile processing department | HFM Magazine
sources.claim: The Penelope CS robot was piloted in the central sterile supply clean area at New York-Presbyterian/The Allen Hospital, receiving instruments from a conveyor and autonomously scanning, identifying, counting and segregating them for tray assembly.

sources.title: hawo SealBot
sources.claim: hawo's SealBOT is a commercial automatic packaging system in which a robotic arm loads instrument trays, each tray is automatically placed in a sealable pouch and conveyed through an integrated validatable rotary sealer to a discharge point.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the pouching-and-sealing step of the MA's reprocessing instance: same objects (cleaned instruments/trays) placed into sterile barrier pouches and sealed to a validatable standard.

sources.system: MEDIVATORS ADVANTAGE PLUS Automated Endoscope Reprocessor
sources.title: MEDIVATORS ADVANTAGE PLUS Automated Endoscope Reprocessor | STERIS
sources.claim: The MEDIVATORS ADVANTAGE PLUS automated ... runs a fully automated cleaning and high-level disinfection cycle on flexible endoscopes loaded in a transport cassette, eliminating manual brushing and flushing.

sources.title: AMP's Horowitz on Bringing AI to the Recycling World | Waste360
sources.claim: AMP Cortex robotic sorters autonomously identify and pick soiled mixed-waste items from a moving conveyor and place them into designated streams at 80-120 picks per minute with up ..., with more than 125 units deployed in operating facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soiled-waste segregation. The objects are the same class the MA discards (gloves, wrappers, films, plastics, paper, metal), handled soiled and unfixtured, and the precision required is only reliable identification plus placement into the correct receptacle, matching sharps/red-bag/regular-trash segregation when waste is presented on a line.

sources.title: OnSite Waste Technologies introduces infectious waste sterilization and disposal system
sources.claim: The OnSite TE-5000 is a desktop, approved on-site treatment unit used in medical and dental offices that thermally sterilizes sharps and red-bag waste inside its container, converting regulated medical waste into ordinary solid trash.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the terminal disposal step of the MA's waste instance: once contaminated supplies are in the container, the machine renders them non-infectious without further human handling.

tasks.label: Prepare treatment rooms for patient examinations, keeping the rooms neat and clean.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-patient turnover of a standard exam room in a busy primary-care or specialty clinic: pull and discard soiled table paper, gown and wrappers into regular and biohazard bins, wipe the exam table, counter, and high-touch surfaces with disinfectant wipes, roll out fresh table paper, replace the consumables just used (gloves, gauze, specimen cups, otoscope tips), straighten stool/chairs and cords, and confirm the room is ready — all in 3-5 minutes while patients wait in the corridor.

Setting the room up for a specific procedure or exam type: selecting and laying out the correct instruments and supplies (suture/biopsy or minor-surgery tray, pelvic exam setup, wound-care or injection setup), opening sterile packages onto a Mayo stand without contaminating the field, and positioning drapes, light, and equipment for the provider.

Opening/closing and periodic replenishment duties: restocking each room's drawers and cabinets from a central supply cart (gloves in three sizes, syringes, dressings, specimen containers, gowns and linens, paper rolls), checking that equipment such as otoscope, BP cuff and sharps container is present, functional, and not overfull.

Cleaning a treatment room after a soiled or contaminated visit: blood, urine or emesis spill on table, floor or chair, bagging soiled linens and biohazard waste, disposing of sharps, and performing a full disinfection to infection-control protocol before the room can be reused.

End-of-day or scheduled deep-clean pass of the treatment room: wiping down all surfaces, exam table, counters and equipment with hospital-grade disinfectant, disinfecting the floor, and leaving the room clean and disinfected for the next clinic session.
