sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is an autonomous mobile manipulator that cleans restroom fixtures and floors and picks up trash, marketed as deployed in hospitals and airports on a monthly service basis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact cleaning and trash pickup of a whole small room inside an institution-controlled facility (hospital/airport restroom). Comparable surfaces and precision to wiping an exam room, and the same E2 setting class.

sources.title: Peanut Robotics | Home
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields a mobile manipulator that autonomously navigates and wipes surfaces to clean hotel and commercial-building bathrooms, with thousands of logged cleaning hours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wipe-cleaning of a small, pre-mapped room in a human work facility. Surfaces and precision are comparable to wiping down an exam room; environment class (institution-controlled, fixed layout) matches.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic workcell (6-DOF Staubli arm, vision, 3D-printed dividers/holders) sorts surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays, with fewer instrument-to-instrument collisions than human-assembled trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a correct, ready-to-use instrument set. Same objects (surgical instruments), similar placement precision, and at E1 the medical assistant's tray setup would arrive fixtured exactly as this cell presents instruments and holders.

sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly - Catalyst by Wellstar
sources.claim: RIF Robotics demonstrated autonomous assembly of a minor surgical tray with a robotic arm and computer ..., in a pilot with Wellstar Health System's sterile processing department.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a minor surgical instrument set — the same output a medical assistant produces when laying out a minor-procedure tray, with the same instruments, in a fixtured workcell.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: ORB, a Fetch-based autonomous mobile manipulator, retrieved and restocked operating-room supplies in an environment simulating a hospital supply room, achieving 96% success in restocking with three designated items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing medical consumables onto known shelf locations — the same objects (packaged clinical supplies) and precision as restocking an exam room's supply drawers, though demonstrated with only three item types.

sources.claim: An integrated mobile-manipulator system autonomously stocked supermarket shelves overnight with over 98% pick-and-place success across more than 700 stocking events, though the authors report it is still inferior to human workers in performance and cost.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment of packaged goods in an institution-controlled facility; comparable object sizes and placement precision to filling clinic supply shelves, but demonstrated slower and costlier than human workers.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi, the most widely deployed clinical mobile manipulator, is used in more than 25 U.S. ... but performs item transport (supplies, medications, lab samples), not room cleaning or room preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize what deployed clinical robots actually do (last-mile delivery), showing the deployed fleet does not perform exam-room turnover; it supports no positive judgment here.

tasks.label: Collect blood, tissue, or other laboratory specimens, log the specimens, and prepare them for testing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine venipuncture on a cooperative adult/adolescent in a physician-office draw chair or exam room: verify ID, apply tourniquet, prep site, draw 1-5 vacutainer tubes from an antecubital vein (including obese, elderly and moderately difficult-vein patients), invert tubes, label at the bedside, log in the EHR/LIS, and place in the courier rack or centrifuge.

Venipuncture on patients who cannot be drawn from a seated antecubital position: infants and young children, frail/oncology/dialysis patients, patients needing hand or wrist butterfly draws, and draws done at a wheelchair, gurney, or in a nursing-home/home visit; then label, log and prepare tubes.

Capillary collection: adult fingerstick for point-of-care glucose, A1c, hemoglobin or INR, or a microtainer collection / infant heelstick for a lead or bilirubin test; wipe, lance, milk the site, fill the microtainer or cartridge, label, log the result or specimen, and prep for testing.

Patient-produced specimens: instruct the patient on clean-catch urine (or hand out a stool/24-hour container), receive the filled cup at a restroom pass-through or counter, label with patient ID, log in the LIS/log book, and either run a dipstick/pregnancy test or aliquot and package it for courier pickup.

Respiratory swab on a cooperative adolescent/adult in an exam room: throat swab for strep or nasal/nasopharyngeal swab for flu/COVID/RSV, place the swab in transport medium or a rapid-test buffer, snap the shaft, cap, label, log, and run the rapid test or bag it for send-out.

Provider-obtained and difficult specimens: hold the formalin container while the physician deposits a skin/tissue biopsy, cap and label it; handle Pap/ThinPrep vials; take wound-culture swabs; swab struggling toddlers for strep; complete the pathology requisition, enter the specimen in the log, and package for the pathology courier.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed venipuncture on 1,633 outpatients in Dutch hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments with a 94.5% first-stick success rate and 0.6% mild adverse events, and produced samples analytically equivalent to manual draws.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The Aletta device autonomously executes the full draw sequence - loading pre-labeled tubes from a cartridge, alcohol prep, ultrasound/Doppler vein selection, tourniquet, needle insertion, tube filling and inversion, bandaging and sample storage - with one healthcare professional supervising up to three devices.

sources.title: Automated Phlebotomy Firm Vitestro Eyes 2027 Commercial Launch of Robotic Blood Draw Device (360Dx)
sources.claim: The Aletta system is CE-marked and has been placed in hospitals in the Netherlands and ...; the vendor targets outpatient phlebotomy departments at academic and community hospitals, and 110 of 1,743 subjects were screened out because no suitable vein was found.

sources.system: BC·ROBO-8000/8001 Automated Tube Selecting and Labeling System
sources.title: Laboratory tube labeling system - BC·ROBO-8001RFID - Techno Medica (MedicalExpo)
sources.claim: Techno Medica's BC-ROBO systems automatically select and barcode-label blood collection tubes per the electronic test request and output a complete patient kit with worklist, automating the labeling/logging step of specimen preparation in hospital phlebotomy rooms and clinics.

It substantiates the 'log the specimens and prepare them for testing' component of this task - same objects (barcoded collection tubes), same accuracy requirement (patient-ID matching), in the same hospital outpatient collection setting.

sources.title: cobas p 512 and 612 pre-analytical systems (SelectScience)
sources.claim: Roche cobas p 512/612 pre-analytical systems autonomously perform sorting, centrifugation, decapping, aliquoting, barcode registration and archiving of primary specimen tubes in clinical laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-analytical specimen processing. Covers the 'prepare them for testing' step for collected blood tubes - identical objects (barcoded primary tubes) presented to the machine on racks.

sources.title: Performance of Copan WASP for Routine Urine Microbiology (Journal of Clinical Microbiology)
sources.claim: The Copan WASP/WASPLab robotic specimen processor performs fully automated workup of urine specimen containers - barcode reading, decapping, calibrated inoculation and streaking of plates - in routine clinical microbiology laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receipt, identification and pre-analytical preparation of urine containers. Same specimen type and containers as the clinic urine instance; substantiates logging (barcode capture) and preparation for testing once the container is presented to the machine.

sources.claim: The LINGCAI-II robot performed automatic oropharyngeal swab sampling on 116 COVID-19 patients at a purpose-set robot sampling workstation, completing the whole sampling process, including handling the swab and sample tube, without manual assistance.

tasks.label: Show patients to examination rooms and prepare them for the physician.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary care/urgent care office: MA calls a cooperative ambulatory adult from the waiting room, verifies identity, walks them down the corridor to an open exam room, takes height/weight and a full vital-sign set (BP with correct cuff size, pulse, temp, SpO2), records chief complaint, medications and allergies in the EMR, seats the patient and tells the physician the room is ready. No undressing needed.

Specialty visit or exam requiring disrobing/positioning (derm, ob-gyn, ortho, minor procedure): MA rooms the patient, hands a gown and drape with instructions, sets up the room (instrument tray, supplies, table/stirrups/exam light), positions the patient on the table, and prepares the site or equipment the physician will use.

Pediatric office: MA escorts parent and child (infant through school age) back, weighs/measures a squirming child (infant length, head circumference, or standing height), takes temp and pulse, calms the child, undresses infant as needed, and readies the room for the physician.

Older adult or mobility-impaired patient: MA assists a patient with a walker, cane or wheelchair from waiting room to exam room at their pace, steadies or transfers them onto the exam table or leaves them in the chair, helps with coat/shoes/sleeve for BP, and takes vitals with hands-on positioning.

Patient with a communication barrier, anxiety/agitation, acute pain, or infection-control precautions: MA masks/gowns the patient or self, routes them to a specific room, adapts the intake (interpreter, family member, guardian), judges what to report immediately to the physician, and readies the patient under non-routine conditions.

sources.title: CLOi GuideBot | RSCGD20 | LG Business Solutions | LG USA
sources.claim: LG's CLOi GuideBot is a commercially sold autonomous guide robot that greets visitors and physically escorts them to a requested destination in a facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: visitor wayfinding/escort. It covers only the 'show patients to the exam room' leg of this task - leading a walking person along a mapped corridor route - and provides no patient preparation.

sources.system: LG CLOi guide robot in Bigwave Robotics hospital RaaS

sources.claim: Guide robots of this type are deployed in hospitals under a robotics-as-a-service program for patient guidance, including waiting outside examination rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital visitor/patient guidance. Same corridor-escort leg of the task in a real healthcare facility; these robots are described as handling non-medical guidance only.

sources.title: Giant Eagle to deploy higi health stations | Supermarket News
sources.claim: FDA-cleared automated health stations that physically take a person's blood pressure and pulse are deployed at scale and can push readings into hospital EHRs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vital-sign capture. A fixed station that a seated person presents an arm to performs cuff inflation and measurement under machine control - the physical core of the 'prepare the patient' step - but does no escorting, gowning or positioning.

sources.title: Implementation of a New Kiosk Technology for Blood Pressure Management in a Family Medicine Clinic (WWAMI Region PRN)
sources.claim: A family medicine clinic implemented a self-service blood pressure kiosk that took over part of MA vital-sign work; it cut MA rooming time by only about 1.5 minutes per patient, MAs still entered values in the EMR and frequently rechecked readings, and some patients could not use it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-clinic vital-sign measurement. It measures directly how much of the rooming task an automated station absorbs: a slice of vitals only, with MA rechecks and continued MA rooming.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark

sources.claim: A robot performed a clinical physical procedure on a seated cooperative person's body autonomously at a purpose-built station using vision and force control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous swab sampling on a seated patient. Shows a robot can make controlled contact with a cooperative patient presented at a fixed station - the E1 form of hands-on patient prep - though it remains a single-purpose prototype station.

sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Robot-assisted gowning of a patient has been demonstrated only on a medical manikin in the laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting a hospital gown on a person. Directly relevant to the gowning part of patient prep, but performed on a manikin in a lab, not on real patients at clinic reliability.

sources.title: PTR Robots Introduces World's First Mobile Lifting Robot That Both Transfers and Rehabilitates Patients
sources.claim: Commercial patient lifting/transfer robots are operated by a caregiver rather than acting autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically assisting/transferring a patient. Bears on assisting frail patients onto an exam table; the device is caregiver-driven, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion.

tasks.label: Help physicians examine and treat patients, handing them instruments or materials or performing such tasks as giving injections or removing sutures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine office visit in a clinic exam room: the MA stays with the physician as a second pair of hands - positions and drapes the patient, adjusts the table and light, hands over otoscope specula, tongue depressors, gloves, gauze, swabs and specimen containers on spoken or anticipated request, holds and labels specimens, cleans up afterward.

Administering a routine injection to a cooperative adult in a clinic: verify the order and patient, draw up or select the dose, choose and clean the deltoid/subQ site, inject (vaccine, B12, depo, allergy shot, TB skin test), dispose of the sharp, bandage, observe and document.

Injections and exam assistance with infants, young children, or frightened/uncooperative adult patients: comforting and distracting, positioning and gently holding a squirming child's arm or head while the physician examines or while the MA gives immunizations, then soothing and bandaging.

Assisting a physician with a minor in-office procedure (laceration repair, skin biopsy or excision, cryotherapy, joint injection, IUD insertion, colposcopy): set up the sterile tray and field, hand instruments and sutures to the physician as the procedure unfolds, hold retraction/light/gauze, receive specimens, apply the dressing.

Suture or staple removal and wound care under physician direction: inspect the healed wound, clean it, grasp and snip each suture knot or lift each staple, extract without dragging contaminated material through the skin, verify all material is out, apply steri-strips/dressing, document.

sources.title: Aletta - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a commercially launched (CE-marked) autonomous robotic phlebotomy device installed in European hospital and laboratory blood-draw centers; the patient's arm is placed in the device's cradle and the machine performs the whole draw, with one human supervisor overseeing up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture rather than injection. Transfer is close - same patient population, same arm, same aseptic needle insertion under imaging, same clinic setting - but it requires the arm to be brought to and fixtured in the machine.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: Aletta met its EU pivotal trial endpoints with 95% first-stick success across 609 participants, comparable to reported manual venipuncture first-stick rates of 93-97%, establishing worker-comparable reliability for the needle step when the arm is presented to the device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: blood draw. Cited to establish that an autonomous needle-on-arm procedure reaches human-comparable success rates when the patient's arm is fixtured at the machine.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi platform autonomously administered an intramuscular needle-free jet injection into a human's arm, identifying the patient and selecting the injection site itself, with no healthcare professional involved.

sources.title: Cobionix ready to expand with $3M for healthcare robotics - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Cobionix's current clinical platform CODI is teleoperated for its flagship ultrasound application, with autonomy and clinical pilots still forward-looking as of mid-2025; no autonomous clinical deployment is documented.

sources.developer: TU Munich / Klinikum rechts der Isar group (Wagner et al.)
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis | Communications Medicine
sources.claim: A research robotic scrub nurse that predicts and hands over surgical instruments from laparoscopic video reached only 71.54% correct anticipation/handover in a study built on 62 recorded cholecystectomies - a laboratory prototype well below the reliability a human assistant provides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handing instruments to a physician. Closest published system to the 'handing instruments' element of this task; cited as the ceiling of demonstrated capability, which falls short of worker quality.

sources.title: RoboNurse-VLA: Robotic Scrub Nurse System based on Vision-Language-Action Model
sources.claim: RoboNurse-VLA is a laboratory vision-language-action system that grasps surgical instruments from a tray and hands them over on the surgeon's spoken command; it is a research prototype with no clinical deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instrument handover to a clinician. Cited to bound what is demonstrated for the 'handing instruments' element; the demonstration is a bench setup, not an exam room with a patient present.

sources.title: Task Autonomous Medical Robot for Both Incision Stapling and Staples Removal
sources.claim: An autonomous robot that both staples surgical incisions and removes the staples afterward has been demonstrated only as a bench prototype, without patient use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: staple removal, the closest published analogue to suture removal. Cited to show this capability exists only as a laboratory prototype, not at clinic quality on patients.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling / wound redressing framework
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Robotic wound redressing (lifting tape and placing dressings) remains at the stage of laboratory evaluation on phantoms, anatomical models and skin samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wound dressing, a component of the suture-removal/wound-care instance. Cited as evidence that only laboratory-stage capability exists.

tasks.label: Perform routine laboratory tests and sample analyses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Physician-office lab bench: patient hands in a urine cup at the pass-through; MA dips a reagent strip, reads it on a Clinitek-type strip reader (or visually), sometimes spins the sample and sets up a microscopic/wet prep, then logs the result in the EMR and flags abnormals for the provider.

Rapid infectious-disease kit test in a clinic lab: swab in transport/extraction tube (strep A, flu A/B, COVID, RSV, mono); MA mixes reagents, applies drops to a cassette or inserts a cartridge in a POC analyzer, times the run, reads/interprets the line or readout, records and reports the result.

Point-of-care blood analysis in the exam room or office lab: capillary fingerstick or small whole-blood sample applied to a glucose meter, HbA1c cartridge (Afinion/DCA), lipid cassette, INR meter or hemoglobin/hematocrit analyzer; MA runs the device and records the value.

Specimen processing for send-out: accession and label blood tubes, centrifuge serum/plasma tubes, aliquot into transport tubes, verify sample integrity, store at correct temperature and package with requisitions for the reference-lab courier.

Other waived kit tests: urine hCG pregnancy test, fecal occult blood card or FIT, H. pylori, urine drug-screen cup; MA applies the sample, waits the timed interval, interprets and documents the result.

Daily/weekly quality control and instrument upkeep: run liquid control levels on each analyzer/meter, compare to acceptable ranges, log results, check reagent and strip lot numbers and expiry, calibrate, clean and troubleshoot out-of-range controls before patient testing resumes.

sources.system: Sysmex UN-Series (UC-3500 / UF-5000) automated urinalysis line
sources.title: Sysmex UN-Series urinalysis analyser
sources.claim: Fully automated urinalysis lines run reagent-strip chemistry and flow-cytometry sediment analysis on rack-loaded urine tubes, with rule-based automatic reflex to sediment and LIS reporting, in hospital laboratories.

sources.title: Panther Fusion Respiratory Virus Assays for the detection of influenza and other respiratory viruses (PMC)
sources.claim: A fully automated random-access molecular analyzer performs extraction, PCR and result reporting for respiratory viruses (flu A/B, RSV, SARS-CoV-2) from specimen tubes loaded in the instrument's racks.

sources.title: Cepheid Introduces GeneXpert Infinity-48 System
sources.claim: A commercial robotic gantry system loads and unloads cartridges from a conveyor into analysis modules and reports results, automating cartridge-based rapid tests (including strep A, flu, COVID) at over 1,300 tests per day.

sources.title: LabCorp is first US laboratory to offer molecular testing with new fully automated cobas 8800 system from Roche
sources.claim: Fully automated molecular systems in production clinical labs run patient specimens with only a few user interactions per run and many hours of walk-away time.

sources.title: A high-throughput test for diabetes care: An evaluation of the next generation Roche Cobas c 513 hemoglobin A1C assay
sources.claim: A dedicated automated analyzer measures HbA1c on rack-loaded blood samples at high throughput with validated accuracy in clinical laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Same measurement the medical assistant runs on a POC HbA1c cartridge; the analyzer performs the full assay on a presented blood tube and reports the value.

sources.title: XN-330 Automated Hematology Analyzer | Sysmex America
sources.claim: Compact automated hematology analyzers marketed for physician offices and clinics sample directly from capped tubes via cap piercing, with integrated rack sampling and automatic rerun/reflex.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the hemoglobin/hematocrit and CBC work medical assistants run on office analyzers, performed automatically from a presented tube.

sources.title: cobas p 512 and 612 pre-analytical systems | SelectScience
sources.claim: Commercial pre-analytical automation systems mechanize pre-sorting, centrifugation, decapping, aliquoting into barcoded secondary tubes and sorting/archiving of clinical specimens.

sources.system: Cobot pre-analytical workcell (commercial cobots plus specialized modules)
sources.developer: Tregub et al. (centralized medical laboratory implementation)
sources.title: Collaborative Robotic Systems for Pre-Analytical Processing of Biological Specimens in a Medical Laboratory (Diagnostics 2026)
sources.claim: Collaborative robots were integrated into the pre-analytical workflow of a large centralized medical laboratory, performing decapping, barcode verification, analyzer loading, aliquoting and sorting with LIS integration and an 87% reduction in labor ....

sources.title: OC-SENSOR PLEDIA | Faecal Testing | Eiken Chemical
sources.claim: A fully automated benchtop analyzer performs fecal immunochemical testing on batches of loaded sample collection tubes with a single start command.
sources.transferJustification: Automates the occult-blood/FIT test medical assistants run from a patient-collected stool sample, from loaded sample tube to reported result.

sources.title: Automation for lateral flow rapid tests: Protocol for an open-source fluid handler and applications to dengue and African swine fever tests
sources.claim: An open-source liquid-handling robot automates execution of cassette-based lateral-flow rapid tests, delivering sample and running buffer from a 48-tube rack to each cassette's wells, with QR-coded sample-to-result traceability.
sources.transferJustification: Same cassette rapid-test format and handling steps (sample plus buffer into cassette wells) as the strep/flu/COVID/pregnancy kits medical assistants run.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device – CAP TODAY
sources.claim: A CE-marked autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs the whole blood draw using AI-driven ultrasound guidance and is being introduced in European hospitals and laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (obtaining a blood specimen from a patient) in a structured healthcare facility; it collects the sample but performs no test or analysis, so it cannot by itself complete this task's instances.

tasks.label: Prepare and administer medications as directed by a physician.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult injection in a clinic exam room: flu/Tdap/shingles vaccine or B12, Depo-Provera, Toradol, testosterone. MA verifies order/allergies, uses a prefilled syringe or single-dose vial, injects deltoid or gluteal site, applies bandage, disposes of sharps, documents.

Preparing and labeling medication for the physician's immediate use during a procedure (draw up 1% lidocaine, reconstitute a vial, load a syringe for a joint injection or laceration repair) and handing it off on the tray; no patient contact by the MA.

Pediatric immunization visit: 2-5 injections into thigh or deltoid of an infant or uncooperative toddler held by a parent, with distraction, restraint, comfort measures, weight/age-appropriate product selection, and post-shot observation.

Non-injected routes given in the office: an oral dose (antibiotic, ibuprofen, oral contrast), a nebulizer treatment with mask/mouthpiece fitted to a wheezing patient, topical anesthetic or ointment on skin, or ophthalmic/otic drops instilled by the MA.

Allergy immunotherapy or intradermal skin test: pull the patient-specific extract vial set, verify the escalating dose and schedule, give subcutaneous injections in both arms or an intradermal PPD wheal, then observe 20-30 minutes for reaction.

Injectable requiring reconstitution or weight-based dose calculation before administration (ceftriaxone with lidocaine diluent, Bicillin, pediatric dosing), drawn from powder/diluent vials and given as a viscous 1-3 mL IM injection.

sources.title: Waterloo startup performs first ever robotic intramuscular injection | Waterloo News
sources.claim: Cobionix's Cobi robot autonomously performed an intramuscular injection on a patient using needle-free jet injection, with LiDAR-based site selection and no clinician involvement.

sources.title: Cobi robot autonomously performs needle-less vaccinations - New Atlas
sources.claim: The Cobi workflow has the patient come to the robot unit, present ID to its camera/touchscreen, follow on-screen positioning instructions, receive the single-dose injection, after which the capsule is dropped into a sanitary waste compartment.

sources.system: Autonomous needle-free vaccine injection robot (Tongji University)
sources.title: China releases its first autonomous intelligent robot for needle-free vaccine injection - Global Times
sources.claim: Tongji University released an autonomous needle-free vaccination robot that identifies the injection site on the human body via 3D modeling, intended for hospitals, community clinics and mobile vaccination vehicles.

sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomously performs the complete needle procedure on a seated patient's arm - tourniquet, skin prep, ultrasound-guided needle insertion, tube handling and ... - in hospital blood-collection rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture. It is the same physical act class as giving an injection - aseptic prep and controlled needle placement in a seated outpatient's arm, sharps handling, bandaging - and demands more targeting precision (a vein) than deltoid/subcutaneous injection, in the same kind of outpatient care facility.

sources.title: Aletta for Laboratory specialists - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta's clinical performance in the A.D.O.P.T. trial across four Dutch hospitals was a 95% first-time success rate with 0.6% hemolysis, with one trained supervisor able to oversee up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (venipuncture): establishes that autonomous needle procedures on human arms reach clinician-comparable reliability under limited supervision, the quality bar an injection instance requires.

sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device - phlebotomy.com
sources.claim: Aletta is CE-marked and being placed into routine use in European hospitals, with US multi-center trials under way.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (venipuncture); establishes commercial deployment rather than one-off demonstration.

sources.title: Omnicell i.v.STATION Non-hazardous Compounding Robot
sources.claim: Omnicell's i.v.STATION robot prepares ready-to-administer syringes and admixtures from vials completely hands-free inside an enclosed compounding cabinet installed in hospital pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile dose preparation. It is the same manipulation the MA performs when preparing a medication - selecting the vial, drawing the ordered dose into a syringe, and labeling it - at equal or greater precision.

sources.title: Robotic chemotherapy compounding: A multicenter productivity approach
sources.claim: KIRO Oncology is a robotic system in routine hospital pharmacy production that manipulates a syringe to withdraw a dose from a vial and fill final syringes or bags, producing up to 8 bags and 4 syringes per cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sterile syringe preparation from vials, peer-reviewed multicenter production data; identical objects (vials, syringes, labels) and higher accuracy requirements than an office lidocaine or reconstitution draw-up.

sources.title: Early Alert: Automated Compounding System Issue from Omnicell | FDA
sources.claim: FDA communications about labeling of syringes produced by i.v.STATION confirm the compounding robots are in active clinical use producing labeled sterile filled syringes at US customer sites.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (sterile syringe preparation); cited as independent regulatory confirmation of real-world deployment.

tasks.label: Authorize drug refills and provide prescription information to pharmacies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Change dressings on wounds.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-procedure/post-op dressing change in a physician's office exam room: MA gloves up, peels adhesive tape and gauze off a sutured incision or excision site on the trunk or a limb, inspects for drainage or infection, cleanses with saline/antiseptic, applies fresh sterile gauze and tape, and documents wound appearance. Patient seated or on an exam table, often flinching or asking questions.

Chronic wound dressing change in a clinic/wound-care setting (diabetic foot ulcer, venous leg ulcer, pressure injury): removal of an exudate-soaked, sometimes adherent dressing, irrigation/cleansing of an irregular open wound bed, measuring, applying topical agent and packing or hydrocolloid/alginate, then securing with a wrap or compression layers on a curved limb.

Minor acute wound in urgent care or family practice: abrasion, laceration, second-degree burn, or the site after suture/staple removal. MA cleans the area, applies ointment and a non-adherent pad, secures it with tape or roller gauze. Patient may be a child or in pain and moving during the procedure.

Awkward site or low-mobility patient in a clinic or long-term-care/skilled-nursing setting: sacral, buttock, perineal, axillary or between-toes wound, or a drain/ostomy-adjacent dressing. Requires repositioning or holding the patient, working in a skin fold or on a soft shifting surface, often with a second staff member assisting.

Home visit by a medical assistant working for a house-call practice or home-health group: dressing change performed on a patient in a recliner or bed in a private home, with variable lighting, clutter, pets and family members present, supplies laid out on whatever surface is available.

sources.system: Autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing (Inspire dexterous hand + manipulator + F/T sensor)
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab / ARCLab) with Cornell
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: UCSD lab framework automates two subtasks of wound redressing (initiating adhesive tape detachment via force-feedback imitation learning, and wrinkle-free tape placement) on skin phantoms and a human arm; the paper states tape grasping is still done manually or by teleoperation and that wound cleaning/debridement automation is still missing, i.e. no whole autonomous dressing change exists.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the target task, but only subtasks are automated on phantoms; it establishes the state of the art rather than completion of a dressing change.

sources.developer: UC San Diego (Liang, Zhang, Liu, Richter, Yip)
sources.title: AutoPeel: Adhesion-aware Safe Peeling Trajectory Optimization for Robotic Wound Care
sources.claim: First reported robotic system for wound dressing ...: adhesion-aware peeling trajectory optimization validated in differentiable simulation and on a benchtop robot with adhesive/phantom samples; covers only the removal step, with no cleansing or reapplication.
sources.transferJustification: Dressing removal is the first step of a dressing change; only that step is shown, on bench samples, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole task.

sources.system: DLR MIRO robot with MICA instrument actuating an ERBEJET 2 waterjet probe
sources.title: Robotic waterjet wound debridement – Workflow adaption for clinical application and systematic evaluation of a novel technology
sources.claim: A surgical robot autonomously planned and executed waterjet debridement (wound cleaning) paths on a porcine skin wound model in a preclinical laboratory comparison against clinicians; the authors state in vivo trials are still needed.
sources.transferJustification: Wound cleansing is a component of a dressing change, but this was done on ex vivo porcine skin in a research rig, with no dressing removal, reapplication, or live-patient validation.

sources.title: Medtech company Vitestro pulls US$70M together for autonomous blood draw tech
sources.claim: CE-marked autonomous phlebotomy device into which a patient places an arm; the machine locates the vein with ultrasound, draws blood and applies an adhesive bandage to the puncture site without a phlebotomist performing the steps.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest deployed patient-contact capability: autonomous placement of an adhesive bandage on a fixtured arm. It does not remove an existing dressing, cleanse or assess a wound, or reach wounds elsewhere on the body, so it does not substantiate a dressing change.

sources.system: Humanoid surrogate platform for dexterous medical interventions
sources.title: Humanoids in Hospitals: A Technical Study of Humanoid Surrogates for Dexterous Medical Interventions
sources.claim: Humanoid surrogates proposed for dexterous medical interventions (ultrasound, auscultation, suture throw on a training ...) are driven by human operators, indicating dexterous patient-contact clinical manipulation remains teleoperated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that humanoid platforms aimed at hands-on clinical tasks operate under teleoperation, so they cannot support an autonomous dressing-change judgment.

tasks.label: Inventory and order medical, lab, or office supplies or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekly count of the clinic's central supply/stock room: open wire shelving and bins of gloves, gauze, syringes, needles, specimen tubes, table paper and drapes; count on-hand against par levels, note what is short, then place the order online with the distributor (e.g., McKesson, Henry Schein).

Between-patient or end-of-day check of supplies in 6-12 exam and treatment rooms: opening cabinets and drawers, checking wall dispensers, mixed loose items and partially used boxes, tallying what is low and adding it to the office order list.

Inventory of lab and medication-refrigerator stock: reagents, urinalysis strips, controls, vaccines and injectables; read lot numbers and expiration dates on individual vials/boxes, pull expired stock, record counts on the vaccine/lab log, and order replacements.

Front-office and general office supply check: copy paper, toner, forms, chart labels, gowns and paper goods in a storage closet or cabinet; count remaining stock and submit the online office-supply order.

Receiving a delivery and reconciling it: open shipping cartons, verify items, quantities and lots against the packing slip and purchase order, note damage or backorders, log the receipt into the inventory list, and reorder shortfalls.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously drives grocery store aisles and scans shelves multiple ... capture inventory/stock condition, deployed across 17 Harmons stores after a five-store pilot; it cut out-of-stocks 20% on high-velocity items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory. Transfer to clinic stockroom counting: same class of objects (labeled boxed consumables on shelving in an institution-controlled facility), same output (on-hand counts and low-stock signals that drive reordering).

sources.title: Simbe upgrades vision platform with AI-powered capabilities - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Simbe's vision platform detects products running low on shelf using volumetric and depth sensing, producing early low-stock signals that drive proactive replenishment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf stock-level assessment feeding replenishment orders; the counting-and-reorder loop is the same one a medical assistant performs against par levels.

sources.title: ProMat 2025: Verity introduces AI-assisted item counting feature for picking locations - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Verity's fully autonomous indoor drones automate item, box and case counting at warehouse picking and storage locations and flag inventory discrepancies; systems are in commercial warehouse use (e.g., Scholl replaced multi-day manual counts of 12,000 pallet locations).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting. Transfer: identifying and counting cartons/items at labeled storage locations inside a human work facility is the perceptual core of stockroom inventory; output is a verified count used for replenishment.

sources.title: Reducing Inventory Cycle Counting Time with a Drone-Powered Monitoring Solution | SupplyChainBrain
sources.claim: Gather AI's drones fly autonomously through warehouses without GPS, Wi-Fi or infrastructure changes to perform inventory cycle counting, and are deployed at 3PL, retail distribution, manufacturing and air cargo operators including GEODIS, NFI Industries and AAFES.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cycle counting of stored goods in a working facility; same output (accurate on-hand counts by location) as the stockroom inventory step of this task.

sources.title: Robot Employs RFID to Manage Warehouse Inventory - RFID Journal

instances.label: Resting 12-lead EKG in a primary care or cardiology office exam room: MA explains the test, has the patient disrobe and lie on the table, preps/shaves skin, palpates landmarks and applies 10 adhesive electrodes (including precordial sites under breast tissue), attaches lead wires, coaches the patient to stay still, re-runs if artifact or lead reversal, then prints/uploads the tracing to the EHR and flags abnormals for the physician.

Vision and hearing screening for school, sports, occupational or pediatric physicals in a clinic hallway or exam room: Snellen/photoscreener acuity, color vision, pure-tone audiometry with headphones and tympanometry - positioning the patient, fitting headphones/occluder, coaching a child or non-English speaker, and recording results.

Limited-scope radiography in an urgent care, orthopedic, podiatry or chiropractic office: MA positions the patient's extremity, chest or spine against the bucky or on the table, applies shielding and markers, selects technique, makes the exposure, checks the image for positioning/motion, repeats if needed, and sends to PACS.

Spirometry / pulmonary function screening in an office or occupational-health clinic: assemble mouthpiece and filter, apply nose clip, demonstrate and loudly coach the forced expiratory maneuver, judge acceptability/repeatability of the curves, repeat maneuvers, and print results (sometimes pre/post bronchodilator).

Ambulatory monitor hook-up in a cardiology or primary care office: prep skin and apply Holter/event-monitor electrodes or an adhesive patch (or fit an ambulatory blood-pressure cuff), program the recorder, secure leads, instruct the patient on the diary and return, and later download the data.

Other point-of-care diagnostic devices used directly on the patient in the exam room: pulse oximetry probe, fingerstick glucose/HbA1c/hemoglobin/INR meters, ankle-brachial index Doppler, non-mydriatic retinal photo for diabetic screening - obtaining the sample or signal from the patient, operating the device, and recording the result.

tasks.label: Examine equipment to detect leaks, worn or loose parts, or other indications of disrepair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prep/pack station in a hospital sterile processing department: tech inspects a decontaminated mixed tray of 30-80 rigid stainless instruments (hemostats, needle holders, scissors, retractors, rongeurs) under lighted magnification for cracks, pitting, corrosion, burrs, chipped tips and residual soil, and functionally checks hinges, box locks, ratchet engagement, jaw/tip alignment and sharpness, setting damaged items aside for repair.

Endoscopy/GI decontamination room: leak test of a flexible endoscope after each patient use - attach the leak tester to the venting connector, pressurize, angulate the tip and observe for bubbles (or run an automated dry leak test), and pull the scope from service if a leak is found.

SPD inspection bench: periodic internal channel inspection of flexible endoscopes and lumened rigid instruments with a borescope, looking for scratches, gouges, delamination, debris, fluid and channel damage, and documenting findings per scope.

SPD prep area: inspection of powered and accessory equipment - electrosurgical pencils and bipolar cords, fiber-optic light cables, camera heads, suction and insufflation tubing, drill/saw handpieces and hoses - for frayed cords, cracked or breached insulation, broken fibers, worn couplings and leaking connections, including energizing a handpiece to check function.
Daily/weekly integrity testing of a prevacuum steam sterilizer: run the vacuum leak test cycle on the empty chamber, read the leak rate, log it and report an out-of-range result for service.

Checks of non-instrument equipment before reissue: washer-disinfector spray arms and door gaskets, case carts and wheels, rigid container gaskets/latches/filters, and mobile patient-care items (IV pumps and poles, beds, wheelchairs, suction regulators) examined for damage, missing or loose parts and leaking connections in an equipment room or on the unit.

tasks.label: Check sterile supplies to ensure that they are not outdated.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine sweep of the sterile storage room in a hospital SPD/sterile core: rows of open wire shelving holding peel-pouched instrument sets, wrapped trays with load/expiry labels, and manufacturer-sterile items. The tech handles each package, reads the printed date, checks the sterile barrier (tears, wetness, seal), rotates stock FIFO, pulls outdated packs for reprocessing, and documents the round.

Case cart assembly / OR sterile core picking: tech pulls items against a preference card or pick list, verifying each item's expiration date and package condition as it goes onto the cart, under time pressure before scheduled cases; mixed item types (pouches, boxes, trays, implants).

Point-of-use verification during procedure or OR setup: as sterile packs are staged and opened onto the field, the tech confirms each pack is in date and the barrier intact, rejecting and replacing any outdated or compromised item within minutes.

Periodic expiration audit of unit-level stock across many small locations: clinic exam-room drawers, crash carts, procedure carts, ED bins holding small quantities of loose, mixed sterile items; expired items pulled, replacements stocked, audit sheet signed.

Central storeroom receiving and bulk stock check: incoming cases and cartons from distributors checked for dating on receipt, bulk boxes on racking checked during cycle counts, short-dated or expired cases segregated for return, remaining stock put away FIFO.

tasks.label: Organize and assemble routine or specialty surgical instrument trays or other sterilized supplies, filling special requests as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine tray assembly in a hospital sterile processing department (SPD) prep-and-pack area: tech pulls a rack of clean, dried general/standard instruments (e.g., minor, basic, C-section sets, 25-80 items), verifies each against the count sheet in the tracking system, arranges ring instruments open on a stringer, lays out remaining instruments in the tray with tip protectors and absorbent mat, adds the chemical indicator and internal paperwork, then closes the tray in a rigid container or wraps it and labels it.

Specialty/complex set assembly: orthopedic and spine sets with implant caddies, screw racks and torque handles, vendor loaner trays that arrive with an unfamiliar count sheet, laparoscopic and robotic instruments that must be reassembled from multiple parts (sheath, insert, handle), rigid scopes, powered drills with attachments and delicate microsurgical/ophthalmic instruments. Requires consulting IFUs, matching serialized parts and multi-layer stacked containers.

Peel-pack packaging of individual instruments and small item groups: select the item(s) from clean stock, choose the correct pouch size, insert with tip protection, add indicator, run through the validated heat sealer, label with load/lot and item identity. Dozens of pouches per shift, mixed item types and sizes.

Assembling case carts / picking sterilized supplies for the day's scheduled cases: read the pick list/preference card, pull wrapped trays, containers, peel packs, basins, linen packs and disposables from the sterile store shelving, check expiry and integrity of each package, load them onto the correct case cart in a set order, and stage the cart for delivery to the OR.

Urgent/special request: the OR calls for a specific sterilized package or set mid-schedule or as an add-on; the tech locates the item in the sterile store or in process, prioritizes it, checks the package, and dispatches it to the requesting room within minutes.

Special request that requires building a non-standard set: a surgeon wants extra or substituted instruments added to a tray, or a one-off custom tray/pack built from stock instruments per a written request, documented in the tracking system and packaged for sterilization.

instances.label: Hospital central sterile processing department (CSSD/SPD): technician stages wrapped instrument trays, rigid containers and peel packs on sterilizer racks/loading carts, pushes the cart into a large double-door steam sterilizer, selects the correct cycle (prevac 270F, gravity, etc.), starts it, unloads after the cycle, allows the hot load to cool on the clean side, and records load number, cycle data and tray contents in the instrument tracking system (T-DOC, Censitrac, SPM).

Dental office, physician office, veterinary/podiatry clinic or small ambulatory surgery center: staff member loads pouches and instrument cassettes into a tabletop or small chamber autoclave, fills the reservoir with distilled water, runs the appropriate cycle, unloads and dries pouches, and writes/prints a cycle log entry with load contents, date, operator and indicator result.

Clinical or research laboratory: preparer autoclaves mixed loads — glassware, pipette tips, culture media bottles, and red-bag biohazard waste — in a floor-standing lab autoclave, choosing liquid vs. gravity vs. vacuum cycles, handling spill trays and hot liquids, and logging each run (load contents, cycle parameters, indicator/spore test results) in the autoclave use log.

Routine sterilizer quality assurance and maintenance in any of the above settings: daily Bowie-Dick/air-removal test packs and leak tests, placing and incubating biological indicator process challenge devices, wiping the chamber and door gasket, cleaning drain strainers, descaling/flushing reservoirs, changing printer paper and filters, checking recorder charts, and completing the maintenance and test log.

Point-of-use / immediate-use steam sterilization in an OR sub-sterile room: a single dropped or urgently needed instrument or tray is cleaned, placed in an IUSS container, run through a short flash cycle on a small sterilizer while the case waits, then transferred hot to the sterile field, with the cycle and item documented for the patient record.

tasks.label: Clean instruments to prepare them for sterilization.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital sterile processing department (SPD) decontamination room: a case cart of general/orthopedic instrument trays arrives from the OR with dried blood and tissue. The tech sorts and disassembles instruments, rinses off gross soil, brushes hinges/box locks and serrations at the sink, runs an ultrasonic cycle, then racks the set and runs a washer-disinfector cycle.

Hospital SPD decontamination room: complex lumened and minimally-invasive devices - laparoscopic instruments, cannulated orthopedic reamers, suction tips, da Vinci EndoWrist robotic arms. Requires disassembly, enzymatic soak, syringe flushing and brushing of narrow channels per device IFU, then mechanical washing on a lumen/irrigation rack.

Endoscopy reprocessing room: a soiled flexible endoscope (colonoscope, gastroscope, bronchoscope) is leak-tested, immersed in enzymatic detergent, channels brushed and flushed, ports and valves cleaned, then connected into an automated endoscope reprocessor for cleaning and high-level disinfection.

Hospital SPD: non-immersible or delicate items - powered drill/saw handpieces and battery housings, camera heads, fiber-optic light cords, microsurgical and ophthalmic instruments. Cleaned by wiping and controlled hand-cleaning per IFU because they cannot withstand standard mechanical washing.

Dental office, physician clinic, or ambulatory surgery center sterilization area: small batches of used instruments (often in cassettes) are hand-scrubbed or placed in an ultrasonic bath / tabletop instrument washer, rinsed and dried before packaging for the tabletop autoclave.

Operating room or procedure room, point-of-use treatment: during and immediately after the case, instruments are wiped with sterile water, lumens flushed, gross soil removed, and instruments kept moist with pre-treatment spray or gel before transport to decontamination.

tasks.label: Disinfect and sterilize equipment, such as respirators, hospital beds, or oxygen or dialysis equipment, using sterilizers, aerators, or washers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital sterile processing (SPD) decontamination side: soiled surgical instrument sets return from the OR on case carts; the tech sorts/opens instruments into wire baskets, racks them on wash-carts, selects and runs the washer-disinfector (plus ultrasonic/cart washer) cycle, then unloads on the clean side.

Delicate, lumened and channeled devices at the decontamination sink: flexible endoscopes, laparoscopic and robotic instruments - leak testing, manual brushing and flushing of channels, wiping, attaching the correct channel connectors and loading the automated endoscope reprocessor/ultrasonic, then drying and hanging.

Steam sterilization runs: building sterilizer loads of wrapped trays, peel packs and rigid containers onto sterilizer carts, placing chemical/biological indicators, selecting and running the autoclave cycle, unloading the hot cart, cooling, and verifying indicators and cycle records.

Low-temperature sterilization of heat-sensitive items - vaporized hydrogen peroxide/gas plasma (STERRAD, V-PRO) or ethylene oxide with an aerator - for respirator and ventilator/anesthesia components, cables, cameras and scopes; loading the chamber, running the cycle, and handling the aeration stage.

Bulky washable patient equipment in the equipment-processing/bed area: hospital bed frames, mattresses, stretchers, wheelchairs and transport carts are cleaned and disinfected, either in a bed/trolley washer-disinfector or by hand with germicidal solution, then stored for reissue.

Non-immersible electro-medical equipment: ventilators, oxygen concentrators and regulators, infusion pumps and dialysis machines are wiped down externally with hospital disinfectant at the bedside or in an equipment room, filters/circuits changed, and the machine's internal disinfection cycle started and verified.

tasks.label: Purge wastes from equipment by connecting equipment to water sources and flushing water through systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sterile processing decontamination room: worker retrieves soiled cannulated/lumened surgical instruments (suction tips, laparoscopic and robotic instruments, orthopedic reamers) from case carts, flushes each lumen with a water flush gun or syringe at the sink, then seats them on injector/irrigation manifolds in the ultrasonic irrigator and washer-disinfector so pumped water flushes the internal channels; verifies effluent runs clear.

Endoscopy reprocessing suite: bedside pre-clean flushing of detergent/water through the scope's air-water, biopsy and suction channels immediately after the case, then in the decon room leak-test, manual channel flush at the sink, hook the model-specific channel connector tubes to the automated endoscope reprocessor, and run the cycle that flushes water/detergent/disinfectant and final rinse water through every channel.

Soiled utility / decon room: surgical fluid-waste handling — docking a mobile suction/fluid rover to its docking station so waste is offloaded and the canisters flushed with fresh water and detergent, or capping and loading reusable suction canisters into a safety station that empties, washes and rinses them; flushing the hopper/drain line afterward.

Dialysis clinic / equipment room: connecting hemodialysis machines and portable RO carts to the treated-water supply and drain, placing dialysate concentrate connectors in the rinse ports, and running the rinse plus heat or chemical disinfection cycles that purge residual disinfectant, dialysate and waste from the machine hydraulics; testing for residual before return to service.

Ward/clinic utility rooms and treatment areas: flushing miscellaneous reusable equipment with water — suction collection bottles and tubing, bedpans/commode pots, wound-irrigation and hydrotherapy equipment, dental unit waterlines and evacuation lines — either at the flushing sink or by loading them into a bedpan/utensil washer-disinfector and running its flush cycle.

sources.claim: PROCECO RDB-700 is a commercial six-axis robotic cell that positions a high-pressure water lance into the machined holes and internal cavities of a fixtured workpiece and flushes chips and debris out, then blows the part dry — i.e., a robot connecting a water source to internal passages and purging wastes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-pressure water flushing of machined parts. Transfer: the physical act is the same as purging lumened medical devices — mate a nozzle/lance to a small internal port on a fixtured workpiece and flush water through the channel until debris is cleared, at sub-millimetre positioning accuracy, inside an enclosed water-handling cell.

sources.claim: Scott Automation's Robofuel autonomously locates a vehicle's fuel tank port with vision and couples a fluid nozzle to it to transfer fluid, supervised remotely, at mine refuelling bays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous refuelling. Transfer: it substantiates the 'connecting equipment to a fluid source' element — perceiving a standard port, driving a coupling into it without spillage, and running a controlled fluid transfer — done in a purpose-built bay where the equipment is brought to the machine, the same presentation assumed at E1.

tasks.label: Maintain records of inventory or equipment usage and order medical instruments or supplies when inventory is low.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Central sterile processing technician logs instrument-set usage and tray counts in the department's instrument tracking software (e.g., SPM, Censitrac) during/after each shift, noting which sets are in circulation and which consumables are running low.

Technician performs a periodic par-level review of disposable supplies (peel pouches, chemical/biological indicators, filters, wrap, gowns) in the sterile storage room and enters the resulting counts into the hospital inventory system.

Technician submits requisitions or purchase requests through the hospital's materials management/ERP system (e.g., Workday, Lawson, Infor) or notifies supply chain/purchasing when items fall below reorder points, and follows up on backorders and substitutions.
Technician maintains usage, check-out/check-in, rental and service records for movable medical equipment (infusion pumps, scopes, warming units), reconciling logs with biomed and rental vendors.
Small clinic, ambulatory surgery center, or dental office: technician keeps a paper log or spreadsheet of supply usage and phones/emails a vendor rep or distributor to reorder when stock is low.

tasks.label: Start equipment and observe gauges and equipment operation to detect malfunctions and to ensure equipment is operating to prescribed standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/large ASC central sterile processing: technician loads a rack or cart of wrapped trays into a large pre-vacuum steam sterilizer, selects the cycle program, presses start, then watches chamber temperature/pressure gauges and the cycle printout during the run, confirms exposure time/temperature met, and releases the load.

Decontamination area: starting washer-disinfectors, ultrasonic cleaners and cart washers - checking detergent/chemistry levels and water temperature and pressure gauges, selecting and starting cycles, watching for low-chemistry or thermal-disinfection alarms during the run, and confirming the cycle finished to standard.

Low-temperature sterilizers (VH2O2/plasma, formaldehyde, EtO) and automated endoscope reprocessors: install cartridge/chemistry, connect or load heat-sensitive scopes and instruments, start the cycle, and monitor vacuum/pressure/concentration readouts, leak-test results and error codes for the duration.

Start-of-day and per-cycle equipment quality checks: run the air-removal (Bowie-Dick) and vacuum leak-test cycles on each sterilizer, read the test result, place and later incubate/read a biological-indicator challenge pack, check and file printouts, log gauge readings, and hold the machine if a test fails.

Small facility (dental office, physician clinic, small ambulatory surgery center, veterinary or lab setting): check/fill the distilled-water reservoir of a tabletop autoclave or small ultrasonic unit, load pouches, latch the door, start the cycle, watch the temperature/pressure dial and cycle-complete/error indicator, and record the cycle in a log.

Malfunction response during operation: an alarm sounds or a gauge reads out of range mid-cycle (steam pressure drop, failed vacuum, door seal leak, water supply fault); technician stops/aborts the cycle, removes and reprocesses the load, does basic checks, tags the unit out of service and notifies biomed/service.

tasks.label: Stock crash carts or other medical supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restocking a crash/code cart after a code or at scheduled check in a hospital: pulling the used cart to the supply/pharmacy prep area, working a checklist to replace used medications, syringes, airway and IV supplies, checking every item's expiration date, confirming defibrillator/O2, closing drawers, applying a numbered tamper seal and documenting the restock.

Par-level replenishment of nursing-unit supply rooms and nurse servers: pushing a stock cart through occupied corridors, scanning/counting bins, placing dozens of heterogeneous items (glove boxes, syringes, dressings, IV sets, catheter kits) into labeled shelves/bins, front-rotating older stock and pulling expired items.

Building procedure/case carts in sterile processing or the OR core to a preference-card pick list: pulling instrument trays and disposables of many shapes and weights from human-height shelving onto a case cart, verifying counts and expirations, and staging the cart for the room.

Receiving and stocking the central supply storeroom: breaking down pallet and parcel deliveries, opening cases, putting cases and eaches on storeroom shelving and in bins in FIFO order, breaking down cardboard and updating inventory counts.

Stocking equipment-linked supplies in occupied clinical spaces: restocking exam/procedure room bins, ED bays, endoscopy or dialysis stations, and the supply drawers of mobile equipment carts, working around staff, patients, cords and parked equipment.

tasks.label: Assist hospital staff with patient care duties, such as providing transportation or setting up traction.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wheelchair transport of a stable patient inside the hospital (ambulatory outpatient going to imaging/therapy, or a discharge ride to the lobby). Tech fetches a chair, confirms patient identity, the patient can stand and seat themselves with minimal help, tech carries belongings/chart, navigates corridors and elevators, hands off at the destination, and returns the chair.

Stretcher or bed transport of a non-ambulatory but clinically stable patient between units (e.g., floor to radiology, unit-to-unit bed move). Nursing staff help slide/position the patient; the tech pushes the loaded stretcher or bed with an IV pole attached through corridors and elevators and returns it. Critically ill patients on drips/ventilators are accompanied by clinical staff and are not this occupation's work.

Hands-on assistance to nurses at the bedside with patient handling: boosting or repositioning a patient in bed, log-rolling, bed-to-chair transfer using a mechanical lift and sling, holding a limb during casting or dressing changes.

Setting up traction: attaching a Balkan/overhead frame and trapeze to the bed, threading rope over pulleys, applying a Buck's boot or connecting a skeletal traction bow, hanging the ordered weights free of the floor, and adjusting alignment per the physician's order.

Bringing patient-care equipment to the room and setting it up for use: specialty mattress or low-air-loss bed, infusion or feeding pump on a pole, sequential compression device, suction/oxygen regulator; plugging in, connecting tubing/cuffs, powering up and testing, then standing by to assist staff during care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Physician-office/clinic back office: process the day's incoming mail - collect it from the box or courier drop, slit and open mixed envelopes, remove and unfold contents (lab results, referrals, payer EOBs, checks), date-stamp, sort by recipient/document type, and place in staff trays or the transcription queue. Mixed sizes, staples, thick and delicate items.

Prepare outgoing mail in a medical office: print transcribed reports, patient letters and statements, match pages to the right recipient, fold, insert into windowed envelopes, seal, weigh, apply postage, and place in the outgoing bin or take to the post office. Includes occasional certified/return-receipt pieces.

Filing: file loose paper documents (lab reports, consults, consent forms, correspondence) into the correct patient chart in a filing cabinet or shelf file, or scan and index them into the EHR/EDMS; pull and refile charts for upcoming appointments. Documents arrive in mixed condition and must land in the right record.

Workstation keyboard work: type letters, forms and logs; key charges and diagnosis/procedure codes; complete CMS-1500/837 insurance claims in the practice-management or EHR system and submit them to the clearinghouse; correct rejections. Purely on-screen data entry and transmission at a desk.

Operating office machines in the clinic: photocopy stacks of chart pages, scan batches to PDF, fax signed reports to referring physicians, run the printer for report batches, plus loading paper, swapping toner and clearing jams.

Hospital HIM/transcription department: hand-carry completed reports, charts and dictation materials between the department and nursing units, physician mailboxes, radiology and the lab, and pick up items on the return leg; routine runs on a fixed internal route during the shift.

Independent community pharmacy: aide types free-text directions and auxiliary warning selections into an older or less-integrated pharmacy software package, adjusts label formatting, and prints the vial label plus monograph on a shared printer.

Same pharmacy counter, but the customer pays cash (occasionally a check): aide rings the sale, takes bills, makes change from the till and coin drawer, prints the receipt; sometimes an OTC item is added to the prescription sale.

Transaction requiring restricted handling or judgment: Schedule II/controlled prescription needing photo-ID check and log, a refrigerated item (insulin, vaccine) fetched from the fridge, an insurance rejection or price dispute, coupon/discount-card application, or a partial fill - resolved with the pharmacist while the customer waits.

Front-store / OTC register duty at or near the pharmacy counter: ringing up OTC analgesics, first-aid, vitamins, sundries and behind-the-counter pseudoephedrine (ID scan + electronic logbook), applying coupons, mixed cash and card tender, bagging.

Hospital outpatient, employee or clinic pharmacy window: discharge and staff prescriptions, copay collected by card or payroll deduction, receipt and signature, often after-hours or during shift-change rushes in an institution-controlled lobby.

Small independent or grocery-store pharmacy: one aide rings prescriptions and front-store goods on a single register between phone calls, takes delivery-driver payments, and opens/closes and reconciles the drawer.

Hospital or long-term-care pharmacy: logging receipts from central supply and outside vendors into the materials-management/inventory system, recording deliveries dispatched to nursing units and refill of automated dispensing cabinets, and maintaining delivery manifests.

Controlled-substance recordkeeping: entering CII receipts against DEA Form 222/CSOS records, maintaining the perpetual inventory log for scheduled drugs, and reconciling counts and invoices in the required record formats under pharmacist oversight.

Central-fill, mail-order or high-volume outpatient pharmacy: pallets/cases received at a dedicated receiving dock, cases opened and inducted, bulk stock put away in the stockroom, and dispensing automation (cells, canisters, carousels) replenished from bulk containers.

tasks.label: Compound, package, and label pharmaceutical products, under direction of pharmacist.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Community/retail chain pharmacy: pull the stock bottle for a high-volume oral solid (e.g., lisinopril, metformin), count the prescribed quantity, pour into the correct-size amber vial, apply the printed prescription and auxiliary labels, cap, and stage for pharmacist check and will-call bagging. Fast pace, many scripts per hour, staff working around each other at an open counter.

Retail pharmacy: prepare a liquid prescription - reconstitute a powder-for-suspension antibiotic (uncap the manufacturer bottle, add the exact measured volume of purified water, optionally add flavoring, shake to disperse), recap, apply the patient label and refrigeration/shake-well auxiliary labels; or pour/measure a bulk oral liquid into a dispensing bottle and label.

Hospital inpatient pharmacy: repackage bulk oral solids into patient- or batch-specific unit-dose packages (blisters, strips, or bagged doses) carrying a barcoded, printed label with drug, strength, lot and expiry, for cart fill and cabinet restock. Clean, fixed-layout pharmacy suite, institution-controlled access.

Long-term-care / adherence-packaging pharmacy: assemble multi-dose blister cards or pouch strips for nursing-home or med-sync patients - placing multiple different tablets/capsules in each day/time cell, sealing, and applying the patient-specific label with dose times, then batching for delivery.

Hospital sterile compounding suite (ISO Class 5 hood / cleanroom): prepare an IV admixture or patient-specific syringe - reconstitute a drug vial, withdraw the ordered volume, inject into a bag or syringe, cap, and apply the patient/dose label, with gravimetric or visual verification, under pharmacist check. Gowned, restricted-access environment.

Non-sterile extemporaneous compounding (compounding or hospital pharmacy): weigh API/bulk powder and base, mix a cream, ointment, oral suspension, troche, suppository or capsules per formula, fill jars, tubes, molds or capsule shells, and label the finished container with beyond-use date and ingredients.

instances.label: Hospital: aide runs filled medication totes, cassettes, IV bags and refill bins from the central inpatient pharmacy to nursing units and treatment areas (ED, ICU, OR), riding elevators through busy corridors, handing off to nursing staff or stocking the unit's med room per scheduled and ad-hoc runs.

Long-term-care or closed-door pharmacy courier: van run on public roads with multiple stops at nursing homes, assisted living facilities, group homes and outpatient clinics — carrying locked totes in from the parking lot, exchanging empties, signing logs, or using an after-hours lockbox/med room key.
