roles.title: Veterinary Assistants and Laboratory Animal Caretakers
roles.description: Feed, water, and examine pets and other nonfarm animals for signs of illness, disease, or injury in laboratories and animal hospitals and clinics. Clean and disinfect cages and work areas, and sterilize laboratory and surgical equipment. May provide routine postoperative care, administer medication orally or topically, or prepare samples for laboratory examination under the supervision of veterinary or laboratory animal technologists or technicians, veterinarians, or scientists.

tasks.label: Hold or restrain animals during veterinary procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal clinic exam room: assistant lifts an awake dog onto the table (or kneels with it on the floor), holds it sitting/standing/in lateral recumbency and continuously adjusts the hold while the vet does a physical exam, gives vaccines, draws cephalic or jugular blood (assistant occludes the vein), trims nails or examines ears. Must control the head, read the dog's body language, and release safely.

Clinic exam room, cat or small pet (rabbit, ferret, guinea pig, bird): towel-wrap/'burrito', scruff or chest-and-elbow hold for exam, subcutaneous injection, medial saphenous or jugular blood draw, ear cleaning, nail trim. Species-specific gentle handling; excessive force can fracture a rabbit's spine or cause a cat to escalate.

Treatment area / radiology: positioning and holding a sedated, anesthetized or lightly restrained patient for radiographs, ultrasound, dental work, IV catheter placement, bandage change or wound care — extending limbs, holding the head, keeping the patient still and monitored, often in lead gowns for the duration of the procedure.

Fractious, fearful or aggressive patient: applying a muzzle, cat bag, gauntlets or towel, pinning to a mat, two-person hold, restraining during sedation induction, then keeping control while the vet works — with bite/scratch and escape risk and rapidly changing animal behavior.

Research vivarium / lab animal facility: restraining mice, rats or rabbits by hand or in a tube for IP/SC injection, oral gavage, tail or saphenous blood collection, ear notching/tagging, or a veterinary health exam performed by the lab animal vet or technician.

Research vivarium: holding a lab animal immobile in a dedicated apparatus for the duration of an imaging or physiology procedure (e.g., head-restraining an implanted mouse for cortical imaging/optogenetics, or immobilizing a zebrafish larva for microscopy), where the animal is presented to a purpose-built rig rather than held in the hands.

Mobile or field setting: house-call visit, mobile spay/neuter or vaccination clinic, shelter intake in a borrowed space or trailer — restraining animals of unknown temperament on the floor, a folding table or the owner's lap, with variable layout, footing and lighting.

sources.system: Automated self-initiated head-fixation home-cage imaging system (Murphy lab, UBC)
sources.title: High-throughput automated home-cage mesoscopic functional imaging of mouse cortex | Nature Communications
sources.claim: A fully automated, self-initiated head-fixation system holds mice immobile in a purpose-built rig attached to their home cage for cortical imaging sessions, running unsupervised for months with minimal investigator involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanically restraining a laboratory rodent so a procedure (functional imaging) can be performed. It substantiates machine restraint of a live lab animal in a purpose-built rig, but only for surgically head-plated mice presenting themselves to the fixture.

sources.system: Fully autonomous home-cage head-fixation and optogenetics workflow
sources.developer: Hao et al. (Janelia/Zhejiang collaboration, published in eLife)
sources.title: Fully autonomous mouse behavioral and optogenetic experiments in home-cage | eLife
sources.claim: Naive mice living in an instrumented home cage learned voluntary head-fixation and were clamped and held by the machine during difficult behavioral and optogenetic procedures for two months without human supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: holding a lab rodent still for the duration of an experimental procedure. Transfer is limited to implanted rodents that enter the fixture themselves; it shows autonomous clamping restraint in a machine-built setting.

sources.title: Tools for automating the imaging of zebrafish larvae (Methods, 2016) / VAST Platform Overview
sources.claim: A commercial benchtop instrument automatically draws live zebrafish larvae from a plate or cup, loads them into a capillary, and positions and holds them in a chosen orientation for imaging before returning them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restraining/positioning a live laboratory animal so a diagnostic procedure (microscopy) can be performed. Comparable in kind to holding an animal for imaging, though the animal is a millimetre-scale larva handled in fluid inside a dedicated machine.

sources.title: 20 years of using Racewell Sheep Handlers | Te Pari
sources.claim: A commercially deployed sheep handler uses optical sensors to automatically clamp and hold a live, awake sheep that walks into the machine, so that drenching, vaccination, tagging, hoof trimming and inspection can be performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine restraint of an awake live animal for veterinary procedures. Cited as the closest existing capability boundary; it handles livestock funnelled single-file into a fixed race and does not transfer to positioning a dog, cat or rabbit for venipuncture or exam in a clinic.

tasks.label: Monitor animals recovering from surgery and notify veterinarians of any unusual changes or symptoms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General companion-animal practice: dogs and cats recovering from routine surgery (spay/neuter, dental extraction, mass removal) in a recovery ward or kennel run. The assistant watches for return of swallowing reflex and times extubation, takes temperature/pulse/respiration and mucous-membrane color every 5-15 minutes, keeps the patient warm and positioned/sternal, checks the incision and IV catheter site, scores pain and dysphoria, and pages the DVM on abnormalities (hypothermia, prolonged recovery, bleeding, vomiting/regurgitation, pain).

Emergency/specialty hospital ICU: patients recovering from major orthopedic, thoracic or abdominal surgery, with IV lines, urinary catheters, drains, oxygen and multiparameter monitors. Hourly hands-on assessments (TPR, CRT, blood pressure cuff, pulse-ox probe placement, bandage/drain checks, bladder palpation, recumbency turning), interpreting monitor alarms versus artifact, and escalating changes to the clinician on duty.

Laboratory animal facility: rodents (and occasionally rabbits) recovering from survival surgery, on warming pads in the recovery rack and then in home cages. Post-op checks per IACUC protocol at intervals over 3-14 days: body weight, posture/grimace and activity, hydration, food/water intake, and lifting/handling each animal to inspect the incision and sutures for dehiscence or infection; records findings and notifies the attending lab-animal veterinarian.

Large-animal or large-species recovery: a horse recovering from general anesthesia in a padded recovery stall at an equine hospital, or a pig, sheep or nonhuman primate recovering in a research facility pen. Monitoring from outside and then in-stall, judging when the animal can safely attempt to stand, controlling head ropes/tail ropes, watching respiration and nasal edema, and calling the veterinarian for a rough or prolonged recovery.

High-volume spay/neuter, shelter, or mobile-unit setting: rows of cages holding dozens of animals in various stages of recovery, sometimes in a converted or pop-up space. The assistant walks continuous rounds, spotting the abnormal animal in the group (bleeding through a bandage, non-arousal, vocalizing, hypothermic, vomiting) among many normal ones, handles fractious or feral cats in traps, and reports to the veterinarian.

sources.title: Tecniplast DIGILAB | DVC - Digital Ventilated Cage for digital vivarium
sources.claim: Tecniplast's Digital Ventilated Cage is a deployed automated home-cage monitoring technology that senses rodent locomotion 24/7 and flags welfare deviations, but it is a capacitance-sensing rack with no manipulator: it does not handle animals, inspect incisions, or perform any physical act on the animal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated welfare surveillance of caged rodents. It is not a robotic system under the definition used here (it senses but does not act on the physical world), and it covers only locomotion, not the hands-on wound, hydration and body-condition checks that post-surgical monitoring requires.

sources.system: DVC-based home-cage monitoring with machine learning (multicentric study)
sources.title: Enhanced health evaluation in mice using continuous home-cage monitoring and machine learning: a multicentric study | Lab Animal
sources.claim: Continuous machine-learning home-cage monitoring can detect distress in mice earlier than human visual checks, confirming that the sensing/alerting half of rodent health surveillance is automatable — but the study system is instrumented cages plus software, with no robot performing the physical inspection or handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of illness/distress in laboratory rodents. Transfer fails for this task because the system is sensor-only (not embodied action) and does not perform the incision checks, weighing/handling, or intervention that post-operative monitoring includes.

sources.system: Automated mouse tail vein cannulation robot (Balter/Chang et al., Rutgers)
sources.title: Design and Evaluation of a Robotic Device for Automated Tail Vein Cannulations in Rodent Models - PMC
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic device physically restrains a rodent on a holding platform and cannulates its tail vein using stereo NIR vision and pressure feedback, succeeding in 10 of 12 trials — showing robots can act on a fixtured small animal in a purpose-built bench setup, but only for a single discrete procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic physical handling of a live rodent in a fixtured, purpose-built station. It does not transfer to post-operative monitoring, which requires repeated multi-modal assessment (temperature, mucous membranes, wound, posture, pain) of a freely recovering animal plus clinical judgment about when to escalate.

sources.developer: Foxconn with Kawasaki Heavy Industries / NVIDIA
sources.title: Could AI nursing robots help healthcare staffing shortages? | CNN Business
sources.claim: Hospital 'nursing' robots now entering wards (Nurabot) perform deliveries, guidance and telepresence rounds; reporting describes testing and imminent commercial launch, with no autonomous acquisition of patient vital signs or physical patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile robot working alongside clinical staff in a structured care facility. It does not substantiate post-operative patient monitoring: the demonstrated functions are logistics and telepresence, not hands-on vital-sign acquisition or clinical escalation.

sources.system: Veterinary clinic robot (history-taking kiosk robot) described in Today's Veterinary Business
sources.developer: various vendors reported by Today's Veterinary Business
sources.title: The Automation Evolution | Today's Veterinary Business
sources.claim: Veterinary trade coverage of automation in practice describes robots used for history-taking via voice/touchscreen with the physical examination portion handled by a remote televeterinarian instructing the client — i.e., no robot performs the physical patient assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic presence in a veterinary clinic workflow. It shows the physical animal-handling portion is still done by humans under remote instruction, so it cannot substantiate autonomous post-surgical monitoring.

tasks.label: Fill medication prescriptions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic in-house pharmacy: for a discharge or refill order in the practice management system, count out a quantity of tablets or capsules from a bulk stock bottle into a dispensing vial, cap it, print and affix the label (patient/owner name, drug, strength, directions, warnings), and stage it for the veterinarian's check and client pickup.

Dispensing manufacturer unit-of-use products from clinic pharmacy shelves: flea/tick or heartworm preventive cartons, tubes of ointment, ear/eye drop bottles, bottled shampoos and prepackaged liquids. Pull the correct product and count/strength for the pet's weight band, apply the prescription label, bag it, and record the sale/inventory.

Liquid and injectable take-home preparations: pour or aliquot an oral suspension into a dispensing bottle, reconstitute a powdered antibiotic with the correct diluent volume, draw measured doses into oral dosing syringes, or prepare pre-drawn insulin/injection syringes; label each with dose and directions.

In-clinic custom dose preparation for small or exotic patients: split or quarter commercial tablets to the prescribed strength, weigh out or triturate powder, hand-fill gelatin capsules to a custom milligram dose, and label the resulting container.

Research vivarium / laboratory animal facility: fill drug orders written by the attending veterinarian for study or clinical animals — dilute a stock analgesic or antibiotic to the working concentration, draw per-animal doses into labeled syringes, and prepare medicated drinking-water bottles or dosing solutions for a treatment protocol.

sources.system: ScriptPro SP 200 robotic prescription dispensing system
sources.title: SP 200 with Open Control Center Robotic Prescription Dispensing System
sources.claim: The ScriptPro SP 200 is a commercially deployed robotic prescription dispensing system that receives the prescription electronically and autonomously counts tablets/capsules into vials, prints and applies the prescription ... collates the finished vials at up to 150 per hour with 99.7% count accuracy.

sources.title: ScriptPro Robot Fills Pet Prescriptions at 1-800-PetMeds
sources.claim: A ScriptPro vial-filling robot is used in production at a pet pharmacy (1-800-PetMeds) to fill animal prescriptions, showing the same automation counting and labeling veterinary tablet/capsule prescriptions rather than only human ones.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (filling animal medication prescriptions) as performed by a veterinary assistant, but done at a pet mail-order pharmacy; objects (tablets/capsules, vials, labels) are identical.

sources.system: Omnicell XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System
sources.title: Pharmacy Robot Increases Safety, Efficiency | Owensboro Health
sources.claim: Omnicell's XR2 Automated Central Pharmacy System is a deployed hospital pharmacy robot that autonomously retrieves packaged medications by barcode, then bags, seals and labels them for each patient order.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order-driven retrieval, labeling and dispensing of prepackaged medication units. Transfers to dispensing manufacturer-packaged veterinary products (preventive cartons, ointment tubes) — same class of rigid packaged items, same barcode-verified pick-label-dispense loop.

sources.system: BD Rowa Vmax storage and dispensing robot
sources.title: BD Rowa - store & pick medications automatically
sources.claim: BD Rowa Vmax automated pharmacy stockroom robots store and pick heterogeneous manufacturer medication packs of varying sizes and deliver them to the dispensing counter, with vendor-reported 99.9% reliability across roughly 15,000 installed robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated retrieval of boxed medications for a specific order. Comparable objects (manufacturer cartons, tubes, bottles) to the unit-of-use products a veterinary assistant pulls from clinic shelves.

sources.title: Automating the Chemo Compounding Process - ARxIUM
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA is a fully automated robotic compounding cell that reconstitutes drug vials with diluent and transfers accurately measured doses into syringes or fluid bags, verifying drug identity by barcode/image recognition and dose by gravimetric weighing, and printing customizable labels and barcodes on the finished preparations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reconstituting a powdered drug and drawing measured liquid doses into labeled syringes. Same operations and tighter precision than pouring an oral suspension or drawing a take-home syringe in a vet clinic.

sources.title: ARxIUM Celebrates Major RIVA Milestone
sources.claim: RIVA robotic compounding cells are in routine hospital-pharmacy production worldwide, having supported preparation of more than nineteen ... compounded doses across the installed base.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployed, worker-quality reliability for the robotic liquid-dose preparation cited above.

sources.title: Queue Raises $12.6 Million to Launch the World's First Fully Autonomous Robotic Pharmacy
sources.claim: Queue has a working, autonomously operating robotic pharmacy unit that takes sealed wholesale pill bottles as input and outputs filled, verified prescription vials for 250 of the most-prescribed US medications, with an early commercial deployment at a US pharmacy chain.

sources.title: BOTTLE & CAGE AUTOMATION (IWT brochure)
sources.claim: Robotic bottle- and cage-handling automation lines are installed in more than 100 laboratory animal facilities worldwide, mechanically handling animal drinking-water bottles through the vivarium washroom process.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and filling of animal drinking-water bottles in vivarium washrooms; supports the container-handling half of preparing medicated water bottles, with dose preparation covered by the compounding-robot evidence.

tasks.label: Clean and maintain kennels, animal holding areas, examination or operating rooms, or animal loading or unloading facilities to control the spread of disease.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal veterinary hospital ward: terminal cleaning of a kennel run or cage after a patient is discharged — strip soiled bedding/newspaper, remove bowls and litter pans, scrub and hose the enclosure, apply disinfectant with contact time, squeegee/dry, then re-bed and restock the empty enclosure for the next patient.

Veterinary ward during the day with patients present: spot-cleaning occupied kennels and runs — scooping feces, removing urine-soaked or vomit-soiled bedding around a recovering or fractious animal, wiping cage fronts and bars, changing litter, shifting the animal to a clean cage as needed.

Clinical rooms in a clinic or teaching hospital: turnover cleaning of exam and treatment rooms between appointments (disinfect exam table, counters, scale, remove hair and body fluids from the floor, dispose of waste, restock) and terminal cleaning of the surgery suite (equipment moved out and wiped, floors and walls mopped and disinfected).

Boarding kennel, doggy daycare or animal shelter: high-volume cleaning of banks of concrete/epoxy runs and cat condos — dogs shifted to holding runs, bedding and toys removed for laundering, runs hosed and scrubbed, disinfectant applied, drains and aisles flushed, bowls washed.

Laboratory animal facility cage-wash room: processing soiled rodent caging — dumping bedding at the dump station, loading cage bases, lids, bottles and racks into tunnel/rack washers, re-bedding, and stacking clean caging for return to holding rooms.
Facility-wide hard floors: end-of-shift scrubbing and disinfecting of ward aisles, corridors, lobby and the animal loading/unloading area, including picking up debris and hair before scrubbing.

sources.title: Robotic Cage Handling System for Tunnel Washers - Getinge
sources.claim: Getinge sells a commercial robotic cage-handling system that combines industrial robots with a ... to process laboratory animal cages through the cleaning cycle in a vivarium cage-wash room.
sources.transferJustification: Directly this task: sanitizing animal holding enclosures to control disease spread; the robot cell handles the same soiled caging a laboratory animal caretaker washes by hand.

sources.system: Tecniplast/IWT Apollo and Pegasus cage automation cells
sources.title: Cage automation - Tecniplast - PDF Catalogs | Technical Documentation
sources.claim: Tecniplast/IWT sell robotic cage-automation cells (Apollo, Pegasus) that disassemble individually ventilated cages, dump soiled bedding and diet, and present components to tunnel and rack washers at throughputs of thousands of cages per week.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: emptying and sanitizing animal cages/holding enclosures, including the soiled-side bedding dumping a caretaker performs manually.

sources.system: Robotic cage washing lines in vivaria (e.g., Ohio State University)
sources.title: Automation: robots in the vivarium | Lab Animal (Nature)
sources.claim: Robotic cage-wash automation is in operational use in university vivaria, where robots load and unload the tunnel washer so staff no longer hand-feed cages.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cleaning animal holding equipment to control disease spread); establishes real deployment rather than vendor claims.

sources.title: ProCleaner XT100 - Washpower
sources.claim: Washpower's ProCleaner washing robots have been sold commercially for over a decade to pressure-wash animal pens in pig and poultry houses; the robot runs a programmed wash cycle along the pen rows (guided by side wheels or rails, with ultrasound end-stop) and an optional module lets it also apply disinfectant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing and disinfecting animal holding pens for disease control — the same physical operation as hosing out a kennel run, on comparable hard-surface enclosures in a fixed-layout animal facility.

sources.developer: Pipestone Research / Swine Health Information Center
sources.title: Robotic Power Washing vs. Manual Power Washing: Which is Better? - Pork Business
sources.claim: A controlled SHIC/Pipestone trial of robotic versus manual barn power washing found the robotically washed room still required a manual touch-up crew to reach the 'very clean' standard, and that the robot could not easily access feeders.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the Washpower evidence (washing out animal pens); shows autonomous pen washing in an as-found animal facility does not yet reach the accepted sanitation standard unaided.

sources.system: Avidbots Neo / Neo 2 autonomous floor scrubber
sources.date: September 2021; Neo 2 disinfection add-on coverage October 2025
sources.title: Avidbots Expands Neo's Capabilities With Disinfection Add-On for Autonomous Sanitation of High-Touch Surfaces (Business Wire)
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor scrubber ... deployed worldwide, including in healthcare facilities, cleaning hard floors without an operator, with an add-on that sprays disinfectant on high-touch surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scrubbing and disinfecting institutional hard floors — the same corridor, aisle and dock floors this task requires be cleaned for disease control.

sources.system: Tru-D SmartUVC ('Trudy') at Texas A&M Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital
sources.title: Disinfection Robot Boosts Sanitation At Veterinary Medical Teaching Hospital – Texas A&M Stories
sources.claim: A veterinary teaching hospital added a UVC disinfection robot as a supplement to, not a replacement for, manual room cleaning; the unit is stationary and is used after staff manually clean operating rooms, walls, floors and each piece of equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task setting (veterinary exam/operating room disinfection); shows the robot performs only terminal light disinfection while manual cleaning of surfaces and equipment remains.

sources.title: This robot will clean toilets for $1,000 a month | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Somatic markets an autonomous bathroom cleaning robot that sprays, mops, disinfects and vacuum-dries restroom fixtures and floors and picks up trash, offered as a service in office buildings and reported in medical facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wet cleaning and disinfecting hard-surfaced institutional rooms with fixtures; bears on whether room-level cleaning of exam rooms or kennels is automatable, though demonstrated rooms are waterproof restrooms.

tasks.label: Examine animals to detect behavioral changes or clinical symptoms that could indicate illness or injury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Barrier vivarium: daily health-check round of mouse/rat cages on IVC racks — pulling each cage, looking through the walls, and when needed lifting animals to check for hunched posture, ruffled coat, ocular/nasal discharge, fight wounds, dehydration, malocclusion, dystocia or dead animals; flagging sick cages for the vet tech and recording findings.

Veterinary hospital ward/ICU: monitoring hospitalized dogs and cats in kennels — observing attitude, appetite, vomiting/diarrhea, respiratory effort, urination; opening the kennel to check the surgical incision, bandage, IV catheter, mucous membranes and skin turgor, and taking TPR; reporting changes to the technician or veterinarian.

Exam room / triage of a companion-animal appointment: greeting and restraining a dog or cat, watching gait and demeanor as it enters, noting lameness, coughing, itching, weight loss, lumps, ear or eye discharge, and reporting observations to the veterinarian before the exam.

Animal shelter or boarding kennel: rounds down the runs each morning, checking every dog or cat for kennel cough, sneezing, diarrhea or blood in stool, inappetence, lethargy, limping or wounds; entering runs and handling animals as needed; logging and escalating sick animals.

Research facility housing non-rodent species (beagles, NHPs, rabbits, swine, aquatics): daily observation and hands-on checks of individual animals in pens/runs/tanks for clinical signs, wounds, appetite and stool changes, per IACUC health-surveillance SOPs.

Agricultural research or production animal facility: walking a poultry house, swine barn or dairy barn to spot sick, lame, injured or dead animals among a group, and reporting them for treatment or removal.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: challenges and opportunities (arXiv preprint)
sources.claim: Scout (formerly ChickenBoy, Faromatics) is a ceiling-suspended autonomous robot that travels over broiler flocks with thermal and visual cameras and sensors to monitor bird condition without human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated inspection of live animals in their housing to detect illness. Same output as the rated task (flagging animals whose behaviour/appearance indicates disease or death) for small animals observed visually in an institution-controlled animal facility.

sources.title: W 1259 Pioneering Poultry Robotics (University of Tennessee Extension)
sources.claim: Extension review describes the commercially sold Scout robot as delivering real-time bird behaviour analysis and mortality detection in broiler houses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine detection of sick/dead animals in a housing facility; the accepted output (a flagged animal/health alert for a human to act on) matches the rated task's output for group-housed animals.

sources.title: Poultry farming: The robots are coming | WATTAgNet
sources.claim: Trade press reports the ceiling-mounted ChickenBoy robot autonomously monitors a chicken house for health issues and locates dead birds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detecting illness and death in animals by automated observation inside an animal housing facility; identical detection output to the rated task at group level.

sources.title: Industrializing behavioral testing to redefine neuropsychiatric drug discovery (Nature)
sources.claim: SmartCube is a commercial robotic enclosure into which a single mouse is placed; cameras and computer vision automatically extract thousands of behavioural features per session to detect behavioural change.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated detection of behavioural change in an individual laboratory rodent presented to a purpose-built machine — the same modality (vision-based behavioural readout of a mouse) the rated task uses to spot abnormal animals.

sources.title: PsychoGenics SmartCube prompts CNS drug discovery rethink
sources.claim: PsychoGenics' developers describe SmartCube explicitly as a robot in which the mouse is placed and mechanically challenged, i.e. an embodied machine acting on the animal rather than a passive camera.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the embodiment of the SmartCube platform cited above; the related task is automated rodent behavioural assessment in a purpose-built station.

sources.title: Supervised machine learning approaches for early detection of metabolic and udder health disorders in dairy cows using sensor-derived data (Frontiers in Veterinary Science)
sources.claim: Commercial robotic milking systems (Lely Astronaut) autonomously attach to cows and evaluate somatic cell count, milk temperature and conductivity to raise udder-health (mastitis) alerts — a robot detecting clinical illness in animals presented to a purpose-built station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-based detection of a clinical condition (mastitis) in animals that come to a purpose-built machine; transfers to the rated task only where the animal is presented to the machine and the sign is instrument-measurable.

sources.system: Continuous home-cage monitoring (HCM) with machine learning
sources.title: Enhanced health evaluation in mice using continuous home-cage monitoring and machine learning: a multicentric study (Lab Animal)
sources.claim: Context only (NOT a robotic system): fixed home-cage sensor/camera systems with machine learning detect distress in mice earlier than human visual checks, showing the perception problem is tractable, but no embodied machine performs the health-check round.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as context for rodent health surveillance; it is a fixed sensor/camera installation, not an embodied machine acting on the world, so on its own it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Perform routine laboratory tests or diagnostic tests, such as taking or developing x-rays.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal clinic radiology room: assistant lifts an awake or lightly sedated dog/cat onto the x-ray table, positions it in lateral and VD recumbency (extending limbs, using sandbags/troughs, sometimes holding), measures thickness, sets/confirms technique on the digital unit, exposes, checks the image for positioning and diagnostic quality, retakes if needed, saves to PACS.

In-clinic blood work: after the vet/tech draws the sample, the assistant mixes/labels tubes, spins the sample in the bench centrifuge, transfers serum/plasma into cups, loads the chemistry analyzer and the hematology analyzer, runs QC, monitors for errors, and records results in the patient record.

In-clinic urinalysis, fecal flotation, ear/skin cytology and snap tests: preparing the sample (flotation solution, spinning urine, smearing and staining slides), running dipsticks/refractometer, loading the sediment analyzer or scanning slides, reading the microscope, and recording findings.

Preparing and packaging specimens for the outside reference lab: labeling tubes, centrifuging and separating serum, aliquoting, matching to the requisition, and packing with cold packs for the courier.

Research/lab-animal facility: routine sampling and testing of rodents on a study schedule (timed blood micro-samples, urine/feces collection, glucose or hematocrit readings), sample labeling and preparation for analysis in the procedure room.

Preclinical imaging in a research facility: anesthetized rodents placed on an imaging bed for routine x-ray/micro-CT scans, image acquisition, reconstruction, and archiving of images for the study record.

sources.system: Total laboratory automation (TLA) lines (Abbott, Roche, Siemens Healthineers, Beckman Coulter)
sources.developer: Abbott / Roche / Siemens Healthineers / Beckman Coulter
sources.title: Collaborative Robotics, Mobile Platforms, and Total Laboratory Automation in Clinical Diagnostics
sources.claim: Commercial total laboratory automation lines from Abbott, Roche, Siemens Healthineers ... autonomously carry specimens through sample receipt, sorting, centrifugation, decapping, ..., routing to analyzers, and storage inside purpose-built track systems in high-volume clinical labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-analytical and analytical processing of human blood/urine specimens. The objects (capped blood tubes, serum aliquots), the precision required, and the accepted output (validated test results) match the veterinary assistant's in-house and send-out lab work; species differs but tube handling and analyzer chemistry do not.

sources.system: Cobot pre-analytical modules in a centralized medical laboratory
sources.developer: Komarov et al. (commercially available cobots integrated by the laboratory)
sources.title: Collaborative Robotic Systems for Pre-Analytical Processing of Biological Specimens in a Medical Laboratory
sources.claim: Commercially available collaborative robots were integrated into the pre-analytical workflow of a large centralized medical laboratory, performing decapping, barcode orientation/verification, analyzer loading, aliquoting and specimen ... LIS integration; a 90-day pilot-industrial run processed more than 4.77 million samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pre-analytical specimen handling (decapping, aliquoting, loading analyzers). These are exactly the manual steps a veterinary assistant performs between sample receipt and running a routine test; objects and precision are comparable.

sources.system: IDEXX SediVue Dx Urine Sediment Analyzer
sources.title: Automatic urine sediment analyzer - SediVue Dx - Idexx Laboratories
sources.claim: The IDEXX SediVue Dx is a benchtop veterinary urine sediment analyzer deployed in clinics: after a 165 µL sample is injected into a cartridge it centrifuges onboard, images the sediment with an inverted microscope, and classifies elements with a neural network, producing the urinalysis result.

sources.title: Evaluation of the VETSCAN IMAGYST: an in-clinic canine and feline fecal parasite detection system integrated with a deep learning algorithm
sources.claim: The VETSCAN IMAGYST in-clinic system uses an automated microscope scanner plus a deep-learning algorithm that locates, classifies and identifies parasite ... on prepared fecal flotation slides, replacing the technician's manual microscope read; it is also used for blood smear and dermatology slide analysis.

sources.system: Sysmex SP-50 slidemaker/stainer with DI-60 digital cell morphology system
sources.title: DI-60 - Products Detail | Sysmex Europe
sources.claim: Sysmex hematology systems prepare and stain blood smears fully automatically with the SP-50 slidemaker/stainer and then acquire and pre-classify white cells on the DI-60 digital morphology analyzer, automating the manual differential workflow in clinical labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making, staining and reading a blood smear. This is the same manual bench procedure veterinary assistants perform for in-house smears and cytology; slides, stains and microscope reading are identical in kind.

sources.system: BASi Culex / Culex NxT Automated Blood Sampling System
sources.title: BASi Launches Embrace Automation Grant Program With Culex NxT Automated Blood Sampling System
sources.claim: The BASi Culex automated in vivo sampling system collects programmed, timed blood micro-samples from conscious, freely moving catheterized rodents and larger animals housed in its purpose-built Raturn caging, and is used worldwide in pharmaceutical and CRO vivaria.

sources.system: Bruker preclinical PET/CT with automated animal transport system
sources.title: PET/CT | PET System | Preclincal CT | Total Body | Bruker
sources.claim: Bruker preclinical PET/CT scanners include a fully automated motorized animal transport system that positions the anesthetized animal precisely in the gantry and performs automatic image co-registration and fusion, with acquisition run from the study protocol.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: acquiring diagnostic x-ray/CT images of a small animal. Once the anesthetized rodent is presented on the bed, positioning, exposure and image production are machine-controlled, which is the imaging portion of the assistant's radiography task.

sources.developer: University of Liverpool (Burger, Cooper et al.)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator operated autonomously for eight days in a human-scale laboratory, moving between stations to handle sample vials and run 688 experiments, showing autonomous multi-station bench sample handling in a research lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of sample vials and operation of bench instruments across stations, comparable to moving specimens between centrifuge, pipette and analyzer; however it ran a fixed set of purpose-fitted stations, not a clinic bench with patient specimens.

sources.title: Siemens Healthcare Unveils Twin Robotic X-Ray System
sources.claim: The Multitom Rax twin robotic ... positions its two ceiling-mounted robotic arms around a patient automatically at the push of a ..., obtaining multiple projections without moving the patient; the operator remains in control of the system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: radiographic projection geometry. It automates tube/detector placement for a human patient positioned by a technologist, but it does not handle, restrain or position the patient and is operator-commanded, so it cannot support autonomous completion.

tasks.label: Assist veterinarians in examining animals to determine the nature of illnesses or injuries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal clinic exam room, dog wellness or sick visit: assistant lifts the dog to the table or kneels on the floor, applies standing/sternal/lateral restraint, controls the head, lifts lips and ears for the vet's oral/otic/ophthalmic exam, presents limbs and abdomen for palpation, takes temperature, pulse, respiration and weight, and hands instruments while the vet works; patient is awake, may wiggle, lunge or vocalize.

Same clinic, cat or small exotic (rabbit, ferret, bird, rodent) exam: towel-wrap or low-stress restraint, scruff or burrito hold, holding the head for otoscope/oral exam and the leg for a blood draw, muzzling or gauntlet handling of fractious patients; high bite/scratch risk and rapidly changing animal behavior.

Clinic treatment area diagnostics: positioning and holding the animal (awake or sedated) for radiographs, ultrasound, ECG or blood pressure; clipping/prepping a site; restraining for cystocentesis, ear cytology, skin scrape or jugular draw; then handing samples off for lab work, all under the vet's direction.

Emergency/urgent triage in an ER or busy day practice: assistant helps the vet examine an injured, painful or collapsing animal — muzzling, transferring on a gurney or blanket, stabilizing a fractured limb, holding an oxygen mask, restraining for rapid TPR, mucous membrane and wound assessment while the animal struggles or is unresponsive.

Laboratory animal facility clinical rounds: caretaker assists the attending veterinarian in examining rodents or rabbits flagged as sick — removing animals from ventilated cages inside a biosafety cabinet, tunnel/scruff or towel restraint, presenting the animal for inspection of skin lesions, tumors, body condition and dehydration, weighing, and holding for sample collection, in PPE under barrier conditions.

Off-site variant: mobile/shelter or farm-call exam — shelter intake exams in kennels or a mobile unit, or holding a horse or small ruminant by halter in a barn aisle or paddock while the vet examines it; unfamiliar footing, no fixed layout, animals of unknown temperament.

sources.developer: Tecniplast / Yaskawa; installed at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
sources.title: Automation: robots in the vivarium (Lab Animal)
sources.claim: Industrial robot arms deployed in vivaria (e.g., Mount Sinai's Center for Comparative Medicine and ..., Tecniplast/Yaskawa systems) handle rodent CAGES — dumping, washing, refilling — but do not pick up, restrain, or examine the live animals themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed automation in the laboratory-animal instance's own setting. It substantiates cage logistics only; the animals are still caught, restrained and presented by humans, so it does not transfer to assisting a veterinarian's clinical examination of a live rodent.

sources.title: Tools for automating the imaging of zebrafish larvae - PubMed
sources.claim: The VAST BioImager is a commercial instrument that autonomously loads, positions and orients sedated live zebrafish larvae and images them for morphological/phenotypic assessment inside a purpose-built machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and positioning of live animals for visual examination of abnormalities. It transfers only to millimetre-scale, sedated, water-borne larvae in a flow cell; it does not substantiate restraint of an awake dog, cat, rabbit or rodent for a veterinarian's hands-on physical exam.

sources.title: Lely Astronaut A4 milking robot lets cows milk themselves (New Atlas)
sources.claim: Automatic milking systems autonomously handle a live cow that enters a purpose-built box, locate and attach to teats with 3D vision, and screen milk for signs of mastitis and other health issues.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous physical contact with a live large animal plus automated health screening. Transfer is limited: the cow voluntarily fixtures herself in a box built around the machine and only the udder is touched; the robot cannot restrain a patient or present body regions for a veterinarian's directed examination.

sources.title: Vaccination - Maskon
sources.claim: Commercial fish-vaccination machines singularize, orient and process anesthetized live fish with machine vision and automatically sort out incorrectly positioned or off-spec individuals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and orientation of live (anesthetized) animals in a purpose-built line. It shows E1 live-animal handling is possible only for uniform, sedated, small-bodied animals in bulk; it does not substantiate individualized, vet-directed exam assistance on awake mammals.

sources.system: auto-RUSS autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system
sources.developer: Sun Yat-sen University (Lin, Li et al.)
sources.title: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning system: a key to enhancing image analysis reproducibility and observer consistency in ultrasound imaging - PubMed
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound scanning has been demonstrated on cooperative human subjects in a research setting, improving image reproducibility versus manual scanning; no equivalent deployment exists for awake veterinary patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-held diagnostic probe placement on a live body. It applies to a still, cooperating human subject in a lab; it does not cover restraining and positioning a struggling animal patient, which is the substance of the diagnostic-assist instance.

sources.system: Veterinary clinic robotics/AI landscape (AI ultrasound presets, wearable vital-sign sensors, teleoperated surgical robots)
sources.title: Clarius Debuts First AI-Powered Ultrasound Tool for Veterinary Care
sources.claim: Reporting on veterinary robotics as of 2025-2026 describes AI imaging analysis, teleoperated surgical concepts and wearable monitors, with autonomous in-clinic patient handling still prospective rather than deployed.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to document the state of the art in ... task's own setting: the automation being fielded in companion-animal practice is software (image-preset selection, AI triage, wearable sensors) held or applied by a human, not an embodied system that handles or restrains the patient.

tasks.label: Administer medication, immunizations, or blood plasma to animals as prescribed by veterinarians.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic/hospital: give oral medication (tablet, capsule, compounded liquid) to a dog or cat — retrieve and verify the prescription, restrain or have a colleague hold the patient, place the pill over the tongue or syringe liquid into the cheek pouch, confirm swallowing, and record the dose.

Clinic exam room or treatment area: draw up and give a subcutaneous or intramuscular injection/vaccine to a dog, cat, rabbit or other pet — including squirmy, fearful or fractious patients requiring scruffing, towel wrap or muzzle — then monitor for reaction and log the vaccine serial number.

Clinic, ward or boarding kennel: apply topical, otic, ophthalmic or transdermal medication — ear drops with canal massage, eye ointment on a blinking patient, spot-on parasiticide parting fur at the scruff, medicated bath or ear cleaning.

Hospital ward/ICU: administer medication by the intravenous route to a hospitalized dog or cat — clip and place or maintain an IV catheter, flush lines, give slow IV push or set fluids, and run a plasma/blood transfusion with monitoring for transfusion reaction.

Research vivarium, study animals on protocol: scheduled/chronic dosing of rats or mice enrolled in a pharmacokinetic or chronic-treatment study, where animals are instrumented (implanted jugular/gastric catheter and tether, or RFID-tagged in an instrumented cage) and doses must be delivered accurately at set times and logged.

Research vivarium, routine colony work: hand-restrained dosing of mice/rats from standard cages — intraperitoneal or subcutaneous injection, oral gavage, post-operative analgesia, treating a colony health issue — retrieving each animal, scruffing it, injecting and returning it to the cage.

sources.developer: Woodard / open-source academic system (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: PiDose: an open-source system for accurate and automated oral drug administration to group-housed mice | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: PiDose is an automated apparatus attached to a mouse home cage that identifies individual RFID-tagged mice, weighs them, and dispenses accurately measured oral drug-solution drops, dosing group-housed mice over weeks without experimenter handling.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (administering prescribed medication to laboratory animals), oral route, in a purpose-built cage module.

sources.system: Empis Automated Drug Infusion System (with Culex / Raturn)
sources.title: Empis® Automated Dosing System - BASI Culex
sources.claim: The BASi Empis is a commercial automated drug infusion/dosing device that delivers programmed doses to catheterized laboratory animals (rodents through large animals) in tethered home-cage systems with no personnel present.

sources.title: WHY AUTOMATE? - BASI Culex (whitepaper)
sources.claim: In a controlled comparison, catheter-implanted rats received doses from a programmable syringe pump with no humans in the room, standing in directly for the manual restraint-and-gavage dosing a caretaker would perform.

sources.system: Robotic device for automated tail vein cannulation in rodents (successor to A-VAS)
sources.title: Design and Evaluation of a Robotic Device for Automated Tail Vein Cannulations in Rodent Models - PMC
sources.claim: Robotic tail-vein cannulation/injection devices for rodents remain laboratory prototypes: the reported evaluation is on tissue-mimicking phantoms, with in vivo validation against manual technique still listed as future work.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (injecting/cannulating live rodents); cited to show the parenteral-injection robots are not validated in live animals at caretaker quality.

sources.title: Vaccybot vaccination robot | Agri Advanced Technologies
sources.claim: Vaccybot is a fully automatic poultry vaccination robot that injects birds in the breast using 3D vision after they are presented and weighed by an inline sorting system, at up to 2,800 birds per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine injection of live animals. It works only on uniform, line-presented birds mechanically oriented for a fixed injection site, so it does not carry over to awake, size-variable dogs, cats or hand-held rodents.

sources.system: Skala Maskon automated fish vaccination machine
sources.title: Maskon automated vaccination machine for farmed fish | Business Norway
sources.claim: Automatic fish vaccination machines commercially inject anesthetized farmed salmon/trout with vaccines after machine orientation, running as fully automatic hatchery lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated injection of live animals, but only for anesthetized, uniformly sized fish conveyed into a fixture; the animal handling, restraint and site selection do not transfer to companion animals or hand-held rodents.

tasks.label: Collect laboratory specimens, such as blood, urine, or feces, for testing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic treatment area: assistant restrains a conscious, often anxious dog or cat (or draws it themselves where state law allows) for cephalic, lateral saphenous or jugular venipuncture, raises the vein, fills EDTA/serum tubes, inverts, labels and delivers to the in-house analyzer.

Small-animal clinic: obtaining a urine sample - walking a leashed dog outside with a collection ladle for free catch, setting a cat cage up with non-absorbent litter and retrieving the void, or restraining the patient while the veterinarian performs ultrasound-guided cystocentesis - then transferring to a sterile tube and labelling.

Small-animal clinic/kennel: obtaining a fecal specimen - picking a fresh sample from a kennel run, litter box or exam-room floor, or passing a fecal loop into the rectum of a dog or cat - and placing a pea-sized portion in a labelled ova-and-parasite vial or fecal container.

Research vivarium procedure room: routine bleeds on uninstrumented rodents - manual or restrainer-tube restraint of mice/rats for submandibular, lateral saphenous, tail-vein or terminal cardiac sampling at scheduled study timepoints, into capillary/microtainer tubes matched to individual animal IDs on a rack of dozens of animals.

Research facility, surgically instrumented animals: serial timed blood sampling from jugular-catheterized rats or port-implanted dogs/swine on PK, toxicology or telemetry studies over 24 hours, plus timed 24-hour urine and feces collection from animals housed in metabolic caging.

Equine, exotic, shelter or field settings: jugular blood draw from a horse held in a barn aisle, fecal sample from a stall or pasture, blood or droppings from birds/reptiles in an exotics practice, or samples collected on a mobile/shelter intake day.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed blood draws on human outpatients in three Dutch hospital phlebotomy departments with 94.5% first-stick success; it is CE-marked. It works on a cooperative human arm placed in a cradle, not on animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = human venipuncture. I do NOT claim transfer to veterinary specimen collection: the device requires a cooperative, stationary human forearm presented in a fixed cradle with bare skin and 3-5 mm antecubital veins, whereas clinic patients are furry, unrestrained animals with 1-2 mm cephalic veins that must first be physically restrained; no animal use is reported.

sources.system: BASi Culex NxT / Raturn / Culex-L automated in vivo sampling system
sources.date: 2016-12 (review); product line commercially sold and in use through 2026
sources.title: Automated Microsampling Technologies and Enhancements in the 3Rs | ILAR Journal
sources.claim: The BASi Culex NxT automated in vivo sampling system automatically collects blood and other fluids at preprogrammed timepoints from awake, freely moving catheterized rodents tethered inside a proprietary rotating cage (Raturn); the Culex-L extends this to dogs, nonhuman primates and swine.

sources.title: ABS2 Sampler | Automated Blood Sampler | Instech Laboratories
sources.claim: Instech's ABS2 is a commercially sold automated blood sampler that draws blood from a tethered, freely moving catheterized laboratory animal on a programmed schedule and deposits the sample into refrigerated vials or onto dried-blood-spot paper.

sources.system: Automated blood sampling (ABS) system in canine telemetry studies
sources.developer: reported by pharmaceutical safety-pharmacology laboratories (J Pharmacol Toxicol Methods)
sources.title: Automated blood sampling in canine telemetry studies: Enabling enhanced assessments of cardiovascular liabilities and safety margins - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Automated blood sampling systems are used in routine canine telemetry/toxicology studies to collect multi-timepoint samples from conscious dogs carrying surgically implanted vascular access ports.

sources.system: Culex automated blood sampler robot station with metabolic caging / i-cup
sources.title: A robot station for sampling blood, urine, and feces while monitoring behavior in four rats (figure)
sources.claim: The automated blood sampler robot station also collects urine and feces from rats housed in the sampling/metabolic caging, with samples deposited into refrigerated vials; BASi sells metabolic caging that separates urine and feces and stores urine in a chilled i-cup as part of a Culex study.

sources.system: Stereo-vision based robotic mouse tail vein injection system
sources.title: Development of a Stereo-Vision Based High-Throughput Robotic System for Mouse Tail Vein Injection
sources.claim: A stereo-vision robotic device autonomously located and punctured the tail vein of non-anesthetized mice held in a purpose-built jig with tourniquet and tail-end fixture, successfully injecting saline in 37 of 40 mice within three attempts; it performs injection, not sample withdrawal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = tail-vein injection in a fixtured mouse, which shares the vein-finding and puncture step with tail-vein blood sampling. Transfer is only partial: the prototype was never shown to aspirate, volume-verify, achieve hemostasis, or deliver identified specimens, so I do not credit it with completing a blood-collection instance.

tasks.label: Clean, maintain, and sterilize instruments or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic: reprocessing a surgical/dental instrument pack after a spay, neuter or dental. Rinse and scrub blood and tissue from scalpel handles, hemostats, needle holders, scissors and elevators; run the ultrasonic cleaner; rinse, dry, lubricate box locks, inspect for damage; sort instruments into correct pack order; wrap or pouch with indicator strips; load, run and unload the tabletop autoclave; date and shelve the packs.

Clinic prep/treatment area: reprocessing reusable patient-contact equipment between cases - endotracheal tubes, anesthesia breathing circuits, rebreathing bags, masks, laryngoscope blades, dental scaler tips, feeding and suction tubing. Wash out mucus and debris, disinfect (thermal or cold-sterilant soak), rinse, dry, inspect cuffs and valves, and return items to storage ready for use.

Between-patient cleaning and disinfection of in-room equipment in exam, treatment and surgery rooms: wipe down exam tables, scales, wet tables and surgery table; clean hair from clipper heads, disassemble, brush, disinfect and oil blades; wipe stethoscopes, thermometers, otoscope cones, ultrasound probes and monitor cables; clean kennel dryers and vacuum hair filters.

Laboratory animal facility cage wash: move dirty racks and cages from animal rooms to the cage wash, dump soiled bedding, load cages, bottles, lids and racks into the tunnel/rack washer, run the cycle, unload the clean side, refill cages with bedding and bottles with water, and autoclave caging/bedding for barrier rooms; also clean washer screens and sumps.

Maintaining and cleaning support and diagnostic equipment: daily/weekly maintenance of blood and chemistry analyzers (wiping optics, replacing reagents, running cleaning cycles), centrifuge bowl and rotor cleaning, microscope lens cleaning, changing ultrasonic cleaner solution, descaling and wiping out the autoclave chamber and filling its reservoir, changing anesthesia machine soda lime and cleaning valves and scavenging lines.

sources.system: Getinge Automatiq (Envoy mobile robot, Loaders, Hub)
sources.title: Getinge transforms sterile reprocessing with Automatiq - a full range of logistic automation modules
sources.claim: Getinge's Automatiq family provides commercial CSSD automation modules - a self-navigating mobile robot plus loaders that automatically load and unload the 8668 washer-disinfector and GSS67H steam ... - i.e., machine-controlled handling of instrument loads through wash and sterilization inside a purpose-built reprocessing line.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cleaning and sterilizing surgical instruments) at hospital scale; veterinary instrument packs are the same stainless instruments run through the same wash and steam-sterilize cycles.

sources.title: Bryan Health Uses New Robotic Technology to Clean and Sterilize Surgical Instruments
sources.claim: STERIS ATLAS Workflow Automation Vehicle is a deployed autonomous vehicle in a hospital sterile processing department that picks up instrument racks, delivers them unattended to available washer-disinfectors, loads them, and transfers racks onward to prep and pack.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on the same objects (soiled surgical instrument sets), one scale up from a veterinary clinic.

sources.system: Miele G 7889 / PG 8581 washer-disinfector, veterinary configuration
sources.title: Medical Washer - Veterinarian Use G 7889 - Miele Professional (PDF catalog)
sources.claim: Miele's veterinary-configured washer-disinfectors are commercial machines that automatically clean, thermally disinfect and dry veterinary surgical and dental instruments held in fixtured baskets and injector racks, replacing manual washing in veterinary practices.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L, YOLO12/ResNet perception)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell (calibrated vision, Staubli TX2-60L arm, custom gripper) autonomously identifies, sorts and packs surgical instruments into sterile ..., with statistically fewer tool-to-tool collisions than human-assembled trays - the inspection and assembly stage of instrument reprocessing.

sources.title: What is a Medical Washer-Disinfector? | STERIS Knowledge Center
sources.claim: Medical washer-disinfectors are validated, machine-controlled units that reprocess anesthesia and respiratory equipment - breathing ... - as well as surgical instruments, basins and trays, on dedicated fixtured racks.
sources.transferJustification: Covers exactly the items a veterinary assistant reprocesses (ET tubes, circuits, bags, masks), with the same soil and disinfection standard.

sources.system: IWT/Tecniplast cage automation (Pegasus, Apollo, RRE5) and bottle wash/fill automation
sources.title: IWT AUTOMATION - Tecniplast (PDF catalog)
sources.claim: IWT/Tecniplast robotic cage-processing cells (Pegasus, Apollo, RRE5) automate the whole vivarium cage-wash flow - dirty-side dumping and washer loading, washing, clean-side reassembly with bedding and water - running unattended for up to 90 minutes, with over 100 robots installed ... vivaria worldwide.

sources.system: Tecniplast cage-washing robots at Baylor College of Medicine
sources.title: Automation: robots in the vivarium | Lab Animal (Nature)
sources.claim: Robotic cage-washing systems are in real vivarium service: Baylor College of Medicine installed ... facility in 2006 and retrained a former manual cage-wash employee to maintain them.

sources.system: MULTIVAC line solutions for medical products (thermoform packaging line with loading robots)
sources.title: Line solutions for medical products | MULTIVAC
sources.claim: Fully automated industrial lines with loading robots place small metal medical devices into thermoformed sterile-barrier packs and seal, print and inspect them - the packaging step of instrument reprocessing performed by machine in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sterile-barrier packaging of small stainless medical devices (cannulas, syringes). Objects, seal integrity requirement and sterility standard match pouching instrument packs before autoclaving.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile robot with a manipulator physically wipes hospital surfaces and adds UV-C irradiation, assessed in a hospital environment; it addresses flat surface disinfection only, not disassembly, brushing and oiling of handheld clinical devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-situ cleaning/disinfection of clinical equipment surfaces; cited to mark the limit of current in-room capability.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide emergency first aid to sick or injured animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal clinic/ER triage of an incoming emergency (hit-by-car dog, collapsed or dyspneic pet): assistant meets the owner at the door or car, moves the animal on a stretcher or in a blanket, muzzles and restrains it, applies direct pressure to bleeding wounds, places it in an oxygen cage or holds a flow-by mask, takes temperature/pulse/respiration and reports to the vet.

Hemorrhage control and temporary wound care in the treatment area on a conscious, painful, often fractious dog or cat: muzzle/towel restraint, clipping fur, flushing and cleaning the wound, applying a pressure wrap, temporary splint or bandage until the veterinarian can treat.

Critical support during arrest or crisis: performing external chest compressions on a dog or cat, bag-mask ventilation, holding off a vein and restraining for IV catheter placement, handing/administering emergency drugs under veterinary direction.

Toxicity, seizure or heatstroke emergency: inducing vomiting per veterinary order, cooling a hyperthermic dog with fans and wet towels, protecting and monitoring a seizing animal, clearing airway secretions, monitoring vitals during stabilization.

Laboratory animal facility rounds: a sick or injured rodent/rabbit is found (dehydration, fight wound, prolapse, dystocia). The caretaker removes the animal from the cage, examines it, gives immediate supportive care (warming, subcutaneous fluids, wound cleaning, separation from cage mates), and alerts veterinary staff or euthanizes per protocol.

Emergency outside the controlled treatment area: animal collapses or bleeds in the parking lot, lawn or waiting room, or an injured stray is carried in by a member of the public; assistant goes out with a stretcher/blanket, restrains and stabilizes the animal amid bystanders, uneven ground and weather, and carries it inside.

sources.system: Stereo-vision high-throughput mouse tail vein injection robot
sources.developer: Preferred Networks / Chugai (Ko, Nishiwaki et al.)
sources.title: Development of a Stereo-vision based High-throughput Robotic System for Mouse Tail Vein Injection
sources.claim: A stereo-vision robotic device autonomously performs tail-vein injections in non-anesthetized mice held in a purpose-built restraint mechanism, succeeding in 37/40 mice; the animal must be loaded into the fixture by a person and the system does only the injection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: administering an injection to a live laboratory rodent, the closest automated physical intervention on a live animal relevant to first aid (fluids/drugs). Transfer is limited: it acts only on a tail fixed in a tourniquet/vacuum fixture and performs no assessment, handling, warming, wound care or triage, so it cannot complete a whole first-aid instance.

sources.developer: University Heart Center Freiburg-Bad Krozingen / University of Freiburg
sources.title: Development and evaluation of a mechanical chest compression device for standardized rodent cardiopulmonary resuscitation
sources.claim: A motorized mechanical chest compression device delivers standardized chest compressions to anesthetized, instrumented rats in a laboratory cardiac-arrest model, outperforming manual compressions for rate and position consistency; positioning of the animal and all other resuscitation steps are done by researchers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the chest-compression component of CPR on a small animal. Transfer is limited: the device is a bench research instrument applied to an anesthetized, surgically instrumented rat placed by a human, with no airway management, drug administration, patient assessment or handling of a conscious clinical patient.

sources.developer: Johns Hopkins University / Children's National Hospital
sources.title: Robot performs laparoscopic surgery, suturing intestinal tissue - ASME
sources.claim: The Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot performed autonomous laparoscopic intestinal suturing on live pig soft tissue under human supervision in a research operating room, showing autonomous manipulation of living tissue is confined to anesthetized animals in a fixed surgical setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic manipulation of living animal tissue (suturing a bowel). It marks the frontier but does not transfer to first aid: the patient is anesthetized, immobilized and surgically prepared, and the robot performs one pre-specified tissue task rather than restraining, examining and stabilizing a conscious injured animal.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling framework for robotic wound redressing
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Liang, Shen, Richter, Yip et al.)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic wound redressing is still a research problem addressed only at the level of individual subtasks (adhesive tape detachment and placement) on phantoms, anatomical models and human skin; clinical wound care remains entirely manual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying and removing dressings/bandages, a core first-aid action. It shows the frontier is a single subtask on static phantoms and cooperative human skin, far from bandaging a struggling, painful conscious animal.

sources.title: Robotic Cage Handling System for Tunnel Washers - Getinge
sources.claim: Commercially deployed robotics in laboratory animal facilities handles cages and the washing process, not the animals themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automation in the vivarium. It substantiates that deployed animal-facility robots manipulate rigid cages on conveyors, providing no capability for examining or treating a live sick or injured animal.

tasks.label: Prepare surgical equipment and pass instruments or materials to veterinarians during surgical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-animal general practice: between/after surgeries the assistant reprocesses instruments — rinse and ultrasonic-clean, dry, inspect and lubricate hinges, assemble the standard spay/neuter/dental pack, wrap in cloth or paper with a chemical indicator and autoclave tape, load and run the tabletop autoclave, unload and shelve the dated packs.

Small-animal practice: pre-op setup of the surgical suite — disinfect the table, assemble/leak-test the anesthesia machine and fill the vaporizer, position monitors and warming devices, gather the surgeon's preferred suture, blades, gauze and electrocautery, then open the sterile pack onto a draped Mayo stand and add sterile items without contaminating the field.

Routine soft-tissue or dental surgery: unscrubbed circulating support while the veterinarian operates — peel open suture/blade/gauze pouches and present contents onto the sterile field, hand materials, fetch an additional pack or instrument from a cabinet, adjust the light and suction, all while the case proceeds.

Specialty/referral or teaching hospital: scrubbed-in assistant serving the Mayo stand during a longer procedure (orthopedic repair, complex soft tissue) — passing scalpel, hemostats, retractors and needle drivers on verbal request or anticipation, receiving used instruments back, keeping the stand ordered and tracking counts.

Laboratory animal facility: prepare and sterilize instrument packs for rodent survival surgeries — clean and inspect small standard instruments, pouch or wrap sets, run the autoclave, and stock the surgery station with sterile packs, drapes and supplies.

Laboratory animal facility procedure room: assist the veterinarian/surgeon during rodent survival surgery — pass fine micro-instruments and suture at the small sterile field, re-sterilize tips in the hot-bead sterilizer between animals, open sterile supplies.

tasks.label: Prepare examination or treatment rooms by stocking them with appropriate supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General companion-animal clinic: restocking an exam room before/between appointments — checking par levels in drawers and counter organizers, walking to the central supply closet or pharmacy, and putting away heterogeneous small items (syringes, needles, gauze, alcohol swabs, thermometer covers, slides, vaccine vials from the fridge, gloves, treats, forms) into designated drawers, wall dispensers and jars, discarding expired stock.

Companion-animal hospital treatment/prep area and ward: restocking bandage and crash carts, IV fluid bags and lines, catheters, tape, syringes, sharps containers and PPE at multiple work stations from a rolling supply cart; rotating stock by expiry; done amid staff and animals moving through.

Surgery suite prep: stocking the room for scheduled procedures — pulling the correct sterile instrument packs, suture, blades, drapes, gowns, endotracheal tubes, fluid lines and gloves in the right sizes, laying them out on the Mayo stand/back table and replenishing surgery cabinets, maintaining sterility.

Laboratory animal facility (vivarium): stocking procedure and housing rooms with autoclaved cages, bedding, feed, water bottles, PPE, syringes, cage cards and sharps containers, moved by cart from cage-wash/clean-supply corridors under barrier/biosecurity protocols.

Large-animal/equine practice or mobile unit: restocking the ambulatory truck's compartments and the exam stall/mobile clinic work surface with drugs, sleeves, syringes, bandage material and dosing equipment, on a farm, barn aisle or parking-lot mobile clinic, in varying weather and clutter.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator deployed at scale in US hospitals, autonomously fetches supplies from supply closets/central supply and delivers them to patient rooms and nursing units, but its documented workflows are fetch-and-deliver (items carried in its own drawers), not putting supplies away into a room's cabinets and dispensers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply running. It covers the fetch-and-transport portion of room stocking in a comparable clinical facility, which is why it is the best E2 candidate; it does not cover put-away into drawers, dispensers or sterile layout.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Scale and maturity of the Moxi hospital fleet as of early 2026: roughly 100 robots doing fetch/deliver work in more than 25 hospital facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply and specimen delivery. Establishes that the deployed clinical-facility capability is delivery, bounding what E2 systems currently achieve.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual products of widely varying shape, size and weight from totes inside fenced fulfillment-center workcells where inventory is conveyed to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking heterogeneous packaged goods into containers. Exam-room stocking at E1 reduces to picking varied small packaged consumables from presented totes and placing them into fixtured trays/drawer inserts — comparable objects and precision.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics Introduces the RightPick 4 System
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick system performs autonomous piece-picking of individual items, explicitly including pharmaceutical products and general merchandise, in order-fulfillment workcells fed by totes.

sources.title: These speedy BD robot arms store and retrieve medications in seconds

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is a deployed, fixed rail-mounted robot that autonomously replenishes refrigerated store shelves with bottled and canned drinks in about 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, with rare remote human takeover.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment. Closest existing stocking system, but it is an installation built into one cooler handling a single product class — it shows placement-into-shelving works where the work zone is built for the machine.

sources.system: Vivus washer integrated robotic cell / Tecniplast vivarium automation
sources.title: Getinge Vivus Washer Series Vivarium Washer Solutions (product brochure)
