sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing clean, stocked caging and consumables for a lab animal facility. Same facility and supply items as vivarium room stocking, and it works because the cages are conveyed and fixtured for the machine.

sources.system: FANUC SR-3iA / SR-6iA medical assembly cells
sources.title: Medical Device & Equipment Manufacturing | FANUC America
sources.claim: Automated medical-device cells using FANUC SCARA robots perform assembly, tray loading and part transfer of medical components with vision inspection in fenced production cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic tray loading and kitting of sterile medical components. Supports the E1 counterfactual for surgery-suite stocking, where pack contents are presented fixtured and assembled into a tray.

tasks.label: Prepare feed for animals according to specific instructions, such as diet lists or schedules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Veterinary hospital/clinic treatment-area kitchen: assistant reads the whiteboard/PIMS diet orders for 8-20 hospitalized patients and prepares individual meals — weighed or measured portions of prescription canned and dry diets, warmed, sometimes with a topper or crushed/liquid medication mixed in, plated in labeled bowls matched to each cage card.

Rodent vivarium: caretaker provisions feed per protocol during cage change/room rounds — filling wire-bar hopper with irradiated pellets to a set level, topping racks, and issuing special diets (high-fat, medicated, purified) and hydration/nutrition gel packs only to the cages listed on the protocol/diet sheet, inside a barrier facility.

Animal shelter or boarding kennel: batch preparation of 30-100 bowls per feeding chart — scooping measured kibble (house or owner-supplied food), adding canned topper or soaked food, portioning by weight/size class, labeling and staging bowls on a cart for the run rows.

Non-rodent research species (dogs, rabbits, ferrets, nonhuman primates): weighing out biscuit/chow rations per animal body weight and study diet list, plus washing/chopping produce and preparing foraging or enrichment food items into individual pans.

Critical-care and neonatal feed preparation: blending canned recovery diet with warm water to a set kcal/ml consistency for syringe or feeding-tube use, reconstituting powdered milk replacer and filling warmed bottles/syringes for orphan puppies, kittens or nursery animals, per the clinician's written feeding plan.

sources.system: Chef Robotics ChefOS robotic food assembly system
sources.title: Physical AI Company Chef Robotics Completes 100 Million Servings in Production
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-enabled robotic arms autonomously portion measured servings of deformable foods (rice, sauces, proteins, vegetables) into meal trays on production lines, with 100 million servings completed in production across more than a dozen customer ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning measured servings of wet/dry deformable food into individual containers on a line. Transfers to preparing per-animal feed portions — comparable objects (canned/scoopable food, kibble), comparable precision (weight-controlled servings), same container-on-conveyor presentation.

sources.system: Chef Robotics system at Chef Bombay
sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: A deployed Chef Robotics system varies the recipe unit-by-unit: it picks and places multiple different ingredients at different portion sizes into several tray types and positions on existing conveyor lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: per-unit customized meal assembly. Transfers to 'prepare feed according to a diet list' because the machine selects different ingredients and portion sizes for each individual container, which is the core of following per-animal diet orders.

sources.title: Sweetgreen Goes All-In with Automated Restaurants — QSR Magazine
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline dispenses portioned ingredients into individual bowls per digital order at up to 500 bowls/hour in operating restaurants, with reported portioning consistency and near-perfect order accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order-driven bowl assembly. Transfers to filling animal bowls from a feeding chart — same object class (bowls on a line), same requirement to match a written per-recipient specification, same portioning precision.

sources.title: Blendid opens robotic food kiosk at California Walmart
sources.claim: Blendid operates autonomous robotic kiosks containing a robotic arm, blenders, refrigeration and ingredient dispensers that measure ingredients and blend made-to-order drinks without an operator, installed in Walmart stores and college campuses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measured multi-ingredient dispensing plus blending to a recipe and delivering the mixture in a container. Transfers to blending canned recovery diet with warm water or reconstituting formula: same liquid/semi-solid mixing, recipe-driven quantities, enclosed purpose-built cell.

sources.title: New Automated Robot System in Renown Health
sources.claim: ARxIUM's RIVA robotic compounding system autonomously prepares patient-specific syringes and IV bags to precise volumes inside an enclosed ISO-class workcell in hospital pharmacies; staff only load drugs and supplies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order-driven preparation of measured doses drawn into labeled syringes. Transfers to filling syringes with tube-feeding formula: same container, comparable or tighter volumetric precision, same 'prepare per written order for a named patient' workflow, in a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.system: In-line and metered cage-fill dispensers used with robotic cage-wash lines

sources.title: Feed and Bedding — Management of Animal Care and Use Programs in Research, Education, and Testing (NCBI Bookshelf)
sources.claim: Laboratory-animal facilities use automated metered dispensers that fill rodent cages with a set quantity of granular material as the cages pass on the cage-wash conveyor, in line with articulated-arm/foundry robotic cage-processing systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: metered dispensing of a dry granular material into rodent cages moving on a purpose-built line. Transfers to filling cage feed hoppers with pellets — same cages, same facility, same free-flowing granular product and volumetric metering.

sources.claim: SychemFILL is an automated clean-bedding dispenser for vivarium cage filling with programmable per-cage dispense volumes and ±4% dispensing accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: programmable metered filling of lab-animal cages with granular material; shows the achievable dose accuracy for feed-type dispensing. Operator presents each cage, so autonomy is not established and this item is supporting context only.

sources.title: Automation: robots in the vivarium | Lab Animal
sources.claim: A vivarium at Mount Sinai's Center for Comparative Medicine and ... runs a robotic cage-processing line in which an industrial robotic arm handles dirty rodent cages and an automatic dispenser refills clean cages on the clean side.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and refilling of the exact cage components whose hoppers hold feed. Establishes that the purpose-built (E1) cage-processing cell exists inside real vivaria and that cages can be presented to a dispensing station under machine control.

sources.title: Quick Feed Automatic Feeders
sources.claim: Quick Feed timer-driven automatic feeders dispense scheduled portions of dry feed and are sold for and used in pet boarding facilities and ... as well as stables and homes.

sources.system: Chef Robotics piece-picking and portioning system (Packline partnership)
sources.title: Chef Robotics and Packline Partner on End-to-End Meal Production Automation
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' robots also handle produce: placing discrete items such as ... packages and portioning scoopable produce such as corn into trays.

tasks.label: Provide assistance with euthanasia of animals or disposal of corpses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Companion-animal clinic euthanasia appointment with the owner present: assistant preps the room and euthanasia solution, places/holds an IV catheter, gently restrains and comforts a conscious, often anxious dog or cat while the veterinarian injects, monitors for death, then wraps the body and returns it or logs it for cremation while supporting the grieving client.

Clinic, ER or shelter euthanasia without the owner present: hospitalized patient, stray, or fractious/unsocialized cat or dog; assistant helps sedate, scruffs/muzzles or towel-restrains the live animal, holds off the vein, monitors, confirms with the vet, then bags and tags the body.

Clinic body care and corpse disposal only (no live-animal handling): a patient that died in hospital or was brought in deceased; assistant positions and cleans the body, makes a paw-print keepsake, bags/wraps and tags it, moves it to the walk-in cooler or freezer, keeps disposal records and loads it for the crematory service pickup.

Laboratory animal facility batch rodent euthanasia by CO2: caretaker pulls cages of mice from the rack, docks them on a CO2 euthanasia station, runs the prescribed charge/dwell cycle, then transfers carcasses/cage contents into biohazard bags and the carcass freezer, and returns cages to the wash line.

Laboratory euthanasia requiring hands-on technique or non-rodent species: cervical dislocation, decapitation or thoracotomy as a required secondary confirmation of death, anesthetic overdose/perfusion, rabbit or fish or nonhuman-primate euthanasia; plus per-animal carcass bagging, labeling and record entry.

In-home or field euthanasia and body removal: mobile veterinary visit in a client's living room or yard, or removal of a large dead dog/exotic from a home or vehicle; assistant restrains the pet on the family's floor or bed, then lifts and carries the wrapped body out to the van for transport to the crematory.

sources.title: Euthanex EZ-DOCK SMARTBOX Euthanasia Station | ARES Scientific
sources.claim: A commercially sold, fully automated CO2 euthanasia station for laboratory rodents runs the AVMA-compliant euthanasia cycle automatically once a mouse cage is docked, with no manual operation of the gas delivery.

sources.system: Vivarium robotic cage-wash cell at Mount Sinai Center for Comparative Medicine and Surgery
sources.developer: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (integrator-supplied industrial robot cell)
sources.title: Automation: robots in the vivarium | Lab Animal
sources.claim: Industrial robot arms are deployed in real vivaria to pick up rodent cages, dump their contents into the waste stream, and feed them to tunnel washers, i.e. machine handling of cage contents in a purpose-built robotic cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dirty-cage handling and waste dumping in a vivarium. It transfers to the disposal half of this task because the objects (rodent cages and their contents, routed to the facility waste stream) and the purpose-built cage-wash cell are the same ones a caretaker uses when clearing euthanized rodents.

sources.title: Robotic Cage Handling System for Tunnel Washers - Getinge
sources.claim: Robotic cage handling for laboratory animal facilities is a commercially available, installed product line that automates movement of animal cages through the wash process without operator handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated laboratory-animal cage logistics. Transfers to the corpse-disposal step because it shows machine transport and inversion of the same cages/containers in which euthanized rodents and their bedding are cleared, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: KUKA meat-processing robot cells (KR AGILUS HM / KR DELTA HM with AI 3D vision)
sources.title: Automated solutions for meat processing | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Vision-guided industrial robots handle and process whole pig and chicken carcasses at high throughput in purpose-built, fenced meat-plant cells where the carcass is presented on a line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of whole animal carcasses on a slaughter/dressing line. It transfers to corpse disposal because the objects are dead animal bodies of comparable or greater mass, the precision required is gross grasp-and-move plus identification/labeling, and the carcass arrives fixtured on a conveyor exactly as an E1 setting would present it.

sources.system: Broiler mortality removal robot (Li et al., Applied Engineering in Agriculture)
sources.title: Design and Development of a Broiler Mortality Removal Robot – IJERT
sources.claim: A research robot autonomously detected and picked up dead broilers by the shank, achieving 90% pickup success under favorable lighting, but only as a developed prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous location and pickup of dead animals in an animal-housing facility. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to retrieving a carcass in a clinic or vivarium, but at prototype maturity and ~90% success it falls short of worker-quality corpse handling outside a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Survey of dead-body detection and removal robots (128 studies reviewed)
sources.title: Death Detection and Removal in High-Density Animal Farming: Technologies, Integration, Challenges, and Prospects
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of death detection and dead-body removal in animal facilities finds that removal systems remain hardware-design research with limited validation on real farms and are not yet integrated into fully automated detect-and-remove operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous carcass removal in animal facilities. Cited as the state of the art showing that carcass pickup and disposal in a working, human-occupied animal facility (E2) is not yet demonstrated at deployable reliability.

tasks.label: Write reports, maintain research information, or perform clerical duties.

tasks.label: Perform hygiene-related duties, such as clipping animals' claws or cleaning and polishing teeth.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine nail trim on a cooperative-to-wiggly dog in a clinic exam or treatment room: a second person restrains the dog on a table or floor, the assistant lifts each paw, identifies the quick (often on dark nails), clips or Dremels 16-20 nails plus dewclaws, and applies styptic powder if a nail bleeds.

Nail trim on a fractious or fearful patient — most often a cat, sometimes a defensive dog: towel-wrap or scruff restraint, cat bag or muzzle, the animal struggles, kicks and may bite; the assistant works fast between struggles, decides when to stop and when sedation is needed.

Dental hygiene work: assisting or performing supragingival/subgingival scaling with an ultrasonic scaler and polishing with a prophy cup and paste on an anesthetized dog or cat positioned on a wet dental table with a mouth gag, suction and monitoring; or brushing the teeth of an awake hospitalized patient.

Other awake-patient hygiene work in the clinic: flushing and swabbing ears with cleaner and cotton, expressing anal glands, sanitary and paw-pad trims, trimming matted fur, cleaning eyes and skin folds — on a restrained pet that may resist.
Routine bath and dry of a healthy dog in the clinic's bathing/grooming area: shampoo (sometimes medicated with a contact time), rinse, towel and forced-air dry, brush out.

Laboratory animal hygiene in a barrier vivarium procedure room: trimming overgrown nails or incisors on rabbits and guinea pigs, cleaning soiled or urine-scalded fur, grooming/condition checks on rodents, performed in PPE under biosecurity with the animal manually restrained.

sources.system: Woofwoof Lux AI dog wash machine
sources.title: Phoenix dog gym debuts Arizona's first AI dog wash machine
sources.claim: Woof Woof Lux markets an automated dog-washing chamber that washes and dries a dog on its own once the dog is inside; a unit is installed and running as self-service at Paws 48 Dog Wash & Gym in Phoenix, using sensors, cameras and temperature gauges, with cycles of 5-20 minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: bathing/drying a live dog is one of the hygiene-related duties in this task; the machine is a purpose-built enclosure into which the dog is loaded, i.e. the work is brought to the machine.

sources.title: Perceptive Completes World's First Fully Automated Dental Procedure on a Human Using AI-Driven Robotic System
sources.claim: Perceptive reported the first fully automated robotic dental procedure on a human ... — a crown preparation performed by an AI-guided robotic arm with 3D imaging on an immobilized patient; a single unreviewed demonstration, not a scaling-and-polishing prophylaxis and not on animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (human restorative dentistry). Transfer does NOT carry to veterinary dental prophylaxis: the demonstrated act is drilling/crown prep on one tooth of a cooperative, brace-fixtured human, not full-mouth ultrasonic scaling, subgingival curettage and prophy-cup polishing across the widely varying dentition of an anesthetized, intubated dog or cat; it is a one-off, non-peer-reviewed demonstration with no animal work reported.

sources.system: Nova-Tech Poultry Support Platform / Hatchling Support System
sources.title: Nova-Tech Engineering - Poultry India Exhibition Hyderabad (YouTube)
sources.claim: Hatchery machines from Nova-Tech Engineering automatically perform infrared beak treatment, toe treatment ('de-clawing'), vaccination and counting on day-old poultry chicks conveyed through the machine — the only automated claw-treatment of live animals found.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (claw treatment of live animals in a purpose-built machine). Transfer does NOT carry: the machine handles uniform day-old poults on a hatchery conveyor with a fixed infrared applicator; it cannot grasp, restrain or clip the nails of a 3-45 kg dog or a struggling cat, whose nail size, curvature and quick position vary per animal and per nail.

sources.title: ASTER Labs | Automatic Nail Trimmer
sources.claim: ASTER Labs built a hands-free robotic toenail-trimming prototype for elderly users, using optical and infrared imaging to trim human toenails to recommended lengths, with safety cut-off if the toe moves; a research/development prototype rather than a fielded product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic nail trimming). Transfer does NOT carry: the device trims the toenails of a cooperative human who deliberately holds still and halts on any motion, whereas clipping a dog's or cat's claws requires restraining a resisting animal, holding and extending the paw, and cutting keratin ahead of a vascular quick; the system is also an unfielded prototype with no reported animal use.

sources.title: Tecniplast Vivarium Automation
sources.claim: Vivarium automation from Tecniplast consists of robotic arms and handling systems for cages — cage washing, waste disposal, loading/unloading — not for handling or grooming the animals themselves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (laboratory animal facility robotics). It shows the deployed automation envelope in vivaria is cage-level material handling; no cited system performs hygiene procedures such as nail or incisor trimming on live rabbits, guinea pigs or rodents.

tasks.label: Perform enemas, catheterizations, ear flushes, intravenous feedings, or gavages.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ear flush/otic cleaning on a dog (occasionally cat) in a small-animal clinic treatment area: awake or lightly sedated patient held by a colleague, otic cleanser instilled into the canal, canal base massaged, head-shake managed, debris wiped out with gauze/cotton, repeat until clean, patient's ears rechecked and animal returned to a kennel.

Placing an IV catheter and starting IV fluids/nutrition on a dog or cat: clip fur over the cephalic vein, aseptic prep, hold off the vein, insert over-the-needle catheter, advance and secure with tape, flush with saline, connect and start the fluid or parenteral-nutrition line, monitor the site.

Urinary catheterization of a sedated or restrained dog/cat on a treatment table: positioning the patient, aseptic prep of the vulva/prepuce, passing a sterile urinary catheter into the bladder, collecting urine or connecting a closed collection system, securing the catheter.

Enema on a constipated dog/cat, or orogastric/nasoesophageal tube feeding of a debilitated patient or neonatal kitten/puppy, in a clinic treatment area: measuring and lubricating the tube, gentle passage, verifying placement, slow warmed delivery, cleanup and patient monitoring.

Oral gavage dosing of laboratory mice or rats in a vivarium procedure room: retrieving animals from cages, scruff restraint, measuring the gavage needle to the last rib, passing it down the esophagus, delivering a weight-based volume, returning the animal to its cage; dozens of animals per session.

Intravenous dosing/fluid administration into the tail vein of restrained laboratory mice or rats in a vivarium or imaging suite: animal placed in a restrainer, tail warmed/dilated, needle placed in the lateral tail vein, measured volume of saline/compound/contrast infused, hemostasis at the site.

sources.system: Stereo-vision robotic mouse tail vein injection system (Ko et al., Preferred Networks / Chugai)
sources.developer: Preferred Networks with Chugai Pharmaceutical (Ko, Nishiwaki et al.)
sources.title: Development of a Stereo-vision based High-throughput Robotic System for Mouse Tail Vein Injection
sources.claim: A benchtop robot with a purpose-built mouse holding mechanism (tourniquet, vacuum port, tail-end fixture) autonomously locates the tail vein with stereo vision and injects saline into non-anesthetized mice, succeeding in 37 of 40 animals within three trials, ~1.5 min per animal.
sources.transferJustification: Tail-vein injection is the intravenous administration route used for rodent IV dosing/fluid delivery, i.e. the 'intravenous feedings' element of this task for laboratory rodents: same animals, same vessel, same fluid-delivery endpoint.

sources.system: Ultrasound-guided robotic blood drawing system (6-DoF arm + 3-DoF end-effector)
sources.developer: Tongji University group (Peng Qi et al.)
sources.title: Ultrasound-Guided Robotic Blood Drawing and In Vivo Studies on Submillimetre Vessels of Rats
sources.claim: An image-guided (ultrasound) robotic vascular-access system with a 6-DoF arm and 3-DoF end-effector performed in vivo needle insertion and blood drawing on the sub-millimetre tail veins of 40 rats with 95% first-attempt success.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic venipuncture in restrained/anesthetized rodents shares the decisive step of rodent IV access (needle placed in a <1 mm tail vein) with rodent intravenous dosing; it corroborates that vascular access in fixtured rodents is machine-achievable.

sources.developer: University of British Columbia (Woodard et al.)
sources.title: PiDose: an open-source system for accurate and automated oral drug administration to group-housed mice
sources.claim: PiDose is a home-cage attached automated device that weighs individual RFID-tagged group-housed mice and delivers a daily weight-based drug dose through drinking-water drops, explicitly as an alternative to manual gavage; it does not intubate the animal or perform gavage.
sources.transferJustification: Closest automation to oral gavage dosing: it automates oral drug delivery but by voluntary licking, so it cannot deliver a timed bolus of an arbitrary/unpalatable vehicle by intragastric intubation and does not substitute for the gavage procedure itself.

tasks.label: Exercise animals or provide them with companionship.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vet clinic / attached boarding kennel: exercising healthy boarded or kenneled dogs — take the dog out of its run, leash it, walk it outside or turn it out into the exercise yard for 10–20 minutes, several dogs per shift, then return it to its run.

Animal hospital ward: short mobility walks and gentle exercise for hospitalized, post-operative, geriatric or fragile patients — dogs with IV catheters, e-collars, bandages or sling support, walked slowly to a grass strip and back, pace and effort adjusted to the animal's condition.

Shelter / boarding kennel: individual play, attention and enrichment session with a dog in its kennel run or a play room — tossing treats and toys, chase and fetch games, short training games to relieve kennel stress, done daily per the facility's enrichment schedule.
Cattery / clinic cat ward: daily play and exercise session for caged cats — wand-toy and chase play, out-of-cage playtime in a cat room, logged as enrichment for each cat.

Laboratory animal facility: socialization handling and enrichment of rodents and rabbits — gentle cupping/handling to habituate mice and rats, placing tunnels, chew items and nesting material into cages inside a change hood, out-of-cage exercise pen time for rabbits.

Clinic ward / vivarium: providing comfort and companionship to anxious, fearful or recovering animals — sitting with a dog waking from anesthesia, stroking and talking to a frightened cat, hand-feeding and cuddling a hospitalized patient or a lab beagle during required human-contact time.

sources.system: Centaur Hound Walker (Automated Dog Walker) Models 400 / 600
sources.title: Automated Hound Walkers | Hound Exercise Equipment | Centaur Horse Walkers
sources.claim: Centaur Horse Walkers manufactures and sells commercial 'hound walkers' — motor-driven automated dog walkers with 4 or 6 arms, quick-release leads, variable speed up to about 5 mph in both directions (Model 400 $5,600, Model 600 $7,700) — marketed to breeders, boarding and training facilities to exercise dogs once they are clipped to the arms.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: the machine performs the exercise portion of this task (walking dogs) once each dog is clipped to a lead, which is the fixtured presentation an E1 setting supplies.

sources.developer: Companion Labs (Companion Professional, Inc.), San Francisco
sources.title: What's included with the Companion Device
sources.claim: The Companion device is a fixed kennel-mounted machine with a wide-angle camera, on-board computer vision and a precision treat launcher that recognizes a dog's pose and movement and launches treats to create chase and lure games, running interactive sessions with the dog without a person present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous positive-reinforcement training/play; it transfers because the accepted output here is an interactive attention/enrichment session with a kenneled dog, delivered by the same treat-launching chase and game behaviours.

sources.developer: Companion Labs, with San Francisco SPCA
sources.title: SF SPCA Partners with Companion on an Innovative Approach to Training - San Francisco SPCA
sources.claim: The San Francisco SPCA reports that Companion can engage and train shelter dogs independently to high levels of responsiveness and that the shelter began installing CompanionPro devices in its own kennels to give dogs individual attention and enrichment that staff and volunteers cannot always provide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated training of shelter dogs; the shelter frames it as substituting for the individual daily attention/enrichment that caretakers give kenneled dogs, which is the companionship leg of this task.

sources.developer: Companion Labs (with Google TensorFlow Lite / Edge TPU)
sources.title: Autonomous Dog Training with Companion — The TensorFlow Blog
sources.claim: Companion's developers describe a device that trains dogs on its own, detecting the behaviour with sensors and rewarding it immediately, building duration over repeated unattended sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the autonomy (no human in the loop) of the system cited for kenneled-dog enrichment sessions.

sources.title: VARRAM - Apps on Google Play
sources.claim: The VARRAM Pet Fitness Robot is a shipped consumer robot that drives itself around a room on a schedule with time-of-flight obstacle avoidance, luring dogs and cats into chase play and dispensing treats to get them moving and exercising.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: the robot delivers the play/exercise session for a cat or dog placed in the same space with it, which is the accepted output of a play-enrichment session.

sources.title: ORO: Your Dog's Pawfect Companion — CES Innovation Awards 2024
sources.claim: ORo, a dog companion robot from Ogmen Robotics, won a CES 2024 Innovation Award in robotics; it uses autonomous mobility and on-board AI to follow a dog, launch a ball for fetch and provide mental stimulation while owners are away.
sources.transferJustification: Direct: autonomous fetch/chase play with a dog is the exercise-and-companionship output of this task, though maturity is only award/demo stage.

tasks.label: Dust, spray, or bathe animals to control insect pests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Flea/tick or medicated bath of a cooperative dog in a clinic, boarding or shelter bathing room: dog lifted into a stainless tub, secured with a grooming loop, wet down, insecticidal shampoo lathered to the skin including a lather 'collar' at the head/neck, held for contact time, rinsed, towel/force dried, flea-combed.

Applying a flea/tick spray, mist or powder over a dog's coat in the exam or treatment area: dog restrained on a table or floor, product misted or dusted against the lay of the hair over the whole body, worked in by hand, eyes/nose shielded, excess wiped, owner instructions given.

Cat treated for fleas: flea dip/bath of an infested cat or kitten, or a flea spray/dust applied while the cat is scruffed, towel-wrapped or in a restraint bag; high risk of scratching/biting, animal fights the water, two staff often needed.

Heavily infested, matted, fearful or debilitated dog at shelter/stray intake or a neglect case: dense flea burden, feces- or urine-soaked matted coat, animal may be fractious or too weak to stand, repeated dips/baths, careful drying and warming afterwards.

Laboratory rodents or rabbits in a vivarium treated for fur mites/lice: animals removed from cages inside a biosafety cabinet, dusted/sprayed or topically treated individually, or pesticide dust applied to animals and bedding across a rack of cages, with PPE and cage-card documentation.

Exotic and small companion animals (rabbit, guinea pig, ferret, bird, reptile) dusted with mite powder or lightly sprayed: fragile animal held in a towel or gentle grip, powder worked into fur/feathers by hand, avoiding eyes, nares and, in birds, wetting the plumage.

sources.system: Lavakan LVK automatic pet washing cabins (LVK-IO, LVK-120 Silence, LVK-180 XL)
sources.date: 2024-02 (product brochure); product line commercially sold since 1999
sources.title: "Invest in their Wellness: A Spa, a World of Opportunities" - Cabinas Lavakan (EN) brochure
sources.claim: Lavakan manufactures stainless-steel enclosed dog washing cabins sold commercially (installed in Spain, Andorra, Miami and elsewhere) that run a bath in a fully automatic mode: the dog is placed in the closed cabin, and the machine applies shampoo, rinses and dries it with an automatic drying system, with no person handling the animal during the cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: machine-applied bathing of a dog with a dispensed shampoo product; the brochure lists '3 Shampoo programs' and an 'Automatic drying system', i.e. the wash/rinse/dry cycle is executed by the machine on the animal.

sources.system: Dog washing machines (Lavakan de Aste, PetSpa and similar automated bathing cabins)
sources.title: What are Dog Washing Machines? Alternatives to Bathing your Dog - PetPlace
sources.claim: Commercial dog washing machines are enclosed cabins with lathering and rinsing jets, dryers and a dosing system for administering topical products, running an automated car-wash-style cycle (wet-down, lather, rinse, temperature-controlled dry) that bathes and dries a dog in under half an hour; the machines keep the pet's head out of the jet spray and nervous pets can still be sprayed in the eyes or ears.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: the 'dosing system for topical product ...' plus lathering jets is the mechanism by which an insecticidal shampoo/antiparasitic solution would be applied to a dog inside the cabin; the same source records the head-exclusion limitation.

sources.title: Autolavado de Mascotas - ProWash
sources.claim: ProWash sells enclosed automatic pet self-wash cabins in Spain that are configured with dispensers for shampoo, conditioner, perfume and an antiparasitic product plus integrated drying, and are marketed for installation in veterinary clinics, pet shops and boarding kennels without permanent staff.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that antiparasitic product is a standard dispensed program in commercial pet-wash cabins of this class; autonomy of the cabin's own wash cycle is not established from the vendor page, so this item is supporting context only.

sources.system: Lavakan cabins, Andorra la Vella centres
sources.title: Bathe your pet in an easy and hygienic way with Lavakan - Guia Andorra
sources.claim: Lavakan pet-wash centres deliver insect-repellent treatment (natural andiroba oil) alongside the cabin's bathing programmes, indicating that insect-control products are part of the service offered through these automatic bathing cabins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (insect-repellent application at a cabin centre); it is cited only to show insect-control products are used with these machines, not to establish autonomous application.

sources.system: Tecniplast vivarium automation (AGV/AMR and robotic cage-handling systems)
sources.title: How Technology Stacking Is Redefining Laboratory Animal Science - Tecniplast USA
sources.claim: Robotic automation deployed in modern laboratory animal facilities consists of cage-handling equipment - AGVs, autonomous mobile robots and articulating arms integrated into cage wash and transport lines; the animals themselves are still handled by staff, and no cited system dusts, sprays or bathes live rodents.
sources.transferJustification: Related-task evidence showing the boundary of deployed vivarium robotics: it moves and washes cages, not animals, so it does not transfer to dusting or spraying live rodents for mites.

tasks.label: Administer anesthetics during surgery and monitor the effects on animals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine small-animal surgery in a companion-animal clinic surgical suite (spay/neuter, mass removal, orthopedic): assistant verifies the IV catheter, gives the induction agent to effect, intubates the dog or cat, connects the ET tube to the circle circuit, titrates isoflurane/sevoflurane, places and reads ECG/SpO2/capnograph/BP, checks jaw tone, palpebral and pedal reflexes, charts vitals every 5 minutes, responds to apnea, bradycardia and hypotension under DVM direction, then extubates and recovers the patient.

High-volume spay/neuter or shelter clinic: assistant weighs and restrains multiple cats and dogs, draws and gives IM/IV injectable protocols (e.g., ketamine/dexmedetomidine/butorphanol), uses chamber or mask induction for fractious cats, monitors depth largely by observation (respiration, reflexes, mucous membranes) with minimal instrumentation while several patients are anesthetized in parallel, and gives reversal agents at the end.

Laboratory rodent survival surgery in a vivarium procedure room: caretaker weighs the mouse/rat, induces in an isoflurane chamber, confirms loss of righting reflex, transfers the animal to a nose cone on a warmed platform or stereotaxic frame, applies eye ointment, verifies surgical plane by toe pinch, adjusts vaporizer percent and monitors respiration/color/temperature through the procedure per the approved IACUC protocol, and recovers the animal.

Sedation or light anesthesia for dentals, radiographs, wound care and endoscopy in a clinic treatment area: assistant gives sedatives, maintains the patient on gas or top-up boluses, watches for apnea, bradycardia, arousal and airway obstruction, bags the patient or adjusts flow, suctions the mouth during dentals, and alerts the veterinarian to changes.

Compromised, geriatric/pediatric, emergency or exotic patients (rabbits, birds, reptiles, ferrets) in a clinic or exotics practice: species-specific masks or small ET tubes, difficult airways, thermoregulation support, unstable vitals requiring frequent hands-on intervention, fluid and drug boluses, and close minute-to-minute monitoring during an unpredictable procedure.

sources.title: A technical description of a novel pharmacological anesthesia robot | Journal of Clinical Monitoring and Computing
sources.claim: McSleepy is a closed-loop 'pharmacological anesthesia robot' that autonomously titrates intravenous hypnotic, opioid and muscle relaxant in human patients using BIS, analgoscore and phonomyography feedback; it controls drug delivery only, with clinicians performing IV access, airway management and patient handling, and it has not been shown administering or monitoring anesthesia in animals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated titration of anesthetic drugs in human surgical patients. It is the closest demonstrated automation of the 'administer and monitor' core, but it operates on a pre-placed IV line in a human OR with an anesthesiologist securing the airway, so it does not cover the veterinary assistant's intubation, restraint, reflex checks or species-specific dosing.

sources.developer: National Cerebral and Cardiovascular Center / Akita Cerebrospinal and Cardiovascular Center, Japan
sources.title: Computer-controlled closed-loop norepinephrine infusion system for automated control of mean arterial pressure in dogs under isoflurane-induced hypotension: a feasibility study
sources.claim: A computer-controlled closed-loop norepinephrine infusion system autonomously monitored invasive arterial pressure and titrated drug to correct isoflurane-induced hypotension in six anesthetized Beagles in a research laboratory; the anesthetic itself was set and delivered by humans, and no handling, intubation or depth assessment was automated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated hemodynamic management of an anesthetized dog. It shows machine control of one monitored effect in the same species, but it does not administer the anesthetic, secure the airway, assess anesthetic depth or handle the patient, so it cannot substitute for the assistant's whole anesthesia role.

sources.system: Soft-actuator robotic tracheal intubation system; Kepler Intubation System (KIS)
sources.developer: Chinese research group (soft-actuator system); Thomas Hemmerling, McGill University (KIS)
sources.title: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system based on a soft actuator? - PubMed
sources.claim: A robot-assisted tracheal intubation system using a soft actuator performed automated intubation only on an airway manikin; no robotic system has been shown intubating live dogs, cats or exotic patients, and the widely cited Kepler Intubation System is remote-controlled rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic endotracheal intubation. Intubation is a required step of the clinic instances; the demonstration is manikin-only and in human airway anatomy, so it does not substantiate intubating a live animal patient.

sources.system: Robotic device for automated tail vein cannulation in rodent models
sources.developer: Rutgers University (Balter, Chen, Yarmush et al.)
sources.title: Design and Evaluation of a Robotic Device for Automated Tail Vein Cannulations in Rodent Models - PMC
sources.claim: An image-guided robotic device performs automated needle insertion into the tail vein of a rodent held in a purpose-built animal holding platform, showing that vascular access in a fixtured rodent can be automated; the work is bench-level device evaluation and includes no anesthetic administration, depth assessment or intraoperative monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated intravenous access in rodents. It covers only the injection step for a rodent already fixtured in a holder; the paper's own text lists live-animal evaluation as future work, and nothing in it addresses inducing, maintaining or monitoring surgical anesthesia.

sources.system: Brain-machine interface for closed-loop control of medically-induced coma (rodent CLAD)
sources.developer: MIT / Massachusetts General Hospital (Shanechi, Ching, Brown et al.)
sources.title: A Brain-Machine Interface for Control of Medically-Induced Coma | PLOS Computational Biology
sources.claim: Closed-loop anesthetic delivery systems in rats use EEG burst-suppression feedback to control intravenous propofol infusion automatically, but these are neuroscience demonstrations of medically induced coma in instrumented, already-catheterized rats, not surgical-plane anesthesia with airway, thermal and reflex management.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated anesthetic dosing in rodents. It is the closest system to the vivarium instance, but the target is burst suppression in a coma model with human-placed catheters and electrodes, not maintenance of a surgical plane with nociceptive stimulation, warming and recovery.

tasks.label: Groom, trim, or clip animals' coats.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Surgical/procedure prep clipping in a small-animal clinic: with the patient sedated or anesthetized on a prep table (or manually restrained for an IV catheter site or ultrasound window), the assistant runs a #40 clipper over the site, clipping with and against hair growth, tensioning loose skin, avoiding nicks over prepuce/nipples/skin folds, and vacuuming loose hair.

Routine brushing, combing and de-shedding of hospitalized or boarded dogs and cats in the clinic ward/kennel area: animal on a table, on the floor, or in the run; loose hair removed, small tangles worked out, coat checked for fleas/wounds, with the animal free to move and sometimes wriggly or sore.
Bathing and drying a cooperative dog in the clinic tub area: wet-down, shampoo (routine or medicated with contact time), rinse, and blow/cage dry before discharge or after soiling.

Full clipper groom on a dog at the clinic grooming station: bathe, dry, then a body clip plus sanitary, face, feet and ear trim to a requested length/style, with scissoring to blend, on a standing animal that shifts position.

Clipping out heavy mats or feces-soiled fur on an anxious, fractious or painful patient (often a cat, sometimes sedated): blade worked under tight mats against loose, fragile skin, with restraint, frequent repositioning, and high risk of clipper burn or laceration.

sources.developer: Lavakan (Lavakan de Aste / Lavakan Factory S.L., Spain)
sources.title: Pampered Pets: Lavakan in Miami offers hands-free spa service for your fur babies - WSVN 7News
sources.claim: Lavakan sells commercially deployed enclosed automatic pet-washing cabins that run a wash-and-dry program on a dog placed inside; the US location in Miami operates them as a self-service pet spa.
sources.transferJustification: Bathing and drying a dog's coat is one grooming variant of this task; the machine performs the whole wet-down/shampoo/rinse/dry sequence on the live animal.

sources.system: Lavakan de Aste and PetSpa automatic dog washing machines
sources.title: What are Dog Washing Machines? Alternatives to Bathing your Dog | PetPlace
sources.claim: Automatic dog washing machines are sold to grooming salons, veterinary offices, kennels and boarding ..., and run a fixed automated cycle of wet-down, lather, rinse and temperature-controlled drying with a topical product dosing system, bathing and drying a dog in under half an hour; they must be supervised and some pets do not tolerate the enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Bathing/drying a dog's coat in a clinic or salon is a grooming variant of this task; these units are explicitly sold into veterinary offices and grooming salons for that work.

sources.system: AWI Robotic Assisted Shearing (Robotic Assisted Shearing Scoping Study, with Ranken Research / Robo Shear)
sources.date: 2019 project start; project page current as of 2026
sources.title: Wool Harvesting Innovations | Australian Wool Innovation
sources.claim: The closest analog to machine clipping of a live animal's coat, Australian Wool Innovation's robotic-assisted shearing work, has only reproduced shearing motions on a life-size 3D-printed sheep, i.e. no live-animal robotic clipping capability.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic shearing is the nearest related task (a machine running a cutting head over a live animal's body); it remains a scripted prototype on a printed model, so it cannot substantiate clipping a live patient's coat.

sources.system: Robotic hair combing system on a Kinova-class general-purpose arm
sources.developer: University of Southern California (Dennler, Shin, Matarić, Nikolaidis)
sources.title: Design and Evaluation of a Hair Combing System Using a General-Purpose Robotic Arm
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic hair care exists only as laboratory research: a general-purpose arm that plans and executes combing paths through hair, evaluated in user studies rather than deployed work.
sources.transferJustification: Combing hair is the related task closest to brushing an animal's coat, but the demonstrations are on stationary human/wig hair in a lab, not on a live moving animal, and are research-grade, so they cannot substantiate worker-quality completion.

sources.system: Haircutting robots (survey of gantry-, manipulator- and hybrid-based systems)
sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: Robotic haircutting — the closest analog to clipping a coat to a style — is described in a 2025 peer-reviewed perspective as an emerging, not-yet-realized market, with foundational technologies still under review.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting hair to a length/style on a living subject is the nearest related task to clipping an animal's coat; the literature shows only emerging prototypes, so no positive transfer is available.

roles.title: Phlebotomists
roles.description: Draw blood for tests, transfusions, donations, or research. May explain the procedure to patients and assist in the recovery of patients with adverse reactions.

tasks.label: Confirm the identities of patients by verifying their personal information.
Match laboratory requisition forms to specimen tubes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient patient service center / hospital outpatient draw station: phlebotomist pulls up the electronic order or paper requisition, selects the correct tube types and number of tubes for the ordered tests, applies the printed patient labels, verifies each labeled tube against the requisition after the draw, and puts the matched tubes plus paperwork in the transport rack/bag.

Hospital inpatient bedside draw: at the patient's room, phlebotomist scans the wristband, matches the order labels/requisition to the tubes drawn, labels each tube at bedside, cross-checks tube type against ordered test, and bags the tubes with the requisition for transport to the lab; performed on a crowded cart in a patient room with staff and equipment present.

Clinical laboratory specimen receiving/accessioning bench: batches of tubes arrive in transport bags from clinics and floors; the worker opens each bag, matches every tube to its requisition or LIS order, checks that tube type and volume fit the tests ordered, flags mismatches/unlabeled tubes, and sorts the matched tubes into department racks.

Physician-office lab or clinic drawing for multiple referring labs: mostly paper requisitions (some handwritten, varied formats, checkbox test panels). The worker reads the form, picks the right tubes for the checked tests, handwrites/applies labels, staples or bags the requisition with the matching tubes for courier pickup.

Mobile work — home draws, insurance paramedical exams, nursing-home rounds, and mobile blood drives: tubes and forms handled on a portable tray or folding table in a living room, resident's room, or gym; worker matches donor/patient forms to the tubes and packs them into the collection kit.

sources.date: 2021 (product pages; product line in service since 2000s)
sources.title: Automated Tube Selecting and Labeling System BC・ROBO-8001RFID | Techno Medica Co., Ltd
sources.claim: Techno Medica's BC-ROBO is a commercial automated tube selecting and labeling machine that reads the test request, selects the correct blood collection tubes, applies patient barcode labels, and outputs an all-in-one patient kit of labeled tubes plus a work list — i.e., it creates and delivers the requisition-to-tube match.
sources.transferJustification: Same task, machine-side: the accepted output of 'match requisition to specimen tube' is the correct tube set bound to the correct order; BC-ROBO produces exactly that pairing from the test request, with the same objects (blood collection tubes) and the same labeling precision.

sources.developer: Techno Medica (deployed at a 3,800-bed academic medical center, Taiwan)
sources.title: Reduction in Hospital-Wide Clinical Laboratory Specimen Identification Errors following Process Interventions: A 10-Year Retrospective Observational Study (PLOS One)
sources.claim: Two BC-ROBO 787 automated tube selecting and label ... were installed at the outpatient phlebotomy station of a 3,800-bed academic medical center, replacing manual barcode labeling, and specimen identification errors were tracked over a decade — real deployment in a working outpatient draw area.
sources.transferJustification: The deployed function is the tube/order match itself (selecting and labeling the tubes that correspond to the patient's test request) at an outpatient phlebotomy station, the same setting and objects as the task instance.

sources.system: Automated tube dispensing/labeling robot (pre-analytical modular automation)
sources.title: Right-Sizing Laboratory Automation | Clinical Lab Products
sources.claim: Trade press confirms that order-driven tube dispensing/labeling robots are in routine use at scale in phlebotomy areas, dispensing the labeled tubes for each patient's blood testing order into a dedicated tray or bag.
sources.transferJustification: Dispensing the correct labeled tubes into a per-patient tray keyed to that patient's order is the physical realization of matching requisition to specimen tubes; same objects and same accepted output.

sources.title: Pre-analytical phase: The automated ProTube device supports quality assurance in the phlebotomy process (Clinica Chimica Acta)
sources.claim: Inpeco's ProTube is a compact automated device used at the point of collection that identifies the patient and prints/applies labels to the correct tubes for the order; in a published comparison it labeled 48,776 tubes for 15,010 patients with complete traceability of the collection process.
sources.transferJustification: The device performs the order-to-tube binding at the draw station (correct tube types, correct patient label), which is the phlebotomist's requisition-to-tube match, at scale and at accepted clinical quality.

sources.system: cobas p 512 / cobas p 612 pre-analytical system
sources.title: cobas p 512 p 612 pre-analytical systems — Roche Dialog
sources.claim: Roche's cobas p 512 / p 612 pre-analytical systems automatically register primary samples, rotate and read tube barcodes, identify tube type, check sample volume/quality, and sort tubes into freely defined output areas at up to 1,400 samples/hour — the machine-side accessioning match of tube to LIS order.
sources.transferJustification: Accessioning is the lab-side form of the same task: each arriving tube is read and bound to the correct order record and routed accordingly; identical objects (barcoded blood tubes) and identical accepted output (tube correctly associated with its order).

sources.title: Sample Processing System AutoMate 2500 SLGP — McKesson Medical-Surgical
sources.claim: Beckman Coulter's AutoMate 2500 sample processing system reads each tube's barcode to establish positive sample identification with the LIS and uses 3-D cap-color analysis to validate that the tube type matches the test that was ordered, then robotically sorts tubes to destination racks.
sources.transferJustification: Validating tube type against the ordered test and binding the tube to its order record is precisely the verification content of matching requisition forms to specimen tubes, performed on the same blood tubes.

sources.system: Two UR5 collaborative robots (blood sample handling/sorting cell)
sources.developer: Universal Robots (integrated at Copenhagen University Hospital, Gentofte)
sources.title: Cobots work collaboratively at Gentofte hospital lab | Universal Robots case story
sources.claim: Two UR5 collaborative robots were installed in the clinical laboratory of Copenhagen University Hospital Gentofte, where one robot picks up each blood sample, presents it to a barcode scanner, and places it in the correct rack, handling about 3,000 samples per day.
sources.transferJustification: Reading each tube's identity and routing it to the rack corresponding to its ordered analysis is the physical sorting half of requisition-to-tube matching, on the same specimen tubes, in a hospital laboratory.

sources.system: Review of cobots, AMRs and total laboratory automation in clinical diagnostics
sources.title: Collaborative Robotics, Mobile Platforms, and Total Laboratory Automation in Clinical Diagnostics
sources.claim: A 2026 peer-reviewed review of clinical-laboratory robotics states that, despite total laboratory automation, bench-level manipulation and specimen transport in the human-configured parts of the lab remain manual — indicating no deployed robot performs the matching work in the ordinary human bench workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as a limiting/negative datum on E2 capability in clinical labs, not to support any positive judgment.

tasks.label: Dispose of contaminated sharps, in accordance with applicable laws, standards, and policies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient/ED bedside draw: after venipuncture the phlebotomist activates the needle safety device and immediately drops the needle-and-holder or butterfly set (with attached tubing, wet with blood) into a portable sharps container carried on the phlebotomy tray/cart, in an occupied patient room with bed rails, IV poles, visitors and clutter around the bedside.

Outpatient patient service center / clinic or hospital outpatient draw station: high-volume seated draws where the used needle assembly is dropped into a fixed wall-mounted or countertop sharps container within arm's reach of the draw chair, dozens of times per shift, standard layout and equipment.

Blood donation center or mobile blood drive: after a whole-blood or apheresis collection the 16G needle with attached tubing/collection set is sealed off, the safety shield engaged, and the needle placed into a sharps container at the donor bed, per AABB/FDA and center policy.

Sharps container management: checking fill lines, closing and locking full containers, removing them from wall brackets or carts, replacing with fresh containers, carrying sealed containers to the soiled-utility/biohazard storage room for the waste vendor, and logging it per policy.

Mobile/home phlebotomy (home health, homebound patients, insurance paramedical exams, nursing-home room visits): carrying a portable sharps container to the point of use, discarding the used needle immediately in a living room, kitchen table or resident's room, and transporting the closed container back to base for disposal.

sources.system: RIVA (Robotic IV Automation), Intelligent Hospital Systems / ARxIUM
sources.title: How RIVA works at Greenville Hospital Systems | Healthcare Packaging
sources.claim: The RIVA automated IV compounding robot, working inside an enclosed ISO Class 5 cell in hospital pharmacies, presents syringes to a decapper/deneedler and discards the removed needles and caps into a sharps waste container as part of its normal autonomous cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic de-needling and sharps discard in pharmacy compounding. The object (a hypodermic needle on a syringe hub) and the action (grip the sharp and deposit it in a sharps waste container without a needlestick or drop) are the same as a phlebotomist's disposal step; the compounding version demands equal or greater precision, and the sharp is presented to the robot in a fixtured, known position, which is exactly the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: ARxIUM Celebrates Major RIVA Milestone
sources.claim: RIVA is a mature commercial product with a global installed base in hospital pharmacies, having supported preparation of more than nineteen ... compounded doses, indicating the needle-handling/discard cycle runs routinely at production reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the cited E1 sharps-handling capability is a deployed commercial system at scale, not a one-off demonstration.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy ... autonomously picks up a single-use 21G blood collection set, inserts and withdraws the needle and completes the draw in outpatient phlebotomy departments; 1633 patients were drawn in routine use with a 94.5% first-stick rate and 0.6% mild adverse events, with one supervisor per three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous machine handling of the very blood-collection needle set a phlebotomist must discard. It shows a robot can grip, manipulate and release a contaminated venipuncture needle within its own purpose-built station; the published procedure description does not document deposit of the used set into a sharps container, so it supports handling of the sharp at a machine-structured station (E1), not free-standing disposal in a human clinic.

sources.system: Washsmart robotic washline / Sharpsmart reusable sharps containers
sources.title: Daniels Robotic Washline Technology
sources.claim: Daniels Health's Washsmart system is a fully automated ... line at dedicated processing facilities that empties (decants) full reusable Sharpsmart sharps containers and feeds them through washing, sanitizing and drying stages.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of full, contaminated sharps containers. It is the same object class (clinical sharps containers) and the same handling problem (lift, open/close, move without spillage or needlestick), performed on a purpose-built line where containers are presented to the machine, which is the E1 counterfactual for a container change-out.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, the largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulators, autonomously picks supplies from supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms in US hospitals; its documented duties are fetch-and-deliver of supplies, lab samples and medications, not handling of contaminated sharps or sharps containers.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterize the state of the art for autonomous manipulation inside a structured hospital (E2): the most capable deployed hospital mobile manipulator handles packaged supplies and samples, and no source shows it or any peer grasping a used needle or servicing a sharps container, which grounds the negative E2 judgments.

tasks.label: Dispose of blood or other biohazard fluids or tissue, in accordance with applicable laws, standards, or policies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outpatient draw station / hospital outpatient lab: after each routine venipuncture, the phlebotomist activates the safety needle and drops the needle-and-holder into the wall- or counter-mounted sharps container, and discards contaminated gauze, gloves, alcohol pads and wrappers into the correct (red-bag vs regular) stream, dozens of times per shift, with the patient still seated.

Inpatient bedside rounds: after a draw at the bedside (sometimes an isolation room, low light, lines and clutter on the overbed table), the needle goes into the portable sharps container on the phlebotomy tray/cart, blood-soaked gauze and gloves into the room's biohazard bin; nothing contaminated may be left in the room or bed linens.

Periodic waste round: close and seal full sharps containers at draw stations, install replacements, tie off and replace red biohazard bags, and carry regulated medical waste to the soiled utility room or waste holding area, documenting per state/OSHA requirements.

Specimen-processing area of the lab: discard leftover, rejected, or storage-expired blood tubes, aliquots, capillary devices and contaminated processing consumables into biohazard waste at the end of the retention period or shift.

Mobile blood drive, bloodmobile, nursing-home or home draw: gather used needles/collection sets, blood-soaked gauze and contaminated supplies into a portable sharps container and biohazard bag in a found space (school gym, church hall, patient's living room), and carry them back for disposal.

Cleanup of a blood spill: a tube breaks, a site bleeds through, or a patient faints and bleeds onto the chair/floor; the phlebotomist absorbs the fluid, disinfects the surface, and disposes of the saturated absorbent and gloves as regulated medical waste.

sources.title: Blood drawing robot heading for pivotal trials | pharmaphorum
sources.claim: Vitestro's autonomous blood-drawing robot performs the entire venipuncture procedure end-to-end, including disposal of the used needle, without an operator performing the steps.

sources.title: Vitestro launches new website and first public video of Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: The Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy ... is CE marked and in clinical use in European outpatient/laboratory phlebotomy departments, autonomously performing routine diagnostic draws including handling of the needle and tubes inside the device.

sources.title: cobas p 701 post-analytical unit — Roche Diagnostics
sources.claim: Roche's cobas p 701 post-analytical unit, fed by automation transport lines in clinical labs, automatically discards blood specimen tubes into waste once their storage period expires, replacing manual 'sample wasting'.

sources.title: Daniels Robotic Washline Technology
sources.claim: Daniels Health processes full reusable sharps containers with a fully automated robotic washline that decants (empties) the sharps-filled containers and returns them clean, i.e. machines handle sealed sharps waste containers end-to-end in a purpose-built plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emptying and handling of full sharps containers. It substantiates that machines can invert, empty and reprocess sharps waste containers autonomously when containers are presented on a purpose-built line — the E1 counterfactual for the phlebotomist's container-swap step.

sources.system: ZenRobotics Fast Picker / Heavy Picker sorting robots

sources.claim: ZenRobotics AI sorting robots autonomously pick heterogeneous waste items off a moving conveyor and place them into separate output streams at high rates in dedicated sorting facilities.

Comparable object variety and pick precision, and it establishes that stream-correct waste segregation is achievable when waste is presented to the machine on a purpose-built conveyor (E1), not when it lies about a human work area.

sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi operates autonomously in hospital corridors doing non-patient-facing logistics including delivering lab samples and removing soiled linen bags; it does not seal sharps containers or segregate contaminated disposables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-hospital transport of contaminated linen bags. Shows autonomous mobile pickup and transport of bagged soiled material in an E2 hospital, but not the sharps/red-bag segregation and container sealing this task requires.

tasks.label: Collect specimens at specific time intervals for tests, such as those assessing therapeutic drug levels.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient bedside timed draw on a routine adult ward patient: the phlebotomist works a timed list (e.g., 0530 vancomycin trough before the dose, gentamicin peak 30 min post-infusion, 12-hour tacrolimus level), walks to the room at the ordered clock time, checks the ID band, draws into pre-labeled tubes at the bedside while the patient lies in bed (often with an IV in one arm), documents the exact collection time, and sends tubes to the lab.

Inpatient timed draw on a hard-access or complex patient: ICU, oncology, dialysis, dehydrated elderly, confused/combative or pediatric patient; superficial antecubital veins unusable, so a hand vein, ultrasound guidance, heel/finger stick, or coordination with an existing line/port is needed, still inside the ordered timing window.

Outpatient patient service center or hospital outpatient lab: glucose tolerance test series on an ambulatory adult — fasting draw, then 1-hour and 2-hour draws at exact intervals after the glucose load, patient waits on site, each draw a standard antecubital venipuncture at a fixed draw chair with pre-labeled tubes and documented times.

Outpatient lab or clinic draw station: single scheduled timed therapeutic-drug-level draw on an ambulatory adult arriving by appointment (tacrolimus/cyclosporine trough before the morning dose, 12-hour lithium level, digoxin, post-infusion vancomycin); routine antecubital venipuncture that must fall inside a specified window with the collection time recorded.

Clinical research / pharmacokinetic unit: serial sampling at many precise time points (pre-dose, 15 min, 30 min, 1, 2, 4, 8 h) on a study subject, usually through an indwelling cannula with a waste draw and saline flush, tight +/- minute windows and immediate on-site processing.

Mobile/home or long-term-care timed draw: phlebotomist travels to a private home or a nursing-facility resident's room to collect a level at the ordered hour, working in whatever chair, bed or lighting is available, then transports the specimen under a time limit.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device performed routine venipunctures on 1,633 outpatients at three Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments with a 94.5% first-stick success rate, 0.6% mild adverse events, and analytical equivalence to manual draws.
sources.transferJustification: The trial covers routine diagnostic venipuncture rather than explicitly timed collections; a timed specimen collection is the same antecubital draw into the same vacuum tubes performed at a scheduled clock time, so needle precision, tube filling/inversion and specimen quality carry over, with timing set by the order/queue system.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry) — procedure description
sources.claim: The device runs the whole venipuncture sequence itself once staff load a cartridge of pre-labeled tubes and the patient places an arm in the machine: NIR/ultrasound vein selection, alcohol prep, tourniquet, needle insertion, tube filling and inversion, needle withdrawal and bandage.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the human-machine division of labour for any draw, timed or not: staff label and load tubes and retrieve specimens, while the robot performs the puncture and tube handling with the arm presented to it in a fixture.

sources.title: Automated Phlebotomy Firm Vitestro Eyes 2027 Commercial Launch of Robotic Blood Draw Device (360Dx)
sources.claim: As of April 2026 Aletta is CE-marked with several units placed at hospitals in the Netherlands and ..., used within clinical trials; 110 of 1,743 subjects were screened out because no suitable vein was found, and the company targets outpatient phlebotomy departments rather than bedside work.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the deployment environment (fixed stations in outpatient phlebotomy departments) and the residual failure population (no suitable vein identified), which bounds which timed-draw instances the machine could take over.

sources.title: Aletta® - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro states Aletta performs the complete blood draw autonomously from tourniquet to bandage, is CE-marked and in clinical use in Europe, and that one trained supervisor can oversee up to ... devices while patients use them largely independently.
sources.transferJustification: Vendor description of the same routine-venipuncture capability plus the supervision ratio (one supervisor to three devices), which is the level of human intervention a timed draw at such a station would also involve.

sources.claim: The MagicNurse intelligent venipuncture and blood collection robot was used in a Shanghai hospital's blood collection service on 6,255 patients with a 94.3% puncture success rate, and anticoagulant specimen results were clinically comparable to manual draws.

tasks.label: Draw blood from veins by vacuum tube, syringe, or butterfly venipuncture methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine seated outpatient draw at a patient service center, physician-office lab, or hospital outpatient phlebotomy department: ambulatory adult, cooperative, palpable antecubital vein, standard multi-tube evacuated (vacuum tube) collection with labeled tubes in correct order of draw.

Seated outpatient draw on an adult with challenging but antecubital-accessible veins: obesity, frail elderly, self-reported history of difficult venous access; requires careful vein selection and sometimes a smaller-gauge/butterfly set, still at the antecubital fossa.

Hospital inpatient bedside draw during morning rounds or a timed/STAT order: patient supine or semi-recumbent in bed on a ward, ICU, or ED bay, often with IV lines on one arm, telemetry, isolation precautions, sleeping or confused patients; phlebotomist goes room to room with a cart.

Pediatric and hardest-access draws: infants and young children needing restraint/comfort holds and butterfly microtubes, and adults with no usable antecubital vein (oncology, dialysis, chemotherapy-sclerosed, severely dehydrated) requiring hand/wrist butterfly venipuncture.

Blood donation collection at a donor center or mobile blood drive: large-bore (16G) needle into a donor's antecubital vein, ~500 mL whole-blood unit with tubing/segments and sample tubes, donor monitored for vasovagal reactions throughout.

Mobile/home phlebotomy: draws at a patient's residence, assisted-living or nursing home bedside/chair, workplace health fair, or insurance paramedical exam; variable lighting, seating, and patient positioning, equipment carried in a kit.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy ... performed venipuncture autonomously in routine use in the outpatient phlebotomy departments of three Dutch hospitals; 1,633 patients in cohort 2, 94.5% first-stick success where a suitable vein was identified, 92.7% in difficult venous access, 97.4% in obesity, 93.4% in age >=65, 0.6% mild adverse events.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: The same trial reports that the device works autonomously with one supervisor per three devices, was run in hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments, enrolled patients aged 16 and older, and screened out 6% of patients for whom no suitable vein was found (referred to manual phlebotomy), giving an 88.5% overall collection success rate.

sources.claim: Aletta units have been placed in hospitals in the Netherlands and ..., so far within clinical trials rather than routine care, with broad commercial launch targeted for 2027; the system is not FDA cleared in the US.

sources.title: First-in-human evaluation of a hand-held automated venipuncture device for rapid venous blood draws | TECHNOLOGY
sources.claim: A portable/hand-held automated venipuncture robot using near-infrared and ultrasound imaging was evaluated first-in-human, drawing blood with 87% overall success and 97% in participants without difficult venous access; the device is a research prototype positioned over the arm by an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (venipuncture blood draw); cited only as context for a portable device usable away from a fixed station. Operator holds/positions it, so autonomy is unclear and it does not support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Organize or clean blood-drawing trays, ensuring that all instruments are sterile and all needles, syringes, or related items are of first-time use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient rounds: between bedside draws the phlebotomist wipes the plastic draw tray with a germicidal wipe, discards the used needle/holder into the sharps container, and replenishes the tray from the cart with unopened vacutainer tubes (multiple additive types), safety needles/butterflies, alcohol pads, gauze, tape and a clean tourniquet, working in patient rooms and corridors under time pressure.

Outpatient draw station (hospital outpatient lab, physician office, or patient service center): start- and end-of-shift setup and breakdown of the draw chair tray/drawer — sorting tubes by additive into bins, stocking needles, holders, wipes, bandages, checking lot numbers and expiration dates that all items are sealed and single-use, wiping the tray and arm-rest, swapping a full sharps container.

Restocking from the lab's central supply room: pulling cases of tubes, needles and consumables, breaking them down, checking expiry/sterile-package integrity, and loading them into the phlebotomy carts, tray bins and drawer inserts in the lab work area.

Blood donation / plasma center: preparing donor collection trays and kits before each donor (sealed single-use collection set, scale/sealer supplies, antiseptic swabsticks, gauze, bandages), then clearing the tray, discarding the used set into biohazard/sharps waste and disinfecting the tray and donor bed area between donors inside the fixed donor center.

Mobile phlebotomy (home visits, nursing homes, insurance exams): after each draw the phlebotomist cleans the portable draw kit/tray in the patient's home or in the vehicle, disposes of sharps in a portable container, and repacks and restocks the kit with fresh sterile supplies from base stock.

sources.system: Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly system (Stäubli TX2-60L + YOLO12/ResNet perception)
sources.developer: Univ. of Louisville / UMass / Saint Vincent's Hospital research group
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell (vision + 6-DOF Stäubli arm + custom gripper) sorts surgical instruments and packs them into compartmented sterile trays, verifying identity and correct placement, in a purpose-built laboratory workcell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a sterile instrument tray. It transfers to organizing a blood-drawing tray because both require vision-based identification of small medical items, verification that the correct complete set is present, and placement into designated tray compartments at comparable (millimetre-level) precision.

sources.system: RIF Robotics robotic tray assembly system
sources.developer: RIF Robotics (pilot with Wellstar Health System)
sources.title: RIF Robotics pioneers autonomous surgical tray assembly — Catalyst by Wellstar

sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital instrument tray assembly with completeness checking; the robot works at a purpose-built loading station inside the SPD, showing that tray stocking/verification of medical items is done by machine in a fixtured cell rather than in the room as found.

sources.system: Getinge Automation System (AGS) / Automatiq loaders and Envoy
