sources.claim: Automated conveyor-and-shuttle systems load wash carts of trays and instruments into washer-disinfectors and move them through cleaning, disinfection and packing in hospital central sterile departments; the newer Automatiq line adds robotic loaders and a self-navigating transport robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cleaning and disinfection of soiled medical trays and carts. A plastic phlebotomy tray is a simpler, non-lumened item than surgical instrument sets, so machine washing/disinfection to a validated standard carries over directly.

sources.system: Inpeco ProTube and Techno Medica BC ROBO automated tube selecting/labeling systems
sources.title: Pre-analytical phase: The automated ProTube device supports quality assurance in the phlebotomy process — PubMed
sources.claim: Automated tube-preparation machines select and label the correct unused blood-collection tubes for each patient at phlebotomy points, producing an all-in-one patient kit; a six-month hospital study covered 15,010 patients and 48,776 tubes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing the correct, unused collection tubes for each draw. This is the highest-volume element of stocking a blood-drawing tray, and the machines are enclosed cartridge-fed units serving real phlebotomy stations at worker-acceptable error rates.

sources.system: KNAPP Pick-it-Easy Robot powered by Covariant
sources.title: McKesson delivers for customers with the KNAPP Pick-it-Easy Robot, powered by Covariant
sources.claim: AI-driven piece-picking robots pick individually packaged pharmaceutical and medical items from totes into order containers in distribution centres, handling a wide, changing item range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: goods-to-robot piece picking of packaged medical consumables. Restocking a tray or supply bin with sealed needles, wipes, gauze and bandages involves the same object class, similar grasping difficulty, and placement into a container, when the stock is presented as a fixtured cell would present it.

sources.title: AMP Robotics — MCJ Collective portfolio
sources.claim: Vision-guided sorting robots autonomously pick used, mixed items off fast-moving conveyors and separate them into correct streams at high rates in more than a hundred processing facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sorting of used items into waste streams on a conveyor. Clearing spent disposables from a returned draw tray into sharps/biohazard streams is the same perception-and-pick problem with a smaller, more constrained item set, when items are presented on a purpose-built line.

sources.system: ORB (Operating Room Bot), built on a Fetch mobile manipulator

sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator built to fetch and restock item-level operating-room supplies achieved 80% success in supply retrieval and 96% in restocking in laboratory experiments — short of the reliability required for unattended clinical stocking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level retrieval and restocking of sterile clinical supplies inside a hospital room. It is the closest attempt at doing this work in the facility as found, and its laboratory-only, 80%-success status is why no E2 judgment is supported.

sources.title: Moxi — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Hospital service robots deployed in US hospitals autonomously fetch and deliver supplies, lab samples and medications between rooms, but their manipulation is limited to transporting items rather than stocking or cleaning trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply logistics. It shows what mobile robots reliably do in an E2 hospital today — transport of bulk items — and not item-level tray stocking, cleaning or sharps handling.

tasks.label: Conduct standards tests, such as blood alcohol, blood culture, oral glucose tolerance, glucose screening, blood smears, or peak and trough drug levels tests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient/ED bedside blood culture collection: reach an acutely ill, often febrile patient in the room, perform stringent skin and bottle-septum antisepsis, draw two sets from two separate venipuncture sites, inoculate aerobic and anaerobic bottles to exact fill volumes in the correct order, label and route to microbiology within contamination-rate limits.

Outpatient patient service center or prenatal clinic oral glucose tolerance / gestational glucose challenge test: verify fasting status, draw the baseline specimen, hand the patient the 50/75/100 g glucose beverage and time its consumption, keep the patient seated 1-3 hours, monitor for nausea, vomiting or syncope, and draw timed serial specimens labeled with exact collection times.

Timed peak and trough therapeutic drug level draws (vancomycin, gentamicin, digoxin, anticonvulsants) on a hospital ward or in an infusion clinic: coordinate with nursing on dose timing, go to the bedside, draw from the arm opposite the infusion line into the specified tubes, and document the exact draw time.

Walk-in outpatient draw station: standard-protocol venous specimen collection for glucose screening / fasting or random plasma glucose and similar standardized chemistry tests on a seated cooperative ambulatory adult - identify the patient, tourniquet, disinfect, multi-tube antecubital venipuncture in correct order of draw, mix, label, bandage.

Blood alcohol determination for a clinical ethanol order in the ED or a legal chain-of-custody request (jail, occupational or law-enforcement collection): non-alcohol antiseptic prep, gray-top sodium fluoride tubes filled to volume, tamper-evident seals, custody forms and witness signatures, sometimes with an agitated or restrained subject.

Peripheral blood smear preparation at the collection site or bench: obtain the specimen (fingerstick or EDTA tube), place a drop on a glass slide, spread a wedge film of proper length with a feathered edge, air-dry, label, and in some settings stain the film for morphology or malaria review.

tasks.label: Process blood or other fluid samples for further analysis by other medical professionals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital inpatient/ED floor phlebotomist post-collection handling: at the bedside and on the cart, apply/verify patient barcode labels on filled tubes, invert-mix additive tubes, sort tubes by destination test, bag with requisitions, and batch them into the pneumatic tube or carry to the core lab.

Outpatient patient service center bench processing: after the draws, spin tubes in a benchtop centrifuge per test requirements, aliquot serum/plasma into labeled transfer tubes, refrigerate or freeze aliquots, and pack specimens with ice packs and manifests into courier boxes for pickup.

Hospital or reference-lab specimen processing/accessioning area: receive bagged and boxed specimens from couriers and tube stations, unbag, verify labels against orders/accession, centrifuge, decap, aliquot, sort by department, load analyzer racks, and store/retrieve retained tubes for add-ons.

Blood or plasma donation center unit processing: after collection, seal and strip tubing segments, label the unit and pilot/sample tubes, centrifuge and separate the whole-blood unit into components, and stage units and test tubes into transport coolers for the testing lab.

Mobile phlebotomy / home draws / nursing-home and insurance-exam visits: process specimens in the field — label at the point of care, spin in a portable centrifuge in the vehicle or a spare room, aliquot, and pack a transport kit for courier or lab drop-off.

sources.title: Carter BloodCare First to Complete the Transition to Automated Whole Blood Processing With Terumo Blood and Cell Technologies
sources.claim: Terumo BCT's Reveos, FDA-cleared in 2023 and in routine use at US blood centers (Carter BloodCare completed its transition in January 2025), automatically centrifuges loaded whole-blood units, separates them, and expresses and seals the component bags.

tasks.label: Monitor blood or plasma donors during and after procedures to ensure health, safety, and comfort.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Source-plasma donation center (e.g., a 40-bed CSL/Grifols/BioLife floor): phlebotomist watches a bank of donors on apheresis machines for 45-90 minutes each — checking venipuncture sites for infiltration/hematoma, responding to machine alarms and flow problems, spotting citrate reactions (tingling, chills, nausea), asking donors how they feel, adjusting arm position/blanket, taking vitals as required, and clearing the donor at the end.

Fixed whole-blood donor center: during a 6-10 minute draw the phlebotomist watches the donor's color, sweating and speech, keeps the donor talking, checks the cuff/flow and mixer, then removes the needle, applies pressure and bandage, sits the donor up slowly, walks them to the canteen and observes them 10-15 minutes with snacks/fluids before release.

Mobile blood drive in a school gym, church hall, office conference room or bloodmobile: layout improvised for the day, cots and chairs crowded together, ambient noise and bystanders; the phlebotomist scans several donors at once during and after donation, escorts donors to the refreshment table, and watches for wobbly donors near hard floors and doorways.

Adverse-reaction episode at a donor center or drive (roughly 1 in 100 donations): donor becomes pale/clammy, faints, vomits, has a hematoma or, rarely, a convulsive syncope. Worker must immediately stop the draw or withdraw the needle, recline the chair and elevate legs, apply cold compress and pressure, protect the airway/head, give fluids, take vitals, summon the medical supervisor and document the reaction.

Platelet/double-red apheresis or hospital-based donor room: 90-120 minute procedure with periodic vital-sign checks, calcium supplementation for citrate toxicity, monitoring return-line pressures and donor comfort (warmth, bathroom, position), plus 15-minute post-procedure observation before release.

sources.title: Robotic Phlebotomy Study Signals Automation Shift for Clinical Labs - Dark Daily
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is an autonomous robotic ... evaluated in a multicenter trial in hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments; it performs the venipuncture (arm positioning, vein location, draw, bandage) but is a supervised device intended for routine diagnostic draws, not for monitoring donors or managing donor reactions.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: the robot works on the same body part, in the same donor/patient chair, with the same needle and cannula. It substantiates autonomous needle work but not the monitoring task, since the device performs a draw and does not observe donor wellbeing or intervene in reactions.

sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device (Center for Phlebotomy Education)
sources.claim: Aletta operates under trained-personnel supervision and public materials do not describe any capability for managing syncope, severe pain, ... — i.e., the human staff, not the robot, handle donor/patient adverse events.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (robotic venipuncture) as above; cited to show the boundary of the demonstrated capability — reaction monitoring and response remain with human staff.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: contactless patient vital-sign measurement in a clinical setting, the sensing half of donor monitoring. It does not transfer to the whole task because it was remote controlled and performs no assessment-driven physical intervention.

sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed in more than 25 ..., but its demonstrated work is materials logistics (supply, lab-specimen and pharmacy deliveries), not patient observation or patient-contact care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation among patients and staff in a controlled healthcare facility. Shows navigation/fetching is solved, but it involves no human physiological monitoring or physical assistance, so it does not carry over to donor monitoring.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: catching/supporting a collapsing human, the physical core of responding to a fainting donor. It cannot support a positive judgment because it is teleoperated and unproven outside the lab.

instances.label: Hospital inpatient/ED rounds: phlebotomist finishes draws on nursing units, then carries a labeled rack/tote of tubes (some on ice, some stat, chain-of-custody logged) through patient corridors and elevators to the on-site clinical lab, or loads a pneumatic tube carrier at the unit station.

Outpatient patient service center or hospital outpatient draw station: specimens batched, bagged with requisitions, and walked or wheeled to the lab receiving window in the same building or another building on the same controlled campus.

Off-site collection site (physician office, standalone patient service center, urgent care): specimens packed in a validated cooler/biohazard transport box and driven by the phlebotomist on public roads, sometimes with several stops, to a regional or central laboratory's receiving dock.

Mobile/home phlebotomy and nursing-home or assisted-living visits: after drawing at a private residence or resident's room, the phlebotomist packs specimens into a carry bag, walks them to a personal vehicle parked on the street, and drives to a lab or an after-hours drop box.

Mobile blood or plasma drive at a community venue (church hall, school gym, bloodmobile): collected units plus pilot/serology tubes are packed into temperature-validated coolers, loaded into a van, and transported to the blood center's processing laboratory.

tasks.label: Draw blood from capillaries by dermal puncture, such as heel or finger stick methods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Donor screening finger stick at a blood or plasma donation center (or fixed donor room): healthy, cooperative seated adult; lance a fingertip, wipe first drop, collect a drop/microcuvette or capillary tube for hemoglobin/hematocrit/total protein, apply pressure and bandage, log result before donation proceeds.

Outpatient patient service center, physician office or POC clinic: cooperative adult, capillary draw because veins are poor or only a small specimen is needed (glucose, HbA1c, hemoglobin, lead, small microtainer chemistry/CBC); warm/clean finger, puncture, express and collect 100-500 uL without hemolysis or clotting, bandage and label.

Hospital newborn nursery/NICU heel stick: swaddled or incubator-bound infant, warm the heel, puncture the lateral plantar surface to controlled depth, massage and collect bilirubin/glucose microtainers or fill circles on a newborn-screening filter card, hold pressure, soothe the crying baby.

Infant, toddler or young child in a pediatric clinic or hospital: finger or heel stick on a frightened, squirming patient who must be held or distracted by a parent/aide; site selection on small digits, repeated milking to fill the tube, comforting and bandaging.

Adult inpatient bedside on a ward/ICU/isolation room: patient in bed, often edematous, cold, poorly perfused, on IVs or contact precautions; phlebotomist brings a tray to the bedside, positions the hand, punctures and collects a capillary specimen, holds pressure.

Off-site draws: nursing home rooms, home visits, and community health-fair/mobile screening tables; variable furniture and lighting, frail or unpredictable patients, phlebotomist positions the patient's hand and performs the finger stick with a portable kit.

sources.system: Automatic fingertip blood-sampling device (Hitachi High-Tech / Fujita Health University)
sources.developer: Hitachi High-Tech Corporation with Fujita Health University Hospital
sources.title: Hospital robots collect and deliver blood samples (Nature Portfolio partner content)
sources.claim: An automated fingertip blood-collection device co-developed by Hitachi High-Tech and Fujita Health University autonomously punctures a patient's fingertip and collects up to ~400 uL of capillary blood; the patient rests a palm on the device, which grips a finger, images capillaries with near-infrared cameras, punctures, and uses an automated finger tourniquet to express and then staunch blood. Trialled at Fujita Health University Hospital.

sources.system: FBS-FV automatic fingertip blood-sampling system with fingertip vessel-puncture function
sources.developer: Hitachi High-Tech / Fujita Health University (Irie et al.)
sources.title: Evaluation of Blood-Sampling Performance of Automatic Fingertip-Blood-Sampling System and Correlation Between Fingertip-Blood-Vessel Image and Blood-Sampling Volume
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed evaluation of the same system (FBS-FV) with 18 adult volunteers: it autonomously selects a puncture point from fingertip blood-vessel images, punctures within <1 mm of the ..., and alternately compresses/releases the fingertip to express blood; however only 42% of samples exceeded the 650 uL target volume, showing volume consistency is still prototype-level.

sources.system: Fingertip blood collection robot (Li et al., binocular vision + NIR)
sources.developer: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications et al. (surveyed in Frontiers review)
sources.title: Intelligent blood collection robot: key technologies, clinical applications, and future challenges
sources.claim: Review of intelligent blood-collection robots reports laboratory fingertip blood-collection robots (Li et al.) that use binocular vision plus near-infrared imaging and laser guidance to locate a fingertip puncture point and drive a lancet/needle there with sub-0.2 mm deviation in under 10 seconds; these are bench prototypes on adult volunteers, not clinical products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fingertip puncture-point location and needle placement. It shows the perception/positioning half of dermal puncture is solved on adult fingertips in a fixtured tabletop setting, supporting the capillary-collection judgments for cooperative adults.

sources.title: Vitestro gains CE mark for autonomous blood drawing robot
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device received an EU CE mark in August 2024 and has been used for routine venous blood collection in Dutch hospital outpatient labs; it autonomously images veins, positions the arm, inserts the needle, fills tubes and bandages the arm under staff supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venous blood draw on seated outpatients in hospital labs. It shows an autonomous blood-collection machine can meet clinical standards in an institution-controlled facility, but its scope (adults, both arms available, station-based) bounds what transfers to dermal puncture.

sources.developer: Vitestro (analysis by Center for Phlebotomy Education)
sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device
sources.claim: Independent phlebotomy trade commentary on Aletta's published trial data and scope: the device is aimed at routine outpatient venipuncture on adults, requires supervision, and explicitly excludes pediatric patients; no autonomous system is offered for infant heel sticks or difficult bedside patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venipuncture. Cited to bound transfer - the only clinically deployed autonomous blood-collection robots are adult, station-based and supervised, so they do not substantiate neonatal, pediatric or bedside dermal puncture.

sources.system: Fully automatic blood collection robot (self-service draw station)
sources.developer: Chinese medical-robotics vendor deployed at Jiaxing Second Hospital
sources.title: 效率高还“不疼”的采血机器人上岗！更多新产品新场景正在解锁 (China Daily)
sources.claim: A fully automatic blood-collection robot installed at Jiaxing Second Hospital (Zhejiang) performed nearly 16,000 unattended draws in eight months: the patient sits at the self-service station, extends an arm, and the robot performs infrared vein location, needle insertion and collection with voice guidance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous venous draw at a self-service station inside a hospital. It establishes that autonomous blood-collection machines operate unattended at clinical volume inside institution-controlled human facilities, the environment claimed for the cooperative-adult capillary instances.

tasks.label: Conduct hemoglobin tests to ensure donor iron levels are normal.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed community blood donation center or hospital donor room: routine adult repeat whole-blood donor at the screening station; worker cleans a fingertip, lances it, wipes the first drop, draws capillary blood into a HemoCue microcuvette, reads the hemoglobin value in ~1 minute, applies gauze, records the result and the pass/defer decision in the donor record.

Mobile blood drive at a community venue taken as found (high school gym, church hall, corporate conference room, bloodmobile): the same fingerstick-plus-photometer hemoglobin screen performed at a folding-table screening station within a temporary privacy-screened setup, under variable lighting, seating and traffic, with high donor throughput during a 4-6 hour drive.

Source plasma donation center, high-throughput screening line: routine repeat donor screened for hematocrit/hemoglobin (and total protein) by fingerstick before apheresis, with results entered into the donor management system and eligibility determined against center cutoffs.

Difficult screening encounter at either a center or a drive: cold hands or poor peripheral perfusion, callused/small fingers, insufficient drop requiring a second stick on the other hand, a borderline or below-cutoff first reading requiring a recheck or venous confirmation, and an anxious, first-time or teenage donor needing coaching, reassurance and low-hemoglobin deferral counseling.

sources.title: Prepare for Your Donation — Gulf Coast Blood (OrSense FAQ)
sources.claim: The OrSense NBM-200 is used in routine service at a large US blood center (Gulf Coast Blood, Houston) to perform the pre-donation hemoglobin screen: the donor places a finger in a machine-controlled pneumatic ring cuff, the device occludes the finger, measures hemoglobin optically and displays the value used for eligibility, with no fingerstick or blood sample.

sources.title: OrSense NBM-200 Non-Invasive Hemoglobin Device Implemented by Children's Hospital Los Angeles
sources.claim: The NBM-200 was cleared by FDA's CBER division specifically for use in US blood donation centers and is installed in blood donation and plasma collection ..., i.e. it performs the donor hemoglobin eligibility test itself in both whole-blood and plasma collection settings.

sources.system: Automatic finger blood sample collection device (FBS-FV)
sources.developer: Hitachi / Hitachi High-Tech with Fujita Health University
sources.title: Value-based Innovation: Safety and Security — Research & Development, Hitachi Review
sources.claim: Hitachi's automatic finger blood sample collection device is a robotic unit into which a person inserts a finger; it controls a cassette and finger tourniquet, punctures the fingertip, promotes and collects the blood (250 µL for a blood count, which includes hemoglobin) and stops the bleeding. Evaluated with Fujita Health University, blood-count results correlated well with venous samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated capillary fingerstick sampling for a complete blood count. Hemoglobin is one of the blood-count parameters validated against venous samples, and the objects (fingertip, lancet, microtainer) and precision are those of donor hemoglobin screening.

sources.system: Fujita/Hitachi High-Tech automated fingertip blood collection device
sources.developer: Fujita Health University with Hitachi High-Tech
sources.title: Hospital robots collect and deliver blood samples (Nature Portfolio)
sources.claim: Autonomous fingertip and venous blood-collection robots have been trialled on patients at Fujita Health University Hospital in Japan; the fingertip device uses near-infrared imaging of finger capillaries, an automated tourniquet and collects up to 400 µL.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated capillary blood sampling from a seated person in a healthcare facility; the puncture, bleed-promotion and sample-capture steps are the same physical acts as the fingerstick in donor hemoglobin screening.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial — Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed multicenter trial of the Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy ... in 1,633 patients across three outpatient ... reported a 94.5% first-stick success rate, low hemolysis and analytical equivalence of the resulting laboratory test results to manual draws.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining a diagnostic blood sample from a seated person without human hands on the needle, at first-attempt success comparable to phlebotomists; the sample-acquisition step of hemoglobin screening transfers, and hemoglobin is measured from such tubes by standard automated hematology analyzers.

sources.title: Vitestro raises $70 million to advance robotic blood collection
sources.claim: The Aletta autonomous phlebotomy robot is CE-marked and approved for commercial use in ..., and is being deployed in clinical and ..., i.e. it operates in ordinary outpatient blood-collection facilities rather than only in laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the Clinical Chemistry item: autonomous acquisition of a blood sample from a person inside a structured healthcare facility.

sources.system: MagicNurse intelligent puncture blood collection robot
sources.title: Intelligent blood collection robot: key technologies, clinical applications, and future challenges (Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology)
sources.claim: Autonomous venous blood-collection robots are in routine hospital service in China: a hospital established a blood-collection area with three MagicNurse puncture robots that completed collections for more than 5,100 patients between late 2023 and May 2024, with reported puncture success around 94%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended blood sampling from walk-in patients in a hospital collection area; it substantiates that machine-controlled sampling from a cooperative seated person meets service quality in a structured human work facility.

tasks.label: Train other medical personnel in phlebotomy or laboratory techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lead/senior phlebotomist precepts a newly hired phlebotomist during hospital rounds: demonstrates venipuncture on real inpatients (patient ID, tourniquet, vein selection, order of draw, labeling at bedside), then watches the trainee's sticks, physically corrects needle angle/anchoring, coaches on difficult veins and patient reactions, and documents competency over several shifts.

Bench-side training of medical assistants, nurses or new lab aides in a clinic/outpatient lab: hands-on instruction with real tubes, butterfly sets, centrifuge and specimen-handling equipment (order of draw, mixing, labeling, spin/aliquot, POCT), demonstrating each step and watching each trainee repeat it until correct.

Structured classroom/skills-lab session at a hospital education center or phlebotomy program: short didactic segment, instructor demonstration on a training arm, supervising students practicing on manikin arms and on each other, correcting hand position and technique, scoring skill checklists and remediating failures.

Blood donor-center staff training: teaching collection staff donor screening, 16G needle insertion, unit/tubing handling and donor-reaction response, both at a fixed donor center and at mobile drives set up in school gyms, church halls and workplace conference rooms whose layout changes with every site.

Ride-along / ad hoc in-service training of a mobile or nursing-home draw phlebotomist: instructor accompanies the trainee into patients' homes and long-term-care rooms, demonstrates draws in cramped, variable spaces on frail or difficult-access patients, coaches on kit setup and specimen transport, and signs off competency.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomously performs diagnostic venipunctures on outpatients in the phlebotomy departments of three Netherlands hospitals, with one human professional supervising up to three devices; it draws blood but does not instruct, observe or credential human trainees.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing venipuncture. It substantiates that a robot can execute the blood-draw motion itself in a hospital (E2) setting, but the training task requires teaching, demonstrating to, observing, correcting and signing off human trainees, none of which this device does; it cannot therefore complete any training instance.

sources.developer: Penn State University / Penn State Hershey Medical Center
sources.title: Investigating the Effect of Simulator Functional Fidelity and Personalized Feedback on Central Venous Catheterization Training
sources.claim: The Dynamic Haptic Robotic Trainer is a haptic robot-arm simulator that lets surgical residents practice ultrasound-guided needle insertion in a university simulation lab and delivers automated personalized performance feedback, reducing but not eliminating preceptor involvement, and covering only the needle-insertion sub-skill of one procedure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: training clinicians in a needle-insertion psychomotor skill with automated feedback. It is the closest robotic analogue to phlebotomy instruction, but it teaches one sub-skill on its own simulated tissue and is described as reducing preceptor time rather than replacing the instructor; it does not deliver curriculum, live-patient supervision, hands-on correction or competency sign-off, so it cannot complete a whole training instance.

sources.developer: university research group (Frontiers in Robotics and AI publication)
sources.title: Humanoid patient robot for diagnostic training in medical and psychiatric education
sources.claim: Humanoid robots are used in medical and psychiatric education as simulated patients that reproduce disease-specific behaviour for students to practise on; the robot is the object of the training exercise, and human educators still design, run and assess the session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot use in clinical skills education. It shows robots serving as training aids/simulated patients, not as the trainer; behaviour is pre-programmed and autonomy is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment that a robot conducts the instruction instance.

tasks.label: Serve refreshments to donors to ensure absorption of sugar into their systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mobile whole-blood drive at a host site (high-school gym, church hall, workplace conference room, community center). After donation the collections staffer walks the donor to a folding-table canteen, hands out juice/water and cookies, encourages the donor to eat and drink, and keeps an eye on them for 10-15 minutes. The venue, floor surface, aisle widths and clutter (cables, cases of supplies, folding chairs, cots) differ every drive day.

Fixed community blood donor center canteen. Donors walk from the draw chairs to a dedicated refreshment area with tables and a stocked counter; the phlebotomist offers and hands over juice boxes, water, cookies or crackers, refills drinks, and clears cups before releasing the donor. Fixed layout, standard furniture, staff-controlled premises.

Plasma or apheresis donation center. Ambulatory donors are given fluids before donating and a snack/juice at a standardized refreshment counter afterward; staff hand out cups and packaged snacks and prompt donors to hydrate. Consistent purpose-built center layout across the chain.

Donor with an adverse reaction (lightheaded, pale, sweating, or fainted) in the donation chair or canteen. The staffer brings juice or sugared drink to the reclined donor, hands or holds it while they sip, may add a cold compress and elevate the legs, and stays with the donor until color and blood pressure recover.

Preparing and replenishing the refreshment station in either a fixed center or at a drive: pouring juice into cups, opening boxes of cookies/crackers, restocking coolers and ice, checking expiration dates, and wiping the canteen table between donors.

sources.system: Bear Robotics Servi / Servi Plus / Servi Q
sources.title: Bear Robotics Introduces Servi Q, The Compact Service Robot
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi line of autonomous service robots carries food and drinks from the ... and busses dishes in restaurants, hotels, cafés and other venues, navigating existing floor plans without redesign; latest model markets stable liquid delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running drinks and food to seated guests in a dining room. Same objects (cups/juice, packaged snacks on a tray), same act of bringing refreshment to a seated person in an institutionally controlled room; the donor canteen is a dining-room-like space.

sources.title: Juniper Communities Pilots the Use of Robots to Enhance Dining Services
sources.claim: Self-driving Servi robots were deployed in senior living communities to expedite food delivery to residents' dining tables and to bus tables, in a rollout across multiple communities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: serving meals and drinks to seated older residents in an institutional dining room. Comparable clientele (seated people who may be unsteady), comparable objects and precision, and an institution-controlled facility like a donor canteen.

sources.title: Pudu Robotics Releases Catering and Retail Service Robot, BellaBot Pro
sources.claim: Pudu's BellaBot delivery robot, using lidar and visual SLAM navigation, has been deployed in high-traffic food-service and retail settings by major brands, with the company shipping tens of thousands of service robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tray delivery of food and drinks to seated customers in restaurants; establishes that multiple vendors' serving robots work at scale in structured human food-service facilities, the same class of setting as a donor canteen.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves drinks at Kennedy Space Center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM, a stationary dual-arm robot with closed-loop AI vision control of pouring, has served more than 16,000 drinks ... a commercial Las Vegas beverage location and serves drinks at arena bars and one-off events such as the MLB All-Star Game and a Kennedy Space Center event.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing and serving beverages from a fixed counter station to people who walk up. Same objects (cups of juice/soft drinks), same purpose (getting sugar/fluid into a person), with supplies fixtured in known positions — the E1 form of the refreshment station.

sources.title: Humanoid bartender robot ADAM debuts at Texas Rangers stadium - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM robot bartender was deployed at a Major League Baseball stadium bar, serving cocktails and ... to fans alongside human bartenders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: counter beverage service to a stream of walk-up members of the public; equivalent to a canteen counter where donors collect a juice, with the machine's supplies in a purpose-built station.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator has completed over 1.25 million autonomous ... with nearly 100 robots in more than 25 US ..., navigating clinical corridors alongside staff and patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous item transport inside a healthcare facility among patients and staff. Supports that mobile robots reliably move small items through mapped clinical premises; it does not demonstrate hand-to-person refreshment service or care of a reacting donor.

sources.title: Which service restaurant automation solutions include the implementation of robot waiters for food delivery?
sources.claim: Commercial serving-robot deployments require a vendor mapping and route-programming step at each fixed venue (typically hours to a couple of days per site), i.e. they are installed in permanently mapped premises rather than one-day pop-up spaces.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class (robot food/drink running); cited to characterize the environment these systems need — a mapped, fixed venue — which bears on whether they could serve a canteen at a different mobile-drive site each day.

tasks.label: Draw blood from arteries, using arterial collection techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Adult inpatient on a general medical/pulmonary ward: phlebotomist verifies order and ID, performs modified Allen test, palpates the radial pulse, punctures at ~45° with a pre-heparinized ABG syringe, lets the pulsatile flow self-fill, holds firm compression ~5 minutes, expels air bubbles, caps, mixes, labels and transports the sample STAT with FiO2 documented.

ICU or emergency department critically ill adult: STAT ABG on a hypotensive, edematous, vasopressor-dependent or agitated patient surrounded by lines, monitors and staff; weak or absent radial pulse may force ultrasound guidance, an alternate wrist, or brachial site; extended compression needed if anticoagulated.

Ambulatory outpatient in a pulmonary function lab / clinic draw station: cooperative seated patient, wrist hyperextended over a rolled towel on an armboard, resting room-air ABG or oxygen-qualification draw under calm, controlled, scheduled conditions.

Difficult-access adult: obese, elderly, hypothermic, or with scarred/thrombosed radial arteries from repeated punctures; requires site hunting, repeat attempts, switch to the contralateral wrist or brachial artery, and careful hematoma prevention, sometimes escalated to a second operator.

Neonatal/pediatric arterial sampling: tiny superficial vessels, immobilization and comfort measures with a second person holding the child, minimal blood volume, or drawing an ABG from an existing indwelling arterial line with waste/flush protocol.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial | Clinical Chemistry
sources.claim: The most advanced clinically deployed blood-collection robot, Vitestro's CE-marked Aletta, autonomously performs venipunctures (venous draws) in outpatient phlebotomy departments; its indication and validated scope are venous, not arterial.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is venipuncture. Capability does NOT transfer to arterial collection: the device images and targets superficial veins with a tourniquet and vacuum tubes, whereas arterial draws require pulse palpation/Allen testing, a deeper pulsatile vessel entered at a steep angle, a self-filling heparinized syringe, air-bubble expulsion, and several minutes of held compression. No arterial indication or arterial data are reported.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Shows High Success Rates in Multicenter Trial | Clinical Lab Products
sources.claim: Detailed multicenter clinical results for the autonomous venipuncture robot confirm it was evaluated only for diagnostic venous blood draws, in outpatient phlebotomy departments, with 94.5% first-stick success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is venous phlebotomy in a structured clinical facility (E2). It bounds the frontier: the only clinically validated autonomous needle-insertion robot is restricted to veins, so it cannot substantiate completion of arterial puncture.

sources.system: Robotic ultrasound-guided automatic femoral vessel cannulation system (Carnegie Mellon / Choset lab)
sources.title: Automatic Cannulation of Femoral Vessels in a Porcine Shock Model (arXiv:2506.14467)
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic arterial access remains at the animal-experiment stage: a 2025 robotic ultrasound system achieved femoral vein and artery cannulation only in a porcine hemorrhagic shock ..., and the authors note that for femoral access only semi-autonomous methods previously existed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is arterial cannulation. It is the closest robotic arterial work found, but it is a laboratory animal demonstration of catheter placement, not a human diagnostic arterial blood sample collected, handled and delivered at clinical quality, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.system: MagicNurse, Aixam, Hagong intelligent blood collection robots
sources.developer: Various (Chinese manufacturers), reviewed in Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
sources.title: Intelligent blood collection robot: key technologies, clinical applications, and future challenges | Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
sources.claim: A 2025 review of intelligent blood collection robots finds that commercially deployed systems in leading hospitals (MagicNurse, Aixam, Hagong) automate venous blood collection; no commercial robot for arterial blood collection is identified.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is venous blood collection by robot. Reviewed state of the art shows deployed systems target veins only; arteries are mentioned only as anatomy, with no clinical arterial-puncture robot reported, so no transfer to arterial collection is substantiated.

sources.system: AUSmart-Astrup automatic arterial puncture sensorial device (concept)
sources.developer: Academic authors (Joint International Conference on Mechanisms, Mechanical Transmissions and Robotics)
sources.title: Automatic Arterial Puncture Sensorial Device for Fast Arterial Blood Gas Sampling from Radial Artery During Covid-19 Pandemic | SpringerLink
sources.claim: Work specifically aimed at automating radial-artery blood gas sampling exists only as a device concept/prototype description (limb immobilization plus artery localization and needle-angle maintenance), with no reported autonomous clinical sampling in patients.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (radial arterial sampling), but it is a design concept with no demonstrated autonomous puncture or accepted clinical specimens; autonomy is unclear, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Collect fluid or tissue samples, using appropriate collection procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine venipuncture on a cooperative adult at a fixed draw station (hospital outpatient lab, patient service center, clinic draw chair): verify ID and order, seat patient, tourniquet, palpate/select antecubital vein, disinfect, draw 1-4 evacuated tubes in order, withdraw needle, apply gauze/bandage, mix and label tubes, watch for syncope.

Bedside venipuncture on hospitalized patients during ward rounds, ED, or ICU: phlebotomist wheels a cart to the bed, works around IV lines, telemetry, gowns, side rails, isolation precautions and sleeping or uncooperative patients; includes stat and timed draws and blood culture sets.
Capillary fingerstick on a cooperative adult (small-volume chemistry, hemoglobin, point-of-care) or a throat/nasopharyngeal swab collected at a lab or clinic collection station.

Pediatric and neonatal collection (newborn heelstick screening cards, infant/toddler capillary and small-vein venipuncture requiring holding and comforting) plus patient-provided fluid specimens (clean-catch urine, 24-hour urine, stool, saliva/sputum) where the phlebotomist instructs the patient, receives, verifies, labels and processes the specimen.

Whole-blood or apheresis donation collection at a donor center or mobile blood drive: donor screening hemoglobin check, large-bore needle into a collection set, monitoring donor for 8-10 minutes and for adverse reactions, mixing/sealing the unit and attached segment tubes.

Off-site draws taken as found: homebound patient's living room or bedroom, assisted-living resident's room, workplace wellness event or insurance paramedical exam, with the phlebotomist carrying supplies, improvising positioning and lighting, and transporting specimens.

sources.system: Vitestro Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ARPD)
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performed venipuncture in routine use in outpatient phlebotomy departments of three Dutch hospitals, achieving 94.5% first-stick success in 1,633 patients with a 0.6% mild adverse-event rate.

sources.title: Vitestro unveils Aletta robotic phlebotomy device – CAP TODAY
sources.claim: The CE-marked Aletta device carries out the complete blood-draw sequence itself — tourniquet, skin prep, ultrasound vein identification, needle insertion, tube handling and ... — not just the needle stick.

sources.title: Automated Phlebotomy Firm Vitestro Eyes 2027 Commercial Launch of Robotic Blood Draw Device | 360Dx
sources.claim: In the ADOPT cohort the device screened 1,743 outpatients and could not find a suitable vein in 110 (6%), who were handed back to staff; devices are placed in Dutch and Danish hospital outpatient phlebotomy departments, with European commercial launch planned for 2027.

sources.claim: A fully automated intelligent puncture blood collection robot installed at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University drew blood from 6,255 consenting outpatients with a 94.3% puncture success rate and specimen quality that did not affect diagnosis.

sources.system: MagicNurse blood collection robots (digital intelligent blood collection area)
sources.developer: Beijing Magicnurse / First Hospital of Anhui Medical University
sources.title: Intelligent blood collection robot: key technologies, clinical applications, and future challenges (Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed review documents routine hospital deployments of blood collection robots, including a three-robot digital blood collection area at the First Hospital of Anhui ... that collected from more than 5,100 patients.

sources.developer: Hitachi High-Tech Corporation with Fujita Health University Hospital
sources.title: Hospital robots collect and deliver blood samples (Nature partner content, Fujita Health University)
sources.claim: An automated fingertip blood collection device developed by Hitachi High-Tech and trialled at Fujita Health University Hospital maps finger capillaries with near-infrared cameras, punctures, and collects up to 400 microlitres, showing good correlation with venous results.
sources.transferJustification: Capillary fingerstick collection is the capillary variant of this task; the device performs site selection, puncture, blood-flow encouragement and sample capture on a patient's finger.

sources.title: Value-based Innovation: Safety and Security – Hitachi Review
sources.claim: Hitachi's technical review describes the same device as automatically puncturing the fingertip, encouraging and then stopping blood flow, and collecting a sample sufficient for biochemical analysis, using a cassette of disposable puncture instruments and sample bottles.
sources.transferJustification: Same fingerstick capillary collection task; the quote establishes end-to-end autonomous execution including hemostasis and sample handling.

sources.developer: Chinese research group (IEEE Transactions on Medical Robotics and Bionics)
sources.title: The LINGCAI-II System: A Sampling Robotic System for Autonomous Oropharyngeal Swab Sampling
sources.claim: The LINGCAI-II robot performs autonomous oropharyngeal swab sampling end-to-end at a sampling workstation and was used clinically on 116 COVID-19 patients, with 96 diagnoses obtained from robot-collected samples.
sources.transferJustification: Throat/nasal swab collection is one of the non-blood 'fluid or tissue sample' collections phlebotomists perform; the robot handles swab, patient contact and specimen containment autonomously.

sources.developer: Vitestro (reviewed by Center for Phlebotomy Education)
sources.title: Aletta: An Update About Vitestro's Robotic Blood Draw Device (Center for Phlebotomy Education)
sources.claim: Aletta runs with one phlebotomist or nurse overseeing several devices rather than step-by-step control, but is limited to routine adult outpatient venipuncture and cannot handle pediatric draws, alternative sites, special positioning or mid-procedure complications.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Calibrate or maintain machines, such as those used for plasma collection.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital/outpatient draw station or clinic lab: routine upkeep of the specimen centrifuge and small bench equipment — wipe the exterior, open and clean the chamber/rotor of blood spills and broken-tube debris, check gaskets and lid latch, verify speed/timer, balance loads, and record the maintenance log entry.

Clinic or lab: scheduled quality-control / calibration-verification runs on instruments the phlebotomist operates (point-of-care glucose or hematocrit devices, small chemistry/hematology analyzers) — load control or calibrator material, run the routine, compare results with acceptance ranges, document, and repeat or lock out the device on failure.

Plasma donation center: scheduled daily/weekly/monthly preventive maintenance on automated plasmapheresis machines — run the machine's calibration/verification routine, inspect and clean pumps, sensors, and clamps, replace consumable service parts (pressure-monitor filters, sealer wire), complete the maintenance record, and tag out-of-tolerance units.

Plasma donation center donor floor: between-donor machine turnaround — remove and discard the used disposable set and collection bottle, disinfect the machine, donor bed and cuff per SOP, confirm the machine powers up and passes its self-check, restock supplies for the next donor.

Donor center or clinic: verification/calibration of ancillary measuring devices against standards — donor scale checked with certified test weights, hematocrit centrifuge timer, protein refractometer/analyzer set with a standard solution, thermometers — adjusting where allowed and recording results.

Corrective maintenance and out-of-service handling when a machine alarms or fails a check (in a donor center, clinic, or at an off-site mobile drive): diagnose the fault, reseat or swap the failed part/consumable, re-run the verification, or remove the unit from service and coordinate vendor service and replacement equipment.

sources.title: 5 Benefits of Automated Quality Control on the Atellica Solution
sources.claim: The Siemens Atellica Solution stores QC material onboard under refrigeration and deploys it to the analyzers automatically on a pre-set schedule, so the instrument's own robotics run scheduled QC/calibration rounds without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running scheduled QC/calibration material through a diagnostic instrument and comparing results with acceptance ranges. This is the same output the phlebotomist's QC/calibration-verification run produces, performed by the instrument's own pipetting robotics inside a purpose-built analyzer enclosure.

sources.title: Robotic Mass Comparator Balances
sources.claim: Commercial robotic mass comparators use a robot arm to place certified reference and test weights on a balance pan and complete whole weight-set calibrations with no operator present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: weight-based calibration of a weighing device. The physical act the phlebotomist performs on a donor scale — placing certified test weights, reading and recording the indication — is executed autonomously here in a purpose-built calibration cell with the weights presented in a magazine.

sources.system: Automated gravimetric calibration on Tecan Freedom EVO
sources.title: Automated Gravimetric Calibration to Optimize the Accuracy and Precision of TECAN Freedom EVO Liquid Handler
sources.claim: A fully automated gravimetric calibration procedure was implemented on Tecan Freedom EVO and other liquid handlers, with pipetting scripts, data acquisition, and calibration reporting run without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: calibrating a laboratory instrument against a measurement standard (a balance) and documenting the result — the same verify-adjust-document cycle the phlebotomist performs on bench devices, done unattended on a fixtured instrument deck.

sources.system: Intelligent Autonomous Wiping and UV-C Disinfection Robot
sources.title: Transforming hospital sanitation: Autonomous robots for wiping and UV-C disinfection
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile robot with a manipulator physically wipes hospital surfaces and applies UV-C disinfection, validated in real-world testing at a hospital.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: disinfecting equipment surfaces in a healthcare facility. It substantiates only the surface-wiping step of the cleaning instances; it does not open or service machines.

sources.system: Total laboratory automation (TLA) installations; Moxi mobile manipulator
sources.developer: Multiple vendors; review by Ohgami et al. (Diagnostics)
sources.title: Collaborative Robotics, Mobile Platforms, and Total Laboratory Automation in Clinical Diagnostics
sources.claim: A 2026 review of clinical-laboratory automation reports that even in advanced total-laboratory-automation installations, humans still load and unload instruments, handle irregular items and resolve exceptions.
sources.transferJustification: Directly characterizes what deployed clinical-lab robotics do and do not do: sample logistics and analysis are automated, while hands-on instrument servicing, loading and exception handling remain human work.

sources.title: Fully Automated, Scalable, Cell Therapy Manufacturing
sources.claim: The Cell Shuttle automates transfer and docking of sealed consumable cartridges and reagent bottles between feedthroughs, a reagent vault and bioprocessing instruments inside a closed, purpose-built manufacturing machine.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest analogue to installing a fluidic disposable on a collection machine, but the cartridges are engineered for robotic docking inside the vendor's own enclosure; it does not show a robot threading a human-designed apheresis tubing set into an external machine.

Implement speech and language programs or activities as planned and directed by speech-language pathologists. Monitor the use of alternative communication devices and systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform support duties, such as preparing materials, keeping records, maintaining supplies, and scheduling activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School-based SLPA prepares the day's session materials in a shared speech room: prints/copies target-word worksheets and home-practice sheets, cuts and laminates picture/articulation cards, assembles a bin or folder per student with cards, a game, manipulatives, mirror and reinforcer stickers, and sets them out in the order of the caseload schedule.

Clinic or school SLPA maintains supplies: checks stock of consumables (gloves, wipes, tongue depressors, straws, thickener, laminating pouches, stickers, printer paper), walks to the supply closet or stockroom, retrieves needed items, restocks the therapy room cabinet and treatment carts, and flags/submits items for reorder.

Record keeping: tallies trial-by-trial accuracy data on paper data sheets or a tablet during sessions, writes daily session notes into the EMR or school documentation/Medicaid billing system, summarizes data for the supervising SLP's progress reports, and files signed consent/attendance paperwork.

Scheduling activities: coordinates session times around class schedules with teachers and parents by phone, email and in person, updates the therapy calendar and posts/prints student pass slips, and reshuffles the day when a student is absent or a room is unavailable.

AAC device and equipment upkeep: collects speech-generating devices/tablets and switches, plugs them in to charge, wipes and sanitizes them between users, powers them up to verify the device and page set work, replaces batteries and worn symbol overlays, and carries devices between the speech room and classrooms.

Home- and community-based early intervention SLPA support: packs and loads a therapy bag with toys, books and picture materials for the day's home visits, sets materials up and cleans/sanitizes them in each family's living room, and logs visit records between stops.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously picks supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetching/restocking. Transfer to 'maintaining supplies': same class of objects (boxed/packaged consumables), same fetch-from-storeroom-and-stock-the-room workflow, and the same kind of institutional building (corridors, closets, treatment rooms) as a clinic or school speech room.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics hits 1M picks with Moxi robot in healthcare settings - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi fleets run routine autonomous supply, specimen and medication deliveries at scale across US health systems, surpassing 1 million deliveries and 125,000 autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply logistics. Establishes reliability at commercial scale for the fetch-and-deliver portion of maintaining supplies in a human-occupied institutional facility.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robot autonomously scans shelves in grocery stores to report real-time product availability and out-of-stocks, deployed fleet-wide at a US grocer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory auditing. Transfer to 'maintaining supplies': detecting which stocked items are low or missing on shelves in a people-occupied facility is the monitoring half of keeping therapy-room supplies stocked.

sources.title: Rockwell Automation makes strategic investment in RightHand Robotics - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick piece-picking systems are deployed commercially picking diverse SKUs into order containers at Staples, Apotea (online pharmacy) and APO fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: goods-to-robot order picking/kitting. Transfer to 'preparing materials': assembling a per-student kit is picking a specified list of small, varied items (cards, small toys, office supplies) from presented bins into a tote, the same object class and precision as retail/pharmacy piece picking.

sources.title: Meet RightPick One: Autonomous Piece Picking, Simplified
sources.claim: RightHand's picking cells operate as autonomous piece-picking production systems rather than teleoperated demos.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the RightPick deployment item; cited to establish autonomy of the picking cells used for the kitting transfer.

sources.title: Inline Finishing | KONICA MINOLTA
sources.claim: Commercial digital print-finishing units automatically cut, crease and perforate printed sheets on demand from the digital job, and matching lamination units are sold for the same workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand print production and finishing. Transfer to 'preparing materials': printing, trimming and laminating worksheets and picture cards is exactly sheet-fed print finishing, done to tighter tolerances than a therapy card requires, when the stock is fed to the machine.

sources.title: KUKA Robots Used in Refurbishment of Electronics | KUKA Global

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated mobile-device inspection and processing. Transfer to AAC device upkeep: plugging a tablet-class device into its port (charging/diagnostics), handling it without damaging ports, checking its condition, and moving batches of devices are the same objects and precision as servicing speech-generating devices.

tasks.label: Select or prepare speech-language instructional materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School speech room or outpatient clinic: before a day of back-to-back sessions, the SLPA pulls existing materials matched to the SLP's plan - articulation card decks, picture books, language games, worksheet masters, file-folder activities - from shelves, cabinets, bins and file drawers, and groups them into a set per student.

School workroom / clinic office: making new materials - printing target-sound picture cards, visual schedules and worksheets from digital libraries, trimming with a paper cutter, running sheets through a laminator, cutting the laminate apart, and assembling into decks, binders or file folders with rings, envelopes and labels.

Therapy room: setting up the work surface for a session and resetting it between clients - laying out manipulatives, toys, game boards and pieces, mirror, timer, token board, reinforcers and the day's stimulus items in the arrangement the activity requires, then clearing them back to storage.

Preparing low-tech AAC/visual supports: printing symbol sets sized to a core board or PECS book, cutting them out, laminating, applying hook-and-loop dots, and mounting them onto boards, strips or binder pages; docking/charging a speech-generating device and swapping its printed overlays.

Clinic office before travel: packing a portable kit for a home-visit or community caseload - selecting and loading toys, books, card sets, bubbles, snack items and data forms into a rolling bag for several scheduled visits.

In a family's home during an early-intervention visit: choosing and adapting materials on the spot from the household's own toys, books and everyday objects (kitchen items, laundry, bath toys) to target the session's goals in whatever room and clutter is found there.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Piece-Picking System for Warehouse Order Fulfillment
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick 4 autonomously picks individual, previously unseen items out of bins and places them into order totes in fulfillment cells, including office-supply and general-merchandise SKUs; deployed commercially (e.g. multi-year Staples agreement).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking. Selecting named items (books, card packs, small boxed games, paper goods, office supplies) from presented bins and consolidating them into a per-order tote is physically the same act, with the same object class and precision, as pulling a specified set of instructional materials into a per-student set.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, picks and moves individual products from containers into destination totes inside fulfillment centers, after a year of real-world operation at San Marcos, TX, and is being rolled out more widely.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-picking of mixed consumer goods. The item mix (books, boxed goods, poly-bagged small items, paper products) covers the objects an SLPA gathers, so item-level selection and consolidation transfers.

sources.title: Humanoids and beyond: The state of mobile manipulators in 2025
sources.claim: Brightpick Autopicker mobile manipulators run a production e-commerce distribution centre, picking customer orders 24/7 including lights-out shifts without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile order picking in a robot-configured storage aisle. Shows retrieval of specified items from storage into an output container at commercial reliability, matching the retrieval/kitting half of material preparation.

sources.system: Rollem Revolution card cutting and collating system
sources.title: Revolution - Rollem USA
sources.claim: The Rollem Revolution takes full printed sheets and produces finished, cut and collated card packs in one fully automatic in-line system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: playing-card production. Turning printed sheets into trimmed, collated card decks is the same physical operation as producing picture/articulation card decks from printed sheets, at tighter tolerances than therapy materials require.

sources.title: System 2760 Automatic Laminator - D & K Group
sources.claim: D&K's System 2760 laminates digital prints with an automatic sheet feeder, one-sided laminator and automatic sheet separator; automatic sheet-fed laminators feed, laminate and trim digital ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial print lamination. Laminating printed sheets is exactly the step an SLPA performs on picture cards and visuals; the machine handles feeding, laminating and separating without an operator.

sources.system: Zuend Q-Line cutter with Robot PortaTable 130

sources.claim: Zuend digital cutters with the Robot PortaTable 130 automatically pick and sort cut parts off the cutting table with a robotic arm, and Zuend's cutting solutions increasingly produce independently and autonomously in print-finishing production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: digital die-cutting and part sorting of printed/laminated sheet stock. Cutting laminated card shapes out of a sheet and sorting them into sets is the cutting-and-sorting half of preparing card decks and symbol sets.

sources.claim: A vision-guided robot kitting cell at Danfoss picks an assortment of different parts directly from supplier pallets and assembles them into trays, running with improved cycle times and reliability after a 3D vision upgrade.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial kitting. Assembling a defined assortment of small items into a tray in specified positions is the same physical operation as laying out a session's materials on a tray/table or packing a per-visit kit.

sources.title: Automated Labeling
sources.claim: Commercial robotic labeling cells autonomously pick adhesive labels and apply them to products with high precision and high application rates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: adhesive label pick-and-apply. Placing adhesive-backed hook-and-loop dots or laminated symbols onto a board or binder page is the same pick, align and press operation on similar-sized flexible adhesive parts.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi performs autonomous fetch-and-deliver runs in hospitals - transporting pharmacy, lab and supply items over more than a million deliveries in 25+ US hospitals - but its work is point-to-point transport of packaged items, not item-level selection, fabrication or set-up of materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous logistics inside a structured human facility. It marks the current ceiling of E2 mobile manipulation - navigation and transport of packaged loads - and does not extend to selecting assorted items from open shelves or fabricating materials.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: Home humanoids remain dependent on remote human operators; NEO's household work is teleoperated or expert-assisted rather than reliably autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household object handling. Shows no cited system autonomously selects and adapts everyday objects in a private home at worker quality.

tasks.label: Assist speech-language pathologists in the conduct of client screenings or assessments of language, voice, fluency, articulation, or hearing.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School-based speech-sound/articulation screening: SLPA seats a K-3 child in a small therapy room or a quiet corner, opens a screening kit, presents picture-naming cards and elicits connected speech, listens and marks sound errors and intelligibility on a scoring form, and passes results to the supervising SLP. Child may be shy, wiggly, or off-task.

Assisting during an SLP-administered formal assessment (school or outpatient clinic): SLPA sets up the testing environment, gathers and preps test kits, stimulus books, manipulatives and toys, hands materials to the SLP on cue, runs the audio/video recorder, takes notes and tallies responses as directed, redirects the client, then cleans and disinfects and re-shelves materials.

School hearing screening support: SLPA takes a child to a quiet room, otoscopically inspects/inquires as trained, places supra-aural headphones correctly on the child's head, operates a portable pure-tone audiometer sweep, conditions the young child to raise a hand or drop a block on hearing tones, records pass/refer results, and rescreens failures.

Early-intervention or home-health screening assist: play-based language/communication screening in a family home or a daycare room, working on the floor with toys, caregiver and siblings present, variable furniture, pets and background noise; SLPA presents objects, elicits vocalizations and gestures, and records observations for the SLP.

Adult client screening assist in a medical facility (skilled nursing, hospital, outpatient rehab): SLPA positions the patient upright at bedside or in a treatment room, sets up amplifier/glasses/dentures and reading or picture stimuli, presents screening items for speech, language and cognition (and sometimes a headphone hearing screen), records responses and reports to the SLP.

sources.system: Pepper humanoid robot with RoboMate software (Behavior Labs)
sources.developer: IRCCS Centro Neurolesi Bonino Pulejo / Behavior Labs / University of Catania

sources.claim: A Pepper humanoid robot administered the MMSE cognitive screening to 50 MCI patients in an Italian clinical research institute, but the robot's voice and movements were remotely controlled through the RoboMate app and a psychologist monitored and recorded the patient's responses on a separate tablet, so administration was not autonomous.

It fails to transfer because control was remote and a human clinician recorded and scored responses; the robot also handled no test materials.

sources.title: Child-Robot Interaction Studies During COVID-19 Pandemic (arXiv:2105.00215)
sources.claim: In the RoboRehab project a Pepper robot was used to support audiometry testing of six 6-7 year-old children with cochlear implants in a hospital consultation room, using a tablet-gamified auditory test; the robot provided engagement/feedback while clinicians ran the test and equipment, and no transducer placement or independent administration by the robot is reported.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to the hearing-screening instance: it is the nearest robotic involvement in pediatric audiometry found, but the robot only supports engagement in a research pilot and does not place headphones, operate the audiometer, or score pass/refer.

sources.system: NAO social robot in speech therapy
sources.developer: Softbank Robotics NAO platform, study by university research team
sources.title: A Case Study of a Robot-Assisted Speech Therapy for Children with Language Disorders
sources.claim: A NAO-type social robot was used in individual speech-therapy sessions with five children aged 9-12 with language disorders in an ordinary therapy setting; the study reports motivational and attention benefits under therapist supervision, and covers intervention activities rather than administering or scoring screenings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered speech/language activities with children in a clinical/school room. It does not transfer to screening because the robot delivers scripted therapy activities with a therapist present and does not elicit, transcribe, score, or handle test materials.

sources.transferJustification: Same occupational domain (SLP practice); cited to show the state of the art is prospective design work for therapy support, with no system administering screenings or assessments.
