tasks.label: Test or maintain equipment to ensure correct performance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: School-based SLPA does a routine check of students' AAC/speech-generating devices and therapy tablets: charge overnight, power on, confirm the touchscreen responds across the display, confirm voice output volume and speaker quality, confirm the access method (touch, switch, eye gaze) registers, and log/report any failures to the supervising SLP. Devices are handled in a therapy room or classroom.

Clinic/hospital rehab department: clean, disinfect and check therapy materials and equipment between clients (plastic and plush toys, mirrors, oral-motor tools, feeding utensils, headphones, keyboard/screen surfaces), confirming items are intact, functional and restocked to infection-control standard.

Therapy-room technology check before sessions or telepractice: verify laptop/tablet/AV cart works — connect power and cables, confirm display, speaker output, microphone pickup, camera image, headphone jack and app launch; adjust volume and swap a faulty cable or headset.

Speech/hearing screening equipment: daily biologic listening check of a portable audiometer (tones at each frequency in both earphones, listening for distortion or intermittency), wiggle-test and visual inspection of cords, cleaning of earphone cushions, battery replacement, and flagging the unit for annual calibration.

Home health / early-intervention / bedside visit: check and adjust the client's equipment in place with the client present — reseat the device mount on a wheelchair or bed rail, reposition a switch, replace batteries, verify the client can activate it, and coach the caregiver.

Battery and consumables maintenance across a caseload of simple-tech devices in the school storeroom or clinic office: open battery doors and replace AA/coin cells in switches, single-message buttons and toys, re-record messages, replace worn charging cords, and confirm each unit works before it goes back into circulation.

sources.title: Automating Smartphone Testing in Device Refurbishment | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT, a commercial device-testing robot from Adapta Robotics, autonomously runs a full functional test sequence on a smart device placed in its test bay — touchscreen responsiveness and dead-zone detection, physical buttons and knobs, speaker/microphone verification with external microphones, camera, vibration and charging current/voltage — and issues pass/fail reports flagging failed components. This is essentially the 'does this tablet/AAC device still work correctly' check.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line/refurbishment functional testing of consumer smart devices. AAC speech-generating devices are tablets or dedicated tablet-class hardware; the same checks (touch response, audio output, buttons, charging) are exactly what an SLPA verifies, at equal or finer precision, on a device presented to the machine.

sources.title: TOUCH: Automated touch screen testing | OptoFidelity
sources.claim: OptoFidelity TOUCH is a commercial gantry test robot that locates the device under test with a camera and runs scripted-then-automated touch performance and functionality tests on final products, generating test reports; used in device makers' test labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated verification that a touch device's screen and UI respond correctly. This is the core of an SLPA's check that an AAC tablet's touch targets all register, on comparable hardware in a fixtured test position.

sources.title: How Apple Robots are Closing the Waste Recycling Loop | Technology Magazine
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy robot, running in an Apple facility in Austin, autonomously opens fixtured iPhones — punching out screws and removing the battery — at 200 devices per hour, showing that opening a consumer device's fasteners and extracting/handling its battery is a solved, deployed, purpose-built-cell operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated opening of a small consumer device and removal of its battery. The SLPA battery-maintenance instance requires opening a battery door and extracting cells from small devices of the same scale, with the device presented to the machine.

sources.title: Apple expands global recycling programs - Apple Newsroom
sources.claim: Apple states Daisy handles 15 different iPhone models at 200 per hour, i.e. the cell copes with model variation rather than a single fixtured part.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Daisy item above; cited for model-variety tolerance, which matters because an SLPA's switches and devices are not all identical.

sources.title: Drone company Airobotics takes flight - Australian Mining
sources.claim: The Airobotics Optimus Airbase, a fielded drone-in-a-box station at industrial sites, uses a robotic arm to autonomously remove and replace the aircraft's battery (and payloads) with no operator present — a complete, verified battery-swap maintenance loop in a purpose-built enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous battery replacement in equipment to keep it serviceable. The SLPA instance is the same maintenance act — depleted cells out, fresh cells in, unit confirmed operational — on smaller devices presented to the machine.

sources.system: Rocsys autonomous charging robot (M1 and port systems)
sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M | Electrek
sources.claim: Rocsys' rail-mounted robotic charging arm autonomously detects an arriving vehicle, opens the charge port, mates the connector, charges and disconnects; deployed for hands-free charging at ports and logistics yards, showing autonomous vision-guided connector mating outside a fenced factory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plug-in charging. Supports the 'put the device on charge and confirm it charges' step of the equipment check; the connector is larger than USB-C, so it is cited only as corroboration alongside MATT's charging-current verification.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous infection-control disinfection in a clinical facility. Cited to show the limit: it irradiates room and equipment surfaces but does not pick up, wash or wipe individual soiled therapy items, so it does not complete the cleaning instance.

roles.title: Endoscopy Technicians
roles.description: Maintain a sterile field to provide support for physicians and nurses during endoscopy procedures. Prepare and maintain instruments and equipment. May obtain specimens.

tasks.label: Clean, disinfect, or calibrate scopes or other endoscopic instruments according to manufacturer recommendations and facility standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine reprocessing of a standard flexible GI endoscope (gastroscope/colonoscope) between cases in the endoscopy decontamination/reprocessing room: receive the soiled scope from its transport container, leak test, brush and flush all channels in the sink with enzymatic detergent, attach the model-specific channel connectors, run the automated endoscope reprocessor (AER) high-level disinfection cycle, alcohol flush/air purge, then hang the scope in a drying/storage cabinet and record the cycle. High volume, tight turnaround between cases.

Point-of-use precleaning in the procedure room immediately after the case: wipe the insertion tube with a wet cloth while the scope is still attached to the light source, aspirate detergent solution and air through suction/biopsy and air-water channels, detach the scope, place it in a closed transport bin and carry it to the decontamination room within the required time window.

Reprocessing a complex scope with an elevator or extra channels (duodenoscope, linear echoendoscope, bronchoscope): removable distal cap handling, meticulous manual brushing of the elevator recess and all channels per the scope maker's IFU, cleaning-verification testing, then AER cycle with duodenoscope connectors, plus double high-level disinfection or low-temperature sterilization per facility policy.

Reprocessing the unit's other reusable devices between cases: rigid/semi-rigid scopes, TEE probes, and detachable accessories such as air/water and suction valves, distal caps, water bottles and irrigation tubing — cleaned and high-level disinfected in an AER or washer-disinfector, or ultrasonically cleaned and sent for steam sterilization, then inspected and reassembled.

Cleaning and disinfecting non-immersible equipment in the procedure and reprocessing rooms between cases: video processor/light source tower, monitors, keyboards, carts, insufflator, suction canisters, ultrasound console, and the reprocessing sinks — wiped with facility-approved disinfectant wipes according to each manufacturer's IFU, observing wet-contact times.

Quality control and functional checks on scopes and reprocessing equipment: manual leak test outside the AER, borescope inspection of channels for debris/damage, ATP or protein cleaning-verification swab tests, high-level disinfectant minimum-effective-concentration test strips, checking angulation, image and white balance, and logging all results for the scope's record.

sources.system: MEDIVATORS ADVANTAGE PLUS Automated Endoscope Reprocessor
sources.title: MEDIVATORS ADVANTAGE PLUS Automated Endoscope Reprocessor | STERIS
sources.claim: The MEDIVATORS ADVANTAGE PLUS automated ... runs a programmed wash + high-level-disinfection cycle with continuous automated leak testing and alcohol flush, and with INTERCEPT detergent is labeled to remove the need for manual brushing ... endoscopes (duodenoscopes excepted). Technicians load the scope into the basin and connect it; the machine then runs the cycle unattended.

sources.title: EVOTECH® endoscope cleaner and reprocessor (ECR) simulated-use and clinical-use evaluation of cleaning efficacy | BMC Infectious Diseases
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed simulated-use and clinical-use study of the EVOTECH Endoscope Cleaner and ..., an FDA-cleared machine that performs the cleaning as well as the high-level disinfection of colonoscopes, gastroscopes, duodenoscopes and bronchoscopes, i.e. the machine itself performs the channel cleaning once the scope is loaded and connected.

sources.title: EVOTECH™ Endoscope Cleaner and Reprocessor (ECR) | ASP
sources.claim: ASP's current product page confirms the EVOTECH ECR is a commercially available dual-basin machine that automates both cleaning and high-level disinfection of ...; a footnote on the same page cautions that it does not eliminate precleaning or manual cleaning and that facilities must follow their own policies, so machine-only cleaning is not universally accepted in US practice.

sources.system: Dual Franka Emika Panda robotic endoscope reprocessing/transfer cell (TU Munich / Garmisch-Partenkirchen endoscopy unit)
sources.developer: Allescher et al., Technical University of Munich (Haddadin lab)
sources.title: Integration of robotic in the reprocessing and transfer of endoscopes — Endoscopy International Open
sources.claim: A dual-arm Franka Emika Panda robot cell integrated with a pass-through endoscope washer-disinfector and drying cabinet performed the handling around the reprocessing cycle — removing the processed endoscope on an adapted tray and placing it into the storage/venting cabinet — over 50 consecutive simulated daily-throughput runs with no failures.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the scope-handling steps that bracket the cleaning/disinfection cycle (unloading the washer-disinfector, transferring to the drying/storage cabinet) on the same objects (flexible endoscopes) in the same reprocessing room, using purpose-adapted trays and lifting devices.

sources.system: Dual Franka Emika Panda robotic endoscope reprocessing/transfer cell
sources.developer: Allescher et al., Technical University of Munich
sources.title: Thieme E-Journals - Endoscopy International Open / Full Text
sources.claim: The same robotic reprocessing/transfer cell was field-tested on the clean side of a working endoscope reprocessing room after achieving 100% accuracy on its transfer routines, establishing the environment as a purpose-adapted station inside a hospital reprocessing room.
sources.transferJustification: Same as prior item: handling steps around the machine cleaning/disinfection cycle for flexible endoscopes in the reprocessing room.

sources.system: Steelco EW 2 S Series automatic endoscope reprocessor
sources.title: EW 2 S Series - Steelco
sources.claim: Commercial automatic endoscope reprocessor that washes and disinfects not only flexible endoscopes but also rigid scopes and TEE probes in a closed chamber once the items are loaded into its racks/connectors.

sources.title: Olympus Launches New ETD Endoscope Washer Disinfector - Olympus EMEA
sources.claim: Olympus' ETD endoscope washer-disinfector performs machine cleaning and chemical disinfection of endoscopes, including pulsed water/air cleaning of elevator channels, in a closed chamber after the scope is loaded and connected.

sources.title: STATUS EVALUATION REPORT: Automated endoscope reprocessors (ASGE)
sources.claim: Limiting evidence: the ASGE technology status evaluation of automated endoscope reprocessors states that manual cleaning of the scope is still required even where AER makers claim it is not, so an AER cycle alone is not accepted as the whole reprocessing procedure in many US facilities, particularly for elevator-bearing scopes.

sources.developer: single-center endoscopy unit (prospective comparative trial, Gastrointestinal Endoscopy)
sources.title: The effect of autonomous mobile robots on improving endoscope reprocessing efficiency: a prospective comparative trial (with video)
sources.claim: Eight autonomous mobile robots were deployed in an endoscopy center to distribute and retrieve endoscopes between procedure rooms and the reprocessing area, cutting transport workload by 2.18 FTE in a prospective comparative trial — autonomous scope transport inside a hospital, but not precleaning or cleaning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (intra-facility transport of soiled and clean endoscopes) shows autonomous scope logistics in an E2 hospital setting, but it does not perform any cleaning, brushing or disinfection step of this task.

tasks.label: Collect specimens from patients, using standard medical procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Screening/surveillance colonoscopy with multiple site-specific biopsies (e.g., IBD or microscopic colitis protocol): in a hospital or ASC endoscopy room with a sedated patient, the tech passes biopsy forceps down the scope channel, opens/closes them on the endoscopist's command, withdraws them, dislodges each 2-6 mm tissue fragment from the forceps cup with a needle or toothpick into the correct pre-labeled formalin jar for that segment, keeps segment jars separate, and completes labels/requisition with the RN's verification of patient ID.

Polypectomy specimen retrieval during colonoscopy: tech closes the snare on command, then recovers the resected polyp by suction into a specimen trap or with a Roth net/tripod at the scope tip, transfers the polyp (sometimes fragmented, sometimes needing orientation or pinning) into formalin, one container per polyp with site noted, and labels it.

Upper endoscopy (EGD) tissue sampling: gastric antral/body biopsies with one fragment placed into a rapid urease (CLO) test kit and the rest jarred, duodenal biopsies oriented mucosa-up on filter paper/mesh for celiac work-up, and Barrett's esophagus biopsies jarred by level; sedated patient, physician calling out sites rapidly.

Cytology and fluid specimens: brush cytology (brush cut into fixative or smeared on slides and fixed immediately), EUS-FNA aspirate expressed onto slides for rapid on-site evaluation and into CytoLyt/cell-block medium, bile/cyst fluid or bronchial washings captured in a Lukens trap; time-critical handling to avoid air-drying or clotting, then labeling and transport to the lab.

Non-endoscopic specimens in the pre-procedure or recovery bay with an awake patient: instructing the patient and receiving a urine cup or stool sample container, handling and bagging it, running or forwarding a point-of-care test (pregnancy, occult blood, capillary glucose fingerstick), and labeling/logging the sample.

Pre-procedure infectious-disease screening swab: tech collects a nasopharyngeal/oropharyngeal swab from a seated, cooperative patient in the pre-op bay, breaks the swab into transport medium, caps and labels the tube, and sends it for testing.

sources.title: Homepage - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta performs the complete venipuncture blood-collection process on awake patients autonomously (AI Doppler-ultrasound vein selection, robotic needle insertion, sample collection); it is CE-marked and commercially available in the EU, with clinical validation in thousands of patients and hospital customers taking delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collecting a diagnostic specimen from a patient in a clinical facility. It substantiates autonomous needle-based blood collection from a seated awake patient at an outpatient draw station, but not endoscopic tissue sampling, forceps handling, or transfer of millimetre tissue fragments into fixative.

sources.developer: University of Southern Denmark / collaborators (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening | Scientific Reports
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot station (SR-NOCS) collected combined naso- and oropharyngeal specimens from patients in two clinical studies, with sampling results matching manual collection.

sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: Lifeline Robotics built a fully automatic throat-swab robot that takes a pharyngeal specimen from a patient seated at the robot station without a human operator guiding the swab.

sources.developer: STORM Lab / University of Leeds and collaborators (Advanced Intelligent Systems case study)
sources.title: Teleoperated Magnetic Endoscopy: A Case Study and Perspective
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic GI endoscopy remains teleoperated, and the biopsy and associated specimen operations in a robotic magnetic endoscopy case were carried out by a human clinician, with robotic automation of tool actuation described only as a future possibility.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (endoscopic specimen acquisition): shows the tissue-sampling and specimen steps that the endoscopy technician performs are still done by humans on robotic endoscopy platforms.

sources.system: Magnetically actuated endoscope with autonomous biopsy mechanism
sources.developer: Academic research group (Robotic Autonomy for Magnetic Endoscope Biopsy)
sources.title: Robotic Autonomy for Magnetic Endoscope Biopsy
sources.claim: Research on autonomous biopsy with a magnetically actuated endoscope reports sampling success rates well below clinical acceptability and only in laboratory/animal-model conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the specimen-acquisition step of this task; the reported success rates show autonomous endoscopic tissue collection is far below the reliability an endoscopy unit would accept.

tasks.label: Perform safety checks to verify proper equipment functioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-procedure setup and function check of a flexible video endoscope and tower in the procedure room: connect light guide/video connector to the processor, attach water bottle and suction tubing, white-balance, verify image and illumination on the monitor, test air/water insufflation and suction, check angulation knobs and locks, seat biopsy valve/cap before the case starts.

Leak test and channel/patency verification of a used flexible endoscope at point of use or in the decontamination room: attach the leak-test connector, pressurize, watch for pressure loss or bubbles while angulating the distal tip, judge pass/fail and quarantine/document a failed scope.

Daily or per-case checks of ancillary procedural equipment in the endoscopy suite: power up and verify the electrosurgical generator and return-electrode alarm, CO2 insufflator, suction regulators and wall suction, oxygen supply/cylinder pressure, patient monitor and cables, emergency cart/defibrillator ready-status, and sign the check sheet.

Checks of reprocessing-room equipment: AER power-up self-test, verifying cycle parameters and connector hookups, testing high-level disinfectant minimum effective concentration with test strips, alarm and filter checks, drying-cabinet airflow, reviewing/filing cycle printouts.

Detailed external inspection of endoscopes and accessories for damage or wear: distal lens and light guides, bending rubber, insertion tube, connectors and valves, plus reusable accessories (forceps, snares, water bottles) under lighted magnification, removing damaged items from service.

Borescope inspection of internal endoscope channels (working, air/water, elevator) for scratches, debris, corrosion or fluid, threading a 1-2 mm borescope the full length of the scope and interpreting the images before the scope is released for use.

tasks.label: Maintain or repair endoscopic equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Leak test of a flexible GI endoscope after a case, in the hospital/ASC reprocessing room: attach the leak tester to the venting connector, pressurize, watch for pressure decay or bubbles during immersion/angulation, record pass/fail, and pull the scope from service if it fails.

Pre-use / periodic functional check and preventive maintenance of a flexible scope in the equipment or reprocessing room: inspect distal lens, bending rubber and insertion tube for dents/kinks, verify angulation knob travel and locks, check air/water and suction patency, clean/defog the lens, and replace worn air-water and suction valves, biopsy-port caps and O-rings.

Troubleshooting and minor repair of the endoscopy tower and ancillary equipment in the procedure room, often mid-case: light source lamp or LED module replacement, reseating video-processor and scope connectors, swapping CO2/insufflator tubing and tanks, fixing suction lines and canisters, resetting the electrosurgical unit, chasing a bad monitor cable.

Handling a damaged scope: identify and tape/seal the damage, clean and high-level disinfect before shipment, tag and document the fault, pack the scope in its case with paperwork for the repair vendor courier, then receive and check a loaner scope into service and log it.

Scheduled maintenance of reprocessing and support equipment: change AER water/air filters and detergent and disinfectant containers, replace disinfectant per MRC test strip results, clean basins and connector sets, replace worn AER channel connectors, service drying-cabinet filters, change printer paper, complete PM logs.

Bench-level repair in an in-house scope repair shop or vendor lab: diagnose the fault on a returned scope, disassemble the control body or bending section, replace bending rubber, angulation wires, light guide fibers or a channel, re-glue and re-seal, reassemble and run leak and image tests before returning to service.

sources.title: Automatic Leak Tester Facilitates Endoscope Reprocessing - HospiMedica
sources.claim: The Olympus ALT-Pro is a commercially sold benchtop automated endoscope leak tester: after the operator scans the scope and connects it, the machine performs a fully computerized dry pressure leak test on up to two scopes and reports the result, replacing manual submersion and bubble observation.

sources.developer: Wientjes, Noordmans et al., University Medical Center Utrecht
sources.title: Automated Objective Routine Examination of Optical Quality of Rigid Endoscopes in a Clinical Setting (PLoS ONE)
sources.claim: An opto-electronic test bench installed in a hospital central sterilization department automatically measures illumination-fibre transmission and lens contrast of a mounted rigid endoscope and issues pass/fail criteria to reject scopes or accept them after repair; 1,599 measurements on 46 scope types were made over eight months with an operator mounting each scope.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated quality-control testing of endoscopes in a sterile processing department. It substantiates machine-performed instrument condition testing when the scope is mounted in a fixture, i.e. the E1 presentation, but it covers only optical measurement of rigid scopes, not handling, part replacement or repair.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L + YOLO12/ResNet perception)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications (arXiv:2602.01679)
sources.claim: The closest robotics work in sterile processing is a lab-cell system that autonomously sorts and packs surgical instruments into trays with a 6-DOF Staubli arm, vision and 3D-printed holders; it addresses tray assembly only, not diagnosis, disassembly or repair of endoscopic equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of surgical instruments in a sterile processing department. It does not transfer to maintaining or repairing endoscopic equipment: the objects are rigid hand instruments rather than delicate flexible scopes and towers, and the demonstrated actions are pick-and-place packing, with no fault diagnosis, disassembly, part replacement or functional testing.

tasks.label: Assist physicians or registered nurses in the conduct of endoscopic procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine diagnostic colonoscopy/EGD with biopsies in a hospital or ASC endoscopy room: tech stands at the bedside with a sedated patient, threads and operates biopsy forceps through the scope's working channel, opening/closing on the endoscopist's verbal cue while watching the monitor, withdraws the forceps, retrieves the tissue and jars it in labeled formalin, and between passes applies manual abdominal pressure and helps reposition the patient.

Therapeutic GI intervention (polypectomy, hemostasis, dilation) in the same endoscopy room: tech preps and loads snares, hemoclips, injection needles and hemostatic powder, feeds them down the channel, opens/closes the snare around a polyp and holds it during cautery, deploys clips on the physician's timed command, and manages electrosurgical generator and irrigation settings, sometimes in an urgent bleeding scenario.

ERCP or EUS in a fluoroscopy-equipped suite: tech in lead apron performs coordinated wire-guided exchanges (fixing the guidewire while the physician advances/withdraws catheters), loads and deploys sphincterotomes, baskets, and biliary stents, injects contrast on command, and handles FNA needles and cytology slides.

Bronchoscopy/EBUS or a portable bedside case in an ICU, ED, or OR: tech wheels in and sets up the portable tower at an unfamiliar bedside, assists with needle aspiration, brushings and lavage, manages suction traps and specimen containers, and works around ventilator tubing, drips and other staff.

Equipment set-up and in-case management in the procedure room: connecting light source, water bottle, CO2 insufflation and suction, leak-testing and checking the scope, opening sterile accessory packages onto the field, positioning monitors, and troubleshooting or swapping failing equipment mid-procedure while the case continues.

In-case runner errands within the endoscopy unit: fetching an unanticipated accessory, stent size or supply from the unit storeroom and carrying labeled specimen containers out to the lab drop-off while the case continues, moving along the unit's corridors and elevators.

sources.system: Shanghai Operation Robot flexible-endoscopy master–slave system (robot-assisted ERCP)
sources.developer: Shanghai Operation Robot Co., Ltd. / affiliated clinical group
sources.title: Feasibility study of robot-assisted endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography for biliary stent placement in an in vivo porcine model
sources.claim: The most advanced system built to perform the endoscopy assistant's role (accessory advance/retract, guidewire delivery, accessory exchange) during ERCP is a master–slave console driven by the physician with a joystick and foot pedal, tested only in live pigs; it is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task: the module explicitly replaces the endoscopy assistant's accessory and guidewire handling during ERCP. It shows the capability exists only under continuous human control, in porcine models.

sources.system: Robotic scrub nurse (RSN) with three-stage instrument-anticipation network
sources.developer: Technical University of Munich (Wagner, Mayer et al.)
sources.title: Robotic scrub nurse to anticipate surgical instruments based on real-time laparoscopic video analysis (Communications Medicine)
sources.claim: The leading autonomous robotic scrub nurse anticipates and hands laparoscopic instruments from real-time video, but it was developed and evaluated against recorded cholecystectomy video with a robot arm in a research setting, handling rigid OR instruments rather than flexible endoscopic accessories, and is not in clinical use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handing instruments to an operator during a minimally invasive procedure. It is the closest analog to endoscopy-tech assisting, and its scope (predicting and presenting rigid instruments, ~72% correct anticipation, lab evaluation) falls far short of channel-fed accessory operation on a live patient.

sources.title: For the First Time, Newly Developed Robot Assists Doctors and Nurses in Operating Room (NewYork-Presbyterian)
sources.claim: A robotic instrument server handed and retrieved rigid surgical instruments on voice request during an actual operation in a hospital OR — the only demonstration of a robot acting as an in-procedure instrument assistant with a patient present; it had no patient contact and was never commercialized.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passing instruments to a physician during a procedure in an OR. Transfer to endoscopy assisting is limited — Penelope moved rigid instruments between a tray and the surgeon's hand and never touched the patient or an endoscope accessory.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics hits 1M picks with Moxi robot in healthcare settings (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile manipulator is deployed across US hospitals doing fetch-and-deliver runs, including lab specimens, medications and supplies, navigating corridors and elevators without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply and specimen courier runs. This is the same errand an endoscopy tech makes mid-case — same objects (supply items, labeled specimen containers), same institution-controlled corridors, same delivery-accuracy standard.

sources.title: Deploying physical AI to aid clinicians using AWS with Diligent Robotics (AWS case study)
sources.claim: Moxi's hospital deployment is broad and current: placed in 25 US hospitals with more than 1.3 million completed deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the prior item (hospital courier runs); cited to establish current, at-scale commercial deployment as of 2026.

sources.system: Teleoperated humanoid robot surgical team (proof of concept)
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Yip lab) and collaborators
sources.title: Surgeons Use Teleoperated Humanoid Robots to Perform Live Surgery–a World First (Newswise)
sources.claim: The state of the art for humanoid robots taking assistive roles in the operating room as of mid-2026 is teleoperation by surgeons in proof-of-concept experiments, not autonomous in-procedure assisting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid robots assisting a procedural team. Cited as the current ceiling — the assisting role is still performed under continuous human control, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for endoscopy assisting.

tasks.label: Place devices, such as blood pressure cuffs, pulse oximeter sensors, nasal cannulas, surgical cautery pads, and cardiac monitoring electrodes, on patients to monitor vital signs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-procedure prep in a hospital or ASC endoscopy room for a routine adult EGD/colonoscopy under moderate sedation: tech opens the gown, wipes/preps skin, peels the liners off 3-5 adhesive ECG electrodes, places them at RA/LA/LL (and precordial) landmarks on a variably hairy, obese, or elderly chest, snaps on lead wires, routes cables, and confirms a clean trace on the monitor.

Placing the non-invasive blood pressure cuff (correct size, artery marker aligned, wrapped and velcroed snugly on the upper arm, often over/under a gown and around an IV line) and the pulse oximeter probe (clip or adhesive wrap on finger, sometimes ear or toe if nails are polished/perfused poorly), then connecting cables and verifying plausible readings before sedation.

Placing a nasal cannula (or simple mask) for supplemental oxygen: prongs curved into the nares, flexible tubing looped over both ears and cinched under the chin, tubing routed clear of the bite block and scope, connected to the O2 source with flow set; done on an anxious, talking or already drowsy patient just before the scope goes in.

Applying the electrosurgical dispersive (cautery grounding) pad for polypectomy/APC cases: choosing a clean, dry, well-vascularized site over large muscle (thigh/flank), clipping hair if needed, peeling the liner and smoothing the large flexible pad wrinkle-free with full skin contact, connecting the cable, and clearing the generator's contact-quality alarm.

Mid-procedure adjustment or replacement in the crowded, dim procedure room: leads or pulse-ox probe dislodge when the patient is rolled from left lateral to supine/prone or bucks during scope advancement; tech reaches around the endoscopist, drapes, scope tower and IV poles to re-site an electrode, re-clip the oximeter on a cold/moving finger, or reseat a displaced cannula without breaking the sterile field.

Portable/bedside endoscopy in an ICU, ED or OR: monitoring devices placed on a critically ill, sometimes intubated, edematous, restrained or uncooperative patient already covered with existing lines, dressings, telemetry leads and a ventilator circuit, working around other staff in a space not laid out for endoscopy.

sources.title: Aletta for Hospital Leadership - Vitestro
sources.claim: Vitestro's Aletta is a commercial, hospital-deployed autonomous phlebotomy device: the patient's arm is presented into a purpose-built cradle and the machine autonomously finds a vein, inserts the needle, draws blood and applies a bandage, with one professional supervising up to three units. It is the closest deployed example of a machine acting on a patient's arm, but it performs no monitoring-device placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture with bandage application. It shows autonomous, sub-millimetre contact with a fixtured patient arm and application of one adhesive item to a self-located puncture site; it does not demonstrate peel-and-place of monitoring electrodes at anatomic landmarks, cuff wrapping, or cable/tubing handling, so it cannot substantiate this task's instances.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Independent multicenter clinical trial confirms the Aletta device performs venipunctures autonomously on patients in clinical laboratories under 1:3 supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: blood collection on a seated patient in a clinic. Establishes maturity/autonomy of patient-contact robotics, but the manipulated objects (needle cartridge, bandage) and the fixtured arm workspace do not cover placing cuffs, oximeter probes, cannulas, cautery pads or chest electrodes.

sources.system: Autonomous cardiac ultrasound scanning robotic system (human posture recognition + image servo control)
sources.developer: academic group (Frontiers in Robotics and AI publication)
sources.title: Autonomous ultrasound scanning robotic system based on human posture recognition and image servo control: an application for cardiac imaging
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic ultrasound systems can locate human body landmarks from RGB-D pose estimation and press a probe against a person's chest with force control, but they hold a rigid probe on the robot and attach nothing to the patient; work is at research-demo stage on volunteers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a probe on a patient's chest. Comparable body region and contact-force safety, but the system never grasps, peels or affixes an adhesive electrode, wraps a cuff, or manages lead wires, so it cannot complete electrode or cuff placement.

sources.title: Brain Navi develops new robot that performs nasal swab tests autonomously
sources.claim: A robot has autonomously located a person's nostril from facial recognition and inserted a swab, showing autonomous instrument insertion at the face, but only a rigid single swab and no cannula tubing routing or oxygen connection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: nostril access with an instrument. Shares the face/nostril target of nasal cannula placement, but the cannula instance requires bimanual handling of soft prongs and flexible tubing looped over both ears and connected to an O2 source, which this system does not do.

sources.system: Force-Constrained Visual Policy robot-assisted dressing system
sources.title: Force-Constrained Visual Policy: Safe Robot-Assisted Dressing via Multi-Modal Sensing
sources.claim: Dressing a garment sleeve onto a real person's arm remains an open research problem addressed in laboratory studies with force-limited policies, indicating that robotic manipulation of soft, deformable items onto a human limb (as required to wrap a BP cuff) is not a fielded capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing a soft item onto a human arm. Nearest analogue to wrapping and fastening a blood-pressure cuff; it is a lab demo of a single simplified sleeve pull, with no fastening, sizing, artery alignment or cable connection, so it does not substantiate cuff placement at worker quality.

sources.system: Semi-autonomous vital sign measurement robot (PPG-equipped robotic arm)
sources.title: Automatic Vital Sign Measurement Enabled by a Semi-Autonomous Robot
sources.claim: A robotic arm can autonomously find measurement sites on a person's arm and press integrated PPG sensors to obtain heart rate, SpO2 and respiratory rate, but the sensors stay on the robot: no monitoring device is placed on the patient for continuous procedural monitoring, and the system is described as semi-autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: obtaining vital signs by contacting a patient. It substitutes a spot measurement rather than placing a cuff, probe or electrodes on the patient for continuous monitoring, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

tasks.label: Prepare suites or rooms according to endoscopic procedure requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-case turnover of a GI endoscopy procedure room in a hospital unit or ambulatory endoscopy center for a routine EGD/colonoscopy: wipe down tower, monitors, bed rails and cart, change stretcher linen and pads, discard used accessories, hang a clean reprocessed scope, connect the umbilical to the light source/processor, attach water bottle and CO2/suction tubing, seat air-water and suction valves, confirm image and insufflation, and lay out biopsy forceps, snares, specimen containers, lubricant and bite block for the next case, in 10-15 minutes under schedule pressure.

First-case-of-the-day full room setup: power up and boot the video processor, light source, insufflator, electrosurgical unit and suction, white-balance the scope, verify oxygen, suction canisters, monitoring leads, reversal/emergency supplies, drape and position the stretcher and tables, and stage the day's scopes and accessories per the posted schedule.

Setup for an advanced/therapeutic case (ERCP, EUS, EMR/ESD, PEG, hemostasis): add fluoroscopy or ultrasound processor, sterile back table with drapes, guidewires, catheters, contrast, needles, clips, injection agents, cautery generator and grounding pad, lead aprons and shields, arranged to the physician's preference card while maintaining a sterile field.

Stocking/restocking the procedure room and procedure cart from bulk supply: replenishing bins and drawers with peel-packed accessories, syringes, tubing, gauze, PPE, sterile water bottles and linens to par levels, rotating stock and pulling expired items, at end of shift or between blocks.

Setting up portable endoscopy outside the endoscopy unit: rolling the cart/tower to an ICU room, ED bay or operating room for an emergent bleed, bedside PEG or intubated patient, fitting equipment around ventilators, IV poles and staff, connecting power and wall suction, and staging accessories on whatever surface is available.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: CMU's Operating Room Bot, an autonomous Fetch mobile manipulator with a suction gripper, restocks OR supply items from a rolling cart into marked shelf bins and retrieves items on request, evaluated in a simulated hospital supply room with three item types (boxes, bottles).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level supply restocking of OR shelves. Transfers to the endoscopy-room stocking instance because the objects (boxed and bottled consumables), bin-to-par placement and controlled indoor setting are comparable; it does not cover equipment hookup or sterile-field layout.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: The same system reports 96% success on restocking and 80% on retrieval over dozens of autonomous trials, with failures driven by deformable packaging and segmentation errors.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; the reliability figures bound how far the restocking capability can be credited toward worker-quality room stocking.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L cell)
sources.developer: Sankaranarayanan et al., University of Louisville and collaborators
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A fixtured robot cell with a Staubli TX2-60L arm, vision pipeline and 3D-printed holders autonomously sorts and packs 31 types of surgical instruments into sterile trays for sterile processing, with a human technician performing inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling medical instrument sets into trays in a purpose-built cell. Transfers to the E1 counterfactual for kitting/stocking endoscopy consumables — comparable small medical items, placement precision, fixtured presentation — but the cell is stationary and performs no room-level setup.

sources.developer: Hospital Clinic de Barcelona and collaborators
sources.title: Performance of an Autonomous Sanitary Sterilisation Ultraviolet Machine (ASSUM) on terminal disinfection of surgical theaters and rooms of an intensive-intermediate care unit
sources.claim: An autonomous programmable UV-C disinfection robot was used over ten months for terminal disinfection of six operating theatres and ICU rooms in a tertiary hospital; it disinfects surfaces but performs no equipment setup, linen change or supply layout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: room disinfection during turnover. It covers only the surface-decontamination slice of preparing a procedure room and demonstrates no manipulation of scopes, tubing, linens or supplies.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator fleet is deployed in US hospitals performing autonomous point-to-point delivery of medications, lab samples and supplies, passing 300,000 pharmacy deliveries by May 2025; its manipulation is limited to grasping bins/bags and pressing buttons.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply logistics in real corridors and clinical units. It shows the deployed state of the art in hospital mobile manipulation is transport and simple pick-and-place, not procedure-room preparation.

tasks.label: Maintain inventories of endoscopic equipment and supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital endoscopy suite, daily par-level restocking: between and after cases the tech pulls consumables (biopsy forceps, snares, guidewires, syringes, tubing, lubricant, gauze, PPE) from the unit supply room and stocks procedure-room shelves and cart drawers back to par; mixed package sizes and shapes, rooms and corridors busy with staff, patients and equipment.

Periodic (weekly/monthly) physical inventory of the endoscopy storeroom: count boxes and bin quantities, scan barcodes, check expiration dates, rotate stock front-to-back (FIFO), pull expired or recalled items, and produce the reorder/par-adjustment list for materials management.

Receiving: totes/cartons arrive from central supply or a distributor; tech verifies contents against the packing list, breaks down cartons, and puts items away into labeled bins and shelves in the endoscopy storeroom, updating the inventory record.

Endoscope and capital-equipment inventory: accounting for scopes, valves, water bottles, light sources/processors and specialty accessories; verifying serial numbers and each item's location/status (in reprocessing, in use, out for repair, vendor loaner), checking condition, and reconciling consignment accessory stock with vendor reps.

Ambulatory endoscopy center or small GI clinic: a single tech maintains all inventory in a crowded storage closet with ad hoc stacking, unpacks deliveries, stocks the one or two procedure rooms and carts, counts weekly and places orders with the distributor.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: ORB, a Fetch-based autonomous mobile manipulator, performed OR-supply restocking (picking items from a rolling cart into the correct labeled shelf bin) with 96% success and retrieval with 80% success, in a lab environment simulating a hospital supply room with ArUco/QR-marked bins.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (medical supply restocking/retrieval into labeled bins), but demonstrated only in a marker-instrumented mock supply room with three item types, so it substantiates a purpose-built (E1) setting rather than a live hospital storeroom.

sources.system: BD Rowa Vmax (with EasyLoad automated inputting)
sources.title: BD Rowa Vmax storage and dispensing robot
sources.claim: BD Rowa Vmax is a commercially deployed automated stockroom robot that takes in packages, reads them including expiry dates, stores them, keeps a continuous stock record and picks them back out on demand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated stockroom management of boxed pharmacy packages. Objects (cartons/boxes of similar size and weight to endoscopy consumables), the record-keeping (counts, expiry, FIFO) and the acceptance standard are comparable; the machine is a purpose-built enclosure, i.e. E1.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare: Transforming Pharmacy Storage with BoxPicker
sources.claim: Swisslog BoxPicker is an automated pharmacy storage and retrieval robot installed in hospital pharmacies; it stores medication inventory in high-density automated storage and picks products robotically with barcode verification on every movement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital-pharmacy stock storage, picking and inventory control. Same class of boxed clinical supplies and same accuracy expectations as endoscopy consumable stock, achieved inside a purpose-built machine (E1) sited in a hospital.

sources.title: Apotea Expands Agreement with RightHand Robotics to Deploy RightPick Item Handling System in New Logistics Center
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick piece-picking robots autonomously pick individual medication and health products for order fulfillment at production scale in a pharmacy distribution centre.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking assorted medical/pharmacy items into orders. Assembling a par-level replenishment kit for a procedure room is the same pick-to-order operation with the same object class, when the goods are presented to the machine (E1).

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots autonomously restock refrigerated beverage shelves inside working convenience stores, deployed at hundreds of FamilyMart stores under a service model with remote monitoring for exceptions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing shelf stock to par in a human-facing retail facility. It substantiates only rail-mounted restocking of uniform bottles/cans into one fixed, purpose-built shelf face, not shelf-to-cart replenishment of varied clinical packaging.

sources.title: RAIN RFID-Enabled Robot Automates Grocery Store Inventory
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously traverses store aisles alongside shoppers and scans shelves to track item availability, location and expiration dates, and is commercially deployed across grocery chains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous shelf inventory audit in a structured human facility. It covers the counting/expiry-monitoring half of a storeroom inventory, but it performs no manipulation, so it cannot pull expired stock, rotate stock or replenish bins.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators operate autonomously in more than 25 US ..., having completed over a million item deliveries including 300,000 pharmacy deliveries; the deployed work is point-to-point transport of items and totes, not shelf-level stocking or inventory counting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital materials logistics. It establishes what is actually fielded in real hospital corridors (autonomous transport), and by its limits shows that item-level storeroom stocking and counting are not performed at E2.

tasks.label: Attend in-service training to validate or refresh basic professional skills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Conduct in-service training sessions to disseminate information regarding equipment or instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Endoscopy tech presents a short in-service at a departmental staff huddle or unit meeting in a hospital conference room, walking nurses and techs through the features, indications, and handling precautions of a newly purchased scope model or accessory (e.g., a new video processor, hemostasis clip, or EUS needle) using slides, the manufacturer's IFU, and Q&A. Purpose is conveying information; attendees later use the device themselves.

Tech gives a hands-on show-and-tell in the reprocessing room or procedure room: passes around the new device, points out ports, channels, and connectors while explaining leak testing, channel flushing, or connector attachment steps, and answers colleagues' questions. Any manipulation is illustrative — the informational content is the deliverable, and the same in-service is often given by video or IFU review.

Annual/periodic competency refresher in-service on high-level disinfection and reprocessing protocol changes (e.g., updated AER cycle, new detergent, single-use valve policy), delivered to peers with a sign-in sheet and documentation of attendance for accreditation/Joint Commission records.

Vendor-led in-service on newly installed capital equipment where the lead endoscopy tech co-presents and translates the vendor's instructions into unit-specific workflow, then relays key points to staff on other shifts who could not attend.

tasks.label: Position or transport patients in accordance with instructions from medical personnel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hospital or ambulatory endoscopy unit: tech moves a pre-procedure patient on a stretcher/gurney from the prep bay through unit corridors into the procedure room, managing IV pole, monitor cables, side rails, doors, and other traffic, then parks and locks the stretcher beside the table.

Procedure room: tech and nurse transfer the patient from stretcher to the endoscopy table (slide sheet/board or patient self-scoots) and position them in left lateral decubitus per the endoscopist's instruction — knees flexed, dependent arm placed, bite block side clear, pillow/wedge support, safety strap applied, pressure points checked.

During the procedure: repositioning a sedated patient at the endoscopist's verbal instruction — rolling supine or to the right side with the scope in situ, elevating a hip, and applying/holding targeted abdominal pressure to aid scope advancement while avoiding lines and airway.

Post-procedure: tech moves the sedated, sometimes unresponsive patient on the stretcher out of the room to the recovery bay, aligning and locking the stretcher, then later assists the recovered patient to a wheelchair for discharge.

Escort of an awake, ambulatory patient within the unit — wheelchair or walking assist from waiting area to prep bay, to the restroom for bowel-prep completion, or from recovery to the exit — following nurse instruction on mobility restrictions.

sources.title: Haneda International Airport Implements WHILL Autonomous Mobility Service - Inside Unmanned Systems
sources.claim: WHILL's Autonomous Drive System is in commercial service at Haneda International Airport, self-driving passengers with reduced mobility to their gate without a human pusher, then returning on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously conveying a seated person along a route inside a controlled facility. Transfers to escorting/transporting a patient within a clinic because the payload (a person on wheels), speeds, and human-populated indoor route are comparable.

sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. with Unifi Aviation / Wayne County Airport Authority
sources.title: Unifi Aviation Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: Autonomous wheelchair service using WHILL chairs launched for airline customers at Detroit Metropolitan Airport in 2025, and at Rome Fiumicino and Schiphol, showing repeat commercial deployment of person-carrying autonomous mobility in structured facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (person transport inside an institution-controlled facility); shows durability beyond a one-off trial.

sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. with Keio University Hospital
sources.title: Keio University Hospital Begins Technical Trial of WHILL Autonomous Driving Technology to Improve Patient Mobility
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous drive system was trialed inside a hospital, mapping the building and driving patients with limited mobility to designated locations to reduce staff escort workload.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the escort-within-a-clinical-facility case: same objects (a seated patient), same corridor environment, same purpose (moving a patient to a designated point).

sources.title: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robot showcased at RIA
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots move heavy wheeled loads through hospital corridors and elevators in scores of US hospitals with no human escort.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous towing/navigation of heavy wheeled carts (up to ~1,000 lb) along mapped hospital routes. Supports the navigation-and-towing half of stretcher transport; it does not cover patient handling or clinical monitoring.

sources.developer: Rovex Technologies (pilot at BayCare Morton Plant Hospital)
sources.title: Rovex and Sphaira pioneer autonomous patient transport - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced hospital stretcher-towing robot pilot in the US is explicitly not yet moving patients — early testing covers navigation only — so autonomous gurney transport of real patients is not demonstrated in an as-found endoscopy unit.

sources.date: 2019-04 (IFU rev E); in clinical use through 2024
sources.title: INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE RotoProne Therapy System (Arjo)
sources.claim: The RotoProne Therapy System is a commercial hospital bed that mechanically moves an immobile, secured patient from supine to prone and holds clinician-programmed lateral rotation angles, with tube management, in ICU rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine placement of a sedated patient's whole body into a prescribed non-supine posture and holding it. Same object (an adult patient), same instruction-driven purpose, and lower precision demand than endoscopy table positioning; the securing step is what an E1 fixture would supply.

sources.title: RotoProne® Therapy System for prone bed positioning | Arjo
sources.claim: Arjo states the RotoProne turns and repositions patients at the touch of a ... and lets caregivers program prescribed turn angles and pause times, i.e. the machine executes the positioning rather than a person manually handling the patient.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: prescribed patient positioning carried out by the machine on clinician instruction.

sources.system: 6-DOF robotic patient positioning couches / robotic-arm patient positioners
sources.date: 2010-05-13 (review; technology in routine clinical use since)
sources.title: Patient positioning in the proton radiotherapy era (J Exp Clin Cancer Res, PMC)
sources.claim: In radiotherapy, patients are routinely placed in prescribed positions by automatic 6-degree-of-freedom couches and, in fixed-beam rooms, by robotic-arm patient positioners inside purpose-built treatment vaults.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a patient, already placed and immobilized, to a commanded body position under machine control in a room built around the machine. Same object and far tighter precision than endoscopy positioning requires.

sources.developer: Able Innovations (deployed at Lahey Hospital & Medical Center and Canadian hospitals)
sources.title: Able Innovations Deploys Robotic Patient Delivery Platform in the U.S.
sources.claim: Able Innovations' ALTA Platform is a deployed robotic patient-handling device that moves patients between stretchers, beds and procedure-suite tables, but it requires a staff operator to drive and command it throughout.
sources.transferJustification: Lateral transfer of a patient onto a procedure table — the first half of the positioning instance — but operator-driven, so it is treated as teleoperated and does not by itself support a positive judgment.
