tasks.label: Maintain order, discipline, and security within assigned areas in accordance with relevant rules, regulations, policies, and laws.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine supervisory security rounds in a jail/prison housing unit or pod during a shift: the sergeant/lieutenant walks the tier, physically shakes doors and inspects locks, bars, windows and vents for tampering, verifies formal inmate counts, reads the mood of the unit and verbally redirects inmates who are out of place or escalating, checks that officers are at post and performing required checks, and signs logs.

Taking charge of a disturbance or emergency: an inmate fight, assault on staff, self-harm attempt, medical emergency, refusal to lock down, or a planned cell extraction. The supervisor directs responding officers, physically separates and restrains resisting inmates, applies handcuffs/leg irons, authorizes or deploys OC spray, and escorts the inmate to segregation or medical, all under contested, fast-moving conditions.

Contraband and security searches: supervising and taking part in cell shakedowns and unit-wide searches — turning mattresses and bedding, emptying lockers and property bins, probing plumbing chases, light fixtures and recreation-yard ground — plus pat searches of inmates returning from visits or work details; seizing, bagging and documenting contraband.

Supervising controlled movement and access: staging and releasing mass movements to chow, recreation, work details, medical and court; escorting individual inmates through sally ports; overseeing control-room door and gate operation; key, tool and chemical-agent accountability; ID-checking staff, visitors and contractors; and re-counting at each movement.

Enforcing discipline for a rule violation: investigating the incident, interviewing inmate and staff witnesses, reviewing and approving the disciplinary report for accuracy and policy compliance, conducting an informal hearing or imposing sanctions, and carrying out the sanction — physically relocating the inmate to restrictive housing, inventorying and securing property, and adjusting privileges.

sources.title: A look at a pilot program in Georgia that uses 'jailbots' to track inmates : NPR
sources.claim: DEKA 'Sentry' robots ('jailbots') were piloted for 90 days at the Cobb County (GA) Adult Detention Center, patrolling dormitories, hallways and the perimeter. They monitor with cameras, night vision and heat detection and are explicitly not intended to make contact with inmates; jail staff supervise them remotely and react to what they see.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: this is a robot operating inside a US jail on order/security-maintenance duties, so it bounds what corrections robots actually do (surveillance and alerting) versus the supervisor's full task.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development Corporation / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office Unveils Next-Gen Security with DEKA's Sentry Robots
sources.claim: The Cobb County Sheriff's Office describes the Sentry jailbots as an assistive tool for deputies that conducts patrols and documents incidents, i.e., a force multiplier rather than a replacement for officer or supervisor duties.
sources.transferJustification: Primary source from the deploying agency establishing the scope of the robot's role in a correctional facility: patrol and incident documentation only.

sources.title: Knightscope K5 Upgrade Expands Market Reach
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots are commercially deployed for patrol and monitoring in structured human facilities such as schools, hospitals, corporate campuses, casinos and transportation hubs; their function is sensing and alerting, not physical intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol in an institution-controlled facility (E2). It substantiates only the observation/deterrence sub-step of maintaining security, not physical order maintenance, searching, or supervision of staff.

sources.title: Cobalt Robotics | SecurityInfoWatch
sources.claim: Cobalt Robotics indoor security robots patrol autonomously in corporate, financial and manufacturing facilities, building models of 'normal' and flagging ..., with remote human specialists handling response through the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor patrol and anomaly detection in a structured facility. Shows the state of the art for machine 'security presence' is detect-and-escalate, with humans performing any physical response.

sources.system: CSD Patrol Robot / Robotic Patrol Dog (smart prison)
sources.title: news.gov.hk - CE launches HK's first smart prison
sources.claim: Hong Kong's Correctional Services Department launched a Patrol Robot at its first 'smart prison' (Tai Tam Gap Correctional Institution) alongside a robotic patrol dog under development; the smart-prison package is surveillance and monitoring technology (video analytics, wristbands, kiosks), not robotic physical control of inmates.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant setting (a correctional institution), but autonomy is not established and the robot's role is patrol/monitoring; it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.developer: Asian Forum for Corrections / Korean Ministry of Justice
sources.title: The Carceral Automaton: Digital Prisons and Technologies of Detention
sources.claim: Academic review of prison technology records that the South Korean prison guard robot trial involved robots patrolling while supervised by a remote ..., and that corrections technology otherwise consists of CCTV, facial recognition, video analytics and tracking wristbands — no robot performing physical order maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant: a corrections patrol robot. Its role is remote-supervised patrol, which covers only observation, not the supervisor's physical control, search, or disciplinary duties.

sources.title: How Police Robots Work | HowStuffWorks
sources.claim: Police and corrections robots used around people, including any that could deliver force, are remote-controlled devices operated by officers rather than autonomous systems; no autonomous robot performs restraint or use of force.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical intervention against a resisting person by law-enforcement robots. Establishes that such systems are teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive judgment on incident response or restraint.

tasks.label: Maintain knowledge of, comply with, and enforce all institutional policies, rules, procedures, and regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Respond to emergencies, such as escapes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inmate-on-inmate assault or group fight in a housing unit, dayroom or chow hall: supervisor runs to the scene with responding officers, gives verbal orders, deploys OC spray or physically separates combatants, takes resisting inmates to the ground, applies handcuffs/leg irons, escorts them to segregation and medical, secures the area and witnesses, and re-establishes control of the unit.

Medical or mental-health emergency in a cell or dorm: overdose, seizure, fall, or attempted hanging. Supervisor opens the cell, cuts down the ligature, moves the person to the floor, starts CPR/first aid or administers naloxone, clears other inmates back, opens gates and directs EMS to the cell, and stays until medical assumes care.

Fire, alarm activation, or facility-wide disturbance/disorder: supervisor initiates lockdown, directs officers to secure doors and control points, uses extinguishers or evacuates a smoke-filled tier, moves inmates to a secure area, deploys chemical agents or the emergency response team, and restores order and accountability.

Escape, attempted escape, breach of a fence/roof, or an unresolved count discrepancy: supervisor orders emergency count and lockdown, launches search teams through cells, ceilings, tunnels, vehicles and grounds, checks the perimeter and gates, notifies outside agencies, and directs apprehension and return of the inmate.

Barricaded, self-harming or non-compliant inmate requiring a planned cell extraction or forced move: supervisor briefs and leads the five-person team, videotapes, deploys chemical agents, breaches the cell, controls limbs behind a shield, applies restraints, and moves the inmate to a holding or medical cell.

Emergency outside the secure perimeter: escape or medical crisis on an outside work detail, during transport, at a courthouse, or during a hospital watch; supervisor responds on public roads, hospital grounds or open land, secures the inmate, and coordinates pursuit or recovery with local police.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development Corp. / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office enhances security at the Adult Detention Center with cutting-edge DEKA Sentry Robots
sources.claim: The first US jail robot deployment (DEKA Sentry at Cobb County Adult Detention Center) is limited to autonomous perimeter patrol, dormitory rounds, surveillance and two-way audio; complex situations are handed to a human live operator, and the robots assist personnel rather than physically intervene in incidents.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot to this task: it works in the same environment (jail housing units and perimeter) during the same events, but its role is surveillance and alerting, establishing that no deployed correctional robot performs the physical emergency response itself.

sources.title: Ga. sheriff's office piloting robot patrol program at jail to enhance security
sources.claim: The 2025 continuation of the same program confirms the robots' scope remains perimeter patrols and security rounds ... as an added layer of monitoring, not incident intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Same facility type and same class of events (violence, medical emergencies, escapes) as this task; shows the deployed capability stops at detection and reporting for human responders.

sources.title: A $100,000 robot dog is becoming standard in policing — and raising ethical alarms
sources.claim: The tactical robot most widely fielded by US law enforcement for standoffs, hostage situations and hazmat calls is remotely controlled by an ...; it does not autonomously resolve an incident or make physical contact to restrain a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tactical police response to violent and barricade incidents, the closest analogue to cell extractions and escape pursuits. Capability does not transfer, because the robot is teleoperated and performs reconnaissance and communication relay, not restraint or rescue.

sources.title: Security Robots vs. Human Guards – Which is more effective
sources.claim: Industry review of commercially deployed autonomous security robots states they observe, record and alert but cannot physically apprehend a person, which is the core physical act in most of these emergency responses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guard-force response to on-site incidents in institutional facilities. It bounds what deployed autonomous ground robots can physically do, which is exactly what this task requires.

sources.system: FlytBase autonomous drone security (drone-in-a-box) for corrections
sources.title: Drones for Corrections & Detention | FlytBase
sources.claim: Autonomous drone-in-a-box systems marketed to corrections provide continuous perimeter monitoring and alarm verification; the advertised 'escape response' is aerial observation and evidence capture that reduces staff dispatch, not lockdown, facility search, or apprehension.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the escape-response instance: it is the most capable autonomous system operating over prison grounds, and it performs only surveillance, so the whole instance is not completed.

tasks.label: Supervise and direct the work of correctional officers to ensure the safe custody, discipline, and welfare of inmates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Supervise or perform searches of inmates or their quarters to locate contraband items.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shakedown of a two-person cell in a prison housing unit: the supervisor (with an officer) strips bedding and probes mattress seams, empties property bins and lockers, checks books, clothing, shoes, hygiene items, vents, light fixtures, bunk welds, plumbing chase and window frames for weapons, cell phones, tobacco and drugs; distinguishes authorized property from contraband, seizes and bags items, leaves the cell habitable and writes a search/seizure report.

Person searches at movement points: pat-down/frisk searches of inmates leaving work details, dining, visitation or court, including running hands over clothing, checking waistbands, shoes, hair and mouth, and supervising strip searches in a designated area; subjects are sometimes uncooperative or actively concealing items.

Supervising a planned team shakedown of a dorm or unit: briefing and assigning officers and K9, staging and controlling inmates, timing and sequencing the search, monitoring officer conduct and thoroughness, spot-checking areas already searched, taking custody of seized contraband, and reviewing incident/evidence paperwork.

Searches of common and outdoor areas controlled by the institution: dayrooms, showers, recreation yards and equipment, industry shops and kitchens (tool and sharps control), plus vehicles and carts passing through the sallyport; irregular surfaces, hidden voids, weather and inmate presence.

Intake/booking searches at a county jail: searching newly arrested persons and their clothing and property, inventorying valuables, running the arrestee through the body scanner and metal detector, and handling occasional combative or intoxicated subjects.

Screening operations: overseeing body-scanner passes and image review for inmates returning from court or visits, X-ray screening of incoming mail, packages and personal property, drug trace swabbing, and resolving every alarm with a hands-on search and recovery of the item.

sources.developer: DEKA Research & Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office Unveils Next-Gen Security with DEKA's Sentry Robots
sources.claim: The most advanced robots actually deployed inside a US correctional facility (DEKA Sentry 'jailbots' at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center) conduct patrols and surveillance with cameras, night vision, heat detection ...; they have no manipulators and perform no searching of cells, property or persons.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed corrections robot; cited to show that deployed correctional robotics is patrol/observation only, with no manipulation or search capability, so it cannot substantiate completion of a search task.

sources.system: Soter SR / CLEARPASS AI-assisted transmission X-ray body scanners
sources.developer: OD Security / LINEV Systems (deployed by Jackson County Detention Center and Oklahoma DOC)
sources.title: ODOC deploys full-body scanners to strengthen fight against contraband
sources.claim: Contraband-detection technology deployed in jails and prisons consists of fixed X-ray body scanners and mail/parcel X-ray units whose AI merely highlights anomalies for staff; a human operator interprets images and must still perform the hands-on search and recovery, so the machine does not complete a search.
sources.transferJustification: Screening of inmates and property is the technological substitute closest to this task; cited to show the deployed systems are operator-dependent imaging aids, not robotic systems that locate and recover contraband on their own.

sources.system: Survey of state-of-the-art autonomous robots (Physical Intelligence, Figure, 1X and others)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: A 2026 systematic assessment of autonomous robot capabilities finds that even the most advanced lived-space manipulation task, tidying a bedroom (picking up loose items and placing them away), is only 'validated in lab', with transfer to new environments largely undemonstrated; nothing approaching a concealed-contraband search of a room or a person has been shown.
sources.transferJustification: Bedroom tidying is the nearest demonstrated task to searching living quarters (navigating a lived-in room, handling bedding, clothing and loose personal items); it is only lab-validated and involves no detection of concealed items, no seam/void probing and no judgment about contraband, so capability does not carry over.

tasks.label: Monitor behavior of subordinates to ensure alert, courteous, and professional behavior toward inmates, parolees, fellow employees, visitors, and the public.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Restrain, secure, or control offenders, using chemical agents, firearms, or other weapons of force as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Housing unit or corridor of a jail/prison: a supervising sergeant responds to an inmate who refuses orders and physically resists; the supervisor gives commands, then with officers takes the inmate to the floor, controls limbs, applies handcuffs, stands the inmate up and escorts him to segregation, documenting the force used. Resistance is active and unpredictable; injury to staff and inmate must be minimized.

Dayroom, chow hall, or recreation yard: an inmate-on-inmate fight or assault breaks out among two or more combatants. The supervisor directs responding officers, issues verbal orders, deploys OC spray or a pepperball/less-lethal launcher as needed, separates and prones out combatants, applies restraints, and secures the area and any weapons.

Cell front in a segregation unit: an inmate refuses to cuff up, has covered the window or barricaded the door, or is destroying property. The supervisor attempts negotiation, authorizes and deploys chemical agents through the food port or vent, then leads a five-person cell-extraction team with shield to enter, control, and restrain the inmate, with camera documentation and post-force decontamination/medical check.

Booking/intake area or medical unit: a combative, intoxicated, or self-harming inmate must be placed in mechanical restraints — restraint chair, leg irons, waist chain, or soft restraints — with the supervisor authorizing, directing limb control, checking restraint tightness and circulation, and conducting periodic welfare checks until release from restraints.

Armed post, sallyport, or perimeter response: the supervisor draws and carries a firearm or less-lethal launcher for a high-risk escort, vehicle sallyport movement, perimeter breach, or major disturbance; secures and controls offenders at gunpoint, applies restraints for transport, and clears/secures weapons per policy.

sources.title: Roaming Robots in Public? Knightscope Moves with Precision and Purpose
sources.claim: Knightscope's autonomous security robots are commercially deployed for autonomous patrol in institutional facilities, but the developer states explicitly that they carry no weapons and do not physically touch or apprehend people — i.e., no physical restraint capability.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue to correctional security work: autonomous patrol inside institutionally controlled facilities. It bounds the state of the art — the deployed autonomous security platform explicitly excludes weapons use and physical apprehension, the core of this task.

sources.system: Security robots (sector survey of 602 tracked robots)
sources.title: Security Robots 2026: Autonomous Patrol & Surveillance Systems Guide
sources.claim: A 2026 industry survey of deployed security robots concludes that physical intervention and incident response remain human work, with robots limited to patrol and detection.
sources.transferJustification: Security patrol/response is the nearest commercial robotic analogue to correctional officer force application; the survey states the physical-intervention portion is not performed by robots.

sources.title: Logon Technology's Spherical RT-G Robot Helps Police Patrol the Streets of Wenzhou
sources.claim: The RT-G spherical police robot, deployed alongside police in Wenzhou, China and fitted with net guns and tear gas dispensers, is operated remotely by a human rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest system that applies less-lethal force to non-compliant people (net gun, tear gas). It is teleoperated, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous restraint or chemical-agent deployment.

sources.developer: Asian Forum of Corrections / Korea Ministry of Justice (Kyonggi University consortium)
sources.title: South Korea's mood-sensing robotic prison guards
sources.claim: Prison guard robots trialled in a South Korean correctional facility patrol corridors and detect abnormal behavior, then summon human officers; they perform no restraint or force application.
sources.transferJustification: This is the only robot actually trialled inside a correctional housing environment. Its scope is monitoring and alerting; it explicitly hands off to humans for intervention, showing restraint/force is outside demonstrated robotic capability in this exact setting.

sources.system: DOGO with Less Lethal Weapon (LLW) payload
sources.title: This robot will pepper spray targets
sources.claim: The DOGO tactical robot carries a remote-controlled pepper spray and dazzling light as less-lethal payloads for police and special forces; the payloads are commanded by a remote human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the 'chemical agents' element of the task, but the deployment is remote-controlled, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of chemical-agent use on a non-compliant offender.

tasks.label: Carry injured offenders or employees to safety and provide emergency first aid when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fight or assault in a housing unit/dayroom: supervisor responds to an inmate with lacerations, a broken nose or a head injury, secures the scene, applies direct pressure and gauze, and helps or drags the injured person out of the immediate area to a sally port or medical holding area to await facility medical staff.

Unresponsive inmate found in a cell (suspected opioid overdose): supervisor enters, checks responsiveness and breathing, administers intranasal naloxone, delivers rescue breaths/CPR, moves the person off the bunk or out of the confined cell into the tier or corridor where medical staff and a gurney can reach them.

Sudden medical collapse of an officer or inmate in a common area (cardiac arrest, seizure, diabetic emergency, heat illness) during chow, count or program movement: supervisor initiates CPR, applies an AED, protects/repositions the person, and moves them clear of hazards until EMS arrives.

Self-harm/hanging attempt in a cell: supervisor and officers cut the ligature, support and lower the inmate's body to the floor, control bleeding from cutting wounds, and begin CPR or airway support while the inmate is moved out of the cell.

Disturbance, fire or chemical-agent incident: an injured officer or inmate must be carried or dragged out of a smoke-filled, debris-strewn or hostile area (wet floors, broken fixtures, OC spray residue, active crowd) to a secured area, then given first aid there.

Injury on an outdoor work detail, recreation yard, farm or off-site road crew: an inmate falls from height, is struck by equipment or suffers heat stroke; supervisor carries or assists them to shade or a transport vehicle over uneven ground and provides first aid until transport arrives.

sources.developer: Ukrainian UGV manufacturers / National Guard 13th Khartiia and 92nd Assault Brigades
sources.title: Ground robots are transforming battle-casualty evacuation in Ukraine | The Strategist
sources.claim: The closest deployed robotic casualty evacuation is Ukrainian ground robots (e.g., TERMIT, Tarhan) that tow or carry wounded soldiers; they are radio/satellite remote-controlled, loaded by humans, and do not lift a casualty or provide first aid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving an injured human out of a dangerous area. It is the nearest real-world analogue to 'carry injured offenders to safety', and it shows the capability exists only under continuous remote control with human loading.

sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch | RIKEN
sources.claim: Research robots that physically lift a human, such as RIKEN's ROBEAR, remain experimental bed-to-wheelchair transfer machines guided by a caregiver; none had been deployed in care facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and transferring a human body. Even in the highly structured case of a cooperative patient on a bed, the capability is experimental and caregiver-guided, so it cannot transfer to lifting an unresponsive person from a cell floor.

sources.title: Eldercare robot helps people sit and stand, and catches them if they fall
sources.claim: MIT's E-BAR robot can lift a person from the floor and support their full body weight, but the prototype is driven by a human operator with remote control; autonomy is future work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: raising a fallen human from the floor in a home/lab setting. Directly relevant to the lifting element of this task; it shows the state of the art is teleoperated and confined to cooperative users.

sources.system: DARPA MASH / autonomous 'smart tourniquet' medic robots (program solicitation)
sources.title: DARPA launches search for robot medics to treat battlefield casualties
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic first aid (hemorrhage control, tourniquet application) is a DARPA research goal solicited in 2025-2026, indicating no such fielded system exists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency hemorrhage control. Cited as state-of-the-art context: as of 2026 autonomous application of first aid to a human casualty is still being solicited as research, not demonstrated.

sources.title: US Army seeks robots for frontline resupply and casualty evacuation
sources.claim: The U.S. Army in April 2026 was still soliciting an unmanned ground vehicle able to move casualties without further harm, showing autonomous casualty carriage is not yet a fielded capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting injured people to safety. A 2026 requirements notice, not a demonstration, confirming that autonomous casualty movement remains an unmet requirement.

sources.developer: Asian Forum of Corrections / Korea (Pohang prison trial)
sources.title: Robot guards being tested in South Korea
sources.claim: Robots trialled inside correctional facilities are autonomous patrol/monitoring platforms that alert human officers to abnormal behaviour; they perform no physical intervention, lifting, or medical aid.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (a correctional facility). Establishes that robots operating in this setting are limited to surveillance and communication, with humans performing all physical emergency response.

tasks.label: Complete administrative paperwork or supervise the preparation or maintenance of records, forms, or reports.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Supervise activities, such as searches, shakedowns, riot control, or institutional tours.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled shakedown of a prison housing unit: the sergeant briefs and assigns search teams, has inmates secured and pat-searched out of their cells, personally searches cells, mattresses, lockers and property for weapons, phones and drugs, corrects officers' search technique, takes custody of and bags contraband, and signs off on the search and incident reports. Cluttered cells, resistant inmates, concealment inside fixtures.

Overseeing routine daily searches inside the secure perimeter: pat-downs at movement checkpoints, metal detector / body-scanner stations, visitor and employee entry screening, cell-phone sweeps with handheld detectors. Supervisor watches officers, resolves alarms and refusals, authorizes strip searches, decides what is confiscated, and intervenes physically when a search is resisted.

Commanding a response to a disturbance, group fight, or planned cell extraction: assembling and positioning the response team, ordering and personally applying force options (OC spray, shields, restraints), physically controlling and escorting resistive inmates, coordinating with the control room and medical, restoring order and completing use-of-force documentation. Fast-moving, violent, unpredictable.

Conducting and supervising an institutional tour: escorting legislators, students, job candidates, contractors, or families through the secure perimeter; briefing them on rules, operating and controlling doors and sally ports, keeping the group counted and physically separated from inmates, adapting or aborting the route when a count or incident occurs.

Supervising exterior searches on institution grounds: yard and recreation-area searches, fence-line sweeps for drone drops and throw-overs, vehicle and delivery searches at the vehicle sally port, and work-detail/industry-shop tool and area searches. Outdoor, weather-exposed, uneven ground, inmates present.

County jail booking/intake: supervising searches of newly arrested persons (pat and strip searches, property inventory), searching holding cells and transport vehicles, and physically managing intoxicated or combative arrestees while the search is completed.

sources.developer: DEKA Research & Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Meet the nearly 6-foot tall robots patrolling a Ga. jail
sources.claim: The only robots actually working inside a US jail housing environment are patrol/surveillance platforms: DEKA Sentry robots piloted at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center do perimeter patrols and security rounds ... selected dormitories with cameras, night vision and ..., with a live operator taking control for complex tasks. They have no manipulators and perform no searches, no use of force, and no supervision of officers.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic deployment to this task's setting (a jail housing unit). Cited to show in-facility robots are limited to camera rounds under operator takeover; searches, shakedowns and force remain human, so it does not substantiate completion of any instance.

sources.system: Viken Nighthawk / Broadwing / Foxhound contraband detection tools (human-carried, non-robotic)
sources.developer: Viken Detection / Georgia Department of Corrections
sources.title: Case study: How technology-driven contraband detection is transforming the Ga. Department of Corrections
sources.claim: State-of-the-art contraband shakedowns in a large state prison system remain manual searches by human teams aided by handheld imagers and analyzers (Viken Nighthawk, Broadwing, Foxhound); the labor-intensive, physically demanding hands-on search of housing units has not been automated.
sources.transferJustification: Directly describes the shakedown work supervised in this task; shows current technology is hand-held sensing used by human search teams, not robots that search cells and inmate property.

sources.system: Autonomous drone platform at Red Rock Correctional Center
sources.developer: Oklahoma Department of Corrections with drone/AI vendors
sources.title: ODOC takes contraband fight airborne with new drone technology
sources.claim: Correctional agencies' aerial robotics are surveillance-only: Oklahoma DOC's Red Rock facility deploys an autonomous drone platform for continuous perimeter and yard observation, with correctional officers trained as certified pilots overseeing yard activity. The drones observe and alert; they do not conduct or supervise searches.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the outdoor yard/perimeter search-supervision instance; establishes robotic capability there is aerial observation feeding human responders, not autonomous conduct or supervision of a search.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (police units, e.g., MSP 'Roscoe', LAPD)
sources.title: How police departments are putting robot dogs to work
sources.claim: Robots used by US law enforcement in force and high-risk search situations (Boston Dynamics Spot, e.g., Massachusetts State Police 'Roscoe', LAPD Spot) are remotely operated reconnaissance platforms sent in ahead of officers; they assess and deter but do not autonomously control subjects or direct a team.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to supervising a disturbance or cell extraction; shows such robots are teleoperated scouts, which under the rules cannot support a positive judgment for commanding and executing a use-of-force response.

sources.system: Agentic museum guide robot (autonomous navigation and visitor interaction)
sources.developer: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (Garello et al.)
sources.title: Next-Gen Museum Guides: Autonomous Navigation and Visitor Interaction with an Agentic Robot
sources.claim: Autonomous tour-guide robots exist and can navigate and narrate a route for visitors, but demonstrations are in museums and similar public venues and the authors report continuing limitations in complex real-world deployment; none performs the access control, head count, and inmate-separation duties of a correctional escort.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is guided touring of an institution. It does not transfer to a prison tour: the correctional supervisor controls sally ports, keeps visitors counted and separated from inmates, and aborts on a count or incident, none of which the museum robot performs.

tasks.label: Conduct roll calls of correctional officers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Instruct employees or provide on-the-job training.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Resolve problems between inmates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine interpersonal dispute in a housing unit or dorm: a sergeant/corporal is called by a line officer about cellmates or dayroom neighbors arguing over TV/phone time, cleanliness, borrowed property or a small commissary debt. The supervisor walks the unit, separates and interviews each inmate, de-escalates verbally, negotiates an agreement or orders a bunk swap, and logs the outcome. Noisy, crowded, other inmates watching.

Active physical altercation: a fight or assault between two or more inmates in a dayroom, cell, chow hall or corridor. The supervisor responds, gives verbal commands, physically separates or takes down the combatants with responding officers, applies handcuffs, escorts the inmates to medical and to segregation, and then works out the underlying dispute. Resisting, sometimes injured, sometimes armed with improvised weapons.

Threat/keep-separate management: an inmate reports pressure, extortion or a gang conflict, or intelligence indicates a planned assault. The supervisor interviews the parties and informants, decides on protective housing, physically moves the inmate and his property boxes to another cell or unit, escorts him through controlled corridors and sally ports, and updates separation orders with classification.

Investigation and adjudication of an inmate-on-inmate incident after the fact (theft from a cell, bullying, gambling debt, sexual harassment/PREA allegation): interviewing both parties and witnesses, reviewing camera footage, taking written statements, deciding on informal resolution versus a disciplinary report, and writing the incident report and referral.

Group-level tension or disturbance: racial/gang factions squaring off in a dayroom or on the recreation yard, a group refusing to lock down, or a multi-inmate melee. The supervisor orders the unit secured, directs officers and the response team, may authorize or deploy chemical agents/less-lethal munitions, restores order, then identifies principals and resolves or contains the underlying conflict.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Georgia jail welcomes state-of-the-art robots to security team
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic system actually deployed in a US jail (DEKA Sentry 'Jail Bots' at the Cobb County, GA jail) performs perimeter patrols, security rounds in dorms, surveillance and communications, notifying deputies of issues; a live operator drives it for complex tasks and the sheriff states it does not replace human officers.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing robotic capability inside the exact setting (jail housing dorms and corridors). It substantiates patrol and alerting only, not interviewing, mediating, restraining or escorting inmates, so it cannot complete this task.

sources.developer: Asian Forum for Corrections / Kyonggi University
sources.title: South Korea's 'humane and friendly' robotic prison guards
sources.claim: The South Korean 'Robo-Guard' prison robots trialled at Pohang autonomously patrol corridors and monitor cells for abnormal behaviour such as fights, but their function is to summon human officers rather than to intervene in or resolve inmate conflicts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous monitoring of inmate conflict in a prison housing unit. It shows detection transfers, but the physical and interpersonal resolution step is explicitly left to human guards.

sources.system: SMP Robotics S5.3 security patrol robot
sources.title: Security robots outdoor patrolling, video & thermal surveillance for security service companies
sources.claim: Commercially sold autonomous security patrol robots detect intrusions and abnormal events on their own, but the vendor states that a human guard is still required for any physical counteraction against a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol in institution-controlled premises. Establishes that state-of-the-art commercial security robots do not physically engage, separate or restrain non-compliant people, which the fight-response instances require.

sources.title: Exploring Socially Assistive Peer Mediation Robots for Teaching Conflict Resolution to Elementary School Students
sources.claim: Robot mediation of interpersonal conflict between people remains exploratory laboratory research (role-play practice of peer mediation with elementary school students), not a deployed capability at worker quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted mediation of a dispute between two people. It is an exploratory study with children practising role-play, so it does not substantiate authoritative resolution of adult inmate disputes in a correctional facility.

tasks.label: Examine incoming or outgoing mail to ensure conformance with regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk incoming general correspondence at a jail/prison mailroom: trays of sealed letters, greeting cards, drawings and photos. The officer/supervisor opens each envelope, removes and unfolds contents, inspects paper and enclosures for contraband (stains, strips, drug-soaked or altered paper), checks sender/return address and content against facility rules, then scans or forwards approved items and documents rejections.

Outgoing inmate mail deposited unsealed (or opened for random inspection): contents are removed and reviewed for escape plans, threats, gang codes, third-party mailing and enclosed contraband; cleared mail is re-enveloped, sealed, metered/logged and dispatched to the post office; disallowed pieces are held and reported.

Incoming publications and packages (books, magazines, approved-vendor parcels): verify the sender is an approved vendor and the item is permitted, cut open the parcel, fan book pages, check bindings, spines and covers for concealed contraband, remove hard covers or staples, and either forward, hold in property, or return to sender.

Legal/privileged mail: identify properly marked attorney, court or official mail, verify the sender against records, open it in the presence of the addressed inmate (housing unit or mailroom window), inspect for contraband without reading content, log the piece in the legal-mail register and obtain the inmate's signature.

Flagged or suspicious mail escalated to the supervisor: re-inspect the item, run a presumptive narcotics field test or T-ray/X-ray screen, photograph and bag the item as evidence, complete chain-of-custody and incident paperwork, notify investigators, and issue the rejection notice to inmate and sender.

sources.title: Eagle™ Remittance Processor | Fast & Secure Payment Processor
sources.claim: The OPEX Eagle is a commercial mail-processing machine that runs the whole inbound-envelope chain automatically inside an enclosed paper path: it feeds unopened envelopes, opens them, images contents and sorts them into bins by configured business rules at up to 16,000 envelopes/hour with a single operator loading and monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-volume inbound mail opening and rule-based sorting in a lockbox mailroom. Same objects (sealed letter envelopes and their paper contents) and same physical steps (feed, open, extract, image, decide, pocket) that examining mail for conformance requires.

sources.system: OPEX Eagle extractor module / automatic feeder
sources.title: Eagle™ Remittance Processor | Fast & Secure Payment Processor
sources.claim: The Eagle performs machine extraction of envelope contents and physically screens envelopes before opening: its automatic feeder out-sorts envelopes that are too thick ..., and its extractor module qualifies each envelope before automated extraction, routing non-conforming pieces aside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated de-enveloping in remittance processing. Shows machine extraction of paper contents from sealed envelopes and automatic out-sorting of anomalous (thick or metal-bearing) envelopes, the physical core of mail inspection.

sources.system: Agilis / Agilis Falcon ballot sorting system
sources.title: Press Releases - Runbeck Election Services
sources.claim: The Runbeck Agilis / Agilis Falcon sorter examines inbound mail envelopes against legal requirements automatically - reading barcodes, capturing signature images, checking dates and envelope weight/thickness to verify correct contents - and sorts them into accept/exception pockets in county election offices, with humans only adjudicating flagged pieces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: examining incoming mail for conformance with regulations (signature, deadline, correct enclosures) and sorting accepted versus rejected. Identical object class (letter mail) and identical decision structure to correctional mail screening.

sources.system: Agilis Election Mail Sorting & Processing System
sources.title: Agilis - Runbeck Election Services
sources.claim: Agilis lines can be configured with an in-line envelope opener, so inbound envelopes are inspected, sorted and opened within the same automated machine line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inbound mail conformance processing. Demonstrates opening integrated into an automated inspection/sorting line, the same physical operation a mailroom officer performs on inmate correspondence.

sources.system: Smiths Detection X-ray screening systems with iCMORE automatic detection
sources.title: iCMORE | Smiths Detection
sources.claim: Conveyor-fed X-ray screening systems running iCMORE automatically detect concealed contraband (narcotics, weapons, cigarettes, batteries) in parcels and cargo, supporting alarm-only viewing workflows rather than operator primary detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated contraband screening of enclosed items on a machine line. Covers the contraband-detection element of mail examination for the same classes of prohibited objects on comparable parcel/envelope-scale items.

sources.system: Relia-Vote (BlueCrest inserters with content verification and sortation)
sources.title: BlueCrest | Mail Ballots & Vote-By-Mail Solutions with Relia-Vote
sources.claim: BlueCrest's Relia-Vote mail-ballot line combines automated inserters with inline envelope printing, machine content verification and sortation - commercial machinery that assembles documents into addressed, sealed envelopes and verifies the correct contents went into each envelope.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated enveloping/sealing with machine verification of contents. Supplies the re-enveloping and dispatch step needed after outgoing inmate mail is opened and inspected, on the same class of paper documents.

sources.title: OPEX Model 72 | Automated Envelope Opening Systems
sources.claim: Industry-standard mailroom openers still leave content extraction to a person: the OPEX Model 72 opens the envelope and presents it, but an operator removes the contents; the machine only verifies the envelope is empty afterwards.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (opening and de-enveloping mail in a mailroom). Shows the limit of current automation on mixed folded mail: the machine opens, a person extracts and inspects.

sources.system: Smart Communications MailGuard off-site mail processing (with RaySecur MailSecur in-facility screening)
sources.title: Inmate Mail Rules and Guidelines | Department of Corrections | Commonwealth of Pennsylvania
sources.claim: Prison mail screening as actually deployed is performed by human staff: state DOCs route general correspondence to a vendor whose staff open, scan and upload the mail, and in-facility tools such as RaySecur MailSecur present a live 3D image an officer must interpret.
sources.transferJustification: Same task. Documents that even in dedicated high-volume inmate-mail processing centers the opening, inspection and scanning is done by people, not machines.

tasks.label: Transfer or transport offenders on foot or by driving vehicles, such as trailers, vans, or buses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine within-facility escort on foot: supervisor moves a compliant inmate or small group from a housing unit to medical, visitation, intake, classification or a program area — applying and removing handcuffs/waist chains, pat-searching, coordinating electronic door and sallyport control, keeping hands-on positional control, maintaining count and logging the movement. Jail/prison interior.

High-risk or uncooperative inmate move on foot: escorting a segregation, protective-custody, mental-health or combative inmate — full restraints, two-officer hold, resistance and assault risk, possible use-of-force or cell extraction, restraint-chair placement, video documentation. Jail/prison interior.

Off-facility vehicle transport: supervisor drives or supervises a van/bus/trailer run on public streets and highways to court, another correctional facility, a hospital or a receiving/discharge point — restraint application and shackle checks in the sallyport, loading and seating by security classification, armed en-route security, radio check-ins, response to medical emergencies, escape attempts or breakdowns, then unloading and custody hand-off.

Off-site foot escort at destination: moving restrained inmates through courthouse hallways and holding cells, hospital corridors and exam rooms, or medical/funeral appointments — maintaining custody among members of the public and outside staff, controlling restraint removal for court appearances, watching for contraband passes and escape.

Inside-perimeter group movements and bus loading: marshalling chained lines of inmates across the compound to chow, work detail, yard or the transport sallyport; loading and unloading the transport bus inside the secure vehicle trap; counting and verifying identity and transfer paperwork before the gate opens.

sources.system: DEKA Sentry robot (Cobb County Sheriff's Office jail pilot)
sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office piloting robot patrol program at jail
sources.claim: DEKA Sentry robots piloted at the Cobb County (GA) Adult Detention Center patrol dormitories, hallways and the ... and document incidents; they surveil and report but never escort, restrain or take custody of inmates, and a live operator takes control for more complex tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robotic system inside a US correctional facility. It substantiates autonomous navigation of jail corridors only; it performs no inmate handling, restraint application or custodial escort, so it cannot substantiate this task.

sources.title: WHILL - Winnipeg Airports Authority
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs carry a cooperating passenger from check-in through security to the departure gate inside airport terminals and return empty; deployed at Winnipeg, Detroit and Anchorage and across 100+ US airport installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a person point-to-point inside a structured facility (E2). It transfers only to the ambulatory-conveyance element; it presumes a voluntary passenger and supplies no restraint, search, control of a resisting person, or custody accountability, which are constitutive of escorting an offender.

sources.title: Waymo goes driverless in Las Vegas, with Denver, San Diego, Tampa next
sources.claim: Waymo operates fully driverless, paid passenger transport on public streets at large scale across multiple US metros (roughly 500,000 paid rides per week in 2026, with driverless launches in Las Vegas and further cities announced July 2026).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving passengers on public roads with no ... driver. It covers only the steering-the-vehicle element of inmate transport; it provides no restraint application, security seating, en-route custody supervision or armed response, and its riders are unsecured volunteers, not prisoners.

sources.title: Aurora Autonomous Trucks Are Delivering Without a Driver in the Lone Star State
sources.claim: Aurora runs commercial driver-out Class 8 trucking on public Texas highways, with regular driverless hauls between ... and no person in the cab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously operating a large highway vehicle of comparable class to a transport bus or trailer. It transfers to the driving element only; the payload is inert freight, not restrained persons requiring loading, counting, supervision and custody hand-off.

tasks.label: Supervise or provide security for offenders performing tasks, such as construction, maintenance, laundry, food service, or other industrial or agricultural operations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supervising an inmate work detail in a prison industries or fabrication shop (sign/plate shop, furniture, metal or garment shop) inside the secure perimeter: issuing and reconciling tools and sharps against shadow boards, conducting formal and informal counts, watching 20-60 inmates for contraband manufacture, horseplay and assault, directing the correctional officers posted to the shop, and physically responding to injuries or fights.

Supervising the food service/kitchen detail: knife and chemical accountability, controlling access to the loading dock and coolers, pat-searching inmates leaving the kitchen for stolen food or brewing material, keeping counts, resolving disputes among inmate workers and directing subordinate officers on the post.

Supervising laundry, janitorial and housekeeping crews that move through the facility: escorting crews between housing units and work areas, unlocking and securing areas, searching carts and linen bags for contraband and hidden persons, maintaining custody and count of the crew.

Supervising inmate maintenance and construction work inside the perimeter: crews using hand and power tools, ladders and scaffolding, sometimes alongside outside contractors; the supervisor controls tool issue/return, keeps inmates away from restricted areas and contraband sources, and enforces safety and security rules.

Supervising off-site work crews on public ground - highway right-of-way litter and brush crews, community work squads, disaster cleanup or wildland fire crews: armed or unarmed supervision, frequent counts, controlling tools and public contact, preventing escape and contraband drops, in variable terrain, traffic and weather.

Supervising agricultural operations on prison farmland: field crews, livestock handling and tractor/implement work over open acreage, with vehicle or mounted perimeter watch, count checks, tool and equipment control, and intervention in escapes or medical emergencies far from the housing compound.

sources.developer: DEKA Research & Development (deployed by Cobb County Sheriff's Office)
sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office enhances security at the Adult Detention Center with cutting-edge DEKA Sentry Robots
sources.claim: DEKA Sentry robots were piloted at the Cobb County (GA) Adult Detention Center for perimeter patrols and security rounds ..., providing cameras, lights, heat detection and two-way ...; they navigate autonomously but a live operator takes control for complex tasks.
sources.transferJustification: This is the closest real corrections deployment to the task: a machine present in a custodial facility for security. Transfer fails, however - the Sentry is a mobile camera and intercom that patrols corridors and dorms; it does not issue or reconcile tools, count and control a working crew, search inmates, direct subordinate officers, or physically intervene, and complex situations are handled by a human operator.

sources.title: How the K5 Robot Patrols Without Human Help
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot patrols mapped routes at malls, offices, parking lots and campuses on its own, self-charging and reporting to a remote security operations center; its role is surveillance and visible deterrence, not physical intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol in human-occupied facilities. It substantiates only presence, video monitoring and escalation to humans; it cannot supervise people performing work, account for tools, search for contraband, or respond physically to a disturbance, so it does not carry over to custodial supervision of an inmate work detail.

sources.title: Ascento Guard 2.0 is ready for security duty at large facilities
sources.claim: Ascento Guard 2.0 is a commercially deployed autonomous wheeled-legged robot that patrols outdoor perimeters of large industrial facilities, detecting fence holes, intruders, ladders and open gates over full eight-hour shifts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor patrol and anomaly detection on institution-controlled grounds, the nearest analogue to watching an outdoor work crew. Transfer fails because the robot detects and reports anomalies at a perimeter; it does not maintain custody of a crew, run counts, control tools, or prevent and stop escapes or assaults.

instances.label: Roll-call/shift-briefing training at a police station: sergeant delivers short instruction to the squad on a new department policy, a court decision affecting search or arrest procedure, or a revised report form, answering questions and confirming understanding.

Field-training supervision: sergeant or FTO rides with or shadows a probationary officer on patrol, observes handling of traffic stops, calls, and report writing, then debriefs and instructs on correct procedure and documents the trainee's progress.

Hands-on skills instruction at a range, mat room, or driving track: supervisor demonstrates and coaches handcuffing, defensive tactics, firearms qualification, TASER or first-aid recertification, correcting technique verbally and by demonstration.

Classroom or scenario-based in-service training session: supervisor presents a lesson plan (de-escalation, use-of-force policy, crisis intervention, evidence handling), runs role-play scenarios, and critiques trainees' decisions afterward.

One-on-one remedial or corrective training after a performance problem or complaint: supervisor reviews the incident and body-camera footage with the officer, explains the correct procedure, sets a written training plan, and follows up.

tasks.label: Conduct raids and order detention of witnesses and suspects for questioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Sergeant leads a narcotics/firearms search-warrant entry at a private residence or apartment: pre-raid briefing, approach and knock-and-announce or breach, room-by-room clearing, physically controlling and handcuffing occupants (some resisting, dogs, children present), separating witnesses from suspects, and ordering transport of detainees to the station for questioning. Unknown interior layout, low light, possible weapons.

Supervisor commands a high-risk SWAT/tactical operation against a barricaded or fortified target (stash house, motel room): armored vehicle approach, teleoperated recon robot or drone sent in, chemical agents/distraction devices, entry team clears structure, suspect taken into physical custody and moved to a transport vehicle.

Raid on an illicit or licensed commercial premises during operating hours (gambling parlor, unlicensed massage/trafficking business, after-hours bar): team enters a crowded, cluttered space of varying layout, controls and pat-searches a roomful of people, sorts witnesses from suspects by ID and interview, detains some and releases others, escorts detainees out.

Field/street incident (large fight, shooting scene, gang sweep): supervisor arrives, directs officers to stop and detain suspects and material witnesses on a public street, physically assists in restraining and pat-searching people, places them in patrol cars, and orders transport to the station for questioning.

Planned enforcement action at a workplace or institutional facility (warehouse, factory, licensed business) with a standard layout and an operator controlling access: team enters, secures and assembles workers in one area, verifies identities, physically detains a subset, and escorts them to transport for questioning.

Post-raid custody handling inside the police station/booking facility: supervisor orders and oversees detention of transported witnesses and suspects — searching them, escorting them into holding cells and interview rooms, applying/removing restraints, monitoring welfare, and releasing or booking them after questioning.

sources.title: Spot to the Rescue | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot is deployed by US police agencies for reconnaissance in barricaded-suspect standoffs; it locates the suspect while human officers make the arrest. It is operated from a tablet by a human operator, i.e., remotely piloted rather than autonomously conducting the operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tactical reconnaissance inside a raid/standoff target structure. It bears on this task because it is the closest robotic involvement in police entries; it shows the robot supplies video only and humans perform entry, custody and detention.

sources.title: Unleashed: LAPD SWAT integrates 'robot dog' into the unit
sources.claim: LAPD SWAT's Boston Dynamics quadruped is a remote-controlled device used to give the team a live look at barricaded ...; it does not perform entry, arrest or detention itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: SWAT reconnaissance during high-risk entries. Shows the state of the art in US tactical robotics is human-piloted sensing, so no autonomous robot completes the raid or the detention.

sources.title: When Robots Can't Replace Humans: The Critical Role of Personal Protection in Robotic Law Enforcement Operations
sources.claim: Trade coverage of robotic law-enforcement operations states explicitly that after a police robot scouts a location, human officers must still ... — the physical custody step has no robotic substitute.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted SWAT operations. Directly characterizes the limit of current police robots relative to raids and detention of suspects.

sources.title: Dublin, Ohio, robot cop sent back after zero arrests in parking garage | Fox News
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot, the most widely fielded autonomous law-enforcement ground robot in the US, patrols a controlled facility (a parking garage) but cannot stop, detain or cite anyone; after ~10 months of service in Dublin, Ohio it produced zero arrests, tickets or criminal ... and was returned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous police patrol in a structured facility. Establishes that even a genuinely autonomous police robot operating in an E2 facility performs observation only and never takes a person into custody.

sources.title: Chinese police trial amphibious crime-fighting robot sphere
sources.claim: The most aggressive claimed capture capability is China's RT-G spherical patrol robot, trialled with police patrols in a Wenzhou commercial zone and marketed with a net gun and tear gas; the 'capture' function is vendor-reported, tied to street patrol rather than warrant service, and its degree of autonomy in immobilizing a person is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pursuit/immobilization of a suspect by a patrol robot. Cited only to show that even this claim does not cover entering a structure, clearing rooms, sorting witnesses from suspects, or taking and holding custody; autonomy is unclear so it cannot support a positive judgment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-shift roll-call inspection of officers themselves: uniform and grooming standards, body armor worn, duty belt loadout (handcuffs, OC spray, TASER, spare magazines), condition and cleanliness of the issued sidearm, ID/credentials — conducted in the station roll-call room with officers in formation, with on-the-spot correction.

Readiness inspection of a patrol vehicle: interior/trunk checked for required equipment (patrol rifle/shotgun locked in rack, first-aid kit/AED, flares, extinguisher, spare tire, forms), rear seat searched for contraband, cleanliness, and function check of emergency lights, siren, radio and MDT — done in the station lot before or after shift.

Condition/mechanical inspection of fleet vehicles: walk-around for new body damage, scratches and dents, tire tread and pressure, fluid leaks and undercarriage damage, lighting, wipers — documented on a fleet condition form and referred to the motor pool for repair.

Walkthrough inspection of the station facility: holding cells and sally port, locker rooms, report-writing room, evidence-processing area and common areas checked for cleanliness, safety hazards, secured doors, working lights and posted-standard compliance; deficiencies logged for facilities staff.

Inspection of supplies and stores: shelf stock levels in the supply room and armory (forms, gloves, evidence bags, evidence-collection kits, ammunition, less-lethal munitions, batteries), expiration dates on kits and OC/medical items, correct labeling and secure storage; shortages ordered.

Inspection of off-site, institution-controlled outdoor assets: impound/vehicle storage lot, substation or parking structure, K9 kennels, trailer or special-event equipment cache — checking fencing/lighting, inventory present, orderly condition, weather damage.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performs nightly autonomous inspection rounds in a working cement plant, covering 450+ predefined checkpoints across six ... scanning equipment for defects, overheating and leaks without human supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine conformance walkthrough of a facility. Same core act as a supervisor's station walkthrough — traverse a fixed indoor route, compare each checkpoint against a standard (temperature, leaks, defects, readings), and log deficiencies — in a comparably cluttered, human-occupied building.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs scheduled autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, capturing 4K, thermal and acoustic data, reading gauges and raising work orders; Spot 5.1 adds autonomous multi-modal site monitoring.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled asset/facility inspection rounds inside a working plant. Transfers to inspecting station equipment and spaces against standards — same route-following, sensing, anomaly comparison and reporting workflow in an institution-controlled building.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot performs 24/7 autonomous patrols of corporate offices and similar facilities, including scheduled facility checks and environmental ..., with remote human specialists handling escalations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guard-style facility check rounds in offices. A police station is a comparable indoor human work facility; the robot's scheduled checks (doors, hazards, environmental anomalies) mirror the supervisor's conformance walkthrough.

sources.title: Built for the Real World: How the K5 Robot Handles Weather, People, and Parking Lots
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 autonomous security robot is deployed commercially for outdoor patrol of parking lots, parking structures, self-storage sites and campuses along defined routes, capturing and analyzing activity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol/observation rounds of institution-controlled outdoor lots. Transfers to inspecting an impound lot or substation grounds: same traversal of a fenced lot, imaging of vehicles/plates and flagging of anomalies against expected condition.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously navigates store aisles and scans shelves to capture item-level availability, pricing and placement data, deployed across 17 Harmons grocery locations after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous shelf audit against a planogram/stock standard. A police supply room or armory shelf check is the same act on comparable boxed, labeled goods in an institution-controlled indoor facility.

sources.title: ProMat 2025: Verity introduces AI-assisted item counting feature for picking locations
sources.claim: Verity's fully autonomous indoor drones fly warehouse racking to count items, boxes and cases, detect discrepancies and flag issues; deployments have replaced manual full-warehouse counts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous stock audit in a storage facility. Same as verifying supply-room/armory stock against required levels — locate labeled stock positions, count and report shortages.

sources.title: UVeye, Amazon Announce AI-powered Automated Vehicle Inspection
sources.claim: UVeye's Automated Vehicle Inspection scans a fleet vehicle in seconds as it ... camera-and-sensor tunnel, detecting body, tire and undercarriage problems; deployed at Amazon delivery stations to automate most of the daily van inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: daily fleet vehicle condition inspection. Same objects (light-duty fleet vehicles) and same defects a police supervisor logs — body damage, tire wear, leaks, missing parts — with the vehicle brought to a purpose-built inspection station.

tasks.label: Provide emergency medical services as required, and perform light to heavy rescue functions at emergencies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: EMS response to a private residence (the largest share of company runs): officer arrives with the crew, gains access, finds the patient in a bedroom/bathroom/stairwell, performs assessment and vitals, administers oxygen/AED/CPR/bleeding control or ALS interventions, packages the patient, and carries or moves them out to the ambulance. Cluttered, unknown interior layouts, family members present, patient condition and body habitus vary.

EMS response inside an institutional or commercial building (nursing home, school, office tower, mall, gym, airport terminal): staff meet the crew and lead them to the patient in a corridor, room, or public space; officer performs assessment and treatment, coordinates with facility staff, packages and moves the patient to the ambulance via elevators/corridors.

Motor vehicle crash on a public roadway: officer sizes up the scene, directs stabilization of the vehicle, performs or supervises extrication with hydraulic spreaders/cutters and glass management around a trapped, injured occupant, provides spinal motion restriction and patient care, and hands the patient to EMS. Live traffic, debris, fuel/battery hazards, weather, night.

Structure fire with reported occupants: officer leads or performs primary search in heat and zero visibility, forces entry, locates a victim, drags/carries them out through smoke and debris, and begins resuscitation; may include rapid-intervention rescue of a downed firefighter.

Technical/heavy rescue: trench or structural collapse, confined space, machinery entrapment, rope/high-angle, or swift-water/ice rescue. Officer performs or directs shoring, cribbing, lifting with airbags, cutting, packaging in a Stokes basket, and hauling the patient to safety in an unstable, hazardous, site-specific environment.

Lift assist / public-assist medical call: fallen elderly person at home or in assisted living, no acute injury; officer assesses for injury, lifts the person from the floor back to bed or chair, checks vitals, and clears or refers to EMS.

tasks.label: Maintain fire suppression equipment in good condition, checking equipment periodically to ensure that it is ready for use.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-shift apparatus readiness check in the station apparatus bay: the company officer and crew walk the engine/truck, open every compartment, inventory and physically handle ~150-250 items (nozzles, appliances, hand tools, hydrant wrenches, EMS bags), check engine fluid levels and tire pressure, start the pump and run it briefly, test warning lights, sirens and scene lighting, verify SCBA cylinder pressures and mount seating, and log discrepancies in the daily check sheet.

Scheduled weekly/monthly hands-on preventive maintenance in the station: cleaning and sanitizing SCBA facepieces and harnesses and checking regulators and hydro dates, inspecting ground ladders (rungs, halyards, heat sensors) and lubricating slides, running and servicing small-engine tools (chain saws, rotary saws, PPV fans, generators, hydraulic rescue tools) including fuel, oil, chain sharpening and battery care, inspecting hose and couplings, and documenting each item.

Monthly walkthrough inspection of the station's wall-mounted portable fire extinguishers and other fixed station fire protection devices: confirm each unit is in its bracket and unobstructed, gauge needle in the operable range, pin and tamper seal intact, no visible damage or corrosion, and record the inspection.

Post-incident restoration to put the unit back in service, mostly in the apparatus bay and sometimes at the scene: unload, wash, dry and repack hose into the hose bed and crosslays, swap and refill SCBA air cylinders, decontaminate and re-stow hand tools and nozzles, refill or replace discharged extinguishers, replace damaged sections, and top off fuel and water.

Annual/periodic service testing conducted or supervised by the officer at the station or drill yard: NFPA service test of every length of hose (lay out, couple to a test manifold, pressurize, mark and record, re-roll and repack), annual pump service test with drafting/hydrant supply, ground ladder testing, and SCBA flow testing on a bench, plus tagging and paperwork.

Minor repairs and defect handling: replacing gaskets, hose couplings, nozzle parts, batteries and light bulbs, swapping out failed equipment from reserve stock, tagging and removing defective gear from service, and arranging shop or vendor repair.
