sources.claim: Drone-as-First-Responder programs launch docked drones under autonomous control to 911 incidents ahead of ground units, but the drone only streams live video; ground crews still perform every physical element of the response.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated arrival on scene of an emergency call. It shows autonomous travel to an incident is achievable in the air, but delivers only situational awareness — no entry, patient care, extrication, suppression, or alarm reset.

sources.developer: Hyundai Motor Group / Korea National Fire Agency
sources.title: Autonomous firefighting robot can drive straight into a 1,000 degree blaze | Popular Science
sources.claim: Hyundai's Unmanned Firefighting Robot, donated to two South Korean fire stations in early 2026, is an unmanned tracked/wheeled water-cannon vehicle sent into hot zones ahead of firefighters; it is a support asset in testing, not a system that answers calls by itself.

sources.system: Spot with Teledyne FLIR MUVE C360
sources.title: Boston Dynamics' Robot Dog Detects Gas Leaks
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous inspection rounds at a midstream gas plant and detected a combustible gas leak, but its response was to shut down and alert the human safety team, which then went in to address the leak.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously traveling to and assessing a hazardous condition inside an institution-controlled industrial facility. It is the closest deployed analogue to alarm investigation, and it establishes that current systems detect and report but do not mitigate.

tasks.label: Search to locate fire survivors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Primary search of a burning single-family home or apartment: crew enters ahead of/with the hoseline under IDLH conditions — zero visibility from smoke, high heat, unknown floor plan — and sweeps bedrooms, closets, under beds, behind doors and furniture to find unconscious or trapped occupants within minutes.

Primary search of a commercial, institutional or large multi-unit building fire (store, office, warehouse, school, senior housing): large compartmentalized floor area, smoke-charged, heat, locked/closed doors, victims may be anywhere; coordinated multi-crew search under active fire conditions.

Secondary search after knockdown: fire out or controlled, building cooled and partially ventilated but wet, dark, cluttered with burned contents and collapsed ceiling/debris; a thorough room-by-room re-search to confirm no victims were missed, including under debris.

Vehicle fire or motor-vehicle crash on a roadway: check the passenger compartment (possibly burning or heavily damaged), trunk, and surrounding ditch/brush for occupants and ejected victims, at night or in traffic.

Outdoor/wildland incident: search of a burned-over or burning brush area, campground, or the exterior of a fire building for reported missing occupants — uneven terrain, vegetation, smoke, large area to cover.
Post-fire or explosion structural collapse (USAR-type): search of an unstable, rubble-filled building for survivors in voids, using void search, listening devices and cameras.

sources.system: CERBERUS ANYmal-C team (ANYbotics ANYmal + NTNU/ETH autonomy stack)
sources.developer: Team CERBERUS (NTNU, ETH Zurich, ANYbotics, Flyability, et al.)
sources.title: LiDAR-guided object search and detection in Subterranean Environments
sources.claim: In the DARPA SubT Challenge Finals, team CERBERUS deployed four ANYmal-C legged robots that autonomously explored an unknown constructed underground course (tunnel, urban and cave sections) while detecting and localizing placed artifacts, one class of which was 'Human Survivor' manikins.
sources.transferJustification: The scored artifacts included 'Human Survivor' manikins; autonomously exploring an unknown space and reporting the location of a human survivor is the same act as searching to locate fire survivors, in a comparable low-visibility, cluttered, GPS-denied setting.

sources.system: CERBERUS multi-robot team (ANYmal legged robots + aerial robots)
sources.title: Team CERBERUS wins DARPA Subterranean Challenge, takes home $2 million in prize money
sources.claim: At the SubT Finals the robots had to explore purpose-built course sections with visual degradation including smoke and report artifact locations; the winning team found and localized 23 of the 40 artifacts present in the one-hour run.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: the artifact set includes survivor manikins, and the run measures autonomous search-and-localize performance; the 23/40 recall also bounds how thorough such autonomous search currently is.

sources.title: Paris Firefighters Used This Remote-Controlled Robot to Extinguish the Notre Dame Blaze - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: The firefighting robot used inside a major structure fire (Notre-Dame) is remote-controlled by firefighters, not autonomous; it performs suppression and debris clearing rather than autonomous victim search.

sources.title: Spot to the Rescue | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Fire and police agencies (e.g., FDNY) send Spot into hazardous fire and collapse scenes to look for survivors and survey structures, but the robot is driven by a human operator.

sources.system: Research survey of indoor primary-search robots (Gelfert/Talavera UGVs, Pritzl/Han UAVs, Unitree Go2 simulation study)
sources.title: Training and Simulation of Quadrupedal Robot in Adaptive Stair Climbing for Indoor Firefighting: An End-to-End Reinforcement Learning Approach
sources.claim: A 2026 review of the state of the art states that robots for indoor firefighting primary search remain research concepts — tracked UGVs limited to a single floor for victim detection in smoke, and UAVs that can only enter through open windows — with the paper's own quadruped work done in simulation.

sources.title: Fire Departments Adopt Robotic Technologies for Their Operations
sources.claim: US fire departments' fielded firefighting robots are remote-controlled machines used for suppression and reconnaissance at structure fires (LAFD's Thermite RS3 at 39 commercial structure fires since 2020).

sources.developer: Örebro University-led EU H2020 consortium (with Dortmund fire brigade)
sources.title: SmokeBot – a robot serving rescue units - Örebro University
sources.claim: The SmokeBot research platform demonstrated reliable autonomous navigation in dense smoke at a fire-brigade training centre using radar, thermal and lidar, producing maps for rescue teams — mobility in smoke, not verified victim search.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous navigation/mapping in smoke-filled buildings) shows the mobility half of interior search is feasible in low visibility, but the source substantiates no autonomous victim location.

sources.system: Skydio Dock for X10 / Dock Hive site security
sources.title: Automated site security drones | Patrol, deter, and respond with Skydio
sources.claim: Commercially deployed docked drone systems fly autonomous patrol and alarm-verification missions over institution-controlled outdoor sites, with detections reviewed by remote operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous aerial patrol of a controlled site) is the closest fielded analogue to outdoor victim search, but the person-finding judgment is made by remote human operators, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

tasks.label: Operate pumps connected to high-pressure hoses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential structure fire: engine spots at a hydrant on a neighborhood street; the driver-operator sets the parking brake, engages the pump from the cab, charges one or two 1¾-in. attack lines at ~120–150 psi off tank water, transitions to hydrant supply without a pressure spike or cavitation, then raises/lowers pressures on radio requests while watching intake, tank level and engine gauges amid smoke, traffic and darkness.

Larger commercial, industrial or multi-story incident: pumping into a building FDC/standpipe at elevated pressure, supplying an aerial or deck master stream, relay pumping from a second engine or drafting from a static source; several discharges at different pressures, sustained duration, coordination with other pump operators over the radio.

Wildland/brush, grass or vehicle fire on a roadside or off-road: small booster reel or 1-in. forestry line off a brush truck's PTO/auxiliary pump, including pump-and-roll while the vehicle moves, limited tank water, uneven ground, dust and heat.

Training evolutions and pump maintenance/testing at the station apron or department drill ground: weekly pump checks and hydrant hookups, driver-operator hose-lay evolutions with known lengths and nozzles, annual NFPA 1911 pump service test drafting from a test pit and holding rated flows at 150/200/250 psi.

Non-fire water operations: drafting from a pond, portable tank or dry hydrant for a tanker shuttle; filling and dumping tanks; running a portable pump to dewater a flooded basement; supplying washdown/decon lines at a hazmat or MVA scene; hydrant flow testing.

sources.system: FlameRanger (Unifire TARGA robotic nozzle + IR3/thermal detection)
sources.developer: Unifire AB (installed/serviced by distributors such as Nobel Fire Systems)
sources.title: FlameRanger - Nobel Fire Systems
sources.claim: Unifire's FlameRanger autonomous robotic fire suppression system detects a fire, aims a robotic monitor nozzle and automatically opens the valve or starts the pump, delivering a high-flow water/foam stream and shutting off when the fire is out — i.e., machine-controlled pump operation in a fixed, plumbed installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic fire suppression by a robotic monitor. It transfers because the machine performs the pump-operator function proper — starting the pump and delivering pressurized water through fixed piping to a discharge — with the supply and nozzle purpose-built and fixed, i.e. the E1 presentation of this task.

sources.title: LASHFIRE tests Unifire AB's new autonomous fire fighting robot FlameRanger
sources.claim: FlameRanger was tested fully autonomously against multiple live outdoor fires at a fire training site, detecting, locating and suppressing four separate fires with no human involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: the robotic nozzle system runs the pressurized water delivery autonomously, but only from a fixed, pre-plumbed mounting position.

sources.system: Tornatech GPD/GPX diesel and electric fire pump controllers (NFPA 20)
sources.title: Installation and Maintenance Manual for Diesel Engine Fire Pump Controllers
sources.claim: Listed fire pump controllers start and stop stationary fire pumps automatically on sensed pressure drop (and on scheduled weekly tests), running pumps that feed standpipe hose valves and sprinkler systems in buildings without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic operation of a stationary fire pump supplying standpipe hose connections. It is the same physical act as this task — starting a pump and holding fire-service pressures to charged hose lines — in a purpose-built, plumbed pump room.

sources.system: Automatic pump pressure governor (Class 1 Total Pressure Master, FRC PumpBoss/InControl class devices)
sources.developer: Class 1/Fire Research Corp. and other apparatus component makers
sources.title: Tips for Automatic Pump Pressure Governors — Fire Engineering
sources.claim: Fire apparatus pressure governors are closed-loop machine controllers that hold pump discharge pressure automatically as hoselines are opened and closed, provided the supply is adequate; they are required equipment on NFPA 1901 pumpers.

sources.title: Waterous Announces New Pressure Governor — Firehouse
sources.claim: A commercially sold fire-pump pressure governor automatically regulates discharge pressure to a set point within ±2.5% of full scale on in-service fire apparatus.

sources.system: Trident AirPrime air-operated pump primer (AUTO PRIME mode)
sources.title: Product of the Day: Trident Emergency Products AirPrime Air-Operated Pump Priming System — Firehouse
sources.claim: Apparatus pump primers offer an automatic mode that engages the primer whenever no discharge pressure is sensed, automating the priming step of drafting and maintaining prime during supply changes.

sources.system: Firefighting Robot System 'Scrum Force' (Water Cannon Robot + Hose Extension Robot)
sources.title: A firefighting robot system that can be applied to large-scale fires in petroleum complexes — JSME
sources.claim: Japan's deployed 'Scrum Force' firefighting robot system (MHI water-cannon and hose-laying robots, in service with Ichihara City Fire Department at a refinery) drives itself, lays supply hose and discharges 4,000 L/min at 1 MPa autonomously — but firefighters, not the robots, connect and operate the pumps at the water source.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded mobile system to fireground water supply in a structured industrial facility; cited to show the pump-operation step at an incident scene is still done by humans, so E2 is not substantiated.

sources.developer: Howe & Howe Technologies / Los Angeles City Fire Department
sources.title: Firefighting Robots Go Autonomous — Scientific American
sources.claim: The most capable firegound robot in US fire service use, LAFD's RS3, is human-controlled rather than autonomous, and autonomous firefighting bots had not been tested on real fires.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as negative/limiting evidence for E2 and E3: fireground water-delivery robots in service are teleoperated, so they cannot support positive judgments.

tasks.label: Maintain contact with fire dispatchers at all times to notify them of the need for additional firefighters and supplies, or to detail any difficulties encountered.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Extinguish flames and embers to suppress fires, using shovels or engine- or hand-driven water or chemical pumps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential structure fire: crew stretches a 1.75-inch handline off the engine, advances into a smoke-filled, heated house of unknown layout, locates the seat of a room-and-contents fire and knocks it down with water/foam, moving furniture and debris as needed.

Wildland/vegetation fire: brush, grass or WUI fire on open ground; crew attacks the flaming front with engine-driven booster/progressive hose lays, backpack pumps and hand tools (shovels, McLeods), working uneven terrain, wind and shifting fire behavior.

Vehicle, dumpster or outside rubbish fire on a public street or lot: single engine company, short attack line or booster line, unknown contents (fuel, batteries, cylinders), traffic and bystanders present.

Large commercial/industrial fire (warehouse, plant, refinery, tank farm): defensive operation applying master streams from deck guns, portable monitors or elevated streams onto a large fire load inside an institution-controlled facility, plus exposure cooling with foam or water.

Incipient/contained fire inside a commercial or institutional facility (waste bunker, recycling pit, hangar, warehouse, kitchen or utility room): fire in the open within the building, knocked down quickly with an extinguisher, water can or short hoseline before it spreads.

Overhaul / mop-up after knockdown: with shovels, rakes, pike poles and hooks, firefighters dig out, stir and turn burning debris, open walls and ceilings, and wet down remaining embers and hidden hot spots until the fire is declared out.

sources.system: Unifire FlameRanger (robotic nozzle / automatic fire monitor with TARGA control)
sources.developer: Unifire AB (Sweden); distributed by Kidde Australia, Nobel Fire Systems
sources.title: Automated Waste and Recycling Fire Fighting Technology - Asia Pacific Fire
sources.claim: Unifire's FlameRanger is a commercially sold autonomous robotic fire-suppression system: flame detectors locate the fire, a PLC aims the robotic water/foam nozzle and opens the valve, and the system suppresses the fire until it is extinguished.

sources.title: LASHFIRE tests Unifire AB's new autonomous fire fighting robot FlameRanger
sources.claim: In EU LASH FIRE project live-fire tests at a fire training ground, FlameRanger autonomously detected four separate fires, located them in 3D and suppressed them in seconds with no human involvement; the scenario was cargo/vehicle fires on ro-ro ship weather decks.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (extinguishing flames with a pump-fed water/foam stream); fuels are burning vehicles/cargo on a deck, matching the vehicle-fire and Class A pile instances.

sources.title: Unifire's FlameRanger: Revolutionizing Autonomous Robotic Fire Suppression
sources.claim: FlameRanger systems are installed and operating in real human work facilities - waste-to-energy plants, recycling centres, aircraft hangars, logistics warehouses - with over 130 systems sold worldwide, detecting and suppressing fires 24/7 typically within 15 seconds.

sources.system: MHI Firefighting Robot System (Water Cannon Robot + Hose Extension Robot)
sources.developer: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries with Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency (FDMA)
sources.title: MHI Develops Autonomous "Water Cannon Robot" and "Hose Extension Robot" for Use in Firefighting
sources.claim: MHI's Water Cannon Robot and Hose Extension Robot self-drive to a designated position at a fire and discharge water or foam at 4,000 L/min to extinguish and cool fires at petrochemical plants; the hose robot autonomously lays up to 300 m of supply hose.

sources.system: Scrum Force firefighting robot system (Water Cannon, Tough Reeler, Sky Eye, Land Eye)
sources.developer: FDMA / Mitsubishi Heavy Industries; operated by Ichihara City Fire Department
sources.title: 日本唯一の消防ロボットシステム「スクラムフォース」
sources.claim: The system, named 'Scrum Force', was placed in service with Ichihara City Fire Department (Japan) in 2019 for refinery/petrochemical complex fires; the water cannon robot recognises stream drift caused by wind changes and corrects its nozzle aim while discharging.

sources.developer: Howe & Howe Technologies (Textron); Los Angeles Fire Department
sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The LAFD's Thermite RS3 firefighting robot, the first in US fire service use, flows 2,500 gpm but is operated by a firefighter with a remote controller and video feed - continuous teleoperation, not autonomy.

sources.system: Hyundai Unmanned Firefighting Robot (based on Hyundai Rotem HR-Sherpa)
sources.developer: Hyundai Motor Group / Korea National Fire Agency
sources.title: Hyundai Motor Group Donates Unmanned Firefighting Robots to Korea National Fire Agency for Safeguarding Firefighters
sources.claim: Hyundai's Unmanned Firefighting Robots were donated to Korea's National Fire Agency in Feb 2026 and are used in live fire operations by 119 rescue units, but they are directed by a remote operator; fully autonomous suppression is described as a future plan.

sources.system: Sikorsky MATRIX autonomy Black Hawk + Rain wildfire mission autonomy
sources.title: Rain and Sikorsky Test Advanced Aerial Firefighting Technologies Using Autonomous Black Hawk Helicopter
sources.claim: Sikorsky and Rain flew an optionally piloted Black Hawk that autonomously located and dropped water on staged propane and brush-pile fires in Southern California hills, demonstrating autonomous suppression of early-stage wildfires as a staged test rather than routine operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial water delivery onto a wildland fire rather than ground attack with hoselines and shovels; cited to bound what autonomous suppression achieves outdoors.

tasks.label: Maintain knowledge of current firefighting practices by participating in drills and by attending seminars, conventions, and conferences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Company-level hands-on drill at the fire station apparatus bay or department drill yard: stretching and charging preconnected hoselines, coupling and repacking hose, throwing 24-35 ft ground ladders, donning SCBA and turnout gear on time standards, operating pumps, saws, forcible-entry props and hydraulic tools with the crew, critiqued by the company officer.

Classroom, online-module, seminar, conference and convention attendance: recertification lectures, tactics/case-study sessions, NFPA and department policy updates, FDIC-style conference sessions, watching and discussing near-miss videos, taking notes and testing.

Live-fire training evolution at the department burn tower or regional training academy: interior attack with charged line in heat and smoke, primary search with victim mannequin, ventilation, mayday/RIT drill, in full PPE with an instructor cadre and safety officer.

EMS and rescue skills practice: CPR/airway/AED skills on mannequins, patient packaging and lifting, cardiac-arrest scenario drills, and vehicle-extrication practice cutting donated cars with hydraulic tools at the training ground.

Multi-company or mutual-aid drill at an off-site location taken as found: an acquired vacant structure, a high-rise or industrial site walkthrough, a swiftwater/ice rescue drill at a river or lake, or a wildland hoselay drill on brush terrain.

sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States | Los Angeles Fire Department
sources.claim: The most prominent firefighting robot in US fire-service use, the Thermite RS3 fielded by the Los Angeles Fire Department, is a remote-operated (teleoperated) vehicle driven by a firefighter with a controller and video feed; it flows water and pushes obstacles but performs no autonomous multi-step firefighting evolutions.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest fire-ground robotic system to the physical work practiced in firefighter drills (hose/water delivery, moving through a fire building); it establishes that such systems are teleoperated, so they cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Fire Departments Adopt Robotic Technologies for Their Operations
sources.claim: Trade coverage of fire-department robotics describes tracked firefighting robots as remote-controlled tools, while the only 'fully autonomous' unit named, Boston Dynamics' Spot, is used by first responders for situational assessment and reconnaissance rather than for performing firefighting evolutions or training drills.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is fire-ground reconnaissance; it is cited to show that the autonomous capability actually fielded in fire departments is sensing/navigation, not the tool handling, hose work, ladder work or PPE use that constitute firefighter drills.

sources.system: Firefighting robots in current fire-service use (Thermite RS3, Colossus class)
sources.title: Firefighting Robots Go Autonomous | Scientific American
sources.claim: As of the mid-2020s the firefighting machines actually in service are predominantly remote-controlled; autonomous decision-making versions remain in research, and no one expects the machines to replace firefighters on the fire line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is structural/wildland fire suppression, the subject matter of the drills; it establishes the field-wide autonomy ceiling relevant to whether a robot could carry out a drill evolution unattended.

sources.system: Water Cannon Robot and Hose Extension Robot (Firefighting Robot System)
sources.title: MHI Develops Autonomous "Water Cannon Robot" and "Hose Extension Robot" for Use in Firefighting | Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
sources.claim: The most autonomous fielded firefighting robots, MHI's Water Cannon Robot and Hose Extension Robot, autonomously drive to a fire, lay their own hose and discharge water at petrochemical-plant scale fires; their scope is water application at inaccessible fire scenes, not the varied tool, ladder, PPE, search and EMS evolutions of a firefighter training drill.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is large-scale fire suppression at petrochemical complexes; cited because hose laying and water delivery overlap with engine-company drill content, but the system operates only as a self-driving monitor and has no manipulation, PPE, ladder or search capability.

sources.system: Fire and rescue service firefighting robot (Kent FRS, West Midlands FRS)
sources.title: Firefighting Robots | Firefighter Magazine (Fire Brigades Union)
sources.claim: Newly adopted fire and rescue service robots in the UK are deployed to industrial and commercial incidents under remote operation for imaging and hose work, confirming that current service robots are operator-driven rather than autonomous participants in evolutions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is fire attack and size-up at commercial fires; cited to show that even the newest fire-service robot adoptions in 2025 rely on continuous remote operation, which cannot substantiate autonomous completion of a drill.

tasks.label: Select and attach hose nozzles, depending on fire type, and direct streams of water or chemicals onto fires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior fire attack at a residential structure fire (single-family home or apartment): firefighter selects a combination/smooth-bore nozzle for the 1¾-inch attack line, couples it, stretches the line through a door, advances into heat and zero-visibility smoke down halls and stairs, and applies water on the seat of the fire room by room until knockdown and overhaul.

Exterior/defensive stream operations at a working building fire on a public street: nozzle or tip selection for a deck gun, portable monitor or ladder pipe, connecting supply lines, and directing master streams onto a fully involved structure and onto exposures, with collapse zones, parked cars, wires and bystanders around.

Vehicle fires, dumpster fires and outside rubbish/trash fires on roadways, parking lots and yards: pull a booster or 1¾-inch line, pick a fog/straight-stream nozzle (or foam for a fuel spill), approach at an angle, and flow water onto burning tires, engine compartment, cargo or refuse pile until out.

Wildland, brush and grass fire attack: attach a forestry/adjustable-gallonage nozzle to a live reel or 1-inch forestry line off a brush truck, knock down the flame front along an irregular perimeter over uneven terrain, then mop up hot spots and stumps with the nozzle and hand tools.

Fire at an industrial or large commercial facility (plant, refinery, warehouse, waste site) or a flammable-liquid/hazmat incident: select foam nozzle and eductor or master-stream appliance, apply water/foam onto a tank, pile or spill fire, and provide cooling streams on exposed vessels.

Live-fire training burns and hoseline drills at a fire academy burn building, drill tower or burn prop: select and attach the specified nozzle, take the line in, and apply water on the prop fire under controlled, instructor-supervised conditions.

sources.system: Firefighting Robot System 'Scrum Force' (Water Cannon Robot / Hose-Laying Robot)
sources.developer: Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency National Research Institute of Fire and Disaster with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
sources.title: A firefighting robot system that can be applied to large-scale fires in petroleum complexes — JSME Award
sources.claim: Japan's FDMA/MHI 'Scrum Force' firefighting robot system (water cannon robot + hose-laying robot + recon robots) autonomously drives to the fire, lays and connects its supply hose, and discharges water at flames with autonomously adjusted discharge angle; the operator selects a proposed plan rather than teleoperating. Deployed to Ichihara City Fire Department for petrochemical-complex fires.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: directing a high-volume water/foam stream from a nozzle onto a fire, including getting the hose and nozzle connected; the crew only makes the final coupling at the water source in the safe zone.

sources.system: Water Cannon Robot and Hose Extension Robot
sources.title: MHI Develops Autonomous "Water Cannon Robot" and "Hose Extension Robot" for Use in Firefighting
sources.claim: The Water Cannon Robot carries a nozzle that discharges water or foam at 4,000 L/min and the paired Hose Extension Robot automatically lays up to 300 m of 150 mm hose; both self-drive to the fire scene with GPS and laser sensors.

sources.system: FlameRanger (Force robotic nozzles + TARGA PLC + IR flame detectors)
sources.developer: Unifire AB (tests with RISE, EU LASH FIRE project)
sources.title: Unifire's FlameRanger™ Fire Fighting Robot Tested for Ro-Ro Ship Safety
sources.claim: Unifire's FlameRanger autonomous robotic nozzle system detected four separate fires, located them in 3D and suppressed them without human involvement during RISE/LASH FIRE tests at the Guttasjön fire training site, Borås, Sweden, aimed at protecting ro-ro ship vehicle decks.
sources.transferJustification: Same core task: aiming a nozzle and applying a water/foam stream onto a fire until extinguished; nozzle selection/attachment is fixed piping in this configuration, matching the E1/E2 counterfactual where the line and nozzle are presented already made up.

sources.system: FlameRanger with six FORCE 50 BLDC robotic monitors
sources.title: Major Waste Site — FlameRanger deployed at major waste site (Case Study)
sources.claim: A UK city waste and recycling facility installed six FORCE 50 BLDC robotic monitors with a FlameRanger PLC; on IR flame detection the system automatically activates the robotic water cannon to sweep and suppress the fire in the waste bay, without a human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same core task as applied to refuse/waste-pile fires: directing a high-flow water stream onto the burning material until suppression, in a facility built for human work.

sources.system: Optionally piloted Black Hawk with MATRIX autonomy + Rain Wildfire Mission Autonomy System
sources.title: Sikorsky, Rain test autonomous wildfire suppression in Southern California
sources.claim: A Sikorsky Black Hawk with MATRIX autonomy and Rain's wildfire mission autonomy located and suppressed firefighter-ignited brush piles with autonomous water drops in wildfire-prone Southern California terrain at 3,300 ft, with San Bernardino County Fire.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous delivery of water onto burning wildland fuel. It substitutes for aerial knockdown only — it involves no nozzle selection, hoseline work, perimeter knockdown or mop-up, so it does not cover the whole wildland instance.

sources.title: LAFD Unveils New RS3 Firefighting Robot
sources.claim: The mobile firefighting robots actually fielded by US fire departments for fireground stream application, such as the LAFD's Thermite RS3, are remotely operated by a firefighter with video feedback, not autonomous.

tasks.label: Collaborate with other firefighters as a member of a firefighting crew.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Working structure fire in a private dwelling: the firefighter operates as one of a 2-4 person engine company, taking an assignment from the officer, stretching and advancing a charged hoseline through a door and up stairs with a partner, staying together in zero visibility and high heat, sharing air/conditions by radio and touch, and backing out together on the officer's order.

Fireground support work at a structure fire (residential or small commercial): truck-company crew members coordinate forcible entry, throw ground ladders in pairs, perform horizontal/vertical ventilation timed to the attack crew's advance, conduct a two-person primary search with a partner, or stand by as RIT — all under a common incident command with other arriving companies.

EMS/medical response as a company (the largest share of runs): two to three crew members enter a residence, business, or public space, divide roles for patient assessment, CPR/airway, spinal packaging or lift assist, and coordinate hand-off with an arriving ambulance crew in cluttered, unpredictable surroundings.

Motor-vehicle crash or technical rescue on a roadway: the crew works together to stabilize the vehicle, deploy hydraulic tools, cut and displace metal while a partner protects the patient, and coordinate the removal and transfer of the patient in live-traffic conditions.

Outside fires: brush/grass, vehicle, dumpster and trash fires, plus infrequent large industrial or bulk-storage fires. The crew pulls and advances hand lines together, uses hand tools on a fire edge, or sets and supplies master streams and large-diameter supply lines in coordination with other companies.

Station and training-ground crew activity: multi-company drills and evolutions (hose lays, ladder raises, search drills, mask confidence), morning apparatus and equipment checks done as a company, and pre-incident walkthroughs — carried out inside the fire station and on the department's training grounds.

sources.developer: Howe & Howe Technologies (Textron) / Los Angeles Fire Department
sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The first robotic firefighting vehicle put in service by a US fire department (LAFD's Thermite RS3) is a remotely operated water-delivery rover, not an autonomous crew member.

sources.developer: Hyundai Motor Group with Korea National Fire Agency
sources.title: Hyundai unveils firefighting robot for hazardous fire scene deployment - IFSJ
sources.claim: The newest fire-service ground robot delivered to a national fire agency (Hyundai's Unmanned Firefighting Robot, handed to South Korea's National Fire Agency / Seoul 119 rescue team in Feb 2026) is remotely operated with driver-assist; full autonomy is stated as a future plan.

sources.system: Firefighting Robot System (Water Cannon Robot + Hose Extension Robot)
sources.developer: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries / Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency
sources.title: A firefighting robot system that can be applied to large-scale fires in petroleum complexes (JSME award)
sources.claim: MHI's multi-robot Firefighting Robot System (water-cannon robot, hose-laying robot, recon robots, command vehicle) is deployed operationally with the Ichihara City Fire Department and executes moving, hose laying and water discharge autonomously after a fire-crew operator selects the plan, working alongside firefighters who connect pumps at the water source.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unmanned master-stream placement and supply-hose laying at petroleum-complex fires. It bears on crew collaboration only for the narrow outdoor industrial master-stream role; it performs no interior work, hand-line, tool or patient handling.

sources.developer: Virginia Tech / Office of Naval Research
sources.title: U.S. Navy Improves Robotic Firefighter to Fight Shipboard Fires at Sea
sources.claim: The Navy's shipboard humanoid firefighting robot SAFFiR was demonstrated under operator guidance rather than autonomously.

sources.title: Autonomous Fire Fighting with a UAV-UGV Team at MBZIRC 2020
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed account of an autonomous UAV-UGV firefighting team built for the MBZIRC 2020 competition arena states that fielded firefighting robots are mostly manually controlled; the autonomous systems extinguished small competition fire targets in a purpose-built arena, not real fires alongside a human crew.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detection and extinguishing of small staged fires by a robot team. Shows autonomous multi-robot firefighting only in a purpose-built competition arena with simulated fire targets, far from crew-integrated fireground work.

sources.system: Rain wildfire mission autonomy on Sikorsky MATRIX Black Hawk
sources.title: Rain and Sikorsky Test Advanced Aerial Firefighting Technologies Using Autonomous Black Hawk Helicopter
sources.claim: An uncrewed Sikorsky Black Hawk running Rain's mission autonomy performed autonomous wildfire water drops on brush piles in California in front of fire agency observers - an aerial suppression demonstration, not ground crew work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial initial-attack water drops on wildland fire. Relevant to outdoor fire suppression, but the aircraft is a separate air asset and does not perform a ground crew member's coordinated hand-line or tool work.

tasks.label: Train new employees to control and suppress fires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Company-level / academy classroom instruction of probationary firefighters: lecture on fire behavior, ventilation, water supply and department SOPs in a station or academy classroom, combined with hands-on show-and-tell of PPE, SCBA, nozzles, hand tools and appliances passed around the room; instructor answers questions, corrects handling, and administers written and practical checks.

Drill-ground skills training on a department training ground/tower: instructor physically demonstrates then coaches recruits through hose loads and advances, hydrant hook-ups, ground ladder throws, forcible entry on a door prop, SCBA donning and mask-confidence/maze evolutions; repositions props and hose, physically corrects body position and grip, times evolutions, and signs off competency.

Live-fire evolution in a department burn building or gas-fired prop: instructor acts as ignition officer and safety officer under NFPA 1403 — sets and lights the fuel package, modulates fire intensity, stays with the crew inside heat and smoke, coaches nozzle technique and door control, monitors trainee condition and orders/physically assists evacuation if conditions deteriorate.

Apparatus and equipment operator training: teaching new firefighters pump operation, drafting, aerial ladder setup and driver skills on the apparatus floor, training yard and public streets; instructor rides along, demonstrates panel and controls, takes over controls when the trainee errs.

On-the-job mentoring of a probationary firefighter at real incidents and at the station: coaching during actual structure and vehicle fires and post-incident critique in found environments — private homes, streets, occupied buildings — with the instructor working alongside, physically directing the recruit's hose line, tool use and search technique amid unpredictable conditions.

sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The most capable fire-service ground robot fielded by a US department, the Thermite RS3 used by LAFD, is a remotely operated suppression vehicle — it is driven by a human operator with a controller and does not act as an autonomous firefighter, let alone an instructor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fire suppression itself. Cited to show that even the core suppression skill being taught is performed by fire-service robots only under continuous human teleoperation, so no such system could demonstrate, supervise, or certify a recruit's suppression work.

sources.title: Paris Firefighters Used This Remote-Controlled Robot to Extinguish the Notre Dame Blaze - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Colossus, the best-known European firefighting robot (Notre Dame fire), is likewise a remote-controlled machine directed by firefighters from standoff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior fire attack. Shows the frontier of embodied fire-service robotics remains operator-driven, providing no basis for a machine to instruct recruits in controlling and suppressing fire.

sources.system: LION Live Fire Training Props (Pilot Module / Control Console)
sources.title: Live Fire Firefighter Training Props | Fire Safety Training Tools
sources.claim: Commercial live-fire training props are computer-controlled gas systems, but the fire is started, modulated and stopped by a human instructor at a console; the prop is an instrument the instructor uses, not an instructor.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the live-fire instance: the only automated element of burn-building training is fuel/flame control, which remains under human command, and it covers none of the demonstration, coaching, evaluation or safety-intervention duties of the trainer.

sources.title: Training with moving targets: Are you doing enough? | Police1
sources.claim: Autonomous robots are used in live-fire training in another domain — Marathon Targets' AI-driven robotic humanoids move autonomously on firearms ranges — but they serve as targets and scorekeepers while human instructors deliver the training.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conducting live-fire (firearms) training. Transfer fails: the robots are moving targets on a controlled range that provide hit feedback; they do not demonstrate technique, correct trainees physically, control a real fire, or certify competency, which is what firefighter fire-suppression instruction requires.

sources.title: TeachBot: Towards teaching robotics fundamentals for human-robot collaboration at work
sources.claim: The nearest thing to an autonomous robotic instructor of physical work skills teaches robot-arm fundamentals to factory workers from a fixed workstation in a research study.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic instruction of workers. Transfer fails: TeachBot lectures and replays programmed arm motions at a bench about its own operation; it cannot handle hose, ladders, SCBA or live fire, coach body mechanics, or assume safety-officer responsibility for recruits in an IDLH environment.

sources.developer: National Fire Protection Association / authorities having jurisdiction
sources.title: Planning a Training Fire Compliant with NFPA 1403 in an Acquired Structure | Fire Engineering
sources.claim: Firefighter live-fire instruction is a safety-critical human role with mandated instructor staffing and designated ignition and safety officers responsible for participants' lives.
sources.transferJustification: Context on the acceptance standard for this task: the output must be competent, safely supervised recruits under designated human instructor/ignition-officer accountability, a bar no cited robotic system approaches.

tasks.label: Position and climb ladders to gain access to upper levels of buildings, or to rescue individuals from burning structures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Working fire in a single-family or small multi-family residence: firefighter pulls a 24–35 ft extension ladder off the apparatus, carries it over a lawn/driveway with obstructions (fences, wires, bushes), raises, extends and heels it to a second-floor window or porch roof at proper climbing angle, then ascends in full PPE/SCBA with a hand tool or hoseline through smoke and heat to gain access or provide egress.

Ladder rescue: ladder thrown to a window where a civilian is trapped; firefighter climbs, controls a panicked or unconscious occupant at the sill, and brings the person (often 100–220 lb, limp) down the ladder to the ground while other crew heel the ladder.

Multi-story apartment/commercial building: driver-operator spots the apparatus on a street with parked cars and overhead wires, sets outriggers on uneven pavement, raises and spots the aerial ladder or platform to a specific window, balcony or roof edge; firefighters climb the aerial to reach the fire floor, roof, or to remove occupants.

Roof operations: ground ladders and a roof ladder placed to a pitched or flat roof of a burning structure; firefighter ascends carrying a chainsaw/rotary saw and hook, hooks the roof ladder over the ridge, sounds the roof, and works from the ladder for vertical ventilation, then descends.

Non-fire elevated access at an institution-controlled commercial/industrial property (automatic alarm, water leak, rooftop HVAC check, stranded person or animal, storm damage): ladder placed to a roof or landing, or a building's fixed roof-access ladder climbed, to reach the elevated level and look/act, under no fire conditions and no time compression.

Ladder evolutions during company drills and academy training on the department drill ground/training tower: standard aluminum ground ladders carried, raised, extended and placed to marked windows of the tower, climbed and descended, on a flat prepared drill pad supervised by instructors.

sources.system: ANYmal quadruped with hooked end-effectors (ETH Zurich RSL)
sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab / ANYbotics
sources.title: ANYMal quadruped robot masters ladders with its custom hooked feet
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's Robotic Systems Lab gave an ANYbotics ANYmal quadruped hooked end-effectors and a reinforcement-learning policy that autonomously climbs standard industrial ladders at 70°–90° inclination with a 90% hardware success rate; a research demonstration, not a fielded product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ascending a fixed industrial ladder to reach an elevated inspection location. It transfers only to the climbing portion of firefighter ladder work — same object class (rung ladder at firefighting climbing angles) — but with no payload, no ladder placement and no thermal exposure.

sources.system: ANYmal quadruped with hooked end-effectors (ETH Zurich RSL)
sources.title: Robust Ladder Climbing with a Quadrupedal Robot (arXiv preprint PDF)
sources.claim: The same ANYmal ladder-climbing work relies on an external motion-capture system to supply the ladder's pose to the controller, i.e., an instrumented setting where the workpiece position is known to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; cited to establish the environment class (fixtured/instrumented lab rig) in which the climbing capability was shown.

sources.title: Quadruped Robots Can Climb Ladders Now - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: A Tokyo Metropolitan University quadruped with gripping feet climbed a vertical handrail-free ladder fully autonomously, though the controller was trained for that specific ladder and several attempts failed on torque limits.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ascent of a fixed vertical ladder to an upper platform. Transfers only to the bare climb-to-upper-level element, on a single known ladder, with a 7 kg robot carrying no tools.

sources.title: Multi-contact vertical ladder climbing with an HRP-2 humanoid | Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: The HRP-2 humanoid was made to climb vertical industrial-norm ladders using a multi-contact planner and closed-loop control, in a laboratory setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid ascent of a fixed industrial ladder. Supports only the fixtured-ladder climb element; the demonstrated cycle takes minutes per few rungs and carries no firefighting load.

sources.title: Firefighting robot Colossus helps put out Notre-Dame fire
sources.claim: The firefighting robots actually fielded by fire services (Shark Robotics Colossus, used at Notre-Dame) are remote-controlled tracked hose platforms; they neither place nor climb ladders and are not autonomous.

sources.title: From China, a Firefighting Robot Dog
sources.claim: Quadruped fire robots now deployed with fire brigades (Unitree B2-based) negotiate steps up to 40 cm and spray water under autonomous or remote control; no ladder ascent or victim removal capability is claimed.

sources.title: Magirus turntable ladder M42L is fast and extremely secure
sources.claim: State-of-the-art aerial (turntable) ladders are computer-monitored and hydraulically assisted but remain operator-driven from a control stand; positioning and spotting the ladder is a human judgment task.

tasks.label: Create openings in buildings for ventilation or entrance, using axes, chisels, crowbars, electric saws, or core cutters.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Forcible entry through a locked exterior door of a single-family home or apartment at a working fire or rescue call: size up the door (inward/outward swing, deadbolt, storm door), set the halligan and flat-head axe, force it in seconds in full PPE/SCBA, at night, in smoke and heat, controlling the door against flow paths.

Horizontal ventilation on a residential structure: clearing windows with pike pole, axe or hook from the ground, a ground ladder or the interior, clearing sash and glass fully, and opening or removing doors, coordinated with the attack line and interior crew.

Vertical ventilation: carrying a chainsaw or rotary saw up a ground/roof ladder onto the pitched or flat roof of a burning residence or small commercial building, sounding the roof, cutting a 4'x4' or larger hole between rafters, and punching down the ceiling, on a heated, structurally suspect roof.

Forcible entry at a commercial or multi-family occupancy: steel doors in metal frames, drop bars, roll-down security gates, window bars or lexan, defeated with a rotary saw with metal/carbide blades, hydraulic spreaders or through-the-lock tools, often at odd hours with alarms sounding.

Opening walls and ceilings inside the structure to find and cut off hidden fire, or breaching a wall or floor for access or firefighter escape: pulling drywall or lath and plaster, cutting stud bays and ceilings with axe, hook or saw, occasionally cutting masonry with a core cutter, in zero visibility.

Non-fire forced entry on service calls: welfare check, medical patient behind a locked door, automatic alarm or lockout, where crews must get in quickly but with the least damage practical (through-the-lock, shove knife, window removal) and secure the opening afterward.

sources.title: WEINMANN multifunction bridges - HOMAG
sources.claim: WEINMANN (HOMAG) multifunction bridges are CNC gantry machines used in prefabricated house plants that automatically saw, trim and cut all openings (window and door openings, cut-outs) in fixtured timber-frame wall, roof, ceiling and floor elements.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting door/window/service openings in building wall and roof elements with saws and routers. Same physical act on the same materials (framing, sheathing, plasterboard, roof decks) with the same tool class named in the task (electric saws), performed under machine control on a fixtured workpiece - exactly how a purpose-built (E1) setting would present the work.

sources.title: The WALLTEQ M-300 multifunction bridge by WEINMANN - Wood Industry
sources.claim: The WALLTEQ M-300 is a CNC-controlled machine for house construction that produces door and window openings in wall elements.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer: making a person-sized opening (door/window) in a building element with programmed saw/router passes; substantiates completion of the cutting instances in a purpose-built, fixtured setting.

sources.system: Robotic plasma cutting systems (FANUC Arc Mate, ABB IRB 2600, KUKA KR CYBERTECH)
sources.developer: T.I.E. Industrial / robot OEMs (FANUC, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa Motoman)
sources.title: Plasma Cutting Robots: Metal Fabrication Automation | Robots.com
sources.claim: Industrial robot cells (FANUC, ABB IRB 2600, KUKA KR CYBERTECH, Motoman) equipped with plasma torches routinely cut steel and other metals to programmed contours, including automated cutting of large steel plate, inside fenced production cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting through steel plate to a programmed contour. Commercial forcible entry means cutting an opening through steel doors, frames and roll-down gates; with the panel fixtured and presented as an E1 cell would present it, robotic cutting of comparable steel thicknesses is established practice.

sources.title: Jaibot Semi-Autonomous Drilling Robot - Hilti GB
sources.claim: Hilti's Jaibot is a semi-autonomous mobile robot in commercial use that, once positioned by a worker and referenced to a total station, drills large numbers of anchor holes in concrete ceilings autonomously from a digital plan on active construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-made holes in an existing building structure. It marks the limit of in-situ autonomy - small BIM-planned anchor holes in flat overhead concrete on a surveyed site, not person-sized openings cut in pitched roofs, doors or walls under fire conditions - so it does not transfer to this task at E2/E3.

sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The robots actually used on US firegrounds for structural fires are remotely operated vehicles that flow water and carry equipment; the LAFD's Thermite RS3 is driven by an operator with a controller and has no forcible-entry or ventilation-cutting function.

sources.title: The Colossus Robot for Extreme Firefighting - 3MON
sources.claim: Colossus, the fireground robot used at Notre-Dame and by fire services, is a remotely operated tracked machine for firefighting, casualty evacuation and equipment transport - not autonomous, and it does not force entry or cut ventilation openings.

sources.title: VentVortex Robot: Safer Vertical Ventilation for Firefighters | Responder Robotics
sources.claim: The one purpose-built roof-ventilation robot found, VentVortex, is described by its developer as remote-controlled and is not yet a shipping product: pre-orders were to open in April 2026 with production units expected in 2027.

tasks.label: Participate in fire drills and demonstrations of fire fighting techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Live-fire training evolution at a regional/departmental training academy burn building: firefighter dons turnout gear and SCBA, stretches and advances a charged 1.75-inch attack line up stairs, coordinates with a crew on ventilation and door control, locates and knocks down a room-and-contents fire, searches for and removes a victim manikin, then is critiqued by an instructor.

Routine company drill on the station apparatus floor and drill yard: hose lays and nozzle/stream management, ground-ladder throws and climbs, standpipe and pump-operator evolutions, SCBA confidence/maze and emergency-procedure drills, forcible-entry and hand-tool evolutions, timed and repeated for proficiency records.

Participating in a scheduled fire drill or pre-incident walk-through at an occupied institutional building (school, hospital, nursing home, high-rise office): riding in with the company, observing and timing the evacuation, checking alarms, stairwells and standpipe connections with facility staff, and running a standpipe or evacuation-assist evolution.

Public demonstration of firefighting techniques at a school assembly, station open house, fair, or community event: extinguisher (PASS) demonstration on a controlled pan fire, hoseline/nozzle demonstration with children, PPE and SCBA show-and-tell, kitchen-fire or sprinkler demo, sometimes a vehicle-extrication demonstration, with continuous narration and crowd control.

Off-site scenario training taken as found: acquired vacant structure burns and forcible entry, ventilation and search drills in a donated house, RIT/mayday and rope-rescue drills in a vacant building, or wildland hose-lay and hand-line construction drills on brushy terrain.

sources.developer: Howe & Howe Technologies / Textron (operated by Los Angeles Fire Department)
sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The most capable firefighting ground robot fielded by a US fire department, the Thermite RS3 used by LAFD since 2020, is a remotely operated water-flowing vehicle, not an autonomous one, and it performs only stream application and hose dragging, not crew evolutions.
sources.transferJustification: Fire attack is a core technique practiced in drills and demonstrations; this shows the state of fielded US fire-service robots is teleoperated stream application only.

sources.developer: Hyundai Motor Group / Hyundai Rotem with Korea National Fire Agency
sources.title: Hyundai Motor Group Donates Unmanned Firefighting Robots to Korea National Fire Agency for Safeguarding Firefighters
sources.claim: Hyundai's Unmanned Firefighting Robot, donated to and already in use by Korea's National Fire Agency in 2026, is fully remote-operated for both driving and firefighting functions.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that even 2026 state-of-the-art fire-service suppression robots require continuous human control, so they cannot satisfy the limited-intervention requirement when standing in for a firefighter in a drill.

sources.system: Firefighting Robot System (Water Cannon Robot + Hose Extension Robot)
sources.developer: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries / Japan Fire and Disaster Management Agency
sources.title: Mitsubishi develops autonomous firefighting robots
sources.claim: MHI's Firefighting Robot System (water cannon robot plus hose extension robot) has autonomous mobility and automatically lays up to 300 m of hose, shown in an open demonstration at Japan's National Research Institute of Fire and Disaster; it covers only large-flow water supply and application at industrial fires, not gear donning, ladders, search or crew evolutions.
sources.transferJustification: Hose deployment and master-stream application are components of hose-evolution drills; cited to mark the outer limit of autonomous fire-service robotics, which still excludes the rest of a drill evolution.

sources.title: Freddie the Fire Truck Robot - Robotronics
sources.claim: Robots used by fire departments in public fire-safety demonstrations are remote-controlled animated props operated and voiced by a firefighter, not autonomous demonstrators of firefighting technique.
sources.transferJustification: This is the robot actually used in the public fire-safety demonstration setting of this task; it is teleoperated by the very firefighter it would have to replace.

sources.system: Skyeye team UAV/UGV fire-extinguishing system (MBZIRC 2020 Challenge 3)
sources.developer: Universidad Politecnica de Madrid / Universidad Pablo de Olavide (Skyeye team)
sources.title: Skyeye Team at MBZIRC 2020: A team of aerial and ground robots for GPS-denied autonomous fire extinguishing in an urban building scenario
sources.claim: Fully autonomous fire detection, location and extinguishing by ground and aerial robots has been demonstrated only in a purpose-built competition arena with token flames and modest reliability (7th of 20 teams).
sources.transferJustification: Closest autonomous analogue to a fire-attack drill; performed in a competition test-bed with small flames and low success rates, far below the scope and reliability of an academy live-fire evolution.

sources.title: Watch China's firefighting robot dogs rain 60-meter jets, scale stairs
sources.claim: Robot dogs have taken part in Chinese live-fire drills, but in a reconnaissance role alongside human crews and with no established autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Directly a fire drill setting, but the robot contributes a reconnaissance sub-step under human direction rather than completing a firefighter's participation in the drill.

sources.system: autonomous firefighting robot prototypes (contrasted with LAFD RS3)
sources.title: Firefighting Robots Go Autonomous
sources.claim: As of 2024, autonomous firefighting robots remained untested in real fires, with mobility in built environments identified as the outstanding obstacle, while the machines actually fielded by fire departments are human-controlled.
sources.transferJustification: General state-of-the-art assessment of autonomous fire suppression, bearing on whether any cited system could carry out drill evolutions without continuous human control.

tasks.label: Assess fires and situations and report conditions to superiors to receive instructions, using two-way radios.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structure fire arrival size-up: first-due company observes the building on approach, completes a 360-degree walk-around, and transmits a size-up (construction/size, occupancy, smoke and fire conditions, exposures, water supply) to incident command over the two-way radio, then receives an assignment.

Interior tactical progress report ('CAN' report): a crew operating on the fire floor or in a search assignment radios conditions, actions taken, and needs to the IC and receives instructions to continue, redeploy, or evacuate; heavy smoke, heat, and noise degrade both observation and radio traffic.

Non-fire emergency scene assessment: motor vehicle collision, medical call, gas odor, water rescue, or hazmat spill; the firefighter assesses hazards, patients, and resource needs and radios the report to dispatch or a supervisor to request additional units or instructions.

Outdoor fire assessment: vegetation/wildland, vehicle, or dumpster fire; the firefighter judges fire size, rate of spread, fuels, wind, and threatened exposures and reports by radio to the battalion chief or dispatch, receiving tactical direction.

Automatic alarm, odor investigation, or minor incident: brief 'nothing showing / investigating' transmission, walk-through of the premises, and a follow-up radio report of findings (alarm malfunction, burnt food, activated detector) before receiving a return-to-service instruction.

tasks.label: Inspect fire sites after flames have been extinguished to ensure that there is no further danger.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family dwelling or apartment after knockdown: crew performs overhaul — thermal-imager sweeps, feeling walls, pulling ceilings, baseboards and drywall with hooks, opening attic and void spaces, checking mattresses/furniture, verifying utilities are secured — in a dark, smoke-charged, water-soaked interior full of debris and partially burned structural members, then reports the building safe from rekindle before releasing the scene.

Small contained fire (kitchen appliance, mattress dragged outside, dumpster, trash compactor, mulch bed, chimney): after knockdown the crew breaks apart and turns over the burned contents, checks them with a thermal imager and by hand/hose stream for residual heat, wets down remaining material, and confirms it is cold before clearing.

Vehicle fire on a roadway or parking lot, including hybrid/EV: after extinguishment the crew opens hood/trunk/wheel wells, checks the engine bay, tires and battery pack with a thermal imager, watches for reignition or thermal runaway over a monitoring period, checks for leaking fuel and runoff, and hands the vehicle to a tow operator with instructions.

Commercial, industrial or multi-unit building fire: post-knockdown walkthrough of a large fire-damaged occupancy — checking concealed spaces, drop ceilings, HVAC chases, stock piles and cocklofts for hidden extension, assessing collapse hazards and remaining hazardous materials, securing utilities, and coordinating handover to the fire investigator and building owner.

Wildland, brush or wildland-urban-interface fire mop-up: gridding and cold-trailing the burned area and control-line interior, locating smoldering stumps, root runs and ash pits by sight, thermal imagery and bare-hand feel, digging them out with hand tools, stirring and wetting, and declaring the segment cold.

sources.title: FDNY to Place Two Boston Dynamics "Spot" Robots in Service
sources.claim: FDNY's fire-service quadrupeds, used for tasks such as assessing structural integrity and hazardous atmospheres after collapses and fires, are operated by firefighters remotely rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Post-incident structural/atmospheric assessment is the closest deployed analogue to post-fire scene inspection; the source shows such work in US fire service is remotely driven, not autonomous.

sources.title: Firefighting Robots Go Autonomous | Scientific American
sources.claim: The main robotic firefighting vehicle in US fire-service use (LAFD's Thermite RS3) is human-controlled, with cameras feeding a human operator.

sources.title: Fire Departments Adopt Robotic Technologies for Their Operations
sources.claim: LAFD's RS3 is used for defensive suppression and thermal-camera search at commercial structure fires, not for autonomous post-fire overhaul inspection.

sources.system: DJI Mavic 3T / Matrice 350 RTK (LA County Fire)
sources.developer: DJI / Los Angeles County Fire Department
sources.title: Automatic Response: Drones & autonomy in aerial firefighting - Vertical Mag
sources.claim: Fire departments use piloted thermal drones to spot hot spots and ash pits after knockdown, but human crews still perform the mop-up and the ladder-pipe wetting the drone's findings direct.

sources.title: Drone-powered Hot Spot Detection after Wildfires
sources.claim: LAFD, DJI and Nova run automated thermal mapping workflows to find hot spots during wildfire mop-up; the workflow is flown by department pilots and produces imagery for ground crews rather than clearing an area itself.

sources.system: Orglmeister IR early detection + FireDos fire monitors
sources.title: IR Detection with Autonomous Suppression
sources.claim: In purpose-built waste-processing bays, fixed infrared cameras pinpoint hot spots in piled burned material and robotic monitors extinguish them without a human in the ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: residual hot-spot detection and knock-down on a contained pile of burned refuse. Same objects (smoldering trash), same output (no remaining heat source), same precision, in a bay built around the machine — the machine equivalent of a firefighter's post-knockdown check of dumpster/refuse contents.

sources.system: FlameRanger with FORCE 50 BLDC robotic monitors
sources.title: Major Waste Site - Nobel Fire Systems (FlameRanger deployed at major waste site)
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic fire-suppression installation (six robotic monitors driven by IR detectors and a PLC) is in service at a UK waste and recycling facility, activating automatically on detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic re-check and knock-down of heat in a contained burned pile. Shows machine-only detect-and-wet coverage of stored burned material in a purpose-built bay, the E1 analogue of a firefighter re-checking contained burned contents.

sources.system: Hyundai Motor Group unmanned firefighting robot
sources.title: Autonomous firefighting robot can drive straight into a 1,000 degree blaze | Popular Science
sources.claim: The newest fire-service ground robot fielded (Hyundai's unmanned firefighting robot, donated to two Korean stations) is a driverless suppression and reconnaissance platform sent ahead of crews, not a post-fire overhaul inspector.

sources.system: Ground robots for wildfire risk reduction (survey of fire services)
sources.developer: academic survey (Elsevier, Safety in Extreme Environments-type review)
sources.title: Ground robot technologies in wildfire risk reduction. The viewpoint of the fire service - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed fire-service assessment finds ground robots are not in common use in wildfire work.

tasks.label: Patrol burned areas after fires to locate and eliminate hot spots that may restart fires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Overhaul and re-check of a burned single-family home or apartment after knockdown: firefighters move through smoke-filled, debris-strewn rooms, sweep with a thermal imaging camera, pull ceilings, open walls and void spaces with pike poles and hooks, dig into charred furnishings and insulation, and wet down each hot spot until cold.

Wildland/brush fire mop-up in the black: crews grid steep, uneven, ash-covered terrain among snags and stump holes, chop and grub smoldering stumps and root systems with Pulaskis and shovels, stir and mix dirt with hot ash, apply water from hose lays or backpack pumps, and cold-trail the edge by feeling with a bare hand.

Grass, roadside, or vacant-lot fire mop-up in the wildland-urban interface: a smaller blackened area next to roads, fences and yards; firefighters walk the burn, wet down smoking fence posts, mulch, tires and debris with a hose line or water can, and rake apart smoldering piles.

Overhaul of a burned vehicle, dumpster, mulch/debris pile or trash-compacted load: firefighters break apart and spread the burned contents with rakes, pike poles or an assisting loader, then saturate deep-seated smoldering material until no heat remains.

Extended post-fire patrol/fire watch over a burned area (a WUI neighborhood or several acres of black) for hours or days: driving and walking the perimeter and interior, scanning for smokes at night and in wind, and knocking down any hot spot found before it can re-establish.

sources.system: DJI Matrice/Mavic thermal drones with Nova workflow (LAFD)
sources.developer: DJI / Nova / Los Angeles Fire Department
sources.title: Drone-powered Hot Spot Detection after Wildfires
sources.claim: Drone thermal mapping is used in wildfire mop-up with LAFD to identify hot spots, but the workflow covers detection/mapping only; elimination of the hot spots remains with ground crews.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = aerial hot-spot detection during mop-up. It substantiates only the 'locate' sub-step; no cited system performs the digging, stirring and wetting needed to eliminate hot spots, so it cannot support completion of the whole instance.

sources.system: Sikorsky MATRIX autonomous Black Hawk with Rain wildfire mission autonomy
sources.title: Rain and Sikorsky Test Advanced Aerial Firefighting Technologies Using Autonomous Black Hawk Helicopter
sources.claim: An autonomous Black Hawk with Rain mission autonomy located a staged fire and dropped water on it in a California demonstration; the capability is aerial suppression of visible fire, not ground mop-up of residual heat.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous initial-attack water drop on a staged burn. Bulk aerial water does not substitute for gridding the black, digging out smoldering stumps and cold-trailing, so it does not transfer to hot-spot elimination at worker quality.

sources.developer: Hyundai Motor Group / Korea National Fire Agency
sources.title: Autonomous firefighting robot can drive straight into a 1,000 degree blaze
sources.claim: Hyundai's Unmanned Firefighting Robot is a six-wheeled driverless suppression vehicle with a hose and thermal sensors being tested at two Korean fire stations; it sprays water but has no manipulator for opening walls, digging out stumps or stirring ash.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = ground fire suppression with a water monitor on the fireground. It shows current fireground UGVs deliver water only; mop-up/overhaul requires tool work on charred material, which this platform cannot perform.

sources.title: BurnBot can help US fight wildfires with safer, prescribed burns
sources.claim: State-of-the-art wildland fuel robots working in the same vegetation and terrain as mop-up are operated remotely by trained personnel rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = machine work on wildland fuels in burned/burnable terrain. It is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive autonomy judgment for hot-spot elimination.

sources.title: Prediction and prevention: Robotic applications for wildfire management
sources.claim: Robotic units used in the mop-up phase today are remotely operated and limited to scanning/monitoring hot spots rather than eliminating them.

sources.system: human mop-up practice (baseline for accepted output)
sources.title: Understanding Mop-Up Operations in Wildfire Suppression
sources.claim: Accepted mop-up output is labor-intensive hand-tool work: turning over and breaking apart burning material, cooling ash pits, felling fire-damaged trees, and cold-trailing by feeling the ground with the back of the hand.

tasks.label: Take action to contain any hazardous chemicals that could catch fire, leak, or spill.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motor-vehicle crash or disabled vehicle on a public road/parking lot: engine company confines a gasoline/diesel/oil leak — plug or upright the leaking tank, deploy absorbent or a dike to keep product out of storm drains, apply foam blanket if needed, then wash down. Traffic, weather, and bystanders present.

Odor-of-gas or leaking propane/natural gas call at a private residence or small business: crew meters the structure with a 4-gas detector, finds the source (appliance line, meter, damaged service, tipped 20-lb or 500-gal LP tank), shuts the valve or has utility isolate it, ventilates, and secures the area.

Leaking or spilled container at an institution-controlled commercial/industrial site (warehouse, plating shop, water plant, lab, loading dock): hazmat team in PPE identifies the product from labels/placards/SDS, plugs or patches the drum or tote, dikes and absorbs the pool, overpacks the container, and turns it over to a cleanup contractor.

Unknown or mixed household/illicit chemicals in a dwelling or vehicle (spilled pool chemicals, mercury, clandestine lab or reactive waste): crew isolates, identifies with field detection, and packages or neutralizes the material amid clutter, furniture, and unknown layout.

Cargo tank truck, intermodal tank, or rail car leak at a highway crash or rail siding: large-scale containment — earthen/absorbent dikes, foam blanket for vapor suppression, patching a valve or shell breach, cooling exposures, and coordinating product transfer.

At a working fire or industrial incident, act to keep stored flammable/hazardous material from igniting or spreading: wet down and cool exposed propane cylinders, drums, or IBCs and lay a foam/water blanket over a flammable-liquid pool within a defined area.

sources.system: Telerob teleMAX Hybrid UGV (TU Darmstadt / German Rescue Robotics Center task force)
sources.developer: Telerob / TU Darmstadt SIM Group with DRZ
sources.title: Lessons from the Field: A Case Study of Robotic Intervention in an Industrial Emergency
sources.claim: A UGV (Telerob teleMAX Hybrid) was deployed at a German chemical plant after a fire to open a valve and inert a reactor containing shock-sensitive explosive gas — a real hazardous-chemical containment intervention — but the robot was manually teleoperated throughout, with no autonomy or assistance functions available.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task: acting on a hazardous chemical release (opening an inerting valve on a reactor) at an industrial incident. It shows the state of practice for robotic hazmat intervention is direct teleoperation.

sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The first US fire-service firefighting robot, in service with LAFD, is a remotely operated tracked vehicle with a monitor nozzle; it has no autonomous capability and cannot perform manipulation such as plugging, patching, or valve work.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fielded fire-service robot for hazardous fire/spill scenes; establishes that fire-ground robots in US departments require continuous human control.

sources.title: Colossus firefighting robot - Shark Robotics
sources.claim: The most widely fielded European firefighting UGV, used at Notre-Dame and in industrial plant fires, is fully remote-controlled by a firefighter operator.
sources.transferJustification: Same work domain (fire and industrial hazardous incidents); shows that even in institution-controlled plants the fielded machines are teleoperated, not autonomous.

sources.system: FlameRanger (Unifire Force robotic nozzle + flame detection)
sources.title: Waste & Recycling – Unifire
sources.claim: A commercially sold, fully automatic robotic nozzle system detects fires or hotspots with IR/thermal flame detectors and automatically aims and discharges water or foam onto flammable material within its covered zone, without human intervention; it is marketed and installed for waste, recycling and other flammable-material storage occupancies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic detection and application of water/foam onto flammable material to stop ignition spreading. It transfers to the 'wet down / foam-blanket flammable material in a defined bay' instance — same agent, same stream-application action, same class of flammable solids/liquids — but only within a fixed, engineered coverage zone.

sources.system: ANYmal with Gas Leak and Presence Detection
sources.title: ANYbotics Launches New Gas Leak & Presence Detection Solution for its ANYmal Inspection Robot
sources.claim: An autonomous quadruped inspection robot deployed on oil, gas and chemical sites automates gas concentration measurement and leak ..., but its capability stops at detection and reporting — it has no manipulator and performs no isolation, plugging, or containment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous gas-leak location in industrial facilities. It covers only the size-up half of the gas-leak instance; no cited system closes a valve or otherwise stops the release autonomously.

sources.title: 6 Alternatives to Fire Sprinkler Systems - Fire Rover
sources.claim: The leading commercial early-suppression system for hazardous-material fires in waste and recycling facilities relies on remote human operators to verify the threat and trigger and aim the suppression stream.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preventing hazardous-material (e.g., lithium battery) fires in stored waste. Shows human operators remain in the loop for the judgment and aiming steps in this closest commercial analogue.

sources.system: Water Cannon Robot and Hose Extension Robot ('Scrum Force' Firefighting Robot System)
sources.developer: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries with Japan's Fire and Disaster Management Agency
sources.title: MHI Develops Autonomous "Water Cannon Robot" and "Hose Extension Robot" for Use in Firefighting
