sources.claim: A firefighting robot system built for petrochemical-plant fires and fielded with a Japanese fire department navigates autonomously to a mapped position and lays hose automatically, then discharges water or foam to extinguish and cool; the aiming/discharge decisions are made through an operator command system, so end-to-end autonomy of the suppression action is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cooling and foam application at petrochemical hazardous-material fires. Cited for context only; autonomy of the suppression action itself is unclear, so it does not support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Prepare written reports that detail specifics of fire incidents.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Protect property from water and smoke, using waterproof salvage covers, smoke ejectors, and deodorants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-family house fire, post-knockdown salvage: crew works in a smoke-filled, water-soaked, partially charred dwelling with debris and low visibility; they spread canvas/vinyl salvage covers over furniture, electronics and heirlooms, bundle and carry out valuables, sweep/squeegee/channel standing water out doors or into catch-alls, and set an electric smoke ejector or PPV blower in a window/doorway with an exhaust opening to clear smoke.

Apartment or multi-family building fire: firefighters protect units below and adjacent to the fire apartment from water running through ceilings and floors - covering furniture and belongings, building tarp 'water chutes'/catch-alls, punching drains, and running smoke ejectors in stairwells and public hallways to clear smoke from unaffected units; layouts and contents differ apartment to apartment.

Commercial, retail, warehouse or institutional building fire: crews cover or relocate stock, merchandise, records, computers and machinery with salvage covers before and during suppression, divert water from sprinkler and hose streams away from goods, and set multiple large smoke ejectors/PPV fans to ventilate a big, smoke-logged space cluttered with racking and fire debris.

Non-fire water emergency (burst pipe, broken sprinkler head, failed water heater, storm intrusion) in a home or small business: firefighters shut off the water, cover or move contents with waterproof salvage covers, catch and channel dripping water, vacuum or squeegee standing water, and place fans to dry the space before turning it over to the owner or a restoration contractor.

Smoke/odor-only call with little or no fire damage (food on the stove, burned-out motor, electrical odor, small contained fire): crew locates and removes the source, sets a smoke ejector in a window or door to clear smoke and CO, checks the space with a gas meter, and applies deodorant/odor-neutralizer before returning the occupancy to the owner.

sources.date: 2020-10 (in service; still in use per 2024-2025 trade press)
sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The most capable fireground robot fielded by a US fire department, the Thermite RS3 used by LAFD since 2020, is a remotely operated water-flowing vehicle; it performs no salvage-cover, water-removal or deodorizing work and is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Same occupational setting (structure fires) - cited to show the best-fielded fireground robot is teleoperated and limited to suppression, not salvage/ventilation work.

sources.title: Colossus firefighting robot - Shark Robotics
sources.claim: Colossus, the fire-service UGV used by the Paris Fire Brigade (including at Notre-Dame), can carry a smoke-extraction fan into a structure, but it is piloted remotely by a firefighter at all times.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: smoke extraction on the fireground. Cited to show that even the ventilation portion of this task is done under continuous remote control, not autonomously, and that no salvage-cover or deodorizing function exists.

sources.title: Robotic Technology for Safety: The Story of 'A Safer Way Home' and the Advancement of Physical AI
sources.claim: Hyundai's Unmanned Firefighting Robot, donated to the Korea National Fire Agency, has only autonomous-driving assistance; mission functions are performed under remote control by an operator, and its payloads are suppression/monitor equipment, not salvage covers or ejectors.
sources.transferJustification: Newest fireground robot; cited to establish that autonomy in fire-service robots today covers mobility only, with mission work remote-controlled.

sources.title: Oswego County Uses Spot to Keep the Community Safer
sources.claim: Fire departments' legged robots (Boston Dynamics Spot at FDNY, Oswego County) are used inside fire buildings only as sensor carriers for thermal imaging and atmospheric assessment; they perform no salvage, covering, ventilation or water-control manipulation.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (interior of a fire building) - cited to show the only mobile robots that enter such spaces carry sensors, and no cited system manipulates tarps, fans or contents there.

sources.title: Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport to Deploy Floor Cleaning Robot
sources.claim: Autonomous floor-scrubbing robots pick up water from hard floors in structured facilities (airports, malls, hospitals) without pre-programmed routes, but they only clean open floor - they do not cover contents, divert dripping water, place ventilation fans, or work over fire debris.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of water from floors in an institutional building (E2). Transfer is partial only - the object (clear standing water on a level, obstacle-free floor) and conditions (intact, lit, no debris) differ from a post-fire salvage scene, and no covering/ventilation/deodorizing capability exists.

sources.title: Breezy One disinfecting robot deployed at Albuquerque International Sunport airport
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots dispense a chemical fog through large institutional spaces at night (Albuquerque airport), showing that space-wide chemical treatment can be automated in a structured facility, but the robot only drives and sprays - it does not locate a smoke source, place or run an ejector, or handle contents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous whole-room chemical fogging, comparable to applying deodorant to a smoke-affected space. Transfer covers only that sub-step; the instance also requires source removal, fan placement and atmospheric clearance, which this system cannot do.

sources.title: Stretch Hood Machines - Secure Pallet Protection (Votech)
sources.claim: Fully automatic stretch-hood machines pull waterproof film over palletized loads in packaging lines, an automated purpose-built way to protect goods from water - but only for uniform, conveyor-presented pallets, not irregular building contents in place.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-applied waterproof covering of goods in a purpose-built cell (E1). Considered for the E1 counterfactual, but it covers only regular palletized loads presented by conveyor and performs none of the water diversion, ventilation or deodorizing that the instance also requires.

sources.title: Unfolding the Literature: A Review of Robotic Cloth Manipulation
sources.claim: Robotic manipulation of large fabrics (sheets, blankets, quilts) remains a laboratory research problem; demonstrated systems smooth sheets and spread quilts on beds in controlled setups, far short of dragging and deploying heavy salvage covers over varied furnishings at worker reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of large deformable covers. Cited to bound capability - these are lab demonstrations on beds/tables, not deployment-grade covering of furniture in a damaged building.

tasks.label: Inspect buildings for fire hazards and compliance with fire prevention ordinances, testing and checking smoke alarms and fire suppression equipment as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-service company inspection of a small commercial occupancy (strip-mall retail store, restaurant, small office): engine company walks the tenant space and back-of-house, checks that exits are unlocked/unobstructed and exit signs and emergency lights work (press test buttons), verifies extinguisher mounting, gauge and annual service tag, checks 18-inch sprinkler clearance, blocked electrical panels, extension cords/power strips, kitchen hood system tag and filters, address numbers and Knox box; then discusses findings with the manager and writes an inspection report/violation notice with code citations.

Inspection of a large institutional or multi-unit building (school, hospital wing, hotel, apartment complex, distribution warehouse): multi-floor walk-through with stairwells and elevators, fire alarm control panel checked for trouble/supervisory signals and current test tag, sprinkler riser valves supervised and open, FDC caps and standpipe hose valves, fire/smoke doors closing and latching, storage clearances and high-piled racking, generator/emergency lighting, review of contractor test records; occupants and staff present throughout.

Residential smoke alarm and home fire safety visit (public-education/alarm-installation program or complaint-driven dwelling check): crew enters a private home, tests existing ceiling-mounted smoke and CO alarms with the test button or aerosol, replaces batteries or installs new alarms with drill and screws, checks heating appliances, dryer vent, extension cords, exits and escape plan, and explains findings to the occupant.

Witnessing or conducting periodic/acceptance testing of fire protection systems at a commercial building: sprinkler main-drain or inspector's-test flow, water-flow alarm transmission to the monitoring company, fire pump churn/flow test, fire alarm device-by-device test with the contractor, kitchen hood suppression discharge/tag verification; requires operating valves, reading gauges, coordinating with the alarm company, and signing off on results.

Inspection of an active construction site or industrial/hazardous occupancy: temporary standpipes and fire protection during construction, hot-work permits and welding operations, fuel storage and dispensing, hazmat placards and SDS, aerosol/flammable liquid storage in an industrial yard; layout changes week to week, trades working, debris and open floors.

Outdoor and special-event fire-prevention inspections: temporary tents and carnival/fireworks stands, food trucks with propane and hood suppression, fire hydrant access and clearance surveys, and defensible-space/weed-abatement checks on residential parcels in the wildland-urban interface.

sources.system: Spot (with Smart Inspection software), Wien Energie "Energy Dog"
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Wien Energie / Smart Inspection
sources.title: Spot Makes Austria's Largest Power Plant Safer | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot has run autonomous inspection routes at Wien Energie's Simmering power plant since 2022, automatically photographing fire-safety equipment such as fire extinguishers and reading analog gauges at predetermined waypoints; software then counts whether the prescribed extinguishers are present. This is a fixed-route visual presence check inside an industrial plant, not a code-compliance inspection with device testing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine industrial inspection rounds that include photographing fire extinguishers. It is the closest deployed analogue to a fire-prevention inspection, so it bounds what is demonstrated: presence/appearance checks on a pre-trained route, with no testing of alarms or suppression equipment, no opening of doors or panels, and no judgment of ordinance compliance.

sources.title: Automated Perimeter Security | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets Spot for automated health-and-safety patrols that can detect trip hazards, confirm fire ..., and flag open doors; assessing suspected hazards, however, is done by teleoperating the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: facility safety patrol in industrial/commercial premises. It covers a few observational sub-items of a fire inspection (extinguisher obstruction, propped doors) but the same page shows hazard assessment relies on teleoperation, and nothing demonstrates testing alarms or suppression systems or issuing code findings.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously patrols mapped office and commercial interiors around the clock, running scheduled facility and environmental checks and flagging anomalies such as open doors or leaks, with remote human specialists piloting the robot when an event is detected.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor patrol of a structured human workplace. It shows reliable autonomous navigation and anomaly flagging in E2 interiors, but the deliverable is a security alert reviewed by a human, not a completed fire-code inspection with equipment testing and written violations.

sources.system: Kiwa/Vinçotte smoke-detector inspection drone (aerosol canister payload, patent pending)
sources.title: Drone Inspection of smoke detectors | Kiwa
sources.claim: The commercially offered method for checking smoke detectors at high ceilings in industrial buildings uses a drone carrying an aerosol canister that is flown and aimed by a qualified Vinçotte/Kiwa inspector on site, i.e. a piloted tool rather than an autonomous inspection robot.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the sub-step 'testing smoke alarms'. Because the drone is hand-piloted by the qualified inspector who still performs and certifies the inspection, it cannot support an autonomous-completion judgment at any tier.

sources.title: Towards automatic smoke detector inspection: Recognition of the smoke detectors in industrial facilities and preparation for future drone integration
sources.claim: Autonomous smoke-detector inspection remains at the perception-research stage: a 2026 study reports only object-detection models for recognizing smoke detectors, described as a component that could later be integrated into a drone inspection system.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (smoke detector inspection). It substantiates the absence of a fielded autonomous system: as of 2026 only the recognition module exists, with drone integration stated as future work.

tasks.label: Collaborate with police to respond to accidents, disasters, and arson investigation calls.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Motor-vehicle collision on a public street or highway, dispatched jointly with police: engine company arrives, blocks lanes and sets traffic control with the officers, stabilizes vehicles, mitigates fuel/electrical hazards, forces doors or cuts roof/posts with hydraulic tools to extricate trapped occupants, packages patients for EMS, then exchanges scene information (vehicle positions, occupants, hazards) with the officer writing the crash report. Night, rain, live traffic, bystanders.

Structure or vehicle fire where police are on scene for perimeter, evacuation and traffic control: firefighters size up, stretch lines, force entry, search for occupants, suppress, ventilate and overhaul, while coordinating face-to-face and by radio with officers on evacuation of adjacent occupancies and control of onlookers/occupants.

Suspicious or incendiary fire generating an arson investigation call: fire crew or fire investigator secures and preserves the scene with police, works the burned structure/vehicle — digging out debris, reading burn patterns, photographing, collecting and packaging accelerant samples with chain of custody — and briefs police detectives/ATF, sometimes standing by for witness interviews.

Large-scale disaster or multi-agency incident (tornado, flood, severe storm, building collapse, mass-casualty crash, rescue task force at a violent incident): unified command with police, area search and rescue across damaged/flooded terrain, triage and treatment of victims, hazard mitigation (gas, wires, debris) over many hours or days with shifting conditions.

Other joint police-fire calls: wires down, gas leak or odor investigation, vehicle into a building or waterway, forced entry on a welfare check, standby at a police scene or barricaded subject, water/ice or animal rescue — firefighters mitigate the hazard and provide manpower/lighting while police control the area and the people involved.

sources.system: Hyundai Motor Group Unmanned Firefighting Robot (HR-SHERPA)
sources.title: Hyundai Motor Group Donates Unmanned Firefighting Robots to Korea National Fire Agency for Safeguarding Firefighters
sources.claim: The most capable fielded municipal firefighting ground robot (Hyundai Rotem HR-SHERPA based, donated to Korea's National Fire Agency and used at a real factory fire) operates by remote control, not autonomously, and performs only water-cannon suppression and reconnaissance.
sources.transferJustification: Fire suppression/reconnaissance at incident scenes is the physical core of joint fire-police response; the source shows the fielded system is operator-driven and limited to one sub-step.

sources.title: Paris Firefighters Used This Remote-Controlled Robot to Extinguish the Notre Dame Blaze - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Colossus, the best-known firefighting robot in service with a major fire brigade (Paris, Notre Dame), is a remote-controlled machine that supports crews rather than working on its own.

sources.title: Autonomous navigation of non-perception firefighting robot through CCTV-informed vision sharing - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed 2025 work states that firefighting robots still depend on manual control or pre-input information and that full autonomy in fire scenes remains an open research problem because smoke defeats visual and LiDAR sensing.

sources.system: Skydio X10 with Dock for X10 / DFR Command
sources.title: FAQs about DFR: Drone as First Responder | Skydio
sources.claim: Deployed drone-as-first-responder systems fly fully autonomously from docks when triggered by a 911 call, but their output is live aerial video/situational awareness streamed to responders, not physical intervention at the scene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous first-response overwatch of accident/fire calls alongside police. It transfers only to the information-gathering fragment of the instance; the drone cannot extricate, suppress, treat patients, or collect evidence.

sources.title: Situational Awareness for Remote Investigation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Legged robots used by fire and police agencies at hazardous incidents (including FDNY) are marketed and operated for remote investigation and situational awareness under operator control.

sources.system: Wheeled/tracked/aerial robotic platforms for fire scene examination
sources.title: The Use of Robotics in Fire Scene Examination - Ohio Arson School
sources.claim: Robotics in fire-scene/arson examination is used as a remote documentation and access tool for unsafe structures; the investigative determination, sampling decisions and chain of custody remain with human investigators.

tasks.label: Salvage property by removing broken glass, pumping out water, and ventilating buildings to remove smoke.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Post-knockdown salvage and overhaul at a residential structure fire (single-family home or apartment): crews set positive-pressure ventilation fans at the doorway, open/clear windows and rake out broken glass, throw salvage covers over furniture and belongings, squeegee and vacuum standing water out of rooms, and carry valuables clear — all in a smoke-filled, debris-strewn, partly collapsed and unlit interior.

Water-removal call at a residence or small business: flooded basement or cellar from storm runoff, a burst pipe, or firefighting water. Firefighters carry in a portable/submersible or trash pump and generator, rig suction and discharge hose out a window or up the stairs to the street, pump the standing water down, then mop/vacuum the residue and check for hazards (fuel oil, energized circuits, submerged debris).

Smoke clearing and clean-up after a minor incident in a commercial or institutional building kept to a working standard (store, restaurant, school, office): burnt food/appliance or small contained fire, light smoke throughout. Crews set fans in doorways, open windows or run the building smoke-control system, meter the air until clear, mop up extinguisher/sprinkler water, and sweep glass from a forced-entry door.

Exterior property-securing after fire, storm or vehicle-into-building: raking remaining broken glass out of window frames and storefronts, sweeping glass off the sidewalk, covering broken openings with tarps or plywood, and tarping roofs — done from ladders or the street with hand tools amid traffic and bystanders.

Salvage in a large structure: pumping water out of a flooded parking garage, elevator pit, or high-rise floor after a sprinkler activation, and clearing smoke from stairwells and corridors with large mobile fans and the building's smoke-control equipment, working with building engineers over multiple floors.

sources.title: LAFD Debuts the RS3: First Robotic Firefighting Vehicle in the United States
sources.claim: The LAFD's Thermite RS3, the first US fire-service robotic vehicle, works on the fireground including pushing smoldering wet fire debris, but is operated by remote control with video feedback, not autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Closest fire-service analogue to salvage/overhaul (moving fire debris on the fireground); cited to show the deployed system is continuously teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: The first firefighting robot in America is here – and it has already helped fight a major fire in Los Angeles
sources.claim: At a large Los Angeles commercial fire the RS3 was used to push piles of smoldering wet ... to open a path for crews — debris handling in a burned structure, done under remote control.
sources.transferJustification: Debris clearing in a fire-damaged building is the nearest demonstrated analogue to removing broken glass and salvaging property; it is performed by a human pilot, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.title: Fire Departments Adopt Robotic Technologies for Their Operations
sources.claim: Fire departments' adoption of ground robots remains limited to pilot-operated machines; the LAFD RS3 was assigned to 39 commercial structure ... over three years, always with an operator at the controls.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the state of fireground robot deployment for tasks adjacent to salvage (debris pushing, hose work); all such use is remotely piloted.

sources.title: Colossus firefighting robot - Shark Robotics
sources.claim: Colossus, the tracked support robot used at Notre-Dame and by French fire brigades, offers smoke extraction and debris-zone work but is a remote-controlled machine always piloted by a firefighter.
sources.transferJustification: Smoke extraction is directly part of this task; the evidence shows the only fielded robot doing it is continuously teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous floor scrubbers (Tennant X6 ROVR, Avidbots Neo, Gausium Scrubber 50)
sources.title: 2026 Comparative Guide: Autonomous Commercial Cleaning Robots for Medium to Large Facilities
sources.claim: Commercial autonomous floor scrubbers (Tennant, Avidbots, Gausium) recover water from floors without an operator, but only inside facilities that have been pre-mapped and with supporting water-management infrastructure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous recovery of water from floors in structured facilities. Transfer fails here — scrubbers recover thin films on mapped, obstacle-free floors, not standing flood water in unmapped, glass- and debris-strewn post-incident spaces, and they do no glass removal or ventilation.

sources.title: Autonomous firefighting robot can drive straight into a 1,000 degree blaze
sources.claim: Hyundai's Unmanned Firefighting Robot, in testing at two South Korean fire stations, is a driverless water-cannon platform for suppression and search support; it performs no salvage, glass removal, water pumping or building ventilation.
sources.transferJustification: Most recent fielded fire-service robot; cited to show even the newest platform addresses suppression/reconnaissance, not the salvage, dewatering and ventilation work of this task.

tasks.label: Clean and maintain fire stations and fire fighting equipment and apparatus.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/weekly hard-floor care inside the station: sweeping and wet-scrubbing the concrete apparatus bay (oil drips, road salt, tracked-in grit), mopping hallways and kitchen floors, vacuuming dayroom/bunkroom carpet. Fixed layout, but rigs, hose carts, gear racks and crew move through; work is interrupted by calls.

Cleaning station restrooms, showers and locker rooms: toilets/urinals, sinks, mirrors, shower stalls, restocking paper/soap, emptying trash cans throughout the station. Commercial-style institutional fixtures, done on a daily housekeeping rotation.

Living-quarters and cab interior cleaning: kitchen dishes, counters, stove and refrigerator, wiping tables, making up bunks and changing linen, dusting, windows, plus wiping down/disinfecting apparatus cab interiors and EMS compartments. Cluttered, varied objects.

Washing the exterior of engines, ladders, tankers and ambulances after runs and on weekly detail day: pre-rinse, soap with brushes or foam, rinse road salt/mud from body and undercarriage, dry, wipe windows and chrome. Done in the bay or on the station apron.

Daily/weekly apparatus and equipment checks and preventive maintenance: SCBA bottle pressure and mask checks, starting and testing saws/generators/PPV fans, checking fluid levels, pump and light checks, inspecting ground ladders and hand tools, restocking compartments and EMS supplies, re-racking hose beds after use, minor repairs.

Machine cleaning/decontamination of hose and PPE at the station's wash equipment: running used 1.75in/5in hose through the hose washer and hanging it in the drying cabinet/tower, laundering turnout gear in the NFPA 1851 programmable washer-extractor and drying it, washing SCBA facepieces. Work is carried to fixed station wash machines.

sources.system: Avidbots Neo / Neo 2W autonomous floor scrubber
sources.date: 2022-04 (product line still marketed and deployed through 2025)
sources.title: Avidbots Neo Cleaning Robot Used by Many of the Newly Named Best Global Airports | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo, an autonomous floor-scrubbing robot, is deployed for routine hard-floor cleaning in large institutional facilities (airports, warehouses, universities), navigating around people and obstacles without an operator aboard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial hard-floor scrubbing in airports/warehouses. Transfers to a fire station apparatus bay and corridors: same machine class, same soils (grit, salt, oil film), same sealed-concrete/tile surfaces, comparable moving obstacles, and the station is an institution-kept facility.

sources.system: BrainOS-powered robotic floor scrubbers (e.g., Tennant T7AMR)
sources.title: About Brain Corp: Robotics, AI, and data-driven autonomy for autonomous machines
sources.claim: BrainOS-powered autonomous floor scrubbers (Tennant, Minuteman and others) operate at fleet scale in retail stores, grocery, airports and warehouses, cleaning tens of billions of square feet per year with no operator aboard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: janitorial floor scrubbing in human-occupied commercial facilities. Same equipment and soil types as apparatus-bay and station floor care; demonstrates worker-substitute reliability at scale on institution-controlled premises.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's Bathroom Cleaning Robot autonomously cleans commercial restrooms - toilets, urinals, floors - opens doors, picks up trash and refills itself, and is sold as a deployed monthly service in hospitals and airports.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (restroom cleaning and trash pickup) performed in another institution-controlled facility; fire-station restrooms and locker rooms use the same commercial fixtures the BCR is built around.

sources.title: Toilet-cleaning robot makes us feel better about all this AI business - New Atlas
sources.claim: Third-party reporting confirms the Somatic robot runs autonomously day to day after a one-time mapping/VR teaching setup performed remotely by the vendor.
sources.transferJustification: Independent confirmation of autonomy for the restroom-cleaning system cited above; establishes it is not continuously teleoperated.

sources.system: InterClean municipal drive-through and rollover gantry vehicle wash systems

sources.title: Municipal Vehicle Wash Systems - Cleaning Applications for City Vehicles | InterClean
sources.claim: InterClean builds automated drive-through, rollover/gantry and touchless wash systems for municipal fleets and lists fire trucks among the vehicles these systems are built to wash, with programmable wash modes configured per vehicle type.

sources.claim: In InterClean automatic wash bays the operator drives the vehicle ... bay and the machine executes the wash cycle without further human action.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the washing itself is machine-executed fixed automation, not step-by-step human control, once the vehicle is presented - the E1 presentation condition.

sources.date: 2025 (current product page; company supplying fire service since 1940)
sources.title: RotoJet Hose Washer - Circul-Air Corp.
sources.claim: Circul-Air's RotoJet hose washer is a purpose-built fire-service machine that mechanically washes fire hose in place of manual scrubbing; the same maker supplies the matching hose and PPE drying cabinets used in fire stations.

sources.system: Programmable NFPA 1851 gear washer-extractors sold to fire departments
sources.developer: commercial laundry equipment makers via fire-service distributors
sources.date: 2020-09 guidance article; equipment standard in US stations through 2026
sources.title: 5 must-haves for firefighting gear washers | FireRescue1
sources.claim: NFPA 1851-compliant cleaning of soiled turnout gear is performed by highly programmable front-load washer-extractors installed in fire stations, which run the full wash chemistry, temperature and extraction cycle automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (decontaminating turnout gear) done by fixed automation to the governing standard; the accepted output is gear cleaned to NFPA 1851, which the machine cycle produces.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report

sources.transferJustification: Bears on the station kitchen/bunkroom cleaning and multi-item equipment-check instances, which need general dexterous manipulation of varied objects; the leading systems are teleoperated and so cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Participate in physical training activities to maintain a high level of physical fitness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mandatory on-duty workout period in the fire station fitness room: the firefighter performs resistance training (barbells, dumbbells, machines), cardio on treadmill/rower/bike, and mobility work, frequently interrupted by alarms. The purpose is to build and maintain the firefighter's own cardiovascular and muscular capacity.

Job-specific functional conditioning on the apparatus floor or department training grounds, often in full turnout gear and SCBA: hose drags and advances, high-rise stair climbs with hose packs, rescue-dummy drags, ladder raises and extensions, sledge/Keiser force machine strikes, done as timed circuits.

Crew group PT led by a peer fitness trainer: calisthenics, HIIT circuits, kettlebell/bodyweight sessions in the bay, and group runs on streets and trails near the station, with the officer adjusting intensity for members returning from injury.

Periodic fitness assessment and preparation for it at a training academy or evaluation site: WFI/annual physical ability evaluations, CPAT-style event sequences, treadmill or step-test aerobic capacity measurement, strength and flexibility screening, with results recorded for the member's readiness file.

Off-duty individual conditioning maintained by the firefighter on personal time: running or cycling on public roads and trails, lifting in a home garage gym or commercial fitness club, swimming, on days between shifts.

tasks.label: Orient self in relation to fire, using compass and map, and collect supplies and equipment dropped by parachute.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Smokejumper load lands in remote, roadless timber near a new start: jumper orients with map/compass/GPS to the smoke and the cargo spot, then hikes to locate and retrieve 3-6 paracargo boxes (chainsaws, pumps, hose, fuel, water, food; roughly 50-150 lb each) that landed under cargo chutes in brush, blowdown and uneven ground, dragging or carrying them to the jump spot.

Paracargo hangs up in the tree canopy or lands on a steep, rocky or brush-choked slope; the firefighter must climb or rig, cut suspension lines, lower the bundle, and recover it downslope without damaging contents.

Open meadow, old burn or clearing used as the cargo spot: boxes land in the open near the fire, firefighter walks bearings from a known point, collects the boxes and carries them to the fireline staging point.

Recovery of the cargo parachutes and rigging themselves: pulling canopies and lines out of brush and small trees, shaking out, rolling and stuffing the nylon canopies into cargo/pack-out bags so nothing is left on the ground.

Orientation only: on arrival (after the jump, or after being flown/hiked in), the firefighter shoots bearings on the smoke column and terrain features, orients the map, fixes own position relative to the fire and the drop point, plans route in, escape routes and safety zone, and reports position.

Pack-out/consolidation: after the fire is out, gather all retrieved gear, tools and used chutes into pack-out bags of roughly 110 lb each and haul them 1-3 miles cross-country over unimproved terrain to a road, helispot or trailhead for pickup.

sources.system: FANUC robotic palletizing systems (M-410/M-710 series cells)
sources.developer: FANUC America / integrators (e.g., Motion Controls Robotics, Tinsley)
sources.title: Robotic Palletizing Systems | FANUC America
sources.claim: Industrial robotic palletizing cells routinely pick, orient and stack heavy boxes and industrial-sized bags (including ~100 lb bags) that are presented by conveyor in a purpose-built, fenced cell — the E1 analogue of picking up and staging a heavy supply box.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy case/bag palletizing and depalletizing. Transfer: the residual physical act in collecting a paracargo box once it is presented in a fixture is grasping and moving a 50-150 lb rigid/semi-rigid package to a staging position, which these cells do continuously at industrial reliability.

sources.title: Robotic Destrapper (RCU) | Signode
sources.claim: Purpose-built robotic cells autonomously locate and cut the straps/bands securing a load and remove them before the load is handled, i.e., freeing a strapped bundle is automated in a fixtured setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated strap detection, cutting and removal from a presented load. Transfer: paracargo boxes arrive strapped to a cargo chute; in a purpose-built cell the same detect-cut-remove operation frees the box before it is picked.

sources.title: Warehouse Automation | Boston Dynamics; From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator autonomously unloads floor-loaded cases up to 50 lb from trailers and builds palletized loads in warehouses; DHL had 10 units in production case unloading across three countries as of mid-2025 with an order for 1,000 more.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous collection of boxed supplies inside a structured facility. Shows the limit of current facility-grade box handling: clean, stacked cardboard cases up to 50 lb — not chute-draped, irregular bundles lying on open ground.

sources.title: Walmart brings autonomous forklifts to 4 distribution centers | Grocery Dive
sources.claim: Autonomous forklifts using machine vision and planning unload heavy palletized loads from trailers in distribution centers under a multi-year commercial deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous heavy-load pickup and transport in a controlled facility. Transfer: the haul portion of collecting and moving supplies is substantiated for palletized/containerized loads on prepared surfaces.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Legged robots run autonomous mapped inspection routes at hundreds of industrial sites, localizing themselves on a stored map and replanning around obstacles, having inspected over 130,000 industrial assets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous self-localization and route following against a stored map. Transfer: the informational core of 'orient self using compass and map' is machine localization plus route planning, done routinely by Spot in institution-controlled facilities.

sources.title: RACER Speeds Into a Second Phase With Robotic Fleet Expansion and Another Experiment Success
sources.claim: Fully unoccupied robotic vehicles navigated autonomously through 15 square miles of previously unseen off-road terrain with vegetation, trees, slopes, ditches and creek crossings, including at night, over 150 autonomous miles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous off-road localization and route planning in unfamiliar wildland terrain — the same capability a firefighter exercises when orienting to the fire and choosing a route in unmapped country.

sources.developer: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab / ANYbotics
sources.title: How robots learn to hike | ETH Zurich
sources.claim: A quadruped robot autonomously traversed a rough alpine hiking route (roots, scree, steps, slippery ground), climbing 120 vertical metres in 31 minutes without falls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous legged traverse of unimproved wildland terrain. Transfer: supports the mobility half of ground orientation and movement toward a fire in steep, unprepared country.

sources.system: Black Hawk with Sikorsky MATRIX and Rain wildfire mission autonomy
sources.title: Sikorsky & Rain demonstrate autonomous flight capability to combat wildfires
sources.claim: An optionally piloted helicopter running mission autonomy software autonomously took off, identified the location and size of ... fire, and dropped water on it during staged burns witnessed by California fire agencies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously fixing a fire's position and one's own position relative to it in wildland. Transfer: this is precisely the output of 'orient self in relation to fire', produced by machine sensing and georeferencing rather than compass and map.

tasks.label: Package collected pieces of evidence in securely closed containers, such as bags, crates, or boxes, to protect them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Structure fire scene, origin area: investigator kneels in wet, collapsed, soot-covered debris, transfers cut samples of charred flooring, carpet, padding or wood into unlined metal quart cans or nylon/Kapak bags for ignitable-liquid analysis, presses lids on or heat-seals bags, applies evidence tape, initials, dates and labels each container, and logs it for chain of custody.

Bulky or heavy artifacts recovered at the scene (space heater, range, dryer motor, electrical panel, wiring runs, mattress or furniture remnants, appliance controls): wrapped, cushioned and placed in boxes or wooden crates, taped/strapped shut and sealed, often needing two people and load-out through a damaged structure.

Vehicle fire or exterior/outdoor scene (roadside, driveway, tow yard, wildland origin area): fluid samples, burned components, ignition sources and comparison samples packaged into cans, bags and boxes in the open, in wind, mud or rain, then sealed and labeled at the tailgate of the investigator's vehicle.

Small non-debris items at the scene: lighters, matches, incendiary device fragments, documents, clothing, phones/electronics, timers — individually placed in paper bags, envelopes or small boxes (never plastic if wet/biological), folded and sealed with tamper-evident tape, initialed and labeled.

Back at the fire station, investigations office or property/evidence room: items are air-dried, repackaged into secondary containers, consolidated into boxes for shipment to the state lab, sealed with tape, labeled with case numbers and barcodes, and placed into the evidence locker.

sources.system: OSARO Robotic Bagging System (with Pregis automated bagger)
sources.title: OSARO and Zenni deploy robotic bagging system - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: OSARO's autonomous piece-picking robot, deployed at Zenni's Novato fulfillment center, picks individual customer-order items and places them into an automated bagging machine that seals and labels the bag — the same act of putting a collected item into a securely closed, labeled container.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: e-commerce bagging. Transfer: the physical act is identical to evidence bagging — grasp a small irregular item presented at a station, place it into the correct container, close/seal it, and label it correctly; OSARO notes the items are high-value special orders where mis-bagging is unacceptable, i.e. worker-level accuracy in a fixed cell.

sources.title: OSARO's AI-Driven Automation Enhances Fulfillment Speed and Accuracy | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: OSARO's AutoModel system in an e-commerce fulfillment center identifies, picks and places single items into bags, orienting each item correctly before the bag is sealed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order bagging. Transfer: confirms current (2026) deployed autonomy for placing varied individual objects into bags that are then sealed, which is the packaging step of this task when the item is presented at a station.

sources.system: Amazon made-to-fit paper bag and box-on-demand packaging machines
sources.title: Amazon to deploy automated packaging machines across Europe, reducing waste for millions of customer orders
sources.claim: Amazon has deployed automated packaging machines in fulfilment centres that measure each order, form a made-to-fit protective paper bag or corrugated box around the item and heat-seal or glue it closed, then label it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand protective packaging. Transfer: the purpose matches — enclosing an object of unknown size in a securely closed container that protects it in transit — and the machines run unattended on a conveyor line, i.e. with the work brought to the machine (E1).

sources.system: CMI Industries Denester automatic can lidding/sealing system
sources.title: Automatic can sealer - Making.com
sources.claim: Commercial automatic lidding/sealing equipment places and closes metal lids on friction-lid paint, glue and solvent cans on a production line — the same container type (unlined metal cans) used to seal fire-debris samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: paint-can lidding. Transfer: fire-debris evidence is sealed in exactly these unlined friction-lid metal cans; the machine performs the securing-closure step to a leak-tight standard when the can is presented on a conveyor.

sources.system: FANUC R-2000iC/165F and M-410iC palletizing cells
sources.title: FANUC R-2000iC/165F Robot | Heavy Payload Material Handling | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC heavy-payload palletizing cells use vision and conveyors to verify dunnage, pick heavy irregular parts (wheels), interleave protective sheets and band the finished load — the heavy-item crating/protecting analogue.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy-part packing with dunnage and banding. Transfer: comparable mass and awkward geometry to a recovered appliance or electrical panel, and the same operations — placing the item into a container with protective material and securing the closure — inside a fenced cell.

sources.title: The Extraordinary Robotic Sample-Gathering System of NASA's Perseverance Mars Rover
sources.claim: NASA's Perseverance Sample Caching System autonomously places each collected core into a sealing station where a mechanism ... a cap, then returns it to onboard storage; the sealing itself occurs in a purpose-built onboard station, not in the open terrain.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sample sealing and caching. Transfer supports E1 only: the containers are purpose-designed tubes handled by a dedicated internal mechanism with fixtured presentation, so it shows machine sealing of collected samples but not packaging of arbitrary charred artifacts in a fire-damaged structure.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics Expands Spot Product Line | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot Arm, the leading commercial field manipulator for damaged/industrial sites, grasps and manipulates objects only semi-autonomously or by telemanipulation, indicating that unstructured-scene object handling is not autonomous at worker quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field manipulation of arbitrary objects. Cited to show the limit: the best-deployed field manipulator still needs an operator for grasp-and-place, so no cited system packages evidence autonomously at an E3 or E2 scene.

sources.title: Inside an Autonomous Soil Sampling Robot | Central Valley Ag
sources.claim: Rogo's commercial autonomous soil-sampling machines still carry a human operator in the machine to bag the collected samples, showing that packaging field-collected samples into containers is not yet autonomous outdoors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field sample collection and bagging. Cited as a negative bound for E3: even with a purpose-built sampling rig on managed farmland, the bagging step is done by a person.

tasks.label: Conduct inspections and acceptance testing of newly installed fire protection systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wet-pipe sprinkler acceptance inspection in a new commercial or multifamily building still in construction/punch-list phase: witness the 200 psi 2-hour hydrostatic test, main drain test and inspector's-test-connection flow with waterflow alarm timing; verify head type/temperature rating, spacing, obstructions and clearance to storage, escutcheons, hanger and seismic bracing, FDC and signage, control valve supervision; compare against the approved shop drawings, review the contractor's material and test certificate, use ladders/lifts to view concealed piping, write corrections and reinspect.

Fire alarm system acceptance test in a new office, school, retail or apartment building nearing completion: 100% device functional test (aerosol smoke into detectors, heat detectors, duct detectors, manual pull stations, waterflow and tamper switches), notification appliance audibility/visibility checks with a sound meter, panel primary/secondary power, ground fault and trouble tests, sequence-of-operation verification (elevator recall, HVAC shutdown, door hold-open release, smoke control), and confirmation of signals at the supervising station; sign off or fail the test.

Fire pump and standpipe acceptance in a new high-rise or large industrial building: witness churn, 100% and 150% flow points using hose monitors or a flowmeter, record suction/discharge pressures and amperage, verify controller start/stop settings, automatic transfer switch and emergency power operation, jockey pump, relief valve, and 6-hour run for diesel; witness standpipe hydrostatic and flow tests at the topmost outlet; verify FDC and pressure-regulating device settings.

Commercial kitchen wet-chemical hood suppression acceptance in a new restaurant build-out: verify nozzle types, placement and coverage per the listing, appliance line-up, fusible links, manual pull location, duct and plenum protection, then witness a function test confirming agent line release, fuel/electric shutoff, hood damper closure, and alarm panel supervisory/alarm signal; verify Class K extinguisher and hood cleaning access.

Small residential new construction: NFPA 13D/13R sprinkler and interconnected smoke/CO alarm acceptance at a single-family home or townhouse under construction — flow/pressure test at the remote head, verify head placement and coverage, check the water supply arrangement, sound-test and interconnect-test alarms; conditions include unfinished floors, mud, ladders, and trades still working.

Special hazard system acceptance in an occupied, institutionally controlled facility where one room is newly fitted out (data center clean agent, MRI room, or paint spray booth suppression): verify cylinder charge, nozzle layout, detection and abort/release logic, witness the discharge or simulated discharge test, room integrity (door fan) test results, HVAC/damper interlocks and alarm panel integration, and pre-discharge notification.

sources.title: Case Study: Practical Autonomy on Construction Sites | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot running FieldAI's autonomy software walks active construction sites without prior maps or pre-planned routes and performs inspection and monitoring data capture during a job walk; it captures imagery/scan data but does not functionally test building systems or render code determinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous construction-site inspection walks. It establishes that a robot can traverse the E3 setting where fire protection acceptance testing occurs, but the capability shown is navigation and image/scan capture only — no actuation of test valves, no aerosol testing of detectors, no fire pump operation, and no code-compliance determination — so it does not carry over to conducting and accepting the tests.

sources.system: Spot-based fire safety equipment inspection system (Aziz et al.)
sources.developer: academic research team using Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: (PDF) Fully Autonomous Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Missions on a Legged Robot
sources.claim: A Boston Dynamics Spot ran autonomous fire-safety-equipment inspection missions inside a building, walking a predefined waypoint route while detecting fire extinguishers and visually inspecting them (gauge, label) with onboard cameras and learned models.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fire safety equipment (extinguisher) inspection in a building. It is the closest robotic analogue to fire inspection work, but it is purely visual presence/condition checking of portable equipment; acceptance testing of installed systems requires actuating devices, flowing water, running pumps and verifying installation against approved plans, none of which the system performs.

sources.title: Automation and digitalization with ANYmal the case at BASF - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal quadruped performs autonomous routine inspection rounds inside a chemical plant, reading gauges, taking acoustic measurements and thermal scans — perception-only inspection with no functional testing or manipulation of the equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous equipment inspection rounds in a structured industrial facility (E2). It shows the ceiling of deployed autonomous inspection — instrument reading and anomaly flagging — and does not include the device actuation, water flow, or pass/fail code judgment that acceptance testing of a fire protection system requires.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot's manipulator arm turns valves, flips levers and opens doors only semi-autonomously, initiated by an operator through a ... interface, rather than as an unsupervised autonomous manipulation capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: valve and lever manipulation, the physical action needed for main drain tests, control valve checks and pump test valves. Because the manipulation is operator-triggered rather than autonomous, it cannot support a positive judgment on autonomous completion of an acceptance test.

sources.system: Drone smoke-detector inspection system (Brno University of Technology)
sources.developer: Brno University of Technology et al.
sources.title: Towards automatic smoke detector inspection: Recognition of the smoke detectors in industrial facilities and preparation for future drone integration
sources.claim: Research toward drone-based inspection of installed smoke detectors in industrial facilities is still at the object-recognition stage as of March 2026; the airborne mechatronic subsystem that would actually apply test aerosol and evaluate detector activation remains future work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: functional testing of installed smoke detectors, the core of a fire alarm acceptance test. The paper shows only detector recognition and states the testing mechatronics and reliable indoor navigation are not yet built, so no robot completes even this sub-step autonomously.

sources.title: Remote Operated TESTanDRAIN Valve for Wet-pipe Fire Sprinkler Systems - Fire Engineering
sources.claim: AGF's RemoteTEST is a UL-listed/FM-approved solenoid-actuated inspector's test valve that flows water through the inspector's test connection on command from a switch or panel, automating one recurring sprinkler waterflow-alarm test step but performing no installation verification or acceptance determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: the sprinkler waterflow alarm test. It is a fixed, human-initiated actuator covering a single sub-step of one test; it does not inspect head spacing, hangers, clearances or documentation, and does not issue the acceptance, so it cannot complete the whole instance.

tasks.label: Analyze evidence and other information to determine probable cause of fire or explosion.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential structure fire: investigator reviews scene documentation (photos, diagrams, burn and char patterns), occupant and firefighter statements, utility and alarm data, and lab results, then reasons through NFPA 921 hypotheses to reach an area-of-origin and cause determination (accidental, incendiary, or undetermined) for the report.

Minor or routine incident (cooking fire, dumpster, chimney, grass/brush, small appliance fire): investigator weighs a small set of straightforward facts and witness accounts to classify the cause and code it for NFIRS reporting, usually same day.

Commercial or industrial fire/explosion: investigator correlates equipment maintenance records, electrical and gas system data, process documentation, engineering or product-failure lab findings, and recall history to identify the ignition source and first fuel ignited, often alongside outside experts.

Suspected incendiary fire: investigator integrates accelerant lab (GC-MS) results, ignitable-liquid detection canine alerts, video, phone/financial/insurance records, and interview inconsistencies to determine whether the fire was deliberately set, and defends the opinion under peer review and in court.

Vehicle fire: investigator analyzes damage documentation, wiring and fuel system findings, service history, and manufacturer bulletins to determine whether the cause was mechanical/electrical failure, external ignition, or intentional.

tasks.label: Photograph damage and evidence related to causes of fires or explosions to document investigation findings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single- or multi-family residential fire: investigator produces the full photographic record of one incident — exterior overview of all four sides, room-by-room interior overviews showing burn/V-patterns, mid-range and close-up shots of the area of origin, and detail photos with scales of suspected ignition sources (outlets, appliances, wiring, ignitable-liquid pour patterns) as debris is excavated. Scene is dark, wet, soot-covered, strewn with collapsed drywall and furnishings, with unstable footing.

Commercial, industrial, or large multi-family fire: same full photo documentation product but over a larger, more complex partially collapsed structure — machinery, electrical panels, sprinkler/alarm components, stock, plus exterior and interior views; often joint work with insurance/ATF, with photographs of items before and after removal.

Vehicle fire: burned car, truck, or RV photographed at roadside, driveway, or a tow/impound yard — all four sides and VIN, undercarriage, wheel wells, engine compartment with hood opened, passenger compartment and dash, plus close-ups of wiring, fuel lines, and arcing evidence.

Large-loss, collapsed, or otherwise unsafe fire scene documented from outside: overall establishing imagery of the whole property, roof and upper-floor damage, fire spread across exposures, and a scaled photogrammetric record captured before overhaul or demolition. Interior entry is restricted or prohibited, so the accepted deliverable is the comprehensive exterior/overhead photo set and model.

Bench/lab photography at the fire marshal's office or evidence facility: collected artifacts and exemplars (burned receptacle, appliance controls, lighter, arced conductors, sample cans) placed on a bench or copy stand and photographed with scale and identifier from multiple angles, including step-by-step photos during appliance disassembly.

Explosion or outdoor incident scenes: gas or dust explosion debris field, fireworks or grill fire, dumpster/brush fire, or wildland origin area — wide-area overview plus gridded ground-level photographs of scattered fragments, blast damage, and origin-area burn indicators, often over uneven terrain.

sources.title: Skydio autonomous drone programs for fire departments
sources.claim: Skydio markets and supplies X10 drones with 3D Scan software to fire departments specifically for post-fire cause-and-origin documentation, with the capture flight flown autonomously and data pushed to evidence management systems.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan | Autonomous Drone Flights for 3D Mapping
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan plans and executes the photo capture itself: the operator selects the area, then the drone discovers the structure's geometry and flies an obstacle-aware path that guarantees complete photographic coverage of complex outdoor structures.

sources.system: Skydio X10 3D scan at Katonah (NY) Fire Department
sources.title: Drones for the Fire Service: No Longer Flying Under the Radar (Firehouse)
sources.claim: A working fire service captain reports repeatedly using the X10's autonomous 3D scan capability on his department's structure fires, and trade press describes the feature as serving cause-and-origin fire investigation through photogrammetry.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan Release Notes / 3D Scan FAQ
sources.claim: Skydio's indoor capture mode is scoped to orderly interior spaces (construction sites, factories, warehouses); the product FAQ states 3D Scan does not support interior room scanning, indicating autonomous interior photo documentation is limited to structured, navigable spaces rather than debris-filled burned interiors.

sources.title: Automated Product Photography Equipment by PhotoRobot / Product Photography Glossary
sources.claim: Commercial robotic photography workstations (motorized turntable plus multi-generation robotic camera arm, driven by capture software) produce complete multi-angle still image sets of objects placed in the cell with minimal manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated multi-angle photography of small objects placed on a fixture. Fire-investigation bench photography of collected artifacts (a burned receptacle, lighter, appliance part) involves the same object sizes, working distances, lighting control and image-detail requirements, differing only in the metadata/scale placed alongside the item.

sources.system: Ortery PhotoBench / PhotoCapture 360 automated photography studios
sources.title: Forensic and Scientific Photography Examples Using Automation
sources.claim: The same class of automated lighting-studio/turntable photography systems is offered and illustrated for forensic and scientific item documentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated studio photography of evidence-type items. Transfers to photographing collected fire artifacts because the objects, fixturing, and documentation-image quality requirements are the same; only the chain-of-custody labelling differs.

sources.title: Cox Automotive's vAuto and UVeye Bring AI-Powered Vehicle Inspections to Market
sources.claim: Automated drive-through vehicle imaging systems installed at hundreds of US dealerships photograph a vehicle's exterior, underbody and tires in seconds and generate standardized damage imagery, but the coverage is exterior/underbody only and requires the vehicle to pass through a purpose-built arch.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated photographic damage documentation of a whole vehicle in a purpose-built imaging cell. Relevant to burned-vehicle documentation, but it images only exterior/underbody surfaces of a vehicle that drives through, not engine-compartment or passenger-compartment cause evidence.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics' Spot
sources.claim: Leica's BLK ARC autonomous laser-scanning payload on Boston Dynamics Spot can execute a previously recorded Autowalk mission without human intervention and is marketed for documenting enclosed structures including fire investigation; the route must first be taught by a human operator and the product is a point cloud rather than evidentiary photographs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous reality capture inside buildings. Cited to show the limits: missions are repeats of human-taught routes and yield LiDAR point clouds, so they do not substantiate autonomous evidentiary photography of a novel, debris-filled fire scene.

sources.system: Wheeled, tracked and aerial robots used in fire scene examination (general)
sources.developer: various (guidance published by Ohio Arson School)
sources.title: The Use of Robotics in Fire Scene Examination - Ohio Arson School
sources.claim: Fire-investigation training guidance treats robotic platforms as a supplement for hazardous-scene access and documentation, not a replacement for the investigator's interpretation and evidence work under NFPA 921.

tasks.label: Inspect buildings to locate hazardous conditions and fire code violations, such as accumulations of combustible material, electrical wiring problems, and inadequate or non-functional fire exits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine periodic inspection of a small commercial occupancy (restaurant, retail store, salon, storefront office): inspector walks the sales floor, kitchen/hood, stock room and rear exit; checks combustible storage and housekeeping, extension cords/power strips and panel clearance, extinguisher mounting/charge/service tag, exit door hardware operation and blocked or locked exits, exit signs and emergency lights, then writes a code-cited violation notice and reviews it with the owner.

Inspection of an institutional or assembly occupancy (school, church, nursing home, hospital wing): large fixed-layout building; checks corridor egress width and storage, fire/smoke door closing and latching, sprinkler head clearance, alarm and sprinkler test records, kitchen and boiler/mechanical rooms, occupant load and decorations; produces a formal inspection report.

Inspection of an industrial or warehouse occupancy: high-piled storage height and aisle/sprinkler clearances, commodity and hazardous-material storage and labeling, forklift battery charging areas, electrical rooms and panel clearances, exit access from racking aisles, fire pump and system records; report with code citations.

Inspection of a multifamily residential building: common corridors and stairwells, laundry and storage rooms, boiler/electrical rooms, trash chutes, self-closing fire doors, smoke alarm and extinguisher checks, sometimes entry into individual units with the occupant present.

New-construction or acceptance inspection on an active job site: partially built, cluttered structure with trades working; verifies fire-rated assemblies, firestopping, sprinkler/standpipe rough-in, alarm device placement, egress during construction and hot-work/temporary heat hazards; witnesses functional system tests.

Complaint-driven inspection or re-inspection: hoarding or heavy combustible accumulation in a dwelling or shop, reported blocked or chained exits, nightclub/event occupancy load check, or follow-up to confirm previously cited violations were corrected; often unannounced, with uncooperative occupants and variable cluttered conditions.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit performs autonomous, repeated inspection rounds inside industrial facilities, navigating pre-taught routes and collecting visual/thermal data on tens of thousands of assets; this is asset condition monitoring, not code-compliance determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine industrial asset inspection rounds. It transfers to the locomotion and imaging portion of a fire walkthrough (including thermal imaging of electrical gear), but only to pre-taught inspection points on known assets; it does not cover judging code violations, testing exit hardware, reading service tags/records, or issuing a citation.

sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Orbit 5.0 adds AI that automatically flags visual anomalies such as debris, ... from Spot's autonomous patrols; the flagged categories are maintenance anomalies against a learned baseline, not fire-code violations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: visual anomaly detection on autonomous patrols. Closest commercial analogue to spotting 'accumulations of combustible material', but it detects deviation from a baseline image at fixed waypoints rather than classifying storage, clearances and egress obstruction against code.

sources.title: Robotic inspection solution capabilities - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal executes taught inspection missions autonomously in industrial plants, reading gauges and capturing thermal and acoustic data without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plant inspection rounds. Shows reliable autonomous traversal of a human-built industrial facility, but the mission is a fixed list of pre-taught inspection points on process assets; no demonstration of fire-code assessment, manipulation of doors or panels, or violation reporting.

sources.claim: Research case study: a legged robot autonomously ran a predefined route on one ... and detected fire safety equipment (extinguishers, emergency call points, smoke detectors, fire safety signs) with a vision model — presence detection only, on a taught route.

It substantiates only detection of the presence of equipment classes on a mapped route; it does not test exit doors or emergency lighting, judge combustible accumulation or wiring hazards, or produce an inspector-quality code report.

Transfer is partial: the robot monitors designated machines, not the building's egress, storage and wiring compliance as a whole.

sources.title: Levatas' AI Robot Dogs Train as Safety Inspectors in Florida
sources.claim: Levatas trains Spot inspection AI in a lab that mocks up industrial scenes, including change detection for a missing fire extinguisher; the capability is shown in a company test lab rather than as an accepted fire inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: safety-equipment change detection. Even at face value it covers only whether a known extinguisher is present, not its charge, service tag, mounting, obstruction or any other code item; autonomy of the lab demonstration is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Examine fire sites and collect evidence such as glass, metal fragments, charred wood, and accelerant residue for use in determining the cause of a fire.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fire-gutted single-family home or apartment: investigator walks the burned structure over collapsed ceiling material, standing water and unstable flooring, reads burn/char patterns to isolate the origin area, hand-excavates and layers debris back, and collects charred wood/flooring, carpet and pad, glass and metal fragments plus a comparison sample into clean vapor-tight metal cans and nylon bags, sealing, labeling and logging each for chain of custody.

Commercial or industrial fire (restaurant, retail store, warehouse, small plant): larger footprint, partial collapse, heavy overhaul debris, machinery and stock to move; investigator identifies and recovers electrical panels, appliance components, ignition-source artifacts and accelerant-residue samples, coordinating with utility and safety personnel before the scene is released.

Vehicle fire: burned car or truck examined at a secured tow yard, impound lot or agency garage bay; investigator inspects the engine compartment, wiring, fuel system and passenger compartment, cuts/removes suspect components, and collects seat foam, carpet and fluid samples into evidence containers.

Wildland or outdoor fire (brush, grass, vehicle-adjacent roadside, trash/dumpster fire): investigator reads fire-spread indicators over terrain, flags and protects the specific origin area, then sifts soil and ash and recovers matches, cigarettes, incendiary-device remains, fusees or fragments of failed equipment, with soil comparison samples.

Small contained fire in an otherwise intact occupied dwelling or small business (kitchen appliance, space heater, electrical outlet, lithium-battery device): limited damage, confined room; investigator documents patterns, removes the suspect appliance or wiring section intact, and collects nearby char/residue samples for laboratory examination.

Explosion or fatal/large-loss fire requiring systematic grid excavation: multi-agency scene with layered debris removal, shoring, sifting screens and recovery of hundreds of fragments (glass, metal shrapnel, device components) with mapped locations for reconstruction.

sources.system: Leica BLK ARC on Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Introducing BLK ARC and BLK2FLY laser scanners | HxGN Spotlight
sources.claim: An autonomous laser-scanning module mounted on Boston Dynamics' Spot is marketed and used for fire and crime scene documentation; it captures 3D reality data autonomously but performs no physical evidence collection (no excavation, sampling, or packaging).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous reality capture at fire scenes. It shows mobile robots can traverse and document a fire scene, but the cited capability stops at scanning; it substantiates no collection of glass, metal fragments, charred wood or accelerant residue, so it cannot support a positive judgment on this task.

sources.system: generic ground robots and drones used in fire scene examination
sources.title: The Use of Robotics in Fire Scene Examination - Ohio Arson School
sources.claim: A fire-investigation training organization's survey of robotics in fire scene examination describes camera/sensor-equipped ground robots and drones as operator-driven aids requiring specialized operator training, and states explicitly that robotics supplements rather than replaces the investigator's interpretation; no named autonomous evidence-collecting system is identified.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task survey; it names no specific autonomous system and lists operator training and navigation in extreme debris as limitations, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion at any tier.

sources.system: RAICo / NRS Oldbury robotic waste sorting trials (incl. Auto-SAS programme)
sources.developer: Robotics and AI Collaboration (RAICo), Nuclear Restoration Services, UK NDA
sources.title: Adapting robots to sort radioactive debris on decommissioning sites - RAICo
sources.claim: Robotic sorting of irregular rubble-like debris in the nuclear sector is being trialled in purpose-built decommissioning cells, but current working practice is teleoperated: operators watch screens and drive grippers to pick and allocate individual debris pieces; fully autonomous mixed-waste sorting remains a longer-term programme.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grasping and segregating irregular debris (metal, glass, rubble) inside a fenced/shielded cell — the closest analogue to picking evidence out of fire debris. It is teleoperated and occurs in an E1 cell with the material already delivered, so it cannot substantiate autonomous in-situ fire-scene evidence recovery.

sources.system: UK NDA radioactive waste sorting robots / Auto-SAS
sources.title: Radioactive waste-sorting robots to accelerate nuclear plant decommissioning | Engineering and Technology Magazine
sources.claim: UK nuclear decommissioning is trialling remote and autonomous sorting/segregation of radioactive waste, with the autonomous identification-and-categorisation element (Auto-SAS) described as a longer-term programme rather than a fielded capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous debris segregation in an engineered cell. Even taken at face value it covers sorting delivered waste into containers, not scene examination, origin-area excavation, selection of forensic samples, or vapour-tight packaging with chain of custody.

sources.system: n/a (task description of human fire investigator practice)
sources.title: 6.05 Ignitable Liquids — Forensic Science course text
sources.claim: Fire-debris evidence collection is defined by expert selection: the investigator must decide, from burn and pour patterns, which materials will yield ignitable-liquid residue and which to leave, and must also take comparison samples — a discrimination task no cited robotic system performs.
sources.transferJustification: Not robot evidence; it characterizes the acceptance standard for the task (selective, judgment-driven sampling plus comparison samples) against which the robotic evidence above falls short.
