tasks.label: Conduct fire code compliance follow-ups to ensure that corrective actions have been taken in cases where violations were found.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Re-inspection of a small commercial occupancy (restaurant, retail store, salon, office suite) during business hours: inspector meets the owner/manager, walks the sales floor, kitchen, storage and back-of-house, and re-checks the 2-6 cited items - extinguisher recharged and tagged within 12 months, exit door unblocked/unlocked with working panic hardware, exit sign and emergency light functioning (test button pressed), extension cords/junction boxes corrected, hood suppression tag current, storage clearance - then documents pass/fail, explains findings to the owner, and closes or re-cites the case.

Re-inspection of a multifamily residential property: common corridors, stairwells, laundry and boiler rooms plus entry into individual dwelling units to verify smoke/CO alarms installed and working, stored combustibles removed from stairwells and balconies, self-closing fire doors repaired, and unit egress clear; access depends on tenants being home and layouts and clutter differ unit to unit.

Re-inspection of an institutional or assembly occupancy (school, church, nursing home, hospital wing, bar/nightclub): meet the facility manager, review contractor documentation for corrected sprinkler/alarm/kitchen-suppression deficiencies, then walk corridors and back rooms to confirm fire doors latch and hold-opens release, corridor storage removed, occupant load and egress restored, exit lighting repaired; sign off in the records system.

Multi-item re-inspection of an industrial, warehouse or storage occupancy: verify storage lowered to maintain 18-inch sprinkler clearance, exit aisles and doors cleared, extinguishers remounted/serviced with current tags, 36-inch electrical panel clearance restored, flammable-liquid cabinets and hazmat labeling corrected, and hot-work/battery-charging areas fixed; write the report and close out.

Simple single-item visual re-check inside a large fixed-layout industrial plant or distribution center where the violation was an obstruction: confirm the blocked fire extinguisher/exit path or propped fire door noted in the notice has been cleared or restored, capture a dated photographic record, and close the item.

Follow-up at a construction/renovation site or temporary event venue: confirm the previously cited condition has been corrected - fire watch posted, standpipe/temporary water supply usable, apparatus access lane cleared of material and parked equipment, egress from work areas restored, extinguishers distributed, tent exits and separation corrected - amid changing site conditions, mud, trades working overhead and no fixed layout.

sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped runs autonomous patrols of a facility, photographs points of interest, and its Orbit software evaluates the images with vision-language prompts to flag safety issues such as spills or missing fire extinguishers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated health-and-safety rounds in an industrial facility. It touches the same objects a fire-code re-check touches (extinguishers, doors, obstructions) and yields a dated pass/fail record, so it transfers to a single-item obstruction re-check, but not to tag-date, latching or device-test items.

sources.title: Automated Perimeter Security | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics markets Spot for recurring health and safety inspection rounds in workplaces, including confirming fire extinguishers are unobstructed and flagging open or propped doors using change-detection vision models.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: recurring safety-compliance rounds. Same objects (extinguishers, doors, egress obstructions) in a human-built industrial facility; supports verifying that an obstruction violation has been cleared, not the multi-item code judgments of a full re-inspection.

sources.title: Spot Makes Austria's Largest Power Plant Safer | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: At Vienna's Simmering power plant a Spot robot has run trained inspection routes autonomously since 2022, automatically photographing fire-safety systems such as fire ..., with software checking the prescribed number of extinguishers is present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fire-safety equipment checks on fixed routes in a power plant. It is the closest real deployment to a single-item fire-code re-check of extinguisher presence/obstruction in a structured facility; routes must be pre-taught per site.

sources.title: ANYbotics | Siemens
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal performs autonomous routine inspection missions in process plants, navigating multi-floor facilities built for humans and checking equipment health and conformity with plant rules.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial inspection rounds. Shows mobile robots can autonomously reach inspection points in human-built plants (E2), but the checkpoints are equipment-condition readings, not fire-code corrective-action verification.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Doxel's lidar-equipped autonomous robots scan construction sites daily and use deep learning to verify that components have been installed correctly and ... the right place.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous as-built verification on construction sites (E3). It verifies installed work against a model, but not fire-code corrective actions (fire watch, standpipe usability, apparatus access, egress) or the inspector's determination.

tasks.label: Inspect properties that store, handle, and use hazardous materials to ensure compliance with laws, codes, and regulations, and issue hazardous materials permits to facilities found in compliance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Annual hazmat permit inspection of an orderly retail/service occupancy: gas station/convenience store (motor fuel dispensing, propane exchange cage, aerosol stock), dry cleaner, or nail salon. Inspector walks sales floor, back stockroom, mechanical/electrical rooms; opens flammable-liquid cabinets; checks container labels, closure and quantities against permit limits; verifies signage, extinguisher tags, exit paths, emergency shutoffs; interviews the manager, reviews SDS binder, writes findings and issues/renews the permit.

Inspection of a cluttered small trades occupancy: auto repair/body shop, welding or paint shop, small print shop. Variable layouts, oil-stained floors, parts and hoses on the ground, open waste-oil and solvent drums, spray booth filters, cylinder storage outside the roll-up door. Inspector verifies cabinet storage, cylinder restraint and separation, booth interlocks, waste accumulation limits, then documents violations or issues the hazmat permit.

Inspection of a warehouse/distribution center or manufacturing plant storing hazardous materials: racked aerosols and chemicals, flammable liquid storage rooms, forklift battery charging, plating or coating lines. Inspector walks aisles and process areas with a facility escort, compares the hazardous materials inventory statement to what is on the racks, checks segregation of incompatibles, secondary containment, gas cabinet ventilation, sprinkler clearance and exit obstruction, then issues the permit.

Inspection of an institutional facility: hospital, university research building, high school chemistry storage, or biotech/semiconductor site. Inspector checks lab chemical storage cabinets, fume hoods, compressed and cryogenic gas rooms, silane/toxic gas cabinets, medical gas storage, waste accumulation areas; reviews chemical inventories and hazardous materials management plans with the EHS officer before issuing permits.

Inspection of bulk hazardous materials storage, mostly outdoors on a controlled industrial site: propane distributor or LPG bulk plant, fuel bulk plant/tank farm, chemical process plant, cryogenic bulk tanks. Inspector examines tank spacing and impoundment, bollards, valves and relief devices, placards, transfer areas, electrical classification, emergency shutoff and fire protection, then issues or renews the operational permit.

Inspection of a temporary or ad hoc hazmat use taken as found: fuel tanks and fuel trailers on an active construction site, mobile fueling operations, agricultural pesticide or anhydrous ammonia storage, cannabis extraction rooms, seasonal fireworks stands. No fixed layout, changing conditions, uneven ground, work in progress around the inspector; inspector evaluates the setup against code and issues a permit or orders corrections.

sources.system: Spot with Spot CAM+IR, Teledyne FLIR MUVE C360 and Enhanced Autonomy Payload
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds inside an operating midstream gas plant, carrying thermal and gas-detection payloads, and autonomously detected a combustible gas plume from a pinhole leak during a routine round.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine plant safety/condition rounds in a hazardous-materials facility. It shows autonomous traversal and hazardous-atmosphere sensing in the same kind of premises a fire inspector visits, but the checkpoints are pre-taught on known assets and the output is an anomaly alert, not a code-compliance determination or permit.

sources.title: ANYmal X — The World's First Ex-Proof Legged Robot - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal X is an ATEX/IECEx Zone 1 certified legged robot marketed and sold for automating routine autonomous inspection rounds in oil, gas and chemical plants, including process areas with explosive atmospheres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inspection rounds inside chemical and fuel-handling plants. Comparable environment (hazmat process areas, stairs, tight passages), but the robot collects sensor readings on predefined assets; no evidence it evaluates storage against fire-code requirements or issues permits.

sources.system: Spot legged robot with YOLO-based fire safety equipment detection
sources.developer: Ruhr University Bochum (Aziz, Herbers, Bayer, König)
sources.title: Fully Autonomous Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Missions on a Legged Robot
sources.claim: A research study demonstrated a fully autonomous fire-safety-equipment inspection mission on a Spot legged robot in a building: the robot walked a predefined route autonomously, detected fire extinguishers with onboard cameras, and read maintenance date tags from the labels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fire safety equipment inspection, a narrow element of fire inspection work. It shows autonomous detection and tag reading on a pre-mapped route in one building, far short of surveying an unfamiliar hazmat occupancy, opening cabinets, checking quantities and segregation, and issuing a permit.

sources.title: SpotWalk comes to construction in HoloBuilder, Boston Dynamics teamup
sources.claim: Spot can autonomously walk construction job sites on repeated routes capturing 360-degree imagery for progress documentation, showing that the frontier capability in unstructured settings is data capture rather than regulatory assessment.

tasks.label: Inspect and test fire protection or fire detection systems to verify that such systems are installed in accordance with appropriate laws, codes, ordinances, regulations, and standards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic/annual inspection and functional test of a fire alarm and detection system in an occupied commercial or institutional building (office tower, school, hospital): walk all floors, operate manual pull stations, apply canned smoke or heat to a sample of ceiling- and duct-mounted detectors (often 10-30 ft up), verify audible/visual notification appliances, panel annunciation, battery and trouble/supervisory signals, confirm the monitoring center received signals, then reset, document on NFPA 72 forms and cite deficiencies against the approved plans.

Inspection and testing of water-based fire protection in an occupied commercial/industrial facility: riser and pump rooms, verify control valves open/locked/supervised, read water and air pressure gauges, perform or witness main drain and inspector's test valve flow tests with correct waterflow alarm timing, witness fire pump churn/flow test, check backflow preventer, verify sprinkler head type, spacing, clearance to storage and spare-head cabinet; write up violations.

Acceptance / rough-in inspection of newly installed fire protection and detection systems at an active construction site: partially finished building with open ceilings, ladders, debris and other trades working; verify device counts and locations against approved shop drawings, witness hydrostatic and flow tests, verify alarm cause-and-effect matrix (elevator recall, damper and door release, HVAC shutdown), and sign off or reject before occupancy.

Routine code inspection of a small business or mixed occupancy (strip-mall restaurant, retail store, salon, small office): test the kitchen hood suppression system tags/nozzle placement and fusible links, check portable extinguishers for presence, mounting, charge and current service tag, verify sprinkler head clearance and unobstructed exits, test the local alarm and emergency lighting, working around clutter and stock in back-of-house areas.

Inspection and testing of detection/protection systems in residential settings: apartment or condominium common areas and sampled dwelling units, group homes, and in-home daycares; test smoke/CO alarms and interconnection, check unit sprinkler heads for paint/obstruction, verify standpipes and alarm panel in the lobby, all inside occupant-controlled private spaces with varied furnishings and access constraints.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with autonomous fire-safety-equipment inspection mission (Aziz et al.)
sources.developer: academic research team (i3CE 2023 conference paper) using Boston Dynamics Spot
sources.title: Fully Autonomous Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Missions on a Legged Robot
sources.claim: A Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped autonomously walked a predefined route on one ... and used vision to detect fire safety equipment such as fire extinguishers, taking close-up photos of inspection tags; it is a research case study that only records images, performing no functional testing of detection or suppression systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous visual survey of fire-safety equipment inside a building. It is the closest published system to this task, but it only photographs equipment and tags; it does not actuate pull stations, apply test aerosol to detectors, operate valves, verify panel signalling, or issue a code-compliance determination.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Orbit and Levatas gauge-reading add-on
sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities and, with the Levatas computer-vision add-on, reads analog gauges and flags abnormal readings; the commercial capability is data capture and anomaly alerting, not functional testing of fire protection systems or code-compliance judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous gauge reading on industrial inspection rounds, comparable to reading a sprinkler riser pressure gauge in a structured facility. It does not transfer to the whole task, which requires physically actuating test devices and valves and rendering a code determination.

sources.title: Automate industrial inspection - ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal is a commercially deployed autonomous inspection quadruped for industrial plants that reads manometers, gauges, counters, displays and valve/lever status without physical interaction with the equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous routine inspection rounds in a structured industrial facility, which covers the observational part of a fire protection walkthrough (gauge and valve-position checks). It explicitly involves no physical interaction, so it cannot perform drain tests, detector tests or device actuation.

sources.system: Kiwa/Vinçotte smoke-detector test drone with aerosol canister
sources.title: Drone Inspection of smoke detectors | Kiwa
sources.claim: Kiwa offers a commercial service in which a human inspector pilots a drone carrying an aerosol canister to functionally test ceiling smoke detectors in high-ceilinged rooms; the drone is an inspector's tool, not an autonomous inspection system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task element (applying test aerosol to detectors), but the drone is flown by the qualified inspector who still performs the inspection and judgment; being teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: smoke detector recognition pipeline (YOLOv11 / SSD / RT-DETRv2) for future drone integration

sources.claim: As of March 2026 automatic smoke-detector inspection remains prospective research: the published work delivers only the detector-recognition component and describes drone integration as a future step, indicating no fielded autonomous system inspects and tests building fire detection devices.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (inspection of installed smoke detectors). It substantiates the negative: only perception is demonstrated, with the physical test and the compliance decision still unautomated.

tasks.label: Test sites and materials to establish facts, such as burn patterns and flash points of materials, using test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Origin-and-cause examination inside a fire-damaged structure (house, apartment, store): reading and interpreting burn/char patterns on walls, ceilings and contents, probing char depth and calcination with gauges, excavating and reconstructing collapsed debris, layering, and documenting the evidence that establishes the area of origin. Water, soot, unstable floors, no lighting, layout unique to each address.

Field testing/screening at a fire scene: sweeping suspect floor areas and debris with a combustible-gas/hydrocarbon detector ('sniffer') or portable field GC, selecting sampling points, cutting/scooping flooring and debris into lined evidence cans, taking comparison samples, sealing and labeling for the lab.

Testing recovered artifacts suspected as ignition sources - appliances, space heaters, lithium batteries, receptacles, wiring, vehicle components - at the scene, in a shop or in an evidence bay: disassembly, continuity/resistance checks with a multimeter, examination of arc beads, x-ray or bench energization of a fire-damaged, unknown item.

Laboratory analysis of submitted fire debris for ignitable liquid residues: opening the sealed evidence can, passive headspace concentration on an activated charcoal strip (ASTM E1412) or SPME, solvent elution into a vial, GC-MS run and classification per ASTM E1618, with QC blanks and a reported result.

Laboratory determination of material fire properties on liquids or products - flash point by closed-cup apparatus (ASTM D93/D7094), ignitability/flammability screening - to establish whether a recovered liquid or product could have started or spread the fire; samples run on standardized bench instruments in a lab.

Fire-prevention inspection side: on-site functional testing at an inspected occupied building - hydrant/sprinkler flow test, smoke/heat detector and alarm device functional test at ceiling height, extinguisher and egress hardware checks - in a commercial facility during business operations.

sources.title: eraflash s10 - eralytics
sources.claim: Commercial flash point analyzer with a 10-position autosampler runs standardized closed-cup flash point determinations (ASTM D6450/D7094/IP 620) unattended after the operator fills cups and loads the carousel; the instrument heats, ignites and evaluates each sample automatically.

sources.system: PAL3 Series 2 / PAL RTC robotic autosampler (CTC Analytics)
sources.date: product line commercial since ~2017; page retrieved 2026-07
sources.title: PAL3 autosampler, automated solid phase extraction | Agilent
sources.claim: Robotic tool-change autosamplers perform automated liquid, headspace and SPME sample preparation and injection into GC-MS instruments, running sample trays unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated headspace/SPME extraction and GC-MS injection in analytical labs. Fire debris ignitable-liquid analysis (ASTM E1618) uses the same vial formats, the same headspace/SPME extraction chemistry and the same GC-MS instrument, so the robotic handling and injection steps carry over when samples are presented in the instrument's tray.

sources.system: Solvent-desorbed SPME GC-MS method for ignitable liquids
sources.title: GC-MS of ignitable liquids using solvent-desorbed SPME for automated analysis - PubMed
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed work shows fire debris ignitable liquid analysis can be run through automated SPME-GC-MS sampling rather than manual extraction.
sources.transferJustification: This is the task's own laboratory instance (testing fire debris to establish whether an ignitable liquid is present); it establishes that the extraction-plus-analysis chain is instrument-automatable when samples are presented in vials.

sources.developer: University of Liverpool (Burger, Cooper et al.)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A free-roaming mobile manipulator operated autonomously for eight days in a conventional wet chemistry laboratory, moving between human benchtops, handling vials and operating benchtop analytical instruments without step-by-step human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of benchtop analytical instruments and vial/liquid handling in a human lab. Transfers to loading a flash point tester or GC in a forensic lab - same object class (small vials/cups of liquid), millimetre-scale placement precision, and the same kind of institutionally controlled laboratory room.

sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the Nature paper: autonomous benchtop instrument operation and sample handling in a laboratory, which is the setting of the flash point and fire debris testing instances.

sources.title: The Use of Robotics in Fire Scene Examination - Ohio Arson School
sources.claim: Robotics currently used in fire scene examination are remotely operated wheeled, tracked or aerial platforms used for access, documentation and assisted evidence collection - no autonomous scene testing is described.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about the task's scene instances; autonomy is not established (operator-piloted platforms), so under the rules it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Drone Inspection of smoke detectors | Kiwa
sources.claim: Drone-based checking of smoke detectors in high-ceiling spaces is offered as an inspection service, but it is an operator-flown service offering rather than a demonstrated autonomous functional test.
sources.transferJustification: Relates to the building-inspection instance (functional testing of installed detection devices); autonomy is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Dust evidence or portions of fire scenes for latent fingerprints.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior of a fire-damaged residence after debris excavation: the investigator selects likely-touched non-porous surfaces in situ (door hardware, window glass and frames, light-switch plates, appliance controls, a pried safe), chooses a contrasting powder, applies it with a fiber or magnetic brush at light pressure over soot-stained, wet, heat-checked surfaces, examines with oblique light, photographs with scale, tape-lifts onto latent cards, and labels/documents each lift. Footing is unstable, lighting is poor, and surfaces vary from charred to lightly smoked.

Portable items recovered at the scene (gasoline can, cigarette lighter, glass bottle from an incendiary device, matchbook, wire/timer components, a pried padlock) processed on a tailgate, in the mobile command unit, or at the vehicle: powder applied to curved and textured surfaces, prints examined, photographed, lifted onto cards, then the item packaged and chain-of-custody documented.

Burned vehicle examined where it sits at the roadside scene or in a tow yard: dusting exterior door handles, hood release, mirror housings, fuel filler door, and less-damaged interior surfaces (steering column trim, glass) in variable weather and lighting, then lifting and carding any developed ridge detail.

Small or incipient fire in an occupied commercial/institutional building (attempted arson, tampered fire extinguisher or pull station, forced point of entry): most surfaces are intact and clean, staff and equipment are present; the investigator dusts glass, door hardware, metal panels and the tampered device, then photographs and lifts prints.

Agency evidence-processing room or crime-lab bench: recovered items are processed under controlled lighting with powders, magnetic applicators, or chemical/fuming development; developed prints are located, photographed with scale, lifted onto cards, and documented in the case file.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Science, Ministry of Public Security (Beijing) with Tsinghua University
sources.title: Rapid, autonomous and ultra-large-area detection of latent fingerprints using object-driven optical coherence tomography (Optics Express 32, 31090)
sources.claim: A research robotic-arm optical coherence tomography system (object-driven OCT) autonomously detects and visualizes latent fingerprints on flat and curved substrates over ~400 cm2 in ~52 s on a laboratory bench, without powder or contact.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: non-contact detection/visualization of latent prints on objects, which serves the same purpose as powder dusting (making latent ridge detail recordable). Transfer is only partial: the demonstration is on laboratory-prepared substrates on an optical bench, not soot-covered, wet, heat-damaged fire-scene surfaces, and it does not select processing areas, lift prints onto cards, or produce case documentation.

sources.developer: Bin He et al. (Institute of Forensic Science MPS / Tsinghua University)
sources.title: Robotic Raman-OCT for Non-Destructive Visualization of Concealed Latent Fingerprints and Trace-Residue Profiling (Small Methods)
sources.claim: A follow-on robotic Raman-OCT platform uses a robotic arm that autonomously repositions and auto-focuses a probe to visualize concealed latent fingerprints and profile trace residues in a laboratory setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic non-destructive visualization of latent prints, same output purpose as dusting. It is a benchtop research instrument for clean laboratory samples; it neither applies powder nor lifts/cards prints, and no fire-scene or field operation is shown.

sources.system: Safefume / Safefume 360 automatic cyanoacrylate fuming chamber (also Mystaire Advanced CA Series)
sources.title: Cyanoacrylate Fuming Method | Air Science
sources.claim: Commercially deployed automated cyanoacrylate fuming chambers develop latent prints on evidence placed inside under fully automatic machine-controlled cycles (hot plate, humidity, circulation, purge) in forensic laboratories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine development of latent prints on non-porous evidence, an alternative to powder dusting. It is an enclosure, not a manipulator: a human must select, load, and unload evidence, and afterwards locate, photograph, lift and document the developed prints, so it does not complete the instance.

sources.title: Situational Awareness for Remote Investigation | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Legged robots deployed with US public-safety agencies for scene work provide reconnaissance and remote inspection of items with an arm, under operator control; no fingerprint processing capability is described.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile robotic work at incident and investigation scenes. It shows the state of field-deployable robots at such scenes is remote sensing and operator-directed item handling, not autonomous powdering, examination and tape-lifting of latent prints.

tasks.label: Conduct wildland firefighting training.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classroom (or blended online/classroom) delivery of NWCG basic courses — S-130 Firefighter Training, S-190 Intro to Wildland Fire Behavior, L-180 Human Factors, I-100 ICS — to seasonal agency crews, new hires, or agency partners; lecture, slides, scenario discussion, question handling, written testing and certification paperwork.

Instructor-led outdoor field exercise day at a training site or district compound: explaining and demonstrating hand-tool fireline construction, water handling/hose lays and pump operation, PPE and fire shelter deployment drills, then observing, coaching, and scoring each trainee against the NWCG field-exercise checklists.

Annual fireline safety refresher (RT-130) and work-capacity/pack test day for returning firefighters and militia, delivered at a ranger district office, fire hall, or fairground: safety briefings, lessons-learned case studies, LCES/Standard Firefighting Orders review, and administering the test walk.

Training delivered to cooperators — rural volunteer fire departments, county crews, contractors, landowner associations — at their own station or a community hall, tailored to local brush trucks, engines, and terrain; evening or weekend sessions with mixed-experience students.

Live-fire / prescribed-burn training evolution on a burn unit: pre-burn briefing, assigning trainees to drip-torch, holding, and mop-up roles, supervising the ignition and suppression exercise as instructor/burn-boss trainer, and conducting the after-action review.

tasks.label: Estimate sizes and characteristics of fires, and report findings to base camps by radio or telephone.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Direct crews working on firelines during forest fires.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small initial-attack wildfire on state or federal forest land: the specialist acts as incident commander, sizes up fire behavior, and directs an engine crew and hand crew by radio and face-to-face orders on where to anchor and construct line, when to disengage, and where to place lookouts and escape routes.

Extended attack on a larger fire: serving as a division/group supervisor on a fireline segment, briefing squad bosses at the start of an operational period, assigning tactics along a section of line, adjusting assignments as wind and fire behavior shift, and reporting progress to the incident commander over radio.

Directing mop-up and patrol crews after containment: walking the black with crew leaders, telling crews which areas to cold-trail, grid, and extinguish, setting rehab priorities, and releasing crews as sections are declared secure.

Prescribed burn or hazard-reduction burn on managed forest/wildland-urban interface: directing ignition and holding crews on firing patterns, sequencing, and holding-line assignments, and calling for a halt or shift if conditions leave prescription.

Directing crews at the wildland-urban interface during a fire threatening structures: assigning crews to structure triage and protection, coordinating with local fire departments and law enforcement over radio and in person at a roadside command point, and relaying evacuation-related instructions.

tasks.label: Locate forest fires on area maps, using azimuth sighters and known landmarks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Staffed fire lookout tower during fire season: worker spots a distant smoke column, rotates the Osborne Fire Finder sighting arm onto the smoke, reads the azimuth (and vertical angle), cross-references with a second lookout's bearing or a known landmark/section line, plots the point on the area map, and relays the location to dispatch.

Prevention specialist on vehicle patrol or at a high vantage point in the field: sees or is directed to a smoke column, takes a bearing with a handheld compass/GPS/mapping app off known ridges, roads, or landmarks, estimates distance, and converts the fix to a legal description or lat-long for the report.

Office or dispatch setting: worker receives azimuths and descriptions from lookouts, detection camera operators, aircraft, or public callers, triangulates the intersecting bearings, and fixes the fire's point on a paper or GIS area map for the dispatch record.

Aerial or elevated detection observation: observer on a detection flight or at a temporary high point identifies the fire relative to known landmarks and drainages and plots its location on an area map for reporting.

Verification and reference work: worker checks a reported or camera-detected smoke bearing against known landmarks and reference panoramas, resolves false alarms (dust, mill steam, water glare), and corrects or annotates the plotted location on the area map.

tasks.label: Extinguish smaller fires with portable extinguishers, shovels, and axes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prevention specialist on patrol finds an abandoned or unattended campfire at a developed or dispersed campsite: douses the fire ring with water from a bladder bag or canteen, stirs coals and ash with a shovel, breaks up unburned chunks, and re-soaks and feels for heat until the fire is cold out, all on uneven forest ground with duff, roots and rocks.

Small spot fire found on patrol along a forest road, right-of-way or grassy edge (cigarette, exhaust, dragging chain, escaped ember), a few square feet up to a fraction of an acre in grass or light brush: knocked down with a backpack pump and/or portable extinguisher, edge scraped to mineral soil with a shovel or pulaski, in wind, slope, smoke and heat.

Escaped debris burn, illegal campfire or warming fire creeping into brush and slash on private or public land: specialist holds and extinguishes the edge with hand tools and water, cuts light fuels away with an axe, and keeps it contained until an engine or crew arrives.

Mop-up / cold-trailing of smoldering material: chopping open a burning stump, log or snag with an axe or pulaski, digging out smoldering roots and duff, separating and stirring burning material into dirt, and feeling with a bare hand for residual heat until declared out.

Small fire at a station, work center, campground facility, vehicle or piece of equipment (trash-can fire, engine compartment, generator, grill, dumpster) knocked down with a portable ABC extinguisher during an inspection or patrol.

sources.system: FlameRanger (Unifire AB robotic nozzles + IR3 flame detectors)
sources.title: What is FlameRanger? - Unifire AB
sources.claim: Unifire's FlameRanger is a commercially sold autonomous robotic fire suppression system: fixed IR flame detectors locate a fire and the system's software autonomously opens the valve and aims robotic water/foam nozzles at the fire source, closing the valve once the fire is extinguished and re-arming for reignition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: incipient-fire extinguishment by an automatic robotic monitor rather than by a person with an extinguisher or bladder bag. It transfers because the object (a small open fire of comparable size to a campfire, trash fire or spot fire), the agent (water/foam applied at the seat of the fire), and the accepted output (fire out, with the detector re-triggering on reignition) are the same; only the delivery device differs, and the coverage zone is engineered around the machine (fixed mounts, sight lines, water main), i.e. an E1 setting.

sources.title: Waste & Recycling - Unifire AB
sources.claim: FlameRanger systems are installed and in service in real waste and recycling plants worldwide, protecting facility areas fully automatically around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: establishes that autonomous extinguishment of real, unplanned small fires is a fielded capability, but only inside fixed installations whose detector/nozzle geometry is engineered around the machine.

sources.system: Autonomous UAV-UGV firefighting team ('Bob' UGV + UAVs), University of Bonn
sources.developer: University of Bonn, Autonomous Intelligent Systems
sources.title: Autonomous Fire Fighting with a UAV-UGV Team at MBZIRC 2020
sources.claim: In MBZIRC 2020 Challenge 3 a UAV-UGV team autonomously detected, approached and extinguished simulated fires around and inside ... purpose-built mock building, with the UGV delivering the maximum amount of water into the fire in the Grand Challenge.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous detect-approach-and-spray on simulated fires in a competition arena. It supports mobile autonomous water delivery onto a small fire at close range in a purpose-built, pre-mapped setting (E1), but the fires were propane/heated-plate mock-ups scored by water delivered, so it does not establish real extinguishment in field conditions.

sources.system: Sikorsky MATRIX autonomous Black Hawk + Rain wildfire mission autonomy
sources.title: Rain and Sikorsky Test Advanced Aerial Firefighting Technologies Using Autonomous Black Hawk Helicopter
sources.claim: A Sikorsky Black Hawk with MATRIX flight autonomy plus Rain's mission autonomy autonomously searched for, located and dropped water on burning brush piles in wildfire-prone Southern California terrain, with safety pilots hands-off and a ground operator assigning tasks from a tablet; the tests were characterised as suppression of early-stage wildfires, not as mop-up or declared extinguishment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial initial attack on small brush-pile fires. Closest available field (E3) evidence, but it is a staged two-week test on firefighter-built piles at prepared hilltop sites beside a dedicated water tank, delivering bucket drops rather than the hand-tool knockdown, lining and cold-trailing that closes out this task.

sources.system: Overland AI ULTRA with OverDrive autonomy
sources.title: CAL FIRE and Overland AI Lead First Evaluation of Autonomous Ground Vehicles for Wildfire Response
sources.claim: CAL FIRE's first evaluation of autonomous ground vehicles for wildfire response used Overland AI ULTRA vehicles autonomously driving austere terrain to deliver supplies and provide camera overwatch; the fire-suppression contribution was via a pan-tilt-zoom camera, not autonomous application of suppressant or hand tools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous off-road mobility in wildland fire operations. It shows field ground autonomy has reached logistics and overwatch in wildland (E3) but does not substantiate autonomous extinguishment of a fire with water, extinguisher or hand tools.

sources.title: Firefighting Robotic Vehicle System
sources.claim: Lockheed Martin's Fire Ox unmanned ground vehicle is offered for suppression, trenching and mop-up support but is described as semiautonomous, i.e. it depends on operator control for its work functions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanised suppression and mop-up in the wildland. Recorded as unclear/semiautonomous, so under the autonomy rule it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous field extinguishment.

tasks.label: Patrol assigned areas, looking for forest fires, hazardous conditions, and weather phenomena.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Vehicle patrol of an assigned block of forest roads and rural highways on an elevated fire-danger day: driving mapped and unmapped gravel/dirt routes for a shift, scanning ridgelines and drainages for smoke, spotting unattended campfires, burning debris piles, hot logging or roadside equipment, downed lines, and noting wind, humidity and fuel-dryness changes to report to dispatch.

Foot patrol of developed campgrounds, trailheads and dispersed camping areas: walking loops and short trails, checking fire rings and abandoned campfires for live heat, spotting hazardous conditions (fireworks, camp stoves, dry slash near sites), verifying posted restrictions, over rough footing, brush and variable weather.

Fixed-point observation from an agency fire lookout tower or high vantage during fire season: systematically scanning the detection area with binoculars/firefinder for smoke, taking and radioing periodic weather observations, and reporting azimuths and locations of any smoke seen.

Aerial detection patrol of an assigned zone after a lightning bust or during extreme conditions: flying a set grid or route over wildland as an observer, locating smokes and holdover fires (including with infrared), and reporting locations and conditions to dispatch.

Patrol of wildland-urban interface neighborhoods, road corridors and active industrial/forest operations during red-flag conditions: looking for hazardous conditions such as inadequate defensible space, unsecured slash and burn piles, hot equipment, and unsafe contractor practices, and documenting and reporting them.

sources.system: UAVONIC / FlytBase DJI drone-in-a-box wildfire detection (Slovakia Military Forest, Zahorie)
sources.title: How Slovakia's Military Forest Enhances Wildfire Detection with Autonomous Drones
sources.claim: A deployed drone-in-a-box system (DJI dock + Mavic 3T on FlytBase) flies scheduled autonomous patrol missions with visual and thermal cameras over 27,000 hectares of pine forest for early wildfire detection, alerting operators to heat anomalies.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: repeated patrol of an assigned wildland area looking for fires; the pine forest is terrain taken as found (E3).

sources.system: XPRIZE Wildfire Autonomous Wildfire Response finalists (Anduril Ghost-X/Lattice Fire; Dryad Silvanet+Silvaguard; AURA Foresight)
sources.developer: Anduril Industries; Dryad Networks; AURA Foresight (tested by XPRIZE Foundation)
sources.title: Finals Testing Recap: Autonomous Wildfire Response
sources.claim: In XPRIZE Wildfire finals testing in rural Nenana, Alaska, autonomous systems (Anduril Lattice Fire with Ghost-X aircraft, Dryad Silvanet/Silvaguard, AURA Foresight) monitored a large wildland area and detected, located and suppressed controlled incipient fires without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the detection core of the patrol task over unstructured wildland; a supervised field competition rather than a routine deployment, so used alongside the deployed Slovakia system.

sources.developer: Pano AI (deployed with Xcel Energy and state/fire agencies)
sources.title: Xcel Energy brings AI-driven wildfire detection to Wisconsin
sources.claim: Pano AI's mechanically scanning 360-degree camera stations continuously monitor wildfire-prone landscapes; AI flags smoke and human analysts verify before notifying fire agencies and dispatch centers.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates the lookout-style scan-verify-report function; it is a fixed mechanically panning sensor station rather than a mobile robot, so it is treated as supporting, not decisive, evidence.

sources.date: 2022-04 (FPL deployment); FAA nationwide BVLOS waiver 2022-11; product ongoing
sources.title: Percepto unveils world's largest autonomous commercial drone deployment at leading US electric utility
sources.claim: Percepto's autonomous drone-in-a-box units perform scheduled, unattended inspection and monitoring rounds of industrial facilities (substations, power plants, refineries, mines) with AI anomaly detection, under an FAA nationwide BVLOS waiver; Florida Power & Light deployed them statewide to monitor substations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine unattended patrol of an assigned area of an institution-controlled site looking for thermal and visual anomalies and reporting them - the same look-and-report duty cycle as fire-hazard patrol, at E2.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Autowalk/Orbit and thermal payload
sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot executes recorded autonomous inspection rounds on schedule in factories, power plants and other facilities, including thermal rounds that detect overheating equipment; customers logged hundreds of miles of autonomous missions and over 130,000 assets inspected.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: walking a fixed patrol route in a human work facility to look for hot spots and abnormal conditions and log them - the on-foot analogue of patrolling for fires and hazardous conditions, in an E2 setting.

sources.system: Skydio drones with Skydio Dock and Remote Ops (BNSF program)
sources.title: Breaking Regulatory Barriers for Remote Operations
sources.claim: The FAA approved BNSF Railway to operate dock-based Skydio drones beyond visual line of ... over rural portions of its network ... infrastructure inspection and patrol, with the aircraft flying itself and the operator off-site and on the loop.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended dock-launched aerial patrol of a long assigned corridor across rural, unstructured land looking for anomalies - shows autonomous wide-area patrol flight outside a controlled facility.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 / K7 Autonomous Security Robots
sources.title: Knightscope Unveils the All-New K7 Autonomous Security Robot
sources.claim: Knightscope's autonomous security robots patrol outdoor grounds continuously with 360-degree video and thermal imaging and push alerts on anomalies including temperature changes; the K7 extends this to large outdoor sites with off-road capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended roving patrol of institution-controlled grounds with thermal sensing and automatic reporting of anomalies; supports the ground patrol-and-report duty at E2 but is not decisive on its own.

tasks.label: Compile and report meteorological data, such as temperature, relative humidity, wind direction and velocity, and types of cloud formations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Examine and inventory firefighting equipment, such as axes, fire hoses, shovels, pumps, buckets, and fire extinguishers, to determine amount and condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Annual/seasonal inventory of a district or interagency fire cache or warehouse: walking racks and bins of Pulaskis, shovels, axes, McLeods, coiled 1.5" and 1" hose, backpack pumps, fittings and extinguishers; counting each NFES item against the cache list and judging serviceability (loose or cracked handles, dull or chipped bits, rust, cut/abraded hose jackets, leaking bladder bags), flagging items for sharpening, repair or condemnation.

Pre-season or periodic check of firefighting equipment carried on engines, patrol trucks, ATVs and trailers in the station bay or fleet shop: verifying the compartment inventory list (hoses, nozzles, fittings, hand tools, drip torch, extinguishers), running the slip-on pump to confirm it starts and holds pressure, checking hose for leaks and couplings for damage, checking extinguisher charge and tags.

Field compliance inspection of an industrial operation (logging, land clearing, right-of-way work) under fire-precaution rules: at the landing or job site in the woods, checking that required fire tools (shovels, Pulaskis, backpack pumps, water supply/tender) are present in the required numbers and serviceable, and that extinguishers mounted on each piece of powered equipment are charged and undamaged; documenting deficiencies.

Routine inspection round of fire extinguishers and fixed fire equipment at agency buildings — ranger station offices, shops, warehouses, bunkhouses: confirming each unit is in its place and unobstructed, gauge in the green, pin and seal intact, no visible damage, and recording/initialing the inspection tag.

Post-incident receiving and inventory of equipment returned from a fire: at the cache receiving bay or incident base, sorting dirty and mixed loads of hose, hand tools, pumps, hardware and extinguishers off waybills, counting quantities against the manifest, and separating serviceable items from those needing refurbishment or condemnation.

sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot quadruped runs autonomous inspection routes across a 40-acre midstream plant performing anomaly detection, thermal inspection and analog gauge reading, docking to recharge between routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment-condition rounds in an industrial facility. Reading a pressure gauge and flagging visual anomalies is the same perceptual act as checking an extinguisher charge gauge or spotting damage on stored equipment.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Orbit at Cargill Multiseed
sources.title: Cargill Deploys Boston Dynamics' Robot Dog at Amsterdam Facility | Food Engineering
sources.claim: Cargill's Amsterdam Multiseed crush and refinery plant runs Spot at scale, roughly 10,000 autonomous inspections per week, collecting thermal, acoustic and visual data on plant equipment.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Orbit at Cargill Multiseed
sources.title: Boston Dynamics Robot Dog Spot Inspects for Safety Hazards | IoT World Today
sources.claim: In the same Cargill deployment the robot's inspection checklist explicitly covers fire extinguishers — whether they are in place and working — plus 5S tool boards and safety signage, inside a working processing plant.

sources.system: Spot-based autonomous fire safety equipment (FSE) inspection
sources.developer: Aziz et al., Computing in Civil Engineering
sources.title: Fully Autonomous Fire Safety Equipment Inspection Missions on a Legged Robot
sources.claim: A legged robot executed fully autonomous fire-safety-equipment inspection missions on a predefined route on a building floor, detecting fire extinguishers and other fire safety equipment and capturing close-up photos of inspection tags for automated analysis.

sources.title: Independent US grocer Harmons deploys Simbe Tally inventory robot across 17 of its locations
sources.claim: Tally, an autonomous shelf-scanning inventory robot, is deployed across 17 grocery store locations, capturing shelf-level data on product availability and placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: counting stock on racks in a controlled facility. The 'amount' half of this task is the same act — autonomously enumerating labelled items on shelving — though Tally does not judge item condition.

sources.title: Reducing Inventory Cycle Counting Time with a Drone-Powered Monitoring Solution | SupplyChainBrain
sources.claim: Autonomous drones fly warehouse aisles without GPS or infrastructure changes and photograph inventory locations to perform cycle counts, in service at 3PL, retail distribution, manufacturing and air-cargo warehouses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting. Establishes autonomous determination of 'amount' for stock held on fixed racks in a facility, the counting half of this inventory task.

sources.system: Automatic hose testing machine (Senwell); FireCatt automated hose test system
sources.title: Automatic Hose Testing Machine for Fire Hose Pressure Test
sources.claim: Commercial automatic hose testing machines pressurize fire hose on a purpose-built bench to verify its strength, running the pressure cycle automatically and returning instrumented pass/fail results; service providers use automated remote pressure-release testing for fire departments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: service testing of fire hose. Determining hose condition is precisely what this purpose-built machine does once the hose is coupled to it — the E1 case of work brought to the machine.

sources.system: Cognex Deep Learning / metal surface inspection
sources.title: Metal Inspection and Quality Control | Cognex
sources.claim: AI-based machine vision systems for factory automation are commercially deployed to judge the surface condition of metal parts — scratches, dents, corrosion and similar defects — as parts are presented in line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-line surface-defect inspection of metal parts. Judging whether a tool head is chipped, cracked or corroded is the same visual discrimination on comparable metal objects when the item is fixtured and presented.

sources.title: Manual Inspections Bleed Money: Why the Future of Industrial Inspection is Automated | ANYbotics
sources.claim: ANYmal legged robots perform autonomous industrial inspection rounds that include temperature monitoring, digital readout of analog gauges, and visual checks for structural issues such as corrosion or cracks, at process plants and offshore platforms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous condition-inspection rounds of plant equipment. Shows visual condition assessment and gauge reading are autonomous in structured facilities, but only for fixed assets requiring no handling.

tasks.label: Administer regulations regarding sanitation, fire prevention, violation corrections, and related forest regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fire-restriction patrol of campgrounds and dispersed recreation areas during fire season: drive/hike to scattered sites over rough forest roads and trails, check campfires, stoves and smoking compliance, feel/probe abandoned fires for heat and douse them with water and dirt, contact visitors about restrictions, issue verbal warnings or written citations, and log the contacts.

Sanitation and site-condition enforcement at recreation sites: inspect for trash, food storage violations, human waste, illegal dumping and unsanitary conditions around camps and trailheads; document conditions, post notices, order the responsible party to clean up, sometimes bag and remove debris, then re-inspect the site.

Fire-prevention inspection of industrial/commercial operations on forest land (logging jobs, timber sales, roadside contractors, utility right-of-way crews): walk the active operating area, open engine compartments to verify spark arresters, check extinguishers, water tanks/pumps, shovels and tool caches, confirm fire watch, write a deficiency notice, and re-inspect for correction.

Burn-permit administration on private/rural parcels: travel to the site, inspect pile size and spacing, clearance to vegetation and structures, availability of water and hand tools, and current weather/fuel conditions; issue, condition or deny the permit with the landowner present; return to verify conditions were met.

Complaint and violation follow-up: respond to a report of an illegal or escaped debris burn, unauthorized fireworks, or an uncorrected hazard on a parcel; investigate and photograph evidence, identify and interview the responsible party, order abatement, coordinate a citation with law enforcement, and re-inspect until the violation is corrected.

sources.system: A2Z Drone Delivery multi-use BVLOS drone dock network
sources.title: Patrolling, rescuing, delivering: A2Z's docked drone fleet does it all
sources.claim: A2Z Drone Delivery operates a docked, BVLOS drone network that autonomously patrols urban waterways and monitors for illegal dumping and unauthorized construction — aerial detection of possible violations, but no contact with violators, no citation, and no physical abatement or re-inspection of a correction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial compliance monitoring of a jurisdiction. It is the closest deployed analogue to patrolling for regulation violations, but it only detects and reports; it cannot inspect equipment up close, contact a responsible party, issue a notice, abate a hazard, or verify a correction, which is what administering the regulation requires.

sources.system: Rain wildfire mission autonomy on Sikorsky MATRIX-equipped Black Hawk
sources.title: Rain and Sikorsky Test Advanced Aerial Firefighting Technologies Using Autonomous Black Hawk Helicopter
sources.claim: Rain and Sikorsky demonstrated an autonomous Black Hawk making water drops on live brush-pile fires in California wildland terrain, showing autonomous aerial operation in forest conditions — but the capability is suppression water delivery, not inspection or enforcement of fire regulations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous action against wildland fire. It establishes that autonomous aircraft can operate over unstructured forest terrain, but delivers water on a designated target rather than performing site inspections, permit decisions, violation notices, or correction verification.

sources.title: BurnBot: California's High-Tech Tool for Safer Prescribed Fire
sources.claim: BurnBot's RX machines perform vegetation mastication and contained prescribed burning for wildfire fuels reduction in wildland-urban interface terrain, but the machines are remote-operated rather than autonomous, so the physical hazard-abatement work still depends on continuous human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical wildland fuel-hazard abatement, the corrective action side of these instances. It is remote-controlled, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment, and it performs no inspection or regulatory determination.

sources.system: SMP Robotics S5 series outdoor security patrol robot
sources.title: Autonomous Outdoor Security Robots for Patrol & Inspection | RaaS Solutions
sources.claim: Outdoor autonomous security patrol robots (SMP Robotics S5 series) patrol grounds and stream AI-analyzed video for detection and deterrence, with one operator supervising many robots; they detect and report but take no enforcement, inspection or corrective action.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous ground patrol of an outdoor site. Closest ground-robot analogue to walking a campground checking for violations, but it operates on maintained, mapped, institution-controlled premises and only observes; it cannot examine a fire ring, extinguish a fire, contact a camper, or issue a notice.

tasks.label: Restrict public access and recreational use of forest lands during critical fire seasons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Posting and maintaining closure and fire-restriction notices across a ranger district during a Stage I/II restriction: driving forest roads, walking to trailheads, kiosks, dispersed-camping pullouts and road junctions, and nailing, screwing or zip-tying placards to wooden posts, signboards and trees; replacing weathered, missing or vandalized signs; terrain, weather and sign hardware vary site to site.

Physically closing access points on forest lands: swinging and padlocking heavy steel pipe gates on forest roads, hauling and setting portable barricades, cones, cable/chain and boulders across dispersed access points and trailheads, clearing brush and rocks out of the gate swing, and hanging the closure placard on the gate.

Patrolling closed or restricted areas by patrol truck, ATV and on foot during red-flag conditions to find dispersed campers, OHV riders, shooters and woodcutters; contacting them face to face, explaining the order, directing them out of the closure, drowning out illegal campfires, and issuing warnings or citations for violations.

Holding an entry checkpoint or developed-area gate during a closure: stationed at a fixed forest entrance station, campground gate or trailhead barrier controlled by the agency, stopping arriving vehicles, denying public entry, admitting permitted traffic (permittees, residents, contractors, fire personnel), and turning the rest around.

Shutting down a developed recreation site for a fire closure: locking restroom and gate padlocks at a campground or day-use area, shutting off the water system, chaining the loop road, posting the closure notice on the entrance kiosk, and walking the loops to confirm no one remains.

sources.date: 2026-06 (page retrieved); product line in agency use for years
sources.title: Flooded Roadways Warning Gates for Highways - Automated Solutions for Flood Management | Versilis
sources.claim: Versilis automated closure gates are field-installed mechanisms that physically deploy a barrier across a roadway to prevent entry, operated from a traffic management center or triggered through ITS sensors, and marketed and installed with agencies for extreme-event closures including wildfires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated closure of a public roadway. It transfers to closing a forest road access point: the same act of driving a physical barrier across a travelway to deny vehicle entry, at a fixed purpose-built installation.

sources.system: Versilis SwiftGate Automated Lane Closure System
sources.title: Versilis SwiftGate Lane Closure System | Construction Equipment
sources.claim: The SwiftGate system deploys a continuous physical obstacle line across a travelway on a single remote command, without workers placing cones or barrels at the site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: erecting a physical closure barrier on a road. Comparable objects (gate arms/barrier line) and outcome (public vehicles excluded) to setting a barricade at a forest road access point.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: agency-operated road closure. Same purpose as restricting public vehicle access to forest lands, executed by permanently installed machinery at fixed access points.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: fastening a flat part to a fixtured workpiece with screws. Attaching a closure placard to a post presented in a fixture is the same class of manipulation — planar part, few fasteners, one-sided access, coarse tolerance.

sources.title: How Autonomous Robots are Revolutionizing Public Safety | Knightscope
sources.claim: Autonomous outdoor security robots patrol institution-controlled outdoor premises (parking lots, corporate campuses, parks), detecting people and providing public address, but they alert human officers rather than contacting, removing, or citing intruders.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: patrolling premises for unauthorized people. It bounds what patrol robots do — detection and deterrence on paved, mapped routes — and does not extend to face-to-face visitor contact, eviction, or extinguishing campfires in wildland.

sources.system: Delta Scientific barrier control systems (beam barricades, crash gates, retractable bollards)
sources.title: Barrier Control Systems | Delta Scientific
sources.claim: Automated vehicle barrier and gate control systems are installed at institution-controlled entrances (military bases, government and large office facilities) to admit authorized vehicles and physically deny entry to others.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: staffing a controlled vehicle entrance. The output — unauthorized vehicles physically stopped at a fixed entry station while credentialed traffic passes — is the same as holding a closure checkpoint at a forest entrance.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: credential-based vehicle admission at a facility gate. Same decision the checkpoint worker makes during a closure — admit permittees, exclude the public — executed by the gate machinery.

sources.system: USFS infrared drone patrols, Tahoe National Forest
