sources.claim: The Forest Service used infrared-equipped drones over a holiday weekend in Tahoe National Forest to spot illegal campfires under fire restrictions; the flights detect fires but do not contact visitors or enforce the restrictions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial detection of illegal fires during restrictions. Cited only to bound capability in wildland: aircraft find violations, but the physical restriction and visitor contact remain human work.

tasks.label: Inspect camp sites to ensure that campers are in compliance with forest use regulations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fire-season patrol of a developed Forest Service or state campground: driving the gravel loop road, walking into occupied numbered sites, checking that campfires are inside the provided ring, attended, of legal size, with water/shovel present, checking site registration/tag and posted stay limits, and contacting campers to explain current restrictions.

Inspection of dispersed/backcountry camps: driving rough forest roads and hiking to unimproved camp spots, checking for a valid campfire permit, stove/fire clearance, spark arrestors on OHVs and generators, food/trash and vehicle-off-road issues; sites are often unoccupied and hard to find.

Contact during active fire restrictions (Stage 1/2) where a violation is found: determining whether the observed situation is a violation, deciding between education, verbal warning, written warning or violation notice, taking names/vehicle and permit information, and de-escalating with uncooperative or hostile campers.

Follow-up on an abandoned or unattended campfire (from public report, night patrol, or aerial infrared detection): locating the smoldering fire off-road, extinguishing it with water and dirt, stirring ash until cold to the touch, and documenting the site and any evidence for a possible investigation.

Holiday-weekend and after-dark patrol of high-use dispersed recreation areas (river bars, lake shores, trailhead pullouts): checking for illegal fires and fireworks in the dark, contacting large groups, and coordinating with law enforcement officers.

sources.system: Forest Service infrared UAS campfire-detection patrol (Tahoe National Forest)
sources.developer: USDA Forest Service, Tahoe National Forest
sources.title: Tahoe National Forest entering Stage 1 fire restrictions June 26
sources.claim: Tahoe National Forest deployed night-flying infrared UAS over the 2026 July 4th weekend to help spot unauthorized campfires in heavily used dispersed camping areas; the aircraft only assist ground resources, which perform the actual contact/inspection, and the flights are agency-piloted rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial detection of illegal campfires. It does not substantiate completion of campsite compliance inspection — it is a detection aid for human ground crews, covers only fire signatures (not permits, spark arrestors, stay limits, camper contact), and autonomy is not established, so it is treated as teleoperated.

sources.title: Security Robots 2026: Autonomous Patrol & Surveillance Systems Guide
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 is a commercially deployed autonomous outdoor security patrol robot, but it is limited to relatively flat paved surfaces such as parking lots and campuses and cannot operate on unpaved ground; it records and reports anomalies rather than judging regulatory compliance or contacting people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous premises security patrol. Transfer fails: campground loops and dispersed camps are unpaved forest terrain outside the platform's stated operating envelope, and the robot performs surveillance reporting rather than a regulatory compliance determination or camper contact.

sources.system: SMP Robotics Argus S5.3 outdoor patrol robot
sources.title: Night patrol of amusement parks by security robots
sources.claim: SMP Robotics Argus outdoor autonomous patrol robots are sold and used for night patrols of parks and amusement grounds, but the vendor states they are not designed to patrol parks while visitors are present, which is precisely the condition of campsite inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor night patrol of a recreation property. Transfer fails: the vendor restricts operation to times when visitors are absent, whereas campsite inspection requires working among occupied sites and contacting campers.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Singapore National Parks Board
sources.title: Robots patrol Singapore parks and streets to enforce social distancing
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot used for park patrols in Singapore to broadcast public-safety messages was remote controlled and always escorted by a human park ranger, showing that public-facing park patrol by legged robots remains teleoperated and human-supervised.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot patrol of a public recreation area with rule-compliance messaging. It cannot support a positive judgment because it is remote controlled with a ranger present, i.e., not autonomous completion.

tasks.label: Inspect forest tracts and logging areas for fire hazards such as accumulated wastes or mishandling of combustibles, and recommend appropriate fire prevention measures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ground patrol/inspection of a forest tract on public or industrial timberland during fire season: driving forest roads and walking off-trail through timber stands and brush, judging surface fuel and slash accumulation, ladder fuels, dead-and-down material, hazard trees, unauthorized campfires and dumped combustible debris; recording findings by GPS and writing a hazard assessment recommending thinning, piling/pile burning, roadside fuel breaks or closures.

Inspection of an active logging/timber-harvest or thinning operation for fire-regulation compliance: checking slash disposal and landing housekeeping, spark arrestors on skidders/chippers/chainsaws, on-site water tank, extinguishers and hand tools, fuel and oil storage and refueling practices, and industrial fire precaution level restrictions; discussing findings with the operator and issuing written corrective recommendations.

Wildland-urban interface property inspection: walking a private parcel and its outbuildings, assessing defensible space zones, vegetation clearance, firewood and combustible storage against structures, propane tanks, roof and gutter debris, and access; explaining required corrections to the homeowner and issuing a written notice with prevention recommendations.

Fire-season inspection of a developed recreation or administrative site inside the forest (campground, picnic area, trailhead, work center): checking fire rings, unattended or improperly extinguished campfires, refuse and combustible debris accumulation, fuel and equipment storage, and posted restrictions, with visitors and vehicles present; logging deficiencies and recommending corrections to the site manager.

Inspection of a fixed permitted industrial operation associated with forest use (mill or log yard, chipping/biomass yard, fuel and equipment storage yard, contractor shop) for accumulated combustible waste, sawdust/bark piles, hot equipment and hot-work areas, fuel handling and housekeeping; producing a deficiency list and prevention recommendations for the permittee.

sources.system: Spot (Spot CAM+IR, FLIR MUVE C360, Enhanced Autonomy Payload)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs fully autonomous inspection rounds at a 40-acre midstream gas plant, detecting combustible gas leaks, thermal anomalies and other hazards and recharging on its dock between routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine autonomous safety-inspection rounds of an industrial facility for combustible-gas, thermal and housekeeping anomalies. Transfers to inspecting a fixed forest-industry facility (mill/log yard, fuel storage yard) for mishandled combustibles and hot spots: same hazard class, same sensing (visual, thermal, gas), same institution-controlled fixed-layout premises, same flagged-deficiency deliverable.

sources.title: ANYmal deployed at Northern Lights CCS Facility
sources.claim: An ANYmal quadruped has been deployed at Equinor's Northern Lights CCS plant to provide autonomous inspection of a normally unmanned process facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hazard/condition inspection rounds replacing human walk-downs at an industrial plant; transfers to combustible-waste and fuel-handling housekeeping inspection at a fixed forest-industry yard, with comparable objects (tanks, equipment, storage areas) and comparable structured premises.

sources.system: Autonomous forest inventory system on ANYmal (DigiForest)
sources.developer: Oxford Robotics Institute / ETH Zurich / ANYbotics
sources.title: Autonomous Forest Inventory with Legged Robots: System Design and Field Deployment (arXiv:2404.14157)
sources.claim: An ANYmal quadruped autonomously navigated and mapped forest plots under canopy and estimated tree traits in field campaigns in Finland and the UK, as a research prototype for inventory data collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous under-canopy traversal and mapping of forest plots. It shows a robot can move through and sense a real forest tract, but its output is tree-trait inventory, not identification of accumulated slash/waste or mishandled combustibles with prevention recommendations, so it does not substantiate completing the inspection.

sources.title: Towards autonomous photogrammetric forest inventory using a lightweight under-canopy robotic drone
sources.claim: A lightweight under-canopy drone was flown autonomously in forest plots to collect photogrammetric inventory data; the work is framed as progress toward autonomous inventory rather than an operational service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous under-canopy forest data collection. Relevant to whether a robot can survey a forest tract, but it yields inventory metrics, not a fire-hazard determination or prevention recommendation.

sources.system: DJI Dock drone-in-a-box with FlytBase autonomy software (UAVONIC deployment)
sources.title: How Slovakia's Military Forest Enhances Wildfire Detection with Autonomous Drones
sources.claim: A docked drone system runs automated patrol missions over 27,000 hectares of military forest in Slovakia for early wildfire detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous aerial patrol of forest land. It substantiates unattended flight over forest, but the deliverable is smoke/fire detection, not inspection of tracts for accumulated wastes or mishandled combustibles with prevention recommendations.

sources.title: Mapping Forest Fuels with Drones to Improve Wildfire Prediction and Response
sources.claim: Autonomous drones able to fly beneath forest canopies and map wildfire fuels are still being designed and tested under a research grant, indicating no operational autonomous fuel-hazard inspection system.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (forest fuel hazard assessment); cited to show the capability remains at the research-development stage, supporting the negative judgments.

emergingTasks.label: Operate drones to monitor and assess fire conditions, track fire progress, and identify safe access points for firefighters.
emergingTasks.status: Proposed for future data collection; not treated as established task evidence

roles.title: Bailiffs
roles.description: Maintain order in courts of law.

tasks.label: Screen persons entering courthouse using magnetometers, x-ray machines, and other devices to collect and retain unauthorized firearms and other contraband.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Peak morning public entry line at a county courthouse: bailiff directs a continuous queue to divest keys, phones, belts and place purses/briefcases into bins on the X-ray belt, watches the X-ray monitor, staffs the walk-through magnetometer, clears routine nuisance alarms with a handheld wand and re-run, hands bins and property back, and keeps the line moving at hundreds of people per hour.

Secondary screening of a person who alarms the walk-through detector after divesting: bailiff performs a handheld-wand sweep and, where the wand localizes something, a limited pat-down/frisk, directs the person to remove the item, and physically recovers items from pockets, waistband, boots or clothing of a fully clothed, sometimes uncooperative adult.

Hand search of a bag flagged on the X-ray image: bailiff opens a purse, backpack, briefcase or tote of unknown, cluttered contents, unzips compartments, moves loose items and paperwork, locates and removes the flagged item (pocket knife, multi-tool, scissors, pepper spray, box cutter), repacks and returns the bag.

Contraband found and retained: bailiff takes custody of a firearm, knife or chemical spray, makes a firearm safe (unload, clear the chamber), tags and logs it, secures it in a weapons locker or property room, issues a claim receipt, and where the item is illegal detains the person and summons a deputy for arrest.

Non-routine screening of persons requiring accommodation or de-escalation: wheelchair and walker users, people with pacemakers, implants or prosthetics, small children and infants in carriers, the elderly and infirm, plus argumentative or agitated litigants who refuse to divest — requiring alternative screening methods, verbal explanation and judgment calls.

Screening of deliveries, contractor tool bags, vendor carts and mail arriving at a service entrance: bailiff X-rays boxes and tool bags, opens and hand-inspects items too dense or cluttered for the image, and holds or refuses prohibited tools/weapons.

sources.title: Evolv Express®: AI Walk-Through Weapons Detection
sources.claim: Evolv Express is a commercially deployed AI walk-through weapons detection portal used at courthouses and venues; it autonomously senses concealed metallic weapons as people walk through, but it only alerts human operators, who perform any resolution, search or seizure. It is a fixed sensor portal with no manipulator.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (entrance weapons screening). It substantiates automated detection only; the portal has no arms and cannot divest, wand, pat down, search a bag, or take and retain a weapon, so it cannot complete any instance end to end.

sources.title: Evolv Express Weapons Detection Screening | Solution Brief
sources.claim: Evolv's own solution brief describes the screening system as alerting human operators to potential threats for issue resolution, confirming that alarm resolution and any physical recovery of a weapon remain with staff.
sources.transferJustification: Same task. Shows the state of the art in automated entrance screening still requires human operators for resolution and seizure.

sources.developer: TSA / DHS Science and Technology Directorate
sources.title: TSA and DHS S&T to prototype self-service screening system at Harry Reid International Airport
sources.claim: The most advanced automated checkpoint in operational trial, the TSA/DHS S&T self-service screening system at Harry Reid International Airport, is a prototype lane in which the traveler performs the divesting and screening steps and automated doors release them; Transportation Security Officers remain on hand for assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (checkpoint screening). Even here the physical labour is done by the human being screened and by officers; no machine wands, pat-downs, searches bags, or confiscates items.

sources.system: Automated checked baggage inspection testbed (Baxter research robot)
sources.developer: Rethink Robotics platform; academic research group (SPIE conference paper)
sources.title: Towards an automated checked baggage inspection system augmented with robots
sources.claim: Robotic retrieval of a prohibited item from luggage exists only as a laboratory research testbed: a Baxter research robot with an overhead RGB-D sensor used to identify and retrieve objects of interest from checked baggage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating and removing a prohibited item from a bag. It is an unvalidated lab testbed on staged luggage, not worker-quality checkpoint bag search, so it does not substantiate completion even in a purpose-built cell.

sources.date: 2022-05 first Tennessee deployment; continuing commercial deployments through 2025
sources.title: Knightscope Deploys First K5 Autonomous Security Robot (ASR) in Tennessee
sources.claim: Deployed autonomous security robots such as Knightscope's K5 patrol mapped routes in facilities and stream sensor data to human operators; they observe and report and have no manipulator, so they neither screen individuals at a checkpoint nor seize contraband.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical security duty in human facilities. Shows that commercially deployed security robotics is limited to patrol and surveillance, with no capability for entrance screening, searching persons or bags, or confiscating weapons.

tasks.label: Escort prisoners to and from courthouse and maintain custody of prisoners during court proceedings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prisoner intake at the courthouse: bailiff/judicial marshal meets the jail transport van in the secure sally port, verifies identities and paperwork against the custody list, pat-searches each in-custody defendant, applies or checks handcuffs, belly chains and leg irons, and walks a chained line of 6-15 prisoners through secure elevators and corridors into courthouse holding cells, doing headcounts and locking them in.

Single-prisoner courtroom movement: bailiff removes one in-custody defendant from a holding cell, cuffs and escorts him through a secure passage into the courtroom, seats him at counsel table, removes or leaves restraints per the judge's order, stands custody watch within arm's reach during a 5-45 minute hearing (arraignment, plea, sentencing), then re-cuffs and returns him to holding.

Sustained custody during a multi-day jury trial with one or more in-custody defendants: bailiff remains posted in the courtroom, keeps continuous line-of-sight on the defendant, controls attorney and family contact to prevent passing of contraband or weapons, escorts the defendant to restroom breaks and to the jury-out holding area, and stays alert for escape or self-harm.

Uncooperative or high-risk prisoner: a defendant refuses to leave the holding cell, becomes combative after a verdict, attempts to flee toward the courtroom doors, or is in mental-health crisis; the bailiff and backup deputies physically control and take the person to the ground, apply additional restraints (leg shackles, restraint chair, spit hood), and remove him from the courtroom while preserving order.

Movement outside the secure perimeter: at older or rural courthouses with no sally port, the bailiff unloads a shackled prisoner curbside and walks him across a public sidewalk, parking lot or plaza with bystanders present into the building; also includes escorting a prisoner to a hospital, another courthouse, or back to the jail on foot or by vehicle.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 / K3 Autonomous Security Robots
sources.title: Knightscope — The Nation's First Autonomous Security Force
sources.claim: Knightscope's autonomous security robots are commercially deployed across many US sites but function as patrolling sensor platforms (cameras, lasers, radar, sonar, emergency communication) that observe and report; they do not take physical custody of people.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest deployed analogue to a bailiff's custody post — an autonomous machine keeping watch in a controlled facility — but it is limited to detection and alerting, establishing that no fielded security robot exercises physical control over a person.

sources.system: Autonomous security robots (industry-wide survey incl. Knightscope, RAD)
sources.title: Security Guards vs. Robots vs. Drones: 2026 Cost Comparison
sources.claim: Industry comparison of guards, security robots and drones states plainly that current robotic security systems do not physically intervene ... humans who then respond.
sources.transferJustification: Maintaining custody of a prisoner requires hands-on control, restraint application and use of force; this source documents that the commercially available security-robot fleet performs none of these functions.

sources.developer: Asian Forum for Corrections / Korea Correctional Service
sources.title: South Korea's 'humane and friendly' robotic prison guards
sources.claim: The most-cited correctional-facility guard robots (Pohang, South Korea) patrol corridors and monitor cells to alert human officers; they do not escort, restrain, or hold custody of inmates.
sources.transferJustification: Closest custodial-setting robot to the bailiff's prisoner-custody role; even in a purpose-controlled jail it only observes and reports, with all physical handling of inmates left to human officers.

sources.title: Cobalt Robotics Autonomous Security Robots - OLogic Inc.
sources.claim: Cobalt's mostly-autonomous indoor security robot is deployed in corporate facilities for alarm response, roving audits and accompanying vendors, but it is a sensing/communication platform without manipulators for handling people.
sources.transferJustification: 'Vendor escort' is the nearest related task to escorting a person through a building, but it means accompanying a cooperative visitor with badge checks; it involves no restraint, search, or control of a resisting person.

tasks.label: Maintain order in courtroom during trial and guard jury from outside contact.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine trial or hearing session in a state/county courtroom: the bailiff stands or sits post for hours, calls the court to order and announces the judge, watches the gallery and counsel tables, enforces decorum (no phones, recording, talking, gum, hats), quiets or warns spectators, hands exhibits, and responds immediately to the judge's spoken directions.

Jury duty: escorting the panel between the jury box, deliberation room, restrooms and lunch through courthouse corridors and elevators; standing post at the deliberation room door so no party, lawyer, witness, reporter or family member speaks to or approaches jurors; taking jury notes to the judge; verifying nobody has contacted jurors and reporting any attempt.

Custody control inside the courtroom: moving a shackled or handcuffed in-custody defendant from the holding cell to counsel table, applying/removing restraints per the judge's order, positioning between the defendant and the gallery/exit, watching for escape or attack cues, and controlling contact between defendant and family.

Active disturbance: a spectator outburst, a shouting match between victim's and defendant's families, a juror or defendant medical emergency, or a defendant lunging at counsel or bolting for the door; the bailiff verbally commands, physically removes or restrains the person, handcuffs, clears the gallery, and calls backup within seconds.

High-profile or high-security trial: crowded gallery with media, victim advocates and rival groups; the bailiff controls who is seated where, screens and monitors entrants, watches for weapons, gestures and gang signals, keeps witnesses separated, and coordinates with other deputies during recesses.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously patrols corporate offices and similar indoor facilities, but functions as a sensing platform that detects anomalies and escalates events to a human security team and remote robot specialists rather than enforcing order itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: indoor guard patrol inside a controlled institutional facility, the closest commercial analogue to a bailiff's watch. It shows the state of the art is autonomous navigation plus detect-and-alert; the robot is explicitly 'the eyes' with humans acting, so it does not transfer to maintaining courtroom order, which requires authoritative verbal control and physical intervention.

sources.system: DEKA Sentry security robot (Cobb County Adult Detention Center pilot)
sources.title: Meet the nearly 6-foot tall robots patrolling a Ga. jail
sources.claim: DEKA Sentry robots were piloted for security rounds inside a county jail's dormitories and perimeter, acting as a visible deterrent with cameras and two-way audio, with a live operator taking control for anything complex.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guarding people held in custody inside a controlled justice facility — the nearest setting to courtroom custody control and jury guarding. It shows robots are limited to deterrent presence and observation, with human operators and deputies handling any interaction or intervention.

sources.title: Knightscope K5 Autonomous Security Robots Deployed at Dozens of Self-Storage Facilities Nationwide
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots are deployed commercially across US sites (e.g., all SecureSpace Self Storage locations, and a 2023 NYPD trial in the Times Square subway ...) performing autonomous patrol, surveillance and public communication, not physical enforcement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol in facilities and transit stations. Transfer fails for bailiff work: the K5 is a wheeled sensor platform with no arms, cannot escort or physically separate people, and produces alerts for human officers rather than maintaining order.

sources.system: Xavier patrol robot (HTX / Home Team Science and Technology Agency)
sources.title: Singapore tests patrol robots to police 'undesirable social behaviour'
sources.claim: Singapore's Xavier patrol robots autonomously patrolled a public housing/shopping district detecting rule-breaking behaviour and broadcasting warning messages, while relaying alerts to a human command centre for any actual enforcement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: enforcing behavioural rules on people in a monitored space, the abstract core of 'maintaining order'. The robot only detects and broadcasts recorded warnings and cannot compel compliance, remove a person, or respond to a judge's order, so it does not transfer to courtroom order maintenance.

sources.system: Security patrol robots (general market survey: K5, Spot-based, etc.)
sources.title: Security Guards vs. Robots vs. Drones: 2026 Cost and Performance Comparison
sources.claim: Industry comparisons of security guards versus robots state that current robotic security systems do not physically intervene ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial guarding. Establishes the boundary of deployed capability relevant here — no fielded security robot performs the physical control, restraint or escort actions that constitute maintaining courtroom order.

tasks.label: Provide security by patrolling interior and exterior of courthouse and escorting judges and other court employees.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Business-hours interior patrol of a county/state courthouse: walking public corridors, lobbies, stairwells, courtroom hallways and elevator banks; watching for suspicious behavior, unattended items, people in restricted areas or propped secure doors; giving occasional directions to the public and radioing/reporting anything found.

Exterior patrol of courthouse grounds: perimeter walk-around, staff and public parking lots and garages, loading dock and prisoner sally-port area, checking for loiterers, suspicious or illegally parked vehicles, unsecured exterior doors; day and night, all weather.

Escorting a judge inside the building: meeting the judge at the secure garage or chambers, clearing and walking the private corridor/elevator route to the courtroom bench and back, controlling access along the way, staying alert to threats from litigants and the public.

Escorting a judge, juror, witness or court clerk off the controlled premises: across the public plaza, sidewalk or street to a vehicle after hours or after a high-profile case, sometimes with media, protesters or a known threat present.

After-hours / weekend security sweep of a closed courthouse: covering each floor, confirming courtrooms and offices are empty, verifying doors and windows are secured, checking for leaks, alarms and anomalies, and logging the round.

Responding to something found on patrol: an agitated litigant or family argument in a hallway, a fight, an intoxicated or trespassing person to be removed, a suspicious package, or a medical emergency — requiring verbal commands, physical intervention/detention and hands-on assistance.

sources.title: How the K5 Robot Patrols Without Human Help
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 Autonomous Security Robot runs programmed patrol routes autonomously, avoiding obstacles, rerouting, and self-docking to recharge without onsite human control; remote human staff back it up.

sources.title: Autonomous public safety robots on patrol, connected by Verizon (RCR Wireless News)
sources.claim: K5 robots are fielded as guard-round patrol units on institutional grounds — hospital and college campuses, parking lots and property perimeters — and hold a federal ATO from the VA.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contract security guard patrol rounds. Same output as a bailiff's exterior courthouse round — visible deterrent presence, anomaly/vehicle detection and reporting over institution-controlled grounds and lots.

sources.developer: Knightscope for U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs Police
sources.title: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR) Privacy Impact Assessment, FY24
sources.claim: A Knightscope autonomous security robot was procured for the VA South Texas Health Care System so VA Police could monitor patrolled areas, enforce parking rules and deter undesirable behavior on a government campus.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: police/security patrol of a government facility campus. Comparable to courthouse patrol — a public government building with sworn police, mixed public and staff traffic, interior/exterior rounds.

sources.title: Huntington Park Police Renews Knightscope Contract for 6th Year
sources.claim: Municipal police have kept an autonomous Knightscope patrol robot in continuous service for multiple contract years, with reported reductions in calls for service and crime reports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: law-enforcement patrol of a public, institution-controlled outdoor site (city park/civic property), which matches the deterrent-presence and reporting output of courthouse exterior patrol.

tasks.label: Guard lodging of sequestered jury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Overnight watch on the hotel floor/corridor housing a sequestered jury: bailiff holds the post through the night, observes everyone who approaches the jurors' rooms, challenges and turns away hotel staff, other guests, reporters or family, answers jurors who come out (ice, medication, complaint), keeps jurors from leaving the floor, and logs the watch so the court can be told no improper contact occurred.

Meals inside the lodging: muster the jurors, walk them as a group to a reserved dining room or private area, keep other patrons and staff at a distance, sit with them and stop any case discussion or outside conversation, take a head count, and return them to their rooms.

Daily movement between lodging and courthouse: knock rooms, assemble jurors, load them on a van or bus, count heads, shield them from waiting media, bystanders and family in the hotel driveway, parking lot and sidewalk, and walk them into the secure courthouse entrance (and reverse at day's end).

Control of communications and media in the lodging: collect and secure jurors' cell phones, place and monitor supervised calls to family, screen deliveries, mail and room service, remove or redact newspapers, and disable or supervise TV/news access in juror rooms; return devices on release.

Supervised outings and incidents: escort jurors off-premises to a restaurant, walk, gym or religious service; handle an unauthorized contact attempt, a juror who becomes ill, an argument between jurors, or a juror who breaks the sequestration rules, then report the incident to the judge.

tasks.label: Enforce courtroom rules of behavior and warn persons not to smoke or disturb court procedure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine in-session decorum in a general trial courtroom: bailiff stands/moves at the rail scanning a gallery of 10-40 people, spots a ringing or recording phone, a hat, gum, food, whispering or a sleeping spectator, and quietly approaches to direct the person to stop, then escorts a repeat offender out to the hallway.

Pre-session rule-setting and door control: bailiff announces courtroom rules to the assembled gallery (phones off, no food/drink, no cameras, remain seated, no talking), stops entrants carrying prohibited items, seats people so opposing parties are separated, keeps aisles clear, and calls the court to order.

Emotionally charged proceeding (criminal sentencing, domestic/family matter): a spectator or family member shouts, sobs loudly, curses the judge, or makes threatening gestures toward a witness; bailiff issues a firm verbal warning, positions his body between parties, and on the judge's order physically escorts or removes the person, sometimes restraining or handcuffing.

Courthouse corridor, lobby, or entrance area outside the courtroom: bailiff/court security officer warns people not to smoke or vape near the doorway or in a restroom, tells loud groups in the hall to quiet down because a trial is in session, stops hallway filming of jurors, and moves loiterers along.

Small municipal, traffic, or juvenile court session with high crowd churn: dozens of defendants and families cycling in and out, children present, people talking on phones or arguing in the gallery; bailiff repeatedly warns individuals, quiets the room, and controls the flow to the bench.

High-profile or high-security trial: packed gallery with media and supporters of both sides, attempted photography, a coordinated protest outburst or gang-affiliated spectators; bailiff and deputies issue warnings, identify offenders in a crowd, and clear or remove disruptive individuals under the judge's direction.

tasks.label: Arrest persons in court when arrest warrants have been issued.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In open court, the judge revokes bond or executes a bench warrant and remands the defendant; the bailiff/deputy approaches the defense table, orders the person to stand and turn, applies handcuffs behind the back, and escorts them through the secure door to the holding cell while the hearing continues.

A person appearing for a hearing is found (via records/warrant check at screening or by the clerk) to have an outstanding warrant; the bailiff takes them into custody in the courtroom or adjacent corridor, pat-searches them, seizes phone/keys/wallet, completes arrest paperwork and hands them to transport/booking deputies.

A non-compliant subject: on hearing the remand order the person bolts for the gallery doors or braces and pulls away from cuffing; the bailiff must physically control them, often with a second deputy, take them to the floor, and apply cuffs and possibly leg restraints without injuring them or bystanders.

An emotionally charged arrest in a full courtroom (family, juvenile or sentencing docket): the defendant is crying or pleading, relatives in the gallery stand up, shout or crowd forward, and the bailiff must complete the cuffing and removal while controlling the gallery and protecting the judge and parties.

Arrest of a person with special handling needs: intoxicated, in mental-health crisis, elderly, pregnant, or in a wheelchair/on crutches; the bailiff must choose modified restraint (front cuffs, waist chain, or none), assess medical risk, and summon EMS or a mental-health deputy as needed.

tasks.label: Check courtroom for security and cleanliness and assure availability of sundry supplies, such as notepads, for use by judge, jurors, and attorneys.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-session security sweep of the courtroom: bailiff walks the room before the public is admitted, physically checks concealed spots (under and behind gallery benches, under counsel tables, jury box, lectern, trash receptacles) for weapons, contraband or items planted by accomplices, confirms holding-cell/secure-corridor doors are locked, exits are clear, and the bench duress alarm and cameras are working.

Setting out juror and attorney supplies before a session: distributing fresh notepads, pens/pencils, and water pitchers or cups to each seat in the jury box and to both counsel tables, removing used pads between sessions, and confirming exhibit-handling supplies (tags, envelopes) are on hand.

Cleanliness check and light tidying between or before sessions: scanning the courtroom for leftover papers, cups and litter on gallery benches, counsel tables and the floor, removing them, straightening benches/chairs and the gallery, wiping counsel tables, and notifying custodial staff of spills or problems the bailiff cannot fix.

Judge's bench and clerk station preparation: fresh water carafe and glass, notepads and pens laid out, bench surface cleared and tidy, gavel and bench book in place, verifying microphone, monitor and panic button are functional before the judge takes the bench.

Jury deliberation room prep between panels: verify the room is empty and secure (no materials left by the prior jury, door lock and restroom clear), restock notepads, pens and drinking water, and set out the verdict forms area for the incoming panel.

tasks.label: Stop people from entering courtroom while judge charges jury.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine jury trial in a typical county courthouse: when the judge begins the charge the bailiff closes the courtroom doors and posts at them for 20-45 minutes; a handful of members of the public, a late spectator or a family member tries the door and is quietly turned away and told to wait until the charge ends. Court policy is that no one enters or leaves while instructions are being given.

Low-traffic courtroom (rural docket, afternoon civil session, near-empty gallery): the bailiff simply closes and secures the doors at the start of the charge and stays posted; nobody actually approaches the door during the charge, and the doors are reopened when the jury retires.

Busy urban courthouse or high-profile/emotionally charged case: during the charge several people (family members, media, waiting attorneys, other deputies, jurors for other panels) congregate at the closed doors, some persistent or loud; the bailiff must hold the door shut, refuse entry to each of them, and keep the corridor quiet enough that the charge is not disrupted.

Someone with a colorable claim to enter arrives mid-charge: co-counsel returning, a clerk with a message for the judge, a witness, another officer, or a juror's relative with an emergency. The bailiff must judge whether the judge would permit entry, obtain direction if needed, and either refuse or admit and seat the person silently without interrupting the instructions.

Courtroom with multiple entrances or an in-custody / security-sensitive trial: the bailiff must cover the public door while also keeping watch on the defendant, gallery and second door, and be ready to physically intervene if someone forces the door or a disturbance begins during the charge.

tasks.label: Screen, control, and handle evidence and exhibits during court proceedings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During live testimony in an open courtroom, the bailiff takes a marked documentary or photographic exhibit (paper, photo in a sleeve, small bagged item) from counsel on the judge's cue, carries it quietly to the witness stand or the bench, waits, retrieves it after examination, and returns it to the clerk's exhibit table without disrupting proceedings.

Admitted document/photo exhibits (binders, photo sets, small items in evidence bags) are distributed into the jury box juror-by-juror during deliberation-adjacent viewing or testimony, then collected back in full count and returned to the clerk.

Oversized or demonstrative exhibits: setting up foam boards on easels, positioning scale models or large physical objects (bicycle, machinery part), rolling out the exhibit monitor/cart, and operating playback of video or audio exhibits for the courtroom.

Weapon, narcotics, or biohazard evidence: confirming a firearm has been rendered safe (unloaded, action open, trigger-tied) before it enters the well, keeping it under continuous control while a witness handles it, keeping it away from the defendant and jurors, and resealing/resecuring it afterward.

Secure custody and transport: retrieving sealed evidence containers from the courthouse evidence locker or secure storage, moving them through courthouse corridors and elevators to the assigned courtroom, logging custody transfers, locking exhibits away during recess, and returning them to storage at adjournment.

Screening items brought into the courtroom by parties or witnesses — boxes and bags of exhibits, bulky objects, items arriving outside the main checkpoint — inspecting them for contraband or hazards and controlling whether and how they enter the well.

Under the E1 counterfactual the exhibit arrives fixtured/presented, so exhibit passing reduces to reading the exhibit identifier and moving a small, light object (document sleeve, photo, bagged item) to a designated point without damage — the same objects, precision and cell environment.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics Integrates First Put Wall in Capacity Fulfillment Center
sources.claim: RightHand piece-picking has been integrated with put walls in a live fulfillment center, i.e., picked items are placed into a specific one of many designated compartments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting individual items into many distinct designated slots. Transfers to distributing copies of a document exhibit to fixed designated positions (a jury-box equivalent) under the E1 counterfactual, where the recipients' positions are fixed and known.

sources.title: 700,000 submunitions demilitarized by Sandia-designed robotics system
sources.claim: An automated nine-robot system at the Anniston Munitions Center disassembles live submunitions in fenced workcells; computer vision flags abnormalities but human operators in a control room make the safety determinations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine manipulation of dangerous ordnance in a purpose-built cell. It shows weapon-item handling is mechanically feasible at E1, but the safety adjudication — the core of screening a firearm before it enters the courtroom well — is still referred to human operators.

sources.system: Automated evidence storage carousels / VLM evidence systems
sources.title: 7 Public Safety Evidence Room Space Saving Storage Ideas
sources.claim: Automated evidence storage systems in public-safety property rooms use a software-controlled robotic mechanism to retrieve specific evidence bins and deliver them to a secure operator ..., with access control protecting chain of custody.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine retrieval and controlled presentation of actual evidence containers with custody tracking — the storage-side half of the bailiff's secure custody instance, in a purpose-built machine environment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Maintain court docket.
