tasks.label: Provide jury escort to restaurant and other areas outside of courtroom to prevent jury contact with public.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lunch recess in a courthouse: bailiff gathers the seated panel (12-14 jurors plus alternates) in the jury room, walks them as a group through non-public corridors, elevators or stairwells to the courthouse cafeteria or jury dining room, keeps stragglers with the group, physically positions himself between jurors and attorneys/witnesses/press/other visitors who may be in the halls, listens for and stops any case discussion or contact, then returns the panel to the jury room on time for the judge.

Off-site lunch: bailiff walks the whole panel out a side door, along public sidewalks and across street crossings several blocks to a nearby restaurant, keeps them clustered and moving, screens the seating area, keeps passersby, reporters and case-connected persons from approaching or speaking to jurors, tells the restaurant staff the ground rules, sits within earshot to stop case talk, and walks the group back through pedestrian traffic.

Short breaks on courthouse premises: escorting jurors in ones and twos to public restrooms, to the designated smoking area outside the main entrance, or to the parking garage at the end of the day; standing watch at the restroom door, keeping members of the public and parties to the case from striking up conversation, and returning each juror to the jury room.

Sequestered jury: bailiff moves jurors between courthouse, a chartered van/bus, and a hotel — through the hotel lobby, elevators and corridors to the hotel restaurant or a private dining room — after checking the route and dining area, keeping hotel guests, media and family members from contacting jurors, monitoring conversations at the table, and controlling who enters the jurors' floor.

Jury view off-site: bailiff transports and escorts the panel to a crime scene, accident location, or disputed property (street, business, residence, or open ground), keeps jurors together in a cordoned group while counsel and the judge conduct the view, prevents bystanders, neighbors or parties from talking to jurors, and returns them to the courthouse.

sources.date: 2017-07 (still in service in later airport robot deployments)
sources.title: Robots Will Lead Passengers to Their Gate at Seoul's Airport
sources.claim: LG's airport guide robots at Incheon International Airport autonomously lead individual passengers from their current location to a destination such as a departure gate inside the terminal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guiding a person through an institution-controlled indoor facility, the closest analog to walking jurors from the jury room to a cafeteria. Transfer is only partial: the robot leads one cooperative follower along a mapped route and takes no action to keep a group together or to prevent third parties from approaching or speaking to the people it leads, which is the purpose of the bailiff's escort.

sources.title: How the K5 Robot Patrols Without Human Help
sources.claim: The Knightscope K5 autonomous security ... mapped routes at customer properties without hands-on human oversight, capturing and streaming video and anomaly alerts to human operators who must respond; it does not act on or control people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol of institution-controlled premises, the nearest deployed robotic analog to a bailiff's protective presence. Transfer fails for this task because the K5 observes and alerts along fixed routes; it cannot shepherd a group of people, interpose itself between jurors and the public, or enforce a no-contact rule.

sources.developer: Knightscope / New York City Police Department
sources.title: NYPD 'robocop' no longer patrolling following end of pilot program
sources.claim: In the NYPD's Times Square subway pilot, the Knightscope K5 had to be accompanied ... police officers while on patrol, and the pilot was ended after roughly six months.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic security presence in a crowded public transit concourse, comparable to escorting jurors through public areas. It shows the state of the art requires human officers alongside the machine rather than replacing the protective human, supporting a negative judgment here.

sources.title: Wayfinding & Guide Robots
sources.claim: Commercial guide robots such as the LG CLOi GuideBot are marketed and deployed to greet visitors and physically lead them through large venues along mapped indoor routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting visitors through a structured facility. It substantiates only route-leading for willing individuals; nothing in the product covers group accountability, screening a dining area, or blocking public contact, so it cannot substitute for a jury escort.

roles.title: Correctional Officers and Jailers
roles.description: Guard inmates in penal or rehabilitative institutions in accordance with established regulations and procedures. May guard prisoners in transit between jail, courtroom, prison, or other point. Includes deputy sheriffs and police who spend the majority of their time guarding prisoners in correctional institutions.

tasks.label: Conduct head counts to ensure that each prisoner is present.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Formal standing/ID count in a multi-tier cellblock of a prison or jail: all movement frozen, officer walks the tiers, looks into each cell through a window or bars, verifies a live person (often an ID card or wristband) for each assigned occupant, tallies, and reports the number to the control center for the count to clear.

Night / lights-out count and 30-minute security rounds in a housing unit: cells dark, inmates asleep under blankets, officer uses a flashlight to confirm living, breathing flesh in each bunk, wakes or prompts inmates whose bodies are obscured, and logs each check.

Count in an open-bay dormitory or direct-supervision jail pod: 40-100 inmates ordered to sit on assigned bunks or stand at their racks; officer counts bodies by bunk position, reconciles the number against the housing roster, and reports it.

Out-counts of inmates away from housing inside the facility: kitchen, laundry, industries shop, school, chapel, medical, yard or gym; officer counts inmates present against pass/callout lists and the numbers are reconciled facility-wide with housing counts.

Counts during movement and transport: chain-in/chain-out at intake, loading and unloading a transport bus or van, court holding cells; officer counts and verifies each inmate by name/photo/wristband at each transfer point, often with inmates restrained and in unfamiliar spaces.

Count does not clear: officer conducts an emergency recount, physically re-verifies identities cell by cell or one inmate at a time against photos/ID cards, searches showers, dayrooms, closets and other spaces, and works with staff to locate the missing or miscounted inmate until the count clears.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office enhances security at the Adult Detention Center with cutting-edge DEKA Sentry Robots
sources.claim: DEKA 'Sentry' robots (jailbots) were deployed in a 90-day pilot at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center, autonomously navigating the jail for perimeter patrols and security rounds ... selected dormitories, equipped with 360-degree cameras, night ... and heat detection; a live operator takes control for complex tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security rounds in jail dormitories. It establishes that a mobile robot can traverse the actual correctional housing environment and image inmates (night vision, thermal) — the traverse-and-observe part of a head count — but the source does not show the robot producing or clearing an accountability count.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: A look at a pilot program in Georgia that uses 'jailbots' to track inmates (NPR/WABE)
sources.claim: Reporting on the same Cobb County pilot describes the robots as patrolling to verify inmate whereabouts using AI/facial recognition, but they are supervised remotely by jail staff and the press demonstration was conducted with no inmates present.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published claim to the head-count task, but the robots are remotely supervised and no source documents a count being conducted and cleared by a robot, so it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment on its own.

sources.title: A New Perspective for Facilities Inspection
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous, route-based inspection and security patrol missions in industrial facilities, including automatic person detection with PTZ and radiometric thermal imaging and alerting, plus autonomous door opening (2,500 doors opened across 18 beta customers).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous scheduled rounds of a facility with reliable detection of human presence in the dark via thermal/visual sensing — the perception core of confirming a body is present at a station. It does not demonstrate enumeration against a roster or handling of deliberately concealed persons.

sources.title: Autonomous warehouse drones streamline inventory control (TechTarget)
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous inventory drones fly scheduled missions in warehouses, scanning tens of thousands of fixed pallet locations without a human pilot and reconciling findings against ERP/WMS records; a Scholl/DSV deployment replaced a multi-day manual count of 12,000 pallet locations, with reported inventory accuracy around 99.9%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cycle counting. A count is enumeration of units at known assigned positions, reconciled against a record with exceptions flagged — the same structure as a head count once subjects are presented at fixed known positions — at accuracy the employer accepts in place of manual counters.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt Robotics' indoor security robots patrol corporate facilities autonomously along designated routes, detect people, and interact with building systems (doors, elevators, badge readers), with remote human specialists taking over for exceptions such as verifying a detected person's credentials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor guard rounds in an institution-controlled facility with person detection and credential checks; shows traverse-and-observe capability, but identity verification of a detected person is handed to a remote human specialist rather than performed autonomously.

tasks.label: Inspect conditions of locks, window bars, grills, doors, and gates at correctional facilities to ensure security and help prevent escapes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shift security check of an occupied housing unit/tier: officer walks the range, physically pulls/tugs each cell door to confirm it is secured, works the lock or key, looks for paper, gum or shims in strike plates and tracks, and flags any door that does not lock. Inmates are present and moving.

Bar and grill inspection: tapping cell window bars, dayroom grills, vent covers and security screens with a mallet and listening for a dull tone, shaking bars, and checking welds and fasteners for cuts, spread, or fill (soap/putty/paint) indicating an escape attempt.

Detailed cell inspection during or after a shakedown or cell turnover: full inspection of the assembled cell's security fixtures in place - door and frame, hinges, lock body and keeper, window, grill, vent, bunk welds, walls - searching for concealed tampering and damage.

Perimeter and outdoor round: inspecting sally-port gates, vehicle and pedestrian gates, padlocks and chains, gate motors and latches, and fence line hardware, in all weather, confirming each is locked, undamaged and free of tampering.

Scheduled documented facility-wide security inspection with a checklist: corridors, workshops, visiting rooms, service chases, stairwell doors and gates across the institution, recording deficiencies and writing maintenance work orders.

Testing operation of powered/electronic detention locking devices: cycling doors and interlocks from a control point or at the door, verifying each locks and unlocks correctly and that mechanical overrides work, and reporting faults.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Ga. sheriff's office piloting robot patrol program at jail to enhance security
sources.claim: DEKA Sentry 'jailbots' were piloted at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center for perimeter patrols and security rounds ... dormitories, using cameras, night vision, heat detection ...; they observe and deter but do not physically test locks, doors or bars, and an operator drives them for complex tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jail security patrol rounds. It is the closest deployed corrections robot, but it is a sensing/deterrence platform with a human operator for anything beyond driving a route, so it does not substantiate physical inspection of lock, bar and gate condition.

sources.title: Badger Technologies Introduces PatrolBot Autonomous Robot for Security Guard Industry
sources.claim: Badger PatrolBot is an autonomous indoor security robot that verifies windows and doors are secured and checks equipment placement and floor hazards; it was deployed on patrol at the National Veterans Memorial and Museum. Verification is camera/sensor based - it does not manipulate or test locking hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guard patrol rounds verifying doors/windows are secured in a structured facility. It shows the state of the art for autonomous in-facility security checks is remote visual verification of closure, not inspection of lock, bar or grill condition.

sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot runs autonomous Autowalk inspection missions in industrial plants (thermal, acoustic, gauge reading) and, in a 2025 release, the Spot Arm can open doors autonomously during those missions - manipulation of door hardware, but not assessment of lock integrity or tampering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial inspection rounds including door manipulation. Shows a robot can traverse a structured facility and operate a door handle, but the released capability is passage and sensor data capture, not verifying that a lock is sound, engaged and untampered.

sources.system: High Precision Door Lock Testing Machine (also Rim Lock Testing Machine, Door Lock Handle Testing Machine)
sources.title: High Precision Door Lock Testing Machine by Kamtronix Automation
sources.claim: Commercially built door-lock testing machines hold a lockset in a fixture and run automated cycles that open, close, lock and unlock the lock while instrumenting its performance - an automated station that determines whether a presented lock operates correctly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated functional/durability testing of door locks in manufacturing. Same objects (locksets, deadbolts, latches, padlock-type mechanisms) and the same acceptance question the officer answers by working the lock - does the bolt throw, engage the keeper and release properly - performed by machine when the lock is fixtured.

sources.system: CIRCOGRAPH DA eddy current bar inspection system
sources.title: Detecting Longitudinal Cracks in SBQ Bars with Eddy Current Testing
sources.claim: FOERSTER's CIRCOGRAPH DA is a purpose-built in-line eddy-current system that scans the whole circumference of steel bars moving through a test line and flags surface-breaking cracks and other flaws automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated non-destructive inspection of steel bars in a mill. Bar tapping in a jail asks the same physical question - is this steel bar cut, cracked or otherwise compromised - and inline NDT answers it with higher sensitivity than a mallet when the bar is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Cognex AI-powered machine vision defect detection systems
sources.title: Defect Detection & Automated Inspection | Cognex
sources.claim: Machine-vision inspection stations are standard, deployed factory equipment for detecting surface damage and defects on fixtured parts presented to the camera.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated visual defect inspection of manufactured parts. Supplies the visual half of the officer's check - pry marks, deformation, damaged or missing components on hardware - for door, lock, grill and gate parts presented in a fixture.

sources.system: Door hardware cycling test fixture (UL Verification program)
sources.title: Door Hardware - Verify - UL Solutions
sources.claim: Door hardware certification testing installs the lockset in a cycling test fixture with the manufacturer's strike and machine-cycles it under load, an established purpose-built rig for judging whether a lock functions to standard.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: standards-based lock cycle testing. Confirms that fixtured, machine-driven actuation and pass/fail assessment of installed-style lock/strike assemblies is routine practice, which is the E1 form of 'inspect the condition of the lock'.

tasks.label: Monitor conduct of prisoners in housing unit, or during work or recreational activities, according to established policies, regulations, and procedures, to prevent escape or violence.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: State prison / county jail housing unit during lockdown, count, or the overnight shift: officer walks the tier or dorm on staggered security rounds, looks into each cell for signs of life and disturbance, verifies inmates are where they belong, and logs the round. Inmates are secured in cells or bunks; the route is fixed and repetitive.

Day-shift supervision of an occupied housing unit (direct-supervision pod or tier) with 50-120 inmates out of cells: dayroom, phones, showers, TV area, cleaning details. Officer reads inmate mood and group dynamics, gives verbal direction, spots contraband passing and brewing conflicts, and stays positioned to intervene before a fight or escape attempt.

Recreation supervision: outdoor yard, gym, or ball field with large mixed groups of inmates, weights and sports equipment, and blind spots behind buildings; officer monitors gang groupings, tracks head count, and watches for weapons, assaults and fence approaches in varying weather.

Supervision of inmates at work assignments inside the facility: kitchen, laundry, sanitation, maintenance, prison industries shop. Officer monitors inmates handling tools, chemicals and food, watching for theft, weapon manufacture, horseplay or assaults among workers in cluttered active workspaces.

Jail booking/holding tanks, segregation units, and special watches (suicide watch/constant observation, mental-health and medical housing): frequent or continuous direct observation of agitated, intoxicated or self-harming detainees, requiring immediate recognition and immediate response.

Supervision of inmates beyond the secure perimeter: road/litter crews, farm and grounds details, community work crews; officer watches an unfenced work area that varies site to site, with public and traffic present, primarily to prevent escape and unauthorized contact.

sources.title: Meet the nearly 6-foot tall robots patrolling a Ga. jail (Corrections1)
sources.claim: DEKA 'Sentry' jailbots patrol a county jail's perimeter, hallways and select dormitories with 360-degree cameras, night vision, ..., running autonomously on patrol with a live operator taking control for complex tasks, to alert deputies to contraband, medical emergencies or violence.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: A look at a pilot program in Georgia that uses 'jailbots' to track inmates (NPR/WABE)
sources.claim: In the Cobb County jail pilot the robots are kept away from inmates (announcing a 20-30 foot standoff, no contact) and are supervised remotely by jail staff ... react to what they see; the unveiling demonstration was run with no inmates in the halls or cells.
sources.transferJustification: Same task and setting (monitoring inmates in a jail housing unit); establishes the operating limits of the only inmate-monitoring robot deployment found.

sources.title: Knightscope's Autonomous Security Robots Delivers Technology for Public Safety (Vicor)
sources.claim: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robots drive patrol routes 24/7 without human intervention, using lidar, GPS, sonar, cameras and audio to gather and report security data, and are commercially deployed across dozens of US states in parking structures, campuses and public buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol and anomaly reporting on a set route in a controlled facility - the same route-following, observe-and-escalate function as a correctional security round, though performed where no inmates are present.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: The Cobalt indoor security robot autonomously patrols indoor facilities on designated routes, uses onboard AI over 60+ sensors (thermal, 360-degree cameras, lidar, microphones) to flag anomalies such as people, open ... and unusual sounds, and escalates verified events to a monitoring team; sold commercially for offices and data centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous interior patrol rounds with anomaly detection and escalation inside a facility built for people - the closest commercial analogue to an officer's routine housing-unit security round.

sources.system: Skydio autonomous drone with Levatas AI
sources.title: ODOC takes contraband fight airborne with new drone technology
sources.claim: Oklahoma DOC launched a pilot at Red Rock Correctional Center using Skydio drones with Levatas AI for continuous autonomous aerial coverage of the facility, alerting staff to safety and security issues; correctional officers are being trained as certified pilots to oversee yard activities and the perimeter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial monitoring of prison yards and perimeter for security threats; shows autonomous surveillance supporting, not replacing, the officers who oversee yard activity.

sources.developer: Asian Forum for Corrections / ETRI / Kyonggi University
sources.title: South Korea's mood-sensing robotic prison guards (The Week)
sources.claim: A five-foot 'Robo-guard' was trialled in Pohang, South Korea, patrolling corridors and monitoring cells with 3-D cameras and microphones for erratic or dangerous behaviour such as suicide attempts, summoning human guards when needed; it could also be driven from a computer terminal.

tasks.label: Search prisoners and vehicles and conduct shakedowns of cells for valuables and contraband, such as weapons or drugs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine pat-down/frisk of an inmate at a movement checkpoint (leaving the yard, work detail, chow, or program): officer directs the inmate into a search position, runs hands over clothing, waistband, collar, groin, socks and shoes, checks pockets and property, removes and bags any contraband found, and documents the find. Inmate may be sweaty, hostile, or resistant; dozens of searches per shift under time pressure.

Single-cell shakedown: officer removes/secures the occupant, then searches the cell - lifts and probes mattress and pillow seams, strips bedding, empties lockers and property bins, leafs through books and legal papers, checks vents, light fixture, bunk welds, window bars, sink/toilet plumbing chase, under the desk and behind the mirror, taps walls for hollow spots, distinguishes allowed property from altered items and weapons, seizes contraband, writes the report and leaves the cell habitable.

Strip / unclothed visual body search in a private search room after a contact visit, before or after transport, or at intake: officer gives verbal directions, inspects removed clothing seam by seam plus shoes, visually inspects hair, ears, mouth, armpits, body folds and feet, observes squat-and-cough, then returns clothing; must handle refusals and follow strict dignity, privacy and documentation rules.

Team shakedown of a full housing unit, dayroom, yard or work area: inmates removed and pat-searched, then a squad searches bunks, common furniture, ceiling tiles, gym and kitchen equipment, ductwork, ground and turf for buried or hidden weapons, phones, hooch and drug packages, often with metal detectors and K-9 support; hours of work over a large, cluttered, partly outdoor area.

Vehicle search at the sallyport or perimeter gate: delivery trucks, contractor and staff vehicles, and transport vans checked in and out - undercarriage checked with a mirror or pit, engine bay, wheel wells, fuel cap, cab, seats, cargo/trunk and load contents inspected, transport van interior swept before and after inmate movement for weapons or discarded contraband, and any find seized and reported.

sources.date: 2024-10 (pilot launch; still cited in 2026 trade press)
sources.title: Ga. sheriff's office piloting robot patrol program at jail to enhance security
sources.claim: The most advanced robots actually fielded inside a US jail are DEKA Sentry patrol robots at the Cobb County (GA) Adult Detention Center; they patrol perimeters and dormitories with cameras, night vision, heat detection ..., acting as sensors and deterrents. They have no manipulators and perform no searching of inmates, cells or vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security patrol and observation rounds in the same correctional environment. It shows mobile robots can operate among inmates in a jail, but the platform has no arms and no search capability, so it does not transfer to hands-on searching of persons, cells or vehicles.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics' robot dog, Spot, is becoming standard in policing
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot is the mobile robot most widely used by US law-enforcement agencies for entering and inspecting spaces during standoffs and searches, but police use is remote-controlled reconnaissance rather than autonomous work, and it does not conduct hands-on contraband searches of people, cells or vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tactical search and inspection of rooms and vehicles by police. Performance does not carry over because the deployments are operator-driven remote reconnaissance with no manipulation of clothing, bedding, property or vehicle compartments.

sources.developer: Hong Kong Correctional Services Department with a local technology firm
sources.date: 2019-02 (pilot planned for Lai Chi Kok Reception Centre)
sources.title: Tracking wristbands, video monitoring systems and drug-detecting robots - Hong Kong tests how to make its prisons 'smart'
sources.claim: Hong Kong's Correctional Services Department piloted a purpose-built robotic arm that processes an intake inmate's faecal sample held in a fixed container, jetting water to break it down so swallowed drug packages are revealed - the only fielded robot found performing any part of a prisoner contraband search, and only for this single fixtured sub-step, with officers still judging the result.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: searching for internally concealed contraband at intake. It is a fixed-program arm acting on a sample presented in a fixture, with no ability to search a person's body or clothing, a cell, or a vehicle, so it does not transfer to the listed instances.

tasks.label: Guard facility entrances to screen visitors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Social/public visiting day at a jail or prison front lobby: verify each visitor's photo ID against the approved visitor list, check dress code and signs of intoxication, require phones/keys/purses into lockers, run visitors through the walk-through metal detector, hand-wand and pat-search those who alarm, physically inspect permitted carried items (diaper bags, medical devices, ID/money), stamp or badge them, and buzz them through interlocking doors. High volume, children and elderly, occasional refusals.

Employee/contractor/volunteer entrance: check badge or ID, admit through the control vestibule, require pass-through of metal detector or body scanner, hand-search lunch containers, backpacks, tool bags and equipment carts, conduct random pat searches (staff are a leading contraband vector), issue and account for keys, radios and chits, and log entry and exit.

Professional/official visitors at the secure vestibule: attorneys, clergy, medical and mental-health providers, investigators, and transporting police officers. Verify varied credentials and appointment authorization, ensure firearms and OC spray are secured in lock boxes, inspect briefcases, legal papers and equipment for contraband, operate the interlocking doors/sally port, and record the entry.

Vehicle and delivery gate / vehicle sally port: stop the vehicle at the outer gate, check driver identity and delivery manifest, inspect cab, cargo area, trunk and undercarriage for contraband and stowaways, count tools and equipment in and out, then operate outer and inner gates in sequence so both are never open at once.

Exception handling at the entrance: a visitor alarms repeatedly, is caught with drugs, a phone or a weapon, arrives intoxicated, belligerent, or is on a banned/no-entry list. The officer refuses entry, seizes and secures contraband, calls for backup, detains the person pending local law enforcement, and documents the incident.

sources.developer: DEKA Research & Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Ga. sheriff's office piloting robot patrol program at jail to enhance security
sources.claim: The most advanced robots actually deployed inside a US jail are DEKA Sentry 'jailbots' at the Cobb County Adult Detention Center, used for perimeter patrols and security rounds as a visible deterrent with cameras and two-way audio; they do not screen or search people at entrances, and are operated in combination with a live human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior security patrol in a correctional facility. It is the closest deployed robotic system to this occupation and shows the state of the art in corrections is observation and deterrence, not credential checking, contraband searching or physical entry control.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's commercially deployed indoor security robot reads badges, opens doors and responds to access-control alarms, but when it encounters a person needing to be challenged or credentialed, a remote human specialist takes over the interaction; it performs no search of persons or property.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: indoor building access enforcement in an office (a structured human work facility). Transfers only to badge reading and door actuation; person-facing challenge and resolution is done by a remote human, so it does not substantiate autonomous screening of visitors.

sources.developer: Multiple vendors (IN Groupe, Vision-Box, IDEMIA); deployment tracked by Valour Consultancy
sources.title: 11,700+ Biometric Solutions at Airport Borders Drives Wider Automation in Airports
sources.claim: Automated border control eGates are deployed at scale in airports worldwide: self-service biometric barriers that verify a traveler's identity and travel authorization and physically admit or refuse them, with officers supervising rather than processing each traveler.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: border clearance at a controlled facility entrance — verify identity/authorization and physically admit or refuse a person. Transfers only to the identity-check-and-admit fragment; eGates perform no contraband search of the body or property and refer every exception to a human officer.

sources.system: HHLA automated container terminal road gate (OCR gate + self-service kiosk)
sources.developer: HHLA (Hamburger Hafen und Logistik AG); comparable system documented at DCT Gdańsk
sources.title: No more freezing at the gate - HHLA
sources.claim: Container terminal road gates are automated end to end: OCR/LPR portals and self-service kiosks check a truck in and open the gate without the driver meeting a gate clerk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vehicle entry processing at a controlled facility gate (a container port, an E2 setting). Transfers to credential/manifest verification and barrier operation, but not to physical inspection of cab, cargo, trunk and undercarriage for contraband or stowaways, which the port gate never performs.

sources.developer: TSA and DHS Science & Technology Directorate
sources.title: Feature Article: A Self-Service Screening Option is Coming to the Airport
sources.claim: The most automated people-screening checkpoint yet fielded is a TSA/DHS S&T self-service screening prototype at one airport, restricted to pre-vetted PreCheck travelers, in which the passenger performs the divesting and screening steps themselves; officers remain responsible for alarm resolution, pat-downs and denials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security screening of people and their belongings at a facility entrance. It is passenger-operated equipment rather than a robot performing the officer's role, remains a single-airport prototype for pre-vetted low-risk travelers, and does not perform searches, refusals or detentions.

tasks.label: Record information, such as prisoner identification, charges, and incidents of inmate disturbance, keeping daily logs of prisoner activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Inspect mail for the presence of contraband.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bulk incoming general correspondence at a jail or DOC mailroom (or centralized mail distribution center): officer slits each sealed envelope, removes and unfolds letters, cards and photos, shakes out the envelope, feels and eyeballs pages for powder residue, oily stains, strips under stamps or glued-together card layers, discards envelopes, then sorts cleared mail (or photocopies) into housing-unit bins. Hundreds to thousands of pieces per shift, mixed sizes and thicknesses.

Incoming packages, publications and property parcels: officer opens cartons and padded mailers, checks approved-vendor/publication rules, flips through books and magazines, flexes spines and bindings, unwraps items, checks hygiene products and clothing, may run the parcel through an X-ray or mmWave scanner, then repacks and forwards or rejects and returns to sender.

Legal/privileged mail: officer takes the envelope to the housing pod or intake counter, opens and inspects it in the presence of the incarcerated person without reading the content — checks the envelope interior, fans the pages, inspects tape and staples — then hands it over and logs the delivery.

Suspicious piece follow-up: a letter shows a stain, unusual stiffness, or a thickened card. Officer dons gloves/mask, isolates the item on a work surface, swabs it for an ion-scan or runs a presumptive field test, photographs it, seizes and bags it as evidence, completes a contraband/incident report and notifies investigators or K-9.

Outgoing mail inspection: officer inspects outgoing inmate correspondence before dispatch — checks envelopes for enclosed items, unauthorized enclosures, metal or bulk, verifies sender identification, then reseals and bundles the mail for the postal carrier.

sources.title: VADOC First Corrections System to Pilot State-of-the-Art Drug and Contraband Detection Scanner from ScanTech — Virginia Department of Corrections
sources.claim: ScanTech AI's SENTINEL fixed-gantry CT scanner was loaned to the Virginia DOC for a six-month pilot at its Centralized Mail Distribution Center to screen incoming inmate mail; its AI automates detection but explicitly serves to assist human operators, and it neither opens mail nor extracts or seizes contraband.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task setting (corrections mail screening), but the machine only images sealed mail for an operator; opening, content examination, seizure and logging remain human.

sources.system: Eagle Remittance Processor / Model 72 mail opener-extractor
sources.title: OPEX Products | Automation Equipment & Systems
sources.claim: OPEX's Eagle remittance processor automatically opens envelopes, extracts contents, images and sorts mail at high speed, showing that envelope opening and content extraction are mechanizable — but it makes no contraband determination and handles clean remittance mail, not drug-laced paper or concealed items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = high-volume remittance mail opening/extraction. Transfer fails for this task: the machine performs no inspection or contraband judgment, and its feed assumes uniform paper contents, not pills, strips, powders or thickened cards.

sources.title: Inmate Legal Mail Use Case | Smuggling Contraband | RaySecur
sources.claim: RaySecur's MailSecur mmWave desktop scanners, marketed to corrections for letter and legal-mail screening, depend on a human operator watching the real-time image to identify powders, liquids and soaked paper; detection is not autonomous and the item still must be handled by staff.

sources.title: Correctional Facilities Have a Mail Problem - Correctional News
sources.claim: Trade coverage of corrections mailrooms states that X-ray screening machines are ineffective against the dominant mail contraband — drug-laced paper, suboxone strips and small traces of powder or liquid — so machine screening cannot substitute for officers opening and examining the contents.

sources.title: Mail & Parcel X-Ray Screening Machines - Point Security Inc
sources.claim: Commercial mail and parcel X-ray inspection machines are built around an operator: the machine flags a foreign object and notifies a person, who must then investigate, open and resolve the item.

sources.system: ABOT M1 Automated Box Opening system
sources.title: ABOT Automated Box Opening - DAC Robotics
sources.claim: DAC Robotics' ABOT autonomously opens mixed-size cartons fed by conveyor in warehouse decant lines, showing autonomous box opening exists — but the system only removes lids/tops for downstream picking and performs no inspection of contents for concealed contraband.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = warehouse carton opening/decanting. Transfer fails: opening a box is only the first step; no cited system inspects books, bindings, wrappers or clothing for concealed contraband or makes a seize/reject decision.

tasks.label: Maintain records of prisoners' identification and charges.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Use weapons, handcuffs, and physical force to maintain discipline and order among prisoners.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine restraint application on a cooperative inmate in a housing unit or sally port: ordering the inmate to back up to the cuff port, applying handcuffs (often behind the back), adding leg irons/waist chain for escort or transport, double-locking and checking for tightness, escorting with a hands-on grip, then removing restraints at the destination. Standard-issue restraints, many repetitions per shift.

Spontaneous hands-on force: breaking up an inmate fight or controlling a combative inmate in a dayroom, chow hall, or recreation yard. Verbal commands, then physical control holds/takedown of a resisting adult, separating fighters, gaining wrist control and applying cuffs while the person struggles, minimizing injury to inmate and staff, coordinating with responding officers.

Planned use-of-force cell extraction of a barricaded or refusing inmate: team formation with shield and protective gear, chemical agent introduction, forced cell entry, pinning and restraining the inmate on the bunk or floor, applying cuffs and leg irons, decontamination and escort to a holding cell, all on video and within policy.

Deploying less-lethal weapons to stop a disturbance or assault: OC spray at close range, pepperball or 40mm foam baton rounds from a housing-unit floor, tier, or control post during a multi-inmate fight or riot; judging the threat, giving warnings, choosing target and munition, then transitioning to restraint and medical checks.

Booking/intake control of an intoxicated, mentally ill, or combative arrestee in a jail booking area: taking the person to the ground or wall, search control, removing arrest cuffs and applying facility restraints, placing and strapping the person into a restraint chair or soft restraints, then periodic checks.

Armed post and armed escort duty: carrying a firearm on a perimeter/tower post or on outside escorts to court or a hospital, presenting or discharging the weapon to halt an escape or a life-threatening assault, and maintaining restraint and weapon control over inmates in transit or in an outside holding area.

sources.developer: DEKA Research & Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Meet the nearly 6-foot tall robots patrolling a Ga. jail
sources.claim: Robots piloted inside a US jail are patrol/observation platforms: DEKA Sentry robots at the Cobb County (GA) Adult Detention Center do perimeter patrols and security rounds ... dormitories; no restraint, hands-on force, or weapon use is part of the deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic deployment to this task's own setting (a US jail); shows the fielded capability envelope in corrections is patrol and observation, not restraint or force.

sources.title: Knightscope’s Autonomous Security Robots Delivers Technology for Public Safety
sources.claim: Commercially deployed autonomous security robots operate as mobile sensing and alerting platforms; they do not physically detain, restrain, or apply force to people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous security patrol of institutional facilities); establishes that the most mature autonomous security robots stop at detection and alerting, leaving all physical force to human officers.

sources.system: Robo-Guard correctional patrol robot (Pohang prison trial)
sources.developer: Asian Forum for Corrections / Kyonggi University
sources.title: Robot guards being tested in South Korea
sources.claim: Prison guard robots trialed in a correctional facility monitored inmates for abnormal behavior and could be manually driven by human guards; they performed no physical intervention with inmates.
sources.transferJustification: Same occupational setting (guarding inmates); shows correctional robots serve as monitoring aids under human control, with discipline and force retained by officers.

sources.title: China Debuts Anbot, The Police Robot
sources.claim: Police robots that carry force options deliver them under remote human control rather than autonomously: the AnBot patrol robot's riot-control function is a remotely fired electric-shock device.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (riot control by a security robot); the force element is remotely triggered, so it cannot support an autonomous judgment for applying force to prisoners.

sources.title: China's AI spherical robot cop can capture criminals, patrol streets
sources.claim: The RT-G spherical police robot, tested with Chinese police on streets, can be fitted with net guns, tear gas and sound devices to immobilize a person; its capture/weapon deployment is not established as operating without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic apprehension of a resisting person); even this most advanced example nets a person rather than restraining and cuffing, and its capture function is not shown to run autonomously.

sources.title: Axon halts its plans for a Taser drone as 9 on ethics board resign over the project
sources.claim: Robotic delivery of a less-lethal weapon against people was developed and then halted; no fielded robot autonomously selects a human target and deploys a less-lethal weapon in US law enforcement or corrections.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic use of a less-lethal weapon on a person); the leading US effort stopped at development, so no cited system substantiates weapon use to control inmates.

sources.title: Development of a nursing-care assistant robot RIBA that can lift a human in its arms
sources.claim: Whole-body robotic handling of a human remains a research prototype demonstrated only with cooperative subjects: RIBA lifted a person between bed and wheelchair in the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (a robot physically manipulating a human body); performance does not transfer, since it requires a cooperative, non-resisting person in a lab and remains a prototype, far from controlling a resisting inmate.

tasks.label: Use nondisciplinary tools and equipment, such as a computer.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Housing-unit or booking-area officer works at a networked computer terminal in the jail/prison: enters shift log entries, inmate counts, movement and incident data into the offender/jail management system, and completes required electronic forms and email. Output is a record in the institutional information system.

Officer queries facility information systems on a computer: looks up inmate records, charges, classification, housing assignments, visitor lists, court dates, and property/commissary accounts to answer questions or verify identity before movement.

Control-room officer operates the console: two-way radio, telephone/switchboard and intercom, CCTV monitors, and the electronic door-control panel/touchscreen used to open and close security passages for staff, visitors, and inmates.

Officer carries and uses routine handheld non-force equipment in the housing unit or corridor: portable radio, flashlight, keys or fob for doors, and a handheld reader/barcode scanner used to register security-round checkpoints and inmate ID wristbands.

Intake/screening officer runs specialized nondisciplinary equipment at a fixed station: body-scanner or mail x-ray console, Live Scan fingerprint capture, ID camera, and breath/drug-test devices, following the device's prompts and transmitting results into the records system.

tasks.label: Conduct fire, safety, and sanitation inspections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/weekly sanitation and fire-hazard inspection of inmate cells and dormitory living areas with inmates present: officer enters or opens each cell, checks bunks, lockers, shelves, sinks/toilets, floors, walls, vents and light fixtures for filth, excess combustible paper/linen, covered vents or altered fixtures; orders inmates to correct deficiencies and records violations.

Shift fire and life-safety walkthrough of housing-unit common areas, corridors, dayrooms, stairwells and sallyports: verify extinguishers present and charged, egress paths and exits unobstructed, fire doors not propped, exit/emergency lighting intact, spills/trash/damaged fixtures noted; findings logged.

Scheduled documented inspection/testing of fire and life-safety equipment: handling extinguishers to check pin, seal, weight and tag, pressing emergency-light test buttons, checking pull stations, hose cabinets and sprinkler risers, verifying fire doors latch, then initialing tags and filing the inspection form.

Sanitation inspection of food service, laundry, medical and barber/shower areas: cleanliness under and behind equipment, food holding temperatures taken with a probe, dish-machine/sanitizer chemical checks, chemical and sharps/tool accountability, pest evidence; written report of deficiencies.

Outdoor grounds, recreation-yard and perimeter safety inspection: walk fence lines and yard for damage, tampering, tripping hazards, debris, standing water, burned-out lighting, improperly stored flammables and thrown-over contraband; log findings.

Housekeeping/safety inspection of vocational shops, maintenance, storage and support areas (often unoccupied at time of inspection): blocked electrical panels or egress, debris and spills, flammable/chemical storage condition, tool shadow-board/5S board status, signage and PPE stations; findings logged.

sources.system: Spot with Orbit AI visual inspections
sources.title: Spot at Cargill | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot runs unaided autonomous inspection missions through Cargill's Amsterdam Multiseed food plant, including AI visual safety checks for seed spills, emergency doors propped open, 5S/safety signage and whether fire extinguishers are in place and working.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = routine fire/safety/housekeeping walkthrough inspection of a work facility. The perception targets (extinguisher present and working, propped emergency doors, spills and debris on floors) and the output (a logged deficiency record replacing a human walk-through) are the same ones a correctional officer's common-area fire/safety and sanitation round produces.

sources.title: See Your Facility Like Never Before | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Orbit release lets Spot autonomously patrol a facility, capture images at points of interest and have vision-language prompts flag safety issues such as spills or missing fire extinguishers, logging results digitally.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as the Cargill item: a scheduled autonomous visual hazard round with a digital record, which is what the fire/safety walkthrough portion of a correctional inspection consists of; it does not cover physically handling or testing equipment.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously navigates occupied human work buildings on scheduled routes performing security patrols and facility checks, with anomaly detection (open doors, leaks, spills) and remote specialists handling escalations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = indoor patrol/facility-check rounds in a structured, human-occupied building. It demonstrates autonomous navigation of human corridors and doorways plus anomaly reporting, the mobility and reporting substrate of a corridor-level safety round.

sources.developer: DEKA Research & Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office Enhances Security at the Adult Detention Center with Cutting-Edge DEKA Sentry Robots
sources.claim: Cobb County Sheriff's Office deployed DEKA Sentry robots inside its Adult Detention Center for perimeter patrols and security rounds ... selected inmate dormitories; the robots navigate the facility autonomously with an operator taking control for complex tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = routine security rounds inside an occupied jail. It establishes that a mobile robot can autonomously run repeated rounds through jail corridors, dorms and the perimeter with inmates present — the environmental condition that the industrial inspection robots do not themselves demonstrate.

sources.title: How Swiss Robotics Company ANYbotics and SAP Are Turning Dirty, Dusty, and Dangerous Industrial Inspections into Business Insights
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot autonomously navigates industrial sites (refineries, offshore platforms, cement and chemical plants) collecting visual, thermal, acoustic and gas-leak inspection data on routine rounds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = scheduled hazard-detection inspection rounds (hot spots, leaks) in indoor and outdoor institutional facilities; confirms multi-sensor safety rounds with automatic reporting are a mature commercial capability in structured facilities.

sources.title: Autonomous public safety robots on patrol, connected by Verizon
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots are deployed on pre-defined outdoor patrols of campuses, parking lots and grounds, detecting people and anomalies day and night with video and thermal sensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous outdoor grounds/perimeter patrol on an institutional campus, the mobility and observation basis for an outdoor yard and fence-line safety walk; it covers presence and anomaly detection, not hands-on checks.

tasks.label: Take prisoners into custody and escort to locations within and outside of facility, such as visiting room, courtroom, or airport.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine intra-facility escort of a compliant inmate: officer opens the cell/housing unit, applies handcuffs (often behind the back, sometimes through a cuff port), takes physical control of the inmate's arm, walks him through corridors and sally ports to the visiting room, medical clinic, law library or program area, coordinating door control, pat-searching before and after, and returning him to his cell.

Escort of a high-risk, restricted-housing or potentially non-compliant inmate: two-officer escort with waist chain and leg irons applied through the food port, hands-on control of the inmate's arms during movement, readiness to take the inmate to the ground or apply additional restraints if he pulls away, spits, or resists; may include a resistive extraction and placement in a holding cell or restraint chair.

Taking custody at intake/booking: receiving an arrestee from arresting officers in the sally port, transferring/removing their handcuffs, performing a hands-on pat or strip search, controlling an often intoxicated, agitated or uncooperative person, and walking them to a holding cell, medical screening, or fingerprint station.

Court run: applying full restraints (cuffs, belly chain, leg irons) to several inmates, escorting them from the housing unit to a transport van, securing them in the van, driving to the courthouse, then escorting them through courthouse corridors and holding cells into the courtroom, unshackling/reshackling as the judge directs, and returning them to the jail.

Outside escort trip: hospital appointment, emergency-room bedside watch, airport extradition, or funeral/deathbed visit — restraining and escorting a single inmate through public and semi-public spaces (ER waiting rooms, airport concourses, curbside, private premises), maintaining continuous physical control and supervision among uninvolved members of the public.

sources.title: Ga. sheriff's office piloting robot patrol program at jail to enhance security
sources.claim: The most advanced robots actually deployed inside a U.S. jail (DEKA Sentry, Cobb County Adult Detention Center) perform perimeter patrol and dormitory security rounds with cameras, night vision and ...; they make no physical contact with inmates and a live operator takes over for complex tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed correctional-robot evidence: same environment (jail housing units and grounds) but limited to surveillance/deterrence, establishing that no fielded system takes custody of, restrains, or escorts an inmate.

sources.developer: RIKEN and Sumitomo Riko Company Limited
sources.title: Engineering a robot that assists in direct nursing care
sources.claim: Robots capable of physically handling a human body exist only as experimental research prototypes that lift cooperative, non-resisting patients in a lab setting; none are deployed and none control an unwilling person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically moving a human body. It is the state of the art for robot-human physical handling, yet involves compliant patients in a lab, so it does not transfer to restraining and escorting a potentially resistive prisoner.

sources.title: China Tests Autonomous 'Spherical' Robot Police Unit in Cities
sources.claim: Police patrol robots fielded in public spaces (RT-G spherical robot, Wenzhou/Shenzhen) at most detect and immobilize suspects with stand-off non-lethal tools; they do not cuff, take custody of, or escort a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: police control of a person. Even the most aggressive fielded law-enforcement robot only applies stand-off non-lethal force, showing no system performs the manual restraint-and-escort control this task requires.

tasks.label: Participate in required job training.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mandated classroom or e-learning in-service blocks at the facility training room or agency academy: policy and legal updates, PREA, suicide prevention/mental health, ethics, report writing; officer attends, participates in discussion, takes and passes a written test to receive credit hours.

Defensive tactics / use-of-force refresher in the academy gym or facility multipurpose room: officer practices handcuffing and restraint application, escort holds, takedowns and ground defense on mats with a partner, plus cell-extraction team drills in shield/helmet gear, and is signed off as proficient by an instructor.

Annual firearms training and live-fire qualification at the agency's range: officer receives weapon, performs safe handling, loading, drawing and firing a timed qualification course at varying distances with handgun (and shotgun/rifle for tower or transport posts), must meet a minimum passing score to remain post-eligible.

Facility-based scenario and on-the-job training inside the institution: fire and evacuation drills, disturbance/emergency response drills, search-and-contraband practice, hands-on familiarization with radios, keys, restraints, chemical agents and OC exposure, done on shift with supervisors observing while the housing unit is occupied.

CPR/AED/first-aid and bloodborne-pathogen recertification: officer performs compressions and rescue breathing on manikins, applies AED pads, practices bleeding control and PPE donning, and must demonstrate the skills to a certified instructor to earn the card.

sources.date: 2026 (product in commercial service; company site retrieved 2026)
sources.title: MARATHON – Autonomous Robotic Targets for Live Fire Tactical Training
sources.claim: Autonomous armored humanoid robots are commercially fielded on live-fire ranges as moving targets for law enforcement and military marksmanship training; the robot is the training aid, not a trainee, and it does not receive, perform or complete any required officer training curriculum.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic presence in correctional/law-enforcement training environments, but it does NOT transfer: the robot serves as a shootable moving target on a range, whereas the task requires the trainee to attend, perform and be certified in firearms, defensive tactics, medical and policy training. No capability to undergo or complete training is demonstrated.

sources.system: Marathon Targets autonomous robotic targets (police range use)
sources.title: Day two at SHOT Show: From AI-driven robots for live-fire training to intelligent noise-cancellation tech
sources.claim: Trade press confirms these autonomous robotic humanoids are used in police live-fire training programs at agency ranges, again strictly as targets operated by instructors rather than as participants completing a training curriculum.
sources.transferJustification: Same non-transfer as above: the system is training equipment on a controlled range, not an entity that participates in, is evaluated on, and is certified through required correctional officer training.

tasks.label: Serve meals, distribute commissary items, and dispense prescribed medication to prisoners.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cell-front meal tray service in segregation/lockdown/medical-isolation housing: officer moves an insulated tray cart down the tier, has each food port unlocked, passes the correct tray (including special/medical diets) to an inmate locked behind the door, then returns to retrieve trays and count utensils, logging refusals and hunger strikes.

Chow-hall/dining-line service in a prison: standardized trays portioned and passed out along a serving line (often with inmate food-service workers), officer moves lines of inmates through, enforces portions and diet cards, watches for utensil theft and food passing, and clears the hall on a tight schedule.

Jail housing-pod meal service: cart of trays wheeled into the dayroom, inmates called up by cell or table, officer hands each a tray and drink, tracks who has been fed, then collects and counts trays, cups and spoons before the cart leaves.

Commissary distribution: pre-bagged vendor orders brought to the housing unit, officer calls each inmate, verifies ID/wristband against the receipt, hands over the bag, obtains a signature, and handles shortages, damaged goods, refusals and indigent items.

General-population medication pass at a med window or med cart line: inmates queue, officer/med tech verifies identity, issues the pre-packaged prescribed dose with water, watches the inmate swallow and does a mouth check, documents administration and refusals.

Cell-front medication pass in segregation, infirmary or lockdown: doses carried cell to cell, passed through the food port to a confined inmate, ingestion observed through the door window, refusals documented.

sources.title: US Army pilots first autonomous dining facility in South Korea
sources.claim: US Army pilot autonomous dining facility where a robotic kitchen autonomously portions, cooks and plates a meal that the diner picks up at the machine inside a working dining facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: institutional meal service. Same output as a chow line - a portioned, plated meal handed to the eater at the point of service - with food fixtured in the machine's hoppers, i.e. the work brought to the machine.

sources.title: Sweetgreen automated kitchen concept improves retention, margins
sources.claim: Automated makeline assembles and portions food orders into bowls in operating restaurants, running as the production line of the store.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning food into serving vessels on a line. Comparable objects (bulk food, trays/bowls) and precision to a correctional serving line, with ingredients presented in fixed hoppers - a purpose-built machine station.

sources.title: Zara taps Cleveron parcel automation solution for faster, easier Click and Collect delivery
sources.claim: Robotic parcel machines store pre-packed orders and release the correct order to a recipient after a code/ID scan, in seconds, in retail stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing a pre-bagged order to a verified recipient. Commissary distribution is the same transaction - match a pre-packed bag to an identified person, release it, log it - with bags loaded into the machine as a purpose-built setting would present them.

sources.title: Cleveron AS - Parcel and Postal Technology International
sources.claim: Cleveron's automated pickup machines are in wide commercial service internationally.
sources.transferJustification: Same system as above; establishes maturity and scale of automated order handover to verified recipients.

sources.system: InSite In-Facility Medication Packaging and Dispensing System
sources.title: Facing a Nursing Staffing Crisis, Correctional Facilities Seek Solutions to Streamline Medication Management
sources.claim: Fully automated in-facility system packages and dispenses per-inmate medication doses inside correctional facilities, with dose-level accountability.

sources.title: Municipality - Service description | Evondos
sources.claim: A medicine-dispensing robot releases only the correct prescribed dose at the scheduled time directly to the person taking it, with adherence logging; in service across hundreds of Nordic municipalities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled medication administration to a patient. Same objects (unit-dose pouches), same requirement (right person, right dose, right time, documented), with medication fixtured inside the machine.

sources.title: Amazon Pharmacy Kiosk: A New Era for Patients
sources.claim: Robotic dispensing kiosks release prescription medication to an identified patient on site in clinics and retail pharmacies, with a remote pharmacist verifying by video.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispensing a prescribed medication to an identified individual who presents at the machine. Same objects and accountability requirements as a jail med window; the remote pharmacist is oversight, not teleoperation of the mechanism.

sources.title: Moxi the Robot: Delivering Meds and Stealing Hearts
sources.claim: Mobile manipulator robots make autonomous medication and supply deliveries at scale inside hospitals, but the deliveries are staff-facing hand-offs, not deliveries into the hands of patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: last-mile medication delivery inside an institution. Establishes that autonomous transport in E2 corridors is solved, while the recipient-facing hand-off (the officer's actual act) is explicitly out of scope.

sources.title: The robotic delivery of hospital meals
sources.claim: Autonomous hospital transport robots move meal trays and medications through corridors between kitchen/pharmacy and nursing units; ward staff distribute the individual trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk meal-cart transport in an institution. Covers only the transport sub-step of cell-front service; the per-recipient hand-off and tray/utensil retrieval are not performed.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Cobb jail deploys sentry robots in 90-day pilot program
sources.claim: Autonomous security robots have been deployed inside a US county jail for patrols and rounds in housing areas; their functions are surveillance and deterrence, not meal, commissary or medication service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobility inside jail housing areas. Shows navigation in the actual E2 setting is possible, but no service or hand-off capability is demonstrated.

sources.title: Hospitality Robotics: Room Service and Delivery Robots
sources.claim: Hotel delivery robots autonomously carry items to a recipient's door and unlock a bin for the recipient to take the item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: door-level item delivery to a named recipient in an institution-controlled building. Recipients are cooperative guests who open their own doors; it does not cover locked cells, positive inmate identification, or contraband/diversion control.

tasks.label: Settle disputes between inmates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine verbal dispute in a housing-unit dayroom (TV channel, phone/kiosk turn, seating, food tray, noise, borrowed property). Officer reads body language, steps between the two inmates, gives directives, separates them, reassigns seats or orders lock-in, and verifies the unit settles.

Cellmate/bunkmate conflict reported or observed. Officer interviews each inmate separately, judges credibility and safety concerns (debt, hygiene, sexual pressure), mediates an agreement or arranges a bunk/cell move with the housing sergeant or classification, and follows up.

Active physical altercation between two or more inmates in a dayroom, tier, or shower area. Officer calls a code, issues loud commands, physically separates or takes combatants to the ground with backup, applies handcuffs, escorts them to medical and segregation, secures the unit, and writes reports.

Group or gang-linked tension during mass movement (dining hall, rec yard, work detail, gym) with dozens of inmates present and a crowd forming. Officer intervenes amid onlookers, disperses the group, isolates instigators, and coordinates radio response before it becomes a mass fight.

Dispute in a booking/holding cell, court holding, or on a transport bus: unclassified, often intoxicated, withdrawing, or mentally ill detainees in a crowded confined space; officer verbally intervenes through the bars or shackled seating, splits the cell, or moves one detainee, with limited backup.

sources.system: DEKA Sentry robot (Cobb County Adult Detention Center pilot)
sources.developer: DEKA Research & Development / Cobb County Sheriff's Office
sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office Enhances Security at the Adult Detention Center with Cutting-Edge DEKA Sentry Robots
sources.claim: Three DEKA Sentry robots were deployed on a pilot at the Cobb County (GA) Adult Detention Center, assisting deputies with perimeter patrols and security ... selected dormitories; they patrol and report while human deputies handle incidents and inmate conflict.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed corrections robot to this task: it operates inside jail housing units (same environment and population), but its function is patrol and observation, with no capability to intervene in or resolve an inmate dispute.

sources.title: Cobb County Sheriff's Office piloting robot patrol program at jail
sources.claim: The same jail robots patrol dorms, hallways and the perimeter and are described as helping detect contraband, medical emergencies or ... - i.e., sensing and alerting staff rather than intervening in or settling inmate conflicts.
sources.transferJustification: Detecting violence in a jail dorm is the sensing precursor to this task; the source shows the robot's role ends at detection, with officers performing the intervention and resolution.

sources.system: Korean robotic prison guard (Asian Forum for Corrections)
sources.developer: Asian Forum for Corrections / Kyonggi University
sources.title: South Korean Prison To Feature Robot Guards
sources.claim: The best-known 'robot prison guard' trial (Pohang, South Korea) placed patrol robots in a jail purely in a support role to monitor for abnormal behavior and notify human officers; it did not intervene between prisoners.
sources.transferJustification: Same setting (jail housing area) and population; establishes that purpose-built corrections robots are limited to monitoring and alerting, not settling disputes between inmates.

sources.developer: Singapore Home Team Science and Technology Agency / A*STAR
sources.title: Singapore trials patrol robots to warn people of "undesirable" behavior: "It reminds me of Robocop"
sources.claim: Autonomous public-space patrol robots (Singapore's Xavier) detect 'undesirable social behaviour' and broadcast pre-set warnings while relaying video to a human command centre; they do not mediate between people or physically separate them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous verbal behavioural intervention with unruly members of the public in an institution-controlled facility. It shows the ceiling of deployed capability is scripted broadcast warnings plus escalation to humans, far short of resolving an inmate conflict.

sources.title: AI in Prison? Robot Guards? How the Criminal Justice System Is Adopting Tech
sources.claim: Reporting on AI and robotics in US corrections as of 2025 describes officer-support robots (meal, medication, escort delivery) and AI-driven corrections robots as prospective, with proponents hoping for deployment within roughly ten years.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes absence of any currently deployed robotic system performing inmate-supervision duties such as dispute resolution; used only to support negative judgments.

tasks.label: Provide to supervisors oral and written reports of the quality and quantity of work performed by inmates, inmate disturbances and rule violations, and unusual occurrences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Drive passenger vehicles and trucks used to transport inmates to other institutions, courtrooms, hospitals, and work sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Metro/suburban court run: a transport team (2+ officers, one designated driver) moves 5-12 restrained inmates in a caged van or small bus from the county jail vehicle sallyport to the courthouse holding-cell garage on city streets, on a fixed weekday schedule; escorting officers load, restrain and monitor the inmates, the driver's deliverable is the secure road leg plus pre-trip vehicle inspection and gate/radio coordination.

Small-agency solo run: one officer pat-searches, shackles and loads one or two inmates, drives them across town or to a neighboring county (jail-to-jail, court, probation/clinic appointment), monitors them through the cage the whole way, and escorts them inside at the destination; no second officer aboard.

Medical transport in a metro area: driver plus guard officer take 1-2 inmates in an unmarked car or caged van to a hospital, dialysis or specialty clinic, often unscheduled and at night or on weekends, in traffic and weather, with hospital-garage/ER-entrance approaches and a wait-and-return leg.

Inter-facility transfer: prison bus or transport van with escort officers runs a recurring hub-and-spoke corridor between institutions (reception center to prison, county to state DOC), 1-6 hours mostly on interstates and state highways, including rural stretches and secure yard/sallyport entries at both ends.

Work-crew transport: officer drives a crew van or flatbed truck, sometimes towing a trailer of mowers/tools, carrying 6-12 minimum-custody inmates to outdoor work sites (roadside litter pickup, county grounds, farm, forestry), with unpaved access lanes, ad-hoc shoulder staging, multiple stops and midday moves between sites.

Movement inside institution grounds: driving inmates in a van or utility truck between housing units, intake, industries buildings or the prison farm over campus service roads, through vehicle sallyports, gate interlocks and loading docks on the secured perimeter.

sources.title: Waymo crosses 450,000 weekly paid rides as Alphabet robotaxi unit widens lead on Tesla
sources.claim: Waymo runs a fully driverless commercial passenger-carrying service on public city streets in multiple US metros, with no employee aboard, at very large scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless passenger transport on public roads. It transfers to the driving leg of an inmate transport because the road environment (metro streets, traffic, curbside/garage pickup and drop-off, night and weather) and the deliverable (occupants carried point-to-point without an operator) are the same; only the vehicle's secure cage differs.

sources.title: Waymo begins offering freeway robotaxi rides in San Francisco, LA and Phoenix
sources.claim: Waymo's driverless vehicles carry passengers on freeways at highway speeds in three major markets, extending the demonstrated envelope beyond surface streets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-speed freeway passenger transport. Court, hospital and inter-facility inmate runs use the same freeway segments, so demonstrated driverless freeway operation covers that portion of the driving.

sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Aurora operates commercial Class 8 trucks with no human in the ... on public Texas highways, the heavy-vehicle analogue of a prison bus road leg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless operation of a heavy vehicle over a fixed public-highway corridor between two terminals. An inter-facility inmate transfer is the same repeated corridor drive in a bus-class vehicle, so heavy-vehicle highway autonomy carries over to the road leg.

sources.title: Aurora Expands Driverless Trucking Service from Fort Worth to El Paso
sources.claim: Aurora has scaled driverless heavy-truck operation to a second 600-mile public-highway corridor and past 100,000 driverless miles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-distance driverless heavy-vehicle runs including long rural highway stretches, matching the rural interstate portion of prison-to-prison transfer runs.

sources.title: Groundbreaking 2025 Milestone: Kodiak Driverless Trucks Revolutionize Permian Oilfield Logistics
sources.claim: Kodiak-equipped driverless trucks run commercially on rough, dusty private lease roads in the ..., an operator-controlled off-highway site with livestock and unpaved surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless heavy-vehicle operation on unpaved site roads. It transfers to work-crew transport driving on graded access lanes within a controlled site, but only where routes are pre-mapped and the site operator manages traffic.

sources.system: May Mobility driver-out Toyota Sienna autonomous shuttles
sources.title: May Mobility Now Offers Autonomous Driverless Rides in Peachtree Corners
sources.claim: May Mobility runs commercial passenger shuttle service with no operator on board on public suburban roads, showing driverless vehicles carrying groups of riders on fixed local routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless multi-passenger shuttle service over fixed short local routes. This matches campus-road and fixed-route inmate movement where riders are loaded by staff and the vehicle only has to drive the leg.
