tasks.label: Issue clothing, tools, and other authorized items to inmates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Intake/booking: officer issues a newly booked inmate a correctly sized jumpsuit/uniform, underwear, shoes, towel, bedroll (sheets, blanket, mattress) and a hygiene kit at the receiving counter; identity and issued-property record entered in the jail management system; arrestee may be uncooperative or intoxicated.

Weekly clothing/linen exchange on a housing unit: officer works a laundry cart in the dayroom, inmates line up, one-for-one exchange of soiled uniforms/towels/sheets for clean ones in the right size, counts reconciled and refusals/shortages documented.

Routine supply issue at the unit officer's station or supply window: hygiene items, indigent kits, paper, pens, requested authorized property or commissary items handed to a verified inmate and charged/logged to that inmate's account.

Tool issue in prison industries, a vocational shop or on a maintenance detail: tools drawn from a shadow-boarded crib and signed out to a named inmate worker, restricted-tool rules applied, return verified and counts reconciled before the detail is released.

Controlled-item issue at cell fronts, including restrictive housing: razors, cleaning chemicals, recreation gear or legal supplies passed through food/cuff ports to individual inmates in locked cells, then retrieved and counted after use.

sources.system: Polytex workwear dispensing units (D200 PRO and standard models)
sources.title: Workwear Dispensing Units | Polytex
sources.claim: Polytex commercial workwear/scrub dispensing units automatically dispense garments to an individual after a card tap, with optional UHF RFID tagging so each issued item is recorded against the user; sold and installed in healthcare facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing institutional clothing to authenticated individuals. Same objects (folded uniforms/scrubs, sized), same accountability requirement (per-person record of what was issued), same kind of counter/corridor point-of-issue as a jail clothing room.

sources.title: GME Policy #245 SCRUBEX SYSTEM USE
sources.claim: A deployed hospital scrub dispensing system (ScrubEx) enforces one-for-one exchange: staff authenticate with an ID badge or PIN and must deposit soiled scrubs to be credited and to draw a clean set.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clean-for-soiled garment exchange with per-person accountability, which is the mechanism of an inmate laundry/linen exchange (one-for-one swap, credit tracked per individual).

sources.system: Scrub dispensary/vending machines at Nebraska Medicine
sources.developer: University of Nebraska Medical Center / Nebraska Medicine (vendor unnamed in source)
sources.title: New scrub vending machines being dispensed | Newsroom | University of Nebraska Medical Center
sources.claim: Automated scrub dispensing cabinets in operation at a US academic medical center authenticate the user by ID badge, hold inventory assigned by size and piece, and read the RFID of every garment removed to associate it with that individual and flag over-draws.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing sized institutional clothing to a verified individual with an auditable record — the same output a booking officer produces when issuing a jumpsuit and logging it to the inmate.

sources.system: Snap-on AutoCrib RoboCrib VX1000 / TX750 industrial vending machines
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved); product line in service for over a decade
sources.title: RoboCrib® VX1000 | Industrial Vending Machine | Snap-on AutoCrib®
sources.claim: The RoboCrib industrial vending machine uses counter-rotating carousels to dispense virtually any stocked item in under 10 seconds and manages the secure issue and return ... to authenticated users; AutoCrib machines are installed in over 20,000 locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tool-crib issue and return with per-user accountability. Objects (hand tools, power tools, gauges), precision (correct item to correct authenticated worker), and the check-in/count discipline match a prison-industries tool issue window.

sources.title: VENDING CASE STUDY – MACHINERY MANUFACTURING
sources.claim: A machinery manufacturer deployed Fastenal FAST 5000 industrial vending machines across most of its plants to dispense and track consumables and PPE per user, producing documented control over who drew which items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: controlled issue of consumable supplies (gloves, safety glasses, abrasives) to identified workers with a usage record — the same act as issuing hygiene/supply items to a named inmate and charging the account.

sources.system: Commissary vending machines, Scott County Jail housing units
sources.developer: Scott County (Iowa) Sheriff's Office with contracted commissary vendor
sources.title: Housing | Scott County Iowa
sources.claim: A US county jail operates vending machines located inside inmate housing units from which inmates purchase authorized commissary items, i.e. automated dispensing of authorized goods to inmates inside a secure facility.
sources.transferJustification: Direct analog in the target setting: a machine, rather than an officer, dispenses authorized items to inmates, confirming that machine-stocked dispensing is an accepted mode of issue in corrections.

sources.title: Press | Hotel Delivery Robot Deployed in Los Angeles, California
sources.claim: Relay autonomous delivery robots are deployed in hotels, self-driving through corridors and elevators to guest room doors to deliver towels, amenities and other supplies without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport and doorside handover of small authorized items inside an institution-controlled building; shows what mobile robots can do at E2 (carrying a pre-loaded item), but not selection, recipient verification or retrieval.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi mobile manipulation robots operate autonomously in more than 25 US ..., running supply, lab and pharmacy deliveries through corridors, elevators and badge-controlled doors, with over one million deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point delivery of supplies inside a structured institution. Establishes E2 navigation and drop-off, but the cited deployments do not include person-by-person issue, sizing, or retrieval of controlled items.

tasks.label: Arrange daily schedules for prisoners, including library visits, work assignments, family visits, and counseling appointments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Search for and recapture escapees.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Count discrepancy or attempted escape inside a secure prison/jail: officers lock down, sweep housing units, utility chases, kitchens, ceiling voids and recreation yards inside the secure perimeter, find the inmate concealed on the premises, physically control and handcuff him (often resisting), and return him to segregation with a use-of-force/incident report.

Breach of the secure perimeter just discovered: officers sweep the institution's grounds, fence line, sally port, outbuildings, motor pool and outbound delivery vehicles, and take the escapee into custody hiding on institution property (under a truck, in a trash bin, in a maintenance shed), restraining and returning him inside.

Walkaway from a minimum-security camp, work-release center, or outside work detail: officers search adjacent fields, woods, ditches, roadsides and known local addresses, often with tracking dogs and local police, then confront a usually non-violent but sometimes fleeing escapee in open terrain and cuff and transport him back.

Inmate flees during a transport or outside trip (hospital, clinic, courthouse, vehicle stop): the officer gives immediate foot chase through parking lots, streets, hospital grounds or wooded lots, physically tackles or overtakes the running inmate, re-applies restraints, and secures him in the transport vehicle.

Escapee at large in the community: correctional staff join a multi-agency manhunt over hours or days — perimeter posts, roadblocks, grid searches of rural terrain and neighborhoods, clearing barns and outbuildings, following K9 and aerial leads — ending in physical apprehension of a possibly armed, resisting fugitive.

sources.developer: DEKA / Cobb County Sheriff's Office deployment
sources.title: Georgia jail welcomes state-of-the-art robots to security team | FOX 5 Atlanta
sources.claim: DEKA Sentry 'jail bots' at the Cobb County (GA) jail navigate the facility autonomously on perimeter patrols and dorm security rounds with cameras, night vision and heat detection, but only detect and alert deputies; a live operator takes over for complex tasks and the robots perform no detention or physical control of inmates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior/perimeter security patrol of a correctional facility — the same searching environment as an in-facility escape sweep. It shows robots can traverse and observe jail spaces, but the cited deployment stops at alerting deputies and never takes a person into custody.

sources.title: Can robots help keep us safe? | National Geographic
sources.claim: Knightscope autonomous security robots patrol facilities continuously but are explicitly not built to police people or apprehend suspects; they function as remote sensing platforms that summon human officers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol/response, the closest commercial analogue to searching for an escapee. The vendor's own scope statement establishes that the apprehension half of the task is outside the capability of fielded autonomous security robots.

sources.title: Drone Technology Leads to Swift Arrest of Escaped Inmate in New Hampshire — DroneXL
sources.claim: Police drones with thermal imaging locate hiding or fleeing suspects and escapees, but human officers close the perimeter and make the physical arrest; in a New Hampshire case a state police drone found an escaped state-prison inmate at night and troopers took him into custody.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task for the search half (locating an escaped inmate at large). It substantiates aerial search only: the recapture was performed by troopers, so the whole instance is not completed by the robotic system.

sources.system: Skydio X10 / DFR dock system (Albuquerque PD)
sources.title: APD launches Skydio Docks across Albuquerque | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio drone-as-first-responder aircraft launched from docks locate armed suspects hiding outdoors and relay position, after which human officers move in and bring the suspect into custody.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: locating a fleeing/hiding suspect in the community, equivalent to the search phase of a manhunt for an escapee. Transfer stops at search: the arrest is made by officers, and flight is supervised by a remote pilot.

sources.title: Police Robot Dog Shot Three Times by Barricaded Suspect, Police Claim | Gizmodo
sources.claim: Ground robots used by police in standoffs, including Boston Dynamics Spot with Massachusetts State Police, are sent in to locate barricaded suspects and are driven by a human operator via remote control; they provide reconnaissance rather than making arrests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic building search for a hiding, potentially violent person — the same search problem as clearing structures for an escapee. It is teleoperated reconnaissance and does not include taking the person into custody.

sources.developer: Arkansas Department of Corrections / U.S. Border Patrol BORTAC
sources.title: Ex-police chief who escaped Arkansas prison while serving time for murder recaptured: Authorities - ABC News
sources.claim: In the June 2025 recapture of escaped Arkansas inmate Grant Hardin, agencies deployed helicopters, drones and K9 teams for the search, but tactical officers made the physical apprehension in the field.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task (recapture of a prison escapee). It documents current best practice: robotic aircraft support the search, while the recapture itself is done by human officers.

tasks.label: Process or book convicted individuals into prison.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: County jail booking area: officer takes custody of a newly arrested/committed person from the arresting or transport officer, removes handcuffs, conducts a pat-down/frisk search, inventories and bags personal property and money, takes LiveScan fingerprints and a mugshot, enters identifiers and charges into the jail management system, asks medical/mental-health screening questions, issues a wristband, and places the person in a holding cell.

State prison reception/diagnostic center: a busload of newly sentenced inmates arrives; officers remove chains and leg irons, conduct strip searches, supervise showering/delousing, issue state-issue clothing, linens and hygiene items, inventory property (store or mail home), take photos, prints and issue an ID card, and complete classification interviews and housing assignment.

Intake of an uncooperative, intoxicated, mentally ill or combative individual: officers use physical control holds and restraints (sometimes a restraint chair), remove clothing and property against resistance, place the person in a sobering or safety cell, and complete delayed booking paperwork and observation logs.

Intake complicated by contraband or medical/suicide risk: search turns up drugs or a weapon requiring seizure, evidence bagging and reporting; or the person has injuries, withdrawal symptoms or suicidal statements requiring medical clearance, an anti-suicide smock, and constant-observation placement before booking is completed.

Small or rural jail / court holding facility with minimal staff: one officer handles the entire booking of a person remanded after sentencing — receipt of commitment paperwork, search, property, prints/photo, phone call, bond or fine processing, clothing exchange, and cell assignment.

sources.system: Asian Forum for Corrections robotic prison guards (Pohang trial)
sources.developer: Asian Forum for Corrections / Kyonggi University (South Korea)
sources.title: Robot guards to patrol South Korean prisons
sources.claim: The most advanced robots trialed inside prisons are wheeled patrol units carrying cameras and sensors that alert human guards; they perform no manipulation and no intake/booking functions.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic deployment inside a correctional facility; cited to show that corrections robots are limited to patrol and observation and cannot search persons, handle property, or take prints, so they cannot substantiate booking.

sources.title: Knightscope on X: What is the Knightscope K5 Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)?
sources.claim: Commercially deployed autonomous security robots patrol defined routes and capture/analyze activity, but have no arms and perform no physical processing of people or property.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous security patrol in institutional settings. Cited as the state of the art in deployed security robotics; it lacks manipulation entirely, so no transfer to searching persons, inventorying property, or fingerprinting is possible.

sources.system: PACLINE / Southwest Solutions inmate property storage conveyor
sources.developer: Pacline Conveyors Inc.; Southwest Solutions Group
sources.title: Inmate Property Storage Conveyor Systems | Bag Storage | Pacline
sources.claim: The only automated equipment routinely installed in jail intake for this task is a property storage/retrieval conveyor: it indexes and rotates already-bagged inmate property to a human operator, leaving the search, inventory, printing, photographing and clothing issue to officers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated storage and retrieval of property bags inside jail booking areas. It covers only the storage sub-step after officers have searched the person and inventoried the items, so it cannot complete the whole booking instance.

tasks.label: Supervise and coordinate work of other correctional service officers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Take fingerprints of arrestees, prisoners, or the general public.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Jail booking area, routine arrestee intake: officer positions the arrestee at a livescan station, physically guides and rolls each of the ten fingers nail-to-nail plus slap/thumb impressions, cleans/dries or lotions dirty, sweaty or worn fingertips, checks each image for quality and retakes rejected fingers, and verifies the prints belong to the named subject. Arrestee is broadly compliant but often intoxicated, agitated, handcuffed on one side, or unfamiliar with the process.

Booking area, non-compliant or impaired arrestee: subject clenches fists, pulls hands away, is combative or heavily intoxicated; two or more officers control the person, pry/steady the hand, and roll prints under resistance, or document refusal and re-attempt later after a court order or once the subject sobers up.

Correctional institution intake/records area, printing sentenced inmates: prison reception, inter-facility transfer, work-release, court-ordered re-prints or release identity verification; a queue of cooperative inmates is printed on livescan or ink cards, with rolled prints plus palm prints, sequence checks and re-rolls for scarred or worn ridges.

Sheriff's office / jail public lobby, civil applicant fingerprinting of the general public: appointment-based livescan for background checks, licensing, concealed-carry permits or employment; cooperative civilians including elderly people with faint ridges and manual laborers with worn or callused fingertips; officer positions hands, applies ridge builder or lotion, captures rolled and flat impressions, and verifies ID documents.

Ink-and-card (FD-258/FD-249) fingerprinting when livescan is unavailable or an out-of-state/FBI hard card is required, including at court holding or transport points: officer inks the plate, rolls each finger onto the card in one continuous motion, avoids smudges/ghosting, and completes the demographic fields.

sources.system: N/A - FBI Next Generation Identification ten-print standard (reference document)
sources.developer: FBI Criminal Justice Information Services Division
sources.title: Recording Legible Fingerprints | Law Enforcement (FBI)
sources.claim: FBI CJIS standard for criminal ten-print submissions requires ten individually rolled nail-to-nail impressions plus plain impressions used to verify sequence and accuracy; this defines the physical act and accepted output of the task (reference document, not a robotic system).
sources.transferJustification: Not a robotic system; cited only to fix what output an employer accepts (nail-to-nail rolled impressions of AFIS-submittable quality), against which any candidate robot must be measured.

sources.title: Vitestro's robotic blood drawing device meets trial endpoints
sources.claim: The Vitestro Aletta device autonomously performs venipuncture on a patient's presented arm inside clinics/hospitals, meeting a 95% first-stick endpoint in a multicenter trial - the closest demonstrated case of a robot autonomously performing a precision procedure on a human limb in a structured facility. It does not capture fingerprints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic action on a cooperative human limb held in a fixture. Transfer to fingerprinting fails - the device performs one needle insertion on a passive arm and has no fingerprint imaging, no ten-finger rolling with nail-to-nail pressure control, no image-quality retake loop, and no capability with resistant subjects.

sources.title: Ulta Beauty Introduces Five-Step Robotic Manicure by Robotics Firm 10Beauty
sources.claim: 10Beauty's robotic manicure system autonomously performs multi-step work on a customer's fingers (polish removal, cuticle care, filing, polish, topcoat) in retail stores, showing robots can act on presented human fingers commercially - but it produces no fingerprint record.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous contact work on a cooperative human hand placed in a machine fixture. Transfer to fingerprinting fails - the machine works on nail surfaces of a self-presenting paying customer, does not roll finger pads across a platen to AFIS quality, does not verify identity or re-roll rejected fingers, and cannot handle a resisting arrestee.

sources.system: MorphoWave contactless fingerprint terminals (sensor, not a robot)
sources.title: Meet New MorphoWave Contactless Fingerprint Terminals
sources.claim: Biometric capture in law enforcement is automated at the sensing and matching layer (livescan devices, contactless wave scanners, self-service kiosks, AFIS matching); search surfaced no robotic system that physically takes a person's fingerprints.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a negative-boundary reference: the state of the art in fingerprint acquisition is a passive scanner that depends on the subject presenting and moving their own hand; it is not a physically embodied machine acting on the world, so it cannot substantiate a robotic system completing this task.

tasks.label: Investigate crimes that have occurred within an institution, or assist police in their investigations of crimes and inmates.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Inmate-on-inmate assault or fight in a housing unit/dayroom: officer responds, separates and restrains involved inmates, secures the area, locates and seizes the weapon (e.g., a shank) and bloodied clothing, photographs injuries and scene, takes statements from inmate and staff witnesses, packages evidence with chain of custody, and writes the investigative/incident report.

Contraband investigation following a tip or positive drug test: targeted search of a cell, bunk, mattress and personal property; find and seize drugs, a cell phone, or a homemade weapon; determine ownership, document location and photograph, package and log evidence, interview the occupants, and refer for discipline or prosecution.

Desk/interview-room investigative work inside the institution: review surveillance video, listen to recorded inmate telephone calls, screen mail and kites, interview suspects and witnesses inside the facility, cross-check housing and movement records, and compile the investigative report or disciplinary charge.

Assist outside police/detectives on an outside case or an in-custody case: pull and preserve video and records, escort and produce the inmate for a detective interview, take buccal swabs or fingerprints, transfer custody of seized evidence, and later testify.

Serious incident (in-custody death, overdose, serious assault, escape attempt): lock down and clear the area, preserve it as a crime scene, control and log access, provide initial observations and evidence to the agency's investigative unit or state police when they arrive.

Perimeter/grounds investigation after a suspected throw-over or drone drop: search the yard, fence line and adjacent grounds in variable weather, recover the package, document where it was found, and tie it to an inmate through video and phone records.

sources.developer: DEKA Research and Development (deployed by Cobb County Sheriff's Office)
sources.title: Cobb jail deploys sentry robots in 90-day pilot program - Cobb Courier
sources.claim: DEKA 'Sentry' robots were fielded in a 90-day pilot at the Cobb County (GA) jail, patrolling dormitories, hallways and the perimeter with cameras, night vision, thermal and two-way audio; they patrol autonomously but a live operator takes over for complex tasks. Their role is deterrence, surveillance and incident detection — not conducting investigations, seizing evidence, or interviewing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security patrol/monitoring inside a jail. Cited to show the state of the art for mobile robots in correctional facilities is fixed-route surveillance; the robot has no manipulator to seize or package evidence, cannot search a cell or a person, and cannot interview witnesses or produce an investigative report, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: ScanTech AI Sentinel fixed-gantry CT scanner
sources.developer: ScanTech AI Systems (piloted by Virginia Department of Corrections)
sources.title: VADOC First Corrections System to Pilot State-of-the-Art Drug and Contraband Detection Scanner from ScanTech
sources.claim: The most advanced automation actually in US corrections for contraband work is fixed screening equipment: an AI-assisted CT scanner piloted by the Virginia DOC to inspect incoming inmate mail at a central mail center. It screens items presented to it; it does not search cells, recover evidence, attribute it to an inmate, or build a case.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contraband screening of mail. Cited as a negative bound — it is a stationary sensing gantry with no mobility or manipulation, covering only a detection sub-step of a contraband investigation, so it cannot complete any instance of this task even with work brought to it.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.developer: University of Bath / UK police collaboration
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response (Journal of Field Robotics)
sources.claim: Robotic systems aimed specifically at crime-scene investigation remain research prototypes and are confined to a narrow niche: PRIME is an autonomous surface vessel prototype for mapping underwater evidence for police, not a system that documents, collects and processes evidence at an indoor crime scene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crime-scene search and evidence mapping. Cited as a negative bound: the only autonomous forensic robot found is a prototype limited to sonar search of submerged scenes; it neither collects nor packages evidence, and gives no capability inside a housing unit.

sources.system: Spot with Leica/Trimble scanning payload (Autowalk autonomous missions)
sources.title: 3D Laser Scanning Solutions & Autonomous Reality Capture | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots can repeatedly document a physical space in 3D: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous laser-scanning/reality-capture missions with survey payloads at industrial sites. This covers scene documentation only, not scene securing, evidence recovery, interviewing, or report writing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous 3D documentation of a site, analogous to photographing/diagramming a scene. Transfer fails for this task because the demonstrated environments are pre-mapped industrial plants on fixed routes, and the robot performs no evidence handling, no person-facing interviewing, and no case documentation.

roles.title: Detectives and Criminal Investigators
roles.description: Conduct investigations related to suspected violations of federal, state, or local laws to prevent or solve crimes.

tasks.label: Prepare reports that detail investigation findings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Obtain and verify evidence by interviewing and observing suspects and witnesses or by analyzing records.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Preserve, process, and analyze items of evidence obtained from crime scenes and suspects, placing them in proper containers and destroying evidence no longer needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-scene preservation and collection at an active crime scene (residence, street, vehicle, business): locating and photographing items in situ, recovering cartridge casings, weapons, latent-print lifts, bloodstain swabs, and wet or soiled clothing, then air-drying and packaging each in the proper paper bag/envelope/box, sealing with tamper-evident tape and initialing, all under variable lighting, weather, clutter and bystander presence.

Evidence taken from a person at the station/booking area: buccal DNA swab, gunshot-residue kit from hands, fingernail scrapings, seized clothing and personal effects from a possibly uncooperative arrestee; each item placed in its own container, sealed, labeled with case/item numbers, and logged.

Evidence intake at the department: repackaging seized drugs, phones, firearms (rendered safe), documents and cash into the proper containers, tamper-evident sealing, barcode labeling, chain-of-custody entry into the property system, and placement into the appropriate property-room storage location (shelf, locker, refrigerated or high-value vault).

Bench processing and analysis of submitted items: cyanoacrylate fuming and powdering for latent prints, swab cuttings and DNA extraction-to-profile workflows, presumptive and confirmatory drug/chemistry testing, examination and re-preservation of trace items in a laboratory or forensic unit.

Purge and destruction of evidence no longer needed: pulling adjudicated items from shelves per disposition orders, bulk narcotics incineration, firearm shredding/melting, disposal of biohazard and bulk property, with witnessed documentation of destruction.

sources.system: Hamilton Microlab VANTAGE Liquid Handling System
sources.title: Validation of a High-Throughput Automated Liquid Handling DNA Extraction System to Maximize Efficiency in Forensic Casework
sources.claim: A high-throughput robotic liquid-handling system was validated per SWGDAM guidelines for DNA extraction and purification ... samples (blood, saliva, semen on cotton, wood, metal, ceramic) in a crime-laboratory workflow, running up to 384 samples in ~1.5 hours.

sources.system: ANDE 6C Rapid DNA Analysis System; RapidHIT ID
sources.title: Rapid DNA | Law Enforcement (FBI)
sources.claim: The FBI lists fully automated Rapid DNA instruments that take a mouth swab to a searchable DNA profile with no human interpretation or review, approved for the National DNA Index System and used in booking stations.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout – GeekWire
sources.claim: A robotic arm autonomously picks individual, heterogeneous products out of containers and places them into designated totes at production scale inside fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking into containers. Transfer: the same class of items (small heterogeneous objects such as phones, boxes, bags, tools) must be recognized, grasped without damage and placed into a specified container, which is the physical core of putting an evidence item into its proper container.

sources.title: CVP Impack | Packsize
sources.claim: An inline automated packaging machine measures each presented item set, builds a right-sized box, tapes, weighs and applies the printed label, at roughly one package every seven seconds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fit-to-size boxing, sealing and labeling of goods. Transfer: sealing a container with tape and applying a machine-printed identifying label is the same physical operation as sealing and labeling an evidence package.

sources.title: C&D Waste | Sorting Bulky Waste | ZenRobotics
sources.claim: AI-driven sorting robots pick heavy, bulky and heterogeneous objects (wood, plastics, metals, inert material up to 40 kg) off a conveyor and drop them into designated destination chutes unattended, in operating recycling and scrap facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sorting and disposal of bulky mixed items. Transfer: bulk destruction of purged evidence requires the same physical act of identifying items on a presented stream and routing them into a destruction/disposal container or shredder feed.

sources.system: Automated evidence storage AS/RS (vertical lift/carousel units)
sources.developer: Southwest Solutions Group / Modern Handling (AS/RS vendors)
sources.title: 7 Public Safety Evidence Room Space Saving Storage Ideas
sources.claim: Automated storage and retrieval systems installed in police evidence rooms use a software-controlled robotic mechanism to store and retrieve evidence bins and deliver them to a secure operator ... with computer-driven inventory tracking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage and retrieval of containers. Transfer: placing sealed evidence packages into their storage location and pulling them again for disposition is the same store/retrieve motion the AS/RS performs on evidence carriers.

sources.title: MVC/D fingerprint fuming cabinets 1000 | 3000 | 5000 (foster+freeman brochure)
sources.claim: Cyanoacrylate fuming cabinets used for developing latent fingermarks on evidence items run the complete humidification, fuming and fume-extraction cycle under automatic preset control once the item is placed inside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: latent-print development on seized items. Transfer: this is one of the standard 'processing' steps applied to evidence items after intake, performed inside a purpose-built chamber on items presented to it.

sources.system: SWING DRU-X-TOR automated sample preparation and GC-MS platform
sources.title: Automated Sample Preparation & GC-MS Analysis for e.g. Drug Analysis
sources.claim: A commercial forensic laboratory workstation performs fully automated sample extraction, derivatization and GC-MS analysis of forensic samples at 64 samples per day with logged, LIMS-exported run data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated chemical analysis of forensic/drug samples. Transfer: the analytical 'processing and analysis' of seized substances presented in vials is the same operation performed by a forensic chemist at the bench.

sources.developer: Lifeline Robotics / University of Southern Denmark
sources.title: Throat swabbing robot developed for COVID-19 testing by Danish startup
sources.claim: A prototype robot performs a throat swab on a seated human subject, claimed by its developer to be the first fully automatic swab robot; it remained an early-stage prototype tested on trial subjects rather than a fielded system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic swab collection from a person. Cited to show the nearest system to buccal-swab collection from a suspect; it is a developer-claimed prototype covering only the swabbing motion, not packaging, sealing or chain of custody.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response
sources.claim: The state of the art for robotics at crime scenes is inspection and mapping: a prototype autonomous surface/underwater vehicle surveys underwater scenes with sonar, and other work uses drones for scene imaging; no cited system collects and packages physical evidence at a scene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic crime-scene work. Cited as the closest fielded/published robotic crime-scene capability, showing it is limited to sensing and mapping rather than recovering, preserving and packaging evidence items.

tasks.label: Note, mark, and photograph location of objects found, such as footprints, tire tracks, bullets and bloodstains, and take measurements of the scene.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Interior of a private home or apartment after a homicide, assault, or burglary: investigator walks the as-found rooms, recognizes items of evidentiary value (blood drops and spatter, shell casings, a shoe impression on a floor, pry marks), places numbered evidence markers next to each, shoots overall/mid-range/close-up photographs with and without scales, and records room and object-to-object measurements for a scaled diagram.

Outdoor street, alley, or roadway scene (drive-by shooting, hit-and-run, fatal crash): cones/markers placed at casings, tire friction marks, gouge marks and debris on pavement under traffic control and variable light/weather; photographs of each item in place plus overall scene coverage; measurements of point of impact, roadway geometry and evidence positions for reconstruction.

Interior of a commercial or institutional building kept to a working standard (convenience store, bank lobby, office, school): robbery or shooting scene where fixed layout and standard fixtures exist but merchandise and furniture are disturbed; mark and photograph bullet strikes, casings, blood, footwear impressions on tile; measure positions relative to walls, counters and doorways.

Open or rural terrain (field, wooded area, embankment, unpaved lot): body recovery or dump-site scene with footwear and tire impressions in soil, scattered items in vegetation; markers/flags placed, impressions photographed obliquely with scale before casting, distances measured across irregular ground in outdoor weather.

Agency-controlled facility (police impound garage or evidence processing bay): a recovered or seized vehicle, or recovered items, examined under controlled lighting; bullet holes, trajectories, bloodstains, damage and transfer evidence marked with labels/rods, photographed with scales, and measured relative to vehicle datum points.

sources.system: Skydio X10 / Skydio 3D Scan and Map Capture
sources.title: Cutting-edge Drones for Effective Crime Scene Analysis (Drones for Crash & Crime Scene Documentation)
sources.claim: Skydio drones execute autonomous mapping and 3D Scan missions over outdoor crash and crime scenes, capturing the imagery from which scaled 2D orthomosaics and 3D point clouds (and measurements) are produced; the investigator still identifies evidence, places markers and takes evidentiary close-ups, and drops evidence annotations in software afterward.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (scene photography and dimensioning for court), showing that autonomy today covers bulk scene capture only, not recognizing, marking or close-up imaging of individual items of evidence.

sources.title: Skydio's Autonomy Could Change the Game for Public Safety
sources.claim: US police agencies field Skydio X10 aircraft operationally, including for accident reconstruction, confirming real deployment of drone scene documentation rather than a lab demo.
sources.transferJustification: Deployment context for scene documentation flights; establishes maturity of the related capture task, not autonomous evidence marking.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Leica BLK ARC
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics' Spot
sources.claim: A legged robot carrying a certified laser scanner can run a pre-taught route and capture dimensional reality-capture scans of as-found interiors and construction sites without a human in the ...; the output is a point cloud, with no recognition, marking or evidentiary close-up photography of individual objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous dimensional documentation of an as-found site. It shows the measurement sub-step is automatable in unstructured settings, but not the noting/marking/close-up photography that the whole task requires.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich (Virtopsy project)
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: A six-axis industrial robot installed in a purpose-built forensic imaging suite performs automated photogrammetric and optical 3D surface documentation of a subject presented on the scanner table, and places physical instruments at computer-planned target locations to 1.4 mm accuracy; it is in routine casework use.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: forensic photographic/photogrammetric documentation of features (wounds) on an object presented to the machine, with dimensional records used in casework, plus precise physical placement at a designated point - the fixtured-cell analogue of marking, photographing and measuring located items.

sources.title: ZEISS ScanBox: Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine | automation
sources.claim: Commercial automated optical measuring cells hold a part in a fixture inside an enclosed robot cell and autonomously digitize it, localize and quantify features and deviations, and issue dimensional inspection reports at production quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: photographing/scanning a fixtured object and recording the position and dimensions of features on it. Comparable objects and far tighter precision than crime-scene measurement, but only when the work is presented to the machine in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: How It Works - UVeye
sources.claim: Drive-through automated inspection gantries image a vehicle presented to the machine and automatically detect, localize and photograph surface anomalies across every body panel, producing a per-vehicle condition record; over a thousand systems are installed and millions of vehicles are scanned monthly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatically finding, locating and photographing marks on a vehicle brought into a purpose-built scanning structure - the E1 form of documenting where objects/marks are found on a recovered vehicle.

tasks.label: Secure deceased body and obtain evidence from it, preventing bystanders from tampering with it prior to medical examiner's arrival.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Homicide or suspicious death inside a private residence/apartment: detective takes custody of the body where it lies in a cluttered room, keeps family members, EMS and patrol officers from moving or covering it, photographs and documents position, wounds, lividity and rigor, protects the hands and clothing from contamination (paper bagging), notes/recovers items on the body (ID, phone, pill bottles, cartridge cases under the body), and releases it to the medical examiner with chain-of-custody documentation.

Death in a public outdoor place (street shooting, alley overdose, hit-and-run body in a roadway): detective establishes and holds a perimeter over the body amid a crowd, traffic, weather and news cameras, shields the body from view and from rain/heat, photographs and documents it in situ, collects fragile evidence on and immediately around it, and guards it until the ME's investigator arrives.

Death inside a business or hospitality premises (bar, store, hotel room, office, parking structure) that is controlled by an operator: detective clears patrons and staff, keeps cleaning/management from disturbing the body, documents it and the evidence on it, retrieves personal effects, and holds the body for the ME.

Death inside an institution the agency can control — hospital room/ED, jail cell or prison, nursing home: body is undisturbed on a bed or floor with staff present; detective secures it against staff moving, cleaning or resuscitation-debris removal, photographs and documents its external condition (ligature, injuries, medications, restraints), and turns it over to the ME.

Remains found outdoors in rural, wooded, water or wreck settings, often decomposed, partially skeletonized, scattered or trapped: detective secures the remains and the immediate area against animals, weather and onlookers, documents and recovers evidence from the body and clothing, and maintains the scene until the ME/coroner or recovery team arrives.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich (Virtopsy project)
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: Virtobot 2.0 is a ceiling-mounted robotic system in a forensic imaging suite that performs automated photogrammetric/optical surface documentation of corpses and CT-image-guided needle placement for post-mortem tissue and liquid sampling, with automatic tool change and automatic CT data registration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated forensic external documentation and sampling of a human corpse. It transfers only to the 'obtain evidence from the body' element and only where that element is documentation/sampling of an undisturbed body: same object (a human decedent), presented fixtured on a scanning table inside a purpose-built robotic suite from which people are excluded.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich
sources.title: Virtobot - A Robot System for Optical 3D Scanning in Forensic Medicine (3DBST 2013 Proceedings)
sources.claim: The Virtobot robot system is used in routine casework at the Zurich forensic institute for whole-body surface and wound documentation of corpses, producing 24 surface documentations over 11 months.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: routine automated documentation of decedents' external surfaces in a purpose-built robotic scanning room is the machine analogue of the investigator's photographic/evidentiary documentation of an undisturbed body, but it does not include recovering items from the body or judging what to collect.

sources.date: 2021-08 (product still marketed for police scene documentation 2025-2026)
sources.title: How Skydio Drones with 3D Scan Work for Public Safety
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan autonomously plans and flies its own capture pattern to photo-document crime and crash scenes for police reconstruction; a mock crime scene was captured in 13 minutes with 110 ..., but the drone only images the scene and cannot secure a body, handle it, or collect physical evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous outdoor crime-scene photo documentation. It shows only the imaging sub-step is automated in unstructured settings; it provides no manipulation, no custody of the body, and no ability to stop bystanders, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task at E2 or E3.

sources.system: Knightscope K3 / K5 Autonomous Security Robots
sources.title: This egg-shaped security robot is now roaming hospitals
sources.claim: Knightscope autonomous security robots (K3/K5) patrol hospitals, malls, parking lots and government facilities without an operator, but function as mobile security cameras that detect and report; they have no manipulators and cannot physically prevent anyone from touching an object or person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous guarding of a controlled facility. It is the closest deployed analogue to 'preventing bystanders from tampering', and it shows current guard robots only observe and alert, so the guarding element of this task is not substantiated at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Government | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Police agencies deploy Boston Dynamics Spot at scenes for remote situational awareness and camera views; the robot is operated remotely by officers rather than performing scene or evidence work on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: law-enforcement scene reconnaissance. Cited only to establish that fielded police ground robots are remotely driven camera platforms; being teleoperated, it cannot support a positive judgment for this task.

tasks.label: Determine scope, timing, and direction of investigations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Search for and collect evidence, such as fingerprints, using investigative equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential burglary/assault scene in a private home or apartment: detective walks the as-found, cluttered scene, identifies likely touch surfaces (window frames, door handles, jewelry boxes), dusts with powder, lifts latent prints onto tape/cards, photographs prints in place, swabs suspected blood/touch DNA, and bags and labels seized items with chain-of-custody documentation.

Outdoor scene (shooting, assault, or vehicle crime on a street, parking lot, alley, or field): grid search for shell casings, projectiles, blood, discarded weapon or clothing; markers placed, items photographed in situ, collected and packaged; wind, rain, darkness, bystanders and time pressure.

Execution of a search warrant at a residence or small business: systematic room-by-room search for documents, narcotics, firearms, currency, and electronics hidden in furniture, walls, vehicles; each find photographed in place, seized, inventoried and packaged; layout unknown in advance.

Processing a recovered vehicle (stolen car, suspect vehicle) inside a police garage/impound bay: exterior and interior powder dusting and lifting, swabbing steering wheel/gear shift for DNA, recovering casings, documents and electronics from footwells and consoles, photographing and packaging.

Processing recovered items and reference samples at the station evidence-processing room or lab bench: superglue fuming or powdering a handgun, bottle, phone or document, photographing and lifting developed prints, taking a buccal reference swab from an arrestee, then sealing, labeling and logging each item.

Commercial premises scene (convenience store, bank, warehouse burglary/robbery): process point of entry, counter, cash tray and pried doors for prints and tool marks, collect surveillance media and dropped items, in a facility that is institution-controlled but disturbed by the crime.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot / iRobot PackBot in police service
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / iRobot (operated by police agencies)
sources.title: Police 'Robot Dogs' Raise Concerns as More Departments Adopt Them
sources.claim: Police-deployed ground robots (Spot, PackBot) used at incidents to handle or inspect objects are operated by human teleoperators, not autonomously collecting evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed police manipulation capability; object handling at scenes is human-driven, so it cannot substantiate autonomous evidence search and collection.

sources.title: 'Spot' the robot dog assists Mass. State Police in high-risk situations
sources.claim: Massachusetts State Police use Spot to investigate suspicious packages ... secure areas; the work is remote inspection under operator control rather than evidence collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task of scene inspection by a police robot; it establishes deployment but is remote-controlled reconnaissance, not autonomous collection and packaging of evidence.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.developer: University of Bath / UK policing partners
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response
sources.claim: PRIME is an autonomous uncrewed ... searches underwater crime scenes and flags targets, but physical recovery of evidence is left to human divers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (searching a crime scene for evidence) performed autonomously, but limited to sonar search and highlighting; no physical collection, lifting, or packaging of evidence.

sources.system: OD-OCT (object-driven optical coherence tomography latent print scanner)
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Chinese forensic research group (He, Shi, Zhang et al.)
sources.title: Rapid, autonomous and ultra-large-area detection of latent fingerprints using object-driven optical coherence tomography
sources.claim: A benchtop robotic-arm optical coherence tomography scanner autonomously detects and images latent fingerprints over large areas of objects placed under it (research prototype).
sources.transferJustification: Related sub-step of latent print detection on an item presented to the machine; it images prints but does not develop, lift, photograph for court, package, or log evidence.

sources.system: R2-OCT robotic Raman-optical coherence tomography system
sources.developer: He et al., published in Small Methods
sources.title: Robotic Raman-OCT for Non-Destructive Visualization of Concealed Latent Fingerprints and Trace-Residue Profiling
sources.claim: A robotic Raman-OCT bench system autonomously repositions a probe to characterize latent print residues on samples in the laboratory (research prototype).
sources.transferJustification: Related task of analyzing prints/trace residue on fixtured samples; it is analysis of an already-collected item, not the search, lifting, and packaging that the detective task requires.

sources.system: Hamilton forensic automation (ID NIMBUS / Microlab STAR workstations)
sources.title: Forensic Science Automation | Forensic DNA Extraction With Hamilton
sources.claim: Commercial forensic laboratory robotics automate DNA extraction and sample preparation from evidence samples that humans have already collected and submitted.
sources.transferJustification: Related downstream task (laboratory analysis of submitted samples); it presupposes that evidence has already been searched for, collected and packaged by a human, so it cannot substantiate the collection task.

sources.developer: German research consortium (published in Scientific Reports)
sources.title: Autonomous swab robot for naso- and oropharyngeal COVID-19 screening
sources.claim: An autonomous swab robot station performed naso- and oropharyngeal swabbing of human subjects in a clinical trial, showing autonomous swab sampling from a cooperative person is feasible in a clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task of taking an oral swab from a seated cooperative person, comparable to a buccal reference swab; it covers only the swabbing motion, not sealing, labeling, or chain-of-custody handling of the sample.

sources.system: Police UAS crime scene photogrammetry (Skydio/Axon, SkyeBrowse workflows)
sources.developer: Various drone vendors used by US law enforcement
sources.title: Police UAV: How Law Enforcement Uses Drones
sources.claim: Police drones are widely used to document crime scenes photogrammetrically, producing spatial records rather than collecting physical evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task of crime scene documentation; imaging the scene does not include locating, lifting, swabbing, or packaging physical evidence, so it cannot substantiate the collection task.

tasks.label: Organize scene search, assigning specific tasks and areas of search to individual officers and obtaining adequate lighting as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Examine records and governmental agency files to find identifying data about suspects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Examine records to locate links in chains of evidence or information.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prepare and serve search and arrest warrants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Search warrant at a private residence: detective drafts the affidavit and gets a judge's signature, then the team knocks and announces, makes entry, secures and identifies occupants, conducts a room-by-room search for the described items, photographs, seizes and inventories evidence, and leaves a copy of the warrant and receipt. Cluttered, unfamiliar home; pets, children, hostile occupants possible.

Arrest warrant served on a suspect found at a home, on the street, or at a vehicle stop: verify identity, approach, verbally control, physically take into custody and handcuff, search incident to arrest, secure in vehicle, transport and book. Resistance, flight, and concealed weapons are routine risks.

Warrant prepared and served in an institution-controlled setting: search warrant served on a business, bank, or records custodian; warrant for a hospital blood draw; or arrest warrant served on a person already held in a jail, courthouse, or probation office. Fixed layout, staff cooperation, controlled access.

Warrant for an already-seized item held by the agency: draft and obtain the warrant, then execute the search of a vehicle in the impound lot or a phone/computer in the evidence room or forensics lab, documenting and inventorying what is found.

High-risk/tactical warrant service on an armed, violent, or barricaded subject, planned with a SWAT team: surveillance and operational plan, breach or callout, clearing the structure, taking the subject into custody, sometimes using teleoperated throwbots or drones for reconnaissance.

sources.system: Teledyne FLIR FirstLook / PackBot / SUGV tactical robots
sources.title: Police Robots: What They Are & How They're Used | Built In
sources.claim: Police tactical ground robots (Teledyne FLIR FirstLook, PackBot, SUGV; Robotex Avatar) are used to assist SWAT teams on high-risk warrant service, but they are remote-controlled reconnaissance/EOD platforms operated by an officer, not autonomous systems that serve warrants, arrest people, or search and inventory evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: these are the robots actually fielded on warrant service, and they perform only teleoperated reconnaissance sub-steps, which cannot substantiate autonomous completion of the whole task.

sources.title: NYPD Adds 'Spot,' the Robot Dog, to Force — and More Tech
sources.claim: The NYPD's Digidog (Boston Dynamics Spot) is explicitly a remote-controlled robot used to assess hazardous situations; it does not autonomously enter premises, control occupants, or make arrests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (hazard assessment during tactical operations including warrant entries); capability does not transfer because operation is continuous teleoperation and involves no arrest, search, or evidence handling.

sources.title: Law Enforcement | Ghost Robotics
sources.claim: Ghost Robotics markets its Vision 60 quadruped for law-enforcement high-risk operations and patrol support, with a top-mounted arm that is remote-controlled rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (tactical support on high-risk operations); the manipulator is remote-controlled and no source shows autonomous entry, suspect control, or evidence seizure.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 / K3 Autonomous Security Robots
sources.title: Knightscope's Autonomous Security Robots Delivers Technology for Public Safety | Vicor
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5/K3 autonomous security robots are genuinely autonomous and widely deployed on controlled campuses, but their function is patrol, sensing and reporting; they have no manipulator and cannot detain a person, search a structure, or seize and inventory evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous security patrol in a structured facility). It marks the ceiling of deployed autonomous policing robotics — observation and reporting only — so it cannot substantiate warrant preparation, entry, arrest, or evidence seizure.

sources.title: China Tests Autonomous 'Spherical' Robot Police Unit in Cities | eWeek
sources.claim: China's RT-G spherical police robot is described as autonomous and carries non-lethal means to immobilize suspects, but it operates alongside human officers on patrol and there is no evidence it independently serves legal process, effects an arrest, handcuffs, or searches premises.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (suspect pursuit/immobilization). Even taken at face value it covers only a fragment of arrest-warrant service and its autonomy in real apprehensions is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid | The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most advanced home-capable humanoid, 1X's NEO, still depends on human teleoperators for complex tasks and no humanoid has been shown completing an ordinary household chore end-to-end autonomously — indicating that autonomous room-by-room manipulation and object retrieval inside an unfamiliar residence is not available.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous mobile manipulation in a home). Searching a residence for described items and seizing them requires comparable or harder perception and manipulation, so the shortfall transfers.

tasks.label: Obtain summary of incident from officer in charge at crime scene, taking care to avoid disturbing evidence.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Homicide/death investigation at a private residence: the detective arrives after patrol has secured the scene, meets the patrol sergeant or first officer at the perimeter tape, and takes a verbal briefing on what was found, who is present, actions already taken, and the path of contamination before entering; the detective stays outside marked evidence areas while listening and taking notes.

Property or violent crime at a business or institutional premises (burglary, robbery, assault): the detective receives a walkthrough summary from the responding officer in charge inside the building, noting point of entry, witnesses held on scene, and untouched evidence such as tills, safes, or discarded items.

Outdoor public scene (street shooting, stabbing, fatal collision, recovered vehicle) with a live perimeter, crowd, traffic, weather, and media: the detective takes the incident summary from the sergeant or scene supervisor amid ongoing activity, while avoiding shell casings, blood, tire marks, and other evidence on the roadway or sidewalk.

Federal or specialized investigator arriving at a scene controlled by another agency (bank robbery, arson/explosion, hazmat or industrial fatality, task-force execution): the summary is obtained from the incident commander or local officer in charge at a staging area or command post, including jurisdiction and evidence-handling arrangements.

Summary obtained remotely first — by phone, radio, or in-car mobile data terminal from the officer in charge while the detective is en route or on call-out — then briefly confirmed and supplemented at the scene edge; common for after-hours call-outs and lower-priority incidents.

tasks.label: Testify before grand juries concerning criminal activity investigations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Secure persons at scene, keeping witnesses from conversing or leaving the scene before investigators arrive.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor public scene of a violent crime (street, sidewalk, parking lot, park) — shooting or assault. First-arriving investigator must hold multiple bystanders, victims' relatives and witnesses at the scene, physically separate them so they cannot confer, block the crowd from entering the taped area, and keep everyone present until case detectives arrive; people are agitated, some want to leave, some are uncooperative.

Private residence — domestic assault, unattended death or burglary. Investigator must place involved parties in separate rooms or vehicles, stand between them so they cannot talk or coordinate stories, prevent anyone from walking out or contaminating the scene, and hold that control for 20–90 minutes until the detective unit arrives.

Commercial business premises open to the public (convenience store, bar, bank, retail store) after a robbery or assault. Employees and customers are witnesses; the investigator must stop customers walking out, take and hold them apart, keep employees from comparing accounts, and manage the manager and arriving public, inside a fixed, institutionally controlled floor plan.

Institutional facility (school, hospital, jail, workplace, government building) after an assault, theft or in-custody incident. Investigator secures the involved area, holds staff/students/patients who saw the event in separate rooms, stops them conversing, and coordinates with facility security until investigators arrive.

Roadway scene — fatal or serious traffic collision, DUI, or vehicle stop turned criminal. Investigator must keep drivers, passengers and stopped motorist-witnesses at the roadside, separated and not conferring, amid traffic, weather and darkness, until the reconstruction or detective unit arrives.

sources.title: New York bins subway surveillance robot
sources.claim: The NYPD's Knightscope K5 autonomous security robot, deployed as a patrol presence in a Times Square subway station, had to be accompanied by human officers and was retired after four months; it detects and reports but exercises no control over people.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: autonomous security patrol of a public transit station (an E2 facility). It shares presence and detection with 'securing persons at a scene', but the deployment shows the robot could not act on people at all and itself required human minders, so nothing transfers to holding or separating witnesses.

sources.title: Are Autonomous Security Robots the Way of the Future? - TSS
sources.claim: Commercially deployed U.S. autonomous security robots patrol campuses, malls and airports and alert human security, but are slow, unarmed and cannot detain anyone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous guard patrol in structured facilities, the nearest commercially deployed capability to holding people at a scene. The source states explicitly that these machines cannot detain, so it cannot substantiate keeping witnesses from leaving.

sources.title: China Unveils Weaponized Robot Security Guard - Newsweek
sources.claim: China's AnBot security robot patrols autonomously but its coercive 'riot control' function is triggered by a remote human operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic use of force / crowd control, the coercive element behind keeping persons at a scene. The force function is human-triggered by remote control, so it is teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: China Tests Autonomous 'Spherical' Robot Police Unit in Cities
sources.claim: The RT-G spherical police robot is reported to patrol streets and immobilize suspects with a net gun and other non-lethal devices, but the reporting is vendor/press-sourced and the level of autonomy in deploying force is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically stopping a fleeing person, one component of keeping people at a scene. Autonomy of the force function is unestablished, and momentary net capture is not the same as holding and separating several restless witnesses for an extended period.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot ('Roscoe', Massachusetts State Police)
sources.title: Police Robot Dog Shot Three Times by Barricaded Suspect, Police Claim
sources.claim: Police quadruped robots used at live incidents (e.g., a barricaded-suspect call in Massachusetts) are driven by a human trooper over remote control and are used for reconnaissance, not for controlling people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot presence at an active crime scene. The role is teleoperated reconnaissance inside a structure; the robot exerts no authority over persons, so it does not transfer to securing witnesses.

tasks.label: Participate or assist in raids and arrests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Execute a search/arrest warrant at a private residence with an entry team: stack at the door, knock-and-announce or breach, clear rooms, physically control and handcuff occupants (some non-compliant), pat-down for weapons, separate children/pets, and hold the scene while the search proceeds.

Field arrest of a wanted suspect in a public or outdoor place (sidewalk, parking lot, doorstep): approach and identify, give commands, take hands/wrists under control against possible resistance or flight, handcuff, search the person, seat and belt the arrestee in a vehicle.

Raid on commercial or semi-public premises taken as found (drug house, illicit business, warehouse, motel room, gang location): coordinated entry with a tactical team, detain and handcuff multiple people, control bystanders, secure rooms and weapons.

Vehicle-based takedown/felony stop: box in or approach the target vehicle, issue commands, remove occupants one at a time, prone or wall them out, handcuff, search occupants and the passenger compartment.

Support/assist role in a planned operation inside an institutionally controlled facility: taking custody of a defendant at a jail, courthouse or precinct booking area, or arresting a cooperating white-collar defendant by appointment at an office; then escorting, transporting and processing (property, fingerprints) the arrestee.

sources.title: Police 'Robot Dogs' Raise Concerns as More Departments Adopt Them (Bloomberg via Governing)
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot is used by 60+ US/Canada bomb squads and SWAT teams for standoffs and warrant service, but it is driven by a human operator with a game-controller-style tablet and relies on the operator for decision making; it observes and de-escalates rather than apprehending.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about robots participating in raids, warrant service and standoffs; shows the state of practice is remote control for reconnaissance, not autonomous apprehension.

sources.title: How Spot is Changing the Game for Public Safety | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: The vendor's own public-safety material frames Spot as a remotely operated tool for investigating and de-escalating hazardous situations, not as a system that autonomously detains or arrests people.

sources.system: Undaunted security robot dogs (Columbia Crest Apartments deployment)
sources.title: Robot dogs help catch car break-in suspects at Atlanta apartment complex
sources.claim: Autonomous patrol robot dogs at an Atlanta apartment complex detected and followed fleeing break-in suspects and summoned police, but the robots make no physical contact; the physical apprehension and arrest were done by human officers.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed autonomous system to apprehension work: it locates and tracks suspects on real premises, and the source states the limit of its role, bounding what autonomous ground robots contribute to an arrest.

sources.system: Skydio X10 / dock-based DFR (Axon-Skydio public safety programs)
sources.title: Revolutionizing Public Safety: Skydio and Axon's Drone as First Responder (DFR) Programs
sources.claim: Dock-based Drone as First Responder programs fly fully autonomously to incident scenes and deliver real-time situational awareness to officers; the capability is aerial overwatch only, with no ability to detain, handcuff or transport a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial overwatch/containment support during warrant service and suspect apprehension. Shows autonomy exists for the sensing part of a raid but not for any physical control of a suspect.

sources.title: Suspect in Texas standoff tries to shoot police robot - but it outsmarts him, runs him over (NY Post via AOL)
sources.claim: In the most cited case of a robot physically subduing a barricaded suspect (Lubbock, Texas), a teleoperated bomb-squad ground robot deployed gas and pinned the man until officers took him into custody; the machine was driven by officers, not acting autonomously, and did not handcuff, search or take custody.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (physical engagement of a suspect during a tactical operation); recorded as teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Check victims for signs of life, such as breathing and pulse.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shooting/stabbing scene on a public street, sidewalk or parking lot, often at night: investigator reaches a person down on the pavement amid blood, bystanders and patrol activity, feels for a carotid pulse, looks/listens for chest rise and breath, and determines whether to begin/continue life-saving measures or treat the scene as a death scene.

Private residence: victim found on the floor of a bedroom, bathroom, kitchen or stairwell amid furniture and clutter, low light, possibly partly clothed, covered by bedding, wedged in a confined space; investigator moves in, checks carotid/wrist pulse and breathing, notes skin temperature, rigor or lividity.

Victim inside a vehicle at a roadside, driveway or parking garage: slumped in a seat, seatbelted, airbag deployed or glass and blood present; investigator reaches through a door or window to check for breathing and a pulse without disturbing evidence.

Commercial or institutional premises under an operator's control (convenience store, bar, office, school, hospital ward, jail housing unit): person down on a floor in a fixed, maintained layout with staff present; investigator checks for pulse and respiration and coordinates with responding medics/staff.

Found body in an outdoor or remote location (field, wooded area, alley, embankment, water's edge), possibly hours or days old with decomposition, insect activity, rigor or lividity; investigator confirms the absence of breathing and pulse and documents the determination.

sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Chinese PLA General Hospital / Air Force Medical Center
sources.title: Towards expert-level autonomous carotid ultrasonography with large-scale learning-based robotic system | Nature Communications
sources.claim: UltraBot is a fully autonomous robotic arm system that performs a complete carotid artery ultrasound examination on human subjects positioned at a clinical scanning station, reported at over 90% success and expert-level accuracy, including locating the carotid on the neck and imaging the vessel and its flow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous carotid ultrasonography. Transfer: the robot autonomously localizes and contacts the carotid artery on a positioned human neck and images pulsatile arterial flow, which is exactly the anatomical target and the physiological signal a manual carotid pulse check reads; objects (a human neck), contact precision and the presented/positioned subject match an E1 presentation of the signs-of-life check.

sources.system: DARPA Triage Challenge Event 2 systems (Coordinated Robotics, Battelle DART, RoboScout, UAS-DTU)
sources.developer: DARPA with competing teams (Coordinated Robotics, Battelle, university teams)
sources.title: DART and MSAI triumph at DARPA Triage Challenge | DARPA
sources.claim: In the DARPA Triage Challenge Event 2 systems competition, fully autonomous unmanned ground and aerial robots located simulated casualties (manikins and actors) and assessed their vital signs and injuries in mock C-130 crash and night-ambush courses with smoke, darkness and rubble at the Guardian Centers training site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic primary triage. Transfer: the robots must reach a casualty in situ and judge heart rate and respiration, the same determination as checking a victim for signs of life; it is a staged research competition, not a deployment, so it shows the capability exists only at prototype reliability.

sources.system: PRONTO multi-robot triage platform (Falcon UAV + Clearpath Jackal UGVs)
sources.developer: University of Pennsylvania GRASP / Penn Trauma
sources.title: A Multi-Robot Platform for Robotic Triage Combining Onboard Sensing and Foundation Models
sources.claim: The Penn PRONTO DARPA Triage Challenge system paper reports that camera-based heart-rate methods were unsuitable in the field, that the deployed mmWave heart-rate sensor required the robot to ask casualties over a speaker to hold still, and that the thermal respiration method fails when ambient temperature approaches body temperature.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (robotic assessment of breathing and pulse on a casualty in the field); the reported failure modes and the need for a cooperative, still subject show why an as-found check on an unresponsive crime victim is not yet met at worker reliability.

sources.system: Dr. Spot (Boston Dynamics Spot with contactless vital-sign sensing)
sources.developer: MIT / Brigham and Women's Hospital / Boston Dynamics
sources.title: Mobile Robotic Platform for Contactless Vital Sign Monitoring - PMC
sources.claim: Dr. Spot, the most-cited mobile robot for measuring heart rate, respiratory rate, skin temperature and oxygen saturation on patients in hospital clinical environments, is driven by a remote human operator; the vital-sign sensing is contactless camera/radar based and was evaluated in emergency-department settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic vital-sign measurement on people inside a structured human facility (hospital). It bears on the E2 question and shows the leading facility-based system is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive E2 judgment.
