tasks.label: Block or rope off scene and check perimeter to ensure that entire scene is secured.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Urban street/sidewalk violent-crime scene (shooting, homicide) on a residential or commercial block: string barrier tape between light poles, fences, trees and patrol cars across streets and sidewalks, set inner and outer perimeters, then walk the whole boundary looking for gaps (alleys, driveways, gates) while bystanders, residents and media press against the line.

Residential interior scene (house or apartment) for a death investigation or burglary: tape across the front doorway and interior hallways, secure rear doors, windows and garage, establish a single controlled entry/exit point, then walk the structure inside and out to confirm no unsecured opening remains.

Commercial or institutional interior (convenience store, bank, office, school) robbery or assault scene: cordon the affected area inside the building with tape and portable barriers, block public entrances, coordinate with staff/security, then walk the boundary confirming customers and employees cannot re-enter the scene.

Roadway or vehicle scene (fatal hit-and-run, roadside shooting, recovered suspect vehicle): position patrol cars, cones and flares to close lanes, tape off the vehicle and debris field, then walk the closure to verify the full evidence area (casings, skid marks, fluid) lies inside and that traffic and pedestrians cannot enter.

Large open outdoor area (field, wooded area, park, expansive parking lot) for body or evidence recovery: drive stakes and run tape over a wide irregular area with uneven ground and vegetation, mark access corridors, then walk the entire perimeter to verify continuity and that all approaches are controlled.

sources.developer: Hong Kong Highways Department with Hong Kong Productivity Council
sources.title: Highways Department - Robot System for Placement and Collection of Traffic Cones and Warning Lanterns at High Speed Roads
sources.claim: Hong Kong's Highways Department and the Productivity Council built RoadBot, a truck-mounted robot with cameras, LiDAR and robot arms that places and collects traffic cones and warning lanterns on high-speed roads to delineate/close a work area; prototype demonstrated 2019, follow-on unit in development.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out traffic cones/lanterns to close and delineate a roadway work zone. It transfers to 'block off scene' on roadways because the objects (cones, warning lanterns), the accuracy needed, and the purpose (an unbroken delineated boundary excluding traffic) match the roadway cordon a detective sets; it does not cover tying barrier tape to fixed anchors.

sources.system: Széchenyi István University autonomous cone deployment/retrieval robot platform
sources.title: YOLO-Based Object and Keypoint Detection for Autonomous Traffic Cone Placement and Retrieval for Industrial Robots
sources.claim: A four-wheel-drive outdoor UGV with a collaborative arm, RTK-GNSS and YOLO vision carries up to 30 traffic cones and autonomously executes placement at positions an operator marks on a digital map, and locates and collects them again using visual detection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous roadside cone deployment and retrieval. Transfers to 'block off scene and check the perimeter' when the boundary is specified and the ground prepared: same delineator objects, centimetre-level placement, and a vision pass that re-detects each placed marker along the line.

sources.system: Robotic highway safety markers (robotic safety barrels)
sources.developer: Shen et al. (University of Nebraska–Lincoln research program)
sources.title: Are Work Zones and Connected Automated Vehicles Ready for a Harmonious Coexistence? A Scoping Review and Research Agenda
sources.claim: Self-propelled robotic safety barrels/markers that reposition themselves to form work-zone boundaries were built and tested on realistic highway environments, achieving final positioning error better than manual barrel placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated placement of barrels/barricades that form a work-zone perimeter. Transfers to blocking off an outdoor scene because the devices are the same class of physical barrier used to exclude traffic and people and are positioned to specified boundary coordinates.

sources.developer: Highway Care Ltd with National Highways
sources.title: Falcon 100 Automated Cone Laying Machine (ACLM) | Highway Care
sources.claim: The Falcon 100 Automated Cone Laying ..., approved by National Highways for UK roads, mechanically drops and collects cones from a traffic-management vehicle, but it is operated by a person from the vehicle cab rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cone laying to close a roadway. Recorded to show that the most mature commercial cone-laying product is cab-controlled, so it cannot support a positive autonomous judgment.

sources.title: The Force — Autonomous Security Force | Knightscope (K5 product page)
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 is a commercially deployed autonomous security robot that patrols parking lots, campuses and walkways of client facilities, sensing entry points and activity; it has no manipulator arms and cannot place tape, cones or barriers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous perimeter patrol of a facility. It substantiates only the 'check the perimeter' half of this task inside institutionally controlled premises; with no arms it cannot erect the cordon, so it cannot complete an instance on its own.

sources.title: This robot crossed a line it shouldn't have because humans told it to | TechCrunch
sources.claim: A commercially operating sidewalk delivery robot drove under police tape and through an active Los Angeles crime scene, showing that fielded autonomous ground robots do not reliably interpret crime-scene cordons in public settings.
sources.transferJustification: Context for unstructured public-street scenes: even mature autonomous sidewalk robots do not handle real crime-scene cordons, supporting the negative judgment at E3.

tasks.label: Maintain surveillance of establishments to obtain identifying information on suspects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Static covert stakeout of a suspect business or residence from an unmarked vehicle or nearby vantage point on a public street: hours-long watch, logging arrivals and departures, long-lens photos of individuals, recording license plates, repositioning to avoid being burned, and writing up the observations.

Surveillance of an establishment sited inside institution-controlled premises \a ttel a tenant unit in an industrial park, a storefront in a mall, a warehouse in a logistics yard or port, an apartment complex or campus \a la: sustained observation of the entrance/lot, capture of plates and usable imagery of visitors, coordinated with on-site security and CCTV.

Covert camera surveillance of an establishment: placing or servicing a concealed/pole camera on a utility pole, parked vehicle or adjacent structure covering the entrance on a public street, then maintaining coverage over days or weeks and extracting plates, faces and pattern-of-life identifiers.

Close/undercover observation inside the establishment itself \a la bar, nightclub, pawn shop, massage parlor, retail store \a la: entering, blending with patrons and staff, watching transactions and specific individuals, obtaining names, descriptions and associates, sometimes with brief conversational contact.

Mobile surveillance off the establishment: following a subject who leaves, on foot or by vehicle through city traffic, to establish identity, residence, vehicle and associates, staying undetected and coordinating with a surveillance team.

sources.title: How the K5 Robot Patrols Without Human Help
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots run continuous unattended patrols on client property, navigating complex sites and self-recharging without hands-on human oversight.

sources.title: Prevent Crime with Knightscope
sources.claim: Persistent autonomous K5 patrol has produced exactly the investigative product of this task: identifying information on suspects (license-plate identifications, HD video of persons) handed to law enforcement, including sustained coverage over a four-month BOLO.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous security patrol; it transfers because the output sought here — plate reads and usable imagery of persons frequenting a location, over an extended watch — is the same identifying information the detective's surveillance produces.

sources.title: Knightscope Begins Shipping 5th Generation K5 ASR
sources.claim: K5 units have autonomously operated for years across institution-controlled human work facilities: parking structures, corporate campuses, hospitals, transit hubs, casinos, malls and warehouses.

sources.title: Percepto Security Solutions: AI-Powered Autonomous Site Monitoring
sources.claim: Percepto's drone-in-a-box performs persistent AI-driven security patrols of industrial sites to detect intruders and monitor perimeters, operating BVLOS with no on-site personnel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous perimeter surveillance of a facility; it transfers because maintaining continuous camera coverage of a site's approaches and capturing imagery of the people who appear is the same sensing-and-recording function as staking out an establishment.

sources.system: Asylon DroneDog (Q-UGV) and Guardian sUAS with DroneIQ
sources.title: Case Studies — Asylon Robotics (Kia Georgia, GXO)
sources.claim: Asylon's ground robot and aerial drones fly/drive routine perimeter patrols with day/night EO and thermal imaging at manufacturing plants, distribution centers and stadiums, with hundreds of thousands of autonomous missions logged.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic perimeter security at fixed facilities; consistent scheduled observation of a site's access points with recorded video is the sensing core of maintaining surveillance on an establishment.

sources.title: Asylon Robotics' DroneDogs and other robots will test warplanes for the Air Force
sources.claim: Asylon's fielded robotic security systems have accumulated large numbers of autonomous missions for civilian and military clients.
sources.transferJustification: Same perimeter-surveillance transfer as above; cited to establish deployment maturity and autonomy at scale.

sources.system: Skydio X10 with Dock for X10 / Skydio Autonomy
sources.title: DSEI 2025: Autonomous Skydio Dock for X10 expands US police emergency response and infrastructure security
sources.claim: Skydio's docked X10 flies independently, avoids obstacles and tracks subjects without operator input for police response and persistent monitoring, but is fielded as incident-response overwatch under a remote pilot in command rather than as a multi-hour covert stakeout of a specific address.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous aerial overwatch for police; cited to test whether public-street (E3) covert surveillance of an establishment is substantiated — the fielded use is short incident response with a supervising pilot, not sustained covert identification work.

tasks.label: Perform undercover assignments and maintain surveillance, including monitoring authorized wiretaps.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Fixed-point surveillance ('stakeout') of an outdoor location: sitting in an unmarked vehicle or covert observation post for hours watching a residence, business, storage unit or parking lot; logging arrivals/departures, photographing people, recording license plates, and radioing the team when the target moves. Public street, all weather, day or night.

Mobile vehicle surveillance: following a target vehicle through city streets and highways over a period of hours to identify destinations, stash houses and contacts, using multi-unit rotation so the tail is not 'burned', and handing off to an arrest or interdiction team.

Foot and interior surveillance: following a subject on foot from a vehicle drop, through stores, malls, transit stations, hotel lobbies, apartment buildings and bars; observing meetings and hand-offs indoors, staying close enough to see but not be recognized.

Short-term undercover contact operations: posing as a buyer or seller for a controlled narcotics buy, a stolen-goods purchase, a vice/decoy sting, or a meeting arranged from an online chat; negotiating face-to-face with the suspect while wearing a wire, handling buy money and evidence, and signaling the cover team.

Wire-room monitoring of court-authorized Title III intercepts at the agency facility: live-listening to intercepted calls with headphones at a monitoring console, minimizing non-pertinent calls per the order, logging and summarizing pertinent calls, identifying voices, and alerting surveillance teams to real-time developments.

Technical surveillance work: covertly installing and servicing a pole camera, covert video unit, or court-authorized GPS tracker on a target vehicle at night; and monitoring the resulting remote camera feeds and tracker data from the office.

sources.system: Skydio X10 / Dock for X10 / DFR Command
sources.title: Drone as First Responder (DFR) for Public Safety | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio's Drone as First Responder system keeps X10 drones in city-wide docks charged around the clock; drones autonomously reach incidents and can be flown fully autonomously BVLOS with no visual observer, giving persistent aerial overwatch of locations in ordinary urban settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial overwatch on police calls for service. Transfers to detective fixed-point surveillance because the object of observation (people and vehicles at an outdoor address), the sensing precision (zoom/thermal ID of persons and plates) and the environment (public streets) are the same.

sources.system: Skydio X10 / X10D with Skydio Autonomy, Dock for X10
sources.title: DSEI 2025: Autonomous Skydio Dock for X10 expands US police emergency response and infrastructure security
sources.claim: Skydio Autonomy on the X10/X10D allows the aircraft to fly independently, avoid obstacles and ..., so one operator can supervise several aircraft rather than fly each one.

sources.system: Flock Aerodome (Vehicle Follow, Inflight LPR, Multi-Drone Operations)
sources.title: Flock Aerodome Software Updates: Fall 2025
sources.claim: Flock's Aerodome DFR platform, used by police agencies, adds autonomous vehicle following: with one click the drone trails a moving vehicle, matching speed and direction and predicting its path behind obstructions, while reading plates in flight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: DFR pursuit/overwatch of a suspect vehicle. Transfers to investigative mobile surveillance because it is the same act - keeping continuous covert visual contact with a moving target vehicle on public roads and recording its plate and destinations.

sources.title: Skydio X10 | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio X10 tracking autonomy keeps people and vehicles in frame and automatically reacquires them when they briefly leave view, outperforming manual flight for sustained tracking.

sources.system: Autonomous Surveillance Towers (Anduril Sentry / AST program)
sources.developer: Anduril Industries / US Customs and Border Protection
sources.title: CBP Is Expanding Its Surveillance Tower Program at the U.S.-Mexico Border–And We're Mapping It | EFF
sources.claim: CBP has installed hundreds of Autonomous Surveillance Towers along the US border; the towers automatically detect and track people and vehicles at long range in open, unimproved terrain and cue agents, replacing agents watching a sector by eye.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: persistent border sector watch by a federal law-enforcement agency. Transfers to detective fixed-point surveillance: continuous unattended observation of an outdoor area with automatic detection, tracking and alerting on persons and vehicles.

sources.system: DFR drone program (San Francisco PD, presented at IACP 2025)
sources.title: IACP 2025 Quick Take: How three agencies are scaling Drone as First Responder (DFR) programs
sources.claim: In real operations, agency DFR drones have maintained visual contact with fleeing suspects across city waterfronts and streets and directed officers to them, showing the platforms work in ordinary unstructured public environments; the degree of autonomy in these specific flights is not stated.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the environment only: shows the deployment setting (public streets and waterfront) in which the autonomous tracking features cited above are used. Not relied on for a positive judgment.

roles.title: Police Identification and Records Officers
aliases: Police Crime Scene Technician (Police Crime Scene Tech)
roles.description: Collect evidence at crime scene, classify and identify fingerprints, and photograph evidence for use in criminal and civil cases.

tasks.label: Photograph crime or accident scenes for evidence records.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor crime scene in a private residence or apartment (burglary, assault, unattended death): tech works room to room in a cluttered, as-found space with mixed/low light, shoots overall, mid-range and close-up frames, places evidence placards, scales and off-camera flash for latent marks, blood, weapons and points of entry.

Traffic collision on a public roadway needing the full photographic record: overall views of final rest positions, tire marks and debris, plus ground-level close-ups of vehicle damage, VIN plates, occupant compartment, restraints and fluid trails, often at night, in weather, under traffic control.

Major crash or large outdoor scene where the deliverable produced by the mapping/reconstruction member is the aerial photogrammetric photoset of the scene (vehicle positions, roadway evidence, debris field) captured before the road is cleared and used for the court-ready orthomosaic/3D model.

Crime scene inside a business or institution (convenience store robbery, bank, school, hospital, office): overall and mid-range views of the premises, close-ups of tills, doors, damage, blood or casings with scales, worked around fixed shelving and counters while staff are excluded.

Open-air crime scene in a parking lot, alley, yard or field: locating and close-up photographing small evidence items (shell casings, blood drops, footwear/tire impressions) with placards and scales, oblique lighting for impressions, plus overall establishing frames.

Vehicle or large item towed to the agency's processing bay/impound garage and photographed there for the evidence record: full exterior 360, damage detail, undercarriage and tires, VIN plate, interior views and items in situ, under controlled lighting on department premises.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan for Documenting Evidence for Public Safety
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan lets a police drone autonomously fly the capture pattern over a defined volume (a crash or crime scene, a vehicle) and return a complete high-resolution photoset for photogrammetric reconstruction.

sources.system: Skydio X10 with Map Capture / 3D Scan
sources.title: Drones for Crash & Crime Scene Documentation
sources.claim: Skydio's own crash/crime scene guidance describes the drone-derived orthomosaic and 3D model as a supplement to scene photography, indicating aerial autonomous capture does not replace the ground-level photographic record.

sources.system: Police drone photogrammetry workflow (drone + Global Mapper Pro Pixels to Points)

sources.title: Drone Mapping Transforms Police Crash Investigations: A Blue Marble Geographics Case Study
sources.claim: A US police forensic mapping team documents serious crash scenes on public roadways by flying a planned drone mission that captures hundreds of overlapping high-resolution images, yielding court-ready scene documentation.

sources.system: Maryland State Police drone mapping program (PIX4Dmatic / PIX4Dcatch)
sources.title: Interview: forensic accident reconstruction with PIX4D
sources.claim: A state police crash team has used drone mapping as its routine scene-documentation method on hundreds of crash and crime scenes, cutting scene mapping to about 20 minutes, though terrestrial scans are merged in for full coverage.

sources.system: PhotoRobot Carousel 5000 / Robotic Arm studio systems
sources.title: Car Turntables - 360-Degree Automotive Photography
sources.claim: Commercial robotic photo studios (motorized heavy-duty turntables plus robot camera arms) capture complete standardized photo sets of whole automobiles at high throughput in a purpose-built booth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated vehicle merchandising photography. It documents the same object class (a whole vehicle) to a fixed, repeatable frame list under controlled lighting in a machine-built booth, which is what evidentiary vehicle documentation in a processing bay requires.

sources.title: UVeye Unveils UV360: Instant AI-Powered Pre-Owned Vehicle Merchandising
sources.claim: Automated drive-through vehicle scanners in commercial use at hundreds of dealerships capture high-resolution imagery of a vehicle's exterior, underbody and tires in seconds and flag damage, producing 360-degree image sets without a photographer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated vehicle condition inspection. Same object (a vehicle brought to a fixed station), same output type (a complete high-resolution image record of exterior, underbody and damage), so it transfers to photographing a towed vehicle at a processing bay.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Leica BLK ARC
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics' Spot
sources.claim: The leading autonomous mobile reality-capture system for interiors runs pre-recorded Autowalk routes on a quadruped in plants, warehouses and enclosed ... and returns laser scans, not evidence-grade photographs of newly encountered items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor reality capture. It is the closest deployed analogue to robotic indoor scene documentation; its need for a human-taught route and its laser-scan output show why it does not deliver forensic photography of an unfamiliar scene.

sources.claim: Robotic documentation of an indoor crime scene (mapping/gathering evidence, analyzing blood smears) exists only as a speculative research prototype with sub-90% task performance.

tasks.label: Submit evidence to supervisors, crime labs, or court officials for legal proceedings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-scene/end-of-shift evidence booking at the agency: the ID officer packages collected items (clothing, swabs, cartridge casings, latent lift cards, drugs, a cleared firearm) in the correct container type, seals each with tamper-evident tape and initials, writes/prints item labels, completes the property/chain-of-custody record in the RMS, and places packages in numbered temporary evidence lockers in the property intake room. Items are heterogeneous in size, wet/dry, and hazard class; the room is a controlled, badge-access police facility.

In-facility submission run: carrying already sealed, labeled evidence packages plus completed lab request forms from the CSI/ID unit to the crime lab or property-room evidence-receiving counter in the same building or government campus, transferring custody to a receiving technician who scans/signs and issues a receipt. Interior corridors, elevators, badge-controlled doors, staff present.

Across-town transport: loading sealed evidence packages/boxes into a vehicle and driving on public streets to a regional crime lab, medical examiner, or state lab drop point, parking, and delivering the packages to the receiving dock/window (or handing to a contracted courier for shipment).

Court submission: pulling a specific sealed item from property-room shelving on a subpoena, transporting it to the courthouse (public roads and sidewalks), clearing courthouse security screening with credentials, signing the item over to the clerk or prosecutor for admission, and re-securing/returning it afterward.

Digital evidence submission from the ID office: offloading camera/body-cam media, uploading crime-scene photos and video to the digital evidence management system, submitting latent prints to AFIS/NGI, and producing labeled disc/USB copies that are packaged and routed to the prosecutor. Desk workstation and publishing appliance in a controlled office.

sources.system: ST Engineering Aethon Zena RX / TUG
sources.title: ST Engineering Aethon Launches ZenaRx: Redefining Secure Delivery of Medications, Specimens and Sensitive Goods in Hospitals
sources.claim: Aethon's Zena RX / TUG autonomous mobile robots are deployed in hospitals to move medications and laboratory specimens between pharmacy, labs and units, with latched cabinets, biometric and PIN authentication so only authorized staff can take custody of the load.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: secure intra-facility transfer of custody-sensitive sealed specimen packages. It transfers to submitting sealed evidence to a lab/property counter inside a building: comparable object size and fragility, corridor/elevator navigation, and an authenticated handover that documents who took the item.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators operate in more than 25 US ... running deliveries including lab samples, having completed over 300,000 pharmacy deliveries by May 2025 and 1 million deliveries overall.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fetch-and-deliver of lab samples and pharmacy items through occupied hospital corridors. Same physical act as walking sealed evidence packages to a lab or property-room receiving counter in an institutionally controlled building.

sources.title: SP 200 with Open Control Center Robotic Prescription Dispensing System
sources.claim: ScriptPro robotic prescription dispensing systems autonomously fill, label and collate up to 150 vials per ... under barcode control in working pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: barcode-controlled containerizing, labeling and collating of legally accountable items. Packaging and labeling booked evidence into containers with a machine-readable record is the same class of act at comparable precision, when the item is presented to the machine.

sources.title: WASP - Copan Diagnostics
sources.claim: Copan's WASP walk-away specimen processor autonomously handles specimen containers in clinical labs, decapping and recapping tubes and reading barcode labels on containers from any angle with LIS integration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pre-analytic handling, identification and routing of chain-of-identity-critical samples inside a purpose-built machine line. Comparable to machine intake, labeling and binning of sealed evidence containers when items are presented on a fixtured line.

sources.system: Amazon automated packaging machines / Universal Robotic Labeller
sources.title: Amazon to deploy automated packaging machines across Europe, reducing waste for millions of customer orders
sources.claim: Amazon has deployed automated packaging machines that build made-to-fit paper bags and boxes around individual items and apply shipping labels, including a high-speed Universal Robotic Labeller for irregularly shaped packages.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: enclosing a heterogeneous single item in a container, sealing it and applying a tracked identifying label. That is the physical core of packaging and sealing an evidence item for submission, given the item is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Gatik Becomes First U.S. Company to Operate Fully Driverless Trucks at Scale for Commercial Deliveries
sources.claim: Gatik operates fully driverless (no driver or safety observer) box trucks making daily commercial deliveries on public highways and surface streets in Texas, Arkansas and Arizona, with 60,000 driverless orders completed since mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless transport of sealed, accountable cargo between two fixed facilities on public roads, with staff loading and receiving at each end. This is the transport leg of taking evidence packages across town to a crime lab or ME drop point.

sources.title: Matternet Begins Drone Delivery Operations for NHS Across Central London
sources.claim: Matternet's M2 drones fly autonomous BVLOS routes carrying diagnostic samples and laboratory specimens between hospital campuses, operating commercially in Switzerland since 2017, the US since 2019, and London for the NHS in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-to-point transport of small sealed specimen packages between institutions over uncontrolled public space, with authenticated load/unload at fixed stations — the same function as couriering sealed evidence packages to a lab.

sources.title: Serve Robotics Builds 2,000 Autonomous Delivery Robots, Creating Largest Sidewalk Delivery Fleet in the U.S.
sources.claim: Serve Robotics operates the largest US sidewalk delivery fleet, having built and deployed more than 2,000 autonomous delivery robots by December 2025 for last-mile deliveries on public sidewalks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended last-mile carriage of a small sealed parcel in a locked compartment across public sidewalks, released only to the authenticated recipient — comparable to short-haul courier delivery of a sealed evidence package.

sources.title: Law Enforcement – Rimage
sources.claim: Rimage Evidence Disc Systems are robotic disc-publishing appliances used by local, state and federal law ... to automatically copy, print and export digital evidence to portable disc media.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain: producing the physical media copy of digital evidence for submission to prosecutors and courts. The appliance's robotic picker loads blanks, burns, prints identifying labels and outputs finished discs without an operator.

tasks.label: Testify in court and present evidence.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Look for trace evidence, such as fingerprints, hairs, fibers, or shoe impressions, using alternative light sources when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential or commercial burglary scene: officer walks the premises as found (cluttered rooms, forced windows/doors, counters, glass, drawers), uses oblique/flashlight and powder to hunt latent prints on entry points and moved objects, scans floors and windowsills for dust shoe impressions, marks and photographs what is found.

Indoor violent-crime scene (homicide, assault, sexual assault) in a home or apartment: room darkened, orange goggles and ALS swept over bedding, carpet, furniture and clothing to locate biological stains, hairs and fibers; suspected areas marked for collection amid disturbed furnishings and biohazard.

Vehicle brought into the agency's processing bay or impound garage: exterior painted panels, glass and door handles dusted for latents; interior seats, footwells and headliner searched with ALS and tape lifts for hairs, fibers and shoe impressions on pedals/kick panels.

Outdoor scene (yard, alley, parking lot, roadside): search in daylight or at night with portable ALS/oblique light for shoe and tire impressions in soil, mud or dust, discarded items bearing prints, and trace on fences or points of entry, under weather and lighting the officer takes as found.

Evidence-processing room at the agency: submitted items (clothing, bedding, weapons, packaging, documents) laid out and examined item by item — visual/oblique inspection, ALS sweep in a darkened room, cyanoacrylate fuming and powders, tape-lifting of garments — to locate latent prints, hairs and fibers.

Bench-instrument screening in the lab of already-collected samples: tape lifts, debris and GSR stubs presented to a microscope or SEM stage and searched systematically for microtrace particles and fibers, with findings classified and reported.

sources.system: Automated SEM particle search and characterization (GSR)
sources.date: 1987 (method established; still the basis of current automated GSR search)
sources.title: Automated gunshot residue particle search and characterization - PubMed
sources.claim: Automated SEM particle-search programs run an unattended search of a presented specimen stub, sizing, chemically typing and identifying gunshot-residue particles without an operator driving each step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine search of a presented specimen for microscopic trace particles. It transfers to bench screening of collected trace samples (tape lifts, stubs) because the objects (micron-scale particles/fibers), the required detection precision, and the fixtured in-instrument environment are the same; it does not transfer to in-situ scene searching, which involves locomotion, surface selection and powder/ALS application on uncontrolled surfaces.

sources.title: Optimizing the Automated Analysis of Inorganic Gunshot Residue Particles by SEM-EDX: From Synthetic Particle Standards to More Time-Efficient Settings for Daily Casework
sources.claim: Automated SEM-EDX particle analysis is used as routine, validated casework procedure in operating forensic laboratories for detecting and classifying inorganic GSR particles on presented stubs.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: it substantiates that machine search of a fixtured specimen for microscopic trace evidence is accepted at casework quality, which is the bench-screening portion of 'look for trace evidence'.

sources.system: Desktop SEM-EDS with automated particle search (e.g., Phenom-class)
sources.title: Desktop SEM for Forensics | GSR & Trace Evidence | NanoImages
sources.claim: Commercial desktop SEM-EDS systems sold to forensic labs perform automated particle search that locates GSR particles and also support fiber morphology examination on presented samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated microtrace particle/fiber search on a fixtured specimen in a laboratory instrument; comparable objects and precision to bench screening of collected trace samples.

sources.title: CRIME-LITE AUTO - Guard-All
sources.claim: The leading forensic 'automated' evidence-search product for item examination is an operator-held/operator-driven semi-automated screening workstation, not an autonomous machine: an examiner presents and illuminates the item and runs preset examinations.

sources.developer: EU H2020 SHUTTLE consortium (incl. Netherlands Forensic Institute)
sources.title: Interpol review of fibres and textiles 2019-2022 - PMC
sources.claim: Automated search and classification of ... tape lifts for forensic laboratories was still at the prototype stage under an EU pre-commercial procurement project.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (Massachusetts State Police bomb squad)
sources.title: 'Spot' the robot dog assists Mass. State Police in high-risk situations
sources.claim: Robots fielded by police at actual crime scenes are teleoperated platforms used for standoff situational awareness and hazardous-scene entry, not for searching surfaces for trace evidence.

tasks.label: Dust selected areas of crime scene and lift latent fingerprints, adhering to proper preservation procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Residential burglary scene inside a private home: the officer surveys the point of entry and rooms the suspect touched, selects likely surfaces (window sills and frames, glass panes, door edges, jewelry box, dresser drawers, ransacked items), applies black or magnetic powder with a fiberglass/feather brush using very light pressure appropriate to each surface, evaluates ridge detail, photographs prints of value with scale, lifts with clear tape or hinge lifters onto backing cards, and labels each card with location, date, orientation and case number.

Vehicle processing: a burglarized or recovered stolen car handled at the scene, at an impound lot, or in the agency's processing bay. The officer dusts exterior door handles, window glass, mirrors, trunk lid and interior surfaces (rearview mirror, console, gearshift, door panels) in confined and awkward positions, works around dirt, weather residue and textured plastics, then photographs and lifts developed prints onto cards.

Commercial burglary at a retail store, restaurant, warehouse or office: after-hours processing of a forced door or smashed window, cash register/till, safe or pried cabinet, with broken glass, tool marks and merchandise disturbed. Officer dusts selected surfaces, avoids over-powdering, lifts and preserves prints, and works alongside responding officers and the business owner.

Bench processing in the ID unit/crime lab of items submitted or seized (bottles, cans, firearms and magazines, tools, packaging, documents, recovered property), often after cyanoacrylate fuming: item placed on the bench or in a downdraft powder station, dusted with an appropriate powder, developed prints photographed and tape-lifted onto backing cards, packaging resealed and chain of custody documented.

Major or violent crime scene (homicide, shooting, aggravated assault, sexual assault) indoors or outdoors: methodical, heavily documented dusting of selected surfaces amid biohazards, blood, clutter and other evidence that must not be disturbed, with lifts preserved, sequenced against other collection methods (DNA swabs first), and defensible in court.

sources.title: MVC/D fingerprint fuming cabinets
sources.claim: The most automated commercially available latent-print development hardware is the cyanoacrylate fuming cabinet, which runs preset humidification/fuming/extraction cycles on items a human loads into the chamber. It does not select areas, apply powder with a brush, or tape-lift and mount prints, so it does not complete the task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated chemical development of latent prints on submitted items in a lab. Transfer fails: the cabinet is a fixed chamber with no manipulator, so it cannot dust selected areas, judge ridge detail, or lift and mount prints; a human loads the item and performs all powdering, photography and lifting.

sources.system: Contactless automated latent fingerprint extraction prototype (Metropolitan Police Service collaboration)
sources.developer: University research team with UK Metropolitan Police Service
sources.title: Contactless automated lifting of latent fingerprints from difficult curved surfaces - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: State-of-the-art automated latent print 'lifting' research is photographic and contactless, implemented as a handheld device operated by a person rather than a robotic manipulator; no robotic system performs the powder-and-tape lift.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: capturing latent prints from objects at a scene. Transfer fails: the device is held and aimed by a human officer (no embodied autonomy), and the 'automation' is image processing, not physical dusting, lifting or preservation of a lift card.

sources.title: Figure Humanoid Robots Sort Packages Non-Stop in 24/7 Demo
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous general-purpose manipulation demonstrated at scale is repetitive parcel handling in a structured warehouse; no demonstration exists of light-touch fiberglass-brush powdering, ridge-detail assessment, or adhesive tape lifting of latent prints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-duration autonomous dual-arm manipulation of varied objects. Transfer fails: parcel induction involves coarse grasp-and-place of rigid packages with wide error tolerance, whereas latent print work needs sub-millimetre force control on fragile deposits, perceptual judgment of ridge quality, and court-defensible preservation - none demonstrated.

tasks.label: Analyze and process evidence at crime scenes, during autopsies, or in the laboratory, wearing protective equipment and using powders and chemicals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Burglary/theft scene at a private residence or small business: officer suits up (gloves, mask), surveys point of entry and touched surfaces, brushes black or magnetic powder on door frames, window glass, drawers and items, photographs developed marks with scale, tape-lifts and mounts them on backing cards, swabs touch-DNA areas, packages and logs items on scene.

Violent-crime scene (homicide, shooting, assault), indoors or on a public street: photograph and document, place markers, collect cartridge cases and projectiles, perform presumptive blood/GSR tests, swab bloodstains, apply chemical enhancement (luminol, amido black, leucocrystal violet) to floors or walls in situ, collect and package weapons and clothing, all while wearing PPE and often in poor light or weather.

Vehicle processed in the agency's secure evidence bay/garage: officer superglue-tents or powders the interior and exterior, examines with an alternate light source, photographs and lifts prints from glass, mirrors, door handles and dash, swabs steering wheel and airbag, recovers trace evidence and casings from the cabin, then packages and documents.

Bench processing of items collected from scenes in the ID unit's processing lab: sequence the methods for each item (firearm, plastic bag, bottle, knife, paper), run cyanoacrylate fuming, apply fluorescent dye stain or ninhydrin/DFO to porous items, examine in a darkroom under an ALS, photograph developed marks to AFIS quality, lift where appropriate, repackage and record chain of custody.

Attending an autopsy at the medical examiner's morgue: photograph the decedent, wounds and clothing, collect and air-dry clothing, take fingernail scrapings, hair standards and GSR/oral swabs, obtain postmortem fingerprints from the decedent, receive and package projectiles or trace handed over by the pathologist, all in PPE.

Instrument-based analysis of a collected sample in the agency lab or booking area: load a buccal or evidence swab into a Rapid DNA instrument or an automated extraction deck and produce a searchable DNA profile / screening result for the case file.

sources.system: ANDE 6C / RapidHIT ID Rapid DNA booking systems
sources.developer: ANDE Corporation / Thermo Fisher (FBI-approved for NDIS)
sources.title: Rapid DNA | Law Enforcement (FBI)
sources.claim: Rapid DNA instruments approved by the FBI for booking stations (e.g., ANDE 6C, RapidHIT ID) take a swab and produce a CODIS-searchable DNA profile fully automatically, without human interpretation, and are deployed in US law enforcement booking stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laboratory analysis of an evidence swab. It matches the ID officer's instrument-based lab instance in object (a swab), setting (a closed purpose-built instrument on a bench), and accepted output (a searchable profile), so performance carries over directly.

sources.system: Hamilton Microlab VANTAGE Liquid Handling System (forensic casework extraction)
sources.developer: Hamilton Company (validation by a public crime laboratory)
sources.title: Validation of a High-Throughput Automated Liquid Handling DNA Extraction System to Maximize Efficiency in Forensic Casework
sources.claim: Robotic liquid-handling workstations are validated and used in crime laboratories to extract and purify DNA from forensic evidence samples, replacing manual chemical bench work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chemical processing of evidence samples in a laboratory. The robot pipettes reagents onto forensic swab extracts in a purpose-built enclosed deck, the same chemistry-handling step an ID officer performs at the bench for sample screening.

sources.title: Safefume 360 Automatic Cyanoacrylate Fuming Chambers
sources.claim: Commercial cyanoacrylate fuming chambers run the complete glue-development cycle under machine control once a human has hung the evidence inside; the chamber does not examine, photograph, lift, or repackage the item.

sources.title: RECOVER LFT | Foster + Freeman
sources.claim: The most advanced commercial fingerprint chemistry system for difficult surfaces is described by its maker as only semi-automating the chemistry, with human handling, examination and imaging still required.

sources.system: Object-driven optical coherence tomography (OD-OCT) latent fingerprint scanner
sources.developer: Tsinghua University / Institute of Forensic Science China (He et al.)
sources.title: Rapid, autonomous and ultra-large-area detection of latent fingerprints using object-driven optical coherence tomography (Optics Express)
sources.claim: A laboratory research system uses a robotic arm plus optical coherence tomography and deep learning to autonomously scan objects, locate latent fingerprints over large areas, and image them without powders; it is a bench prototype, not validated casework equipment, and does not lift, package or document evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: detecting and imaging latent fingermarks on items. Objects are placed inside the scanner's workspace, so it speaks to fixtured bench processing of small items, not to in-situ scene work or to lifting and packaging.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich/Bern (Virtopsy project)
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine
sources.claim: A robotic system installed at a forensic medicine institute performs automated photogrammetric/optical surface documentation of corpses and image-guided post-mortem needle placement ... and liquid sampling; it does not collect clothing, swabs, nail clippings or postmortem prints.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: documentation and sampling of a body during autopsy. It covers the imaging/sampling portion of the morgue instance on real corpses, but not the collection and packaging of physical evidence items.

sources.system: Mobile robotic surface scanning system for legal medicine
sources.developer: Hamburg University of Technology (TUHH) with forensic medicine partners
sources.title: A mobile robotic approach to autonomous surface scanning in legal medicine (Int J CARS)
sources.claim: A mobile robot performs autonomous full-body RGB-D surface scanning of actual corpses in a legal-medicine setting, achieving ~92% surface coverage; the work is documentation only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: photographic/3D documentation of a body at autopsy. Same setting and subject as the morgue instance, but it performs no evidence collection with powders, chemicals or swabs.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot (Massachusetts State Police bomb squad)
sources.title: 'Spot' the robot dog assists Mass. State Police in high-risk situations
sources.claim: Robots fielded by US police at crime and incident scenes are remotely operated tactical/bomb-squad platforms used for reconnaissance, not autonomous evidence-processing machines.

tasks.label: Package, store and retrieve evidence.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At a crime scene (house, apartment, street, vehicle, business), the technician packages routinely encountered items just collected: swabs and blood-stained clothing into paper bags, cartridge casings and jewelry into envelopes/boxes, drug baggies, a phone or knife into a suitable container; each container is folded/closed, sealed with evidence tape, and marked with case number, item number, date and initials across the seal.

At a scene, packaging bulky, hazardous or awkward items: loaded/unloaded firearms secured in boxes with zip ties, long guns, bloody mattresses and bedding, sharps and biohazard/needles, wet items, vehicle parts, large tools; requires making items safe, contamination control and improvised containers.

Property-room intake/booking: receiving items from officers' temporary lockers and from scene kits, checking each item against the property report, drying wet biological items, weighing narcotics, repackaging/heat-sealing into agency-standard containers, applying barcode labels and entering the item into the evidence management system.

Storing booked evidence inside the property room/warehouse: shelving packages in assigned bin locations, placing biological samples in refrigerators/freezers, firearms in gun racks or vaults, narcotics and cash/jewelry in secured high-value lockers, and recording the storage location for each item.

Retrieving stored evidence on request: locating an item by its recorded location, pulling it from shelf/freezer/vault, verifying package and seal integrity, documenting the chain-of-custody transfer to a detective, lab, prosecutor or defense examiner, and re-storing or routing it for destruction/return after use.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks up individual, diverse products and moves them into specified totes inside fulfillment-center robotic workcells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level piece picking of heterogeneous goods into designated containers. Transfers to evidence handling at E1 because the objects (small clothing, boxed items, bagged goods) are comparable, the required precision is grasp-and-place into a container, and the setting is a purpose-built fenced cell where the work is presented to the machine.

sources.title: CVP Impack | Packsize
sources.claim: The CVP Impack auto-boxing machine automatically measures each single- or multi-item order, constructs a right-sized box around it, tapes it closed, weighs it and applies a printed label, at up to 500 orders/hour with two operators feeding it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fit-to-size packaging, sealing and labeling of individual items in a fulfillment line. Transfers to evidence packaging at E1: the machine chooses a container for the presented item, closes and tapes it (a tamper-evident closure), weighs it and applies a machine-printed identity label equivalent to the case/item label and barcode.

sources.date: 2025-09 (Henry Ford Health deployment announcement); product in market for years
sources.title: BD Rowa Vmax storage and dispensing robot
sources.claim: The BD Rowa Vmax is a commercially deployed pharmacy storage robot that automatically stores individual boxed packs picked from an input belt and retrieves/dispenses them on demand, with over 14,000 installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage and dispensing of individually identified, barcoded small packages in a regulated, audit-tracked setting (pharmacy). Comparable object class (boxes, sealed packets), comparable precision, and full store-and-retrieve cycle with inventory records analogous to chain-of-custody location records.

sources.system: AutoStore (supplied by Dematic, Kardex, Swisslog and others)
sources.date: 2024-09 to 2025-10 (product updates); commercially installed for years
sources.title: AutoStore Automated Storage and Retrieval System | Dematic
sources.claim: AutoStore cubic AS/RS uses fleets of robots that autonomously store and retrieve bins in a dense grid and deliver them to ports ...; it is a widely installed commercial system, including multi-temperature versions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-density automated storage and on-demand retrieval of binned goods with authoritative location records. Directly analogous to placing packaged evidence in an assigned bin location and pulling it back on request in a purpose-built storage machine.

sources.system: BioArc Ultra / BioStore automated cold sample storage
sources.date: 2026-02 (product page); VUMC BioStore II installation reported 2024
sources.title: BioArc™ Ultra Cold Storage System -80°C, Automated, High Density | Azenta Life Sciences
sources.claim: Azenta's BioArc Ultra automated -80 °C store robotically stores and retrieves diverse labware (tubes, vials, bottles, plates, racks, cryoboxes) through up to ten picking stations, and such automated biobank stores are installed at institutions such as VUMC.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: refrigerated/frozen automated storage and retrieval of barcoded biological samples with full custody/inventory audit trail. Directly comparable to freezer storage and retrieval of biological evidence (swabs, blood tubes, sexual-assault kit samples).

sources.system: Automated vertical carousels / automated evidence storage units (Kardex-class VLM/carousel)
sources.title: Use Vertical Space with Automated Evidence Shelving Units
sources.claim: Police property and evidence rooms already install automated vertical carousels that hold evidence in enclosed locking bins and rotate to deliver the requested bin to the operator, with automatic inventory management.
sources.transferJustification: Same domain (police evidence rooms). Shows the purpose-built storage machine is already used for evidence, but the machine only delivers the bin; a human still transfers the item, so it supports E1 storage/retrieval only in combination with the robotic put/pick systems cited above.

sources.title: Humanoid Robotics In 2026: The Race From Pilot To Platform
sources.claim: Agility's Digit humanoid works full-time in a GXO logistics facility moving standardized totes between autonomous mobile robots ..., surpassing 100,000 totes moved without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile handling of containers inside a human work facility. Cited to bound E2: the demonstrated work is uniform totes at fixed presentation points, not locating and pulling heterogeneous sealed packages from open shelving, freezers and vaults in an evidence room.

tasks.label: Process film and prints from crime or accident scenes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Take fingerprints.
Perform emergency work during off-hours.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Middle-of-the-night callout to a violent-crime scene inside a private residence or apartment (homicide, shooting, suspicious death): secure and walk the scene, shoot overall/mid-range/close-up photographs with scales under artificial light, sketch and measure the room, dust and lift latent prints from doors, glass and weapons, locate, swab, photograph and package biological and trace evidence, maintain chain of custody, and write the scene report.

Night or weekend callout to an outdoor scene taken as found (fatal traffic collision, street shooting, body in a field or parking lot) in rain, cold or darkness: set portable lighting, photograph the scene and roadway, map it with total station/laser scanner or drone, place and photograph evidence markers, recover cartridge casings, blood swabs, vehicle debris and personal property while traffic and bystanders are managed around the scene.

After-hours response to a commercial burglary, robbery or arson scene (store, warehouse, pharmacy, bank): photograph forced entry and damage, process broken glass, counters, safes and cash drawers for latent prints, cast or photograph tool marks and shoe impressions, recover surveillance video and packaged evidence from a ransacked interior.

Off-hours response to a hospital emergency department or the medical examiner's facility: photograph a living victim's or suspect's injuries, collect and package clothing, swabs and bullet fragments handed over by medical staff, and take postmortem fingerprints/palm prints from a decedent for identification.

Called back to the police ID unit/garage after hours for urgent processing: photograph and process an impounded vehicle bay by bay, fume/powder and photograph latent prints on recovered firearms, bottles and documents, fingerprint an in-custody arrestee or unidentified decedent, package and log evidence, and run an urgent AFIS search and comparison.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan - Accident Reconstruction | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio's 3D Scan autonomously plans and flies the capture path to build high-resolution 3D documentation of accident and crime scenes; it is a commercial product used by police agencies, but it only produces imagery/photogrammetry and performs no evidence handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aerial/photogrammetric scene documentation, one sub-step of crime-scene processing. It transfers only to overhead imaging; it cannot dust and lift latent prints, swab or package evidence, or maintain chain of custody, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

sources.system: Spot + Leica BLK ARC (Autowalk reality capture)
sources.title: Leica BLK ARC now the first certified reality capture device available for Boston Dynamics' Spot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot carrying a Leica BLK ARC can execute a laser-scanning Autowalk mission without human intervention, but deployments are routine reality capture of plants, warehouses and enclosed structures, with no manipulation of objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous 3D documentation of an indoor facility, comparable to scene mapping. Transfer is limited to repeated scans of a pre-taught route in a controlled facility; it provides no evidence recognition, latent print processing, or collection, so it cannot complete an evidence-processing instance.

sources.system: PRIME (Police Robot for Inspection and Mapping of underwater Evidence)
sources.developer: University of Bath / UK police collaboration
sources.title: A prototype autonomous robot for underwater crime scene investigation and emergency response - Journal of Field Robotics
sources.claim: PRIME is a research prototype police USV that autonomously runs search patterns and detected a submerged body-like target in a harbour; it maps and images underwater scenes but does not recover or process evidence.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic search of a crime scene environment. It is a prototype sensing platform with no manipulator, so it cannot photograph with scales, lift prints, or package evidence; it does not substantiate completion of any instance here.

sources.title: Boston Dynamic Robot Dogs Increasingly Used By Police Departments - Bloomberg
sources.claim: Police quadrupeds such as Spot are being adopted by US departments for standoffs, hostage situations and hazmat incidents, where they are driven by operators rather than working autonomously on scene-processing tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic entry into police incident scenes. Operator-driven tactical reconnaissance does not carry over to autonomous evidence documentation and collection, and teleoperated use cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Biomek 2000 / Qiagen BioRobot EZ1 forensic workstations
sources.title: Automated Processing of Forensic Casework Samples Using Robotic Workstations Equipped with Nondisposable Tips: Contamination Prevention
sources.claim: Forensic laboratories run liquid-handling robots (e.g., Biomek workstations, BioRobot EZ1) that automate DNA extraction and PCR setup from fixtured tubes and plates; these are bench instruments confined to biology-section sample chemistry.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated laboratory sample processing in a purpose-built instrument (E1). It transfers only to pipetting of pre-extracted, fixtured samples in a DNA section; it does nothing for vehicle processing, latent print development and lifting, evidence photography, or postmortem printing.

tasks.label: Serve as technical advisor and coordinate with other law enforcement workers or legal personnel to exchange information on crime scene collection activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Create sketches and diagrams, by hand or computer software, to depict crime scenes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rough field sketch drawn on a clipboard/notepad at an indoor death or assault scene in a residence or business: officer notes room outline, doors/windows, body position, and evidence markers with noted measurements, not to scale.

Finished, to-scale diagram produced later at the ID unit office using drafting software (FARO Zone 2D/3D, The Crime Zone, CAD, SmartDraw) from field notes and measurements, formatted with legend, north arrow, and case data for the case file and court exhibit.

Outdoor scene diagram of a traffic fatality or shooting on a roadway/parking lot: roadway geometry, vehicle rest positions, skid marks, shell casings and shot trajectories, sketched in the field and later drafted to scale.

Diagram generated from instrument data — total station point files or laser-scan point clouds imported into diagramming software, then cleaned up, labeled, and rendered into a 2D floor plan or 3D exhibit.

Small-scope detail sketches: a single room's blood-spatter pattern with stringing/area-of-origin annotations, a bullet-trajectory schematic, or a close-up evidence layout sketch appended to the main diagram.

instances.label: Real-time crime center / fusion center shift: operating the agency's networked street CCTV and PTZ cameras (plus ALPR feeds) to locate, follow and record a subject, vehicle or unfolding incident across public streets - slewing/zooming cameras, handing off between poles, capturing evidentiary imagery and time-stamped clips. Cameras look at uncontrolled public roadway scenes, day and night, all weather.

Persistent surveillance of a target location: emplacing and running a pole camera, covert camera or vehicle-mounted camera to document who and what comes and goes at a residence, lot, warehouse or roadway approach over hours to weeks; photographing people, vehicles and plates in an ordinary neighborhood or rural setting with no institutional control.

Aerial documentation: launching and operating a small UAS (DFR dock or hand-launch) to overfly an incident scene, event, or target area in public airspace, streaming and recording video, following a fleeing vehicle, and capturing imagery for the case file.

Radio / spectrum work from a fixed monitoring post inside a police facility, fusion center or collection site: operating scanners, SDR receivers, recorders and direction-finding gear to monitor target nets and radio traffic, logging and recording intercepted transmissions for later exploitation.

Documenting activity at an institutionally controlled site: operating fixed and PTZ cameras, thermal sensors or patrol imagery at a secure facility, military base perimeter, port, courthouse, transit hub or ticketed venue during an operation or event, where the operator's institution controls the premises.

Covert deployment and recovery of collection equipment in the field: concealing and mounting a camera on a pole/tree/utility box, running power or antennas, placing an audio device or tracker on or near a target, then retrieving it without being detected.

sources.claim: CBP's Anduril Autonomous Surveillance Towers autonomously scan open border terrain with radar, slew a camera onto detected movement, classify people/vehicles and alert agents - i.e., the camera-operating and activity-documentation loop performed unattended outdoors.

sources.claim: Fielded scale and currency of autonomous surveillance towers: 350+ standard Sentry towers deployed and 40+ Extended Range towers delivered under a Dec-2025 CBP contract, providing autonomous long-range surveillance of unstructured border terrain.

sources.claim: Commercial off-the-shelf PTZ surveillance cameras used in municipal and public-space video systems detect, classify and automatically pan-tilt-zoom to track people and vehicles without an operator on the joystick.

sources.system: Skydio X10 + Dock, DFR Command (Skydio Autonomy)
sources.title: The BVLOS Revolution Continues: Introducing Multi-Drone Operations
sources.claim: Dock-based Skydio X10 drones fly beyond visual line of ... over US cities for police Drone-as-First-Responder work; onboard autonomy navigates to and from the scene so a single remote pilot can oversee up to four aircraft, with FAA waivers held by NYPD, SFPD, LVMPD and others.

sources.title: Flock Aerodome Software Updates: Fall 2025
sources.claim: Flock's DFR drones autonomously fly to an incident and, on one click, autonomously follow a moving vehicle with the camera slaved to it, reading plates in flight - camera operation and activity documentation over public streets without continuous piloting.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot + Orbit 5.1 with Spot Cam 2
sources.title: Boston Dynamics releases Spot and Orbit 5.1 with new Spot Cam
sources.claim: Spot runs autonomous security-patrol missions inside customer facilities, detecting people and capturing PTZ, panoramic and thermal imagery and alerting operators - unattended camera operation and activity documentation in a structured human work facility.

sources.title: Anduril Industries Announces Pulsar-L
sources.claim: Field-deployable software-defined EW/RF systems autonomously detect, identify and track radio emitters at the tactical edge without an operator tuning the equipment; Pulsar variants are in low-rate production and fielded with US forces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated radio-spectrum collection. The analyst's radio work is scanning/tuning receivers to find, record and log target transmissions; Pulsar performs the same physical receive-and-search function (antennas plus software-defined receivers) autonomously - detect, ID, track emitters - so the equipment-operating step transfers, though content exploitation differs.

sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots patrol parking lots, campuses and malls unattended, streaming 360-degree video and reading license plates while moving; contracts closed across many US states.
